e.en: Aid is money, equipment, or services that are provided for people, countries, or organizations who need them but cannot provide them for themselves.

ex.en: ...regular flights carrying humanitarian aid to Cambodia.
ex.zh: …向柬埔寨运送人道主义援助的定期班机。

ex.en: They have already pledged billions of dollars in aid.
ex.zh: 他们已经承诺了数十亿美元的援助。

e.en: If you perform a task with the aid of something, you need or use that thing to perform that task.

ex.en: He succeeded with the aid of a completely new method he discovered.
ex.zh: 借助于一个他所发现的全新方法，他取得了成功。

e.en: To aid a country, organization, or person means to provide them with money, equipment, or services that they need.

ex.en: ...U.S. efforts to aid Kurdish refugees.
ex.zh: …美国援助库尔德难民的努力。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: 援助的

ex.en: ...government-aided research.
ex.zh: …政府援助的研究。

d: n. 帮助；援助，救助；辅助物，辅助设施；助手；特别津贴，国库税
v. 帮助，援助；促进，有助于
【名】 （Aid）（英、阿拉伯、印）艾德（人名）
n. 布鲁塞尔（比利时首都）
adj. 更长的，较长的，更久的（long 的比较级）
adv. 更久地，更长时间地（long 作副词的比较级）；不再，已不（用于 no longer / not any longer）

e.en: An approved method or course of action is officially accepted as appropriate in a particular situation.

ex.en: The approved method of cleaning is industrial sand-blasting.
ex.zh: 得到正式认可的清洁方法是工业喷砂处理。

ex.en: Approved methods might include destruction of nests and eggs, and the trapping and destruction of geese.
ex.zh: 得到正式认可的方法可能包括对巢和蛋的捣毁以及对鹅的捕杀。

d: adj. （正式）认可的，核准的
v. 同意，赞成；批准，通过；核准（approve 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, usually outdoors.

ex.en: He sold boots at a market stall.
ex.zh: 他在市场的一个摊位上卖靴子。

e.en: The market for a particular type of thing is the number of people who want to buy it, or the area of the world in which it is sold. 需求量;

ex.en: The foreign market was increasingly crucial.
ex.zh: 国外的市场越来越关键了。

e.en: The market refers to the total amount of a product that is sold each year, especially when you are talking about the competition between the companies who sell that product.

ex.en: The two big companies control 72% of the market.
ex.zh: 这两家大公司控制了72%的市场份额。

e.en: If you talk about a market economy, or the market price of something, you are referring to an economic system in which the prices of things depend on how many are available and how many people want to buy them, rather than prices being fixed by governments.

ex.en: Their ultimate aim was a market economy for Hungary.
ex.zh: 他们的最终目标是为匈牙利建立市场经济。

ex.en: He must sell the house for the current market value.
ex.zh: 他必须按照目前的市场价格出售这套房子。

d: n. 集市，市场；交易，交易量；行销地区，购买人群；市场机制；股市；市面，市况
v. 推销，促销；出售；做买卖
adj. 市场的，由市场决定的
【名】 （Market）（塞）马尔凯特 （人名）

e.en: of necessity

ex.en: we must needs go
we will go, if needs must

e.en: what is required; necessities

ex.en: the needs of the third world
his needs are modest

d: v. 需要；有必要，必须（后接带 to 的不定式）（need 的第三人称单数）
n. 需要，需求，必需品（need 的复数）
adv. 必须地，必然地（古语或文学用语，只与 must 连用）

e.en: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

ex.en: He opened the window and looked out.
ex.zh: 他打开窗户往外看。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open window.
ex.zh: …一扇开着的窗户。

e.en: If you open something such as a bottle, box, parcel, or envelope, you move, remove, or cut part of it so you can take out what is inside.

ex.en: I opened the letter.
ex.zh: 我拆开了那封信。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open bottle of milk.
ex.zh: …一瓶打开的牛奶。

d: adj. 开放的，营业的；开着的，敞开的；（身体部位）张开的；露天的，无遮盖的；开阔的，未围上的；可通行的，畅通的；伸开的，展开的；坦率的；不保密的，公开的；易受影响的，易受攻击的；人人可以参加的；（对特定群体）开放的 ；可得到的，可使用的；思想开明的；尚未决定的；（文件夹、文档等）正在使用中的；（胜利者）赢得公开赛的；（票子）未注明旅行日期的；（支票）未签注的；（数）（集合）开的；（元音）开的；（乐）开放的 ；（电路）开路的，断路的；（纺织品）松散的
v. 开，打开；开封，开启；睁开（眼睛），张开（嘴巴）；翻开，展开；开通，开放；开门，营业 ；开业，开幕；（股市）开盘，开市；着手，开始；启动（计算机程序或文件）；开立账户；通往，通向；展现，出现；使某人更乐意考虑某事；断开（电路）；畅谈
n. 户外，野外；公开，泄露；公开赛（Open）；断开（电路）

e.en: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe. 支付;

ex.en: Owners who have already paid for repairs will be reimbursed.
ex.zh: 已经付了修缮费的业主将会得到退费。

ex.en: The wealthier may have to pay a little more in taxes.
ex.zh: 更有钱的人可能得多交点税。

e.en: When you are paid, you get your wages or salary from your employer.

ex.en: The lawyer was paid a huge salary.
ex.zh: 这个律师拿了很高的薪金。

ex.en: I get paid monthly.
ex.zh: 我拿月薪。

e.en: Your pay is the money that you get from your employer as wages or salary.

ex.en: ...their complaints about their pay and conditions.
ex.zh: …他们对薪水和工作条件的不满。

e.en: If you are paid to do something, someone gives you some money so that you will help them or perform some service for them.

ex.en: There are people who are paid to sit around and play games.
ex.zh: 有人受雇闲坐着玩游戏。

d: v. 支付，付款；注意，留心（pay attention 的现在分词/动名词）；（某种做法）有好处，有益（pay 的现在分词）
adj. 有利可图的，赢利的，合算的；付酬的，有报酬的

e.en: If you wave or wave your hand, you move your hand from side to side in the air, usually in order to say hello or goodbye to someone. 挥 (手以示意)

ex.en: Jessica caught sight of Lois and waved to her.
ex.zh: 杰茜卡看到洛伊丝，向她挥了挥手。

ex.en: He grinned, waved, and said, "Hi!"
ex.zh: 他咧嘴笑笑，挥挥手，说道：“嗨！”

e.en: Wave is also a noun. 挥 (手)

ex.en: Steve stopped him with a wave of the hand.
ex.zh: 史蒂夫把手一挥，制止了他。

e.en: If you wave someone away or wave them on, you make a movement with your hand to indicate that they should move in a particular direction. 挥手 (示意某人离开、前进等)

ex.en: Leshka waved him away with a show of irritation.
ex.zh: 廖什卡生气地挥手示意他离开。

ex.en: He waited for a policeman to stop the traffic and wave the people on.
ex.zh: 他等着一位警察来让车辆停下，挥手让众人前行。

e.en: If you wave something, you hold it up and move it rapidly from side to side.

ex.en: Hospital staff were outside to welcome him, waving flags and applauding.
ex.zh: 医院工作人员在院外迎接他，一边挥舞旗帜一边鼓掌。

d: v. 挥手；挥手示意；挥舞，挥动；飘扬，摆动，摇晃；使（头发）略呈波形；（威胁地）举起（某物）
n. 海浪；大海（the waves）；（活动、行为的）爆发，浪潮；涌现的人（或物）；挥手；波，波状运动；（头发的）卷曲；波浪形；（地震、爆炸的）冲击波；人浪（the wave）

e.en: A second is one of the sixty parts that a minute is divided into. People often say "a second" or "seconds" when they simply mean a very short time. 秒;

ex.en: For a few seconds nobody said anything.
ex.zh: 有几秒钟没一个人说话。

ex.en: It only takes forty seconds.
ex.zh: 这只需40秒。

e.en: The second item in a series is the one that you count as number two.

ex.en: ...the second day of his visit to Delhi.
ex.zh: …他访问德里的第二天。

ex.en: ...their second child.
ex.zh: …他们的第二个孩子。

e.en: Second is used before superlative adjectives to indicate that there is only one thing better or larger than the thing you are referring to. 第二…的 (用于形容词最高级前)

ex.en: The party is still the second strongest in Italy.
ex.zh: 该党仍是意大利第二大党。

e.en: You say second when you want to make a second point or give a second reason for something. 第二;

ex.en: First, the weapons should be intended for use only in retaliation after a nuclear attack. Second, the possession of the weapons must be a temporary expedient.
ex.zh: 首先，这些武器应当只在遭受核袭击后反击时才使用。其次，这些武器的拥有必须是一种临时的应急手段。

d: num. 第二（的），第二个（的）；（重要性、规模、质量等）居第二位的；另外的，外加的
n. 秒（时间单位）；片刻，瞬间；秒（角度单位）；次品，二等货；第二次上菜，添菜（seconds）；（车辆的）第二挡；（英国大学本科的）二等成绩学位；（学校或大学的）二年级；（棒球的）二垒；正式支持，附议；（体育俱乐部的）预备队（the seconds）；粗面粉，粗粉面包；（尤指拳击比赛或旧时决斗中的）助手；（乐）二度音程
v. 支持，附议；临时调派，短期调任
adv. 以第二位；第二，其次

e.en: A plant is a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.

ex.en: Water each plant as often as required.
ex.zh: 按要求经常给每棵植物浇水。

e.en: When you plant a seed, plant, or young tree, you put it into the ground so that it will grow there.

ex.en: He says he plans to plant fruit trees and vegetables.
ex.zh: 他说他计划栽种果树和蔬菜。

e.en: 栽种

ex.en: Extensive flooding in the country has delayed planting and many crops are still under water.
ex.zh: 该国大范围的洪水已经延误了栽种，许多庄稼现在还泡在水中。

e.en: When someone plants land with a particular type of plant or crop, they put plants, seeds, or young trees into the land to grow them there. 将 (土地) 种植 (植被)

ex.en: They plan to plant the area with grass and trees.
ex.zh: 他们计划在这个地区植树种草。

ex.en: Recently much of their energy has gone into planting a large vegetable garden.
ex.zh: 最近，他们的大部分精力已经花在种植一个大型蔬菜园上。

d: n. 植物；工厂，发电厂（plant 的复数）
v. 栽种，种植；安置，使固定；秘密放置（如埋设炸弹、栽赃、安插卧底）；灌输，使（想法等）植根于（plant 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A semiconductor is a substance used in electronics whose ability to conduct electricity increases with greater heat.

d: n. 半导体；半导体装置

e.en: A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.

ex.en: I had a letter from my mother last week.
ex.zh: 我上星期收到了母亲的一封信。

ex.en: This has been on my mind all week.
ex.zh: 我整个星期都在想这件事。

e.en: A week is a period of about seven days.

ex.en: Her mother stayed for another two weeks.
ex.zh: 她母亲又呆了两周时间。

ex.en: Only 12 weeks ago he underwent major heart transplant surgery.
ex.zh: 仅仅12周之前，他接受了一次心脏移植的大手术。

e.en: Your working week is the hours that you spend at work during a week. 工作周 (指一周的工作时数)

ex.en: It is not unusual for women to work a 40-hour week.
ex.zh: 女性1周工作40小时并不少见。

e.en: The week is the part of the week that does not include Saturday and Sunday. (除星期六和星期日以外的)

ex.en: ...the hard work of looking after the children during the week.
ex.zh: …除周末外每天都照看孩子的辛苦活。

d: n. 星期，周；一个星期的时间，一周；一周工作时间，工作周；（除去星期六和星期日的）星期，周；活动周（举行某项活动的一周）；（从某天算起的）一周；（某天之前的）一周；一周又一周，接连好几个星期

e.en: An administrator is a person whose job involves helping to organize and supervise the way that an organization or institution functions. 行政人员;

ex.en: On Friday the company's administrators sought permission from a Melbourne court to keep operating.
ex.zh: 在星期五，该公司的管理人员们从一家墨尔本法院取得了继续经营的许可。

d: n. administrator 的复数形式；管理员，行政人员，管理者；（计算机、网络）系统管理员；（法律）遗产管理人；（公司破产）破产管理人

e.en: Advertising is the activity of creating advertisements and making sure people see them.

ex.en: I work in advertising.
ex.zh: 我在广告业工作。

d: n. 广告活动，广告业；（总称）广告
v. 登广告；公布，征聘；宣扬（advertise 的现在分词形式）

e.en: An applicant for something such as a job or a college is someone who makes a formal written request to be considered for it.

ex.en: We have had lots of applicants for these positions.
ex.zh: 对这些职位我们已有了很多申请人。

d: n. 申请人，申请者，应征者（applicant 的复数形式）

e.en: A college is an institution where students study after they have left secondary school. 大学;

ex.en: Their daughter Joanna is taking business courses at a local college.
ex.zh: 他们的女儿乔安娜正在当地一所大学修习商务课程。

ex.en: Stephanie took up making jewellery after leaving art college this summer.
ex.zh: 斯特凡妮今年夏天从艺术学院毕业以后开始从事珠宝的制作工作。

e.en: At some universities in the United States, colleges are divisions which offer degrees in particular subjects. (美国某些大学中的)

ex.en: ...a professor at the University of Florida College of Law.
ex.zh: …一位佛罗里达大学法学院的教授。

e.en: A college is one of the institutions which some British universities are divided into. (英国某些大学中的)

ex.en: He was educated at Balliol College, Oxford.
ex.zh: 他毕业于牛津大学贝列尔学院。

d: n. 大学，专科学校；学院，分院；公学；学会，社团；学院的全体师生

e.en: You use added to say that something has more of a particular thing or quality.

ex.en: For added protection choose moisturizing lipsticks with a sunscreen.
ex.zh: 要额外的保护，请选择有防晒成分的保湿唇膏。

d: adj. 额外的，更多的，附加的（常作定语）
v. 增加，添加，补充说（add 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you move or look along something such as a road, you move or look toward one end of it.

ex.en: Pedro walked along the street alone.
ex.zh: 佩德罗独自一人沿着这条街走。

ex.en: The young man led Mark Ryle along a corridor.
ex.zh: 那个青年男子带着马克·赖尔沿着一条走廊走。

e.en: If something is situated along a road, river, or corridor, it is situated in it or beside it. 在…里;

ex.en: ...enormous traffic jams all along the roads.
ex.zh: …各条道路上严重的交通堵塞。

e.en: When someone or something moves along, they keep moving in a particular direction.

ex.en: She skipped and danced along.
ex.zh: 她向前蹦跳着、舞蹈着。

ex.en: He raised his voice a little, talking into the wind as they walked along.
ex.zh: 当他们向前走时, 他提高了一点儿嗓门, 迎风讲着话。

e.en: If you say that something is going along in a particular way, you mean that it is progressing in that way.

ex.en: ...the negotiations which have been dragging along interminably.
ex.zh: …这场一直以来无限地拖沓着的谈判。

d: prep. 沿着，顺着；靠着……边；在某处
adv. 向前；一起，一道；进行，进展；（前）来，到某处；到相当的程度；传播

e.en: To be positioned around a place or object means to surround it or be on all sides of it. To move around a place means to go along its edge, back to your starting point.

ex.en: She looked at the papers around her.
ex.zh: 她看了看她四周的报纸。

ex.en: Today she wore her hair down around her shoulders.
ex.zh: 今天她把头发披在了肩上。

e.en: Around is also an adverb.

ex.en: ...a village with a rocky river, a ruined castle and hills all around.
ex.zh: …一个有一条多石的河流和一座被毁的城堡、四面环山的村庄。

e.en: If you move around a corner or obstacle, you move to the other side of it. If you look around a corner or obstacle, you look to see what is on the other side.

ex.en: The photographer stopped clicking and hurried around the corner.
ex.zh: 该摄影师停止按动快门，匆匆绕过那个拐角。

e.en: If you move around a place, you travel through it, going to most of its parts. If you look around a place, you look at every part of it. 四处 (走动、看)

ex.en: I've been walking around Moscow and the town is terribly quiet.
ex.zh: 我一直在莫斯科四处走动，城里极其安静。

d: adv. 围绕，环绕；大约；周围，四周；以圆周计算；到处，向各处；转弯，掉头；闲散地，无目的地；循环往复地；出现，可用；活跃
prep. 围绕，环绕；到处，向各处；在那边，到那边；在……周围，在附近；大约，大概；以……为中心；避开，绕过

e.en: If you say how things are arranged, you are talking about their position in relation to each other or to something else. ...

ex.en: The house itself is three storeys high and arranged around a courtyard.
ex.zh: 房子本身有三层高，绕着一个庭院而建。

d: adj. 安置于……的，……布置的
v. 安排，筹备；整理，排列，布置；谱写，改编（乐曲）（arrange的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Built is the past tense and past participle of . (build)
If you say that someone is built in a particular way, you are describing the kind of body they have.

ex.en: ...a strong, powerfully-built man of 60.
ex.zh: …一位体格健壮的60岁男子。

d: adj. 具有……特性，适合做……；有……身材的； ……制造的
v. 建造；发展，建立；逐渐增强（build 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: The community is all the people who live in a particular area or place.

ex.en: He's well liked by people in the community.
ex.zh: 他很受社区人们的喜爱。

e.en: A particular community is a group of people who are similar in some way.

ex.en: The police haven't really done anything for the black community in particular.
ex.zh: 警方并没有特别为黑人团体做什么。

e.en: Community is friendship between different people or groups, and a sense of having something in common.

ex.en: Two of our greatest strengths are diversity and community.
ex.zh: 我们的两个最大优点是多样性和团体精神。

d: n. 社区，社会；（由同国籍、同宗教等构成的）群体，界；（多个国家的）共同体；归属感；（动植物的）群落

e.en: A company is a business organization that makes money by selling goods or services.

ex.en: Sheila found some work as a secretary in an insurance company.
ex.zh: 希拉在一家保险公司找到了一份做秘书的工作。

e.en: A company is a group of opera singers, dancers, or actors who work together.

ex.en: ...the Phoenix Dance Company.
ex.zh: …凤凰舞蹈团。

e.en: A company is a group of soldiers that is usually part of a battalion or regiment, and that is divided into two or more platoons.

ex.en: The division will consist of two tank companies and one infantry company.
ex.zh: 该师将由两个坦克连和一个步兵连组成。

e.en: Company is having another person or other people with you, usually when this is pleasant or stops you feeling lonely.

ex.en: "I won't stay long."—"No, please. I need the company."
ex.zh: “我不会呆很久。” — “别，请别走。我需要陪伴。”

ex.en: Ross had always enjoyed the company of women.
ex.zh: 罗斯总是喜欢女人的陪伴。

d: n. 公司；陪伴，同伴；宾客，来宾；在一起的一群人；连队；剧团，歌舞团；女童军大队
v. 结交，交往；陪伴
【名】 （Company）（美、瑞）孔帕尼（人名）

e.en: Commitment is a strong belief in an idea or system.

ex.en: ...commitment to the ideals of democracy.
ex.zh: …对民主理想的信奉。

e.en: A commitment is something which regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

ex.en: I've got a lot of commitments.
ex.zh: 我有很多要做的事。

e.en: If you make a commitment to do something, you promise that you will do it.

ex.en: We made a commitment to keep working together.
ex.zh: 我们作了承诺要继续在一起工作。

e.en: Commitment is the process of officially sending someone to a prison or a hospital. 送交 (监狱、医院)

d: n. 忠诚，献身；承诺，保证；奉献，投入；热情，决心；义务，责任；花费，使用（资金、时间、人力）；需要定期支付的款项

e.en: A county is a region of the U.S., Britain, or Ireland, which has its own local government. (英国、爱尔兰的) 郡; (美国的)

ex.en: He arrived at the Palm Beach County courthouse with his mother.
ex.zh: 他和母亲来到了棕榈滩县法院大楼。

d: n. （英国、爱尔兰的）郡，（美国的）县；郡运动队，县运动队
adj. 有世家地位（或特点）的

e.en: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

ex.en: They wanted to design a machine that was both attractive and practical.
ex.zh: 他们想设计一台既美观又实用的机器。

e.en: When someone designs a survey, policy, or system, they plan and prepare it, and decide on all the details of it.

ex.en: We may be able to design a course to suit your particular needs.
ex.zh: 我们也许能策划一个课程来满足你的特定需求。

e.en: Design is the process and art of planning and making detailed drawings of something.

ex.en: He was a born mechanic with a flair for design.
ex.zh: 他天生是个有设计才华的机械师。

e.en: The design of something is the way in which it has been planned and made.

ex.en: ...a new design of clock.
ex.zh: …一种新款时钟。

d: n. 设计，布局，安排；设计艺术，构思；设计图，图纸；图案，花纹；计划，意图
v. 设计，制图，构思；筹划，制订；预定，指定
【名】 （Design）（俄、巴、印）迪赛（人名）

e.en: Eleven is the number 11. 11

ex.en: ...the Princess and her eleven friends.
ex.zh: …该公主和她的11个朋友。

d: num. 十一；十一个
n. 十一；十一个；（体育）由十一人组成的运动队
adj. 十一的；十一个的

e.en: The effect of one thing on another is the change that the first thing causes in the second thing.

ex.en: Parents worry about the effect of music on their adolescent's behaviour.
ex.zh: 家长们担心音乐对于其青少年子女行为的影响。

e.en: An effect is an impression that someone creates deliberately, for example in a place or in a piece of writing.

ex.en: The whole effect is cool, light, and airy.
ex.zh: 整体印象是凉爽、明亮和通风。

e.en: A person's effects are the things that they have with them at a particular time, for example when they are arrested or admitted to a hospital, or the things that they owned when they died.

ex.en: His daughters were collecting his effects.
ex.zh: 他的女儿们正在收集他的个人物品。

e.en: The effects in a film are the specially created sounds and scenery. (影片中音响或布景的)

ex.en: It's got a gripping story, great acting, superb sets, and stunning effects.
ex.zh: 电影有扣人心弦的故事情节、精湛的表演、绝妙的布景和惊人的特效。

d: n. 作用，影响；（刻意制造的）效果，印象；所有物，财产；生效，实行
v. 实现，引起

e.en: Exact means correct in every detail. For example, an exact copy is the same in every detail as the thing it is copied from. 精确的;

ex.en: I don't remember the exact words.
ex.zh: 我不记得确切的话了。

ex.en: The exact number of protest calls has not been revealed.
ex.zh: 抗议电话的确切次数尚未披露。

e.en: 精确地;

ex.en: Try to locate exactly where the smells are entering the room.
ex.zh: 设法确定气味是从哪里进入房间的。

ex.en: Both drugs will be exactly the same.
ex.zh: 两种药将会完全一样。

e.en: You use exact before a noun to emphasize that you are referring to that particular thing and no other, especially something that has a particular significance. 正好的 (用于名词前表示强调)

ex.en: I hadn't really thought about it until this exact moment.
ex.zh: 一直到此时此刻我才真正考虑它。

e.en: 正好

ex.en: These are exactly the people who do not vote.
ex.zh: 这些正好是那些不投票的人。

d: adj. 确切的，精确的；严谨的，一丝不苟的；精密的，严密的
v. 强取，勒索；实施（报复）；造成重大苦难（或损失等）

e.en: Your employer is the person or organization that you work for.

ex.en: He had been sent to Rome by his employer.
ex.zh: 他被雇主派到罗马去了。

d: n. 雇主

e.en: If two or more people exchange things of a particular kind, they give them to each other at the same time.

ex.en: We exchanged addresses.
ex.zh: 我们交换了地址。

ex.en: The two men exchanged glances.
ex.zh: 那两个人交换了眼神。

e.en: Exchange is also a noun.

ex.en: He ruled out any exchange of prisoners with the militants.
ex.zh: 他拒绝考虑与好战分子交换囚犯。

e.en: If you exchange something, you replace it with a different thing, especially something that is better or more satisfactory. 调换;

ex.en: ...the chance to sell back or exchange goods.
ex.zh: …回售或调换货物的机会。

e.en: An exchange is a brief conversation, usually an angry one. 短暂的交谈;

ex.en: There've been some bitter exchanges between the two groups.
ex.zh: 两组之间有过些激烈的争吵。

d: n. 交换，互换；短暂的交谈，争吵；交战，交火；兑换，汇兑；交流，互访；交易所；（商品的）调换；电话局，电话交换台；换子，兑子
v. 调换，更换；交流，交谈；交换，互换；兑换，交易

e.en: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

ex.en: ...a workman who expects to lose his job in the next few weeks.
ex.zh: …一个预料会在接下来几周里失业的工人。

ex.en: The talks are expected to continue until tomorrow.
ex.zh: 会谈预料将持续到明天。

e.en: If you are expecting something or someone, you believe that they will be delivered to you or come to you soon, often because this has been arranged earlier. (常指因已安排而)

ex.en: I wasn't expecting a visitor.
ex.zh: 我没有预期会有访客。

e.en: If you expect something, or expect a person to do something, you believe that it is your right to have that thing, or the person's duty to do it for you.

ex.en: He wasn't expecting our hospitality.
ex.zh: 他没有期待我们的热情款待。

ex.en: I do expect to have some time to myself in the evenings.
ex.zh: 我真期待晚上能有点儿自己的时间。

e.en: If you tell someone not to expect something, you mean that the thing is unlikely to happen as they have planned or imagined, and they should not hope that it will.

ex.en: Don't expect an instant cure.
ex.zh: 别指望会有立竿见影的疗效。

ex.en: You cannot expect to like all the people you will work with.
ex.zh: 你不能指望喜欢所有和你一起工作的人。

d: adj. 预料的，预期的
v. 期待；预计；要求，指望（expect 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A hundred or one hundred is the number 100. 100;

ex.en: According to one official more than a hundred people have been arrested.
ex.zh: 据一名官员说，已有一百多人被捕。

e.en: If you refer to hundreds of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them. 许许多多;

ex.en: Hundreds of tree species face extinction.
ex.zh: 很多树种濒临灭绝。

e.en: You can also use hundreds as a pronoun.

ex.en: Hundreds have been killed in the fighting and thousands made homeless.
ex.zh: 成百上千的人在战斗中丧生，并有成千上万的人变得无家可归。

e.en: You can use a hundred percent or one hundred percent to emphasize that you agree completely with something or that it is completely right or wrong.

ex.en: Are you a hundred percent sure it's your neighbour?
ex.zh: 你百分百肯定这是你的邻居？

d: n. 一百；许多，数量大；一百美元（英镑）的纸币；百位数；（表示24小时制的整点）一点、两点、三点等整；（板球）击球手获得的一百（或以上）的得分
adj. 一百的；许多的

e.en: Learning is the process of gaining knowledge through studying.

ex.en: The brochure described the library as the focal point of learning on the campus.
ex.zh: 这本小册子把图书馆描述为校园学习的中心。

d: n. 学习；知识，学问
v. 学习，学会；得知，获悉；背熟，熟记；认识到，（从……）吸取教训 （learn 的现在分词）

e.en: A line is a long thin mark which is drawn or painted on a surface.

ex.en: Draw a line down that page's centre.
ex.zh: 沿着那一页的中心向下画一条线。

ex.en: ...a dotted line.
ex.zh: …一条虚线。

e.en: The lines on someone's skin, especially on their face, are long thin marks that appear there as they grow older.

ex.en: He has a large, generous face with deep lines.
ex.zh: 他宽大的面庞上带着很深的皱纹。

e.en: A line of people or things is a number of them arranged one behind the other or side by side. (一)

ex.en: The sparse line of spectators noticed nothing unusual.
ex.zh: 稀稀疏疏的一排观众并没注意到什么特别之处。

e.en: A line of people or vehicles is a number of them that are waiting one behind another, for example, in order to buy something or to go in a particular direction.

d: n. 线，线条；（运动场地的）场界，场地线；皱纹，褶子；分界线，边界线；（思想或行为等的）界限；轮廓，外形；排，行，列；队列，队伍；一系列（类似事物），家族；各级人员；字行，诗行；（戏剧或电影的）台词，对白；罚抄写（对学童的处罚）（lines）；妙语，谎话；线，绳，索；电话线（路）；热线（电话），电话服务；（铁道或公交）线路；铁轨，轨道；管线；（行进的）方向，路线；路径，渠道；（尤指公开表明的）态度，看法；方法，方式；行业，行当；种类，类型；运输公司，航运公司；防线，前线，战线；生产线，流水线；一串音符；（准备吸用的）散放成细线的毒品；赤道（the Line）；（印刷，计算机）线条的；字母底部水平线（the line）；（正规）战斗部队（the line）
v. 沿……形成行（或列、排）；给……安衬里，铺，垫；（在某物的内部）形成一层；击出（平直球）；用线条标出，布满线条（lined）
【名】 （Line）（英）莱恩，（俄）利涅（人名）

e.en: A list of things such as names or addresses is a set of them which all belong to a particular category, written down one below the other.

ex.en: We are making a list of the top ten men we would not want to be married to.
ex.zh: 我们正在列一个我们最不想嫁的10种男人的名单。

ex.en: There were six names on the list.
ex.zh: 单子上有6个名字。

e.en: A list of things is a set of them that you think of as being in a particular order. (按一定顺序排列的)

ex.en: High on the list of public demands is to end military control of broadcasting.
ex.zh: 高居公众要求事项前列的是结束对广播的军事控制。

ex.en: The criminal judicial system always comes up at the top of the list of voters' concerns in focus groups.
ex.zh: 刑事司法制度总是出现在焦点小组中投票者关注事项之首。

e.en: To list several things such as reasons or names means to write or say them one after another, usually in a particular order.

ex.en: The pupils were asked to list the sports they loved most and hated most.
ex.zh: 学生们被要求列出他们最喜欢的和最讨厌的运动。

e.en: To list something in a particular way means to include it in that way in a list or report. 把…列入 (表、报告)

ex.en: A medical examiner has listed the deaths as homicides.
ex.zh: 验尸官已将这些死亡列为他杀案件。

d: n. 列表，清单；（船）倾侧；围栏；（织物的）镶边；渴望，喜好；（尤指按重要程度排列的）事物清单；赛场，战场
v. 列清单，拟订清单；把……列入名单；（使）（公司）上市；标价；（船）倾斜；征召（士兵）；想要，喜好
n. 洛雷恩（美国一城市名）

e.en: A marriage is the relationship between a husband and wife.

ex.en: In a good marriage, both husband and wife work hard to solve any problems that arise.
ex.zh: 在一桩美满的婚姻中，夫妻双方共同致力于解决出现的任何问题。

ex.en: When I was 35 my marriage broke up.
ex.zh: 35岁时我的婚姻破裂了。

e.en: A marriage is the act of marrying someone, or the ceremony at which this is done. 结婚;

ex.en: I opposed her marriage to Darryl.
ex.zh: 我反对她嫁给达里尔。

d: n. 结婚，婚姻；婚礼；紧密结合；配对（指伯齐克和其他牌戏中同花色K与Q组合）
【名】 （Marriage）（英）马里奇（人名）

e.en: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe. 支付;

ex.en: Owners who have already paid for repairs will be reimbursed.
ex.zh: 已经付了修缮费的业主将会得到退费。

ex.en: The wealthier may have to pay a little more in taxes.
ex.zh: 更有钱的人可能得多交点税。

e.en: When you are paid, you get your wages or salary from your employer.

ex.en: The lawyer was paid a huge salary.
ex.zh: 这个律师拿了很高的薪金。

ex.en: I get paid monthly.
ex.zh: 我拿月薪。

e.en: Your pay is the money that you get from your employer as wages or salary.

ex.en: ...their complaints about their pay and conditions.
ex.zh: …他们对薪水和工作条件的不满。

e.en: If you are paid to do something, someone gives you some money so that you will help them or perform some service for them.

ex.en: There are people who are paid to sit around and play games.
ex.zh: 有人受雇闲坐着玩游戏。

d: v. 支付；偿还，缴纳；付给（某人）工资或报酬；赢利，产生收益；划算，值得；付出代价，受到惩罚（pay 的第三人称单数）
n. 工资，报酬；雇工（pay 的复数）；Pays（法、英、美等地的人名或姓氏）佩伊

e.en: Production is the process of manufacturing or growing something in large quantities.

ex.en: That model won't go into production before late 2007.
ex.zh: 那种型号要到2007年底才会投入生产。

e.en: Production is the amount of goods manufactured or grown by a company or country.

ex.en: We needed to increase the volume of production.
ex.zh: 我们必须增加产量。

e.en: The production of something is its creation as the result of a natural process. 产生;

ex.en: These proteins stimulate the production of blood cells.
ex.zh: 这些蛋白质促进血细胞的生成。

e.en: Production is the process of organizing and preparing a play, movie, programme, or CD, in order to present it to the public. (戏剧、电影、节目等的)

ex.en: She is head of the production company.
ex.zh: 她是该制片公司的头儿。

d: n. （以销售为目的的）生产，制造；（对自然物的）加工，采集，生产；产量；（自然的）产生；（交通工具的）大量生产；（戏剧、电影、电视节目、唱片等的）制作；（戏剧、电影等的）上映，上演；（尤指从制作与公演等特点来看）影片，戏剧；音响效果，制作方式；出示，提供；非常费力的事，非常复杂的事

e.en: When you program a machine or system, you set its controls so that it will work in a particular way. 设定 (机器、系统等的)

ex.en: Parents can program the machine not to turn on at certain times.
ex.zh: 父母可设定机器在某些时候不启动。

e.en: A program is a set of instructions that a computer follows in order to perform a particular task. (计算机)

ex.en: The chances of an error occurring in a computer program increase with the size of the program.
ex.zh: 计算机程序出错的几率随程序的增大而增高。

e.en: When you program a computer, you give it a set of instructions to make it able to perform a particular task. 给 (计算机)

ex.en: He programmed his computer to compare the 1,431 possible combinations of pairs in this population.
ex.zh: 他给他的计算机编了程来比较这些人中1431种可能的成对组合。

ex.en: ...45 million people, about half of whom can program their own computers.
ex.zh: 4500万人，其中约有一半会给他们自己的计算机编程。

e.en: 编程

ex.en: ...programming skills.
ex.zh: …编程技巧。

d: n. （计算机）程序（=programme）；计划，规划；（音乐会、戏剧等演出的）节目单，（体育运动、比赛等的）项目介绍；（电视或广播）节目；课程，大纲
v. （给计算机）编写程序，设计程序；设置，预设；使……有倾向；为……安排节目
adv. 轻轻地，安静地；悄悄地，不张扬地；轻声地，低声地；安静地（指不抗议、不抱怨、不吵架）

e.en: You use single to emphasize that you are referring to one thing, and no more than one thing. 单个的;

ex.en: A single shot rang out.
ex.zh: 一声枪响。

ex.en: Over six hundred people were wounded in a single day.
ex.zh: 一天内六百多人受伤。

e.en: You use single to indicate that you are considering something on its own and separately from other things like it. 个别的; 一个个的;

ex.en: Every single house in town had been damaged.
ex.zh: 镇上的每一座房子都被毁坏了。

e.en: Someone who is single is not married. You can also use single to describe someone who does not have a girlfriend or boyfriend. 未婚的;

ex.en: Is it difficult being a single mother?
ex.zh: 当单身母亲难吗？

e.en: A single room is a room intended for one person to stay or live in. 单人的 (房间)

ex.en: Each guest has her own single room, or shares, on request, a double room.
ex.zh: 每位客人都有自己的单人房间，经要求也可共用双人间。

d: adj. 单一的，单个的；单身的，未婚的；各自的，分别的；单人的，单人用的；（票）单程的；统一的；由一个部分构成的；（花）单瓣的；唯一的；（酒的）一份
n. 单曲唱片；（板球中的）一分打，（棒球中的）一垒打；单身者，未婚者； 单程票；（旅馆等的）单人房间；单打（比赛）； 一元纸币；（鸣钟术）不同次序鸣钟法；（影剧院的）一张票，一个座位；一份酒
v. 挑选，选出；（棒球）击出一垒打；对（幼苗，幼树）进行间苗；将（铁轨）变成单线；以一垒打使（跑垒）得分

e.en: You use specific to refer to a particular exact area, problem, or subject. 特定的 (部位、问题、主题等)

ex.en: Massage may help to increase blood flow to specific areas of the body.
ex.zh: 按摩也许会帮助加快血液流向身体各个特定部位。

ex.en: There are several specific problems to be dealt with.
ex.zh: 有好几个特定问题要解决。

e.en: If someone is specific, they give a description that is precise and exact. You can also use specific to describe their description.

ex.en: She declined to be more specific about the reasons for the separation.
ex.zh: 她拒绝给出导致分手的更确切的原因。

e.en: Something that is specific to a particular thing is connected with that thing only.

ex.en: Send your resume with a cover letter that is specific to that particular job.
ex.zh: 将你的简历和专门为那份工作而写的附信一并寄送。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: Specific is also used after nouns. 针对…的 (用于名词后)

ex.en: Most studies of trade have been country-specific.
ex.zh: 大多数贸易研究一直都是针对某个国家的。

d: adj. 明确的，具体的；特定的；特有的，独特的；有特殊功能的，有特效的；（生物）种的；（关税，税）按数量（根据固定税率）征取而非按货价征取的；（物理）（与参照物同一性质成）比率的
n. 细节，详情；特效药

e.en: A specification is a requirement which is clearly stated, for example about the necessary features in the design of something.

ex.en: I'd like to buy some land and have a house built to my specification.
ex.zh: 我想买块地并按照我的要求建一座房子。

d: n. 规格（specification 的复数形式），技术参数；说明书，规格说明

e.en: When you spend money, you pay money for things that you want or need. 花 (钱)

ex.en: By the end of the holiday I had spent all my money.
ex.zh: 到那个假期结束时我已经花光了我所有的钱。

ex.en: Businessmen spend enormous amounts advertising their products.
ex.zh: 商人们花巨额资金为他们的产品做广告。

e.en: If you spend time or energy doing something, you use your time or effort doing it. 花 (时间、精力)

ex.en: Engineers spend much time and energy developing brilliant solutions.
ex.zh: 工程师们花大量时间和精力开发出色的解决方案。

e.en: If you spend a period of time in a place, you stay there for a period of time. 度过 (一段时间)

ex.en: We spent the night in a hotel.
ex.zh: 我们在一家宾馆过了夜。

d: v. 度过，花（时间）；花（钱），花费；消耗，用尽（精力等）
n. 花费，开销
n. 预算

e.en: (of a pipe or tube, esp an organ pipe) closed at one end and thus sounding an octave lower than an open pipe of the same length

d: v. 停止，停下来（stop 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 停止的，停顿的；（鼻子）堵塞的（常作 stopped-up）

e.en: A syllabus is an outline or summary of the subjects to be covered in a course.

ex.en: The course syllabus consisted mainly of novels by African-American authors, male and female.
ex.zh: 该课程的教学大纲主要包括了非裔美国男女作家的小说。

e.en: You can refer to the subjects that are studied in a particular course as the syllabus.

d: n. 教学大纲；（罗马天主教会用教令宣布的）事项举要

e.en: A student is a person who is studying at an elementary school, secondary school, college, or university.

ex.en: Warren's eldest son is an art student.
ex.zh: 沃伦的长子是一名学艺术的学生。

e.en: Someone who is a student of a particular subject is interested in the subject and spends time learning about it.

ex.en: ...a passionate student of history and an expert on nineteenth century prime ministers.
ex.zh: …一位热衷历史的学者和一个研究19世纪首相们的专家。

d: n. 学生（student 的复数）

e.en: Thirty is the number 30. 30

When you talk about the thirties, you are referring to numbers between 30 and 39. For example, if you are in your thirties, you are aged between 30 and 39. If the temperature is in the thirties, the temperature is between 30 and 39 degrees.

ex.en: Mozart clearly enjoyed good health throughout his twenties and early thirties.
ex.zh: 莫扎特显然在二十几岁和三十刚出头时身体很好。

e.en: The thirties is the decade between 1930 and 1939. 20世纪30

ex.en: She became quite a notable director in the thirties and forties.
ex.zh: 她在20世纪的三四十年代成为一位名导演。

d: n. 二十世纪三十年代（the thirties）；三十（数字 30）；三十几（复数 thirties，指 30 至 39）
num. 三十
adj. 三十个的；（作表语）三十岁的

e.en: You can use tuition to refer to the amount of money that you have to pay for being taught in a university, college, or private school.

ex.en: Angela's $7,000 tuition at university this year will be paid for with scholarships.
ex.zh: 安吉拉今年$7000的大学学费将用奖学金来支付。

e.en: If you are given tuition in a particular subject, you are taught about that subject.

d: n. （尤指对个人或小组的）教学，指导；（尤指学院、大学或私立学校的）学费

e.en: To weld one piece of metal to another means to join them by heating the edges and putting them together so that they cool and harden into one piece.

ex.en: It's possible to weld stainless steel to ordinary steel.
ex.zh: 将不锈钢和普通钢焊接在一起是可能的。

ex.en: Where did you learn to weld?
ex.zh: 你在哪里学会的焊接技术？

e.en: a joint formed by welding

d: v. 焊接（物件），即通过熔化或软化连接；（使）紧密结合，成整体（weld 的现在分词）
n. 焊接，锻接，熔接

e.en: You use unusually to emphasize that someone or something has more of a particular quality than is usual.

ex.en: He was an unusually complex man.
ex.zh: 他是个异常复杂的人。

e.en: You can use unusually to suggest that something is not what normally happens.

ex.en: Unusually, for a Japanese politician, he's a fluent English speaker.
ex.zh: 不同寻常的是，作为一位日本政府官员，他能讲流利的英语。

d: adv. 特别地，极其，非常；异常地，不同寻常地

e.en: When you wait for something or someone, you spend some time doing very little, because you cannot act until that thing happens or that person arrives.

ex.en: I walk to a street corner and wait for the school bus.
ex.zh: 我走到一个街道拐角处等校车。

ex.en: I waited to see how she responded.
ex.zh: 我等着看她如何反应。

e.en: 等候

ex.en: The waiting became almost unbearable.
ex.zh: 等待变得几乎令人难以忍受了。

e.en: A wait is a period of time in which you do very little, before something happens or before you can do something.

ex.en: ...the four-hour wait for the organizers to declare the result.
ex.zh: …组织者们宣布结果前4个小时的等待。

e.en: If something is waiting for you, it is ready for you to use, have, or do. 等 (你) 使用; 等 (你)

ex.en: There'll be a car waiting for you.
ex.zh: 将会有辆车等着你。

ex.en: When we came home we had a meal waiting for us.
ex.zh: 我们回到家时，有一顿饭正等着我们去享用。

d: n. 等，等待；服侍，侍候，当服务员；宫廷侍候
v. 等候；盼望，期待；推迟，延缓（wait 的现在分词）
【名】 （waiting）（英、印、美）韦廷（人名）
n. 小时（hour 的复数）；（非正式）很长时间，许久（常用于 for hours、take hours 等）；工作、营业或开放时间（用于 working hours、office hours、opening hours 等）；Hours：（希腊神话）时序女神（Horae）；（Hours）（法）乌尔（人名）

e.en: A debt is a sum of money that you owe someone.

ex.en: Three years later, he is still paying off his debts.
ex.zh: 三年后，他仍旧在还他的债务。

e.en: If you are in debt or get into debt, you owe money. If you are out of debt or get out of debt, you succeed in paying all the money that you owe. 负债;

ex.en: He was already deeply in debt through gambling losses.
ex.zh: 赌博输的钱让他已经负债累累。

e.en: Debt is the state of owing money.

ex.en: ...a monthly report on the amount of debt owed by consumers.
ex.zh: …一份消费者欠款数额月报。

e.en: You use debt in expressions such as I owe you a debt or I am in your debt when you are expressing gratitude for something that someone has done for you.

ex.en: He was so good to me that I can never repay the debt I owe him.
ex.zh: 那时他对我太好了，我永远都还不清欠他的人情债。

ex.en: I owe a debt of thanks to Joyce Thompson, whose careful and able research was of great help.
ex.zh: 我欠乔伊斯·汤普森一份感谢之情，他谨慎杰出的研究是极大的帮助。

d: n. 欠款，债务；负债情况；人情债

e.en: Industry is the work and processes involved in collecting raw materials, and making them into products in factories.

ex.en: Our industry suffers through insufficient investment in research.
ex.zh: 我们的工业因研究投入不足而大吃苦头。

e.en: A particular industry consists of all the people and activities involved in making a particular product or providing a particular service.

ex.en: ...the motor vehicle and textile industries.
ex.zh: …机动车与纺织行业。

e.en: If you refer to a social or political activity as an industry, you are criticizing it because you think it involves a lot of people in unnecessary or useless work.

ex.en: ...the industry of western capitalism.
ex.zh: …西方资本主义的大张旗鼓。

e.en: Industry is the fact of working very hard.

ex.en: No one doubted his ability, his industry or his integrity.
ex.zh: 没有人怀疑他的能力、勤奋和正直。

d: n. 工业，生产制造；行业，产业；勤奋，勤劳；范围，领域

e.en: A speaker or writer uses your to indicate that something belongs or relates to the person or people that they are talking or writing to. 你的;

ex.en: Emma, I trust your opinion a great deal.
ex.zh: 埃玛，我非常相信你的观点。

ex.en: I left all of your messages on your desk.
ex.zh: 我把你的所有便条都放到你的书桌上了。

e.en: In spoken English and informal written English, your is sometimes used to indicate that something belongs to or relates to people in general. 你的 (口语中用于泛指属于或有关任何人的)

ex.en: Painkillers are very useful in small amounts to bring your temperature down.
ex.zh: 小剂量的止痛药对于降低体温非常有用。

e.en: In spoken English, a speaker sometimes uses your before an adjective such as "typical" or "normal" to indicate that the thing referred to is a typical example of its type. 人们所认为的 (口语中用于形容词前，表示所指事物为某类事物的典型)

ex.en: This isn't your typical economics class.
ex.zh: 这不是人们所认为的典型的经济学课。

d: det. 你的，你们的；泛指任何人的；（用于 typical、normal 等形容词前）通常所说的，典型的；（用于尊称头衔前）您的

e.en: You use ago when you are referring to past time. For example, if something happened one year ago, it is one year since it happened. If it happened a long time ago, it is a long time since it happened.

ex.en: He was killed a few days ago in a skiing accident.
ex.zh: 他几天以前在一次滑雪事故中丧生。

ex.en: The meeting is the first ever between the two sides since the war there began 14 years ago.
ex.zh: 这是自从14年前双方爆发战争以来的第一次会晤。

d: adv. 以前，从前
adj. 以前的
【名】 （Ago）（美）阿戈（人名）

e.en: A person is a man, woman, or child.

ex.en: At least one person died and several others were injured.
ex.zh: 至少一人死亡，另有几人受伤。

ex.en: They were both lovely, friendly people.
ex.zh: 他们俩都是可爱、友好的人。

e.en: Persons is used as the plural of person in formal, legal, and technical writing. (person)
e.zh: 的复数形式，用于正式、法律和技术文体中

ex.en: ...removal of the right of accused persons to remain silent.
ex.zh: …对被告人沉默权的剥夺。

e.en: If you talk about someone as a person, you are considering them from the point of view of their real nature. (从其真正本质出发而言的)

ex.en: Robin didn't feel good about herself as a person.
ex.zh: 罗宾对她自己的为人感觉不佳。

e.en: If you do something in person, you do it yourself rather than letting someone else do it for you.

ex.en: You must collect the mail in person and take along some form of identification.
ex.zh: 你必须亲自去取邮件，并带上某种身份证明。

d: n. 人；自然人，法人；（用于不知其人是谁时）某人，家伙；（语法）人称；（用于复合词）从事……工作（或担任……职务）的人；人品，为人；身体，人身；喜爱（某事物）的人；（戏剧或故事中的）人物，角色；（基督教神学）（圣父、圣子、圣灵三位一体的）位；容貌，外表
【名】 （Person）（法、俄、德、瑞典）佩尔松，（英）珀森（人名）

e.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

ex.en: I presume you're here on business.
ex.zh: 我想你是来这儿出差的吧。

ex.en: "Had he been home all week?"—"I presume so."
ex.zh: “他整个星期都在家吗？”—“我想是。”

e.en: If you say that someone presumes to do something, you mean that they do it even though they have no right to do it. 擅自 (做某事)

ex.en: They're resentful that outsiders presume to meddle in their affairs.
ex.zh: 他们对外人擅自干预他们的事务怨恨不已。

e.en: If an idea, theory, or plan presumes certain facts, it regards them as true so that they can be used as a basis for further ideas and theories. 假定 (某事实)

ex.en: The legal definition of "know" often presumes mental control.
ex.zh: “知情”的法律界定通常以思维控制力为前提。

d: adj. 假定的，推测的，推定的
v. presume 的过去式和过去分词，表示假定、推测；用于 presume to do 结构，表示擅自、冒昧
公共卫生

e.en: Twenty is the number 20. 20

When you talk about the twenties, you are referring to numbers between 20 and 29. For example, if you are in your twenties, you are aged between 20 and 29. If the temperature is in the twenties, the temperature is between 20 and 29 degrees.

ex.en: They're both in their twenties and both married with children of their own.
ex.zh: 他们俩都二十几岁了，都已结婚有了自己的孩子。

e.en: The twenties is the decade between 1920 and 1929. 20世纪20

ex.en: It was written in the Twenties, but it still really stands out.
ex.zh: 它写于20世纪20年代，但现在仍很引人注目。

d: num. 二十
n. 二十；二十几（用复数形式 twenties，指年龄、温度等二十至二十九之间的数字）；二十年代（the twenties，指二十世纪二十年代）；二十美元纸币（常作 a twenty）
adj. 二十的，二十个的

e.en: A particular kind of worker does the kind of work mentioned.

ex.en: She ate her sandwich alongside several other office workers taking their break.
ex.zh: 她在其他几位正在休息的办公室人员旁边吃自己的三明治。

e.en: Workers are people who are employed in industry or business and who are not managers. 工人;

ex.en: Wages have been frozen and workers laid off.
ex.zh: 工资已被冻结，员工们下岗了。

e.en: You can use worker to say how well or badly someone works. 工作 (好或坏)

ex.en: He is a hard worker and a skilled gardener.
ex.zh: 他是一个工作努力的人，一个技艺娴熟的园艺工。

d: n. 工作者，工作人员；劳工，工人（worker 的复数）

e.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind does not think. 睡眠;

ex.en: They were exhausted from lack of sleep.
ex.zh: 他们因睡眠不足而疲惫不堪了。

ex.en: Be quiet and go to sleep.
ex.zh: 安静，睡觉吧。

e.en: When you sleep, you rest with your eyes closed and your mind and body inactive. 睡着;

ex.en: During the drive, the baby slept.
ex.zh: 在行驶中那个婴儿睡了。

ex.en: I've not been able to sleep for the last few nights.
ex.zh: 最近几个晚上我一直无法入睡。

e.en: A sleep is a period of sleeping. (一段)

ex.en: I think he may be ready for a sleep soon.
ex.zh: 我想他可能准备好了马上睡一觉。

e.en: If a building or room sleeps a particular number of people, it has beds for that number of people.

ex.en: The villa sleeps 10.
ex.zh: 这幢别墅可供10人住宿。

d: v. 睡，睡觉；供……住宿；（尤指入夜后某地或建筑物）沉寂，静寂；安息，安眠；发生性关系
n. 睡眠，睡觉；（一段）睡眠时间；眵，眼屎；死，长眠
【名】 （Sleep）斯利普（姓氏）

e.en: If you promise that you will do something, you say to someone that you will definitely do it.

ex.en: The post office has promised to resume first class mail delivery to the area on Friday.
ex.zh: 邮局已承诺在星期五恢复该地区第一类邮件的递送。

ex.en: He had promised that the rich and privileged would no longer get preferential treatment.
ex.zh: 他已承诺富人和特权阶层将不会再得到优待。

e.en: If you promise someone something, you tell them that you will definitely give it to them or make sure that they have it. 向 (某人) 承诺 (给予他们某物); 向 (某人) 保证 (他们获得某物)

ex.en: In 1920 the great powers promised them an independent state.
ex.zh: 1920年，列强们曾答应让他们成为一个独立国家。

e.en: A promise is a statement that you make to a person in which you say that you will definitely do something or give them something.

ex.en: If you make a promise, you should keep it.
ex.zh: 如果你许下一个诺言，你就应该遵守它。

e.en: If a situation or event promises to have a particular quality or to be a particular thing, it shows signs that it will have that quality or be that thing.

ex.en: While it will be fun, the seminar also promises to be most instructive.
ex.zh: 这次专题讨论会将会很有趣，也一定会非常有启发性。

d: v. 承诺，保证；使很可能，预示；指望，期待（promise oneself）；把（某人，尤指女人）许配给；有指望，有前途
n. 承诺，诺言；前途，指望；迹象，预示

e.en: If you are able to do something, you have skills or qualities which make it possible for you to do it. (因具有某技能或素质而)

ex.en: The older child should be able to prepare a simple meal.
ex.zh: 这个大点儿的孩子应该能做顿简单的饭菜。

ex.en: The company says they're able to keep pricing competitive.
ex.zh: 这个公司说他们能够保持价格竞争力。

e.en: If you are able to do something, you have enough freedom, power, time, or money to do it. (因有足够的自由、权力、时间或财力而)

ex.en: You'll be able to read in peace.
ex.zh: 你将可以安静地看书。

ex.en: Have you been able to have any kind of contact?
ex.zh: 你取得任何联系了吗?

e.en: Someone who is able is very intelligent or very good at doing something.

ex.en: ...one of the brightest and ablest members of the government.
ex.zh: …最聪明、最有才能的政府成员之一。

d: adj. 能够，有能力的；聪明能干的，精通（某事）的
【名】 （Able）（英）埃布尔，（伊朗）阿布勒（人名）

e.en: When you accumulate things or when they accumulate, they collect or are gathered over a period of time.

ex.en: Lead can accumulate in the body until toxic levels are reached.
ex.zh: 铅可以在体内积聚直至到达有毒的程度。

d: v. 积累，积攒

e.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true. 承认 (不好、不快或尴尬的事实)

ex.en: I am willing to admit that I do make mistakes.
ex.zh: 我愿意承认我确实会犯错误。

ex.en: Up to two thirds of 14 to 16 year olds admit to buying alcohol illegally.
ex.zh: 14至16岁的少年中有多达2/3的少年承认非法买过酒。

e.en: If someone is admitted to a hospital, they are taken into the hospital for treatment and kept there until they are well enough to go home. 接收 (入院)

ex.en: She was admitted to the hospital with a soaring temperature.
ex.zh: 她因高烧被接收入院。

e.en: If someone is admitted to an organization or group, they are allowed to join it. 接收 (加入)

ex.en: He was admitted to the Académie Culinaire de France.
ex.zh: 他被接收加入法国厨艺学会。

e.en: To admit someone to a place means to allow them to enter it.

ex.en: Embassy security personnel refused to admit him or his wife.
ex.zh: 使馆保安人员拒绝让他或他的妻子进入。

d: v. （勉强）承认；招认，招供；准许进入（某处）；接纳，接收（入学、入院、入会）；容许，有…的可能（用于 admit of）（admit 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: An advertisement is an announcement in a newspaper, on television, or on a poster about something such as a product, event, or job. 广告;

ex.en: Miss Parrish recently placed an advertisement in the local newspaper.
ex.zh: 帕里什小姐最近在当地报纸上登出了一则启事。

e.en: If you say that an example of something is an advertisement for that thing in general, you mean that it shows how good that thing is.

ex.en: The Treviso team was an effective advertisement for the improving state of Italian club rugby.
ex.zh: 特雷维索队是意大利俱乐部橄榄球改进状况的一个有效展示。

d: n. 广告（advertisement 的复数）；宣传

e.en: If something you want or need is available, you can find it or obtain it.

ex.en: Since 1978, the amount of money available to buy books has fallen by 17%.
ex.zh: 自1978年以来，可供买书的钱已减少了17%。

ex.en: The shop has about 500 autographed copies of the book available for purchase.
ex.zh: 这家书店有大约500本该书的签名版本可供购买。

e.en: 可获得性

ex.en: ...the easy availability of guns.
ex.zh: …获取枪支的容易性。

e.en: Someone who is available is not busy and is therefore free to talk to you or to do a particular task.

ex.en: Mr. Leach is on holiday and was not available for comment.
ex.zh: 利奇先生在休假，没空作评论。

d: adj. 可用的，可获得的；有空的，有闲暇的；未婚的，单身的

e.en: You use anyone or anybody in statements with negative meaning to indicate in a general way that nobody is present or involved in an action. 任何人 (用于含否定意义的陈述句中)

ex.en: I won't tell anyone I saw you here.
ex.zh: 我不会告诉任何人我在这儿看见了你。

ex.en: You needn't talk to anyone if you don't want to.
ex.zh: 如果你不想你就不需要和任何人说话。

e.en: You use anyone or anybody in questions and conditional clauses to ask or talk about whether someone is present or doing something. 某个人 (用于疑问句和条件分句中)

ex.en: Why would anyone want that job?
ex.zh: 为什么会有人想要那份工作？

ex.en: How can anyone look sad at an occasion like this?
ex.zh: 在像这样的一个场合怎么会有人看上去悲伤呢？

e.en: You use anyone or anybody before words that indicate the kind of person you are talking about. 任何…的人 (接后置修饰语)

ex.en: I always had been the person who achieved things before anyone else at my age.
ex.zh: 我过去一直是那种在任何同龄人之前达成目标的人。

ex.en: It's not a job for anyone who is slow with numbers.
ex.zh: 这不是一种适合任何对数字反应慢的人的工作。

e.en: You use anyone or anybody to refer to a person when you are emphasizing that it could be any person out of a very large number of people.

ex.en: Anyone could be doing what I'm doing.
ex.zh: 任何一个人都可以做我在做的事。

d: pron. 任何人，无论谁，任何一个人（泛指）；某个人，有人（用于疑问句、条件句等）；任何……的人（后接定语）；没有一个人（用于否定句，与否定词连用）；重要人物（用于 anyone who is anyone）

e.en: A bedroom is a room used for sleeping in.

ex.en: ...the spare bedroom.
ex.zh: …那间空卧室。

e.en: A bedroom community or suburb is the same as a  community or suburb. (指通勤者居住的)

ex.en: This town is becoming a bedroom community of Columbus, 20 miles to the north.
ex.zh: 这座小镇正成为距此北面20英里处哥伦布市的卧室社区。

d: n. 卧室
adj. 两性关系的；城郊住宅区的

e.en: If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.

ex.en: I first became interested in Islam while I was doing my nursing training.
ex.zh: 我在进行护理训练的时候，我初次对伊斯兰教产生了兴趣。

e.en: If something becomes someone, it makes them look attractive or it seems right for them. 适合;

ex.en: Does khaki become you?
ex.zh: 卡其布适合你吗？

e.en: If you wonder what has become of someone or something, you wonder where they are and what has happened to them. (某人、某事物)

ex.en: She thought constantly about her family; she might never know what had become of them.
ex.zh: 她经常想着她的家人；她也许永远都不知道他们怎么样了。

d: v. 变得，变成，成为；适合，使显得漂亮

e.en: If you buy something, you obtain it by paying money for it.

ex.en: He could not afford to buy a house.
ex.zh: 他买不起房子。

ex.en: Lizzie bought herself a mountain bike.
ex.zh: 莉齐给自己买了一辆山地自行车。

e.en: If you talk about the quantity or standard of goods an amount of money buys, you are referring to the price of the goods or the value of the money.

ex.en: About $70,000 buys a habitable house.
ex.zh: 大约七万美元才买得到一栋适合居住的房子。

e.en: If you buy something like time, freedom, or victory, you obtain it but only by offering or giving up something in return.

ex.en: It was a risky operation, but might buy more time.
ex.zh: 这是一项冒险的举动，但也许能换得更多的时间。

e.en: If you say that a person can be bought, you are criticizing the fact that they will give their help or loyalty to someone in return for money.

ex.en: Any number of our military and government officials can be bought.
ex.zh: 我们的军官和政府官员中有许多可以被收买。

d: v. 购买，能买；相信，接受；（付出代价）获得，赢得；收买，贿赂；买，购买
n. 合算的东西，便宜货；购买

e.en: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

ex.en: The ambassador appealed for a change in U.S. policy.
ex.zh: 该大使呼吁美国政策的变革。

ex.en: There are going to have to be some drastic changes.
ex.zh: 一定得有些重大变革。

e.en: If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.

ex.en: It is a complex system, but it certainly makes a change.
ex.zh: 这是个复杂系统，但肯定有所改进。

e.en: If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.

ex.en: His physician modified the dosage but did not change to a different medication.
ex.zh: 他的医生调整了剂量，但没有改换成别的药方。

e.en: When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different. 改变;

ex.en: We are trying to detect and understand how the climates change.
ex.zh: 我们在努力探测并了解气候是怎样变化的。

ex.en: In the union office, the mood gradually changed from resignation to rage.
ex.zh: 在工会办公室，情绪渐渐由依从变成了愤怒。

d: v. 改变，变化；更换，替换；换乘；兑换，找零；交换，互换
n. 变化，变革；找回的钱，零钱；换乘；替代物，替换衣物；全新体验；转成新月；钟乐敲打的一种套路

e.en: Better is the comparative of good.
Better is the comparative of well.
If you like one thing better than another, you like it more.

ex.en: I like your interpretation better than the one I was taught.
ex.zh: 与我所学的相比，我更喜欢你这种解释。

ex.en: They liked it better when it rained.
ex.zh: 他们更喜欢下雨天。

e.en: If you are better after an illness or injury, you have recovered from it. If you feel better, you no longer feel so ill.

ex.en: He is much better now, he's fine.
ex.zh: 他现在病好多了，他没什么事了。

d: adj. 较好的，更好的；能力更强的，更熟练的；（健康状况）好转的，康复的；更合适的，更得体的
adv. 较好地，更好地；更，更大程度上；更妥，更恰当
n. 更好的事物，较好者；更好的表现，更好的待遇；上司，比自己能力强的人；打赌者（=bettor）
v. 超过，胜过；改善，改进
adj. 最便宜的（cheap 的最高级形式）
adv. 以最低的价格（cheap 的最高级形式）
adv. 清楚地，清晰地；毫无疑问，显然；明智地，清醒地

e.en: A clinician is a doctor who specializes in clinical work.

d: n. 临床医生，临床医师（clinician 的复数）
adj. 靠近的，更近的；更密切的；更仔细的（close 的比较级）
adv. 更近地，靠近些（close 的比较级）
n. 闭合器，自动关闭装置；负责收尾或促成交易的人；（棒球）终结投手；（演出等的）最后的节目，压轴节目

e.en: If you are doing something in comfort, you are physically relaxed and contented, and are not feeling any pain or other unpleasant sensations.

ex.en: This will enable the audience to sit in comfort while watching the shows.
ex.zh: 这能使观众看演出时舒服地坐着。

e.en: Comfort is a style of life in which you have enough money to have everything you need.

ex.en: Surely there is some way of ordering our busy lives so that we can live in comfort and find spiritual harmony too.
ex.zh: 一定会有办法把我们繁忙的生活安排得既舒适又能找到内心平静。

e.en: Comfort is what you feel when worries or unhappiness stop.

ex.en: He welcomed the truce, but pointed out it was of little comfort to families spending Christmas without a loved one.
ex.zh: 他欢迎休战，但指出这对于没有亲人共度圣诞节的家庭并无多少安慰。

ex.en: They will be able to take some comfort from inflation figures due on Friday.
ex.zh: 他们将会从预定在周五发布的通货膨胀数字中得到些安慰。

e.en: If you refer to a person, thing, or idea as a comfort, you mean that it helps you to stop worrying or makes you feel less unhappy.

ex.en: It's a comfort talking to you.
ex.zh: 与你谈谈是一种安慰。

d: n. 舒服，舒适；安慰，慰藉；令人感到安慰的人（或事物）；舒适的设施（或条件）；生活富足
v. 安慰，抚慰

e.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

ex.en: Mike commutes to Miami every day.
ex.zh: 迈克每天通勤去迈阿密。

ex.en: McLaren began commuting between Philadelphia and New York.
ex.zh: 麦克拉伦开始在费城和纽约之间通勤。

e.en: 通勤者

ex.en: There are significant numbers of commuters using our streets.
ex.zh: 有相当多的通勤者使用我们的街道。

e.en: A commute is the journey that you make when you commute.

ex.en: The average Los Angeles commute is over 60 miles a day.
ex.zh: 洛杉矶平均通勤路程每天超过60英里。

d: v. 通勤，上下班往返；减轻（刑罚）；代偿；（两个运算，两个量）可交换
n. 通勤，上下班交通路程
n. child 的复数形式；孩子们，儿童；子女，儿女

e.en: When one firm or country competes with another, it tries to get people to buy its own goods in preference to those of the other firm or country. You can also say that two firms or countries compete. (与…)

ex.en: The banks have long competed with American Express's charge cards and various shop cards.
ex.zh: 这些银行长期以来一直与美国运通公司的记账卡和各种商店卡竞争。

ex.en: Hardware shops are competing fiercely for business.
ex.zh: 各五金店正在为抢生意而激烈竞争。

e.en: If you compete with someone for something, you try to get it for yourself and stop the other person from getting it. You can also say that two people compete for something.

ex.en: Kangaroos compete with sheep and cattle for sparse supplies of food and water.
ex.zh: 袋鼠与绵羊和牛争夺为数不多的食物和水的供应。

ex.en: Young men compete with each other for membership in these societies and fraternities.
ex.zh: 年轻人为获取这些社团和兄弟会的会员身份而相互争夺。

e.en: If you compete in a contest or a game, you take part in it. 参加 (竞赛或比赛)

ex.en: He will be competing in the 100-metre race.
ex.zh: 他将参加100米比赛。

d: v. 竞争，对抗（compete 的过去式和过去分词）；争夺；参加比赛

e.en: Culture consists of activities such as the arts and philosophy, which are considered to be important for the development of civilization and of people's minds.

ex.en: There is just not enough fun and frivolity in culture today.
ex.zh: 当今文化中太缺少乐趣和轻松。

ex.en: ...aspects of popular culture.
ex.zh: …大众文化的方方面面。

e.en: A culture is a particular society or civilization, especially considered in relation to its beliefs, way of life, or art. (与某种特定信仰、生活方式或艺术相连的)

ex.en: ...people from different cultures.
ex.zh: …来自不同文化的人们。

e.en: The culture of a particular organization or group consists of the habits of the people in it and the way they generally behave. (组织或团体的)

ex.en: But social workers say that this has created a culture of dependency, particularly in urban areas.
ex.zh: 但是社会工作者说，这造成了一种依赖习惯，在城区尤其如此。

e.en: In science, a culture is a group of bacteria or cells which are grown, usually in a laboratory as part of an experiment. 一组培养菌;

ex.en: ...a culture of human cells.
ex.zh: …一组人类培养细胞。

d: n. 文化，文明；（团体或组织中共同的）态度，习俗；文化群落，（处于历史上特定时期的）社会；艺术活动；修养；（细胞、细菌等的）培养，培养物；栽培，养殖
v. 培育，养殖

e.en: A confession is a signed statement by someone in which they admit that they have committed a particular crime.

ex.en: They forced him to sign a confession.
ex.zh: 他们强迫他签了供状。

e.en: Confession is the act of admitting that you have done something that you are ashamed of or embarrassed about.

ex.en: I have a confession to make.
ex.zh: 我要作个坦白。

ex.en: The diaries are a mixture of confession and observation.
ex.zh: 这些日记混合着自白和一些观察。

e.en: If you make a confession of your beliefs or feelings, you publicly tell people that this is what you believe or feel. (对信念、情感的)

ex.en: ...Tatyana's confession of love.
ex.zh: …塔蒂安娜的爱的表白。

e.en: In the Catholic church and in some other churches, if you go to confession, you privately tell a priest about your sins and ask for forgiveness. (私下对神父的)

ex.en: He never went to Father Porter for confession again.
ex.zh: 他再也没私下去向波特神父忏悔。

d: n. 供认，供状；承认，坦白；忏悔，告解；声明，告白

e.en: When you make a decision, you choose what should be done or which is the best of various possible actions.

ex.en: I don't want to make the wrong decision and regret it later.
ex.zh: 我不想作出错误的决定，以后后悔。

e.en: Decision is the act of deciding something or the need to decide something.

ex.en: The growing pressures of the crisis may mean that the moment of decision can't be too long delayed.
ex.zh: 这次危机不断增长的压力可能意味着作决定的时刻不会拖延很久。

e.en: Decision is the ability to decide quickly and definitely what to do.

ex.en: He is very quick-thinking and very much a man of decision.
ex.zh: 他思维很敏捷，是个很果断的人。

d: n. 决定，抉择；判决，裁定；果断，决断力；作决定，决策

e.en: A device is an object that has been invented for a particular purpose, for example, for recording or measuring something.

ex.en: ...the electronic device that tells the starter when an athlete has moved from his blocks prematurely.
ex.zh: …能在运动员抢跑时通知发令员的电子仪器。

d: n. 装置，设备；手段，方法；花招，诡计；炸弹，爆炸装置；图画，设计；（某物的）样式，外表

e.en: Dim light is not bright.

ex.en: She stood waiting in the dim light.
ex.zh: 她站在昏暗的灯光下等待着。

e.en: 昏暗地

ex.en: Two lamps burned dimly.
ex.zh: 两盏油灯昏暗地燃烧着。

e.en: A dim place is rather dark because there is not much light in it.

ex.en: The room was dim and cool and quiet.
ex.zh: 这房间昏暗、阴冷且安静。

e.en: A dim figure or object is not very easy to see, either because it is in shadow or darkness, or because it is far away.

ex.en: Pete's flashlight picked out the dim figures of Bob and Chang.
ex.zh: 皮特的手电筒照射出鲍勃和常的蒙胧身影。

d: adj. 暗淡的，昏暗的；模糊的，看不清的；愚笨的，迟钝的；前景暗淡的，不乐观的
v. （使）变暗；变淡漠，失去光泽；（使）变模糊
【名】 （Dim）（俄）季姆，（柬）丁（人名）

e.en: If things are distributed throughout an area, object, or group, they exist throughout it.

ex.en: These cells are widely distributed throughout the body.
ex.zh: 这些细胞遍布身体各处。

d: adj. 分布的，分散的；（计算机）分布式的
v. distribute 的过去式和过去分词；分配，分发；分布

e.en: Economics is the study of the way in which money, industry, and commerce are organized in a society.

ex.en: His younger sister is studying economics.
ex.zh: 他的妹妹在学经济学。

d: n. 经济学；经济情况；经济体制
n. 电子邮件，电邮（email 的复数形式）：通过互联网发送和接收的电子信息。
v. 发送电子邮件，给某人发电子邮件（email 的第三人称单数形式）。
n. 免除，豁免；免税，免税额
adj. 最快速的（fast 的最高级）
adv. 最快地，最迅速地（fast 的副词最高级）

e.en: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as "She smiled."
e.zh: 与表示身体动作的名词连用，表示做这一动作

ex.en: She stretched her arms out and gave a great yawn.
ex.zh: 她伸开手臂，打了个大呵欠。

ex.en: He gave her a fond smile.
ex.zh: 他充满柔情地朝她微微一笑。

e.en: You use give to say that a person does something for another person. For example, if you give someone a lift, you take them somewhere in your car.

ex.en: I gave her a lift back to her house.
ex.zh: 我让她搭我的车回家。

ex.en: He was given mouth-to-mouth resuscitation.
ex.zh: 对他进行了口对口的人工呼吸。

e.en: You use give with nouns that refer to information, opinions, or greetings to indicate that something is communicated. For example, if you give someone some news, you tell it to them.

ex.en: He gave no details.
ex.zh: 他没有提供任何细节。

ex.en: Would you like to give me your name?
ex.zh: 能告诉我你的名字吗？

e.en: You use give to say how long you think something will last or how much you think something will be.

ex.en: A recent poll gave Campbell a 68 percent support rating.
ex.zh: 最近的一次民意调查预计坎贝尔的支持率为68%。

d: v. 给，交给；赠送，赠与，送给；提供，供给；捐赠；支付，付款；将（时间、精力等）用于；举办，举行；表演，公开进行；允许；使产生（某种感觉）；使拥有（某一特性）；生产，引起；给（某人）打（电话）；告诉，说出，说明；给……评定（等级）；（把药等）注入，服入；看待，承认；做（动作）；传染；使受惩罚，让（某人）做；作出（决定或判决）；预计将持续（时间）；伸长，弯曲，断裂；让步，妥协；表示一种可能的情况或状态
n. 伸展性，弹性；适应（或顺应）能力，灵活性
【名】 （Give）（意）吉韦（人名）

e.en: If you flex your muscles or parts of your body, you bend, move, or stretch them for a short time in order to exercise them. 屈伸 (肌肉或身体某部分)

ex.en: He slowly flexed his muscles and tried to stand.
ex.zh: 他缓慢地活动了一下肌肉，想站起来。

e.en: A flex is an electric cable containing two or more wires that is connected to an electrical appliance. (电器用的)

d: v. 弯曲，曲折（四肢，关节）；活动，绷紧（肌肉）；（材料）有弹性
n. （电器用的）皮线，花线；屈曲；松紧带
adj. 弹性工作制的
【名】 （Flex）（意）弗莱克斯，（法）弗莱（人名）

e.en: Guilt is an unhappy feeling that you have because you have done something wrong or think that you have done something wrong.

ex.en: Her emotions had ranged from anger to guilt in the space of a few seconds.
ex.zh: 她的情绪在几秒钟内由愤怒转为内疚。

e.en: Guilt is the fact that you have done something wrong or illegal.

ex.en: The trial is concerned only with the determination of guilt according to criminal law.
ex.zh: 审判只是根据刑法进行定罪。

d: n. 内疚；罪行；罪责

e.en: If you have a holding in a company, you own shares in it.

ex.en: That would increase Olympia & York's holding to 35%.
ex.zh: 这将使奥林匹亚约克公司的持有股增加至35%。

d: v. 持有；召开；担任；握住（hold 的现在分词）
n. 股份；私有财产；馆藏；控股（用于 holding company 等复合词）；租种的土地；（Holding）霍尔丁（人名）

e.en: An inbox is a shallow container used in offices to put letters and documents in before they are dealt with. (办公室里存放待处理的来函及文件等的)
On a computer, your inbox is the part of your mailbox which stores e-mails that have arrived for you. (电子邮箱中的)

ex.en: I returned home and checked my inbox.
ex.zh: 我回家后查看了收件箱。

d: n. （电子邮件）收件箱；（办公室中存放待处理信件、文件等的）收件盘，收文匣
v. 在社交网站上给（某人）发私信

e.en: You can use increasingly to indicate that a situation or quality is becoming greater in intensity or more common.

ex.en: He was finding it increasingly difficult to make decisions.
ex.zh: 他发现决策越来越困难了。

ex.en: The U.S. has increasingly relied on Japanese capital.
ex.zh: 美国越来越依赖日本资本。

d: adv. 越来越多地，不断增加地

e.en: A job is the work that someone does to earn money.

ex.en: Once I'm in Miami I can get a job.
ex.zh: 一旦我到了迈阿密就能找到工作。

ex.en: Thousands have lost their jobs.
ex.zh: 数千人都丢了工作。

e.en: A job is a particular task.

ex.en: He said he hoped that the job of putting together a coalition wouldn't take too much time.
ex.zh: 他说他希望结成联盟这项任务不会花太长时间。

e.en: The job of a particular person or thing is their duty or function.

ex.en: Their main job is to preserve health rather than treat illness.
ex.zh: 他们的主要职责是保健而不是治病。

ex.en: His first job will be to try and get talks going between the two sides.
ex.zh: 他的首要职责将是设法让双方的谈话进行下去。

e.en: If you say that someone is doing a good job, you mean that they are doing something well.

ex.en: We could do a far better job of managing it than they have.
ex.zh: 我们会比他们管理得好得多。

d: n. 工作（job 的复数形式）

e.en: Intervention is the act of intervening in a situation.

ex.en: ...the role of the United States and its intervention in the internal affairs of many countries.
ex.zh: …美国所扮演的角色及其对许多国家内政的干涉。

d: n. 干预，介入；调停，斡旋；（为改善情况尤指病痛采取的）措施，做法

e.en: If you talk about a particular kind of thing, you are talking about one of the types or sorts of that thing.

ex.en: The party needs a different kind of leadership.
ex.zh: 该党需要一种不同的领导。

ex.en: Had Jamie ever been in any kind of trouble?
ex.zh: 杰米曾经遇到过什么样的麻烦吗？

e.en: If you refer to someone's kind, you are referring to all the other people that are like them or that belong to the same class or set.

ex.en: I can take care of your kind.
ex.zh: 我能对付你这类人。

e.en: You can use all kinds of to emphasize that there are a great number and variety of particular things or people.

ex.en: Adoption can fail for all kinds of reasons.
ex.zh: 收养可能因为各种各样的原因失败。

e.en: You use kind of when you want to say that something or someone can be roughly described in a particular way.

ex.en: It was kind of sad, really.
ex.zh: 这真的有点伤感。

d: n. 种类；同类的人；特征，性质；圣餐的圣体（指面包或葡萄酒）
adj. 宽容的，体贴的，亲切友好的；温和的，无害的；关爱的，好心的（尤用于答谢语中）
【名】 （Kind）（德、法、俄、捷）金德，（瑞典）欣德（人名）

e.en: Land is an area of ground, especially one that is used for a particular purpose such as farming or building.

ex.en: Good agricultural land is in short supply.
ex.zh: 肥沃的农业用地短缺。

ex.en: ...160 acres of land.
ex.zh: …160英亩土地。

e.en: You can refer to an area of land which someone owns as their land or their lands.

ex.en: Their home is on his father's land.
ex.zh: 他们的家坐落在他父亲的土地上。

e.en: If you talk about the land, you mean farming and the way of life in farming areas, in contrast to life in the cities.

ex.en: Living off the land was hard enough at the best of times.
ex.zh: 即使是在最好的时期靠种地生活也是很艰难的。

e.en: Land is the part of the world that consists of ground, rather than sea or air.

ex.en: It isn't clear whether the plane went down over land or sea.
ex.zh: 不清楚飞机是落在陆地上还是海里。

d: n. 土地，地产，领地（land 的复数形式）；国家，国土，地区（文学用语）；平原，开阔地带；（技术）平面，凸面；（Lands）人名，姓氏（葡萄牙语人名“兰茨”）
v. 降落，着陆，登陆；使降落，使着陆，使登陆（land 的第三人称单数形式）；（非正式）陷入，落到，使陷入（某种境地）；（非正式）获得，谋到（工作、合同等）

e.en: Late means near the end of a day, week, year, or other period of time. (时间)

ex.en: It was late in the afternoon.
ex.zh: 那是在接近傍晚的时候。

ex.en: His autobiography was written late in life.
ex.zh: 他的自传是在晚年写的。

e.en: Late is also an adjective.

ex.en: The talks eventually broke down in late spring.
ex.zh: 会谈最终在暮春时破裂。

ex.en: He was in his late 20s.
ex.zh: 他年近三十。

e.en: If it is late, it is near the end of the day or it is past the time that you feel something should have been done. 晚的;

ex.en: It was very late and the streets were deserted.
ex.zh: 天很晚了，街道上空无一人。

e.en: 晚

ex.en: A large crowd had gathered despite the lateness of the hour.
ex.zh: 尽管时间很晚了，还有一大群人聚集在了一起。

d: adj. 晚期的，末期的；晚的，迟的；近日暮的，近深夜的；已故的；不久前的，最近的
adv. 晚，迟；（时间上）接近终了，在晚年；临近日暮，接近午夜；（时间上）接近终了，临近末了，在晚年

e.en: You use at least to say that a number or amount is the smallest that is possible or likely and that the actual number or amount may be greater. The forms at the least and at the very least are also used. (在数量上)

ex.en: Aim to have at least half a pint of milk each day.
ex.zh: 目标是每天至少喝半品脱牛奶。

ex.en: About two-thirds of adults consult their doctor at least once a year.
ex.zh: 大约三分之二的成年人一年至少看一次医生。

e.en: You use at least to say that something is the minimum that is true or possible. The forms at the least and at the very least are also used. 至少 (最小的可能性)

ex.en: She could go on a nice holiday at least.
ex.zh: 她至少能过一个美好的假期。

ex.en: His possession of classified documents in his home was, at the very least, a violation of navy security regulations.
ex.zh: 他把机密文件放在家里，这最起码是违反了海军安全条例。

e.en: You use at least to indicate an advantage that exists in spite of the disadvantage or bad situation that has just been mentioned.

ex.en: We've no idea what his state of health is but at least we know he is still alive.
ex.zh: 我们不清楚他健康状况怎样，尽管如此我们知道他还活着。

e.en: You use at least to indicate that you are correcting or changing something that you have just said. 至少 (修正刚说过的话)

ex.en: It's not difficult to get money for research or at least it's not always difficult.
ex.zh: 获得研究的资金不难，至少说，不总是很难。

d: adj. 一点儿；最少的（little 的最高级）；最微不足道的（little 的最高级形式）；用于极小动植物的名称，如least shrew（little 的最高级形式）
adv. 最低程度地；最少，至少
n. 最不重要的事物，最微小的事物；至少，起码
pron. 最少量；起码

e.en: general appearance or outline 总体外观;

ex.en: a car with fine lines

d: n. line 的复数：线，线条，纹路；行列，队伍；（文字的）一行，诗行；台词；航线，线路，路线；外形，轮廓；姓氏 Lines，莱恩斯
v. line 的第三人称单数：使排成一行；在……上画线

e.en: If a noise is loud, the level of sound is very high and it can be easily heard. Someone or something that is loud produces a lot of noise. 大声的;

ex.en: Suddenly there was a loud bang.
ex.zh: 突然砰地一声响。

ex.en: His voice became harsh and loud.
ex.zh: 他的声音变得又尖又响。

e.en: Loud is also an adverb. 大声地;

ex.en: She wonders whether Paul's hearing is OK because he turns the television up very loud.
ex.zh: 她怀疑保罗的听力有问题，因为他把电视机的音量调得很大。

e.en: 大声地;

ex.en: His footsteps echoed loudly in the tiled hall.
ex.zh: 他的脚步声响亮地回荡在铺着瓷砖的大厅里。

e.en: If you describe something, especially a piece of clothing, as loud, you dislike it because it has very bright colours or very large, bold patterns which look unpleasant. (尤指衣服)

ex.en: He liked to shock with his gold chains and loud clothes.
ex.zh: 他喜欢戴金链子，穿花哨衣服，以此制造轰动。

d: adj. 大声的，响亮的；（人或举止）吵闹的，聒噪的；大声疾呼的，坚定的；（衣服）花哨的
adv. 大声地，响亮地
【名】 （Loud）（英）劳德（人名）
adj. 低级的；品质低劣的

e.en: If you manage an organization, business, or system, or the people who work in it, you are responsible for controlling them. 管理; 经营 (机构、企业、系统等)

ex.en: Within two years he was managing the shop.
ex.zh: 两年内他经营着该商店。

ex.en: There is a lack of confidence in the government's ability to manage the economy.
ex.zh: 对政府管理经济的能力缺乏信心。

e.en: If you manage time, money, or other resources, you deal with them carefully and do not waste them. 管理 (时间、金钱等)

ex.en: In a busy world, managing your time is increasingly important.
ex.zh: 在一个忙碌的世界里，管理好你的时间越来越重要。

e.en: If you manage to do something, especially something difficult, you succeed in doing it. 设法 (做成某事)

ex.en: Somehow, he'd managed to persuade Kay to buy one for him.
ex.zh: 不管怎么说，他已设法说服了凯给他买一个。

ex.en: I managed to pull myself up onto a wet, sloping ledge.
ex.zh: 我设法爬上了一个潮湿的倾斜岩脊。

e.en: If you manage, you succeed in coping with a difficult situation.

ex.en: She had managed perfectly well without medication for three years.
ex.zh: 她3年没用药，却成功地挺了过来。

d: adj. 妥善照看的，受监督的；政府控制的
v. 管理，处理；操纵，控制；设法做到，勉力完成（manage 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A mattress is the large, flat object which is put on a bed to make it comfortable to sleep on.

d: n. 床垫，褥垫；（工程）垫层，沉排，钢筋网

e.en: You use measured to describe something that is careful and deliberate. 慎重的;

ex.en: The men spoke in soft, measured tones.
ex.zh: 这些人说话的语气轻柔，语调平和。

ex.en: Her more measured response will appeal to voters.
ex.zh: 她那经过斟酌的答复会受到选民的欢迎。

d: adj. 慎重而缓慢的，慎重的；慢而稳的，有节奏的；量过的；基于标准的
v. 测量；（指尺寸、长短、数量等）量度为；估量，判定（重要性、价值或影响等）（measure 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you need something, or need to do something, you cannot successfully achieve what you want or live properly without it.

ex.en: He desperately needed money.
ex.zh: 他急需钱。

ex.en: I need to make a phone call.
ex.zh: 我需要打个电话。

e.en: Need is also a noun.

ex.en: Charles has never felt the need to compete with anyone.
ex.zh: 查尔斯从未感觉到与人竞争的需要。

ex.en: ...the child who never had his need for attention and importance satisfied.
ex.zh: …那个受关注和重视的需要从未得到过满足的孩子。

e.en: If an object or place needs something done to it, that action should be done to improve the object or place. If a task needs doing, it should be done to improve a particular situation.

ex.en: The building needs quite a few repairs.
ex.zh: 这栋楼不少处需要修缮。

ex.en: ...a garden that needs tidying.
ex.zh: …一个需要整理的花园。

e.en: If there is a need for something, that thing would improve a situation or something cannot happen without it. 需要;

ex.en: Mr. Forrest believes there is a need for other similar schools throughout the country.
ex.zh: 福里斯特先生相信全国上下有对其他类似学校的需要。

ex.en: "I think we should see a specialist."—"I don't think there's any need for that."
ex.zh: “我想我们应该看个专家。”—“我认为没那必要。”

d: v. 需要；（表示应该或不得不做）有必要（need 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 需要的，必需的

e.en: The night is the part of each day when the sun has set and it is dark outside, especially the time when people are sleeping.

ex.en: The fighting began in the late afternoon and continued all night.
ex.zh: 那场战斗傍晚开始，持续了一整夜。

ex.en: Finally night fell.
ex.zh: 夜幕终于降临了。

e.en: The night is the period of time between the end of the afternoon and the time that you go to bed, especially the time when you relax before going to bed. 晚上 (尤指睡前)

ex.en: So whose party was it last night?
ex.zh: 那么昨天晚上是谁的晚会？

e.en: A particular night is a particular evening when a special event takes place, such as a show or a play. (演出等的)

ex.en: The first night crowd packed the building.
ex.zh: 首次夜场演出，观众全场爆满。

e.en: If it is a particular time at night, it is during the time when it is dark and is before midnight.

ex.en: It's eleven o'clock at night in Moscow.
ex.zh: 现在莫斯科是晚上11点。

d: n. 夜间，夜晚；晚上，傍晚；黄昏；（特殊活动之）夜；黑夜，夜色；挫败时期
adj. 夜晚的；夜晚使用的；夜间进行的；夜晚活动的
int. 晚安（goodnight 的简称）

e.en: Nine is the number 9. 9

ex.en: We still sighted nine yachts.
ex.zh: 我们还是看到了九艘游艇。

d: n. 九，九个
num. 九；九个
adj. 九的，九个的
n. （Nine）人名；（塞）尼内

e.en: Output is used to refer to the amount of something that a person or thing produces.

ex.en: Government statistics show the largest drop in industrial output for ten years.
ex.zh: 政府的统计数字显示出10年来工业产量最大幅度的下降。

e.en: The output of a computer or word processor is the information that it displays on a screen or prints on paper as a result of a particular program. (计算机或文字处理机的)

ex.en: You run the software, you look at the output, you make modifications.
ex.zh: 运行这个软件，看看输出信息，并做修改。

d: n. 产量，作品；产生，生产过程；输出功率；（计算机的）输出信息；输出端
v. 输出

e.en: If you are given notification of something, you are officially informed of it.

ex.en: Names of the dead and injured are being withheld pending notification of relatives.
ex.zh: 伤亡者的姓名在通知亲属前不被公布。

d: n. 通知；通告；（计算机）系统或应用程序推送的提醒消息；（法律）告示（notification 的复数）

e.en: Your parents are your mother and father.

ex.en: Children need their parents.
ex.zh: 孩子们需要父母。

ex.en: This is where a lot of parents go wrong.
ex.zh: 正是在这一点上许多父母都错了。

e.en: An organization's parent organization is the organization that created it and usually still controls it. 创始的 (组织); 母 (公司)

ex.en: Each unit including the parent company has its own, local management.
ex.zh: 每家单位，包括母公司，都有自己的地方管理层。

d: n. 父母，双亲（parent 的复数）；（Parents）人名；（法）帕朗
v. 教养；引起（parent 的三单形式）

e.en: If someone permits something, they allow it to happen. If they permit you to do something, they allow you to do it.

ex.en: He can let the court's decision stand and permit the execution.
ex.zh: 他能让法院的判决成立，并允许处决。

ex.en: The guards permitted me to bring my camera and tape recorder.
ex.zh: 守卫允许我带上相机和录音机。

e.en: A permit is an official document which says that you may do something. For example, you usually need a permit to work in a foreign country.

ex.en: He has to apply for a permit, and we have to find him a job.
ex.zh: 他必须申请一个许可证，而我们必须给他找一份工作。

e.en: If a situation permits something, it makes it possible for that thing to exist, happen, or be done or it provides the opportunity for it. 使成为可能;

ex.en: Try to go out for a walk at lunchtime, if the weather permits.
ex.zh: 如果天气条件允许，午饭时尽量出去散散步。

ex.en: This method of cooking also permits heat to penetrate evenly from both sides.
ex.zh: 这种烹调方法还能使两面均匀受热。

d: v. 允许；批准；（使）有可能；允许有（permit 的过去式及过去分词）
adj. 被允许的，获准的，许可的

e.en: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

ex.en: He asked permission to leave the room.
ex.zh: 他请求离开房间的许可。

ex.en: They cannot leave the country without permission.
ex.zh: 没有许可他们不得离开这个国家。

d: n. 同意，许可；许可证，书面许可

e.en: A pillow is a rectangular cushion that you rest your head on when you are in bed.

d: n. 枕头（pillow 的复数）；靠垫，装饰性软垫（pillow 的复数）
v. 靠（pillow 的第三人称单数形式）；把（头）搁在枕上；给……当枕头

e.en: If you pitch something somewhere, you throw it with some force, usually aiming it carefully.

ex.en: Simon pitched the empty bottle into the lake.
ex.zh: 西蒙把空瓶子投进湖里。

e.en: In the game of baseball, when you pitch the ball, you throw it to the batter for them to hit it. 投 (球)

ex.en: We passed long, hot afternoons pitching a baseball.
ex.zh: 我们以打棒球来消磨一个个漫长的炎热午后。

e.en: To pitch somewhere means to fall forwards suddenly and with a lot of force. (向前)

ex.en: The movement took him by surprise, and he pitched forward.
ex.zh: 突然的移动让他猝不及防，向前跌倒。

ex.en: Alan staggered sideways, pitched head-first over the low wall and fell into the lake.
ex.zh: 艾伦两侧摇晃着，一头栽过矮墙，掉进湖里。

e.en: If someone is pitched into a new situation, they are suddenly forced into it. 迫使进入 (一种新的处境)

ex.en: They were being pitched into a new adventure in which they would have to fight the whole world.
ex.zh: 他们当时正被胁迫参与到一次不得不与整个世界抗衡的新冒险中。

d: n. 体育场地，球场；程度，强度；音准，音高；推销用语；投球；沥青，柏油；（船或飞机的）颠簸；倾斜度，高度；摊位，（街头艺人的）表演场所；（高尔夫）下旋高球；露营地；（技）螺距，节距
v. 扔，抛，掷；（棒球中）投（球）；击地，（使球）定点落地；重跌，坠落；（船或飞机）颠簸；把……定于某水平；使（产品）针对，面向；推销；为……定音高；向下倾斜；扎，搭建；（高尔夫）击下旋高球；用石头铺（路）；（酿酒用语）给（麦芽汁）加酵母；盖上沥青，涂上沥青

e.en: Someone's presence in a place is the fact that they are there.

ex.en: They argued that his presence in the town could only stir up trouble.
ex.zh: 他们争辩说他在城里出现只会搅起麻烦。

e.en: If you say that someone has presence, you mean that they impress people by their appearance and manner.

ex.en: They do not seem to have the vast, authoritative presence of those great men.
ex.zh: 他们似乎没有那些大人物的轩昂威严的风采。

e.en: A presence is a person or creature that you cannot see, but that you are aware of.

ex.en: She started to be affected by the ghostly presence she could feel in the house.
ex.zh: 她开始受到那个幽灵的困扰，她能感觉到它就在屋子里。

e.en: If a country has a military presence in another country, it has some of its armed forces there.

ex.en: The Philippine government wants the U.S. to maintain a military presence in Southeast Asia.
ex.zh: 菲律宾政府希望美国保留在东南亚的驻军。

d: n. 出席，存在；（某人的）所在地方；感觉中的存在物（如鬼魂）；驻扎部队，驻扎的警力；风度，气质；（公司在某地的）工人（或产品），势力

e.en: Private companies, industries, and services are owned or controlled by individuals or stockholders, rather than by the government or an official organization.

ex.en: ...a joint venture with private industry.
ex.zh: …一个与私有企业合资的企业。

ex.en: They sent their children to private schools.
ex.zh: 他们送孩子们上私立学校。

e.en: 私有地

ex.en: No other European country had so much state ownership and so few privately owned businesses.
ex.zh: 没有任何别的欧洲国家有这么多的国有企业和这么少的私有企业。

e.en: Private individuals are acting only for themselves, and are not representing any group, company, or organization.

ex.en: Private individuals with money to lend are more difficult to find than traditional lenders.
ex.zh: 有钱借的个人比传统的放贷者更难找。

ex.en: The king was on a private visit to enable him to pray at the tombs of his ancestors.
ex.zh: 国王在做一次私访以便能祭拜其祖坟。

e.en: Your private things belong only to you, or may only be used by you. 私人的 (财物)

ex.en: They want more state control over private property.
ex.zh: 他们想要对私人财产更多国家控制。

d: adj. 私有的，自用的；（服务，行业）私营的，民营的；没有股票上市的；私下的，秘密的；（交易未涉及商业机构的）私下里的；（想法、感觉）私密的；未担任公职的，无官职的；与官职（或工作）无关的；安静的，不受打扰的；（人）内敛的，不喜欢谈论私事的；（尤指两人）单独的；私下辅导的；（教育，医疗）私立的；只有自己人明白的
n. （美、英陆军或美国海军陆战队）二等兵； 私处，阴部（privates）

e.en: A problem is a situation that is unsatisfactory and causes difficulties for people.

ex.en: ...the economic problems of the inner city.
ex.zh: …内城的经济问题。

ex.en: I do not have a simple solution to the drug problem.
ex.zh: 我并没有一个简单的解决毒品问题的方法。

e.en: A problem is a puzzle that requires logical thought or mathematics to solve it.

ex.en: With mathematical problems, you can save time by approximating.
ex.zh: 对于数学题，你可以用近似法省时间。

d: n. 问题，难题，困难；疾病；（通过算数或仔细思考而解决的）题；（感觉上）不喜欢，不情愿；（尤指国际象棋等）棋式，排局
adj. 难对付的，成问题的

e.en: Productivity is the rate at which goods are produced.

ex.en: The third-quarter results reflect continued improvements in productivity.
ex.zh: 第三季度的结果反映了生产率的持续提高。

d: n. 生产率，生产力

e.en: When you purchase something, you buy it.

ex.en: He purchased a ticket and went up on the top deck.
ex.zh: 他买了张票，上了顶层。

e.en: 购买者

ex.en: The broker will get 5% if he finds a purchaser.
ex.zh: 这个中间人如果找到一个买主就将提成5%。

e.en: The purchase of something is the act of buying it.

ex.en: This week he is to visit China to discuss the purchase of military supplies.
ex.zh: 本周他将访问中国，讨论军用物资的采购。

e.en: A purchase is something that you buy.

ex.en: She opened the tie box and looked at her purchase. It was silk, with maroon stripes.
ex.zh: 她打开领带盒子，看着自己买的东西。那是真丝的，有栗色的条纹。

d: n. 购买，采购
adj. 购买的，采购的
v. 购买，采购；（努力或艰难地）获得，得到；（航海）（用滑轮或杠杆）升起，举起（绳，索，锚）（purchase 的现在分词）

e.en: You use rather than when you are contrasting two things or situations. Rather than introduces the thing or situation that is not true or that you do not want.

ex.en: The problem was psychological rather than physiological.
ex.zh: 这是个心理而不是生理问题。

e.en: Rather is also a conjunction.

ex.en: She made students think for themselves, rather than telling them what to think.
ex.zh: 她让学生们自己思考，而不是告诉他们思考什么。
