e.en: You use rather when you are correcting something that you have just said, especially when you are describing a particular situation after saying what it is not. (尤指修正上文时)

ex.en: Twenty million years ago, Idaho was not the arid place it is now. Rather, it was warm and damp, populated by dense primordial forest.
ex.zh: 2000万年前，爱达荷州不像现在这样干旱。确切地说，它那时温暖潮湿，生长着茂密的原始森林。

e.en: If you say that you would rather do something or you'd rather do it, you mean that you would prefer to do it. If you say that you would rather not do something, you mean that you do not want to do it. 宁愿/

ex.en: If it's all the same to you, I'd rather work at home.
ex.zh: 如果对你来说都一样，我宁愿在家工作。

ex.en: Kids would rather play than study.
ex.zh: 孩子们宁愿玩而不愿学习。

d: adv. 颇，相当；宁愿，最好（would rather）；而不是；更确切地说；（用以使表达的语气婉转）有几分，有点儿；恰恰相反，而是
int. 当然，的确（表同意）
【名】  （Rather）（英）拉瑟（人名）

e.en: to support or enclose (a picture, photograph, etc) in a new or different frame 再构造(图画、照片等)

d: v. reframe 的过去式和过去分词：重新框定，重新构建，即改变（问题、议题等）的表述、解释或观点，以新的方式理解或呈现；给（图画、照片等）重新装框。

e.en: The rest is used to refer to all the parts of something or all the things in a group that remain or that you have not already mentioned.

ex.en: It was an experience I will treasure for the rest of my life.
ex.zh: 这是一次我将终生珍视的经历。

e.en: Rest is also a pronoun.

ex.en: The first payment was made yesterday, and the rest will be paid next month.
ex.zh: 第一笔款在昨天支付了，其余部分将在下个月支付。

e.en: to continue to be (as specified); remain 仍然是;

ex.en: rest assured

e.en: You can add and the rest or all the rest of it to the end of a statement or list when you want to refer in a vague way to other things that are associated with the ones you have already mentioned. 诸如此类;

ex.en: ...a man with nice clothes, an SUV, and the rest.
ex.zh: …一个衣着考究、开一辆四轮驱动，诸如此类的男人。

d: v. 休息，歇息；使（运动员）暂时离队； （问题，事情）被搁置；（被）支撑，（使）倚靠；安息，长眠；在于，存放于；（目光）停留（rest on）；依靠，仰仗（rest on/upon）；寄（希望）于，相信；让（土地）休耕；（原告或被告）完成向法庭提出证据（或辩论）；保持不变；（演员）无戏可演
n. 休息（时间）；剩余部分，余下的人（物）（the rest）；静止，停止；（音乐的）休止，休止符；（演说或诗句的）停顿；撑架，支座；（剖）（器官或组织的）一小碎块；（网球）对打，回合
【名】 （Rest）（美）雷斯特（人名）

e.en: If you sell something that you own, you let someone have it in return for money.

ex.en: Catlin sold the paintings to Philadelphia industrialist Joseph Harrison.
ex.zh: 卡特林把这些画卖给了费城实业家约瑟夫·哈里森。

ex.en: The directors sold the business for $14.8 million.
ex.zh: 董事们把这个公司以1480万美元卖掉了。

e.en: If a shop sells a particular thing, it is available for people to buy there. 出售;

ex.en: It sells everything from hair ribbons to oriental rugs.
ex.zh: 这里出售各种商品，从扎头发的发带到东方小地毯都有。

e.en: If something sells for a particular price, that price is paid for it.

ex.en: Unmodernized property can sell for up to 40 percent of its modernized market value.
ex.zh: 未经现代化改造的房地产售价至多是其现代化改造后市价的40%。

e.en: If something sells, it is bought by the public, usually in fairly large quantities. 有销路;

ex.en: Even if this album doesn't sell and the critics don't like it, we wouldn't ever change.
ex.zh: 即使这张专辑没有销路，并且也不讨评论家们喜欢，我们也决不会改变。

d: v. （sell 的第三人称单数形式）卖，出售，经销；经营；（商品）售价为；有销路；推销，推荐，使接受；促进…的销路；出卖，背叛
n. （Sells）人名；塞尔斯

e.en: In a sport or game, if a player scores a goal or a point, they gain a goal or point. (比赛中) 得分;

ex.en: Patten scored his second touchdown of the game.
ex.zh: 帕顿在比赛中第2次持球触地得分。

ex.en: He scored late in the third quarter to cut the gap to 10 points.
ex.zh: 他在第3节快结束时进了一球，把分差缩小到10分。

e.en: If you score a particular number or amount, for example, as a mark in a test, you achieve that number or amount. (测试)

ex.en: Kelly had scored an average of 147 on three separate IQ tests.
ex.zh: 凯利在3次单独进行的智商测试中平均得到147分。

ex.en: Congress scores low in public opinion polls.
ex.zh: 国会在民意测验中得分很低。

e.en: Someone's score in a game or test is a number, for example, a number of points or runs, which shows what they have achieved or what level they have reached. 得分;

ex.en: The U.S. Open golf tournament was won by Ben Hogan, with a score of 287.
ex.zh: 美国高尔夫球公开赛由本·霍根以287分夺冠。

ex.en: He won this year's title with a score of 9.687.
ex.zh: 他以9.687分赢得本年度的冠军。

e.en: The score in a game is the result of it or the current situation, as indicated by the number of goals, runs, or points obtained by the two teams or players.

ex.en: 4-1 was the final score.
ex.zh: 最终比分是4：1。

ex.en: They beat the Giants by a score of 7 to 3.
ex.zh: 他们以7比3战胜了巨人队。

d: n. 比分（score 的复数）；考试成绩，分数（score 的复数）；大量，许多（scores of）
v. 得分（score 的第三人称单数形式）；刻痕，划线（score 的第三人称单数形式）
n. 严重性；严肃；认真
adv. in all seriousness：严肃地，一本正经地

e.en: Seven is the number 7. 7;

ex.en: Sarah and Ella have been friends for seven years.
ex.zh: 萨拉和埃拉已经是7年的朋友了。

d: num. 七，七个
n. 七；七个人；七点钟；七岁；（Seven）（土、法、俄）谢文（人名）
adj. 七的，七个的

e.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.

ex.en: He stopped, shifting his cane to his left hand.
ex.zh: 他停下来，把手杖移到左手。

ex.en: He shifted from foot to foot.
ex.zh: 他从一只脚换到另一只脚。

e.en: If someone's opinion, a situation, or a policy shifts or is shifted, it changes slightly.

ex.en: Attitudes to mental illness have shifted in recent years.
ex.zh: 对精神病的态度近年来已稍微有所改变。

e.en: Shift is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a shift in government policy.
ex.zh: …政府政策的些许改变。

e.en: If someone shifts the responsibility or blame for something onto you, they unfairly make you responsible or make people blame you for it, instead of them. 推卸;

ex.en: It was a vain attempt to shift the responsibility for the murder to somebody else.
ex.zh: 把这项谋杀的罪责转嫁于他人是徒劳之举。

d: v. （使）移动，（使）转移；（使）转换到（另一个人或另一事物）；（使）改变意见（或信仰等）；赶快；换（挡）；（计算机）移位；按（计算机键盘上的）Shift 键；摆脱，消除；（尤指大量）销售，出售；狼吞虎咽地吃；含糊其辞，拐弯抹角
n. 改变，转变；轮班工作时间；轮班工作的人；（计算机键盘上的）Shift 键；（计算机）移位；（机动车的）换挡装置；宽松直筒连衣裙（=shift dress）；长而宽松的内衣；（建筑）错位；（美橄）（开赛前）球员位置的变换；（天文）（光谱线的）偏移；语音演变（sound shift 的简称）；计谋，诡计

e.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves slightly.

ex.en: He stopped, shifting his cane to his left hand.
ex.zh: 他停下来，把手杖移到左手。

ex.en: He shifted from foot to foot.
ex.zh: 他从一只脚换到另一只脚。

e.en: If someone's opinion, a situation, or a policy shifts or is shifted, it changes slightly.

ex.en: Attitudes to mental illness have shifted in recent years.
ex.zh: 对精神病的态度近年来已稍微有所改变。

e.en: Shift is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a shift in government policy.
ex.zh: …政府政策的些许改变。

e.en: If someone shifts the responsibility or blame for something onto you, they unfairly make you responsible or make people blame you for it, instead of them. 推卸;

ex.en: It was a vain attempt to shift the responsibility for the murder to somebody else.
ex.zh: 把这项谋杀的罪责转嫁于他人是徒劳之举。

d: v. 转移；移动（shift 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you shorten an event or the length of time that something lasts, or if it shortens, it does not last as long as it would otherwise do or as it used to do.

ex.en: Smoking can shorten your life.
ex.zh: 吸烟会缩短你的寿命。

ex.en: The trading day is shortened in observance of the Labour Day holiday.
ex.zh: 交易日为了庆祝劳动节而缩短。

e.en: If you shorten an object or if it shortens, it becomes smaller in length. 使变短;

ex.en: Her father paid $5,000 for an operation to shorten her nose.
ex.zh: 她父亲为一个缩短她的鼻子的手术花了$5000。

e.en: If you shorten a name or other word, you change it by removing some of the letters.

ex.en: Originally called Lili, she eventually shortened her name to Lee.
ex.zh: 她原本叫莉莉，最后她把名字缩写成了莉。

d: vt. 缩短，使变短，减少；缩写（名字、单词等），删节
vi. 缩短，变短

e.en: A sign is a mark or shape that always has a particular meaning, for example, in mathematics or music.

ex.en: Equations are generally written with an equal sign.
ex.zh: 等式通常用等号来写。

e.en: A sign is a movement of your arms, hands, or head which is intended to have a particular meaning. 姿势;

ex.en: They gave Lavalle the thumbs-up sign.
ex.zh: 他们给拉瓦列做了一个竖起大拇指的手势。

e.en: If you sign, you communicate with someone using sign language. If a programme or performance is signed, someone uses sign language so that deaf people can understand it. 打手势; (节目或表演)

ex.en: All programmes will be either "signed" or subtitled.
ex.zh: 所有的节目都配有手势语或者字幕。

e.en: A sign is a piece of wood, metal, or plastic with words or pictures on it. Signs give you information about something, or give you a warning or an instruction.

ex.en: ...a sign saying that the motorway was closed because of snow.
ex.zh: …一个写着公路因大雪封闭的指示牌。

d: n. 指示牌，标志；迹象，征兆；示意动作，手势；手语动作；符号，记号；踪迹，踪影；（医）征，体征；神迹（主要用于《圣经》和文学作品中）；（野生动物的）足迹，臭迹；（占星）（黄道12宫中的）宫，星座；（数）正负号；暗号，信号；（表示某人状况或经历的）动作，反应
v. 签名，署名；（与机构、公司等）签约；示意，打手势；打手语；用标志杆（或其他记号）表示

e.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind does not think. 睡眠;

ex.en: They were exhausted from lack of sleep.
ex.zh: 他们因睡眠不足而疲惫不堪了。

ex.en: Be quiet and go to sleep.
ex.zh: 安静，睡觉吧。

e.en: When you sleep, you rest with your eyes closed and your mind and body inactive. 睡着;

ex.en: During the drive, the baby slept.
ex.zh: 在行驶中那个婴儿睡了。

ex.en: I've not been able to sleep for the last few nights.
ex.zh: 最近几个晚上我一直无法入睡。

e.en: A sleep is a period of sleeping. (一段)

ex.en: I think he may be ready for a sleep soon.
ex.zh: 我想他可能准备好了马上睡一觉。

e.en: If a building or room sleeps a particular number of people, it has beds for that number of people.

ex.en: The villa sleeps 10.
ex.zh: 这幢别墅可供10人住宿。

d: v. sleep 的第三人称单数形式：睡觉，睡眠，进入一种自然的、周期性的休息状态，意识减弱，肌肉松弛；（房间、建筑物、车辆等）可供…人住宿；sleep with 的第三人称单数形式：与…同床（委婉地指与…发生性关系）。
n. sleep 的复数形式：多段睡眠时间；多次睡眠。

e.en: Sold is the past tense and past participle of . (sell)

d: v. 卖，销售（sell 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已售出的，已卖出的（多作表语）；sold out：售罄的，脱销的，（门票等）全部售完的
n. （Sold）人名，（瑞典）索尔德

e.en: Your status is your social or professional position. 社会地位;

ex.en: People of higher status tend more to use certain drugs.
ex.zh: 社会地位较高的人更倾向于使用某些药物。

ex.en: ...women and men of wealth and status.
ex.zh: …有钱有势的男男女女。

e.en: Status is the importance and respect that someone has among the public or a particular group. (在公众中或某一团体中的) 威望;

ex.en: Nurses are undervalued, and they never enjoy the same status as doctors.
ex.zh: 护士们没有得到足够重视，她们从未享受和医生一样的地位。

e.en: The status of something is the importance that people give it.

ex.en: Those things that can be assessed by external tests are being given unduly high status.
ex.zh: 那些能通过外部测试进行评估的东西受到过高重视。

e.en: A particular status is an official description that says what category a person, organization, or place belongs to, and gives them particular rights or advantages.

ex.en: The Snoqualmie tribe regained its status as a federally recognized tribe.
ex.zh: 斯诺夸尔米部落重新获得了联邦政府所承认的部落的身份。

d: n. 法律地位（或身份）；（尤指在社会中的）地位，身份；高级职位，社会上层地位；重视（或崇尚）程度；状况，情形

e.en: If you stay where you are, you continue to be there and do not leave.

ex.en: "Stay here," Trish said. "I'll bring the car down the drive to take you back."
ex.zh: “呆在这儿，”特里希说道，“我会把车开下来送你回去。”

e.en: If you stay in a town, or hotel, or at someone's house, you live there for a short time. (在某城市、酒店、某人家里) 暂住;

ex.en: Gordon stayed at The Park Hotel, Milan.
ex.zh: 戈登住在了米兰的帕克酒店。

ex.en: Can't you stay a few more days?
ex.zh: 你不能多住几天吗？

e.en: Stay is also a noun. 暂住;

ex.en: An experienced Indian guide is provided during your stay.
ex.zh: 在你逗留期间给你配备一位经验丰富的印第安向导。

e.en: anything that supports or steadies, such as a prop or buttress 支撑物;

d: n. 刚性结合；撑法；加劲；拉线
vt. 停留（stay 的现在分词形式）
vi. 停留（stay 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

ex.en: ...a relaxed and happy atmosphere that will allow you to study to your full potential.
ex.zh: …一个将使你学习到充分发挥潜能的轻松又愉快的氛围。

ex.en: He studied History and Economics.
ex.zh: 他学过历史和经济学。

e.en: Study is the activity of studying.

ex.en: ...the use of maps and visual evidence in the study of local history.
ex.zh: …在当地历史的学习中地图和图像证据的使用。

e.en: A study of a subject is a piece of research on it.

ex.en: Recent studies suggest that as many as 5 in 1,000 new mothers are likely to have this problem.
ex.zh: 最近的研究表明，1000个新妈妈中有多达5个可能有这个问题。

e.en: You can refer to educational subjects or courses that contain several elements as studies of a particular kind.

ex.en: ...a centre for Islamic studies.
ex.zh: …一个伊斯兰教学科中心。

d: n. （专题）研究，调查；（尤指通过书本的）学习，攻读；用于某些学科名称（studies）；功课，课业，学业（studies）；学术专著，专题论文；学习者；学习对象，研究对象；（绘画的）试画， 习作；书房，书斋；细致考虑，仔细检查，审视； 特别的事物（或人）；以特定速度背台词的演员（舞台俚语）；描写，描绘；练习曲
v. 学习，攻读；认真阅读，仔细看；研究，调查；仔细考虑，慎重思考；（演员）记住（或背下）（台词）
【名】 （Study）（英）斯塔迪 （人名）

e.en: A subscription is an amount of money that you pay regularly in order to belong to an organization, to help a charity or campaign, or to receive copies of a magazine or newspaper. 会员费; 捐赠款;

ex.en: You can become a member by paying the yearly subscription.
ex.zh: 你通过支付年度会员费可以成为一名会员。

e.en: Subscription television is television that you can watch only if you pay a subscription. A subscription channel is a channel that you can watch only if you pay a subscription. (电视或频道)

ex.en: Premiere, a subscription channel which began in 1991, shows live football covering the top two divisions.
ex.zh: 始于1991年的一个付费频道实况转播两大顶级足球赛。

d: n. （杂志等的）订阅费，（服务的）用户费；订阅，订购； （组织或俱乐部的）会费，捐赠款；集体资助，集体捐助；（对组织或项目的）捐赠协议，认捐书；（文件末尾的）签名，附注；季票（文化活动的季票）；（股票的）认购（协议）；通过预订来全部或部分支付出版费用的方法
adj. （电视或电视频道）付费的，收费的

e.en: A streetlight is a tall post with a light at the top, which stands by the side of a road to light it up, usually in a city. 街灯;

ex.en: As the day darkened the streetlights came on.
ex.zh: 天色渐暗，街灯亮了。

d: n. 街灯，路灯（streetlight 的复数）

e.en: Something that is a symbol of a society or an aspect of life seems to represent it because it is very typical of it.

ex.en: To them, the monarchy is the special symbol of nationhood.
ex.zh: 对他们而言，君主政体是国家的特殊象征。

e.en: A symbol of something such as an idea is a shape or design that is used to represent it.

ex.en: Later in this same passage Yeats resumes his argument for the Rose as an Irish symbol.
ex.zh: 后来在这同一篇文章里，叶芝再次提到把玫瑰作为爱尔兰象征的观点。

e.en: A symbol for an item in a calculation or scientific formula is a number, letter, or shape that represents that item.

ex.en: What's the chemical symbol for mercury?
ex.zh: 水银的化学符号是什么？

d: n. 象征，标志；符号；代表性的人（物）

e.en: You use today to refer to this day on which you are speaking or writing.

ex.en: How are you feeling today?
ex.zh: 你今天感觉怎么样？

e.en: Today is also a noun.

ex.en: Today is Friday, September 14th.
ex.zh: 今天是9月14日，星期五。

e.en: You can refer to the present period of history as today.

ex.en: The United States is in a serious recession today.
ex.zh: 美国当今处于严重的经济萧条期。

e.en: Today is also a noun.

ex.en: In today's America, health care is one of the very biggest businesses.
ex.zh: 在当今的美国，医疗保健是几个最大的行业之一。

d: adv. 今天，今日；现今，在当代
n. 今天，今日；现在，当代
【名】 （Today）（印度、美、俄）托迪（人名）

e.en: If you are uncomfortable, you are slightly worried or embarrassed, and not relaxed and confident. 不自在的;

ex.en: The request for money made them feel uncomfortable.
ex.zh: 要钱的事使他们感到很尴尬。

ex.en: If you are uncomfortable with your therapist, you must discuss it.
ex.zh: 如果你在自己的治疗师面前不自在，你必须提出来。

e.en: 不自在地;

ex.en: Sandy leaned across the table, his face uncomfortably close to Brad's.
ex.zh: 桑迪将身体探过桌子，他的脸贴近布拉德的脸，使布拉德感觉很不自在。

ex.en: I became uncomfortably aware that the people at the next table were watching me.
ex.zh: 我意识到旁桌的人在看我，感到很不自在。

e.en: Something that is uncomfortable makes you feel slight pain or physical discomfort when you experience it or use it.

ex.en: Wigs are hot and uncomfortable to wear constantly.
ex.zh: 假发常戴让人感到又热又不舒服。

ex.en: The ride back to the centre of the town was hot and uncomfortable.
ex.zh: 乘车返回市中心一路上又热又不舒服。

e.en: 令人不舒服地

ex.en: The water was uncomfortably cold.
ex.zh: 水冷得让人不舒服。

d: adj. 身体不适的，感到不舒服的；令人不舒服的；不自在的，不安的；使人不自在的，使人不安的；（处境、事实等）令人不快的，棘手的
adj. 不能到达的，无法接近的（指地点、区域等）；不能得到的，不能达到的（指目标、理想、愿望等）；无法联系的，联系不上的（指人、机构等）；（计算机网络）不可达的，无法访问的；（编程、规则系统）不可达的，不会执行的

e.en: Wearable clothes are practical, comfortable, and suitable for ordinary people to wear, rather than being very unusual or extreme.

ex.en: His clothes are comfortable and wearable.
ex.zh: 他的衣服舒适并适于穿着。

d: adj. 可穿戴的，穿戴舒适的，适于穿着的
n. 可穿戴设备（尤指可穿戴计算机）；衣服

e.en: If you have a weakness for something, you like it very much, although this is perhaps surprising or undesirable.

ex.en: Stephen himself had a weakness for cats.
ex.zh: 史蒂芬自己偏爱猫。

d: n. 虚弱，软弱；缺点，不足；疲软；癖好，嗜好，宠爱

e.en: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.

ex.en: Don't worry, your luggage will come on afterwards by taxi.
ex.zh: 不要担心，你的行李随后将由出租车送到。

ex.en: I worry about her constantly.
ex.zh: 我一直在为她担心。

e.en: If someone or something worries you, they make you anxious because you keep thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might be connected with them.

ex.en: I'm still in the early days of my recovery and that worries me.
ex.zh: 我仍处于恢复期的初始阶段，这使我担心。

e.en: If someone or something does not worry you, you do not dislike them or you are not annoyed by them. 使烦恼 (用于否定句中)

ex.en: The cold doesn't worry me.
ex.zh: 寒冷不会使我烦恼。

e.en: Worry is the state or feeling of anxiety and unhappiness caused by the problems that you have or by thinking about unpleasant things that might happen.

ex.en: Modern American life is full of worry: the job, the kids, money, the stock market.
ex.zh: 现代美国生活充满了忧虑：工作、孩子、金钱、股市。

d: v. 担心，发愁；使担忧，使发愁，使焦虑；烦扰，使不安宁；（狗）追赶，撕咬（其他动物）
n. 令人担忧的事，令人发愁的问题；担心，忧虑

e.en: Your wellness is how healthy you are, and how well and happy you feel.

d: n. 健康，安康，身心健康；健康养生，保健及相关的项目、服务、行业，常用于 wellness program、wellness center 等复合词

e.en: A young person, animal, or plant has not lived or existed for very long and is not yet mature. 年轻的; 幼小的 (人、动物、植物等)

ex.en: ...sex information written for young people.
ex.zh: …为年轻人写的性知识。

ex.en: I crossed the hill, and found myself in a field of young barley.
ex.zh: 我翻过那座山，发现自己来到了一块大麦苗地。

e.en: The young are people who are young.

ex.en: The association is advising pregnant women, the very young and the elderly to avoid such foods.
ex.zh: 该协会在建议孕妇、幼儿和老人避免这类食品。

e.en: You use young to describe a time when a person or thing was young. 幼小的; 年轻的 (时期)

ex.en: In her younger days my mother had been a successful saleswoman.
ex.zh: 在年轻的时侯，我母亲曾是位成功的推销员。

e.en: Someone who is young in appearance or behaviour looks or behaves as if they are young. (外表、行为)

ex.en: I was twenty-three, I suppose, and young for my age.
ex.zh: 我想我那时是23岁，看起来比我实际年龄小。

d: adj. 幼小的，年轻的；存在不久的，新成立的；（显得）年轻的，（显得）岁数不大的；适合年轻人的；由年轻人（或儿童）构成的，青少年的，平均年龄小的；夭折的，早逝的
n. 年轻人（the young）；幼崽，雏鸟
【名】 （Young）（英、葡）扬，（柬）永，（中）杨，（广东话）威妥玛（人名）

e.en: The growth of something such as an industry, organization, or idea is its development in size, wealth, or importance.

ex.en: ...the growth of nationalism.
ex.zh: …民族主义的高涨。

ex.en: ...Japan's enormous economic growth.
ex.zh: …日本经济巨大的发展。

e.en: The growth in something is the increase in it.

ex.en: A steady growth in the popularity of two smaller parties may upset the polls.
ex.zh: 两个较小政党声誉的持续增长也许会搅乱大选。

ex.en: The area has seen a rapid population growth.
ex.zh: 这个地区人口快速增长。

e.en: A growth industry, area, or market is one that is increasing in size or activity.

ex.en: Computers and electronics are growth industries and need skilled technicians.
ex.zh: 计算机与电子属于发展中的行业，需要熟练的技术人员。

e.en: Someone's growth is the development and progress of their character. (性格的)

ex.en: ...the child's emotional and intellectual growth.
ex.zh: …孩子情感和智力方面的成长。

d: n. 成长，生长；增长，发展；肿瘤，赘生物；生长物，产物；种植，栽培
adj. 发展的，增长的
n. （Leuven）鲁汶，勒芬（比利时城市）
n. （Leuven）（美）勒文（人名）

e.en: A district is a particular area of a town or country.

ex.en: I drove around the business district.
ex.zh: 我绕着商业区行驶。

d: n. 区域，地域，行政区（district 的复数形式）
v. 把……划分为区（district 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A city is a large town.

ex.en: ...the city of Bologna.
ex.zh: …波洛尼亚市。

d: n. 城市，都市；市民，全市居民；市政府；充满……的地方；伦敦金融、商业区；（国王或女王授权的）特许市；（由州政府划定市界并授予特权的）特权市

e.en: If someone or something becomes a particular thing, they start to change and develop into that thing, or start to develop the characteristics mentioned.

ex.en: I first became interested in Islam while I was doing my nursing training.
ex.zh: 我在进行护理训练的时候，我初次对伊斯兰教产生了兴趣。

e.en: If something becomes someone, it makes them look attractive or it seems right for them. 适合;

ex.en: Does khaki become you?
ex.zh: 卡其布适合你吗？

e.en: If you wonder what has become of someone or something, you wonder where they are and what has happened to them. (某人、某事物)

ex.en: She thought constantly about her family; she might never know what had become of them.
ex.zh: 她经常想着她的家人；她也许永远都不知道他们怎么样了。

d: v. 变得，变成，成为（become 的第三人称单数现在时）；适合，与……相称（become 的第三人称单数现在时，及物用法）；用于 what becomes of... 结构，表示……怎么样了，……遭遇了什么

e.en: When you answer someone who has asked you something, you say something back to them. (口头)

ex.en: Just answer the question.
ex.zh: 只回答这个问题。

ex.en: He paused before answering.
ex.zh: 他在回答前停了下来。

e.en: If you answer a letter or advertisement, you write to the person who wrote it.

ex.en: Did he answer your letter?
ex.zh: 他回复你的信了吗？

e.en: When you answer the telephone, you pick it up when it rings. When you answer the door, you open it when you hear a knock or the bell.

ex.en: She answered her phone on the first ring.
ex.zh: 她在响第一声铃时就接了电话。

e.en: Answer is also a noun.

ex.en: I knocked at the front door and there was no answer.
ex.zh: 我敲了前门，没有应答。

d: v. 回答，答复；回复；接电话；应门；答（题）；回应，反击；满足，适合；与……相符，相配；解决（问题）
n. 回答，答复；答案；解决办法；回信，回函；接听，应门；相当的人，对应物

e.en: You use everyone or everybody to refer to all the people in a particular group. (某群体中的)

ex.en: Everyone on the street was shocked when they heard the news.
ex.zh: 听到这个消息，街上所有人都感到震惊。

ex.en: Not everyone thinks that the government is being particularly generous.
ex.zh: 并不是所有人都认为政府是在特别慷慨。

e.en: You use everyone or everybody to refer to all people.

ex.en: Everyone wrestles with self-doubt and feels like a failure at times.
ex.zh: 人人都会有与不自信作斗争、感觉自己是个失败者的时候。

ex.en: Everyone needs some free time for rest and relaxation.
ex.zh: 人人都需要一些休息和放松的空闲时间。

d: pron. 每个人，人人，大家

e.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

ex.en: ...the younger generation of party members.
ex.zh: …较年轻一代的党员。

e.en: A generation is the period of time, usually considered to be about thirty years, that it takes for children to grow up and become adults and have children of their own. 代 (通常约为三十年)

ex.en: Within a generation, flight has become the method used by many travellers.
ex.zh: 在不到一代的时间里，飞行已成为许多旅行者的出行方式。

e.en: You can use generation to refer to a stage of development in the design and manufacture of machines or equipment. (机械、设备的设计和制造的)

ex.en: ...a new generation of Apple computers.
ex.zh: …新一代苹果电脑。

e.en: Generation is used to indicate how long members of your family have had a particular nationality. For example, second generation means that you were born in the country you live in, but your parents were not. (指家庭成员拥有某国国籍的时间)

ex.en: ...second-generation Jamaicans in New York.
ex.zh: …在纽约的第二代牙买加人。

d: n. 一代（人）；一代人的时间；（产品发展的）代；产生

e.en: You refer to the buildings in which people live as housing when you are talking about their standard, price, or availability.

ex.en: ...a shortage of affordable housing.
ex.zh: …廉价住房的短缺。

e.en: a part designed to shelter, cover, contain, or support a component, such as a bearing, or a mechanism, such as a pump or wheel

ex.en: a bearing housing
a motor housing

d: n. 房屋，住宅；住房供给，住房建设；（机器的）外壳，外罩；（木块上的）槽，榫眼；遮盖物，遮蔽物
v. 覆盖；给……房子住；把……储藏在房内（house 的现在分词形式）

e.en: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The deaths occurred when police acted to stop widespread looting and vandalism.
ex.zh: 当警方行动起来去制止大范围的洗劫和蓄意破坏时，死亡事件发生了。

e.en: If you act on advice or information, you do what has been advised or suggested. (按照建议或信息)

ex.en: A patient will usually listen to the doctor's advice and act on it.
ex.zh: 病人通常会听从医生的建议并且按照它行动。

e.en: If someone acts in a particular way, they behave in that way.

ex.en: ...a gang of youths who were acting suspiciously.
ex.zh: …一帮表现可疑的年轻人。

ex.en: He acted as if he hadn't heard any of it.
ex.zh: 他表现得好像一点都没有听过这件事一样。

e.en: If someone or something acts as a particular thing, they have that role or function.

ex.en: Among his other duties, he acted both as the ship's surgeon and as chaplain for the men.
ex.zh: 另外，他兼任船上的外科医生以及船员们的牧师。

d: v. 行动；举动，表现；假装；表演，演出；担任；起作用；代理；（心理分析）行为表现
n. 行为，行动；法案；装模作样；（戏剧、歌剧等的）一幕；一段表演；节目；表演者，演出团体；发现某人正在（做某事）；判决书；会议记录，公报

e.en: The next period of time, event, person, or thing is the one that comes immediately after the present one or after the previous one.

ex.en: I got up early the next morning.
ex.zh: 第二天早晨我起得很早。

ex.en: ...the next available flight.
ex.zh: …下一趟可以乘坐的航班。

e.en: You use next in expressions such as next Friday, next day and next year to refer, for example, to the first Friday, day, or year that comes after the present or previous one. 下一 (年、月、星期等)

ex.en: Let's plan a big night next week.
ex.zh: 我们下周组织一次盛大的晚会吧。

ex.en: He retires next January.
ex.zh: 他明年1月份退休。

e.en: Next is also an adjective. 下一 (年、月、星期等)

ex.en: I'll be 26 years old next Friday.
ex.zh: 我下周五就26岁了。

e.en: Next is also a pronoun.

ex.en: He predicted that the region's economy would grow by about six percent both this year and next.
ex.zh: 他预测该地区的经济在今年和明年都会以约6%的速度增长。

d: adj. 下一个的，接下来的；（时间）紧接着来到的，下次的；紧邻的；其他的
adv. 紧接着，随后；仅次于；下次，再次；（用于询问，表示吃惊或困惑）
n. 下一个人或事件
det. 下一（年、月、星期等）

e.en: When you run, you move more quickly than when you walk, for example because you are in a hurry to get somewhere, or for exercise.

ex.en: I excused myself and ran back to the telephone.
ex.zh: 我道了歉，跑回去接电话。

ex.en: He ran the last block to the White House with two cases of gear.
ex.zh: 他带着两箱工具跑过最后一个街区到了白宫。

e.en: When someone runs in a race, they run in competition with other people. 参加…赛跑;

ex.en: ...when I was running in the New York Marathon.
ex.zh: …当我正参加纽约马拉松赛跑时。

ex.en: He ran a tremendous race.
ex.zh: 他参加了一场大规模赛跑。

e.en: When a horse runs in a race or when its owner runs it, it competes in a race. 使 (马) 参加比赛; (马)

ex.en: He was overruled by the owner, Peter Bolton, who insisted on Cool Ground running in the Gold Cup.
ex.zh: 他的意见被坚持让酷地参加金杯赛的主人彼得•博尔顿否决了。

e.en: If you say that something long, such as a road, runs in a particular direction, you are describing its course or position. You can also say that something runs the length or width of something else. (道路等)

ex.en: ...the sun-dappled trail which ran through the beech woods.
ex.zh: …一条穿过山毛榉树林的阳光斑驳的小路。

d: v. 跑，奔跑；参加（赛跑），举行（比赛）；跑垒，持球跑动进攻；奔忙，赶快去；管理，经营，使用（车辆）；（使）运转，操作；刊登，播放；（使）行驶；（使）移动，揉擦；闯红灯；（使）流动，流淌；掉色，渗色；变成，变得；达到（一定数量或比率）；（对……）进行（测试或检验）；参加竞选；（连裤袜、长统袜）抽丝，脱线；（使）延伸；（感觉或想法）掠过，迅速传遍；包含（某种词语、内容等）；持续，延续；偷运，走私；印刷；（特征）共有，世代相传（run in）；（物品，行动）花费（某人）（特定数额的钱）
n. 跑步，赛跑；旅程，航程；一系列（成功或失败）；连续上演（或放映）；尝试，努力；额定产量；抛售（美元、英镑等）；争购，挤兑；滑道，路径；（板球或棒球中的）得分；使用自由，出入自由（the run of）；竞选；普通人，普通事物；饲养场；急奏，走句；顺子；腹泻（the runs）；（长统袜或连裤袜的）抽丝；（油漆或类似物刷得过厚引起的）挂流，小溪；（航海）船尾端部
【名】 （Run）（塞）鲁恩（人名）

e.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true. 承认 (不好、不快或尴尬的事实)

ex.en: I am willing to admit that I do make mistakes.
ex.zh: 我愿意承认我确实会犯错误。

ex.en: Up to two thirds of 14 to 16 year olds admit to buying alcohol illegally.
ex.zh: 14至16岁的少年中有多达2/3的少年承认非法买过酒。

e.en: If someone is admitted to a hospital, they are taken into the hospital for treatment and kept there until they are well enough to go home. 接收 (入院)

ex.en: She was admitted to the hospital with a soaring temperature.
ex.zh: 她因高烧被接收入院。

e.en: If someone is admitted to an organization or group, they are allowed to join it. 接收 (加入)

ex.en: He was admitted to the Académie Culinaire de France.
ex.zh: 他被接收加入法国厨艺学会。

e.en: To admit someone to a place means to allow them to enter it.

ex.en: Embassy security personnel refused to admit him or his wife.
ex.zh: 使馆保安人员拒绝让他或他的妻子进入。

d: v. （勉强）承认；招认，招供；准许进入（某处）；接纳，接收（入学）；收治，接收入院；承认……有效；容许，为……留有余地

e.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings.
The architect of an idea, event, or institution is the person who invented it or made it happen. 设计师;

ex.en: James Madison was the principal architect of the constitution.
ex.zh: 詹姆斯·麦迪逊是该宪法的主设计师。

d: n. （建）建筑师（architect 的复数形式）；（思想、事件、制度等的）设计者，缔造者（常与 of 连用）
v. 设计，规划；建造，缔造（architect 的三单形式）

e.en: If one thing is an alternative to another, the first can be found, used, or done instead of the second.

ex.en: New ways to treat arthritis may provide an alternative to painkillers.
ex.zh: 治疗关节炎的新方法可能会提供一种止痛药的替代品。

e.en: An alternative plan or offer is different from the one that you already have, and can be done or used instead.

ex.en: There were alternative methods of travel available.
ex.zh: 有另外的旅行方式可采用。

e.en: Alternative is used to describe something that is different from the usual things of its kind, or the usual ways of doing something, in modern Western society. For example, an alternative lifestyle does not follow conventional ways of living and working.

ex.en: ...unconventional parents who embraced the alternative lifestyle of the Sixties.
ex.zh: …信奉60年代另类生活方式的与众不同的家长们。

e.en: Alternative medicine uses traditional ways of curing people, such as medicines made from plants, massage, and acupuncture. 替代性的 (疗法)

ex.en: ...alternative health care.
ex.zh: …替代性保健。

d: n. 可供选择的事物，替代物
adj. 可替代的，备选的；非传统的，另类的；（两者）互不相容的，非此即彼的

e.en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

ex.en: The committee is concerned about players' behaviour, especially arguing with referees.
ex.zh: 该委员会担心运动员的表现，尤其担心他们与裁判争吵。

e.en: If you argue with someone about something, you discuss it with them, with each of you giving your different opinions.

ex.en: He was arguing with the king about the need to maintain the cavalry at full strength.
ex.zh: 他在和国王讨论保留骑兵全部兵力的必要性。

ex.en: They are arguing over foreign policy.
ex.zh: 他们在讨论外交政策。

e.en: If you tell someone not to argue with you, you want them to do or believe what you say without protest or disagreement.

ex.en: Don't argue with me.
ex.zh: 不要和我争辩。

e.en: If you argue that something is true, you state it and give the reasons why you think it is true.

ex.en: His lawyers are arguing that he is unfit to stand trial.
ex.zh: 他的律师们在辩称他不适宜受审。

d: v. 主张，认为；说服；争论，争辩；争吵；提出质疑；提出理由
【名】 （Argue）（英、法）阿格（人名）

e.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

ex.en: My parents can't even afford a new refrigerator.
ex.zh: 我父母甚至买不起一台新冰箱。

ex.en: The arts should be available to more people at prices they can afford.
ex.zh: 艺术品应该以人们支付得起的价格提供给更多人。

e.en: If you say that you cannot afford to do something or allow it to happen, you mean that you must not do it or must prevent it from happening because it would be harmful or embarrassing to you.

ex.en: We can't afford to wait.
ex.zh: 我们等不起。

d: v. 买得起；有（时间）做某事；承担得起；提供，给予
n. （Afford）（英、美）阿福德（人名）

e.en: An argument is a statement or set of statements that you use in order to try to convince people that your opinion about something is correct.

ex.en: There's a strong argument for lowering the price.
ex.zh: 有一个支持降低价格的有力论据。

ex.en: The doctors have set out their arguments against the proposals.
ex.zh: 医生们已经说明了反对这些提案的理由。

e.en: An argument is a discussion or debate in which a number of people put forward different or opposing opinions. 讨论;

ex.en: The incident has triggered fresh arguments about the role of the extreme right in U.S. politics.
ex.zh: 该事件引发了有关美国政治中极右势力角色的新讨论。

e.en: An argument is a conversation in which people disagree with each other angrily or noisily.

ex.en: Anny described how she got into an argument with one of the marchers.
ex.zh: 安妮描述了她是如何与游行者中的一个人争吵起来的。

e.en: If you accept something without argument, you do not question it or disagree with it.

ex.en: He complied without argument.
ex.zh: 他没有争辩就服从了。

d: n. 争论，争吵，辩论；论据，理由（argument 的复数）；（计算机/数学）参数，实参，自变量

e.en: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

ex.en: "How is Frank?" he asked.
ex.zh: “弗兰克怎么样？”他问道。

ex.en: I asked him his name.
ex.zh: 我问了他的名字。

e.en: If you ask someone to do something, you tell them that you want them to do it. 让 (某人做某事)

ex.en: We had to ask him to leave.
ex.zh: 我们不得不让他离开。

e.en: If you ask to do something, you tell someone that you want to do it.

ex.en: I asked to see the Director.
ex.zh: 我要求见总经理。

e.en: If you ask for something, you say that you would like it.

ex.en: I decided to go to the next house and ask for food.
ex.zh: 我决定到隔壁房子去要吃的。

d: v. 询问；请求；要求；要价；指望（从某人那里）得到；邀请（ask 的现在分词）
n. 请求

e.en: Arithmetic is the part of mathematics that is concerned with the addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers.

ex.en: ...teaching the basics of reading, writing and arithmetic.
ex.zh: …教授读、写、算的基本知识。

e.en: You can use arithmetic to refer to the process of doing a particular sum or calculation.

ex.en: 4,000 women put in ten rupees each, which if my arithmetic is right adds up to 40,000 rupees.
ex.zh: 4千名妇女每人交10卢比，如果我的计算准确的话加起来总共是4万卢比。

e.en: If you refer to the arithmetic of a situation, you are concerned with those aspects of it that can be expressed in numbers, and how they affect the situation. (某形势的)

ex.en: The arithmetic was discouraging. In less than two months, they had used up six months' worth of food.
ex.zh: 数据不容乐观。在不到两个月里，他们已经吃完了6个月的食物。

d: n. 算术；演算，计算；数据统计
adj. 算术的

e.en: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

ex.en: "How is Frank?" he asked.
ex.zh: “弗兰克怎么样？”他问道。

ex.en: I asked him his name.
ex.zh: 我问了他的名字。

e.en: If you ask someone to do something, you tell them that you want them to do it. 让 (某人做某事)

ex.en: We had to ask him to leave.
ex.zh: 我们不得不让他离开。

e.en: If you ask to do something, you tell someone that you want to do it.

ex.en: I asked to see the Director.
ex.zh: 我要求见总经理。

e.en: If you ask for something, you say that you would like it.

ex.en: I decided to go to the next house and ask for food.
ex.zh: 我决定到隔壁房子去要吃的。

d: v. 问，询问；请求，要求给予；邀请；要价；期望（ask 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: To begin to do something means to start doing it. 开始 (做某事)

ex.en: He stood up and began to move around the room.
ex.zh: 他站了起来，开始在屋子里走来走去。

ex.en: The weight loss began to look more serious.
ex.zh: 体重的减轻开始显得更严重。

e.en: When something begins or when you begin it, it takes place from a particular time onward. 使开始发生;

ex.en: The problems began last November.
ex.zh: 问题于去年11月开始出现。

ex.en: He has just begun his fourth year in hiding.
ex.zh: 他刚刚开始他东躲西藏的生活的第4个年头。

e.en: If you begin with something, or begin by doing something, this is the first thing you do. 以 (某事、做某事)

ex.en: Could I begin with a few formalities?
ex.zh: 我可以从一些例行程序开始吗？

ex.en: ...a businessman who began by selling golf shirts from the boot of his car.
ex.zh: …一个从销售汽车行李箱里的高尔夫衬衫起家的商人。

e.en: You use begin to mention the first thing that someone says. 开始说;

ex.en: "Professor Theron," he began, "I'm very pleased to see you."
ex.zh: “西伦教授，”他开始说道，“我非常高兴见到你。”

ex.en: He didn't know how to begin.
ex.zh: 他不知道如何开场。

d: v. begin 的第三人称单数形式：开始；以……开始，以……开头（常与 with 或 by 连用）

e.en: A block of a substance is a large rectangular piece of it.

ex.en: ...a block of ice.
ex.zh: …一大块冰。

e.en: A block of apartments or offices is a large building containing them.

ex.en: ...a white-painted apartment block.
ex.zh: …一幢漆成白色的公寓楼。

e.en: A block in a town or city is an area of land with streets on all its sides, or the area or distance between such streets.

ex.en: He walked around the block three times.
ex.zh: 他绕着这个街区走了3圈。

ex.en: She walked four blocks down High Street.
ex.zh: 她沿着高街走了4个街区。

e.en: Blocks are wooden or plastic cubes, such as those used as toys by children.

d: n. 大块，一块（木料、石头等）；（四面临街的）街段，街区；大楼，大厦；栋，座，幢；障碍物，阻碍；（短时间的）思维停滞，思维中断；一组，一批，一叠；（连续的）一段时间；阻挡，拦截；积木；（古代斩首用的）垫头木；一大片土地；（物体的）平面，纯色色块；滑轮，滑轮组；区块
v. 阻塞，堵塞（道路、管道等）；遮住（视线）；封锁，挡住（去路）；阻挠，阻止；阻截，拦截（对方的球）；对……进行块操作；用模具使（帽等）成形
【名】 （Block）（英、法、德、西、葡、芬、罗）布洛克（人名）

e.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

ex.en: She is blunt about her personal life.
ex.zh: 她对自己的私生活直言不讳。

e.en: 直言不讳地

ex.en: "I don't believe you!" Jeanne said bluntly.
ex.zh: “我不信你！” 珍妮直言不讳地说。

e.en: A blunt object has a rounded or flat end rather than a sharp one.

ex.en: One of them had been struck 13 times over the head with a blunt object.
ex.zh: 他们其中一人的头部被钝器砸了13下。

e.en: A blunt knife or blade is no longer sharp and does not cut well.

ex.en: The edge is as blunt as an old butter knife.
ex.zh: 刃钝得跟一把老黄油刀一样。

d: adj. 钝的，不锋利的；直言不讳的，说话生硬的
v. 减弱；使不锋利，使变钝
【名】 （Blunt）（英）布伦特（人名）

e.en: Something that is brief lasts for only a short time.

ex.en: She once made a brief appearance on television.
ex.zh: 她曾在电视上短暂露面。

e.en: A brief speech or piece of writing does not contain too many words or details. (讲话、文章)

ex.en: In a brief statement, he concentrated entirely on international affairs.
ex.zh: 在一个简短的陈述中,他完全集中在了国际事务上。

e.en: If you are brief, you say what you want to say in as few words as possible. (说话)

ex.en: Now please be brief – my time is valuable.
ex.zh: 现在请长话短说–我的时间很宝贵。

e.en: You can describe a period of time as brief if you want to emphasize that it is very short.

ex.en: For a few brief minutes we forgot the anxiety and anguish.
ex.zh: 短短的几分钟,我们忘却了忧伤和痛苦。

d: n. 摘要，简报，法律案情摘要（brief 的复数）；贴身的短内裤，三角裤（复数型名词）
v. brief 的第三人称单数：向……提供必要信息，作简要介绍或指示；作……的摘要

e.en: If something is calculated to have a particular effect, it is specially done or arranged in order to have that effect. 故意作出的;

ex.en: Their movements through the region were calculated to terrify landowners into abandoning their holdings.
ex.zh: 他们在整个地区的行动意在恐吓地主们放弃其财产。

e.en: If you say that something is not calculated to have a particular effect, you mean that it is unlikely to have that effect.

ex.en: The liberal agenda is not calculated to help minority groups.
ex.zh: 自由党的议题是不太可能帮助少数派的。

e.en: You can describe a clever or dishonest action as calculated when it is very carefully planned or arranged.

ex.en: Irene's use of the mop had been a calculated attempt to cover up her crime.
ex.zh: 艾琳使用拖把是个精心安排的举动，意在掩盖她的罪行。

e.en: If you take a calculated risk, you do something which you think might be successful, although you have fully considered the possible bad consequences of your action. 全盘衡量过的 (风险)

ex.en: The president took a calculated political risk in throwing his full support behind the rebels.
ex.zh: 总统在全盘计算过后，冒着风险全力支持反叛分子。

d: adj. 计算出的，核算出的；蓄意的，有计划的，故意安排的；be calculated to do sth 旨在…的，适合…的，很可能…的（not calculated to do sth 意为“不大可能…的”）
v. 计算；估计；打算（calculate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A car is a motor vehicle with room for a small number of passengers.

ex.en: He had left his tickets in his car.
ex.zh: 他把票落在自己的小汽车里了。

e.en: A car is the same as a .
The separate sections of a train are called cars when they are used for a particular purpose. (有特殊用途的)

ex.en: He made his way into the dining car for breakfast.
ex.zh: 他挤进餐车吃早点。

d: n. 汽车，轿车；（火车的）车厢；（火车上作特殊用途的）车厢（如餐车、卧铺车厢）；（电梯的）梯厢，（索道或气球的）吊舱；战车
【名】 （Car）（土）贾尔，（法、西）卡尔，（塞）察尔（人名）

e.en: A bus is a large motor vehicle that carries passengers from one place to another. Buses drive along particular routes, and you usually have to pay to travel in them.

ex.en: He missed his last bus home.
ex.zh: 他没赶上回家的末班公共汽车。

e.en: When someone is bused to a particular place or when they bus there, they travel there on a bus. 用公共汽车运送;

ex.en: On May Day hundreds of thousands used to be bused in to parade through East Berlin.
ex.zh: 昔日每逢五一劳动节，成千上万的人们通常会被公共汽车载着游行穿过东柏林。

ex.en: To get our Colombian visas we bused back to Medellin.
ex.zh: 为了获得哥伦比亚签证，我们又乘公共汽车回到麦德林。

e.en: To bus tables means to clear away dirty dishes and reset the tables. 收拾 (餐桌)

ex.en: As a fund-raiser, police officers will don aprons, take orders and bus tables today.
ex.zh: 作为募捐方，警官们今天将穿上围裙，接受点菜，收拾餐桌。

d: n. 公共汽车（bus 的复数形式）
v. 乘公共汽车；用公共汽车运送（bus 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you complain about a situation, you say that you are not satisfied with it.

ex.en: Miners have complained bitterly that the government did not fulfil their promises.
ex.zh: 矿工们已愤愤地抱怨政府没有兑现他们的承诺。

ex.en: The couple complained about the high cost of visiting Europe.
ex.zh: 这对夫妇抱怨了游览欧洲的高昂花费。

e.en: If you complain of pain or illness, you say that you are feeling pain or feeling ill. 诉说 (病痛)

ex.en: He complained of a headache.
ex.zh: 他说他头疼。

d: v. 诉说 （病痛）；悲叹，悲鸣；（构造，机械装置）（因拉力或压力）呻吟，咯吱作响；抱怨，投诉

e.en: A coalition is a government consisting of people from two or more political parties.

ex.en: Since June the country has had a coalition government.
ex.zh: 从6月起，这个国家有了一个联合政府。

e.en: A coalition is a group consisting of people from different political or social groups who are cooperating to achieve a particular aim.

ex.en: He had been opposed by a coalition of about 50 civil rights, women's, and Latino organizations.
ex.zh: 他遭到一个联盟的反对，该联盟由大约五十个民权组织、妇女组织和拉美人组织构成。

d: n. 联合政府；联合体，联盟；联合，结合

e.en: embarrassed, unnatural, or forced 拘泥的;

ex.en: a constrained smile

d: adj. 受约束的，受限制的；（多指表情、态度、文风等）拘泥的，不自然的，勉强的，被强迫的
v. 驱使，强迫，束缚（constrain 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A convent is a building in which a community of nuns live.

d: n. 女修道院；女修道会（共同生活的修女团体）

e.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city.

ex.en: The city council has voted almost unanimously in favour.
ex.zh: 市议会几乎全部投了赞成票。

e.en: Council is used in the names of some organizations.

ex.en: ...the National Council for Civil Liberties.
ex.zh: …国家公民自由委员会。

ex.en: ...the Arts Council.
ex.zh: …艺术委员会。

e.en: In some organizations, the council is the group of people that controls or governs it.

ex.en: The permanent council of the Organization of American States meets today here in Washington.
ex.zh: 美洲国家组织常务委员会今天在华盛顿召开会议。

e.en: A council is a specially organized, formal meeting that is attended by a particular group of people.

ex.en: President Najibullah said he would call a grand council of all Afghans.
ex.zh: 纳吉布拉总统说他将召开全阿富汗人大会。

d: n. 委员会，理事会；政务委员会，地方议会；会议；（教会的）集会
adj. 地方政府廉租的
【名】 （Council）（英）康斯尔（人名）

e.en: The cost of something is the amount of money that is needed in order to buy, do, or make it.

ex.en: The cost of a loaf of bread has increased five-fold.
ex.zh: 一块面包的价格已经涨了5倍。

ex.en: In 1989 the price of coffee fell so low that in many countries it did not even cover the cost of production.
ex.zh: 1989年咖啡的价格跌得那么低，以致在许多国家还抵不上其生产成本。

e.en: If something costs a particular amount of money, you can buy, do, or make it for that amount.

ex.en: This course is limited to 12 people and costs $150.
ex.zh: 这门课程限招12人，费用为$150。

ex.en: Painted walls look much more interesting and don't cost much.
ex.zh: 粉刷过的墙壁看上去更有趣，要价也不高。

e.en: When something that you plan to do or make is costed, the amount of money you need is calculated in advance.

ex.en: The building work has not been fully costed but runs into millions of dollars.
ex.zh: 建筑工作的费用还未完全估算出来，但要高达几百万美元。

e.en: If an event or mistake costs you something, you lose that thing as the result of it.

ex.en: ...a six-year-old boy whose life was saved by an operation that cost him his sight.
ex.zh: …一个通过手术保住生命但双目失明的6岁男孩。

d: n. 价钱，费用；成本，开支；代价，损失；诉讼费用
v. 价钱为，需花费；估算成本，估价；使丧失，使损失；使付出努力，使做不愉快的事；使花许多钱
【名】 （Cost）（英、美、罗、巴、法、荷）科斯特（人名）

e.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

ex.en: Natural disasters have obviously contributed to the continent's economic crisis.
ex.zh: 自然灾害显然促使了该大陆的经济危机。

ex.en: ...someone to turn to in moments of crisis.
ex.zh: …在危机时刻可以向其求助的人。

d: n. 危机，紧要关头；决定性时刻，关键时刻；（病情的）转折点，危象
adj. 用于处理危机的

e.en: A declaration is an official announcement or statement.

ex.en: The opening speeches sounded more like declarations of war than offerings of peace.
ex.zh: 那些开幕辞听起来更像宣战书而不是和平倡议。

e.en: A declaration is a firm, emphatic statement which shows that you have no doubts about what you are saying.

ex.en: ...declarations of undying love.
ex.zh: …永恒爱情的宣言。

e.en: A declaration is a written statement about something which you have signed and which can be used as evidence in a court of law.

ex.en: On the customs declaration, the sender labelled the freight as agricultural machinery.
ex.zh: 在报关单上，发货方将货物列为农业机械。

d: n. 声明，表白；申报（单）；（板球）对一赛局结束的宣布；公告，宣告

e.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example, 1980 to 1989. 10年 (尤指起始年末尾为0)

ex.en: ...the last decade of the nineteenth century.
ex.zh: …19世纪的最后10年。

d: n. 十年，十年期；十进

e.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university. A department is also one of the sections in a large shop. (政府、企业等机构的) 部; (大学的) 系; (大型商店的)

ex.en: ...the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
ex.zh: …美国健康和公共事业部。

ex.en: He moved to the sales department.
ex.zh: 他调到了销售部。

d: n. （组织或机构中的）部，司，系，处，科；（商场里的）部；专长，专责；（法国等国的）省

e.en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.

ex.en: His guerrillas defeated the colonial army in 1954.
ex.zh: 他的游击队在1954年打败了殖民军。

e.en: If a proposal or motion in a debate is defeated, more people vote against it than for it. (以多数票)

ex.en: The bill was defeated with support from only two congressmen.
ex.zh: 由于只得到两位议员的支持，那个议案被否决了。

e.en: If a task or a problem defeats you, it is so difficult that you cannot do it or solve it.

ex.en: The book he most wanted to write was the one which nearly defeated him.
ex.zh: 他最想写的书恰恰是几乎难倒他的那一本。

e.en: To defeat an action or plan means to cause it to fail.

ex.en: The navy played a limited but significant role in defeating the rebellion.
ex.zh: 在平息叛乱中海军起了有限但却重要的作用。

d: v. 击败，战胜；困惑，难住；使失败，阻挠；反对（动议或提议）
n. 失败，战败；战胜，击败

e.en: A developer is a person or a company that buys land and builds houses, offices, stores, or factories on it, or buys existing buildings and makes them more modern. (房地产)

ex.en: ...common land which would have a high commercial value if sold to developers.
ex.zh: …卖给开发商便有很高商业价值的普通地皮。

e.en: A developer is someone who develops something such as an idea, a design, or a product.

ex.en: John Bardeen was also co-developer of the theory of superconductivity.
ex.zh: 约翰·巴丁也是超导理论的共同发展人。

d: n. 开发商，房地产开发商；开发者，研制者，发展者；（摄）显影剂（developer 的复数）

e.en: If two people or things are different, they are not like each other in one or more ways.

ex.en: London was different from most European capitals.
ex.zh: 伦敦与大多数的欧洲首都城市不同。

ex.en: If he'd attended music school, how might things have been different?
ex.zh: 如果他上的是音乐学校，一切会怎样地不同呢？

e.en: People sometimes say that one thing is different than another. This use is acceptable in American English, but is often considered incorrect in British English. 与…不同的 (美式英语中可用，英式英语常认为是错的)

ex.en: We're not really any different than they are.
ex.zh: 我们与他们其实没有什么不同。

e.en: 不同地

ex.en: Every individual learns differently.
ex.zh: 每个人的学习方式都不一样。

e.en: You use different to indicate that you are talking about two or more separate and distinct things of the same kind.

ex.en: Different countries specialized in different products.
ex.zh: 不同的国家专门生产各不相同的产品。

d: adj. 不同的；分别的，各别的；与众不同的

e.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

ex.en: Order and discipline have been placed in the hands of governing bodies.
ex.zh: 秩序与纪律已交由管控机构负责。

e.en: Discipline is the quality of being able to behave and work in a controlled way which involves obeying particular rules or standards.

ex.en: It was that image of calm, control, and discipline that appealed to millions of voters.
ex.zh: 正是那冷静、克制和自律的形象吸引了数以百万计的选民。

e.en: If you refer to an activity or situation as a discipline, you mean that, in order to be successful in it, you need to behave in a strictly controlled way and obey particular rules or standards. 训练;

ex.en: The discipline of studying music can help children develop good work habits and improve self-esteem.
ex.zh: 学习音乐的规范训练能帮助孩子们养成良好的做事习惯和增强自尊心。

e.en: If someone is disciplined for something that they have done wrong, they are punished for it.

ex.en: The workman was disciplined by his company but not dismissed.
ex.zh: 这名工人被他的公司处罚了，但没有被开除。

d: n. 纪律，风纪；惩罚，处分；训导，管教；训练，锻炼；自制力，自律能力；（尤指大学的）科目，学科
v. 惩罚，处分；训练，管教

e.en: Earlier is the comparative of . (early)
Earlier is used to refer to a point or period in time before the present or before the one you are talking about.

ex.en: As mentioned earlier, the university supplements this information with an interview.
ex.zh: 正如早些时候提到的，该大学用一次采访来补充这个资料。

ex.en: ...political reforms announced by the president earlier this year.
ex.zh: …今年早些时候总统宣布的政治改革。

e.en: Earlier is also an adjective.

ex.en: Earlier reports of gunshots have not been substantiated.
ex.zh: 早先关于枪击的报道还没有被证实。

d: adv. 早些时候地
adj. 早些时候的

e.en: An election is a process in which people vote to choose a person or group of people to hold an official position.

ex.en: ...Poland's first fully free elections for more than fifty years.
ex.zh: …五十多年来波兰首次完全自由选举。

ex.en: During his election campaign he promised to put the economy back on its feet.
ex.zh: 在竞选活动期间他承诺要重振经济。

e.en: The election of a particular person or group of people is their success in winning an election.

ex.en: ...the election of the Democrat candidate last year.
ex.zh: …去年民主党候选人的当选。

ex.en: ...Vaclav Havel's election as president of Czechoslovakia.
ex.zh: …瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔当选捷克斯洛伐克总统。

d: n. 选举；当选；选举权；上帝的选拔

e.en: If something exceeds a particular amount or number, it is greater or larger than that amount or number. 超过 (某数量)

ex.en: Its research budget exceeds $700 million a year.
ex.zh: 其研究预算每年超过7亿美元。

e.en: If you exceed a limit or rule, you go beyond it, even though you are not supposed to or it is against the law. 超越 (限制、规定)

ex.en: He accepts that he was exceeding the speed limit.
ex.zh: 他承认他当时超过了速限。

d: v. 超过（exceed 的过去式和过去分词）；越出，超出（权限、限制等）；exceed in（exceeded in）：在…方面超过

e.en: If something expands or is expanded, it becomes larger. 扩大;

ex.en: Engineers noticed that the pipes were not expanding as expected.
ex.zh: 工程师们注意到管子并未像预期的那样膨胀。

ex.en: We have to expand the size of the image.
ex.zh: 我们不得不扩大图像的尺寸。

e.en: If something such as a business, organization, or service expands, or if you expand it, it becomes bigger and includes more people, goods, or activities. 使…发展;

ex.en: The popular ceramics industry expanded toward the middle of the 19th century.
ex.zh: 大众陶瓷业在19世纪中叶得到了发展。

d: v. 扩大，增加；扩展，发展；细谈，详述；变得更自信（善谈）；（宇宙）膨胀

e.en: European means belonging or relating to, or coming from Europe.

ex.en: ...in some other European countries.
ex.zh: …在其他一些欧洲国家。

e.en: A European is a person who comes from Europe.

ex.en: Three-quarters of working-age Americans work, compared with roughly 60% of Europeans.
ex.zh: 3/4处于工作年龄的美国人在工作，相比之下欧洲约为60%。

d: adj. 欧洲的；欧洲人的
n. 欧洲人

e.en: To export products or raw materials means to sell them to another country.

ex.en: The nation also exports beef.
ex.zh: 该国也出口牛肉。

ex.en: They expect the antibiotic products to be exported to Southeast Asia and Africa.
ex.zh: 他们期望抗生素产品出口到东南亚和非洲。

e.en: Export is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the production and export of cheap casual wear.
ex.zh: …廉价休闲服的生产与出口。

ex.en: A lot of our land is used to grow crops for export.
ex.zh: 我们很多的土地用来种植出口作物。

e.en: Exports are goods sold to another country and sent there.

ex.en: Ghana's main export is cocoa.
ex.zh: 加纳的主要出口产品是可可。

e.en: To export something means to introduce it into another country or make it happen there.

ex.en: It has exported inflation at times.
ex.zh: 它有时将通货膨胀引入他国。

d: v. （贸易）出口，输出（export 的现在分词和动名词）；（计算机）导出数据或文件
n. （贸易）出口
adj. （贸易）出口的，输出的

e.en: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.

ex.en: There's room in there for a family of five.
ex.zh: 那儿能住得下一家5口。

ex.en: Does he have any family?
ex.zh: 他有什么家人吗？

e.en: When people talk about a family, they sometimes mean children.

ex.en: They decided to start a family.
ex.zh: 他们决定了要孩子。

e.en: When people talk about their family, they sometimes mean their ancestors.

ex.en: Her family came to Los Angeles at the turn of the century.
ex.zh: 她的祖先在世纪之交时来到了洛杉矶。

e.en: You can use family to describe things that belong to a particular family.

ex.en: He returned to the family home.
ex.zh: 他回到了自己家。

d: n. 家庭（family 的复数）；家人，家属；家族，宗族；（生物学）科
adv. 不可能地，无法可想地；难以置信地，出奇地

e.en: Five is the number 5. 5

ex.en: I spent five years there and had a really good time.
ex.zh: 我在那里呆了5年，过得很愉快。

d: num. 五，五个
n. 五，五个；（口语）五点钟；五美元钞票；（篮球）五人球队；（人名）Five（挪威姓氏菲弗）
adj. 五的，五个的

e.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

ex.en: The labour secretary said the reforms would generate new jobs.
ex.zh: 劳动部长说这些改革将带来新的工作。

e.en: To generate a form of energy or power means to produce it. 产生 (电等能量)

ex.en: The company, New England Electric, burns coal to generate power.
ex.zh: 新英格兰电力公司燃烧煤来发电。

d: v. 产生，生成（generate 的过去式及过去分词）；引发（讨论、关注等）
adj. 由……产生的，生成的（常用于 wind-generated、computer-generated 等复合词）

e.en: You use intended to describe the thing you are trying to achieve or the person you are trying to affect. 预期的;

ex.en: The intended target had been a military building.
ex.zh: 原定目标本来是一座军事建筑物。

d: adj. 预期的，打算中的；为……打算（或设计）的；故意的，蓄意的
n. 未婚夫，未婚妻
v. 意指，意思是；计划，打算；准备，预留（作某种用途或给某人用）（intend 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you find something interesting, it attracts your attention, for example, because you think it is exciting or unusual.

ex.en: It was interesting to be in a different environment.
ex.zh: 换一换环境很有趣。

d: adj. 有趣的，有吸引力的；怪异的
v. 使感兴趣，引起……的关注；劝说（某人）做（或参与）（interest 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Morals are principles and beliefs concerning right and wrong behaviour.

ex.en: ...Western ideas and morals.
ex.zh: …西方的思想和道德。

e.en: Moral means relating to beliefs about what is right or wrong.

ex.en: She describes her own moral dilemma in making the film.
ex.zh: 她描述了自己拍摄这部电影时面临的道德困境。

e.en: 道德上

ex.en: When, if ever, is it morally justifiable to allow a patient to die?
ex.zh: 假如可以的话，什么情况下允许病人放弃生命在道德上是正当的？

e.en: Moral courage or duty is based on what you believe is right or acceptable, rather than on what the law says should be done.

ex.en: The government had a moral, if not a legal, duty to pay compensation.
ex.zh: 政府即使没有法律上的义务也有道义上的义务进行赔偿。

d: adj. 有关道德的；基于道德的，道义上的；品行端正的，有道德的；伦理的；能辨别是非的
n. 道德准则（标准）；寓意，道德上的教训
【名】 （Moral）（德、法、西、葡、土）莫拉尔（人名）

e.en: Itself is used as the object of a verb or preposition when it refers to something that is the same thing as the subject of the verb.

ex.en: Scientists have discovered remarkable new evidence showing how the body rebuilds itself while we sleep.
ex.zh: 科学家们已经发现了非同寻常的新证据，证明睡眠时我们的身体如何自行恢复。

e.en: You use itself to emphasize the thing you are referring to. 本身 (表示强调)

ex.en: I think life itself is a learning process.
ex.zh: 我认为生活本身是一个学习的过程。

e.en: If you say that someone is, for example, politeness itself or kindness itself, you are emphasizing that they are extremely polite or extremely kind. (加在词后表示强调)

ex.en: He is rarely satisfied with anything less than perfection itself.
ex.zh: 他对任何不十分完美的事情都极少满意。

d: pron. 它自己；它本身（表强调）；与抽象品质名词连用，表示“非常……，是……的化身”
adv. in itself：就其本身而言，本质上；by itself：单独地；自动地；of itself：自行，自发地
v. speak for itself：不言而喻，有目共睹

e.en: The maintenance of a building, vehicle, road, or machine is the process of keeping it in good condition by regularly checking it and repairing it when necessary.

ex.en: ...maintenance work on government buildings.
ex.zh: …政府各大楼的检修工作。

ex.en: The window had been replaced last week during routine maintenance.
ex.zh: 那窗在上星期的例行检修中已被换掉了。

e.en: Maintenance is money that someone gives regularly to another person to pay for the things that the person needs. 赡养费;

ex.en: ...the government's plan to make absent fathers pay maintenance for their children.
ex.zh: …让那些不在孩子身边的父亲为孩子提供抚养费的政府计划。

e.en: If you ensure the maintenance of a state or process, you make sure that it continues.

ex.en: ...the maintenance of peace and stability in Asia.
ex.zh: …亚洲和平与稳定的维持。

d: n. 维护，保养；保持，维持；（依法应负担的）生活费，抚养费；包揽诉讼罪，非法资助诉讼罪

e.en: The mayor of a town or city is the person who has been elected for a fixed period of time to run its government.

ex.en: ...the new mayor of New York.
ex.zh: …新任纽约市长。

d: n. mayor 的复数形式（市长）

e.en: If you have an obligation to do something, it is your duty to do that thing.

ex.en: When teachers assign homework, students usually feel an obligation to do it.
ex.zh: 老师布置家庭作业时，学生们通常感觉做作业是一种义务。

e.en: If you have an obligation to a person, it is your duty to take care of them or protect their interests. 义务;

ex.en: The United States will do that which is necessary to meet its obligations to its own citizens.
ex.zh: 美国会尽其对国民应尽的义务。

e.en: In advertisements, if a product or a service is available without obligation, you do not have to pay for that product or service until you have tried it and are satisfied with it.

ex.en: If you are selling your property, why not call us for a free valuation without obligation.
ex.zh: 如果你打算出售房产，为什么不打电话让我们做个免费的评估呢。

d: n. （法律上或道义上的）义务，责任；恩惠，人情债；（承诺付款等的）合同，契约；必须要做的事情

e.en: An office is a room or a part of a building where people work sitting at desks.

ex.en: By the time Flynn arrived at his office it was 5:30.
ex.zh: 弗林到达办公室时已经5:30了。

ex.en: Telephone their head office for more details.
ex.zh: 给他们总部打电话询问更多的详细情况。

e.en: An office is a department of an organization, especially the government, where people deal with a particular kind of administrative work. (尤指政府的)

ex.en: Thousands have registered with unemployment offices.
ex.zh: 数千人已在失业服务处登记了。

ex.en: ...the Congressional Budget Office.
ex.zh: …国会预算办公室。

e.en: An office is a small building or room where people can go for information, tickets, or a service of some kind.

ex.en: The tourist office operates a useful room-finding service.
ex.zh: 这个旅游办事处开办了实用的找房业务。

e.en: A doctor's or dentist's office is a place where a doctor or dentist sees their patients.

ex.en: The chance of getting AIDS at the doctor's or dentist's office is extremely low.
ex.zh: 在诊所或牙医诊所感染艾滋病的可能性极小。

d: n. 办公室；办公楼，办事处；（提供某项服务的）室，处，局；（尤指政府的）部，局，厅；诊所；（办公室、办公楼、事务所等的）全体办事人员，全体工作人员；重要官职，重要职务；（天主教牧师、教徒等）每日的祈祷 （=Divine Office）

e.en: Official means approved by the government or by someone in authority. 官方的;

ex.en: According to the official figures, over one thousand people died during the revolution.
ex.zh: 根据官方数字，有一千多人在革命中丧命。

ex.en: An official announcement is expected in the next few days.
ex.zh: 一份官方声明预计会在接下来的几天内发表。

e.en: 正式地

ex.en: The election results have still not been officially announced.
ex.zh: 选举结果仍未正式宣布。

e.en: Official activities are carried out by a person in authority as part of their job.

ex.en: The president is in Brazil for an official two-day visit.
ex.zh: 总统正在巴西进行为期两天的正式访问。

e.en: Official things are used by a person in authority as part of their job.

ex.en: ...the official residence of the head of state.
ex.zh: …国家元首的官邸。

d: n. 官员，行政人员（official 的复数）；裁判人员

e.en: A park is a public area of land with grass and trees, usually in a town, where people go in order to relax and enjoy themselves.

ex.en: ...Central Park.
ex.zh: ...中央公园。

ex.en: ...a brisk walk with the dog around the park.
ex.zh: …带着狗在公园里的一次轻快的散步。

e.en: You can refer to a place where a particular activity is carried out as a park. (作为专用场地的) …区; …

ex.en: ...a science and technology park.
ex.zh: …一个科技园。

e.en: When you park a vehicle or park somewhere, you drive the vehicle into a position where it can stay for a period of time, and leave it there.

ex.en: Greenfield turned into the next side street and parked.
ex.zh: 格林菲尔德拐进下一个小巷停了车。

ex.en: He found a place to park the car.
ex.zh: 他找到了一个停车的地方。

e.en: If you park yourself somewhere, you sit there.

ex.en: Every Friday, I would park myself in front of the TV.
ex.zh: 每个周五，我都会坐在电视前。

d: n. 公园；自然保护区；（乡间大宅的）庭园，园林；足球场，橄榄球场；运动场，（尤指）棒球场；专用区，园区；停车场；（汽车）制动
v. 停车，泊车；存放，寄存； （在某处）坐，站立（park yourself）；把……搁置，推迟
【名】 （Park）（英、芬、瑞典）帕克（人名）

e.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

ex.en: Companies are increasingly eager to contract out peripheral activities like training.
ex.zh: 公司越来越渴望把像培训这样的次要活动外包出去。

ex.en: ...peripheral and boring information.
ex.zh: …无关紧要且无聊的信息。

e.en: Peripheral areas of land are ones that are on the edge of a larger area.

ex.en: ...urban development in the outer peripheral areas of large towns.
ex.zh: …大城市外部周边地区的城市发展。

e.en: Peripherals are devices that can be attached to computers. (计算机的)

ex.en: ...peripherals to expand the use of our computers.
ex.zh: …扩展计算机用途的外围设备。

d: adj. 次要的，附带的；外围的，周边的；（计算机设备）外围的；（剖）体表的；周围神经系统的，末梢的
n. （计算机的）外部设备

e.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

ex.en: My husband persuaded me to come.
ex.zh: 我丈夫说服我来的。

ex.en: We're trying to persuade manufacturers to sell them here.
ex.zh: 我们正试图说服制造商们在这里销售它们。

e.en: If something persuades someone to take a particular course of action, it causes them to take that course of action because it is a good reason for doing so. 引发 (某人采取行动)

ex.en: It was the lack of privacy that eventually persuaded us to move after Ben was born.
ex.zh: 正是因为缺少隐私感才最终迫使我们在本出生后搬了家。

e.en: If you persuade someone that something is true, you say things that eventually make them believe that it is true.

ex.en: I've persuaded Mrs. Tennant that it's time she retired.
ex.zh: 我已经使坦南特夫人相信是她该退休的时候了。

ex.en: We had managed to persuade them that it was worth working with us.
ex.zh: 我们已经设法使他们相信和我们一起共事是值得的。

d: v. 说服，劝说；使相信，使确信（persuade 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 确信的，信服的（常作表语）

e.en: Physical qualities, actions, or things are connected with a person's body, rather than with their mind. 肉体的;

ex.en: ...the physical and mental problems caused by the illness.
ex.zh: …这种疾病引起的生理和心理问题。

ex.en: Physical activity promotes good health.
ex.zh: 身体运动促进健康。

e.en: 身体上地

ex.en: You may be physically and mentally exhausted after a long flight.
ex.zh: 长途飞行后你可能身心都很疲惫。

e.en: Physical things are real things that can be touched and seen, rather than ideas or spoken words. 实物的;

ex.en: Physical and ideological barriers had come down in Eastern Europe.
ex.zh: 物质和意识形态上的障碍在东欧都已减少。

ex.en: ...physical evidence to support the story.
ex.zh: …支持这种说法的实物证据。

e.en: 有形地

ex.en: ...physically cut off from every other country.
ex.zh: …地理上与所有其他国家分割开来。

d: adj. 身体的，肉体的；物质的，有形的；外形的，外在的；物理的，物理学的；根据自然规律的，符合自然法则的；粗暴的，粗野的；性欲的，肉欲的；（人）喜欢动手动脚的；肢体活动的
n. 体格检查；（股票）（与期货相对的）现货股票

e.en: A pipe is a long, round, hollow object, usually made of metal or plastic, through which a liquid or gas can flow.

ex.en: The liquid can't escape into the air, because it's inside a pipe.
ex.zh: 液体不会漏到空气中，因为它在管子里。

e.en: A pipe is an object that is used for smoking tobacco. You put the tobacco into the cup-shaped part at the end of the pipe, light it, and breathe in the smoke through a narrow tube.

ex.en: Do you smoke a pipe?
ex.zh: 你抽烟斗吗？

e.en: A pipe is a simple musical instrument in the shape of a tube with holes in it. You play a pipe by blowing into it while covering and uncovering the holes with your fingers.
An organ pipe is one of the long hollow tubes in which air vibrates and produces a musical note.

d: n. （pipe 的复数）管子，管道；烟斗；管乐器；（管风琴的）音管；（计算机）管道；Pipes（人名，英译派普斯）
v. （pipe 的第三人称单数）用管道运输，输送；传送，播送（音乐、录音）；用管乐器吹奏

e.en: A place is any point, building, area, town, or country. (任何)

ex.en: ...a list of museums and places of interest.
ex.zh: …一份博物馆和名胜地的列表。

ex.en: We're going to a place called Platoro.
ex.zh: 我们要去一个叫普拉托罗的地方。

e.en: You can use the place to refer to the point, building, area, town, or country that you have already mentioned. (提到过的点、建筑、地区、城镇、国家等)

ex.en: Except for the remarkably tidy kitchen, the place was a mess.
ex.zh: 除了异常整洁的厨房外，这个地方一团糟。

e.en: You can refer to somewhere that provides a service, such as a hotel, restaurant, or institution, as a particular kind of place. (旅馆、饭店、机构等某种提供服务的)

ex.en: He found a bed-and-breakfast place.
ex.zh: 他找到一个提供住宿带早餐的地方。

ex.en: My wife and I discovered some superb places to eat.
ex.zh: 我妻子和我发现了一些很棒的吃饭的地方。

e.en: When something takes place, it happens, especially in a controlled or organized way. (尤指在控制或组织下) 发生;

ex.en: The discussion took place in a famous villa on the lake's shore.
ex.zh: 讨论在湖滨一座著名别墅举行。

ex.en: She wanted Randy's wedding to take place quickly.
ex.zh: 她想让兰迪的婚礼马上举行。

d: n. 地点，地方，位置；名次；名额；位数，数位（place 的复数）
v. 放置，安放；使处于（place 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Planning is the process of deciding in detail how to do something before you actually start to do it.

ex.en: The trip needs careful planning.
ex.zh: 这次旅行需要认真计划。

e.en: Planning is control by the local government of the way that land is used in an area and of what new buildings are built there.

ex.en: New York City's Planning Commissions rejected the builder's proposals.
ex.zh: 纽约市市政规划委员会拒绝了那个建筑商的提案。

d: n. 计划，规划；城镇规划管理，市政规划
v. 计划，筹划；打算；设计；期望，预料（plan 的现在分词）

e.en: You use point to refer to something that someone has said or written.

ex.en: We disagree with every point she makes.
ex.zh: 我们不同意她提出的任何观点。

ex.en: The following account will clearly illustrate this point.
ex.zh: 以下的陈述将清楚地阐明这一看法。

e.en: If you say that someone has a point, or if you take their point, you mean that you accept that what they have said is important and should be considered.

ex.en: "If he'd already killed once, surely he'd have killed Sarah?" She had a point there.
ex.zh: “如果他已经杀过一次人，莎拉就一定是他杀的了吗？”她这句话有道理。

e.en: The point of what you are saying or discussing is the most important part that provides a reason or explanation for the rest.

ex.en: "Did I ask you to talk to me?"—"That's not the point."
ex.zh: “我要你跟我说了吗？”—“问题不在这儿。”

e.en: If you ask what the point of something is, or say that there is no point in it, you are indicating that a particular action has no purpose or would not be useful. 意义;

ex.en: What was the point of thinking about him?
ex.zh: 想着他有什么意义呢？

d: n. 观点，论点；要点，核心问题；目的，意图；具体细节；特点，特征；地点；时刻，阶段；得分；小数点，点；罗盘（方位）点；点（标度）；（电影的）利润百分比；尖端，尖头；岬角；光点，色点；插座；（字号的）磅值；轨尖，道岔（points）；（芭蕾）脚尖（points）；（分电器中的）接点；称赞，认可（points）；（板球）防守；尖兵队；排头位置；（动物的）外部位；（猎）直窜（位置）；束衣带；束帆绳；狗指方向；（乐曲的）重要乐句或主题
v. 指，指向；对准，瞄准；朝向，对着；指路；引导，指引；暗示，表明；强调（话语或行动）；（用水泥）勾缝；绷直（脚趾）；削尖；使（光标）指着；插入点号；（狗）示意有（猎物）
【名】 （Point）（法）普安（人名）

e.en: Political means relating to the way power is achieved and used in a country or society.

ex.en: All other political parties there have been completely banned.
ex.zh: 那里的其他所有政党都已经完全被取缔了。

ex.en: The government is facing another political crisis.
ex.zh: 该政府正面临着另一场政治危机。

e.en: 政治上地

ex.en: They do not believe the killings were politically motivated.
ex.zh: 他们相信这些谋杀案没有什么政治动机。

e.en: Someone who is political is interested or involved in politics and holds strong beliefs about it. 对政治感兴趣的;

ex.en: Oh I'm not political, I take no interest in politics.
ex.zh: 哦，我不关心政治，对政治不感兴趣。

d: adj. 政治（上）的，政府的；政党的，党派的；对政治感兴趣的，参与政治的；反政府的；（组织内部人际间）牵涉权力关系的，争权夺利的

e.en: A pool is the same as a .

ex.en: ...a heated indoor pool.
ex.zh: …一个室内温水游泳池。

e.en: A pool is a fairly small area of still water.

ex.en: The pool had dried up and was full of bracken and reeds.
ex.zh: 该水池已经干涸，长满了欧洲蕨和芦苇。

e.en: A pool of liquid or light is a small area of it on the ground or on a surface. 一滩 (液体); 一片 (光)

ex.en: She was found lying in a pool of blood.
ex.zh: 她被发现躺在一滩血泊中。

ex.en: It was raining quietly and steadily and there were little pools of water on the gravel drive.
ex.zh: 雨正静静地下着，砂砾车道上积了一滩滩的水。

e.en: A pool of people, money, or things is a quantity or number of them that is available for an organization or group to use. 一拨人; 一笔钱;

ex.en: The available pool of healthy manpower was not as large as military officials had expected.
ex.zh: 一拨可用的健康劳力人数达不到军方官员们的期望值。

d: n. 游泳池；池塘，水坑；一小片（液体或光）；（河的）深水处，深潭；后备人员，备用物品；共用的资源（或资金）；（有相同职业或共同从事某项活动的）人群；赌球（或其他体育比赛），赌注；足球普尔（the pools)；落袋台球；垄断性联营；预赛组
v. 集中（资源、钱财等）以备共用；积水成洼；（血液）在静脉中淤积
【名】 （Pool）（英、西）普尔，（芬、德）波尔（人名）

e.en: Your predecessor is the person who had your job before you.

ex.en: He maintained that he learned everything he knew from his predecessor.
ex.zh: 他坚称他所知道的一切都是从他的前任那儿学到的。

e.en: The predecessor of an object or machine is the object or machine that came before it in a sequence or process of development.

ex.en: Although the car is some 2 inches shorter than its predecessor, its boot is 20 percent larger.
ex.zh: 尽管这款汽车比其上一代产品短2英寸，但它的行李箱大了20%。

d: n. predecessor 的复数：前任，前辈，前人；前身，前代事物

e.en: Previously means at some time before the period that you are talking about.

ex.en: Guyana's railways were previously owned by private companies.
ex.zh: 圭亚那的铁路先前为私营公司所拥有。

ex.en: The contract was awarded to a previously unknown company.
ex.zh: 该合同给了一家先前不知名的公司。

e.en: You can use previously to say how much earlier one event was than another event. (某时长)

ex.en: He had first entered the House 12 years previously.
ex.zh: 他12年前首次进入了众议院。

d: adv. 以前地，先前地

e.en: The price of something is the amount of money that you have to pay in order to buy it.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in the price of petrol.
ex.zh: …燃气价格的一次猛涨。

ex.en: They expected house prices to rise.
ex.zh: 他们预期房价会上涨。

e.en: The price that you pay for something that you want is an unpleasant thing that you have to do or suffer in order to get it.

ex.en: There may be a price to pay for such relentless activity, perhaps ill health or even divorce.
ex.zh: 这样没完没了的活动可能是要付出代价的，也许是不良健康状况甚至是离婚。

e.en: If something is priced at a particular amount, the price is set at that amount.

ex.en: The bond is currently priced at $900.
ex.zh: 这种债券当前定价为$900。

ex.en: Analysts predict that Digital will price the new line at less than half the cost of comparable IBM mainframes.
ex.zh: 分析家们预测迪吉多公司会将其新线产品的价格定在低于可比的IBM公司大型主机成本的一半的水平。

e.en: 定价

ex.en: It's hard to maintain competitive pricing.
ex.zh: 很难保持有竞争力的定价。

d: v. 给……定价；为……标价，贴价格标签；询问、调查或比较……的价格（price 的过去式及过去分词）
adj. 附有定价的，定价为……的

e.en: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.

ex.en: Money will also go into local development projects in Vietnam.
ex.zh: 资金也会流入越南本地开发项目。

ex.en: ...an international science project.
ex.zh: …一个国际科研项目。

e.en: A project is a detailed study of a subject by a student. (学生研究的)

ex.en: Students complete projects for a personal tutor, working at home at their own pace.
ex.zh: 学生们为个人导师完成课题研究，在家里按自己的速度工作。

e.en: If something is projected, it is planned or expected. 计划;

ex.en: 13% of Americans are over 65; this number is projected to reach 22% by the year 2030.
ex.zh: 13%的美国人在65岁以上；这个数字预计到2030年会达到22%。

ex.en: The government had been projecting a 5% consumer price increase for the entire year.
ex.zh: 政府一直在预计全年5%的消费价格增长。

e.en: If you project someone or something in a particular way, you try to make people see them in that way. If you project a particular feeling or quality, you show it in your behaviour. (以某方式)

ex.en: Bradley projects a natural warmth and sincerity.
ex.zh: 布拉德利表现出一种自然的热情和真诚。

ex.en: He just hasn't been able to project himself as the strong leader.
ex.zh: 他只是还没能把自己表现得是个强有力的领导。

d: n. 项目，计划；（学校的）课题，研究项目；廉租房区，公共房屋区
v. 预计，推算；计划，规划；伸出，突出；投掷，喷射；投射，投影；展现，表现；使（声音，尤指嗓音）扩及远处；传播；想像（自己、场景等）在另一地点或时间；（尤指无意地把情感、愿望）投射转移（给别人）；使（某人）迅速成功，让（某人）获得更好的工作；作（曲线）的射影图；把（地球，天空等）投影在平面上

e.en: A question is something that you say or write in order to ask a person about something.

ex.en: They asked a lot of questions about China.
ex.zh: 他们问了许多有关中国的问题。

e.en: If you question someone, you ask them a lot of questions about something.

ex.en: This led the therapist to question Jim about his parents and their marriage.
ex.zh: 这让治疗师询问起吉姆关于其父母以及他们的婚姻情况。

e.en: 询问

ex.en: The police have detained thirty-two people for questioning.
ex.zh: 警方拘留了32个人进行审问。

e.en: If you question something, you have or express doubts about whether it is true, reasonable, or worthwhile.

ex.en: It never occurs to them to question the doctor's decisions.
ex.zh: 他们从来没有想到去怀疑那个医生的决定。

d: n. 问题，疑问；试题，题目；（待讨论或处理的）事情，议题；不确定，怀疑
v. 向……提出问题，盘问；对……提出质疑（异议），怀疑

e.en: Someone or something that is quiet makes only a small amount of noise. 轻声的;

ex.en: Tania kept the children reasonably quiet and contented.
ex.zh: 塔妮娅把孩子们料理得安心而满足。

e.en: 轻声地;

ex.en: "This is goodbye, isn't it?" she said quietly.
ex.zh: “这就算告别了，不是吗？”她轻声地说道。

e.en: If a place is quiet, there is very little noise there.

ex.en: She was received in a small, quiet office.
ex.zh: 她在一间寂静的小办公室里受到接见。

e.en: 寂静

ex.en: I miss the quietness of the countryside.
ex.zh: 我怀念农村的寂静。

d: adj. 轻声的，安静的；不出声的；沉默寡言的，文静的；寂静的，平静的；不受打扰的，悠然的；（感情）不外露的，不张扬的；秘密的，私下的；（颜色、服饰）素净的，朴素大方的；清淡的
n. 安静，静谧
v. （使）平静，安静；消除，减轻（恐惧），平息（抱怨）

e.en: When someone or something reaches a place, they arrive there. 到达 (某地)

ex.en: He did not stop until he reached the door.
ex.zh: 他到门口才停住。

e.en: If someone or something has reached a certain stage, level, or amount, they are at that stage, level, or amount. 达到 (某一阶段、水平或数量)

ex.en: The process of political change in South Africa has reached the stage where it is irreversible.
ex.zh: 南非的政治变革进程已经到了不可逆转的阶段。

e.en: If you reach somewhere, you move your arm and hand to take or touch something. 伸手去 (拿或够东西)

ex.en: Judy reached into her handbag and handed me a small, printed leaflet.
ex.zh: 朱迪把手伸进手提袋中，递给我一张小小的印刷传单。

e.en: If you can reach something, you are able to touch it by stretching out your arm or leg. (伸展手臂或腿)

ex.en: Can you reach your toes with your fingertips?
ex.zh: 你能用手指尖触到脚趾头吗？

d: v. 到达，抵达；被看见，被听到；达到（特定的水平或数量）；达到（一个特定的时间或阶段）；（经讨论或思考后）达成，实现；伸，伸手；能伸到，能够到；把……递给；（大或长等）足够达到；（用电话等）与……联系；影响，打动；（航海）横风航驶；为……提供帮助（reach out to）
n. （臂的）伸出；伸手可及的距离；可到达的距离；（权力或能力）能及的范围；边远地区；层级，层次；河段，直水道；（特定时期内）观众人数，听众人数；（航海）横风行程
【名】  (Reach)(柬)列（人名）

e.en: If you refuse to do something, you deliberately do not do it, or you say firmly that you will not do it.

ex.en: He refused to comment after the trial.
ex.zh: 该审判之后他拒绝发表评论。

ex.en: I could hardly refuse, could I?
ex.zh: 我很难拒绝，是不是？

e.en: If someone refuses you something, they do not give it to you or do not allow you to have it.

ex.en: The United States has refused him a visa.
ex.zh: 美国当局已拒绝给予他签证。

e.en: If you refuse something that is offered to you, you do not accept it.

ex.en: The patient has the right to refuse treatment.
ex.zh: 病人有权拒绝治疗。

e.en: Refuse consists of the rubbish and all the things that are not wanted in a house, shop, or factory, and that are regularly thrown away; used mainly in official language. 垃圾;

ex.en: The town made a weekly collection of refuse.
ex.zh: 该镇每周收一次垃圾。

d: v. 拒绝，不肯，抵制（refuse 的第三人称单数形式）；拒绝接受，推辞；拒绝给予，不准

e.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

ex.en: Is religion still relevant to most people's lives?
ex.zh: 宗教和大多数人的生活还有关系吗？

d: adj. 有关的，切题的；正确的，适宜的；有价值的，有意义的

e.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change. 继续;

ex.en: The three men remained silent.
ex.zh: 这3个人保持沉默。

ex.en: The government remained in control.
ex.zh: 政府继续控制着局势。

e.en: If you remain in a place, you stay there and do not move away. 留在;

ex.en: They have asked the residents to remain in their homes.
ex.zh: 他们已经要求居民待在自己家里。

e.en: You can say that something remains when it still exists. 继续存在;

ex.en: The wider problem remains.
ex.zh: 更广泛的问题依然存在。

e.en: If something remains to be done, it has not yet been done and still needs to be done. 剩下; 余留;

ex.en: Major questions remain to be answered about his work.
ex.zh: 关于他工作的主要问题仍有待回答。

d: v. 逗留，留下；剩余，遗留；保持不变，一直是；仍需去做（或处理）
n. 剩余（物），遗迹；遗体，残骸

e.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second. 代替;

ex.en: One species of tree replaces another as a forest ages.
ex.zh: 随着森林老化，一种树会取代另一种树。

ex.en: ...the lawyer who replaced Robert as chairman of the company.
ex.zh: …取代罗伯特成为公司主席的那位律师。

e.en: If you replace one thing or person with another, you put something or someone else in their place to do their job. 用…代替;

ex.en: I clean out all the grease and replace it with oil so it works better in very low temperatures.
ex.zh: 我清除掉了所有的油脂，以油替换，因此它在很低的温度下运转得更好。

e.en: If you replace something that is broken, damaged, or lost, you get a new one to use instead. 换下 (坏的); 换上 (新的)

ex.en: The shower that we put in a few years back has broken and we cannot afford to replace it.
ex.zh: 我们几年前安装的淋浴器坏了，但没钱换新的。

e.en: If you replace something, you put it back where it was before.

ex.en: Replace the caps on the bottles.
ex.zh: 把瓶盖盖回到瓶子上。

d: v. replace 的过去式和过去分词：取代；替换；放回原处
adj. 被替换的
n. 提及，谈到；参考，查阅；（引自书或诗歌的）引言，引文；引文的作者，参考书目；（帮助或意见的）征求，征询； (为方便查询所用的）标记，编号；推荐信，介绍信；介绍人，推荐人
adj. 参考的，用于查阅的；文献索引的，参照的
v. 列出……的参考书目；提及，提到；引用，参照（某书或某作者）

e.en: A result is something that happens or exists because of something else that has happened.

ex.en: Compensation is available for people who have developed asthma as a direct result of their work.
ex.zh: 直接因工作原因患哮喘的人会获得赔偿。

e.en: If something results in a particular situation or event, it causes that situation or event to happen.

ex.en: Fifty percent of road accidents result in head injuries.
ex.zh: 50%的公路交通事故致使头部受伤。

e.en: If something results from a particular event or action, it is caused by that event or action.

ex.en: Many hair problems result from what you eat.
ex.zh: 很多头发问题是由你吃的东西引起的。

e.en: A result is the situation that exists at the end of a contest.

ex.en: The final election results will be announced on Friday.
ex.zh: 最终选举结果将在周五被公布。

d: v. 发生，产生；终归，导致（result 的第三人称单数，常与 in 连用）；由…引起，因…而产生（常与 from 连用）
n. 结果，后果；得分，成绩（考试、比赛或选举等的最终结果）；研究、检验或计算等得出的结果，答案；成功实现的事，成果；经营业绩，财务业绩（result 的复数）

e.en: When you reuse something, you use it again instead of throwing it away. 再使用;

ex.en: Try where possible to reuse paper.
ex.zh: 尽可能重复使用纸张。

e.en: Reuse is also a noun. 再使用;

ex.en: Copper, brass, and aluminium are separated and remelted for reuse.
ex.zh: 铜、黄铜和铝被分门别类重新熔化以供再利用。

d: v. 再次使用，重复使用
n. 再次使用，重复使用

e.en: Revenue is money that a company, organization, or government receives from people. (公司、组织或政府的)

ex.en: ...a boom year at the movies, with record advertising revenue and the highest ticket sales since 1980.
ex.zh: …电影业欣欣向荣的一年，广告及票房收入都创下1980年以来的最高纪录。

d: n. （企业、组织的）收入，收益；（政府的）税收；税务局，税务署（the revenue）

e.en: A road is a long piece of hard ground that is built between two places so that people can drive or ride easily from one place to the other.

ex.en: There was very little traffic on the roads.
ex.zh: 那时这些公路上车辆很少。

ex.en: We just go straight up the Boston Post Road.
ex.zh: 我们就径直沿着波士顿邮政大道走。

e.en: The road to a particular result is the means of achieving it or the process of achieving it. 途径;

ex.en: We are bound to see some ups and downs along the road to recovery.
ex.zh: 在复苏的道路上我们一定会经历一些波折起伏。

e.en: If you say that someone is on the road to something, you mean that they are likely to achieve it. 在 (取得成功的)

ex.en: The government took another step on the road to political reform.
ex.zh: 政府又在政治改革的道路上迈进了一步。

d: n. 路，公路，马路，街； 途径，方法，路子；（矿）地下巷道；贸易路线；铁路；（列车可通行的）无障碍铁路路轨，特殊情况铁路路轨；近岸锚地，港外锚地
【名】 （Road）（英）罗德（人名）

e.en: When a telephone rings, it makes a sound to let you know that someone is phoning you. (电话)

ex.en: As soon as he got home, the phone rang.
ex.zh: 他一到家，电话就响了。

e.en: Ring is also a noun. (电话)

ex.en: After at least eight rings, an ancient-sounding maid answered the phone.
ex.zh: 电话至少八声后，一位听上去很老的女仆接了。

e.en: (电话)

ex.en: She was jolted out of her sleep by the ringing of the telephone.
ex.zh: 她被电话响铃惊醒了。

e.en: When you ring someone, you telephone them.

ex.en: Would you ring me as soon as you find out? My number's in the phone book.
ex.zh: 你一查清就给我打电话好吗？我的号码在电话簿里。

ex.en: A friend of mine gave me this number to call.
ex.zh: 我的一个朋友让我打这个号码。

d: n. 戒指，指环；环状物，圈形物；圆圈；圆形表演场（或竞技场）；围成一圈的人（或物）；团伙，帮派；铃声，钟声，按铃，敲钟；（说法、讨论、辩论等的）特性；圆形灶盘，炉头；肛门；（化）环；（数）环
v. 包围；绕……画圆，把……圈起来；（尤指在动物身上）套环；敲钟，按铃；（给……）打电话；嗡嗡作响；回响；充满；非法将（汽车）改头换面
【名】 （Ring） （美、挪、德、爱、英、波、丹）林（人名）

e.en: A school is a place where children are educated. You usually refer to this place as school when you are talking about the time that children spend there and the activities that they do there.

ex.en: ...a boy who was in my class at school.
ex.zh: …上学时我班上的一个男孩。

ex.en: Even the good students say homework is what they most dislike about school.
ex.zh: 就连好学生也说家庭作业是他们最讨厌学校的一点。

e.en: A school is the students or staff at a school.

ex.en: Deirdre, the whole school's going to hate you.
ex.zh: 迪尔德丽，全校师生都要恨你了。

e.en: A privately-run place where a particular skill or subject is taught can be referred to as a school.

ex.en: ...a riding school.
ex.zh: …一所私立骑术学校。

e.en: A university, college, or university department specializing in a particular type of subject can be referred to as a school. 学院;
