ex.en: ...a lecturer in the school of veterinary medicine at the University of Pennsylvania.
ex.zh: …宾夕法尼亚大学兽医学系的一名讲师。

d: n. （中、小）学校；全校师生；上学时间；上学期间；专科学校；大学，大学期间；（大学的）系，学院；学派，流派；（鱼、鲸、海豚等的）群；（牛津大学的）期末考试大厅；（牛津大学的）期末考试；一伙赌徒；（轮番到酒吧请客喝酒的）酒友
v. 教育，培养（儿童）；训练，教育；（尤指为竞赛）驯马；（鱼，海兽）成群；强迫自己（做难事）
adj. （科萨人）受过西化教育的；（名字）源自西方的

e.en: A service is something that the public needs, such as transportation, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body. 公共服务机构;

ex.en: The postal service has been trying to cut costs.
ex.zh: 邮政系统一直在试图削减成本。

ex.en: We have started a campaign for better nursery and school services.
ex.zh: 我们已开展了一场运动，以改善幼儿园和学校的服务。

e.en: You can sometimes refer to an organization or private company as a particular service when it provides something for the public or acts on behalf of the government. 官方机构;

ex.en: The Agriculture Department has ultimate control over the Forest Service.
ex.zh: 农业部对林务局有最终控制权。

e.en: If an organization or company provides a particular service, they can do a particular job or a type of work for you. 服务;

ex.en: The kitchen maintains a twenty-four hour service and can be contacted via reception.
ex.zh: 厨房提供24小时服务，可通过接待处联系。

e.en: Services are activities such as tourism, banking, and selling things which are part of a country's economy, but are not concerned with producing or manufacturing goods. 服务性工作;

ex.en: Mining rose by 9.1%, manufacturing by 9.4% and services by 4.3%.
ex.zh: 采矿业增长了9.1%，制造业增长了9.4%，服务业增长了4.3%。

d: n. 维修，检修，保养（对机器、车辆、设备等的定期维护）
v. 为……服务；维修，保养；（金融）按期为（贷款、债务）支付利息和本金，还本付息（service 的现在分词/动名词形式）

e.en: You use simply to emphasize that something consists of only one thing, happens for only one reason, or is done in only one way. 只不过;

ex.en: The table is simply a chipboard circle on a base.
ex.zh: 这张桌子只不过是基座加圆形刨花板。

ex.en: Most of the damage that's occurred was simply because of fallen trees.
ex.zh: 大部分损失仅仅是因横倒在地面的树木造成的。

e.en: You use simply to emphasize what you are saying. 简直;

ex.en: This sort of increase simply cannot be justified.
ex.zh: 这种增长完全没有道理。

d: adv. 仅仅，只，不过；简直，的确； 简单地，简明地；朴素地，简朴地

e.en: You use spare to describe something that is the same as things that you are already using, but that you do not need yet and are keeping ready in case another one is needed.

ex.en: If possible keep a spare pair of glasses accessible in case your main pair is broken or lost.
ex.zh: 如有可能留一副备用眼镜以防你常用的那副打碎或丢失。

ex.en: He could have taken a spare key.
ex.zh: 他原本可以带上一把备用钥匙的。

e.en: Spare is also a noun.

ex.en: Give me the boot key and I'll get the spare.
ex.zh: 给我行李箱钥匙，我去配一把备用。

e.en: You use spare to describe something that is not being used by anyone, and is therefore available for someone to use.

ex.en: They don't have a lot of spare cash.
ex.zh: 他们并没有很多多余的现金。

ex.en: The spare bedroom is on the second floor.
ex.zh: 闲置的卧室在2楼。

e.en: If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.

ex.en: You got here with ninety seconds to spare.
ex.zh: 你们到达这里时还剩有90秒钟。

d: adj. 备用的，外加的；不用的，闲置的；空闲的，空余的；多余的；简单的，简朴的；瘦的，瘦高的；少量的；节约的
v. 抽出，拿出（时间、金钱等）；饶恕，赦免；省得，免去；节约，吝惜；保证（或满足）自己的需要（spare oneself）；剩余，剩下（时间、金钱或空间）；分让；删节
n. 备用品；（车辆或机器的）零件，备件；（十柱保龄球戏中的）二击全倒
【名】 (Spare)（美、英、瑞典、加、拉脱维亚、印、法）史琶尔（人名）

e.en: A square is a shape with four sides that are all the same length and four corners that are all right angles.

ex.en: Serve the cake warm or at room temperature, cut in squares.
ex.zh: 端上温的或房间温度的蛋糕，把它切成正方形。

ex.en: There was a calendar on the wall, with large squares around the dates.
ex.zh: 墙上有一副日历，日期周围是大的方框。

e.en: In a town or city, a square is a flat open place, often in the shape of a square.

ex.en: The house is located in one of the city's prettiest squares.
ex.zh: 该房子位于市区最漂亮的广场之一。

e.en: Something that is square has a shape the same as a square or similar to a square. 正方形的;

ex.en: Round tables seat more people in the same space as a square table.
ex.zh: 在同一空间里，圆桌比方桌可以坐更多的人。

e.en: Square is used before units of length when referring to the area of something. For example, if something is three feet long and two feet wide, its area is six square feet. 平方的 (用于长度单位前表示面积)

ex.en: The new complex will provide 10 million square feet of office space.
ex.zh: 这座新的综合建筑群将提供1千万平方英尺的办公空间。

d: adj. 正方形的，四方形的；成直角的；平方的；两清的，互不欠账的；诚实公正的；古板守旧的；平行的，水平的；宽阔结实的；打平的，平局的；一致的，可共存的；长宽为…...的；整齐的；（韵律）简单易懂的
n. 正方形，四方形；广场；平方，二次幂；古板守旧的人；（棋盘上的）方格；直角尺，丁字尺；（步兵的）方阵；方围巾；托灰板，灰浆板；（板球）内场；（军营中的）操练场；街区；（占星）90度星位；美餐，饱餐
v. 使成平方，使成二次幂；使（比赛的比分）打平；挺起胸膛；使成正方形，使成方形；贿赂，收买；使谐调，符合；就…...征得…...的同意；结账，付清欠款；横（向）传（球）；（占星）处于方照位置
adv. 直接地；成直角，垂直地；公正地，诚实地

e.en: If you have been doing something and then you stop doing it, you no longer do it.

ex.en: Stop throwing those stones!
ex.zh: 别再扔那些石头了！

ex.en: Does either of the parties want to stop the fighting?
ex.zh: 双方中有谁想停止战斗呢？

e.en: If you stop something from happening, or you stop something happening, you prevent it from happening or prevent it from continuing.

ex.en: He proposed a new diplomatic initiative to try to stop the war.
ex.zh: 他提出了一个新的试图阻止战争的外交倡议。

ex.en: He would do what he must to stop her from destroying him.
ex.zh: 他将做该做的事来阻止她把他毁了。

e.en: If an activity or process stops, it is no longer happening.

ex.en: The rain had stopped and a star or two was visible over the mountains.
ex.zh: 雨停了，山上的天空可见一两颗星星。

ex.en: The system overheated and filming had to stop.
ex.zh: 系统过热，拍摄工作不得不停下。

e.en: If something such as machine stops or is stopped, it is no longer moving or working. 停止 (转动或工作)

ex.en: The clock stopped at 11:59 Saturday night.
ex.zh: 钟在星期六晚11点59分停了。

ex.en: Arnold stopped the engine and got out of the car.
ex.zh: 阿诺德关闭发动机然后下了车。

d: v. （使）停止，结束；（使）中断；（机器等）停止运转；（汽车或火车）停靠；暂时中断（以便做某事）；防止，阻拦；堵塞；短暂停留；停付，扣除；处于，表现
n. 停止，终止；车站；停车路口；（旅行中的）逗留，停留；塞音；（风琴的）音栓；（管风琴的）音管；（让银行）止付；救球；句号；光圈

e.en: A street is a road in a city, town, or village, usually with houses along it.

ex.en: He lived at 66 Bingfield Street.
ex.zh: 他住在宾菲尔德街66号。

e.en: You can use street or streets when talking about activities that happen out of doors in a city or town rather than inside a building.

ex.en: Changing money on the street is illegal – always use a bank.
ex.zh: 在街头兑换货币是非法的–始终要去银行。

ex.en: Their aim is to raise a million dollars to get the homeless off the streets.
ex.zh: 他们的目的是募集100万美元以使无家可归者不再流浪街头。

d: n. 街道（street 的复数）；街头，指城市中在建筑物外进行的活动或发生的情况（常用于 in/on the streets、take to the streets 等搭配）

e.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual. 显著的;

ex.en: The most striking feature of those statistics is the high proportion of suicides.
ex.zh: 那些统计数据最显著的特征是高自杀率。

ex.en: He bears a striking resemblance to Lenin.
ex.zh: 他与列宁有着不同寻常的相似之处。

e.en: 显著地;

ex.en: In one respect, however, the men really were strikingly similar.
ex.zh: 然而，在一方面，这些男人的确惊人地相似。

ex.en: ...a strikingly handsome man.
ex.zh: …一个异乎寻常地英俊的男人。

e.en: Someone who is striking is very attractive, in a noticeable way.

ex.en: She was a striking woman with long blonde hair.
ex.zh: 她曾是一个留着金色长发的俊秀女子。

d: adj. 惊人的，异常的；妩媚动人的，标致的；罢工的；打击的
n. 撞击，碰撞
v. 打，撞；（用手或武器等）打；罢工（strike 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A student is a person who is studying at an elementary school, secondary school, college, or university.

ex.en: Warren's eldest son is an art student.
ex.zh: 沃伦的长子是一名学艺术的学生。

e.en: Someone who is a student of a particular subject is interested in the subject and spends time learning about it.

ex.en: ...a passionate student of history and an expert on nineteenth century prime ministers.
ex.zh: …一位热衷历史的学者和一个研究19世纪首相们的专家。

d: n. 学生；学者

e.en: You use suspect when you are stating something that you believe is probably true, in order to make it sound less strong or direct.

ex.en: I suspect they were right.
ex.zh: 我觉得他们是正确的。

ex.en: The above complaints are, I suspect, just the tip of the iceberg.
ex.zh: 上述的这些抱怨，我觉得，不过是冰山的一角。

e.en: If you suspect that something dishonest or unpleasant has been done, you believe that it has probably been done. If you suspect someone of doing an action of this kind, you believe that they probably did it.

ex.en: He suspected that the woman staying in the flat above was using heroin.
ex.zh: 他怀疑住在楼上公寓里的那位女子在吸食海洛因。

ex.en: It was perfectly all right, he said, because the police had not suspected him of anything.
ex.zh: 一点儿没事，他说，因为警察对他没有任何怀疑。

e.en: A suspect is a person who the police or authorities think may be guilty of a crime.

ex.en: Police have arrested a suspect in a series of killings and sexual assaults in the city.
ex.zh: 警方逮捕了该城市一系列杀人强奸案件中的一名嫌疑犯。

e.en: Suspect things or people are ones that you think may be dangerous or may be less good or genuine than they appear.

ex.en: Delegates evacuated the building when a suspect package was found.
ex.zh: 一个可疑包裹被发现后，代表们撤离了这栋大楼。

d: v. 猜想，认为（某事有可能）；怀疑……有罪，认为……有嫌疑；不信任，怀疑……的真实性
n. 嫌疑犯，可疑分子；（某坏事物的）可能导致者
adj. 不可靠的，不可信的；可疑的，可能有危险的；有问题的，运转不好的

e.en: Swimming is the activity of swimming, especially as a sport or for pleasure.

ex.en: Swimming is probably the best form of exercise you can get.
ex.zh: 游泳可能是你能采取的最佳的锻炼方式。

d: n. 游泳，游泳运动；目眩，眩晕
adj. 游泳的；游泳用的；善于游泳的；晕眩的
v. 游泳；漂浮；眩晕；旋转（swim 的 ing 形式）

e.en: Tax is an amount of money that you have to pay to the government so that it can pay for public services such as road and schools.

ex.en: No-one enjoys paying tax.
ex.zh: 没人喜欢缴税。

ex.en: ...a pledge not to raise taxes on people below a certain income.
ex.zh: …一个对收入低于一定水平的人不提高税收的承诺。

e.en: When a person or company is taxed, they have to pay a part of their income or profits to the government. When goods are taxed, a percentage of their price has to be paid to the government. (对个人、公司、货物)

ex.en: Husband and wife may be taxed separately on their incomes.
ex.zh: 丈夫和妻子可能会分别被征收所得税。

d: n. 税款；负担，重负
v. 对……征税；缴纳车辆牌照税；使负重担，使费力气；责备；审定（诉讼费用）
【名】 （Tax）（美、荷、奥、印、俄、德）塔克斯（人名）

e.en: A tower is a tall, narrow building, that either stands alone or forms part of another building such as a church or castle.

ex.en: ...an eleventh century castle with 120-foot high towers.
ex.zh: …一座11世纪的城堡，有着120英尺高的塔楼。

e.en: Someone or something that towers over surrounding people or things is a lot taller than they are.

ex.en: He stood up and towered over her.
ex.zh: 他站起来，高出她许多。

e.en: A tower is a tall structure that is used for sending radio or television signals. (无线电或电视信号的)

ex.en: Troops are still in control of the television and radio tower.
ex.zh: 军队仍然控制着电视和无线电的发射塔。

e.en: A tower is a tall box that contains the main parts of a computer, such as the hard disk and the drives. (计算机)

d: n. 塔，塔楼；发射塔，信号塔；（化工、能源）塔器；（计算机）塔式机箱；空中跳台（tower 的复数）；（Towers）人名（亦译“托尔斯”）
v. （tower 的第三人称单数）高耸，高出（常与 over、above 连用）

e.en: A town is a place with streets and buildings, where people live and work. Towns are larger than neighbourhoods and smaller than cities. In informal English, cities are sometimes called towns.

ex.en: ...the northern California town of Albany.
ex.zh: …加利福尼亚北部的奥尔巴尼镇。

e.en: You can use the town to refer to the people of a town. (某一城镇的)

ex.en: The town takes immense pride in recent achievements.
ex.zh: 镇上的居民为最近的成就感到无比自豪。

e.en: You use town in order to refer to the town where you live. (自己居住的)

ex.en: He admits he doesn't even know when his brother is in town.
ex.zh: 他承认甚至不知道他的兄弟什么时候在镇上。

e.en: You use town in order to refer to the central area of a town where most of the stores and offices are.

ex.en: I walked into town.
ex.zh: 我走进了市中心。

d: n. 城镇，市镇； （生活、工作或刚提到的）城镇；（城镇的）商业区，中心区；全体镇民，全镇人；城市生活（与乡村生活相对）；镇政府
【名】 （Town）（英）汤（人名）

e.en: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave toward them or deal with them in that way. 对待;

ex.en: Artie treated most women with indifference.
ex.zh: 阿蒂对待大多数女性颇为冷淡。

ex.en: Police say they're treating it as a case of attempted murder.
ex.zh: 警方说他们正将其作为谋杀未遂案件来处理。

e.en: When a doctor or nurse treats a patient or an illness, he or she tries to make the patient well again.

ex.en: Doctors treated her with aspirin.
ex.zh: 医生用阿斯匹林给她治疗。

ex.en: The boy was treated for a minor head wound.
ex.zh: 那个男孩因头部轻伤而接受治疗。

e.en: If something is treated with a particular substance, the substance is put onto or into it in order to clean it, to protect it, or to give it special properties. (用某种物质)

ex.en: About 70% of the cocoa acreage is treated with insecticide.
ex.zh: 大约70%的可可豆种植区都用杀虫剂处理过。

e.en: If you treat someone to something special which they will enjoy, you buy it or arrange it for them.

ex.en: She was always treating him to ice cream.
ex.zh: 她总请他吃冰淇淋。

ex.en: Tomorrow I'll treat myself to a day's gardening.
ex.zh: 明天我要好好享受一天的园艺活儿。

d: v. treat 的过去式和过去分词：治疗；对待、看待；处理、加工；款待、招待
adj. treat 的过去分词作形容词：经治疗的；已处理过的

e.en: If something is unfamiliar to you, you know nothing or very little about it, because you have not seen or experienced it before.

ex.en: She grew many wonderful plants that were unfamiliar to me.
ex.zh: 她种了很多我从未见过的奇异植物。

e.en: If you are unfamiliar with something, you know nothing or very little about it.

ex.en: She speaks no Japanese and is unfamiliar with Japanese culture.
ex.zh: 她不说日语并且不熟悉日本文化。

d: adj. 不熟悉的，陌生的；不常见的，生疏的；对……不熟悉的，不熟知的，没有经验的

e.en: If you say that something is unthinkable, you are emphasizing that it cannot possibly be accepted or imagined as a possibility. 无法接受的;

ex.en: Her strong Catholic beliefs made abortion unthinkable.
ex.zh: 笃信天主教使她无法接受堕胎。

e.en: The unthinkable is something that is unthinkable. 无法接受的事物;

ex.en: Teresa Zapata told her family the unthinkable; she was going to work in the United States.
ex.zh: 特雷莎·扎帕塔告诉了那件她的家人很难想像的事实，她打算到美国工作。

d: adj. 不能想象的，难以想象的，不可思议的；无法接受的
n. the unthinkable：难以想象或无法接受的事情

e.en: A vote is a choice made by a particular person or group in a meeting or an election.

ex.en: He walked to the local polling place to cast his vote.
ex.zh: 他走到当地的投票点去投票。

ex.en: Mr. Reynolds was re-elected by 102 votes to 60.
ex.zh: 雷诺兹先生以102票对60票再次当选。

e.en: A vote is an occasion when a group of people make a decision by each person indicating his or her choice. The choice that most people support is accepted by the group.

ex.en: Why do you think we should have a vote on that?
ex.zh: 你为什么认为我们应该对那件事进行投票表决？

e.en: The vote is the total number of votes or voters in an election, or the number of votes received or cast by a particular group. 投票总数;

ex.en: Opposition parties won about fifty-five percent of the vote.
ex.zh: 反对党赢得大约55％的选票。

e.en: If you have the vote in an election, or have a vote in a meeting, you have the legal right to indicate your choice.

ex.en: Before that, women did not have a vote at all.
ex.zh: 在那之前，妇女根本就没有选举权。

d: v. 投票，表决（vote 的过去式及过去分词）；投票选出，推举；投票赞成，投票同意，投票支持；投票否决；罢免；淘汰（常与 down/out/off 连用）；认为，判定，公认为（多用于被动）；建议，主张（非正式，多用于 I vote that...）；投票通过，同意提供（资金、援助等）；用脚投票，以离去表示反对（vote with one's feet 的过去式）

e.en: A vote is a choice made by a particular person or group in a meeting or an election.

ex.en: He walked to the local polling place to cast his vote.
ex.zh: 他走到当地的投票点去投票。

ex.en: Mr. Reynolds was re-elected by 102 votes to 60.
ex.zh: 雷诺兹先生以102票对60票再次当选。

e.en: A vote is an occasion when a group of people make a decision by each person indicating his or her choice. The choice that most people support is accepted by the group.

ex.en: Why do you think we should have a vote on that?
ex.zh: 你为什么认为我们应该对那件事进行投票表决？

e.en: The vote is the total number of votes or voters in an election, or the number of votes received or cast by a particular group. 投票总数;

ex.en: Opposition parties won about fifty-five percent of the vote.
ex.zh: 反对党赢得大约55％的选票。

e.en: If you have the vote in an election, or have a vote in a meeting, you have the legal right to indicate your choice.

ex.en: Before that, women did not have a vote at all.
ex.zh: 在那之前，妇女根本就没有选举权。

d: v. 投票选举，投票表决；投票评选；（通过投票）决定给予（资助），同意提供（款项）；表明，公认（某事好或坏）；投票同意；建议，主张
n. 选票，票；投票，表决；（选举中的）选票总数（the vote）；选举权，表决权；投票结果，表决结果；投票者，选民（the vote）；特定投票群体，特定选民
【名】 （Vote）（英、法）沃特（人名）

e.en: Voters are people who have the legal right to vote in elections, or people who are voting in a particular election.

ex.en: The turnout was at least 62 percent of registered voters.
ex.zh: 至少有62%的登记选民参加了投票。

d: n. 选民，投票人（voter 的复数）

e.en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

ex.en: I want a drink.
ex.zh: 我想要点喝的。

ex.en: People wanted to know who this talented designer was.
ex.zh: 人们想知道这位天才的设计者是谁。

e.en: You can say that you want to say something to indicate that you are about to say it. 想要 (说)

ex.en: I want to say how delighted I am that you're having a baby.
ex.zh: 我想要说，你怀孕了我是多么高兴啊。

e.en: If you say to someone that you want something, or ask them if they want to do it, you are firmly telling them what you want or what you want them to do. 想要得到;

ex.en: I want an explanation from you, Jeremy.
ex.zh: 我要你给我一个解释，杰里米。

ex.en: Do you want to tell me what all this is about?
ex.zh: 你是否想告诉我这究竟是怎么回事？

e.en: If you tell someone that they want to do a particular thing, you are advising them to do it.

ex.en: You want to be very careful not to have a man like Crevecoeur for an enemy.
ex.zh: 你必须非常小心，不要与像克雷弗克那样的人为敌。

d: adj. 被警方追捕的，被通缉的；为人渴望和喜爱的，受人照料的
v. 需要；想要，希望；（用于提出建议）应该（want 的过去式和过去分词形式）
adj. 适于步行的；可以走去的，步行可达的

e.en: A warehouse is a large building where raw materials or manufactured goods are stored until they are exported to other countries or distributed to stores to be sold. 仓库;

d: n. 仓库，货栈，货仓；仓储式批发商店，仓储式零售商店
v. 将（商品）存库，使入库；将（某人，尤其是犯人或精神病患者）安置在条件差的仓库式的收容所中

e.en: You use whether when you are talking about a choice or doubt between two or more alternatives.

ex.en: To this day, it's unclear whether he shot himself or was murdered.
ex.zh: 直到今天，他是自杀还是被谋杀仍然不清楚。

ex.en: Whether it turns out to be a good idea or a bad idea, we'll find out.
ex.zh: 最终这个点子是好还是坏，我们会搞清楚的。

e.en: You use whether to say that something is true in any of the circumstances that you mention.

ex.en: This happens whether the children are in two-parent or one-parent families.
ex.zh: 这种情况无论在双亲家庭还是单亲家庭的孩子身上都会发生。

ex.en: Whether they say it aloud or not, most men expect their wives to be faithful.
ex.zh: 无论他们是否说出来，大部分男人都希望他们的妻子忠贞不渝。

d: conj. 是否（表选择或可能性）；不管，无论
pron. 两个中的哪一个

e.en: A word is a single unit of language that can be represented in writing or speech. In English, a word has a space on either side of it when it is written.

ex.en: The words stood out clearly on the page.
ex.zh: 这些单词清晰地呈现在页面上。

ex.en: The word "ginseng" comes from the Chinese word "Shen-seng."
ex.zh: 这个词来自中文的“人参”。

e.en: Someone's words are what they say or write.

ex.en: I was devastated when her words came true.
ex.zh: 她的话应验时，我感到震惊。

e.en: The words of a song consist of the text that is sung, in contrast to the music that is played.

ex.en: Can you hear the words on the album?
ex.zh: 你能听清那张专集里的歌词吗？

e.en: If you have a word with someone, you have a short conversation with them.

ex.en: I think it's time you had a word with him.
ex.zh: 我认为该是你和他谈一谈的时候了。

d: n. word 的复数：词，单词；话语，言语，言辞；歌词，台词；（用于 have words 等）争吵，口角；in other words 换句话说，也就是说；eat one's words 收回前言，承认说错；（计算机）字
v. word 的第三人称单数形式：措辞，用言语表达

e.en: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it from somewhere else.

ex.en: Fresh groups of guests arrived.
ex.zh: 新客成批到达了。

ex.en: ...a small group of commuters waiting for their train, which arrived on time.
ex.zh: …几个等候火车准点到达的通勤者。

e.en: When you arrive at a place, you come to it for the first time in order to stay, live, or work there.

ex.en: ...in the old days before the European settlers arrived in the country.
ex.zh: …在欧洲定居者们初次到这个国家之前的古老岁月。

e.en: When something such as letter or meal arrives, it is brought or delivered to you.

ex.en: Breakfast arrived while he was in the bathroom.
ex.zh: 早餐在他在浴室里时送到了。

e.en: When something such as a new product or invention arrives, it becomes available. (产品、发明)

ex.en: Several long-awaited movies will finally arrive in the stores this month.
ex.zh: 几部期盼已久的影片最终将于本月在各家商店露面。

d: v．到达，抵达：到达某地或达到某个状态。

e.en: Batteries are small devices that provide the power for electrical items such as radios and children's toys.

ex.en: The shavers come complete with batteries.
ex.zh: 这些电动剃须刀带有电池。

ex.en: ...a battery-operated cassette player.
ex.zh: …用电池的磁带放音机。

e.en: A car battery is a rectangular box containing acid that is found in a car engine. It provides the electricity needed to start the car. (汽车)

ex.en: ...a car with a dead battery.
ex.zh: …一辆蓄电池没电了的汽车。

e.en: Battery is the crime of hitting or beating someone.

ex.en: Lawrence punched a man in a Los Angeles nightclub and was charged with battery.
ex.zh: 劳伦斯在洛杉矶的一家夜总会里打了人，结果被指控犯了殴打罪。

e.en: A battery of equipment such as guns, lights, or computers is a large set of it kept together in one place. 一排;

ex.en: They stopped beside a battery of abandoned guns.
ex.zh: 他们停在一排废弃的大炮旁。

d: n. （电）电池（battery 的复数形式）；一组，一套，一系列（battery 的复数形式）

e.en: If someone has power, they have a lot of control over people and activities.

ex.en: In a democracy, power must be divided.
ex.zh: 在民主政体中，权力必须被分散。

e.en: Your power to do something is your ability to do it.

ex.en: Human societies have the power to solve the problems confronting them.
ex.zh: 人类社会有能力解决他们面临的问题。

ex.en: Fathers have the power to dominate children and young people.
ex.zh: 父辈们有控制孩子们和年轻人的能力。

e.en: If it is in or within your power to do something, you are able to do it or you have the resources to deal with it.

ex.en: Your debt situation is only temporary, and it is within your power to resolve it.
ex.zh: 你的债务状况只是暂时的，解决它在你的能力范围里。

e.en: If someone in authority has the power to do something, they have the legal right to do it. (法律赋予的)

ex.en: The police have the power of arrest.
ex.zh: 警察有逮捕权。

d: n. 控制力，操控力；政权，统治；权力，职权；强国，大国；有影响力的人（或组织）；能力，本领；支配力，实力；（某事物或社会集团的）影响力，势力；力量，体能；能量，电力；动力，功率；幂，乘方，指数；放大率；神灵，神力；（基督教）掌权天使（powers）；（旨在提升某群体地位的）权力运动
v. 驱动，推动（机器或车辆）；（使）迅猛移动，快速前进；猛力踢（或推、顶）（尤指球）
adj. 电力的，电动的；强大的；有重要人士参与的；（服装）礼服的，显示权势的

e.en: Batteries are small devices that provide the power for electrical items such as radios and children's toys.

ex.en: The shavers come complete with batteries.
ex.zh: 这些电动剃须刀带有电池。

ex.en: ...a battery-operated cassette player.
ex.zh: …用电池的磁带放音机。

e.en: A car battery is a rectangular box containing acid that is found in a car engine. It provides the electricity needed to start the car. (汽车)

ex.en: ...a car with a dead battery.
ex.zh: …一辆蓄电池没电了的汽车。

e.en: Battery is the crime of hitting or beating someone.

ex.en: Lawrence punched a man in a Los Angeles nightclub and was charged with battery.
ex.zh: 劳伦斯在洛杉矶的一家夜总会里打了人，结果被指控犯了殴打罪。

e.en: A battery of equipment such as guns, lights, or computers is a large set of it kept together in one place. 一排;

ex.en: They stopped beside a battery of abandoned guns.
ex.zh: 他们停在一排废弃的大炮旁。

d: n. 电池，蓄电池；一组，一系列；炮组，排炮；殴打罪；（棒球队的）投手和接球手
adj. 笼养的，层架式养殖的

e.en: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.

ex.en: I always wanted to call the dog Mufty for some reason.
ex.zh: 出于某种原因，我总想叫那条狗穆夫蒂。

ex.en: "Doctor..."—"Will you please call me Sarah?"
ex.zh: “…医生” — “请叫我萨拉好吗？”

e.en: If you call someone or something a particular thing, you suggest they are that thing or describe them as that thing. 把…描述为;

ex.en: The speech was interrupted by members of the Republican Party, who called him a traitor.
ex.zh: 演讲被称他为叛徒的共和党成员们打断了。

ex.en: She calls me lazy and selfish.
ex.zh: 她说我又懒又自私。

e.en: If you call something, you say it in a loud voice, because you are trying to attract someone's attention.

ex.en: He could hear the others downstairs calling his name.
ex.zh: 他能听到其他人在楼下喊他的名字。

e.en: Call out means the same as call.

ex.en: The butcher's son called out a greeting.
ex.zh: 那屠夫的儿子声音洪亮地招呼了一声。

d: v. 给……命名，称呼；认为……是，把……看作；喊，叫；召开，召集；召唤，呼唤；传唤（证人）；打电话；打电话叫……来；点（名），从（清单上）读出；（动物）啼叫，鸣叫；（模仿动物的叫声）把……引过来；短暂拜访；（火车、船、公共汽车等）短暂停留；预测，推测；猜掷币结果；（比赛中裁判等）判定；取消（比赛等）；决定（进攻战术）；叫（对方）摊牌，叫牌；执行子程序命令
n. 打电话，通话；喊叫，呼叫；（动物的）叫声；短暂拜访；号召，呼吁；需求，需要；需要关注或努力的事；吸引力，魅力；登机广播；器乐声；决定，抉择；裁定，判决；叫牌，吊牌；掷钱币猜正反面；舞步指示；催交；买入期权，购买选择权；执行子程序的命令
【名】 （Call）（瑞典、罗）卡尔，（英）考尔（人名）

e.en: Your capacity for something is your ability to do it, or the amount of it that you are able to do.

ex.en: Our capacity for giving care, love, and attention is limited.
ex.zh: 我们给予照顾、爱护和关心的能力是有限的。

ex.en: Her mental capacity and temperament are as remarkable as his.
ex.zh: 她的智慧和气质与他的同样出众。

e.en: The capacity of a container is its volume, or the amount of liquid it can hold, measured in units such as quarts or gallons.

ex.en: ...containers with a maximum capacity of 200 gallons of water.
ex.zh: …最大容量为200加仑水的容器。

e.en: The capacity of something such as a factory, industry, or region is the quantity of things that it can produce or deliver with the equipment or resources that are available.

ex.en: ...the amount of spare capacity in the economy.
ex.zh: ...经济中的过剩产能。

ex.en: Bread factories are working at full capacity.
ex.zh: 面包厂正在满负荷进行生产。

e.en: The capacity of a piece of equipment is its size or power, often measured in particular units.

ex.en: ...an aircraft with a bomb-carrying capacity of 1000 pounds.
ex.zh: …一架炸弹装载量达1000磅的飞机。

d: n. 能力，才能；容积，容纳能力；职位，职责；功率，容积；生产量，生产能力
adj. 无虚席的，满场的

e.en: Electricity is a form of energy that can be carried by wires and is used for heating and lighting, and to provide power for machines.

ex.en: We moved into a cabin with electricity but no running water.
ex.zh: 我们搬进了一间有电但是没有自来水的小木屋。

d: n. 电，电流，电力；强烈感情

e.en: The evening is the part of each day between the end of the afternoon and the time when you go to bed. 傍晚;

ex.en: All he did that evening was sit around the house.
ex.zh: 那天晚上他所做的就是闲坐在家里。

ex.en: Supper is from 5:00 to 6:00 in the evening.
ex.zh: 晚餐是在傍晚5至6点间。

d: n. 晚上，傍晚；晚会，晚间活动；暮年，晚年
int. 晚上好（good evening 的简称）
adj. 在晚上的，为晚上的

e.en: A grid is something which is in a pattern of straight lines that cross over each other, forming squares. On maps, the grid is used to help you find a particular thing or place. 网格; (地图上的)

ex.en: ...a grid of ironwork.
ex.zh: …铁格栅。

ex.en: ...a grid of narrow streets.
ex.zh: …网格式的狭窄街道。

e.en: A grid is a network of wires and cables by which sources of power, such as electricity, are distributed throughout a country or area. 系统网络 (指输电网等)

ex.en: ...breakdowns in communications and electric-power grids.
ex.zh: …通信与输电网故障。

e.en: The grid or the starting grid is the starting line on a car-racing track.

ex.en: The Ferrari driver was starting second on the grid.
ex.zh: 那位法拉利赛车手排在起跑线的第二位。

d: n. 网格，方格；栅栏；输电网，电力网；赛车起跑线；美式橄榄球球场，橄榄球赛；（控制）栅极；计算机联网
v. 使……构成网格状，布置成网格结构

e.en: A gap is a space between two things or a hole in the middle of something solid. 缺口;

ex.en: He pulled the thick curtains together, leaving just a narrow gap.
ex.zh: 他把厚厚的窗帘拉到一起，只留了一条窄缝。

e.en: A gap is a period of time when you are not busy or when you stop doing something that you normally do.

ex.en: There followed a gap of four years, during which William joined the Army.
ex.zh: 之后有4年的间隔，期间威廉参军了。

e.en: If there is something missing from a situation that prevents it from being complete or satisfactory, you can say that there is a gap.

ex.en: The manifesto calls for a greater effort to recruit young scientists to fill the gap left by a wave of retirements expected over the next decade.
ex.zh: 该声明呼吁加大力度招募年轻的科学家，以填补预期未来十年内一波退休高峰所留下的空缺。

e.en: A gap between two groups of people, things, or sets of ideas is a big difference between them.

ex.en: ...the gap between rich and poor.
ex.zh: …贫富差距。

ex.en: America's trade gap widened.
ex.zh: 美国的贸易差额加大了。

d: n. 缝隙，缺口；（时间上的）间隔；空白，缺漏；隔阂，差距

e.en: You use less to indicate that there is a smaller amount of something than before or than average. You can use "a little," "a lot," "a bit," "far," and "much" in front of less. 较少的;

ex.en: People should eat less fat to reduce the risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 人们应该少吃脂肪以减少患心脏病的风险。

ex.en: ...a dishwasher that uses less water and electricity than older machines.
ex.zh: …一台比老式机器用水用电更少的洗碗机。

e.en: Less is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Borrowers are striving to ease their financial position by spending less and saving more.
ex.zh: 借款者都在努力通过少花多存来缓解经济紧张状况。

e.en: Less is also a quantifier.

ex.en: Last year less of the money went into high-technology companies.
ex.zh: 去年，投入到高科技公司的钱较少。

e.en: You use less than before a number or amount to say that the actual number or amount is smaller than this.

ex.en: ...a country whose entire population is less than 12 million.
ex.zh: …一个总人口少于1200万的国家。

d: adv. 更少地，程度较低地
det. （与不可数名词连用）较少的，更少的
prep. 减去，扣除
pron. 更少，较小；更小（或更无关紧要）的事物

e.en: You can use make with a wide range of nouns to indicate that someone performs an action or says something. For example, if you make a suggestion, you suggest something.
e.zh: 与名词连用，表示做动作或说某事

ex.en: I'd just like to make a comment.
ex.zh: 我只想做一下评论。

ex.en: I made a few phone calls.
ex.zh: 我打了几个电话。

e.en: You can use make with certain nouns to indicate that someone does something well or badly. For example, if you make a success of something, you do it successfully, and if you make a mess of something, you do it very badly.
e.zh: 与某些名词连用，表示做得好或做得糟

ex.en: Apparently he made a mess of his audition.
ex.zh: 显然他把试演搞得一团糟。

e.en: If you make as if to do something or make to do something, you behave in a way that makes it seem that you are just about to do it. 摆出 (要做某事的姿态)

ex.en: Mary made as if to protest, then hesitated.
ex.zh: 玛丽似乎要抗议，又犹豫了。

e.en: If you make do with something, you use or have it instead of something else that you do not have, although it is not as good. (拿…)

ex.en: Why make do with a copy if you can afford the genuine article?
ex.zh: 如果你买得起正品，为什么还拿复制品凑合呢？

d: v. 做，制作，制造；使，使得，让（make 的第三人称单数）
n. 品牌，型号，种类；品质；产量；制作过程（make 的复数）

e.en: If you refer to the storage of something, you mean that it is kept in a special place until it is needed.

ex.en: ...the storage of toxic waste.
ex.zh: …有毒废弃物的贮藏。

ex.en: Some of the space will at first be used for storage.
ex.zh: 一些空间将首先用于贮藏。

d: n. 储存，贮藏；（信息的）存储，存储空间；（家具等的）存放，保管；储存空间，储藏场所；仓库费，仓租
adj. 储存的

e.en: You use almost to indicate that something is not completely the case but is nearly the case. 差不多;

ex.en: The couple had been dating for almost three years.
ex.zh: 这对情侣谈恋爱差不多三年了。

ex.en: The effect is almost impossible to describe.
ex.zh: 这影响几乎无法言表。

d: adv. 几乎，差不多

e.en: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

ex.en: "How is Frank?" he asked.
ex.zh: “弗兰克怎么样？”他问道。

ex.en: I asked him his name.
ex.zh: 我问了他的名字。

e.en: If you ask someone to do something, you tell them that you want them to do it. 让 (某人做某事)

ex.en: We had to ask him to leave.
ex.zh: 我们不得不让他离开。

e.en: If you ask to do something, you tell someone that you want to do it.

ex.en: I asked to see the Director.
ex.zh: 我要求见总经理。

e.en: If you ask for something, you say that you would like it.

ex.en: I decided to go to the next house and ask for food.
ex.zh: 我决定到隔壁房子去要吃的。

d: vt. （ask 的第三人称单数）问，询问；要求，请求；需要；邀请；要价，讨价
vi. （ask 的第三人称单数）问，询问；要求；问候（ask after）

e.en: In finance, arbitrage is the activity of buying securities or currency in one financial market and selling it at a profit in another.

ex.en: Astute Singaporeans quickly spotted an arbitrage opportunity.
ex.zh: 精明的新加坡人很快看到了一个套利机会。

d: n. 套汇，套利；仲裁（旧义）
v. 从事套利，进行套利交易

e.en: The past is the time before the present, and the things that have happened.

ex.en: In the past, about a third of the babies born to women with diabetes died.
ex.zh: 在过去，患有糖尿病的妇女生的婴儿中大约有三分之一都死了。

e.en: If you accuse someone of living in the past, you mean that they think too much about the past or believe that things are the same as they were in the past.

ex.en: What was the point in living in the past, thinking about what had or had not happened?
ex.zh: 活在过去有什么意义，思考已经发生的或者没有发生的事情？

e.en: Your past consists of all the things that you have done or that have happened to you.

ex.en: ...revelations about his past.
ex.zh: …关于他的过往经历的揭露。

e.en: Past events and things happened or existed before the present time.

ex.en: I knew from past experience that alternative therapies could help.
ex.zh: 我知道根据以前的经验其他的治疗方法可能有效。

ex.en: ...a return to the turbulence of past centuries.
ex.zh: …回到过去几个中世纪的动荡。

d: adj. 过去的，昔日的；刚过去的，刚结束的；完成的，结束的；（语法）过去时的
n. 过去，昔日（the past）；往事，经历；（语法）过去时，（动词的）过去式（the past）
prep. 晚于，在…...之后；在…...的更远处；经过，越过；超出，超过
adv. 从一侧到另一侧，经过；（时间）过去，逝去

e.en: If you spread something somewhere, you open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

ex.en: She spread a towel on the sand and lay on it.
ex.zh: 她把一块浴巾铺在沙地上，然后躺在上面。

e.en: Spread out means the same as . 铺开 (同)(spread)

ex.en: He extracted several glossy prints and spread them out on a low coffee table.
ex.zh: 他抽出几张光面照片铺在一张矮咖啡桌上。

e.en: If you spread your arms, hands, fingers, or legs, you stretch them out until they are far apart. 伸展开 (手臂、手、手指、腿等)

ex.en: Sitting on the floor, spread your legs as far as they will go without overstretching.
ex.zh: 坐在地板上，尽可能分开双腿，但不要过度拉伸。

e.en: Spread out means the same as .

ex.en: David made a gesture, spreading out his hands as if he were showing that he had no explanation to make.
ex.zh: 大卫做了个手势，双手一摊，似乎表示他没有什么可解释的。

d: v. 展开，打开；张开，伸开（手臂、手指、腿）；扩散，蔓延；传播，传染；散布，（使）流传；（人，动物，植物）分布，分散开来；撒，散播；传递；（脸上）露出，渐渐表现出；涂，敷；分摊，分配；延伸，伸展，扩张；分散（于某一时段内），分期还清（债务）；分散（风险）
n. 扩散，蔓延；范围，幅度，种类；延展度，宽度，覆盖面；涂抹食品的酱类；盛宴，酒席；（尤指横贯两版的）文章，广告；床罩；大农场，大牧场；翼展；一大片；（两种价格或比率的）差额，差幅；（两支对抗的运动队之间比分的）差距；（物理，生理）点源能量传播
adj. 伸展的

e.en: When an accountant audits an organization's accounts, he or she examines the accounts officially in order to make sure that they have been done correctly.

ex.en: Each year they audit our accounts and certify them as being true and fair.
ex.zh: 每年他们都会审核我们的账目，以证明其准确合理。

e.en: Audit is also a noun.

ex.en: The bank first learned of the problem when it carried out an internal audit.
ex.zh: 银行是在进行内部审计时最先得知这个问题的。

d: n. 审计，查……的账目；审查，审核；审计报告
v. 审计，查账；旁听

e.en: An awkward situation is embarrassing and difficult to deal with.

ex.en: I was the first to ask him awkward questions but there'll be harder ones to come.
ex.zh: 我是第一个问他尴尬问题的人，但后面还会有更棘手的问题。

e.en: 令人尴尬地

ex.en: There was an awkwardly long silence.
ex.zh: 有一段令人尴尬的长时间的沉默。

e.en: Something that is awkward to use or carry is difficult to use or carry because of its design. A job that is awkward is difficult to do. (使用) 不便的; 棘手的 (工作)

ex.en: It was small but heavy enough to make it awkward to carry.
ex.zh: 它虽然小，却沉重得不便携带。

e.en: 不便地;

ex.en: The front window switches are awkwardly placed on the dashboard.
ex.zh: 前窗的开关安装在仪表板上，使用不便。

d: adj. 令人尴尬的，使人难堪的；难对付的，难处理的；局促不安的；不方便的；笨拙的，不雅观的；不舒适的

e.en: The way that you behave is the way that you do and say things, and the things that you do and say. 行为;

ex.en: I couldn't believe these people were behaving in this way.
ex.zh: 我无法相信这些人竟这样行事。

e.en: If you behave or behave yourself, you act in the way that people think is correct and proper. 使…规矩;

ex.en: You have to behave.
ex.zh: 你得守规矩。

e.en: In science, the way that something behaves is the things that it does. (科学领域)

ex.en: Under certain conditions, electrons can behave like waves rather than particles.
ex.zh: 在某些条件下，电子能像波而不是粒子那样运动。

d: v. 行为，表现；守规矩，举止得体；起反应，起作用（behave 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Begun is the past participle of . (begin)

d: v. 开始（begin 的过去分词）
n. （Begun）人名；（俄）别贡；（英）贝根

e.en: If something belongs to you, you own it.

ex.en: The house had belonged to her family for three or four generations.
ex.zh: 这座房子属于她家已有三四代了。

e.en: You say that something belongs to a particular person when you are guessing, discovering, or explaining that it was produced by or is part of that person. (某人) 所做;

ex.en: The handwriting belongs to a male.
ex.zh: 这笔迹出自一名男子之手。

e.en: If someone belongs to a particular group, they are a member of that group.

ex.en: I used to belong to a youth club.
ex.zh: 我曾是一个青年俱乐部的成员。

e.en: If something or someone belongs in or to a particular category, type, or group, they are of that category, type, or group. 属 (某一类别、类型、群)

ex.en: The judges could not decide which category it belonged in.
ex.zh: 法官们无法决定它属于哪一类别。

d: v. 应在……地方，应处于……状况；适应，合得来；归……所有；是……的成员，属于（某团体或组织）；居住

e.en: The way that you behave is the way that you do and say things, and the things that you do and say. 行为;

ex.en: I couldn't believe these people were behaving in this way.
ex.zh: 我无法相信这些人竟这样行事。

e.en: If you behave or behave yourself, you act in the way that people think is correct and proper. 使…规矩;

ex.en: You have to behave.
ex.zh: 你得守规矩。

e.en: In science, the way that something behaves is the things that it does. (科学领域)

ex.en: Under certain conditions, electrons can behave like waves rather than particles.
ex.zh: 在某些条件下，电子能像波而不是粒子那样运动。

d: v. 行为，表现；（科学或技术语境）起反应，起作用；守规矩，举止得体（behave 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. （与 well-、ill- 等副词连用构成复合形容词）有…行为的；守规矩的；（数学）良态的

e.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example, in the number of things that are being bought and sold. (经济)

ex.en: An economic boom followed, especially in housing and construction.
ex.zh: 接着是一个经济的繁荣，尤其在住房和建筑方面。

ex.en: The 1980s were indeed boom years.
ex.zh: 20世纪80年代确实是繁荣的时代。

e.en: A boom in something is an increase in its amount, frequency, or success.

ex.en: The boom in the sport's popularity has meant more calls for stricter safety regulations.
ex.zh: 该项运动普及程度的大幅提高带来了更多要求更严格安全法规的呼声。

e.en: If the economy or a business is booming, the number of things being bought or sold is increasing.

ex.en: By 1988 the economy was booming.
ex.zh: 到1988年为止经济一直很繁荣。

ex.en: Sales are booming.
ex.zh: 销售量在激增。

e.en: When something such as someone's voice, a cannon, or a big drum booms, it makes a loud, deep sound that lasts for several seconds.

ex.en: "Ladies," boomed Helena, without a microphone, "we all know why we're here tonight."
ex.zh: “女士们”，海伦娜没用话筒朗声说道，“我们都知道今晚我们为什么在这儿。”

ex.en: Thunder boomed over Crooked Mountain.
ex.zh: 雷声在克鲁克德山上空轰鸣。

d: n. 繁荣；流行，风靡；隆隆声；吊杆；帆桁；水栅
v. 迅速发展，繁荣；轰鸣，轰响；用低沉的声音说
【名】 （Boom）（英、美、荷、俄、比、德）博姆（人名）

e.en: If you buy something, you obtain it by paying money for it.

ex.en: He could not afford to buy a house.
ex.zh: 他买不起房子。

ex.en: Lizzie bought herself a mountain bike.
ex.zh: 莉齐给自己买了一辆山地自行车。

e.en: If you talk about the quantity or standard of goods an amount of money buys, you are referring to the price of the goods or the value of the money.

ex.en: About $70,000 buys a habitable house.
ex.zh: 大约七万美元才买得到一栋适合居住的房子。

e.en: If you buy something like time, freedom, or victory, you obtain it but only by offering or giving up something in return.

ex.en: It was a risky operation, but might buy more time.
ex.zh: 这是一项冒险的举动，但也许能换得更多的时间。

e.en: If you say that a person can be bought, you are criticizing the fact that they will give their help or loyalty to someone in return for money.

ex.en: Any number of our military and government officials can be bought.
ex.zh: 我们的军官和政府官员中有许多可以被收买。

d: vt. 购买；（金钱）买得到，足够购买；获得，换取，争取；收买，贿赂；相信，接受（buy 的第三人称单数）
vi. 买，采购（buy 的第三人称单数）
n. 购买，买卖；所购的物品；合算的东西，划算的买卖（buy 的复数）
n. 加利福尼亚（美国一个州）

e.en: Business is work relating to the production, buying, and selling of goods or services.

ex.en: Jennifer has an impressive academic and business background.
ex.zh: 詹妮弗有着了不起的学术和商业背景。

ex.en: ...Harvard Business School.
ex.zh: …哈佛商学院。

e.en: Business is used when talking about how many products or services a company is able to sell. If business is good, a lot of products or services are being sold and if business is bad, few of them are being sold.

ex.en: They worried that German companies would lose business.
ex.zh: 他们担心德国公司会失去生意。

e.en: A business is an organization that produces and sells goods or that provides a service.

ex.en: The company was a family business.
ex.zh: 这家公司是一个家族企业。

ex.en: The majority of small businesses fail within the first twenty-four months.
ex.zh: 大多数小企业在最初的两年内倒闭。

e.en: Business is work or some other activity that you do as part of your job and not for pleasure.

ex.en: I'm here on business.
ex.zh: 我在这里出差。

ex.en: You can't mix business with pleasure.
ex.zh: 你不能把工作和娱乐混在一起。

d: n. 商业，买卖，生意；商务，公事；公司，企业；行业，职业；事务，职责；私事；事情；（顾客对商店的）惠顾；系列事件

e.en: If you capture someone or something, you catch them, especially in a war. 俘虏;

ex.en: The guerrillas shot down one aeroplane and captured the pilot.
ex.zh: 那些游击队员击落了一架飞机，并俘虏了飞行员。

e.en: Capture is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the final battles which led to the army's capture of the town.
ex.zh: …部队夺取该镇的最后几场战斗。

e.en: If something or someone captures a particular quality, feeling, or atmosphere, they represent or express it successfully.

ex.en: Chef Idris Caldora offers an inspired menu that captures the spirit of the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: 伊德里斯·卡尔多拉厨师的菜单很有创意，充分体现了地中海风情。

e.en: If something captures your attention or imagination, you begin to be interested or excited by it. If someone or something captures your heart, you begin to love them or like them very much.

ex.en: ...the great names of the past who usually capture the historian's attention.
ex.zh: …那些常常为史学家所关注的伟人们。

d: v. 俘获，捕获；夺取，占领；吸引，引起；记录，体现；拍摄，录制（capture 的现在分词）
n. 同类相食；（商业）市场蚕食，指企业的新产品、新服务或新渠道削弱并分流其自身原有产品、服务或渠道的销售；（机械维修）拆用旧件，指从旧设备或损坏设备上取用可用零件来维修其他设备
adj. cheap 的比较级：成本更低，更便宜的

e.en: A code is a set of rules about how people should behave or about how something must be done. 法典;

ex.en: ...Article 159 of the state's penal code.
ex.zh: …该国刑法第159条。

e.en: A code is a system of replacing the words in a message with other words or symbols, so that nobody can understand it unless they know the system. 密码;

ex.en: They used elaborate secret codes, as when the names of trees stood for letters.
ex.zh: 他们用的是精心设计的密码，用树木的名称代表字母。

e.en: A code is a group of numbers or letters which is used to identify something, such as a mailing address or part of a telephone system.

ex.en: Callers dialling the wrong area code will not get through.
ex.zh: 打电话的人拨错区号时电话就接不通。

e.en: A code is any system of signs or symbols that has a meaning.

ex.en: It will need other chips to reconvert the digital code back into normal TV signals.
ex.zh: 需要用其他芯片把数字代码重新转换成普通的电视信号。

d: n. 密码，暗码；（邮政）编码，（电话）区号；（计算机）编码；道德准则，行为规范；法典，法规
v. 把……编码（或编号）；把……译成密码；（给计算机）编写指令
【名】 （Code）（英、法、西）科德（人名）

e.en: A century is a period of a hundred years that is used when stating a date. For example, the 19th century was the period from 1801 to 1900.

ex.en: The material position of the Church had been declining since the late eighteenth century.
ex.zh: 自18世纪晚期以来，教堂的世俗地位一直在下降。

e.en: A century is any period of a hundred years.

ex.en: The drought there is the worst in a century.
ex.zh: 那里的旱情百年不遇。

d: n. 世纪；一百年；（板球）一百分

e.en: Someone who is cautious acts very carefully in order to avoid possible danger.

ex.en: The scientists are cautious about using enzyme therapy on humans.
ex.zh: 科学家们对于人体使用酶疗法持谨慎态度。

e.en: 谨慎地

ex.en: David moved cautiously forward and looked over the edge.
ex.zh: 大卫小心翼翼地向前移动，视线越过边缘看过去。

d: adj. 小心的，谨慎的

e.en: Goods or services that are cheap cost less money than usual or than you expected.

ex.en: I'm going to live off campus if I can find somewhere cheap enough.
ex.zh: 如果我能找到一个足够便宜的地方，我打算住在校外。

ex.en: Operating costs are coming down because of cheaper fuel.
ex.zh: 经营成本在下降是因为燃料更便宜了。

e.en: 便宜地

ex.en: It will produce electricity more cheaply than a nuclear plant.
ex.zh: 它将以比核电厂更低廉的成本生产电力。

e.en: If you describe goods as cheap, you mean they cost less money than similar products but their quality is poor.

ex.en: Don't resort to cheap imitations; save up for the real thing.
ex.zh: 不要买价廉质劣的赝品，把钱存起来买真货。

e.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as cheap, you mean that they are unkindly or insincerely using a situation to benefit themselves or to harm someone else.

ex.en: These tests will inevitably be used by politicians to make cheap political points.
ex.zh: 这些测试难免会被政客们利用以炮制损人利己的政治观点。

d: adj. 便宜的，廉价的；价低质劣的；小气的，吝啬的；卑劣的，可耻的；无足轻重的；简单的，容易获取的
adv. 低价地，便宜地

e.en: If a piece of furniture or an item of clothing is comfortable, it makes you feel physically relaxed when you use it, for example because it is soft.

ex.en: ...a comfortable fireside chair.
ex.zh: …一把令人舒服的炉边椅子。

e.en: If a building or room is comfortable, it makes you feel physically relaxed when you spend time in it, for example because it is warm and has nice furniture.

ex.en: A home should be comfortable and friendly.
ex.zh: 家应使人感到舒适与和睦。

e.en: 令人舒适地

ex.en: ...the comfortably furnished living room.
ex.zh: …布置舒适的起居室。

e.en: If you are comfortable, you are physically relaxed because of the place or position you are sitting or lying in.

ex.en: Lie down on your bed and make yourself comfortable.
ex.zh: 躺在床上让你自己舒服些。

d: adj. 令人舒适的；感到舒服的，安逸的；自信的，自在的；富裕的，宽裕的；满意的；易取胜的，轻松领先的；（病、伤后）疼痛减缓的，状况良好的；足够的
n. 温暖的盖被

e.en: Compressed air or gas is squeezed into a small space or container and is therefore at a higher pressure than normal. It is used especially as a source of power for machines.

d: adj. 压缩的，被压缩的；精简的，浓缩的；（生物学）扁的，侧扁的
v. （被）压紧，压缩；精简，浓缩；压缩（文件等）；压缩声音信号的动态范围（compress 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The consequences of something are the results or effects of it. 结果;

ex.en: Her lawyer said she understood the consequences of her actions and was prepared to go to jail.
ex.zh: 她的律师说她明白自己行为的后果并准备去坐牢。

e.en: If one thing happens and then another thing happens in consequence or as a consequence, the second thing happens as a result of the first.

ex.en: His death was totally unexpected and, in consequence, no plans had been made for his replacement.
ex.zh: 他的死纯粹出乎意料，因此还没有为他的替代人定出计划。

ex.en: Maternity services were to be reduced as a consequence of falling birth rates.
ex.zh: 孕产服务因下降的出生率而将被削减。

d: n. 结果，后果；重要性，价值

e.en: Concrete is a substance used for building which is made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones, and water.

ex.en: The posts have to be set in concrete.
ex.zh: 这些柱子必须固定在混凝土中。

ex.en: We sat on the concrete floor.
ex.zh: 我们坐在混凝土地板上。

e.en: When you concrete something such as a path, you cover it with concrete. 给 (道路等)

ex.en: He merely cleared and concreted the floors.
ex.zh: 他只是清理了地板并浇上了混凝土。

e.en: You use concrete to indicate that something is definite and specific.

ex.en: I had no concrete evidence.
ex.zh: 我当时没有明确而具体的证据。

ex.en: There were no concrete proposals on the table.
ex.zh: 没有提交讨论的具体提议。

e.en: A concrete object is a real, physical object.

ex.en: ...using concrete objects to teach addition and subtraction.
ex.zh: …用实物教加减运算。

d: adj. 确实的，具体的；实在的，有形的；混凝土的；物质的
n. 混凝土
v. 用混凝土覆盖（或做成）；（使）凝固，（使）凝结；使真实（化），使具体（化）

e.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

ex.en: ...in-depth coverage of today's complex issues.
ex.zh: …对当今复杂问题的深入报道。

ex.en: ...a complex system of voting.
ex.zh: …一套复杂的选举体制。

e.en: A complex is a group of buildings designed for a particular purpose, or one large building divided into several smaller areas.

ex.en: ...a low-cost apartment complex.
ex.zh: …一个低价公寓楼群。

d: adj. 复杂的，难懂的；组合的，合成的；（句子）复合的；复数的，复的；配合的，络合的
n. 综合大楼，建筑群；复合体，综合体；情结；强烈（或过度）的关心（或忧虑）；配合物，络合物
adv. 在计算上，从计算方面来讲

e.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

ex.en: Their decision to abandon the trip was made because of financial constraints.
ex.zh: 他们放弃这次旅行的决定是因财务限制而作出的。

e.en: Constraint is control over the way you behave which prevents you from doing what you want to do.

ex.en: Journalists were given the freedom to visit, investigate, and report without constraint.
ex.zh: 新闻记者被赋予在没有约束下参观、调查和报道的自由。

d: n. 限制，束缚；克制，拘束

e.en: Delivery or a delivery is the bringing of letters, packages, or other goods to someone's house or to another place where they want them.

ex.en: Please allow 28 days for delivery.
ex.zh: 请留出28天的递送时间。

ex.en: The uprising is threatening the delivery of humanitarian supplies of food and medicine.
ex.zh: 这场暴乱正威胁到食物和药品等人道主义物资的运送。

e.en: Delivery is the process of giving birth to a baby.

ex.en: In the end, it was an easy delivery: a fine baby boy.
ex.zh: 最终，分娩顺利——一个健康的男婴。

e.en: A delivery of something is the goods that are delivered.

ex.en: I got a delivery of fresh eggs this morning.
ex.zh: 今天早上我收到了一批新鲜鸡蛋。

e.en: A delivery person or service delivers things to a place.

ex.en: ...a pizza delivery man.
ex.zh: …一个送比萨饼的男子。

d: n. 递送，投递；递送物；演讲风格，演说方式；分娩，生产；投球方式
adj. 运送的

e.en: A dependency is a country which is controlled by another country.

ex.en: ...the tiny British dependency of Montserrat in the eastern Caribbean.
ex.zh: …东加勒比地区英国的小附属国蒙特塞拉特岛。

e.en: You talk about someone's dependency when they have a deep emotional, physical, or financial need for a particular person or thing, especially one that you consider excessive or undesirable.

ex.en: We saw his dependency on his mother and worried that he might not survive long if anything happened to her.
ex.zh: 我们看到他对母亲的依赖，担心万一她有个闪失，他也会活不长。

e.en: If you talk about alcohol dependency or chemical dependency, you are referring to a situation where someone is an alcoholic or is addicted to drugs. (毒、酒)

ex.en: In 1985, he began to show signs of alcohol and drug dependency.
ex.zh: 1985年，他开始表现出酗酒和吸毒成瘾的迹象。

d: n. 依赖，依靠，从属；属国，附属国，属地；从属物；（多用于美式英语）（对药物、酒精等的）成瘾，依赖；（计算机软件）依赖项或依赖关系

e.en: If a particular factor determines the nature of a thing or event, it causes it to be of a particular kind.

ex.en: The size of the chicken pieces will determine the cooking time.
ex.zh: 鸡块的大小决定烹饪时间。

e.en: 决定

ex.en: ...the gene which is responsible for male sex determination.
ex.zh: …决定男性性别的基因。

e.en: To determine a fact means to discover it as a result of investigation.

ex.en: The investigation will determine what really happened.
ex.zh: 该调查将查明真相。

ex.en: Experts say testing needs to be done on each contaminant to determine the long-term effects on humans.
ex.zh: 专家说需要对每种污染物进行测试，以查明对人类的长期影响。

e.en: If you determine something, you decide about it or settle it.

ex.en: The Baltic people have a right to determine their own future.
ex.zh: 波罗的海人民有权决定他们自己的未来。

d: v. determine 的一般现在时第三人称单数形式；决定，支配，控制；查明，确定，测定；下定决心（后接不定式）

e.en: A contest is a competition or game that people try to win. 竞赛;

ex.en: Few contests in the recent history of boxing have been as thrilling.
ex.zh: 在近期拳击史上没有几场比赛曾如此惊心动魄。

e.en: A contest is a struggle to win power or control.

ex.en: The state election in November will be the last such ballot before next year's presidential contest.
ex.zh: 11月的州选举将是明年的总统竞选前最后一轮这类投票。

e.en: If you contest a statement or decision, you object to it formally because you think it is wrong or unreasonable.

ex.en: Your former employer has to reply within 14 days in order to contest the case.
ex.zh: 你的前雇主得在14天内做出答复以对本案提出抗辩。

e.en: If someone contests an election or competition, they take part in it and try to win it. 参加 (竞选或比赛)

ex.en: He quickly won his party's nomination to contest the elections.
ex.zh: 他迅速赢得了其党派的提名来参加竞选。

d: n. 比赛，竞赛；争夺，竞争；争论，争执
v. 争辩，提出异议；争取赢得，角逐

e.en: When someone designs a garment, building, machine, or other object, they plan it and make a detailed drawing of it from which it can be built or made.

ex.en: They wanted to design a machine that was both attractive and practical.
ex.zh: 他们想设计一台既美观又实用的机器。

e.en: When someone designs a survey, policy, or system, they plan and prepare it, and decide on all the details of it.

ex.en: We may be able to design a course to suit your particular needs.
ex.zh: 我们也许能策划一个课程来满足你的特定需求。

e.en: Design is the process and art of planning and making detailed drawings of something.

ex.en: He was a born mechanic with a flair for design.
ex.zh: 他天生是个有设计才华的机械师。

e.en: The design of something is the way in which it has been planned and made.

ex.en: ...a new design of clock.
ex.zh: …一种新款时钟。

d: v. 设计；计划（design 的过去式和过去分词）；be designed to/for 旨在，为…而设计
adj. 精心设计的；有计划的；故意的

e.en: A direction is the general line that someone or something is moving or pointing in.

ex.en: St. Andrews was ten miles in the opposite direction.
ex.zh: 圣安德鲁斯在相反方向的10英里处。

ex.en: He got into Margie's car and swung out onto the road in the direction of Larry's shop.
ex.zh: 他钻进玛吉的汽车，摇晃着开上马路，朝拉里商店的方向驶去。

e.en: A direction is the general way in which something develops or progresses.

ex.en: They threatened to lead a mass walk-out if the party did not sharply change direction.
ex.zh: 他们威胁说，如果该党对其发展方向不作大的调整，他们就发动大家集体退党。

e.en: Directions are instructions that tell you what to do, how to do something, or how to get somewhere. 说明书; (指示路线的)

ex.en: I should know by now not to throw away the directions until we've finished cooking.
ex.zh: 我现在应该明白，饭没做完之前，不要把食谱扔掉。

d: n. 方向，方位；趋势，动向；指示，说明；目标；方面；管理，指导；导演

e.en: If you discover something that you did not know about before, you become aware of it or learn of it.

ex.en: She discovered that they'd escaped.
ex.zh: 她发觉他们已经逃走了。

ex.en: It was difficult for the inspectors to discover which documents were important and which were not.
ex.zh: 检查员们难以发现哪些文件重要，哪些不重要。

e.en: If a person or thing is discovered, someone finds them, either by accident or because they have been looking for them. 发现;

ex.en: A few days later his badly beaten body was discovered on a roadside outside the city.
ex.zh: 几天之后，他曾被毒打的尸体在城外一个路边被发现了。

e.en: When someone discovers a new place, substance, scientific fact, or scientific technique, they are the first person to find it or become aware of it. (首次)

ex.en: ...the first European to discover America.
ex.zh: …第1个发现美洲的欧洲人。

e.en: When an actor, musician, or other performer who is not well known is discovered, someone recognizes that they have talent and helps them in their career. 发现 (人才)

ex.en: The Beatles were discovered in the early 1960s.
ex.zh: 披头士乐队是在20世纪60年代初期被发现的。

d: v. 发现，找到，发觉（discover 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已被发现或经观察确定的；（古旧或戏剧用语）被揭开而显露的

e.en: An engineer is a person who uses scientific knowledge to design, construct, and maintain engines and machines or structures such as roads, railroads, and bridges.
An engineer is a person who repairs mechanical or electrical devices.

ex.en: They send a service engineer to fix the disk drive.
ex.zh: 他们派一位维修师来修理磁盘驱动器。

e.en: An engineer is a person who is responsible for maintaining the engine of a ship while it is at sea.
When a vehicle, bridge, or building is engineered, it is planned and constructed using scientific methods.

ex.en: Its spaceship was engineered by Bert Rutan, renowned for designing the Voyager.
ex.zh: 它的飞船由伯特·鲁坦设计建造，此人因设计“旅行者”号飞船而闻名。

d: n. 工程师（engineer 的复数）；机械师，维修技师（engineer 的复数）
v. 设计，建造（engineer 的第三人称单数形式）；策划，谋划（engineer 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Enough means as much as you need or as much as is necessary.

ex.en: They had enough cash for a one-way ticket.
ex.zh: 他们有足够的现金买一张单程票。

e.en: Enough is also an adverb.

ex.en: I was old enough to work and earn money.
ex.zh: 我到了可以工作、挣钱的年龄了。

ex.en: Do you believe that sentences for criminals are tough enough at present?
ex.zh: 你认为对犯罪分子目前的刑罚足够严厉吗？

e.en: Enough is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Although the police say efforts are being made, they are not doing enough.
ex.zh: 尽管警方说他们正在努力，但是他们做得还不够。

e.en: Enough is also a quantifier.

ex.en: All parents worry about whether their child is getting enough of the right foods.
ex.zh: 所有父母都担心他们的孩子是否得到足够量的恰当的食物。

d: adj. 充足的，足够的
pron. 足够，充分
adv. 充分地，足够地；相当，很；说来奇怪，说起来有趣（strangely/interestingly enough）
n. 足够的（数目或数量），充分

e.en: Entirely means completely and not just partly.

ex.en: ...an entirely new approach.
ex.zh: …一种全新的方法。

ex.en: Their price depended almost entirely on their scarcity.
ex.zh: 他们的价格几乎完全靠他们的供不应求。

e.en: Entirely is also used to emphasize what you are saying.

ex.en: I agree entirely.
ex.zh: 我完全赞同。

d: adv. 完全地，完整地；仅仅，只

e.en: If you earn money, you receive money in return for work that you do. 挣 (钱)

ex.en: What a lovely way to earn a living.
ex.zh: 一个多好的谋生方式啊！

e.en: If something earns money, it produces money as profit or interest. 赢 (利)

ex.en: ...a bank account that earns little or no interest.
ex.zh: …一个很少或不生利息的银行账户。

e.en: If you earn something such as praise, you get it because you deserve it.

ex.en: Companies must earn a reputation for honesty.
ex.zh: 公司必须赢得诚信。

d: v. （earn 的第三人称单数形式）赚得，挣得：通过工作或提供服务获得金钱或报酬；获得，赢得：通过努力或表现获得成果、荣誉或认可；赢利，生息：（资金、账户或公司等）产生利润、利息或收入。

e.en: When someone drowns or is drowned, they die because they have gone or been pushed under water and cannot breathe.

ex.en: A child can drown in only a few inches of water.
ex.zh: 儿童在仅仅几英寸深的水中就能溺死。

ex.en: Last night a boy was drowned in the river.
ex.zh: 昨晚一名男孩在那条河里溺水身亡。

e.en: If you say that a person or thing is drowning in something, you are emphasizing that they have a very large amount of it, or are completely covered in it.

ex.en: ...people who gradually find themselves drowning in debt.
ex.zh: …逐渐发现自己深陷债务的人们。

e.en: If something drowns a sound, it is so loud that you cannot hear that sound properly. (一声音) 盖过 (另一声音)

ex.en: Clapping drowned the speaker's words for a moment.
ex.zh: 掌声盖过了发言人的说话声有一阵儿。

e.en: Drown out means the same as drown. 淹没 (同drown)

ex.en: Their cheers drowned out the protests of demonstrators.
ex.zh: 他们的欢呼声淹没了示威者的抗议。

d: v. drown 的现在分词：（使）溺死；（医学）淹溺；淹没，浸没；（声音）盖过（常作 drown out）
n. 溺死，溺水，淹溺
adj. 溺水的，正在溺水的

e.en: If something is expensive, it costs a lot of money.

ex.en: Broadband is still more expensive than dial-up services.
ex.zh: 宽带还是要比拨号服务费钱得多。

e.en: 昂贵地

ex.en: She was expensively dressed, with fine furs and jewels.
ex.zh: 她衣饰奢华，穿戴着上好的毛皮和珠宝。

d: adj. 花钱多的，昂贵的；（错误或决定）代价高的

e.en: Fallen is the past participle of . (fall)

d: adj. 倒下的，落下的；（士兵）阵亡的；（基督教中指人或天使）堕落的；（女子）失贞的
v. 降落，落下；跌倒，倒塌；（水平、数量、价格等）下跌，减少（fall 的过去分词）
adj. 更快的
adv. 更快地
n. 禁食者，斋戒者；（Faster）（俄、美）法斯特（人名）

e.en: If you flatten something or if it flattens, it becomes flat or flatter. 使变平;

ex.en: He carefully flattened the wrappers and put them between the leaves of his book.
ex.zh: 他小心翼翼地弄平包装纸，把它们夹在书页里。

ex.en: The dog's ears flattened slightly as Cook spoke his name.
ex.zh: 当库克叫狗的名字时，狗的耳朵稍稍耷拉了下来。

e.en: Flatten out means the same as . 使变平;

ex.en: The hills flattened out just south of the mountain.
ex.zh: 在山的南边丘陵就变得平坦起来。

e.en: To flatten something such as a building, town, or plant means to destroy it by knocking it down or crushing it. 夷平 (建筑物、城镇或植物)

ex.en: ...explosives capable of flattening a five-storey building.
ex.zh: …足以把一幢5层建筑夷为平地的炸药。

ex.en: ...bombing raids flattened much of the area.
ex.zh: …空袭把该地区的许多地方夷为平地。

e.en: If you flatten yourself against something, you press yourself flat against it, for example, to avoid getting in the way or being seen. 使自己贴着 (以免挡道或被看见)

ex.en: He flattened himself against a brick wall as I passed.
ex.zh: 我经过的时候，他紧贴着一堵砖墙站着。

d: adj. 被压平的，扁平的；没精打采的，垂头丧气的
v. （flatten 的过去式和过去分词）使变平，弄平，平整；变平，趋平；夷平，击倒，打倒；彻底击败，打得落花流水（flatten oneself against 指紧贴）

e.en: A fleet is a group of ships organized to do something together, for example, to fight battles or to catch fish. 舰队;

ex.en: A fleet sailed for New South Wales to establish the first European settlement in Australia.
ex.zh: 一支舰队驶向新南威尔士去建立欧洲在澳大利亚的第一个移民地。

e.en: A fleet of vehicles is a group of them, especially when they all belong to a particular organization or business, or when they are all going somewhere together.

ex.en: With its own fleet of trucks, the company delivers most orders overnight.
ex.zh: 因为有自己的运输车队，该公司的大部分订货可以第二天就送到。

e.en: rapid in movement; swift

d: n. 船队，舰队；（某家公司控制的）车队；小湾，水道
adj. 快速的；快速的；（水）浅的
adv. 浅，不深地
v. 疾驰，飞逝

e.en: A fierce animal or person is very aggressive or angry. 凶猛的;

ex.en: They look like the teeth of some fierce animal.
ex.zh: 它们看上去像是某种猛兽的牙齿。

e.en: 凶猛地;

ex.en: "I don't know," she said fiercely.
ex.zh: “我不知道。”她非常愤怒地说。

e.en: Fierce feelings or actions are very intense or enthusiastic, or involve great activity. 激烈的;

ex.en: Consumers have a wide array of choices and price competition is fierce.
ex.zh: 消费者的选择面很广，价格竞争也很激烈。

ex.en: The town was captured after a fierce battle with rebels.
ex.zh: 与叛军的一场激战后，这个城市被占领了。

e.en: 激烈地;

ex.en: He has always been ambitious and fiercely competitive.
ex.zh: 他一直都野心勃勃，极其争强好斗。

d: adj. （动作或情感）强烈的，激烈的；（人或动物）凶猛的，狂怒的；（天气等）狂暴的，恶劣的
adv. 很，非常
【名】 （Fierce）（英）菲尔斯（人名）

e.en: If a liquid, gas, or electrical current flows somewhere, it moves there steadily and continuously.

ex.en: A stream flowed gently down into the valley.
ex.zh: 一条小溪缓缓地流进山谷。

ex.en: The current flows into electric motors that drive the wheels.
ex.zh: 电流流进电机，驱动轮子。

e.en: Flow is also a noun.

ex.en: It works only in the veins, where the blood flow is slower.
ex.zh: 它只在血液流动较缓的静脉中起作用。

e.en: If a number of people or things flow from one place to another, they move there steadily in large groups, usually without stopping. (大量人或物)

ex.en: Large numbers of refugees continue to flow from the troubled region into the no-man's land.
ex.zh: 大批的难民持续从骚乱地区涌进无人区。

e.en: Flow is also a noun.

ex.en: She watched the frantic flow of cars and buses along the street.
ex.zh: 她注视着街道上川流不息的小车和巴士。

d: v. flow 的过去式和过去分词：（液体、气体、电流等）流动，流出；（人群、车流等）大量移动，川流不息；（信息、资金等）流通，传播；（头发、衣物等）垂下，飘拂

e.en: Found is the past tense and past participle of . find
When an institution, company, or organization is founded by someone or by a group of people, they get it started, often by providing the necessary money.

ex.en: The New York Free-Loan Society was founded in 1892.
ex.zh: 纽约无息贷款协会成立于1892年。

ex.en: His father founded the American Socialist Party.
ex.zh: 他的父亲创建了美国社会党。

e.en: 成立

ex.en: ...the foundation of the National Association of Evangelicals in 1942.
ex.zh: …1942年全国福音协会的成立。

e.en: When a town, important building, or other place is founded by someone or by a group of people, they cause it to be built.

ex.en: The town was founded in 1610.
ex.zh: 该城镇兴建于1610年。

d: v. 创办，成立；建造，兴建；根据，以……为基础；熔铸，铸造
adj. 偶然（或意外）发现的；（艺术）原汁原味的；装备好的；（用餐、供暖）不另外收费的
v. 找到，找回；发现，发觉；（经过研究）找出，查明（find 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A forecaster is someone who uses detailed knowledge about a particular activity in order to work out what they think will happen in that activity in the future.

ex.en: Some of the nation's top economic forecasters say the economic recovery is picking up speed.
ex.zh: 一些国家顶级经济预报员表示，经济回暖正在加速。

d: n. 预测者，预报员：预测未来事件或趋势的人，尤指气象预报员（forecaster 的复数）。

e.en: The frequency of an event is the number of times it happens during a particular period.

ex.en: The frequency of Kara's phone calls increased rapidly.
ex.zh: 卡拉打电话的频率迅速增加。

e.en: In physics, the frequency of a sound wave or a radio wave is the number of times it vibrates within a specified period of time. (物理学)

ex.en: You can't hear waves of such a high frequency.
ex.zh: 你听不到这么高频率的声波。

ex.en: ...a frequency of 24 kilohertz.
ex.zh: …24千赫的频率。

d: n. 出现次数；频繁；频率

e.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

ex.en: The labour secretary said the reforms would generate new jobs.
ex.zh: 劳动部长说这些改革将带来新的工作。

e.en: To generate a form of energy or power means to produce it. 产生 (电等能量)

ex.en: The company, New England Electric, burns coal to generate power.
ex.zh: 新英格兰电力公司燃烧煤来发电。

d: v. 产生，引起

e.en: Gas is a substance like air that is neither liquid nor solid and burns easily. It is used as a fuel for cooking and heating.

ex.en: Coal is actually cheaper than gas.
ex.zh: 煤炭实际上比煤气便宜。

e.en: A gas is any substance that is neither liquid nor solid, for example oxygen or hydrogen.

ex.en: Helium is a very light gas.
ex.zh: 氦是一种很轻的气体。

e.en: Gas is a poisonous gas that can be used as a weapon.

ex.en: The problem was that the exhaust gases contain many toxins.
ex.zh: 问题是废气含有很多毒素。

e.en: Gas is the same as .

d: n. 气体；气体燃料；（手术）麻醉气；毒气，瓦斯；汽油；有趣的人（或事）；胀气，胃气
v. 用毒气杀死；闲聊，空谈
【名】 （Gas）（法、德、西）加斯（人名）

e.en: A generator is a machine which produces electricity.

ex.en: The house is far from water mains and electricity and relies on its own generators.
ex.zh: 这座房子远离自来水总管和供电网，依靠自备的发电机。

e.en: A generator of something is a person, organization, product, or situation which produces it or causes it to happen.

ex.en: The company has been a very good cash generator.
ex.zh: 这家公司是台非常出色的赚钱机器。

d: n. 发电机；产生者；电力公司；母点，母线，母面

e.en: To govern a place such as a country, or its people, means to be officially in charge of the place, and to have responsibility for making laws, managing the economy, and controlling public services.

ex.en: They go to the polls on Friday to choose the people they want to govern their country.
ex.zh: 他们周五去投票站选出他们希望来治理国家的人。

e.en: If a situation or activity is governed by a particular factor, rule, or force, it is controlled by that factor, rule, or force.

ex.en: Marine insurance is governed by a strict series of rules and regulations.
ex.zh: 海上保险受一系列严格的规章条例所制约。

d: v. 统治，管理；控制，影响；（语法）支配；可用来裁定（某案例）
【名】 （Govern）（英）戈文（人名）
n. 吉瓦，千兆瓦，十亿瓦特
格网比例尺；（测）方眼尺；电网规模

e.en: Half of a number, an amount, or an object is one of two equal parts that together make up the whole number, amount, or object.

ex.en: She wore a diamond ring worth half a million dollars.
ex.zh: 她戴了一枚价值50万美元的钻戒。

ex.en: More than half of all U.S. households are heated with natural gas.
ex.zh: 超过半数的美国家庭用天然气供暖。

e.en: Half is also a predeterminer.

ex.en: We just sat and talked for half an hour or so.
ex.zh: 我们只是坐着谈了半小时左右。

ex.en: They had only received half the money promised.
ex.zh: 他们只收到了一半当初承诺的钱。

e.en: Half is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...a half measure of fresh lemon juice.
ex.zh: …半量杯的新鲜柠檬汁。

e.en: You use half to say that something is only partly the case or happens to only a limited extent. 部分地;

ex.en: His eyes were half closed.
ex.zh: 他的双眼半闭着。

ex.en: His refrigerator frequently looked half empty.
ex.zh: 他的冰箱经常看上去有点儿空。

d: n. 一半，二分之一；半场，半局；（足球、橄榄球等的）中场队员；半品脱；儿童半票；半学年，一学期；（高尔夫）一穴击球得分与对手相等
pron. 一半；（时间）……点半（=half past）；大量，许多
det. 一半
adj. 一半的；不完整的，部分的

e.en: A grown man or woman is one who is fully developed and mature, both physically and mentally.

ex.en: Few women can understand a grown man's love of sports.
ex.zh: 很少有女人能够理解成年男人对运动的喜爱。

d: adj. 长大的，成年的
v. 成长，发育；改善；扩大，增加（grow 的过去分词）

e.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

ex.en: She had decided she must go on as usual, follow her normal routine, and hope and pray.
ex.zh: 她已决定自己必须一如既往地过下去，遵循自己的日常生活规律，同时心存希望并祈祷。

ex.en: He hesitates before leaving, almost as though he had been hoping for conversation.
ex.zh: 他离开前有些犹豫，好像希望跟人说些什么。

e.en: If you say that you cannot hope for something, or if you talk about the only thing that you can hope to get, you mean that you are in a bad situation, and there is very little chance of improving it.

ex.en: Things aren't ideal, but that's the best you can hope for.
ex.zh: 事情并不理想，但你只能指望这些了。

e.en: Hope is also a noun.

ex.en: The only hope for underdeveloped countries is to become, as far as possible, self-reliant.
ex.zh: 欠发达国家的惟一指望就是尽可能地做到自力更生。

e.en: Hope is a feeling of desire and expectation that things will go well in the future.

ex.en: Now that he has become president, many people once again have hope for genuine changes in the system.
ex.zh: 既然他已成为总统，许多人又一次寄期望于体制的真正改革。

ex.en: But Kevin hasn't given up hope of getting in shape.
ex.zh: 但是凯文仍没有放弃康复的希望。

d: v. 希望
n. 希望；期盼的东西，盼望的事；（发生好事的）可能性；被寄予希望的人（或物）；信赖感
【名】 （Hope）（美）奥普（人名）

e.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

ex.en: If the case succeeds, it is inevitable that other trials will follow.
ex.zh: 如果这场官司获胜，其他审判必将效法。

e.en: The inevitable is something that is inevitable.

ex.en: "It's just delaying the inevitable," he said.
ex.zh: “那只是拖延该发生的事罢了，”他说。

d: adj. 必然发生的，不可避免的；总会发生的，惯常的
n. 必然发生的事，不可避免的事

e.en: All the people in the world can be referred to as humanity.

ex.en: They face charges of committing crimes against humanity.
ex.zh: 他们面临犯有反人类罪的指控。

e.en: A person's humanity is their state of being a human being, rather than an animal or an object.

ex.en: He was under discussion and it made him feel deprived of his humanity.
ex.zh: 他受到议论，这使他觉得自己被剥夺了人格。

e.en: Humanity is the quality of being kind, thoughtful, and sympathetic toward others. 仁慈;

ex.en: Her speech showed great maturity and humanity.
ex.zh: 她的演讲表现出高度的成熟和博爱。

e.en: The humanities are the subjects such as history, philosophy, and literature which are concerned with human ideas and behaviour. (历史、哲学、文学等)

ex.en: The number of students majoring in the humanities has declined by about half.
ex.zh: 主修人文学科的学生数量已经下降了近一半。

d: n. 人类（总称）；人性，人的属性；人道，仁慈；（历史、哲学、文学等）人文学科

e.en: If you install a piece of equipment, you put it somewhere so that it is ready to be used.

ex.en: They had installed a new phone line in the apartment.
ex.zh: 他们在公寓里安装了一根新的电话线。

e.en: 安装

ex.en: Hundreds of lives could be saved if the installation of alarms was more widespread.
ex.zh: 如果警报器的安装范围更为广泛，成百上千人的生命就可能获救。

e.en: If someone is installed in a new job or important position, they are officially given the job or position, often in a special ceremony.

ex.en: A temporary government was installed.
ex.zh: 一届临时政府被正式任命。

ex.en: Professor Sawyer was formally installed as president last Thursday.
ex.zh: 上星期二，索耶教授被正式任命为校长。

e.en: 任命仪式;

ex.en: He sent a letter inviting Naomi to attend his installation as chief of his tribe.
ex.zh: 他给娜奥米寄了封信，邀请她来参加他就任部落酋长的仪式。

d: adj. 安装的，已装入的（installed capacity 装机容量）
vt. 安装（install 的过去式和过去分词）；正式任命（install 的过去式和过去分词，常用于被动语态，如 be installed as/in）

e.en: If you inspect something, you look at every part of it carefully in order to find out about it or check that it is all right. 检查;

ex.en: Elaine went outside to inspect the playing field.
ex.zh: 伊莱恩到外边去检查运动场。

e.en: 检查;

ex.en: "Excellent work," he said when he had completed his inspection of the painted doors.
ex.zh: “干得好，”他在检查完刷过油漆的门之后说道。

e.en: When an official inspects a place or a group of people, they visit it and check it carefully, for example, in order to find out whether regulations are being obeyed.

ex.en: The Public Utilities Commission inspects us once a year.
ex.zh: 公用设施委员会每年到我们这里视察一次。

e.en: 视察

ex.en: Officers making a routine inspection of the vessel found fifty kilograms of cocaine.
ex.zh: 对船只做例行检查的警官们发现了50公斤可卡因。

d: v. 检查，审视；检阅，视察；进行检查，进行视察

e.en: An installation is a place that contains equipment and machinery that are being used for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The building was turned into a secret military installation.
ex.zh: 该楼被改建成一个秘密军事设施处。

d: n. installation 的复数形式；安装，安装过程；装置，设备；设施，场所（常指军事、核能、工业等专用设施）；装置艺术作品

e.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

ex.en: ...financial institutions.
ex.zh: …金融机构。

e.en: An institution is a building where certain people are cared for, such as people who are mentally ill or children who have no parents.

ex.en: Larry has been in an institution since he was four.
ex.zh: 拉里从4岁起就在孤儿院生活。

e.en: An institution is a custom or system that is considered an important or typical feature of a particular society or group, usually because it has existed for a long time. 习俗;

ex.en: I believe in the institution of marriage.
ex.zh: 我相信婚姻制度。

e.en: The institution of a new system is the act of starting it or bringing it in.

ex.en: There was never an official institution of censorship in Albania.
ex.zh: 阿尔巴尼亚从来就没有正式建立过审查制度。

d: n. 机构，团体；社会收容机构；制度，习俗（institution 的复数）

e.en: An investor is a person or organization that buys securities or property in order to receive a profit.

ex.en: The main investor in the project is the French bank Credit National.
ex.zh: 该项目的主要投资方是法国国民信贷银行。

d: n. （经）投资者（investor 的复数），投资人，投资方

e.en: If you describe a decision, action, or idea as justified, you think it is reasonable and acceptable.

ex.en: In my opinion, the decision was wholly justified.
ex.zh: 在我看来，这个决定是完全合理的。

e.en: If you think that someone is justified in doing something, you think that their reasons for doing it are good and valid.

ex.en: He's absolutely justified in resigning. He was treated shamefully.
ex.zh: 他完全有理由辞职。他受了侮辱。

d: adj. 有正当理由的，有合理解释的；（页面文字）右侧/左侧对齐的；（在上帝的眼中）称义的，使有义的
v. 证明……正当；为（某人的行为）辩解；使齐行（justify 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: a person's ideas, knowledge, or understanding 想法; 知识;

ex.en: he did it according to his lights

e.en: the lungs, esp of sheep, bullocks, and pigs, used for feeding pets and occasionally in human food (供宠物食用，偶尔也给人吃的)

d: n. 灯、灯光、灯火（light 的复数）；（供食用的）家畜的肺脏；（according to one's lights）想法、知识、理解、判断标准；lights out：熄灯号、熄灯时间
v. 点亮、点燃、照亮（light 的第三人称单数）
磷酸铁锂：一种锂离子电池正极材料，具有高能量密度、长寿命、高安全性等特点，被广泛应用于电动汽车、储能系统等领域。

e.en: The work that you do for a living is the work that you do in order to earn the money that you need.

ex.en: Father never talked about what he did for a living.
ex.zh: 父亲从未谈起他是做什么来谋生的。

e.en: You use living when you are talking about the quality of people's daily lives.

ex.en: Olivia has always been a model of healthy living.
ex.zh: 奥利维亚一直是健康生活的榜样。

e.en: You use living to talk about the places where people relax when they are not working.

ex.en: The spacious living quarters were on the second floor.
ex.zh: 宽敞的起居间在二楼。

d: adj. 活着的，活的；在使用的，在实施的；居住的，起居的；（水）流淌不息的；活跃的；逼真的
n. 生计，收入；生活方式；活着的人（the living）；教区牧师的圣职（圣俸）
v. 居住；生活；生长；继续存在（live 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Living）（英）利文（人名）

e.en: A means of doing something is a method, instrument, or process which can be used to do it. Means is both the singular and the plural form for this use. 方法; 手段;

ex.en: The move is a means to fight crime.
ex.zh: 这个行动是打击犯罪的一种手段。

ex.en: The army had perfected the use of terror as a means of controlling the population.
ex.zh: 军队已经能很好地利用恐怖手段来控制这里的人们。

e.en: You can refer to the money that someone has as their means.

ex.en: ...a person of means.
ex.zh: …一个富有的人。

e.en: If you do something by means of a particular method, instrument, or process, you do it using that method, instrument, or process. 通过 (方法、手段或过程)

ex.en: This is a two-year course taught by means of lectures and seminars.
ex.zh: 这是一门通过讲座和研讨会形式讲授的两年制课程。

e.en: You can say "by all means" to tell someone that you are very willing to allow them to do something.

ex.en: "Can I come and have a look at your house?"—"Yes, by all means."
ex.zh: “我能过来看看你的房子吗？”—“可以，当然可以。”

d: n. 手段，方法；金钱
v. 意味着；表示……的意思，作……的解释；打算，意欲（mean 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A machine is a piece of equipment that uses electricity or an engine in order to do a particular kind of work.

ex.en: I put the coin in the machine and pulled the lever.
ex.zh: 我把硬币投进机器，然后拉了控制杆。

e.en: You can use machine to refer to a large and well-controlled system or organization.

ex.en: ...Nazi Germany's military machine.
ex.zh: …纳粹德国的军事机构。

e.en: If you machine something, you make it or work on it using a machine. 用机器制造;

ex.en: The material is machined in a factory.
ex.zh: 该材料在一家工厂用机器加工而成。

ex.en: ...machined brass zinc alloy gears.
ex.zh: …机器加工的黄铜锌合金齿轮。

d: n. 机器，机械（装置）；计算机，电脑；（组织的）核心机构，领导核心；车辆（常指摩托车）；效率高的人（或动物）；机械般工作的人；（投币式）自动售货机
v. 用机器制造（加工）；机器缝制，用缝纫机缝
【名】 （Machine）（意）马基内（人名）

e.en: A margin is the difference between two amounts, especially the difference in the number of votes or points between the winner and the loser in an election or other contest.

ex.en: They could end up with a 50-point winning margin.
ex.zh: 他们最后可能会以50点的优势获胜。

e.en: The margin of a written or printed page is the empty space at the side of the page.

ex.en: She added her comments in the margin.
ex.zh: 她在页边空白处加上了她的评语。

e.en: If there is a margin for something in a situation, there is some freedom to choose what to do or decide how to do it.

ex.en: The money is collected in a straightforward way with little margin for error.
ex.zh: 这笔钱是直接募集上来的, 几乎没有出错的余地。

e.en: The margin of a place or area is the extreme edge of it.

ex.en: ...the low coastal plain along the western margin.
ex.zh: …沿着西部边缘地带的低洼海岸平原。

d: n. 边际（margin 的复数）；利润，利润空间，利润率；页边空白，页边距；（选举、比赛等的）差额，领先幅度；边缘，边界；余地，余量，裕度；（金融）保证金；（社会中的）边缘地位
adj. 更脏的；更凌乱，更不整洁的；更难以处理的，更复杂棘手的；更令人厌烦的
n. （Messier）梅西耶（人名，尤指法国天文学家查尔斯·梅西耶）

e.en: Midday is twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.

ex.en: At midday everyone would go down to Reg's Café.
ex.zh: 中午每个人都去雷吉的小餐馆。

e.en: Midday is the middle part of the day, from late morning to early afternoon.

ex.en: People were beginning to tire in the midday heat.
ex.zh: 在中午的炎炎烈日下，人们开始感到疲劳。

d: n. 中午，正午

e.en: A millisecond is a unit of time equal to one thousandth of a second. 毫秒;

d: n. （计量）毫秒，即千分之一秒（millisecond 的复数形式，符号为 ms）

e.en: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the sum that you have in a bank account.

ex.en: A lot of the money that you pay at the movies goes back to the film distributors.
ex.zh: 你付给电影院的钱有很多又回到了电影发行人的手里。

ex.en: Players should be allowed to earn money from advertising.
ex.zh: 应该允许运动员拍广告挣钱。

e.en: Monies is used to refer to several separate sums of money that form part of a larger amount that is received or spent.

ex.en: We drew up a schedule of payments for the rest of the monies owed.
ex.zh: 我们制定了一个剩余欠款的还款计划。

e.en: If you say that someone has money to burn, you mean that they have more money than they need, or that they spend their money on things that you think are unnecessary. 有花不完的钱;

ex.en: He was a high-earning broker with money to burn.
ex.zh: 他是一个收入高得花不完的经纪人。

e.en: If you are in the money, you have a lot of money to spend.

ex.en: If you are one of the lucky callers chosen to play, you could be in the money.
ex.zh: 如果你是一个幸运打进电话的人，且被选中参赛，你就可能要发财了。

d: n. 钱，钞票，货币；财产，财富；款项，金额；工资，薪金
【名】 （Money）（英）莫尼，（西、法）莫内（人名）

e.en: When something multiplies or when you multiply it, it increases greatly in number or amount. 使大大增加;

ex.en: Such disputes multiplied in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
ex.zh: 此类争论在18世纪和19世纪大大增加。

e.en: When animals and insects multiply, they increase in number by giving birth to large numbers of young.

ex.en: These creatures can multiply quickly.
ex.zh: 这些生物能迅速大量繁殖。

e.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

ex.en: What do you get if you multiply six by nine?
ex.zh: 6乘以9得多少？

d: v. （multiply 的过去式和过去分词）乘，乘以；成倍增加，大大增加；繁殖，增殖
adj. 成倍的，倍增的

e.en: a narrow part of a strait, river, current, etc (海峡、河、水流等)

d: n. 纽约湾海峡（位于美国）

e.en: None of something means not even a small amount of it. None of a group of people or things means not even one of them.

ex.en: None of us knew how to treat her.
ex.zh: 我们中没有任何人知道该如何对待她。

e.en: None is also a pronoun. 没有任何人;

ex.en: I searched bookstores and libraries for information, but found none.
ex.zh: 我查找了多家书店和图书馆，但没查到任何信息。

ex.en: No one could imagine a great woman painter. None had existed yet.
ex.zh: 没人能想像会有出色的女画家。还没有那样的人存在过。

e.en: If you say that someone will have none of something, or is having none of something, you mean that they refuse to accept it.

ex.en: He knew his own mind and was having none of their attempts to keep him at home.
ex.zh: 他知道自己想要什么，不会接受他们要把他留在家里的企图。

e.en: You use none too in front of an adjective or adverb in order to emphasize that the quality mentioned is not present.

ex.en: He was none too thrilled to hear from me at that hour.
ex.zh: 他在那个时刻接到我的电话不太高兴。

d: pron. 全无
adv. 毫无，绝不（none the）；（与 too 加形容词或副词连用）绝不
n. 申初经（天主教七段祈祷时间中的一部分，通常在一天中的第九个小时 下午3点）
【名】 （None）（葡、罗）诺内（人名）
adv. 显著地，明显地，引人注目地

e.en: You use o'clock after numbers from one to twelve to say what time it is. For example, if you say that it is 9 o'clock, you mean that it is nine hours after midnight or nine hours after noon. …

ex.en: The trouble began just after ten o'clock last night.
ex.zh: 麻烦在昨晚刚过10点时开始了。

d: adv. ……点钟，整点（用于数字 1 至 12 后表示准确钟点，等于 of the clock）；……点钟方向（用于航空、军事或口语，指以钟面位置表示的方向，如 twelve o'clock 为正前方）

e.en: An operator is a person who connects telephone calls at a telephone exchange or in a place such as an office or hotel.

ex.en: He dialled the operator and put in a call to Rome.
ex.zh: 他拨通了接线员，往罗马打了一个电话。

e.en: An operator is a person who is employed to operate or control a machine.

ex.en: ...computer operators.
ex.zh: …电脑操作员。

e.en: An operator is a person or a company that runs a business.

ex.en: ...the nation's largest cable TV operator.
ex.zh: …全国最大的有线电视运营商。

e.en: If you call someone a smooth or shrewd operator, you mean that they are skilful at achieving what they want, often in a slightly dishonest way.

ex.en: He is a smooth operator. Don't underestimate him.
ex.zh: 他是个精明圆滑的人，别低估他。

d: n. operator 的复数：经营者、运营商；操作员、操作者；电话接线员；[计]运算符、操作符；[数]算子

e.en: When you pack a bag, you put clothes and other things into it, because you are leaving a place or going on holiday. 打点 (行装)

ex.en: When I was 17, I packed my bags and left home.
ex.zh: 在我17岁的时候，打起行囊离开了家。

ex.en: I began to pack a few things for the trip.
