ex.zh: 我开始为旅行收拾些东西。

e.en: 打包;

ex.en: She left Frances to finish her packing.
ex.zh: 她让弗朗西斯把她的行李收拾完。

e.en: When people pack things, for example, in a factory, they put them into containers or boxes so that they can be shipped and sold. 包装;

ex.en: They offered me a job packing boxes in a warehouse.
ex.zh: 他们为我提供了一份在仓库装箱的工作。

ex.en: Machines now exist to pack olives in jars.
ex.zh: 现在有可以把橄榄装进罐里的机器。

e.en: 包装;

ex.en: The shipping and packing costs are passed along in the item price.
ex.zh: 运输和装箱费用已经含在单价中了。

d: v. （把……）打包，收拾（行李）；包装，装箱；（用柔软材料）把……裹（包）起来；在（容器中的食物）上覆盖物质（以防止腐烂）；可折叠运输（或存放）；挤进，塞满；聚集；把……盖上，填封；把……大量放进，装满；（把……）压实，（使）堆积；在（委员会或会议）中安插（支持者、利己的人或事物）；具有，能产生（强大之物或能量）；携带（武器）；（橄榄球）形成对阵争球
n. 包，包裹，捆；（尤指士兵或野外徒步者的）背包；（一般为纸质的）小盒，小包；一副纸牌；（一起生活猎食的）兽群（尤指狼群）；（尤指不受人喜欢的）一帮，一伙；（比赛或竞赛中的）集群，集团；（放在伤口上止血或消肿的）裹布，敷料；（美容用的）面膜，贴膜；一队（男或女幼童军）；（军事交通工具，尤指飞机或潜水艇的）一组，一队；（英橄）全体前锋；（极地海洋中的）流冰群，浮冰群
【名】 （Pack）（英、德）帕克（人名）

e.en: The peak of a process or an activity is the point at which it is at its strongest, most successful, or most fully developed. (过程、活动的)

ex.en: The firm has slashed its workforce from a peak of 150,000 in 2000.
ex.zh: 2000年那家公司把其员工从15万峰值进行了大幅裁减。

ex.en: ...a flourishing career that was at its peak at the time of his death.
ex.zh: …在他去世时处于鼎盛时期的兴旺事业。

e.en: When something peaks, it reaches its highest value or its highest level.

ex.en: Temperatures have peaked at over 90 degrees.
ex.zh: 温度已达到峰值，超过了90度。

e.en: The peak level or value of something is its highest level or value.

ex.en: Today's price is 59% lower than the peak level of $1.5 million.
ex.zh: 今天的价格比150万美元的峰值水平低了59%。

e.en: Peak times are the times when there is most demand for something or most use of something. 高峰的 (时期)

ex.en: It's always crowded at peak times.
ex.zh: 在高峰期总是很拥挤。

d: n. 巅峰，顶点；山顶；有尖峰的山；尖端，尖顶；帽檐，帽舌；极值，峰值；（艏或艉的）尖舱；斜桁外端，（帆的）后上角
v. 达到高峰，达到最大值；消瘦，衰弱，精神萎靡
adj. 巅峰状态的，最高的；高峰时期的
【名】 （Peak）（英）皮克（人名）

e.en: The phone is an electrical system that you use to talk to someone else in another place, by dialling a number on a piece of equipment and speaking into it.

ex.en: "I didn't tell you over the phone," she said. "I didn't know who might be listening."
ex.zh: “我没有在电话里告诉你，”她说。“我不知道谁会在听。”

ex.en: She looked forward to talking to her daughter by phone.
ex.zh: 她盼望着和她女儿通电话交谈。

e.en: The phone is the piece of equipment that you use when you dial someone's phone number and talk to them.

ex.en: Two minutes later the phone rang.
ex.zh: 两分钟后，电话铃响了。

e.en: If you say that someone picks up or puts down the phone, you mean that they lift or replace the receiver.

ex.en: She picked up the phone, and began to dial Maurice's number.
ex.zh: 她拿起电话听筒，开始拨莫里斯的号码。

e.en: When you phone someone, you dial their phone number and speak to them by phone.

ex.en: He'd phoned Laura to see if she was better.
ex.zh: 他给劳拉打电话，看她是不是好些了。

d: n. 电话，电话系统；受话器，听筒；（语音）音子，音素
v. 给…...打电话
【名】 （Phone）（老、缅）蓬（人名）

e.en: The price of something is the amount of money that you have to pay in order to buy it.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in the price of petrol.
ex.zh: …燃气价格的一次猛涨。

ex.en: They expected house prices to rise.
ex.zh: 他们预期房价会上涨。

e.en: The price that you pay for something that you want is an unpleasant thing that you have to do or suffer in order to get it.

ex.en: There may be a price to pay for such relentless activity, perhaps ill health or even divorce.
ex.zh: 这样没完没了的活动可能是要付出代价的，也许是不良健康状况甚至是离婚。

e.en: If something is priced at a particular amount, the price is set at that amount.

ex.en: The bond is currently priced at $900.
ex.zh: 这种债券当前定价为$900。

ex.en: Analysts predict that Digital will price the new line at less than half the cost of comparable IBM mainframes.
ex.zh: 分析家们预测迪吉多公司会将其新线产品的价格定在低于可比的IBM公司大型主机成本的一半的水平。

e.en: 定价

ex.en: It's hard to maintain competitive pricing.
ex.zh: 很难保持有竞争力的定价。

d: n. 价格；代价；开价，价码；投注赔率； 价值
v. 为……定价；给（商店中的产品）标价；比较……的价格；问……的价格
【名】 （Price）（英）普赖斯，（法）普里斯，（葡、瑞典）普里塞（人名）

e.en: When you push something, you use force to make it move away from you or away from its previous position.

ex.en: The woman pushed back her chair and stood up.
ex.zh: 那女人把椅子向后一推，站了起来。

ex.en: They pushed him into the car.
ex.zh: 他们把他推进了汽车。

e.en: Push is also a noun.

ex.en: He gave me a sharp push.
ex.zh: 他猛地推了我一下。

e.en: If you push through things that are blocking your way or push your way through them, you use force in order to move past them.

ex.en: I pushed through the crowds and on to the escalator.
ex.zh: 我挤过人群，上了自动扶梯。

ex.en: Dix pushed forward carrying a glass.
ex.zh: 迪克斯拿着一个玻璃杯往前挤。

e.en: If an army pushes into a country or area that it is attacking or invading, it moves further into it.

ex.en: One detachment pushed into the eastern suburbs toward the airfield.
ex.zh: 一支小分队挺进了东郊往机场去。

d: v. 推，移动；按；挤，推搡；推动，促使；推销，推广；说服，强迫；鼓励，督促；努力争取；坚持地做；（军队）挺进；赶走；贩卖（毒品）；接近（某年龄或数字）；使（栈）准备接收顶层数据；对（底片）作增感处理
n. 推 ；按；努力；鼓励，敦促；挺进，进攻 ；毅力，进取心；棘手的事

e.en: The reason for something is a fact or situation which explains why it happens or what causes it to happen.

ex.en: There is a reason for every important thing that happens.
ex.zh: 发生的每一件重要事情都是有原因的。

e.en: If you say that you have reason to believe something or to have a particular emotion, you mean that you have evidence for your belief or there is a definite cause of your feeling. 道理;

ex.en: They had reason to believe there could be trouble.
ex.zh: 他们有理由相信会有麻烦。

e.en: The ability that people have to think and to make sensible judgments can be referred to as reason.

ex.en: ...a conflict between emotion and reason.
ex.zh: …情感与理智的冲突。

e.en: If you reason that something is true, you decide that it is true after thinking carefully about all the facts.

ex.en: I reasoned that changing my diet would lower my cholesterol level.
ex.zh: 我推断改变我的饮食会降低我的胆固醇水平。

d: n. 原因，理由；充分理由，正当理由；道理，情理；判断力，理智
v. 推理，逻辑思考；推论出，推断出（reason sth. out）；对（某人）以理相劝，劝告（reason with）
【名】 （Reason）（英）里森（人名）

e.en: A regulator is a person or organization appointed by a government to regulate an area of activity such as banking or industry. 监管人;

ex.en: An independent regulator will be appointed to ensure fair competition.
ex.zh: 一个独立的监管机构将受委派来确保公平竞争。

e.en: 监管的

ex.en: ...the U.S.'s financial regulatory system.
ex.zh: …美国的金融监管系统。

d: n. （regulator 的复数形式）监管者，监管机构，监管部门；调节器，调节阀，稳压器；调整者，调节因子，调节剂

e.en: Regulations are rules made by a government or other authority in order to control the way something is done or the way people behave. 法规;

ex.en: The European Union has proposed new regulations to control the hours worked by its employees.
ex.zh: 欧盟已经提出了新的法规来控制其雇员的工作时间。

e.en: Regulation is the controlling of an activity or process, usually by means of rules.

ex.en: Some in the market now want government regulation in order to reduce costs.
ex.zh: 市场上现在有人想要政府来管理以降低成本。

d: n. 规章制度，规则；（运用规则条例的）管理，控制
adj. （使用或穿戴）符合规定的，正规的； 公式化的，用俗套话堆砌而成的

e.en: When you respond to something that is done or said, you react to it by doing or saying something yourself.

ex.en: They are likely to respond positively to the president's request for aid.
ex.zh: 他们有可能积极地回应该总统的援助请求。

ex.en: The army responded with gunfire and tear gas.
ex.zh: 军方以炮火和催泪弹回应。

e.en: When you respond to a need, crisis, or challenge, you take the necessary or appropriate action.

ex.en: This modest group size allows our teachers to respond to the needs of each student.
ex.zh: 这个适中的小组规模使得我们的老师们可以应对每个学生的需要。

e.en: If a patient or their injury or illness is responding to treatment, the treatment is working and they are getting better.

ex.en: I'm pleased to say that he is now doing well and responding to treatment.
ex.zh: 我很高兴地说他现在正在顺利恢复，治疗是有效果的。

d: v. （respond 的第三人称单数现在时）回答，回应；作出反应，响应；应对（需求、危机、挑战等）；对治疗有良好反应，病情好转

e.en: When you return to a place, you go back there after you have been away.

ex.en: There are unconfirmed reports that Aziz will return to Moscow within hours.
ex.zh: 有未经证实的报道称阿齐兹将在数小时内返回莫斯科。

e.en: Your return is your arrival back at a place where you had been before.

ex.en: Kenny explained the reason for his sudden return to Dallas.
ex.zh: 肯尼解释了他突然返回达拉斯的理由。

e.en: If you return something that you have borrowed or taken, you give it back or put it back.

ex.en: I enjoyed the book and said so when I returned it.
ex.zh: 我很喜欢这本书，归还它的时候就这么说了。

e.en: Return is also a noun.

ex.en: The main demand of the Indians is for the return of one-and-a-half-million acres of forest to their communities.
ex.zh: 印第安人的主要要求是把150万英亩的森林归还给他们的族群。

d: n. 回报，收益；退货，退回的商品；纳税申报表（常作 tax returns）；往返票，来回票；（选举）结果（return 的复数）
v. 回来，回去；归还，退还；回报，回应（return 的第三人称单数）
adv. 粗略地，大约；粗暴地，粗鲁地；粗糙地，不精细地

e.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you.

ex.en: Tourists were scrambling over the rocks looking for the perfect camera angle.
ex.zh: 旅行者们爬上岩石，寻找最完美的拍摄角度。

e.en: If you scramble to a different place or position, you move there in a hurried, awkward way.

ex.en: Ann threw back the covers and scrambled out of bed.
ex.zh: 安掀开被子，急忙下了床。

e.en: If a number of people scramble for something, they compete energetically with each other for it.

ex.en: More than three million fans are expected to scramble for tickets.
ex.zh: 预计会有三百万以上的歌迷抢购门票。

e.en: Scramble is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the scramble for jobs.
ex.zh: …工作的竞争。

d: v. （迅速而吃力地）爬，攀登；不规则地生长；匆忙地移动；仓促完成（困难的事）；匆忙穿（衣）（scramble into）；争夺，抢夺；变换……的无线电信号，倒换……的频率；扰乱（思维）；炒蛋；命令（飞机）紧急起飞，紧急起飞；（四分卫）持球跑进；打乱
n. 攀爬，爬行；（互相推撞的）争夺，争抢；（因赶任务出现的）忙乱，乱作一团； 摩托车越野赛；（四分卫的）持球跑进；战斗机紧急起飞

e.en: Six is the number 6. 六;

ex.en: ...a glorious career spanning more than six decades.
ex.zh: …六十多年辉煌的职业生涯。

d: num. 六，数字 6；六个；六个人（或物）一组；六岁；六点钟
n. （Six）西克斯（人名）

e.en: Computer programs are referred to as software. Compare .

ex.en: ...the people who write the software for big computer projects.
ex.zh: …大型计算机项目的软件开发人员。

d: n. 软件；（计算机）程序及相关文档资料的总称，与 hardware（硬件）相对

e.en: Solar is used to describe things relating to the sun.

ex.en: A total solar eclipse is due to take place some time tomorrow.
ex.zh: 预计日全食会出现在明天的某个时候。

e.en: Solar power is obtained from the sun's light and heat.

ex.en: ...the financial savings from solar energy.
ex.zh: …使用太阳能带来的资金节约。

d: adj. 太阳的，和太阳有关的；（与）太阳能（有关）的
n. （中世纪房屋的）屋顶室，顶层房间
【名】 （Solar）（法、英、意、西、塞、捷）索拉尔（人名）

e.en: You use somewhere to refer to a place without saying exactly where you mean.

ex.en: I've got a feeling I've seen him before somewhere.
ex.zh: 我有一种感觉，我以前在某个地方见过他。

ex.en: I'm not going home yet. I have to go somewhere else first.
ex.zh: 我还不会回家。我得先去别的地方。

e.en: You use somewhere when giving an approximate amount, number, or time.

ex.en: He is believed to be worth somewhere between seven million and ten million dollars.
ex.zh: 据说他身价约在700万到1000万美元之间。

ex.en: Caray is somewhere between 73 and 80 years of age.
ex.zh: 凯瑞大约在73岁到80岁之间。

e.en: If you say that you are getting somewhere, you mean that you are making progress toward achieving something.

ex.en: At last they were agreeing, at last they were getting somewhere.
ex.zh: 最终他们取得了一致，最终他们取得了一些进展。

d: adv. 在某处；到某处
n. 某个地方

e.en: A spike is a long piece of metal with a sharp point.

ex.en: ...a 15-foot wall topped with iron spikes.
ex.zh: …顶上装有长铁锥的15英尺高的墙。

e.en: to add alcohol to (a drink) (向饮料中)
to hit (a ball) sharply downwards with an overarm motion from the front of one's own court into the opposing court (排球中的)

d: n. 猛增，急升；尖状物，金属钉，尖木；（运动鞋上的）鞋钉；钉鞋（spikes）；细高跟鞋（spikes）；（尤指铁轨上的）道钉，大钉；穗，穗状花序；（电子）脉冲尖峰；临时简易床位；（排球中的）扣球；票插，纸插；皮下注射用的针头
v. 在……中偷偷掺入（烈酒、毒药或毒品）；给……添加风味，给……增加趣味；迅速提升，急剧增加；（用尖物）刺入，扎入；形成尖状物，以尖状物覆盖；（排球中的）大力扣杀；摔球触地；弃置（新闻稿）不用，拒绝发表；停止（计划，任务），制止，毁掉；用大钉堵住火门使枪无用；在……中加某种放射性同位素
【名】 （Spike）（瑞典）斯皮克（人名）

e.en: A station or a train station is a building by a railway track where trains stop so that people can get on or off.

ex.en: Ingrid went with him to the train station to see him off.
ex.zh: 英格丽德和他一起去火车站送他。

e.en: A bus station is a building, usually in a town or city, where buses stop, usually for a while, so that people can get on or off. (汽车)

ex.en: I walked the two miles back to the bus station and bought a ticket home.
ex.zh: 我走了两英里回到汽车站买了一张回家的票。

e.en: If you talk about a particular radio or television station, you are referring to the company that broadcasts programmes. (电、电视)

ex.en: ...an independent local radio station.
ex.zh: …一家独立的地方广播电台。

e.en: If soldiers or officials are stationed in a place, they are sent there to do a job or to work for a period of time.

ex.en: Reports from the capital, Lome, say troops are stationed on the streets.
ex.zh: 来自首都洛美的报道说部队驻扎在街道上。

d: n. （公共汽车、火车等的）车站；电视台，广播电台；站，所，局；社会地位，身份；须坚守的位置，岗位；驻地，基地；（电台或电视的）频率，频道；（澳大利亚或新西兰的）大牧场
vt. 驻扎，派驻；派往，安置在

e.en: If you stay where you are, you continue to be there and do not leave.

ex.en: "Stay here," Trish said. "I'll bring the car down the drive to take you back."
ex.zh: “呆在这儿，”特里希说道，“我会把车开下来送你回去。”

e.en: If you stay in a town, or hotel, or at someone's house, you live there for a short time. (在某城市、酒店、某人家里) 暂住;

ex.en: Gordon stayed at The Park Hotel, Milan.
ex.zh: 戈登住在了米兰的帕克酒店。

ex.en: Can't you stay a few more days?
ex.zh: 你不能多住几天吗？

e.en: Stay is also a noun. 暂住;

ex.en: An experienced Indian guide is provided during your stay.
ex.zh: 在你逗留期间给你配备一位经验丰富的印第安向导。

e.en: anything that supports or steadies, such as a prop or buttress 支撑物;

d: v. 停留，逗留；保持原状，维持；坚持；（到访或作客时）留宿，暂住；不去，远离某地；避开，不参与（麻烦或不利局面）；停止，延期，延缓；控制，中止，抑制；定居；暂时解除（饥饿）；用支索支撑（桅杆），用牵索固定；支持，支撑
n. 暂住，逗留；（审判的）推迟，延缓；（船桅的）支索，（杆子等的）牵索，撑条；（衬衫衣领的）撑条；控制，中止，抑制；胸衣，紧身褡，紧身背心；支撑物，稳固物；（飞机的）拉杆，拉索

e.en: The subject of something such as a conversation, letter, or book is the thing that is being discussed or written about. 话题;

ex.en: It was I who first raised the subject of plastic surgery.
ex.zh: 是我首先提起了整形手术这个话题。

ex.en: ...the president's own views on the subject.
ex.zh: …该总统对此问题的个人观点。

e.en: Someone or something that is the subject of criticism, study, or an investigation is being criticized, studied, or investigated. (批评、研究或调查的)

ex.en: Over the past few years, some of the positions Mr. Meredith has adopted have made him the subject of criticism.
ex.zh: 在过去的几年里，梅雷迪恩先生所采取的一些立场已使他成为了被批评的对象。

e.en: A subject is an area of knowledge or study, especially one that you study in school, or college. (尤指在学校学习的)

ex.en: Surprisingly, maths was voted their favourite subject.
ex.zh: 令人吃惊的是，数学被评为他们喜爱的科目。

e.en: In an experiment or piece of research, the subject is the person or animal that is being tested or studied. 实验对象;

ex.en: "White noise" was played into the subject's ears through headphones.
ex.zh: “白色噪音”通过耳机被送进实验对象的耳朵里。

d: n. 主题，话题；学科，科目，课程；主语；（绘画、摄影等的）主题，题材；实验对象；（批评、学习、调查的）对象；国民；起因；（逻）主词，主项，主概念；（乐）主旋律；（哲）主体，主观；中心实体
v. 使臣服，征服，压服；使经受，使遭受
adj. 隶属的，臣服的；可能受……影响的，易遭受……的；受……支配的，服从于……的；取决于，视……而定
adj. subtle 的比较级：更微妙的；更精细的；更敏感的；更狡猾的

e.en: Success is the achievement of something that you have been trying to do.

ex.en: It's important for the success of any diet that you vary your meals.
ex.zh: 膳食多样化对任何饮食的成效都是重要的。

e.en: Success is the achievement of a high position in a particular field, for example in business or politics. (在商业、政治等领域的)

ex.en: We all believed that work was the key to success.
ex.zh: 我们都曾经相信工作是成功的关键。

e.en: The success of something is the fact that it works in a satisfactory way or has the result that is intended. (某事物的)

ex.en: We were amazed by the play's success.
ex.zh: 我们惊叹该剧的成功。

e.en: Someone or something that is a success achieves a high position, makes a lot of money, or is admired a great deal. 成功的人;

ex.en: We hope it will be a commercial success.
ex.zh: 我们希望它会是一次商业成功。

d: n. 成功，胜利；发财，成名；成功的人（或事物）

e.en: If something happens suddenly, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.

ex.en: Suddenly, she looked ten years older.
ex.zh: 突然间，她看上去老了10岁。

ex.en: Her expression suddenly altered.
ex.zh: 她的表情突然变了。

d: adv. 突然地，出乎意料地

e.en: A system is a way of working, organizing, or doing something which follows a fixed plan or set of rules. You can use system to refer to an organization or institution that is organized in this way.

ex.en: The present system of funding for higher education is unsatisfactory.
ex.zh: 目前高等教育的经费体制并不令人满意。

ex.en: ...a flexible and relatively efficient filing system.
ex.zh: …一个灵活且相对高效的文件归档方法。

e.en: A system is a set of devices powered by electricity, for example a computer or an alarm.

ex.en: Viruses tend to be good at surviving when a computer system crashes.
ex.zh: 病毒往往在电脑系统瘫痪时仍然存在。

e.en: A system is a set of equipment or parts such as water pipes or electrical wiring, which is used to supply water, heat, or electricity. (水管或电线等的)

ex.en: ...a central heating system.
ex.zh: …一个中央供暖系统。

e.en: A system is a network of things that are linked together so that people or things can travel from one place to another or communicate.

ex.en: ...Australia's road and rail system.
ex.zh: …澳大利亚的公路网和铁路网。

d: n. （协同工作的）系统；（计算机、警报器等的）系统；体制，制度，方式，方法；现行体制，既成制度（the system）；身体，（器官）系统；人体的活动方式（尤指消化和排泄方式）；（度量，分类中的）方法（或规则）；条理，秩序；（交通、通信）网，网络；（地质）（年代地层学用语）系；（天文）系；下赌注法；（乐）用弧线连为一体的谱表；晶系（crystal system 的简称）

e.en: Temporal powers or matters relate to ordinary institutions and activities rather than to religious or spiritual ones. 凡尘的;

ex.en: ...the spiritual and temporal leader of the people.
ex.zh: ...人们的精神及俗世领袖。

e.en: Temporal means relating to time.

ex.en: One is also able to see how specific acts are related to a temporal and spatial context.
ex.zh: 人们也能看到具体的行为如何与时间和空间背景相关联。

e.en: of, relating to, or near the temple or temples 颞部的;

d: adj. 世俗的，现世的；时间的，与时间有关的；太阳穴的，颞部的；（语法）表示时间的，时态的；暂时的
n. 世间万物，暂存的事物；颞部
【名】 （Temporal）（法）唐波拉尔（人名）

e.en: Ten is the number 10. 10;

ex.en: Over the past ten years things have changed.
ex.zh: 在过去的10年中，情况已经发生了变化。

d: num. 十个，十
adj. 十的
det. 十个；十个（东西）
n. （Ten）（美、俄、加、德、荷、西、英）登（人名）

e.en: A trader is a person whose job is to trade in goods or stocks. 商人;

ex.en: Market traders display an exotic selection of the island's produce.
ex.zh: 市场商家们展示了该岛具有异国情调的农产品系列。

d: n. 交易员；贸易商（trader 的复数形式）

e.en: Transition is the process in which something changes from one state to another.

ex.en: The transition from a dictatorship to a multi-party democracy is proving to be difficult.
ex.zh: 从专政国家到多党民主国家的转型证明是很艰难的。

e.en: If someone transitions from one state or activity to another, they move gradually from one to the other. (逐渐地)

ex.en: Most of the discussion was on what needed to be done now as we transitioned from the security issues to the challenging economic issues.
ex.zh: 大多数讨论都集中在目前需要做什么，因为我们已从安全问题逐渐转到具有挑战性的经济问题上。

d: n. 过渡，转变；（分子生物）转换；（乐）临时转调；（物理）跃迁，转变
v. 转变，过渡

e.en: A train is a number of containers on wheels which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Trains carry people and goods from one place to another.

ex.en: The train pulled into a station.
ex.zh: 那列火车驶入了一个车站。

ex.en: We can catch the early morning train.
ex.zh: 我们能赶上清晨的那班火车。

e.en: A train of vehicles, people, or animals is a long line of them travelling slowly in the same direction. (行进中的)

ex.en: In the old days this used to be done with a baggage train of camels.
ex.zh: 在古时候，这常常由一队拉行李的骆驼来完成。

e.en: A train of thought or a train of events is a connected sequence, in which each thought or event seems to occur naturally or logically as a result of the previous one. (一) 连串 (想法或事件)

ex.en: He lost his train of thought for a moment, then recovered it.
ex.zh: 他一时断了思路，接着又重新想起来了。

e.en: If someone trains you to do something, they teach you the skills that you need in order to do it. If you train to do something, you learn the skills that you need in order to do it. 培训;

ex.en: He was training us to be soldiers.
ex.zh: 他正把我们训练成士兵。

d: adj. 受过训练的，训练过的，受过培训的
v. 训练（train 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.

ex.en: The new ship will be powered by two gas turbines and four diesel engines.
ex.zh: 那艘新轮船将由2台燃气涡轮机和4台柴油机驱动。

d: n. （动力）涡轮机（turbine 的复数），涡轮，透平；汽轮机

e.en: If you undermine something such as a feeling or a system, you make it less strong or less secure than it was before, often by a gradual process or by repeated efforts. 逐渐削弱;

ex.en: Offering advice on each and every problem will undermine her feeling of being adult.
ex.zh: 每个问题都为她提出忠告会逐渐削弱她的成年意识。

e.en: If you undermine someone or undermine their position or authority, you make their authority or position less secure, often by indirect methods. (通常以间接方式) 动摇 (某人的地位或权威)

ex.en: She undermined him and destroyed his confidence in his own talent.
ex.zh: 她动摇了他的地位，摧毁了他对自己才能的信心。

e.en: If you undermine someone's efforts or undermine their chances of achieving something, you behave in a way that makes them less likely to succeed. 破坏; 损害 (某人的努力或成功的机会)

ex.en: The continued fighting threatens to undermine efforts to negotiate an agreement.
ex.zh: 持续的战斗有可能破坏通过谈判达成协议的努力。

d: vt. （undermine 的第三人称单数）逐渐损毁，逐渐削弱，损害；暗中破坏，动摇（某人的地位或权威）；在……下挖掘，侵蚀……的基础

e.en: lacking in glamour, allure, or fascination

ex.en: the unglamorous side of the music business

d: adj. 缺乏魅力的，不浪漫的；单调乏味的，平淡无奇的

e.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

ex.en: The warning lights were clearly visible.
ex.zh: 警示灯清晰可见。

e.en: You use visible to describe something or someone that people notice or recognize.

ex.en: The most visible sign of the intensity of the crisis is unemployment.
ex.zh: 危机加剧的最明显迹象是失业情况。

e.en: 明显地

ex.en: The Russians were visibly wavering.
ex.zh: 俄国人显然犹豫不决。

d: adj. 看得见的；明显的，引人注目的；（进出口贸易）有形商品的；（物理）（光）可见的；现有的，可得到的
n. 有形进出口货物（visibles）

e.en: A wire is a long thin piece of metal that is used to fasten things or to carry electric current. (用以绑东西或导电的)

ex.en: ...fine copper wire.
ex.zh: …细铜丝。

e.en: A wire is a cable that carries power or signals from one place to another. 电线;

ex.en: I ripped out the telephone wire that ran through to his office.
ex.zh: 我拔掉连接到他办公室的电话线。

e.en: If you wire something such as a building or piece of equipment, you put wires inside it so that electricity or signals can pass into or through it.

ex.en: ...learning to wire and plumb the house herself.
ex.zh: …她学会自己在房子里装设电线和水管。

ex.en: Each of the homes has a security system and is wired for cable television.
ex.zh: 每一家都有安全系统，并装设了有线电视线。

e.en: Wire up means the same as .

ex.en: Wire the thermometers up to trigger off an alarm bell if the temperature drops.
ex.zh: 把温度计的电线连接上，当温度下降时，就会触发警报。

d: n. 金属丝，金属线；电线，导线；隐蔽式电子收听器；电报；（赛马）起跑线，终点线（the wire）；铁丝网（the wire）；用金属丝制的，用金属线制的；通讯社
v. 给……接上电线，接通（电源）；（用电线）接通，连接；电汇（钱款）；发电报给（某人）；用金属线固定（或加固）；给……安装窃听器；用金属网诱捕（动物）；（槌球）在拱门边阻挡（球，射球，选手）
【名】 （Wire）怀尔（人名）

e.en: Something that is wide measures a large distance from one side or edge to the other.

ex.en: All worktops should be wide enough to allow plenty of space for food preparation.
ex.zh: 所有的厨房操作台都必须足够宽，以便有充足的空间准备食物。

e.en: If you open or spread something wide, you open or spread it as far as possible or to the fullest extent.

ex.en: "It was huge," he announced, spreading his arms wide.
ex.zh: “它大极了，”他大张开双臂比划着说。

e.en: You use wide to talk or ask about how much something measures from one side or edge to the other. …

ex.en: ...a corridor of land four miles wide.
ex.zh: …一条4英里宽的陆地走廊。

ex.en: The road is only one lane wide.
ex.zh: 这条路只有一个车道那么宽。

e.en: You use wide to describe something that includes a large number of different things or people.

ex.en: The brochure offers a wide choice of hotels, apartments and holiday homes.
ex.zh: 这本手册提供了选择范围很广的旅馆、公寓及度假屋。

d: adj. 宽的，宽阔的，广阔的；…宽的（用于数词或度量短语后）；张大的，完全张开的（指眼睛、嘴等）；广泛的，范围广的；差距大的，程度大的；偏离的，未中的，远离目标的；宽松的，肥大的（指衣物）
adv. 广泛地，广阔地，远及各处；充分地，完全地；偏离目标地，未中地
n. 大千世界，广阔的世界；（板球）投偏的球，偏球；（Wide）维德（瑞典、芬兰人名）

e.en: If you describe something or someone as wonderful, you think they are extremely good.

ex.en: The cold, misty air felt wonderful on his face.
ex.zh: 那凉凉的雾气使他脸上感觉好极了。

ex.en: It's wonderful to see you.
ex.zh: 见到你好极了。

e.en: 极好地

ex.en: It's a system that works wonderfully well.
ex.zh: 它是一个运行极好的系统。

d: adj. 绝妙的，令人惊叹的，极好的

e.en: The world is the planet that we live on.

ex.en: The satellite enables us to calculate their precise location anywhere in the world.
ex.zh: 这颗卫星使得我们可以计算他们在地球上的任何准确位置。

e.en: The world refers to all the people who live on this planet, and our societies, institutions, and ways of life.

ex.en: The world was, and remains, shocked.
ex.zh: 世人震惊了，并且仍然震惊。

ex.en: He wants to show the world that anyone can learn to be an ambassador.
ex.zh: 他想向世人展示，任何人都能够学做一名大使。

e.en: You can use world to describe someone or something that is one of the most important or significant of its kind on earth.

ex.en: China has once again emerged as a world power.
ex.zh: 中国再次成为一个世界性的强国。

e.en: You can use world in expressions such as the Arab world, the Western world, and the ancient world to refer to a particular group of countries or a particular period in history. 世界 (指某些国家或时期)

ex.en: Athens had strong ties to the Arab world.
ex.zh: 雅典与阿拉伯世界有着紧密的联系。

d: n. 世界，地球，天下；星球，天体；地区，国家，时代；社会，生活；领域，界，圈子；生物界，自然界；人生，生活圈子，阅历；人世，今生，来世；世俗；（有某种特色的）地方，情景；大量，无数；一切，重要性（the world）
adj. 世界上最重要的，世界闻名的；世界（性）的；环球的

e.en: An American person or thing belongs to or comes from the United States of America. 美国的;

ex.en: ...the American ambassador at the United Nations.
ex.zh: ...美国驻联合国大使。

ex.en: ...the influence of American television and movies.
ex.zh: ...美国电视和电影产生的影响。

e.en: An American is someone who is American.

ex.en: The 1990 Nobel Prize for medicine was won by two Americans.
ex.zh: 两名美国人获得了1990年度诺贝尔医学奖。

d: n. 花旗布

e.en: A congressional policy, action, or person relates to the U.S. Congress.

ex.en: The president explained his plans to congressional leaders.
ex.zh: 总统向国会领导人说明了他的计划。

d: adj. 立法机构的，代表大会的，（美国）国会的

e.en: A billion is a thousand million. 10

ex.en: The Ethiopian foreign debt stands at 3 billion dollars.
ex.zh: 埃塞俄比亚的外债达30亿美元。

e.en: If you talk about billions of people or things, you mean that there is a very large number of them but you do not know or do not want to say exactly how many.

ex.en: Biological systems have been doing this for billions of years.
ex.zh: 生物系统亿万年来都在这样做。

e.en: You can also use billions as a pronoun.

ex.en: He thought that it must be worth billions.
ex.zh: 他认为它一定值亿万元。

d: n. 数十亿（billion 的复数）；无数，亿万，大量；（数位）十亿位

e.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try very hard to do it.

ex.en: He made no effort to hide his disappointment.
ex.zh: 他不试图隐瞒自己的失望。

ex.en: Finding a cure requires considerable time and effort.
ex.zh: 找到一种治愈方法需要相当的时间和努力。

e.en: If you say that someone did something with effort or with an effort, you mean it was difficult for them to do.

ex.en: She took a deep breath and sat up slowly and with great effort.
ex.zh: 她深吸一口气，慢慢地、吃力地坐了起来。

e.en: An effort is a particular series of activities that is organized by a group of people in order to achieve something.

ex.en: ...a famine relief effort in Angola.
ex.zh: …一个在安哥拉的饥荒救援活动。

e.en: If you say that something is an effort, you mean that an unusual amount of physical or mental energy is needed to do it.

ex.en: Even carrying the camcorder while hiking in the forest was an effort.
ex.zh: 在森林徒步旅行时，即使背着摄像机也是件极难的事。

d: n. effort 的复数：努力；尝试；有组织的活动；努力的结果，成就；质量不高的成果

e.en: A federal country or system of government is one in which the different states or provinces of the country have important powers to make their own laws and decisions.

ex.en: Five of the six provinces are to become autonomous regions in a new federal system of government.
ex.zh: 在新的联邦政府体制下，6个省中的5个将成为自治区。

e.en: Federal also means belonging or relating to the national government of a federal country rather than to one of the states within it.

ex.en: The federal government controls just 6% of the education budget.
ex.zh: 联邦政府只掌控教育预算的6％。

e.en: 联邦政府地

ex.en: ...residents of public housing and federally subsidized apartments.
ex.zh: …公共住房的住户和享受联邦政府补贴的公寓住户。

d: adj. 联邦（制）的；（与）联邦政府（有关）的；中央集权式的；（美国内战时期）北部联邦政府的
n. 联邦探员，联邦政府官员；（美国南北战争时期）北部联邦政府支持者
【名】  （Federal）（英）费德勒尔（人名）

e.en: The dollar is the unit of money used in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and some other countries. It is represented by the symbol $, the dollar sign. A dollar is divided into one hundred smaller units called cents. 元 (美国、加拿大、澳大利亚以及其他一些国家的货币单位)

ex.en: She gets paid seven dollars an hour.
ex.zh: 她的报酬是每小时7元。

e.en: The dollar is also used to refer to the American currency system.

ex.en: In early trading in Tokyo, the dollar fell sharply against the yen.
ex.zh: 在东京的早盘交易中，美元对日元的汇率急剧下跌。

d: n. 美元（dollar 的复数）；也泛指以 dollar 为单位的货币，常特指美元

e.en: Lost is the past tense and past participle of . (lose)
If you are lost or if you get lost, you do not know where you are or are unable to find your way.

ex.en: Barely had I set foot in the street when I realized I was lost.
ex.zh: 我刚走上那条街就发现自己迷路了。

e.en: If something is lost, or gets lost, you cannot find it, for example, because you have forgotten where you put it.

ex.en: ...a lost book.
ex.zh: …一本丢失的书。

ex.en: He was scrabbling for his pen, which had got lost somewhere under the sheets of paper.
ex.zh: 他当时正在翻找钢笔，那支笔在纸堆下的某个地方找不到了。

e.en: If you feel lost, you feel very uncomfortable because you are in an unfamiliar situation.

ex.en: Of the funeral he remembered only the cold, the waiting, and feeling very lost.
ex.zh: 有关那次葬礼，他只记得当时很冷，等了很长时间，而且感到很迷惘。

d: adj. 迷路的，迷失的；失去的，丢失的；不复存在的，不再拥有的；不知所措，一筹莫展；糊涂的，困惑的；全神贯注的；（时间或机会）浪费的，错过的；输了的；遭难的，阵亡的；彻底毁坏的
v. 遗失，丢失；失去；输掉（比赛、战斗、争论等）（lose 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 调查，审查；科学研究，学术研究

e.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

ex.en: There are a number of distinguishing characteristics by which you can identify a Hollywood epic.
ex.zh: 通过其诸多与众不同的特点,你可以识别出好莱坞的史诗影片。

e.en: If you identify someone or something, you name them or say who or what they are.

ex.en: Police have already identified 10 murder suspects.
ex.zh: 警方已经确认了10名谋杀嫌疑犯。

e.en: If you identify something, you discover or notice its existence. 发现;

ex.en: Scientists claim to have identified chemicals produced by certain plants which have powerful cancer-fighting properties.
ex.zh: 科学家们声称已经发现某些植物产生的化学物质有强大的抗癌功能。

e.en: If a particular thing identifies someone or something, it makes them easy to recognize, by making them different in some way. 是…的标志;

ex.en: She wore a little nurse's hat on her head to identify her.
ex.zh: 她头上戴了一顶小护士帽，这使她易于辨认。

d: v. （identify 的第三人称单数）认出，识别；查明，确认；发现，指出；成为…的明显标志，使易于辨认；认同，与…产生共鸣（identify with）；认为…与…等同或密切相关；自我认同为（identify as）；证明自己的身份（identify oneself）

e.en: If a company goes online, its services become available on the Internet. (公司服务)

ex.en: ...the first bank to go online.
ex.zh: …第一家开通网上业务的银行。

ex.en: ...an online shopping centre.
ex.zh: …一个在线购物中心。

e.en: If you are online, your computer is connected to the Internet. Compare .

ex.en: You can chat to other people who are online.
ex.zh: 你可以与其他在线的人聊天。

e.en: Online is also an adverb.

ex.en: ...the cool stuff you find online.
ex.zh: …你在网上找到的好东西。

d: adj. （产品、服务或信息）在线的，网上的；（计算机）联机的
adv. 在网上，利用网际网路（购买、获得等）；联机地，在电脑操控下；开始运行，存在着

e.en: A gap is a space between two things or a hole in the middle of something solid. 缺口;

ex.en: He pulled the thick curtains together, leaving just a narrow gap.
ex.zh: 他把厚厚的窗帘拉到一起，只留了一条窄缝。

e.en: A gap is a period of time when you are not busy or when you stop doing something that you normally do.

ex.en: There followed a gap of four years, during which William joined the Army.
ex.zh: 之后有4年的间隔，期间威廉参军了。

e.en: If there is something missing from a situation that prevents it from being complete or satisfactory, you can say that there is a gap.

ex.en: The manifesto calls for a greater effort to recruit young scientists to fill the gap left by a wave of retirements expected over the next decade.
ex.zh: 该声明呼吁加大力度招募年轻的科学家，以填补预期未来十年内一波退休高峰所留下的空缺。

e.en: A gap between two groups of people, things, or sets of ideas is a big difference between them.

ex.en: ...the gap between rich and poor.
ex.zh: …贫富差距。

ex.en: America's trade gap widened.
ex.zh: 美国的贸易差额加大了。

d: n. 缝隙，缺口，裂口；差距，差异，隔阂；空白，缺漏，不足；时间间隔，空档（gap 的复数）
v. 裂开；使豁裂，使出现缺口（gap 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.

ex.en: He has helped to raise a lot of money.
ex.zh: 他帮着筹到了很多钱。

ex.en: You can of course help by giving them a donation directly.
ex.zh: 你当然可以通过直接给他们一笔捐赠来帮助他们。

e.en: Help is also a noun.

ex.en: Thanks very much for your help.
ex.zh: 非常感谢你的帮助。

e.en: If you say that something helps, you mean that it makes something easier to do or get, or that it improves a situation to some extent.

ex.en: The right style of swimsuit can help to hide, minimize, or emphasize what you want it to.
ex.zh: 款式得当的泳衣有助于按你的意愿掩饰、缩小或突出某些部位。

ex.en: Building more bypasses will help the environment by reducing pollution and traffic jams in towns and cities.
ex.zh: 修建更多的支路将减少城镇中的污染和交通堵塞，从而改善环境。

e.en: If you help someone go somewhere or move in some way, you give them support so that they can move more easily.

ex.en: Martin helped Tanya over the rail.
ex.zh: 马丁扶着塔尼娅翻过栏杆。

d: v. 帮助，援助；改善状况，对……有益；给（自己或某人）食物或饮料；擅自拿走，窃取；搀扶，带领
n. 帮助，协助；有助益的东西（如忠告、钱等）；有用；救助；有帮助的人（或事物）；佣人；（计算机程序提供使用说明的）求助程序
int. 救命（呼救用语）
【名】 （Help）（芬）海尔普 （人名）

e.en: a person who perpetrates a scam; swindler 诈骗犯;

d: n. scammer 的复数形式；骗子，诈骗者

e.en: When you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again. 痊愈;

ex.en: He is recovering from a knee injury.
ex.zh: 他的膝伤正在痊愈。

e.en: If you recover from an unhappy or unpleasant experience, you stop being upset by it. (从不愉快的经历中)

ex.en: ...a tragedy from which he never fully recovered.
ex.zh: …一场他再也没有完全从中恢复过来的悲剧。

e.en: If something recovers from a period of weakness or difficulty, it improves or gets stronger again. (从弱势或困境中)

ex.en: He recovered from a 4-2 deficit to reach the quarter-finals.
ex.zh: 他从4－2的失利中恢复过来，进入1/4决赛。

e.en: If you recover something that has been lost or stolen, you find it or get it back.

ex.en: Police raided five houses in Brooklyn and recovered stolen goods.
ex.zh: 警察突击搜查了位于布鲁克林的5栋住宅，找回了被盗物品。

d: v. 恢复（健康，精神，体力）；康复，复原（be recovered）；（从不愉快的经历中）恢复；（从弱势或困境中）好转，扭转；重新获得，寻回；收回（开支、投资等）；恢复（意识、神志或身体状态）；挽回（地位），弥补（时间损失）；提取（能源或化工品等），回收利用； 给……换上新面
n. （军事操练）枪还原，收枪（the recover）
【名】  （Recover）（西）雷科韦尔（人名）

e.en: Halloween is the night of the 31st of October and is traditionally said to be the time when ghosts and witches can be seen. On Halloween, children often dress up in costumes and go from door to door asking their neighbours for sweets.

d: n. 万圣节前夕（指十月三十一日夜晚）

e.en: A pumpkin is a large, round, orange vegetable with a thick skin.

ex.en: Quarter the pumpkin and remove the seeds.
ex.zh: 把南瓜一切四块，把南瓜子取出来。

d: n. 南瓜（pumpkin 的复数）

e.en: A million or one million is the number 1,000,000.

ex.en: Up to five million people a year visit the county.
ex.zh: 每年多达500万人到这个县游览。

e.en: If you talk about millions of people or things, you mean that there is a very large number of them but you do not know or do not want to say exactly how many.

ex.en: The program was viewed on television in millions of homes.
ex.zh: 无数的家庭从电视上收看了这个节目。

d: n. 数百万；大量，无数

e.en: If you are disposed to do something, you are willing or eager to do it.

ex.en: We passed one or two dwellings, but were not disposed to stop.
ex.zh: 我们经过一两处住所，却无意停下。

e.en: You can use disposed when you are talking about someone's general attitude or opinion. For example, if you are well or favourably disposed to or toward someone or something, you like them or approve of them. 持…态度的;

ex.en: I saw that the publishers were well disposed toward my book.
ex.zh: 我看出版商对我的书有好感。

d: adj. 有……倾向的，愿意的，打算做……的（通常作表语，后接不定式）；持（某种）态度的，有好感的（常与 well、favourably、ill 等副词连用，后接 to 或 toward）；〈旧式〉（身体）有某种健康状态的
v. 处理，处置，解决（dispose of 的过去式或过去分词）；布置，排列，配置（dispose 的过去式或过去分词）；使倾向于，使有意（dispose 的过去式或过去分词）

e.en: Horror is a feeling of great shock, fear, and worry caused by something extremely unpleasant. 震惊;

ex.en: I felt numb with horror.
ex.zh: 我惊呆了。

e.en: If you have a horror of something, you are afraid of it or dislike it very much. 恐惧;

ex.en: ...his horror of death.
ex.zh: …他对死亡的恐惧。

e.en: The horror of something, especially something that hurts people, is its very great unpleasantness.

ex.en: ...the horror of this most bloody of civil wars.
ex.zh: …这场极其血腥的内战的惨状。

e.en: You can refer to extremely unpleasant or frightening experiences as horrors.

ex.en: Can you possibly imagine all the horrors we have undergone since I last wrote you?
ex.zh: 你能想像得出自从上次我写信给你以来，我们所经历的所有恐怖的事情吗？

d: n. 震惊，恐惧；惧怕，憎恶；恐怖性；极其不愉快的（或可怕的）经历；恐怖故事（或电影等）；调皮捣蛋的孩子

e.en: If something or someone frightens you, they cause you to suddenly feel afraid, anxious, or nervous.

ex.en: He knew that Soli was trying to frighten him, so he smiled to hide his fear.
ex.zh: 他知道索利想吓唬他，因此微笑着掩饰自己的恐惧。

e.en: If something frightens the life out of you, frightens the wits out of you, or frightens you out of your wits, it causes you to feel suddenly afraid or gives you a very unpleasant shock.

ex.en: Fairground rides are intended to frighten the life out of you.
ex.zh: 露天游乐场的飞车就是要把你们吓得魂不附体。

d: v. 使惊吓，使惊恐

e.en: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.

ex.en: I was sitting on the floor shivering with fear because a bullet had been fired through a window.
ex.zh: 我坐在地板上吓得浑身发抖，因为有一颗子弹射穿窗户打了进来。

e.en: A fear is a thought that something unpleasant might happen or might have happened.

ex.en: These youngsters are motivated by fear of failure.
ex.zh: 这些年轻人因担心失败而被激发。

ex.en: Then one day his worst fears were confirmed.
ex.zh: 后来有一天，他最大的担心被证实了。

e.en: If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely. (发生坏事的)

ex.en: There is a fear that the freeze on bank accounts could prove a lasting deterrent to investors.
ex.zh: 冻结银行帐户很可能对投资者是一个长期的威慑因素。

e.en: If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.

ex.en: He also spoke of his fears for the future of his country's culture.
ex.zh: 他也谈及了他对祖国文化前景的担忧。

d: n. （fear 的复数）恐惧；担心；（Fears）人名；费尔斯
v. （fear 的第三人称单数）害怕，恐惧；担心；敬畏

e.en: If something is full, it contains as much of a substance or as many objects as it can.

ex.en: Once the container is full, it stays shut until you turn it clockwise.
ex.zh: 该容器一旦满了就会保持关闭，直到你将其按顺时针方向旋转。

e.en: If a place or thing is full of things or people, it contains a large number of them.

ex.en: The case was full of clothes.
ex.zh: 该箱子满是衣服。

ex.en: The streets are still full of debris from two nights of rioting.
ex.zh: 那些街上依然满是两夜暴乱后的狼藉。

e.en: You say that a place or vehicle is full when there is no space left in it for any more people or things. (某处、车辆)

ex.en: The parking lot was full when I left about 10:45.
ex.zh: 停车场在我10:45左右离开时已满了。

ex.en: They stay here a few hours before being sent to refugee camps, which are now almost full.
ex.zh: 他们在这里呆了几个小时后被送到了难民营，难民营现在几乎满了。

e.en: If your hands or arms are full, you are carrying or holding as much as you can carry. (双手) 拿满的; (双臂)

ex.en: Sylvia entered, her arms full of packages.
ex.zh: 西尔维娅进来了，怀里抱满了包裹。

d: adj. 满的，满是……的；饱的；最大量的；完整的，详尽的；足足的；圆润的，浓郁的；充实的；正式的；宽松的；丰满的；（书面装订材料）用于全书面装订的；（头发）过肩的，披肩的
adv. 充分地，完全地；恰好，直接地；非常，极其
n. 盛期，顶点；月亮的满月（期）；全部，整个
v. 装满，使充满；把（织物）打多褶（或大褶）以使（衣服）宽松；（月）变圆,（潮）涨；使（布料）缩呢（或缩绒、毡化）

e.en: a metallic ore found esp in the E Congo, consisting of columbite and tantalite (a source of the element tantalum)

d: 钶钽铁矿（非洲口语对钶铁矿-钽铁矿这种复合矿物的称呼）

e.en: If you watch someone or something, you look at them, usually for a period of time, and pay attention to what is happening.

ex.en: The man was standing in his doorway watching him.
ex.zh: 那个男人正站在自家门道里看着他。

ex.en: He seems to enjoy watching me work.
ex.zh: 他似乎喜欢看我干活。

e.en: If you watch something on television or an event such as a sports contest, you spend time looking at it, especially when you see it from the beginning to the end. 观看 (电视节目、比赛等)

ex.en: I'd stayed up late to watch the movie.
ex.zh: 我熬夜看了那部电影。

e.en: If you watch a situation or event, you pay attention to it or you are aware of it, but you do not influence it.

ex.en: Human rights groups have been closely watching the case.
ex.zh: 人权组织一直在密切关注着这件案子。

ex.en: He watched as nine people were swept into the crevasse.
ex.zh: 他眼看着9个人被卷入冰缝中。

e.en: If you watch people, especially children or animals, you are responsible for them, and make sure that they are not in danger.

ex.en: Parents can't be expected to watch their children 24 hours a day.
ex.zh: 不能指望父母全天24小时都照看自己的孩子。

d: v. watch 的现在分词/动名词；观看，注视；守望；监视，注意；照看
n. 观察；观看（行为或活动）

e.en: When you write, you use something such as a pen or pencil to produce words, letters, or numbers.

ex.en: Simply write your name and address on a postcard and send it to us.
ex.zh: 只要在明信片上写下你的名字和地址，然后寄给我们。

ex.en: They were still trying to teach her to read and write.
ex.zh: 他们当时仍在试图教她读书写字。

e.en: If you write something such as a book, a poem, or a piece of music, you create it and record it on paper or perhaps on a computer.

ex.en: I had written quite a lot of orchestral music in my student days.
ex.zh: 我在学生时代创作了许多管弦乐曲。

ex.en: Thereafter she wrote articles for papers and magazines in Paris.
ex.zh: 从那以后，她为巴黎的报纸和杂志撰稿。

e.en: Someone who writes creates books, stories, or articles, usually for publication.

ex.en: Jay wanted to write.
ex.zh: 杰伊那时想搞创作。

e.en: When you write someone or to someone or write them a letter, you give them information, ask them something, or express your feelings in a letter. 写 (信)

ex.en: Apparently she had written to her aunt in Holland asking for advice.
ex.zh: 显然，她已给她荷兰的姑妈写信征求意见了。

ex.en: She had written him a note a couple of weeks earlier.
ex.zh: 两周前她曾给他写过一张便条。

d: v. write 的第三人称单数：写，书写；创作，写作；写信

e.en: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

ex.en: I started working in a recording studio.
ex.zh: 我开始在一个录音棚里工作。

ex.en: He worked as a teacher for 50 years.
ex.zh: 他从事教师工作50年了。

e.en: When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.

ex.en: I can't talk to you right now – I'm working.
ex.zh: 我这会儿不能和你说话–我正在工作。

ex.en: He was working at his desk.
ex.zh: 他正在伏案工作。

e.en: When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.

ex.en: Linda spends all her time working on the garden.
ex.zh: 琳达用所有的时间在那座花园里劳作。

ex.en: The government expressed hope that all the sides will work toward a political solution.
ex.zh: 该政府希望所有各方致力于一个政治解决方案。

e.en: If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.

ex.en: Professor Bonnet has been working for many years on molecules of this type.
ex.zh: 博内特教授多年来一直在研究这类分子。

d: n. 工作，职业；劳动，活计；职责，工作内容；作品，著作；工作成果，作为；工作地点，工作时间；工作所需的材料（或档案等）；（机器的）活动部件（the works）；所有东西，全套物品（the works）；土木工程，建筑（works）；工厂（works）；善行，德行（works）；防御工事；（物理学）功；整形手术
v. 工作，干活儿；从事体力（或脑力）劳动；从事……工作，在……工作；努力取得，力争；运转，运行；开动，操作（机器、装置等）；奏效，成功；产生……作用；（使）变成，逐步移动；（使）（身体某部位）抽动；（用某种材料）画画，创作；使成形，加工；博得，赢得（众人的支持或欢心）；计算，算出；思考，动脑筋；以（某种假定或思想）为基础（或前提）；安排；耕种；开采（矿）
adj. 工作的，与工作有关的；适合工作时穿戴的；用于工作的
【名】 （Work）（英、埃塞、丹、冰、美）沃克（人名）

e.en: An abandoned place or building is no longer used or occupied.

ex.en: The digging had left a network of abandoned mines and tunnels.
ex.zh: 挖掘留下了满地密布的废弃矿井和隧道。

d: adj. 被抛弃的；废弃的，被丢弃的；放纵的，不羁的；放弃的，不再考虑的
v. 抛弃，遗弃；离弃，逃离（某地方或交通工具等）；放弃，中止（abandon 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If someone or something goes across a place or a boundary, they go from one side of it to the other.

ex.en: She walked across the floor and lay down on the bed.
ex.zh: 她走过地板躺在了床上。

ex.en: He watched Karl run across the street to Tommy.
ex.zh: 他看着卡尔横穿那条街道向汤米跑去。

e.en: Across is also an adverb.

ex.en: Richard stood up and walked across to the window.
ex.zh: 理查德站起来，走到了窗户那边。

e.en: If something is situated or stretched across something else, it is situated or stretched from one side of it to the other.

ex.en: ...the floating bridge across Lake Washington in Seattle.
ex.zh: …横跨西雅图华盛顿湖的浮桥。

ex.en: He scrawled his name across the bill.
ex.zh: 他在账单上草草地写了他的名字。

e.en: Across is also an adverb.

ex.en: Trim toenails straight across using nail clippers.
ex.zh: 用指甲刀整块地剪脚指甲。

d: adv. 从一边到另一边；在……对面；朝，向；宽；横向字谜答案
prep. 从一边到另一边；横过，穿过；在……对面；遍及；在……上；跨越（政治、宗教、社会隔阂等）

e.en: If something is illegal, the law says that it is not allowed.

ex.en: It is illegal to intercept radio messages.
ex.zh: 窃听无线电信息是违法的。

ex.en: ...illegal drugs.
ex.zh: …非法毒品。

e.en: 非法地

ex.en: He was convicted of illegally using a handgun.
ex.zh: 他被判非法使用手枪。

e.en: Illegal immigrants or workers have travelled into a country or are working without official permission. (移民) 非法入境的; (工人)
Illegal immigrants or workers are sometimes referred to as illegals. 非法移民;

ex.en: ...a clothing factory where many other illegals also worked.
ex.zh: …一家允许很多其他非法劳工工作的服装厂。

d: adj. 非法的，违法的；违规的
n. 非法移民，非法劳工

e.en: A miner is a person who works underground in mines in order to obtain minerals such as coal, diamonds, or gold.

d: n. （矿业）矿工（miner 的复数）；煤矿工人；（加密货币）矿工，挖矿者；（Miners）人名；迈纳斯

e.en: Gold is a valuable, yellow-coloured metal that is used for making jewellery and ornaments, and as an international currency.

ex.en: ...a sapphire set in gold.
ex.zh: …一颗镶嵌在金子里的蓝宝石。

ex.en: The price of gold was going up.
ex.zh: 黄金的价格上涨了。

e.en: Gold is jewellery and other things that are made of gold. 金饰物;

ex.en: We handed over all our gold and money.
ex.zh: 我们把所有的金饰物和钱都交了出来。

e.en: Something that is gold is a bright yellow colour, and is often shiny.

ex.en: I'd been wearing Michel's black and gold shirt.
ex.zh: 我一直穿着米歇尔那件黑色和金色相间的衬衫。

e.en: A gold is the same as a .

ex.en: His ambition was to win gold at the Atlanta Games in 1996.
ex.zh: 他的目标是在1996年的亚特兰大奥运会上夺得金牌。

d: n. 金；金币，黄金制品；金色，金黄色；金牌；宝贵的东西，难能可贵的人；（箭术中的）靶心
adj. 金色的；金制的
【名】 （Gold）（英、法、德、西、罗、捷、瑞典）戈尔德（人名）

e.en: Action is doing something for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The government is taking emergency action to deal with a housing crisis.
ex.zh: 该政府正在采取紧急行动来处理一次住房危机。

e.en: The fighting which takes place in a war can be referred to as action. (军事)

ex.en: Our leaders have generally supported military action if it proves necessary.
ex.zh: 我们的领导者们一般都支持必要军事行动的。

e.en: An action is something that you do on a particular occasion.

ex.en: As always, Peter had a reason for his action.
ex.zh: 如往常一样，彼得对他的行为总有理由。

e.en: To take legal action or to bring a legal action against someone means to bring a case against them in a court of law.

ex.en: Two leading law firms are to prepare legal actions against tobacco companies.
ex.zh: 两大律师事务所准备对烟草公司提起法律诉讼。

d: n. 行动；行为；战斗；诉讼；令人激动的事；动作；情节；惊险刺激的活动（或事件）；作用；开始（电影导演开拍的指令）；赚钱的机会；性交；运转方式
v. 处理
adj. 动作（片）的，动作片中的
【名】 （Action）（英）埃克申（人名）
abbr. 动物（animal 的缩写，也可指牲畜）；活泼地（animato 的缩写，音乐术语）；有生命的（animate 的缩写，也指有生气的）；灵魂存在论，泛灵论（animism 的缩写）；动画（animation 的简写，常见于软件、游戏与动画制作语境）；ANIM（动画文件格式，ILBM 的变体）
n. Anim（人名；葡萄牙语译作“阿宁”，加纳人名译作“阿尼姆”）

e.en: An animal is a living creature such as a dog, lion, or rabbit, rather than a bird, fish, insect, or human being. 动物 (不包括鸟类、鱼类、昆虫和人类)

ex.en: He was attacked by wild animals.
ex.zh: 他被野兽袭击了。

e.en: Any living creature other than a human being can be referred to as an animal. 兽类; 动物 (不包括人类)

ex.en: Language is something that fundamentally distinguishes humans from animals.
ex.zh: 语言是从根本上把人类与动物区分开的事物。

e.en: Any living creature, including a human being, can be referred to as an animal. (包括人类在内的)

ex.en: Watch any young human being, or any other young animal.
ex.zh: 观察任意一个年少的人，或者任意其他幼小的动物。

e.en: Animal products come from animals rather than from plants.

ex.en: ...food high in animal fats such as red meat and dairy products.
ex.zh: …富含动物脂肪的食物，如红色肉类和奶制品。

d: n. 动物（animal 的复数）；牲畜，家畜（animal 的复数）；（生物学）包括人类在内的动物界成员

e.en: If you say that something appears to be the way you describe it, you are reporting what you believe or what you have been told, though you cannot be sure it is true.

ex.en: There appears to be increasing support for the leadership to take a more aggressive stance.
ex.zh: 似乎有不断增长的对领导层采取更强立场的支持。

e.en: If someone or something appears to have a particular quality or characteristic, they give the impression of having that quality or characteristic.

ex.en: She did her best to appear more self-assured than she felt.
ex.zh: 她竭力表现得比她感觉的更为自信。

ex.en: He is anxious to appear a gentleman.
ex.zh: 他急于表现得像一位绅士。

e.en: When someone or something appears, they move into a position where you can see them.

ex.en: A woman appeared at the far end of the street.
ex.zh: 一个女人在街那端出现了。

e.en: When something new appears, it begins to exist or reaches a stage of development where its existence can be noticed.

ex.en: ...small white flowers which appear in early summer.
ex.zh: …在初夏出现的小白花。

d: v. 出现，显现，呈现；显得，看上去好像，似乎；（书刊、文章等）出版，发表，问世；（在戏剧、电影、电视节目等中）露面，出演；（在法庭等正式场合）出庭，出席（appear 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: An area is a particular part of a town, a country, a region, or the world.

ex.en: ...the large number of community groups in the area.
ex.zh: …该地区大量的社团。

ex.en: The survey was carried out in both urban and rural areas.
ex.zh: 该调查在城市和乡村地区都开展了。

e.en: Your area is the part of a town, country, or region where you live. An organization's area is the part of a town, country, or region that it is responsible for. 居住区域;

ex.en: Local authorities have been responsible for the running of schools in their areas.
ex.zh: 地方政府一直负责其辖区内各校的运作。

e.en: A particular area is a piece of land or part of a building that is used for a particular activity. (作某用途的)

ex.en: ...a picnic area.
ex.zh: …一个野餐区。

e.en: An area is a particular place on a surface or object, for example, on your body.

ex.en: You will notice that your baby has two soft areas on the top of his head.
ex.zh: 你会注意到你孩子的头顶有两个柔软的部位。

d: n. 地区，区域；场地，地方；领域；面积；部位；罚球区
【名】 （Area）（西）阿雷亚（人名）

e.en: Activity is a situation in which a lot of things are happening or being done.

ex.en: Changes in the money supply affect the level of economic activity and the interest rate.
ex.zh: 货币供给的变化影响经济活动水平和利率。

ex.en: Children are supposed to get 60 minutes of physical activity every day.
ex.zh: 儿童应该每天获得60分钟的体育活动。

e.en: An activity is something that you spend time doing. (个体性的)

ex.en: For lovers of the great outdoors, activities range from canoeing to bird watching.
ex.zh: 对于户外活动的爱好者们来说，有从划船到观鸟的各种活动。

e.en: The activities of a group are the things that they do in order to achieve their aims. (群体性的)

ex.en: ...a jail term for terrorist activities.
ex.zh: …一个针对恐怖主义活动的刑期。

d: n. 活跃状况，热闹；活动；（Activity）热力活性，活度
n. 非洲

e.en: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it from somewhere else.

ex.en: Fresh groups of guests arrived.
ex.zh: 新客成批到达了。

ex.en: ...a small group of commuters waiting for their train, which arrived on time.
ex.zh: …几个等候火车准点到达的通勤者。

e.en: When you arrive at a place, you come to it for the first time in order to stay, live, or work there.

ex.en: ...in the old days before the European settlers arrived in the country.
ex.zh: …在欧洲定居者们初次到这个国家之前的古老岁月。

e.en: When something such as letter or meal arrives, it is brought or delivered to you.

ex.en: Breakfast arrived while he was in the bathroom.
ex.zh: 早餐在他在浴室里时送到了。

e.en: When something such as a new product or invention arrives, it becomes available. (产品、发明)

ex.en: Several long-awaited movies will finally arrive in the stores this month.
ex.zh: 几部期盼已久的影片最终将于本月在各家商店露面。

d: v. 到达，抵达（arrive 的过去式和过去分词）；（船舶等）抵港；arrived at：到达；得出（结论），达成（决定）
adj. 已到达的

e.en: A charity is an organization which raises money in order to help people who are ill, disabled, or very poor.

ex.en: ...an AIDS charity.
ex.zh: …一个艾滋病慈善机构。

e.en: If you give money to charity, you give it to one or more charitable organizations. If you do something for charity, you do it in order to raise money for one or more charitable organizations.

ex.en: He made substantial donations to charity.
ex.zh: 他做了大量的慈善捐赠。

ex.en: Gooch will be raising money for charity.
ex.zh: 古奇将为慈善筹集款项。

e.en: People who live on charity live on money or goods which other people give them because they are poor. 救济金;

ex.en: Her husband is unemployed and the family depends on charity.
ex.zh: 她的丈夫失业了，全家靠救济度日。

d: n. 慈善组织，慈善机构；慈善事业；仁慈，宽厚；赈济，施舍
n. 科拉（女子名）；（希腊神话）珀耳塞福涅（Persephone）的别名（也作 Kore）

e.en: If there is a chance of something happening, it is possible that it will happen.

ex.en: Do you think they have a chance of beating Australia?
ex.zh: 你认为他们有可能击败澳大利亚队吗?

ex.en: There was really very little chance that Ben would ever have led a normal life.
ex.zh: 那时本几乎不可能过上正常的生活。

e.en: If you have a chance to do something, you have the opportunity to do it.

ex.en: The electoral council announced that all eligible people would get a chance to vote.
ex.zh: 选举委员会曾宣布所有符合条件者都将获得投票机会。

ex.en: Most refugee doctors never get the chance to practise medicine in our hospitals.
ex.zh: 绝大部分难民医生在我们的医院里从未得到行医的机会。

e.en: A chance meeting or event is one that is not planned or expected.

ex.en: ...a chance meeting.
ex.zh: …一次邂逅。

e.en: Chance is also a noun. 偶然;

ex.en: ...a victim of chance and circumstance.
ex.zh: …一个时运不济的倒霉者。

d: n. 机会，时机；可能性；危险，冒险；运气，偶然
v. 偶然，碰巧；冒险做
adj. 偶然的，碰巧的
【名】 （Chance）（英）钱斯（人名）

e.en: The claws of a bird or animal are the thin, hard, curved nails at the end of its feet. (鸟、动物的)

ex.en: The cat tried to cling to the edge by its claws.
ex.zh: 那只猫试图用爪子抓紧边沿。

e.en: The claws of a lobster, crab, or scorpion are the two pointed parts at the end of its legs which are used for holding things. (龙虾、蟹、蝎的)
If an animal claws at something, it scratches or damages it with its claws. (用爪)

ex.en: The wolf clawed at the tree and howled the whole night.
ex.zh: 那只狼在那颗树上抓挠，还嗥叫了整整一个晚上。

e.en: To claw at something mean to try very hard to get hold of it.

ex.en: His fingers clawed at Blake's wrist.
ex.zh: 他的手指使劲抓住布莱克的手腕。

d: n. （动物的）爪，爪子；（水生有壳动物的）螯，钳；爪形器具，钳形工具
v. （用爪）撕，抓；挠痒；（帆船）迎风而行

e.en: the outermost wall or court of a castle 城堡外墙;

d: n. 城壁，外栅；城堡外庭；Bailey 人名（贝利，贝莉（女名），拜莱）；Old Bailey（老贝利，伦敦中央刑事法庭）

e.en: The driver of a vehicle is the person who is driving it.

ex.en: The driver got out of his van.
ex.zh: 司机从货车里下来。

e.en: A driver is a computer program that controls a device such as a printer.

ex.en: Printer driver software includes standard features such as print layout and fit-to-page printing.
ex.zh: 打印机驱动程序软件包含标准功能，比如打印版面设定和符合纸张大小的打印。

d: n. 司机，驾驶员；驱动程序（driver 的复数）；（经济、管理）驱动因素

e.en: If people or animals dig, they make a hole in the ground or in a pile of earth, stones, or rubbish.

ex.en: I grabbed the spade and started digging.
ex.zh: 我抓起铁锹开始挖了起来。

ex.en: Dig a large hole and drive the stake in first.
ex.zh: 先挖个大洞，把桩子打进去。

e.en: If you dig into something such as a deep container, you put your hand in it to search for something. 将手伸入… (以探寻某物)

ex.en: He dug into his coat pocket for his keys.
ex.zh: 他把手伸进大衣口袋里找钥匙。

e.en: If you dig one thing into another or if one thing digs into another, the first thing is pushed hard into the second, or presses hard into it. 刺入;

ex.en: She digs the serving spoon into the moussaka.
ex.zh: 她把分菜匙插进茄合里。

e.en: If you dig into a subject or a store of information, you study it very carefully in order to discover or check facts.

ex.en: ...as a special congressional enquiry digs deeper into the alleged financial misdeeds of his government.
ex.zh: …随着一项国会特别调查行动对其政府所谓的不当财政行为的深入调查。

ex.en: He has been digging into the local archives.
ex.zh: 他一直在仔细研究当地的档案。

d: v. 搜寻，寻找；喜欢；挖，掘
n. 挖苦，嘲讽；（用手指或肘部）轻碰，轻戳；考古发掘
【名】 （Dig）（罗）迪格（人名）

e.en: If you have a dozen things, you have twelve of them.

ex.en: You will be able to take ten dozen bottles free of duty through customs.
ex.zh: 你可以携带120瓶免税通过海关。

e.en: You can refer to a group of approximately twelve things or people as a dozen. You can refer to a group of approximately six things or people as half a dozen.

ex.en: In half a dozen words, he had explained the bond that linked them.
ex.zh: 他用五六个字解释了将他们联系在一起的那种关系。

e.en: If you refer to dozens of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

ex.en: ...a storm which destroyed dozens of homes and buildings.
ex.zh: …一场毁坏了许多房屋和建筑物的暴风雨。

e.en: You can also use dozens as a pronoun.

ex.en: Just as revealing are Mr. Johnson's portraits, of which there are dozens.
ex.zh: 透过约翰逊先生的许多肖像画，同样也可以了解其人。

d: n. 许多，几十（dozen 的复数；常作 dozens of；数词后通常仍用单数 dozen）

e.en: If there is dirt on something, there is dust, mud, or a stain on it. 灰尘;

ex.en: I started to scrub off the dirt.
ex.zh: 我开始擦除灰尘。

e.en: You can refer to the earth on the ground as dirt, especially when it is dusty.

ex.en: They all sit on the dirt in the dappled shade of a tree.
ex.zh: 他们都坐在斑驳的树荫下的地上。

e.en: A dirt road or track is made from hard earth. A dirt floor is made from earth without any cement, stone, or wood laid on it.

ex.en: I drove along the dirt road.
ex.zh: 我行驶在一条土路上。

e.en: If you say that you have the dirt on someone, you mean that you have information that could harm their reputation or career.

ex.en: ...a sleazy reporter assigned to dig up dirt on Jack.
ex.zh: …一名受人指使去挖掘有关杰克的流言蜚语的低级庸俗的记者。

d: n. 污物，尘土；泥土，松土；丑闻，流言蜚语
adj. 土的，泥的

e.en: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the final point in it.

ex.en: The report is expected by the end of the year.
ex.zh: 这份报告预期年底前出台。

ex.en: ...families who settled in the region at the end of the 17th century.
ex.zh: …于17世纪末定居该地区的家庭。

e.en: An end to something or the end of it is the act or result of stopping it so that it does not continue any longer.

ex.en: The government today called for an end to the violence.
ex.zh: 政府今天呼吁结束暴力。

ex.en: I was worried she would walk out or bring the interview to an end.
ex.zh: 我担心她会突然退席或者终止采访。

e.en: The two ends of something long and narrow are the two points or parts of it that are farthest away from each other.

ex.en: The company is planning to place surveillance equipment at both ends of the tunnel.
ex.zh: 该公司计划在隧道的两端安装监视设备。

e.en: The end of a long, narrow object such as a finger or a pencil is the tip or smallest edge of it, usually the part that is furthest away from you.

ex.en: He tapped the ends of his fingers together.
ex.zh: 他用手指尖相互轻叩。

d: n. 最后部分，末尾；结束，结局；端点；目的；剩余物，残余；过世；部分，方面；半边球场；城区；边锋
v. 结束，终止
【名】 （End）（英、德）恩德（人名）

e.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

ex.en: Every day of our lives we encounter major and minor stresses of one kind or another.
ex.zh: 生活中的每一天，我们会遇到或大或小的这样那样的压力。

e.en: If you encounter someone, you meet them, usually unexpectedly.

ex.en: Did you encounter anyone in the building?
ex.zh: 你在那栋大楼里偶然遇到什么人了吗？

e.en: An encounter with someone is a meeting with them, particularly one that is unexpected or significant.

ex.en: The author tells of a remarkable encounter with a group of South Vietnamese soldiers.
ex.zh: 作者讲述了他与一群南越士兵的惊人邂逅。

e.en: An encounter is a particular type of experience.

ex.en: ...a sexual encounter.
ex.zh: …一次性经历。

d: v. encounter 的现在分词和动名词；遭遇，遇到（困难、问题等）；遇见，邂逅（尤指意外地）

e.en: Given is the past participle of . (give)
If you talk about, for example, any given position or a given time, you mean the particular position or time that you are discussing.

ex.en: In chess there are typically about 36 legal moves from any given board position.
ex.zh: 在国际象棋中，从棋盘的任何一个特定方格通常都可以移动大致36步。

e.en: Given is used when indicating a possible situation in which someone has the opportunity or ability to do something. For example, given the chance means "if I had the chance." 如果有 (机会等)

ex.en: Write down the sort of thing you would like to do, given the opportunity.
ex.zh: 如果有机会，请写下你想做的那类事。

e.en: If you say given that something is the case, you mean taking that fact into account.

ex.en: Usually, I am sensible with money, as I have to be, given that I don't earn that much.
ex.zh: 我花钱通常是很明智的。考虑到自己挣得不多，必须这样做。

d: adj. 规定的，指定的；倾向于；（文件）（已在某日期由某人）签署的；赠送的；假定的，假设的
prep. 考虑到；如果，倘若
n. 假定事实
v.  给予（give 的过去分词形式）

e.en: An injured person or animal has physical damage to part of their body, usually as a result of an accident or fighting.

ex.en: The other injured man had a superficial stomach wound.
ex.zh: 另一名受伤男子是腹部表层受伤。

e.en: The injured are people who are injured.

ex.en: Army helicopters tried to evacuate the injured.
ex.zh: 军用直升机设法撤出伤员。

e.en: If you have injured feelings, you feel upset because you believe someone has been unfair or unkind to you. (感情)

ex.en: ...a look of injured pride.
ex.zh: …自尊心受伤的表情。

d: adj. 受伤的，有伤的；委屈的，受到伤害的
n. 伤者，伤员（the injured）

e.en: You use her to refer to a woman, girl, or female animal.

ex.en: I went in the room and told her I had something to say to her.
ex.zh: 我走进房间，告诉她我有话要对她说。

e.en: Her is also a possessive determiner.

ex.en: Liz travelled around the world for a year with her boyfriend James.
ex.zh: 莉兹跟她的男友詹姆斯到世界各地旅行了一年。

e.en: In written English, her is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use "him or her" or "them." 她 (有时在无需说明性别的情况下指人)

ex.en: Talk to your baby, play games, and show her how much you enjoy her company.
ex.zh: 跟你的婴儿谈话，玩游戏，向她表明你是多么喜欢与她在一起。

e.en: Her is also a possessive determiner.

ex.en: The non-drinking, non-smoking model should do nothing to risk her reputation.
ex.zh: 这名烟酒不沾的女模特儿不应该做任何对她的名誉不利的事情。

d: pron. 她（she的宾格）；她的（she的所有格）；她（指某个国家；一艘船）
n. （法）埃尔（人名）

e.en: If you say that something is ineffective, you mean that it has no effect on a process or situation.

ex.en: Economic reform will continue to be painful and ineffective.
ex.zh: 经济改革将仍是痛苦和不见效的。

d: adj. 无效果的，不起作用的；不能胜任的

e.en: Led is the past tense and past participle of lead. (lead)

d: v. 领导；通向；指引；导致（lead 的过去分词）
n. 约翰尼斯堡（位于南非东北部）

e.en: Mining is the industry and activities connected with getting valuable or useful minerals from the ground, for example coal, diamonds, or gold.

ex.en: ...traditional industries such as coal mining and steel making.
ex.zh: …像采煤和炼钢这样的传统工业。

d: n. 采矿，采矿业

e.en: A mark is a small area of something such as dirt that has accidentally got onto a surface or piece of clothing.

ex.en: The dogs are always rubbing against the wall and making dirty marks.
ex.zh: 这些狗总是往墙上蹭，留下了点点污斑。

e.en: If something marks a surface, or if the surface marks, the surface is damaged by marks or a mark. 玷污;

ex.en: Leather overshoes were put on the horses' hooves to stop them from marking the turf.
ex.zh: 皮套子被套在了马蹄上，防止它们弄脏了跑马场。

e.en: A mark is a written or printed symbol, for example a letter of the alphabet.

ex.en: He made marks with a pencil.
ex.zh: 他用铅笔作了记号。

e.en: If you mark something with a particular word or symbol, you write that word or symbol on it.

ex.en: The bank marks the cheque "certified."
ex.zh: 银行在支票上标有“保付”的字样。

ex.en: Mark them with a symbol.
ex.zh: 用个记号把他们标出来。

d: n. 痕迹，污点；标识，记号；印记，特征；（品质或情感的）标志，迹象；分数；水平，标准点；（后接数词）型号；燃气挡，温度刻度；（代替签名的）画押；目标，靶子；（比赛的）起点；容易受骗的人；（赛马）附加重量级；（业余英橄）截球后喊 "Mark"射门；马克（德国货币单位，合100芬尼）；马克（旧时西欧使用的金银重量单位）；波黑马克（波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维纳基本货币单位）；（尤指体育比赛的）最好成绩，纪录
v. 做记号，做标记；留下痕迹，弄污；标明方位，标示；分隔，标出（区域）；纪念，庆贺；表明，是……的迹象；成为……的特征；打分，评成绩；注意，留心；盯人防守，盯住（对手）；挑选，指定（mark sb. out for）；认定……为（某一类人）（mark sb. down as）；划掉，勾销；（澳橄）接球；（对人或物）造成永久性伤害
【名】 （Mark）马克（人名）

e.en: Mine is the first person singular possessive pronoun. A speaker or writer uses mine to refer to something that belongs or relates to himself or herself.

ex.en: Her right hand is inches from mine.
ex.zh: 她的右手离我的几英寸远。

ex.en: That wasn't his fault, it was mine.
ex.zh: 那不是他的错，是我的错。

e.en: A mine is a place where deep holes and tunnels are dug under the ground in order to obtain a mineral such as coal, diamonds, or gold.

ex.en: ...coal mines.
ex.zh: …煤矿。

e.en: a lucrative source or abundant supply 摇钱树 ;

ex.en: she was a mine of information

e.en: When a mineral such as coal, diamonds, or gold is mined, it is obtained from the ground by digging deep holes and tunnels.

ex.en: The pit is being shut down because it no longer has enough coal that can be mined economically.
ex.zh: 那个煤矿要关闭了，因为储量不足，难以经济开采。

d: pron. 我的；我的家
n. 矿，矿井；地雷，水雷；宝库，源泉；炸药坑道
v. 采（煤等矿物）；布雷，用雷炸毁（车辆）；寻找（某事物中）蕴含的价值；在（地下）挖洞（或坑道）；挖掘（数据）；挖矿（获取加密货币的勘探方式）
【名】 （Mine）（德、塞、土、毛里塔）米内（人名）

e.en: The meaning of a word, expression, or gesture is the thing or idea that it refers to or represents and which can be explained using other words.

ex.en: I hadn't a clue as to the meaning of "activism."
ex.zh: 我对的意思一无所知。

e.en: The meaning of what someone says or of something such as a book or film is the thoughts or ideas that are intended to be expressed by it.

ex.en: Unsure of the meaning of this remark, Ryle chose to remain silent.
ex.zh: 由于对这个评论的含义不确定，赖尔选择了保持沉默。

e.en: If an activity or action has meaning, it has a purpose and is worthwhile.

ex.en: Art has real meaning when it helps people to understand themselves.
ex.zh: 当艺术有助于人们了解自身时，才有真正的价值。

d: n. 意思，意义，含义；真正重要性，价值；原因
adj. 意味深长的
v. 表示……的意思，作……的解释；意味着；打算，意欲（mean 的现在分词形式）

e.en: The police are the official organization that is responsible for making sure that people obey the law.

ex.en: The police are also looking for a second car.
ex.zh: 警方也在寻找第二辆车。

ex.en: Police say they have arrested twenty people following the disturbances.
ex.zh: 警方称他们已经在骚乱后逮捕了20个人。

e.en: Police are men and women who are members of the official organization that is responsible for making sure that people obey the law.

ex.en: More than one hundred police have ringed the area.
ex.zh: 一百多名警察已经包围了这个地区。

e.en: If the police or military forces police an area or event, they make sure that law and order is preserved in that area or at that event.

ex.en: ...the tiny U.N. observer force whose job it is to police the border.
ex.zh: …维持边界治安的那一小支联合国观察部队。

e.en: If a person or group in authority polices a law or an area of public life, they make sure that what is done is fair and legal.

ex.en: ...the self-regulatory body that polices the investment management business.
ex.zh: …监督投资管理事务的自律机构。

d: n. 警察部门；警察
v. 巡查，维护治安；监督，管制；执行（法律，协议，条约）

e.en: The name of a person, place, or thing is the word or group of words that is used to identify them.

ex.en: "What's his name?"—"Peter."
ex.zh: “他叫什么名字？”—“彼得。”

ex.en: I don't even know if Sullivan's his real name.
ex.zh: 我甚至不知道沙利文是不是他的真名。

e.en: When you name someone or something, you give them a name, usually at the beginning of their life.

ex.en: My mother insisted on naming me Horace.
ex.zh: 我母亲执意给我取名叫霍勒斯。

ex.en: ...a man named John T. Benson.
ex.zh: …一个叫约翰·T·本森的男子。

e.en: If you name someone or something after another person or thing, you give them the same name as that person or thing. 以 (某人或某物的名字)

ex.en: Why haven't you named any of your sons after yourself?
ex.zh: 为什么你没用你名字给你儿子中的任何一个命名？

e.en: If you name someone, you identify them by stating their name.

ex.en: It's nearly thirty years since a journalist was jailed for refusing to name a source.
ex.zh: 一名记者因拒绝说出消息来源而入狱已近三十年了。

d: n. 名字，名称；名声，名誉；名人，有名的事物；（侮辱人的）绰号，别称；（英国）属劳埃德保险社辛迪加的承保人
v. 命名，给……取名；说出……的名称，叫出……的名字；说定，确定；任命，委任；（下议院议长）点名开除（立法委员会成员）的议员身份
adj. 有名的，出名的；姓名的，据以取名的
【名】 （Name）内姆（日）滑（姓）（人名）

e.en: September is the ninth month of the year in the Western calendar. 9

ex.en: Her son, Jerome, was born in September.
ex.zh: 她的儿子杰罗姆出生于9月。

ex.en: We didn't make the original September 30 release date.
ex.zh: 我们没有赶上原定9月30日的发行日。

d: n. 九月
n. 鲁德普特（南非城市名）

e.en: A shaft is a long vertical passage, for example, for a lift. (电梯等的)

ex.en: The fire began in a lift shaft and spread to the roof.
ex.zh: 大火从电梯通道里开始，然后蔓延到了屋顶。

e.en: In a machine, a shaft is a rod that turns around continually in order to transfer movement in the machine.

ex.en: ...a drive shaft.
ex.zh: …一根传动轴。

e.en: A shaft is a long thin piece of wood or metal that forms part of a spear, axe, golf club, or other object. 杆;

ex.en: ...golf clubs with steel shafts.
ex.zh: …带钢柄的高尔夫球棒。

e.en: A shaft of light is a beam of light, for example, sunlight shining through an opening. 一道 (光)

ex.en: A brilliant shaft of sunlight burst through the doorway.
ex.zh: 一道耀眼的阳光从门口照射进来。

d: n. shaft 的复数：（机械）轴，转轴，传动轴；（矿业、建筑）竖井，井道；（光的）束，道，缕；杆，柄，箭杆，车辕
v. shaft 的第三人称单数：（非正式）欺骗，亏待；装杆；用篙撑船

e.en: Someone's sight is their ability to see.

ex.en: My sight is failing, and I can't see to read any more.
ex.zh: 我的视力正在下降，不能再看书了。

e.en: The sight of something is the act of seeing it or an occasion on which you see it.

ex.en: I faint at the sight of blood.
ex.zh: 我一看见血就晕。

e.en: A sight is something that you see.

ex.en: The practice of hanging clothes across the street is a common sight in many parts of the city.
ex.zh: 在大街上晾晒衣服在该市的许多地区是很常见的景象。

e.en: If you sight someone or something, you suddenly see them, often briefly. (在一瞬间)

ex.en: The security forces sighted a group of young men that had crossed the border.
ex.zh: 安全部队在一瞬间突然看见了一群越过了边境的年轻人。

d: n. 视力，视觉；看见，见到；视野，视域；景物，景象；名胜，景点（sights）；志向，目标；（枪或炮上的）瞄准器，（光学仪器的）观测器； 奇怪的人，滑稽的人（或事物）； 许多，大量； 观点，见解
v. （突然）看到，（远远）看见；把（枪）瞄准；（用观测器）观测；调整（火器）的瞄准器，调整（光学仪器）的观测器
adj. 见票即付的；即席的

e.en: If the amount, value, level, or volume of something soars, it quickly increases by a great deal.

ex.en: Insurance claims are expected to soar.
ex.zh: 预计保险索赔会急剧增加。

ex.en: Shares soared on the New York stock exchange.
ex.zh: 纽约证券交易所股票暴涨。

e.en: If something such as a bird soars into the air, it goes quickly up into the air.

ex.en: If you're lucky, a splendid golden eagle may soar into view.
ex.zh: 幸运的话，一只金色雄鹰会跃入视线。

d: v. soar 的过去式和过去分词：急剧上升，飙升，骤然上升；高飞，翱翔；高耸，耸立；（引申）迅速成名，飞黄腾达。

e.en: You use since when you are mentioning a time or event in the past and indicating that a situation has continued from then until now. 自…以来;

ex.en: He's been in exile in India since 1959.
ex.zh: 他自1959年以来一直流亡印度。

ex.en: She had a sort of breakdown some years ago, and since then she has been very shy.
ex.zh: 她几年前曾遭遇精神崩溃，从那以后她一直怯生生的。

e.en: Since is also an adverb.

ex.en: They worked together in the 1960s, and have kept in contact ever since.
ex.zh: 他们在20世纪60年代曾一起工作，自那时起就一直保持着联系。

e.en: Since is also a conjunction.

ex.en: I've earned my own living since I was seven, doing all kinds of jobs.
ex.zh: 我自从7岁就自己谋生，做各种各样的工作。

e.en: You use since to mention a time or event in the past when you are describing an event or situation that has happened after that time.

ex.en: The percentage increase in reported crime this year is the highest since the war.
ex.zh: 今年报道的犯罪增长率是该战争以来最高的。

d: prep. 自……以后，自……以来；（表示气愤）何曾，什么时候
conj. 在……以后，自……以来；因为，由于，既然
adv. 自……以后，自……以来；此后，后来
n. （Since）（法、美）新斯（人名）

e.en: The south is the direction which is on your right when you are looking toward the direction where the sun rises.

ex.en: The town lies ten miles to the south of here.
ex.zh: 该镇位于这里以南10英里。

e.en: The south of a place, country, or region is the part which is in the south.

ex.en: ...vacations in the south of Mexico.
ex.zh: …在墨西哥南部的假期。

e.en: If you go south, you travel toward the south.

ex.en: I drove south on Motorway 9.
ex.zh: 我在9号高速公路上向南行驶。

e.en: Something that is south of a place is positioned to the south of it.

ex.en: They now own and operate a farm 50 miles south of Rochester.
ex.zh: 他们现在在罗彻斯特南部50英里处拥有并经营一个农场。

d: n. 南，（罗盘的）南方；（某个地方、国家、区域的）南部；美国南部各州，英格兰南部（the South）；（南半球的）发展中国家（the South）；（桥牌）坐在南首位置的人（South）
adj. 位于南方的，朝南的；（风）来自南方的；（用于国家、州或地区等的名称中）南部的，南部居民的
adv. 向南，朝南；去南方，在南方；低于（south of）；下滑，恶化
v. 向南方，朝南；（天体）穿过子午线

e.en: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it. 开始 (做某事)

ex.en: John then unlocked the front door and I started to follow him up the stairs.
ex.zh: 接着约翰打开前门，我开始随他上楼。

ex.en: It was 1956 when Susanna started the work on the garden.
ex.zh: 苏珊娜是在1956年开始修建那个花园的。

e.en: Start is also a noun.

ex.en: After several starts, she read the report properly.
ex.zh: 几次起头之后，她正确地读了那份报告。

e.en: When something starts, or if someone starts it, it takes place from a particular time. 使开始发生;

ex.en: The fire is thought to have started in an upstairs room.
ex.zh: 这火被认为是从楼上的一间房开始的。

ex.en: All of the passengers started the day with a swim.
ex.zh: 所有乘客都以游泳开始了这一天。

e.en: Start is also a noun.

ex.en: ...1918, four years after the start of the Great War.
ex.zh: …第一次世界大战开始4年后的1918年。

d: v. 开始，着手；使发生，引发；开动，发动（机器）；创立，创始，开办；出发，启程（start 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: In the United States and Canada, a township is an area of land, especially a part of a county which is organized as a unit of local government. (美国和加拿大的)

ex.en: ...her 20 years of service with the township and county.
ex.zh: ...她为镇区和郡服务的20年。

e.en: In South Africa, a township was a town where only black people lived. (在南非只有黑人居住的)

ex.en: ...the South African township of Soweto.
ex.zh: ...南非的索韦托镇。

d: 镇区
小镇
六英里见方的地区（township 的名词复数）

e.en: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave toward them or deal with them in that way. 对待;

ex.en: Artie treated most women with indifference.
ex.zh: 阿蒂对待大多数女性颇为冷淡。

ex.en: Police say they're treating it as a case of attempted murder.
ex.zh: 警方说他们正将其作为谋杀未遂案件来处理。

e.en: When a doctor or nurse treats a patient or an illness, he or she tries to make the patient well again.

ex.en: Doctors treated her with aspirin.
ex.zh: 医生用阿斯匹林给她治疗。

ex.en: The boy was treated for a minor head wound.
ex.zh: 那个男孩因头部轻伤而接受治疗。

e.en: If something is treated with a particular substance, the substance is put onto or into it in order to clean it, to protect it, or to give it special properties. (用某种物质)

ex.en: About 70% of the cocoa acreage is treated with insecticide.
ex.zh: 大约70%的可可豆种植区都用杀虫剂处理过。

e.en: If you treat someone to something special which they will enjoy, you buy it or arrange it for them.

ex.en: She was always treating him to ice cream.
ex.zh: 她总请他吃冰淇淋。

ex.en: Tomorrow I'll treat myself to a day's gardening.
ex.zh: 明天我要好好享受一天的园艺活儿。

d: v. treat 的现在分词／动名词；对待；处理；（化工）处理；（医学）治疗
n. （化工）处理

e.en: The west is the direction you look toward in the evening in order to see the sun set.

ex.en: I pushed on toward Flagstaff, a hundred miles to the west.
ex.zh: 我继续向西边100英里处的弗拉格斯塔夫市前进。

e.en: The west of a place, country, or region is the part of it which is in the west.

ex.en: Many of the buildings in the west of the city are on fire.
ex.zh: 该城西部的许多建筑都着火了。

e.en: If you go west, you travel toward the west.

ex.en: We are going west to California.
ex.zh: 我们将往西去加利福尼亚。

e.en: Something that is west of a place is positioned to the west of it. …

ex.en: Penryn is about 60 miles west of Philadelphia.
ex.zh: 彭林位于费城以西60英里的地方。

d: n. 西，西方；（某个国家、地区或地方的）西部；西方国家 (指美国、加拿大以及西欧、北欧和南欧诸国)（the West)；（美国）西部（尤指密西西比河以西诸州）(the West, the west)；西方（国家）（与东欧前共产主义国家相对的欧洲和北美洲的非共产主义国家）（the West)；（桥牌）坐在西首位置的人
adj. 西方的,向西的；（风）来自西方的；（用于国家、州和地区的名称中）西部的
adv. 向西方，朝西方；……以西
【名】 （West）（英、德、芬、瑞典）韦斯特（人名）
n. 梵谷水郡；扎马（北非古城）；座间

e.en: A Zulu is a member of a race of black people who live in Southern Africa. (南非)
Zulu is the language spoken by Zulus and also by many other black South Africans.

d: n. 祖鲁人；祖鲁语
adj. 祖鲁人的
n. 梵谷水郡；扎马（北非古城）；座间
v. fuel 的现在分词／动名词（英式拼写），意为给……加油或加燃料；引申为推动，加剧，助长
n. 拉娜（Helen 的异体）；羊毛

e.en: A paramilitary organization is organized like an army and performs either civil or military functions in a country. (组织)

ex.en: Searches by the army and paramilitary forces have continued today.
ex.zh: 军队和准军事部队的搜索今天仍然继续着。

e.en: Paramilitaries are members of a paramilitary organization.

ex.en: Paramilitaries and army recruits patrolled the village.
ex.zh: 准军事组织成员和部队的新兵在村子里巡逻。

e.en: A paramilitary organization is an illegal group that is organized like an army.

ex.en: ...a law which said that all paramilitary groups must be disarmed.
ex.zh: …一个要求所有非法军事组织必须解除武装的法律。

e.en: Paramilitaries are members of an illegal paramilitary organization.

ex.en: Paramilitaries were blamed for the shooting.
ex.zh: 非法军事组织成员因为这次开枪事件而遭谴责。

d: adj. 准军事的，辅助军事的
n. 准军事部队，准军事组织；（常用复数）准军事组织成员

e.en: If you make an accusation against someone, you criticize them or express the belief that they have done something wrong.

ex.en: Kim rejects accusations that country music is over-sentimental.
ex.zh: 金姆反驳了那些说乡村音乐过于伤感的指责。

e.en: An accusation is a statement or claim by a witness or someone in authority that a particular person has committed a crime, although this has not yet been proved.

ex.en: ...people who have made public accusations of rape.
ex.zh: …对强奸进行了公开指控的人们。

d: n. （accusation 的复数）指控，控告；指责，谴责
n. 苏丹（非洲国家）；苏丹地区（非洲北部历史地理区域，位于撒哈拉沙漠以南，西起大西洋沿岸，东至红海，常作 the Sudan）

e.en: A denial of something is a statement that it is not true, does not exist, or did not happen.

ex.en: It seems clear that despite official denials, differences of opinion lay behind the ambassador's decision to quit.
ex.zh: 很清楚，尽管官方否认，人们对大使决定辞职还是有不同看法。

e.en: The denial of something to someone is the act of refusing to let them have it.

ex.en: ...the denial of visas to international relief workers.
ex.zh: …对国际救济工作人员拒发签证。

e.en: In psychology, denial is when a person cannot or will not accept an unpleasant truth. (不愉快事实的)

ex.en: With major life traumas, like losing a loved one, for instance, the mind's first reaction is denial.
ex.zh: 面对人生的重大创痛，例如失去深爱的人，心理的第一反应就是拒绝接受。

d: n. 否认；拒绝接受，拒不承认；剥夺，拒绝给予
n. 候选人资格，候选人身份（同 candidacy，主要见于英式英语）

e.en: Ants are small crawling insects that live in large groups.

ex.en: Ants swarmed up out of the ground and covered her shoes and legs.
ex.zh: 蚂蚁从地里成群地爬出来，爬满了她的鞋和腿。

d: n. 蚂蚁；Ant（人名，土耳其、芬兰人名译作“安特”）

e.en: Arabs are people who speak Arabic and who come from the Middle East and parts of North Africa.
Arab means belonging or relating to Arabs or to their countries or customs. 阿拉伯的;

ex.en: On the surface, it appears little has changed in the Arab world.
ex.zh: 表面上，似乎阿拉伯世界没有什么变化。

d: adj. 阿拉伯的
n. 阿拉伯人；阿拉伯马

e.en: In a movie or play, a supporting actor or actress is one who has an important part, but not the most important part. (演员)

ex.en: ...the winner of the best supporting actress award.
ex.zh: ...最佳女配角奖获得者。

d: adj. 配角的，次要的；支持的，辅助性的，配套的；能确证的，佐证的；承重的，支承的
v. 支持；供养（support 的现在分词）
abbr. 阿拉伯联合酋长国（United Arab Emirates）

e.en: A war is a period of fighting or conflict between countries or states.

ex.en: He spent part of the war in the National Guard.
ex.zh: 他战时在国民警卫队服役了一段时间。

ex.en: ...matters of war and peace.
ex.zh: …战争与和平的问题。

e.en: War is intense economic competition between countries or organizations.

ex.en: The most important thing is to reach an agreement and to avoid a trade war.
ex.zh: 最重要的就是达成协议，避免贸易战。

e.en: If you make war on someone or something that you are opposed to, you do things to stop them from succeeding.

ex.en: She has been involved in the war against organized crime.
ex.zh: 她参与了打击有组织犯罪的斗争。

e.en: If a country goes to war, it starts fighting a war.

ex.en: Do you think this crisis can be settled without going to war?
ex.zh: 你认为不发动战争就能解决这场危机吗？

d: n. 战争，战争状态；竞争，斗争，对抗；（为消灭有害事物的）长期斗争，顽强抵御；舌战，论战；军事，战术
v. 进行战争，斗争

e.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

ex.en: German leaders all took the opportunity to denounce the attacks and plead for tolerance.
ex.zh: 德国领导人们都藉此机会谴责这些攻击，并且恳请宽容。

e.en: If you denounce someone who has broken a rule or law, you report them to the authorities.

ex.en: They were at the mercy of informers who might at any moment denounce them.
ex.zh: 他们完全受那些随时可能告发他们的告密者的支配。

d: v. （denounce 的过去式和过去分词）公开谴责，抨击；向当局告发，揭发；正式声明（条约、协议等）废止或无效
adj. 公开抨击的，受谴责的（denounce 的过去分词）

e.en: A critic is a person who writes about and expresses opinions about things such as books, movies, music, or art.

ex.en: Mather was a film critic for many years.
ex.zh: 马瑟做过多年的电影评论家。

e.en: Someone who is a critic of a person or system disapproves of them and criticizes them publicly.

ex.en: The newspaper has been one of the most consistent critics ever of the government.
ex.zh: 该报纸是政府最坚持的批评者之一。

d: n. 评论家；批评者；吹毛求疵的人（critic 的复数）

e.en: If you cite something, you quote it or mention it, especially as an example or proof of what you are saying.

ex.en: She cites a favourite poem by George Herbert.
ex.zh: 她引用了一首她所喜爱的乔治·赫伯特的诗。

ex.en: Domestic interest rates are often cited as a major factor affecting exchange rates.
ex.zh: 国内利率常常被援引为影响汇率的一个主要因素。

e.en: To cite a person means to officially name them in a legal case. To cite a reason or cause means to state it as the official reason for your case.

ex.en: They cited Alex's refusal to return to the marital home.
ex.zh: 他们援引了亚历克斯拒绝重返婚后住所这一事实为证。

e.en: If someone is cited, they are officially ordered to appear before a court.

ex.en: He is the owner of a restaurant chain that was cited for violations of child labour laws.
ex.zh: 他是那个因违反童工法而被传讯的餐饮连锁店的业主。
