e.en: If a judge cites someone, he or she officially names them in a critical way in court.

ex.en: The judge ruled a mistrial and cited the prosecutors for outrageous misconduct.
ex.zh: 法官裁定判决无效并且指控控方有极其不端的行为。

d: v. 引用，引证（cite 的现在分词）；援引（理由、原因），以……为由

e.en: People who come from a particular nation, or whose ancestors came from it, but who now live in many different parts of the world are sometimes referred to as the diaspora.

ex.en: ...the history of peoples from the African diaspora.
ex.zh: ...非洲大移居人民的历史。

d: n. （犹太人的）大流散（the diaspora）；（住在以色列之外的）海外犹太人；（任何民族的）大移居；流散人口

e.en: If you cite something, you quote it or mention it, especially as an example or proof of what you are saying.

ex.en: She cites a favourite poem by George Herbert.
ex.zh: 她引用了一首她所喜爱的乔治·赫伯特的诗。

ex.en: Domestic interest rates are often cited as a major factor affecting exchange rates.
ex.zh: 国内利率常常被援引为影响汇率的一个主要因素。

e.en: To cite a person means to officially name them in a legal case. To cite a reason or cause means to state it as the official reason for your case.

ex.en: They cited Alex's refusal to return to the marital home.
ex.zh: 他们援引了亚历克斯拒绝重返婚后住所这一事实为证。

e.en: If someone is cited, they are officially ordered to appear before a court.

ex.en: He is the owner of a restaurant chain that was cited for violations of child labour laws.
ex.zh: 他是那个因违反童工法而被传讯的餐饮连锁店的业主。

e.en: If a judge cites someone, he or she officially names them in a critical way in court.

ex.en: The judge ruled a mistrial and cited the prosecutors for outrageous misconduct.
ex.zh: 法官裁定判决无效并且指控控方有极其不端的行为。

d: v. 引用，援引；引证，引以为例；传唤，传讯；嘉奖，表彰
n. 引用，引文

e.en: A diplomat is a senior official who discusses affairs with another country on behalf of his or her own country, usually working as a member of an embassy.

ex.en: ...a Western diplomat with long experience in Asia.
ex.zh: …一名在亚洲有长期经验的西方外交官。

d: n. 外交官，外交家；有手腕的人，善交际的人
五年的

e.en: A general is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, usually in the army.

ex.en: The General's visit to Sarajevo is part of preparations for the deployment of extra troops.
ex.zh: 那位将军对萨拉热窝的访问是为部署更多军队所做的准备工作的一部分。

e.en: If you talk about the general situation somewhere or talk about something in general terms, you are describing the situation as a whole rather than considering its details or exceptions.

ex.en: The figures represent a general decline in employment.
ex.zh: 这些数字表明就业率的总体下降。

ex.en: ...a general deterioration in the quality of life.
ex.zh: …生活质量的总体下降。

e.en: If you describe something in general terms, you describe it without giving details.
You use general to describe several items or activities when there are too many of them or when they are not important enough to mention separately.

ex.en: $2,500 for software is soon swallowed up in general costs.
ex.zh: 用于软件的$2500很快被各种花销耗尽了。

d: adj. 总体的，普遍的；一般的，常规的；大致的，大概的；综合的，广泛的；首席的，总管的
n. 上将，将军；半军事化管理的宗教组织（如耶稣会修士、多明我会修士或救世军）的领袖；大众，公众
【名】 （General）（英）杰纳勒尔（人名）

e.en: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.

ex.en: As soon as he'd finished eating, he excused himself.
ex.zh: 他一吃完就借口离开了。

ex.en: Mr. Gould was given a standing ovation and loud cheers when he finished his speech.
ex.zh: 古尔德先生结束他的演讲时观众起立为他鼓掌并大声欢呼。

e.en: Finish up means the same as .

ex.en: We waited a few minutes outside his office while he finished up his meeting.
ex.zh: 我们在他办公室外面等了几分钟，这时他结束了他的会议。

e.en: When you finish something that you are making or producing, you reach the end of making or producing it, so that it is complete.

ex.en: The consultants had been working to finish a report this week.
ex.zh: 顾问们一直在争取于本周完成一份报告。

e.en: Finish off and finish up mean the same as .

ex.en: Now she is busy finishing off a biography of Queen Caroline.
ex.zh: 现在她正忙于完成卡罗琳女王的传记。

d: n. 成品，制成品；抛光剂，罩面漆，表面饰面材料（finish 的复数）
v. 完成，结束，做完（finish 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If someone forces you to do something, they make you do it even though you do not want to, for example, by threatening you.

ex.en: He took two women hostage and forced them to drive away from the area.
ex.zh: 他劫持了两名女人质并强迫她们开车离开这个地区。

ex.en: They were grabbed by three men who appeared to force them into a car.
ex.zh: 他们被三名男子抓住，这些人看上去强使他们进入了一辆汽车。

e.en: If a situation or event forces you to do something, it makes it necessary for you to do something that you would not otherwise have done.

ex.en: A back injury forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon.
ex.zh: 一处背伤迫使她退出了温布尔登网球赛。

ex.en: He turned right, down a dirt road that forced him into four-wheel drive.
ex.zh: 他向右转弯，开上了一条土路，这迫使他开始四轮驱动行驶。

e.en: If someone forces something on or upon you, they make you accept or use it when you would prefer not to.

ex.en: To force this agreement on the nation is wrong.
ex.zh: 把这项协议强加于这个国家是错误的。

e.en: If you force something into a particular position, you use a lot of strength to make it move there.

ex.en: They were forcing her head under the icy waters, drowning her.
ex.zh: 他们在用力把她的头按到冰冷的水中，淹她。

d: n. 势力，力量，有影响力的人或事物；武装力量，军队，部队；（物理学）力，作用力（force 的复数）
v. 迫使，强迫；强加，强行打开，强行进入；催熟，人工促长（force 的第三人称单数）
adj. 阿联酋的，阿拉伯联合酋长国的
n. 阿联酋人，阿拉伯联合酋长国人

e.en: An emirate is a country that is ruled by an emir.
Human means relating to or concerning people. 人 (类)

ex.en: ...the human body.
ex.zh: …人体。

e.en: You can refer to people as humans, especially when you are comparing them with animals or machines. 人 (类)

ex.en: Like humans, cats and dogs are omnivores.
ex.zh: 和人类一样，猫和狗是杂食性动物。

e.en: Human feelings, weaknesses, or errors are ones that are typical of humans rather than machines. 人的 (感情、弱点); 人为的 (错误)

ex.en: ...an ever-growing risk of human error.
ex.zh: …一种日益增长的人为误差的风险。

d: adj. 人的，人类的；（尤指缺点或弱点）显示人的本性的；有人情味的
n. 人，人类
【名】 （Human）（英）休曼（人名）

e.en: International means between or involving different countries.

ex.en: ...an international agreement against exporting arms to that country.
ex.zh: …一项禁止向那个国家出口武器的国际协议。

e.en: 国际上

ex.en: ...internationally agreed-upon rules.
ex.zh: …国际上公认的章程。

d: adj. 国际的，国际上的
n. 国际比赛；国际比赛选手；外国人；共产国际（International）；国际组织，跨国公司

e.en: You use his to indicate that something belongs or relates to a man, boy, or male animal. 他的; 它的 (指雄性动物)

ex.en: Brian splashed water on his face, then brushed his teeth.
ex.zh: 布赖恩用水拍洗了脸，然后刷了牙。

ex.en: He spent a large part of his career in Hollywood.
ex.zh: 他职业生涯中的大部分时间是在好莱坞度过的。

e.en: His is also a possessive pronoun. 他的 (也作物主代词)

ex.en: Staff say the decision was his.
ex.zh: 员工们说那个决定是他做出的。

d: det. 他的，它的（指雄性动物）
pron. 他的
n. （Guterres）人名；（葡）古特雷斯

e.en: A job is the work that someone does to earn money.

ex.en: Once I'm in Miami I can get a job.
ex.zh: 一旦我到了迈阿密就能找到工作。

ex.en: Thousands have lost their jobs.
ex.zh: 数千人都丢了工作。

e.en: A job is a particular task.

ex.en: He said he hoped that the job of putting together a coalition wouldn't take too much time.
ex.zh: 他说他希望结成联盟这项任务不会花太长时间。

e.en: The job of a particular person or thing is their duty or function.

ex.en: Their main job is to preserve health rather than treat illness.
ex.zh: 他们的主要职责是保健而不是治病。

ex.en: His first job will be to try and get talks going between the two sides.
ex.zh: 他的首要职责将是设法让双方的谈话进行下去。

e.en: If you say that someone is doing a good job, you mean that they are doing something well.

ex.en: We could do a far better job of managing it than they have.
ex.zh: 我们会比他们管理得好得多。

d: n. 工作，职业；零工，任务；职责，责任；罪行，（尤指）盗窃； 东西，物件；费力的事；幸运的事；刺，捅；东西，物件
v. 刺，捅；（尤指经纪人小规模操作）买卖股票；欺骗，出卖；假公济私，营私舞弊
【名】 （Job）（英）乔布，（法、葡）若布，(?-1605)约伯俄罗斯正教会莫斯科牧首，（德、塞、捷、荷、意）约布（人名)

e.en: A member of a group is one of the people, animals, or things belonging to that group. (某群体的)

ex.en: He refused to name the members of staff involved.
ex.zh: 他拒绝说出所涉职员的名字。

ex.en: Their lack of training could put members of the public at risk.
ex.zh: 他们训练的缺乏会使公众成员面临风险。

e.en: A member of an organization such as a club or a political party is a person who has officially joined the organization. 会员;

ex.en: The support of our members is of great importance to the association.
ex.zh: 我们会员的支持对协会来说非常重要。

e.en: A member country or member state is one of the countries that has joined an international organization or group.

ex.en: ...the member countries of the North American Free Trade Association.
ex.zh: …北美自由贸易联盟的会员国。

e.en: A member or Member is a person who has been elected to a legislature or parliament.

ex.en: He was elected to Parliament as the Member for Leeds.
ex.zh: 他被选入国会作为利兹市的议员。

d: n. （社团、政党等组织的）成员，会员；（某群体或类别中的）一分子（可指人、动物、植物或事物）；（常大写 Member）议员；（加入国际组织的）成员国，会员国；（尤指最低级的）勋章获得者；（复杂设备或结构的）构件；（句子的）成分；member 的复数形式；（Members）墨姆伯尔（人名）
abbr. 网络接口对象（java的一种技术，Network Interface Object）；国立海洋学研究所（National Institute of Oceanography ）;上海蔚来汽车有限公司

e.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it. (为工作、职位)

ex.en: This week one of them will be nominated by the Democratic Party for the presidency of the United States.
ex.zh: 本周他们中的一人将被民主党提名为美国总统职位的候选人。

ex.en: The Security Council can nominate anyone for secretary-general.
ex.zh: 安全理事会可以提名任何人为秘书长。

e.en: If you nominate someone to a job or position, you formally choose them to hold that job or position.

ex.en: In 1967 Johnson nominated Thurgood Marshall to the Supreme Court.
ex.zh: 1967年，约翰逊任命瑟古德·马歇尔为最高法院法官。

ex.en: She was nominated by the president as ambassador to Barbados.
ex.zh: 她被总统任命为驻巴巴多斯大使。

e.en: If someone or something such as an actor or a film is nominated for an award, someone formally suggests that they should be given that award. (某人或某物) 被提名 (某奖项)

ex.en: Practically every film he made was nominated for an Oscar.
ex.zh: 他制作的每部电影几乎都获得了奥斯卡提名。

d: adj. 被提名的；被任命的；被指定的
v. 提名；任命；指定（nominate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you monitor something, you regularly check its development or progress, and sometimes comment on it.

ex.en: Officials had not been allowed to monitor the voting.
ex.zh: 官员们未曾获许监控选举。

e.en: If someone monitors radio broadcasts from other countries, they record them or listen carefully to them in order to obtain information.

ex.en: Peter Murray is in Washington and has been monitoring reports out of Monrovia.
ex.zh: 彼得·默里在华盛顿，一直监听来自蒙罗维亚的报道。

e.en: A monitor is a machine that is used to check or record things, for example processes or substances inside a person's body.

ex.en: The heart monitor shows low levels of consciousness.
ex.zh: 心脏监控器显示低意识水平。

e.en: A monitor is a screen which is used to display certain kinds of information, for example on a computer, in airports, or in television studios.

ex.en: He was watching a game of tennis on a television monitor.
ex.zh: 他那时正在电视监控器上观看一场网球赛。

d: n. 显示器，监视器，监控器；监视仪，监护仪，监测器；监督员，监察员，班长（monitor 的复数）
v. 监视，监测，监控；监听（外国广播或电话）；监控（无线电或电视传输信号）（monitor 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A race is a competition to see who is the fastest, for example in running, swimming, or driving. (速度的)

ex.en: The women's race was won by the only American in the field, Patti Sue Plumer.
ex.zh: 女子赛跑被田赛场上惟一的一名美国人帕蒂·休·普卢默赢得了。

e.en: If you race, you take part in a race. 参赛;

ex.en: In the 10 years I raced in Europe, 30 drivers were killed.
ex.zh: 我在欧洲参赛的10年间，有30名车手身亡。

ex.en: We raced them to the summit.
ex.zh: 我们和他们一路赛跑到最高点。

e.en: The races are a series of horse races that are held in a particular place on a particular day. People go to watch and to bet on which horse will win.

ex.en: The high point of this trip was a day at the races.
ex.zh: 这次旅行的高潮是在赛马会上度过的一天。

e.en: A race is a situation in which people or organizations compete with each other for power or control.

ex.en: The race for the White House begins in earnest today.
ex.zh: 为入主白宫而展开的竞选今天正式开始。

d: n. 赛跑，速度竞赛；竞争，角逐；赛马会（the races）；人种，种族；民族；（动植物）种，属；（具有共同特征的）一群（或一批）人（或物）；急流；沟槽，通道；血统，门第
v.  （和……）比赛，参加比赛；使（动物或车辆）参赛参赛；（使）快速移动，快速运转；疾走，全速行进；竞相，赶（时间）；（因害怕、兴奋而）急速跳动，快速转动；（发动机）猛转
【名】 （Race）（英）雷斯，（塞）拉采（人名）
abbr. 共和新芬党（Republican Sinn Féin）；无国界记者（Reporters Without Borders）

e.en: A rapid change is one that happens very quickly. (变化)

ex.en: ...the country's rapid economic growth in the 1980s.
ex.zh: …这个国家在20世纪80年代快速的经济增长。

e.en: 快速地

ex.en: ...countries with rapidly growing populations.
ex.zh: …人口快速增长的国家。

ex.en: Try to rip it apart as rapidly as possible.
ex.zh: 试着尽快把它撕开。

e.en: A rapid movement is one that is very fast. (动作)

ex.en: He walked at a rapid pace along Charles Street.
ex.zh: 他沿着查尔斯大街快步行走。

e.en: 迅速地

ex.en: He was moving rapidly around the room.
ex.zh: 他正在房间里快速地来回走着。

d: adj. 快的，迅速的；（移动，活动）快速的
n. 急流，湍滩；高速交通工具，高速交通网

e.en: If one thing or person replaces another, the first is used or acts instead of the second. 代替;

ex.en: One species of tree replaces another as a forest ages.
ex.zh: 随着森林老化，一种树会取代另一种树。

ex.en: ...the lawyer who replaced Robert as chairman of the company.
ex.zh: …取代罗伯特成为公司主席的那位律师。

e.en: If you replace one thing or person with another, you put something or someone else in their place to do their job. 用…代替;

ex.en: I clean out all the grease and replace it with oil so it works better in very low temperatures.
ex.zh: 我清除掉了所有的油脂，以油替换，因此它在很低的温度下运转得更好。

e.en: If you replace something that is broken, damaged, or lost, you get a new one to use instead. 换下 (坏的); 换上 (新的)

ex.en: The shower that we put in a few years back has broken and we cannot afford to replace it.
ex.zh: 我们几年前安装的淋浴器坏了，但没钱换新的。

e.en: If you replace something, you put it back where it was before.

ex.en: Replace the caps on the bottles.
ex.zh: 把瓶盖盖回到瓶子上。

d: v. 取代；（用……）替换，（以……）接替；更换， 赔还；把......放回原处

e.en: A secretary is a person who is employed to do office work, such as typing letters, answering phone calls, and arranging meetings.
The secretary of a company is the person who has the legal duty of keeping the company's records. (公司负责保管各种记录的)
Secretary is used in the titles of high officials who are in charge of main government departments. 大臣;

ex.en: ...a former Venezuelan foreign secretary.
ex.zh: …一位前任委内瑞拉外交部长。

d: n. 秘书；书记员，干事；部长，大臣；（英国大使、大臣的）助理

e.en: If something is right, it is correct and agrees with the facts.

ex.en: That's absolutely right.
ex.zh: 那是完全正确的。

ex.en: Clocks never told the right time.
ex.zh: 时钟从来都不报正确的时间。

e.en: Right is also an adverb.

ex.en: He guessed right about some things.
ex.zh: 他对有些事情猜对了。

e.en: If you do something in the right way or in the right place, you do it as or where it should be done or was planned to be done. 适当的;

ex.en: Walking, done in the right way, is a form of aerobic exercise.
ex.zh: 走路方法得当的话是一种有氧锻炼。

ex.en: They have computerized systems to ensure delivery of the right pizza to the right place.
ex.zh: 他们有计算机化的系统来确保把相应的比萨饼送到相应的地方。

e.en: Right is also an adverb. 适当地;

ex.en: To make sure I did everything right, I bought a fat instruction book.
ex.zh: 为了确保每件事情都做对，我买了一本厚厚的说明书。

d: n. （法）权利；权限；（对作品、财产等的）使用权、开发权；（金融）认股权

e.en: If you support someone or their ideas or aims, you agree with them, and perhaps help them because you want them to succeed.

ex.en: The vice president insisted that he supported the hard-working people of New York.
ex.zh: 副总统坚持认为他支持勤劳的纽约人民。

e.en: Support is also a noun.

ex.en: The president gave his full support to the reforms.
ex.zh: 该总统对改革予以了全力的支持。

e.en: If you give support to someone during a difficult or unhappy time, you are kind to them and help them. (给处境困难或不幸者的)

ex.en: It was hard to come to terms with her death after all the support she gave to me and the family.
ex.zh: 她曾给我和这个家庭很大的帮助，她的去世让人难以接受。

e.en: Financial support is money provided to enable an organization to continue. (给组织的)

ex.en: State agencies continue to cut budgets and support to a number of organizations.
ex.zh: 国家机关继续削减对一些组织的预算和资助。

d: v. 支持，拥护，鼓励；帮助，援助；支撑，承受（人或建筑物等的重量）；供养，赡养；资助，赞助；追随（或支持）（某个运动队）；证实，确认；（计算机，操作系统）支持（程序，语言，装置的）运行 ；支持……的生存；忍受，容忍；（在流行音乐会上）当助演，担任演出嘉宾；支付……费用，（尤指）用钱维持（不良嗜好，如毒品）；胜任
n. 支持，拥护；帮助，援助；赞助，资助；支撑物，支柱；（身体部位的）支持器，托；支撑，支承；（音乐会、演出的）助演演员，助演乐队；证实，证明；信息供应，信息支持；（战争中的）支援；抚养，供养；支持者，拥护者

e.en: Sudanese means belonging or relating to Sudan, or to its people or culture. 苏丹人的; 苏丹的;
The Sudanese are the people of Sudan.

d: adj. 苏丹的；苏丹人的
n. 苏丹人

e.en: If you talk about something in terms of something or in particular terms, you are specifying which aspect of it you are discussing or from what point of view you are considering it.

ex.en: Our goods compete in terms of product quality, reliability and above all variety.
ex.zh: 我们的产品从质量、可靠性、尤其是多样性来看很有竞争力。

e.en: If you say something in particular terms, you say it using a particular type or level of language or using language which clearly shows your attitude.

ex.en: The video explains in simple terms how the new tax works.
ex.zh: 该录像以浅显易懂的语言解释了新税法的运作方式。

e.en: A term is a word or expression with a specific meaning, especially one which is used in relation to a particular subject.

ex.en: Myocardial infarction is the medical term for a heart attack.
ex.zh: 心肌梗塞是心脏病发作的医学术语。

e.en: If you say that something is termed a particular thing, you mean that that is what people call it or that is their opinion of it.

ex.en: He had been termed a temporary employee.
ex.zh: 他曾被称为临时工。

d: n. 词语，术语；措辞（terms）；学期，开庭期；期限，任期；到期，期满；方面，角度（terms）；条件，条款（terms）；（人们之间的）关系（terms）；（数列、方程等的）项；（三段论中的）项；（建筑）界标
v. 把……称为

e.en: When people are united about something, they agree about it and act together.

ex.en: The entire Brazilian people are united by their love of football.
ex.zh: 整个巴西民族由其对足球的热爱团结在一起。

e.en: United is used to describe a country which has been formed from two or more states or countries.

ex.en: ...the first elections to be held in a united Germany for fifty eight years.
ex.zh: …在统一的德国将举行58年来的第一次竞选。

d: adj. 团结的，统一的；共同的，一致的；联队（用于某些足球队名）；（国家）统一的，合并的
v. （使）联合，（使）团结（unite 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: The top of something is its highest point or part.

ex.en: I waited at the top of the stairs.
ex.zh: 我在楼梯顶端上等着。

ex.en: ...the picture at the top of the page.
ex.zh: …页端的图片。

e.en: Top is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...the top corner of the newspaper.
ex.zh: …报纸顶端的一角。

e.en: The top thing or layer in a series of things or layers is the highest one.

ex.en: I can't reach the top shelf.
ex.zh: 我够不着最上面的架子。

e.en: The top of something such as a bottle, jar, or tube is a cap, lid, or other device that fits or screws onto one end of it. (瓶、罐或软管等的)

ex.en: ...the plastic tops from soda bottles.
ex.zh: …汽水瓶的塑料盖。

d: n. 顶部，顶端，上端；上层表面；最高的级别，最重要的职位；尽头，远端；帽，盖，塞；上衣，上装；（根菜作物的）茎叶；陀螺；特别好的人（或事）（tops）；（用于款额后）最高额（tops）；开始，开端；（棒球比赛的）前半局；（球的）上旋（topspin 的简称）；（待纺的）毛条；（物理）夸克六味之一；用于马蹄螺的名字
adj. 顶端的，顶部的，最上面的；（地位、程度或重要性）最高的；很好的，顶呱呱的；（距说话者、参照点）最远的
v. 高于，超过，高过；优于，胜过；居……之首，为……之冠；覆盖，放在……的上面；到达山顶，达到顶端；杀；切除顶部；（作为主要表演者，受关注者而）出场，露面；（高尔夫）误击（球上部）
adv. 最多，至多（tops）

e.en: If you upend something, you turn it upside down.

ex.en: He upended the beer, and swallowed.
ex.zh: 他把啤酒倒出来，大口喝了。

d: v. upend 的现在分词：1. 颠倒，倒置：使某物翻转到底部朝上或处于相反位置；2. 彻底改变，颠覆：使某事物的秩序、结构或平衡发生根本性改变。
n. upend 的动名词或名词用法：指颠倒、倒置或彻底颠覆体系的行为、事例或结果，常用于 the upending of ... 结构。

e.en: The chief of an organization is the person who is in charge of it.

ex.en: ...a commission appointed by the police chief.
ex.zh: …由警察局长任命的委员会。

e.en: The chief of a tribe is its leader. (部落)

ex.en: ...Sitting Bull, chief of the Sioux tribes of the Great Plains.
ex.zh: …大平原苏人部落的首领西延·布尔。

e.en: Chief is used in the job titles of the most senior worker or workers of a particular kind in an organization.

ex.en: ...the chief test pilot.
ex.zh: …首席试飞员。

e.en: The chief cause, part, or member of something is the most important one.

ex.en: Financial stress is well established as a chief reason for divorce.
ex.zh: 经济压力被充分证实为导致离婚的一个首要因素。

d: adj. 首要的，主要的；为首的，首席的
n. 领袖，首领；酋长；（纹章）上段（盾徽顶部的宽横带）
adv. 主要地；首要地

e.en: If you describe a situation or task as unenviable, you mean that nobody would enjoy dealing with it because it is very difficult, dangerous, or unpleasant. 困难的; 危险的;

ex.en: She had the unenviable task of making the first few phone calls.
ex.zh: 她的不愉快的任务是打头几个电话。

d: adj. 不值得羡慕的，不值得嫉妒的

e.en: Someone's successor is the person who takes their job after they have left.

ex.en: He set out several principles that he hopes will guide his successors.
ex.zh: 他制定出了几条原则,希望能指导其继任者。

d: n. 继承者，接替的事物；（组织、机器等的）接替物

e.en: European Central Bank

d: abbr. 欧洲中央银行（European Central Bank）；电子部件局（Electronic Components Board）；事件控制块，事件控制信息组（Event Control Block）；环境保护局（Environ-mental Conservation Board）

e.en: You use despite to introduce a fact which makes the other part of the sentence surprising.

ex.en: She has been under house arrest for most of the past decade, despite efforts by the United Nations to have her released.
ex.zh: 她在过去10年里大部分时间都被软禁，尽管联合国为她的释放一直在做努力。

e.en: You use despite to introduce an idea that appears to contradict your main statement, without suggesting that this idea is true or that you believe it.

ex.en: She told friends she will stand by husband, despite reports that he sent another woman love notes.
ex.zh: 她告诉朋友说，她将支持丈夫，尽管有报道说他在给别的女人递情书。

d: prep. 尽管，即使；不由自主地，忍不住地
n. 亵渎；轻蔑，鄙视
v. 蔑视；激怒

e.en: To export products or raw materials means to sell them to another country.

ex.en: The nation also exports beef.
ex.zh: 该国也出口牛肉。

ex.en: They expect the antibiotic products to be exported to Southeast Asia and Africa.
ex.zh: 他们期望抗生素产品出口到东南亚和非洲。

e.en: Export is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the production and export of cheap casual wear.
ex.zh: …廉价休闲服的生产与出口。

ex.en: A lot of our land is used to grow crops for export.
ex.zh: 我们很多的土地用来种植出口作物。

e.en: Exports are goods sold to another country and sent there.

ex.en: Ghana's main export is cocoa.
ex.zh: 加纳的主要出口产品是可可。

e.en: To export something means to introduce it into another country or make it happen there.

ex.en: It has exported inflation at times.
ex.zh: 它有时将通货膨胀引入他国。

d: n. 出口商品（export 的复数）；出口额
v. 出口（export 的第三人称单数现在时）

e.en: A gulf is an important or significant difference between two people, things, or groups.

ex.en: Within society, there is a growing gulf between rich and poor.
ex.zh: 在社会的内部，贫富之间有着一道日益加深的鸿沟。

e.en: A gulf is a large area of sea which extends a long way into the surrounding land.

ex.en: Hurricane Andrew was last night heading into the Gulf of Mexico.
ex.zh: 安德鲁飓风昨晚进入墨西哥湾。

d: n. 海湾；鸿沟，分歧；波斯湾；（地面的）裂口，深渊

e.en: If something is near a place, thing, or person, it is a short distance from them.

ex.en: Don't come near me.
ex.zh: 别靠近我。

ex.en: He drew his chair nearer the fire.
ex.zh: 他把他的椅子向炉火拉近了些。

e.en: Near is also an adverb.

ex.en: He crouched as near to the door as he could.
ex.zh: 他蜷缩在尽可能靠近门的地方。

ex.en: She took a step nearer to the barrier.
ex.zh: 她向路障走近了一步。

e.en: Near is also an adjective.

ex.en: He collapsed into the nearest chair.
ex.zh: 他瘫在最近的椅子上。

ex.en: The nearer of the two barges was perhaps a mile away.
ex.zh: 两条驳船中较近的一条约有一英里远。

e.en: If someone or something is near to a particular state, they have almost reached it. 接近 (某一状态)

ex.en: After the war, the firm came near to bankruptcy.
ex.zh: 战后这家公司濒临破产。

ex.en: The repairs to the Hafner machine were near to completion.
ex.zh: 哈芙纳牌机器的维修工作已接近尾声。

d: adv. 距离不远，在附近；不久，很快；差不多，几乎
prep. 在......附近，靠近；接近（某时间、某事件）；（用于数字前）接近；与......相似；近乎（一种状态），就要
adj. 近，在附近；差不多的；与……相似；不久以后；随后，接近；近亲的；（车辆）近路缘一侧的；（人）吝啬的，小气的
v. （时间或空间上）接近，靠近
n. 黑雁
布伦特(英国英格兰东南部城市)
adj. strong 的比较级：更强壮的，更强大的，更有力的

e.en: A profit is an amount of money that you gain when you are paid more for something than it cost you to make, get, or do it.

ex.en: The bank made pre-tax profits of $6.5 million.
ex.zh: 该银行获得了税前650万美元的利润。

ex.en: You can improve your chances of profit by sensible planning.
ex.zh: 你可以通过合理的计划增加盈利的机会。

e.en: If you profit from something, you earn a profit from it. (从…中)

ex.en: No one was profiting inordinately from the war effort.
ex.zh: 没有人在从战争中发大财。

ex.en: He has profited by selling his holdings to other investors.
ex.zh: 他已通过将他所持有的卖给其他投资者们而获利。

e.en: If you profit from something, or it profits you, you gain some advantage or benefit from it. 使 (某人) 获利;

ex.en: Jennifer wasn't yet totally convinced that she'd profit from a more relaxed lifestyle.
ex.zh: 珍妮弗还没有完全相信她会从更放松的生活方式中获益。

ex.en: So far the French alliance had profited the rebels little.
ex.zh: 到那时为止，法联盟还没让叛军得到多少好处。

d: n. 利润，盈利；（会计）收益，红利（profit 的复数）

e.en: To transform something into something else means to change or convert it into that thing. 使改变;

ex.en: Your metabolic rate is the speed at which your body transforms food into energy.
ex.zh: 你的新陈代谢率就是你身体将食物转换成能量的速度。

e.en: 改变;

ex.en: Norah made plans for the transformation of an attic room into a study.
ex.zh: 诺拉制订了将阁楼间改造为书房的几个方案。

e.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and suddenly so that they are much better or more attractive. 彻底改变 (使更好、更有吸引力)

ex.en: Industrialization transformed the world.
ex.zh: 工业化彻底改变了世界。

e.en: 彻底改变

ex.en: In the last five years he's undergone a personal transformation.
ex.zh: 在过去的5年里，他完全变了个人。

d: v. 使改观，使变形，使转化；变换（电流）的电压；（数）变换（数学实体）
n. （数，语言学）变换式，转换句；（数，语言学）转换规则

e.en: You say that someone is lucky when they have something that is very desirable or when they are in a very desirable situation.

ex.en: I am luckier than most. I have a job.
ex.zh: 我比大多数人幸运，有份工作。

ex.en: He is incredibly lucky to be alive.
ex.zh: 他竟然幸运地活了下来。

e.en: Someone who is lucky seems to always have good luck.

ex.en: Some people are born lucky, aren't they?
ex.zh: 一些人天生好运不断，不是吗？

e.en: If you describe an action or experience as lucky, you mean that it was good or successful, and that it happened by chance and not as a result of planning or preparation.

ex.en: They admit they are now desperate for a lucky break.
ex.zh: 他们承认现在非常渴望交上好运。

e.en: A lucky object is something that people believe helps them to be successful.

ex.en: He did not have on his other lucky charm, a pair of green socks.
ex.zh: 他没穿另一件吉祥物：一双绿袜子。

d: adj. 幸运的，走运的；吉祥的
关键矿物：一种对于经济和国家安全具有重要意义的矿物资源，通常供应有限或易受供应中断影响。

e.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

ex.en: At this rate, we could find ourselves in the divorce courts!
ex.zh: 照这样下去，我们可能会在离婚法庭上对簿公堂！

ex.en: ...a county court judge.
ex.zh: …一名县法院的法官。

e.en: You can refer to the people in a court, especially the judge, jury, or magistrates, as a court. (一次开庭的)

ex.en: A court at Tampa, Florida has convicted five officials on charges of handling millions of dollars earned from illegal drug deals.
ex.zh: 佛罗里达州坦帕市的一个法庭宣布被指控通过非法毒品买卖获取上百万美元的5名官员罪名成立。

e.en: A court is an area in which you play a game such as tennis, basketball, badminton, or squash.

ex.en: The hotel has several tennis and squash courts.
ex.zh: 该旅馆有几个网球场和壁球场。

e.en: The court of a king or queen is the place where he or she lives and carries out ceremonial or administrative duties.

ex.en: She came to visit England, where she was presented at the court of James I.
ex.zh: 她来访问英格兰，在詹姆斯一世的王宫受到了接见。

d: n. 法院，法庭；球场；王宫，宫廷；朝臣；全体审判人员；庭院，院子；董事（会），理事（会）；（用于大型宅第和公寓街区的名称中）宅第，公寓大楼
v. 奉承，讨好；设法取得，追求；招致，引起（不愉快的事）；谈恋爱，求爱
【名】 （Court）（英）考特，（法）库尔（人名）

e.en: having administrative control or authority 管理的;

ex.en: a managing director

d: adj. 主管的，管理的；节省的，节约的
v. （manage 的现在分词）管理，处理，经营；操纵，控制；设法做到，勉力完成

e.en: A website is a set of data and information about a particular subject that is available on the Internet.

ex.en: ...a website devoted to hip-hop music.
ex.zh: …一个嬉蹦乐专门网站。

d: n. 网站（全球资讯网的主机站）

e.en: Freedom is the state of being allowed to do what you want to do. Freedoms are instances of this.

ex.en: ...freedom of speech.
ex.zh: …言论自由。

ex.en: The United Nations Secretary-General has spoken of the need for individual freedoms and human rights.
ex.zh: 联合国秘书长谈到了个人自由和人权的必要性。

e.en: When prisoners or slaves are set free or escape, they gain their freedom.

ex.en: ...the agreement worked out by the UN, under which all hostages and detainees would gain their freedom.
ex.zh: …联合国制定的协议，据此所有人质和被扣押者应获得自由。

e.en: Freedom from something you do not want means not being affected by it.

ex.en: ...all the freedom from pain that medicine could provide.
ex.zh: …药物所能免除的所有痛苦。

d: n. 自由权，自主权；（状态）自由，自主；行动自由（指不在狱中）；摆脱，免受；自由使用权；荣誉市民称号；（讲话，行为）过分亲密，放肆；直率，坦率
【名】 （Freedom）（英）弗里德姆（人名）
n. 开罗（埃及首都）

e.en: If you press something somewhere, you push it firmly against something else. 推;

ex.en: He pressed his back against the door.
ex.zh: 他将背顶在了门上。

e.en: If you press a button or switch, you push it with your finger in order to make a machine or device work.

ex.en: Drago pressed a button and the door closed.
ex.zh: 德拉戈按了一个按钮，门关上了。

e.en: Press is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a TV which rises from a table at the press of a button.
ex.zh: …按一个按钮就会从桌上升起的一台电视机。

e.en: If you press something or press down on it, you push hard against it with your foot or hand. 用力按;

ex.en: The engine stalled. He pressed the accelerator hard.
ex.zh: 引擎熄火了。他猛踩油门。

d: n. 新闻工作者，新闻界，报刊（the press）；新闻报道；新闻舆论，媒体评论；印刷机；出版社，印刷厂；印刷；按，压，熨；压平器，熨烫机；人群，拥挤；大壁橱，衣柜，书柜；（篮球）紧逼；（举重）推举；（尤指海军的）强行征兵；商业压力
v. 压，挤，推，贴；按，揿；困扰，严重影响；挤着走；敦促，逼迫；坚持，竭力要求；压平，熨平；压榨，榨汁；CD 制作，压制（唱片）；（深情地）紧握（某人的手或臂）；前进，推进；（敌人，对手）进逼，进攻；（高尔夫）过猛击球；征用，临时使用；（举重）推举
【名】  (Press) （美、英、加、俄、印、澳）普雷斯（人名）

e.en: The authorities are the people who have the power to make decisions and to make sure that laws are obeyed.

ex.en: This provided a pretext for the authorities to cancel the elections.
ex.zh: 这给当局提供了一个取消选举的借口。

e.en: An authority is an official organization or government department that has the power to make decisions.

ex.en: ...the Philadelphia Parking Authority.
ex.zh: …费城停车管理局。

e.en: Someone who is an authority on a particular subject knows a lot about it. (某一学科的)

ex.en: He's universally recognized as an authority on Russian affairs.
ex.zh: 他被公认为是俄罗斯事务的权威。

e.en: Authority is the right to command and control other people.

ex.en: A family member in a family business has a position of authority and power.
ex.zh: 家庭成员在家族企业中都有职有权。

d: n. 当局，官方；官方机构，主管部门；权威人士（authority 的复数）

e.en: If you are unlicensed, you do not have official permission from the government or from the authorities to do something. (人)

ex.en: ...unscrupulous, and usually unlicensed investment managers who regularly target wealthy widows.
ex.zh: ...不择手段的无执照的投资经理常把有钱的寡妇作为他们的目标。

e.en: If something that you own or use is unlicensed, you do not have official permission to own it or use it. (物品)

ex.en: He went out with an unlicensed shotgun to look for the intruders.
ex.zh: 他带着一把没有执照的霰弹枪出去寻找闯入者。

e.en: If a place such as a bar or restaurant is unlicensed, it does not have a license to sell alcoholic drinks. (饭店、酒吧)
If something such as an activity or product is unlicensed, it takes place or is produced without official permission. (活动、产品)

ex.en: Unlicensed steroids are being disguised as herbal medicines.
ex.zh: 无许可的类固醇被伪装成为草药。

d: adj. 没有执照的，未经当局许可的；（酒吧、餐馆等）无售酒执照的

e.en: Something that happens or is done briefly happens or is done for a very short period of time.

ex.en: He smiled briefly.
ex.zh: 他短促地微微一笑。

e.en: If you say or write something briefly, you use very few words or give very few details.

ex.en: There are four basic alternatives; they are described briefly below.
ex.zh: 有4种基本选择,简略描述如下。

e.en: You can say briefly to indicate that you are about to say something in as few words as possible.

ex.en: Briefly, no less than nine of our agents have passed information to us.
ex.zh: 简言之,至少已经有9位我们的代理商将信息传递给了我们。

d: adv. 简短地，简要地；短暂地，暂时地

e.en: A clampdown is a sudden restriction on a particular activity by a government or other authority.

ex.en: ...a clampdown on the employment of illegal immigrants.
ex.zh: ...对雇佣非法移民的一种制裁。

d: n. 压制，取缔，严禁

e.en: If something happens amid noises or events of some kind, it happens while the other things are happening.

ex.en: Workers are sifting through the wreckage of the airliners amid growing evidence that the disasters were the work of terrorists.
ex.zh: 在越来越多证据证明这些灾难是恐怖分子所为的同时，工人们正在仔细检查那些客机的残骸。

d: prep. 在……过程中，在……中；四周是，被……所环绕
【名】 （Amid）（美）阿米德（人名）

e.en: Concern is worry about a situation.

ex.en: The group has expressed concern about reports of political violence in Africa.
ex.zh: 该集团已对有关非洲政治暴力的报道表示担忧。

ex.en: The move follows growing public concern over the spread of the disease.
ex.zh: 该行动是针对公众日益增长的对该疾病传播的担忧而采取的。

e.en: If something concerns you, it worries you.

ex.en: The growing number of people seeking refuge in Thailand is beginning to concern Western aid agencies.
ex.zh: 日益增多的到泰国寻求避难的人数开始让西方援助机构感到担忧。

e.en: 感到担忧的

ex.en: Academics and employers are concerned that students are not sufficiently prepared for college courses.
ex.zh: 学术界和用人单位都担心学生们对大学课程没有做好足够准备。

e.en: If you concern yourself with something, you give it attention because you think that it is important.

ex.en: I didn't concern myself with politics.
ex.zh: 我不关心政治。

d: v. 涉及，与……相关；让……担心；对……感兴趣（concern 的第三人称单数）
n. 担心；关心的事，关注点；企业，公司（concern 的复数）

e.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

ex.en: In 1977 he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
ex.zh: 在1977年，他因谋杀被判处终生监禁。

ex.en: There was insufficient evidence to convict him.
ex.zh: 没有足够的证据证明他有罪。

e.en: A convict is someone who is in prison.

ex.en: ...Neil Jordan's tale of two escaped convicts who get mistaken for priests.
ex.zh: …尼尔·乔丹的两个越狱囚犯被误认为是牧师的故事。

d: adj. 被判有罪的，已定罪的；已被判刑的
v. convict 的过去式及过去分词：证明……有罪，宣判（某人）有罪；（旧用法）使（某人）知罪

e.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

ex.en: I hope they continue to fight for equal justice after I'm gone.
ex.zh: 我希望我走后他们继续为司法公正而奋斗。

ex.en: Diana and Roy Jarvis are determined to continue working when they reach retirement age.
ex.zh: 戴安娜·贾维斯和罗伊·贾维斯决心到退休年龄后还继续工作。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it does not stop. 使继续;

ex.en: He insisted that the conflict would continue until conditions were met for a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 他坚持认为冲突会持续下去，直至停火条件得到满足为止。

ex.en: Outside the building people continue their vigil, huddling around bonfires.
ex.zh: 在楼外，人们围聚在篝火旁继续守夜。

e.en: If you continue something or continue with something, you start doing it again after a break or interruption. (某人在歇息或被打断后) 继续 (做某事或某事)

ex.en: I went up to my room to continue with my packing.
ex.zh: 我上我房间去继续收拾行李。

ex.en: She looked up for a minute and then continued drawing.
ex.zh: 她抬头看了一会儿，然后继续画。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it starts again after a break or interruption. (某事在停顿或被打断后)

ex.en: He denies 18 charges. The trial continues today.
ex.zh: 他否认18项指控。审判今天继续。

d: v. （使）继续，（使）延续；继续说，接着说；移动，延伸；留任，维持原状

e.en: A country is one of the political units which the world is divided into, covering a particular area of land.

ex.en: Indonesia is the fifth most populous country in the world.
ex.zh: 印度尼西亚是世界上人口第五大国。

ex.en: ...the boundary between the two countries.
ex.zh: …这两个国家的分界线。

e.en: The people who live in a particular country can be referred to as the country.

ex.en: Finally the country got some much-needed good news.
ex.zh: 最后该国人民得到了一些他们最需要的好消息。

e.en: The country consists of places such as farms, open fields, and villages which are away from towns and cities.

ex.en: ...a healthy life in the country.
ex.zh: …在乡村的健康生活。

ex.en: She was cycling along a country road near Compiègne.
ex.zh: 她正沿着贡比涅附近的一条乡间小路骑车。

e.en: A particular kind of country is an area of land which has particular characteristics or is connected with a particular well-known person.

ex.en: Varese Ligure is a small town in mountainous country east of Genoa.
ex.zh: 瓦雷泽·利古里亚是一座位于热那亚东部山区的小镇。

d: n. 国，国家；全国人民，全体国民（the country）；乡下，乡村；地区，区域；乡村音乐；故乡
adj. 乡下的，农村的；乡村音乐的；祖国的，故乡的；粗鲁的

e.en: A crackdown is strong official action that is taken to punish people who break laws. 严惩措施;

ex.en: ...anti-government unrest that ended with the violent army crackdown.
ex.zh: …因遭到暴力武装镇压而告终的反政府动乱。

d: n. 打击，镇压

e.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

ex.en: In 1977 he was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
ex.zh: 在1977年，他因谋杀被判处终生监禁。

ex.en: There was insufficient evidence to convict him.
ex.zh: 没有足够的证据证明他有罪。

e.en: A convict is someone who is in prison.

ex.en: ...Neil Jordan's tale of two escaped convicts who get mistaken for priests.
ex.zh: …尼尔·乔丹的两个越狱囚犯被误认为是牧师的故事。

d: v. convict 的及物动词第三人称单数形式：证明……有罪，宣告……有罪（常与 of 连用）
n. convict 的复数形式：罪犯，囚犯，已决犯

e.en: Custody is the legal right to keep and take care of a child, especially the right given to a child's mother or father when they get divorced.

ex.en: I'm going to go to court to get custody of the children.
ex.zh: 我要打官司以争取对孩子们的监护权。

ex.en: Child custody is normally granted to the mother.
ex.zh: 孩子的监护权一般判给母亲。

e.en: If someone is being held in a particular type of custody, they are being kept in a place that is similar to a prison.

ex.en: The youngster got nine months' youth custody.
ex.zh: 那个小伙子被判少年拘留9个月。

e.en: Someone who is in custody or has been taken into custody has been arrested and is being kept in prison until they can be tried in a court.

ex.en: Three people appeared in court and two of them were remanded in custody.
ex.zh: 3个人出庭，其中2人被还押候审。

d: n. 监护，监护权；监禁，拘留；保管，保护

e.en: Detention is when someone is arrested or put into prison. 拘留;

ex.en: ...the detention without trial of government critics.
ex.zh: …对政府批评者未经审判而进行的关押。

e.en: Detention is a punishment for students who misbehave, who are made to stay at school after the other students have gone home. (为惩罚学生的)

ex.en: The teacher kept the boys in detention after school.
ex.zh: 老师在放学后罚男孩们留了下来。

d: n. 拘留，关押；（作为惩罚的）课后留校

e.en: the controlling editor of a publication

d: n. 总编辑，主编，总主笔（亦作 editor in chief）

e.en: Egyptian means belonging or relating to Egypt or to its people, language, or culture. 埃及(人)的; 埃及语的;
The Egyptians are the people who come from Egypt.
Egyptian means related to or connected with ancient Egypt.

ex.en: ...the Egyptian pharaoh.
ex.zh: ...古埃及法老。

e.en: The Egyptians were the people who lived in ancient Egypt.

d: adj. 埃及的，埃及人的，与埃及语言或文化有关的
n. 埃及人（包括古埃及人）；古代埃及语，古埃及语
n. 埃及（非洲东北部国家）；古埃及（古代尼罗河流域文明）

e.en: A fresh thing or amount replaces or is added to a previous thing or amount.

ex.en: He asked the police, who carried out the original investigation, to make fresh inquiries.
ex.zh: 他要求原先进行调查的警方做一轮新的调查。

e.en: Something that is fresh has been done, made, or experienced recently.

ex.en: There were no fresh car tracks or footprints in the snow.
ex.zh: 雪地里没有新的车辙或脚印。

ex.en: A puppy stepped in the fresh cement.
ex.zh: 一只小狗走到新铺的水泥路面上。

e.en: Fresh food has been picked or produced recently, and has not been preserved, for example, by being frozen or put in a can.

ex.en: ...locally caught fresh fish.
ex.zh: …当地捕获的鲜鱼。

e.en: If you describe something as fresh, you like it because it is new and exciting.

ex.en: These designers are full of fresh ideas.
ex.zh: 这些设计师满是新颖的想法。

d: adj. 新鲜的；新近的，刚经历的；新的，不同的；新颖的，独创的；清新的，清爽的；（水）淡的，无盐的；（风）凉爽的，强劲的；洁净的，亮丽的；精力充沛的；刚来的；（对异性）放肆的，无礼的；年轻可爱但缺乏经验的；气味难闻的
adv. 刚刚，新近地

e.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity. 使…加剧;

ex.en: Both unions and management fear the dispute could escalate.
ex.zh: 各工会与资方都害怕争端会加剧。

ex.en: The protests escalated into five days of rioting.
ex.zh: 抗议逐渐升级为5天的暴乱。

e.en: 加剧

ex.en: The threat of nuclear escalation remains.
ex.zh: 核升级的威胁依然存在。

d: v. 逐步上升，逐步升级（escalate 的现在分词/动名词）
adj. 逐步上升的，不断升级的，逐步上涨的

e.en: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so the first one is not affected or influenced by the second. 无关联的;

ex.en: Your questions should be independent of each other.
ex.zh: 你们的问题应该是相互间毫无关联的。

ex.en: We're going independent from the university and setting up our own group.
ex.zh: 我们将从大学独立出去，成立我们自己的集团。

e.en: 独立地

ex.en: ...several people working independently in different areas of the world.
ex.zh: …在世界不同地区独立工作的几个人。

e.en: If someone is independent, they do not need help or money from anyone else.

ex.en: Phil was now much more independent of his parents.
ex.zh: 菲尔现在不大依赖他的父母了。

e.en: 不依赖地

ex.en: ...helping disabled students to live and study as independently as possible.
ex.zh: …帮助残疾学生尽可能不依赖地生活和学习。

d: adj. 自治的，独立的；自立的，自力更生的；公正的，不受他人影响的；分离的，单独的；私营的；无党派的；有主见的，有独立见解的
n. 独立自主者，独立团体；无党派政治家；公理会教友

e.en: If you intensify something or if it intensifies, it becomes greater in strength, amount, or degree. 加强;

ex.en: I jump, intensifying the pain in all my muscles.
ex.zh: 我跳起来，浑身的肌肉更加疼痛了。

d: v. 加紧，加强，增强（intensify 的现在分词和动名词）
adj. 增强的，加剧的，越来越强烈的

e.en: A journalist is a person whose job is to collect news and write about it for newspapers, magazines, television, or radio.

d: n. 新闻工作者，新闻记者；报人，报纸撰稿人
n. 莉娜（女子名）
adv. （日语 まだ 的罗马字）还，仍然；尚未，还没有；再，更多；重叠形式 mada mada 表示“还差得远”
abbr. （常大写为 MADA）多路存取分立地址系统（Multiple-Access Discrete Address System）；慕达农业发展局
n. （Mada）人名，常音译作“马达”（如塞尔维亚、乍得、印度尼西亚等地）

e.en: An ordered society or system is well-organized and has a clear structure. (社会或制度)

ex.en: An objective set of rules which we all agree to accept is necessary for any ordered society.
ex.zh: 任何井然有序的社会都需要一套客观公正、为大家所接受的规则。

d: adj. 有序的；整齐的；安排好的；（数学/计算机）按固定顺序排列的
v. 命令，要求；定制，订购；点餐；组织，安排（order 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: You can refer to television, radio, newspapers, and magazines as the media.

ex.en: It is hard work and not a glamorous job as portrayed by the media.
ex.zh: 这份工作很辛苦，并不是一份像媒体描述的那样令人向往的工作。

ex.en: They are wondering whether bias in the news media contributed to the president's defeat.
ex.zh: 他们正在想是否新闻媒体的偏见导致了总统的失败。

e.en: of or relating to the mass media 公共媒体的;

ex.en: media hype

e.en: Media is a plural of . 媒体 (medium)(的复数形式)

d: n. 新闻媒体，传媒（medium的复数形式）；媒体工作者；（尤指血管壁的）中间层（复数mediae）；浊塞音；中脉

e.en: News is information about a recently changed situation or a recent event.

ex.en: We waited and waited for news of him.
ex.zh: 我们等啊等啊，等他的消息。

ex.en: They still haven't had any news about when they'll be able to go home.
ex.zh: 他们仍然没有得到任何关于他们何时才能回家的消息。

e.en: News is information that is published in newspapers and broadcast on radio and television about recent events in the country or world or in a particular area of activity.

ex.en: Foreign News is on page 16.
ex.zh: 国外新闻在第16版。

ex.en: Those are some of the top stories in the news.
ex.zh: 那是新闻中的一些顶级报道。

e.en: The news is a television or radio broadcast which consists of information about recent events in the country or the world. (电视、电台等的)

ex.en: I heard all about the bombs on the news.
ex.zh: 我从新闻广播里听到了关于炸弹的所有消息。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is news, you mean that they are considered to be interesting and important at the moment, and that people want to hear about them on the radio and television and in newspapers. 新闻人物;

ex.en: A murder was big news.
ex.zh: 谋杀案是大新闻。

d: n. 消息，新情况；新闻（报道）；新闻人物，新闻事件；电视新闻节目（the news）；（用于报纸名）新闻

e.en: An outlet is a shop or organization which sells the goods made by a particular manufacturer or at a discount price, often direct from the manufacturer. 专卖店;

ex.en: ...the largest retail outlet in the city.
ex.zh: …该市最大的零售专卖店。

ex.en: At the factory outlet you'll find discounted items at up to 75% off regular prices.
ex.zh: 在工厂的直销店里，你会找到比常规价低75%的打折商品。

e.en: If someone has an outlet for their feelings or ideas, they have a means of expressing and releasing them. (感情的) 发泄途径; (思想的)

ex.en: Her father had found an outlet for his ambition in his work.
ex.zh: 她父亲在工作中找到了施展抱负的途径。

e.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow away. 出水口;

ex.en: ...a warm air outlet.
ex.zh: …一个热气排气口。

e.en: An outlet is a place, usually in a wall, where you can connect electrical devices to the electricity supply.

d: n. （情绪或精力的）发泄方式，发泄途径；排出口；商店，分销点；廉价经销店；从事大众媒体行业的公司；电源插座

e.en: If you respond to prompting, you do what someone encourages or reminds you to do. 鼓励;

ex.en: The New York team needed little prompting from their coach Bill Parcells.
ex.zh: 纽约队几乎不需要教练比尔·帕索斯的提醒。

d: n. 促使、鼓励或提醒某人做某事的行为；提示；提词，台词提示
v. 促使，促进；激起；鼓励，鼓舞；给演员提示台词（prompt 的现在分词）

e.en: Someone who is prominent is important and well-known. 重要的;

ex.en: ...the children of very prominent or successful parents.
ex.zh: …非常知名或成功的人士们的孩子们。

e.en: Something that is prominent is very noticeable or is an important part of something else.

ex.en: Here the window plays a prominent part in the design.
ex.zh: 这里，窗户在设计中有着突出的作用。

e.en: 突出地

ex.en: Trade will figure prominently in the second day of talks in Washington.
ex.zh: 贸易在华盛顿会谈的第二天将成为突出的议题。

d: adj. 重要的，著名的；显眼的，突出的；突起的，高耸的
n. 舟蛾（=prominent moth）

e.en: Reading is the activity of reading books.

ex.en: I have always loved reading.
ex.zh: 我一直很喜欢读书。

e.en: A reading is an event at which poetry or extracts from books are read to an audience.

ex.en: ...a poetry reading.
ex.zh: …一场诗歌朗诵会。

e.en: Your reading of a word, text, or situation is the way in which you understand or interpret it. 诠释;

ex.en: My reading of her character makes me feel that she was too responsible a person to do those things.
ex.zh: 我对她性格的了解使我觉得她是个非常负责、绝不会干那些事的人。

e.en: The reading on a measuring device is the figure or measurement that it shows. (测量仪器上的)

ex.en: The gauge must be giving a faulty reading.
ex.zh: 标尺一定是给出了一个错误的读数。

d: n. 阅读，宣读；读物，阅读材料；文学知识；理解，解读；朗诵会，朗诵的作品；（宗教仪式上诵读的）《圣经》章节；（测量仪器的）读数；议案宣读（立法机关审议法案的程序）
v. 阅读，读懂；朗读；理解（read 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Reading）雷丁（人名），雷丁（英，美）（地名）

e.en: If a person or animal is released from somewhere where they have been locked up or cared for, they are set free or allowed to go.

ex.en: He was released from custody the next day.
ex.zh: 他第二天被从拘留中释放。

e.en: When someone is released, you refer to their release.

ex.en: He called for the immediate release of all political prisoners.
ex.zh: 他要求立即释放所有的政治犯。

e.en: If someone or something releases you from a duty, task, or feeling, they free you from it.

ex.en: Divorce releases both the husband and wife from all marital obligations to each other.
ex.zh: 离婚解除了夫妻相互之间的所有婚姻义务。

e.en: Release is also a noun.

ex.en: Our therapeutic style offers release from stored tensions, traumas, and grief.
ex.zh: 我们的治疗方式意在解除蓄积的压力、创伤和悲痛。

d: v. 释放，放走；放开，松开；公布，发布；发行，上映；释放，排放，发泄，宣泄（release 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已释放的；已发布的（由 release 的过去分词转化而来）

e.en: If you shut something such as a door or if it shuts, it moves so that it fills a hole or a space. 关上;

ex.en: Just make sure you shut the gate.
ex.zh: 你务必关上那幢大门。

e.en: Shut is also an adjective.

ex.en: They have warned residents to stay inside and keep their doors and windows shut.
ex.zh: 他们已警告居民待在屋内并关好门窗。

e.en: If you shut your eyes, you lower your eyelids so that you cannot see anything. 闭上 (眼睛)

ex.en: Lucy shut her eyes so she wouldn't see it happen.
ex.zh: 露西闭上了眼睛，以便不会看到它发生。

e.en: Shut is also an adjective.

ex.en: His eyes were shut and he seemed to have fallen asleep.
ex.zh: 他的双眼闭着，看上去像是已经睡着了。

d: v. 关闭，合上；把……关在；（使）停止运作，（使）停止营业；禁止通行，封闭
adj. 关闭的，关上的；打烊的，停止营业的
n. 关闭
【名】 （Shut）（俄）舒特（人名）

e.en: Taken is the past participle of . (take)
If you are taken with something or someone, you are very interested in them or attracted to them.

ex.en: She seems very taken with the idea.
ex.zh: 她好像对这个想法很感兴趣。

d: v. 拿，带（take 的过去分词）
adj. 对……感兴趣的（taken with）；已有伴侣（或已婚）的；（座位、位置、名称等）被占用的，已被使用的；按……理解（或解读）的

e.en: A warning is something said or written to tell people of a possible danger, problem, or other unpleasant thing that might happen. 警告;

ex.en: The minister gave a warning that if war broke out, it would be catastrophic.
ex.zh: 大臣警告说战争一旦爆发，将会是灾难性的。

ex.en: He was killed because he ignored a warning to put stronger cords on his parachute.
ex.zh: 他死了，因为他忽视了要给降落伞装上更结实的绳索的警告。

e.en: A warning is an advance notice of something that will happen, often something unpleasant or dangerous.

ex.en: The soldiers opened fire without warning.
ex.zh: 士兵们未发警告就开了火。

e.en: Warning actions or signs give a warning.

ex.en: She ignored the warning signals and did not check the patient's medical notes.
ex.zh: 她忽视了一些先兆症状，也没有检查病人的病历。

d: n. 警告，警告信息，警报（warning 的复数形式）

e.en: A movie is a series of moving pictures that have been recorded so that they can be shown in a theatre or on television. A movie tells a story, or shows a real situation.

ex.en: In the first movie Tony Curtis ever made he played a grocery clerk.
ex.zh: 在托尼·柯蒂斯制作的第一部影片中，他出演一名杂货店店员。

e.en: You can talk about the movies when you are talking about seeing a movie in a movie theatre.

d: n. 电影；电影院（the movies）；电影业（the movies）；电影（总称）（the movies）

e.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

ex.en: ...a gallery of pictures depicting Lee's most famous battles.
ex.zh: …一批描绘李的最著名战役的图画。

d: v. depict 的现在分词/动名词：描绘，描写，刻画

e.en: If a place is awash with something, it contains a large amount of it.

ex.en: This is a company that is awash with cash.
ex.zh: 这是一家有大量现金的公司。

e.en: If the ground or a floor is awash, it is covered in water, often because of heavy rain or as the result of an accident.

ex.en: The bathroom floor was awash.
ex.zh: 浴室地板浸在水中。

d: adj. （常作表语）被水覆盖的，浸在水中的；被浪冲打的；（航海）指岩石、礁石等与水面齐平的；（常与 with 或 in 连用）充满…的，充斥着…的，有大量…的

e.en: to play a high card before a low one in a suit, usually a conventional signal of a doubleton holding or of strength in that suit 先出大牌后出小牌(表示握有双牌或表示牌很好)
the act of petering
e.zh: 先出大牌后出小牌的行为

e.en: a safe, till, or cash box 保险箱; 钱柜;

d: v. 逐渐减少；先出大牌后出小牌
n. （非正式）阴茎；单人牢房；保险箱；先出大牌后出小牌的行为
n. （Peter）（英、德、丹、斯、塞、瑞）彼得（人名）

e.en: When a person or thing comes to a particular place, especially to a place where you are, they move there. 来 (某地)

ex.en: Two police officers came into the hall.
ex.zh: 两位警官来到大厅里。

ex.en: Come here, Tom.
ex.zh: 来这儿，汤姆。

e.en: When someone comes to do something, they move to the place where someone else is in order to do it, and they do it. Someone can also come do something and come and do something. However, you always say that someone came and did something. 来 (做某事)

ex.en: Eleanor had come to see her.
ex.zh: 埃莉诺是来看她的。

ex.en: I want you to come visit me.
ex.zh: 我希望你来看我。

e.en: When you come to a place, you reach it.

ex.en: He came to a door that led into a passageway.
ex.zh: 他来到一扇通往走廊的门前。

e.en: If something comes up to a particular point or down to it, it is tall enough, deep enough, or long enough to reach that point.

ex.en: The water came up to my chest.
ex.zh: 水漫到了我的胸部。

d: v. 来，来到；来临，发生；来自，从……来（come 的第三人称单数现在时形式）
n. 伴星（天文学，双星或聚星系统中伴随主星的恒星）；伴引血管（解剖学，指伴随动脉或神经走行的血管）；（Comes）人名，又译（法）科姆、（德、西、意）科梅斯

e.en: Violence is behaviour that is intended to hurt, injure, or kill people.

ex.en: Twenty people were killed in the violence.
ex.zh: 有20人在这起暴力事件中被杀害。

ex.en: ...domestic violence between husband and wife.
ex.zh: …夫妻间的家庭暴力。

e.en: If you do or say something with violence, you use a lot of force and energy in doing or saying it, often because you are angry.

ex.en: The violence in her tone gave Tyler a shock.
ex.zh: 她语气激烈，使泰勒大为震惊。

d: n. 暴力，暴行；（言行的）狂暴，激烈，愤怒；巨大的破坏力

e.en: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

ex.en: He rolled down his window and stuck his face out.
ex.zh: 他摇下窗户，探出脸来。

ex.en: He was going red in the face and breathing with difficulty.
ex.zh: 他脸面发红，费力地喘着气。

e.en: If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.

ex.en: He was walking around with a sad face.
ex.zh: 他四处走着，面带哀伤。

e.en: The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it. (悬崖、山、建筑物的)

ex.en: Harrer was one of the first to climb the north face of the Eiger.
ex.zh: 哈勒是第一批登上艾格尔山北坡的人之一。

e.en: The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time. 钟面;

ex.en: It was too dark to see the face of my watch.
ex.zh: 天太黑了，以致看不见我表盘上的时间。

d: adj. 有某种面孔或表情的；有……表面的
v. 面对；面临；面向（face 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Filming is the activity of making a film including the acting, directing, and camera shots.

ex.en: Filming was due to start next month.
ex.zh: 影片摄制预计下个月开始。

d: n. 拍摄，摄影，影片摄制
v. 拍摄（成影片）；以薄膜覆盖；变得朦胧（film 的现在分词）

e.en: A filmmaker is someone involved in making films, in particular a director or producer.

d: n. 电影制作人（参与电影制作的人，尤指导演、制片人等；filmmaker 的复数）

e.en: A documentary is a television or radio programme, or a film, which shows real events or provides information about a particular subject.

ex.en: ...a TV documentary on homelessness.
ex.zh: …一部关于无家可归现象的电视记录片。

e.en: Documentary evidence consists of things that are written down. 书面的 (证据)

ex.en: The government says it has documentary evidence that the two countries were planning military action.
ex.zh: 该政府宣称，它拥有这两个国家正在策划军事行动的书面证据。

d: n. 纪实节目，纪录片
adj. 书面的，文件的，文献的；记录的，纪实的

e.en: Mountaineering is the activity of climbing the steep sides of mountains as a hobby or sport. 登山(运动)

d: n. 登山，登山运动，爬山
v. 登山（mountaineer 的 ing 形式）

e.en: Struck is the past tense and past participle of . (strike)

d: adj. 对……印象很好（be struck on sb./sth.）；受罢工影响的
v. 打，撞；（用手或武器等）打；（使）碰撞（strike 的过去式和过去分词）
【名】 （Struck）（美、德、丹）斯特鲁克（人名）

e.en: A tragedy is an extremely sad event or situation.

ex.en: They have suffered an enormous personal tragedy.
ex.zh: 他们遭受了一场巨大的个人灾难。

e.en: Tragedy is a type of literature, especially drama, that is serious and sad, and often ends with the death of the main character.

ex.en: The story has elements of tragedy and farce.
ex.zh: 这个故事含有悲剧和闹剧的成分。

d: n. 悲惨事件，惨剧；悲剧（作品）；不幸，遗憾；令人非常烦乱（或生气）的情形

e.en: Fearsome is used to describe things that are frightening, for example, because of their large size or extreme nature.

ex.en: He had developed a fearsome reputation for intimidating people.
ex.zh: 他因恐吓他人而得了一个可怕的名声。

d: adj. 可怕的，吓人的，令人畏惧的；令人生畏的，可畏的，难对付的；极大的

e.en: Desperation is the feeling that you have when you are in such a bad situation that you will try anything to change it.

ex.en: This feeling of desperation and helplessness was common to most of the refugees.
ex.zh: 这种不顾一切和无助的感觉在大多数难民中很常见。

d: n. 绝望，拼命；急需，渴求
adj．类似游戏的：具有游戏特征或质感的，通常指非游戏环境中的体验或活动。

e.en: Someone who is jobless does not have a job, although they would like one.

ex.en: He has turned his back on millions of jobless Americans.
ex.zh: 他已经不管上百万失业的美国人了。

e.en: The jobless are people who are jobless.

ex.en: They joined the ranks of the jobless.
ex.zh: 他们加入了失业大军。

d: adj. 失业的，无业的；（关于）失业者的
n. 失业者（常与 the 连用，总称失业的人）

e.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you think about and that you want to happen, especially one that is unlikely to happen.

ex.en: ...fantasies of romance and true love.
ex.zh: …对浪漫和真爱的幻想。

e.en: You can refer to a story or situation that someone creates from their imagination and that is not based on reality as fantasy. 虚幻的故事;

ex.en: The film is more of an ironic fantasy than a horror story.
ex.zh: 这部电影比较像是讽刺的幻想故事，而不是恐怖片。

e.en: Fantasy is the activity of imagining things.

ex.en: ...a world of imagination, passion, fantasy, reflection.
ex.zh: …一个想像、激情、幻想和反思的世界。

e.en: Fantasy football, baseball, or another sport is a game in which players choose an imaginary team and score points based on the actual performances of the members of their team in real games. 梦幻的 (运动类电子游戏)

ex.en: Haskins said he has been playing fantasy baseball for the past five years.
ex.zh: 哈斯金斯说他在过去的５年里一直在打梦幻棒球游戏。

d: n. 幻想，想象；想象产物，幻想作品；虚拟比赛（游戏）；幻想曲，集成曲；期望
v. 想象，幻想

e.en: A star is a large ball of burning gas in space. Stars appear to us as small points of light in the sky on clear nights.

ex.en: The nights were pure with cold air and lit with stars.
ex.zh: 那些夜晚十分清静，空气清凉、繁星点点。

e.en: You can refer to a shape or an object as a star when it has four, five, or more points sticking out of it in a regular pattern. 星形;

ex.en: Children at school receive coloured stars for work well done.
ex.zh: 上学的孩子们表现好会得到彩星。

e.en: You can say how many stars something such as a hotel or restaurant has as a way of talking about its quality, which is often indicated by a number of star-shaped symbols. The more stars something has, the better it is. (宾馆或饭店等的)

ex.en: ...five star hotels.
ex.zh: …五星级酒店。

e.en: Famous actors, musicians, and sports players are often referred to as stars.

ex.en: ...star of the TV series Scrubs.
ex.zh: …电视连续剧《实习医生风云》里的明星。

ex.en: By now Murphy is Hollywood's top male comedy star.
ex.zh: 现在墨菲已是好莱坞顶级男喜剧明星。

d: n. 明星类，明星（star 的复数形式）
v. 点缀；成辐射状开裂；使担任主角（star 的第三人称单数）
abbr. specialized training and reassignment students经过专门训练后再分配的学生; stationary automotive road stimulator （Toyota）汽车公路固定刺激物（丰田汽车）

e.en: Something that is strange is unusual or unexpected, and makes you feel slightly nervous or afraid.

ex.en: Then a strange thing happened.
ex.zh: 接着一件怪事发生了。

ex.en: There was something strange about the flickering blue light.
ex.zh: 那闪烁的蓝光有点儿奇怪。

e.en: 奇怪地

ex.en: She noticed he was acting strangely.
ex.zh: 她注意到他行为怪异。

e.en: A strange place is one that you have never been to before. A strange person is someone that you have never met before.

ex.en: I ended up alone in a strange city.
ex.zh: 我最终是独自呆在了一个陌生的城市。

d: adj. 奇怪的，不寻常的；陌生的，不熟悉的；令人局促不安的，令人不自在的，令人难受的；（亚原子粒子）有奇异性非零值的，奇异性的
adv. 奇怪地，不寻常地
【名】 （Strange）（英）斯特兰奇，（瑞典、塞）斯特朗格（人名）

e.en: The lee of a place is the shelter that it gives from the wind or bad weather. 庇护处;

ex.en: ...the cathedral, which nestles in the lee of a hill beneath the town.
ex.zh: ...大教堂坐落于小镇下面一座小山的背风处。

e.en: In sailing, the lee side of a ship is the one that is away from the wind. (船)背风面的;

d: n. 保护；背风处
adj. 保护的；庇荫的；避风的
n. （Lee）人名；（朝）李；（中）李（普通话·威妥玛）；（柬）利；（中）李（广东话·威妥玛）

e.en: A squid is a sea creature with a long soft body and many soft arms called tentacles.
Squid is pieces of this creature eaten as food.

ex.en: Add the prawns and squid and cook for 2 minutes.
ex.zh: 加入虾和鱿鱼，煮2分钟。

e.en: a pound sterling

d: n. 枪乌贼，（食用的）鱿鱼；乌贼状人造鱼饵；超导量子干涉器件（SQUID）；英镑
v. 用枪乌贼作饵捕鱼

e.en: You can use take followed by a noun to talk about an action or event, when it would also be possible to use the verb that is related to that noun. For example, you can say "she took a shower" instead of "she showered."
e.zh: 后接名词描述动作或事件

ex.en: She was too tired to take a shower.
ex.zh: 她累得不想淋浴了。

ex.en: Betty took a photograph of us.
ex.zh: 贝蒂给我们拍了一张照片。

e.en: In ordinary spoken or written English, people use take with a range of nouns instead of using a more specific verb. For example, people often say "he took control" or "she took a positive attitude" instead of "he assumed control" or "she adopted a positive attitude."
e.zh: 与许多名词连用，代替更具体的动词

ex.en: The Patriotic Front took power after a three-month civil war.
ex.zh: 爱国阵线经过3个月的内战后夺取了政权。

ex.en: I felt it was important for women to join and take a leading role.
ex.zh: 我感觉妇女参与并担任领导角色很重要。

e.en: If you take something, you reach out for it and hold it.

ex.en: Here, let me take your coat.
ex.zh: 来，我帮你拿大衣。

ex.en: Colette took her by the shoulders and shook her.
ex.zh: 科利特抓住她的双肩，摇晃着她。

e.en: If you take something with you when you go somewhere, you carry it or have it with you.

ex.en: Mark often took his books to Bess's house to study.
ex.zh: 马克经常带着书去贝丝家学习。

ex.en: You should take your passport with you when changing money.
ex.zh: 你换汇时应该带着你的护照。

d: vt. take 的第三人称单数现在时；取走
n. take 的复数名词：（影视、录音）镜头，片段；（非正式）看法，解读

e.en: The future is the period of time that will come after the present, or the things that will happen then.

ex.en: The spokesman said no decision on the proposal was likely in the immediate future.
ex.zh: 该发言人称近期不太可能有有关该提案的决议。

ex.en: He was making plans for the future.
ex.zh: 他正在为将来制定计划。

e.en: Future things will happen or exist after the present time.

ex.en: She said if the world did not act conclusively now, it would only bequeath the problem to future generations.
ex.zh: 她说如果这个世界现在不采取正确的行动，那只会把问题遗留给后代。

ex.en: ...the future king and queen.
ex.zh: …未来的国王和王后。

e.en: Someone's future, or the future of something, is what will happen to them or what they will do after the present time. (某人、某事物的)

ex.en: His future depends on the outcome of the elections.
ex.zh: 他的未来取决于该选举的结果。

ex.en: ...a proposed national conference on the country's political future.
ex.zh: …一次拟议的有关该国政治未来的全国会议。

e.en: When people trade in futures, they buy stocks and shares, commodities such as coffee or oil, or foreign currency at a price that is agreed at the time of purchase for items which are delivered some time in the future.

ex.en: This report could spur some buying in corn futures when the market opens today.
ex.zh: 这份报告会在今天开市时刺激玉米期货的一些购买行为。

d: n. 未来，将来；前途，前景；期货；（动词的）将来时态
adj. 将来的，未来的；（动词）将来时态的
n. 蒙特利尔（加拿大东南部港市）

e.en: If you announce something, you tell people about it publicly or officially.

ex.en: He will announce tonight that he is resigning from office.
ex.zh: 他今晚将宣布他要辞职。

ex.en: She was planning to announce her engagement to Peter.
ex.zh: 她在计划宣布她与彼得的婚约。

e.en: If you announce a piece of news or an intention, especially something that people may not like, you say it loudly and clearly, so that everyone you are with can hear it.

ex.en: Peter announced that he had no intention of wasting his time at any university.
ex.zh: 彼得声明他无意在任何一所大学里浪费他的时间。

e.en: If an airport or rail employee announces something, they tell the public about it by means of a loudspeaker system.

ex.en: The loudspeaker announced the arrival of the train.
ex.zh: 扬声器宣布了那列火车的到达。

d: adj. 宣布的
v. 宣布，宣告；通知；声称，宣称；宣布（某人）到达；（在广播或电视中）播音，广播（announce 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

ex.en: The two parties were still too much apart to form an alliance.
ex.zh: 这两个党派分歧大得还不能形成联盟。

e.en: An alliance is a relationship in which two countries, political parties, or organizations work together for some purpose.

ex.en: The Socialists' electoral strategy has been based on a tactical alliance with the Communists.
ex.zh: 社会党人的参选策略一直以和共产党人的战略性结盟为基础。

d: n. 联盟，结盟；结盟团体，结盟国家；（人们间的）亲密关系，（尤指）联姻

e.en: A country is one of the political units which the world is divided into, covering a particular area of land.

ex.en: Indonesia is the fifth most populous country in the world.
ex.zh: 印度尼西亚是世界上人口第五大国。

ex.en: ...the boundary between the two countries.
ex.zh: …这两个国家的分界线。

e.en: The people who live in a particular country can be referred to as the country.

ex.en: Finally the country got some much-needed good news.
ex.zh: 最后该国人民得到了一些他们最需要的好消息。

e.en: The country consists of places such as farms, open fields, and villages which are away from towns and cities.

ex.en: ...a healthy life in the country.
ex.zh: …在乡村的健康生活。

ex.en: She was cycling along a country road near Compiègne.
ex.zh: 她正沿着贡比涅附近的一条乡间小路骑车。

e.en: A particular kind of country is an area of land which has particular characteristics or is connected with a particular well-known person.

ex.en: Varese Ligure is a small town in mountainous country east of Genoa.
ex.zh: 瓦雷泽·利古里亚是一座位于热那亚东部山区的小镇。

d: n. 国家（country 的复数）

e.en: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.

ex.en: I always wanted to call the dog Mufty for some reason.
ex.zh: 出于某种原因，我总想叫那条狗穆夫蒂。

ex.en: "Doctor..."—"Will you please call me Sarah?"
ex.zh: “…医生” — “请叫我萨拉好吗？”

e.en: If you call someone or something a particular thing, you suggest they are that thing or describe them as that thing. 把…描述为;

ex.en: The speech was interrupted by members of the Republican Party, who called him a traitor.
ex.zh: 演讲被称他为叛徒的共和党成员们打断了。

ex.en: She calls me lazy and selfish.
ex.zh: 她说我又懒又自私。

e.en: If you call something, you say it in a loud voice, because you are trying to attract someone's attention.

ex.en: He could hear the others downstairs calling his name.
ex.zh: 他能听到其他人在楼下喊他的名字。

e.en: Call out means the same as call.

ex.en: The butcher's son called out a greeting.
ex.zh: 那屠夫的儿子声音洪亮地招呼了一声。

d: adj. 叫做，称作
v. 给……取名；称呼，把……唤作；把……看作，把……算作（ call 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: to coax or cajole or act in a wheedling manner
carnival

d: v. （英国英语，非正式）哄骗，劝诱
n. （非正式）狂欢节（等于 carnival）；（非正式，多用于美国英语）巡回游乐团工作人员；（非正式）哄骗的话，花言巧语；（Carney）卡尼，卡内（人名）
n. 加拿大（北美洲国家）

e.en: Someone who is a citizen of a particular country is legally accepted as belonging to that country.

ex.en: ...American citizens.
ex.zh: …美国公民。

e.en: The citizens of a town or city are the people who live there.

ex.en: ...the citizens of Buenos Aires.
ex.zh: …布宜诺斯艾利斯的市民。

d: n. 公民（citizen 的复数）；市民，城镇居民

e.en: A canopy is a decorated cover, often made of cloth, which is placed above something such as a bed or a seat. 华盖;
A canopy is a layer of something that spreads out and covers an area, for example the branches and leaves that spread out at the top of trees in a forest. 遮盖; (树)

ex.en: The trees formed such a dense canopy that all beneath was a deep carpet of pine needles.
ex.zh: 这些树形成了浓密的冠盖，下面是一层厚厚的松针。

d: n. （座位或床上的）顶罩，华盖；树冠层，顶蓬似的树荫；（飞机的）座舱盖；天篷，顶篷；降落伞的丝质（或尼龙）伞衣，伞盖
v. 用顶篷遮盖

e.en: If you cannot conceive of something, you cannot imagine it or believe it. 想像;

ex.en: I just can't even conceive of that quantity of money.
ex.zh: 我简直无法想像那样一笔数量的钱。

ex.en: We could not conceive that he might soon be dead.
ex.zh: 我们无法相信他可能很快就会死去。

e.en: If you conceive something as a particular thing, you consider it to be that thing.

ex.en: The ancients conceived the earth as afloat in water.
ex.zh: 古人认为地球漂浮在水里。

ex.en: We conceive of the family as being in a constant state of change.
ex.zh: 我们认为家庭是处于不断变化之中的。

e.en: If you conceive a plan or idea, you think of it and work out how it can be done.

ex.en: She had conceived the idea of a series of novels, each of which would reveal some aspect of Chinese life.
ex.zh: 她已经想出了个关于一个系列小说的主意，每一部都将反映中国人生活的某一方面。

e.en: When a woman conceives a child or conceives, she becomes pregnant. 怀 (胎);

ex.en: Women, he says, should give up alcohol before they plan to conceive.
ex.zh: 他说女人在计划怀孕前应该戒酒。

d: v. 构思，构想出；设想，想象，认为；怀孕（conceive 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 构想出的，设想的（常用于构成 well-conceived、ill-conceived 等复合词）

e.en: If you commission something or commission someone to do something, you formally arrange for someone to do a piece of work for you.

ex.en: The Department of Agriculture commissioned a study into organic farming.
ex.zh: 农业部委托了一项有机耕作的研究。

ex.en: You can commission them to paint something especially for you.
ex.zh: 你可以委托他们专门为你画点什么。

e.en: Commission is also a noun.

ex.en: Our china can be bought off the shelf or by commission.
ex.zh: 我们的瓷器可以现货购买或委托定做。

e.en: A commission is a piece of work that someone is asked to do and is paid for.

ex.en: Just a few days ago, I finished a commission.
ex.zh: 就在几天之前我完成了一项委托任务。

e.en: Commission is a sum of money paid to a salesperson for every sale that he or she makes. If a salesperson is paid on commission, the amount they receive depends on the amount they sell.

ex.en: The salespeople work on commission only.
ex.zh: 推销员只拿销售佣金。

d: n. 考察团，委员会；佣金，回扣；犯罪；委托，命令；（军队中的）官职，军衔；（尤指艺术品）委托制作；所授之权，代办权
v. 委托撰写，委托制作；委任，任命……为军官；（使军舰）正式使用，服现役
adj. 最深的；最深切的，极度的，最深刻的
adv. 最深地
n. 欧洲（世界七大洲之一）；欧洲联盟，欧洲国家整体（政治、经济语境中的转喻）
abbr. 区分编码规则（Distinguished Encoding Rules）
n. （Der）人名；（法、西、塞、塞内）德尔

e.en: Friday is the day after Thursday and before Saturday.

ex.en: Mr. Cook is intending to go to the Middle East on Friday.
ex.zh: 库克先生正打算星期五去中东。

ex.en: ...Friday November 6.
ex.zh: …11月6日星期五。

d: n. 星期五；忠仆

e.en: A hedge is a row of bushes or small trees, usually along the edge of a lawn, garden, field, or road.
If you hedge against something unpleasant or unwanted that might affect you, especially losing money, you do something which will protect you from it. 防备 (尤指金钱损失)

ex.en: You can hedge against illness with insurance.
ex.zh: 你可以买保险以备治疗患病之需。

e.en: Something that is a hedge against something unpleasant will protect you from its effects.

ex.en: Gold is traditionally a hedge against inflation.
ex.zh: 黄金传统上是一种防范通货膨胀的手段。

e.en: If you hedge your bets, you reduce the risk of losing a lot by supporting more than one person or thing in a situation where they are opposed to each other.

ex.en: The company tried to hedge its bets by diversifying into other fields.
ex.zh: 该公司试图通过兼营其他领域几面下注。

d: n. 树篱；防范措施，防备手段
v. 拐弯抹角，避免正面回答；用树篱围住；包围，限制；采取保值措施以规避风险
【名】 （Hedge）（美、英、加、澳、印、法）赫奇（人名）

e.en: Geopolitics is concerned with politics and the way that geography affects politics or relations between countries.

d: n. 地缘政治学，地理政治论（研究地理环境、资源等对政治和国际关系影响的学科）；地缘政治，地缘政治格局（指受地理位置、资源等战略因素制约的国际政治关系与态势）

e.en: Like-minded people have similar opinions, ideas, attitudes, or interests.

ex.en: ...the opportunity to mix with hundreds of like-minded people.
ex.zh: …与数百个志趣相投的人打交道的机会。

d: adj. 志同道合的，志趣相投的，具有相似意向或目的的

e.en: If one person joins another, they move or go to the same place, for example, so that both of them can do something together.

ex.en: His wife and children moved to join him in their new home.
ex.zh: 他的妻子和孩子们搬来和他一起住在新家。

e.en: If you join an organization, you become a member of it or start work as an employee of it. 参加 (组织)

ex.en: He joined the Army five years ago.
ex.zh: 他５年前参了军。

e.en: If you join an activity that other people are doing, you take part in it or become involved with it. 参加 (活动)

ex.en: The United States joined the war in April 1917.
ex.zh: 美国于1917年4月参战。

ex.en: The pastor requested the women present to join him in prayer.
ex.zh: 该牧师请在场的妇女和他一起祈祷。

e.en: If you join a line, you stand at the end of it so that you are part of it. 加入 (队列)

ex.en: It is advised that fans seeking autographs join the line before practice starts.
ex.zh: 建议寻求亲笔签名的影迷们在活动开始前排好队。

d: v. 成为……的一员，参加；连接，接合；联合，汇合；上（火车、飞机等）；和……作伴，随同
n. 连接处，接合点

e.en: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

ex.en: His father was a Baptist minister.
ex.zh: 他父亲是一名浸礼会牧师。

e.en: A minister is a person who officially represents their government in a foreign country and has a lower rank than an ambassador.

ex.en: He concluded a deal with the Danish minister in Washington.
ex.zh: 他在华盛顿与丹麦公使达成了一项协议。

e.en: In some countries outside the United States, a minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department.

ex.en: When the government came to power, he was named minister of culture.
ex.zh: 这届政府上台时，他被任命为了文化部长。

d: n. （英国及其他许多国家的）部长，大臣；牧师；公使，外交使节
v. 满足（……的需要），帮助；当牧师；执行（或主持）（圣餐式）

e.en: A nation is an individual country considered together with its social and political structures.

ex.en: Such policies would require unprecedented cooperation between nations.
ex.zh: 这样的一些政策会要求国与国之间前所未有的合作。

e.en: The nation is sometimes used to refer to all the people who live in a particular country, or all the people who belong to a particular ethnic group. 全国国民;

ex.en: It was a story that touched the nation's heart.
ex.zh: 这是一个感动了全民族的故事。

ex.en: ...the former chief of the Cherokee nation.
ex.zh: …前任切罗基族酋长。

d: n. 国家（nation 的复数）；民族，部族群体（nation 的复数）；内申斯（Nations，英语姓氏）

e.en: Nature is all the animals, plants, and other things in the world that are not made by people, and all the events and processes that are not caused by people.

ex.en: The most amazing thing about nature is its infinite variety.
ex.zh: 大自然最让人惊叹的地方在于它的无限多样性。

ex.en: ...grasses that grow wild in nature.
ex.zh: …自然界生长的野草

e.en: The nature of something is its basic quality or character.

ex.en: Mr. Sharp would not comment on the nature of the issues being investigated.
ex.zh: 夏普先生不愿就被调查问题的本质发表评论。

ex.en: The rise of a major power is both economic and military in nature.
ex.zh: 一个大国的崛起本质上既是经济上的，也是军事上的。

e.en: Someone's nature is their character, which they show by the way they behave.

ex.en: Jeya feels that her ambitious nature made her unsuitable for an arranged marriage.
ex.zh: 耶雅觉得她的雄心勃勃的个性使她不适合包办婚姻。

ex.en: She trusted people. That was her nature.
ex.zh: 她信任人，那是她的天性。

e.en: If you say that something has a particular characteristic by its nature or by its very nature, you mean that things of that type always have that characteristic.

ex.en: Peacekeeping, by its nature, makes pre-planning difficult.
ex.zh: 维和行动本质上很难预先计划。

d: n. 大自然，自然界；性格，秉性；本质，特点；类型，种类；具有某种特性的人
【名】 （Nature）（法）纳蒂尔（人名）

e.en: A powerful person or organization is able to control or influence people and events.

ex.en: You're a powerful man – people will listen to you.
ex.zh: 你是个有影响力的人–人们会听你的。

ex.en: ...Russia and India, two large, powerful countries.
ex.zh: …俄罗斯和印度——两个有影响力的大国。

e.en: You say that someone's body is powerful when it is physically strong.

ex.en: Hans flexed his powerful muscles.
ex.zh: 汉斯放松了他强壮的肌肉。

e.en: 强壮地

ex.en: He is described as a strong, powerfully-built man of 60.
ex.zh: 他被描述成一个身强力壮的60岁的人。

e.en: A powerful machine or substance is effective because it is very strong.

ex.en: The more powerful the car the more difficult it is to handle.
ex.zh: 汽车的功效越大，操纵起来越难。

ex.en: ...powerful computer systems.
ex.zh: …强大的计算机系统。

d: adj. （人，组织，国家）强大的，有影响力的；大功率的，高效能的；（文章、演讲或艺术品）极具感染力的，有震撼力的；（感情）强烈的，（效果）巨大的；强壮的，强健的；猛烈的，有力的；（毒品或化学品）强效的；刺耳的，刺眼的，刺鼻的
adv. 非常，很

e.en: Partnership or a partnership is a relationship in which two or more people, organizations, or countries work together as partners.

ex.en: ...the partnership between Germany's banks and its businesses.
ex.zh: …德国的各银行与德国企业之间的伙伴关系。

d: n.  合伙（关系），合股；合伙企业；合伙人；（两个人、组织或国家之间的）合作关系，伙伴关系；合伙契约；（板球）（回合结束前或其中一人被迫退场前）一对击球手的跑动得分数

e.en: You use our to indicate that something belongs or relates both to yourself and to one or more other people.

ex.en: We're expecting our first baby.
ex.zh: 我们要生第一个孩子了。

e.en: A speaker or writer sometimes uses our to indicate that something belongs or relates to people in general. (用于泛指)

ex.en: We are all entirely responsible for our actions, and for our reactions.
ex.zh: 我们都对自己的行为、自己的反应完全负责。

d: det. 我们的，我方的；（泛指）我们（人类、一般人）的

e.en: You use prime to describe something that is most important in a situation.

ex.en: Political stability, meanwhile, will be a prime concern.
ex.zh: 与此同时，政治稳定将是头等大事。

ex.en: It could be a prime target for guerrilla attack.
ex.zh: 它会是游击队进攻的一个主要目标。

e.en: You use prime to describe something that is of the best possible quality.

ex.en: The location of these beaches makes them prime sites for development.
ex.zh: 这些海滩的位置使它们成为开发的最佳选址。

e.en: You use prime to describe an example of a particular kind of thing that is absolutely typical.

ex.en: The prime example is Macy's, once the undisputed king of California retailers.
ex.zh: 最典型的例子是梅西百货，曾是加州零售商们公认的王者。

e.en: If someone or something is in their prime, they are at the stage in their existence when they are at their strongest, most active, or most successful.

ex.en: Maybe I'm just coming into my prime now.
ex.zh: 可能我刚迈入我的最佳时期。

ex.en: We've had a series of athletes trying to come back well past their prime.
ex.zh: 我们有不少早已过了鼎盛时期的运动员在试图复出。

d: adj. 主要的，首要的；优质的，第一流的；最可能的，最适合的；最理想的，最典型的；最初的，原始的；素（或质）数的（如2，3，5，7，11）；互为素或质数的
v. 事先指点，使（某人）做好准备；把（某事物）准备好，使备用；给（表面）涂上底色
n. 盛年，壮年时期；质数，素数；上标符号（'），（数字后）分钟（或英尺）符号；（八个防御姿势的）第一姿势；（自行车比赛中设特别奖的）特设行程；起始，原初；晨经，晨祷（传统上于白天中的第一个小时即早晨六点所做的祈祷，现罕用）
【名】 （Prime）（英）普赖姆，（德）普里梅（人名）

e.en: The president of a country that has no king or queen is the person who is the head of state of that country.

ex.en: ...President Mubarak.
ex.zh: …穆巴拉克总统。

e.en: The president of an organization is the person who has the highest position in it. (某组织的)

ex.en: ...Alexandre de Merode, the president of the medical commission.
ex.zh: …亚历山大·德梅罗德，医学委员会主席。

d: n. 总统，国家主席；（机构、俱乐部、学院等的）负责人，会长，院长，主席；（公司）董事长，（银行）行长，总裁；（基督教）圣餐主持教士

e.en: Protective means designed or intended to protect something or someone from harm.

ex.en: Protective gloves reduce the absorption of chemicals through the skin.
ex.zh: 防护手套可以减少皮肤对化学物质的吸收。

e.en: If someone is protective toward you, they look after you and show a strong desire to keep you safe.

ex.en: He is very protective toward his mother.
ex.zh: 他对母亲爱护备至。

d: adj. 保护的，防护的；呵护的，有保护欲的；有贸易保护倾向的，实行关税保护的
n. 保护物，防护物；避孕套

e.en: A reporter is someone who writes news articles or who broadcasts news reports.

ex.en: ...a TV reporter.
ex.zh: …一名电视台记者。

d: n. 记者（reporter 的复数）

e.en: If you serve your country, an organization, or a person, you do useful work for them. 为…服务;

ex.en: It is unfair to soldiers who have served their country well for many years.
ex.zh: 对忠心效力国家多年的士兵们来说，这是不公平的。

e.en: If you serve in a particular place or as a particular official, you perform official duties, especially in the armed forces, as a civil servant, or as a politician. 服役;

ex.en: During the second world war he served with 92nd Airborne.
ex.zh: 第二次世界大战期间，他在第92空降师服役。

ex.en: They have both served on the school board.
ex.zh: 他们俩都曾在学校董事会任职。

e.en: If something serves as a particular thing or serves a particular purpose, it performs a particular function, which is often not its intended function. 对…有用;

ex.en: She ushered me into the front room, which served as her office.
ex.zh: 她领我进入前厅，那儿用做她的办公室了。

ex.en: I really do not think that an inquiry would serve any useful purpose.
ex.zh: 我真的认为一场咨询不会起什么作用。

e.en: If something serves people or an area, it provides them with something that they need. 供应;

ex.en: This could mean the closure of thousands of small businesses which serve the community.
ex.zh: 这意味着数以千计的为社区提供服务的小企业可能会关闭。

ex.en: ...improvements in the public water-supply system serving the Nairobi area.
ex.zh: …内罗毕地区公共供水系统的改善。

d: v. 为……工作，服役；端上，给……提供（餐饮）；够……吃； 接待，服务；对……有用，满足；（向某地或某群体）供应，提供；服刑，服劳役； 送达（传票、令状等）；（网球、排球等）发球；开（某人）（玩笑）；产生……的效果；（军）操作（枪炮）；（航海）卷缠（绳索）；（雄性种畜）与（雌性）交配；（基督教）在弥撒中担任助祭
n. （网球、排球等的）发球； 申斥
【名】  （Serve）（法）塞尔夫（人名）；（Serve）（法）塞尔夫（人名）

e.en: Shaken is the past participle of . shake

d: v. 摇动，动摇，震动（shake 的过去分词）
adj. 震惊的，不安的，发抖的
n. （Shaken）人名；（俄）沙肯

e.en: Speaking is the activity of giving speeches and talks. 讲话;

ex.en: It would also train women union members in public speaking and decision-making.
ex.zh: 它也将在公开演说和做决策方面培训女工会成员。

e.en: You can say "speaking as a parent" or "speaking as a teacher," for example, to indicate that the opinion you are giving is based on your experience as a parent or as a teacher.

ex.en: Well, speaking as a journalist I'm dismayed by the amount of pressure there is for pictures of combat.
ex.zh: 嗯，作为一名新闻工作者，我为人们对于战斗图片有如此大的需求量而深感不安。

e.en: You use speaking in expressions such as generally speaking and technically speaking to indicate which things or which particular aspect of something you are talking about. 一般说来/大致说来/

ex.en: Generally speaking there was no resistance to the idea.
ex.zh: 总的说来没有对这个主意的抵制。

d: n. 说话；演讲
adj. 讲话的；演讲的；富于表情的；（画像）逼真的；雄辩的；讲某种语言的
v. 讲；交谈；发言；责备；劝告；表明；显示；发出特有的响声（speak 的现在分词）

e.en: A summit is a meeting at which the leaders of two or more countries discuss important matters.

ex.en: ...next week's Washington summit.
ex.zh: …下周的华盛顿峰会。

e.en: The summit of a mountain is the top of it. (山)

ex.en: He made it to the summit of Kilimanjaro before collapsing.
ex.zh: 他成功登上乞力马扎罗山峰顶后倒下了。

d: n. （政府间的）首脑会议，峰会；山顶，顶峰；（成就的）顶点，最高点；最高阶层
adj. 最高级的，政府首脑的
v. 登上（顶峰）

e.en: If someone formally unveils something such as a new statue or painting, they draw back the curtain which is covering it.

ex.en: ...a ceremony to unveil a monument to the victims.
ex.zh: …死难者纪念碑揭幕仪式。

e.en: If you unveil a plan, new product, or some other thing that has been kept secret, you introduce it to the public.

ex.en: Mr. Werner unveiled his new strategy this week.
ex.zh: 沃纳先生本周公布了他的新策略。

d: v. 首次公开，揭示，公布；为……揭幕，揭去……上的覆盖物；除去面纱，显露（unveil 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 未戴面纱的；显露的；公开的

e.en: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong. 兴旺发达;

ex.en: He appears to be thriving.
ex.zh: 他看起来兴旺发达蒸蒸日上。

ex.en: Today her company continues to thrive.
ex.zh: 如今，她的公司继续蓬勃发展。

e.en: If you say that someone thrives on a particular situation, you mean that they enjoy it or that they can deal with it very well, especially when other people find it unpleasant or difficult. 喜欢; 从容应对 (尤指别人不喜欢或认为困难的事)

ex.en: Many people thrive on a stressful lifestyle.
ex.zh: 许多人喜欢有压力的生活方式。

d: v. 茁壮成长，兴旺，繁荣；（尤指在别人觉得困难的时候）以……为乐，可以出色应对

e.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

ex.en: He is utterly unpredictable.
ex.zh: 他这个人完全让人捉摸不透。

e.en: 不可预测性

ex.en: ...the unpredictability of the weather.
ex.zh: …天气的不可预测性。

d: adj. 无法预测的，不定的；（人）善变的，难以捉摸的
n. 不可预言的事
n. 厄休拉（女子名）
n. （Von）（美、菲）文（人名）

e.en: If someone is welcoming or if they behave in a welcoming way, they are friendly to you when you arrive somewhere, so that you feel happy and accepted.

ex.en: When we arrived at her house Susan was very welcoming.
ex.zh: 当我们到达苏珊家时，她非常热情。

d: adj. 欢迎的，热情款待的；舒适的；迎接（某人）的
v. 欢迎（welcome 的现在分词）
v. 使恢复生机，使焕发活力

e.en: A bank is an institution where people or businesses can keep their money.
