ex.en: Students should look to see which bank offers them the service that best suits their financial needs.
ex.zh: 学生们应该去了解哪家银行的服务最适合他们的财务需求。

e.en: A bank is a building where a bank offers its services. 银行 (大楼)
If you bank with a particular bank, you have an account with that bank. (在某银行)

ex.en: I have banked with Coutts & Co. for years.
ex.zh: 我已经使用雇资银行很多年了。

e.en: a small container used at home for keeping money

d: n. 银行；储蓄罐；库存，库；河岸；斜坡；云团，雾团；一排，一组；庄家的赌本；（泥）滩，沙洲
v. 把（钱）存入银行，把……储存入库；与银行有业务往来；（飞机）倾斜飞行；使反弹；（把某物）堆积起来，聚集起来；（用煤等）封炉火
【名】 （Bank）（英、德、俄）班克，（法、匈）邦克（人名）

e.en: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.

ex.en: I was sitting on the floor shivering with fear because a bullet had been fired through a window.
ex.zh: 我坐在地板上吓得浑身发抖，因为有一颗子弹射穿窗户打了进来。

e.en: A fear is a thought that something unpleasant might happen or might have happened.

ex.en: These youngsters are motivated by fear of failure.
ex.zh: 这些年轻人因担心失败而被激发。

ex.en: Then one day his worst fears were confirmed.
ex.zh: 后来有一天，他最大的担心被证实了。

e.en: If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely. (发生坏事的)

ex.en: There is a fear that the freeze on bank accounts could prove a lasting deterrent to investors.
ex.zh: 冻结银行帐户很可能对投资者是一个长期的威慑因素。

e.en: If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.

ex.en: He also spoke of his fears for the future of his country's culture.
ex.zh: 他也谈及了他对祖国文化前景的担忧。

d: v. 害怕，畏惧；担心，忧虑；敬畏
n. 恐惧；担心；（坏事发生的）可能性；敬畏

e.en: Technological means relating to or associated with technology.

ex.en: ...an era of very rapid technological change.
ex.zh: …一个技术飞速变革的时代。

e.en: 技术上地

ex.en: ...technologically advanced aircraft.
ex.zh: …技术先进的飞机。

d: adj. 技术的，科技的，工艺的

e.en: If someone in authority suppresses an activity, they prevent it from continuing, by using force or making it illegal. 镇压;

ex.en: ...drug traffickers, who continue to flourish despite international attempts to suppress them.
ex.zh: …尽管全世界努力镇压却继续猖獗的毒贩子们。

e.en: 镇压;

ex.en: ...people who were imprisoned after the violent suppression of the pro-democracy movement protests.
ex.zh: …赞成民主的抗议活动受暴力镇压后被囚禁的人们。

e.en: If a natural function or reaction of your body is suppressed, it is stopped, for example by drugs or illness. 抑制 (身体功能或反应)

ex.en: The reproduction and growth of the cancerous cells can be suppressed by bombarding them with radiation.
ex.zh: 癌细胞的繁殖和生长可通过放射线辐射加以抑制。

e.en: 抑制

ex.en: Eye problems can indicate an unhealthy lifestyle with subsequent suppression of the immune system.
ex.zh: 眼睛问题表明一种不健康的生活方式以及随后免疫系统所受的抑制。

d: v. 镇压，压制，制止；禁止；抑制，克制，忍住；隐瞒，封锁（suppress 的现在分词）
adj. 制止的，抑制的

e.en: Someone's wages are the amount of money that is regularly paid to them for the work that they do.

ex.en: His wages have gone up.
ex.zh: 他的工资涨了。

e.en: If a person, group, or country wages a campaign or a war, they start it and continue it over a period of time. 发动 (运动或战争)

ex.en: The government, along with the three factions that had been waging a civil war, signed a peace agreement.
ex.zh: 政府和发动了内战的3方一起签订了1份和平协议。

d: n. （wage 的复数）工资，报酬，工钱；应得的报偿或惩罚（如 the wages of sin）
v. 开展，发动（运动、战争等）（wage 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A revolution is a successful attempt by a large group of people to change the political system of their country by force.

ex.en: The period since the revolution has been one of political turmoil.
ex.zh: 自革命以来的这一段时期是一个政治动荡的时期。

e.en: A revolution in a particular area of human activity is an important change in that area.

ex.en: The nineteenth century witnessed a revolution in ship design and propulsion.
ex.zh: 19世纪经历了船舶设计和推进上的一次重大变革。

d: n. （思想、工作方式等的）彻底变革；（使用武力、暴力的）革命；旋转；旋转一周；（马克思主义）共产主义革命（The Revolution）；循环

e.en: You can use winning to describe a person or thing that wins something such as a competition, game, or election.

ex.en: ...the winning lotto ticket.
ex.zh: …中奖的乐透彩票。

e.en: You can use winning to describe actions or qualities that please other people and make them feel friendly toward you.

ex.en: She gave him another of her winning smiles.
ex.zh: 她又给了他一个迷人的微笑。

d: adj. （常作定语）获胜的，胜利的；（票券、奖项等）中奖的，获奖的；制胜的；迷人的，吸引人的，讨人喜欢的
v. （win 的现在分词/动名词）在战斗、比赛、游戏等中赢，获胜；赢得（奖品等）；通过努力得到（某物）
n. （常用复数 winnings）赢得的钱（尤指赌博等赢来的钱）；（Winning）（美、英）温宁（人名）

e.en: Someone who is glum is sad and quiet because they are disappointed or unhappy about something.

ex.en: She was very glum and was obviously missing her children.
ex.zh: 她十分闷闷不乐，显然在思念她的孩子们。

e.en: 闷闷不乐地

ex.en: When Eleanor returned, I was still sitting glumly on the couch.
ex.zh: 埃莉诺回来时，我仍然闷闷不乐地坐在沙发上。

d: adj. 忧郁的，闷闷不乐的，沮丧的；死气沉沉的，阴沉的，沉闷的
n. （Glum）格卢姆（人名）
n. 冠状病毒病

e.en: a tough twill-weave cotton fabric used for hard-wearing trousers, overalls, etc

d: n. 牛仔裤；[纺] 斜纹棉布

e.en: If you spread something somewhere, you open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

ex.en: She spread a towel on the sand and lay on it.
ex.zh: 她把一块浴巾铺在沙地上，然后躺在上面。

e.en: Spread out means the same as . 铺开 (同)(spread)

ex.en: He extracted several glossy prints and spread them out on a low coffee table.
ex.zh: 他抽出几张光面照片铺在一张矮咖啡桌上。

e.en: If you spread your arms, hands, fingers, or legs, you stretch them out until they are far apart. 伸展开 (手臂、手、手指、腿等)

ex.en: Sitting on the floor, spread your legs as far as they will go without overstretching.
ex.zh: 坐在地板上，尽可能分开双腿，但不要过度拉伸。

e.en: Spread out means the same as .

ex.en: David made a gesture, spreading out his hands as if he were showing that he had no explanation to make.
ex.zh: 大卫做了个手势，双手一摊，似乎表示他没有什么可解释的。

d: v. 传播，蔓延，扩散；摊开，铺开，展开；涂敷；分散，分摊（spread 的现在分词）
n. 传播，扩散，蔓延的行为或过程（spread 的动名词）

e.en: If there is an outbreak of something unpleasant, such as violence or a disease, it suddenly starts to happen. (暴动、疾病等的)

ex.en: The four-day festival ended a day early after an outbreak of violence involving hundreds of youths.
ex.zh: 由于一起数百名年轻人参与的暴力事件的爆发，为期4天的庆祝活动提前1天结束。

ex.en: ...an outbreak of chickenpox.
ex.zh: …水痘的暴发。

d: n. （战争、疾病、暴力等的）爆发，突然发生
卡西亚

e.en: (in the US) Center for Disease Control (美国)

d: abbr. （美国）疾病控制与预防中心（Centers for Disease Control and Prevention），疾控中心，疾病防治中心；（美国）市民民防团（Citizens' Defense Corps）；（美国）控制数据公司（Control Data Corporation）

e.en: The centre of something is the middle of it.

ex.en: A large, wooden table dominates the centre of the room.
ex.zh: 一张大木桌占据了房间的中央。

e.en: A centre is a building where people have meetings, take part in a particular activity, or get help of some kind. (会议、活动、援助的)

ex.en: She now also does pottery classes at a community centre.
ex.zh: 她现在还在社区中心上陶艺课。

e.en: If an area or town is a centre for an industry or activity, that industry or activity is very important there. (行业、活动的) 中心;

ex.en: New York is also a major international financial centre.
ex.zh: 纽约也是一个重要的国际金融中心。

e.en: The centre of a town or city is the part where there are the most stores and businesses and where a lot of people come from other areas to work or shop. (镇、市的)

ex.en: ...the city centre.
ex.zh: …市中心。

d: n. centre 的复数（英式拼写）：中心，中央；中心机构，活动中心；市中心；中锋；转轴
v. centre 的第三人称单数（英式拼写）：集中于，以……为主题，围绕；放在中央，使居中，使对准中心

e.en: in Canada Children's Aid Society (加拿大)

d: n. case 的复数：情况，情形；实例，案例；病例，病案；诉讼，官司；案件，案子；容器，箱子；一箱（或一盒）的量；（语法）格；（大写 Cases）卡塞斯（人名）
v. case 的第三人称单数：围绕，包盖；把…装入箱、盒或保护性容器内；（盗抢前）探察，踩点儿

e.en: An accord between countries or groups of people is a formal agreement; for example, to end a war.

ex.en: UNITA was legalized as a political party under the 1991 peace accords.
ex.zh: 根据1991年和平协议，安盟作为一个政党被合法化了。

e.en: If you are accorded a particular kind of treatment, people act toward you or treat you in that way. 给予 (某种待遇)

ex.en: His predecessor was accorded an equally tumultuous welcome.
ex.zh: 他的前任受到了同样热烈的欢迎。

ex.en: On his return home, the government accorded him the rank of Colonel.
ex.zh: 在他回国时，该国政府授予他上校军衔。

e.en: If something happens of its own accord, it seems to happen by itself, without anyone making it happen.

ex.en: In many cases the disease will clear up of its own accord.
ex.zh: 在很多情况下这种疾病会自动地痊愈。

e.en: If you do something of your own accord, you do it because you want to, without being asked or forced.

ex.en: He did not quit as France's prime minister of his own accord.
ex.zh: 他不是自愿地辞去法国总理一职的。

d: prep. 按照，根据，依照（according to，后接名词或名词短语）；据……所说（according to，引出消息来源）
conj. 根据，取决于（according as，后接从句）
adj. 相符的，相应的，一致的
v. accord 的现在分词（给予；符合，一致）

e.en: China is a hard white substance made from clay. It is used to make things such as cups, bowls, plates, and ornaments.

ex.en: ...a small bowl made of china.
ex.zh: …一个小瓷碗。

e.en: Cups, bowls, plates, and ornaments made of china are referred to as china.

ex.en: Judy collects blue and white china.
ex.zh: 朱迪收集青花瓷器。

e.en: a friend or companion 朋友;

d: n. 瓷，瓷料；瓷器，瓷制品；朋友；中国（China）
adj. 瓷制的
n. （Clai）人名；（意）克拉伊

e.en: If you say, for example, that one thing is large or small compared with another or compared to another, you mean that it is larger or smaller than the other thing.

ex.en: The room was light and lofty compared to the basement.
ex.zh: 这个房间与地下室比起来更亮更高。

e.en: You talk about one situation or thing compared with another or compared to another when contrasting the two situations or things.

ex.en: In 1800 Ireland's population was nine million, compared to Britain's 16 million.
ex.zh: 1800年爱尔兰的人口是900万，而英国人口是1600万。

d: v. compare 的过去式和过去分词：比较，对照；compared with/to：与……相比，和……比较起来（也作 as compared with/to）；compared to（用于比喻）：被比作，比喻为

e.en: A current is a steady and continuous flowing movement of some of the water in a river, lake, or ocean.

ex.en: Under normal conditions, the ocean currents of the tropical Pacific travel from east to west.
ex.zh: 在正常情况下，太平洋热带洋流自东流向西。

e.en: A current is a steady flowing movement of air.

ex.en: I felt a current of cool air blowing in my face.
ex.zh: 我感到一股凉气吹在脸上。

e.en: An electric current is a flow of electricity through a wire or circuit.

ex.en: A powerful electric current is passed through a piece of graphite.
ex.zh: 一股强大的电流被传导经过一块石墨。

e.en: A particular current is a particular feeling, idea, or quality that exists within a group of people.

ex.en: Each party represents a distinct current of thought.
ex.zh: 每个党派都代表一种独特的思想倾向。

d: adj. 现行的，当前的；通用的，流行的；最近的
n. 水流，气流；电流；思潮，趋势
【名】 （Current）（英）柯伦特（人名）

e.en: Control of an organization, place, or system is the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run. (对某组织机构的)

ex.en: The restructuring involves Mr. Ronson giving up control of the company.
ex.zh: 公司重组需要罗森先生放弃对公司的控制。

e.en: If something is under your control, you have the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run.

ex.en: All the newspapers are under government control.
ex.zh: 所有的报纸都处在政府控制之下。

e.en: If you are in control of something, you have the power to make all the important decisions about the way it is run.

ex.en: Nobody knows who is in control of the club.
ex.zh: 没有人知道谁掌管这个俱乐部。

e.en: If you have control of something or someone, you are able to make them do what you want them to do. (对某物或某人的)

ex.en: He lost control of his car.
ex.zh: 他失去了对他的车的控制。

d: n. （对国家、地区、机构等的）控制权，支配权；控制能力；操纵装置；管理，管制；指挥（或检查、控制）站，指挥（或检查、控制）人员；（键盘上的）控制键
v. 控制，掌管；限制，限定；阻止蔓延（或恶化）；操纵，控制（机器或系统等）；抑制，克制

e.en: Death is the permanent end of the life of a person or animal.

ex.en: 1.5 million people are in immediate danger of death from starvation.
ex.zh: 150万人正因饥饿而即将面临死亡的危险。

ex.en: ...the thirtieth anniversary of Judy Garland's death.
ex.zh: …朱迪·嘉兰逝世30周年。

e.en: The death of something is the permanent end of it.

ex.en: It meant the death of everything he had ever been or ever hoped to be.
ex.zh: 这意味着他曾拥有或希望拥有的一切的结束。

e.en: If you say that someone is at death's door, you mean they are very ill and likely to die.

ex.en: He told his boss a tale about his mother being at death's door.
ex.zh: 他给老板讲述了自己母亲病危的情况。

e.en: If you say that you will fight to the death for something, you are emphasizing that you will do anything to achieve or protect it, even if you suffer as a consequence.

ex.en: She'd have fought to the death for that child.
ex.zh: 她原想为那个孩子拼尽全力的。

d: n. 死亡数

e.en: The director of a play, film, or television programme is the person who decides how it will appear on stage or screen, and who tells the actors and technical staff what to do.

ex.en: "Cut!" the director yelled. "That was perfect."
ex.zh: “停！”导演叫道。“太好了！”

e.en: In some organizations and public authorities, the person in charge is referred to as the director. 主任;

ex.en: ...the director of the intensive care unit at Buffalo General Hospital.
ex.zh: …布法罗总医院重症监护室的主任。

e.en: The directors of a company are its most senior managers, who meet regularly to make important decisions about how it will be run.

ex.en: He served on the board of directors of a local bank.
ex.zh: 他在当地一家银行的董事会担任董事。

e.en: The director of a choir is the person who is conducting it. (合唱团的)

d: n. 导演；管理者，负责人；董事，理事
【名】 （Director）（英）迪雷克托（人名）

e.en: A disease is an illness which affects people, animals, or plants, for example, one which is caused by bacteria or infection.

ex.en: ...the rapid spread of disease in the area.
ex.zh: …疾病在这一地区的迅速传播。

d: n. 疾病，病害；弊病，恶习
v. 传染，使……有病

e.en: A person's health is the condition of their body and the extent to which it is free from illness or is able to resist illness.

ex.en: Tea contains caffeine. It's bad for your health.
ex.zh: 茶含有咖啡因，对你的健康不利。

e.en: Health is a state in which a person is not suffering from any illness and is feeling well.

ex.en: In the hospital they nursed me back to health.
ex.zh: 在医院里他们精心照料我，使我恢复了健康。

e.en: The health of something such as an organization or a system is its success and the fact that it is working well.

ex.en: There's no way to predict the future health of the banking industry.
ex.zh: 根本无法预测银行业将来的兴旺。

d: n. 身体状况；健康；医疗，卫生；（组织或系统的）运行状况，运作状况；发达，兴旺

e.en: Funding is money which a government or organization provides for a particular purpose. (政府或组织为某目的而提供的)

ex.en: They hope for government funding for the programme.
ex.zh: 他们希望得到政府为这一计划提供的资金。

d: n. 专款，拨款
v. 资助，为……提供资金（fund 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Ebola or the Ebola virus is a virus that causes a fever and internal bleeding, usually resulting in death.

ex.en: Ebola is not as easily spread as viruses such as smallpox.
ex.zh: 埃博拉病毒不像天花这类病毒那样容易传播。

d: n. 埃博拉病毒

e.en: Illness is the fact or experience of being ill.

ex.en: If your child shows any signs of illness, take her to the doctor.
ex.zh: 如果您的孩子出现任何生病的症兆，带她去看医生。

e.en: An illness is a particular disease such as measles or pneumonia.

ex.en: She returned to her family home to recover from an illness.
ex.zh: 她回到自己家里养病。

d: n. 疾病；（某种）病，患病期

e.en: When you hold something, you carry or support it, using your hands or your arms. 拿着;

ex.en: Hold the knife at an angle.
ex.zh: 斜握着刀。

e.en: Hold is also a noun. 拿;

ex.en: He released his hold on the camera.
ex.zh: 他松开了握着照相机的手。

e.en: Hold is used in expressions such as grab hold of, catch hold of, and get hold of, to indicate that you close your hand tightly around something, for example to stop something moving or falling.

ex.en: I was woken up by someone grabbing hold of my sleeping bag.
ex.zh: 有人抓住我的睡袋把我弄醒了。

ex.en: A doctor and a nurse caught hold of his arms.
ex.zh: 一名医生和一名护士抓住了他的双臂。

e.en: When you hold someone, you put your arms around them, usually because you want to show them how much you like them or because you want to comfort them. (常因想表示喜爱和安慰而)

ex.en: If only he would hold her close to him.
ex.zh: 他要是紧紧抱住她就好了。

d: v. 抓住，托住；按住，捂住；拥抱；使保持（在某位置）；支撑……的重量；容纳，包含；监禁，拘留；守卫，控制；（好形势）保持不变；吸引某人的注意/兴趣；（使）保持（价值或水平）；保存，存贮；拥有；担任，任职；获得，赢得；持有，怀有（观点、信念等）；认为，相信；举行，进行；（车辆）抓（地）；（船或飞机）保持航线；持续（一种音符）；别挂断；停下，推迟；有效，适用；（使）具有；大量喝（酒）而不醉；不包括，排除在外；（使）坚持；携有违禁毒品
n. 握，抓；擒拿法；影响，控制；支撑点；底舱，货舱；预定；坚持，继续拥有；理解
【名】 （Hold）（英、德、捷）霍尔德（人名）

e.en: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount. 使增加;

ex.en: The population continues to increase.
ex.zh: 人口持续增长。

ex.en: Japan's industrial output increased by 2%.
ex.zh: 日本的工业产量增长了2%。

e.en: If there is an increase in the number, level, or amount of something, it becomes greater.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in productivity.
ex.zh: …生产率的急速增长。

e.en: If something is on the increase, it is happening more often or becoming greater in number or intensity.

ex.en: Crime is on the increase.
ex.zh: 犯罪活动日益猖獗。

d: v. 增长，增强，增大
n. 增长；增长量
【名】 （Increase）（英、美、印、尼日尼亚）英克里斯（人名）

e.en: A pandemic is an occurrence of a disease that affects many people over a very wide area.

ex.en: They feared a new cholera pandemic.
ex.zh: 他们担心一种新的霍乱流行病。

d: adj. （疾病）大规模流行的
n. 大流行病

e.en: Preparedness is the state of being ready for something to happen, especially for war or a disaster. (尤指军事、灾难)准备;

ex.en: The situation in the capital forced them to maintain military preparedness.
ex.zh: 首都的局势迫使他们时刻做好军事准备。

d: n. 有准备；已准备；做好准备（尤指为战争或灾难等所作的准备）；（正式）愿意，打算（做某事）

e.en: If it is possible to do something, it can be done. (做某事)

ex.en: If it is possible to find out where your brother is, we will.
ex.zh: 如果有可能找到你哥哥的下落，我们会找的。

ex.en: Everything is possible if we want it enough.
ex.zh: 如果我们非常想要的话，任何事都是有可能的。

e.en: A possible event is one that might happen. 可能 (发生)

ex.en: He referred the matter to the attorney general for possible action against several newspapers.
ex.zh: 他将此事交给首席检察官处理，以求可能诉讼几家报社。

ex.en: One possible solution, if all else fails, is to take legal action.
ex.zh: 如果其他方案都不行，一个可能的解决办法就是提起诉讼。

e.en: If you say that it is possible that something is true or correct, you mean that although you do not know whether it is true or correct, you accept that it might be. 可能 (真实)

ex.en: It is possible that there's an explanation for all this.
ex.zh: 这一切可能真有个解释。

e.en: If you do something as soon as possible, you do it as soon as you can. If you get as much as possible of something, you get as much of it as you can. 尽可能的 (早、多等)

ex.en: Please make your decision as soon as possible.
ex.zh: 请尽可能快地出你们的决定。

ex.en: Mrs. Pollard decided to learn as much as possible about the country before going there.
ex.zh: 波拉德夫人决定尽可能多地了解那个国家后再去那儿。

d: adj. 可能的，可能做到的；可能发生的，可能存在的；合乎事实的，合理的；尽可能……的；（用于形容词后表示强调）最好的（或最差的等）；可能的（但可能性很小）；（数字或分数）最高的；如果可能的话
n. 可能适合的人（事物）；可能性，能完成的事（the possible）；（尤指射击比赛的）最高分
n. 预防，防止

e.en: When someone or something reaches a place, they arrive there. 到达 (某地)

ex.en: He did not stop until he reached the door.
ex.zh: 他到门口才停住。

e.en: If someone or something has reached a certain stage, level, or amount, they are at that stage, level, or amount. 达到 (某一阶段、水平或数量)

ex.en: The process of political change in South Africa has reached the stage where it is irreversible.
ex.zh: 南非的政治变革进程已经到了不可逆转的阶段。

e.en: If you reach somewhere, you move your arm and hand to take or touch something. 伸手去 (拿或够东西)

ex.en: Judy reached into her handbag and handed me a small, printed leaflet.
ex.zh: 朱迪把手伸进手提袋中，递给我一张小小的印刷传单。

e.en: If you can reach something, you are able to touch it by stretching out your arm or leg. (伸展手臂或腿)

ex.en: Can you reach your toes with your fingertips?
ex.zh: 你能用手指尖触到脚趾头吗？

d: vt. 抵达；达到；伸出（手，臂）；够到……；将……拿下；（通过电话）联系；与……交流；打动，赢得（reach 的过去式与过去分词）
vi. 伸手去够，伸手去拿；到达（reach 的过去式与过去分词）

e.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

ex.en: Federal leaders continued their efforts to secure a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 联邦政府的领导人们继续他们争取停火的努力。

e.en: If you secure a place, you make it safe from harm or attack. 使 (某地)

ex.en: Staff withdrew from the main part of the prison but secured the perimeter.
ex.zh: 工作人员从监狱的主体区域撤了出来，但封锁了监狱四周。

e.en: A secure place is tightly locked or well protected, so that people cannot enter it or leave it. 锁牢了的;

ex.en: We'll make sure our home is as secure as possible from now on.
ex.zh: 我们将从现在起确保我们的家尽可能安全。

e.en: 锁牢了地;

ex.en: He locked the heavy door securely and kept the key in his pocket.
ex.zh: 他锁牢了那扇重门把钥匙放在了他的口袋里。

d: v. 固定，系牢；锁好，关严；保护，使安全；（经过努力）获得，争取到；以…作担保，抵押；确保，保证（secure 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 固定牢靠的；锁好的；安全的；有担保的（尤指贷款、债券等以抵押品作保）

e.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

ex.en: Such a move is rare, but not unprecedented.
ex.zh: 这样的举动少见，但并非从来没有过。

e.en: If you describe something as unprecedented, you are emphasizing that it is very great in quality, amount, or scale. (质量、数量或规模)

ex.en: The mission has been hailed as an unprecedented success.
ex.zh: 这次使命已被宣布为一次空前的成功。

d: adj. 前所未有的，史无前例的；（大小、数量、程度等）前所未知的，空前的

e.en: You use unless to introduce the only circumstances in which an event you are mentioning will not take place or in which a statement you are making is not true. 除非;

ex.en: Unless you are trying to lose weight to please yourself, it's going to be tough to keep your motivation level high.
ex.zh: 除非你在为了让自己开心而努力减肥，否则要保持驱动力很高将很难。

ex.en: We cannot understand disease unless we understand the person who has the disease.
ex.zh: 除非我们了解有某种疾病的人，否则我们不会了解疾病。

d: conj. 除非，除非在……情况下；若非，如果不
prep.  除……之外；除……之外

e.en: Treatment is medical attention given to a sick or injured person or animal.

ex.en: Many patients are not getting the medical treatment they need.
ex.zh: 许多病人都没有得到他们需要的医疗。

ex.en: ...a veterinary surgeon who specializes in the treatment of caged birds.
ex.zh: …一个专长治疗笼养鸟的兽医。

e.en: Your treatment of someone is the way you behave toward them or deal with them. 对待;

ex.en: We don't want any special treatment.
ex.zh: 我们不需要任何特殊待遇。

e.en: Treatment of something involves putting a particular substance onto or into it, in order to clean it, to protect it, or to give it special properties. (采用某种物质的)

ex.en: There should be greater treatment of sewage before it is discharged.
ex.zh: 污水排放前应该进行更充分的处理。

d: n. 对待，待遇；处理，讨论；治疗，医治；（净化或防治）处理，加工；护理，护理品；极致； 对待，待遇

e.en: If you warn someone about something such as a possible danger or problem, you tell them about it so that they are aware of it. 警告;

ex.en: When I had my first baby friends warned me that children were expensive.
ex.zh: 当我有了第一个孩子时，朋友们提醒我说养小孩是很花钱的。

ex.en: They warned him of the dangers of sailing alone.
ex.zh: 他们警告他独自航行的重重危险。

e.en: If you warn someone not to do something, you advise them not to do it so that they can avoid possible danger or punishment.

ex.en: Mrs. Blount warned me not to interfere.
ex.zh: 布朗特太太告诫我不要插手。

ex.en: "Don't do anything yet," he warned. "Too risky."
ex.zh: “先别行动，”他警告道，“太冒险了。”

d: v. 警告，提醒（warn 第三人称单数）：告诉某人可能发生的危险或问题，以便他们采取行动避免它。
· The lifeguard warns the swimmers about the strong currents.
救生员警告游泳者注意强烈的水流。

e.en: You use suspect when you are stating something that you believe is probably true, in order to make it sound less strong or direct.

ex.en: I suspect they were right.
ex.zh: 我觉得他们是正确的。

ex.en: The above complaints are, I suspect, just the tip of the iceberg.
ex.zh: 上述的这些抱怨，我觉得，不过是冰山的一角。

e.en: If you suspect that something dishonest or unpleasant has been done, you believe that it has probably been done. If you suspect someone of doing an action of this kind, you believe that they probably did it.

ex.en: He suspected that the woman staying in the flat above was using heroin.
ex.zh: 他怀疑住在楼上公寓里的那位女子在吸食海洛因。

ex.en: It was perfectly all right, he said, because the police had not suspected him of anything.
ex.zh: 一点儿没事，他说，因为警察对他没有任何怀疑。

e.en: A suspect is a person who the police or authorities think may be guilty of a crime.

ex.en: Police have arrested a suspect in a series of killings and sexual assaults in the city.
ex.zh: 警方逮捕了该城市一系列杀人强奸案件中的一名嫌疑犯。

e.en: Suspect things or people are ones that you think may be dangerous or may be less good or genuine than they appear.

ex.en: Delegates evacuated the building when a suspect package was found.
ex.zh: 一个可疑包裹被发现后，代表们撤离了这栋大楼。

d: adj. 有嫌疑的，涉嫌的，疑似的
v. 怀疑；疑有，察觉；猜想，觉得（suspect 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: In a military situation, a civilian is anyone who is not a member of the armed forces.

ex.en: The safety of civilians caught up in the fighting must be guaranteed.
ex.zh: 卷入战斗中的平民的安全必须得到保障。

e.en: In a military situation, civilian is used to describe people or things that are not military. 平民的;

ex.en: ...the country's civilian population.
ex.zh: …这个国家的平民人口。

ex.en: ...civilian casualties.
ex.zh: …平民伤亡。

d: n. 平民（civilian 的复数形式）

e.en: A commander is an officer in charge of a military operation or organization. 指挥官;

ex.en: The commander and some of the men had been released.
ex.zh: 指挥官和一些士兵已被释放。

e.en: A commander is an officer in the U.S. Navy or the Royal Navy.

d: n. 指挥官（commander 的复数）

e.en: Something or someone that is an asset is considered useful or helps a person or organization to be successful.

ex.en: Our creativity in the field of technology is our greatest asset.
ex.zh: 我们在技术领域的创造力是我们最大的资本。

e.en: The assets of a company or a person are all the things that they own.

ex.en: By the end of 1989 the group had assets of $3.5 billion.
ex.zh: 到1989年底该集团已有35亿美元的资产。

d: n. 有利条件，有价值的人或物；资产，财产
【名】（Asset）（法）阿塞（人名）

e.en: Sexual feelings or activities are connected with the act of sex or with people's desire for sex. 有关性行为的;

ex.en: This was the first sexual relationship I'd had.
ex.zh: 这是我第一次与人发生性关系。

e.en: 与性行为有关地;

ex.en: ...sexually transmitted diseases.
ex.zh: …性传播疾病。

e.en: Sexual means relating to the differences between male and female people.

ex.en: Women's groups denounced sexual discrimination.
ex.zh: 妇女组织谴责性别歧视。

e.en: 性别上地

ex.en: If you're sexually harassed, you ought to do something about it.
ex.zh: 如果遭到性骚扰，你应该对其采取行动。

d: adj. 性的，性行为的；性别的；性取向的；生殖的，有性繁殖的；（繁殖）配子融合的

e.en: An anniversary is a date that is remembered or celebrated because a special event happened on that date in a previous year.

ex.en: Vietnam is celebrating the one hundredth anniversary of the birth of Ho Chi Minh.
ex.zh: 越南正在庆祝胡志明的百年诞辰。

d: n. 周年纪念（日）

e.en: To ban something means to state officially that it must not be done, shown, or used. (官方)

ex.en: Canada will ban smoking in all offices later this year.
ex.zh: 加拿大将于今年晚些时候禁止在所有办公场所吸烟。

ex.en: Last year arms sales were banned.
ex.zh: 去年军火交易被明令禁止了。

e.en: A ban is an official ruling that something must not be done, shown, or used.

ex.en: The general lifted the ban on political parties.
ex.zh: 将军解除了对政党的官方禁令。

e.en: If you are banned from doing something, you are officially prevented from doing it.

ex.en: He was banned from driving for three years.
ex.zh: 他被禁止驾驶3年。

d: n. 禁止，禁令；逐出令；褫夺公民权的判决；诅咒；巴尼（罗马尼亚货币单位，复数bani）
v. 禁止，取缔；（官方）把（某人）逐出某地
【名】 （Ban）（美、罗马、克罗地亚）班恩（人名）

e.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change. (有计划的) 活动;

ex.en: During his election campaign he promised to put the economy back on its feet.
ex.zh: 竞选活动期间，他许诺要致力于恢复经济。

ex.en: ...a campaign to improve the training of staff.
ex.zh: …改进员工培训的一个活动。

e.en: In a war, a campaign is a series of planned movements carried out by armed forces. 一系列军事行动;

ex.en: The allies are intensifying their air campaign.
ex.zh: 盟军在加强他们的空中军事活动。

e.en: If someone campaigns for something, they carry out a planned set of activities over a period of time in order to achieve their aim.

ex.en: We are campaigning for law reform.
ex.zh: 我们正从事法律改革运动。

d: n. （有计划的）活动，运动；战役，战斗
v. 领导（参加）运动，从事竞选活动

e.en: Conflict is serious disagreement and argument about something important. If two people or groups are in conflict, they have had a serious disagreement or argument and have not yet reached agreement. 争执;

ex.en: Try to keep any conflict between you and your ex-partner to a minimum.
ex.zh: 尽量把你和前合伙人之间的争执控制到最少。

e.en: Conflict is a state of mind in which you find it impossible to make a decision.

ex.en: ...the anguish of his own inner conflict.
ex.zh: …他自己内心矛盾的痛苦。

e.en: Conflict is fighting between countries or groups of people. (国家或团体之间的)

ex.en: ...talks aimed at ending four decades of conflict.
ex.zh: …旨在结束40年冲突的会谈。

e.en: A conflict is a serious difference between two or more beliefs, ideas, or interests. If two beliefs, ideas, or interests are in conflict, they are very different. (信念、观点、利益之间的)

ex.en: There is a conflict between what they are doing and what you want.
ex.zh: 他们在做的和你想要的之间存在冲突。

d: n. 争执，争论，分歧；战斗，战争；抵触，矛盾
v. 冲突，抵触

e.en: An atrocity is a very cruel, shocking action.

ex.en: The killing was cold-blooded, and those who committed this atrocity should be tried and punished.
ex.zh: 这场杀戮非常残酷，那些犯下此暴行的人应该受到审判和惩罚。

d: n. （常伴有暴力伤害的）恶行，暴行

e.en: British means belonging or relating to the United Kingdom, or to its people or culture. 英国的;
The British are the people of Great Britain.

d: adj. 英国的；英国人的；大不列颠的
n. 英国人

e.en: The government of a country is the group of people who are responsible for governing it.

ex.en: The Government has insisted that confidence is needed before the economy can improve.
ex.zh: 政府强调需要有信心经济状况才能改善。

ex.en: ...democratic governments in countries like Britain and the U.S.
ex.zh: …英美等国的民主政府。

e.en: Government consists of the activities, methods, and principles involved in governing a country or other political unit.

ex.en: The first four years of government were completely disastrous.
ex.zh: 头4年的治理彻底失败了。

d: n. 政府，内阁；政体，国家体制；（国家等的）治理，管理；政府掌控经济和社会活动的程度；（语法）支配关系

e.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

ex.en: If the temperature drops below 0°C, water freezes.
ex.zh: 如果温度降到摄氏零度以下，水就会结冰。

ex.en: The ground froze solid.
ex.zh: 地面冻硬了。

e.en: If you freeze something such as food, you preserve it by storing it at a temperature below freezing point. You can also talk about how well food freezes.

ex.en: You can freeze the soup at this stage.
ex.zh: 你此时可以把汤冷藏。

e.en: When it freezes outside, the temperature falls below freezing point.

ex.en: What if it rained and then froze all through those months?
ex.zh: 如果那几个月一直下雨然后又结冰该怎么办？

e.en: Freeze is also a noun.

ex.en: The trees were damaged by a freeze in December.
ex.zh: 那些树被12月的一次冰冻冻坏了。

d: v. 结冰；冻住；冷藏，冷冻；感到很冷，冻僵；突然停止，呆住；使（物价或工资等）固定不动；冻结（钱财）；使定格；（计算机屏幕因系统故障）被暂时锁定
n. 冻结；停止；冰冻期；霜冻

e.en: If someone or something is implicated in a crime or a bad situation, they are involved in it or responsible for it. 牵涉其中的;

ex.en: The president was implicated in the cover-up and forced to resign.
ex.zh: 该总统与此次隐瞒真相的事件有牵连，被迫辞职。

d: adj. 有牵连的，牵涉其中的
v. 牵涉，使卷入；暗示（implicate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If someone or something falls, they move quickly downward onto or toward the ground, by accident or because of a natural force.

ex.en: He has again fallen from his horse.
ex.zh: 他又一次从马上落下来。

ex.en: Bombs fell in the town.
ex.zh: 炸弹落在了城里。

e.en: Fall is also a noun.

ex.en: The helmets are designed to withstand impacts equivalent to a fall from a bicycle.
ex.zh: 头盔设计成能承受相当于从自行车上摔下来的力度。

e.en: If a person or structure that is standing somewhere falls, they move from their upright position, so that they are then lying on the ground.

ex.en: The woman gripped the shoulders of her man to stop herself from falling.
ex.zh: 这个女人紧紧抓住了她男人的肩膀以防自己跌倒。

ex.en: He lost his balance and fell backwards.
ex.zh: 他失去了平衡，往后跌倒了。

e.en: Fall is also a noun.

ex.en: She broke her right leg in a bad fall.
ex.zh: 她在一次严重的跌倒中右腿骨折了。

d: v. 降落，落下；跌倒，倒塌；（水平、数量、价格等）下跌，减少；属于；下垂，低垂；照射（到），（阴影）落在；降临，发生；倒台，失势；被打败，沦陷；阵亡，被击毙；打中，击中；（嗓音或声音）变轻，变小；进入（某状态），开始变成（某事物）
n. 落下，跌倒；（数量、水平、价格等的）下降，降低；秋天，秋季；失败，垮台 ；瀑布；（摔跤或柔道项目中的）摔倒，压倒；（雨、雪等的）降落；堕落
【名】 （Fall）（西）法勒（人名）

e.en: If a person, animal, or other living thing is killed, something or someone causes them to die.

ex.en: More than 1,000 people have been killed by the armed forces.
ex.zh: 已经有一千多人被武装部队杀死。

ex.en: He had attempted to kill himself on several occasions.
ex.zh: 他好几次都企图自杀。

e.en: 杀害

ex.en: There is tension in the region following the killing of seven civilians.
ex.zh: 7名平民被杀害后，该地区的局势紧张。

e.en: The act of killing an animal after hunting it is referred to as the kill.

ex.en: After the kill the men and old women collect in an open space and eat a meal of whale meat.
ex.zh: 猎杀结束后，男人们和年长的妇女们聚在一个空地吃了一顿鲸肉宴。

e.en: If someone or something kills a project, activity, or idea, they completely destroy or end it. 使停止;

ex.en: His objective was to kill the space station project altogether.
ex.zh: 他的目的是使太空站计划完全停止。

d: adj. 被杀死的；镇静的；隔开的
v. kill 的过去式和过去分词
adj. 最大的；最大量的（large 的最高级）

e.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future. 进行中的;

ex.en: There is an ongoing debate on the issue.
ex.zh: 关于这个问题争论还在继续。

d: adj. 持续存在的，仍在进行的，不断发展的

e.en: The leader of a group of people or an organization is the person who is in control of it or in charge of it.

ex.en: We now need a new leader of the party and a new style of leadership.
ex.zh: 我们现在需要一个新的政党领导人和一种新的领导风格。

e.en: The leader at a particular point in a race or competition is the person who is winning at that point.

ex.en: The leaders came in two minutes clear of the field.
ex.zh: 领先的选手们早两分钟到达终点。

e.en: The leader of an orchestra is the most senior violin player, who acts as a deputy to the conductor. (交响乐团的)
A leader in a newspaper is a piece of writing which gives the editor's opinion on an important news item. (报纸上的)

d: n. 领袖，领导人，领导者（leader 的复数）；领导层，领导班子；领先者，市场领先者；（音乐）指挥，指挥者；首席小提琴手；社论，社评；前导字符，引线（印刷排版中引导视线的点线等）

e.en: A mass of things is a large number of them grouped together.

ex.en: On his desk is a mass of books and papers.
ex.zh: 在他书桌上有大堆的书和文件。

e.en: A mass of something is a large amount of it.

ex.en: She had a mass of auburn hair.
ex.zh: 她有一头浓密的棕发。

e.en: Masses of something means a great deal of it.

ex.en: There's masses of work for her to do.
ex.zh: 她有一大堆的工作去做。

e.en: Mass is used to describe something which involves or affects a very large number of people.

ex.en: ...ideas on combating mass unemployment.
ex.zh: …对付失业人数众多的方法。

ex.en: All the lights went off, and mass hysteria broke out.
ex.zh: 所有的灯都熄灭了，大家变得歇斯底里起来了。

d: n. 团，块；大量，许多；（常指混乱的）一群，一堆；大量的东西；群众，平民百姓；大多数，多数；质量；（尤指罗马天主教的）弥撒；弥撒曲
adj. 民众的，大量的
v. （使）聚集，（使）集结

e.en: Military means relating to the armed forces of a country.

ex.en: Military action may become necessary.
ex.zh: 军事行动可能会成为必要。

ex.en: The president is sending in almost 20,000 military personnel to help with the relief efforts.
ex.zh: 总统将派遣近20000名军事人员来协助救援行动。

e.en: 在军事上

ex.en: They remain unwilling to intervene militarily in what could be an unending war.
ex.zh: 他们仍然不愿意对一场可能无休止的战争进行军事干预。

e.en: The military are the armed forces of a country, especially officers of high rank. 军方 (尤指高级军官)

ex.en: The bombing has been far more widespread than the military will admit.
ex.zh: 爆炸波及的范围远大于军方愿意承认的范围。

e.en: Military means well organized, controlled, or neat, in a way that is typical of a soldier.

ex.en: Your working day will need to be organized with military precision.
ex.zh: 你们的工作日需要以军人般的精确性来安排。

d: adj. 军事的，军队的；陆军的；军人般的，军人作风的
n. 军人，军方

e.en: If someone is raped, they are forced to have sex, usually by violence or threats of violence.

ex.en: A young woman was brutally raped in her own home.
ex.zh: 一个年轻妇女在自己家中被粗暴地强奸了。

e.en: Rape is the crime of forcing someone to have sex.

ex.en: Almost 90 percent of all rapes and violent assaults went unreported.
ex.zh: 几乎百分之九十的强奸和暴力攻击都没有报警。

e.en: Rape is a plant with yellow flowers which is grown as a crop. Its seeds are crushed to make cooking oil.
the skins and stalks of grapes left after wine-making: used in making vinegar (用于制醋的)

d: n. 强奸罪，强奸案；（尤指对土地的）破坏，糟蹋；油菜；（榨汁后供制醋用的）葡萄渣
v. 强奸，强暴；蹂躏，破坏（地方）；掠夺，抢夺
v. reading 的非正式拼写（常写作 readin'），表示阅读
n. （计算机）读入（read-in 的不带连字符拼写）

e.en: If someone in authority sanctions an action or practice, they officially approve of it and allow it to be done. 批准;

ex.en: He may now be ready to sanction the use of force.
ex.zh: 他或许现在正准备批准使用武力。

e.en: Sanction is also a noun. 批准;

ex.en: ...a newspaper run by citizens without the sanction of the government.
ex.zh: …未经政府许可的一家民办报纸。

e.en: Sanctions are measures taken by countries to restrict trade and official contact with a country that has broken international law.

ex.en: The continued abuse of human rights has now led the United States to impose sanctions against the regime.
ex.zh: 对人权的不断践踏现已导致美国对该政权实施国际制裁。

d: v. 认可，准许；对……实施制裁，处罚；受到制裁，被处罚（sanction 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 经正式批准或认可的，获准的

e.en: The senior people in an organization or profession have the highest and most important jobs. 级别高的;

ex.en: ...senior officials in the Israeli government.
ex.zh: ...以色列政府里的高级官员们。

ex.en: ...the company's senior management.
ex.zh: …该公司的高级管理人员。

e.en: If someone is senior to you in an organization or profession, they have a higher and more important job than you or they are considered to be superior to you because they have worked there for longer and have more experience. 职务高于…的;

ex.en: The position had to be filled by an officer senior to Haig.
ex.zh: 这个位置必须由一名职位比黑格高的军官来填补。

e.en: Your seniors are the people who are senior to you. 上级;

ex.en: He was described by his seniors as a model officer.
ex.zh: 他被上级称为模范军官。

e.en: Senior is used when indicating how much older one person is than another. For example, if someone is ten years your senior, they are ten years older than you. 年长 (岁数)

ex.en: She became involved with a married man many years her senior.
ex.zh: 她与一名比她年长很多的已婚男子坠入情网。

d: adj. 年龄大些的；（用在家庭内姓名相同的人名后表示）老，年长的；老年人的；（地位、水平或级别）较高的，高级的；（比赛）成人的，高水平的；大于一定年龄（通常为11岁）的学童的；（高中或大学）毕业年级的
n. 较年长的人；老年人，长者；地位（或级别）较高者，上司；（中学或大学的）毕业班学生；资深成人运动员，高水平运动员
【名】 （Senior）（英）西尼尔（人名）

e.en: Saw is the past tense of see. (see)
A saw is a tool for cutting wood, which has a blade with sharp teeth along one edge. Some saws are pushed backward and forward by hand, and others are powered by electricity.
a wise saying, maxim, or proverb
If you saw something, you cut it with a saw.

ex.en: He escaped by sawing through the bars of his cell.
ex.zh: 他锯断牢房的铁栅逃跑了。

d: n. 锯；锯床；格言，谚语；锯齿状部位（或器官）
v. 锯，锯开；乱剪；拉锯似的来回移动；（两人或多人） 通过互让解决，相互妥协
v. 看见；观看（电影、电视节目等）；理解，领会（see 的过去式形式）

e.en: Several is used to refer to a number of people or things that is not large but is greater than two. 几;

ex.en: I had lived two doors away from this family for several years.
ex.zh: 我与相隔两户的这家人做了几年的邻居。

ex.en: Several blue plastic boxes under the window were filled with CDs.
ex.zh: 窗子下面的几个蓝色塑料盒子里装满了激光唱片。

e.en: Several is also a quantifier. 几个;

ex.en: The building was picketed by demonstrators, several of whom were well-known actors.
ex.zh: 这座建筑被示威者们包围了起来，其中几位是著名的演员。

e.en: Several is also a pronoun. 几个;

ex.en: No one drug will suit or work for everyone and sometimes several may have to be tried.
ex.zh: 没有任何一种药会对每个人都适用或有效，有时得试好几种。

d: adj. 不同的，各自的；单独，各个
pron. 几个，数个
det. 几个，数个

e.en: The side of something is a position to the left or right of it, rather than in front of it, behind it, or on it.

ex.en: On one side of the main entrance there's a red plaque.
ex.zh: 大门口的一侧有块红色匾牌。

ex.en: ...a photograph with Joe and Ken on each side of me.
ex.zh: …一张乔和肯在我两侧的照片。

e.en: The side of an object, building, or vehicle is any of its flat surfaces which is not considered to be its front, its back, its top, or its bottom.

ex.en: We put a notice on the side of the box.
ex.zh: 我们在这箱子的一侧贴了一张通知。

ex.en: A carton of milk lay on its side.
ex.zh: 一盒牛奶侧躺着放在那里。

e.en: The sides of a hollow or a container are its inside vertical surfaces.

ex.en: The rough rock walls were like the sides of a deep canal.
ex.zh: 粗糙的岩壁就像一条很深的运河的两岸。

ex.en: Line the base of the dish with greaseproof paper and lightly grease the sides.
ex.zh: 在盘子的底部垫一层防油纸，并在内侧涂上少许油。

e.en: The sides of an area or surface are its edges.

ex.en: Park on the side of the road.
ex.zh: 在那条路边停车。

ex.en: ...a small beach on the north side of the peninsula.
ex.zh: …那个半岛北边上的一个小海滩。

d: n. 边，侧面；身体两侧，肋部；一方，双方；方面，观点；（餐饮）配菜；（戏剧、影视）台词表，台词页，试镜片段；（几何、三维建模）面数，边数；（Sides）人名，塞兹
v. 支持，站在……一边（side 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A siege is a military or police operation in which soldiers or police surround a place in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.

ex.en: We must do everything possible to lift the siege.
ex.zh: 我们必须尽一切可能解除包围。

e.en: If police, soldiers, or journalists lay siege to a place, they surround it in order to force the people there to come out or give up control of the place.

ex.en: The rebels laid siege to the governor's residence.
ex.zh: 叛乱者们包围了那座总督官邸。

d: n. （军队或警察对某地的）围困，包围；不断的攻击
v. 围攻，包围

e.en: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object. 靶; (攻击的)

ex.en: The village lies beside a main road, making it an easy target for bandits.
ex.zh: 该村位于大路边，容易成为匪徒攻击的目标。

e.en: A target is a result that you are trying to achieve. (试图达成的)

ex.en: She's won back her place too late to achieve her target of 20 goals this season.
ex.zh: 她赢回她的位置为时已晚,无法实现她本赛季打进20个球的目标。

e.en: To target a particular person or thing means to decide to attack or criticize them. 把…作为攻击目标;

ex.en: Republicans targeted her as vulnerable in her bid for reelection this year.
ex.zh: 共和党人认为她在今年的再次参选中是不堪一击的攻击目标。

e.en: Target is also a noun. (攻击、批评的)

ex.en: In the past they have been the target of racist abuse.
ex.zh: 过去他们一直是种族虐待的对象。

d: adj. 定向的，有针对性的；被定为攻击目标的，成为（攻击、批评等）对象的；（医学）靶向的，针对特定靶点的
v. 把……作为目标（target 的过去式和过去分词）；be targeted at 以……为目标，针对……

e.en: If large numbers of people or animals are slaughtered, they are killed in a way that is cruel or unnecessary.

ex.en: Thirty four people were slaughtered while lining up to cast their votes.
ex.zh: 有34人在排队投票时遭屠杀。

e.en: Slaughter is also a noun.

ex.en: This was only a small part of a war where the slaughter of civilians was commonplace.
ex.zh: 这只是战争的一小部分，在战争中对平民的屠杀已司空见惯。

e.en: To slaughter animals such as cows and sheep means to kill them for their meat.

ex.en: Lack of chicken feed means that chicken farms are having to slaughter their stock.
ex.zh: 饲料不足意味着养鸡场将不得不宰杀鸡。

e.en: Slaughter is also a noun.

ex.en: More than 491,000 sheep were exported for slaughter last year.
ex.zh: 去年，超过四十九万一千只羊被出口供屠宰。

d: n. （对动物的）屠宰；（对人的）屠杀；彻底击败，一边倒的比赛
v. 宰杀（动物）；屠杀，杀戮；（在体育比赛中）使惨败；严厉批评
【名】  （Slaughter）（美）斯劳特（人名）

e.en: The subject of something such as a conversation, letter, or book is the thing that is being discussed or written about. 话题;

ex.en: It was I who first raised the subject of plastic surgery.
ex.zh: 是我首先提起了整形手术这个话题。

ex.en: ...the president's own views on the subject.
ex.zh: …该总统对此问题的个人观点。

e.en: Someone or something that is the subject of criticism, study, or an investigation is being criticized, studied, or investigated. (批评、研究或调查的)

ex.en: Over the past few years, some of the positions Mr. Meredith has adopted have made him the subject of criticism.
ex.zh: 在过去的几年里，梅雷迪恩先生所采取的一些立场已使他成为了被批评的对象。

e.en: A subject is an area of knowledge or study, especially one that you study in school, or college. (尤指在学校学习的)

ex.en: Surprisingly, maths was voted their favourite subject.
ex.zh: 令人吃惊的是，数学被评为他们喜爱的科目。

e.en: In an experiment or piece of research, the subject is the person or animal that is being tested or studied. 实验对象;

ex.en: "White noise" was played into the subject's ears through headphones.
ex.zh: “白色噪音”通过耳机被送进实验对象的耳朵里。

d: v. 使遭受，使经受，使受到；受…影响；使从属，使臣服（subject 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation: the application of low-voltage electric impulses to the skin to relieve rheumatic pain and provide some pain relief in labour. The pulses are said to stimulate the release of pain-killing endorphins

d: n. ten 的复数形式，表示多个十、十个一组或约略的数十；十进制计数中个位左侧的数位，即十位（tens digit、tens place、tens column）；tens of thousands（数万、成千上万）、tens of millions（数千万）等约数表达；in tens 意为“以十为计、以十个为一组”，也作“十进制”
abbr. （医学）TENS 是 transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation（经皮神经电刺激）的缩写；一种以低电压电脉冲作用于皮肤以缓解疼痛的电疗方法

e.en: A thousand or one thousand is the number 1,000. 1000

ex.en: ...five thousand acres.

e.en: If you refer to thousands of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

ex.en: Thousands of refugees are packed into overcrowded towns and villages.
ex.zh: 成千上万的难民挤入拥挤不堪的城镇与村庄。

e.en: You can also use thousands as a pronoun.

ex.en: Hundreds have been killed in the fighting and thousands made homeless.
ex.zh: 数百人在战斗中丧生，成千上万的人无家可归。

d: n. 数千（thousand 的复数）

e.en: If you travel, you go from one place to another, often to a place that is far away.

ex.en: You had better travel to Nova Scotia tomorrow.
ex.zh: 你最好明天去新斯科舍。

ex.en: I've been travelling all day.
ex.zh: 我一整天都在旅行。

e.en: Travel is the activity of travelling.

ex.en: Information on travel in New Zealand is available at the hotel.
ex.zh: 新西兰的旅游信息在该酒店可以查到。

ex.en: He detested air travel.
ex.zh: 他厌恶空中旅行。

e.en: If you travel the world, the country, or the area, you go to many different places in the world or in a particular country or area.

ex.en: He was a very wealthy man who had traveled the world.
ex.zh: 他是个非常富有的人，曾经周游过世界。

e.en: When light or sound from one place reaches another, you say that it travels to the other place. (光或声音)

ex.en: When sound travels through water, strange things can happen.
ex.zh: 当声音在水中传播时，奇怪的事情会发生。

d: v. （尤指长途）旅行；走动，移动；（以某速度、朝某方向或在某距离内）行进；（光或声音）传播；（食品等）经得起长途运输；周游，走遍；（尤指车辆）快速行进；（消息）流传；盛行各地；（篮球运动中）走步；（目光）扫视，移动；交往；想象来到
n. 旅行；（出国）旅游；（机器部件的）运动范围，运动速度，运动模式

e.en: Protesters are people who protest publicly about an issue.

ex.en: The protesters say the government is corrupt and inefficient.
ex.zh: 抗议者指责政府腐败无能。

d: n. protester 的复数形式：抗议者，示威者；反对者，异议者

e.en: French means belonging or relating to France, or its people, language, or culture. 法国的; 法国人的; 法语的;
The French are the people who come from France.
French is the language spoken by people who live in France and in parts of some other countries, including Belgium, Canada, and Switzerland.

ex.en: The villagers spoke French.
ex.zh: 这些村民们讲法语。

d: adj. 法国的；法语的；法国人的
n. 法国人；法语
n. （美、英、加、澳）弗伦奇（人名）
n. 德国
n. 法国，法兰西（西欧国家，正式名称为法兰西共和国）；法郎士（姓氏，亦指法国作家阿纳托尔·法郎士）

e.en: A demonstration is a march or gathering which people take part in to show their opposition to something or their support for something. 示威游行;

ex.en: Riot police used tear gas to break up the demonstration.
ex.zh: 防暴警察使用了催泪瓦斯驱散示威游行。

e.en: A demonstration of something is a talk by someone who shows you how to do it or how it works.

ex.en: ...a cooking demonstration.
ex.zh: …一次烹调展示。

e.en: A demonstration of a fact or situation is a clear proof of it.

ex.en: It was an unprecedented demonstration of people power by the citizens of Moscow.
ex.zh: 这是莫斯科市民对人民力量史无前例的证明。

e.en: A demonstration of a quality or feeling is an expression of it. (品质、感情的)

ex.en: There's been no public demonstration of opposition to the president.
ex.zh: 还没有反对总统的公开展现。

d: n. 示范，演示，展示（demonstration 的复数形式）；示威游行，示威集会；证明，论证（常与 of 连用）；表现，展现（常与 of 连用）

e.en: If you protest something or protest against something, you say or show publicly that you object to it.

ex.en: They were protesting soaring prices.
ex.zh: 他们在抗议不断飞涨的物价。

e.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

ex.en: The opposition now seems too weak to stage any serious protests against the government.
ex.zh: 反对党现在似乎太弱小，无力针对政府组织什么重大的抗议。

ex.en: The Mexican president cancelled a trip to Texas in protest at the state's execution of a Mexican national.
ex.zh: 墨西哥总统取消了得克萨斯之行，以抗议该州对一名墨西哥侨民的处决。

e.en: If you protest that something is the case, you insist that it is the case, when other people think that it may not be.

ex.en: When we tried to protest that Mo was beaten up they didn't believe us.
ex.zh: 当我们坚持说莫遭到了毒打时，他们都不相信。

ex.en: "I never said any of that to her," he protested.
ex.zh: “我从来没有对她说过那种话，”他断然否认。

d: n. 抗议，反对；抗议活动；声明，断言（protest 的复数）
v. （公开）反对，抗议；坚决表示，严正申明；（法律）声明拒付（账单），拒付（protest 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A place is any point, building, area, town, or country. (任何)

ex.en: ...a list of museums and places of interest.
ex.zh: …一份博物馆和名胜地的列表。

ex.en: We're going to a place called Platoro.
ex.zh: 我们要去一个叫普拉托罗的地方。

e.en: You can use the place to refer to the point, building, area, town, or country that you have already mentioned. (提到过的点、建筑、地区、城镇、国家等)

ex.en: Except for the remarkably tidy kitchen, the place was a mess.
ex.zh: 除了异常整洁的厨房外，这个地方一团糟。

e.en: You can refer to somewhere that provides a service, such as a hotel, restaurant, or institution, as a particular kind of place. (旅馆、饭店、机构等某种提供服务的)

ex.en: He found a bed-and-breakfast place.
ex.zh: 他找到一个提供住宿带早餐的地方。

ex.en: My wife and I discovered some superb places to eat.
ex.zh: 我妻子和我发现了一些很棒的吃饭的地方。

e.en: When something takes place, it happens, especially in a controlled or organized way. (尤指在控制或组织下) 发生;

ex.en: The discussion took place in a famous villa on the lake's shore.
ex.zh: 讨论在湖滨一座著名别墅举行。

ex.en: She wanted Randy's wedding to take place quickly.
ex.zh: 她想让兰迪的婚礼马上举行。

d: n. 地点，场所；城镇（或建筑物等）；有某用途的建筑（或土地）；表面的某处；家，住所；（书本或讲话中的）点；座位，位置；地位，资格；机会，名额；适当的地方；境况；排名；第二名；（数学的）位；广场，短街；乡间住宅；一套餐具
v. 放置；使处于某种境地；以某种态度对待（或看待）；认出，想起；下指示，请求；安置；排名，归类；（赛跑）获前三/四名；定位球得分；证明……在场
【名】 （Place）（罗）普拉切，（法）普拉斯，（英）普莱斯（人名）

e.en: When soldiers march somewhere, or when a commanding officer marches them somewhere, they walk there with very regular steps, as a group. 使齐步走;

ex.en: A U.S. infantry battalion was marching down the street.
ex.zh: 一个美军步兵营沿着街道行进。

ex.en: Captain Ramirez called them to attention and marched them off to the main camp.
ex.zh: 拉米雷斯上校命令他们立正，然后让他们向主营地行进。

e.en: March is also a noun.

ex.en: After a short march, the column entered the village.
ex.zh: 短途行军之后，队伍进入了村子。

e.en: a frontier, border, or boundary or the land lying along it, often of disputed ownership (所有权常有争议的)边界; 边疆; 边地 (Also called marchland)
When a large group of people march for a cause, they walk somewhere together in order to express their ideas or to protest about something.

ex.en: The demonstrators then marched through the capital chanting slogans and demanding free elections.
ex.zh: 示威者然后穿越首都游行，反复喊着口号，要求进行自由选举。

d: v. 齐步走，行军；快步走；强迫（某人）一起走，押送；游行示威；进行，进展
n. 三月（March）；示威游行；行进，行军；稳步发展；进行曲

e.en: Cologne is a kind of weak perfume.

d: n. 古龙水，古龙香水，科隆香水（由香精油和酒精制成的轻淡香水）

e.en: In many countries, a ministry is a government department which deals with a particular thing or area of activity, for example trade, defence, or transportation. (政府的)

ex.en: ...the Ministry of Justice.
ex.zh: …司法部。

d: n. （政府的）部，部办公楼；（全体）牧师；神职，神职任期；一任首相的执政期；照料，服务

e.en: a dance consisting of complicated figures and changes of partners
having the same parents as oneself

ex.en: a brother-german

e.en: having a parent that is a brother or sister of either of one's own parents 亲堂(表)

ex.en: cousin-german

d: adj. 德国的；德语的，德国人的
n. 德语；德国人

e.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

ex.en: The interior of the house was furnished with heavy, old-fashioned pieces.
ex.zh: 房内陈设着些笨重、老式的家具。

e.en: You use interior to describe something that is inside a building or vehicle. (建筑或者车辆)

ex.en: The interior walls were painted green.
ex.zh: 内墙被漆成了绿色。

e.en: The interior of a country or continent is the central area of it.

ex.en: The Yangtze River would give access to much of China's interior.
ex.zh: 长江使得人们能够到达中国内陆许多地方。

e.en: An interior minister, ministry, or department in some countries deals with affairs within that country, such as law and order.

ex.en: The French Interior Minister has intervened in a scandal over the role of a secret police force.
ex.zh: 法国内务部长对一起有关秘密警察部队职责的丑闻进行了干预。

d: adj. 内部的，里面的；国内的，内政的；内心的，本质的；内陆的，腹地的
n. 内部，里面；内陆，腹地；（本国的）内政，内务；（建筑物或房间内的）内景；内心，本质

e.en: When soldiers march somewhere, or when a commanding officer marches them somewhere, they walk there with very regular steps, as a group. 使齐步走;

ex.en: A U.S. infantry battalion was marching down the street.
ex.zh: 一个美军步兵营沿着街道行进。

ex.en: Captain Ramirez called them to attention and marched them off to the main camp.
ex.zh: 拉米雷斯上校命令他们立正，然后让他们向主营地行进。

e.en: March is also a noun.

ex.en: After a short march, the column entered the village.
ex.zh: 短途行军之后，队伍进入了村子。

e.en: a frontier, border, or boundary or the land lying along it, often of disputed ownership (所有权常有争议的)边界; 边疆; 边地 (Also called marchland)
When a large group of people march for a cause, they walk somewhere together in order to express their ideas or to protest about something.

ex.en: The demonstrators then marched through the capital chanting slogans and demanding free elections.
ex.zh: 示威者然后穿越首都游行，反复喊着口号，要求进行自由选举。

d: n. march 的复数：游行，示威游行；进行曲；行军，行进；the Marches 边界地区（尤指英格兰与苏格兰或威尔士的）；the Marches 马尔凯（意大利中东部大区）；（Marches）人名，（意）马尔凯斯
v. （march 的第三人称单数）行进；游行；（时间等）推移

e.en: If you report something that has happened, you tell people about it. 报告;

ex.en: I reported the theft to the police.
ex.zh: 我向警察报告了这起盗窃案。

ex.en: The officials also reported that two more ships were apparently heading for Malta.
ex.zh: 官员们也报告说另有两艘船显然正朝马耳他驶去。

e.en: If you report on an event or subject, you tell people about it, because it is your job or duty to do so. 报道; (工作或职责上)

ex.en: Many journalists based outside of Sudan have been refused visas to enter the country to report on political affairs.
ex.zh: 很多驻在苏丹境外的记者遭到拒签，无法进入该国报道政治事件。

e.en: A report is a news article or broadcast which gives information about something that has just happened. (报刊或广播电视上的)

ex.en: According to a report in the newspaper, he still has control over the remaining shares.
ex.zh: 根据报纸上的报道，他依然控制着剩余的股份。

e.en: A report is an official document which a group of people issue after investigating a situation or event. (调查)

ex.en: The education committee will today publish its report on the supply of teachers for the next decade.
ex.zh: 教育委员会今天将公布关于今后十年师资储备的报告。

d: adj. 报告的，声称的；已汇报的，已举报的
v. 报道；据说，传闻；述说，报告（report 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A union is a workers' organization which represents its members and which tries to improve things such as their working conditions and pay.

ex.en: Do all teachers have a right to join a union?
ex.zh: 所有的教师都有权利加入工会吗？

e.en: When the union of two or more things occurs, they are joined together and become one thing.

ex.en: In 1918 the Romanian majority in this former czarist province voted for union with Romania.
ex.zh: 1918年，这个前沙俄省份的大多数罗马尼亚人投票支持与罗马尼亚合并。

e.en: When two or more things, for example countries or organizations, have been joined together to form one thing, you can refer to them as a union.

ex.en: Tanzania is a union of the states of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
ex.zh: 坦桑尼亚是坦噶尼喀州和桑给巴尔州的联盟。

d: n. 工会；联邦，联盟；协会，俱乐部；联合，合并；结婚，婚姻；美利坚合众国（the Union）；（数）并，并集；联管节，接头；（印度次大陆）村落联合体；教区联合济贫组织；旗帜上象征国家统一的部分；混纺织物

e.en: a fine wool yarn used for tapestry work, etc 柏林羊毛 (Also called berlin wool)

d: n. 柏林（德国首都）；柏林羊毛（用于刺绣、挂毯等的细羊毛线，亦作 berlin wool）；前排与后排座椅之间设有玻璃隔板的豪华轿车

e.en: A blockade of a place is an action that is taken to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving it.

ex.en: It's not yet clear who will actually enforce the blockade.
ex.zh: 目前还不清楚到底谁会来执行封锁。

e.en: If a group of people blockade a place, they stop goods or people from reaching that place. If they blockade a road or a port, they stop people from using that road or port.

ex.en: About 50,000 people are trapped in the town, which has been blockaded for more than 40 days.
ex.zh: 约有五万人被困在这个已经被封锁了40多天的小镇里。

d: n. 封锁；（生理或心理功能，尤指生化受体的）阻滞，阻塞；障碍物，屏障
v. 包围，封锁（尤指港口）

e.en: When people, animals, and plants die, they stop living.

ex.en: A year later my dog died.
ex.zh: 1年后，我的狗死了。

ex.en: Sadly, both he and my mother died of cancer.
ex.zh: 令人悲伤的是，他和我母亲都死于癌症。

e.en: If a machine or device dies, it stops completely, especially after a period of working more and more slowly or inefficiently.

ex.en: Then suddenly, the engine coughed, spluttered, and died.
ex.zh: 突然，发动机发出喀喀声、噼啪声，然后就熄火了。

e.en: You can say that you are dying of thirst, hunger, boredom, or curiosity to emphasize that you are very thirsty, hungry, bored, or curious. (饥渴、厌倦、好奇得)

ex.en: Order me a soda, I'm dying of thirst.
ex.zh: 给我要杯汽水，我快渴死了。

e.en: You can say that you are dying for something or are dying to do something to emphasize that you very much want to have it or do it.

ex.en: I'm dying for a breath of fresh air.
ex.zh: 我真想呼吸点新鲜空气。

d: v. 死亡；消失，灭亡；停止运转；渴望；达到性高潮
n. 骰子；金属模具，压模
【名】 （Die）（法、美、德）迭（人名）

e.en: If you are dressed, you are wearing clothes rather than being naked or wearing your nightclothes. If you get dressed, you put on your clothes.

ex.en: He was fully dressed, including shoes.
ex.zh: 他已穿戴好了，包括鞋子。

e.en: If you are dressed in a particular way, you are wearing clothes of a particular colour or kind.

ex.en: ...a tall thin woman dressed in black.
ex.zh: …一个穿着黑色衣服，高高瘦瘦的女人。

d: adj. 穿好衣服的；穿着……衣服的；打扮好的，盛装的；去内脏及分割加工好的（鱼、禽等）；加工修整过的（木材、皮革、石料等）；已包扎好的（伤口）
v. 给……穿衣；布置，装饰（dress 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.

ex.en: The country's economic problems are largely due to the weakness of the recovery.
ex.zh: 该国的经济问题很大程度上是复苏乏力的结果。

e.en: You can say due to to introduce the reason for something happening. Some speakers of English believe that it is not correct to use due to in this way.

ex.en: Due to the large volume of letters he receives Dave regrets he is unable to answer queries personally.
ex.zh: 由于收到的来信数量太多，戴夫很遗憾不能亲自回复各种询问。

e.en: If you say that something will happen or take place in due course, you mean that you cannot make it happen any quicker and it will happen when the time is right for it.

ex.en: In due course the baby was born.
ex.zh: 婴儿如期降生了。

e.en: You can say "to give him his due," or "giving him his due," when you are admitting that there are some good things about someone, even though there are things that you do not like about them.

ex.en: To give Linda her due, she had tried to encourage John in his school work.
ex.zh: 为琳达说句公道话，她曾尽力在学习方面鼓励约翰。

d: adj. 到期的，预期的；应有的，应得的；应付的，应给的；适当的
adv. 正对着
n. 应得，所得；会费
【名】 （Due）迪尤（人名）
n. 法兰克福市（德国城市）

e.en: You can use lower to refer to the bottom one of a pair of things. (一对物品中)

ex.en: She bit her lower lip.
ex.zh: 她咬着下唇。

ex.en: ...the lower of the two holes.
ex.zh: …两个洞中下面的那个。

e.en: You can use lower to refer to the bottom part of something.

ex.en: Use a small cushion to help give support to the lower back.
ex.zh: 用一个小垫子来辅助支撑腰部。

e.en: You can use lower to refer to people or things that are less important than similar people or things. 下等的;

ex.en: Already the awards are causing resentment in the lower ranks of council officers.
ex.zh: 那些奖励已经引起了委员会下层工作人员的不满。

ex.en: The nation's highest court reversed the lower court's decision.
ex.zh: 该国的最高法院推翻了下级法院的判决。

e.en: If you lower something, you move it slowly downward. (缓慢地) 放下;

ex.en: Two reporters had to help lower the coffin into the grave.
ex.zh: 两名记者不得不帮忙把棺材下放至墓穴中。

ex.en: Sokolowski lowered himself into the black leather chair.
ex.zh: 索科罗斯基缓缓地在黑皮椅里坐下。

d: adj. （尤指在同类中处于）较下的，下方的；在底部的，近底部的；次重要的，较低级的；（数字或数量）较小的；向南的；早期的
v. 减少，降低；把……放低，使……降下；降低，贬低（身份）；变昏暗，变阴沉；露愠色
adv. 处于较低位置地，向低处下降地
【名】 （Lower）（美、英）洛厄（人名）
n. 里昂（法国城市）；苏格兰纹章院长官

e.en: When soldiers march somewhere, or when a commanding officer marches them somewhere, they walk there with very regular steps, as a group. 使齐步走;

ex.en: A U.S. infantry battalion was marching down the street.
ex.zh: 一个美军步兵营沿着街道行进。

ex.en: Captain Ramirez called them to attention and marched them off to the main camp.
ex.zh: 拉米雷斯上校命令他们立正，然后让他们向主营地行进。

e.en: March is also a noun.

ex.en: After a short march, the column entered the village.
ex.zh: 短途行军之后，队伍进入了村子。

e.en: a frontier, border, or boundary or the land lying along it, often of disputed ownership (所有权常有争议的)边界; 边疆; 边地 (Also called marchland)
When a large group of people march for a cause, they walk somewhere together in order to express their ideas or to protest about something.

ex.en: The demonstrators then marched through the capital chanting slogans and demanding free elections.
ex.zh: 示威者然后穿越首都游行，反复喊着口号，要求进行自由选举。

d: adj. 行军的；步进式的
v. march 的现在分词：行军，齐步行进；前进，持续进展，无法阻挡地行进；游行示威；使同行，迫使同行；（因愤怒或决心）快步走
n. 行军，行进；（marching band）军乐队，奏进行曲作操练表演的乐队
n. 组织者（organiser 的复数）

e.en: the court or government of the Ottoman Empire 奥斯曼帝国的朝廷 (Also called Sublime Porte)

d: n. 土耳其宫廷（等于 Sublime Porte）

e.en: If you say that something will happen provided or provided that something else happens, you mean that the first thing will happen only if the second thing also happens.

ex.en: The other banks are going to be very eager to help, provided that they see that he has a specific plan.
ex.zh: 如果他有一个具体的计划，其他的银行才会非常渴望提供资助。

d: conj. 假如，只要，在……条件下
v. 提供；规定；为（可能事件）作充分准备（provide 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you protest something or protest against something, you say or show publicly that you object to it.

ex.en: They were protesting soaring prices.
ex.zh: 他们在抗议不断飞涨的物价。

e.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

ex.en: The opposition now seems too weak to stage any serious protests against the government.
ex.zh: 反对党现在似乎太弱小，无力针对政府组织什么重大的抗议。

ex.en: The Mexican president cancelled a trip to Texas in protest at the state's execution of a Mexican national.
ex.zh: 墨西哥总统取消了得克萨斯之行，以抗议该州对一名墨西哥侨民的处决。

e.en: If you protest that something is the case, you insist that it is the case, when other people think that it may not be.

ex.en: When we tried to protest that Mo was beaten up they didn't believe us.
ex.zh: 当我们坚持说莫遭到了毒打时，他们都不相信。

ex.en: "I never said any of that to her," he protested.
ex.zh: “我从来没有对她说过那种话，”他断然否认。

d: n. 抗议，反对；抗议活动；声明，断言；（多指来自公证人的）拒付证书
v. （公开）反对，抗议；坚决表示，严正申明； 声明拒付（账单），拒付

e.en: Your response to an event or to something that is said is your reply or reaction to it.

ex.en: There has been no response to his remarks from the government.
ex.zh: 政府方面对他的评论一直没有反应。

d: n. 反应，响应；（口头或书面的）回复，答复；（考试题的）答案；（教堂中人们对牧师所说的话作出的）唱和，应答
n. 发言人；代言人

e.en: Stood is the past tense and past participle of . (stand)

d: v. 站立（stand 的过去式和过去分词）；stood out：突出，显眼，出色，坚持立场（stand out 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A union is a workers' organization which represents its members and which tries to improve things such as their working conditions and pay.

ex.en: Do all teachers have a right to join a union?
ex.zh: 所有的教师都有权利加入工会吗？

e.en: When the union of two or more things occurs, they are joined together and become one thing.

ex.en: In 1918 the Romanian majority in this former czarist province voted for union with Romania.
ex.zh: 1918年，这个前沙俄省份的大多数罗马尼亚人投票支持与罗马尼亚合并。

e.en: When two or more things, for example countries or organizations, have been joined together to form one thing, you can refer to them as a union.

ex.en: Tanzania is a union of the states of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
ex.zh: 坦桑尼亚是坦噶尼喀州和桑给巴尔州的联盟。

d: n. 工会；联合，联盟，合并（union 的复数）

e.en: A welt is a mark made on someone's skin, usually by a blow from something such as a whip or sword. (击打或擦伤所致的)

d: n. 鞭痕，条痕；（服装、制鞋）贴边，沿条；殴打；（Welt）人名，韦尔特（英、德、罗）
vt. 鞭打，殴打；使……留下鞭痕；（服装、制鞋）给……加沿条，贴边

e.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able or allowed to go into it. 进入手段;

ex.en: The facilities have been adapted to give access to wheelchair users.
ex.zh: 这些设施已经过改装，使轮椅使用者们能够进入。

ex.en: For logistical and political reasons, scientists have only recently been able to gain access to the area.
ex.zh: 因后勤与政治原因，科学家们直到最近才得以进入该地区。

e.en: If you have access to something such as information or equipment, you have the opportunity or right to see it or use it.

ex.en: ...a Code of Practice that would give patients access to their medical records.
ex.zh: …一个给病人们使用自己病历权利的行业守则。

e.en: If you have access to a person, you have the opportunity or right to see them or meet them. 接触的机会;

ex.en: He was not allowed access to a lawyer.
ex.zh: 他未被允许接触律师。

e.en: If you access something, especially information held on a computer, you succeed in finding or obtaining it. 获取 (尤其电脑信息)

ex.en: You've illegally accessed and misused confidential security files.
ex.zh: 你已经非法获取并盗用了机密文件。

d: n. 入口，通道；获得的机会，使用权；（对计算机存储器的）访问，存取；（情感）爆发，发作；探视权
v. 接近，进入；获取，访问（计算机信息）
adj. （电视节目或时间等）对外公开的

e.en: alpha-fetoprotein

d: abbr. 法新社（Agence France Presse）；美国警察联合会（American Federation of Police）

e.en: an act or instance of addition
of, for, or relating to addition

d: v. 增加，添加，补充（add 的现在分词/动名词形式）
n. adding machine：加法机，算术计算机；（Adding）人名，瑞典人名，音译“阿丁”

e.en: The afternoon is the part of each day that begins at lunchtime and ends at about six o'clock.

ex.en: He's arriving in the afternoon.
ex.zh: 他将于下午到达。

ex.en: He had stayed in his room all afternoon.
ex.zh: 他整个下午都呆在他的房间里。

d: n. 午后，下午
int. 下午好（问候用语）

e.en: An agency is a business that provides a service on behalf of other businesses.

ex.en: We had to hire maids through an agency.
ex.zh: 我们得通过代理公司雇用女佣。

e.en: An agency is a government organization responsible for a certain area of administration.

ex.en: She is calling for a collaboration of local, state and federal agencies to deal with the problem.
ex.zh: 她在呼吁地方、州和联邦等各级政府通力合作来处理这个问题。

d: n. 代理行，经销处；政府专门机构，政府内的局，部，处；（尤指产生某效果的）作用；起作用的事物（或人）;社会行为者独立选择的能力

e.en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement that contrasts with the statement in the main clause.

ex.en: Although he is known to only a few, his reputation among them is very great.
ex.zh: 尽管只有几个人知道他，但是他在他们之中的名声很大。

e.en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which contains a statement that makes the main clause of the sentence seem surprising or unexpected.

ex.en: Although I was only six, I can remember seeing it on TV.
ex.zh: 虽然当时我只有6岁，我还能记得在电视上看见过它。

e.en: You use although to introduce a subordinate clause which gives some information that is relevant to the main clause but modifies the strength of that statement.

ex.en: He was in love with her, although a man seldom puts that name to what he feels.
ex.zh: 他爱上了她，虽然一个男人很少用这个词来形容他的感受。

e.en: You use although when admitting a fact about something that you regard as less important than a contrasting fact.

ex.en: Although they're expensive, they last forever and never go out of style.
ex.zh: 尽管它们贵，它们永远耐用并且永不过时。

d: conj. 虽然，尽管；但是，然而

e.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

ex.en: Police arrested five young men in connection with one of the attacks.
ex.zh: 警方逮捕了与其中一起袭击事件有关的5名年轻男子。

e.en: Arrest is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a substantial reward for information leading to the arrest of the bombers.
ex.zh: …用于奖励为抓捕爆炸犯提供有效信息的一大笔赏金。

ex.en: Police chased the fleeing terrorists and later made two arrests.
ex.zh: 警方追赶逃窜的恐怖分子，后来逮捕了两个人。

e.en: If something or someone arrests a process, they stop it from continuing.

ex.en: The sufferer may have to make major changes in his or her life to arrest the disease.
ex.zh: 患者可能得对自身生活作大的调整以抑制病情。

d: n. （法律）逮捕，拘捕，拘留（arrest 的复数）；（医学）停止，中止（arrest 的复数，尤指心搏停止或呼吸停止）
v. （法律）逮捕，拘捕（arrest 的第三人称单数形式）；阻止，抑制，中止（arrest 的第三人称单数形式）；吸引，引起（注意）（arrest 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you attend a meeting or other event, you are present at it. 参加;

ex.en: Thousands of people attended the funeral.
ex.zh: 数千人参加了葬礼。

ex.en: The meeting will be attended by finance ministers from many countries.
ex.zh: 这次会议将有许多国家的财政部长出席。

e.en: If you attend an institution such as a school, college, or church, you go there regularly. 上 (学); 去 (教堂)

ex.en: They attended college together at the University of Pennsylvania.
ex.zh: 他们一起就读于宾夕法尼亚大学。

e.en: If you attend to something, you deal with it. If you attend to someone who is hurt or injured, you care for them. 处理;

ex.en: He took a short leave of absence to attend to personal business.
ex.zh: 他休了一个短假去处理私事。

d: v. 随同，陪同；经常去，定期去(学校、教堂等)；伴随……而至，（作为结果）伴随；出席，参加；注意，专心；处理，照料；致力于

e.en: If you are attached to someone or something, you like them very much.

ex.en: She is very attached to her family and friends.
ex.zh: 她非常喜欢她的家人和朋友。

e.en: If someone is attached to an organization or group of people, they are working with them, often only for a short time. (临时)

ex.en: Ford was attached to the 101st Airborne Division.
ex.zh: 福特曾属于第101空降师。

d: adj. 非常喜欢……的，热爱……的；为……工作的；隶属于……，附属的；连接的，附加的
v. 系上，贴上；赋予，认为……具有（attach 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: To ban something means to state officially that it must not be done, shown, or used. (官方)

ex.en: Canada will ban smoking in all offices later this year.
ex.zh: 加拿大将于今年晚些时候禁止在所有办公场所吸烟。

ex.en: Last year arms sales were banned.
ex.zh: 去年军火交易被明令禁止了。

e.en: A ban is an official ruling that something must not be done, shown, or used.

ex.en: The general lifted the ban on political parties.
ex.zh: 将军解除了对政党的官方禁令。

e.en: If you are banned from doing something, you are officially prevented from doing it.

ex.en: He was banned from driving for three years.
ex.zh: 他被禁止驾驶3年。

d: adj. 被禁止的，被取缔的
v. 禁止，取缔（ban 的过去式和过去分词）；（官方）把……逐出，禁止（某人）做某事或进入某处（常与 from 连用）；咒骂（ban 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that is black is of the darkest colour that there is, the colour of the sky at night when there is no light at all.

ex.en: She was wearing a black coat with a white collar.
ex.zh: 她穿着一件白领黑上衣。

ex.en: He had thick black hair.
ex.zh: 他有着浓密乌黑的头发。

e.en: A black person belongs to a race of people with dark skins, especially a race originally from Africa.

ex.en: He worked for the rights of black people.
ex.zh: 他为黑人的权利而工作。

ex.en: Sherry is black, tall, slender and soft-spoken.
ex.zh: 谢里是黑人，个头高挑，身材苗条，说话柔声细气。

e.en: Black people are sometimes referred to as blacks. This use could cause offence.

ex.en: There are about thirty-one million blacks in the U.S.
ex.zh: 美国大约有三千一百万黑人。

e.en: Black coffee or tea has no milk or cream added to it. (咖啡、茶)

ex.en: A cup of black tea or black coffee contains no calories.
ex.zh: 一杯红茶或黑咖啡不含任何卡路里。

d: adj. 黑的，黑色的；黑色人种的；不加牛奶的；脏的，布满污垢的；悲伤的，无望的；愤怒的，仇恨的；罪恶的，邪恶的；（幽默）黑色的；（滑雪道）难度最大的；（军事活动）秘密的；黑桃和梅花组牌的
n. 黑，黑色；黑人；黑色衣服；黑色的东西（尤指斯诺克中的黑球）；执黑子的一方
v. 使变黑，弄黑；抵制，拒绝（货品或公司）
【名】 （Black）（英、西）布莱克，（德、葡、捷）布拉克
n. 柏林市民
n. 监狱，牢狱（尤指管理专横的监狱）；城堡，堡垒；巴士底狱（the Bastille，常大写；巴黎历史上的要塞与国家监狱，1789 年法国大革命开始时被攻占并摧毁）

e.en: A bomb is a device that explodes and damages or destroys a large area.

ex.en: Bombs went off at two London train stations.
ex.zh: 炸弹在伦敦的两个火车站爆炸了。

ex.en: It's not known who planted the bomb.
ex.zh: 不知是谁放置了这颗炸弹。

e.en: Nuclear weapons are sometimes referred to as the bomb.

ex.en: They are generally thought to have the bomb.
ex.zh: 他们被普遍认为拥有核武器。

e.en: When people bomb a place, they attack it with bombs.

ex.en: Air force jets bombed the airport.
ex.zh: 空军喷气机轰炸了机场。

e.en: 轰炸

ex.en: Aerial bombing of rebel positions is continuing.
ex.zh: 对叛军阵地的空中轰炸仍在继续。

d: n. 炸弹（bomb 的复数）
v. 轰炸，投弹（bomb 的第三人称单数形式）；彻底失败，惨败（bomb 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: The bottom of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.

ex.en: He sat at the bottom of the stairs.
ex.zh: 他坐在楼梯底部。

ex.en: Answers can be found at the bottom of page 8.
ex.zh: 答案可以在第8页下端找到。

e.en: The bottom thing or layer in a series of things or layers is the lowest one.

ex.en: There's an extra duvet in the bottom drawer of the cupboard.
ex.zh: 在柜子最下层的抽屉里还有一床羽绒被。

e.en: The bottom of an object is the flat surface at its lowest point. You can also refer to the inside or outside of this surface as the bottom.

ex.en: Spread the onion slices on the bottom of the dish.
ex.zh: 把洋葱丝铺在盘底。

ex.en: ...the bottom of their shoes.
ex.zh: …他们的鞋底。

e.en: If you say that the bottom has dropped or fallen out of a market or industry, you mean that people have stopped buying the products it sells. (市场、行业)

ex.en: The bottom had fallen out of the city's property market.
ex.zh: 该市的房地产市场暴跌。

d: n. 底，底部；尽头，远端；最低水平，底层位置；（套装的）下装；臀部；水底；河边洼地；（一局棒球比赛的）后半局；（汽车变速箱的）最低挡；龙骨，船体；底夸克；（尤指马的）持久力，耐力；船（尤指货船）
adj. 底部的，最后的；最不重要的，最差的；离得最远的
v. （船）到达海底，触到海底；钻探……直到矿物层；发现……范围（或本质）；（成绩，局势）到达最低点后趋于平衡
【名】 （Bottom）（英）博顿（人名）

e.en: Broke is the past tense of break. (break)
If you are broke, you have no money.

ex.en: What do you mean, I've got enough money? I'm as broke as you are.
ex.zh: 你什么意思啊，我有足够的钱？我和你一样一文不名。

e.en: If a company or person goes broke, they lose money and are unable to continue in business or to pay their debts.

ex.en: Balton went broke twice in his career.
ex.zh: 伯顿在他的职业生涯中破产过两次。

d: adj. 身无分文的，一文不名的
v. 弄坏；打碎；违反（break 的过去式形式）
【名】 （Broke）（美、印、俄、德）布罗克（人名）

e.en: A calling is a profession or career which someone is strongly attracted to, especially one which involves helping other people.

ex.en: He was a consultant physician, a serious man dedicated to his calling.
ex.zh: 他是一名顾问医生，一个专注于其使命的严肃认真的人。

d: n. 强烈愿望，使命感；行业，职业；（动物或人的）喊叫
v. 打电话；叫作；呼唤（call 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A calm person does not show or feel any worry, anger, or excitement. 冷静的;

ex.en: She is usually a calm and diplomatic woman.
ex.zh: 她通常是个冷静而圆滑的女人。

ex.en: Try to keep calm and just tell me what happened.
ex.zh: 试着保持冷静，告诉我发生了什么。

e.en: Calm is also a noun. 冷静;

ex.en: He felt a sudden sense of calm, of contentment.
ex.zh: 他突然感受到了内心的平静和满足。

e.en: 冷静地;

ex.en: Alan looked at him and said calmly, "I don't believe you."
ex.zh: 艾伦看着他，平静地说，“我不相信你。”

e.en: If someone says that a place is calm, they mean that it is free from fighting or public disorder, when trouble has recently occurred there or had been expected.

ex.en: The city of Sarajevo appears relatively calm today.
ex.zh: 萨拉热窝市今天显得相对平静了些。

d: adj. 镇静的，沉着的；平静的，稳定的；风平浪静的
n. （精神或情感状态的）镇静，平和；宁静，安静
v. 使平静，使镇静；冷静下来，镇静下来；恢复平静，恢复正常
【名】 （Calm）（法、德）卡尔姆（人名）

e.en: You can use calmly to emphasize that someone is behaving in a very controlled or ordinary way in a frightening or unusual situation.

ex.en: The gunmen calmly walked away and escaped in a waiting car.
ex.zh: 枪手镇定地走开，抽身钻进一辆等待的汽车。

d: adv. 冷静地，平静地，安静地

e.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

ex.en: The Russian foreign minister yesterday cancelled his visit to Washington.
ex.zh: 俄外交部长昨天取消了对华盛顿的访问。

ex.en: Many trains have been cancelled and a limited service is operating on other lines.
ex.zh: 许多列车都被取消了，少数班次在其他路线运行。

e.en: 取消

ex.en: Outbursts of violence forced the cancellation of Haiti's first free elections in 1987.
ex.zh: 暴力事件的爆发迫使海地取消了1987年的首次自由选举。

e.en: If someone in authority cancels a document, an insurance policy, or a debt, they officially declare that it is no longer valid or no longer legally exists. 废止;

ex.en: He intends to try to leave the country, in spite of a government order cancelling his passport.
ex.zh: 他不顾废止他的护照的政府命令，仍打算要离开这个国家。

e.en: 废止;

ex.en: ...a march by groups calling for cancellation of Third World debt.
ex.zh: …要求解除第三世界的债务的一场集体游行。

d: v. 取消（计划好的事情）；终止，废除；盖销，注销；（因素，情况）抵消，对消
n. 取消，撤销；邮票注销章，戳记；经修正的版面
【名】 （Cancel）（法）康塞尔（人名）

e.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again.

ex.en: He was greeted by the chant of "Judas! Judas!"
ex.zh: 他迎来的是不绝于耳的呼喊“叛徒！叛徒！”。

e.en: A chant is a religious song or prayer that is sung on only a few notes. 圣歌;

ex.en: ...a Gregorian chant.
ex.zh: …一首格列高利圣歌。

e.en: If you chant something or if you chant, you repeat the same words over and over again.

ex.en: Demonstrators chanted slogans.
ex.zh: 示威者们反复地喊着口号。

ex.en: The crowd chanted "We are with you."
ex.zh: 民众反复喊着“我们支持你。”

e.en: 重复的呼声

ex.en: A lot of the chanting was in support of the deputy prime minister.
ex.zh: 很多不绝于耳的呼声都支持副总理。

d: n. （宗教仪式中）诵经、念咒、唱圣歌；（群众场合）反复呼喊、齐声喊口号

e.en: Capital is a large sum of money which you use to start a business, or which you invest in order to make more money. 资本;

ex.en: Companies are having difficulty in raising capital.
ex.zh: 各公司在融资方面遇到麻烦。

e.en: You can use capital to refer to buildings or machinery which are necessary to produce goods or to make companies more efficient, but which do not make money directly.

ex.en: ...capital equipment that could have served to increase production.
ex.zh: …可用于提高产量的资产设备。

e.en: Capital is the part of an amount of money borrowed or invested which does not include interest. 本金;

ex.en: With a conventional mortgage, the payments consist of both capital and interest.
ex.zh: 一般的抵押借款，偿还包括本金和利息两部分。

e.en: The capital of a country is the city or town where its government or legislature meets.

ex.en: ...Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal.
ex.zh: …加德满都，尼泊尔的首都。

d: n. 资本，资金；资本家，资方；首都，首府，省会；活动（或生产）中心；大写字母；柱顶，柱头
adj. 可处死刑的；大写的；首府的，省会的；顶好的，极好的
【名】 （Capital）（法）卡皮塔尔（人名）

e.en: An actor's or performer's costume is the set of clothes they wear while they are performing.

ex.en: Even from a distance, the effect of his fox costume was stunning.
ex.zh: 即使从远处看，他的狐装造型也非常漂亮。

ex.en: The performers, in costume and makeup, were walking up and down backstage.
ex.zh: 演员们穿着戏服化着妆，在后台走来走去。

e.en: The clothes worn by people at a particular time in history, or in a particular country, are referred to as a particular type of costume. (某一历史时期或某一国家人们穿的)

ex.en: ...men and women in eighteenth-century costume.
ex.zh: …身着18世纪服装的男男女女。

e.en: A costume drama is one which is set in the past and in which the actors wear the type of clothes that were worn in that period.

ex.en: ...a lavish costume drama set in Ireland and the U.S. in the 1890s.
ex.zh: …以19世纪90年代的爱尔兰和美国为背景的一部大型古装戏。

d: n. 服装（costume 的复数形式）；戏装，演出服装，化妆服；（某一时期、国家或社会群体的）传统服装，服饰
n. （Corentin）人名；（法）科朗坦

e.en: In a place such as a shop or café, a counter is a long narrow table or flat surface at which customers are served.

ex.en: ...those guys we see working behind the counter at our local video rental shop.
ex.zh: …我们所见在本地音像出租商店柜台后工作的那些家伙。

e.en: A counter is a mechanical or electronic device which keeps a count of something and displays the total.

ex.en: The new answering machine has a call counter.
ex.zh: 这种新型的电话答录机有一个通话计数器。

e.en: A counter is a small, flat, round object used in board games.

ex.en: ...a versatile book which provides boards and counters for fifteen different games.
ex.zh: …一本为15种不同棋类游戏提供棋盘和棋子的多功能书。

e.en: If you do something to counter a particular action or process, you do something which has an opposite effect to it or makes it less effective. 抵消;

ex.en: The leadership discussed a plan of economic measures to counter the effects of such a blockade.
ex.zh: 领导层讨论了一项经济措施计划来抵消如此封锁的影响。

ex.en: Sears countered by filing an antitrust lawsuit.
ex.zh: 西尔斯通过提交反垄断诉讼进行了反击。

d: n. 柜台；对立面；计数器，计算器；（棋盘游戏的）筹码；记分冰壶
v. 反驳，驳斥；抵制，抵消；（拳击）还击；逆向移动
adv. 相反地，对立地；逆向地
adj. 反面的，对立的

e.en: A crowd is a large group of people who have gathered together, for example, to watch or listen to something interesting, or to protest about something.

ex.en: A huge crowd gathered in a square outside the Kremlin walls.
ex.zh: 一大群人聚集在了克里姆林宫墙外的广场上。

ex.en: It took some two hours before the crowd was fully dispersed.
ex.zh: 用了大约两个小时才把人群完全驱散。

e.en: A particular crowd is a group of friends, or a set of people who share the same interests or job. 一帮 (朋友); 一群 (志趣相投的人)

ex.en: All the old crowd have come out for this occasion.
ex.zh: 所有老朋友都前来参加了这次活动。

e.en: When people crowd around someone or something, they gather closely together around them.

ex.en: The hungry refugees crowded around the tractors.
ex.zh: 饥饿的难民们围在拖拉机旁。

e.en: If people crowd into a place or are crowded into a place, large numbers of them enter it so that it becomes very full. 挤满;

ex.en: Hundreds of thousands of people have crowded into the centre of the Lithuanian capital, Vilnius.
ex.zh: 几十万人涌进了立陶宛首都维尔纽斯的中心。

ex.en: One group of journalists were crowded into a minibus.
ex.zh: 一群记者挤满了一辆面包车。

d: n. 人群；一伙人；百姓，凡夫俗子；（尤指体育运动赛事的）观众，听众
v. 聚集，群集；靠近，盯着；催促，催逼（因而把人激怒或惹恼）；挤满，塞满

e.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet.

ex.en: Her hair was still damp.
ex.zh: 她的头发还有点湿。

ex.en: ...the damp, cold air.
ex.zh: …又潮又冷的空气。

e.en: Damp is moisture on the inside walls of a house or in the air.

ex.en: There was damp everywhere and the entire building was in need of rewiring.
ex.zh: 到处是潮气，整座建筑需要安装新电线。

d: adj. 潮湿的
n. 湿气，潮气；沼气；气馁
v. 使潮湿，弄湿；减弱，抑制；把（火）调小；限止（钢琴或其他乐器琴弦）的音；减幅，阻尼

ex.zh: 一大群人聚集在了克里姆林宫墙外的广场上。

ex.en: It took some two hours before the crowd was fully dispersed.
ex.zh: 用了大约两个小时才把人群完全驱散。

ex.en: All the old crowd have come out for this occasion.
ex.zh: 所有老朋友都前来参加了这次活动。

e.en: When people crowd around someone or something, they gather closely together around them.

ex.en: The hungry refugees crowded around the tractors.
ex.zh: 饥饿的难民们围在拖拉机旁。

e.en: If people crowd into a place or are crowded into a place, large numbers of them enter it so that it becomes very full. 挤满;

ex.en: Hundreds of thousands of people have crowded into the centre of the Lithuanian capital, Vilnius.
ex.zh: 几十万人涌进了立陶宛首都维尔纽斯的中心。

ex.en: One group of journalists were crowded into a minibus.
ex.zh: 一群记者挤满了一辆面包车。

d: n. 人群；大众；观众，听众；一大堆（crowd 的复数）
v. 聚集；涌向；推搡；挤满（crowd 的第三人称单数）
