abbr. 联合国政治事务部，联合国政治部（Department of Political Affairs）；德意志新闻社（Deutsche Presse Agentur）；（美）国防生产局（Defense Production Administration）；数据处理局（Data Processing Agency）；分期付款账（deferred payment account）；国防生产法（Defense Production Act）
n. 德累斯顿（德国东部城市，萨克森州首府，位于易北河畔）

e.en: Eastern means in or from the east of a region, state, or country.

ex.en: ...Eastern Europe.
ex.zh: …东欧。

e.en: Eastern means coming from or associated with the people or countries of the East, such as India, China, or Japan.

ex.en: In many Eastern countries massage was and is a part of everyday life.
ex.zh: 在许多东方国家，按摩过去和现在都是日常生活的一部分。

d: adj. 东方的；向东的，朝东的

e.en: When a volcano erupts, it throws out a lot of hot, melted rock called lava, as well as ash and steam.

ex.en: The volcano erupted in 1980, devastating a large area of Washington state.
ex.zh: 这座火山1980年喷发，摧毁了华盛顿州的大片地区。

e.en: 喷发

ex.en: ...the volcanic eruption of Tambora in 1815.
ex.zh: …1815年坦布拉火山的喷发。

e.en: If violence or fighting erupts, it suddenly begins or gets worse in an unexpected, violent way.

ex.en: Heavy fighting erupted there today after a two-day cease-fire.
ex.zh: 激烈的战斗在两天的停火之后今天在那里爆发了。

e.en: 爆发

ex.en: ...this sudden eruption of violence.
ex.zh: …这起暴力事件的突然爆发。

d: v. （火山等）喷发，爆发；（暴力、冲突等）突然爆发；（情绪、掌声等）突然迸发；（牙齿、皮疹等）长出（erupt 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: You use everywhere to refer to a whole area or to all the places in a particular area. (某区域内的) 所有地方;

ex.en: Working people everywhere object to paying taxes.
ex.zh: 各地劳动人民都反对纳税。

ex.en: We went everywhere together.
ex.zh: 我们到哪里都一起去。

e.en: You use everywhere to refer to all the places that someone goes to.

ex.en: Mary Jo is still accustomed to travelling everywhere in style.
ex.zh: 玛丽·乔仍然习惯于很有气派地到处旅行。

e.en: You use everywhere to emphasize that you are talking about a large number of places, or all possible places. 到处 (强调地方之多或所有可能的地方)

ex.en: I saw her picture everywhere.
ex.zh: 我到处看到她的照片。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is everywhere, you mean that they are present in a place in very large numbers. 遍地 (强调在某地数量之多);

ex.en: There were cartons of cigarettes everywhere.
ex.zh: 到处都是香烟盒。

d: adv. 到处，处处
n. 每个地方，所有地方

e.en: A figure is a particular amount expressed as a number, especially a statistic.

ex.en: It would be very nice if we had a true figure of how many people in this country haven't got a job.
ex.zh: 要是我们有一个确切的数字反映这个国家到底有多少人没有工作就好了。

ex.en: It will not be long before the inflation figure starts to fall.
ex.zh: 过不了多久，通货膨胀的数字就会开始下降。

e.en: A figure is any of the ten written symbols from 0 to 9 that are used to represent a number.

ex.en: ...the glowing red figures on the radio alarm clock which read 4:22 a.m.
ex.zh: …收音机闹钟上闪闪发光的红色数字显示凌晨4点22分。

e.en: You refer to someone that you can see as a figure when you cannot see them clearly or when you are describing them.

ex.en: Ernie saw the dim figure of Rose in the chair.
ex.zh: 厄尼看到了罗斯坐在椅子里的模糊身影。

e.en: In art, a figure is a person in a drawing or a painting, or a statue of a person.

ex.en: ...a life-size bronze figure of a brooding, hooded woman.
ex.zh: …一个真人大小、戴着头巾、正在沉思的女铜像。

d: n. （figure 的复数）数字，统计数字；人物，重要人物，名人；图形，图表，插图；价格，金额；（人的）体形，身材，身影；人像，画像，雕像；（Figures）菲格斯（人名）
v. （figure 的第三人称单数）认为，估计；计算，算出；是……的一部分，出现（常与 in 连用）；想象，设想，描绘

e.en: Something that is festive is special, colourful, or exciting, especially because of a holiday or celebration.

ex.en: The town has a festive holiday atmosphere.
ex.zh: 这个城市充满了喜庆的节日气氛。

e.en: Festive means relating to a holiday or celebration, especially Christmas.

ex.en: With Christmas just around the corner, you should start your festive cooking now.
ex.zh: 圣诞节就快到了，你现在该着手烹饪过节的食物了。

d: adj. 节日的；喜庆的，欢乐的

e.en: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.

ex.en: They saw a big flash and a huge ball of fire reaching hundreds of feet into the sky.
ex.zh: 他们看到一道强光和一个巨大的火球直冲天空达几百英尺。

e.en: Fire or a fire is an occurrence of uncontrolled burning which destroys buildings, forests, or other things.

ex.en: 87 people died in a fire at the Happy Land Social Club.
ex.zh: 87人死于乐土社交俱乐部的火灾中。

ex.en: A forest fire is sweeping across portions of north Maine this evening.
ex.zh: 今天傍晚一场森林大火正席卷着缅因州北部的部分地区。

e.en: A fire is a burning pile of wood, coal, or other fuel that you make, for example, to use for heat, light, or cooking.

ex.en: There was a fire in the grate.
ex.zh: 壁炉里烧着火。

e.en: A fire is a device that uses electricity or gas to give out heat and warm a room. 电炉;

d: adj. 被解雇的，被开除的；用某种燃料的（常用于 coal-fired 燃煤的、gas-fired 燃气的等复合词）；fired up 表示兴奋的，热情高涨的
v. fire 的过去式和过去分词：解雇；射击；发射；烧制；点火；激发

e.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

ex.en: In the evenings, we gathered around the fireplace and talked.
ex.zh: 晚上，我们聚在壁炉旁聊天。

e.en: If you gather things, you collect them together so that you can use them.

ex.en: I suggest we gather enough firewood to last the night.
ex.zh: 我建议我们捡拾足够的木柴来度过这个夜晚。

e.en: Gather up means the same as .

ex.en: When Steinberg had gathered up his papers, he went out.
ex.zh: 斯坦伯格收好文件后，走了出去。

e.en: If you gather information or evidence, you collect it, especially over a period of time and after a lot of hard work.

ex.en: ...a private detective using a hidden tape recorder to gather information.
ex.zh: …一名用一部暗藏的磁带录音机来搜集信息的私家侦探。

d: v. 聚集（gather 的过去式和过去分词）；收集，集中，积聚；（根据间接信息）推断，了解到（尤用于 I gathered that 等表达）
adj. 聚集的，收集到的；（布料、衣物等）打成细褶的，缩褶的

e.en: You use generally to give a summary of a situation, activity, or idea without referring to the particular details of it.

ex.en: University teachers generally have admitted a lack of enthusiasm about their subjects.
ex.zh: 大学教师们已大致承认对他们的学科缺乏热情。

e.en: You use generally to say that something happens or is used on most occasions but not on every occasion.

ex.en: As women we generally say and feel too much about these things.
ex.zh: 作为女人，我们通常对这些事说得、感受得太多了。

ex.en: In the diet, it is generally true that the darker the fruit the higher its iron content.
ex.zh: 在饮食中，水果颜色越深，其铁含量就越高，这通常是正确的。

d: adv. 笼统地，大概；通常，普遍地
n. 汉堡（德国北部港市）

e.en: Someone who is happy has feelings of pleasure, usually because something nice has happened or because they feel satisfied with their life.

ex.en: Marina was a confident, happy child.
ex.zh: 玛丽娜是个自信、快乐的孩子。

e.en: 快乐地

ex.en: Albert leaned back happily and lit a cigarette.
ex.zh: 艾伯特开心地向后斜靠着并点燃一支香烟。

e.en: A happy time, place, or relationship is full of happy feelings and pleasant experiences, or has an atmosphere in which people feel happy.

ex.en: Except for her illnesses, she had a particularly happy childhood.
ex.zh: 除了几场病痛之外，她有个特别快乐的童年。

ex.en: It had always been a happy place.
ex.zh: 这里从前一直是个令人愉快的地方。

e.en: If you are happy about a situation or arrangement, you are satisfied with it, for example, because you think that something is being done in the right way. 对...

ex.en: If you are not happy about a repair, go back and complain.
ex.zh: 如果你对修理不满意，就回去投诉。

ex.en: He's happy that I deal with it myself.
ex.zh: 他对我自己处理这件事感到很满意。

d: adj. 快乐的；幸福的，使人高兴的；满意的；乐意的；幸运的；合适的
comb. 滥用……的
【名】 （Happy）（英、瑞典、喀）哈皮（人名）

e.en: The ground is the surface of the earth.

ex.en: Forty or fifty women were sitting cross-legged on the ground.
ex.zh: 四五十个妇女正盘腿坐在地上。

ex.en: We slid down the roof and dropped to the ground.
ex.zh: 我们从屋顶滑下来，掉到地上。

e.en: Something that is below ground is under the Earth's surface or under a building. Something that is above ground is on top of the earth's surface. 在地面上/
If you say that something takes place on the ground, you mean it takes place on the surface of the earth and not in the air.

ex.en: Coordinating airline traffic on the ground is as complicated as managing the traffic in the air.
ex.zh: 协调飞机在地面上的交通和掌控空中交通一样复杂。

e.en: The ground is the soil and rock on the earth's surface.

ex.en: The ground had eroded.
ex.zh: 地表已遭腐蚀。

d: n. 地，地面；土地，土壤；（某种用途的）场地；充分的理由，根据；话题，知识领域；观点，立场；优势，有利条件；地线；庭院，花园；渣滓；（绘画或印刷的）背景，底子
v. 以……为根据；（在某学科上）给……以扎实的基础教育；使停飞；禁足；（使）搁浅；落地，着陆；把……放在地上，以……触地；把（电器）接地；（击球员）击出内场地滚球被杀出局
adj. 切碎的，磨碎的；（航空用语）地面的，地勤的；打磨成的，磨光的；生活于地面、地下或水底的
v. 研磨（grind 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 荣誉，光荣；名誉，信用，正直；殊荣，荣幸；荣誉称号，头衔，奖章
vt. 尊敬，尊重；向……致敬；给……以荣誉，表彰；（金融）承兑；履行，遵守

e.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

ex.en: She had decided she must go on as usual, follow her normal routine, and hope and pray.
ex.zh: 她已决定自己必须一如既往地过下去，遵循自己的日常生活规律，同时心存希望并祈祷。

ex.en: He hesitates before leaving, almost as though he had been hoping for conversation.
ex.zh: 他离开前有些犹豫，好像希望跟人说些什么。

e.en: If you say that you cannot hope for something, or if you talk about the only thing that you can hope to get, you mean that you are in a bad situation, and there is very little chance of improving it.

ex.en: Things aren't ideal, but that's the best you can hope for.
ex.zh: 事情并不理想，但你只能指望这些了。

e.en: Hope is also a noun.

ex.en: The only hope for underdeveloped countries is to become, as far as possible, self-reliant.
ex.zh: 欠发达国家的惟一指望就是尽可能地做到自力更生。

e.en: Hope is a feeling of desire and expectation that things will go well in the future.

ex.en: Now that he has become president, many people once again have hope for genuine changes in the system.
ex.zh: 既然他已成为总统，许多人又一次寄期望于体制的真正改革。

ex.en: But Kevin hasn't given up hope of getting in shape.
ex.zh: 但是凯文仍没有放弃康复的希望。

d: v. 希望（hope 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 套头衫，连帽衫，卫衣；（非正式，尤指英国，常含贬义）年轻小混混

e.en: If you have an image of something or someone, you have a picture or idea of them in your mind. (头脑里的) 形象;

ex.en: The image of art theft as a gentleman's crime is outdated.
ex.zh: 艺术品盗窃是绅士犯罪这一观念已经过时了。

e.en: The image of a person, group, or organization is the way that they appear to other people. (个人、团体或组织的)

ex.en: ...the government's negative public image.
ex.zh: …政府负面的公众形象。

e.en: An image is a picture of someone or something.

ex.en: ...photographic images of young children.
ex.zh: …小孩子们的摄影图像。

e.en: An image is a poetic description of something.

ex.en: The natural images in the poem are meant to be suggestive of realities beyond themselves.
ex.zh: 诗中自然景象的描写意在使人联想起那以外的现实。

d: n. 图像，影像，图片；（头脑中的）形象，意象，想象；（公众）形象，声誉；肖像，雕像，圣像；文学意象，生动的描绘（image 的复数）
v. 想象，设想，幻想；描绘……的形象，作……的像（image 的第三人称单数）

e.en: An incident is something that happens, often something that is unpleasant. 事件;

ex.en: These incidents were the latest in a series of disputes between the two nations.
ex.zh: 这些事件是两国一系列争端中最近的几起。

d: n. 事件，事故；（两国间的）冲突，严重摩擦；（职务、财产等所有物的）附属特权
adj. 由……产生的；附属的；入射的

e.en: If you have an image of something or someone, you have a picture or idea of them in your mind. (头脑里的) 形象;

ex.en: The image of art theft as a gentleman's crime is outdated.
ex.zh: 艺术品盗窃是绅士犯罪这一观念已经过时了。

e.en: The image of a person, group, or organization is the way that they appear to other people. (个人、团体或组织的)

ex.en: ...the government's negative public image.
ex.zh: …政府负面的公众形象。

e.en: An image is a picture of someone or something.

ex.en: ...photographic images of young children.
ex.zh: …小孩子们的摄影图像。

e.en: An image is a poetic description of something.

ex.en: The natural images in the poem are meant to be suggestive of realities beyond themselves.
ex.zh: 诗中自然景象的描写意在使人联想起那以外的现实。

d: n. 形象，印象；影像，映像，图像；比喻，意象；画像，塑像，雕像；酷似另一个人的人；（人或事物）外形，外表；像点；硬盘备份；（圣经）偶像
v. 作……的像，描绘……的形象；（以探测器或电磁束）扫描出……的直观图；幻想，想像
【名】 （Image）（法）伊马热（人名）

e.en: An incident is something that happens, often something that is unpleasant. 事件;

ex.en: These incidents were the latest in a series of disputes between the two nations.
ex.zh: 这些事件是两国一系列争端中最近的几起。

d: n. 事件，事故；事变，争端事件；插曲，小事件（incident 的复数）

e.en: You use including to introduce examples of people or things that are part of the group of people or things that you are talking about.

ex.en: Thousands were killed, including many women and children.
ex.zh: 数千人被杀，包括许多妇女和儿童。

d: prep. 包括，包含
v. 包含；把……列为一部分，把……算入（include 的现在分词形式）

e.en: It's is the usual spoken form of "it is." (it is)

ex.en: It's the best news I've heard in a long time.
ex.zh: 这是我很长时间以来听到的最好消息。

e.en: It's is the usual spoken form of "it has," especially when "has" is an auxiliary verb. (it has)

ex.en: It's been such a long time since I played.
ex.zh: 自从我上次演奏以来已经过了这么长时间了。

d: abbr. 它是（it is 的缩约形式）；它已，它有（it has 的缩约形式，尤作助动词）

e.en: You use largely to say that a statement is not completely true but is mostly true.

ex.en: The fund is largely financed through government borrowing.
ex.zh: 这项基金基本上靠政府借款资助。

ex.en: I largely work with people who already are motivated.
ex.zh: 我总是与积极性高的人一起工作。

e.en: Largely is used to introduce the main reason for a particular event or situation. (用于说明原因)

ex.en: Retail sales dipped six-tenths of a percent last month, largely because Americans were buying fewer cars.
ex.zh: 零售额上个月下降了0.6%，主要是由于美国人汽车买得更少了。

d: adv. 很大程度上，主要地
n. 杰克逊（男子名）；杰克逊（美国密西西比州的城市）
n. 里尔（法国北部城市）

e.en: Lives is the plural of . (life)
Lives is the third person singular form of live. (live)

d: n. 生活；生命（life 的复数形式）
v. 居住；生活（live 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Local means existing in or belonging to the area where you live, or to the area that you are talking about. 本地的;

ex.en: We'd better check on the game in the local paper.
ex.zh: 我们最好在本地报纸上查一下这场比赛。

ex.en: Some local residents joined the students' protest.
ex.zh: 一些当地居民加入了学生的抗议活动。

e.en: The locals are local people.

ex.en: Camping is a great way to meet the locals as the Portuguese themselves are enthusiastic campers.
ex.zh: 野营是与当地居民接触的好途径，因为葡萄牙人本身就是热情的露营者。

e.en: 在当地

ex.en: We've got cards which are drawn and printed and designed by someone locally.
ex.zh: 我们得到了由某人在当地绘制、印刷和设计的纸牌。

e.en: Local government is elected by people in one area of a country and controls aspects such as education, housing, and transportation within that area.

ex.en: Education comprises two-thirds of all local government spending.
ex.zh: 教育经费占地方政府所有开销的2/3。

d: adj. 当地的，地方的；局部的；（汽车或火车）每站都停的，慢的；（计算机）局域的；（食品或饮料）低热量的
n. 当地人，本地人；住处附近的酒吧；（工会的）地方分会；慢车，市内公交车；炒股散户；本地新闻；局部

e.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material, which you wear over your face so that people cannot see who you are, or so that you look like someone or something else.

ex.en: The gunman, whose mask had slipped, fled.
ex.zh: 面具滑落的持枪歹徒逃走了。

e.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over all or part of your face to protect you from germs or harmful substances.

ex.en: You must wear goggles and a mask that will protect you against the fumes.
ex.zh: 你必须带上护目镜和防护面具，以保护你不被烟熏。

e.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as a mask, you mean that they do not show their real feelings or character.

ex.en: His mask of detachment cracked, and she saw for an instant an angry and violent man.
ex.zh: 他冷静超然的伪装破碎了，她一瞬间看到了一个愤怒而又狂暴的男人。

e.en: A mask is a thick cream or paste made of various substances, which you spread over your face and leave for some time in order to improve your skin.

ex.en: This mask leaves your complexion feeling soft and supple.
ex.zh: 这种面膜使你的皮肤变得柔软娇嫩。

d: n. 面罩，口罩；防毒面具，呼吸面罩；面膜；假面具，假面；伪装，掩饰；表情，面容；遮盖物，遮蔽物；（古希腊和罗马演员佩戴的）人头面具；遮光板，遮光片；（制造微电路用）模板；（蜻蜓幼虫）脸盖
v. 掩饰，伪装，隐瞒；盖住（气味、味道、声音等）；遮盖；戴面具

e.en: a strong cotton fabric with a raised pattern, used for bedspreads, etc (用作床单等的)

d: n. 法国马赛市
玛农（人名）

e.en: If someone is masked, they are wearing a mask.

ex.en: Masked youths threw stones and firebombs.
ex.zh: 戴着面具的年轻人投掷了石头和燃烧弹。

d: v. mask 的过去式及过去分词：掩饰；给……戴面具；遮蔽；盖住（气味等）；（涂刷时）掩盖
adj. 戴面具的，蒙面的，化装的；隐藏的，潜伏的，掩饰的

e.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material, which you wear over your face so that people cannot see who you are, or so that you look like someone or something else.

ex.en: The gunman, whose mask had slipped, fled.
ex.zh: 面具滑落的持枪歹徒逃走了。

e.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over all or part of your face to protect you from germs or harmful substances.

ex.en: You must wear goggles and a mask that will protect you against the fumes.
ex.zh: 你必须带上护目镜和防护面具，以保护你不被烟熏。

e.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as a mask, you mean that they do not show their real feelings or character.

ex.en: His mask of detachment cracked, and she saw for an instant an angry and violent man.
ex.zh: 他冷静超然的伪装破碎了，她一瞬间看到了一个愤怒而又狂暴的男人。

e.en: A mask is a thick cream or paste made of various substances, which you spread over your face and leave for some time in order to improve your skin.

ex.en: This mask leaves your complexion feeling soft and supple.
ex.zh: 这种面膜使你的皮肤变得柔软娇嫩。

d: n. （mask 的复数形式）口罩，防护口罩；面罩，防护面罩；面具，假面具；伪装，掩盖物；面膜；（技术）遮罩，掩模，掩码
v. （mask 的第三人称单数）掩饰，遮掩，掩盖；用面具遮住脸；遮蔽，屏蔽；使……模糊；（技术）给……加遮罩

e.en: A megaphone is a cone-shaped device for making your voice sound louder in the open air.

d: n. 话筒；喊话筒（megaphone 复数）
v. 用喇叭筒说；广泛宣传（megaphone 的第三人称单数）
n. 时髦社交界；上流社会
n. 迈克尔（男子名；亦指犹太教、基督教传统中的天使长米迦勒）
n. （Moret）人名；（西、葡）莫雷特；（意、法）莫雷

e.en: National means relating to the whole of a country or nation rather than to part of it or to other nations.

ex.en: ...major national and international issues.
ex.zh: …重大的国内和国际问题。

e.en: 全国地

ex.en: ...a nationally televised speech.
ex.zh: …一个全国电视讲话。

e.en: National means typical of the people or customs of a particular country or nation. 国民的;

ex.en: ...the national characteristics and history of the country.
ex.zh: …该国的民族特点和历史。

e.en: You can refer to someone who is legally a citizen of a country as a national of that country.

ex.en: ...a Sri-Lankan national.
ex.zh: …一位斯里兰卡国民。

d: adj. 国家的，全国的；国家所有的，国立的；国内的，本国的
n. 国民，侨民；全国性比赛；全国性报纸
n. 慕尼黑（德国巴伐利亚州首府和最大城市）

e.en: Nationwide activities or situations happen or exist in all parts of a country.

ex.en: The rising number of car crimes is a nationwide problem.
ex.zh: 汽车犯罪不断增加是个全国性的问题。

e.en: Nationwide is also an adverb.

ex.en: The figures show unemployment falling nationwide last month.
ex.zh: 数字显示，上个月失业数字正全国性地下降。

d: adj. 全国性的，全国各地的
adv. 在全国

e.en: A newspaper is a publication consisting of a number of large sheets of folded paper, on which news, advertisements, and other information is printed.

ex.en: He was carrying a newspaper.
ex.zh: 他正拿着一份报纸。

ex.en: They read their daughter's allegations in the newspaper.
ex.zh: 他们从报纸上看到女儿的声明。

e.en: A newspaper is an organization that produces a newspaper.

ex.en: It is the nation's fastest growing national daily newspaper.
ex.zh: 这是该国发展最快的全国性日报社。

e.en: Newspaper consists of pieces of old newspapers, especially when they are being used for another purpose such as wrapping things up. (尤指作其他用途的)

ex.en: He found two pots, each wrapped in newspaper.
ex.zh: 他找到了两只罐子，分别用旧报纸包着。

d: n. 报纸，报；报社；（尤指用作他途的）旧报纸
n. 新闻专线

e.en: Someone or something that is notable is important or interesting. 值得注意的;

ex.en: The proposed new structure is notable not only for its height, but for its shape.
ex.zh: 那座提议的新建筑值得注意，不仅因其高度，还因其外形。

ex.en: Mo did not want to be ruled by anyone and it is notable that she never allowed the men in her life to eclipse her.
ex.zh: 莫不想被任何人管制，很显然，她从不允许她生活中的男性使她黯然失色。

d: adj. 显要的，值得注意的；非常成功的，令人尊敬的
n. 显要人物，名流

e.en: November is the eleventh month of the year in the Western calendar. 11

ex.en: He arrived in London in November 1939.
ex.zh: 他于1939年11月到达伦敦。

d: n. 十一月；（北约音标字母）代表字母 N 的代码词

e.en: October is the tenth month of the year in the Western calendar. 10

ex.en: Most seasonal hiring is done in early October.
ex.zh: 多数季节性招聘是在10月初进行。

ex.en: The first plane is due to leave on October 2.
ex.zh: 第一架飞机定于10月2日起飞。

d: n. [天] 十月

e.en: In the armed forces, an officer is a person in a position of authority.

ex.en: ...a retired army officer.
ex.zh: …一位退役陆军军官。

e.en: Members of the police force can be referred to as officers. 警察;

ex.en: The officer saw no obvious signs of a break-in.
ex.zh: 那个警察没看到任何闯入的明显痕迹。

ex.en: Officer Montoya was first on the scene.
ex.zh: 蒙托亚警官是第一个到达现场的人。

e.en: An officer is a person who has a responsible position in an organization, especially a government organization. (尤指政府部门的)

ex.en: ...a local authority education officer.
ex.zh: …一名地方政府教育官员。

d: n. 军官，人员（officer 复数形式）

e.en: If you participate in an activity, you take part in it.

ex.en: They expected him to participate in the ceremony.
ex.zh: 他们希望他参加这个典礼。

ex.en: Over half the population of this country participate in sports.
ex.zh: 这个国家一半以上的人参加体育运动。

e.en: 参加

ex.en: ...participation in religious activities.
ex.zh: …对宗教活动的参与。

d: adj. 参加的，参与的；（金融）（股票等）持有人有权分享利益的，参与分红的
v. 参加，参与（participate 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: To pass someone or something means to go past them without stopping.

ex.en: As she passed the library door, the telephone began to ring.
ex.zh: 她经过图书馆门口时，电话开始响铃了。

ex.en: Jane stood aside to let her pass.
ex.zh: 简站到一边让她过去。

e.en: When someone or something passes in a particular direction, they move in that direction.

ex.en: He passed through the doorway into the kitchen.
ex.zh: 他穿过门道去厨房。

ex.en: He passed down the tunnel.
ex.zh: 他穿过隧道。

e.en: If something such as a road or pipe passes along a particular route, it goes along that route. (沿某路线)

ex.en: A dirt road passes through the town.
ex.zh: 一条土路穿过那座城镇。

e.en: If you pass something through, over, or around something else, you move or push it through, over, or around that thing. 穿; 越;

ex.en: She passed the needle through the rough cloth, back and forth.
ex.zh: 她用针在那块粗布上来来回回地穿进穿出。

ex.en: "I don't understand," the detective mumbled, passing a hand through his hair.
ex.zh: “我不明白，”那个侦探嘟囔着，同时用一只手捋头发。

d: adj. 已经通过的；已经过去的；已被传递的
v. 经过；穿过；通过；绕；传递；转给（pass 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Peaceful activities and situations do not involve war. 和平的 (活动、局面)

ex.en: He has attempted to find a peaceful solution to the Ossetian conflict.
ex.zh: 他曾试图找到一个解决奥塞梯冲突的和平的办法。

e.en: 和平地

ex.en: The U.S. military expects the matter to be resolved peacefully.
ex.zh: 美国军方期望这一事件能和平解决。

e.en: Peaceful occasions happen without violence or serious disorder. 和平的 (场景)

ex.en: The farmers staged a noisy but peaceful protest outside the headquarters of the organization.
ex.zh: 农民们在该组织总部外举行了一次喧闹但和平的抗议活动。

e.en: 和平地

ex.en: The governor asked the crowd of protestors to leave peacefully.
ex.zh: 州长要求抗议人群和平离开。

d: adj. 宁静的，安静的；和平的，非暴力的；爱好和平的；安详的，平和的

e.en: If you say that someone died peacefully, you mean that they suffered no pain or violence when they died. 安详地 (死去)

ex.en: He died peacefully on December 10 after a short illness.
ex.zh: 他在一场短病后于12月10日安详地离开了人世。

d: adv. 平静地，和平地

e.en: Pirates are sailors who attack other ships and steal property from them.

ex.en: In the nineteenth century, pirates roamed the seas.
ex.zh: 19世纪，海盗很猖獗。

e.en: Someone who pirates CDs, DVDs, books, or computer programs copies and sells them when they have no right to do so. 盗版 (CD、DVD、书籍、计算机程序等)

ex.en: Computer crimes include data theft and pirating software.
ex.zh: 计算机犯罪包括数据窃取和盗版软件。

e.en: 非法复制的

ex.en: New technology makes it possible to make pirated copies of music and movies.
ex.zh: 新技术使制作盗版音乐和影片成为可能。

e.en: A pirate version of something is an illegal copy of it.

ex.en: Pirate copies of the DVD are already being sold.
ex.zh: 该DVD的盗版已经有售了。

d: n. 海盗，海上劫掠者；盗版者，侵犯专利权者；非法制作电视或广播节目的人（或组织）；道德败坏者，违法者
v. 盗印，窃用；劫掠（船只）；劫掠（船只）
adj. 盗版的

e.en: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand. 计划;

ex.en: The three leaders had worked out a peace plan.
ex.zh: 这3位领导人已制定出了一份和平计划。

ex.en: He maintains that everything is going according to plan.
ex.zh: 他坚持说一切都在按计划进行。

e.en: If you plan what you are going to do, you decide in detail what you are going to do, and you intend to do it.

ex.en: If you plan what you're going to eat, you reduce your chances of overeating.
ex.zh: 如果你对要吃的东西加以计划，饮食过度的几率就会减少。

ex.en: He planned to leave Baghdad on Monday.
ex.zh: 他计划星期一离开巴格达。

e.en: If you have plans, you are intending to do a particular thing. (具体)

ex.en: "I'm sorry," she said. "I have plans for tonight.".
ex.zh: “抱歉，”她说。“我今晚有安排。”

e.en: When you plan something that you are going to make, build, or create, you decide what the main parts of it will be and do a drawing of how it should be made.

ex.en: It is no use trying to plan an 18-hole golf course on a 120-acre site if you have to ruin the environment to do it.
ex.zh: 要规划一个占地120公顷、拥有18洞的高尔夫球场如果必须破坏环境才能做到，那就毫无益处了。

d: adj. 有计划的；根据计划的
v. 计划，筹划；打算；设计；期望，预料（plan 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: an exclamation of rejection or disdain
deranged; insane

d: n. 鼠，老鼠（rat 的复数）；卑鄙的人（rat 的复数）；告密者（rat 的复数）；（Rats）人名；（俄）拉茨
int. （口语）胡说，瞎扯（表示厌烦、失望或不屑）
v. 捕鼠（rat 的第三人称单数）；告发，背叛，出卖（rat 的第三人称单数，常与 on 连用）

e.en: A previous event or thing is one that happened or existed before the one that you are talking about.

ex.en: She has a teenage daughter from a previous marriage.
ex.zh: 她有个出自前一次婚姻的十几岁的女儿。

e.en: You refer to the period of time or the thing immediately before the one that you are talking about as the previous one.

ex.en: It was a surprisingly dry day after the rain of the previous week.
ex.zh: 这是继前一周的降雨之后出奇干燥的一天。

d: adj. 以前的，先前的；（时间或顺序上）稍前的；过早的，过急的
n. 前科，犯罪记录

e.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party.

ex.en: About three thousand people held a rally to mark international human rights day.
ex.zh: 大约三千人举行集会以纪念国际人权日。

e.en: When people rally to something or when something rallies them, they unite to support it. 一致支持;

ex.en: Her cabinet colleagues have continued to rally to her support.
ex.zh: 她的内阁同僚们继续团结一致地支持她。

e.en: to bring (a group, unit, etc) into order, as after dispersal, or (of such a group) to reform and come to order 重整;

ex.en: the troops rallied for a final assault

e.en: When someone or something rallies, they begin to recover or improve after having been weak. 恢复健康;

ex.en: He rallied enough to thank his doctors.
ex.zh: 他身体恢复得能向医生们道谢了。

d: v. 召集，集合；公开支持（或反对）；重新集合，重整（军队）；恢复，重新振作；动员（全体人员）发愤图强；（价格）回升，升值；参加汽车拉力赛；对……善意打趣，嘲笑
n. 集会，大会；赛车，汽车拉力赛；（网球等比赛中的）相持，拉锯；（球队技艺的）改进，提高；恢复健康，康复；（尤指股价）止跌回升
【名】  (Rally) （美）拉利（人名）

e.en: Reporting is the presenting of news in newspapers, on radio, and on television.

ex.en: This newspaper has achieved a reputation for honest and impartial political reporting.
ex.zh: 这家报纸凭诚实公正的政治报道赢得了声誉。

d: n. 报告，汇报，申报；新闻报道，新闻采写
adj. 报告的，汇报的，报道的
v. report 的现在分词/动名词：报告；报道；报到

e.en: A residence is a house where people live.

ex.en: The house is currently run as a country inn, but could easily convert back into a private residence.
ex.zh: 这栋房子目前被当作一家乡村客栈用，但可以容易地改回成一所私用住宅。

e.en: Your place of residence is the place where you live.

ex.en: There were significant differences among women based on age, place of residence, and educational levels.
ex.zh: 基于年龄、住处和教育水平，妇女们之间存在显著的差异。

e.en: Someone's residence in a particular place is the fact that they live there or that they are officially allowed to live there.

ex.en: They had entered the country and had applied for permanent residence.
ex.zh: 他们已进入了那个国家，并已经申请了永久居住权。

e.en: If someone is in residence in a particular place, they are living there. 住在 (某处)

ex.en: The king and queen of Jordan are in residence.
ex.zh: 约旦的国王和王后住在宫邸。

d: n. 住宅，住所；居住，定居；（在某国的）居住权，居留许可；（大学的）学生宿舍楼

e.en: When you pay an amount of money to someone, you give it to them because you are buying something from them or because you owe it to them. When you pay something such as a bill or a debt, you pay the amount that you owe. 支付;

ex.en: Owners who have already paid for repairs will be reimbursed.
ex.zh: 已经付了修缮费的业主将会得到退费。

ex.en: The wealthier may have to pay a little more in taxes.
ex.zh: 更有钱的人可能得多交点税。

e.en: When you are paid, you get your wages or salary from your employer.

ex.en: The lawyer was paid a huge salary.
ex.zh: 这个律师拿了很高的薪金。

ex.en: I get paid monthly.
ex.zh: 我拿月薪。

e.en: Your pay is the money that you get from your employer as wages or salary.

ex.en: ...their complaints about their pay and conditions.
ex.zh: …他们对薪水和工作条件的不满。

e.en: If you are paid to do something, someone gives you some money so that you will help them or perform some service for them.

ex.en: There are people who are paid to sit around and play games.
ex.zh: 有人受雇闲坐着玩游戏。

d: v. 支付，付；偿还，缴纳；给予，致以；给……付工资；（投资等）产生……利润，（工作等）有……报酬；划算，有好处；付出代价；盈利；用沥青（或焦油）填塞（甲板或木船接缝）以防止漏水；（政府或机构通过提高价格、税率等使某人）为......买单；储蓄
n. 工资，薪水；付款；回报
adj. （电视节目）付费的，收费的

e.en: Someone's home is the house or apartment where they live.

ex.en: Last night they stayed at home and watched TV.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上他们待在家里看电视。

ex.en: The general divided his time between his shabby offices and his home in Hampstead.
ex.zh: 将军的时间一部分在他那破旧的办公室里度过，另一部分在他汉普斯特德的家度过。

e.en: You can use home to refer in a general way to the house, town, or country where someone lives now or where they were born, often to emphasize that they feel they belong in that place. 家乡;

ex.en: She gives frequent performances of her work, both at home and abroad.
ex.zh: 她经常在国内外演出自己的作品。

ex.en: His father worked away from home for much of Jim's first five years.
ex.zh: 在吉姆5岁前的大部分时间里，他的爸爸离家在外地工作。

e.en: Home means to or at the place where you live. 回家;

ex.en: His wife wasn't feeling too well and she wanted to go home.
ex.zh: 他妻子感觉有些不舒服，想要回家。

ex.en: I'll call you as soon as I get home.
ex.zh: 我一到家就给你打电话。

e.en: Home means made or done in the place where you live.

ex.en: ...cheap but healthy home cooking.
ex.zh: …便宜却健康的家常便饭。

d: n. 家庭（home 的复数形式）；房屋，住宅；（Homes）人名；（德）霍梅斯
v. home 的第三人称单数形式：（动物）返回巢穴或栖息地；（导弹、信号等）自动导向目标（常作 home in on）

e.en: Your budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend. The budget for something is the amount of money that a person, organization, or country has available to spend on it.

ex.en: She will design a fantastic new kitchen for you – and all within your budget.
ex.zh: 她将为你设计一个崭新的漂亮厨房–所有的花费都将在你的预算之内。

ex.en: Someone had furnished the place on a tight budget.
ex.zh: 有人用不多的钱把那个地方布置了一下。

e.en: The budget of an organization or country is its financial situation, considered as the difference between the money it receives and the money it spends. (机构、政府等的)

ex.en: The hospital obviously needs to balance the budget each year.
ex.zh: 该医院显然每年都需要平衡其财务收支。

e.en: If you budget certain amounts of money for particular things, you decide that you can afford to spend those amounts on those things. 安排开支;

ex.en: The company has budgeted $10 million for advertising.
ex.zh: 公司已经安排了1千万美元的广告预算。

ex.en: The film is only budgeted at $10 million.
ex.zh: 这部电影的预算只有1千万美元。

e.en: 预算

ex.en: We have continued to exercise caution in our budgeting for the current year.
ex.zh: 在今年的预算方面，我们继续小心谨慎。

d: n. 预算；政府预算案
v. 制定预算，制定开支计划；计划，安排
adj. 廉价的，经济型的

e.en: Someone's home is the house or apartment where they live.

ex.en: Last night they stayed at home and watched TV.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上他们待在家里看电视。

ex.en: The general divided his time between his shabby offices and his home in Hampstead.
ex.zh: 将军的时间一部分在他那破旧的办公室里度过，另一部分在他汉普斯特德的家度过。

e.en: You can use home to refer in a general way to the house, town, or country where someone lives now or where they were born, often to emphasize that they feel they belong in that place. 家乡;

ex.en: She gives frequent performances of her work, both at home and abroad.
ex.zh: 她经常在国内外演出自己的作品。

ex.en: His father worked away from home for much of Jim's first five years.
ex.zh: 在吉姆5岁前的大部分时间里，他的爸爸离家在外地工作。

e.en: Home means to or at the place where you live. 回家;

ex.en: His wife wasn't feeling too well and she wanted to go home.
ex.zh: 他妻子感觉有些不舒服，想要回家。

ex.en: I'll call you as soon as I get home.
ex.zh: 我一到家就给你打电话。

e.en: Home means made or done in the place where you live.

ex.en: ...cheap but healthy home cooking.
ex.zh: …便宜却健康的家常便饭。

d: n. 家，住宅；（可买卖的）房子，寓所；家庭；养育院，收容所；适于存放……的地方；发源地，发祥地；栖息地，生息地；家乡，祖国；（组织、公司等的）本部，基地；（比赛的）主场
adj. 家庭的，家用的；在家里做（或进行）的；本国的，国内的；在主场进行的；总部的
adv. 回家，在家；到正确的位置；朝着球门，进入到球门里
v. 归巢；对准（目标）；把（思想、注意力）集中于；把（动物）养作宠物

e.en: A building is a structure that has a roof and walls, for example, a house or a factory.

ex.en: They were on the upper floor of the building.
ex.zh: 他们在该建筑物的上层。

d: n. 建筑物，房屋，楼房；建筑，建筑业
v. 建造；发展，建立；逐渐增强（build 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Land is an area of ground, especially one that is used for a particular purpose such as farming or building.

ex.en: Good agricultural land is in short supply.
ex.zh: 肥沃的农业用地短缺。

ex.en: ...160 acres of land.
ex.zh: …160英亩土地。

e.en: You can refer to an area of land which someone owns as their land or their lands.

ex.en: Their home is on his father's land.
ex.zh: 他们的家坐落在他父亲的土地上。

e.en: If you talk about the land, you mean farming and the way of life in farming areas, in contrast to life in the cities.

ex.en: Living off the land was hard enough at the best of times.
ex.zh: 即使是在最好的时期靠种地生活也是很艰难的。

e.en: Land is the part of the world that consists of ground, rather than sea or air.

ex.en: It isn't clear whether the plane went down over land or sea.
ex.zh: 不清楚飞机是落在陆地上还是海里。

d: n. 陆地，地面；土地（尤指耕地或建筑用地）；地产，地皮；农耕，农村生活；国度，国土；想象（或虚构）的地方；（枪炮）阳膛线
v. 着陆，降落；使（飞机）平稳着陆；登陆，上岸；（从船或飞机上）卸下（货物）；落下，跌落；使陷入（困境）；（令人不快的事）突然出现；（尤指轻而易举或意外地）获得；打中（一拳）
【名】 （Land）（英、德、葡、瑞典）兰德（人名）

e.en: Social means relating to society or to the way society is organized.

ex.en: ...the worst effects of unemployment, low pay, and other social problems.
ex.zh: …失业、低工资和其他社会问题造成的最坏影响。

ex.en: ...long-term social change.
ex.zh: …长期的社会变革。

e.en: 在社会上

ex.en: Let's face it – drinking is a socially acceptable habit.
ex.zh: 咱们来面对这个事实吧–饮酒是一种为社会所接受的习俗。

e.en: Social means relating to the status or rank that someone has in society.

ex.en: Higher education is unequally distributed across social classes.
ex.zh: 高等教育是不平等分配给各社会各阶层的。

e.en: 在社会地位上

ex.en: For socially ambitious couples this is a problem.
ex.zh: 对在社会地位方面有野心的夫妇来说，这是个问题。

d: adj. 社会的；社会地位的，社会阶层的；社交的，交际的；好交际的，合群的；群居的
n. 社交聚会，联欢会；社会保障（the social）

e.en: A problem is a situation that is unsatisfactory and causes difficulties for people.

ex.en: ...the economic problems of the inner city.
ex.zh: …内城的经济问题。

ex.en: I do not have a simple solution to the drug problem.
ex.zh: 我并没有一个简单的解决毒品问题的方法。

e.en: A problem is a puzzle that requires logical thought or mathematics to solve it.

ex.en: With mathematical problems, you can save time by approximating.
ex.zh: 对于数学题，你可以用近似法省时间。

d: n. 问题，难题；[数]问题，题目，习题（problem 的复数）

e.en: If one thing is above another one, it is directly over it or higher than it.

ex.en: He lifted his hands above his head.
ex.zh: 他双手举过头顶。

ex.en: Apartment 46 was a quiet apartment, unlike the one above it.
ex.zh: 46号公寓是一套安静的公寓，不像它上面的那一套。

e.en: Above is also an adverb.

ex.en: A long scream sounded from somewhere above.
ex.zh: 从上面什么地方传来一声长长的尖叫。

ex.en: ...a picture of the new plane as seen from above.
ex.zh: …一张该新型飞机的俯瞰图片。

e.en: If an amount or measurement is above a particular level, it is greater than that level. (数量或度量)

ex.en: The temperature crept up to just above 40 degrees.
ex.zh: 气温慢慢升至刚过40度。

ex.en: Victoria Falls has had above average levels of rainfall this year.
ex.zh: 维多利亚瀑布今年的降雨量高于平均水平。

e.en: Above is also an adverb.

ex.en: Banks have been charging 25 percent and above for unsecured loans.
ex.zh: 银行一直以来对无担保贷款收取25%或更高的费用。

d: prep. （数量或度量）在……以上，超过；在（或向）……上面；（级别或地位上）高于； （重要性、质量）超过，胜过；（因善良或诚实正直而）不至于，不屑于（做某事）；（声音）比……更响亮，盖过；不受……影响，免于；（重要性、质量）超过，胜过
adv. （级别或地位上）高于；在（或向）上面，在（或向）较高处；高于，超出（特定数量、比率或标准）；上文，前文
adj. 前文述及的，上述的
n. 上文提及之事，前文所提之事（the above）

e.en: Academic is used to describe things that relate to the work done in schools, colleges, and universities, especially work that involves studying and reasoning rather than practical or technical skills.

ex.en: Their academic standards are high.
ex.zh: 他们的学术水平很高。

e.en: 学术上地

ex.en: He is academically gifted.
ex.zh: 他在学术方面有天份。

e.en: Academic is used to describe things that relate to schools, colleges, and universities.

ex.en: ...the start of the last academic year.
ex.zh: …上一个学年的开始。

e.en: Academic is used to describe work, or a school, college, or university, that places emphasis on studying and reasoning rather than on practical or technical skills.

ex.en: The author has settled for a more academic approach.
ex.zh: 该作者已经确定了一种更学术的方法。

d: adj. 学业的，学术的；学校的，学院的；学业（成绩）优秀的，善于学习的；不切实际的，空谈的
n. 大学教师，学者；（学校或学院的）课程；大学生

e.en: An applied subject of study has a practical use, rather than being concerned only with theory.

ex.en: ...Applied Physics.
ex.zh: …应用物理学。

d: adj. 应用的，实用的
v. 申请；涂，敷；施加，实施；应用，运用（apply 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Annual events happen once every year.

ex.en: The issues will be voted on at the company's annual meeting on April 21 in Wilmington.
ex.zh: 这些问题将在该公司4月21日在威尔明顿的年会上投票表决。

e.en: 每年一次地

ex.en: Companies report to their shareholders annually.
ex.zh: 各公司每年向其股东们汇报一次。

e.en: Annual quantities or rates relate to a period of one year.

ex.en: The electronic and printing unit has annual sales of about $80 million.
ex.zh: 电子与印刷部有约八千万美元的年度销售额。

e.en: 年度地

ex.en: El Salvador produces 100,000 tons of refined copper annually.
ex.zh: 萨尔瓦多一年生产10万吨精炼铜。

d: adj. 一年一度的；年度的；（植物）一年生的
n. 一年生植物；年刊，年鉴
adv. 在中心，位于中心地带，向中心；由中央统一地，集中地

e.en: A big person or thing is large in physical size. (体积、体态)

ex.en: Australia's a big country.
ex.zh: 澳大利亚是一个幅员辽阔的国家。

ex.en: Her husband was a big man.
ex.zh: 她丈夫是个身材高大的男人。

e.en: Something that is big consists of many people or things. (数量)

ex.en: The crowd included a big contingent from Cleveland.
ex.zh: 人群中包括一个来自克利夫兰的大型代表团。

e.en: If you describe something such as a problem, increase, or change as a big one, you mean it is great in degree, extent, or importance. 重大的;

ex.en: Her problem was just too big for her to tackle on her own.
ex.zh: 她的问题太严重了，她无法独力应付。

e.en: A big organization employs many people and has many customers. (规模)

ex.en: ...one of the biggest companies in Italy.
ex.zh: …意大利规模最大的公司之一。

d: adj. （尺寸、数量、规模或年龄）大的；重大的，严重的；有影响力的；糟糕的；有雄心的；受欢迎的；热衷于……的；程度深的，效果好的；大方的，大度的；生僻的，晦涩的；大写的
adv. 大大，给人印象深地；夸口地；大量地
v. 招摇
【名】 （Big）（土）比格（人名）

e.en: Chancellor is the title of the head of government in Germany and Austria. (德国、奥地利)

ex.en: ...Chancellor Gerhard Schröder of Germany.
ex.zh: …德国总理格哈德·施罗德。

e.en: The head of some American universities is called the chancellor. (美国)
In Britain, the chancellor is the chancellor of the exchequer. (英国)

d: n. （英国）财政大臣；（德国或奥地利）总理；（英国大学）名誉校长，（美国大学）校长；法官
【名】 （Chancellor）（英）钱塞勒（人名）

e.en: When you make a decision, you choose what should be done or which is the best of various possible actions.

ex.en: I don't want to make the wrong decision and regret it later.
ex.zh: 我不想作出错误的决定，以后后悔。

e.en: Decision is the act of deciding something or the need to decide something.

ex.en: The growing pressures of the crisis may mean that the moment of decision can't be too long delayed.
ex.zh: 这次危机不断增长的压力可能意味着作决定的时刻不会拖延很久。

e.en: Decision is the ability to decide quickly and definitely what to do.

ex.en: He is very quick-thinking and very much a man of decision.
ex.zh: 他思维很敏捷，是个很果断的人。

d: n. 决定（decision 的复数）；（管理）决策；决断

e.en: Duty is work that you have to do for your job.

ex.en: Staff must report for duty at their normal place of work.
ex.zh: 职员必须到他们平常的岗位报到上班。

e.en: Your duties are tasks which you have to do because they are part of your job.

ex.en: I carried out my duties conscientiously.
ex.zh: 我认真执行了我的各项职责。

e.en: If you say that something is your duty, you believe that you ought to do it because it is your responsibility.

ex.en: I consider it my duty to write to you and thank you.
ex.zh: 我觉得我有责任给你写信表示感谢。

e.en: Duties are taxes which you pay to the government on goods that you buy.

ex.en: Import duties still average 30%.
ex.zh: 进口关税平均仍为30%。

d: n. 责任，义务；上班，值班；职责，任务；税，关税；兵役；（牧师的）行礼拜式；（发动机的）功率
【名】 （Duty）（英）迪蒂（人名）

e.en: Financial means relating to or involving money. 金融的;

ex.en: The company is in financial difficulties.
ex.zh: 这个公司处于财务困难之中。

e.en: 金融上;

ex.en: She would like to be more financially independent.
ex.zh: 她想要在财政上更加独立。

d: adj. 财政的，金融的；有钱的；（俱乐部或社团成员）已缴费的
n. （组织或个人的）财务状况；金融公司股票

e.en: You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said. 然而 (用以引出令人吃惊或形成对比的话语)

ex.en: This was not an easy decision. It is, however, a decision that we feel is dictated by our duty.
ex.zh: 这可不是一个轻松的决定。不过我们觉得我们有责任做出这样的的决定。

e.en: You use however before an adjective or adverb to emphasize that the degree or extent of something cannot change a situation. 不管多么 (用于形容词或副词前表强调)

ex.en: You should always strive to achieve more, however well you have done before.
ex.zh: 不管以前做得多么好，你应该始终争取更大的进步。

ex.en: However hard she tried, nothing seemed to work.
ex.zh: 无论她多么努力，好像都无济于事。

e.en: You use however when you want to say that it makes no difference how something is done. 不管用什么方法 (用以表示没有区别)

ex.en: However we adopt healthcare reform, it isn't going to save major amounts of money.
ex.zh: 不管我们采取什么样的医疗改革措施，它都不会节省太多的钱。

e.en: You use however in expressions such as or however long it takes and or however many there were to indicate that the figure you have just mentioned may not be accurate. 无论多久 (表示刚提到的数字不一定准确);

ex.en: Wait 30 to 60 minutes or however long it takes.
ex.zh: 等30到60分钟，或需要的不管多长的时间。

d: adv. 然而，可是，不过；无论如何；（用于表示惊讶）究竟怎样；……左右，……上下
conj. 不管怎样，无论如何；然而，可是
n. （Healey）人名；（英）希利

e.en: Investment is the activity of investing money.

ex.en: He said the government must introduce tax incentives to encourage investment.
ex.zh: 他说，政府必须通过给予税收利益来鼓励投资。

e.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest, or the thing that you invest it in.

ex.en: ...an investment of twenty-eight million dollars.
ex.zh: …2800万美元的投资额。

e.en: If you describe something you buy as an investment, you mean that it will be useful, especially because it will help you to do a task more cheaply or efficiently.

ex.en: When selecting boots, fine, quality leather will be a wise investment.
ex.zh: 在挑选靴子时，买精致、质量上乘的皮靴会是明智的。

e.en: Investment of time or effort is the spending of time or effort on something in order to make it a success.

ex.en: I worry about this big investment of time not working.
ex.zh: 我担心这么多的时间投入不起作用。

d: n. 投资；值得买的东西；（时间、精力的）投入；包围，封锁

e.en: A john is a toilet or bathroom. 卫生间;

ex.en: I've got to go to the john.
ex.zh: 我得去趟卫生间。

d: n. 厕所；嫖客
【名】 （John）约翰（人名）

e.en: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all. 缺乏;

ex.en: Despite his lack of experience, he got the job.
ex.zh: 尽管缺乏经验，他还是得到了那份工作。

ex.en: The charges were dropped for lack of evidence.
ex.zh: 由于缺少证据，起诉被撤销了。

e.en: If you say that someone or something lacks a particular quality or that a particular quality is lacking in them, you mean that they do not have any or enough of it. 缺乏;

ex.en: It lacked the power of the Italian cars.
ex.zh: 它没有意大利汽车那样的动力。

ex.en: He lacked the judgment and political acumen for the post of chairman.
ex.zh: 他缺少作为主席的判断力和政治敏锐性。

e.en: If you say there is no lack of something, you are emphasizing that there is a great deal of it.

ex.en: He said there was no lack of things for them to talk about.
ex.zh: 他说他们不缺话题谈。

d: n. 缺乏，不足
v. 缺乏，不足；需要
【名】 （Lack）（美、德）拉克（人名）
adv. 在当地；在本地；在附近地区；局部地；局部性地；（计算机）在本机；在本地设备上（而非远程服务器）

e.en: Left is the past tense and past participle of leave. (leave)
If there is a certain amount of something left, or if you have a certain amount of it left, it remains when the rest has gone or been used.

ex.en: Is there any gin left?
ex.zh: 还有杜松子酒吗？

ex.en: They still have six games left to play.
ex.zh: 他们还剩下6场比赛要打。

e.en: If there is a certain amount of something left over, or if you have it left over, it remains when the rest has gone or been used.

ex.en: So much income is devoted to monthly mortgage payments that nothing is left over.
ex.zh: 这么多的收入都用来偿还每月的抵押贷款了，因此没什么剩余。

e.en: The left is one of two opposite directions, sides, or positions. If you are facing north and you turn to the left, you will be facing west. In the word "to," the "t" is to the left of the "o."

ex.en: Go back to the last fork in the road and take a left.
ex.zh: 回到路的上一个岔口，然后左转。

ex.en: ...the brick wall to the left of the conservatory.
ex.zh: …温室左边的砖墙。

d: adj. 左边的；剩余的；左派的，左翼的
adv. 在左面，向左
n. 左侧，左方（the left）；左边的道路，左侧的通道；（认为应将财产、金钱和权力更平等地分配的）左翼人士，左派组织（the Left）；（尤指拳击中的）左手拳；（在足球或类似运动中面向对手球门的）左半场；（军队的）左翼
v. 离开（某人或某处）；抛弃，丢弃；不立刻做（leave 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: it is certain 毫无疑问的是;

d: n. 伦敦

e.en: The price of something is the amount of money that you have to pay in order to buy it.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in the price of petrol.
ex.zh: …燃气价格的一次猛涨。

ex.en: They expected house prices to rise.
ex.zh: 他们预期房价会上涨。

e.en: The price that you pay for something that you want is an unpleasant thing that you have to do or suffer in order to get it.

ex.en: There may be a price to pay for such relentless activity, perhaps ill health or even divorce.
ex.zh: 这样没完没了的活动可能是要付出代价的，也许是不良健康状况甚至是离婚。

e.en: If something is priced at a particular amount, the price is set at that amount.

ex.en: The bond is currently priced at $900.
ex.zh: 这种债券当前定价为$900。

ex.en: Analysts predict that Digital will price the new line at less than half the cost of comparable IBM mainframes.
ex.zh: 分析家们预测迪吉多公司会将其新线产品的价格定在低于可比的IBM公司大型主机成本的一半的水平。

e.en: 定价

ex.en: It's hard to maintain competitive pricing.
ex.zh: 很难保持有竞争力的定价。

d: n. 价格，物价（price 的复数）
v. 给……定价；查明……的价格（price 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A percentage is a fraction of an amount expressed as a particular number of hundredths of that amount.

ex.en: Only a few vegetable-origin foods have such a high percentage of protein.
ex.zh: 只有几种来源于植物的食品含有如此高百分比的蛋白质。

d: n. 百分比，百分率；部分，比例；利润分成，提成；利益，好处

e.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

ex.en: There was total agreement to start the peace process as soon as possible.
ex.zh: 全体同意尽快启动和平进程。

ex.en: They decided to spread the building process over three years.
ex.zh: 他们决定在三年内分期完成该建造过程。

e.en: A process is a series of things that happen naturally and result in a biological or chemical change.

ex.en: It occurs in elderly men, apparently as part of the aging process.
ex.zh: 作为衰老进程的一部分，它明显发生在老年男性身上。

e.en: When raw materials or foods are processed, they are prepared in factories before they are used or sold.

ex.en: ...fish which are processed by the best methods: from freezing to canning and smoking.
ex.zh: …用从冷冻到装罐和熏制等最好的方法加工的鱼。

ex.en: The material will be processed into plastic pellets.
ex.zh: 该原料将被加工成塑料颗粒。

e.en: Process is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the cost of reengineering the production process.
ex.zh: …重新设计生产过程的成本。

d: n. 步骤，程序；（自然或偶然的）变化过程；（为达到某目标的）过程，进程；制作方法，加工方法；传票；（生，剖）端突，突起
adj. （印刷）三原色的，三色版的； 经过特殊加工的；照相板的
v. （用化学物品或机器）处理，加工；审核，受理（正式文件或请求）；（计算机）处理（数据）；冲洗（照片）；加工（食品）；列队行进；把（头发）弄成直发

e.en: A scheme is someone's plan for achieving something, especially something that will bring them some benefit.

ex.en: ...a quick money-making scheme to get us through the summer.
ex.zh: …一个能让我们迅速赚到钱以顺利度过这个夏季的计划。

ex.en: They would first have to work out some scheme for getting the treasure out.
ex.zh: 他们首先得想出某种计划把珍宝取出来。

e.en: If you say that people are scheming, you mean that they are making secret plans in order to gain something for themselves.

ex.en: Everyone's always scheming and plotting.
ex.zh: 每个人时刻都在算计和谋划。

ex.en: The bride's family were scheming to prevent a wedding.
ex.zh: 新娘的家人在密谋阻止婚礼。

e.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement involving many people which is made by a government or other organization. (政府或其他机构的)

ex.en: ...a private pension scheme.
ex.zh: …一个私人养老金计划。

e.en: When people talk about the scheme of things or the grand scheme of things, they are referring to the way that everything in the world seems to be organized.

ex.en: We realize that we are infinitely small within the scheme of things.
ex.zh: 我们认识到在大千世界中我们是极其渺小的。

d: n. （政府或其他组织的）计划，方案；（用于组织或整理信息的）系统，体系；组合，布局；阴谋，诡计；社会住宅区
v. 密谋，策划；认为，猜想；按色调布置
【名】 （Scheme）（瑞典）谢默（人名）

e.en: You use situation to refer generally to what is happening in a particular place at a particular time, or to refer to what is happening to you. 情况;

ex.en: Army officers said the situation was under control.
ex.zh: 军方官员说局势已得到控制。

ex.en: And now for a look at the travel situation in the rest of the country.
ex.zh: 现在来看一看该国其他地区的旅行条件。

d: n. 情况，形势；重要问题，突发情况；（建筑物或城镇的）地理位置，环境特点；工作，职位

e.en: A stamp or a postage stamp is a small piece of paper which you lick and stick on an envelope or package before you mail it to pay for the cost of the postage.

ex.en: ...a book of stamps.
ex.zh: …一本邮票册。

ex.en: As of February 3rd, the price of a first class stamp will go up to 29 cents.
ex.zh: 自2月3日起，每张一等邮票的价格将上涨到29分。

e.en: A stamp is a small block of wood or metal which has a pattern or a group of letters on one side. You press it onto an pad of ink and then onto a piece of paper in order to produce a mark on the paper. The mark that you produce is also called a stamp. 印章;

ex.en: ...a date stamp and an ink pad.
ex.zh: …一个日期印章和一个印泥。

e.en: If you stamp a mark or word on an object, you press the mark or word onto the object using a stamp or other device. 盖 (章); 印 (某标记); 打上 (某字)

ex.en: Car manufacturers stamp a vehicle identification number at several places on new cars to help track down stolen vehicles.
ex.zh: 汽车生产商们在新车车身的几个地方打上车辆识别码以帮助追查被盗车辆。

e.en: If you stamp or stamp your foot, you lift your foot and put it down very hard on the ground, for example because you are angry or because your feet are cold. 跺 (脚); 跺脚;

ex.en: Often he teased me till my temper went and I stamped and screamed, feeling furiously helpless.
ex.zh: 他过去经常取笑我直到我生气，又跺脚又尖叫，感觉非常无助。

ex.en: His foot stamped down on the accelerator.
ex.zh: 他一脚猛地踩下油门。

d: n. 邮票；印记，戳记；印，章，戳；跺脚（声），跺蹄（声）；特征，痕迹，烙印；类型，种类，类别；表明，表示；重要影响，持久影响；（捣矿机中用于捣碎矿石的）铁砧；购物券，购买券
vt. 跺（脚），重踩，重踏；迈着重步走，跺着脚走；在……上面印盖（图案、记号、字母等）；显示出（感情）；表明（某人）是……；（用印模）冲压；对…有重要（永久性）的影响；在……上贴邮票；捣碎（矿石），压碎（矿石）
【名】 （Stamp）（德）施坦普，（英）斯坦普（人名）

e.en: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it. 开始 (做某事)

ex.en: John then unlocked the front door and I started to follow him up the stairs.
ex.zh: 接着约翰打开前门，我开始随他上楼。

ex.en: It was 1956 when Susanna started the work on the garden.
ex.zh: 苏珊娜是在1956年开始修建那个花园的。

e.en: Start is also a noun.

ex.en: After several starts, she read the report properly.
ex.zh: 几次起头之后，她正确地读了那份报告。

e.en: When something starts, or if someone starts it, it takes place from a particular time. 使开始发生;

ex.en: The fire is thought to have started in an upstairs room.
ex.zh: 这火被认为是从楼上的一间房开始的。

ex.en: All of the passengers started the day with a swim.
ex.zh: 所有乘客都以游泳开始了这一天。

e.en: Start is also a noun.

ex.en: ...1918, four years after the start of the Great War.
ex.zh: …第一次世界大战开始4年后的1918年。

d: v. 开始，着手；（使）发生；发动，启动；创办，开办；出发，启程；以……起步（或起家）；（由……）起，起始；突然一惊，吓一跳；开始抱怨，开始争论；（比赛中）首发上场；（眼睛）突起，鼓出；使松动，使脱落；使（猎物）离巢
n. 开始，开端；启程，启动；（事业的）最初机遇，起步机会；起点（the start）；比赛，上场；突然一惊；领先的时间（距离）；新工作，新企业，新手；先发上场

e.en: If you tackle a difficult problem or task, you deal with it in a very determined or efficient way.

ex.en: The first reason to tackle these problems is to save children's lives.
ex.zh: 解决这些问题的首要原因是为了挽救孩子们的生命。

e.en: If you tackle someone in a game such as American football or rugby, you knock them to the ground. If you tackle someone in soccer or hockey, you try to take the ball away from them. (美式或英式橄榄球比赛中) 擒抱摔倒; (足球运动或曲棍球运动中)

ex.en: Foley tackled the quarterback.
ex.zh: 福利擒住并摔倒了四分卫。

e.en: Tackle is also a noun. 擒抱撞倒;

ex.en: ...a tackle by fullback Brian Burrows.
ex.zh: …后卫布赖恩•伯罗斯的阻截。

e.en: If you tackle someone about a particular matter, you speak to them honestly about it, usually in order to get it changed or done.

ex.en: I tackled him about how anyone could live amidst so much poverty.
ex.zh: 我坦率地与他谈论哪有人能在如此的极度贫困中生活。

d: v. 应付，解决（难题或局面）；与……交涉；（足球、曲棍球等比赛中）抢断；（橄榄球等比赛中）擒抱并摔倒（对方球员）；擒获；对付，打（尤指罪犯）；质问，责问；反对，反抗
n. （足球等中的）抢断球；（橄榄球或美式足球）擒抱摔倒；（美式足球中的）阻截队员；体育器械，（尤指）渔具；（吊起重物用的）索具，滑轮；男性性器官

e.en: In the United States and some other countries, the Treasury is the government department that deals with the country's finances.

ex.en: ...a senior official at the Treasury.
ex.zh: …财政部的一位高级官员。

e.en: Treasuries are financial bonds that are issued by the United States government in order to raise money. (美国政府发行的)

ex.en: ...people who invest in 10- and 20- and 30-year Treasuries.
ex.zh: …10年、20年和30年期国库券的投资者。

d: n. 财政部；大量珍品，宝藏；（城堡、教堂等的）宝库，珍藏室；国库，金库

e.en: The value of something such as a quality, attitude, or method is its importance or usefulness. If you place a particular value on something, that is the importance or usefulness you think it has. 重要性;

ex.en: The value of this work experience should not be underestimated.
ex.zh: 这项工作经验的重要性不应该被低估。

e.en: If something is of value, it is useful or important. If it is of no value, it has no usefulness or importance. 重要的/

ex.en: This weekend course will be of value to everyone interested in the Pilgrim Route.
ex.zh: 这个周末课程对于每一个对朝圣路线感兴趣的人来说都将是重要的。

e.en: If you value something or someone, you think that they are important and you appreciate them.

ex.en: I value the opinion of my husband and we agree on most things.
ex.zh: 我重视我丈夫的意见，而且我们在大多数事情上看法一致。

e.en: The value of something is how much money it is worth.

ex.en: The value of his investment has risen by more than $50,000.
ex.zh: 他的投资价值已经增长$50000多。

d: adj. 重要的、宝贵的、贵重的；经估价的
v. value 的过去式和过去分词：重视、珍视；估价、评估

e.en: Wealth is the possession of a large amount of money, property, or other valuable things. You can also refer to a particular person's money or property as their wealth.

ex.en: Economic reform has brought relative wealth to peasant farmers.
ex.zh: 经济改革使农民相对富裕起来。

e.en: If you say that someone or something has a wealth of good qualities or things, you are emphasizing that they have a very large number or amount of them.

ex.en: Their websites contain a wealth of information on the topic.
ex.zh: 他们的网站上有大量与该主题相关的信息。

ex.en: The city boasts a wealth of beautiful churches.
ex.zh: 该城引以为荣的是有大量漂亮的教堂。

d: n. 财富；富有；大量

e.en: Working people have jobs that they are paid to do.

ex.en: Like working women anywhere, Asian women are buying convenience foods.
ex.zh: 像其他地方的职业妇女一样，亚洲的妇女们在购买方便食品。

e.en: Working people are ordinary people who do not have professional or very highly paid jobs.

ex.en: The needs and opinions of ordinary working people were ignored.
ex.zh: 那些从事一般工作的普通人的需求和观点被忽视了。

e.en: Your working life is the period of your life in which you have a job or are of a suitable age to have a job.

ex.en: He started his working life as a truck driver.
ex.zh: 他开始工作时是一名卡车司机。

e.en: The working population of an area consists of all the people in that area who have a job or who are of a suitable age to have a job. 有工作的;

ex.en: Almost 13 percent of the working population is already unemployed.
ex.zh: 几乎13％的劳动人口已经失业。

d: adj. 有工作的；处于就业年龄的；与工作有关的；上班时间的，工作时间的；公事上的（早餐或午餐等）；从事体力劳动的；（机器、系统等）运转的，运作的；初步的，暂定的；尚可应付工作的，基本够用的；（议会票数）足够多数的；（动物）用于农业的，用作打猎的，用于看守的；（农场或企业）经营性的，营利性的
n. （设备、组织或系统的）工作方式，运行方式；矿坑，（矿内）工作区；工作，干活，劳动；班次，线路；（数学题的）计算过程，解答
v. 受雇于，从事……工作；工作，劳动；努力取得，力争（work 的现在分词）
【名】 （Working）（美）沃金（人名）

e.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

ex.en: An Illinois House committee voted Thursday to abolish the death penalty.
ex.zh: 伊利诺伊州议院的一个委员会在星期四投票废除了死刑。

d: v. 废除，废止，取消

e.en: If you accept something that you have been offered, you say yes to it or agree to take it.

ex.en: Eventually Esteban persuaded her to accept an offer of marriage.
ex.zh: 最终埃斯特班说服她接受了求婚。

ex.en: All those invited to next week's peace conference have accepted.
ex.zh: 所有应邀参加下周和平会议的人都已接受了邀请。

e.en: If you accept an idea, statement, or fact, you believe that it is true or valid.

ex.en: I do not accept that there is any kind of crisis in American science.
ex.zh: 我不相信美国科学有任何危机。

ex.en: I don't think they would accept that view.
ex.zh: 我不认为他们会相信那个观点。

e.en: If you accept a plan or an intended action, you agree to it and allow it to happen.

ex.en: The Council will meet to decide if it should accept his resignation.
ex.zh: 委员会将开会来决定是否应该接受他的辞呈。

e.en: If you accept an unpleasant fact or situation, you get used to it or recognize that it is necessary or cannot be changed.

ex.en: People will accept suffering that can be shown to lead to a greater good.
ex.zh: 人们将会容忍能被证明会带来更大利益的苦难。

ex.en: Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.
ex.zh: 城市居民常常将噪音作为城市生活的一部分来容忍。

d: v. 接受，收受；同意，赞成；相信，认为……正确；忍受，容忍；吸纳，招收；接纳；承担（责任等），承认；承兑，认付（单据等）；不排斥；适配

e.en: You can use the accused to refer to a person or a group of people charged with a crime or on trial for it.

ex.en: The accused is alleged to be a member of a right-wing gang.
ex.zh: 这名被告据称是一个右翼团伙中的一员。

d: n. 被告（the accused）
v. 控告，指控；指责，谴责，归咎于（accuse 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you describe something such as a story or a piece of music as affecting, you think it is good because it makes you feel a strong emotion, especially sadness or pity.

ex.en: ...an affecting drama about a woman with a terminal illness.
ex.zh: …一部关于一个身患绝症的女人的感人戏剧。

d: adj. 动人的，感人的
v. 影响；（疾病）侵袭，感染；使感动，打动；假装；炫耀，做作地使用（affect 的现在分词）

e.en: If you are affluent, you have a lot of money.

ex.en: Cigarette smoking used to be more common among affluent people.
ex.zh: 吸烟过去在富人中更为普遍。

e.en: The affluent are people who are affluent.

ex.en: The diet of the affluent has not changed much over the decades.
ex.zh: 富人的饮食数十年来没怎么变。

d: adj. 富裕的，富足的；（水）畅流，滔滔流动；丰富的
n. 富人；支流
n. 可购性，负担能力

e.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

ex.en: The children are allowed to watch TV after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们被允许在放学后看电视。

ex.en: Smoking will not be allowed.
ex.zh: 吸烟将被禁止。

e.en: If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.

ex.en: Gifts like chocolates or flowers are allowed.
ex.zh: 像巧克力或者花这样的礼物是准许的。

e.en: If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.

ex.en: He won't allow himself to fail.
ex.zh: 他不容许自己失败。

e.en: If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen. 使能够 (发生)

ex.en: The compromise will allow him to continue his free market reforms.
ex.zh: 这个妥协将使他得以继续他的自由市场改革。

ex.en: ...an attempt to allow the Muslim majority a greater share of power.
ex.zh: …使穆斯林多数派分享更多权力的一种尝试。

d: v. allow 的过去式和过去分词：允许，认可；给予，酌留（机会、时间）；允许进入（或出去、通过）；使可能；承认，接受；（非正式）断言，认为
adj. 允许的，容许的

e.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

ex.en: The children are allowed to watch TV after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们被允许在放学后看电视。

ex.en: Smoking will not be allowed.
ex.zh: 吸烟将被禁止。

e.en: If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.

ex.en: Gifts like chocolates or flowers are allowed.
ex.zh: 像巧克力或者花这样的礼物是准许的。

e.en: If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.

ex.en: He won't allow himself to fail.
ex.zh: 他不容许自己失败。

e.en: If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen. 使能够 (发生)

ex.en: The compromise will allow him to continue his free market reforms.
ex.zh: 这个妥协将使他得以继续他的自由市场改革。

ex.en: ...an attempt to allow the Muslim majority a greater share of power.
ex.zh: …使穆斯林多数派分享更多权力的一种尝试。

d: v. 允许，准许；使有可能，使能够；任凭，听任（allow 的第三人称单数）
n. 安迪（男子名，等于 Andrew）

e.en: You use already to show that something has happened, or that something had happened before the moment you are referring to. Some speakers use already with the simple past tense of the verb instead of a perfect tense.

ex.en: They had already voted for him at the first ballot.
ex.zh: 他们已经在第一轮投票中投了他的票。

ex.en: She says she already told the neighbours not to come over for a couple of days.
ex.zh: 她说她已经告诉了邻居们这两天不要过来。

e.en: You use already to show that a situation exists at this present moment or that it exists at an earlier time than expected. You use already after the verb "be" or an auxiliary verb, or before a verb if there is no auxiliary. When you want to add emphasis, you can put already at the beginning of a sentence.

ex.en: The authorities believe those security measures are already paying off.
ex.zh: 当局相信那些安全措施已经在起作用了。

ex.en: He was already rich.
ex.zh: 他早就富了。

d: adv. 已经，早已；马上，够了（用于表达不耐烦或气恼）

e.en: The amount of something is how much there is, or how much you have, need, or get.

ex.en: He needs that amount of money to survive.
ex.zh: 他需要那笔钱来维持生活。

ex.en: I still do a certain amount of work for them.
ex.zh: 我仍旧为他们做一定数量的工作。

e.en: If something amounts to a particular total, all the parts of it add up to that total.

ex.en: Consumer spending on sports-related items amounted to $9.75 billion.
ex.zh: 消费者在体育相关用品上的消费总共达到了97.5亿美元。

d: v. amount 的过去式和过去分词（常与 to 连用）；总计，共计；等同于，相当于；发展成，有所成就（常与 little、nothing、something 等连用，多用于否定或疑问）
n. （Angela）（美、菲、意）安吉拉（人名）

e.en: When you are angry, you feel strong dislike or impatience about something.

ex.en: Are you angry with me for some reason?
ex.zh: 你是因为某个原因生我的气了吗？

ex.en: I was angry about the rumours.
ex.zh: 我对这些谣言感到生气。

e.en: 生气地

ex.en: Officials reacted angrily to those charges.
ex.zh: 官员们愤怒地回应了那些指控。

d: adj. 愤怒的，生气的；狂风暴雨的，波涛汹涌的；红肿的，感染的

e.en: If you announce something, you tell people about it publicly or officially.

ex.en: He will announce tonight that he is resigning from office.
ex.zh: 他今晚将宣布他要辞职。

ex.en: She was planning to announce her engagement to Peter.
ex.zh: 她在计划宣布她与彼得的婚约。

e.en: If you announce a piece of news or an intention, especially something that people may not like, you say it loudly and clearly, so that everyone you are with can hear it.

ex.en: Peter announced that he had no intention of wasting his time at any university.
ex.zh: 彼得声明他无意在任何一所大学里浪费他的时间。

e.en: If an airport or rail employee announces something, they tell the public about it by means of a loudspeaker system.

ex.en: The loudspeaker announced the arrival of the train.
ex.zh: 扬声器宣布了那列火车的到达。

d: v. 宣布，公布；声称，郑重地说；（尤指通过广播）通知；播报，讲解（体育赛事）；通报……的到来；显示；告知；宣布竞选公职
n. 强迫，施压（指通过直接施压或强硬劝说使对方同意或就范）

e.en: When you approach something, you get closer to it.

ex.en: He didn't approach the front door at once.
ex.zh: 他没有立即走近前门。

ex.en: When I approached, they grew silent.
ex.zh: 当我走近时，他们变得沉默了。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: At their approach the little boy ran away and hid.
ex.zh: 当他们走近时，那个小男孩跑开了并藏了起来。

e.en: If you approach someone about something, you speak to them about it for the first time, often making an offer or request.

ex.en: When Brown approached me about the job, my first reaction was of disbelief.
ex.zh: 当布朗为这份工作找我时，我的第一反应是不相信。

ex.en: He approached me to create and design the restaurant.
ex.zh: 他来找我创办并设计那家餐馆。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: There had already been approaches from buyers interested in the whole of the group.
ex.zh: 已经有一些对整个集团感兴趣的买主来接洽了。

d: v. 靠近，临近；接洽，交谈；对付，处理；近似，接近于
n. 方法，态度；靠近，接近；接洽，要求；通道，路径；进场着陆；近似物

e.en: An article is a piece of writing that is published in a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: ...a newspaper article.
ex.zh: …一篇报上的文章。

ex.en: According to an article in Newsweek the drug could have side effects.
ex.zh: 据一篇《新闻周刊》上的文章，这种药物可能有副作用。

e.en: You can refer to objects as articles of some kind.

ex.en: ...articles of clothing.
ex.zh: …衣物。

ex.en: He had stripped the house of all articles of value.
ex.zh: 他已把那所房子里值钱的东西洗劫一空。

e.en: An article of a formal agreement or document is a section of it that deals with a particular point.

ex.en: The country appears to be violating several articles of the convention.
ex.zh: 该国看来正在违反该公约中的数个条款。

e.en: In grammar, an article is a kind of determiner. In English, "a" and "an" are called the indefinite article, and "the" is called the definite article.

d: n. 文章，论文；物品；条款，条文；冠词；见习契约，见习期
v. 见习，签约做实习生；进行控告；使……受协议条款的约束

e.en: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

ex.en: "How is Frank?" he asked.
ex.zh: “弗兰克怎么样？”他问道。

ex.en: I asked him his name.
ex.zh: 我问了他的名字。

e.en: If you ask someone to do something, you tell them that you want them to do it. 让 (某人做某事)

ex.en: We had to ask him to leave.
ex.zh: 我们不得不让他离开。

e.en: If you ask to do something, you tell someone that you want to do it.

ex.en: I asked to see the Director.
ex.zh: 我要求见总经理。

e.en: If you ask for something, you say that you would like it.

ex.en: I decided to go to the next house and ask for food.
ex.zh: 我决定到隔壁房子去要吃的。

d: v. 询问，打听；要求，请求；邀请，约请 ；指望，期待
【名】 （Ask）（芬、瑞典）阿斯克（人名）

e.en: If someone or something moves or is moved away from a place, they move or are moved so that they are no longer there. If you are away from a place, you are not in the place where people expect you to be.

ex.en: An injured policeman was led away by colleagues.
ex.zh: 一位受伤的警察被同事们带走了。

ex.en: He walked away from his car.
ex.zh: 他从他的车边走开了。

e.en: If you look or turn away from something, you move your head so that you are no longer looking at it. (目光)

ex.en: She quickly looked away and stared down at her hands.
ex.zh: 她迅速转移目光，低头盯着自己的双手。

e.en: If you put something away, you put it where it should be. If you hide someone or something away, you put them in a place where nobody can see them or find them. (收藏)

ex.en: I put my journal away and prepared for bed.
ex.zh: 我把日记收好，准备睡觉。

ex.en: All her letters were carefully filed away in folders.
ex.zh: 她所有的信件都被仔细地归档在文件夹里。

e.en: You use away to talk about future events. For example, if an event is a week away, it will happen after a week. 距离 (某事件的时间)

ex.en: ...the Washington summit, now only just over two weeks away.
ex.zh: …现在离华盛顿峰会的召开只有两个多星期。

d: adv. 距离……有多远，距离……有多久；朝另一个方向；不在，离开；（放）在安全的地方；逐渐消失；一直，继续不断地；移走；（比赛）在客场
adj. （球队比赛）客场的
n. 客场比赛，客场获胜

e.en: The beginning of an event or process is the first part of it. (事情、过程的)

ex.en: This was also the beginning of her recording career.
ex.zh: 这也是她灌片生涯的开始。

e.en: The beginnings of something are the signs or events which form the first part of it.

ex.en: The discussions were the beginnings of a dialogue with Moscow.
ex.zh: 这些会谈是与莫斯科对话的序曲。

e.en: The beginning of a period of time is the time at which it starts. (某时段的)

ex.en: The wedding will be at the beginning of March.
ex.zh: 婚礼将于3月初举行。

e.en: The beginning of a piece of written material is the first words or sentences of it. (文章的)

ex.en: ...the question that was raised at the beginning of this chapter.
ex.zh: …本章开头提出的问题。

d: n. 开始，开端；序曲，开始部分；早期，初期；发端，起源
adj. 初级的，基本的
v. 开始，着手（begin 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A bell is a device that makes a ringing sound and is used to give a signal or to attract people's attention.

ex.en: I had just enough time to finish eating before the bell rang and I was off to my first class.
ex.zh: 我在铃响前刚好有时间吃完，然后就去上第一节课了。

e.en: A bell is a hollow metal object shaped like a cup which has a piece hanging inside it that hits the sides and makes a sound.

ex.en: My brother, Nick, was born on a Sunday, when all the church bells were ringing.
ex.zh: 我的弟弟尼克，出生在一个星期天，当时所有教堂的钟都在鸣响。

e.en: a bellowing or baying cry, esp that of a hound or a male deer in rut 吼叫声;
to utter (such a cry) 发出(叫喊声)

d: n. 钟，铃；钟声，铃声（the bell）；钟状物
v. 系铃，装钟；发出响铃（或敲钟）般的声音； 给……打电话；呈钟状，成钟状鼓起（或张开）

e.en: A block of a substance is a large rectangular piece of it.

ex.en: ...a block of ice.
ex.zh: …一大块冰。

e.en: A block of apartments or offices is a large building containing them.

ex.en: ...a white-painted apartment block.
ex.zh: …一幢漆成白色的公寓楼。

e.en: A block in a town or city is an area of land with streets on all its sides, or the area or distance between such streets.

ex.en: He walked around the block three times.
ex.zh: 他绕着这个街区走了3圈。

ex.en: She walked four blocks down High Street.
ex.zh: 她沿着高街走了4个街区。

e.en: Blocks are wooden or plastic cubes, such as those used as toys by children.

d: n. 街区；积木；大块，方块；大楼，楼群；组，批，段；（计算机）数据块
v. 阻碍，封锁，堵塞；阻止，妨碍，遮挡（视线），干扰（信号）；封堵，拦挡（体育比赛）；使成块

e.en: the practice of grouping schoolchildren according to ability to ensure a balanced intake at different levels of ability to secondary school (按学生能力的)

d: n. 捆扎，绑扎；条带，条纹；（鸟类学）鸟类环志；（英国教育）按学生能力分组（以便中学均衡招生）
v. 联合，结合（band 的现在分词，常与 together 连用）

e.en: Your body is all your physical parts, including your head, arms, and legs.

ex.en: The largest organ in the body is the liver.
ex.zh: 体内最大的器官是肝脏。

e.en: You can also refer to the main part of your body, except for your arms, head, and legs, as your body.

ex.en: Lying flat on the floor, twist your body on to one hip and cross your upper leg over your body.
ex.zh: 平躺在地板上，躯干扭向胯一侧，将上边的腿跨过躯干。

e.en: You can refer to a person's dead body as a body.

ex.en: Officials said they had found no traces of violence on the body of the politician.
ex.zh: 官方说他们在这位政治家的尸体上没有发现任何暴力痕迹。

e.en: A body is an organized group of people who deal with something officially. 团体;

ex.en: She was elected student body president at the University of North Carolina.
ex.zh: 她当选为北卡罗莱纳大学学生社团主席。

d: n. 身体，躯体；躯干；尸体；（与灵魂或精神相对的）肉体；（尤指某种类型或性格的）人；（建筑物、文件等的）主体，主要部分；车身，机身；衣身；器身，（球拍的）拍身；团体，机构，群体；大量；物体，天体；水域；（酒的）醇度，醇厚；（头发的）稠密度，浓密；（妇女或婴儿的）紧身衣裤；（制陶用语）坯体
v. 赋予（抽象事物）以形体，使具体化；制造（汽车）的车身
【名】 （Body）（英、法、罗）博迪（人名）

e.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

ex.en: Lower interest rates can boost the economy by reducing borrowing costs for consumers and businesses.
ex.zh: 低利率可以通过为消费者和商家降低借贷成本来促进经济发展。

e.en: Boost is also a noun.

ex.en: It would get the economy going and give us the boost that we need.
ex.zh: 这会推动经济发展并带给我们所需要的推动力。

e.en: If something boosts your confidence or morale, it improves it. 增强 (信心、士气)

ex.en: We need a big win to boost our confidence.
ex.zh: 我们需要一个大的胜利来增强我们的自信心。

e.en: Boost is also a noun. (信心、士气的)

ex.en: It did give me a boost to win such a big event.
ex.zh: 赢了这么一场大型比赛，的确使我士气大振。

d: v. 使增长，推动；偷窃；宣扬，推广
n. 推动，促进；广告，宣扬
【名】 （Boost）（英）布斯特，（德）博斯特（人名）
n. 英国（大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国的通称）；不列颠（大不列颠岛，包括英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士）

e.en: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.

ex.en: His eighth book came out earlier this year and was an instant best-seller.
ex.zh: 他的第8本书今年早些时候出版了，并很快成为了一本畅销书。

ex.en: ...the author of a book on politics.
ex.zh: …一本政治书的作者。

e.en: A book of something such as stamps, matches, or tickets is a small number of them fastened together between thin cardboard covers. (邮票) 册; (火柴) 纸板; (票)

ex.en: Can I have a book of first class stamps please?
ex.zh: 请给我一版一等邮票，好吗？

e.en: When you book something such as a hotel room or a ticket, you arrange to have it or use it at a particular time.

ex.en: American officials have booked hotel rooms for the women and children.
ex.zh: 美国官员已经为这些妇女和儿童预订了宾馆房间。

ex.en: Laurie booked herself a flight home.
ex.zh: 劳里为自己预订了回家的机票。

e.en: A company's or organization's books are its records of money that has been spent and earned or of the names of people who belong to it. (公司或机构的) 帐簿;

ex.en: For the most part he left the books to his managers and accountants.
ex.zh: 他大多把账簿留给他的经理和会计们处理。

d: n. 书，书籍；本子，簿册；（长篇作品的）篇，卷，部；装订成册之物；赌局，打赌；账册，账簿
v. 预订，预约；（警方）将……记录在案；（裁判）记名警告
【名】 （Book）（英）布克，（瑞典）博克，（朝）北（人名）

e.en: Body tissue that is calcified has become hard because of the presence of substances called calcium salts.

ex.en: ...calcified tissue.
ex.zh: ...钙化组织。

d: adj. 钙化的，石灰化的；僵化的，固执不变的
v. 钙化，石灰化；僵化（calcify 的过去式和过去分词）
n. （Burnham）人名；（英、西）伯纳姆

e.en: If you call someone or something by a particular name or title, you give them that name or title.

ex.en: I always wanted to call the dog Mufty for some reason.
ex.zh: 出于某种原因，我总想叫那条狗穆夫蒂。

ex.en: "Doctor..."—"Will you please call me Sarah?"
ex.zh: “…医生” — “请叫我萨拉好吗？”

e.en: If you call someone or something a particular thing, you suggest they are that thing or describe them as that thing. 把…描述为;

ex.en: The speech was interrupted by members of the Republican Party, who called him a traitor.
ex.zh: 演讲被称他为叛徒的共和党成员们打断了。

ex.en: She calls me lazy and selfish.
ex.zh: 她说我又懒又自私。

e.en: If you call something, you say it in a loud voice, because you are trying to attract someone's attention.

ex.en: He could hear the others downstairs calling his name.
ex.zh: 他能听到其他人在楼下喊他的名字。

e.en: Call out means the same as call.

ex.en: The butcher's son called out a greeting.
ex.zh: 那屠夫的儿子声音洪亮地招呼了一声。

d: n. 电话，通话（call 的复数）；呼吁，要求；（计算机）调用
v. 呼叫，打电话；称呼；召唤（call 的第三人称单数形式）；要求，需要（call for 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you care about something, you feel that it is important and are concerned about it.

ex.en: ...a company that cares about the environment.
ex.zh: …一家关心环境的公司。

ex.en: ...young men who did not care whether they lived or died.
ex.zh: …一群不在乎自己死活的年轻人。

e.en: If you care for someone, you feel a lot of affection for them.

ex.en: He wanted me to know that he still cared for me.
ex.zh: 他想让我知道他仍然爱着我。

e.en: 体贴

ex.en: ...the "feminine" traits of caring and compassion.
ex.zh: …体贴和同情这些“女性”的特质。

e.en: If you care for someone or something, you look after them and keep them in a good state or condition.

ex.en: They hired a nurse to care for her.
ex.zh: 他们雇了个护士来照顾她。

ex.en: ...these distinctive cars, lovingly cared for by private owners.
ex.zh: …这些被私家车主精心呵护着的各具特色的汽车。

d: n. 照料，护理；小心，谨慎；忧虑，烦恼；收养，监护
v. 照顾，照料；在意，担忧；喜欢，想要
【名】 （Care）（英）凯尔，（塞）察蕾（人名）

e.en: If you capture someone or something, you catch them, especially in a war. 俘虏;

ex.en: The guerrillas shot down one aeroplane and captured the pilot.
ex.zh: 那些游击队员击落了一架飞机，并俘虏了飞行员。

e.en: Capture is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the final battles which led to the army's capture of the town.
ex.zh: …部队夺取该镇的最后几场战斗。

e.en: If something or someone captures a particular quality, feeling, or atmosphere, they represent or express it successfully.

ex.en: Chef Idris Caldora offers an inspired menu that captures the spirit of the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: 伊德里斯·卡尔多拉厨师的菜单很有创意，充分体现了地中海风情。

e.en: If something captures your attention or imagination, you begin to be interested or excited by it. If someone or something captures your heart, you begin to love them or like them very much.

ex.en: ...the great names of the past who usually capture the historian's attention.
ex.zh: …那些常常为史学家所关注的伟人们。

d: v. 俘获，捕获；夺取，占领；吸引，引起；记录，体现；拍摄，录制（capture 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A champion is someone who has won the first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

ex.en: ...a former Olympic champion.
ex.zh: …一位前奥运冠军。

ex.en: Kasparov became world champion.
ex.zh: 卡斯帕罗夫成了世界冠军。

e.en: If you are a champion of a person, a cause, or a principle, you support or defend them. 拥护者;

ex.en: He received acclaim as a champion of the oppressed.
ex.zh: 他作为被压迫者的捍卫者而受到了赞誉。

e.en: If you champion a person, a cause, or a principle, you support or defend them. 拥护;

ex.en: He passionately championed the poor.
ex.zh: 他曾热情地捍卫穷人。

d: n. 冠军，第一名；拥护者，斗士
v. 捍卫，拥护，支持
adj. 极好的；冠军的，得一等奖的
【名】 （Champion）（英）钱皮恩，（法）尚皮翁（人名）

e.en: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen. 起因;

ex.en: Smoking is the biggest preventable cause of death and disease.
ex.zh: 吸烟是造成不必要疾病和死亡的最大原因。

e.en: A cause is an aim or principle which a group of people supports or is fighting for. 奋斗目标;

ex.en: Refusing to have one leader has not helped the cause.
ex.zh: 拒绝接受领导无益于该事业。

e.en: To cause something, usually something bad, means to make it happen.

ex.en: The insecticide used on some weeds can cause health problems.
ex.zh: 喷洒在野草上的杀虫剂会引发各种健康问题。

ex.en: This was a genuine mistake, but it did cause me some worry.
ex.zh: 这纯属失误，但它确实令我有些不安。

e.en: If you have cause for a particular feeling or action, you have good reasons for feeling it or doing it.

ex.en: Only a few people can find any cause for celebration.
ex.zh: 只有少数人能找到庆祝的理由。

d: vt. 成为…的原因，导致，引起，造成（cause 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground. 提;

ex.en: He was carrying a briefcase.
ex.zh: 他提着公文包。

ex.en: She carried her son to the car.
ex.zh: 她抱着儿子向车走去。

e.en: If you carry something, you have it with you wherever you go.

ex.en: You have to carry a pager so that they can call you in at any time.
ex.zh: 你得带个传呼机，以便他们随时可以联系到你。

e.en: If something carries a person or thing somewhere, it takes them there.

ex.en: Flowers are designed to attract insects which then carry the pollen from plant to plant.
ex.zh: 花儿天生就能吸引昆虫，昆虫则在植物之间传递花粉。

ex.en: The delegation was carrying a message of thanks to President Mubarak.
ex.zh: 代表团向穆巴拉克总统传达谢意。

e.en: If a person or animal is carrying a disease, they are infected with it and can pass it on to other people or animals. 携带 (病毒)

ex.en: The test could be used to screen healthy people to see if they are carrying the virus.
ex.zh: 这项测试可以用来检查健康人群，看他们是否携带该病毒。

d: v. carry 的现在分词：运送，输送；携带；传染，传播；能记住；承重；承担责任；具有（品质或特点）；带来；获得支持或通过；登载；销售；怀孕；进位
n. 运送，搬运

e.en: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

ex.en: The ambassador appealed for a change in U.S. policy.
ex.zh: 该大使呼吁美国政策的变革。

ex.en: There are going to have to be some drastic changes.
ex.zh: 一定得有些重大变革。

e.en: If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.

ex.en: It is a complex system, but it certainly makes a change.
ex.zh: 这是个复杂系统，但肯定有所改进。

e.en: If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.

ex.en: His physician modified the dosage but did not change to a different medication.
ex.zh: 他的医生调整了剂量，但没有改换成别的药方。

e.en: When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different. 改变;

ex.en: We are trying to detect and understand how the climates change.
ex.zh: 我们在努力探测并了解气候是怎样变化的。

ex.en: In the union office, the mood gradually changed from resignation to rage.
ex.zh: 在工会办公室，情绪渐渐由依从变成了愤怒。

d: v. 改变，变化；更换，替换；换乘（change 的第三人称单数）
n. 变化，变革（change 的复数）
adv. 便宜地，廉价地；简陋地，寒酸地，粗俗地

e.en: A chronic illness or disability lasts for a very long time. Compare . 慢性的;

ex.en: ...chronic back pain.
ex.zh: …长期背痛。

e.en: 慢性地;

ex.en: Most of them were chronically ill.
ex.zh: 他们中大部分人都有慢性病。

e.en: You can describe someone's bad habits or behaviour as chronic when they have behaved like that for a long time and do not seem to be able to stop themselves.

ex.en: ...a chronic worrier.
ex.zh: …一个老是发愁的人。

e.en: A chronic situation or problem is very severe and unpleasant.

ex.en: One cause of the artist's suicide seems to have been chronic poverty.
ex.zh: 那位艺术家自杀的原因之一好像是极度贫困。

d: adj. （疾病）慢性的，长期的；（问题）一直有的，反复出现的；难以根除的，积习难改的；糟透的，拙劣的
【名】 （Chronic）（英）克罗尼克（人名）

e.en: A class is a group of students who are taught together.

ex.en: He had to spend about six months in a class with younger students.
ex.zh: 他不得不在一个比他小的学生的班上呆了大约六个月。

e.en: A class is a course of teaching in a particular subject.

ex.en: He acquired a law degree by taking classes at night.
ex.zh: 他通过上晚上的课获得了法律学位。

e.en: A class of things is a group of them with similar characteristics.

ex.en: Harbour staff noticed that measurements given for the same class of boats often varied.
ex.zh: 港口员工们注意到对同一类小船所给出的尺寸经常不同。

e.en: If you do something in class, you do it during a lesson in school.

ex.en: There is lots of reading in class.
ex.zh: 课上有大量阅读。

d: n. 课程；班，班级；种类，类别；等级，级别；（大学成绩的）等级；阶级，社会阶层；（计算机）类；（生物）纲（class 的复数）
vt. 将……分类，把……归类（class 的第三人称单数）
n. 大块，厚块；大量，大部分；话语组成部分，组块；矮胖的（男）人
v. 将……分成数份；将……组合（或归类）；扔，抛；发出“砰啷”声；切分，切割（数据）

e.en: Considerable means great in amount or degree. 相当多的;

ex.en: To be without Pearce would be a considerable blow.
ex.zh: 要是缺了皮尔斯，那会是相当大的打击。

ex.en: Doing it properly makes considerable demands on our time.
ex.zh: 把这件事做得到位，要花我们相当多的时间。

e.en: 相当多地;

ex.en: Children vary considerably in the rate at which they learn these lessons.
ex.zh: 孩子们学习这些课的速度差别相当大。

d: adj. 相当大的，相当重要的；（人）显要的，值得尊敬的

e.en: A considered opinion or act is the result of careful thought.

ex.en: We would hope to be able to give a considered response to the unions' proposals by the end of the year.
ex.zh: 我们希望在年底能对工会的提议给出一个深思熟虑的答复。

d: adj. 深思熟虑的
v. 考虑，斟酌；认为，视为；体贴，顾及（consider 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Something that is cool has a temperature which is low but not very low.

ex.en: I felt a current of cool air.
ex.zh: 我感觉到了一阵凉风。

ex.en: The water was slightly cooler than a child's bath.
ex.zh: 这水比小孩子的洗澡水稍微凉一点。

e.en: If it is cool, or if a place is cool, the temperature of the air is low but not very low.

ex.en: Thank goodness it's cool in here.
ex.zh: 谢天谢地，这里很凉爽。

ex.en: Store grains and cereals in a cool, dry place.
ex.zh: 把谷物和杂粮储存在凉爽、干燥的地方。

e.en: Cool is also a noun.

ex.en: She walked into the cool of the hallway.
ex.zh: 她走入了凉爽的过道。

e.en: Clothing that is cool is made of thin material so that you do not become too hot in hot weather. (衣服)

ex.en: In warm weather, you should wear clothing that is cool and comfortable.
ex.zh: 天气热时，你应该穿凉快舒适的衣服。

d: adj. 冷却的，被冷却的（常作定语，也用于 air-cooled、water-cooled 等复合词）
