v. cool 的过去式和过去分词：（使）变凉，冷却，降温；（使）冷静下来，平息（情绪、争论等）

e.en: Course is often used in the expression "of course," or instead of "of course" in informal spoken English. See . 当然 (在口语中代替)(of course)
The course of a vehicle, especially a ship or aircraft, is the route along which it is travelling.

ex.en: Aircraft can avoid each other by altering course to left or right.
ex.zh: 飞行器可以通过向左或向右改变航线来避免相撞。

e.en: A course of action is an action or a series of actions that you can do in a particular situation.

ex.en: My best course of action was to help Gill by being sympathetic.
ex.zh: 我最好的做法是通过表达同情去帮助吉尔。

e.en: A course is a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject.

ex.en: ...a course in business administration.
ex.zh: …一门工商管理课程。

d: n. 课程；过程；道路，航线；进程，进展；方针，总方向；行动方式，处理方法；疗程；一道菜；比赛场地；（砖、石等墙的）层；（常sing.）追踪狩猎（尤指野兔）；横帆；一组同音弦；追踪狩猎（尤指野兔）
v. 奔流，快速流动；（感情、思想）涌动；（用猎犬）追踪（兔子）

e.en: A crash is an accident in which a moving vehicle hits something and is damaged or destroyed. 撞车;

ex.en: His elder son was killed in a car crash a few years ago.
ex.zh: 他大儿子几年前死于一次车祸。

e.en: A crash is a sudden, loud noise.

ex.en: Two people recalled hearing a loud crash about 1:30 a.m.
ex.zh: 两人回忆说大约凌晨1：30时听到一声巨响。

e.en: If a moving vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed. 使…撞毁;

ex.en: The plane crashed mysteriously near the island of Ustica.
ex.zh: 飞机在乌斯蒂卡岛附近神秘地坠毁了。

ex.en: Her car crashed into the rear of a van.
ex.zh: 她的汽车撞毁了一辆面包车的尾部。

e.en: If something crashes somewhere, it moves and hits something else violently, making a loud noise. (发出巨响的)

ex.en: The door swung inwards to crash against a chest of drawers behind it.
ex.zh: 门摆向里面，砰的一声猛力撞上了门后的五斗橱。

ex.en: My words were lost as the walls above us crashed down, filling the cellar with brick dust.
ex.zh: 随着上面的墙体轰隆一声倒塌下来，地窖里充满砖灰，我吓得说不出话来。

d: v. 撞车，坠毁；猛撞，发出巨响；破产，倒闭，暴跌；（计算机）瘫痪，死机；（在体育比赛中）惨败；过夜，入睡；心脏停止跳动；不请自来，偷偷混入（派对）；闯红灯
n. 撞车事故，失事；巨响，碰撞声；（计算机）瘫痪，死机；破产，暴跌；（做毛巾、窗帘等用的）粗布
adj. 应急的，速成的
adv. 哗啦一声地

e.en: A database is a collection of data that is stored in a computer and that can easily be used and added to.

ex.en: The state maintains a database of names of people allowed to vote.
ex.zh: 该州有一个可以投票的人的姓名数据库。

d: n. （计算机）数据库，资料库

e.en: A date is a specific time that can be named, for example, a particular day or a particular year.

ex.en: What's the date today?
ex.zh: 今天是几号？

e.en: A date is an appointment to meet someone or go out with them, especially someone with whom you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship.

ex.en: I have a date with Bob.
ex.zh: 我和鲍勃有个约会。

e.en: If you are dating someone, you go out with them regularly because you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship with them. You can also say that two people are dating. (恋爱中)

ex.en: For a year I dated a woman who was a research assistant.
ex.zh: 有一年的时间，我一直和一个女助理研究员约会。

e.en: If you have a date with someone with whom you are having, or may soon have, a romantic relationship, you can refer to that person as your date. (恋爱中的)

ex.en: He lied to Essie, saying his date was one of the girls in the show.
ex.zh: 他对埃西撒谎说他约会的对象是参加演出的女孩儿其中的一个。

d: n. 日期，日子；约会，幽会；约会对象；椰枣，海枣
v. 注明日期；确定年代；谈恋爱，约会；过时，不流行；使显老
【名】 （Date）（英）戴特，（日）伊达（人名）

e.en: If you are debilitated by something such as an illness, it causes your body or mind to become gradually weaker.

ex.en: Stewart took over yesterday when Russell was debilitated by a stomach virus.
ex.zh: 昨天因拉塞尔患有肠炎身体变得虚弱，斯图尔特已经接管了他的工作。

e.en: To debilitate an organization, society, or government means to gradually make it weaker.

ex.en: ...their efforts to debilitate the political will of the Western alliance.
ex.zh: ... 他们努力去逐步削弱西方国家联盟的政治意愿。

d: adj. 使衰弱的，使人虚弱的
v. 使衰弱，使虚弱（debilitate 的现在分词）

e.en: When you deny something, you state that it is not true.

ex.en: She denied both accusations.
ex.zh: 她否认对她的两项指控。

ex.en: The government has denied that the authorities have uncovered a plot to assassinate the president.
ex.zh: 政府否认当局已经发现一个暗杀总统的阴谋。

e.en: If you deny someone something that they need or want, you refuse to let them have it.

ex.en: Two federal courts ruled that the military cannot deny prisoners access to lawyers.
ex.zh: 两联邦法院裁定军方不能拒绝让囚犯聘请律师。

d: v. 否认；拒绝承认；拒绝给予

e.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example, 1980 to 1989. 10年 (尤指起始年末尾为0)

ex.en: ...the last decade of the nineteenth century.
ex.zh: …19世纪的最后10年。

d: n. 数十年（decade 的复数）

e.en: To be dependent on something or someone means to need them in order to succeed or be able to survive.

ex.en: The local economy is overwhelmingly dependent on oil and gas extraction.
ex.zh: 当地经济严重依赖石油和天然气提炼。

e.en: If one thing is dependent on another, the first thing will be affected or determined by the second.

ex.en: ...companies whose earnings are largely dependent on the performance of the Chinese economy.
ex.zh: …盈利很大程度上取决于中国经济表现的公司。

e.en: Dependent is the same as . 同dependant

d: adj. 依赖的，依靠的；取决于；有瘾的
n. 受供养者

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it.

ex.en: The initial deposit required to open an account is a minimum 100 dollars.
ex.zh: 开户需要的首笔存入额是至少100美元。

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is in a bank account or savings account, especially a sum which will be left there for some time.
A deposit is an amount of a substance that has been left somewhere as a result of a chemical or geological process. 沉积物;

ex.en: ...underground deposits of gold and diamonds.
ex.zh: …黄金和钻石的地下矿床。

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which you pay when you start renting something. The money is returned to you if you do not damage what you have rented.

ex.en: I put down a $500 security deposit for another apartment.
ex.zh: 我为另一套公寓支付了$500押金。

d: n. （金融）存款，存款额；订金，押金，保证金；（地质）沉积物，矿床（deposit 的复数）
v. （金融）存储（把钱存入账户）；（地质）使沉积，沉淀；支付订金、押金或保证金（deposit 的单三形式）

e.en: When something develops, it grows or changes over a period of time and usually becomes more advanced, complete, or severe.

ex.en: It's hard to say at this stage how the market will develop.
ex.zh: 在现阶段很难说市场会如何发展。

ex.en: These clashes could develop into open warfare.
ex.zh: 这些冲突可能会发展成公开的战争。

e.en: 发展的;

ex.en: Their bodies were well developed and super fit.
ex.zh: 他们的身体发育良好，极其健康。

e.en: If a problem or difficulty develops, it begins to occur.

ex.en: The space agency says a problem has developed with an experiment aboard the space shuttle.
ex.zh: 航天局说在航天飞机上做的一项实验出了问题。

e.en: If you say that a country develops, you mean that it changes from being a poor agricultural country to being a rich industrial country.

ex.en: All countries, it was predicted, would develop and develop fast.
ex.zh: 据预测，所有的国家都会发达起来，并且很迅速。

d: v. （使）成长，发育，发展；逐渐形成，逐渐养成；开发，研制；出现，产生；修建，开发土地；提高，加强；患病；阐释，展开；冲洗，使底片显影；（修改旋律、和声或节奏以）展开（音乐主题）；（棋）出子

e.en: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

ex.en: The black car drove away from them and disappeared.
ex.zh: 黑色的小汽车驶离了他们便消失了。

e.en: If someone or something disappears, they go away or are taken away somewhere where nobody can find them.

ex.en: ...a Japanese woman who disappeared thirteen years ago.
ex.zh: …一位13年前失踪的日本妇女。

e.en: If something disappears, it stops existing or happening.

ex.en: The immediate threat of the past has disappeared and the security situation in Europe has significantly improved.
ex.zh: 过去的直接威胁不复存在了，欧洲的安全状况有重大改善。

d: v. 消失，不见；失踪，丢失；不复存在，灭绝

e.en: The difference between two things is the way in which they are unlike each other.

ex.en: That is the fundamental difference between the two societies.
ex.zh: 那是两个社会之间的根本差别。

ex.en: ...the vast difference in size.
ex.zh: …在大小方面的巨大差别。

e.en: If people have their differences about something, they disagree about it.

ex.en: The two communities are learning how to resolve their differences.
ex.zh: 这两个团体正在学会如何消除它们之间的分歧。

e.en: A difference between two quantities is the amount by which one quantity is less than the other.

ex.en: The difference is 8532.

e.en: If something makes a difference or makes a lot of difference, it affects you and helps you in what you are doing. If something makes no difference, it does not have any effect on what you are doing. 有 (某程度的) 影响/

ex.en: Where you live can make such a difference to the way you feel.
ex.zh: 你居住的位置会对你的感觉产生很大的影响。

d: n. 差异，不同之处；差额；分歧
v.  区分

e.en: If someone or something discourages you, they cause you to lose your enthusiasm about your actions.

ex.en: It may be difficult to do at first. Don't let this discourage you.
ex.zh: 开始时做起来也许比较困难。不要让这个泄你的气。

e.en: 气馁的

ex.en: She was determined not to be too discouraged.
ex.zh: 她下了决心不要太气馁。

e.en: To discourage an action or to discourage someone from doing it means to make them not want to do it.

ex.en: ...typhoons that discouraged shopping and leisure activities.
ex.zh: …打消购物和休闲活动的念头的数起台风。

d: v. discourage 的第三人称单数现在时形式：使气馁，使灰心；劝阻，阻碍，使某人不再想做某事（常用于 discourage someone from doing something）。

e.en: A dispute is an argument or disagreement between people or groups.

ex.en: They have won previous pay disputes with the government.
ex.zh: 他们曾赢过前几起与政府的工资纠纷。

e.en: If you dispute a fact, statement, or theory, you say that it is incorrect or untrue.

ex.en: He disputed the allegations.
ex.zh: 他驳斥了这些无根据的指控。

ex.en: Nobody disputed that Davey was clever.
ex.zh: 没有人反驳戴维是聪明的。

e.en: When people dispute something, they fight for control or ownership of it. You can also say that one group of people dispute something with another group. 争夺 (控制权、所有权)

ex.en: Russia and Ukraine have been disputing the ownership of the fleet.
ex.zh: 俄罗斯和乌克兰一直在争夺该舰队的所有权。

e.en: If two or more people or groups are in dispute, they are arguing or disagreeing about something. (人或组织)

ex.en: The two countries are in dispute over the boundaries of their coastal waters.
ex.zh: 两国对它们沿海海域的边界是有争议的。

d: n. 争论，辩论，纠纷，争议（dispute 的复数）
v. 对……提出质疑，否认；争论，辩论；争夺，竞争（dispute 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you dodge, you move suddenly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

ex.en: I dodged back into the alley and waited a minute.
ex.zh: 我往后一闪，躲进胡同里等了一会儿。

e.en: If you dodge something, you avoid it by quickly moving aside or out of reach so that it cannot hit or reach you.

ex.en: He desperately dodged a speeding car trying to run him down.
ex.zh: 他拼命地闪身躲开一辆高速撞向自己的汽车。

e.en: If you dodge something, you deliberately avoid thinking about it or dealing with it, often by being deceitful.

ex.en: He boasts of dodging military service by feigning illness.
ex.zh: 他吹嘘说自己装病逃过了兵役。

e.en: Dodge is also a noun.

ex.en: This was not just a tax dodge.
ex.zh: 这不仅仅是逃税的问题。

d: n. 躲避，避开；逃避
v. 闪避，躲开；逃避；（冲洗或放大时）局部遮光（dodge 的现在分词）

e.en: Doesn't is the usual spoken form of "does not." (does not)

d: aux. 表示否定（等于 does not）
adv. 在本国，在国内；在家庭方面，在家庭生活中

e.en: You use double to indicate that something includes or is made of two things of the same kind.

ex.en: ...a pair of double doors into the room from the new entrance hall.
ex.zh: …一道从新门廊进入房间的双扇门。

e.en: You use double before a singular noun to refer to two things of the same type that occur together, or that are connected in some way.

ex.en: ...an extremely nasty double murder.
ex.zh: …一起极残忍的双人谋杀案。

e.en: You use double to describe something which is twice the normal size or can hold twice the normal quantity of something.

ex.en: ...a double helping of ice cream.
ex.zh: …双份冰激凌。

e.en: A double room is a room intended for two people, usually a couple, to stay or live in.

ex.en: ...bed and breakfast for $180 for two people in a double room.
ex.zh: …给两个人共用一个双人间的价格为$180的住宿加早餐。

d: adj. 两倍的，双的；供两人用的；双重的；（花）重瓣的；（多米诺骨牌）两边点数相同的；低八度的
adv. 两倍地
v. 加倍；对折；击出二垒安打；兼任；握紧；兼奏，重复（一个音符）
n. 两倍，两倍量；酷似的人；替身演员；卧室；双打；双料冠军；一杯双份的烈酒；（掷镖游戏中的）得双倍分的一掷；（掷骰子游戏中的）两骰子点数相同的一掷；（赛马中的）复式下注；（棒球比赛中的）二垒打

e.en: To downsize something such as a business or industry means to make it smaller.

ex.en: American manufacturing organizations have been downsizing their factories.
ex.zh: 美国制造商们一直在缩小他们工厂的规模。

ex.en: ...today's downsized economy.
ex.zh: … 今天萎缩了的经济。

e.en: 缩小规模

ex.en: ...a trend toward downsizing in the personal computer market.
ex.zh: …个人电脑市场规模缩小的趋势。

d: v. 裁减人员，裁员；缩小尺寸，缩减规模，减小规模；以较小尺寸设计

e.en: The driving force or idea behind something that happens or is done is the main thing that has a strong effect on it and makes it happen or be done in a particular way.

ex.en: Consumer spending was the driving force behind the economic growth in the summer.
ex.zh: 消费者支出是夏季经济增长背后的推动力。

d: adj. 推动的，强有力的；猛烈的，倾泻而下的
n. 驾驶，（某人的）驾车方式
v. 开车，驾驶；驾车送人；迫使，促使（drive 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If someone or something is dubbed a particular thing, they are given that description or name.

ex.en: Today's session has been widely dubbed as a "make or break" meeting.
ex.zh: 今天的会议被大众称为“不成则散”的会议。

e.en: If a film or soundtrack in a foreign language is dubbed, a new soundtrack is added with actors giving a translation. 为 (影片或声道等)

ex.en: It was dubbed into Spanish for Mexican audiences.
ex.zh: 它已为墨西哥观众配成西班牙语了。

e.en: to invest (a person) with knighthood by the ritual of tapping on the shoulder with a sword (用剑拍肩)
to contribute to the cost of (something); pay 结帐;

d: adj. 被称为…的，绰号为…的；译制的，配音的
v. dub 的过去式和过去分词：称…为，给…起绰号；授予…称号；封…为爵士；为（影片等）配音，译制；（俚语）支付，结账

e.en: Dysfunctional is used to describe relationships or behaviour which are different from what is considered to be normal. (关系或行为)

ex.en: ...the characteristics that typically occur in a dysfunctional family.
ex.zh: ...出现在关系异常家庭的典型特征。

d: adj. 机能失调的，功能障碍的；不正常的，异常的

e.en: An earner is someone or something that earns money or produces profit. 赚钱的人;

ex.en: ...a typical wage earner.
ex.zh: ...一个典型挣工资的人。

d: n. 赚钱的人，挣钱者；能带来收入或利润的事物（如业务、产品或行业）

e.en: food, esp in relation to its quality or taste

ex.en: this fruit makes excellent eating

e.en: relating to or suitable for eating, esp uncooked (生)食的; 可(生)

ex.en: eating pears

d: n. 吃，进食；食物（尤指就其品质、味道而言）
adj. 可（生）食的，供食用的；进餐用的，饮食的
v. 吃，进食，饮食（eat 的现在分词）

e.en: An economy is the system according to which the money, industry, and commerce of a country or region are organized.

ex.en: Zimbabwe boasts Africa's most industrialized economy.
ex.zh: 津巴布韦自夸有着非洲最为工业化的经济体制。

e.en: A country's economy is the wealth that it gets from business and industry.

ex.en: The Japanese economy grew at an annual rate of more than 10 percent.
ex.zh: 日本的经济以每年10%以上的速度增长。

e.en: Economy is the use of the minimum amount of money, time, or other resources needed to achieve something, so that nothing is wasted.

ex.en: ...improvements in the fuel economy of cars.
ex.zh: …在节省汽车燃料方面的一些改进。

e.en: Economy services such as travel are cheap and have no luxuries or extras. 经济的;

ex.en: ...the limitations that come with economy travel.
ex.zh: …伴随经济舱的一些限制。

d: n. 经济；节省，简练；经济舱
adj. 经济实惠的
【名】 （Economy）（英）伊科诺米（人名）

e.en: Economic means concerned with the organization of the money, industry, and trade of a country, region, or society.

ex.en: ...Poland's radical economic reforms.
ex.zh: …波兰激进的经济改革。

e.en: 经济地

ex.en: ...an economically depressed area.
ex.zh: …一个经济萧条地区。

e.en: If something is economic, it produces a profit.

ex.en: Critics say that the new system may be more economic but will lead to a decline in programme quality.
ex.zh: 批评家们说该新系统也许更有利可图，却会导致项目质量的下降。

d: adj. 经济的，经济学的；有利可图的；节约的

e.en: The different elements of something are the different parts it contains.

ex.en: The exchange of prisoners of war was one of the key elements of the UN's peace plan.
ex.zh: 交换战俘是联合国和平计划的主要内容之一。

e.en: A particular element of a situation, activity, or process is an important quality or feature that it has or needs. 要素;

ex.en: Physical fitness has now become an important element in our lives.
ex.zh: 身体健康现已成为我们生活中的重要元素。

e.en: When you talk about elements within a society or organization, you are referring to groups of people who have similar aims, beliefs, or habits. (具有相似目标、信仰或者习惯的) 群体;

ex.en: The government must weed out criminal elements from within the security forces.
ex.zh: 政府必须剔除保安队伍内部的犯罪分子。

e.en: If something has an element of a particular quality or emotion, it has a certain amount of this quality or emotion.

ex.en: These reports clearly contain elements of propaganda.
ex.zh: 这些报告明显带有宣传的成分。

d: n. 基本部分，要素；元素；有点，少量；一群人；恶劣天气（the elements）；基本原理；适宜的环境；电热元件，电热丝；（基督教圣餐中的）面包和酒
【名】 （Element）（英）埃利门特，（德）埃勒门特（人名）

e.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, usually by adding something to it. 充实;

ex.en: It is important to enrich the soil prior to planting.
ex.zh: 栽种之前给土壤施肥很重要。

e.en: To enrich someone means to increase the amount of money that they have.

ex.en: He will drain, rather than enrich, the country.
ex.zh: 他将耗尽而不是增加国家的财富。

d: adj. 丰富的，充实的；强化的（如强化食品）；浓缩的，富集的（如浓缩铀）
v. 使丰富，充实，改善；使富裕；使浓缩，使富集（enrich 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: In finance, your equity is the sum of your assets, for example the value of your house, once your debts have been subtracted from it.

ex.en: To capture his equity, Murphy must either sell or refinance.
ex.zh: 要获取他的资产净值，墨菲必须出售或重新融资。

d: n. 公平，公正；资产净值；普通股；衡平法

e.en: When you enter a place such as a room or building, you go into it or come into it.

ex.en: He entered the room briskly and stood near the door.
ex.zh: 他轻快地进入房间，靠近门站着。

ex.en: When Spinks entered they all turned to look at him.
ex.zh: 当斯平克斯进来的时候，他们都转过来看着他。

e.en: If you enter an organization or institution, you start to work there or become a member of it.

ex.en: He entered the firm as a junior associate.
ex.zh: 他作为一名初级职员进入了该公司。

e.en: If something new enters your mind, you suddenly think about it.

ex.en: Dreadful doubts began to enter my mind.
ex.zh: 可怕的疑虑开始突然出现在我的脑子里。

e.en: If it does not enter your head to do, think, or say something, you do not think of doing that thing although you should have.

ex.en: It never enters his mind that anyone is better than him.
ex.zh: 他从来没有想过有人比他更出色。

d: v. 进入；开始从事，开始做；参加，报名；登记，输入；正式提出；登场
n. 回车键
【名】 （Enter）（英）恩特（人名）

e.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

ex.en: Opposition demonstrators have erected barricades in roads leading to the parliament building.
ex.zh: 反对派示威者在通往议会大厦的路上设置了路障。

ex.en: The building was erected in 1900-1901.
ex.zh: 该建筑建于1900-1901年间。

e.en: If you erect a system, a theory, or an institution, you create it.

ex.en: Japanese proprietors are erecting a complex infrastructure of political influence throughout America.
ex.zh: 日本业主们正在全美国构建复杂的政治影响力网络。

e.en: People or things that are erect are straight and upright. 直立的;

ex.en: Stand reasonably erect, your arms hanging naturally.
ex.zh: 尽可能站直，双臂自然下垂。

d: v. 建造；竖立，搭起；创立（erect 的现在分词）
n. 建造，搭起

e.en: You use especially to emphasize that what you are saying applies more to one person, thing, time, or area than to any others. 特别是 (用于强调所指内容更适合)

ex.en: Millions of wild flowers colour the valleys, especially in April and May.
ex.zh: 成千上万的野花使峡谷五彩斑斓，特别是在四五月份。

e.en: You use especially to emphasize a characteristic or quality. 尤其 (用于强调某种特质)

ex.en: Babies lose heat much faster than adults, and are especially vulnerable to the cold in their first month.
ex.zh: 婴儿比成人散热快得多，在出生第一个月里尤其易受寒。

d: adv. 尤其，特别；专门，特地；在很大程度上，非常

e.en: You use extra to describe an amount, person, or thing that is added to others of the same kind, or that can be added to others of the same kind. 多加的;

ex.en: Police warned motorists to allow extra time to get to work.
ex.zh: 警察告诫开车上下班的人要留出富余时间。

ex.en: There's an extra blanket in the bottom drawer of the cupboard.
ex.zh: 衣橱的底柜有一条备用毯。

e.en: If something is extra, you have to pay more money for it in addition to what you are already paying for something. (费用)

ex.en: For foreign orders postage is extra.
ex.zh: 对于国外订单，邮资是另计的。

e.en: Extra is also a pronoun.

ex.en: She won't pay any extra.
ex.zh: 她不会支付任何额外费用。

e.en: Extra is also an adverb.

ex.en: You may be charged 10% extra for this service.
ex.zh: 你可能会因此项服务而被额外收取10%的费用。

d: adj. 额外的；另外收费的
n. 另收费的事物；临时演员；（非击球所得的）附加分；（报纸的）号外
adv. 额外；特别，格外

e.en: If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or do not succeed in doing it.

ex.en: The party failed to win the election.
ex.zh: 该政党未能赢得选举。

ex.en: He failed in his attempt to take control of the company.
ex.zh: 他的掌控这家公司的企图失败了。

e.en: If an activity, attempt, or plan fails, it is not successful.

ex.en: We tried to develop plans for them to get along, which all failed miserably.
ex.zh: 我们设法制定出让他们相处融洽的计划，但都惨败了。

ex.en: He was afraid the revolution they had started would fail.
ex.zh: 他担心他们发起的革命会失败。

e.en: If someone or something fails to do a particular thing that they should have done, they do not do it.

ex.en: Some schools fail to require any homework.
ex.zh: 有些学校没有布置任何家庭作业。

ex.en: He failed to file tax returns for 1982.
ex.zh: 他没有填报1982年的纳税申报单。

e.en: If something fails, it stops working properly, or does not do what it is supposed to do.

ex.en: The lights mysteriously failed, and we stumbled around in complete darkness.
ex.zh: 灯神秘地熄灭了，我们在完全的黑暗中跌跌撞撞。

d: adj. 失败的；难以为继的；有故障的
v. 失败；未能做到，未能做；辜负，使失望（fail 的过去式和过去分词形式）
adj. 更公平，更公正，更合理（fair 的比较级）；（肤色、发色）更白皙，更浅淡

e.en: Fashion is the area of activity that involves styles of clothing and appearance.

ex.en: There are 20 full-colour pages of fashion for men.
ex.zh: 有20张男士时尚动态的全彩页。

e.en: A fashion is a style of clothing or a way of behaving that is popular at a particular time.

ex.en: In the early seventies I wore false eyelashes, as was the fashion.
ex.zh: 70年代初我戴假睫毛，那是当时的时尚。

ex.en: The demand for perfume resulted in a fashion for fancy scent bottles.
ex.zh: 对香水的需求使别致的香水瓶成为一种时尚。

e.en: If you do something in a particular fashion or after a particular fashion, you do it in that way.

ex.en: There is another drug called DHE that works in a similar fashion.
ex.zh: 另有一种叫作二氢埃托啡的药作用相似。

e.en: If something is in fashion, it is popular and approved of at a particular time. If it is out of fashion, it is not popular or approved of. 流行/

ex.en: That sort of house is back in fashion.
ex.zh: 那种房子又时兴起来了。

d: n. 时髦打扮，流行装扮；时尚，时兴；（做事的）方式；时装领域，时尚界
v. （尤指用手工）制作，使成形；塑造

e.en: Failure is a lack of success in doing or achieving something, especially in relation to a particular activity.

ex.en: This policy is doomed to failure.
ex.zh: 这项政策注定要失败。

ex.en: Three attempts on the 200-metre record ended in failure.
ex.zh: 3次向200米纪录的冲击以失败告终。

e.en: Your failure to do a particular thing is the fact that you do not do it, even though you were expected to do it.

ex.en: They see their failure to produce an heir as a curse from God.
ex.zh: 他们将自己未能生育一个后嗣看作是来自上帝的一个诅咒。

e.en: If something is a failure, it is not a success.

ex.en: The marriage was a failure and they both wanted to be free of it.
ex.zh: 这段婚姻是个失败，他们俩都想从中解放出来。

e.en: If you say that someone is a failure, you mean that they have not succeeded in a particular activity, or that they are unsuccessful at everything they do.

ex.en: Elgar received many honours and much acclaim and yet he often considered himself a failure.
ex.zh: 埃尔加获得了很多荣誉和欢呼，但是他常常把自己看成一个失败者。

d: n. 失败（failure 的复数）；（技术）故障，失效，失灵；（医学）衰竭；（商业、金融）倒闭，破产

e.en: You use him to refer to a man, boy, or male animal. 他; 它 (指雄性动物)

ex.en: John's aunt died suddenly and left him a surprisingly large sum.
ex.zh: 约翰的姑妈突然去世,给他留下一笔令人意想不到的巨款。

ex.en: Is Sam there? Let me talk to him.
ex.zh: 萨姆在吗？让我和他谈谈。

e.en: In written English, him is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use "him or her" or "them." 他 (书面英语中泛指人)

ex.en: If the child encounters "hear," we should show him that this is the base word in "hearing" and "hears."
ex.zh: 如果孩子遇到这个单词，我们应该向他说明这个词是和的词根。

d: pron. 他（宾格）；它（指雄性动物）；（书面英语）用于泛指不限定性别的人

e.en: A star is a large ball of burning gas in space. Stars appear to us as small points of light in the sky on clear nights.

ex.en: The nights were pure with cold air and lit with stars.
ex.zh: 那些夜晚十分清静，空气清凉、繁星点点。

e.en: You can refer to a shape or an object as a star when it has four, five, or more points sticking out of it in a regular pattern. 星形;

ex.en: Children at school receive coloured stars for work well done.
ex.zh: 上学的孩子们表现好会得到彩星。

e.en: You can say how many stars something such as a hotel or restaurant has as a way of talking about its quality, which is often indicated by a number of star-shaped symbols. The more stars something has, the better it is. (宾馆或饭店等的)

ex.en: ...five star hotels.
ex.zh: …五星级酒店。

e.en: Famous actors, musicians, and sports players are often referred to as stars.

ex.en: ...star of the TV series Scrubs.
ex.zh: …电视连续剧《实习医生风云》里的明星。

ex.en: By now Murphy is Hollywood's top male comedy star.
ex.zh: 现在墨菲已是好莱坞顶级男喜剧明星。

d: n. 星，恒星；演艺界明星，体坛名将；（电影、戏剧中的）主角，主演；重要人物，优秀人士；星状，星形物；星号；（饭店、宾馆等的）星级标志；（占星术的）星相，星座（stars）；一定会发生；好心的人，乐于助人者；星章；Y形三相电绕组；星状网；用于海星或类似的棘皮动物的名字中
v. 主演，使主演；给……加上星号；表现杰出；用星形物装饰（或覆盖）
adj. 最好的，最出色的
【名】 （Star）（瑞典）斯塔尔，（德）施塔尔（人名）

e.en: An actor is someone whose job is acting in plays or films. "Actor" in the singular usually refers to a man, but some women who act prefer to be called "actors" rather than "actresses."

ex.en: His father was an actor in the Cantonese Opera Company.
ex.zh: 他父亲曾是粤剧团的一名演员。

d: n. 演员；像在演戏的人；（行动或过程）参与者
n. 帕特里克（男子名）；圣帕特里克（Saint Patrick，爱尔兰主保圣人，5 世纪到爱尔兰传教的基督教传教士）

e.en: If you trek somewhere, you go on a journey across difficult country, usually on foot. (艰难地)

ex.en: ...trekking through the jungles.
ex.zh: …徒步穿越丛林。

e.en: Trek is also a noun.

ex.en: He is on a trek through the South Gobi desert.
ex.zh: 他正徒步穿越南戈壁沙漠。

e.en: If you trek somewhere, you go there heavily and unwillingly, usually because you are tired.

ex.en: They trekked from shop to shop in search of white knee-high socks.
ex.zh: 他们疲惫地奔波于一家又一家商店，寻找高到膝盖的白色长筒袜。

d: v. （尤指徒步）长途跋涉；（尤指在山中）远足，徒步旅行；缓慢行走，没精打采地走；不断旅行，过流浪生活；（牛）拉车，驮运；用围网捕鱼；（随装载自己财物的牛车）迁移，旅行
n. （显得很漫长的）一段路程；（尤指徒步的）长途艰苦旅行；大迁徙（the Trek）；一网鱼；财产，所有物
【名】 （Trek）（俄、美）特里克（人名）

e.en: A bit of something is a small amount of it.

ex.en: All it required was a bit of work.
ex.zh: 它所需要的只是少量工作。

e.en: A bit means to a small extent or degree. It is sometimes used to make a statement less extreme.

ex.en: This girl was a bit strange.
ex.zh: 这个女孩有点儿古怪。

ex.en: I think people feel a bit more confident.
ex.zh: 我认为人们感觉更自信一点儿了。

e.en: You can use a bit of to make a statement less forceful. For example, the statement "It's a bit of a nuisance" is less forceful than "It's a nuisance." 有点儿 (用于使陈述不那么强烈)

ex.en: It's all a bit of a mess.
ex.zh: 它整个有点儿乱。

ex.en: Students have always been portrayed as a bit of a joke.
ex.zh: 学生们总是被描述得有些荒唐可笑。

e.en: Quite a bit means quite a lot.

ex.en: They're worth quite a bit of money.
ex.zh: 它们值很多钱。

ex.en: Things have changed quite a bit.
ex.zh: 情况大有改观。

d: n. 小片，小块；小部分，片段；（一组东西中的）一个；喜剧小品，小笑话；比特；辅币，12.5美分；马嚼子；钻头；（与某活动、过程有关的）所有事情；女孩，姑娘；（人的）生殖器
adj. 很小的
v. 制约，限制；给（马）上嚼子
v. 咬，咬伤；叮，蜇（bite 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: I'd is the usual spoken form of "I had," especially when "had" is an auxiliary verb. (I had)的常用口语形式，尤其是当(had)

ex.en: I felt absolutely certain that I'd seen her before.
ex.zh: 我确信自己以前曾见过她。

e.en: I'd is the usual spoken form of "I would." (I would)

ex.en: There are some questions I'd like to ask.
ex.zh: 有些问题我想问问。

d: abbr. 我愿意（等于 I would）

e.en: You can use really to emphasize a statement. 的确 (用于强调)

ex.en: I'm very sorry. I really am.
ex.zh: 我很抱歉。真的。

e.en: You can use really to emphasize an adjective or adverb. (用于强调形容词或副词)

ex.en: It was really good.
ex.zh: 这非常好。

e.en: You use really when you are discussing the real facts about something, in contrast to the ones someone wants you to believe.

ex.en: My father didn't really love her.
ex.zh: 我父亲实际上并不爱她。

e.en: People use really in questions and negative statements when they want you to answer "no." 果真 (用在疑问句和否定句中，引出否定回答)

ex.en: Do you really think he would be that stupid?
ex.zh: 你果真认为他那么蠢吗？

d: adv. 真正地，事实上；确实的，的确（用于加强语气）；很，十分；（用于带有隐含的否定回答的疑问句和感叹句）真的，是吗；用于缓和否定语气
int. 真的（用来表示兴趣、惊奇或疑惑）；真是的！（用于表示生气或不赞成）；是啊！（用于表示同意某人的意见）

e.en: A career is the job or profession that someone does for a long period of their life.

ex.en: She is now concentrating on a career as a fashion designer.
ex.zh: 她现在专注于时装设计这一行。

ex.en: ...a career in journalism.
ex.zh: …新闻职业。

e.en: Your career is the part of your life that you spend working.

ex.en: During his career, he wrote more than fifty plays.
ex.zh: 在他的创作生涯里，他共写了五十多部剧作。

e.en: Career advice or guidance consists of information about different jobs and help with deciding what kind of job you want to do.

ex.en: She received very little career guidance when young.
ex.zh: 她年轻时没受过什么就业指导。

e.en: If a person or vehicle careers somewhere, they move fast and in an uncontrolled way.

ex.en: His car careered into a river.
ex.zh: 他的车猛地冲进了河里。

d: n. 职业，事业；职业生涯；速度，行程
adj. 就业的，职业的；终身从事的
v. 猛冲

e.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

ex.en: Happiness was an emotion that Jerry was having to relearn.
ex.zh: 幸福是一种杰瑞当时不得不再学习的感情。

e.en: Emotion is the part of a person's character that consists of their feelings, as opposed to their thoughts. (与思想相对的)

ex.en: ...the split between reason and emotion.
ex.zh: …理智与情感间的分离。

d: n. 情感，情绪（emotion 的复数）

e.en: Didn't is the usual spoken form of "did not." (did not)

d: aux. did not 的缩略形式（一般过去时否定助动词，后接动词原形）

e.en: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

ex.en: I looked down the hallway to room number nine.
ex.zh: 我沿着走廊向9号房间看过去。

ex.en: If you look, you'll see what was a lake.
ex.zh: 如果你看一下，就会看到那个曾经是湖的地方。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: Lucille took a last look in the mirror.
ex.zh: 露西尔往镜子里看了最后一眼。

e.en: If you look at a book, newspaper, or magazine, you read it fairly quickly or read part of it.

ex.en: You've just got to look at the last bit of Act Three.
ex.zh: 你只须浏览一下第三幕最后一小段。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: A quick look at Monday's newspapers shows that there's plenty of interest in foreign news.
ex.zh: 快速浏览一下星期一的报纸，就会发现许多有趣的国外新闻。

d: v. 看；寻找；与……外表相似；看似，显得；注意；面向；检查，查看；打算（look to）；预料，期待；浏览；研究，考虑；看待（look at/on）；（用于唤起他人注意）瞧；看上去精神好（look oneself）；四处看看（look round/around）；调查（look into）
n. 看；寻找，搜索；表情，神色；景象，样子；容貌（looks）；风格，样式；察看，考虑
【名】 （Look）（瑞典）洛克，（英）卢克（人名）

e.en: Something that is difficult is not easy to do, understand, or deal with.

ex.en: The lack of childcare provisions made it difficult for single mothers to get jobs.
ex.zh: 儿童保育服务的缺乏使得单身妈妈们很难找到工作。

ex.en: It was a very difficult decision to make.
ex.zh: 这是个非常难作的决定。

e.en: Someone who is difficult behaves in an unreasonable and unhelpful way.

ex.en: I had a feeling you were going to be difficult about this.
ex.zh: 我有种感觉，在这件事情上你将很难对付。

d: adj. 困难的，费力的；不友好的，难对付的

e.en: Your demeanour is the way you behave, which gives people an impression of your character and feelings. 行为;

ex.en: ...her calm and cheerful demeanour.
ex.zh: …她那冷静乐观的态度。

d: n. 行为，举止，态度

e.en: Early means before the usual time that a particular event or activity happens.

ex.en: I knew I had to get up early.
ex.zh: 我知道我得早起。

e.en: Early is also an adjective.

ex.en: I decided that I was going to take early retirement.
ex.zh: 我决定了我将提早退休。

e.en: Early means near the beginning of a day, week, year, or other period of time.

ex.en: ...in the 1970s and the early 1980s.
ex.zh: …在20世纪70年代和20世纪80年代初期。

ex.en: She was in her early teens.
ex.zh: 她有十三四岁了。

e.en: Early is also an adverb.

ex.en: We'll hope to see you some time early next week.
ex.zh: 我们希望在下周初的某个时候见你。

d: adj. 早期的，初期的；提早的，提前的；早开花的，早熟的
adv. 在早期，在初期；提早，提前
【名】 （Early）（英）厄尔利（人名）

e.en: A cockney is a person who was born in the East End of London.

ex.en: ...a Cockney cab driver.
ex.zh: ...一个开出租车的伦敦东区人。

e.en: Cockney is the dialect and accent of the East End of London.

ex.en: The man spoke with a Cockney accent.
ex.zh: 这个男人讲话带着伦敦东区口音。

d: n. 伦敦东区人，伦敦人，伦敦佬；伦敦东区方言，伦敦腔
adj. 伦敦东区人的；伦敦东区方言的

e.en: A person's childhood is the period of their life when they are a child.

ex.en: She had a happy childhood.
ex.zh: 她有过一个快乐的童年。

ex.en: He was remembering a story heard in childhood.
ex.zh: 他一直记着童年时听过的一个故事。

d: n.  童年，幼年时代

e.en: You can refer to information as data, especially when it is in the form of facts or statistics that you can analyse.

ex.en: The study was based on data from 2,100 women.
ex.zh: 此项研究以从2100位女性身上获得的资料为依据。

e.en: Data is information that can be stored and used by a computer program.

ex.en: This system uses powerful microchips to compress huge amounts of data onto a CD-ROM.
ex.zh: 这一系统使用功能强大的微芯片来把大量数据压缩到CD-ROM上。

d: n. 数据，资料；（储存在计算机中的）数据资料
【名】 （Data）（日）驮太，（印、葡）达塔（人名）

e.en: You refer to an activity or situation as fun if you think it is pleasant and enjoyable and it causes you to feel happy.

ex.en: It's been a learning adventure and it's also been great fun.
ex.zh: 那是一次很受教育的冒险活动，也是极大的乐趣。

ex.en: It could be fun to watch them.
ex.zh: 看他们会是乐趣。

e.en: If you say that someone is fun, you mean that you enjoy being with them because they say and do interesting or amusing things.

ex.en: Liz was fun to be with.
ex.zh: 莉兹是与之相处有趣的人。

e.en: If you describe something as a fun thing, you mean that you think it is enjoyable. If you describe someone as a fun person, you mean that you enjoy being with them.

ex.en: It was a fun evening.
ex.zh: 那是个令人愉快的夜晚。

e.en: If you do something for fun or for the fun of it, you do it in order to enjoy yourself rather than because it is important or necessary.

ex.en: We used to drive too fast, just for fun.
ex.zh: 我们过去常常开得太快，就为了好玩。

d: n. 乐趣，享受；嬉戏，玩笑
adj. 有趣的，令人愉快的
v.  开玩笑，取笑

e.en: Gave is the past tense of . (give)

d: v. 给予（give 的过去式）
n. （Gave）人名；（塞内）加韦；（法）加夫

e.en: A friend is someone who you know well and like, but who is not related to you.

ex.en: I had a long talk about this with my best friend.
ex.zh: 我和我最好的朋友就此进行了长谈。

ex.en: She never was a close friend of mine.
ex.zh: 她从来就不是我的密友。

e.en: If one country refers to another as a friend, they mean that the other country is not an enemy of theirs.

ex.en: The president said that Japan is now a friend and international partner.
ex.zh: 总统说日本现在是盟国和国际伙伴。

e.en: If you are friends with someone, you are their friend and they are yours. (与…是)

ex.en: I still wanted to be friends with Alison.
ex.zh: 我仍然希望同艾莉森做朋友。

ex.en: We remained good friends.
ex.zh: 我们一直是好朋友。

e.en: The friends of a country, cause, organization, or a famous politician are the people and organizations who help and support them.

ex.en: ...the friends of Israel.
ex.zh: …以色列的支持者。

d: n. 朋友，友人（friend 的复数）

e.en: the part of the bows of a ship that are furthest forward at the level of the main deck

d: n. 眼睛（eye 的复数）；看法，判断（用于 in someone's eyes 等短语）；（航海）船首，船头；（Eyes）人名（英译“艾斯”）
v. （动词 eye 的第三人称单数）注视，打量，观察
n. 哈德斯菲尔德（位于英国西约克郡）

e.en: I'm is the usual spoken form of "I am." (I am)

ex.en: I'm sorry.
ex.zh: 我很抱歉。

d: abbr. I am 的缩略式（通常译作“我是”）

e.en: A learned person has gained a lot of knowledge by studying.

ex.en: He is a scholar, a genuinely learned man.
ex.zh: 他是个学者，一个真正博学的人。

d: adj. 博学的；学术性的，学者的；后天的，习得的
v. 学习，学会；得知，获悉；背熟，熟记；认识到，（从……）吸取教训 （learn 的过去式和过去分词）
【名】 （Learned）（美）勒尼德（人名）

e.en: A scene in a play, movie, or book is part of it in which a series of events happen in the same place. 场面;

ex.en: ...the opening scene of "A Christmas Carol."
ex.zh: …《圣诞颂歌》的开场。

ex.en: ...Act I, scene 1.
ex.zh: …第1幕，第1场。

e.en: You refer to a place as a scene when you are describing its appearance and indicating what impression it makes on you.

ex.en: It's a scene of complete devastation.
ex.zh: 那是一幅满目疮痍的景象。

ex.en: Thick black smoke billowed over the scene.
ex.zh: 黑色的浓烟从现场滚滚升起。

e.en: You can describe an event that you see, or that is broadcast or shown in a picture, as a scene of a particular kind. 场面;

ex.en: There were emotional scenes as the refugees enjoyed their first breath of freedom.
ex.zh: 难民们享受第一口自由的呼吸时，有一些感人至深的场面。

ex.en: Television broadcasters were warned to exercise caution over depicting scenes of violence.
ex.zh: 电视台受到警告，在描述暴力场面时要采取谨慎态度。

e.en: The scene of an event is the place where it happened.

ex.en: The area has been the scene of fierce fighting for three months.
ex.zh: 这个地区是3个月来激烈战斗的现场。

ex.en: ...traces left at the scene of a crime.
ex.zh: …在犯罪现场留下的痕迹。

d: n. 事发地，现场；事件，场面；（戏剧、书、电影等的）片段，情节；（戏剧的）一场；（戏剧）布景；活动领域，圈子；（某地方或图画中的）景色，景象；（当众）发脾气，吵闹；同性恋者常去的社交场所

e.en: If you have a role in a situation or in society, you have a particular position and function in it. 功能;

ex.en: Until now scientists had very little clear evidence about the drug's role in preventing more serious effects of infection.
ex.zh: 到目前为止，科学家们几乎没有该药物在防止更严重的感染后果的功能的明确证据。

e.en: A role is one of the characters that an actor or singer can play in a movie, play, or opera.

ex.en: She has just landed the lead role in their latest production.
ex.zh: 她刚在他们最新的作品中取得了主角。

d: n. （演员的）角色；作用，职责
【名】 （Role）（意、塞、赤几）罗莱（人名）

e.en: of, relating to, or characteristic of Shakespeare or his works
a student of or specialist in Shakespeare's works
e.zh: 莎士比亚作品的学生或专家

d: adj. 莎士比亚的；莎士比亚似的；莎士比亚风格的
n. 莎士比亚研究家；莎士比亚的崇拜者
n. 托特纳姆（英国伦敦北部哈林盖区的一个地区）；足球语境中又指英格兰足球俱乐部托特纳姆热刺（Tottenham Hotspur），中文常简称“热刺”

e.en: Absolute means total and complete.

ex.en: It's not really suited to absolute beginners.
ex.zh: 这对于纯粹的初学者们不太适合。

e.en: You use absolute to emphasize something that you are saying.

ex.en: About 12 inches wide is the absolute minimum you should consider.
ex.zh: 12英寸左右的宽度是你应该考虑的绝对最小尺寸。

e.en: An absolute ruler has complete power and authority over his or her country.

ex.en: He ruled with absolute power.
ex.zh: 他实行独裁统治。

e.en: Absolute is used to say that something is definite and will not change even if circumstances change.

ex.en: John brought the absolute proof that we needed.
ex.zh: 约翰拿出了我们需要的确凿证据。

d: adj. 完全的，纯粹的；绝对的，无疑的；十足的；不受任何限制的，专制独裁的；（结构）独立的
n. 绝对真理，绝对原则

e.en: A writer is a person who writes books, stories, or articles as a job.

ex.en: Turner is a writer and critic.
ex.zh: 特纳是一位作家和评论家。

ex.en: ...detective stories by American writers.
ex.zh: …美国作家们的那些侦探故事。

e.en: The writer of a particular article, report, letter, or story is the person who wrote it.

ex.en: No one is to see the document without the permission of the writer of the report.
ex.zh: 任何人没有报告撰写者的允许不得看这份文件。

d: n. （职业的）作家，作者；执笔者，撰写人（writer 的复数）

e.en: Someone who speaks with a particular accent pronounces the words of a language in a distinctive way that shows which country, region, or background they come from.

ex.en: He had developed a slight southern accent.
ex.zh: 他有了一点南方口音。

e.en: An accent is a short line or other mark which is written above certain letters in some languages and which indicates the way those letters are pronounced.

ex.en: ...an acute accent.
ex.zh: …一个尖音符。

d: n. 口音，腔调，土音；着重点，强调；重音；（字母上的）读音符号；点缀，特色
v. 强调，突出；重读；以重音演奏

e.en: You use actually to indicate that a situation exists or happened, or to emphasize that it is true. 实际上 (指某种情形真实存在)

ex.en: One afternoon, I got bored and actually fell asleep for a few minutes.
ex.zh: 一天下午，我感到很无聊，实际上有几分钟还睡着了。

e.en: You use actually when you are correcting or contradicting someone. 事实上 (用于纠正或反驳他人)

ex.en: No, I'm not a student. I'm a doctor, actually.
ex.zh: 不，我不是一名学生。事实上，我是一名医生。

e.en: You can use actually when you are politely expressing an opinion that other people might not have expected from you. (用于礼貌地表达观点)

ex.en: "Do you think it's a good idea to socialize with one's patients?"—"Actually, I do, I think it's a great idea."
ex.zh: “你觉得和病人交往是个好主意吗？”——“说实话，我觉得是，我觉得这是一个非常好的主意。”

e.en: You use actually to introduce a new topic into a conversation. (用于开始新话题)

ex.en: Well actually, John, I called you for some advice.
ex.zh: 嗯，约翰，其实我打电话给你是寻求一些建议。

d: adv. 实际上，事实上；（用于开始新话题）其实；竟然，居然

e.en: In science fiction books and films, an android is a robot that looks like a human being.

d: n. （尤指科幻作品中的）人形机器人，机器人；安卓，安卓系统（Google 开发的移动操作系统，通常写作 Android）

e.en: An arsenal is a large collection of weapons and military equipment held by a country, group, or person.

ex.en: Russia is committed to destroying most of its nuclear arsenals.
ex.zh: 俄国承诺销毁其大部分核武器。

e.en: An arsenal is a building where weapons and military equipment are stored.

d: n. 兵工厂；军械库，军火库；武库，武器储备（国家、集团或个人拥有或储备的大批武器和军用设备，常构成 nuclear arsenal 核武库）；比喻可用于某目的的大量资源（如设备、方法等），宝库，珍藏；阿森纳（Arsenal Football Club，英格兰职业足球俱乐部）

e.en: An award is a prize or certificate that a person is given for doing something well.

ex.en: The Institute's annual award is presented to organizations that are dedicated to democracy and human rights.
ex.zh: 该协会的年度奖授予致力于民主与人权的组织。

e.en: In law, an award is a sum of money that a court decides should be given to someone. (赔偿金等的)

ex.en: ...worker's compensation awards.
ex.zh: …工人的赔偿金裁定额。

e.en: If someone is awarded something such as a prize or an examination mark, it is given to them.

ex.en: She was awarded the prize for both films.
ex.zh: 她因这两部电影而获奖。

e.en: To award something to someone means to decide that it will be given to that person.

ex.en: We have awarded the contract to a New York-based company.
ex.zh: 我们已经把这份合同给了一家总部设在纽约的公司。

d: n. 奖，奖品；（收入的）增加；（赔偿）裁定额；（毕业证书等的）授予；奖学金
v. 授予，颁发；判给，裁定
【名】 （Award）（美）艾华尔德（人名）

e.en: Your background is the kind of family you come from and the kind of education you have had. It can also refer to such things as your social and racial origins, your financial status, or the type of work experience that you have. (家庭、职业)

ex.en: The Warners were from a Jewish working-class background.
ex.zh: 沃纳一家人是犹太工人阶级出身。

e.en: The background to an event or situation consists of the facts that explain what caused it.

ex.en: The background to the current troubles is provided by the dire state of the country's economy.
ex.zh: 目前这些问题的背景是严峻的国家经济形势。

ex.en: The meeting takes place against a background of continuing political violence.
ex.zh: 这次会议是在持续的政治暴力背景下召开的。

e.en: The background is sounds, such as music, that you can hear but that you are not listening to with your full attention.

ex.en: I kept hearing the sound of applause in the background.
ex.zh: 我不断听到背景音中有掌声。

e.en: You can use background to refer to the things in a picture or scene that are less noticeable or important than the main things or people in it. (图画、布景等的)

ex.en: ...roses patterned on a blue background.
ex.zh: …印在蓝色背景上的玫瑰。

d: n. 背景；背景图片；出身、经历、社会背景等（background 的复数形式）
v. 作……的背景，以……为背景衬托（background 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you beat someone or something, you hit them very hard.

ex.en: My wife tried to stop them and they beat her.
ex.zh: 我妻子试图阻止他们，他们就猛打她。

e.en: To beat on, at, or against something means to hit it hard, usually several times or continuously for a period of time. (常指多次或连续地)

ex.en: There was dead silence but for a fly beating against the glass.
ex.zh: 若没有一只苍蝇在扑打着玻璃，便是一片死寂。

ex.en: Nina managed to free herself and began beating at the flames with a pillow.
ex.zh: 尼娜设法自救，开始用一个枕头连续地拍打着火焰。

e.en: Beat is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the rhythmic beat of the surf.
ex.zh: …海浪有韵律的拍击。

e.en: 敲打

ex.en: The silence was broken only by the beating of the rain.
ex.zh: 唯有雨的敲击打破了宁静。

d: v. （反复地）敲，击，打；狠打，猛抽；搅拌，混合；拍动，扇动（翅膀）；（心脏）跳动，搏动；击败，战胜；抢……之先，赶在……之前；避开，避免
n. 敲，击；（音乐或诗歌的）强音拍；（经常去或经过的）路线，地点；以之字形航线抢风航行
adj. 筋疲力尽，疲惫不堪；垮掉的一代的
【名】 （Beat）贝亚特（人名）

e.en: Became is the past tense of . (become)

d: v. 成为，变得（become 的过去式）

e.en: Best is the superlative of good.

ex.en: If you want further information the best thing to do is have a word with the driver as you get on the bus.
ex.zh: 如果你想了解得更清楚，最好的办法就是上公共汽车后向司机询问。

e.en: Best is the superlative of well.

ex.en: James Fox is best known as the author of "White Mischief," and he is currently working on a new book.
ex.zh: 詹姆斯·福克斯以其作品《欲望城》最为知名，目前他正在写一本新书。

e.en: The best is used to refer to things of the highest quality or standard.

ex.en: We offer only the best to our clients.
ex.zh: 我们只提供最好的东西给顾客。

e.en: Someone's best is the greatest effort or highest achievement or standard that they are capable of. 最佳状态;

ex.en: Miss Blockey was at her best when she played the piano.
ex.zh: 布洛基小姐弹钢琴那会儿正处于最佳状态。

d: adj. 最好的，最出色的；最愉快的，最幸福的；最合适的，最恰当的
adv. 最，最高程度地；最出色地，最高标准地；最适合地，最恰当地
n. 最好的事物（或人）；（人或事物所能达到的）最高标准；最合乎要求的事物；（个人的）最高水平，最高纪录；最好的衣服，盛装；（书信结尾的）良好祝愿
v. 打败，胜过
n. （英国英语，非正式）男人，家伙，小子

e.en: Blew is the past tense of blow. (blow)

d: v. 动词 blow 的过去式，表示吹、刮、吹响、（被）吹动等动作在过去发生。

e.en: Boots are shoes that cover your whole foot and the lower part of your leg.

ex.en: He sat in a kitchen chair, reached down and pulled off his boots.
ex.zh: 他坐在厨房的椅子上，弯腰脱掉了靴子。

e.en: Boots are strong, heavy shoes that cover your ankle and that have thick soles. You wear them to protect your feet, for example, when you are walking or taking part in sports. (步行或运动时穿的)

ex.en: The soldiers' boots resounded in the street.
ex.zh: 士兵们的厚底靴在街道上发出回响。

e.en: a kick

ex.en: he gave the door a boot

e.en: (esp in football) to kick (尤指足球中)

d: n. 靴子；猛踢；（汽车的）行李箱，后备箱；车轮固定夹；解雇；再者，除此之外（to boot）
v. 猛踢；锁住（非法停车的轮子）；启动（电脑）；在车轮上装制动装置；解雇；（使）穿靴
【名】 （Boot）（英、美、荷、加、德、意、俄）布特（人名）

e.en: (formerly) a shoeblack who cleans the guests' shoes in a hotel (旧时在酒店为客人)

d: n. 靴子（boot 的复数）；（英，旧时）擦靴的仆役
v. boot 的第三人称单数形式：踢；启动（计算机）

e.en: Brought is the past tense and past participle of . (bring)

d: v. 带来（bring 的过去分词）

e.en: having been cheated in a sale of drugs （

d: adj. 烧焦的；（在毒品买卖中）被骗了
v. 烧伤（burn 的过去式和过去分词）；一方斗舞失败

e.en: Can't is the usual spoken form of "cannot." (cannot)

d: contr. 不能（can not）

e.en: In the army, navy, and some other armed forces, a captain is an officer of middle rank. (陆军、海军及其他军种的)

ex.en: ...Captain Mark Phillips.
ex.zh: …马克·菲利普斯上尉。

ex.en: ...a captain in the army.
ex.zh: …一名陆军上尉。

e.en: The captain of a sports team is the player in charge of it. (体育运动队)

ex.en: ...Mickey Thomas, the captain of the tennis team.
ex.zh: …米奇·托马斯，这支网球队的队长。

e.en: The captain of a ship is the sailor in charge of it.

ex.en: ...the captain of an excursion boat.
ex.zh: …一艘游船的船长。

e.en: The captain of an aeroplane is the pilot in charge of it.

d: n. 队长，首领；上尉，上校；船长，机长；警局副官，消防署中队长
v. 率队，指挥

e.en: The cast of a play or film is all the people who act in it.

ex.en: The show is very amusing and the cast is very good.
ex.zh: 表演非常有趣，演员都很优秀。

e.en: To cast an actor in a play or film means to choose them to act a particular role in it.

ex.en: The world premiere of Harold Pinter's new play casts Ian Holm in the lead role.
ex.zh: 哈罗德·品特新戏的首次全球公演选择伊恩·霍姆扮演主要角色。

ex.en: He was cast as a college professor.
ex.zh: 他被选扮演大学教授这个角色。

e.en: If you cast your eyes or cast a look in a particular direction, you look quickly in that direction.

ex.en: He cast a stern glance at the two men.
ex.zh: 他严厉地瞪了那两名男子一眼。

ex.en: I cast my eyes down briefly.
ex.zh: 我往下瞅了瞅。

e.en: If something casts a light or shadow somewhere, it causes it to appear there.

ex.en: The moon cast a bright light over the garden.
ex.zh: 月亮在院子里撒下清辉。

d: v. 投射（光，影）；将（视线，目光）投向；浇铸，铸造；分配角色；扔，掷，抛；描述，描写；投票；使人怀疑；使（魔咒）生效，施法；抛（钓丝），撒（网）；（生长过程中）蜕（皮），脱（角）；（马）失（蹄铁）；用（星相）占卜；（乡村舞蹈中的）转向；（猎）（狗）四处探寻失踪的嗅迹；放开（猎狗）以探寻嗅迹；用绳子绊倒（动物，尤指母牛）
n. 演员阵容；铸型，模型；（固定断骨用的）石膏； 特性，外貌；（眼睛）斜视；掷，投，抛；浅淡的色调；（猎狗）探寻嗅迹；（蚯蚓钻洞时拱到地面的）小土堆；（鹰或猫头鹰的）颗粒状呕吐物；一群鹰，隼
【名】 （Cast）（法）卡斯特（人名）

e.en: The character of a person or place consists of all the qualities they have that make them distinct from other people or places. 性格;

ex.en: Perhaps there is a negative side to his character that you haven't seen yet.
ex.zh: 或许他性格中有你还未看到的消极一面。

e.en: You use character to say what kind of person someone is. For example, if you say that someone is a strange character, you mean they are strange. (具有某种特性的)

ex.en: It's that kind of courage and determination that makes him such a remarkable character.
ex.zh: 正是那种勇气和决心使他成为这样卓越的人。

e.en: The characters in a film, book, or play are the people that it is about. (电影、书、戏剧中的)

ex.en: The film is autobiographical and the central character is played by Collard himself.
ex.zh: 这部影片是自传式的，主角由科勒德亲自扮演。

e.en: A character is a letter, number, or other symbol that is written or printed.

ex.en: ...a shopping list written in Chinese characters.
ex.zh: …用汉字写的一张购物单。

d: n. 性格，品质；特色，特征；人物，角色；勇气，毅力；某种人，古怪有趣的人；（书写或印刷）符号，文字，字体；名誉，名声
v. 刻，写；描述；使具有特征
【名】 （Character）（英）克拉克特（人名）

e.en: A club is an organization of people interested in a particular activity or subject who usually meet on a regular basis.

ex.en: ...the Young Republicans Club.
ex.zh: … 青年共和党会社。

ex.en: ...a youth club.
ex.zh: …青年会社。

e.en: A club is a place where the members of a club meet.

ex.en: I stopped in at the club for a drink.
ex.zh: 我在俱乐部喝一杯歇歇脚。

e.en: A club is a team which competes in sports competitions.

ex.en: ...the New York Yankees baseball club.
ex.zh: …纽约扬基棒球队。

e.en: A club is the same as a .

ex.en: It's a big dance hit in the clubs.
ex.zh: 在各个夜总会这可是个热门舞。

d: n. 俱乐部，社团（club 的复数）；（扑克牌）梅花，草花；运动队；会所；夜总会；棍棒；高尔夫球杆
v. 用棍棒打（club 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Your cheeks are the sides of your face below your eyes.

ex.en: Tears were running down her cheeks.
ex.zh: 眼泪顺着她面颊流下。

e.en: Your cheeks are your buttocks.

ex.en: My butt cheeks are sore from sitting on this bench too long.
ex.zh: 我屁股痛，因为在长凳上坐得太久了。

e.en: You say that someone has cheek when you are annoyed or shocked at something unreasonable that they have done.

ex.en: I'm amazed they had the cheek to ask in the first place.
ex.zh: 我很吃惊，他们最初竟有脸问。

d: n. 脸颊，面颊；厚颜无耻，放肆；半边屁股
v. 对……无礼，对……不懂规矩
【名】 （Cheek）（英）奇克（人名）

e.en: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered. 关闭;

ex.en: If you are cold, close the window.
ex.zh: 如果你冷就关上窗户。

ex.en: Zacharias heard the door close.
ex.zh: 札哈里亚斯听到门关上了。

e.en: When you close something such as an open book or umbrella, you move the different parts of it together. 把 (书、伞等)

ex.en: Slowly he closed the book.
ex.zh: 慢慢地他把书合上了。

e.en: If you close something such as a computer file or window, you give the computer an instruction to remove it from the screen. 关闭 (计算机文件、窗口)

ex.en: To close your document, press CTRL+W on your keyboard.
ex.zh: 要关闭你的文件同时按下键盘上的CTRL和W键。

e.en: When you close your eyes or your eyes close, your eyelids move downward, so that you can no longer see.

ex.en: Bess closed her eyes and fell asleep.
ex.zh: 贝丝闭上眼睛，睡着了。

d: v. （使）关闭；合上，合拢；（使）暂时性关闭；（永久）停业，停止活动；（使）结束，（使）停止；关闭（计算机程序）；（股票等）收盘；拉近（距离），缩小（差距）；抱住，抓住，握住；（使）（伤口）愈合；封锁（公路、公园等）；完成，做成（交易等）；接通（电路）
adj. 接近的；酷似的，几乎相等的；快要……的；（坏事）险些发生的；近亲的；亲近的，亲密的；（关联）密切的；仔细的，全面的；势均力敌的；闷热的，不通风的；密集的，空间很小的；（头发或胡子）齐根的；守口如瓶的，掩饰感情的；吝啬的，小气的；严加保护（守卫）的；闭塞音的
adv. （空间或时间上）接近地
n. 结束，结尾；（大教堂的）围地；死胡同；英国某些传统公学的操场；通路，入口；（股市一日的）收盘（the close）；（板球一日比赛的）终赛（the close）；（乐）短句结尾，收束；关闭（尤指关门）

e.en: A concerted action is done by several people or groups working together.

ex.en: Martin Parry, author of the report, says it's time for concerted action by world leaders.
ex.zh: 这份报道的作者马丁•帕里说是各国领导人采取一致行动的时候了。

e.en: If you make a concerted effort to do something, you try very hard to do it.

ex.en: He made a concerted effort to win me away from my steady, sweet but boring boyfriend.
ex.zh: 他作了极大的努力把我从踏实、可爱但令人乏味的男友手中赢走。

d: adj. 共同筹划的，一致的；尽力的，竭力的；（音乐）分声部的
v. 共同议定，协调（concert 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: You use consummate to describe someone who is extremely skilful.

ex.en: He acted the part with consummate skill.
ex.zh: 他以精湛的演技饰演了这个角色。

e.en: If two people consummate a marriage or relationship, they make it complete by having sex. (通过同房而) 完成 (婚姻)

ex.en: His wife divorced him for failing to consummate their marriage.
ex.zh: 他的妻子因为他未能完婚而跟他离婚了。

d: adj. 完美的，圆满的，至上的；技艺高超的，炉火纯青的；十足的，彻头彻尾的（常作贬义强调）
vt. 完成，实现，做成；圆房，完婚；使达到极点，使臻于完善，使达到完美

e.en: A corpse is a dead body, especially the body of a human being.

ex.en: Detectives placed the corpse in a body bag.
ex.zh: 刑警们把尸体装进了一个运尸袋。

d: n. 尸体
v. 使戏剧演员的演出僵住

e.en: The depth of something such as a river or hole is the distance downward from its top surface, or between its upper and lower surfaces.

ex.en: The depth of the shaft is 520 yards.
ex.zh: 这个通道的深度是520码。

ex.en: The smaller lake ranges from five to fourteen feet in depth.
ex.zh: 这个较小的湖的深度在5至14英尺之间。

e.en: The depth of something such as a wardrobe or drawer is the distance between its front surface and its back.
If an emotion is very strongly or intensely felt, you can talk about its depth. (感情的)

ex.en: I am well aware of the depth of feeling that exists in Ontario.
ex.zh: 我深知安大略人情感的深厚。

e.en: The depth of a situation is its extent and seriousness.

ex.en: The country's leadership had underestimated the depth of the crisis.
ex.zh: 这个国家的领导层低估了这次危机的严重程度。

d: n. 深度，纵深；深刻，深奥；深厚，深切；（声音的）低沉；浓度，强度；严重性，严峻性；渊博，老练；纵深感，景深；最深处，极限；低迷状态，非常糟糕的状态

e.en: The Derby is the name of a race for three-year-old horses that takes place each year. In the United States, it refers particularly to the Kentucky Derby. 德比马赛;
e.zh: 每年举行的三岁马赛马会，在美国尤指肯塔基赛马会

e.en: A derby is a sports competition or race where there are no restrictions or limits on who can enter. (对参赛者没有限制的)比赛;

ex.en: He caught a 6 pound salmon in the annual fishing derby at Lake Winnipesaukee.
ex.zh: 他在温尼珀索基湖边举行的年度钓鱼大赛上钓到一条6磅重的大马哈鱼。

d: n. 德比（英国中部的都市）；德比赛马；大赛马

e.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

ex.en: We asked her to describe what kind of things she did in her spare time.
ex.zh: 我们请她描述她在闲暇时做些什么。

ex.en: She read a poem by Carver which describes their life together.
ex.zh: 她读了一首卡弗描写他们在一起生活的诗。

e.en: If a person describes someone or something as a particular thing, he or she believes that they are that thing and says so. 讲成;

ex.en: He described it as an extraordinarily tangled and complicated tale.
ex.zh: 他把它讲成了一个格外错综复杂的故事。

ex.en: Even his closest allies describe him as forceful, aggressive, and determined.
ex.zh: 甚至他最亲密的同盟者们都说他强势、好斗且坚决。

d: v. 描述，描写，叙述，形容（describe 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被描述的，所述的，上述的

e.en: The distance between two points or places is the amount of space between them.

ex.en: ...the distance between the island and the nearby shore.
ex.zh: …岛屿和附近海岸之间的距离。

e.en: When two things are very far apart, you talk about the distance between them.

ex.en: The distance wouldn't be a problem.
ex.zh: 距离遥远不是问题。

e.en: When you want to emphasize that two people or things do not have a close relationship or are not the same, you can refer to the distance between them.

ex.en: There was a vast distance between psychological clues and concrete proof.
ex.zh: 心理线索和现实证据之间存在着巨大差距。

e.en: Distance is coolness or unfriendliness in the way that someone behaves toward you. 疏远;

ex.en: There were periods of sulking, of pronounced distance, of coldness.
ex.zh: 出现阶段性的愠怒、明显的疏远和冷淡。

d: adj. 疏远的；有距离的
v. （使）远离，疏远；领先于（一匹马）（distance 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: When people, animals, and plants die, they stop living.

ex.en: A year later my dog died.
ex.zh: 1年后，我的狗死了。

ex.en: Sadly, both he and my mother died of cancer.
ex.zh: 令人悲伤的是，他和我母亲都死于癌症。

e.en: If a machine or device dies, it stops completely, especially after a period of working more and more slowly or inefficiently.

ex.en: Then suddenly, the engine coughed, spluttered, and died.
ex.zh: 突然，发动机发出喀喀声、噼啪声，然后就熄火了。

e.en: You can say that you are dying of thirst, hunger, boredom, or curiosity to emphasize that you are very thirsty, hungry, bored, or curious. (饥渴、厌倦、好奇得)

ex.en: Order me a soda, I'm dying of thirst.
ex.zh: 给我要杯汽水，我快渴死了。

e.en: You can say that you are dying for something or are dying to do something to emphasize that you very much want to have it or do it.

ex.en: I'm dying for a breath of fresh air.
ex.zh: 我真想呼吸点新鲜空气。

d: v. die 的过去式和过去分词：死亡，去世；消逝，消失；（机器等）停止运转；（非正式）几乎要死（夸张表示震惊、尴尬等强烈情绪）

e.en: greyhound racing

d: n. 狗，犬（dog 的复数）；（英国英语，非正式）赛狗（the dogs，尤指灰狗赛）；瘦狗类（企业战略中市场增长率低、相对市场份额也低的业务）
v. 紧紧跟踪，尾随（dog 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A door is a piece of wood, glass, or metal, which is moved to open and close the entrance to a building, room, wardrobe, or vehicle.

ex.en: I was knocking at the front door but there was no answer.
ex.zh: 我敲了敲前门，但无人应答。

e.en: A door is the space in a wall when a door is open.

ex.en: She looked through the door of the kitchen. Her daughter was at the stove.
ex.zh: 透过厨房开着的门，她看到女儿正在炉子旁边。

e.en: Doors is used in expressions such as a few doors down or three doors up to refer to a place that is a particular number of buildings away from where you are. 建筑物 (表示两个地点之间的距离)

ex.en: Mrs. Cade's house was only a few doors down from her daughter's apartment.
ex.zh: 从凯德夫人的房子到她女儿的公寓只隔了几座房屋。

e.en: When you answer the door, you go and open the door because a visitor has knocked on it or rung the bell.

ex.en: Carol answered the door as soon as I knocked.
ex.zh: 我刚敲过门，卡罗尔就把门打开了。

d: n.  门；门口，门道；建筑，门户 ；（尤与 open 或 unlock 连用）机会，可能性
v. 车门撞击（骑自行车经过的人）
【名】 （Door）（英）多尔（人名）

e.en: Don't is the usual spoken form of "do not." (do not)

d: aux. do not 的缩略形式，用于构成否定句、否定疑问句和祈使句，表示否定：不，不要，别。
n. 禁忌，不许做的事（常用复数 don'ts，常见于 dos and don'ts）

e.en: Earth or the Earth is the planet on which we live. People usually say Earth when they are referring to the planet as part of the universe, and the Earth when they are talking about the planet as the place where we live.

ex.en: The space shuttle Atlantis returned safely to Earth today.
ex.zh: 亚特兰蒂斯号航天飞机今天安全返回地球。

e.en: The earth is the land surface on which we live and move around. 陆地;

ex.en: The earth shook and swayed and the walls of neighbouring houses fell around them.
ex.zh: 地面晃动起来，附近房子的墙壁在他们周围坍塌了。

e.en: Earth is the substance on the land surface of the earth, for example clay or sand, in which plants grow. 土壤;

ex.en: The road winds for miles through parched earth, scrub and cactus.
ex.zh: 那条路蜿蜒数英里，穿过干热的土地、灌木丛和仙人掌，。

e.en: The earth in an electric plug or piece of electrical equipment is the wire through which electricity passes into the ground and which makes the equipment safe.

ex.en: ...an insulated earth.
ex.zh: …一根绝缘地线。

d: n. 地球，世界；陆地，地面；泥土，土壤；地线，电线；一大笔钱；尘世；兽穴
v. 把（电线）接地；用土掩盖；追赶入洞穴

e.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try very hard to do it.

ex.en: He made no effort to hide his disappointment.
ex.zh: 他不试图隐瞒自己的失望。

ex.en: Finding a cure requires considerable time and effort.
ex.zh: 找到一种治愈方法需要相当的时间和努力。

e.en: If you say that someone did something with effort or with an effort, you mean it was difficult for them to do.

ex.en: She took a deep breath and sat up slowly and with great effort.
ex.zh: 她深吸一口气，慢慢地、吃力地坐了起来。

e.en: An effort is a particular series of activities that is organized by a group of people in order to achieve something.

ex.en: ...a famine relief effort in Angola.
ex.zh: …一个在安哥拉的饥荒救援活动。

e.en: If you say that something is an effort, you mean that an unusual amount of physical or mental energy is needed to do it.

ex.en: Even carrying the camcorder while hiking in the forest was an effort.
ex.zh: 在森林徒步旅行时，即使背着摄像机也是件极难的事。

d: n. 努力，艰难的尝试；力气，精力；有组织的活动；努力的结果，成就

e.en: You use exactly before an amount, number, or position to emphasize that it is no more, no less, or no different from what you are stating.

ex.en: Each corner had a guard tower, each of which was exactly ten metres in height.
ex.zh: 每个角都有1个警戒塔，每个塔刚好10米高。

e.en: If you say "Exactly," you are agreeing with someone or emphasizing the truth of what they say. If you say "Not exactly," you are telling them politely that they are wrong in part of what they are saying.

ex.en: Eve nodded, almost approvingly. "Exactly."
ex.zh: 伊夫几近赞许地点点头。“正是如此。”

e.en: You use not exactly to indicate that a meaning or situation is slightly different from what people think or expect.

ex.en: He's not exactly homeless, he just hangs out in this park.
ex.zh: 他不完全是无家可归，他只是常住在这个公园里。

e.en: You can use not exactly to show that you mean the opposite of what you are saying. 根本不;

ex.en: This was not exactly what I wanted to hear.
ex.zh: 这根本不是我想听的。

d: adv. 精确地，确切地；（用于强调）恰好，完全；（要求得到更多信息）究竟，到底；正是如此，一点不错

e.en: An Englishman is a man who comes from England. 英国男人;

d: n. 英国人

e.en: Facts are pieces of information that can be discovered.

ex.en: There is so much information you can almost effortlessly find the facts for yourself.
ex.zh: 有这么多信息，你几乎能毫不费力地为自己找到实例。

ex.en: His opponent swamped him with facts and figures.
ex.zh: 他的对手用实例和数字让他难以招架。

e.en: You use the fact that after some verbs or prepositions, especially in expressions such as in view of the fact that, apart from the fact that, and despite the fact that, to link the verb or preposition with a clause. …

ex.en: His chances do not seem good in view of the fact that the Chief Prosecutor has already voiced his public disapproval.
ex.zh: 鉴于首席检察官已公开表示反对这一事实，他的机会看起来不好。

ex.en: Despite the fact that the disease is so prevalent, treatment is still far from satisfactory.
ex.zh: 尽管事实上这种疾病非常普遍，治疗却远不尽如人意。

e.en: You use the fact that instead of a simple that-clause either for emphasis or because the clause is the subject of your sentence. …

ex.en: My family now accepts the fact that I don't eat sugar or bread.
ex.zh: 我的家人现在接受了我不吃糖或面包这一事实。

e.en: You use in fact, in actual fact, or in point of fact to indicate that you are giving more detailed information about what you have just said.

ex.en: We've had a pretty bad time while you were away. In fact, we very nearly split up this time.
ex.zh: 我们在你走的那段时间过得非常糟糕。确切地说，我们这次几乎分道扬镳了。

ex.en: He apologized as soon as he realized what he had done. In actual fact he wrote a nice little note to me.
ex.zh: 他一意识到他所做的一切就道歉了。确切地说，他给我写了一张友善的小便条。

d: n. 事实，真相；现实

e.en: If you describe someone as experienced, you mean that they have been doing a particular job or activity for a long time, and therefore know a lot about it or are very skilful at it.

ex.en: ...lawyers who are experienced in these matters.
ex.zh: …在这些事情上有经验的律师们。

ex.en: It's a team packed with experienced and mature professionals.
ex.zh: 这是一支经验丰富的，成熟的专家队伍。

d: adj. 熟练的，有经验的
v. 经历，遭遇；体会到，感受到（experience 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A family is a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children.

ex.en: There's room in there for a family of five.
ex.zh: 那儿能住得下一家5口。

ex.en: Does he have any family?
ex.zh: 他有什么家人吗？

e.en: When people talk about a family, they sometimes mean children.

ex.en: They decided to start a family.
ex.zh: 他们决定了要孩子。

e.en: When people talk about their family, they sometimes mean their ancestors.

ex.en: Her family came to Los Angeles at the turn of the century.
ex.zh: 她的祖先在世纪之交时来到了洛杉矶。

e.en: You can use family to describe things that belong to a particular family.

ex.en: He returned to the family home.
ex.zh: 他回到了自己家。

d: n. 家，家庭；家属，亲属；家族；子女，孩子；（动植物的）科；语族；祖先； 一窝（动物）； 有组织的犯罪团伙；（具有明显共同特征的）一类东西；（在某些方面）像家人一样的一群人；（数）族；派别；氏族
adj. 家庭的；一家所有的；老少咸宜的；全家用的

e.en: If you achieve fame, you become very well-known.

ex.en: At the height of his fame, his every word was valued.
ex.zh: 在他声名鼎盛时，他的每一句话都受到了重视。

ex.en: The film earned him international fame.
ex.zh: 这部影片为他赢得了国际声誉。

d: n. 名誉，名气
v. 使闻名，使有名望

e.en: If you are a fan of someone or something, especially a famous person or a sport, you like them very much and are very interested in them.

ex.en: If you're a Billy Crystal fan, you'll love this film.
ex.zh: 如果你是比利·克里斯特尔的影迷，你就会喜欢这部电影。

ex.en: I am a great fan of rave music.
ex.zh: 我是个狂欢音乐的狂热乐迷。

e.en: A fan is a piece of electrical or mechanical equipment with blades that go around and around. It keeps a room or machine cool or gets rid of unpleasant smells.

ex.en: He cools himself in front of an electric fan.
ex.zh: 他在一个电扇前面吹凉。

e.en: A fan is a flat object that you hold in your hand and wave in order to move the air and make yourself feel cooler.

ex.en: ...hundreds of dancing girls waving peacock fans.
ex.zh: …数百名挥动着孔雀扇的舞女。

e.en: If you fan yourself or your face when you are hot, you wave a fan or other flat object in order to make yourself feel cooler.

ex.en: She would have to wait in the truck, fanning herself with a piece of cardboard.
ex.zh: 她只得在卡车里等候，用一块纸板给自己扇风。

d: n. 风扇，扇子；粉丝，狂热爱好者；扇形；（使风车头迎风的）风叶；（山坡脚下的）地带
v. 扇，为……扇风；煽（火）；煽动，激起；（击球手）三击不中出局；（呼吸，微风）吹拂；驱散，扇走；击球不中
【名】 （Fan）（美、法、俄）法恩（人名）

e.en: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.

ex.en: I am feeling very depressed.
ex.zh: 我感到很沮丧。

ex.en: Suddenly I felt a sharp pain in my shoulder.
ex.zh: 我突然感到肩部一阵剧痛。

e.en: If you talk about how an experience or event feels, you talk about the emotions and sensations connected with it.

ex.en: It feels good to have finished a piece of work.
ex.zh: 完成一项工作让人感觉很好。

ex.en: The speed at which everything moved felt strange.
ex.zh: 一切进展的速度让人感觉怪异。

e.en: If you talk about how an object feels, you talk about the physical quality that you notice when you touch or hold it. For example, if something feels soft, you notice that it is soft when you touch it. 摸上去…;

ex.en: The metal felt smooth and cold.
ex.zh: 这种金属摸上去光滑而冰冷。

ex.en: The ten-foot oars felt heavy and awkward.
ex.zh: 这些10英尺长的船桨拿起来又重又不方便。

e.en: Feel is also a noun.

ex.en: He remembered the feel of her skin.
ex.zh: 他记得她的皮肤摸上去的那种感觉。

d: v. 感受到，体会到；觉得，相信；使人感觉……；察觉到，意识到；触摸；受到；摸索；有知觉，能感知……
n. 感觉，气氛；触觉，手感；触摸；感知，理解；熟练使用；特性，特质

e.en: Felt is the past tense and past participle of . (feel)
Felt is a thick cloth made from wool or other fibres packed tightly together.

ex.en: She had on an old felt hat.
ex.zh: 她戴着一顶旧毡帽。

e.en: to make into or cover with felt 制毡;

d: n. 毛毡
v. （使）毡合；用毡覆盖
v. 感受到，体会到；觉得，相信；使人感觉……（feel 的过去式和过去分词）
【名】 （Felt）（美）费尔特（人名）

e.en: Someone who is finished with something is no longer doing it or dealing with it or is no longer interested in it. 不再做某事的;

ex.en: One suspects he will be finished with boxing.
ex.zh: 有人猜想他将对拳击不再感兴趣了。

e.en: Something that is finished no longer exists or is no longer happening. 不再存在的;

ex.en: After each game is finished, a message flashes on the screen.
ex.zh: 每场比赛结束以后，一条信息就会闪现在屏幕上。

e.en: Someone or something that is finished is no longer important, powerful, or effective. 失势的;

ex.en: Her power over me is finished.
ex.zh: 她对我的控制失效了。

d: adj. 结束了的，完成了的；不再与……打交道；垮台，失败
v. 完成，做好；（使）结束；消耗尽（所剩之物）（finish 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Fire is the hot, bright flames produced by things that are burning.

ex.en: They saw a big flash and a huge ball of fire reaching hundreds of feet into the sky.
ex.zh: 他们看到一道强光和一个巨大的火球直冲天空达几百英尺。

e.en: Fire or a fire is an occurrence of uncontrolled burning which destroys buildings, forests, or other things.

ex.en: 87 people died in a fire at the Happy Land Social Club.
ex.zh: 87人死于乐土社交俱乐部的火灾中。

ex.en: A forest fire is sweeping across portions of north Maine this evening.
ex.zh: 今天傍晚一场森林大火正席卷着缅因州北部的部分地区。

e.en: A fire is a burning pile of wood, coal, or other fuel that you make, for example, to use for heat, light, or cooking.

ex.en: There was a fire in the grate.
ex.zh: 壁炉里烧着火。

e.en: A fire is a device that uses electricity or gas to give out heat and warm a room. 电炉;

d: n. 失火，火灾；火焰；炉火，灶火；取暖器；射击，火力；怒火，激情；严厉批评，猛烈批判
v. 射击，开火；射（箭）；扔，抛；点火，启动；连珠炮似的提出（问题）；解雇，开除；激发；烧制（陶器）

e.en: If you say that someone flaunts their possessions, abilities, or qualities, you mean that they display them in a very obvious way, especially in order to try to obtain other people's admiration.

ex.en: They drove around in Rolls-Royces, openly flaunting their wealth.
ex.zh: 他们开着劳斯莱斯车四处转，公开炫耀他们的财富。

d: vt. （多含贬义）炫耀，卖弄（即招摇地展示财富、才能等）；无视，藐视（规范用法应为 flout）
vi. 炫耀，招摇；（旗帜等）飘扬，招展
n. 炫耀，卖弄（的行为）

e.en: Football is a game played by two teams of eleven players using a round ball. Players kick the ball to each other and try to score goals by kicking the ball into a large net.

American football is a game played by two teams of eleven players using an oval ball. Players carry the ball in their hands or throw it to each other as they try to score goals that are called touchdowns.

ex.en: Two blocks beyond our school was a field where boys played football.
ex.zh: 离我们学校两个街区远，有一个男孩子们玩橄榄球的场地。

e.en: A football is a ball that is used for playing football.

ex.en: ...a heavy leather football.
ex.zh: …一个沉甸甸的皮质橄榄球。

d: n. 足球运动；橄榄球运动；足球，橄榄球；屡起争议的课题，被踢来踢去的难题；（尤指别具一格的）足球风格，踢法

e.en: A game is an activity or sport usually involving skill, knowledge, or chance, in which you follow fixed rules and try to win against an opponent or to solve a puzzle. 游戏;

ex.en: ...the wonderful game of football.
ex.zh: …精彩的足球运动。

ex.en: ...a playful game of hide-and-seek.
ex.zh: …一个有趣的捉迷藏游戏。

e.en: A game is one particular occasion on which a game is played.

ex.en: It was the first game of the season.
ex.zh: 那是本赛季的第一场比赛。

ex.en: He regularly watched our games from the stands.
ex.zh: 他经常从看台上观看我们的比赛。

e.en: A game is a part of a match, for example in tennis or bridge, consisting of a fixed number of points. (比赛中的)

ex.en: She won six games to love in the second set.
ex.zh: 第2盘她以6-0取胜。

e.en: Games are an organized event in which competitions in several sports take place.

ex.en: ...the 1996 Olympic Games at Atlanta.
ex.zh: …1996年亚特兰大奥林匹克运动会。

d: n. 游戏，比赛；一局，一场；运动会；体育课，体育活动；儿戏；诡计，花招；猎物，野味；行当，行业；玩耍，消遣；比赛技巧
adj. 愿意尝试的，有冒险精神的；（腿）残疾的，瘸的
v. 操纵；玩视频（或电视、电脑）游戏；赌博
【名】 （Game）（英）盖姆，（法）加姆，（西）加梅（人名）

e.en: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

ex.en: The seminars are free, with lunch provided.
ex.zh: 研讨会是免费的，还提供午餐。

e.en: Someone or something that is free is not restricted, controlled, or limited, for example, by rules, customs, or other people. 自由的;

ex.en: The government will be free to pursue its economic policies.
ex.zh: 政府将自由实行其经济政策。

ex.en: The elections were free and fair.
ex.zh: 选举是自由公正的。

e.en: 自由地

ex.en: They cast their votes freely and without coercion on election day.
ex.zh: 他们在选举日自由地投票，不受强迫。

e.en: Someone who is free is no longer a prisoner or a slave.

ex.en: He walked from the court house a free man.
ex.zh: 他走出法庭，重获自由。

d: v. 解放，释放，使自由；使摆脱（令人不快的事物）；解除，清除；腾出，空出（时间、空间等）以供使用；（free 的过去式和过去分词，常与 from 连用）
adj. 被释放的，获得自由的；已摆脱（束缚、纠缠等）的，解脱的
n. （Freed）（美、英）弗里德（人名）

e.en: A garden is a piece of land next to someone's house, with grass and plants growing in it.

ex.en: ...the most beautiful garden on Earth.
ex.zh: …地球上最美的花园。

e.en: A garden is the part of a yard which is used for growing flowers and vegetables. 花园;
If you garden, you do work in your garden such as weeding or planting.

ex.en: Jim gardened at the homes of friends on weekends.
ex.zh: 吉姆每逢周末在朋友们的家里干园艺活。

e.en: 园艺活

ex.en: I have taken up gardening again.
ex.zh: 我又开始干起了园艺活。

d: n. 花园，菜园，果园；庭园；公园；（用于街名）街，广场
v. 做园艺工作，种植花木
【名】  (Garden）（英、意、巴基）加登（人名）

e.en: Glamour is the quality of being more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

ex.en: ...the glamour of show biz.
ex.zh: …演艺业的诱惑力。

d: n. 吸引力，诱惑力，魅力；迷人的美，奢华；魔法，巫术
v. 迷住，迷惑

e.en: Good means pleasant or enjoyable.

ex.en: We had a really good time together.
ex.zh: 我们一起度过了非常愉快的时光。

ex.en: I know they would have a better life here.
ex.zh: 我知道他们在这儿会过上更好的生活。

e.en: Good means of a high quality, standard, or level. 质量高的;

ex.en: Exercise is just as important to health as good food.
ex.zh: 锻炼和好的饮食对身体健康一样重要。

ex.en: His parents wanted Raymond to have the best possible education.
ex.zh: 他的父母想让雷蒙德尽可能得到最好的教育。

e.en: If you are good at something, you are skilful and successful at doing it.

ex.en: He was very good at his work.
ex.zh: 他十分擅长他的工作。

ex.en: I'm not very good at singing.
ex.zh: 我不很擅长唱歌。

e.en: If you describe a piece of news, an action, or an effect as good, you mean that it is likely to result in benefit or success.

ex.en: On balance, biotechnology should be good news for developing countries.
ex.zh: 总的来说，生物技术对发展中国家来说应该是好消息。

ex.en: I think the response was good.
ex.zh: 我认为这样的反应很有利。

d: adj. 优良的；能干的，擅长的；令人愉快的，满意的；合适的，方便的；有益的；乖的；虔诚的；健康的；善良的；正直的；相当大的，相当多的；至少；彻底的；明智的，合理的；划算的，收益可观的；赢得赞许的，令人尊敬的；（用于表示回应）好的；表示惊讶、生气或者加强语气；（用于打招呼）好；有趣的；有效的；能提供……的；（踢、射、投）命中；亲密的；够了
n. 善，正义；好事；商品，所有物；（运载的）货物（goods）；优势，利益；真货，正品（the goods）；好人，有道德的人（the good）
adv. 好地；彻底地，完全地
【名】 （Good）（英）古德，（瑞典）戈德（人名）

e.en: If you say that someone has gravitas, you mean that you respect them because they seem serious and intelligent.

ex.en: He is pale, dark, and authoritative, with the gravitas you might expect of a Nobel prize winner.
ex.zh: 他面色苍白、皮肤呈深色、有权威性，带着你可能期待的一位诺贝尔奖得主的那种庄严。

d: n. （不可数名词，较正式）庄重；庄严；令人起敬的举止或威仪

e.en: If you grieve over something, especially someone's death, you feel very sad about it.

ex.en: He's grieving over his dead wife and son.
ex.zh: 他因丧妻失子而悲痛不已。

ex.en: I didn't have any time to grieve.
ex.zh: 我没有时间去悲伤。

e.en: a farm manager or overseer 农场经理;

d: v. 感到悲痛，悲伤（尤指因某人去世等）；（使）某人悲伤（grieve 的现在分词）
adj. （因某人去世等而）悲痛的；哀伤的
n. 哀悼；悲伤（的过程）

e.en: He'd is the usual spoken form of "he had," especially when "had" is an auxiliary verb. (he had)

ex.en: He'd never learned to read.
ex.zh: 他一直没有学会阅读。

e.en: He'd is a spoken form of "he would." (he would)

ex.en: He'd come into the clubhouse every day.
ex.zh: 他会每天到俱乐部会所来。

d: abbr. he would 的缩约形式（他将）；he had 的缩约形式（他已经）

e.en: When you hear a sound, you become aware of it through your ears.

ex.en: She heard no further sounds.
ex.zh: 她再也没有听见任何响声。

ex.en: They heard the protesters shout: "No more fascism!"
ex.zh: 他们听见抗议者在高呼：“打倒法西斯主义！”

e.en: If you hear something such as a lecture or a piece of music, you listen to it.

ex.en: You can hear commentary on the game at halftime.
ex.zh: 你可在中场休息时听到对比赛的评论。

ex.en: I don't think you've ever heard Doris talking about her emotional life before.
ex.zh: 我想你以前从未听过多丽丝谈论自己的感情生活。

e.en: When a judge or a court of law hears a case, or evidence in a case, they listen to it officially in order to make a decision about it.

ex.en: The jury has heard evidence from defence witnesses.
ex.zh: 陪审团听取了被告方证人的证词。

e.en: If you hear from someone, you receive a letter or telephone call from them. 接到 (信或电话)

ex.en: Drop us a line, it's always great to hear from you.
ex.zh: 给我们写封信，能收到你的信总是让人很高兴。

d: v. 听到（hear 的过去式和过去分词）；闻知
n. （Heard）人名；（英）赫德

e.en: You use himself to refer to a man, boy, or male animal. 他自己; 它自己 (指雄性动物)

ex.en: He poured himself a whisky and sat down in the chair.
ex.zh: 他给自己倒了一杯威士忌，然后坐在椅子里。

ex.en: William went away muttering to himself.
ex.zh: 威廉喃喃自语地走了。

e.en: In written English, himself is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use "himself or herself" or "themselves." 他自己 (书面英语里泛指人)

ex.en: There is nothing more dangerous than someone who thinks of himself as a victim.
ex.zh: 没有比自认为是受害者的人更危险的了。

e.en: You use himself to emphasize the person or thing that you are referring to. Himself is sometimes used instead of "him" as the object of a verb or preposition. 他本人 (用以加强语气)

ex.en: The president himself is on a visit to Beijing.
ex.zh: 总统本人正在访问北京。

d: pron. 他自己；他亲自，他本人；他自己；by himself（或 all by himself）独自，独力

e.en: You can refer to the events of the past as history. You can also refer to the past events which concern a particular topic or place as its history.

ex.en: The Catholic Church has played a prominent role throughout Polish history.
ex.zh: 天主教在整个波兰历史中扮演了重要的角色。

ex.en: ...the most evil mass killer in history.
ex.zh: …历史上最邪恶的杀人狂。

e.en: If someone or something goes down in history, people in the future remember them because of particular actions that they have done or because of particular events that have happened.

ex.en: Bradley will go down in history as Los Angeles' longest serving mayor.
ex.zh: 布拉德利将作为洛杉矶任职时间最长的市长载入史册。

e.en: Someone who makes history does something that is considered to be important and significant in the development of the world or of a particular society.

ex.en: Willy Brandt made history by visiting East Germany in 1970.
ex.zh: 威利·勃兰特1970年对东德的访问创造了历史。

e.en: History is a subject studied in schools, colleges, and universities that deals with events that have happened in the past.

ex.en: ...a lecturer in history at Birmingham University.
ex.zh: …伯明翰大学的一位历史讲师。

d: n. 历史；沿革，发展过程；历史课，历史学；史书，历史记载；个人经历，履历

e.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

ex.en: Find the exact grip that allows you to hit the ball hard.
ex.zh: 找到能让你大力击球的准确握拍方法。

e.en: When one thing hits another, it touches it with a lot of force.

ex.en: The car had apparently hit a traffic sign before skidding out of control.
ex.zh: 汽车显然在失控滑出前猛地撞到了一个交通指示牌。

e.en: If a bomb or missile hits its target, it reaches it. (炸弹或导弹)

ex.en: ...multiple-warhead missiles that could hit many targets at a time.
ex.zh: …可以一次击中多个目标的多弹头导弹。

e.en: Hit is also a noun.

ex.en: First a house took a direct hit and then the rocket exploded.
ex.zh: 首先一幢房子被直接击中，接着火箭弹爆炸了。

d: v. 打，击；撞击，碰撞；击中，命中；击（球）；产生不良影响，危害；攻击，袭击；达到（一个特定的水平，阶段，数字）；碰到，遇到（困难、问题等）；使（某人）突然意识到；使（突然）闻到，使看到；按，摁；给（人）一剂毒品（或烈酒）；（产品）面市并产生影响；给（21点纸牌游戏玩家）发另一张纸牌
n. 打击；命中，击中；很受欢迎的人（或事物），成功；（对网站的）访问，点击；毒品的一剂；暴力犯罪，凶杀；很受欢迎的人（或事物）

e.en: If you describe someone as honest, you mean that they always tell the truth, and do not try to deceive people or break the law. 诚实的;

ex.en: I know she's honest and reliable.
ex.zh: 我知道她是诚实可靠的。

e.en: 诚实地;

ex.en: She fought honestly for a just cause and for freedom.
ex.zh: 她正直地为正义事业和自由而战。

e.en: If you are honest in a particular situation, you tell the complete truth or give your sincere opinion, even if this is not very pleasant.

ex.en: I was honest about what I was doing.
ex.zh: 我对我所做的一切毫不隐瞒。

ex.en: He had been honest with her and she had tricked him!
ex.zh: 他对她是真诚的，而她却欺骗了他。

e.en: 坦诚地

ex.en: It came as a shock to hear an old friend speak so honestly about Ted.
ex.zh: 听到一位老朋友如此坦诚地谈论特德真是令人震惊。

d: adj. 诚实的，正直的；坦诚的，直率的；真诚的，显示诚意的；正当获得的；纯正的，不花哨的；无意（伤害别人）的
adv. 真的，确实

e.en: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

ex.en: She has moved to a small house and is living off her meagre savings.
ex.zh: 她搬进了一幢小房子，靠自己微薄的积蓄过日子。

e.en: You can refer to all the people who live together in a house as the house. 一家人;

ex.en: If he set his alarm clock for midnight, it would wake the whole house.
ex.zh: 如果他把闹钟设定在午夜，铃声会把全家人都吵醒。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of places where people go to eat and drink. …馆 (用于某些类型的餐馆名称中)

ex.en: ...a steak house.
ex.zh: …一家牛排馆。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of companies, especially ones which publish books, lend money, or design clothes. …公司 (用于某些类型的公司名称中，尤其是出版、贷款或服装设计等公司)

ex.en: Many of the clothes come from the world's top fashion houses.
ex.zh: 这些服装中有很多来自世界顶级时装设计公司。

d: n. 房子，住宅；一家人，同住一幢房子的人们；（有特定用途的）大楼，大厦；公司，商业机构；观众席，观众；演出场次；餐馆，餐厅；豪斯音乐；王室，皇族（House）；（某些英国学校学生为进行比赛而分的）组；动物的笼舍；议院，议会；（占星）黄道十二宫之一，黄道宫
v. 让……居住，给……提供住房；给……提供场地，收藏存放；包裹，覆盖；住
adj. 家养的，常在室内的；公司的，机构的；（乐队，组合）（在俱乐部或别的场所）常驻的，定期表演的
【名】 （House）（英）豪斯（人名）

e.en: A woman's husband is the man she is married to.

ex.en: Eva married her husband Jack in 1957.
ex.zh: 1957年伊娃与其丈夫杰克结婚。

d: n. 丈夫
v. 节约使用
【名】 （Husband）（英、美、爱）赫斯本德（人名）

e.en: Someone who is insane is severely mentally ill. 精神病的;

ex.en: Some people simply can't take it and they just go insane.
ex.zh: 一些人就是接受不了，于是便变得精神错乱。

e.en: If you describe a decision or action as insane, you think it is very foolish or excessive. 疯狂的;

ex.en: He asked me what I thought and I said, "Listen, this is completely insane."
ex.zh: 他问我是怎么想的，我说，“听着，这十分愚蠢。”

e.en: 疯狂地

ex.en: I would be insanely jealous if Bill left me for another woman.
ex.zh: 如果比尔为了另一个女人而离开我，我会妒忌得发疯的。

d: adj. 疯癫的，精神失常的；蠢极的，荒唐的

e.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or school.

ex.en: The interview went well.
ex.zh: 面试很顺利。

e.en: If you are interviewed for a particular job or school, someone asks you questions about yourself to find out if you are suitable for it.

ex.en: When Wardell was interviewed, he was impressive, and on that basis, he was hired.
ex.zh: 当沃德尔接受面试时，他给人印象深刻，因此他被雇用了。

e.en: An interview is a conversation in which a journalist puts questions to someone such as a famous person or politician.

ex.en: The trouble began when Allan gave an interview to the Chicago Tribune last month.
ex.zh: 麻烦开始于艾伦上个月接受《芝加哥论坛报》的采访。

e.en: When a journalist interviews someone such as a famous person, they ask them a series of questions.

ex.en: I'd interviewed him often in the past.
ex.zh: 我过去经常采访他。

d: n. 面试；采访，访谈；面谈，会谈（interview 的复数）
v. 对…进行面试；采访；询问，盘问；接见；参加面试（interview 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you do one thing instead of another, you do the first thing and not the second thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.

ex.en: They raised prices and cut production, instead of cutting costs.
