ex.zh: 他们提高了价格，减少了产量，而没有削减成本。

e.en: If you do not do something, but do something else instead, you do the second thing and not the first thing, as the result of a choice or a change of behaviour.

ex.en: My husband asked why I couldn't just forget about dieting and eat normally instead.
ex.zh: 丈夫问我为什么就不能忘掉节食而正常吃饭。

d: adv. 代替，顶替，反而

e.en: Someone who feels intimidated feels frightened and lacks confidence because of the people they are with or the situation they are in.

ex.en: Women can come in here and not feel intimidated.
ex.zh: 女人们可以进到这里而不会感觉害怕。

d: adj. 害怕的，被吓倒的，受到恐吓的
v. 威胁，恐吓（intimidate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: working on occasional jobs or by the piece rather than in a regular job

ex.en: a jobbing gardener

d: v. 打零工；买卖股票；（非正式）欺骗；背叛；假公济私；戳；（用尖物）刺进（job 的现在分词）
adj. 打零工的

e.en: Kept is the past tense and past participle of keep. (keep)

d: v. （使）保持，处于；继续，重复（做某事）；使耽搁（keep 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you invite someone to something such as a party or a meal, you ask them to come to it.

ex.en: She invited him to her 26th birthday party in New Jersey.
ex.zh: 她邀请了他参加她在新泽西举办的26岁生日聚会。

ex.en: Barron invited her to accompany him to the races.
ex.zh: 巴伦邀请了她陪他去看比赛。

e.en: If you are invited to do something, you are formally asked or given permission to do it. 邀请;

ex.en: At a future date, managers will be invited to apply for a management buy-out.
ex.zh: 在将来的某一天，经理们将受邀参加一项管理层控股收购。

ex.en: He invited me to go into partnership with him.
ex.zh: 他邀请了我与他合作。

e.en: If something you say or do invites trouble or criticism, it makes trouble or criticism more likely.

ex.en: Their refusal to compromise will inevitably invite more criticism from the UN.
ex.zh: 他们的拒绝让步将不可避免地招致来自联合国的更多批评。

e.en: An invite is an invitation to something such as a party or a meal.

ex.en: She tried to wangle an invite to the party.
ex.zh: 她试图骗取一张聚会请柬。

d: v. 邀请，约请；征求，请求；引起，招致（invite 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被邀请的，受邀的，特邀的

e.en: If you know a fact, a piece of information, or an answer, you have it correctly in your mind.

ex.en: I don't know the name of the place.
ex.zh: 我不知道那个地方的名称。

ex.en: "People like doing things for nothing."—"I know they do."
ex.zh: “人们喜欢白忙活。”—“我知道他们是那样。”

e.en: If you know someone, you are familiar with them because you have met them and talked to them before.

ex.en: Gifford was a friend. I'd known him for nine years.
ex.zh: 吉福德曾是个朋友。我那时认识他已有9年。

e.en: If you say that you know of something, you mean that you have heard about it but you do not necessarily have a lot of information about it.

ex.en: We know of the incident but have no further details.
ex.zh: 我们听说过那个事件，但不了解更多的细节。

ex.en: The president admitted that he did not know of any rebels having surrendered so far.
ex.zh: 总统承认迄今为止他未曾听说有任何反叛分子投降。

e.en: If you know about a subject, you have studied it or taken an interest in it, and understand part or all of it.

ex.en: Hire someone with experience, someone who knows about real estate.
ex.zh: 用一位有经验并了解房地产的人。

ex.en: She didn't know anything about music.
ex.zh: 她对音乐一点都不了解。

d: v. 知道（know 的第三人称单数形式）
n. 利兹市（英国西约克郡城市）；（体育）利兹队（指英国利兹的球队，常指利兹联队）

e.en: Let's is the usual spoken form of "let us." (let us)

d: abbr. 让我们，咱们（let us 的缩约形式，后接动词原形，用于提出建议或请求）

e.en: Life is the quality which people, animals, and plants have when they are not dead, and which objects and substances do not have.

ex.en: ...a baby's first minutes of life.
ex.zh: …婴儿生命的头几分钟。

ex.en: Amnesty International opposes the death penalty as a violation of the right to life.
ex.zh: 大赦国际组织反对死刑，因其侵犯生存权。

e.en: You can use life to refer to things or groups of things which are alive. 生物;

ex.en: Is there life on Mars?
ex.zh: 火星上有生命吗？

e.en: If you refer to someone's life, you mean their state of being alive, especially when there is a risk or danger of them dying. 生存;

ex.en: Your life is in danger.
ex.zh: 你有生命危险。

ex.en: A nurse began to try to save his life.
ex.zh: 一名护士开始设法抢救他。

e.en: Someone's life is the period of time during which they are alive.

ex.en: He spent the last fourteen years of his life in retirement.
ex.zh: 他生命的最后14年退休在家。

d: n. 生命；人命，性命；生物，活物；寿命，一生；（某事物的）存在期；生活，人生；生活方式；（某种）生活；生气，活力；（绘画的）模特儿，实物；（游戏中的）一次机会，命；传记；无期徒刑，终身监禁；今生，来世
adj. 生命的；一生的，终身的

e.en: Your lips are the two outer parts of the edge of your mouth.

ex.en: Wade stuck the cigarette between his lips.
ex.zh: 韦德嘴里叼着烟。

d: n. 嘴唇；（伤口或洞口）边缘；容器边缘，开口； 粗鲁无礼的话
v. （水）拍打；（高尔夫）击球至（洞穴）的边缘（而未落入）；用嘴唇触及，吻；（在吹奏管乐器时）运唇
adj. 口头上的
【名】 （Lip）（法）利普，（中）猎（广东话·威妥玛），(柬）利，（东南亚国家华语）立（人名）

e.en: If you say that one person or thing is like another, you mean that they share some of the same qualities or features.

ex.en: He looks like Father Christmas.
ex.zh: 他长得像圣诞老人。

ex.en: It's a bit like going to the dentist; it's never as bad as you fear.
ex.zh: 这有点像去看牙医，它决不像你所担心的那样糟糕。

e.en: If you talk about what something or someone is like, you are talking about their qualities or features. (指人或事物的品质、特点)

ex.en: What was Bulgaria like?
ex.zh: 保加利亚情况怎么样？

ex.en: What did she look like?
ex.zh: 她长什么样？

e.en: You can use like to introduce an example of the set of things or people that you have just mentioned.

ex.en: The neglect that large cities like New York have received over the past 12 years is tremendous.
ex.zh: 诸如纽约这样的大城市在过去12年里所受到的忽视是巨大的。

e.en: You can use like to say that someone or something is in the same situation as another person or thing.

ex.en: It also moved those who, like me, are too young to have lived through the war.
ex.zh: 它也感动了那些跟我一样、太年轻而没有经历过战争的人。

d: v. 喜欢（like 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 受人喜爱的，被喜欢的（常作 well-liked 等复合词成分）；（社交媒体）被点赞的

e.en: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

ex.en: I looked down the hallway to room number nine.
ex.zh: 我沿着走廊向9号房间看过去。

ex.en: If you look, you'll see what was a lake.
ex.zh: 如果你看一下，就会看到那个曾经是湖的地方。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: Lucille took a last look in the mirror.
ex.zh: 露西尔往镜子里看了最后一眼。

e.en: If you look at a book, newspaper, or magazine, you read it fairly quickly or read part of it.

ex.en: You've just got to look at the last bit of Act Three.
ex.zh: 你只须浏览一下第三幕最后一小段。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: A quick look at Monday's newspapers shows that there's plenty of interest in foreign news.
ex.zh: 快速浏览一下星期一的报纸，就会发现许多有趣的国外新闻。

d: n. 看，注视；搜寻；表情；外表，样子
adj. 有……相貌的，有……样子的，看起来……的（常与形容词或副词连用构成复合形容词）
v. look 的现在分词；看，注视；面向，朝向；看起来像；注意；确保；常构成 looking for，表示寻找

e.en: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

ex.en: I looked down the hallway to room number nine.
ex.zh: 我沿着走廊向9号房间看过去。

ex.en: If you look, you'll see what was a lake.
ex.zh: 如果你看一下，就会看到那个曾经是湖的地方。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: Lucille took a last look in the mirror.
ex.zh: 露西尔往镜子里看了最后一眼。

e.en: If you look at a book, newspaper, or magazine, you read it fairly quickly or read part of it.

ex.en: You've just got to look at the last bit of Act Three.
ex.zh: 你只须浏览一下第三幕最后一小段。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: A quick look at Monday's newspapers shows that there's plenty of interest in foreign news.
ex.zh: 快速浏览一下星期一的报纸，就会发现许多有趣的国外新闻。

d: v. 看，瞧( look的过去式和过去分词 )；注意；面向；寻找

e.en: If you look in a particular direction, you direct your eyes in that direction, especially so that you can see what is there or see what something is like.

ex.en: I looked down the hallway to room number nine.
ex.zh: 我沿着走廊向9号房间看过去。

ex.en: If you look, you'll see what was a lake.
ex.zh: 如果你看一下，就会看到那个曾经是湖的地方。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: Lucille took a last look in the mirror.
ex.zh: 露西尔往镜子里看了最后一眼。

e.en: If you look at a book, newspaper, or magazine, you read it fairly quickly or read part of it.

ex.en: You've just got to look at the last bit of Act Three.
ex.zh: 你只须浏览一下第三幕最后一小段。

e.en: Look is also a noun.

ex.en: A quick look at Monday's newspapers shows that there's plenty of interest in foreign news.
ex.zh: 快速浏览一下星期一的报纸，就会发现许多有趣的国外新闻。

d: n. 相貌，容貌，外观（尤指漂亮的外表）
v. look 的第三人称单数一般现在时形式；表示“看，注视；寻找；显得，看上去”等含义（具体含义由搭配决定）

e.en: If someone loosens restrictions or laws, for example, they make them less strict or severe. 放宽 (限制或法律)

ex.en: Many business groups have been pressing the Federal Reserve to loosen interest rates.
ex.zh: 许多商业团体一直在施加压力要求联邦储备局放宽利率。

e.en: 放宽

ex.en: Domestic conditions did not justify a loosening of monetary policy.
ex.zh: 国内的条件不适宜放宽货币政策。

e.en: If someone or something loosens the ties between people or groups of people, or if the ties loosen, they become weaker. 疏远;

ex.en: The Federal Republic must loosen its ties with the United States.
ex.zh: 联邦共和国必须疏远同美国的关系。

ex.en: The deputy leader is cautious about loosening the links with the unions.
ex.zh: 副领导对疏远和工会的关系持谨慎态度。

e.en: If you loosen your clothing or something that is tied or fastened, you undo it slightly so that it is less tight or less firmly held in place.

ex.en: He reached up to loosen the scarf around his neck.
ex.zh: 他抬手松了松脖子上的围巾。

ex.en: Loosen the bolt so the bars can be turned.
ex.zh: 松开螺栓，这样那些木板就能被翻过来了。

d: v. （使）变松，（使）松开；放宽（限制、法律等）；使（关系）弱化，疏远；使（肠道）在排泄前畅通
【名】 （Loosen）（德）洛森（人名）

e.en: If you love someone, you feel romantically or sexually attracted to them, and they are very important to you.

ex.en: Oh, Amy, I love you.
ex.zh: 啊，埃米，我爱你。

e.en: Love is a very strong feeling of affection toward someone who you are romantically or sexually attracted to.

ex.en: Our love for each other has been increased by what we've been through together.
ex.zh: 我们对彼此的爱因我们共同经历的一切而增强。

ex.en: ...an old fashioned love story.
ex.zh: …一个老套的爱情故事。

e.en: You say that you love someone when their happiness is very important to you, so that you behave in a kind and caring way toward them.

ex.en: You'll never love anyone the way you love your baby.
ex.zh: 你永远不会像疼爱你的孩子那样爱任何人。

e.en: Love is the feeling that a person's happiness is very important to you, and the way you show this feeling in your behaviour toward them.

ex.en: My love for all my children is unconditional.
ex.zh: 我对我所有孩子的疼爱是无条件的。

d: v. 爱，热爱（love 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 受珍爱的，被爱的，心爱的（常作定语，如 loved ones 亲人）
abbr. 视线（Line of Sight）；月球轨道航天器（Lunar Orbiter Spacecraft）
n. （Los）人名；（匈）洛什；（俄、西、瑞典、塞、英）洛斯

e.en: A marina is a small harbour for small boats that are used for leisure. (停泊游艇的)

d: n. 码头，小艇船坞，游艇码头；散步道；（Marina）人名（女子名，用于罗、塞、葡、西、意、英），译作玛丽娜或马里纳

e.en: A match is an organized game of tennis, football, cricket, or some other sport.

ex.en: He was watching a football match.
ex.zh: 他正在看一场英式足球比赛。

e.en: A match is a small wooden stick with a substance on one end that produces a flame when you rub it along the rough side of a matchbox or a matchbook.

ex.en: ...a pack of cigarettes and a book of matches.
ex.zh: …一包香烟和一包火柴。

e.en: If something of a particular colour or design matches another thing, they have the same colour or design, or have a pleasing appearance when they are used together.

ex.en: "The shoes are too tight."—"Well, they do match your dress."
ex.zh: “这双鞋太紧了。” — “不过，它们确实和你的裙子相配。”

ex.en: All the chairs matched.
ex.zh: 所有的椅子都相配。

e.en: Match up means the same as .

ex.en: The pillow cover can match up with the sheets.
ex.zh: 这个枕巾可以和这些被单相配。

d: n. 比赛，竞赛；火柴；敌手，旗鼓相当的人；相配的人（或物）；非常相似的东西；婚姻，配偶；适合，匹配
v. 比得上，敌得过；使成对，使相配，使相称；与……一致，与……相符；使较量，使竞赛；适应，满足；等额提供

e.en: Someone's wife, husband, or sexual partner can be referred to as their mate. 配偶;

ex.en: He has found his ideal mate.
ex.zh: 他已经找到了理想的配偶。

e.en: An animal's mate is its sexual partner.

ex.en: The males guard their mates zealously.
ex.zh: 雄性动物热情地守护它们的交配对象。

e.en: a friend, usually of the same sex: often used between males in direct address (同性称呼语，常用于男性间)哥们; 老兄; 老弟;
an associate, colleague, fellow sharer, etc 同事;

ex.en: a classmate
a flatmate

d: n. 朋友，伙伴；同伴，同事；配偶，伴侣；配对物，一对中的一个；（男人之间常用）哥儿们，伙计；助手，下手；（船上的）大副；（美国海军的）军士；（国际象棋比赛中的）将死
v. （使）交配；连接，配备；（国际象棋中把对方）将死
【名】 （Mat）（日)蛏（姓），（西、意、塞）马特，（波黑）马特，（罗、俄）马泰（人名）

e.en: A movie is a series of moving pictures that have been recorded so that they can be shown in a theatre or on television. A movie tells a story, or shows a real situation.

ex.en: In the first movie Tony Curtis ever made he played a grocery clerk.
ex.zh: 在托尼·柯蒂斯制作的第一部影片中，他出演一名杂货店店员。

e.en: You can talk about the movies when you are talking about seeing a movie in a movie theatre.

d: n. 电影，影片（movie 的复数）；the movies 电影院；看电影

e.en: A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.

ex.en: The trial is due to begin next month.
ex.zh: 审判定于下个月开始。

ex.en: ...an exhibition which opens this month at the Guggenheim Museum.
ex.zh: …本月在古根海姆博物馆开幕的展览。

e.en: A month is a period of about four weeks. 1

ex.en: She was here for a month.
ex.zh: 她在这里呆了1个月。

ex.en: Over the next several months I met most of her family.
ex.zh: 在此后的几个月中，我见到了她大部分家人。

e.en: the period of time (sidereal month) taken by the moon to make one complete revolution around the earth, measured between two successive conjunctions with a distant star; 27.321 66 days (approximately 27 days, 7 hours, 43 minutes, 11 seconds) 恒星月(约27天7小时43分11秒)

the period of time (tropical month) taken by the moon to return to the same longitude after one complete revolution around the earth; 27.321 58 days (approximately 27 days, 7 hours, 43 minutes, 4.5 seconds) 分至月(约27天7小时43分4.5秒)

d: n. 月，月份；一个月的时间；数月，很长时间（months）

e.en: A meeting is an event in which a group of people come together to discuss things or make decisions.

ex.en: Can we have a meeting to discuss that?
ex.zh: 我们可以开个会来讨论那件事吗？

e.en: You can also refer to the people at a meeting as the meeting.

ex.en: The meeting decided that further efforts were needed.
ex.zh: 与会者认为进一步的努力是需要的。

e.en: When you meet someone, either by chance or by arrangement, you can refer to this event as a meeting.

ex.en: In January, 37 years after our first meeting, I was back in the studio with Dennis.
ex.zh: 1月份，在我们初次相遇的37年后，我和丹尼斯一起回到了工作室。

d: n. 会议，集会；偶遇，会面；与会者（the meeting）；运动会，赛马会；宗教聚会；交锋，比赛；交汇处
v. 会面；会合（meet 的现在分词形式）

e.en: An agreement is a formal decision about future action that is made by two or more countries, groups, or people.

ex.en: It looks as though a compromise agreement has now been reached.
ex.zh: 看起来好像现在已经达成了一个妥协协议。

e.en: Agreement on something is a joint decision that a particular course of action should be taken.

ex.en: A spokesman said, however, that the two men had not reached agreement on the issues discussed.
ex.zh: 但是，一位发言人说这两个人对讨论的问题还未达成共识。

e.en: Agreement with someone means having the same opinion as they have.

ex.en: The judge kept nodding in agreement.
ex.zh: 法官不断点头表示同意。

e.en: If you are in agreement with someone, you have the same opinion as they have.

d: n. 协议，协定，契约；共识；应允，同意；（在数、性或人称方面的）一致

e.en: Environmental means concerned with the protection of the natural world of land, sea, air, plants, and animals.

ex.en: Environmental groups plan to stage public protests during the conference.
ex.zh: 各环保组织计划在会议期间举行一些公众抗议行动。

e.en: 环保地

ex.en: ...the high price of environmentally friendly goods.
ex.zh: …环保商品的高昂价格。

e.en: Environmental means relating to or caused by the surroundings in which someone lives or something exists.

ex.en: It protects against environmental hazards such as wind and sun.
ex.zh: 它防范诸如狂风和烈日等环境危害。

d: adj. 自然环境的，生态环境的；环保的，生态环境保护的；与周围环境有关的，由生存环境引起的

e.en: Someone's environment is all the circumstances, people, things, and events around them that influence their life.

ex.en: Students in our schools are taught in a safe, secure environment.
ex.zh: 我校学生在安全无忧的环境中接受教育。

ex.en: The moral characters of men are formed not by heredity but by environment.
ex.zh: 人的品德不是由遗传而是由环境形成的。

e.en: Your environment consists of the particular natural surroundings in which you live or exist, considered in relation to their physical characteristics or weather conditions.

ex.en: ...a safe environment for marine mammals.
ex.zh: …一个适合海洋哺乳动物的安全环境。

e.en: The environment is the natural world of land, sea, air, plants, and animals.

ex.en: ...persuading people to respect the environment.
ex.zh: …劝人们重视自然环境。

d: n. 自然环境，生态环境；周围状况，条件；工作平台，软件包

e.en: Funds are amounts of money that are available to be spent, especially money that is given to an organization or person for a particular purpose. (尤指为特定目的而给予某组织的)

ex.en: The concert will raise funds for research into AIDS.
ex.zh: 这场音乐会将为艾滋病研究筹集资金。

e.en: A fund is an amount of money that is collected or saved for a particular purpose. (为特定目的而筹集或保留的)

ex.en: ...a scholarship fund for undergraduate engineering students.
ex.zh: …一笔用于工程学本科生的奖学金专项资金。

e.en: When a person or organization funds something, they provide money for it.

ex.en: The Bush Foundation has funded a variety of faculty development programmes.
ex.zh: 布什基金会已经资助了各种教职工发展项目。

ex.en: The airport is being privately funded by a construction group.
ex.zh: 该机场正由一建筑集团私家资助。

d: n. 基金，专款；资金，钱款；基金会；储备量
v. 资助，为……提供资金
【名】 （Fund)）（德）丰德（人名）

e.en: You can refer to the political issues that are important at a particular time as an agenda. (政治)

ex.en: Does television set the agenda on foreign policy?
ex.zh: 电视安排了有关外交政策的议题了吗？

e.en: An agenda is a list of the items that have to be discussed at a meeting.

ex.en: This is sure to be an item on the agenda next week.
ex.zh: 这必将成为下周议事日程上的一项议题。

d: n. 待议事项，议事日程；（政治）议题；秘密计划，秘密目标
n. 安徒生（丹麦的童话作家）

e.en: The climate of a place is the general weather conditions that are typical of it.

ex.en: ...the hot and humid climate of Florida.
ex.zh: …佛罗里达炎热潮湿的气候。

e.en: You can use climate to refer to the general atmosphere or situation somewhere. 氛围;

ex.en: The economic climate remains uncertain.
ex.zh: 经济气候依然是不确定。

ex.en: ...the existing climate of violence and intimidation.
ex.zh: … 现有的暴力与恐吓的氛围。

d: n. 气候；气候区；氛围，局势

e.en: A convention is a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

ex.en: It's just a social convention that men don't wear skirts.
ex.zh: 男人不穿裙子仅仅是一个社会习俗。

e.en: In art, literature, or the theatre, a convention is a traditional method or style.

ex.en: We go offstage and come back for the convention of the encore.
ex.zh: 按照惯例，当要求我们再唱一次的时候，我们得先下台然后再返回台上。

e.en: A convention is an official agreement between countries or groups of people.

ex.en: ...the U.N. convention on climate change.
ex.zh: …关于气候变化的联合国公约。

e.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group.

ex.en: ...the annual convention of the Society of Professional Journalists.
ex.zh: …职业新闻工作者协会的年会。

d: n. convention 的复数：惯例，习俗，社会常规；会议，大会；公约，协定；（文学、艺术或戏剧中的）传统手法；[计]约定，规范

e.en: If you fail to do something that you were trying to do, you are unable to do it or do not succeed in doing it.

ex.en: The party failed to win the election.
ex.zh: 该政党未能赢得选举。

ex.en: He failed in his attempt to take control of the company.
ex.zh: 他的掌控这家公司的企图失败了。

e.en: If an activity, attempt, or plan fails, it is not successful.

ex.en: We tried to develop plans for them to get along, which all failed miserably.
ex.zh: 我们设法制定出让他们相处融洽的计划，但都惨败了。

ex.en: He was afraid the revolution they had started would fail.
ex.zh: 他担心他们发起的革命会失败。

e.en: If someone or something fails to do a particular thing that they should have done, they do not do it.

ex.en: Some schools fail to require any homework.
ex.zh: 有些学校没有布置任何家庭作业。

ex.en: He failed to file tax returns for 1982.
ex.zh: 他没有填报1982年的纳税申报单。

e.en: If something fails, it stops working properly, or does not do what it is supposed to do.

ex.en: The lights mysteriously failed, and we stumbled around in complete darkness.
ex.zh: 灯神秘地熄灭了，我们在完全的黑暗中跌跌撞撞。

d: v. 失败；未能做到，未能做；辜负，使失望；不及格，未能通过；出故障，失灵；衰弱，衰退；破产，倒闭；歉收；不下雨，下雨少；忘记
n. 不及格；过失，失败
【名】 （Fail）（葡、捷）法伊尔，（法）法伊（人名）

e.en: If you deliver something somewhere, you take it there.

ex.en: The Canadians plan to deliver more food to southern Somalia.
ex.zh: 加拿大人计划向索马里南部运送更多的食物。

e.en: If you deliver something that you have promised to do, make, or produce, you do, make, or produce it. 实现;

ex.en: They have yet to show that they can really deliver working technologies.
ex.zh: 他们仍需证明他们确实能够实现可用的技术。

ex.en: The question is, can he deliver?
ex.zh: 问题是他能履行吗？

e.en: If you deliver a lecture or speech, you give it in public.

ex.en: The president will deliver a speech about schools.
ex.zh: 校长将发表关于学校的演讲。

e.en: When someone delivers a baby, they help the woman who is giving birth to the baby. 给 (产妇)

ex.en: Although we'd planned to have our baby at home, we never expected to deliver her ourselves!
ex.zh: 尽管我们是打算在家生孩子，可我们从未想过要自己给她接生!

d: v. 投递，运送；履行，兑现；交付，移交；发表，宣布；接生，分娩；解救，拯救；投掷，击打；（法官或法庭）宣布（判决）；拉（选票）；发行，发布（计算机程序）；处理

e.en: In a series of events, things, or people, the final one is the last one.

ex.en: Astronauts will make a final attempt today to rescue a communications satellite from its useless orbit.
ex.zh: 宇航员们今天将做最后一次尝试，把一颗通讯卫星从它无用的轨道上拯救出来。

ex.en: This is the fifth and probably final day of testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee.
ex.zh: 这是第5天，也可能是最后一天在参议院司法委员会面前作证。

e.en: Final means happening at the end of an event or series of events.

ex.en: You must have been on stage until the final curtain.
ex.zh: 你肯定是在台上一直呆到终场。

e.en: If a decision or someone's authority is final, it cannot be changed or questioned.

ex.en: The judges' decision is final.
ex.zh: 该法官的判决是不可更改的。

e.en: The final is the last game or contest in a series and decides who is the winner.

ex.en: ...the Gold Cup final.
ex.zh: …金杯决赛。

d: adj. 最终的，结束的；(出现次序)最后的，末尾的；决定性的，不可变更的；无比的，极度的
n. 决赛；期末考试，课程终结考试；主调音；当日报纸的末版；（飞机进入着陆跑道的）最终边，第五边
n. 实施，执行

e.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

ex.en: There are a number of distinguishing characteristics by which you can identify a Hollywood epic.
ex.zh: 通过其诸多与众不同的特点,你可以识别出好莱坞的史诗影片。

e.en: If you identify someone or something, you name them or say who or what they are.

ex.en: Police have already identified 10 murder suspects.
ex.zh: 警方已经确认了10名谋杀嫌疑犯。

e.en: If you identify something, you discover or notice its existence. 发现;

ex.en: Scientists claim to have identified chemicals produced by certain plants which have powerful cancer-fighting properties.
ex.zh: 科学家们声称已经发现某些植物产生的化学物质有强大的抗癌功能。

e.en: If a particular thing identifies someone or something, it makes them easy to recognize, by making them different in some way. 是…的标志;

ex.en: She wore a little nurse's hat on her head to identify her.
ex.zh: 她头上戴了一顶小护士帽，这使她易于辨认。

d: adj. 被识别的；经鉴定的；被认同的
v. 鉴定；辨认；认同；被认为与…等同（identify 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that is important is very significant, is highly valued, or is necessary.

ex.en: The most important thing in my life was my career.
ex.zh: 我生活中最重要的部分是我的事业。

ex.en: It's important to answer her questions as honestly as you can.
ex.zh: 重要的是你要尽可能如实地回答她的问题。

e.en: 重要地

ex.en: I was hungry, and, more importantly, my children were hungry.
ex.zh: 我饿了，更重要的是，我的孩子们饿了。

e.en: Someone who is important has influence or power within a society or a particular group.

ex.en: ...an important figure in the media world.
ex.zh: …一位传媒界有势力的人物。

d: adj. 重要的，重大的；（人）影响很大的，权威的；大量的，许多的；自负的，自命不凡的

e.en: The morning is the part of each day between the time that people usually wake up and 12 o'clock noon or lunchtime. 早晨;

ex.en: During the morning your guide will take you around the city.
ex.zh: 上午导游将带你们逛逛这座城市。

ex.en: On Sunday morning Bill was woken by the telephone.
ex.zh: 周日早晨，比尔被电话吵醒了。

e.en: If you refer to a particular time in the morning, you mean a time between 12 o'clock midnight and 12 o'clock noon. 从子夜12:00到中午12:00

ex.en: I often stayed up until two or three in the morning.
ex.zh: 我经常熬夜到凌晨两三点钟。

e.en: If you say that something will happen in the morning, you mean that it will happen during the morning of the following day.

ex.en: I'll fly it to St Louis in the morning.
ex.zh: 我会在明天上午把它空运到圣路易斯。

e.en: If you say that something happens morning, noon and night, you mean that it happens all the time. 从早到晚;

ex.en: You get fit by playing the game, day in, day out, morning, noon and night.
ex.zh: 每日坚持做这项运动，你就会变得健壮。

d: n. 早晨，上午，早上；黎明，破晓，清早；初期，开端（多用于文学或比喻）

e.en: Negotiations are formal discussions between people who have different aims or intentions, especially in business or politics, during which they try to reach an agreement. (尤指商业或政治上的)

ex.en: Warren said, "We have had meaningful negotiations and I believe we are very close to a deal."
ex.zh: 沃伦说：“我们已经进行了富有意义的谈判，我相信我们很快就能达成协议。”

d: n. 谈判，磋商（negotiation 的复数）

e.en: A planet is a large, round object in space that moves around a star. The Earth is a planet.

ex.en: The picture shows six of the nine planets in the solar system.
ex.zh: 这张图片展示太阳系9个行星中的6个行星。

d: n. 行星；地球（the planet）；命运星辰
【名】 （Planet）普拉内特（人名）

e.en: The resources of an organization or person are the materials, money, and other things that they have and can use in order to function properly.

ex.en: Some families don't have the resources to feed themselves adequately.
ex.zh: 一些家庭没有钱填饱肚子。

e.en: A country's resources are the things that it has and can use to increase its wealth, such as coal, oil, or land.

ex.en: ...resources like coal, tungsten, oil, and copper.
ex.zh: …像煤、钨、石油和铜等资源。

d: n. 资源，物力，财力（resource 的复数）；自然资源（natural resources）；人力资源（human resources）；人事部门（Human Resources）；（计算机）系统资源
v. 向……提供资源，尤指资金（resource 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Reform consists of changes and improvements to a law, social system, or institution. A reform is an instance of such a change or improvement. 改革;

ex.en: The party embarked on a programme of economic reform.
ex.zh: 这个政党开始了一个经济改革的计划。

e.en: If someone reforms something such as a law, social system, or institution, they change or improve it. 改革;

ex.en: ...his plans to reform the country's economy.
ex.zh: …他改革国家经济的计划。

e.en: When someone reforms or when something reforms them, they stop doing things that society does not approve of, such as breaking the law or drinking too much alcohol. 改造;

ex.en: When his court case was coming up, James promised to reform.
ex.zh: 当他的案件即将被审理时，詹姆斯承诺要改过自新。

e.en: 改过自新的

ex.en: ...a reformed alcoholic.
ex.zh: …一个改过自新的酗酒者。

d: v. 改革，革新；改邪归正，改造；（石油炼制）重整
n. 改革，改良
adj. 犹太教改革（仅保留犹太教部分的传统信条和习俗）（Reform）

e.en: If something is right, it is correct and agrees with the facts.

ex.en: That's absolutely right.
ex.zh: 那是完全正确的。

ex.en: Clocks never told the right time.
ex.zh: 时钟从来都不报正确的时间。

e.en: Right is also an adverb.

ex.en: He guessed right about some things.
ex.zh: 他对有些事情猜对了。

e.en: If you do something in the right way or in the right place, you do it as or where it should be done or was planned to be done. 适当的;

ex.en: Walking, done in the right way, is a form of aerobic exercise.
ex.zh: 走路方法得当的话是一种有氧锻炼。

ex.en: They have computerized systems to ensure delivery of the right pizza to the right place.
ex.zh: 他们有计算机化的系统来确保把相应的比萨饼送到相应的地方。

e.en: Right is also an adverb. 适当地;

ex.en: To make sure I did everything right, I bought a fat instruction book.
ex.zh: 为了确保每件事情都做对，我买了一本厚厚的说明书。

d: adj. 符合道德的，正当的；正确的，真实的；（人、物）合适的，般配的；（意见，判断）对的；右边的，右侧的；（状态或情况）健康的，正常的； 十足的，真正的（用于强调某人或某物多么糟糕）；正面的，外面的；时尚的，上流社会的；（人或政党）支持保守观点的，右翼的
v. 纠正，矫正；补救，扭转；把（尤指小船）扶正，使直立
n. 正当，公正；正当的要求，权利；版权，发行权（rights）；右边，右方（the right）；右拐，右转弯；右边的路（或入口）；（足球等运动）右外场；部队的右翼；右翼组织，右派政党（the right/the Right）；右翼人士的立场，右翼立场（the right）；右手拳
adv. （地方、位置或时间）正好，就在；直接地，径直地；一直地，完全地；立即，毫不耽搁；正确地，确切地；顺利，正常；在右面，向右边；（政治上）右倾地；用右手地；彻底地，十足地

e.en: Saturday is the day after Friday and before Sunday.

ex.en: He called her on Saturday morning at the studio.
ex.zh: 他星期六早上在工作室给她打电话。

ex.en: Every Saturday dad made a beautiful pea and ham soup.
ex.zh: 每个星期六爸爸都做一道鲜美的豌豆火腿汤。

d: n. 星期六，周六

e.en: A significant amount or effect is large enough to be important or affect a situation to a noticeable degree. 重大的;

ex.en: Most 11-year-olds are not encouraged to develop reading skills; a small but significant number are illiterate.
ex.zh: 大多数11岁的儿童没有被鼓励去培养阅读技能。有为数不多、但足以引起人们注意的数目的儿童是文盲。

e.en: 重大地;

ex.en: The number of Senators now supporting him had increased significantly.
ex.zh: 现在支持他的参议员人数已经显著增加了。

e.en: A significant fact, event, or thing is one that is important or shows something. 重要的;

ex.en: I think it was significant that he never knew his own father.
ex.zh: 我想他从不了解自己的父亲这一点就很说明问题。

e.en: 重要地;

ex.en: Significantly, the company recently opened a huge shop in Atlanta.
ex.zh: 重要的是，这家公司最近在亚特兰大开了一家大商店。

d: adj. 显著的，相当数量的；重要的，意义重大的； 别有含义的，意味深长的
n. 象征，有意义的事物

e.en: A summit is a meeting at which the leaders of two or more countries discuss important matters.

ex.en: ...next week's Washington summit.
ex.zh: …下周的华盛顿峰会。

e.en: The summit of a mountain is the top of it. (山)

ex.en: He made it to the summit of Kilimanjaro before collapsing.
ex.zh: 他成功登上乞力马扎罗山峰顶后倒下了。

d: n. summit 的复数：山顶，顶峰（山或高地的最高点）；政治峰会，首脑会议（国家领导人或政府首脑之间的高层次会议）；顶点，巅峰（最高水平、程度或发展阶段）。

e.en: You can refer to countries as states, particularly when you are discussing politics. (政治上所指的)

ex.en: Mexico is a secular state and does not have diplomatic relations with the Vatican.
ex.zh: 墨西哥是个非宗教国家，和梵蒂冈没有外交关系。

e.en: Some large countries such as the U.S. are divided into smaller areas called states. (美国等大国的)

ex.en: Leaders of the Southern states are meeting in Louisville.
ex.zh: 南部各州的领导人们正在路易斯维尔会晤。

e.en: The U.S. is sometimes referred to as the States.

ex.en: She bought it last year in the States.
ex.zh: 她去年在美国买了它。

e.en: You can refer to the government of a country as the state.

ex.en: The state does not collect enough revenue to cover its expenditure.
ex.zh: 政府没有征到足够的税来支付它的费用。

d: n. 状态，状况；国家；州，邦（state 的复数）；（非正式） the States：美国
vt. 陈述，说明（state 的第三人称单数）；规定，公布，载明（state 的第三人称单数）；表现（主题，旋律）（state 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A track is a rough, unpaved road or path. (崎岖不平的)

ex.en: We set off once more, over a rough mountain track.
ex.zh: 我们又一次出发了，走在一条崎岖不平的山间小路上。

e.en: A track is a piece of ground, often oval-shaped, that is used for races involving running, cars, bicycles, horses, or dogs called greyhounds.

ex.en: ...the athletics track.
ex.zh: …那条运动员跑道。

e.en: Railway tracks are the rails that a train travels along.

ex.en: A cow stood on the tracks.
ex.zh: 一头奶牛站在铁轨上。

e.en: A track is one of the songs or pieces of music on a CD, record, or tape. (录制在CD、唱片或磁带上的) 一首歌曲;

ex.en: I only like two of the ten tracks on this CD.
ex.zh: 我只喜欢这张CD上的10首歌曲中的2首。

d: n. 小道，小径；踪迹，足迹，车辙；（铁路的）轨道；（窗帘、推拉门等的）滑竿，滑轨；（火车站的）站台；赛道，跑道；（移动的）路径，方向；（唱片或光盘等上的）歌曲，曲子；音轨，声道；（推土机等的）履带；径赛运动，田径运动；（同龄学生依智力编排的）班，组；思路，行为方式；（分轨制教育的）课程；（机动车辆轮胎的横向）轮距
v. 追查，追踪；（尤指用特殊电子设备）跟踪；记录……的进展；跟踪摄影，移动摄影；（录制设备的移动部件）运转正常；把（学生）按能力分班（或组）；留下（脏）足迹；（以某方式或沿某方向）移动；跟随（利率，股价等）；（电子）统调；从岸上拉（独木舟）前进
n. 埃里温（亚美尼亚共和国首都，亦译耶烈万）

e.en: An activist is a person who works to bring about political or social changes by campaigning in public or working for an organization.

ex.en: The police say they suspect the attack was carried out by animal rights activists.
ex.zh: 警方说他们怀疑这次袭击是由保护动物权利的激进分子实施的。

ex.en: Dobson blames activist judges for undermining families with favourable gay-marriage rulings.
ex.zh: 多布森责备激进派法官们通过赞成同性婚姻的裁决破坏家庭。

d: n. 积极分子（activist 的复数）；活动分子

e.en: You use in addition when you want to mention another item connected with the subject you are discussing.

ex.en: The web site provides regional weather reports, a shipping forecast and gale warnings. In addition, visitors can download satellite images of the U.S.
ex.zh: 这个网站提供地区天气报道、出航预测和大风警报。另外，访客可以下载美国的卫星图像。

e.en: An addition to something is a thing which is added to it.

ex.en: This is a fine book; a worthy addition to the series.
ex.zh: 这是一本好书——是对这套丛书有价值的增补。

e.en: An  addition is a new room or building which is added to an existing building or group of buildings.

ex.en: The couple said they spent $20,000 on building an addition to their kitchen.
ex.zh: 这对夫妻说他们花了2万美元扩建他们的厨房。

e.en: The addition of something is the fact that it is added to something else.

ex.en: It was completely refurbished in 1987, with the addition of a picnic site.
ex.zh: 它于1987年被完全翻修，增添了一个野餐场所。

d: n. 附加物，新增物（addition 的复数）；（建筑，美式英语）扩建部分，增建部分；（会计/财务）固定资产增加额
n. ally 的复数形式，指盟友，盟国，支持者；the Allies 指（第二次世界大战时的）同盟国；（第一次世界大战时的）协约国
v. ally 的第三人称单数形式，结盟，联合（常与 with 连用）

e.en: If you aim for something or aim to do something, you plan or hope to achieve it.

ex.en: He said he would aim for the 100 metre world record at the world championships in August.
ex.zh: 他说他将以在8月举行的世界锦标赛上打破100米世界纪录为目标。

ex.en: Businesses will have to aim at long-term growth.
ex.zh: 企业必须以长期增长为目标。

e.en: If you aim to do something, you decide or want to do it.

ex.en: I didn't aim to get caught.
ex.zh: 我并不想被抓到。

e.en: If your actions or remarks are aimed at a particular person or group, you intend that the person or group should notice them and be influenced by them.

ex.en: His message was aimed at the undecided middle ground of Israeli politics.
ex.zh: 他所传达的信息针对的是以色列政坛中尚未表态的中间派。

e.en: If you aim a weapon or object at something or someone, you point it toward them before firing or throwing it.

ex.en: When he appeared again, he was aiming the rifle at Wade.
ex.zh: 他再次出现时，他正将步枪瞄准维德。

ex.en: ...a missile aimed at the arms factory.
ex.zh: …一枚瞄准了军工厂的导弹。

d: n. 目标，目的；瞄准，对准；枪法，击中目标的能力
v. 瞄准，对准；旨在，致力于；针对，指向

e.en: If people are agreed on something, they have reached a joint decision on it or have the same opinion about it.

ex.en: Okay, so are we agreed on going north?
ex.zh: 好吧，那么我们同意了向北走吗？

d: adj. 同意的，意见一致的；商定的，议定的，约定的
v. 同意，赞成（agree 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: An area is a particular part of a town, a country, a region, or the world.

ex.en: ...the large number of community groups in the area.
ex.zh: …该地区大量的社团。

ex.en: The survey was carried out in both urban and rural areas.
ex.zh: 该调查在城市和乡村地区都开展了。

e.en: Your area is the part of a town, country, or region where you live. An organization's area is the part of a town, country, or region that it is responsible for. 居住区域;

ex.en: Local authorities have been responsible for the running of schools in their areas.
ex.zh: 地方政府一直负责其辖区内各校的运作。

e.en: A particular area is a piece of land or part of a building that is used for a particular activity. (作某用途的)

ex.en: ...a picnic area.
ex.zh: …一个野餐区。

e.en: An area is a particular place on a surface or object, for example, on your body.

ex.en: You will notice that your baby has two soft areas on the top of his head.
ex.zh: 你会注意到你孩子的头顶有两个柔软的部位。

d: n. 区域，领域；面积（area 的复数）
n. 阿拉伯半岛（亚洲西南部，等于 Arabian Peninsula）

e.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them.

ex.en: He appealed to voters to go to the polls tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他呼吁选民们明天去投票站。

ex.en: He will appeal to the state for an extension of unemployment benefits.
ex.zh: 他将呼吁国家延长失业救济。

e.en: If you appeal a decision to someone in authority, you formally ask them to change it.

ex.en: We intend to appeal the verdict.
ex.zh: 我们打算对此裁决提出申诉。

e.en: If something appeals to you, you find it attractive or interesting.

ex.en: On the other hand, the idea appealed to him.
ex.zh: 另一方面，这个主意对他有吸引力。

e.en: An appeal is a serious and urgent request.

ex.en: He has a message from King Fahd, believed to be an appeal for Arab unity.
ex.zh: 他有个来自法赫德国王的口信，相信是对阿拉伯团结的呼吁。

d: v. 呼吁（appeal 的过去式和过去分词），恳求，求助；上诉，申诉，诉请；吸引，使感兴趣
n. 阿根廷（南美洲南部国家）；水珍鱼属（水珍鱼科的模式属）

e.en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

ex.en: The committee is concerned about players' behaviour, especially arguing with referees.
ex.zh: 该委员会担心运动员的表现，尤其担心他们与裁判争吵。

e.en: If you argue with someone about something, you discuss it with them, with each of you giving your different opinions.

ex.en: He was arguing with the king about the need to maintain the cavalry at full strength.
ex.zh: 他在和国王讨论保留骑兵全部兵力的必要性。

ex.en: They are arguing over foreign policy.
ex.zh: 他们在讨论外交政策。

e.en: If you tell someone not to argue with you, you want them to do or believe what you say without protest or disagreement.

ex.en: Don't argue with me.
ex.zh: 不要和我争辩。

e.en: If you argue that something is true, you state it and give the reasons why you think it is true.

ex.en: His lawyers are arguing that he is unfit to stand trial.
ex.zh: 他的律师们在辩称他不适宜受审。

d: v. argue 的过去式和过去分词；争吵；争论，讨论，辩论；论证，说理；争辩；主张；显示出，表明

e.en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

ex.en: The committee is concerned about players' behaviour, especially arguing with referees.
ex.zh: 该委员会担心运动员的表现，尤其担心他们与裁判争吵。

e.en: If you argue with someone about something, you discuss it with them, with each of you giving your different opinions.

ex.en: He was arguing with the king about the need to maintain the cavalry at full strength.
ex.zh: 他在和国王讨论保留骑兵全部兵力的必要性。

ex.en: They are arguing over foreign policy.
ex.zh: 他们在讨论外交政策。

e.en: If you tell someone not to argue with you, you want them to do or believe what you say without protest or disagreement.

ex.en: Don't argue with me.
ex.zh: 不要和我争辩。

e.en: If you argue that something is true, you state it and give the reasons why you think it is true.

ex.en: His lawyers are arguing that he is unfit to stand trial.
ex.zh: 他的律师们在辩称他不适宜受审。

d: v. 争吵，争辩，辩论（argue 的现在分词）
n. 争吵，争论（通常不可数）
n. 亚美尼亚（苏联加盟共和国名）

e.en: Baloney is the same as . 同bologna
If you say that an idea or statement is baloney, you disapprove of it and think it is foolish or wrong.

ex.en: That's a load of baloney.
ex.zh: 那是鬼话连篇。

d: n. 胡扯；熏肠；蠢货
int. 荒谬（表示怀疑的感叹词）
vt. 对……胡扯

e.en: a native or inhabitant of Armenia or an Armenian-speaking person elsewhere
of or relating to Armenia, its inhabitants, their language, or the Armenian Church 亚美尼亚人的; 亚美尼亚语的;

d: n. 亚美尼亚人；亚美尼亚语
adj. 亚美尼亚的；亚美尼亚人的；亚美尼亚语的
n. 阿塞拜疆（南高加索国家，东濒里海，首都巴库，正式全称阿塞拜疆共和国；曾为苏联加盟共和国之一）

e.en: A beautiful person is very attractive to look at.

ex.en: She was a very beautiful woman.
ex.zh: 她是个非常美丽的女人。

e.en: If you describe something as beautiful, you mean that it is very attractive or pleasing.

ex.en: New England is beautiful.
ex.zh: 新英格兰很迷人。

ex.en: It was a beautiful morning.
ex.zh: 那是个迷人的早晨。

e.en: 迷人地

ex.en: The children behaved beautifully.
ex.zh: 孩子们表现甚佳。

e.en: You can describe something that someone does as beautiful when they do it very skilfully.

ex.en: That's a beautiful shot!
ex.zh: 那一射真漂亮！

d: adj. 美丽的，漂亮的；令人愉悦的，美妙的；（完成得）出色的，极好的；仁慈的

e.en: If something attracts people or animals, it has features that cause them to come to it.

ex.en: The Cardiff Bay project is attracting many visitors.
ex.zh: 加的夫湾工程吸引着众多的参观者。

e.en: If someone or something attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them. If a particular quality attracts you to a person or thing, it is the reason why you like them.

ex.en: He wasn't sure he'd got it right, although the theory attracted him by its logic.
ex.zh: 他不能确定自己理解是否正确，尽管该理论的逻辑推理引起了他的兴趣。

e.en: If you are attracted to someone, you are interested in them sexually. (性的)

ex.en: In spite of her hostility, she was attracted to him.
ex.zh: 尽管心存敌意，她还是被他吸引住了。

e.en: 被吸引的

ex.en: He was nice looking, but I wasn't deeply attracted to him.
ex.zh: 他长得挺好看，但我并没有被他深深吸引。

d: v. （attract 的第三人称单数形式）吸引，引起兴趣；产生吸引力：使物体因某种特性而相互靠近；引起（注意力、支持、资金等）；使人产生好感或爱慕（常用被动结构 be attracted to）

e.en: Blood is the red liquid that flows inside your body, which you can see if you cut yourself.

ex.en: His shirt was covered in blood.
ex.zh: 他的衬衫沾满了血。

e.en: You can use blood to refer to the race or social class of someone's parents or ancestors.

ex.en: There was Greek blood in his veins: his ancestors originally bore the name Karajannis.
ex.zh: 他有希腊血统——他的祖先原来姓卡拉扬尼斯。

e.en: If you say that there is bad blood between people, you mean that they have argued about something and dislike each other.

ex.en: There is, it seems, some bad blood between Mills and the Baldwins.
ex.zh: 米尔和鲍德温两家看上去好像有积怨。

e.en: If something violent and cruel is done in cold blood, it is done deliberately and in an unemotional way.

ex.en: The crime had been committed in cold blood.
ex.zh: 这起案件是蓄意犯罪。

d: n. 血，血液；出身，血统；成员，人员；杀戮，流血；气质，脾气；纨绔子弟，花花公子；血样，血检
v. 使取得初次经验；用猎物的血涂（新手的）脸；让（猎狗）第一次尝血
【名】 （Blood）（英、西）布拉德（人名）
n. 卡洛斯（男子名）

e.en: When a hot liquid boils or when you boil it, bubbles appear in it and it starts to change into steam or vapour. 使…沸腾;

ex.en: I stood in the kitchen, waiting for the water to boil.
ex.zh: 我站在厨房里等水开。

ex.en: Boil the water in the saucepan and add the sage.
ex.zh: 把汤锅里的水烧开，然后放进鼠尾草叶。

e.en: When you boil a pot or a kettle, or put it on to boil, you heat the water inside it until it boils.

ex.en: He had nothing to do but boil the kettle and make the tea.
ex.zh: 他除了烧开水和沏茶以外无事可做。

e.en: When a pot is boiling, the water inside it has reached boiling point.

ex.en: The pot was boiling.
ex.zh: 锅里的水烧开了。

e.en: When you boil food, or when it boils, it is cooked in boiling water.

ex.en: Boil the chick peas, add garlic and lemon juice.
ex.zh: 把鹰嘴豆煮了，加进蒜和柠檬汁。

ex.en: I'd peel potatoes and put them on to boil.
ex.zh: 我会削土豆皮，然后把它们煮了。

d: v. （使）沸腾，煮沸，烧开；用开水煮；怒火中烧；（海，云）翻腾
n. 煮沸，沸腾；疖，皮下脓肿；激昂，兴奋；突然浮上来食鱼饵
【名】 （Boil）（美）博伊尔（人名）
adj. broad 的比较级；更宽的；更广大的；更广泛的

e.en: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.

ex.en: Fires were burning out of control in the centre of the city.
ex.zh: 火在市中心燃烧着,失去了控制。

ex.en: There was a fire burning in the fireplace.
ex.zh: 壁炉里有火正燃着。

e.en: If something is burning, it is on fire.

ex.en: When I arrived one of the vehicles was still burning.
ex.zh: 我到达时，其中的一辆车还在燃烧。

ex.en: The building housed 1,500 refugees and it burned for hours.
ex.zh: 这栋楼住着1500个难民，它烧了好几个小时。

e.en: 燃烧

ex.en: When we arrived in our village there was a terrible smell of burning.
ex.zh: 我们到达村子的时候，那里有一股难闻的燃烧的味道。

e.en: If you burn something, you destroy or damage it with fire.

ex.en: Protesters set cars on fire and burned a building.
ex.zh: 抗议者们焚烧汽车，烧毁了一栋建筑。

ex.en: Incineration plants should be built to burn household waste.
ex.zh: 应该建焚化厂来焚烧生活垃圾。

d: n. 络腮胡子
v. [外科]烧伤（burn 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A bunch of people is a group of people who share one or more characteristics or who are doing something together.

ex.en: My neighbours are a bunch of busybodies.
ex.zh: 我的邻居们都是一伙爱管闲事的人。

ex.en: We were a pretty inexperienced bunch of people really.
ex.zh: 我们实际上是一群相当没有经验的人。

e.en: A bunch of flowers is a number of flowers with their stalks held or tied together.

ex.en: He had left a huge bunch of flowers in her hotel room.
ex.zh: 他在她的宾馆房间里留了一大束花。

e.en: A bunch of bananas or grapes is a group of them growing on the same stem.

ex.en: Lili had fallen asleep clutching a fat bunch of grapes.
ex.zh: 莉莉手里抓着一大串葡萄睡着了。

e.en: A bunch of keys is a set of keys kept together on a metal ring.

ex.en: George took out a bunch of keys and went to work on the complicated lock.
ex.zh: 乔治掏出一串钥匙，去设法开这把复杂的锁。

d: n. 束，串，扎；一伙，一群；大量；发辫（bunches）；突起
v. 捆，扎，使集中；收紧，起褶
【名】 （Bunch）（英）邦奇（人名）

e.en: Classified information or documents are officially secret.

ex.en: He has a security clearance that allows him access to classified information.
ex.zh: 他有安全许可，这准许他接触机密。

d: adj. 分类的，归类的；机密的，保密的
n. 分类广告
v. 把……分类，把……分级；把（信息）归入保密级别（classify 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Commitment is a strong belief in an idea or system.

ex.en: ...commitment to the ideals of democracy.
ex.zh: …对民主理想的信奉。

e.en: A commitment is something which regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

ex.en: I've got a lot of commitments.
ex.zh: 我有很多要做的事。

e.en: If you make a commitment to do something, you promise that you will do it.

ex.en: We made a commitment to keep working together.
ex.zh: 我们作了承诺要继续在一起工作。

e.en: Commitment is the process of officially sending someone to a prison or a hospital. 送交 (监狱、医院)

d: n. 承诺，保证；不得不做的事；（资金、人力等的）投入，花费（commitment 的复数）

e.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

ex.en: Larry had concluded that he had no choice but to accept Paul's words as the truth.
ex.zh: 拉里断定他别无选择，只能相信保罗所说为实。

ex.en: So what can we conclude from this debate?
ex.zh: 那么从这场辩论中我们能推断出什么呢？

e.en: When you conclude, you say the last thing that you are going to say. 结束 (说话)

ex.en: "It's a waste of time," he concluded.
ex.zh: “这是浪费时间，”他最后说道。

e.en: When something concludes, or when you conclude it, you end it. 使…结束;

ex.en: The evening concluded with dinner and speeches.
ex.zh: 这个夜晚以晚宴和演讲告一段落。

e.en: If one person or group concludes an agreement, such as a treaty or business deal, with another, they arrange it. You can also say that two people or groups conclude an agreement. 达成 (协议)

ex.en: Mexico and the Philippines have both concluded agreements with their commercial bank creditors.
ex.zh: 墨西哥和菲律宾双方都与他们的商业银行债权人达成了协议。

d: v. conclude 的过去式和过去分词：结束，终止，以…告终；推断，作结论，断定；缔结，达成，订立（协议、条约、合同等）
adj. 已结束的，完结的，终止的；推论的

e.en: If you have confidence in someone, you feel that you can trust them.

ex.en: I have every confidence in you.
ex.zh: 我对你有完全的信任。

ex.en: This has contributed to the lack of confidence in the FDA.
ex.zh: 这导致了对食品与药品管理局信任的缺乏。

e.en: If you have confidence, you feel sure about your abilities, qualities, or ideas.

ex.en: The band is in excellent form and brimming with confidence.
ex.zh: 该乐队处于极好的状态，表现得充满信心。

e.en: If you can say something with confidence, you feel certain it is correct.

ex.en: I can say with confidence that such rumours were totally groundless.
ex.zh: 我可以很有把握地说这些传言完全没有根据。

e.en: If you tell someone something in confidence, you tell them a secret.

ex.en: We told you all these things in confidence.
ex.zh: 我们告诉你的这些事情都是保密的。

ex.en: Even telling Lois seemed a betrayal of confidence.
ex.zh: 甚至告诉洛伊斯似乎也是对保密的背叛。

d: n. 自信，信心；信任，信赖；把握，肯定；保密，机密；秘密，知心话

e.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

ex.en: The consensus among the world's scientists is that the world is likely to warm up over the next few decades.
ex.zh: 全世界科学家的共识是地球可能在未来几十年中变暖。

d: n. 一致看法，共识

e.en: Conservation is saving and protecting the environment. (对环境的)

ex.en: ...a four-nation regional meeting on elephant conservation.
ex.zh: …一次有关大象保护的4国区域性会议。

e.en: Conservation is saving and protecting historical objects or works of art such as paintings, sculptures, or buildings. (对历史文物、艺术品等的)

ex.en: Then he began his most famous work, the conservation and rebinding of the Book of Kells.
ex.zh: 接着，他就开始了他最著名的工作，即对《凯尔经》的维护和重新装订。

e.en: The conservation of a supply of something is the careful use of it so that it lasts for a long time.

ex.en: ...projects aimed at promoting energy conservation.
ex.zh: …旨在促进能源节约的项目。

d: n. 保护，保存；节约，防止浪费；守恒定律
基于一致性的
以共识为基础的

e.en: A conservationist is someone who cares very much about the conservation of the environment and who works to protect it.

ex.en: Conservationists say the law must be strengthened.
ex.zh: 环保主义者称必须加强法制。

d: n. （自然环境、野生动植物等）保护主义者，环保人士

e.en: A cop is a policeman or policewoman.

ex.en: Frank didn't like having the cops know where to find him.
ex.zh: 弗兰克不愿意让警察知道他的去向。

e.en: worth or value

ex.en: that work is not much cop

e.en: to seize or catch

d: n. 警察，警员（cop 的复数形式；非正式）；（纺织）纬管，纬纱管（cop 的复数形式）
v. 抓住，逮住；偷窃，偷取（cop 的第三人称单数形式；非正式）

e.en: A convention is a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

ex.en: It's just a social convention that men don't wear skirts.
ex.zh: 男人不穿裙子仅仅是一个社会习俗。

e.en: In art, literature, or the theatre, a convention is a traditional method or style.

ex.en: We go offstage and come back for the convention of the encore.
ex.zh: 按照惯例，当要求我们再唱一次的时候，我们得先下台然后再返回台上。

e.en: A convention is an official agreement between countries or groups of people.

ex.en: ...the U.N. convention on climate change.
ex.zh: …关于气候变化的联合国公约。

e.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group.

ex.en: ...the annual convention of the Society of Professional Journalists.
ex.zh: …职业新闻工作者协会的年会。

d: n. 习俗，惯例；大会，集会；公约，协定；（文学、艺术上的）传统手法，传统风格

e.en: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly. 破坏;

ex.en: He maliciously damaged a car with a baseball bat.
ex.zh: 他用棒球棍恶意地损坏了一辆汽车。

e.en: To damage something means to cause it to become less good, pleasant, or successful. 损害;

ex.en: ...the electoral chaos that damaged Florida's reputation.
ex.zh: …损害佛罗里达州声誉的选举骚乱。

e.en: 有损害性的

ex.en: The weakened currency could have damaging effects for the economy.
ex.zh: 货币贬值可能会对经济造成破坏性的影响。

e.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to an object. 破坏;

ex.en: The blast had serious effects with quite extensive damage to the house.
ex.zh: 爆炸影响严重，对房屋造成了大面积破坏。

d: adj. 有破坏性的，损害的，有害的；诽谤的
v. 破坏或损害（damage 的现在分词/动名词形式）
n. 戴维斯（男子名）

e.en: Something that degrades someone causes people to have less respect for them. 使贬低身份;

ex.en: ...the notion that pornography degrades women.
ex.zh: …色情作品贬低妇女的这种看法。

e.en: 贬低身份的;

ex.en: Mr. Porter was subjected to a degrading strip search.
ex.zh: 波特先生受到了有辱人格的脱衣搜身。

e.en: To degrade something means to cause it to get worse.

ex.en: ...the ability to meet human needs indefinitely without degrading the environment.
ex.zh: …满足人类无限需求但又不会使环境恶化的能力。

d: adj. 退化的，恶化的；（系统、设备等）降级的，被降级的；堕落的，道德败坏的，低级的
v. （degrade 的过去分词）使降级，贬低，降低……的身份；分解，降解；削减

e.en: If you talk about developing countries or the developing world, you mean the countries or the parts of the world that are poor and have few industries.

ex.en: In the developing world cigarette consumption is increasing.
ex.zh: 在发展中国家香烟消费正在增长。

d: adj. （国家）发展中的；正在生长的，正在发展的
v. （使）成长，发展；研制，研发；形成（观点）（develop 的现在分词）

e.en: Destruction is the act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed.

ex.en: ...an international agreement aimed at halting the destruction of the ozone layer.
ex.zh: …一项旨在停止对臭氧层的破坏的国际协议。

d: n. 破坏，摧毁

e.en: Development is the gradual growth or formation of something. 发育;

ex.en: ...an ideal system for studying the development of the embryo.
ex.zh: …研究胚胎发育的理想系统。

e.en: Development is the growth of something such as a business or an industry.

ex.en: He firmly believes that education and a country's economic development are key factors to progress.
ex.zh: 他坚信教育和一个国家的经济发展是通向进步的关键因素。

e.en: Development is the process of making an area of land or water more useful or profitable.

ex.en: The talks will focus on economic development of the region.
ex.zh: 会谈将聚焦于该地区的经济开发。

e.en: Development is the process or result of making a basic design gradually better and more advanced.

ex.en: It is spending $850M on research and development to get to the market place as soon as possible with faster microprocessors.
ex.zh: 研发上投入了$8.5亿，以期尽快将更快速的微处理器投放市场。

d: n. 发育，成长，发达；发展，进步；动态，进展；开发，研制；研制成果；（土地）开发；新建住宅区，新开发区；开始，出现；显影；出子布局

e.en: Digital systems record or transmit information in the form of thousands of very small signals.

ex.en: The new digital technology would allow a rapid expansion in the number of TV channels.
ex.zh: 新的数码技术可使电视频道的数量得以快速增多。

e.en: Digital devices such as watches or clocks give information by displaying numbers rather than by having a pointer which moves round a dial. Compare .

ex.en: ...a digital display.
ex.zh: …数字显示。

e.en: People sometimes refer to poorer people's lack of access to the latest computer technology as the digital divide.

ex.en: ...an attempt to reduce the "digital divide" between poor students who have no computers and those from well-off families who do.
ex.zh: …缩小没有电脑的贫困生和有电脑的富裕家庭学生之间的“数字鸿沟”的努力。

d: adj. 数字的，数码的；数字显示的；指头的，手指的
n. 数字电视，数位电视

e.en: Something that is disappointing is not as good or as large as you hoped it would be.

ex.en: The wine was excellent, but the meat was overdone and the vegetables disappointing.
ex.zh: 酒好极了，但是肉老了，蔬菜也令人失望。

e.en: 令人失望地

ex.en: Progress is disappointingly slow.
ex.zh: 进展慢得令人失望。

d: adj. 令人失望的，令人扫兴的
v. （使）失望（disappoint 的现在分词形式）
adj. 分裂的，有分歧的；分配的，分享的
v. （使）分开，分散；分配，分享；是……的分界线，分隔（divide 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A donor is someone who gives a part of their body or some of their blood to be used by doctors to help a person who is ill. 器官捐献者;

ex.en: Doctors removed the healthy kidney from the donor.
ex.zh: 医生从捐献者体内取出了健康的肾脏。

e.en: A donor is a person or organization who gives something, especially money, to a charity, organization, or country that needs it.

ex.en: Donor countries are becoming more choosy about which countries they are prepared to help.
ex.zh: 捐赠国对受赠国的选择变得更加慎重了。

e.en: Donor organs or parts are organs or parts of the body which people allow doctors to use to help people who are ill.

ex.en: ...the severe shortage of donor organs.
ex.zh: …捐献器官的严重匮乏。

d: n. 捐献者，捐赠者；（化学）供体；（物理）施主
adj. 捐献的
adj. 地球的；土地的，大地的，泥土的

e.en: If a job or action is easy, you can do it without difficulty or effort, because it is not complicated and causes no problems.

ex.en: The shower is easy to install.
ex.zh: 淋浴器易于安装。

ex.en: This is not an easy task.
ex.zh: 这不是项容易的任务。

e.en: 容易地

ex.en: Dress your child in layers of clothes you can remove easily.
ex.zh: 给你的孩子穿几层你能容易地脱掉的衣服。

e.en: If you describe an action or activity as easy, you mean that it is done in a confident, relaxed way. If someone is easy about something, they feel relaxed and confident about it.

ex.en: He was an easy person to talk to.
ex.zh: 他是个可以与之轻松交谈的人。

e.en: 轻松自如地

ex.en: They talked amiably and easily about a range of topics.
ex.zh: 他们亲切而又轻松地谈着一系列的话题。

d: adj. 容易的，不费力的；舒适的，自如的；随和的；轻浮的；平缓的
adv. 小心；容易地，悠闲地

e.en: An echo is a sound caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

ex.en: He listened and heard nothing but the echoes of his own voice in the cave.
ex.zh: 他听了听，除了自己声音在山洞里的回响什么都没听见。

e.en: If a sound echoes, it is reflected off a surface and can be heard again after the original sound has stopped.

ex.en: His feet echoed on the hardwood floor.
ex.zh: 他的脚步声在硬木地板上回响着。

e.en: In a place that echoes, a sound is reflected off a surface, and is repeated after the original sound has stopped.

ex.en: The room echoed.
ex.zh: 房间发出了回声。

ex.en: The corridor echoed with the barking of a dozen dogs.
ex.zh: 走廊里回荡着十几条狗的吠声。

e.en: If you echo someone's words, you repeat them or express agreement with their attitude or opinion.

ex.en: Their views often echo each other.
ex.zh: 他们的见解常常彼此附和。

d: n. 回声，回音，余音绕梁；重复，附和，共鸣；相似之处，再现；回声插入；（话语结构和内容的）重复；（桥牌）回声信号
v. 回响，发出回声；重复，附和

e.en: An ecosystem is all the plants and animals that live in a particular area together with the complex relationship that exists between them and their environment.

ex.en: ...the forest ecosystem.
ex.zh: …森林生态系统。

d: n. 生态系统（ecosystem 的复数）；由相互关联的产品、服务、用户等构成的网络体系
n. 厄瓜多尔（位于拉丁美洲）
能量消耗
adv. 在环境方面，有关环境地（常与 friendly、sound 等连用，表示“环保的，对生态环境无害的”）

e.en: An executive is someone who is employed by a business at a senior level. Executives decide what the business should do, and ensure that it is done.

ex.en: ...an advertising executive.
ex.zh: …一位广告执行总监。

e.en: The executive sections and tasks of an organization are concerned with the making of decisions and with ensuring that decisions are carried out.

ex.en: A successful job search needs to be as well organized as any other executive task.
ex.zh: 一次成功的寻职要像任何其他执行任务一样精心安排。

e.en: Executive goods are expensive products designed or intended for executives and other people at a similar social or economic level.

ex.en: ...an executive briefcase.
ex.zh: …一个高级公文包。

e.en: The executive committee or board of an organization is a committee within that organization that has the authority to make decisions and ensures that these decisions are carried out.

ex.en: They opted to put an executive committee in charge of the project rather than a single person.
ex.zh: 他们选择由一个执行委员会而非个人来负责这个项目。

d: adj. 行政的，有执行权的；高档的，豪华的；供主管人员使用的；（有关）经营管理的，领导的
n. 主管，经理；行政部门，执行委员会

e.en: An envoy is someone who is sent as a representative from one government or political group to another. 使者;

ex.en: A U.S. envoy is expected in the region this month to collect responses to the proposal.
ex.zh: 一位美国的代表本月将在这个地区收集对该提议的反馈意见。

e.en: An envoy is a diplomat in an embassy who is immediately below the ambassador in rank.
a brief dedicatory or explanatory stanza concluding certain forms of poetry, notably ballades (尤指歌谣的)

d: n. 使者，使节，（谈判等的）代表；公使（级别在大使之下）

e.en: To ensure something, or to ensure that something happens, means to make certain that it happens.

ex.en: We must ensure that all patients have access to high quality care.
ex.zh: 我们必须确保所有的病人都能够得到高质量的护理。

d: v. 确保，保证；保护，使安全

e.en: Existing is used to describe something that is now present, available, or in operation, especially when you are contrasting it with something that is planned for the future. 现有的;

ex.en: ...the need to improve existing products and develop new lines.
ex.zh: …改进现有产品和开发新生产线的需要。

ex.en: Existing timbers are replaced or renewed.
ex.zh: 现有的木材在被替换或更新。

d: adj. 现存的，现行的
v. 存在，实有；生活，生活方式（exist 的现在分词形式）

e.en: An expert is a person who is very skilled at doing something or who knows a lot about a particular subject. 专家;

ex.en: ...a yoga expert.
ex.zh: …一位瑜伽专家。

e.en: Someone who is expert at doing something is very skilled at it.

ex.en: The Japanese are expert at lowering manufacturing costs.
ex.zh: 日本人在降低生产成本方面很在行。

e.en: 在行地

ex.en: Shopkeepers expertly rolled spices up in bay leaves.
ex.zh: 店主在行地把各种香料卷进了月桂叶中。

e.en: If you say that someone has expert hands or an expert eye, you mean that they are very skilful or experienced in using their hands or eyes for a particular purpose.

ex.en: Harvey cured the pain with his own expert hands.
ex.zh: 哈维用他那行家之手治愈了那病痛。

d: n. 专家，行家，人才（expert 的复数）

e.en: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

ex.en: ...a workman who expects to lose his job in the next few weeks.
ex.zh: …一个预料会在接下来几周里失业的工人。

ex.en: The talks are expected to continue until tomorrow.
ex.zh: 会谈预料将持续到明天。

e.en: If you are expecting something or someone, you believe that they will be delivered to you or come to you soon, often because this has been arranged earlier. (常指因已安排而)

ex.en: I wasn't expecting a visitor.
ex.zh: 我没有预期会有访客。

e.en: If you expect something, or expect a person to do something, you believe that it is your right to have that thing, or the person's duty to do it for you.

ex.en: He wasn't expecting our hospitality.
ex.zh: 他没有期待我们的热情款待。

ex.en: I do expect to have some time to myself in the evenings.
ex.zh: 我真期待晚上能有点儿自己的时间。

e.en: If you tell someone not to expect something, you mean that the thing is unlikely to happen as they have planned or imagined, and they should not hope that it will.

ex.en: Don't expect an instant cure.
ex.zh: 别指望会有立竿见影的疗效。

ex.en: You cannot expect to like all the people you will work with.
ex.zh: 你不能指望喜欢所有和你一起工作的人。

d: v. 期待；预计；要求，指望；认为；怀孕

e.en: If you fiddle with an object, you keep moving it or touching it with your fingers.

ex.en: Harriet fiddled with a pen on the desk.
ex.zh: 哈丽雅特不停地摆弄桌上的一支钢笔。

e.en: If you fiddle with something, you change it in minor ways.

ex.en: She told Whistler that his portrait of her was finished and to stop fiddling with it.
ex.zh: 她告诉惠斯勒他为她画的肖像已经完成了，不要再改来改去了。

e.en: If you fiddle with a machine, you adjust it.

ex.en: He turned on the radio and fiddled with the knob until he got a talk show.
ex.zh: 他打开收音机，调动旋钮，直到他收到了一个谈话节目。

e.en: Some people call violins fiddles, especially when they are used to play folk music.

ex.en: Hardy played the fiddle at local dances.
ex.zh: 哈迪在当地的舞会上拉了小提琴。

d: v. （尤指厌烦或紧张地）不停摆弄；篡改，伪造；拉小提琴；略微变动；调整
n. 小提琴；欺诈，骗局；修理，调整；难事；（防止餐具在恶劣天气条件下滚落或滑落的）餐桌缘框

e.en: You use extremely in front of adjectives and adverbs to emphasize that the specified quality is present to a very great degree. 极端地;

ex.en: My mobile phone is extremely useful.
ex.zh: 我的手机极为有用。

ex.en: Three of them are working extremely well.
ex.zh: 他们中的3个人工作极其出色。

d: adv. 极度，非常

e.en: Facing is fabric which is stitched inside the edges of a piece of clothing in order to make them look neat and strengthen them. (衣物的)贴边;

d: v. face 的现在分词：面朝，面向，朝（某方向）；面对，面临（问题、困难等）；（难题等）直逼（某人）；给……加饰面（用……覆盖或涂抹表面）；（士兵）按口令朝特定方向转身
n. （衣服的）贴边，衬里；（建筑物的）饰面（材料）
adj. 面朝……的，朝向……的；对面的

e.en: When someone finances something such as a project or a purchase, they provide the money that is needed to pay for them.

ex.en: The fund has been used largely to finance the construction of federal prisons.
ex.zh: 该基金大部分已用于资助联邦监狱的建造。

e.en: Finance is also a noun.

ex.en: A United States delegation is in Japan seeking finance for a major scientific project.
ex.zh: 1个美国代表团正在日本为一个重大科研项目寻求资助。

e.en: Finance is the commercial or government activity of managing money, debt, credit, and investment. 金融;

ex.en: ...a major player in the world of high finance.
ex.zh: …高层金融界的大腕。

ex.en: The report recommends an overhaul of public finances.
ex.zh: 这份报告建议对公共财政进行彻底检视。

e.en: You can refer to the amount of money that you have and how well it is organized as your finances.

ex.en: Be prepared for unexpected news concerning your finances.
ex.zh: 对关于你财务状况的意外消息要做好准备。

d: n. 财政，金融；资金，财源；财务事务，经济情况
v. 提供资金；贷款购买，赊购
【名】 （Finance）（法）菲南斯（人名）

e.en: A firm is an organization which sells or produces something or which provides a service which people pay for.

ex.en: The firm's employees were expecting large bonuses.
ex.zh: 这家公司的雇员们正期待着大笔的奖金。

ex.en: ...a legal assistant at a Chicago law firm.
ex.zh: …一家芝加哥律师事务所的一名法律助理。

e.en: If something is firm, it does not change much in shape when it is pressed but is not completely hard.

ex.en: Fruit should be firm and in excellent condition.
ex.zh: 水果应该硬实且完好无损。

e.en: If someone's grip is firm or if they perform a physical action in a firm way, they do it with quite a lot of force or pressure but also in a controlled way.

ex.en: The quick handshake was firm and cool.
ex.zh: 那次迅速的握手有力而冷静。

e.en: 强有力地

ex.en: She held me firmly by the elbow and led me to my aisle seat.
ex.zh: 她使劲抓着我的胳膊肘，把我领到靠过道的座位上。

d: n. 公司，厂商（firm 的复数）
v. 变得坚实；使坚实（firm 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

ex.en: The research effort has focused on tracing the effects of growing levels of five compounds.
ex.zh: 研究集中跟踪5种化合物水平上升带来的影响。

ex.en: Today he was able to focus his message exclusively on the economy.
ex.zh: 今天他能够将重点聚焦在经济方面。

e.en: If you focus your eyes or if your eyes focus, your eyes adjust so that you can clearly see the thing that you want to look at. If you focus a camera, telescope, or other instrument, you adjust it so that you can see clearly through it. 使 (眼睛、相机、望远镜或其它仪器) 对焦;

ex.en: Kelly couldn't focus his eyes well enough to tell if the figure was male or female.
ex.zh: 凯利无法看清那个人影是男的还是女的。

ex.en: His eyes slowly began to focus on what looked like a small dark ball.
ex.zh: 他的眼睛开始慢慢聚焦到那个小黑球似的东西上。

e.en: If you focus rays of light on a particular point, you pass them through a lens or reflect them from a mirror so that they meet at that point. 把 (光线)

ex.en: Magnetic coils focus the electron beams into fine spots.
ex.zh: 磁线圈将电子束聚焦成细小的点。

e.en: The focus of something is the main topic or main thing that it is concerned with.

ex.en: The UN's role in promoting peace is increasingly the focus of international attention.
ex.zh: 联合国在促进和平方面的作用越来越成为国际关注的焦点。

ex.en: The new system is the focus of controversy.
ex.zh: 新系统是争议的焦点。

d: n. 重点，中心点；关注，注意；震源；目的，意图；焦距；病灶；调焦装置；目的明确，专注；（椭圆、抛物线等曲线的）焦点
v. 集中，关注；聚焦，调焦；以（句子的一部分）为焦点（或重心）
【名】 （Focus）（瑞典）福库斯 (人名)

e.en: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object. 合身;

ex.en: The sash, kimono, and other garments were made to fit a child.
ex.zh: 这些腰带、和服和其他衣服都做得适合孩子穿。

ex.en: She has to go to the men's department to find trousers that fit at the waist.
ex.zh: 她得去男装部找腰围合适的裤子。

e.en: If you are fitted for a particular piece of clothing, you try it on so that the person who is making it can see where it needs to be altered.

ex.en: She was being fitted for her wedding dress.
ex.zh: 她正在试穿她的结婚礼服。

e.en: If something fits somewhere, it can be put there or is designed to be put there. 合适于 (某地)

ex.en: ...a pocket computer which is small enough to fit into your pocket.
ex.zh: …一台小得足以放进你口袋里的袖珍电脑。

ex.en: He folded his long legs to fit under the table.
ex.zh: 他把腿弯起来伸到桌下。

e.en: If you fit something into a particular space or place, you put it there.

ex.en: ...she fitted her key in the lock.
ex.zh: …她把钥匙插进锁孔。

ex.en: Who could cut the millions of stone blocks and fit them together?
ex.zh: 谁能切割这数百万的石块并将它们垒在一起呢？

d: v. 适合，合身；适应，合得来；可容纳，装进；试穿（衣服）；和……相称，符合；为放置（于……）而设计；安置，安装（在某处）；安排时间会面，安排时间做（某事）；（疾病）发作
adj. 健康的，健壮的；合适的，适当的；合格的，胜任的；性感的；快要，就要
n. 适合，合身；匹配，相配；痉挛，昏厥；一阵，突发
【名】 （Fit）（捷、罗）菲特（人名）

e.en: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them because you want to go to the same place.

ex.en: We followed him up the steps into a large hall.
ex.zh: 我们跟他上了台阶，进入一个大厅。

ex.en: Please follow me, madam.
ex.zh: 夫人，请跟我来。

e.en: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them without their knowledge, in order to catch them or find out where they are going.

ex.en: She realized that the Mercedes was following her.
ex.zh: 她意识到那辆奔驰在跟踪她。

e.en: If you follow someone to a place where they have recently gone and where they are now, you go to join them there.

ex.en: He followed Janice to New York, where she was preparing an exhibition.
ex.zh: 他跟随贾妮丝去了纽约，她正在那儿准备一个展览。

e.en: An event, activity, or period of time that follows a particular thing happens or comes after that thing, at a later time. 在…后到来;

ex.en: ...the rioting and looting that followed the verdict.
ex.zh: …判决之后发生的暴乱和抢劫。

ex.en: Other problems may follow.
ex.zh: 其它问题也许会随之而来。

d: v. 跟着，跟随；跟踪；（时间或顺序）在……后；循着，沿着（道路等）；沿着……伸延；遵循，听从；仿效，追随；理解，明白；可以推断；注视，密切关注；信奉，信仰；（电影、书等）呈现，描述；从事（行业、职业）
n. 跟随，追随

e.en: A form of something is a type or kind of it.

ex.en: He contracted a rare form of cancer.
ex.zh: 他患上了一种罕见的癌症。

ex.en: I am against hunting in any form.
ex.zh: 我反对任何形式的狩猎。

e.en: When something can exist or happen in several possible ways, you can use form to refer to one particular way in which it exists or happens.

ex.en: They received a benefit in the form of a tax reduction.
ex.zh: 他们以减税的方式获得了收益。

e.en: The form of something is its shape.

ex.en: ...the form of the body.
ex.zh: …体型。

e.en: You can refer to something that you can see as a form if you cannot see it clearly, or if its outline is the clearest or most striking aspect of it.

ex.en: His form lay still under the blankets.
ex.zh: 他的身形一动不动地躺在毯子下面。

d: n. 形式；外形，形状；类型，种类；方式；表格（form 的复数）；（计算机）窗体；（语法）词形
v. 构成，组成；形成，产生；排列，组织；组建，创办；养成；塑造（form 的第三人称单数）
n. 搭便车

e.en: In games such as football or hockey, the goal is the space into which the players try to get the ball in order to score a point for their team.

ex.en: The Dragons had only one shot on goal.
ex.zh: 龙队只有一次射门。

e.en: In games such as football or hockey, a goal is when a player gets the ball into the goal, or the point that is scored by doing this.

ex.en: They scored five goals in the first half of the match.
ex.zh: 他们在上半场进了5个球。

e.en: Something that is your goal is something that you hope to achieve, especially when much time and effort will be needed.

ex.en: It's a matter of setting your own goals and following them.
ex.zh: 这是一个设定自己的目标并努力实现它们的问题。

d: n. 球门；进球得分；目标，目的；（旅行）目的地；（赛跑的）终点
v. 射门，射门得分

e.en: The function of something or someone is the useful thing that they do or are intended to do.

ex.en: The main function of the investment banks is to raise capital for industry.
ex.zh: 各投资银行的主要作用是为产业筹集资金。

e.en: A function is a large formal dinner or party. 宴会;

ex.en: ...a private function hosted by one of his students.
ex.zh: …由他的一个学生做东的一场私人宴会。

e.en: If a machine or system is functioning, it is working or operating.

ex.en: The authorities say the prison is now functioning normally.
ex.zh: 当局称该监狱现在在正常运转。

e.en: If someone or something functions as a particular thing, they do the work or fulfil the purpose of that thing. (作为某物)

ex.en: On weekdays, one third of the room functions as workspace.
ex.zh: 在工作日，这个房间的三分之一充当工作场所。

d: n. 功能，职责；宴会，典礼；函数，应变量；由其他事情造成的结果；子例行程序，子例程；官能团，功能团
v. 工作，运转；行使职责，发挥功能

e.en: You can use global to describe something that happens in all parts of the world or affects all parts of the world.

ex.en: ...a global ban on nuclear testing.
ex.zh: …一项全球性核试验禁令。

e.en: 全球地

ex.en: ...a globally familiar trade name.
ex.zh: …一个全球熟知的商标名。

e.en: A global view or vision of a situation is one in which all the different aspects of it are considered.

ex.en: ...a global vision of contemporary societies.
ex.zh: …对当代社会的全面认识。

d: adj. 全球的，全世界的；全面的，整体的；（计算机）全局的；球形的

e.en: When people, animals, and plants grow, they increase in size and change physically over a period of time.

ex.en: We stop growing at maturity.
ex.zh: 我们在成熟后就停止成长了。

e.en: If a plant or tree grows in a particular place, it is alive there.

ex.en: The station had roses growing at each end of the platform.
ex.zh: 车站月台两端生长着玫瑰。

e.en: If you grow a particular type of plant, you put seeds or young plants in the ground and take care of them as they develop.

ex.en: Lettuce was grown by the ancient Romans.
ex.zh: 莴苣是由古罗马人种植的。

e.en: When someone's hair grows, it gradually becomes longer. Your nails also grow. (毛发、指甲等)

ex.en: Then the hair began to grow again and I felt terrific.
ex.zh: 接着头发又长起来了，我感觉棒极了。

d: adj. 增长的，增加的
v. 长大，成长；成活，生长；栽种，种植（grow 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Happenings are things that happen, often in a way that is unexpected or hard to explain. (常指意外或难以解释的)

ex.en: The Budapest office plans to hire freelance reporters to cover the latest happenings.
ex.zh: 布达佩斯办事处计划聘用自由职业记者来报道最近发生的事件。

d: n. 事件，意外发生的事；偶发艺术，即兴艺术表演
adj. （非正式）热闹的，时髦的
v. happen 的现在分词：发生；（作为结果）出现；碰巧，偶然发生；偶然遇到或发现；使遭遇

e.en: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still. 使停住;

ex.en: They halted at a short distance from the house.
ex.zh: 他们停在离房子不远处。

e.en: When something such as growth, development, or activity halts or when you halt it, it stops completely. 使完全停止;

ex.en: Striking workers halted production at the auto plant yesterday.
ex.zh: 昨天，汽车厂的罢工工人完全停止了生产。

e.en: (esp of logic or verse) to falter or be defective (尤指逻辑或诗韵)有缺陷;
an interruption or end to activity, movement, or progress (活动、运动或进展的)中止;

d: v. （使）停止行进；阻止，中断；（口令）立定；跛行；（尤指逻辑或诗韵）有缺陷；踌躇，犹豫
n. 停止，中止；乡间小火车站（只有站台）；跛，瘸； 跛，瘸；（口令）立定
adj. 跛的，瘸的
【名】 （Halt）（美、德、英）哈尔特（人名）

e.en: You use the forms have and has with a past participle to form the present perfect tense of verbs.
e.zh: 后接过去分词，构成现在完成时态

ex.en: Alex has already gone.
ex.zh: 亚历克斯已经走了。

ex.en: What have you found so far?
ex.zh: 迄今为止，你发现了什么？

e.en: You use the form had with a past participle to form the past perfect tense of verbs. (had)
e.zh: 后接过去分词，构成过去完成时态

ex.en: When I met her, she had just returned from a job interview.
ex.zh: 我遇到她时，她刚刚从一次求职面试回来。

e.en: Have is used in question tags.

ex.en: You haven't sent her away, have you?
ex.zh: 你还没有把她送走，是吗？

e.en: You use have when you are confirming or contradicting a statement containing "have," "has," or "had," or answering a question. 代替前一句中的(have)、(has)或(had)
e.zh: 加上动词构成的词组，表示肯定或否定含义

ex.en: "You'd never seen the Marilyn Monroe film?"—"No I hadn't."
ex.zh: “你从来没看过玛丽莲•梦露的电影吗？”—“是的，从来没有。”

d: v. 有，拥有，具有（have 的现在分词／动名词）；接动作性名词表示进行、经历、吃、喝等；接过去分词构成现在分词的完成式，表示动作先于另一动作发生（已经……）；having to do sth 表示必须、不得不

e.en: A dune is a hill of sand near the ocean or in a desert.

ex.en: Large dunes make access to the beach difficult in places.
ex.zh: 在有些地方大沙丘使得靠近海滩很难。

d: n. （由风吹积而成的）沙丘

e.en: A matter is a task, situation, or event which you have to deal with or think about, especially one that involves problems.

ex.en: It was clear that she wanted to discuss some private matter.
ex.zh: 很明显她想讨论一些私事。

ex.en: Business matters drew him to Louisville.
ex.zh: 生意上的事情吸引他去路易斯维尔。

e.en: You use matters to refer to the situation you are talking about, especially when something is affecting the situation in some way.

ex.en: We have no objection to this change, but doubt that it will significantly improve matters.
ex.zh: 我们不反对这种变化，但怀疑这是否将明显地改善事态。

ex.en: If it would facilitate matters, I would be happy to come to New York.
ex.zh: 如果这有利于事态，我将乐意来纽约。

e.en: If you say that a situation is a matter of a particular thing, you mean that that is the most important thing to be done or considered when you are involved in the situation or explaining it.

ex.en: History is always a matter of interpretation.
ex.zh: 历史总是一个诠释的问题。

ex.en: Observance of the law is a matter of principle for us.
ex.zh: 遵守法律对于我们是一个原则问题。

e.en: Printed matter consists of books, newspapers, and other texts that are printed. Reading matter consists of things that are suitable for reading, such as books and newspapers. (印刷或阅读的)

ex.en: ...the government's plans to place a tax on printed matter.
ex.zh: …政府对印刷品征税的计划。

d: n. 事情，问题；事态，情况；困境，麻烦（the matter）；物质；材料，物品，东西；书面材料，印刷品；（身体感染部位排出的）脓，黄水；命题内容；（表示数量或时间之少）大约，左右；（法庭审问或证明的）事项，案件
v. 要紧，有关系；（伤口）化脓，流脓
【名】 （Matter）（英、法）马特，（西）马特尔（人名）
n. 中微子（neutrino 的复数）

e.en: A detector is an instrument which is used to discover that something is present somewhere, or to measure how much of something there is.

ex.en: ...a metal detector.
ex.zh: …一架金属探测器。

d: n. 探测器，检测器，侦测设备（detector 的复数）；（电子学）检波器

e.en: A particle of something is a very small piece or amount of it. 微粒;

ex.en: ...a particle of hot metal.
ex.zh: …热金属微粒。

ex.en: There is a particle of truth in his statement.
ex.zh: 在他的声明中只有极少的事实。

e.en: In physics, a particle is a piece of matter smaller than an atom such as an electron or a proton.

ex.en: ...the sub-atomic particles that make up matter.
ex.zh: …构成物质的次原子微粒。

d: n. 微粒；粒子；极小量；质点；小品词；碎木料（particle 的复数）

e.en: Argon is an inert gas which exists in very small amounts in the atmosphere. It is used in electric lights.

d: n. （化学）氩（原子序数 18，元素符号 Ar；无色无味的惰性气体，指气体时也作“氩气”）；（Argon）阿尔贡（人名，见于西班牙语、土耳其语、英语）

e.en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground.

ex.en: Solid low-level waste will be disposed of deep underground.
ex.zh: 低放射性固体废物将被弃置在地下深处。

e.en: Underground is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an underground parking garage for 2,100 vehicles.
ex.zh: …一座能停放2100辆车的地下停车库。

e.en: The underground in a city is the railway system in which electric trains travel below the ground in tunnels.

ex.en: I don't travel on the underground late at night.
ex.zh: 我深夜不坐地铁。

e.en: Underground groups and activities are secret because their purpose is to oppose the government and they are illegal. 秘密的;

ex.en: ...the underground Kashmir Liberation Front.
ex.zh: 秘密的克什米尔解放阵线。

d: adv. 在地（面）下；；隐蔽地，隐匿地；在地（面）下
adj. 地（面）下的；秘密的，地下的；标新立异的，小众的
v. 铺（电缆）于地下；；铺（电缆）于地下
n.  地铁；（反政府的）地下组织；先锋派团体

e.en: If something is deep, it extends a long way down from the ground or from the top surface of something.

ex.en: The water is very deep and mysterious looking.
ex.zh: 水很深，而且看起来很神秘。

ex.en: Den had dug a deep hole in the centre of the garden.
ex.zh: 登在花园中间挖了一个深洞。

e.en: Deep is also an adverb.

ex.en: Gingerly, she put her hand in deeper, to the bottom.
ex.zh: 她小心翼翼地把手伸得更深，直到底部。

e.en: 深地

ex.en: There isn't time to dig deeply and put in manure or compost.
ex.zh: 没有时间挖得再深些，并放入粪肥或堆肥。

e.en: A deep container, such as wardrobe, extends or measures a long distance from front to back.

ex.en: The wardrobe was very deep.
ex.zh: 橱柜很深。

d: adj. 深的，厚的；纵深的，宽的；有……深的；成……排的；深呼吸的；（声音）低沉的；深色的；酣睡的；严重的；（感情）深厚的；透彻的，深刻的；深奥的；全神贯注，深陷；（人）深沉的；（目光）锐利的，深邃的；靠近场地边界的；神秘的；大幅下降的；有很多优秀选手的
adv. 深深地，至深处；有……深；成……排地；靠近场地边界地
n. 海洋（the deep）；海洋深处（deeps）；中间部分（the deep）；（板球）外围场地（the deep）
【名】 （Deep）迪普（人名）

e.en: Science is the study of the nature and behaviour of natural things and the knowledge that we obtain about them.

ex.en: The best discoveries in science are very simple.
ex.zh: 科学上最好的发现都是非常简单的。

e.en: A science is a particular branch of science such as physics, chemistry, or biology. (科学的)

ex.en: Physics is the best example of a science which has developed strong, abstract theories.
ex.zh: 物理学是一个发展出了强有力的抽象理论的学科的最好例证。

e.en: A science is the study of some aspect of human behaviour, for example, sociology or anthropology. (人类行为的)

ex.en: ...the modern science of psychology.
ex.zh: …现代心理学。

d: n. 科学，科学知识；专门科学；（大学学习的）学科；理科；技术，技巧
【名】 （Science）（英）赛恩斯（人名）

e.en: A particle of something is a very small piece or amount of it. 微粒;

ex.en: ...a particle of hot metal.
ex.zh: …热金属微粒。

ex.en: There is a particle of truth in his statement.
ex.zh: 在他的声明中只有极少的事实。

e.en: In physics, a particle is a piece of matter smaller than an atom such as an electron or a proton.

ex.en: ...the sub-atomic particles that make up matter.
ex.zh: …构成物质的次原子微粒。

d: n. 微粒；极少量；粒子（原子的极微小成分，如电子、质子或中子）；（数）质点；（语法中的）小品词

e.en: A scientist is someone who has studied science and whose job is to teach or do research in science.

ex.en: Scientists say they've already collected more data than had been expected.
ex.zh: 科学家们说他们已经搜集到比预期更多的数据。

d: n. 科学家（scientist 的复数）

e.en: When people assemble or when someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

ex.en: There wasn't even a convenient place for students to assemble between classes.
ex.zh: 甚至没有一个学生们课间集合的方便的地方。

e.en: To assemble something means to collect it together or to fit the different parts of it together. 聚集;

ex.en: Greenpeace managed to assemble a small flotilla of inflatable boats to waylay the ship at sea.
ex.zh: 绿色和平组织设法聚集了一支充气艇小舰队去拦截海上的那艘船。

d: n. 装配，组装；（计算机）汇编
v. 装配；聚集（assemble 的现在分词/动名词）
adj. 装配的，组合的

e.en: Sent is the past tense and past participle of . send
a monetary unit of Estonia, worth one hundredth of a kroon 爱沙尼亚的货币单位(等于百分之一的克鲁恩)

d: v. 送，寄出，派遣（send 的过去式和过去分词）；驱逐离场；寄出，派出（send off 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已寄出的，已发送的（常作定语，多用于邮件、消息等）
n. 分（爱沙尼亚旧货币单位，1 克鲁恩等于 100 分）；（Sent）森特（人名）
n. 太阳（the sun）；日光，阳光；恒星；成功，荣耀；一天，一年；被视为荣誉（或灵感、理解）源泉的人（或物）
v. 晒太阳，（尤指）日光浴
【名】 （Sun）（中）孙（普通话·威妥玛），（柬）孙，（缅）素，（土）松（人名）

e.en: Facilities are buildings, pieces of equipment, or services that are provided for a particular purpose.

ex.en: What recreational facilities are now available?
ex.zh: 什么娱乐设施现在是可用的？

e.en: A facility is something such as an additional service provided by an organization or an extra feature on a machine which is useful but not essential. 附加服务;

ex.en: One of the new models has the facility to reproduce speech as well as text.
ex.zh: 新款型中的一款有复制言语和文本的附加功能。

e.en: If you have a facility for something, for example learning a language, you find it easy to do.

ex.en: He and Marcia shared a facility for languages.
ex.zh: 他和马西娅都具有语言天赋。

d: n. 设施，设备；卫生间；天赋，才能；（机器等的）特别装置，（服务等的）特色；（用作某种用途的）场所

e.en: If you say that someone is beaming, you mean that they have a big smile on their face because they are happy, pleased, or proud about something.

ex.en: Frances beamed at her friend with undisguised admiration.
ex.zh: 弗朗西丝用毫不掩饰的羡慕的神情朝她的朋友们绽开了笑容。

ex.en: "Welcome back," she beamed.
ex.zh: “欢迎回来，”她笑容满面地说。

e.en: A beam is a line of energy, radiation, or particles sent in a particular direction. (能量、辐射、粒子)

ex.en: ...high-energy laser beams.
ex.zh: …高能激光束。

e.en: If radio signals or television pictures are beamed somewhere, they are sent there by means of electronic equipment.

ex.en: The interview was beamed live across America.
ex.zh: 那场访谈同步播送至全美。

ex.en: The Sci-Fi Channel began beaming into 10 million American homes this week.
ex.zh: 科幻频道本周已经开始播送到1000万个美国家庭。

e.en: A beam of light is a line of light that shines from an object such as a lamp. (光)

ex.en: A beam of light slices through the darkness.
ex.zh: 一道光束划破了黑暗。

d: n. 梁，横梁；臀围；光线，光柱；喜色，笑容；（体操的）平衡木
v. 定向发出（无线电信号）；（光，光源）照耀；喜笑颜开，面露喜色
【名】 （Beam）（英）比姆，（阿拉伯）贝亚姆（人名）

e.en: Detection is the act of noticing or sensing something. 察觉;

ex.en: ...the early detection of breast cancer.
ex.zh: …乳腺癌的早期发现。

d: n. 察觉，发现；侦破（案件）
费米实验室

e.en: If a light or flame flickers, it shines unsteadily.

ex.en: Fluorescent lights flickered, and then the room was blindingly bright.
ex.zh: 荧光灯闪了闪，接着房间里就亮得令人目眩了。

e.en: Flicker is also a noun.

ex.en: Looking through the window I saw the flicker of flames.
ex.zh: 透过窗子望出去，我看到了闪烁的火光。

e.en: a visual sensation, often seen in a television image, produced by periodic fluctuations in the brightness of light at a frequency below that covered by the persistence of vision (在光栅扫描显示中的)
any North American woodpecker of the genus Colaptes, esp C. auratus (yellow-shafted flicker), which has a yellow undersurface to the wings and tail
