d: v. 闪烁，摇曳；闪现，一闪而过；（表情）掠过；（眼睛）瞟过；颤动，快速抖动；扑动翅膀；使……突然动一下
n. （火焰，光的）闪烁，摇曳；（感觉或情绪的）闪现，一闪而过；（身体部位的）小而快的动作；（电影或电视每秒帧数过少时的）图像闪烁；（鸟）扑翅䴕属
【名】 （Flicker）（美、澳、英）弗利克（人名）

e.en: A fluid is a liquid.

ex.en: The blood vessels may leak fluid, which distorts vision.
ex.zh: 血管可能渗漏出液体，扰乱视觉。

ex.en: Make sure that you drink plenty of fluids.
ex.zh: 一定要饮用大量流质。

e.en: Fluid movements or lines or designs are smooth and graceful.

ex.en: His painting became less illustrational and more fluid.
ex.zh: 他的画变得更为流畅，没那么生硬了。

d: n. 流体，液体
adj. 液体的，流体的；易变的，不稳定的；流畅优美的
n. 伊利诺伊州（美国中北部一州，亦译伊利诺斯州）

e.en: Intense is used to describe something that is very great or extreme in strength or degree. 剧烈的;

ex.en: He was sweating from the intense heat.
ex.zh: 由于剧烈的热量，他一直出汗。

ex.en: Stevens's murder was the result of a deep-seated and intense hatred.
ex.zh: 史蒂文斯凶杀案源于深仇大恨。

e.en: 剧烈地;

ex.en: The fast-food business is intensely competitive.
ex.zh: 快餐业竞争非常激烈。

e.en: If you describe an activity as intense, you mean that it is very serious and concentrated, and often involves doing a lot in a short time. 集中的;

ex.en: The battle for third place was intense.
ex.zh: 竞争第3名的较量很紧张。

e.en: If you describe the way someone looks at you as intense, you mean that they look at you very directly and seem to know what you are thinking or feeling.

ex.en: I felt so self-conscious under Luke's mother's intense gaze.
ex.zh: 在卢克母亲热切的注视下，我感到很不自在。

d: adj. 很大的，十分强烈的；严肃紧张的，激烈的；热情的，热切的；专注的，认真的

e.en: A hole is a hollow space in something solid, with an opening on one side.

ex.en: He took a shovel, dug a hole, and buried his once-prized possessions.
ex.zh: 他拿了一把铲子，挖了个坑，埋下了他曾经珍爱的物品。

e.en: A hole is an opening in something that goes right through it. (贯穿的)

ex.en: ...kids with holes in the knees of their jeans.
ex.zh: …牛仔裤的膝盖上有破洞的孩子们。

e.en: A hole is the home or hiding place of a mouse, rabbit, or other small animal. (鼠、兔等小动物的)

ex.en: ...a rabbit hole.
ex.zh: …一个兔子窝。

e.en: A hole in a law, theory, or argument is a fault or weakness that it has. (法律、理论、论点等的)

ex.en: There were some holes in that theory, some unanswered questions.
ex.zh: 那个理论中有些漏洞，一些没有得到解答的问题。

d: n. 小孔；破洞（hole 的复数）；（Holes）人名；（匈）霍莱什

e.en: A laboratory is a building or a room where scientific experiments, analyses, and research are carried out. 实验室 (用于分析研究)

ex.en: ...a brain research laboratory at Columbia University.
ex.zh: …哥伦比亚大学的一个大脑研究实验室。

e.en: A laboratory in a school, college, or university is a room containing scientific equipment where students are taught science subjects such as chemistry. 实验室 (用于教学)

ex.en: ...my old school chemistry laboratory.
ex.zh: …我母校的化学实验室。

d: n. 实验室，实验大楼

e.en: If you lead a group of people, you walk or ride in front of them.

ex.en: The president and vice president led the mourners.
ex.zh: 总统和副总统带领着送葬人群。

ex.en: He walks with a stick but still leads his soldiers into battle.
ex.zh: 尽管他拄着拐杖，但他仍带领士兵上战场。

e.en: If you lead someone to a particular place or thing, you take them there.

ex.en: He took Dickon by the hand to lead him into the house.
ex.zh: 他拉着迪肯的手领他进了那幢房子。

ex.en: She confessed to the killing and led police to his remains.
ex.zh: 她承认杀了人，并且带警察找到了他的遗骸。

e.en: If a road, gate, or door leads somewhere, you can get there by following the road or going through the gate or door.

ex.en: ...the door that led to the garden.
ex.zh: …通往院子的门。

ex.en: ...a hallway leading to the living room.
ex.zh: …通往客厅的过道。

e.en: If you are leading at a particular point in a race or competition, you are winning at that point. (在比赛中)

ex.en: He's leading in the presidential race.
ex.zh: 他在总统竞选中领先。

ex.en: So far Fischer leads by five wins to two.
ex.zh: 到目前为止，菲舍尔以５:２领先。

d: v. 引领，带路；通向，通往；（与……）相连，相通；领导，指挥；导致，造成；促使，使得；过（某种生活）；领先，居于首位；开牌；对（证人）进行诱询；用水砣测深
n. 领先地位；超前量，领先的距离；范例，榜样；线索；主角，扮演主角的演员；铅；铅笔芯；狗绳，牵狗带；（报纸或电台的）要闻，头条；子弹；电线，导线；导语；（投球前跑垒员的）离垒；螺距，牙距；水渠，水道；行间距
【名】 （Lead）（英）利德（人名）

e.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example, water.

ex.en: Drink plenty of liquid.
ex.zh: 饮用大量液体。

ex.en: Boil for 20 minutes until the liquid has reduced by half.
ex.zh: 煮沸20分钟直到液体减少一半为止。

e.en: A liquid substance is in the form of a liquid rather than being solid or a gas.

ex.en: Wash in warm water with liquid detergent.
ex.zh: 用液体清洁剂在温水中清洗。

ex.en: The tanker was carrying liquid nitrogen.
ex.zh: 油轮那时正在运送液态氮。

e.en: Liquid assets are the things that a person or company owns which can be quickly turned into cash if necessary. (资金等)

ex.en: The bank had sufficient liquid assets to continue operations.
ex.zh: 该银行拥有足够的流动资产来继续运转。

d: n. 液体，液态物；流音
adj. 液态的，液化的；（资金等）流动的，易变为现金的；流畅自如的，舒展的；明亮的，清澈的；清脆的，流畅的；（市场）活跃的；液态的，液化的
n. （Newbold）人名；（英）纽博尔德

e.en: the body of common people

d: n. 群众；大量的东西（mass 的复数）
v. （使）聚集，（使）集结（mass 的第三人称单数）
【名】 （Masses）（西）马塞斯（人名）

e.en: A mile is a unit of distance equal to 1760 yards or approximately 1.6 kilometres.

ex.en: They drove 600 miles across the desert.
ex.zh: 他们驱车600英里横穿沙漠。

ex.en: She lives just half a mile away.
ex.zh: 她就住在半英里之外。

e.en: Miles is used, especially in the expression miles away, to refer to a long distance.

ex.en: If you enrol at a gym that's miles away, you won't be visiting it as often as you should.
ex.zh: 如果你加入的健身房离这儿很远的话，你就不会像应该地那样经常去了。

e.en: Miles or a mile is used with the meaning "very much" in order to emphasize the difference between two things or qualities, or the difference between what you aimed to do and what you actually achieved. (相差)

ex.en: You're miles better than most of the performers we see nowadays.
ex.zh: 你比我们现今看到的大多数表演者们要好得多。

ex.en: With a Democratic candidate in place they won by a mile.
ex.zh: 随着一位民主党候选人的到位，他们轻松胜出。

d: n. 英里（英制长度单位，1 英里约合 1609 米，mile 的复数形式）； 很远的距离（常用于 miles away）； 非常，远远地（用于比较或强调差距，如 miles better、win by a mile）

e.en: To reveal something means to make people aware of it. 透露;

ex.en: She has refused to reveal the whereabouts of her daughter.
ex.zh: 她已拒绝透露她女儿的行踪。

ex.en: A survey of the American diet has revealed that a growing number of people are overweight.
ex.zh: 一项有关美国人日常饮食的调查表明越来越多的人超重。

e.en: If you reveal something that has been out of sight, you uncover it so that people can see it. 使显露;

ex.en: In the principal room, a grey carpet was removed to reveal the original pine floor.
ex.zh: 在主房间里，一块灰色的地毯被挪开了，使原有的松木地板露了出来。

d: v. 揭示，透露；表明，证明；展示，显示；（通过神或超自然手段）启示
n. （电视节目最后的）揭示；门侧，窗侧

e.en: A physicist is a person who does research connected with physics or who studies physics.

ex.en: ...a nuclear physicist.
ex.zh: …一位核物理学家。

d: n. 物理学家

e.en: Rock is the hard substance which the earth is made of.

ex.en: The hills above the valley are bare rock.
ex.zh: 河谷上面的山是光秃秃的岩石。

e.en: A rock is a large piece of rock that sticks up out of the ground or the sea, or that has broken away from a mountain or a cliff.

ex.en: She sat cross-legged on the rock.
ex.zh: 她盘着腿坐在那块巨石上。

e.en: A rock is a piece of rock that is small enough for you to pick up.

ex.en: She bent down, picked up a rock, and threw it into the trees.
ex.zh: 她弯下腰，拣起一块小石头，把它扔进树林里。

e.en: When something rocks or when you rock it, it moves slowly and regularly backward and forward or from side to side. 使摇晃;

ex.en: His body rocked from side to side with the train.
ex.zh: 他的身体随着火车左右晃动着。

d: n. 岩石；礁石；（尤指凸出地面的）岩块，大石块；碎石，石子；钻石，宝石；摇滚乐；可信赖的人，靠山；棒棒糖；石毒，强效可卡因块；睾丸（rocks）；轻轻摇动，轻轻摇摆
v. （使）轻轻摇晃，缓缓摆动；（使）剧烈摇摆，猛烈晃动；使震惊，使害怕；（尤指自信或惹人注目地）穿（衣）；跳摇滚舞，奏摇滚乐；很好，棒极了
【名】 （Rock）（英、德、匈、意、瑞典）罗克（人名）

e.en: a small wood; thicket; copse 小树林; 灌木丛;
to show
a show

d: n. （古语/方言）小树林，灌木丛，树丛；Shaw（英、德姓氏，人名）肖；Shaw（中文姓氏“邵”的英文拼写）；Shaw（George Bernard Shaw，爱尔兰剧作家萧伯纳）

e.en: Surf is the mass of white bubbles that is formed by waves as they fall upon the shore.

ex.en: ...surf rolling onto white sand beaches.
ex.zh: …翻滚到白色沙滩上的浪花。

e.en: If you surf, you ride on big waves in the sea on a special board.

ex.en: I'm going to buy a surfboard and learn to surf.
ex.zh: 我要去买个冲浪板来学冲浪。

e.en: 冲浪者

ex.en: ...this small fishing village, which continues to attract painters and surfers.
ex.zh: …这个一直吸引着画家和冲浪者的小渔村。

e.en: If you surf the Internet, you spend time finding and looking at things on the Internet. (网上)

ex.en: No one knows how many people currently surf the Net.
ex.zh: 没人知道现在有多少人在网上冲浪。

d: v. 上网；冲浪；坐在高速行驶的车辆（尤指火车）顶部（或外面）享受刺激感；频繁调换电视频道（同 channel-surf）
n. 拍岸浪花；一次冲浪

e.en: You use space to refer to an area that is empty or available. The area can be any size. For example, you can refer to a large area outside as a large open space or to a small area between two objects as a small space. 空间;

ex.en: ...cutting down yet more trees to make space for houses.
ex.zh: …砍掉更多的树以腾出空间来盖房屋。

ex.en: I had plenty of space to write and sew.
ex.zh: 我有足够的空间来写作和缝纫。

e.en: A particular kind of space is the area that is available for a particular activity or for putting a particular kind of thing in.

ex.en: ...the high cost of office space.
ex.zh: …办公场所的高额费用。

ex.en: You don't want your living space to look like a bedroom.
ex.zh: 你不会希望你的起居室看上去像一间卧室。

e.en: If a place gives a feeling of space, it gives an impression of being large and open.

ex.en: Large paintings can enhance the feeling of space in small rooms.
ex.zh: 大幅画作能增加小房间的宽敞感。

e.en: If you give someone space to think about something or to develop as a person, you allow them the time and freedom to do this.

ex.en: You need space to think everything over.
ex.zh: 你需要留有余地来仔细考虑一切。

d: n. 空间，空地；（尤指有特定用途的）空位，处所；（公共汽车等的）空座；开阔地，空旷处；开阔，空旷；太空，外层空间；宇宙空间；一段时间；属于自己的空间；空格，空行；版面，篇幅；广告专页，广告插播时间；（乐）（谱表的）线间空白；（电信）空号
v. 把（某物）隔开；在（词语等）之间加空格；变得昏昏沉沉，瞪着眼发呆

e.en: Something that is abundant is present in large quantities.

ex.en: There is an abundant supply of cheap labour.
ex.zh: 有丰富的廉价劳动力供应。

d: adj. 大量的，丰富的，充足的

e.en: A tonne is a metric unit of weight that is equal to 1,000 kilograms.

ex.en: The Wall Street Journal uses 220,000 tonnes of newsprint each year.
ex.zh: 《华尔街日报》每年使用22万吨新闻纸。

d: n. （计量）公吨（tonne 的复数）

e.en: The accelerator in a car or other vehicle is the pedal that you press with your foot in order to make the vehicle go faster.

ex.en: He eased his foot off the accelerator.
ex.zh: 他把脚慢慢移离了油门。

d: n. （accelerator 的复数形式）：（物理）粒子加速器，加速器；（车辆）油门踏板，加速踏板；（化学）促进剂，加速剂；（商业）创业加速器

e.en: An administrator is a person whose job involves helping to organize and supervise the way that an organization or institution functions. 行政人员;

ex.en: On Friday the company's administrators sought permission from a Melbourne court to keep operating.
ex.zh: 在星期五，该公司的管理人员们从一家墨尔本法院取得了继续经营的许可。

d: n. （公司、学校等的）管理者，行政人员；（死者）遗产管理人，（债务人、其他个人或破产公司）资产管理人

e.en: If you analyse something, you consider it carefully or use statistical methods in order to fully understand it.

ex.en: McCarthy was asked to analyse the data from the first phase of trials of the vaccine.
ex.zh: 麦卡西被要求分析从这种疫苗试验的第一阶段取得的数据。

e.en: If you analyse something, you examine it using scientific methods in order to find out what it consists of.

ex.en: We haven't had time to analyse those samples yet.
ex.zh: 我们还没有时间化验分析那些样本。

d: v. analyse 的现在分词/动名词；分析；化验分析

e.en: When you answer someone who has asked you something, you say something back to them. (口头)

ex.en: Just answer the question.
ex.zh: 只回答这个问题。

ex.en: He paused before answering.
ex.zh: 他在回答前停了下来。

e.en: If you answer a letter or advertisement, you write to the person who wrote it.

ex.en: Did he answer your letter?
ex.zh: 他回复你的信了吗？

e.en: When you answer the telephone, you pick it up when it rings. When you answer the door, you open it when you hear a knock or the bell.

ex.en: She answered her phone on the first ring.
ex.zh: 她在响第一声铃时就接了电话。

e.en: Answer is also a noun.

ex.en: I knocked at the front door and there was no answer.
ex.zh: 我敲了前门，没有应答。

d: n. 答案，回答（answer 的复数）
v. 回答（answer 的第三人称单数形式）
n. 南极洲
n. 反中微子（antineutrino 的变形）

e.en: The apparatus of an organization or system is its structure and method of operation. (机构、体系的)

ex.en: For many years, the country had been buried under the apparatus of the regime.
ex.zh: 多年来，该国一直处于这种政体的统治下。

e.en: Apparatus is the equipment, such as tools and machines, which is used to do a particular job or activity.

ex.en: One of the boys had to be rescued by firemen wearing breathing apparatus.
ex.zh: 其中的一个男孩得由戴着呼吸设备的消防队员们营救。

d: n. 设备，器具；机构，组织；器官；评论性注释

e.en: An apple is a round fruit with smooth red, yellow, or green skin and firm white flesh.

ex.en: I want an apple.
ex.zh: 我要一个苹果。

ex.en: ...his ongoing search for the finest varieties of apple.
ex.zh: …他对最佳品种苹果的不断寻找。

d: n. 苹果；苹果树；苹果公司（Apple Inc.）

e.en: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it from somewhere else.

ex.en: Fresh groups of guests arrived.
ex.zh: 新客成批到达了。

ex.en: ...a small group of commuters waiting for their train, which arrived on time.
ex.zh: …几个等候火车准点到达的通勤者。

e.en: When you arrive at a place, you come to it for the first time in order to stay, live, or work there.

ex.en: ...in the old days before the European settlers arrived in the country.
ex.zh: …在欧洲定居者们初次到这个国家之前的古老岁月。

e.en: When something such as letter or meal arrives, it is brought or delivered to you.

ex.en: Breakfast arrived while he was in the bathroom.
ex.zh: 早餐在他在浴室里时送到了。

e.en: When something such as a new product or invention arrives, it becomes available. (产品、发明)

ex.en: Several long-awaited movies will finally arrive in the stores this month.
ex.zh: 几部期盼已久的影片最终将于本月在各家商店露面。

d: v. 到达，抵达；送达，寄到；发生，出现，诞生；开始，到来；成功，出名；作出（决定）
【名】 （Arrive）（法）阿里夫（人名）

e.en: When a person or vehicle arrives at a place, they come to it from somewhere else.

ex.en: Fresh groups of guests arrived.
ex.zh: 新客成批到达了。

ex.en: ...a small group of commuters waiting for their train, which arrived on time.
ex.zh: …几个等候火车准点到达的通勤者。

e.en: When you arrive at a place, you come to it for the first time in order to stay, live, or work there.

ex.en: ...in the old days before the European settlers arrived in the country.
ex.zh: …在欧洲定居者们初次到这个国家之前的古老岁月。

e.en: When something such as letter or meal arrives, it is brought or delivered to you.

ex.en: Breakfast arrived while he was in the bathroom.
ex.zh: 早餐在他在浴室里时送到了。

e.en: When something such as a new product or invention arrives, it becomes available. (产品、发明)

ex.en: Several long-awaited movies will finally arrive in the stores this month.
ex.zh: 几部期盼已久的影片最终将于本月在各家商店露面。

d: v. arrive 的现在分词或动名词，表示到达、抵达；与 at 连用时表示达到、达成

e.en: An atom is the smallest amount of a substance that can take part in a chemical reaction.

ex.en: ...the news that Einstein's former colleagues Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann had split the atom.
ex.zh: …爱因斯坦的前同事奥托·哈恩和弗里茨·斯特拉斯曼曾分裂了原子的消息。

d: n. 原子；微量，极小量

e.en: An atom is the smallest amount of a substance that can take part in a chemical reaction.

ex.en: ...the news that Einstein's former colleagues Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann had split the atom.
ex.zh: …爱因斯坦的前同事奥托·哈恩和弗里茨·斯特拉斯曼曾分裂了原子的消息。

d: n. （物）原子（atom 的复数）；极小的颗粒，微粒

e.en: If something attracts people or animals, it has features that cause them to come to it.

ex.en: The Cardiff Bay project is attracting many visitors.
ex.zh: 加的夫湾工程吸引着众多的参观者。

e.en: If someone or something attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them. If a particular quality attracts you to a person or thing, it is the reason why you like them.

ex.en: He wasn't sure he'd got it right, although the theory attracted him by its logic.
ex.zh: 他不能确定自己理解是否正确，尽管该理论的逻辑推理引起了他的兴趣。

e.en: If you are attracted to someone, you are interested in them sexually. (性的)

ex.en: In spite of her hostility, she was attracted to him.
ex.zh: 尽管心存敌意，她还是被他吸引住了。

e.en: 被吸引的

ex.en: He was nice looking, but I wasn't deeply attracted to him.
ex.zh: 他长得挺好看，但我并没有被他深深吸引。

d: v. 吸引，引起……的兴趣；引起……的爱慕，诱惑；（物理）吸引（attract 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被吸引的

e.en: If you attempt to do something, especially something difficult, you try to do it. 试图 (尤指做困难的事)

ex.en: The only time that we attempted to do something like that was in the city of Philadelphia.
ex.zh: 我们惟一一次试图做那样的事是在费城。

e.en: If you make an attempt to do something, you try to do it, often without success. (常指不成功的)

ex.en: ...a deliberate attempt to destabilize the defence.
ex.zh: …蓄意削弱防御的企图。

e.en: An attempt on someone's life is an attempt to kill them. (杀人)

ex.en: ...an attempt on the life of the former Iranian prime minister.
ex.zh: …刺杀伊朗前总理的企图。

d: v. 努力，尝试
n. 试图，努力；企图杀害；（运动员创造记录的）尝试，冲击

e.en: Bananas are long curved fruit with yellow skins.

ex.en: ...a bunch of bananas.
ex.zh: …一串香蕉。

d: n. 香蕉；香蕉树；（Banana）巴纳纳（姓氏）
adj. （非正式，通常作 bananas）愚蠢的，发狂的

e.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case. 仅仅;

ex.en: Anastasia could barely remember the ride to the hospital.
ex.zh: 阿纳斯塔西娅只勉强记得被送到了医院。

ex.en: It was 90 degrees and the air conditioning barely cooled the room.
ex.zh: 气温是90度，空调几乎没有使房间凉快下来。

e.en: If you say that one thing had barely happened when something else happened, you mean that the first event was followed immediately by the second.

ex.en: The water had barely come to a simmer when she cracked four eggs into it.
ex.zh: 水刚开她就打了4个鸡蛋进去。

d: adv. 勉强才能；几乎不，几乎没有；刚刚；仅仅，只有；贫乏地，光秃秃；公开地，不加掩饰地

e.en: People's or animals' behaviour is the way that they behave. You can refer to a typical and repeated way of behaving as a behaviour.

ex.en: Make sure that good behaviour is rewarded.
ex.zh: 确保良好的行为受到嘉奖。

ex.en: ...human sexual behaviour.
ex.zh: …人类性行为。

e.en: In science, the behaviour of something is the way that it behaves. (科学领域)

ex.en: It will be many years before anyone can predict a hurricane's behaviour with much accuracy.
ex.zh: 要高精确度地预测飓风的表现尚需要许多年。

e.en: If someone is on their best behaviour, they are trying very hard to behave well.

ex.en: The 1,400 fans were on their best behaviour and filed out peacefully at the end.
ex.zh: 1400名支持者尽全力守着规矩，结束时排成队平静地离场。

d: n. 行为，举止，态度；活动方式，特点，特性；习惯

e.en: If you say that someone is beaming, you mean that they have a big smile on their face because they are happy, pleased, or proud about something.

ex.en: Frances beamed at her friend with undisguised admiration.
ex.zh: 弗朗西丝用毫不掩饰的羡慕的神情朝她的朋友们绽开了笑容。

ex.en: "Welcome back," she beamed.
ex.zh: “欢迎回来，”她笑容满面地说。

e.en: A beam is a line of energy, radiation, or particles sent in a particular direction. (能量、辐射、粒子)

ex.en: ...high-energy laser beams.
ex.zh: …高能激光束。

e.en: If radio signals or television pictures are beamed somewhere, they are sent there by means of electronic equipment.

ex.en: The interview was beamed live across America.
ex.zh: 那场访谈同步播送至全美。

ex.en: The Sci-Fi Channel began beaming into 10 million American homes this week.
ex.zh: 科幻频道本周已经开始播送到1000万个美国家庭。

e.en: A beam of light is a line of light that shines from an object such as a lamp. (光)

ex.en: A beam of light slices through the darkness.
ex.zh: 一道光束划破了黑暗。

d: n. 梁，横梁；光线，光柱；（能量、辐射、粒子等的）束；喜色，笑容（beam 的复数）；（Beams）比姆斯（人名）
v. 喜笑颜开，面露喜色（beam 的第三人称单数）；照耀，发光；定向发出（无线电信号），播送

e.en: Something that is beneath another thing is under the other thing.

ex.en: She could see the muscles of his shoulders beneath his T-shirt.
ex.zh: 她可以看到他T恤衫下的肩部肌肉。

ex.en: Four levels of parking beneath the theatre was not enough.
ex.zh: 剧院底下的四层停车库还不够。

e.en: Beneath is also an adverb.

ex.en: On a shelf beneath he spotted a photo album.
ex.zh: 在下方的书架上他发现了一本相册。

e.en: If you talk about what is beneath the surface of something, you are talking about the aspects of it which are hidden or not obvious. 在 (表面)

ex.en: ...emotional strains beneath the surface.
ex.zh: …表面下的情感压力。

ex.en: Somewhere deep beneath the surface lay a caring character.
ex.zh: 在其外表下心灵深处的某个地方保留着一种关爱别人的品格。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is beneath you, you feel that they are not good enough for you or not suitable for you. 不如;

ex.en: They decided she was marrying beneath her.
ex.zh: 他们认定她嫁的是一个配不上她的人。

d: prep. 在……下方；在……表面之下，隐藏在……之下；（对某人来说）不够好，不相称；低于，次于
adv. 在下面，在底下

e.en: Belgian means belonging or relating to Belgium or to its people. 比利时的;
A Belgian is a person who comes from Belgium.

d: adj. 比利时的
n. 比利时人

e.en: When a baby is born, you refer to this event as his or her birth.

ex.en: It was the birth of his grandchildren that gave him greatest pleasure.
ex.zh: 是孙儿孙女们的降生给了他最大的欢乐。

ex.en: She weighed 5lb 7oz at birth.
ex.zh: 她出生时重5磅7盎司。

e.en: You can refer to the beginning or origin of something as its birth. 开始;

ex.en: ...the birth of popular democracy.
ex.zh: …人民民主的开始

e.en: Some people talk about a person's birth when they are referring to the social position of the person's family.

ex.en: ...men of low birth.
ex.zh: …出身低微的男人们。

e.en: If, for example, you are French by birth, you are French because your parents are French, or because you were born in France.

ex.en: Sadrudin was an Iranian by birth.
ex.zh: 萨德鲁丁在血统上是伊朗人。

d: n. 出生，诞生；出身，血统；开始，起源
v. 生，产

e.en: If something is beyond a place or barrier, it is on the other side of it.

ex.en: On his right was a thriving vegetable garden and beyond it a small orchard of apple trees.
ex.zh: 在他的右边是一片长势旺盛的菜园，另一头是一小片苹果树林。

e.en: Beyond is also an adverb.

ex.en: The house had a fabulous view out to the Strait of Georgia and the Rockies beyond.
ex.zh: 这座房子有很棒的景观，可以看到乔治亚海峡以及另一头的落基山脉。

e.en: If something happens beyond a particular time or date, it continues after that time or date has passed. (时间)

ex.en: Few jockeys continue race-riding beyond the age of 40.
ex.zh: 很少有骑师在40岁以后还继续赛马。

e.en: Beyond is also an adverb. (时间)

ex.en: The financing of home ownership will continue through the 1990s and beyond.
ex.zh: 房屋产权的融资将持续到20世纪90年代及以后。

d: prep. 在（或向）……较远的一边；晚于，迟于；涵盖，包括；除……之外；超出（范围）；非（某人）所能理解
adv. 在另一边，在（或向）更远处；（延续）到……之后
n. 来生，再世（the beyond）；远处的事物（the beyond）

e.en: Some people use blasted to express anger or annoyance at something or someone. 恼怒的;
A blasted landscape has very few plants or trees, and makes you feel sad or depressed when you look at it. (景色)荒凉的;

d: v. blast 的过去式和过去分词：炸开；猛烈抨击；猛踢、猛射；强力喷出
adj. （非正式）该死的，被诅咒的，讨厌的；枯萎的，被害的；（文学）荒凉的，凄凉的；（俚语）喝醉的

e.en: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.

ex.en: Remember to bring an apron or an old shirt to protect your clothes.
ex.zh: 记着带一条围裙或一件旧衬衫来保护你的衣服。

ex.en: Someone went upstairs and brought down a huge kettle.
ex.zh: 有人上楼拿下来一个巨大的水壶。

e.en: If you bring something somewhere, you move it there.

ex.en: Reaching into her pocket, she brought out a cigarette.
ex.zh: 她把手伸进口袋，拿出一根香烟。

e.en: If you bring something that someone wants or needs, you get it for them or carry it to them.

ex.en: He went and poured a brandy for Dena and brought it to her.
ex.zh: 他去给德娜倒了杯白兰地并拿给了她。

e.en: To bring something or someone to a place or position means to cause them to come to the place or move into that position.

ex.en: I told you about what brought me here.
ex.zh: 我告诉过你是什么把我引到这里来的。

ex.en: The shock of her husband's arrival brought her to her feet.
ex.zh: 丈夫的到来惊得她不由自主地站了起来。

d: v. 带来，携带；使发生，引起，导致；使处于（某种状态或境地）（bring 的第三人称单数形式）
n. （Brings）人名，布林斯

e.en: A cavern is a large, deep cave.

d: n. 洞穴，巨穴，大山洞或岩洞内的大洞室（cavern 的复数）
v. 置……于大山洞中；挖空（cavern 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you charge someone an amount of money, you ask them to pay that amount for something that you have sold to them or done for them. 要价;

ex.en: Even local nurseries charge $150 a week.
ex.zh: 即便当地的托儿所每周也要收$150的费用。

ex.en: Some banks charge if you access your account to determine your balance.
ex.zh: 如果你进入自己的账户查看余额，有些银行要收费。

e.en: To charge something to a person or organization means to tell the people providing it to send the bill to that person or organization. To charge something to someone's account means to add it to their account so they can pay for it later. 开帐单;

ex.en: Go out and buy a pair of glasses, and charge it to us.
ex.zh: 出去买一副眼镜，记在我们的账上。

e.en: When the police charge someone, they formally accuse them of having done something illegal.

ex.en: They have the evidence to charge him.
ex.zh: 他们有证据来指控他。

e.en: If you charge toward someone or something, you move quickly and aggressively toward them.

ex.en: He charged through the door to my mother's office.
ex.zh: 他破门而入，进了我母亲的办公室。

ex.en: He ordered us to charge.
ex.zh: 他命令我们冲锋。

d: v. 充电；使……承担责任，赋予……责任；控告，指控；（公开）指责，责备；进攻，冲锋；把……记在账上；要价，收费（金额）；给（枪炮）装弹；斟满（杯子）
n. 电量，电荷；炸药量；掌管，照管；费用，价钱；控告，指控；（书面或口头的）指责，批评；需要照管的人；命令，指示；（人或动物的）猛攻，冲锋；快感，刺激；感召力，感染力；负载
【名】 （Charge）（英）查奇，（法）沙尔热（人名）
n. 芝加哥（美国城市名）

e.en: A closed group of people does not welcome new people or ideas from outside.

ex.en: It was to be a closed circle of no more than twelve women.
ex.zh: 那本来要是个不超过十二个女人的封闭团体。

ex.en: It is a closed society in the sense that they've not been exposed to many things.
ex.zh: 就他们没有机会接触太多事物而言，那是个闭塞的社会。

d: adj. 关着的，闭合的；闭关自守的，不愿接受新思想的；（部件、成员或答案的数量）有限定的，固定的；（商家）（尤指短时间）歇业的；（数）（集合）封闭的；（数）（集合）包含所有极限值的；（曲线，图形）闭合的；不公开的，保密的；形成完整环形的，封闭的；结束的，不再继续的
v. 关，闭；结束，终止；封锁，封闭（close 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Chlorine is a strong-smelling gas that is used to clean water and to make cleaning products.

d: n. [化学] 氯（17号化学元素）

e.en: (of a person) feeling cold (人)

d: adj. （食品、饮料等）冷却的，冰镇的；（人）感觉冷的；（非正式，常作 chilled out）放松的，冷静的，不担心的；（冶金）激冷的，冷硬的
v. chill 的过去式和过去分词：使变冷；使恐惧，使不寒而栗；（非正式）镇静下来，放松；消磨时光

e.en: A combined effort or attack is made by two or more groups of people at the same time.

ex.en: These refugees are taken care of by the combined efforts of the host countries and non-governmental organizations.
ex.zh: 这些难民得到东道国和非政府组织合力照顾。

e.en: The combined size or quantity of two or more things is the total of their sizes or quantities added together.

ex.en: Such a merger would be the largest in U.S. banking history, giving the two banks combined assets of some $146 billion.
ex.zh: 考虑到两家银行加在一起的资产有约一千四百六十亿美元，这样的合并在美国银行史上将会是最大的。

d: adj. 联合的，共同的；总和的，总计的
v. （使）结合，组合（combine 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: The components of something are the parts that it is made of.

ex.en: Enriched uranium is a key component of a nuclear weapon.
ex.zh: 浓缩铀是核武器的一个关键组成部分。

ex.en: The management plan has four main components.
ex.zh: 该管理计划有4个主要组成部分。

e.en: The component parts of something are the parts that make it up.

ex.en: Gorbachev failed to keep the component parts of the Soviet Union together.
ex.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫没能使苏联各组成部分保持在一起。

d: n. 部件；组件；成分；分力（component 的复数）

e.en: Computing is the activity of using a computer and writing programs for it. 计算机应用;

ex.en: Courses range from cooking to computing.
ex.zh: 课程从烹饪到计算机应用都有。

e.en: Computing means relating to computers and their use.

ex.en: Many graduates are employed in the electronics and computing industries.
ex.zh: 许多毕业生受雇于电子与计算机行业。

d: n. 计算机应用，计算机编程，计算机使用；计算，计算过程
adj. 与计算机有关的（常作定语）
v. 估算，计算（compute 的现在分词）

e.en: Construction is the building of things such as houses, factories, roads, and bridges.

ex.en: He'd already started construction on a hunting lodge.
ex.zh: 他已经开始建造一个狩猎用的小屋。

ex.en: ...the downturn in the construction industry.
ex.zh: …建造业的衰退。

e.en: The construction of something such as a vehicle or machine is the making of it. (交通工具、机器等的)

ex.en: ...companies who have long experience in the construction of those types of equipment.
ex.zh: …在制造那种设备方面有长久经验的各公司。

e.en: The construction of something such as a system is the creation of it.

ex.en: ...the construction of a just system of criminal justice.
ex.zh: …公正的刑事司法体制的建立。

e.en: You use construction to refer to the structure of something and the way it has been built or made.

ex.en: The Shakers believed that furniture should be plain, simple, useful, practical, and of sound construction.
ex.zh: 震颤派教徒认为家具应当朴素、简单、有用、实际，且构造很好。

d: n. 建造，建筑；创立，构建；构造，结构；建筑物；语法结构；解释，理解

e.en: Cosmic means occurring in, or coming from, the part of space that lies outside Earth and its atmosphere.

ex.en: ...cosmic radiation.
ex.zh: …外层辐射。

e.en: Cosmic means belonging or relating to the universe.

ex.en: ...the cosmic laws governing our world.
ex.zh: …主宰我们世界的宇宙法则。

d: adj. 宇宙的，外层空间的；巨大的，极重要的；精神的，神灵的

e.en: The core of a fruit is the central part of it that contains seeds.

ex.en: Someone threw an apple core.
ex.zh: 有人扔了一个苹果核。

e.en: The core of an object, building, or city is the central part of it.

ex.en: ...the Earth's core.
ex.zh: …地核。

e.en: If you core a fruit, you remove its core.

ex.en: ...machines for peeling and coring apples.
ex.zh: …苹果削皮去核机。

e.en: The core of something such as a problem or an issue is the part of it that has to be understood or accepted before the whole thing can be understood or dealt with. (问题的)

ex.en: ...the ability to get straight to the core of a problem.
ex.zh: …直击问题核心的能力。

d: n. 果核；中心部分；核心，要点；骨干，核心成员；地核，天体的核心；核反应堆堆芯；芯体
v. 给……去核
adj. 核心的，最重要的；基础的，必修的
【名】 （Core）（英）科尔，（西、意）科雷（人名）

e.en: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist. 创造;

ex.en: We set business free to create more jobs.
ex.zh: 我们让企业自由以创造更多的就业机会。

ex.en: She could create a fight out of anything.
ex.zh: 她可以为了任何事制造争斗。

e.en: 创造

ex.en: These businesses stimulate the creation of local jobs.
ex.zh: 这些企业刺激了当地就业机会的产生。

e.en: When someone creates a new product or process, they invent it or design it. 创造;

ex.en: It is really great for a radio producer to create a show like this.
ex.zh: 一个电台节目制作人能设计出这样的节目真是太了不起了。

d: v. 创造，创建，产生（create 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: A critical time, factor, or situation is extremely important.

ex.en: The incident happened at a critical point in the campaign.
ex.zh: 该事件发生在运动的关键时刻。

ex.en: He says setting priorities is of critical importance.
ex.zh: 他说确定轻重缓急至关重要。

e.en: 关键地

ex.en: Economic prosperity depends critically on an open world trading system.
ex.zh: 经济繁荣关键取决于一个开放的世界贸易体系。

e.en: A critical situation is very serious and dangerous.

ex.en: The German authorities are considering an airlift if the situation becomes critical.
ex.zh: 德国当局正在考虑如果形势危急时进行空运。

e.en: 危急地

ex.en: Moscow is running critically low on food supplies.
ex.zh: 莫斯科的食品供应正严重匮乏。

d: adj. 批判的，爱挑剔的；极其重要的，关键的；严重的，危急的；病重的，重伤的；评论性的，评论家的；临界的

e.en: The crust on a loaf of bread is the outside part.

ex.en: Cut the crusts off the bread and soak the bread in the milk.
ex.zh: 切掉面包皮，将面包浸在牛奶中。

e.en: A pie's crust is its cooked pastry.

ex.en: The Key lime pie was bursting with flavour. Good crust, too.
ex.zh: “基”牌酸橙派味道很浓，外皮也很好。

e.en: A crust is a hard layer of something, especially on top of a softer or wetter substance.

ex.en: As the water evaporates, a crust of salt is left on the surface of the soil.
ex.zh: 水蒸发后，土壤表面留下一层盐。

e.en: The Earth's crust is its outer layer.

ex.en: Earthquakes leave scars in the Earth's crust.
ex.zh: 地震会在地壳上留下痕迹。

d: n. 面包皮；（馅饼或比萨饼等的）酥皮；硬外皮，硬外壳；地壳；生活，生计
v. 形成（或结成）硬皮（或硬壳）
n. 达科他（美国历史上的一个地区，后分为北达科他州和南达科他州）；达科他人（北美原住民苏族的一支）；达科他语（达科他人使用的语言，属苏语语系）
adj. 达科他的，达科他人的

e.en: When it is dark, there is not enough light to see properly, for example, because it is night.

ex.en: It was too dark inside to see much.
ex.zh: 里面太黑，看不见什么东西。

ex.en: People usually draw the curtains once it gets dark.
ex.zh: 天一黑，人们通常就会拉上窗帘。

e.en: 黑暗

ex.en: The light went out, and the room was plunged into darkness.
ex.zh: 灯灭了，房间陷入了黑暗之中。

e.en: If you describe something as dark, you mean that it is black in colour, or a shade that is close to black. 黑色的;

ex.en: He wore a dark suit and carried a black attaché case.
ex.zh: 他穿着深色套装，手提黑色公文包。

e.en: 呈黑色地

ex.en: The freckles on Joanne's face suddenly stood out darkly against her pale skin.
ex.zh: 在苍白的肤色映衬下，乔安脸上的雀斑一下子更明显了。

d: adj. 黑暗的，昏暗的；深色的，暗色的；恐怖的，悲惨的；神秘的，隐秘的；忧郁的，悲观的；邪恶的，阴险的；（头发、眼睛或皮肤）褐色的，黑色的；（剧院）关闭的，停业的；（嗓音）低沉圆润的；（语音）暗的
n. 黑暗，暗处；暗色，阴影；黄昏，夜幕
【名】 （Dark）（英）达克（人名）

e.en: Cubic is used in front of units of length to form units of volume such as "cubic metre" and "cubic foot."

ex.en: ...3 billion cubic metres of soil.
ex.zh: …30亿立方米的土。

d: adj. 立方的；立方体的，立方形的；（量或变量的）三次的
【名】 （Cubic）（罗）库比克（人名）
n. 戴维（男子名）；大卫（《圣经》中的古以色列国王）

e.en: Death is the permanent end of the life of a person or animal.

ex.en: 1.5 million people are in immediate danger of death from starvation.
ex.zh: 150万人正因饥饿而即将面临死亡的危险。

ex.en: ...the thirtieth anniversary of Judy Garland's death.
ex.zh: …朱迪·嘉兰逝世30周年。

e.en: The death of something is the permanent end of it.

ex.en: It meant the death of everything he had ever been or ever hoped to be.
ex.zh: 这意味着他曾拥有或希望拥有的一切的结束。

e.en: If you say that someone is at death's door, you mean they are very ill and likely to die.

ex.en: He told his boss a tale about his mother being at death's door.
ex.zh: 他给老板讲述了自己母亲病危的情况。

e.en: If you say that you will fight to the death for something, you are emphasizing that you will do anything to achieve or protect it, even if you suffer as a consequence.

ex.en: She'd have fought to the death for that child.
ex.zh: 她原想为那个孩子拼尽全力的。

d: n. 死，死亡；破灭，终止；死神

e.en: The details of something are its individual features or elements.

ex.en: The details of the plan are still being worked out.
ex.zh: 计划的细节还在制定中。

ex.en: No details of the discussions have been given.
ex.zh: 会谈的细节尚未透露。

e.en: A detail is a minor point or aspect of something, as opposed to the central ones.

ex.en: Only minor details now remain to be settled.
ex.zh: 只有细枝末节还没确定。

e.en: Details about someone or something are facts or pieces of information about them.

ex.en: See the bottom of this page for details of how to apply for this exciting offer.
ex.zh: 关于如何申请这个令人激动的机会，详情请参看本页末。

e.en: You can refer to the small features of something which are often not noticed as detail.

ex.en: We like his attention to detail and his enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 我们喜欢他对细微之处的关注，以及他的热情。

d: n. 细节，细微之处；（军队中的）任务，特遣队（detail 的复数）;详情，资料
v. 详细说明，详述；彻底清洗（汽车）；（尤指军队中）派遣，选派（detail 的第三人称单数）

e.en: You use dedicated to describe someone who enjoys a particular activity very much and spends a lot of time doing it.

ex.en: Her great-grandfather had clearly been a dedicated and stoical traveller.
ex.zh: 她的曾祖父显然曾是一个很投入的、坚忍的旅行者。

e.en: You use dedicated to describe something that is made, built, or designed for one particular purpose or thing.

ex.en: Such areas should also be served by dedicated cycle routes.
ex.zh: 这些地区也应该可由自行车专用路线到达。

ex.en: ...the world's first museum dedicated to ecology.
ex.zh: …世界上第一家专门的生态博物馆。

d: adj. 专心致志的，献身的；专用的，专门用途的
vt. 致力于，献身于；（在书、音乐或作品的前部）题献词；为（大楼，纪念碑）揭幕（dedicate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: When something such as a dead body, a dead plant, or a tooth decays, it is gradually destroyed by a natural process.

ex.en: The bodies buried in the fine ash slowly decayed.
ex.zh: 埋在细灰里的尸体慢慢腐烂了。

e.en: Decay is also a noun.

ex.en: When not removed, plaque causes tooth decay and gum disease.
ex.zh: 牙斑没有清除就会导致蛀牙和牙龈疾病。

e.en: 腐坏的

ex.en: Even young children have teeth so decayed they need to be pulled.
ex.zh: 连幼儿也有这么严重的龋齿，需要拔掉。

e.en: If something such as a society, system, or institution decays, it gradually becomes weaker or its condition gets worse. (社会、制度或机构)

ex.en: In practice, the agency system has decayed. Most "agents" now sell only to themselves or their immediate family.
ex.zh: 实际上，这种代理制已经衰退。现在，大多数“代理人”都只把产品卖给自己或亲近的家人。

d: v. （建筑、地方等）破败，衰落；（观念、影响力等）衰败；（使）腐朽，腐烂
n. 腐烂；（观念、机构、制度等）衰退
【名】 （Decay）（英、美、法、意、希）德凯（人名）

e.en: To detect something means to find it or discover that it is present somewhere by using equipment or making an investigation.

ex.en: ...a sensitive piece of equipment used to detect radiation.
ex.zh: …一台探测辐射的敏感仪器。

e.en: If you detect something, you notice it or sense it, even though it is not very obvious.

ex.en: Arnold could detect a certain sadness in the old man's face.
ex.zh: 阿诺德能察觉到老人脸上的某种悲伤。

d: v. 查明，察觉；测出，检测，识别

e.en: Distant means very far away.

ex.en: The mountains rolled away to a distant horizon.
ex.zh: 群山绵延至遥远的天边。

e.en: You use distant to describe a time or event that is very far away in the future or in the past.

ex.en: There is little doubt, however, that things will improve in the not too distant future.
ex.zh: 然而毋庸置疑的是，事情在不远的将来会有改观。

e.en: A distant relative is one who you are not closely related to.

ex.en: He's a distant relative of the mayor.
ex.zh: 他是市长的远房亲戚。

e.en: 远亲地

ex.en: The O'Shea girls are distantly related to our family.
ex.zh: 奥谢家的姑娘们和我们家沾点儿亲。

d: adj. 遥远的，久远的；冷淡的；心不在焉的；远亲的；不相似的，不同的

e.en: The difference between two things is the way in which they are unlike each other.

ex.en: That is the fundamental difference between the two societies.
ex.zh: 那是两个社会之间的根本差别。

ex.en: ...the vast difference in size.
ex.zh: …在大小方面的巨大差别。

e.en: If people have their differences about something, they disagree about it.

ex.en: The two communities are learning how to resolve their differences.
ex.zh: 这两个团体正在学会如何消除它们之间的分歧。

e.en: A difference between two quantities is the amount by which one quantity is less than the other.

ex.en: The difference is 8532.

e.en: If something makes a difference or makes a lot of difference, it affects you and helps you in what you are doing. If something makes no difference, it does not have any effect on what you are doing. 有 (某程度的) 影响/

ex.en: Where you live can make such a difference to the way you feel.
ex.zh: 你居住的位置会对你的感觉产生很大的影响。

d: n. （difference 的复数形式）差异，差别，不同之处；分歧，意见不合；差，差额；偏差

e.en: An electric device or machine works by means of electricity, rather than using some other source of power.

ex.en: ...her electric guitar.
ex.zh: …她的电吉他。

e.en: An electric current, voltage, or charge is one that is produced by electricity.
Electric plugs, sockets, or power lines are designed to carry electricity.

ex.en: More people are deciding that electric power lines could present a health risk.
ex.zh: 更多的人在认为电线可能会带来健康隐患。

e.en: Electric is used to refer to the supply of electricity.

ex.en: An average electric bill might go up $2 or $3 per month.
ex.zh: 一张普通电费单可能每月上涨$2或$3。

d: adj. 电的；令人激动的；电子扩音的
n. 电路系统；电气交通工具

e.en: A drawing is a picture made with a pencil or pen.

ex.en: She did a drawing of me.
ex.zh: 她为我画了张素描。

d: n.  图画，素描画；绘画（艺术），制图技巧；抽签，抽奖；图画，素描画
v. 画；拉；吸引（draw 的现在分词）

e.en: When things such as clothes are dry-cleaned, they are cleaned with a liquid chemical rather than with water.

ex.en: Natural-filled duvets must be dry-cleaned by a professional.
ex.zh: 天然材料填充的羽绒被必须由专业人士干洗。

d: v. 干洗；（使）干洗（dry-clean 的现在分词）
n. 干洗

e.en: If you endure a painful or difficult situation, you experience it and do not avoid it or give up, usually because you cannot.

ex.en: The company endured heavy financial losses.
ex.zh: 公司承受了沉重的财务损失。

e.en: If something endures, it continues to exist without any loss in quality or importance.

ex.en: Somehow the language endures and continues to survive.
ex.zh: 由于某种原因，这种语言持续生存下来了。

e.en: 持久的

ex.en: This chance meeting was the start of an enduring friendship.
ex.zh: 这次偶然的相遇是一段持久友情的开始。

d: adj. 持久的，持续的
v. 持续存在，持久；忍受，忍耐（endure 的现在分词）

e.en: Engineering is the work involved in designing and constructing engines and machinery or structures such as roads and bridges. Engineering is also the subject studied by people who want to do this work. 工程;

ex.en: ...graduates with degrees in engineering.
ex.zh: …获得工程学学位的毕业生。

d: n. 工程，工程学；控制，引导，管理；筹划，出谋划策

v. 设计，建造；策划，精心安排（engineer 
 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Something that is enormous is extremely large in size or amount.

ex.en: The main bedroom is enormous.
ex.zh: 主卧室大极了。

e.en: You can use enormous to emphasize the great degree or extent of something. (程度、范围)

ex.en: It was an enormous disappointment.
ex.zh: 这是件令人极为失望的事。

e.en: 极其地

ex.en: This book was enormously influential.
ex.zh: 这本书影响极大。

d: adj. 巨大的，极大的；凶暴的，极恶的

e.en: Evil is a powerful force that some people believe to exist, and that causes wicked and bad things to happen. 恶;

ex.en: There's always a conflict between good and evil in his plays.
ex.zh: 他的戏剧中总是有善与恶的冲突。

e.en: Evil is used to refer to all the wicked and bad things that happen in the world.

ex.en: He could not, after all, stop all the evil in the world.
ex.zh: 他毕竟不能阻止世上所有的恶行。

e.en: If you refer to an evil, you mean a very unpleasant or harmful situation or activity. 不愉快的事;

ex.en: Higher taxes may be a necessary evil.
ex.zh: 提高税率虽不是件令人愉快的事，但可能是必要的。

e.en: If you describe someone as evil, you mean that they are very wicked by nature and take pleasure in doing things that harm other people. 邪恶的;

ex.en: ...the country's most evil terrorists.
ex.zh: …该国最凶恶的恐怖分子。

d: adj. 恶毒的，邪恶的；有害的，易造成伤害的；讨厌的，令人不舒服的；恶魔的，不祥的
n. 有害（或不受欢迎）的事；邪恶，罪恶；坏事，恶行

e.en: An event is something that happens, especially when it is unusual or important. You can use events to describe all the things that are happening in a particular situation. (尤指特殊、重大)

ex.en: A new inquiry into the events of the day was opened in 2002.
ex.zh: 对那天发生的事件的新一轮调查于2002年开始。

e.en: An event is a planned and organized occasion, for example a social gathering or a sports tournament. (有计划、有组织的)

ex.en: ...major sporting events.
ex.zh: …重大体育赛事。

e.en: An event is one of the races or competitions that are part of an organized occasion such as a sports tournament.

ex.en: The main events start at 1 p.m.
ex.zh: 主赛项目下午1点开始。

e.en: You use in the event of, in the event that, and in that event when you are talking about a possible future situation, especially when you are planning what to do if it occurs.

ex.en: The bank has agreed to give an immediate refund in the unlikely event of an error being made.
ex.zh: 银行已同意倘若出现不太可能的错误便立即退款。

d: n. 事件；公开活动，社交场合；比赛项目（event 的复数）；时事（current events）

e.en: If something is exciting, it makes you feel very happy or enthusiastic.

ex.en: The race itself is very exciting.
ex.zh: 比赛本身就令人非常兴奋。

d: adj. 令人兴奋的，令人激动的；惊险刺激的（尤指无法预知下一步将发生什么）
v. 使兴奋，使激动；激发，引起（excite 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Something that is experimental is new or uses new ideas or methods, and might be modified later if it is unsuccessful.

ex.en: ...an experimental air-conditioning system.
ex.zh: …一种试验性的空调系统。

e.en: Experimental means using, used in, or resulting from scientific experiments.

ex.en: ...the main techniques of experimental science.
ex.zh: …实验科学的主要技术。

e.en: 实验地

ex.en: ...an ecology laboratory, where communities of species can be studied experimentally under controlled conditions.
ex.zh: …一个可在受控条件下对物种群落进行实验研究的生态实验室。

e.en: An experimental action is done in order to see what it is like, or what effects it has.

ex.en: The senator is ready to argue for an experimental lifting of the ban.
ex.zh: 该参议员已准备好争取那条禁令的试验性解除。

d: adj. 实验性的，试验性的；根据经验的，经验上的

e.en: An experiment is a scientific test done in order to discover what happens to something in particular conditions.

ex.en: The astronauts are conducting a series of experiments to learn more about how the body adapts to weightlessness.
ex.zh: 那些宇航员正在进行一系列实验，以便更多地了解人体如何适应失重状态。

e.en: If you experiment with something or experiment on it, you do a scientific test on it in order to discover what happens to it in particular conditions.

ex.en: In 1857 Mendel started experimenting with peas in his monastery garden.
ex.zh: 1857年孟德尔开始在其修道院菜园里用豌豆做实验。

ex.en: The scientists have experimented on the tiny neck arteries of rats.
ex.zh: 那些科学家已在老鼠细小的颈动脉上做了实验。

e.en: 实验

ex.en: ...the ethical aspects of animal experimentation.
ex.zh: …动物实验的伦理视角。

e.en: An experiment is the trying out of a new idea or method in order to see what it is like and what effects it has.

ex.en: As an experiment, we bought Ted a watch.
ex.zh: 作为尝试，我们给特德买了块手表。

d: n. 实验，试验（experiment 的复数）；尝试（experiment 的复数）
v. 做实验，进行试验；尝试（experiment 的第三人称单数现在时形式）

e.en: If you fill a container or area, or if it fills, an amount of something enters it that is enough to make it full.

ex.en: She went to the bathroom, filled a glass with water, returned to the bed.
ex.zh: 她去了盥洗室，灌满了一杯水，回到床前。

ex.en: The boy's eyes filled with tears.
ex.zh: 那男孩的眼里充满了泪水。

e.en: Fill up means the same as .

ex.en: Warehouses at the frontier between the two countries fill up with sacks of rice and flour.
ex.zh: 两国交界处的仓库里装满了一袋袋大米和面粉。

e.en: If something fills a space, it is so big, or there are such large quantities of it, that there is very little room left.

ex.en: He cast his eyes at the rows of cabinets that filled the enormous work area.
ex.zh: 他把目光投向了一排排占满了庞大工作区的柜子。

e.en: Fill up means the same as . 占满 (同)(fill)

ex.en: ...the complicated machines that fill up today's laboratories.
ex.zh: …占满了现今实验室的复杂机器。

d: adj. 充满的
v. （使）充满；堵塞，填补（洞、孔）；（声音、气味或光）遍及，弥漫（fill 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Facilities are buildings, pieces of equipment, or services that are provided for a particular purpose.

ex.en: What recreational facilities are now available?
ex.zh: 什么娱乐设施现在是可用的？

e.en: A facility is something such as an additional service provided by an organization or an extra feature on a machine which is useful but not essential. 附加服务;

ex.en: One of the new models has the facility to reproduce speech as well as text.
ex.zh: 新款型中的一款有复制言语和文本的附加功能。

e.en: If you have a facility for something, for example learning a language, you find it easy to do.

ex.en: He and Marcia shared a facility for languages.
ex.zh: 他和马西娅都具有语言天赋。

d: n. 设施，工具，设备（facility 的复数）；（金融）信贷安排，融资便利（常作 credit facilities、loan facilities 等）

e.en: The flagship of a group of things that are owned or produced by a particular organization is the most important one.

ex.en: The company plans to open a flagship shop in New York this month.
ex.zh: 该公司计划本月在纽约开一家旗舰店。

e.en: A flagship is the most important ship in a fleet of ships, especially the one on which the commander of the fleet is sailing.

d: n. 旗舰（舰队司令乘坐的指挥舰）；最重要者，王牌产品，佼佼者；（作定语）一流的，最主要的

e.en: A filling is a small amount of metal or plastic that a dentist puts in a hole in a tooth to prevent further decay. (补牙用的)

ex.en: The longer your child can go without needing a filling, the better.
ex.zh: 你的孩子不需要补牙的时间越长越好。

e.en: The filling in something such as a cake, pie, or sandwich is a substance or mixture that is put inside it. (糕点里的)

ex.en: Spread some of the filling over each cold pancake and then either roll or fold.
ex.zh: 先将一些馅摊在每个凉煎饼上，再卷起来或叠起来。

e.en: The filling in a piece of soft furniture or in a cushion is the soft substance inside it. (软家具或垫子的)

ex.en: ...second-hand sofas with old-style foam fillings.
ex.zh: …旧式海绵芯的二手沙发。

e.en: Food that is filling makes you feel full when you have eaten it. (食物)

ex.en: Although it is tasty, crab is very filling.
ex.zh: 螃蟹虽然好吃，但很容易让人饱。

d: adj. （食品）给人以满足感的，使人得到享受的；容易填饱肚子的
n. 填补物；（靠垫、枕头等的）填充料；（糕点或馅饼里的）馅，夹心
【名】 （Filling）（瑞典）菲林（人名）
v. （使）充满，占满；堵塞，填补；满足（fill 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you act with forethought, you think carefully before you act about what will be needed, or about what the consequences will be.

ex.en: With a little forethought many accidents could be avoided.
ex.zh: 做些事前筹划可防止多起事故的发生。

d: n. 深谋远虑，先见，考虑将来；预先筹划，预谋
adj. 预先计划好的
n. 弗朗西斯（男子名，义为自由之人）；（天主教）方济各（教皇方济各的名号）

e.en: Former is used to describe someone who used to have a particular job, position, or role, but no longer has it.

ex.en: The unemployed executives include former sales managers, directors and accountants.
ex.zh: 失业的高管包括前销售经理、主管和会计。

ex.en: ...former president Richard Nixon.
ex.zh: …前总统理查德·尼克松。

e.en: Former is used to refer to countries which no longer exist or whose boundaries have changed. (国家) 已不存在的;

ex.en: ...the former Soviet Union.
ex.zh: …前苏联。

e.en: Former is used to describe something which used to belong to someone or which used to be a particular thing.

ex.en: ...the former home of Robert E. Lee.
ex.zh: …罗伯特·E·李的故居。

e.en: When two people, things, or groups have just been mentioned, you can refer to the first of them as the former.

ex.en: They grappled with the problem of connecting the electricity and water supplies. The former proved simple compared with the latter.
ex.zh: 他们设法解决供电和供水的连接问题。前者与后者相比证明很简单。

d: adj. 旧时的；以前的，前……；（两者中）前者的
n. 模子，模型；形成某事的人（或事）；线圈架，绕线模；（机翼、机身的）翼肋
pron. （两者中的）前者
【名】 （Former）（法）福尔梅，（德、捷）福尔默（人名）

e.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

ex.en: Our constitution embodies all the fundamental principles of democracy.
ex.zh: 我们的宪法体现了民主的所有基本原则。

ex.en: A fundamental human right is being withheld from these people.
ex.zh: 这些人的一项基本人权正被剥夺。

e.en: You use fundamental to describe something which exists at a deep and basic level, and is therefore likely to continue.

ex.en: But on this question, the two leaders have very fundamental differences.
ex.zh: 但在这个问题上，这两位领导人有着极根本的分歧。

e.en: If one thing is fundamental to another, it is absolutely necessary to it, and the second thing cannot exist, succeed, or be imagined without it.

ex.en: He believes better relations with China are fundamental to the well-being of the area.
ex.zh: 他相信与中国的更好关系对这个地区的福祉是绝对必要的。

e.en: You can use fundamental to show that you are referring to what you consider to be the most important aspect of a situation, and that you are not concerned with less important details.

ex.en: The fundamental problem lies in their inability to distinguish between reality and invention.
ex.zh: 主要问题在于他们不能区分现实和虚构。

d: adj. 根本的，基本的；必需的，必不可少的；不能再分的
n. 基本原理；基音，基频

e.en: Something that is ghostly seems unreal or unnatural and may be frightening because of this.

ex.en: ...Sonia's ghostly laughter.
ex.zh: …索尼娅可怕的怪笑。

e.en: A ghostly presence is the ghost or spirit of a dead person.

ex.en: ...the ghostly presences which haunt these islands.
ex.zh: …经常出没于这些岛屿的幽灵。

d: adj. 幽灵的，鬼的，鬼魂的；幽灵般的，阴森可怕的，影子似的

e.en: Something that is described as giant is much larger or more important than most others of its kind. 巨大的;

ex.en: ...America's giant car maker, General Motors.
ex.zh: …美国的汽车制造巨头——通用汽车公司。

ex.en: ...a giant oak table.
ex.zh: …一张巨大的栎木桌。

e.en: Giant is often used to refer to any large, successful business organization or country. 大企业;

ex.en: ...Japanese electronics giant, Sony.
ex.zh: …日本的电子业巨头——索尼公司。

e.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. (尤指古老故事中虚构的)

ex.en: ...a Nordic saga of giants.
ex.zh: …一部关于巨人的北欧传奇。

d: n. （传说中的）巨人；高大健壮的人；巨兽，巨型植物；大公司，大国；卓越人物，伟人；（天文）巨星
adj. 巨大的，伟大的

e.en: An apology is something that you say or write in order to tell someone that you are sorry that you have hurt them or caused trouble for them.

ex.en: I didn't get an apology.
ex.zh: 我没有得到道歉之词。

ex.en: We received a letter of apology.
ex.zh: 我们收到了一封致歉信。

e.en: If you offer or make your apologies, you apologize. (表达)

ex.en: When Mary finally appeared, she made her apologies to Mrs. Velasquez.
ex.zh: 当玛丽最终露面时，她向委拉斯开兹夫人道了歉。

d: n. 道歉，歉意；道歉语（apology 的复数，可独立成句，相当于“抱歉”“对不起”）；致歉（正式，常用于 make/offer one's apologies 等固定搭配）

e.en: A message is a piece of information or a request that you send to someone or leave for them when you cannot speak to them directly.

ex.en: I got a message you were trying to reach me.
ex.zh: 我得到了一条留言，说你在设法联系我。

e.en: The message that someone is trying to communicate, for example in a book or play, is the idea or point that they are trying to communicate.

ex.en: The report's message was unequivocal.
ex.zh: 报告中传达的信息相当明确。

ex.en: I no longer want to be friends with her but I don't know how to get the message across.
ex.zh: 我再也不想和她做朋友了，但我不知道如何告诉她。

e.en: If you message someone, you send them a message electronically using a computer or another device such as a mobile phone.

ex.en: People who message a lot feel unpopular if they don't get many back.
ex.zh: 如果发送许多短信的人并未得到很多回复，他们会觉得自己不受欢迎。

d: n. 口信，消息；（书籍、演讲等的）要旨，主题思想；（从大脑发给身体某部位或身体某部位向大脑发送的）信息；购物；电视广告；差使；启示，教训；（先知的）预言
v. （尤指以电子形式）传送（信息）；通报

e.en: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear. 清楚的;

ex.en: The book is clear, readable, and adequately illustrated.
ex.zh: 这本书易懂易读，而且图解充足。

ex.en: The space telescope has taken the clearest pictures ever of Pluto.
ex.zh: 太空望远镜拍下了有史以来最清晰的冥王星的照片。

e.en: 清楚地;

ex.en: Whales journey up the coast of California, clearly visible from the beach.
ex.zh: 鲸鱼们朝着加利福尼亚海岸游过来，从海滩就能清楚地看见。

e.en: Something that is clear is obvious and impossible to be mistaken about.

ex.en: It was a clear case of homicide.
ex.zh: 这是一起确信无疑的谋杀案。

ex.en: It became clear that I hadn't been able to convince Mike.
ex.zh: 显然我没能说服迈克。

e.en: 显然无疑地

ex.en: Clearly, the police cannot break the law in order to enforce it.
ex.zh: 显然地，警察不能为了执法而违法。

d: adj. 易懂的，明白的；明显的，明确的；完全了解的，清楚的；透明的，清澈的；易看清的，听得清的；（颜色）明亮的，鲜明的；（皮肤）光洁的；没有问题的，健康的；晴朗的；畅通的，无阻碍的；（时间）空闲的；完整的；问心无愧的，清白的；头脑清醒的，思维敏锐的；（比分）领先的；未碰触的，悬离的；摆脱掉（不愉快事物）的；（钱款）净得的，纯收入的；发音清晰的
v. 清除，清理；恢复畅通，不再受阻；证明……无罪；批准，许可；准许……入境（出境）；（使）不再困惑，（使）变清醒；获利，净赚；清偿（债务）；兑现（支票）；（天气）变晴朗；（液体）变清澈；（视力）变清晰；（烟雾等）开始消失；（皮肤）变光滑，变健康；（表情）放松，舒展；使离开，清场；穿过，越过；解决，成功地处理；做完（所有工作）；踢出解围球
adv. 一直；离开，不靠近；清除了地，理清了地；全地，整地，满地，足地；清楚地，清晰地
n. 清白的，无罪的（in the clear）；不再困难的，已脱险的（in the clear）；清除；空隙

e.en: Gratitude is the state of feeling grateful.

ex.en: I wish to express my gratitude to Kathy Davis for her immense practical help.
ex.zh: 我想向凯西•戴维斯表达谢意，因为她给了我许多实际的帮助。

d: n. 感激之情，感谢

e.en: You use great to describe something that is very large. Great is more formal than big.

ex.en: The room had a great bay window.
ex.zh: 这个房间有个巨大的凸窗。

e.en: Great means large in amount or degree. (数量或程度)

ex.en: Benjamin Britten did not live to a great age.
ex.zh: 本杰明•布里滕没有活到很大的岁数。

e.en: You use great to describe something that is important, famous, or exciting.

ex.en: ...the great cultural achievements of the past.
ex.zh: …过去重大的文化成就。

e.en: 重大

ex.en: A nation must take certain risks to achieve greatness.
ex.zh: 一个国家必须冒一定风险来成就伟大的事业。

d: adj. 伟大的，著名的；大型的，巨大的；（数量或程度）极大的，很大的；美妙的；身心健康的，精力充沛的；重要的，重大的；热心的，热衷的；和蔼的，随和的；（外）曾祖（或曾孙）的；（二人）亲近的，亲密的；擅长……的
adv. 很好地，很棒地
n. 伟人，伟大的事物；金曲

e.en: A note is a short letter.

ex.en: Stevens wrote him a note asking him to come to his apartment.
ex.zh: 史蒂文斯给他写了个便条让他到他的公寓来。

e.en: A note is something that you write down to remind yourself of something. 记录;

ex.en: I knew that if I didn't make a note I would lose the thought so I asked to borrow a pen or pencil.
ex.zh: 我知道如果我不做一个记录我就会忘记这个想法，于是我要求借支钢笔或铅笔。

ex.en: She wasn't taking notes on the lecture.
ex.zh: 她没记讲座笔记。

e.en: In a book or article, a note is a short piece of additional information.

ex.en: See Note 16 on p. 223.
ex.zh: 参见223页的注释16。

e.en: A note is a short document that has to be signed by someone and that gives official information about something. 证明;

ex.en: Since Mr. Bennett was going to need some time off work, he asked for a sick note.
ex.zh: 因为本内特先生需要请假一段时间，所以他要求开一张病假条。

d: n. 短笺，便条；笔记，记录；注释，批注；正式文件，票据，证明书；音，音符；语气，气氛；钞票；重要性，值得注意之处（of note）
v. 留意，注意；指出，提及；记录，记下
【名】 （Note）（美、法）诺特（人名）

e.en: When you read something such as a book or article, you look at and understand the words that are written there.

ex.en: Have you read this book?
ex.zh: 你读过这本书吗？

ex.en: I read about it in the paper.
ex.zh: 我在报上读到有关它的消息。

e.en: Read is also a noun.

ex.en: I settled down to have a good read.
ex.zh: 我舒舒服服地坐下来，想好好读书。

e.en: When you read a piece of writing to someone, you say the words aloud.

ex.en: Jay reads poetry so beautifully.
ex.zh: 杰伊朗读诗歌非常动听。

ex.en: I like it when she reads to us.
ex.zh: 我很喜欢她读书给我们听。

e.en: People who can read have the ability to look at and understand written words.

ex.en: He couldn't read or write.
ex.zh: 他不识字，也不会写字。

ex.en: The kid can read words, but did miserably on the test.
ex.zh: 这孩子能认字，但考试时却一塌糊涂。

d: v. 阅读，读懂；朗读；（在书籍、报纸等中）读到，看到；解读，（按某种方式）理解；看透（想法或心思）；读起来（给人以某种印象）；有……的字样，写着；换用，改作（用于订正讹误）；读取（磁盘中的信息）；（通过无线电）收听到，听明白；（测量仪器）指示，显示；看（度量仪器显示的数字）；攻读；将（议案或其他法令）提交立法机构
n. 阅读，阅读时间；读物；解释，阐明
adj. 博学的，有学问的
【名】 （Read）（英）里德（人名）

e.en: A saying is a sentence that people often say and that gives advice or information about human life and experience. 谚语;

ex.en: We also realize the truth of that old saying: Charity begins at home.
ex.zh: 我们也明白那句老话很有道理：仁爱始于家庭。

d: n. 谚语，格言，警句；（尤指宗教或政治领袖的）重要讲话，教诲
v. 说，讲；宣称，说明；认为，据说（say 的现在分词）

e.en: Your shoulders are between your neck and the tops of your arms.

ex.en: She led him to an armchair, with her arm round his shoulder.
ex.zh: 她把他领到扶手椅上，手臂搂住了他的肩膀。

e.en: When you talk about someone's problems or responsibilities, you can say that they carry them on their shoulders.

ex.en: No one suspected the anguish he carried on his shoulders.
ex.zh: 没有人怀疑他所承受的痛苦。

e.en: If you shoulder the responsibility or the blame for something, you accept it.

ex.en: He has had to shoulder the responsibility of his father's mistakes.
ex.zh: 他不得不肩负起他父亲所犯错误的责任。

e.en: If you shoulder someone aside or if you shoulder your way somewhere, you push past people roughly using your shoulder. 用肩推;

ex.en: The policemen rushed past him, shouldering him aside.
ex.zh: 警察们从他身边匆匆走过，用肩膀把他推到了一边。

ex.en: She could do nothing to stop him as he shouldered his way into the house.
ex.zh: 当他用肩推挤着进那房子时，她根本就阻止不了他。

d: n. 肩，肩膀；双肩，上背部（shoulders）；（衣服的）肩部；（动物的）前腿连肩肉，肘子；山肩，瓶肩； （公路旁的）路肩，紧急停车道；（担负责任或艰难困苦或提供力量的）肩膀；（四足动物的）肩背；（鸟、昆虫的）肩背
v. 承担，担负；挤，闯；（用肩膀）推开，顶开；肩扛，肩挑

e.en: You say "Sorry" or "I'm sorry" as a way of apologizing to someone for something that you have done which has upset them or caused them difficulties, or when you bump into them accidentally.

ex.en: "We're all talking at the same time."—"Yeah. Sorry."
ex.zh: “我们都在同时说话。”—“呃，对不起。”

ex.en: Sorry I took so long.
ex.zh: 对不起，我用了这么长时间。

e.en: If you are sorry about a situation, you feel regret, sadness, or disappointment about it. 遗憾的;

ex.en: She was very sorry about all the trouble she'd caused.
ex.zh: 她对自己造成的麻烦感到很内疚。

ex.en: I'm sorry he's gone.
ex.zh: 他走了我感到遗憾。

e.en: You use I'm sorry or sorry as an introduction when you are telling a person something that you do not think they will want to hear, for example when you are disagreeing with them or giving them bad news. 抱歉 (用于表示不同意或不好的消息)

ex.en: No, I'm sorry, I can't agree with you.
ex.zh: 不，抱歉，我不同意你。

ex.en: "I'm sorry," he told the real estate agent, "but we really must go now."
ex.zh: “对不起，”他告诉房地产经纪人，“但我们的确要走了。”

e.en: You use the expression I'm sorry to say to express regret together with disappointment or disapproval.

ex.en: I've only done half of it, I'm sorry to say.
ex.zh: 我只做了一半，很遗憾。

d: adj. 抱歉的，惭愧的，歉疚的；表示同情的，难过的；后悔的，懊悔的；可怜的，糟糕的
int. （用于表示歉意）对不起，抱歉；没听清，请再讲一遍；（纠正自己说错的话）不对，应该是

e.en: If something usually happens, it is the thing that most often happens in a particular situation.

ex.en: The best information about hotels usually comes from friends and acquaintances who have been there.
ex.zh: 有关旅馆的最佳信息通常来自曾经去过那儿的朋友和熟人。

ex.en: Usually, the work is boring.
ex.zh: 通常这种工作很乏味。

e.en: You use more than usually to show that something shows even more of a particular quality than it normally does.

ex.en: She felt more than usually hungry after her excursion.
ex.zh: 远足后她感到非同寻常地饥饿。

d: adv. 通常地，经常地

e.en: The warmth of something is the heat that it has or produces.

ex.en: She went further into the room, drawn by the warmth of the fire.
ex.zh: 她被火的温暖吸引着，走进了房间。

e.en: The warmth of something such as a garment or blanket is the protection that it gives you against the cold.

ex.en: The blanket will provide additional warmth and comfort in bed.
ex.zh: 毯子能让你睡觉时感觉更温暖更舒适。

d: n. 温暖，暖和；热情，友好；激动

e.en: Abuse of someone is cruel and violent treatment of them.

ex.en: ...investigation of alleged child abuse.
ex.zh: …对涉嫌虐待儿童的调查。

ex.en: ...victims of sexual and physical abuse.
ex.zh: …性虐待和肉体摧残的受害者们。

e.en: Abuse is extremely rude and insulting things that people say when they are angry.

ex.en: I was left shouting abuse as the car sped off.
ex.zh: 当车加速离去时，我在那里破口大骂。

e.en: Abuse of something is the use of it in a wrong way or for a bad purpose.

ex.en: What went on here was an abuse of power.
ex.zh: 这里发生的情况是职权的滥用。

e.en: If someone is abused, they are treated cruelly and violently.

ex.en: Janet had been abused by her father since she was eleven.
ex.zh: 詹妮特自从11岁起就被她的父亲虐待。

ex.en: ...parents who feel they cannot cope or might abuse their children.
ex.zh: …感到自己不能应付或可能虐待孩子的家长们。

d: v. 虐待；滥用，辜负；辱骂；糟蹋（某物）；性侵犯
n. 虐待，凌辱；滥用，妄用；辱骂；舞弊，腐败；糟蹋；性侵犯；恶习，陋习
【名】 （Abuse）（英）阿比斯（人名）

e.en: You use actual to emphasize that you are referring to something real or genuine.

ex.en: The segments are filmed using either local actors or the actual people involved.
ex.zh: 这些片段是用当地的演员或真实的当事人拍摄的。

e.en: You use actual to contrast the important aspect of something with a less important aspect.

ex.en: She had compiled pages of notes, but she had not yet got down to doing the actual writing.
ex.zh: 她已辑录了多篇笔记，但她还没有着手实际的写作。

d: adj. 真实的，实际的，现实的；（用于对比主次方面）真正的；现存的，当前的

e.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack other people.

ex.en: Some children are much more aggressive than others.
ex.zh: 一些孩子比其他孩子好斗得多。

ex.en: These fish are very aggressive.
ex.zh: 这些鱼十分好斗。

e.en: 好斗地

ex.en: They'll react aggressively.
ex.zh: 他们会凶猛地作出反应。

e.en: People who are aggressive in their work or other activities behave in a forceful way because they are very eager to succeed.

ex.en: He is respected as a very aggressive and competitive executive.
ex.zh: 他被尊认为一位十分好强好胜的主管。

e.en: 好强地

ex.en: ...countries noted for aggressively pursuing energy efficiency.
ex.zh: …以拼命追求能效著称的国家。

d: adj. 好斗的，挑衅的；积极进取的；非常严重的；强烈的

e.en: You use albeit to introduce a fact or comment that reduces the force or significance of what you have just said.

ex.en: Charles's letter was indeed published, albeit in a somewhat abbreviated form.
ex.zh: 查尔斯的信确实被刊登了出来，尽管有些删节。

d: conj.  虽然，尽管
【名】 （Albeit）（美、英、马）艾乐贝特（人名）

e.en: Anger is the strong emotion that you feel when you think that someone has behaved in an unfair, cruel, or unacceptable way.

ex.en: He cried with anger and frustration.
ex.zh: 他愤怒而沮丧地哭了。

e.en: If something angers you, it makes you feel angry.

ex.en: The decision to allow more offshore oil drilling angered some Californians.
ex.zh: 这个允许更多海底石油钻探的决定激怒了一些加利福尼亚人。

d: n. 愤怒，怒火
v. 使生气，激怒
【名】 （Anger）（法）安热，（德、捷、瑞典）安格尔，（罗）安杰尔（人名）

e.en: to move a (typewriter carriage) backwards
a typewriter key that effects such a movement

d: n. （打字机或电脑键盘的）退格键；（计算机）退格符，退格字符；（旧式录像机或摄影机上的）返回装置
v. 退格，回退（按退格键使光标或输入位置后退，通常用于删除前一个字符）

e.en: Beauty is the state or quality of being beautiful.

ex.en: ...an area of outstanding natural beauty.
ex.zh: …一处具有非凡自然之美的地区。

e.en: A beauty is a beautiful woman.

ex.en: She is known as a great beauty.
ex.zh: 她是个众所皆知的大美人。

e.en: You can say that something is a beauty when you think it is very good.

ex.en: It was the one opportunity in the game – the pass was a real beauty, but the shot was poor.
ex.zh: 那是比赛中的一个机会–传球的确很漂亮，但射门却很糟。

e.en: The beauties of something are its attractive qualities or features.

ex.en: He was beginning to enjoy the beauties of nature.
ex.zh: 他渐渐喜欢上了大自然的迷人之处。

d: n. 美丽，漂亮；美好的事物，上品；美人，美女；魅力，吸引人之处；优点，妙处；美容品，化妆品
adj. （产品、工作或活动）美容的

e.en: British Coal Corporation (formerly the National Coal Board) 英国煤炭公司;
e.zh: 前身为国家煤炭委员会

d: 体心立方；基底细胞癌(basal cell carcinoma)；英国商会(British Chambers of Commerce)

e.en: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most beautiful woman at a party or in a group.

d: n. （旧式）（尤指某活动或某场合的）美女；Belle（英语及法语人名，常用作女性名字，常见译名：贝儿、贝莱、贝尔等）

e.en: If you describe someone or something as bland, you mean that they are rather dull and unexciting. 没精打采的;

ex.en: Serle has a blander personality than Howard.
ex.zh: 塞尔在个性上比霍华德更沉闷。

ex.en: It sounds like a commercial: easy on the ear but bland and forgettable.
ex.zh: 它听起来像句广告语：顺耳却平淡易忘。

e.en: Food that is bland has very little flavour. (食物)

ex.en: It tasted bland and insipid, like warmed cardboard.
ex.zh: 它吃起来淡而无味，像加热过的卡纸板。

d: adj. 平淡的，枯燥乏味的；（食品，饮料）未加调料的，清淡的；沉稳的，无动于衷的；（评论或话语）温和的，无关痛痒的
【名】 （Bland）（英）布兰德（人名）

e.en: Your breath is the air that you let out through your mouth when you breathe. If someone has bad breath, their breath smells unpleasant.

ex.en: I could smell the whisky on his breath.
ex.zh: 我能从他的呼气中闻到威士忌酒味。

e.en: When you take a breath, you breathe in once.

ex.en: He took a deep breath, and began to climb the stairs.
ex.zh: 他深深地吸了一口气,然后开始爬楼梯。

ex.en: Gasping for breath, she leaned against the door.
ex.zh: 她靠在门上,大口喘着气,

e.en: If you go outside for a breath of fresh air or for a breath of air, you go outside because it is unpleasantly warm indoors. (到户外)

ex.en: I had to step outside for a breath of fresh air.
ex.zh: 我得到外面去透口气。

e.en: If you describe something new or different as a breath of fresh air, you mean that it makes a situation or subject more interesting or exciting.

ex.en: Her brisk treatment of an almost taboo subject was a breath of fresh air.
ex.zh: 她对一个几乎是禁忌话题的干脆处理令人耳目一新。

d: n. 呼吸，气息；一次吸入的空气；（风或气流的）一丝，丝毫；微量，迹象；一瞬间

e.en: Capitalism is an economic and political system in which property, business, and industry are owned by private individuals and not by the state.

ex.en: ...the two fundamentally opposed social systems, capitalism and socialism.
ex.zh: …两种根本对立的社会制度，资本主义与社会主义。

d: n. 资本主义

e.en: In chess, checkmate is a situation in which you cannot stop your king from being captured and so you lose the game.

d: n. （国际象棋）将死，将杀；败局，彻底失败；最终战胜，彻底胜利
v. （国际象棋）把……将死，将杀；使……彻底失败，彻底击败，彻底战胜
int. （国际象棋）将死！

e.en: Chosen is the past participle of . (choose)

d: vt. 选择（choose 的过去分词）
adj. 挑选出来的，选定的，精选的
n. the chosen：被选中的人（们）；（宗教）被神拣选的人（选民）
adv. 仔细地，严密地；（联系）紧密地；秘密地，暗中地；（时间或位置上）接近地，不远地；相似地，不相上下地

e.en: Coded messages have words or symbols which represent other words, so that the message is secret unless you know the system behind the code.

ex.en: In a coded telephone warning, the police were told four bombs had been planted in the area.
ex.zh: 通过一个加密的电话警告，警察得知4枚炸弹被放置在那个地区。

e.en: If someone is using coded language, they are expressing their opinion in an indirect way, usually because that opinion is likely to offend people.

ex.en: They have sent barely coded messages to the secretary of education endorsing this criticism.
ex.zh: 他们毫不隐讳地把信息传达给教育部长，支持该批评意见。

e.en: Coded electronic signals use a binary system of digits which can be decoded by an appropriate machine.

ex.en: The coded signal is received by satellite dishes.
ex.zh: 电码信号通过卫星天线接收。

d: adj. 加密的，用密码写的，编码的；标有代码、编号或颜色等标记以便识别、分类的；间接表达的，隐晦的，含蓄的
v. 把……译成密码；为……编号；编程序，编码；间接或委婉表达；（生化）是（某种氨基酸）的遗传密码，是（某种特征的）遗传决定因素（code 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If there is confusion about something, it is not clear what the true situation is, especially because people believe different things.

ex.en: There's still confusion about the number of students.
ex.zh: 学生的人数依然不清楚。

e.en: Confusion is a situation in which everything is in disorder, especially because there are lots of things happening at the same time.

ex.en: There was confusion when a man fired shots.
ex.zh: 一名男子开了枪，出现了混乱。

d: n. 困惑，不明确；混淆，混同；慌乱，窘迫；混乱局面，乱成一团

e.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

ex.en: For a time he contemplated a career as an army medical doctor.
ex.zh: 他曾一度考虑做一名军医。

e.en: If you contemplate an idea or subject, you think about it carefully for a long time.

ex.en: As he lay in his hospital bed that night, he cried as he contemplated his future.
ex.zh: 那天晚上他躺在医院病床上，当他反复考虑自己的未来时他哭了。

e.en: 考虑再三

ex.en: It is a place of quiet contemplation.
ex.zh: 这是一个适合静静深思的地方。

e.en: If you contemplate something or someone, you look at them for a long time.

ex.en: He contemplated his hands, still frowning.
ex.zh: 他凝视着他的双手，依然皱着眉头。

d: v. 考虑，盘算，打算；沉思，冥想；凝视，注视（contemplate 的现在分词／动名词形式）

e.en: Conversational means relating to, or similar to, casual and informal talk.

ex.en: What is refreshing is the author's easy, conversational style.
ex.zh: 使人耳目一新的是作者流畅的、谈话式的写作风格。

d: adj. （谈话的风格、用语等）会话式的，口语的；谈话的，会话的

e.en: If something is correct, it is right and true.

ex.en: The correct answers can be found at the bottom of page 8.
ex.zh: 正确答案可以在第8页的底部找到。

ex.en: The following information was correct at time of going to press.
ex.zh: 以下信息在付印时是准确无误的。

e.en: 正确地

ex.en: Did I pronounce your name correctly?
ex.zh: 我把你的名字读对了吗？

e.en: If someone is correct, what they have said or thought is true.

ex.en: You are absolutely correct. The leaves are from a bay tree.
ex.zh: 你的看法完全正确。这些是月桂树的叶子。

e.en: The correct thing or method is the thing or method that is required or is most suitable in a particular situation. 合适的;

ex.en: The use of the correct materials was crucial.
ex.zh: 使用合适材料是重要的。

ex.en: White was in no doubt the referee made the correct decision.
ex.zh: 怀特毫不怀疑裁判做出了恰当的判罚。

d: adj. 正确的，无误的；恰当的，合适的；（行为）合乎礼节的，得体的；（行为）被人认可的，赞许的
v. 改正，纠正；批改；指出错误；（医疗）矫正

e.en: A contender is someone who takes part in a competition.

ex.en: Her trainer said yesterday that she would be a strong contender for a place on the Olympic team.
ex.zh: 她的教练昨天说，她会是取得奥运代表队里一个席位的一名强有力的竞争者。

d: n. 竞争者，争夺者

e.en: To deploy troops or military resources means to organize or position them so that they are ready to be used.

ex.en: The president said he had no intention of deploying ground troops.
ex.zh: 总统说他无意调遣地面部队。

d: v. 部署，调度；利用

e.en: A desk is a table, often with drawers, which you sit at to write or work. 书桌;
The place in a hotel, hospital, airport, or other building where you check in or obtain information is referred to as a particular desk. (接待、咨询)

ex.en: I told the girl at the reception desk that I was terribly sorry, but I was half an hour late.
ex.zh: 我对接待服务台的女孩说我很抱歉，迟到了半小时。

e.en: A particular department of a broadcasting company, or of a newspaper or magazine company, can be referred to as a particular desk. …

ex.en: Let our news desk know as quickly as possible.
ex.zh: 尽快通知我们的新闻部。

d: n. 书桌，办公桌，写字台；服务台，问询台；（办理某项业务的）部门；乐谱架，演奏者席；（报社）编辑部
adj. 书桌的，桌上适合用的

e.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

ex.en: We asked her to describe what kind of things she did in her spare time.
ex.zh: 我们请她描述她在闲暇时做些什么。

ex.en: She read a poem by Carver which describes their life together.
ex.zh: 她读了一首卡弗描写他们在一起生活的诗。

e.en: If a person describes someone or something as a particular thing, he or she believes that they are that thing and says so. 讲成;

ex.en: He described it as an extraordinarily tangled and complicated tale.
ex.zh: 他把它讲成了一个格外错综复杂的故事。

ex.en: Even his closest allies describe him as forceful, aggressive, and determined.
ex.zh: 甚至他最亲密的同盟者们都说他强势、好斗且坚决。

d: v. （describe 的第三人称单数形式）：描述，叙述，记述；把…描述为，把…称作；形容，作图

e.en: Someone who is disingenuous is slightly dishonest and insincere in what they say.

ex.en: It would be disingenuous to claim that this is great art.
ex.zh: 称其为伟大的艺术品就有些不真诚了。

d: adj. 不真诚的，不坦率的，虚伪的；不诚实的，不老实的，狡猾的

e.en: You can use dizzying to emphasize that something impresses you, though it makes you a bit confused or unsteady.

ex.en: ...a dizzying array of choices.
ex.zh: ...一系列令人晕眩的服饰。

ex.en: We're descending now at dizzying speed.
ex.zh: 我们正从令人目眩的速度中逐步减速。

d: adj. 令人昏乱的；极快的
vt. 使人眼花缭乱（dizzy 的现在分词）

e.en: an action or the performance of an action 行为;

ex.en: whose doing is this?

d: v. 做，干（do 的现在分词和动名词）
n. 活动；所作所为，行为；在 of someone's doing 等搭配中表示某人的作为或责任，在 take some doing 中表示需要费力

e.en: If you call someone a dolt, you think they are stupid, or have done something stupid.

d: n. 笨蛋，傻瓜，呆子；（Dolt）（法）多尔特（人名）

e.en: If a level or amount drops or if someone or something drops it, it quickly becomes less. 使迅速下降;

ex.en: Temperatures can drop to freezing at night.
ex.zh: 晚上气温能陡降到零度以下。

ex.en: His blood pressure had dropped severely.
ex.zh: 他的血压严重地迅速下降。

e.en: Drop is also a noun.

ex.en: He was prepared to take a drop in wages.
ex.zh: 他准备好了接受一次工资的快速下调。

e.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

ex.en: I dropped my glasses and broke them.
ex.zh: 我不小心掉了眼镜，把它摔破了。

e.en: If something drops onto something else, it falls onto that thing. If something drops from somewhere, it falls from that place.

ex.en: He felt hot tears dropping onto his fingers.
ex.zh: 他感到热泪滴在他的手指上。

d: v. 投，丢；躺倒；剔除，除名；停止，放弃；中途卸客，中途卸货；寄，送，写（信）；（道路、地面等）急剧向下倾斜；突然终止与（某人）的（恋爱）关系；（使）掉落；减少，降低
n. 滴，少量；下降；落差；递送，交付；邮政信箱，邮筒；（赃物、非法物、秘密物品的）藏匿处；垂幕，升降幕；（绞刑架的）下落板

e.en: If you have doubt or doubts about something, you feel uncertain about it and do not know whether it is true or possible. If you say you have no doubt about it, you mean that you are certain it is true.

ex.en: This raises doubts about the point of advertising.
ex.zh: 这引起了人们对于广告作用的怀疑。

ex.en: There is little doubt that man has had an impact on the Earth's climate.
ex.zh: 毫无疑问人类对地球上的气候造成了影响。

e.en: If you doubt whether something is true or possible, you believe that it is probably not true or possible.

ex.en: Others doubted whether that would happen.
ex.zh: 其他人都怀疑那会不会发生。

ex.en: He doubted if he would learn anything new from Marie.
ex.zh: 他怀疑自己是否能从玛丽那里学到什么新东西。

e.en: If you doubt something, you believe that it might not be true or genuine.

ex.en: No one doubted his ability.
ex.zh: 没有人怀疑他的能力。

e.en: If you doubt someone or doubt their word, you think that they may not be telling the truth.

ex.en: No one directly involved with the case doubted him.
ex.zh: 直接涉及此案的人都没有怀疑他。

d: v. 怀疑，不确定；不信任
n. 怀疑，不确定

e.en: A duel is a formal fight between two people in which they use guns or swords in order to settle a quarrel.

ex.en: He killed a man in one duel and was himself wounded in another.
ex.zh: 在一次双人决斗中他杀了人，还有一次他自己受了伤。

d: n. 决斗；对决，斗争，抗争；（Duel）人名；（西）杜埃尔；（英）迪尤尔
vi. 决斗
v. 给（某人）发电子邮件；用电子邮件发送（文件）（email 的现在分词）

e.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

ex.en: Patricia looked beautiful and elegant as always.
ex.zh: 帕特丽夏看上去跟往常一样美丽优雅。

e.en: 优雅

ex.en: The furniture managed to combine practicality with elegance.
ex.zh: 这家具结合了实用与优雅。

e.en: If you describe a piece of writing, an idea, or a plan as elegant, you mean that it is simple, clear, and clever.

ex.en: The document impressed me with its elegant simplicity.
ex.zh: 这份文件以其精妙的简约给我留下了深刻的印象。

e.en: 精妙地

ex.en: ...an elegantly simple idea.
ex.zh: …一个精妙地简单的主意。

d: adj. （人）高雅的，举止优雅的；精美的，雅致的；简练的，巧妙的

e.en: If someone is your enemy, they hate you or want to harm you.

ex.en: Imagine loving your enemy and doing good to those who hated you.
ex.zh: 想像着爱你的敌人，为仇人做好事。

e.en: If someone is your enemy, they are opposed to you and to what you think or do.

ex.en: Her political enemies were quick to pick up on this series of disasters.
ex.zh: 她的政敌很快注意到这一系列的灾难。

e.en: The enemy is an army or other force that is opposed to you in a war, or a country with which your country is at war.

ex.en: The enemy were pursued for two miles.
ex.zh: 敌军被追赶了两英里。

e.en: If one thing is the enemy of another thing, the second thing cannot happen or succeed because of the first thing.

ex.en: Reform, as we know, is the enemy of revolution.
ex.zh: 革新，如我们所知，是革命的敌对面。

d: n. 敌人，反对者；敌国，敌军；大敌，危害物
adj. 敌人的，敌方的
n. 表情符号，绘文字

e.en: To emerge means to come out from an enclosed or dark space such as a room or a vehicle, or from a position where you could not be seen. (从视线以外的地方) 出现;

ex.en: Richard was waiting outside the door as she emerged.
ex.zh: 当她出现的时候，理查德正等候在门外。

ex.en: She then emerged from the courthouse to thank her supporters.
ex.zh: 于是她从法院大楼出来向支持者们表示感谢。

e.en: If you emerge from a difficult or bad experience, you come to the end of it.

ex.en: There is growing evidence that the economy is at last emerging from recession.
ex.zh: 有越来越多的迹象表明经济将最终摆脱萧条。

e.en: If a fact or result emerges from a period of thought, discussion, or investigation, it becomes known as a result of it. 显露 (事实、结果)

ex.en: ...the growing corruption that has emerged in the past few years.
ex.zh: …过去几年中暴露出来的日趋严重的腐败。

ex.en: It soon emerged that neither the July nor August mortgage payment had been collected.
ex.zh: 很快显示的是7月和8月的抵押款都没有被收取。

e.en: If someone or something emerges as a particular thing, they become recognized as that thing.

ex.en: Vietnam has emerged as the world's third-biggest rice exporter.
ex.zh: 越南已立足成为世界第三大稻米出口国。

d: v. （emerge 的过去式和过去分词）出来，出现，浮现；显现，显露；暴露，传开；（与 from 连用）走出，摆脱（困境、衰退等）；（与 as 连用，多用于新闻）成为，崭露头角；（指组织、行业等新事物）兴起，成立，应运而生

e.en: An epistolary novel or story is one that is written as a series of letters. (小说或故事)

d: adj. 书信的；用书信进行的；书信体的（指小说、故事等作品以一系列书信写成）
n．时代，时期：一个特定的历史时期，通常与某种特殊的社会、文化或艺术风格相关。

e.en: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened. 证据;

ex.en: Ganley said he'd seen no evidence of widespread fraud.
ex.zh: 甘利说他没有看见欺骗行为泛滥的证据。

e.en: Evidence is the information that is used in a court of law to try to prove something. Evidence is obtained from documents, objects, or witnesses. (法律上的)

ex.en: The evidence against him was purely circumstantial.
ex.zh: 不利于他的证据纯粹是间接证据。

e.en: If you give evidence in a court of law or an official inquiry, you officially say what you know about people or events, or describe an occasion at which you were present. (在法庭上或官方调查中)

ex.en: The forensic scientists who carried out the original tests will be called to give evidence.
ex.zh: 那些进行了原始化验的法医学家们将被叫去作证。

e.en: If someone or something is in evidence, they are present and can be clearly seen.

ex.en: Few soldiers were in evidence.
ex.zh: 几乎看不见有士兵。

d: n. 根据，证明；（呈上法庭的）证据，证词；迹象，痕迹
v. 证实，证明
adv. 精致地，精巧地；极其，异常，敏锐地（常与 sensitive、beautiful、attuned 等连用）

e.en: favourite

d: adj. 最喜爱的（favourite/favorite 的缩略形式）
n. 最喜爱的人或事物（favourite/favorite 的缩略形式）；Fave（人名，意大利语译作法韦，法语译作法夫）

e.en: If you explain something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood. 解释 (意思)

ex.en: Not every judge, however, has the ability to explain the law in simple terms.
ex.zh: 然而，并非每个法官都能用浅易的话来解释法律。

ex.en: Don't sign anything until your lawyer has explained the contract to you.
ex.zh: 在你的律师向你解释该合同之前什么也别签。

e.en: If you explain, or explain something that has happened, you give people reasons for it, especially in an attempt to justify it. 解释 (原因)

ex.en: "Let me explain, sir."—"Don't tell me about it. I don't want to know."
ex.zh: “让我来解释，先生。”—“别跟我说那事。我不想知道。”

ex.en: Before she ran away, she left a note explaining her actions.
ex.zh: 逃走之前，她留下了张便条为她的行为作了解释。

d: v. 解释，说明；说明（……的）原因，解释（……的）理由

e.en: If you fight something unpleasant, you try in a determined way to prevent it or stop it from happening.

ex.en: More units to fight forest fires are planned.
ex.zh: 已经计划增派部队来扑灭森林大火。

ex.en: I've spent a lifetime fighting against racism and prejudice.
ex.zh: 我花了毕生的时间与种族歧视和偏见作斗争。

e.en: Fight is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the fight against drug addiction.
ex.zh: …与毒品上瘾的斗争。

e.en: If you fight for something, you try in a determined way to get it or achieve it.

ex.en: Lee had to fight hard for his place on the expedition.
ex.zh: 李必须为他在考察队的一席之地而努力奋斗。

ex.en: I told him how we had fought to hold on to the company.
ex.zh: 我告诉他我们是如何为保住公司而奋斗的。

e.en: Fight is also a noun.

ex.en: I too am committing myself to continue the fight for justice.
ex.zh: 我也正致力于继续正义之战。

d: n. 战斗，打斗
adj. 作战用的；好战的，好斗的；适于打斗的；表现出斗志的
v. 与……作斗争，坚决反对；努力争取，为……而斗争；打仗，作战（fight 的现在分词形式）

e.en: You use fellow to describe people who are in the same situation as you, or people you feel you have something in common with. 同种情况的;

ex.en: She discovered to her pleasure, a talent for making her fellow guests laugh.
ex.zh: 她高兴地发现一个把她同来的客人逗笑的本事。

e.en: A fellow is a man or boy. 家伙;

ex.en: By all accounts, Rodger would appear to be a fine fellow.
ex.zh: 根据大家的说法，罗杰应该是个好小伙儿。

e.en: A fellow of an academic or professional association is someone who is a specially elected member of it, usually because of their work or achievements or as a mark of honour.

ex.en: ...the fellows of the Zoological Society.
ex.zh: …动物协会的特别会员们。

e.en: Your fellows are the people who you work with, do things with, or who are like you in some way. 同事;

ex.en: He stood out in terms of competence from all his fellows.
ex.zh: 他在能力方面比他所有同事都突出。

d: n. 小伙子，家伙；同伴，同事，同学；研究员；男朋友；（研究期间领取津贴的）研究生；（大学的）董事；（学术或专业团体）会员；对等者，对手
adj. 同类的，同伴的
【名】 （Fellow）（美、英、印）费洛（人名）

e.en: all the processes involved in the binding of a book subsequent to cutting and up to the fitting of its cover (最后包封面之前的)

d: v. 转递（信）；递交；运送（货物）；促进（forward 的现在分词）
n. 转发；促进；货运；（最后包封面之前的）各项装订工序
adv. 经常地，频繁地

e.en: If someone is friendly, they behave in a pleasant, kind way, and like to be with other people.

ex.en: Godfrey had been friendly to me.
ex.zh: 戈弗雷过去曾经对我是友好的。

ex.en: ...a man with a pleasant, friendly face.
ex.zh: …一个和颜悦色的男子。

e.en: 友善

ex.en: She also loves the friendliness of the people.
ex.zh: 她也喜爱人们的友善。

e.en: If you are friendly with someone, you like each other and enjoy spending time together.

ex.en: I'm friendly with his mother.
ex.zh: 我和他的母亲很要好。

e.en: You can describe another country or their government as friendly when they have good relations with your own country rather than being an enemy. (国家或政府)

ex.en: ...a worsening in relations between the two previously friendly countries.
ex.zh: …两个先前友好的国家之间关系的恶化。

d: adj. 亲切的，友善的；朋友（般）的，要好的；为友谊的，非对抗性的；（国家或政府）友好的，无敌意的；（部队，装备）我军的，友军的；好用的，无害的；支持的，提供帮助的；令人愉快的；（公司的兼并）自愿的
cn. 友谊赛
