【名】 （Friendly）（英）弗兰德利（人名）

e.en: FYI is a written abbreviation for "for your information," often used in notes and documents when giving someone additional information about something. for your information的缩写;

ex.en: FYI: Walton appeared in a grand total of 49 career tournament games.
ex.zh: 供参考：沃尔顿在职业生涯中总共参加了49场锦标赛的比赛。

d: abbr. 供参考（for your information）

e.en: Fury is violent or very strong anger.

ex.en: She screamed, her face distorted with fury and pain.
ex.zh: 她尖叫着，她的脸因愤怒和痛苦而扭曲了。

d: n. 暴怒，狂怒；（暴风雨或洪水的）猛烈，剧烈；激怒者；复仇三女神 （The Furies）

e.en: You can use give with nouns that refer to physical actions. The whole expression refers to the performing of the action. For example, She gave a smile means almost the same as "She smiled."
e.zh: 与表示身体动作的名词连用，表示做这一动作

ex.en: She stretched her arms out and gave a great yawn.
ex.zh: 她伸开手臂，打了个大呵欠。

ex.en: He gave her a fond smile.
ex.zh: 他充满柔情地朝她微微一笑。

e.en: You use give to say that a person does something for another person. For example, if you give someone a lift, you take them somewhere in your car.

ex.en: I gave her a lift back to her house.
ex.zh: 我让她搭我的车回家。

ex.en: He was given mouth-to-mouth resuscitation.
ex.zh: 对他进行了口对口的人工呼吸。

e.en: You use give with nouns that refer to information, opinions, or greetings to indicate that something is communicated. For example, if you give someone some news, you tell it to them.

ex.en: He gave no details.
ex.zh: 他没有提供任何细节。

ex.en: Would you like to give me your name?
ex.zh: 能告诉我你的名字吗？

e.en: You use give to say how long you think something will last or how much you think something will be.

ex.en: A recent poll gave Campbell a 68 percent support rating.
ex.zh: 最近的一次民意调查预计坎贝尔的支持率为68%。

d: v. give 的现在分词：给，赠送，付出，产生；give up 的现在分词：放弃，停止（做某事）；give away 的现在分词：免费分发，泄露
adj. 慷慨的，乐善好施的
n. 给予，捐赠；礼物，给予物
adj. happy 的比较级：更快乐的，更幸福的

e.en: If you harness something such as an emotion or natural source of energy, you bring it under your control and use it.

ex.en: Turkey plans to harness the waters of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers for big hydro-electric power projects.
ex.zh: 土耳其计划利用底格里斯河与幼发拉底河的水来建造大型水力发电工程。

e.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten around their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place. 背带;
A harness is a set of leather straps and metal links fastened around a horse's head or body so that the horse can have a carriage, cart, or plough fastened to it. 马具;
If a horse or other animal is harnessed, a harness is put on it, especially so that it can pull a carriage, cart, or plough.

ex.en: On Sunday the horses were harnessed to a heavy wagon for a day-long ride over the border.
ex.zh: 星期天这些马被套在一辆沉重的货车上，踏上长达一天的旅程越过边境。

d: v. 给（马等）套上挽具；控制，利用（以产生能量）；将……拴在一起；把（动物）拴到车、犁等上（harness 的现在分词）
n. 利用，控制（harness 的动名词用法）

e.en: When you hear a sound, you become aware of it through your ears.

ex.en: She heard no further sounds.
ex.zh: 她再也没有听见任何响声。

ex.en: They heard the protesters shout: "No more fascism!"
ex.zh: 他们听见抗议者在高呼：“打倒法西斯主义！”

e.en: If you hear something such as a lecture or a piece of music, you listen to it.

ex.en: You can hear commentary on the game at halftime.
ex.zh: 你可在中场休息时听到对比赛的评论。

ex.en: I don't think you've ever heard Doris talking about her emotional life before.
ex.zh: 我想你以前从未听过多丽丝谈论自己的感情生活。

e.en: When a judge or a court of law hears a case, or evidence in a case, they listen to it officially in order to make a decision about it.

ex.en: The jury has heard evidence from defence witnesses.
ex.zh: 陪审团听取了被告方证人的证词。

e.en: If you hear from someone, you receive a letter or telephone call from them. 接到 (信或电话)

ex.en: Drop us a line, it's always great to hear from you.
ex.zh: 给我们写封信，能收到你的信总是让人很高兴。

d: v. 听到，听见；聆听，倾听；听说，得知；审理，听审；脑际响起；听明白

e.en: If you describe someone as helpful, you mean that they help you in some way, such as doing part of your job for you or by giving you advice or information.

ex.en: The staff in the branch office are helpful but only have limited information.
ex.zh: 该分支机构的员工是帮忙的，但他们仅有有限的信息。

e.en: 热心地

ex.en: They had helpfully provided us with instructions on how to find the house.
ex.zh: 他们已经热心地给我们提供了如何找到那所房子的说明。

e.en: If you describe information or advice as helpful, you mean that it is useful for you. 有用的 (信息或建议)

ex.en: The catalogue includes helpful information on the different bike models available.
ex.zh: 该目录包含所销售的各种型号自行车的有用信息。

e.en: Something that is helpful makes a situation more pleasant or more easy to tolerate.

ex.en: It is often helpful to have your spouse in the room when major news is expected.
ex.zh: 在等待重大消息时，让你的配偶在场往往是很有好处的。

d: adj. 有帮助的，有用的；愿意帮忙的

e.en: Something that is hollow has a space inside it, as opposed to being solid all the way through.

ex.en: ...a hollow tree.
ex.zh: …一棵空心树

e.en: A surface that is hollow curves inward.

ex.en: He looked young, dark and sharp-featured, with hollow cheeks.
ex.zh: 他看起来很年轻，肤色黝黑，面部棱角分明，双颊凹陷。

e.en: A hollow is an area that is lower than the surrounding surface.

ex.en: Below him the town lay warm in the hollow of the hill.
ex.zh: 在他的下面，小镇温暖地坐落在山坳里。

e.en: If you describe a statement, situation, or person as hollow, you mean they have no real value, worth, or effectiveness. 空洞的;

ex.en: Any threat to bring in the police is a hollow one.
ex.zh: 任何要叫警察来的威胁都是虚张声势。

d: adj. 空的，空心的；凹的，凹陷的；虚伪的，不真诚的；无用的，无价值的；（声音）沉闷回荡的；空腹的；沉闷回荡的
v. 使凹陷，使下陷；挖洞（成某物）；形成空洞
n. 凹陷处，坑洼处；坑，洞；山谷
【名】 （Hollow）（英）霍洛（人名）

e.en: If you imagine something, you think about it and your mind forms a picture or idea of it.

ex.en: He could not imagine a more peaceful scene.
ex.zh: 他想像不出比这更幽静的场景。

e.en: If you imagine that something is the case, you think that it is the case.

ex.en: I imagine you're referring to Jean-Paul Sartre.
ex.zh: 我猜你指的是吉恩-保尔·萨特。

e.en: If you imagine something, you think that you have seen, heard, or experienced that thing, although actually you have not.

ex.en: Looking back on it now, I realized that I must have imagined the whole thing.
ex.zh: 现在回想起来，我意识到这整个事情一定是我幻想出来的。

d: v. 想象，设想；料想，认为；误以为，胡乱猜想

e.en: If you describe someone as ill-tempered, you mean they are angry or hostile, and you may be implying that this is unreasonable. 脾气暴躁的;

ex.en: It was a day of tense and often ill-tempered debate.
ex.zh: 那天的辩论激烈紧张，且常常恶语相向。

d: adj. 脾气暴躁的；坏脾气的

e.en: If you imply that something is the case, you say something that indicates that it is the case in an indirect way.

ex.en: "Are you implying that I have something to do with those attacks?" she asked coldly.
ex.zh: “你在暗指我和那些袭击有关吗？”她冷冷地问道。

e.en: If an event or situation implies that something is the case, it makes you think that it is the case.

ex.en: Exports in June rose 1.5%, implying that the economy was stronger than many investors had realized.
ex.zh: 6月份的出口额增加了1.5%，这意味着经济比许多投资者所了解的要强劲。

d: v. 暗指，暗示；意味着，含有…的意思；（逻辑）蕴含，推出；imply 的第三人称单数

e.en: Something that is incorrect is wrong and untrue. 不正确的;

ex.en: He denied that his evidence about the telephone call was incorrect.
ex.zh: 他否认他关于电话的证词是不真实的。

e.en: 不正确地

ex.en: The magazine suggested, incorrectly, that he was planning to announce his retirement.
ex.zh: 该杂志错误地暗示说他正打算宣布退休。

e.en: Something that is incorrect is not the thing that is required or is most suitable in a particular situation.

ex.en: ...injuries caused by incorrect posture.
ex.zh: …由不当姿势造成的伤害。

e.en: 不适当地

ex.en: He was told that the doors had been installed incorrectly.
ex.zh: 他被告知房门安装不当。

d: adj. 错误的，不真实的；不适当的，不合礼节的

e.en: To import products or raw materials means to buy them from another country for use in your own country.

ex.en: Rich countries benefited from importing Indonesia's timber.
ex.zh: 富国从进口印度尼西亚木材中获利。

ex.en: To import from Russia, a Ukrainian firm needs Russian roubles.
ex.zh: 要从俄罗斯进口，乌克兰公司需要俄罗斯卢布。

e.en: Import is also a noun.

ex.en: Germany, however, insists on restrictions on the import of Polish coal.
ex.zh: 然而德国坚持对波兰煤炭的进口限制。

e.en: 进口

ex.en: ...restrictions concerning the importation of birds.
ex.zh: …关于鸟类进口的种种限制。

e.en: Imports are products or raw materials bought from another country for use in your own country.

ex.en: ...cheap imports from other countries.
ex.zh: …来自其他国家的廉价进口商品。

d: n. 进口，进口商品；输入，引进；重要性；意思，含意
v. 进口，输入，引进；导入（计算机）；意味，表明
adv. 复杂地，错综复杂地；精巧地，精细地

e.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example, if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

ex.en: The house was a total loss and the insurance company promptly paid us the policy limit.
ex.zh: 房屋被定为全损，保险公司按保险限额迅速赔付了我们。

e.en: If you do something as insurance against something unpleasant happening, you do it to protect yourself in case the unpleasant thing happens.

ex.en: Attentive proofreading is the only insurance against the kind of omissions described in this section.
ex.zh: 仔细校对是避免本节提到的那种遗漏问题的惟一预防措施。

d: n. 保险；保险费；保险业；保险赔偿金，保险金；保险单；预防措施，安全保障

e.en: A jockey is someone who rides a horse in a race.
If you say that someone is jockeying for something, you mean that they are using whatever methods they can in order to get it or do it before their competitors can get it or do it.

ex.en: The rival political parties are already jockeying for power.
ex.zh: 各反对党已经在不择手段地谋取权势了。

e.en: If someone is jockeying for position, they are using whatever methods they can in order to get into a better position than their rivals.
e.zh: 不择手段地谋取有利地位

d: n．赛马骑师（复数）：在赛马比赛中骑马的人。
v．（尤指通过不正当手段）竞争，争夺（复数形式）：为了获得优势或成功而与他人竞争，尤指通过不正当手段。

e.en: A kitchen is a room that is used for cooking and for household jobs such as washing dishes.

d: n. 厨房；一套厨具；管弦乐队中的打击乐器组；（语言）不标准的，俚俗的
【名】 （Kitchen）（英）基钦（人名）

e.en: Isn't is the usual spoken form of "is not." (is not)

d: v. is not 的缩略形式，意为“不是”

e.en: If you leave a place or person, you go away from that place or person.

ex.en: He would not be allowed to leave the country.
ex.zh: 他不准离开这个国家。

ex.en: My flight leaves in less than an hour.
ex.zh: 我的航班一小时内起飞。

e.en: If you leave an institution, group, or job, you permanently stop attending that institution, being a member of that group, or doing that job. 离开 (机构、团体或工作)

ex.en: He left school with no qualifications.
ex.zh: 他离开学校时没有拿到证书。

ex.en: I am leaving to concentrate on writing fiction.
ex.zh: 我要离开去专心写小说。

e.en: If you leave your husband, wife, or some other person with whom you have had a close relationship, you stop living with them or you end the relationship. 与…脱离关系; 离开 (某人)

ex.en: He'll never leave you. You needn't worry.
ex.zh: 他永远都不会离开你的，你不必担心。

e.en: If you leave something or someone in a particular place, you let them remain there when you go away. If you leave something or someone with a person, you let them remain with that person so they are safe while you are away.

ex.en: I left my bags in the car.
ex.zh: 我把包留在车里。

ex.en: From the moment that Philippe had left her in the bedroom at the hotel, she had heard nothing of him.
ex.zh: 自从菲利普把她遗弃在旅店房间的那一刻起，她就再没有他的任何消息。

d: v. 离开；留下；舍弃；使……处于某种状态（leave 的现在分词）
n. 离开；离去

e.en: Later is the comparative of . (late)
You use later to refer to a time or situation that is after the one that you have been talking about or after the present one.

ex.en: He resigned ten years later.
ex.zh: 他10年后辞职了。

e.en: You use later on to refer to a time or situation that is after the one that you have been talking about or after the present one.

ex.en: Later on I'll be speaking to Patty Davis.
ex.zh: 以后我会和帕蒂·戴维斯谈谈。

e.en: You use later to refer to an event, period of time, or other thing which comes after the one that you have been talking about or after the present one.

ex.en: At a later news conference, he said differences should not be dramatized.
ex.zh: 在后来的新闻发布会上，他说差异不应该被夸大。

ex.en: The competition should have been re-scheduled for a later date.
ex.zh: 本该把比赛重新安排在一个晚些的日期。

d: adv. 后来，随后；再见，回头见
adj. 较晚的，以后的；较新式的，较现代的；晚期的，末期的
【名】 （Later）（德）拉特（人名）

e.en: Leaves is the plural form of , and the third person singular form of leave. (leaf)的复数形式; (leave)

d: n. （leaf 的复数）树叶，叶片；花瓣；（纸）页，张；薄金属片；活动桌板，折叠桌板；（窗、门等）扇；空心墙的内面（或外面）
v. （leave 的第三人称单数）离开；让……留下

e.en: You use mere to emphasize how unimportant or inadequate something is, in comparison to the general situation you are describing.

ex.en: ...successful exhibitions which go beyond mere success.
ex.zh: …不仅仅是成功，而是大获成功的展览。

ex.en: There is more to good health than the mere absence of disease.
ex.zh: 健康不仅仅指不生病，还包括更多。

e.en: You use mere to indicate that a quality or action that is usually unimportant has a very important or strong effect. 单单的 (用来指某事虽小却有重要影响)

ex.en: The mere mention of food had triggered off hunger pangs.
ex.zh: 单单提到食物就引起了阵阵的饥饿感。

e.en: You use mere to emphasize how small a particular amount or number is. 只不过 (用于强调数量之少)

ex.en: Sixty percent of teachers are women, but a mere five percent of women are principals.
ex.zh: 60％的教师是女性，但只有5％的女性是校长。

e.en: a lake or marsh 湖;

d: adj. 仅仅，只不过；只凭……就足以
n. 小湖，池塘；（尤指毛利人用绿岩制的武器）石棒
【名】 （Mere）（日）目连，（西）梅雷（人名）

e.en: The losers of a game, contest, or struggle are the people who are defeated or beaten.

ex.en: ...the Dallas Cowboys and Buffalo Bills, the winners and losers of this year's Super Bowl.
ex.zh: …达拉斯牛仔队和布法罗比利队，今年超级杯赛的获胜者和失败者。

e.en: If someone is a good loser, they accept that they have lost a game or contest without complaining. If someone is a bad loser, they hate losing and complain about it. 输得起的人/

ex.en: I'm a great winner and I try to be a good loser.
ex.zh: 我赢得起，也要努力做一个输得起的人。

e.en: If you refer to someone as a loser, you have a low opinion of them because you think they are always unsuccessful.

ex.en: They've only been trained to compete with other men, so a successful woman can make them feel like a real loser.
ex.zh: 他们只被训练与其他的男性竞争，所以一个成功的女性会让他们觉得自己确实是失败者。

e.en: People who are losers as the result of an action or event, are in a worse situation because of it or do not benefit from it.

ex.en: Some of the top business successes of the 1980s became the country's greatest losers in the recession.
ex.zh: 20世纪80年代的一些极其成功的商人在该国经济萧条时期沦为损失最惨重的人。

d: n. 比赛、竞争或斗争中的失败者，输家（常构成 good loser（输得起的人）、sore loser（输不起的人）等搭配）；老是失败的人，一事无成者（多含贬义）；因某项行动或事件而受损者，损失者；遗失者，丢失某物的人；（Loser）人名；（德、捷）洛泽；（英）洛瑟；（法）洛塞

e.en: If you let something happen, you allow it to happen without doing anything to stop or prevent it.

ex.en: People said we were interfering with nature, and that we should just let the animals die.
ex.zh: 人们说我们在干涉大自然，还说我们应该任由那些动物去死。

ex.en: I can't let myself be distracted by those things.
ex.zh: 我不能任由自己被那些东西分散注意力。

e.en: If you let someone do something, you give them your permission to do it.

ex.en: I love sweets but Mum doesn't let me have them very often.
ex.zh: 我爱吃糖果，但是妈妈不允许我常吃。

e.en: If you let someone into, out of, or through a place, you allow them to enter, leave, or go through it, for example, by opening a door or making room for them. 允许 (进入、离开、通过等)

ex.en: I had to let them into the building because they had lost their keys.
ex.zh: 我不得不允许他们进楼，因为他们丢了钥匙。

e.en: You use let me when you are introducing something you want to say. 让我 (引出要说的内容)

ex.en: Let me tell you what I saw last night.
ex.zh: 让我告诉你昨晚我见到的事。

ex.en: Let me explain why.
ex.zh: 让我来解释为什么。

d: v. 允许，准许，同意；使通过；任由，随；（用于提出建议或表示赞同）让我们；（提出帮助时说）让，由；（用于引出命令）要；但愿；（用于引出要说的话）让我（们）来；（计算时说）假设，设；（表示犹豫或思考）让我想想；（表示认为某人应该做某事）让；出租（房屋或土地）；（将工程）承包给某一竞标者；  妨碍，阻碍
n. 擦网球，触网重发；出租，租借；待租房，可出租房产；障碍
【名】 （Let）（缅）莱，（俄）莱特（人名）

e.en: The middle of something is the part of it that is farthest from its edges, ends, or outside surface.

ex.en: Howard stood in the middle of the room sipping a cup of coffee.
ex.zh: 霍华德站在房子中间，啜饮着一杯咖啡。

ex.en: They had a volleyball court in the middle of the courtyard.
ex.zh: 他们在院子中央有一个排球场。

e.en: The middle object in a row of objects is the one that has an equal number of objects on each side.

ex.en: The middle button of his uniform jacket was strained over his belly.
ex.zh: 他制服上衣中间的那个扣子在他的肚子上绷得紧紧的。

e.en: The middle of an event or period of time is the part that comes after the first part and before the last part.

ex.en: I woke up in the middle of the night and could hear a tapping on the window.
ex.zh: 我半夜醒来，听到轻敲窗户的声音。

e.en: Middle is also an adjective.

ex.en: Many classical violinists and pianists become conductors in their middle years.
ex.zh: 许多古典小提琴手和钢琴演奏者在中年时变成指挥家。

d: adj. 中间的，中等的；折中的，中庸之道的；（语言）中古的，介于现代与古代之间的；语法中动态的，中间反身态的；（英语及物动词）无被动态的
n. 中间，中部，中等；腰部；语法中动态，中间反身态
v. （板球、网球等中）用球棒（或拍）中部击（球）

e.en: A microwave or a microwave oven is an oven which cooks food very quickly by electromagnetic radiation rather than by heat.
To microwave food or drink means to cook or heat it in a microwave oven. 用微波炉 (烹调或加热)

ex.en: Steam or microwave the vegetables until tender.
ex.zh: 蒸或用微波炉加热蔬菜，直至蔬菜变得软嫩。

d: n. 微波炉；微波
v. 用微波炉烹调（或加热）

e.en: A minute is one of the sixty parts that an hour is divided into. People often say "a minute" or "minutes" when they mean a short length of time. 分钟;

ex.en: The pizza will then take about twenty minutes to cook.
ex.zh: 接下来，比萨饼大约要用20分钟烤好。

ex.en: Bye Mom, see you in a minute.
ex.zh: 再见，妈妈，一会儿见。

e.en: The minutes of a meeting are the written records of the things that are discussed or decided at it.

ex.en: He'd been reading the minutes of the last meeting.
ex.zh: 他一直在看上次会议的记录。

e.en: When someone minutes something that is discussed or decided at a meeting, they make a written record of it.

ex.en: You don't need to minute that.
ex.zh: 你不必记录那些。

e.en: People often use expressions such as wait a minute or just a minute when they want to stop you doing or saying something.

ex.en: Wait a minute, folks, something is wrong here.
ex.zh: 等一下，伙计们，这地方不对劲。

d: n. 分钟（minute 的复数）；会议记录；备忘录
v. 把……记录在案；为……测定时间（minute 的单三形式）

e.en: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.

ex.en: She moved the sheaf of papers into position.
ex.zh: 她把那捆纸移到了位置上。

ex.en: A traffic policeman asked him to move his car.
ex.zh: 一位交警让他挪动一下他的车。

e.en: When you move, you change your position or go to a different place. 移动 (位置)

ex.en: She waited for him to get up, but he didn't move.
ex.zh: 她等着他起来，可他没有动。

ex.en: He moved around the room, putting his possessions together.
ex.zh: 他在屋里走来走去，把他的东西都放在一起。

e.en: Move is also a noun.

ex.en: The doctor made a move toward the door.
ex.zh: 医生朝门口挪了一下。

e.en: If you move, you act or you begin to do something.

ex.en: Industrialists must move fast to take advantage of new opportunities in Eastern Europe.
ex.zh: 实业家们必须快速采取行动，抓住东欧的新机遇。

d: v. （使）改变位置，（使）移动；搬家，搬迁；（使）变换，调动；（使）改变观点（或做法）；前进，进展；采取行动；使感动，打动；促使，驱使；更改（时间或日期）；改变话题；走棋，移动棋子；（在会议或法庭上）提议；快速行进；（商品）被销售，销售（商品）；进行社交活动，交往；离去；使（肠）排空
n. 措施，行动；移动，活动；转变，改变；一步棋，走棋；搬家，迁移

e.en: If you pause while you are doing something, you stop for a short period and then continue.

ex.en: "It's rather embarrassing," he began, and paused.
ex.zh: “这很让人尴尬，” 他开始说道，又停顿了片刻。

ex.en: He talked for two hours without pausing for breath.
ex.zh: 他谈了两个小时，没有停下来喘口气。

e.en: A pause is a short period when you stop doing something before continuing.

ex.en: After a pause Al said sharply: "I'm sorry if I've upset you."
ex.zh: 停了一下之后艾尔突然说：“如果我让你不安了，我很抱歉。”

d: n. 暂停，停顿；暂停键；延长记号
v. 暂停，停顿；（按暂停键）暂停；踌躇

e.en: You use perennial to describe situations or states that keep occurring or that seem to exist all the time; used especially to describe problems or difficulties. 不断出现的; 长期存在的 (问题、困难)

ex.en: ...the perennial urban problems of drugs and homelessness.
ex.zh: …城市长期存在的毒品和无家可归的问题。

e.en: A perennial plant lives for several years and has flowers each year. (植物)

ex.en: ...a perennial herb with greenish-yellow flowers.
ex.zh: …一种开黄绿色花的多年生草本植物。

e.en: Perennial is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a low-growing perennial.
ex.zh: …一种长不高的多年生植物。

d: adj. 多年生的（植物）；长期的，常在的，反复的（问题、困难等）；常年的，四季不断的（河流、湖泊等）
n. 多年生植物

e.en: You can use perfectly to emphasize an adjective or adverb, especially when you think the person you are talking to might doubt what you are saying. 完全地 (尤用在认为对方有疑虑时以示强调)

ex.en: There's no reason why you can't have a perfectly normal child.
ex.zh: 没有理由说明你生不出一个完全正常的孩子。

ex.en: You know perfectly well what happened.
ex.zh: 你完全清楚发生了什么。

e.en: If something is done perfectly, it is done so well that it could not possibly be done better.

ex.en: This ambitious adaptation perfectly captures the spirit of Kurt Vonnegut's acclaimed novel.
ex.zh: 这次大胆的改编完美地把握住了库尔特·冯内古特那部广为称赞的小说的精髓。

d: adv. 完美地，极佳地；绝对地，完全地

e.en: You can use petty to describe things such as problems, rules, or arguments that you think are unimportant or relate to unimportant things.

ex.en: He was miserable all the time and fights would start over petty things.
ex.zh: 他一直都很闷闷不乐，常为一些鸡毛蒜皮的事吵架。

ex.en: ...endless rules and petty regulations.
ex.zh: …没完没了的规则和无足轻重的规定。

e.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

ex.en: He was petty-minded and obsessed with detail.
ex.zh: 他谨小慎微，过于在意细节。

e.en: 狭隘

ex.en: Never had she met such spite and pettiness.
ex.zh: 她以前从来没有碰到过这样的恶意和狭隘。

e.en: Petty is used of people or actions that are less important, serious, or great than others. (人或行动)

ex.en: ...petty crime, such as purse-snatching and minor break-ins.
ex.zh: …诸如抢钱包、不严重的入室盗窃之类的轻罪。

d: adj. 不重要的，琐碎的，小的；小气的，小心眼的；次要的，职位低的；（罪行）轻微的
【名】 （Petty）（英、法）佩蒂（人名）

e.en: Something that is perfect is as good as it could possibly be.

ex.en: He spoke perfect English.
ex.zh: 他讲一口纯正的英语。

ex.en: Nobody is perfect.
ex.zh: 人无完人。

e.en: If you say that something is perfect for a particular person, thing, or activity, you are emphasizing that it is very suitable for them or for that activity.

ex.en: The pool area is perfect for entertaining.
ex.zh: 游泳池一带最适合娱乐。

e.en: If an object or surface is perfect, it does not have any marks on it, or does not have any lumps, hollows, or cracks in it.

ex.en: Use only clean, Grade A, perfect eggs.
ex.zh: 只用洁净的、一级的、无瑕疵的鸡蛋。

e.en: You can use perfect to give emphasis to the noun following it. (用以强调所修饰名词)

ex.en: She was a perfect fool.
ex.zh: 她是个十足的傻瓜。

ex.en: Some people are always coming up to perfect strangers and asking them what they do.
ex.zh: 有些人总是走近完全不认识的人跟前，问人家是干什么的。

d: adj. 无瑕的，完好的；完全正确的，极其准确的；完美的，理想的；最佳的，绝配的；十足的，完全的；通常的，大体的；（语法）完成时的，完成式的；（数字）完全的；（花）有雌雄蕊的；（昆虫）性成熟的；（真菌）有性孢子形成阶段的，有性的；完成时的，完成式的
v. 完善，使完美；双面印完（一页纸）；使（礼物、头衔等）合法转移
n. （语法）完成时，完成体
【名】 （Perfect）（美、爱、英）珀费克特（人名）
adv. 欢快活泼地

e.en: If something gives you pleasure, you get a feeling of happiness, satisfaction, or enjoyment from it.

ex.en: Watching sports gave him great pleasure.
ex.zh: 观看体育运动带给他极大的愉悦。

ex.en: Everybody takes pleasure in eating.
ex.zh: 每个人都在吃中获得愉悦。

e.en: Pleasure is the activity of enjoying yourself, especially rather than working or doing what you have a duty to do.

ex.en: He mixed business and pleasure in a perfect and dynamic way.
ex.zh: 他把工作和娱乐以一种完美而活跃的方式结合了起来。

e.en: A pleasure is an activity, experience, or aspect of something that you find very enjoyable or satisfying.

ex.en: Watching TV is our only pleasure.
ex.zh: 看电视是我们惟一的乐趣。

ex.en: ...the pleasure of seeing a smiling face.
ex.zh: …看到一张笑脸的那种愉悦。

e.en: If you meet someone for the first time, you can say, as a way of being polite, that it is a pleasure to meet them. You can also ask for the pleasure of someone's company as a polite and formal way of inviting them somewhere. 荣幸 (用于初次见面礼貌地打招呼)

ex.en: "A pleasure to meet you, sir," he said.
ex.zh: “很荣幸见到您，先生，”他说。

d: n. 快乐，满足，欣慰；乐事，趣事；（尤指工作、职责之外的）娱乐，消遣
adj. 游乐的，非公务的
v. 从……中获得乐趣；（使）高兴

e.en: If you poke someone or something, you quickly push them with your finger or with a sharp object. 戳;

ex.en: Lindy poked him in the ribs.
ex.zh: 林迪戳了戳他的肋骨。

e.en: Poke is also a noun.

ex.en: John smiled at them and gave Richard a playful poke.
ex.zh: 约翰冲他们笑了笑，还顽皮地捅了理查德一下。

e.en: If you poke one thing into another, you push the first thing into the second thing.

ex.en: He poked his finger into the hole.
ex.zh: 他把手指戳进洞里。

e.en: If something pokes out of or through another thing, you can see part of it appearing from behind or underneath the other thing. 伸出;

ex.en: He saw the dog's twitching nose poke out of the basket.
ex.zh: 他看见那条狗颤搐的鼻子从篮子里露出来。

d: v. （用手指或尖利物品）戳，刺；从……露出（或伸出、探出）；把……戳进，把……插入；戳（洞）；拨（火）；与（某人）性交；吸引（另一用户）的注意
n. 捅，戳；轻微的批评，奚落；张望，寻觅；（汽车的）马力，推进力；（尤指19世纪初的）宽前檐女帽（poke bonnet）；袋，小包；钱包；美国商陆；美国白藜芦（Indian poke）；性交

e.en: If you prefer someone or something, you like that person or thing better than another, and so you are more likely to choose them if there is a choice.

ex.en: Does he prefer a particular sort of music?
ex.zh: 他更喜欢某种特别的音乐吗？

ex.en: I became a teacher because I preferred books and people to politics.
ex.zh: 我成为了一名教师是因为我更喜欢书籍和人而不是政治。

d: adj. 更合意的，更好的
v. 更喜爱，宁可；举报，提出（控告）；提拔（某人），提升（prefer 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A pony is a small or young horse.

d: n. 矮种马，小型马； 赛马（the ponies）；小酒杯，一小杯酒；25 英镑；马尾辫； 小酒杯，一小杯酒
v. （为……）付款（pony up）

e.en: Doctors are sometimes referred to as practitioners or medical practitioners.

d: n. 从业者，执业者，开业者（practitioner 的复数）；实践者
n. 有礼貌；有礼貌的行为；优雅

e.en: A premium is a sum of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy.

ex.en: It is too early to say whether insurance premiums will be affected.
ex.zh: 保险费会不会受到影响现在判定还为时过早。

e.en: A premium is a sum of money that you have to pay for something in addition to the normal cost.

ex.en: Even if customers want "solutions," most are not willing to pay a premium for them.
ex.zh: 即使顾客们想要“解决方案”，大部分人不愿意为此支付附加费。

e.en: Premium products are of a higher than usual quality and are often expensive.

ex.en: At the premium end of the market, business is booming.
ex.zh: 在市场的高端销售区，生意火暴。

e.en: If something is at a premium, it is wanted or needed, but is difficult to get or achieve.

ex.en: If space is at a premium, choose adaptable furniture that won't fill the room.
ex.zh: 如果空间很有限，就选购不太占地方的可改装家具。

d: n. 保险费，保费；额外费用，附加费；赠品，奖品；（金融）溢价（均为 premium 的复数）

e.en: A pressing problem, need, or issue has to be dealt with immediately.

ex.en: It is one of the most pressing problems facing this country.
ex.zh: 它是该国面临的最紧迫的问题之一。

d: adj. （问题，需求，情况）紧迫的，迫切的；难以推却的，不容忽视的
n. 压制品，一批压制品（尤指唱片）；按，压，挤，推
v. 按，压；熨平（衣服）；挤着走（pressing 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Pressing）（匈、法、美）普雷辛（人名）

e.en: To prompt someone to do something means to make them decide to do it.

ex.en: Japan's recession has prompted consumers to cut back on buying cars.
ex.zh: 日本的经济衰退已促使消费者们削减购车花销。

e.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you prompt an actor, you tell them what their next line is when they have forgotten what comes next. 提示; 给 (演员)

ex.en: "You wouldn't have wanted to bring those people to justice anyway, would you?" Brand prompted him.
ex.zh: “你本不想将那些人绳之以法的，是吧？”布兰德提示他说。

e.en: A prompt action is done without any delay. 立即的 (行动)

ex.en: It is not too late, but prompt action is needed.
ex.zh: 还不太晚，但需要立即行动。

e.en: If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late. (做某事)

ex.en: You have been so prompt in carrying out all these commissions.
ex.zh: 你执行所有这些任务非常迅速。

d: v. 提示，提醒，给（演员等）提词；引起，促使（prompt 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A purist is a person who wants something to be totally correct or unchanged, especially something they know a lot about.

ex.en: The new edition of the dictionary carries 7,000 additions to the language, which purists say is under threat.
ex.zh: 新版词典为该语种增加了7000个词条，纯粹派说该语种正受到威胁。

e.en: Purist attitudes are the kind of attitudes that purists have.

ex.en: ...a peculiarly purist argument.
ex.zh: …一个纯粹主义的典型论点。

d: n. （语言、艺术等方面的）纯粹主义者，语言纯正主义者
adj. 纯粹主义的，严格正统的

e.en: Something that is real actually exists and is not imagined, invented, or theoretical.

ex.en: No, it wasn't a dream. It was real.
ex.zh: 不，那不是梦。它是真实的。

e.en: If something is real to someone, they experience it as though it really exists or happens, even though it does not.

ex.en: Whitechild's life becomes increasingly real to the reader.
ex.zh: 怀特菜尔德的生活在读者看来越来越像是真的。

e.en: A material or object that is real is natural or functioning, and not artificial or an imitation. 天然的;

ex.en: ...the smell of real leather.
ex.zh: …真皮的气味。

e.en: You can use real to describe someone or something that has all the characteristics or qualities that such a person or thing typically has. 名副其实的;

ex.en: ...his first real girlfriend.
ex.zh: …他的第一个名副其实的女朋友。

d: adj. 实际存在的，非想象的；名副其实的；真正的，真实的；真的，非人工的；真诚的；强烈的；确实重大的；十足的，绝对的（用来加强语气）；（数量、数字）真实的，实际的；（光学）（图像）实的；（书或电影中的场景）逼真的，似真的；（哲学）实在的
adv. 很，非常地
n. 雷阿尔（巴西1994年以来的基本货币单位，等于100分）；雷阿尔（多个西班牙语国家以前的硬币和货币单位）
【名】 （Real）（德、西、葡、法）雷亚尔，（英）里尔（人名）
vt. （英国英语拼写，同 realize）认识到，明白，意识到；实现，达成；（财务）将（资产）变现，变卖；获得（利润）

e.en: If you associate someone or something with another thing, the two are connected in your mind. 将 (…和…)

ex.en: Through science we've got the idea of associating progress with the future.
ex.zh: 通过科学我们已有了将进步与未来联系起来的观念。

e.en: If you are associated with a particular organization, cause, or point of view, or if you associate yourself with it, you support it publicly. 使 (某人与某组织、事业、观点等)

ex.en: I haven't been associated with the project over the last year.
ex.zh: 我过去一年不曾跟这个项目有关联。

e.en: If you say that someone is associating with another person or group of people, you mean they are spending a lot of time in the company of people you do not approve of. (与某个或某群人)

ex.en: What would they think if they knew that they were associating with a murderer?
ex.zh: 如果他们知道了他们正与一个杀人犯打成一片，他们会怎么想？

e.en: Your associates are the people you are closely connected with, especially at work. (尤指工作中的)

ex.en: ...the restaurant owner's business associates.
ex.zh: …该餐馆老板的商业伙伴们。

d: v. 联想，联系；支持，同意；交往，（尤指）混在一起
n. 同事，伙伴；副学士，准学士；副职，副手；准会员；联想
adj. 副的，准的，非正式的；联合的，有关连的

e.en: Membership in an organization is the state of being a member of it.

ex.en: ...his membership in the Communist Party.
ex.zh: …他的共产党党员身份。

e.en: The membership of an organization is the people who belong to it, or the number of people who belong to it. 全体成员;

ex.en: By 1890 the organization had a membership of 409,000.
ex.zh: 到1890年该组织有409000名成员。

d: n. 会员身份，会籍；会员数；（全体）会员

e.en: Trade is the activity of buying, selling, or exchanging goods or services between people, companies, or countries. 贸易;

ex.en: Texas has a long history of trade with Mexico.
ex.zh: 得克萨斯与墨西哥有着悠久的贸易史。

ex.en: ...negotiations on a new international trade agreement.
ex.zh: …关于一个新的国际贸易协定的谈判。

e.en: When people, companies, or countries trade, they buy, sell, or exchange goods or services between themselves.

ex.en: They may refuse to trade, even when offered attractive prices.
ex.zh: 他们有可能拒绝做生意，即便是报价很有吸引力。

ex.en: They had years of experience of trading with the West.
ex.zh: 他们有数年与西方做生意的经验。

e.en: 交易

ex.en: Trading on the stock exchange may be suspended.
ex.zh: 股票交易可能被暂停。

e.en: A trade is a particular area of business or industry. 生意;

ex.en: They've ruined the tourist trade for the next few years.
ex.zh: 他们已经毁掉了以后几年的旅游生意。

d: n. 贸易，买卖；行业；同行业者，同仁（the trade）；营业额，交易量；（尤指需要特殊技术和手工劳动的）职业，行当；交换，交易； （体育界）转会，交换运动员； 执照酒商；信风，贸易风（trades）；股票交易
v. 做买卖，做生意；营运，营业；（在证券交易所）交易，买卖；用……进行交换，互相交换；（某物）替代（某物）；对打，对骂； 将（运动员）转会（或转队）；交换，对换（位置或处境）

e.en: If the different elements of a piece of writing, a piece of music, or a set of ideas cohere, they fit together well so that they form a united whole. (书写片段、音乐或想法)

ex.en: The various elements of the novel fail to cohere.
ex.zh: 这部小说的各部分之间无法连贯起来。

ex.en: This coheres with Peel's championing of alternative music.
ex.zh: 这与皮尔支持另类音乐的做法相一致。

d: vi. （物体、材料等）粘着，粘合，凝聚；（写作、音乐、思想等的各部分）连贯，一致，协调；cohere with：与……一致，符合

e.en: An American person or thing belongs to or comes from the United States of America. 美国的;

ex.en: ...the American ambassador at the United Nations.
ex.zh: ...美国驻联合国大使。

ex.en: ...the influence of American television and movies.
ex.zh: ...美国电视和电影产生的影响。

e.en: An American is someone who is American.

ex.en: The 1990 Nobel Prize for medicine was won by two Americans.
ex.zh: 两名美国人获得了1990年度诺贝尔医学奖。

d: n. （American）美国人；美国英语；美洲人
adj. （American）美国的；美国人的；美洲的
n. 防御，保卫；防御物，防御能力；国防机构，国防体系；辩解，辩白；被告，辩护律师；（法庭上的）辩护，答辩； 防守队员，防守；（竞赛中的）卫冕，（选举中的）保住席位；戒备心理，自我防卫；国际象棋的防御（黑棋的某种特定走法）

e.en: A designation is a description, name, or title that is given to someone or something. Designation is the fact of giving that description, name, or title. 指定; 名称;

ex.en: Wilderness designation prohibits road building, the use of mechanized equipment and most other developments.
ex.zh: 荒野之地禁止筑路、使用机械设备以及绝大多数其它的开发。

d: n. 指定，委任；名称，称号

e.en: An idea is a plan, suggestion, or possible course of action. 主意;

ex.en: It's a good idea to have your blood pressure checked regularly.
ex.zh: 定期检查你的血压是个好主意。

ex.en: I really like the idea of helping people.
ex.zh: 我非常喜欢帮助他人这个主意。

e.en: An idea is an opinion or belief about what something is like or should be like. 看法;

ex.en: Some of his ideas about democracy are entirely his own.
ex.zh: 他对民主的一些看法完全是个人的。

e.en: If someone gives you an idea of something, they give you information about it without being very exact or giving a lot of detail.

ex.en: This table will give you some idea of how levels of ability in a foreign language can be measured.
ex.zh: 这个表格将告诉你一些如何衡量外语能力级别的大致信息。

e.en: If you have an idea of something, you know about it to some extent. (对某事有)

ex.en: No one has any real idea how much the company will make next year.
ex.zh: 没有人真正知道公司明年将赚多少钱。

ex.en: We had no idea what was happening.
ex.zh: 我们不知道正在发生什么。

d: n. 想法，主意；观点，看法；原则，信念；理解，了解；猜想；目标，意图；（柏拉图哲学）理念

e.en: You use else after words such as "anywhere," "someone," and "what" to refer in a vague way to another person, place, or thing. (不确指人、处、事)

ex.en: If I can't make a living at painting, at least I can teach someone else to paint.
ex.zh: 如果我不能以画画谋生的话，至少我能教别人画画。

ex.en: We had nothing else to do on those long trips.
ex.zh: 在那些漫长的旅途中我们别无他事可做。

e.en: Else is also an adverb.

ex.en: I never wanted to live anywhere else.
ex.zh: 我从未想要到其他任何地方去住。

e.en: You use else after words such as "everyone," "everything," and "everywhere" to refer in a vague way to all the other people, things, or places except the one you are talking about.

ex.en: As I try to be truthful, I expect everyone else to be truthful.
ex.zh: 因为我努力做到诚实，所以我期望每个其他也都诚实。

e.en: Else is also an adverb.

ex.en: Cleveland seems so much dirtier than everywhere else.
ex.zh: 克利夫兰似乎比其他任何地方都脏得多。

d: adv. 此外，其他；否则，要不然
adj. 其他的，另外的
【名】 （Else）（英）埃尔斯，（德）埃尔泽，（芬、丹）埃尔塞（人名）

e.en: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

ex.en: There has been a lively interest in the elections in the last two weeks.
ex.zh: 过去两周人们对选举一直有强烈的兴趣。

ex.en: She'd liked him at first, but soon lost interest.
ex.zh: 最初她喜欢过他，但很快就失去了兴趣。

e.en: Your interests are the things that you enjoy doing.

ex.en: Encourage your child in her interests and hobbies.
ex.zh: 鼓励你的孩子发展她的兴趣和爱好。

e.en: If something interests you, it attracts your attention so that you want to learn or hear more about it or continue doing it.

ex.en: Your financial problems do not interest me.
ex.zh: 我对你的财务问题不感兴趣。

e.en: If you are trying to persuade someone to buy or do something, you can say that you are trying to interest them in it. 引起 (购买或做某事)

ex.en: Can I interest you in a new car?
ex.zh: 我给你介绍一下新车，你感兴趣吗？

d: n. interest 的复数：兴趣，爱好；利益，好处；利益集团；（法律、商业）权益，股权，利害关系；利息（此义通常用单数 interest）
v. interest 的第三人称单数：使感兴趣，引起……的关注；劝说（某人）购买或参与（用于 interest sb in sth 结构）

e.en: A member of a group is one of the people, animals, or things belonging to that group. (某群体的)

ex.en: He refused to name the members of staff involved.
ex.zh: 他拒绝说出所涉职员的名字。

ex.en: Their lack of training could put members of the public at risk.
ex.zh: 他们训练的缺乏会使公众成员面临风险。

e.en: A member of an organization such as a club or a political party is a person who has officially joined the organization. 会员;

ex.en: The support of our members is of great importance to the association.
ex.zh: 我们会员的支持对协会来说非常重要。

e.en: A member country or member state is one of the countries that has joined an international organization or group.

ex.en: ...the member countries of the North American Free Trade Association.
ex.zh: …北美自由贸易联盟的会员国。

e.en: A member or Member is a person who has been elected to a legislature or parliament.

ex.en: He was elected to Parliament as the Member for Leeds.
ex.zh: 他被选入国会作为利兹市的议员。

d: n. 成员，一分子；会员；议员；用于表示荣誉的头衔（尤指最低级）勋章获得者；（建筑或桥的）构件；（句子）成分；（方程式）端边；（一组数字）项；（数学集合）元；身体的一部分（如胳膊或腿）；阴茎

e.en: Musk is a substance with a strong smell that is used in making perfume.

d: n. 麝香；麝香香味；麝香鹿

e.en: A party is a political organization whose members have similar aims and beliefs. Usually the organization tries to get its members elected to the legislature of a country.

ex.en: ...a member of the Republican Party.
ex.zh: …一名共和党党员。

ex.en: ...opposition parties.
ex.zh: …反对党们。

e.en: A party is a social event, often in someone's home, at which people enjoy themselves doing things such as eating, drinking, dancing, talking, or playing games.

ex.en: The couple met at a party.
ex.zh: 这对夫妇相识于一个派对。

ex.en: We threw a huge birthday party.
ex.zh: 我们举办了一次盛大的生日派对。

e.en: If you party, you enjoy yourself doing things such as going out to parties, drinking, dancing, and talking to people.

ex.en: They come to eat and drink, to swim, to party.
ex.zh: 他们来吃饭、喝酒、游泳，尽情欢乐。

e.en: A party of people is a group of people who are doing something together, for example, travelling together. 群; 队;

ex.en: They became separated from their party.
ex.zh: 他们跟他们团队走散了。

ex.en: ...a party of sightseers.
ex.zh: …一群游客。

d: n. 聚会，派对；政党，党派；（契约或争论的）当事人，一方；队，组，群；参加者；人
v.  尽情欢乐，欢宴
adj. （纹章）分割开的，分成不同颜色部分的

e.en: The leader of the government of a country is sometimes referred to as the country's premier.

ex.en: ...Australian premier Paul Keating.
ex.zh: …澳大利亚总理保罗·基廷。

e.en: Premier is used to describe something that is considered to be the best or most important thing of a particular type. 最好的;

ex.en: ...the country's premier opera company.
ex.zh: …这个国家最好的歌剧团。

d: adj. 首要的，最好的；最早的，最初的
n. 总理，首相；（加拿大的）省总理，地方总理；（澳大利亚州或地区的）省长
n. 普拉蒙登（加拿大地名）

e.en: Pressure is force that you produce when you press hard on something. (用力按压而产生的)

ex.en: She kicked at the door with her foot, and the pressure was enough to open it.
ex.zh: 她用脚踢门，其产生的压力足以把门打开。

ex.en: The pressure of his fingers had relaxed.
ex.zh: 他手指的压力已经减弱了。

e.en: The pressure in a place or container is the force produced by the quantity of gas or liquid in that place or container. (某地或某容器内的气体或液体产生的)

ex.en: The window in the cockpit had blown in and the pressure dropped dramatically.
ex.zh: 驾驶舱的窗子已向内破裂，气压骤然下降。

e.en: If there is pressure on a person, someone is trying to persuade or force them to do something. (因极力劝说或强迫某人做某事而造成的)

ex.en: He may have put pressure on her to agree.
ex.zh: 他可能已对她施压让她同意。

ex.en: A lot of dot-coms were under pressure from their investors.
ex.zh: 很多网络公司那时都在承受着来自其投资者的压力。

e.en: If you are experiencing pressure, you feel that you must do a lot of tasks or make a lot of decisions in very little time, or that people expect a lot from you. (因任务紧、决策时间短或别人的期望多而感到的)

ex.en: Can you work under pressure?
ex.zh: 你能在压力下工作吗？

ex.en: Even if I had the talent to play tennis I couldn't stand the pressure.
ex.zh: 即使我有打网球的天资，我也承受不了那种压力。

d: n. 压力，挤压；（气体或液体形成的）压力，压强；心理压力，紧张；催促，要求；气压
v. 对……施加压力，强迫；使……增压
圣皮埃尔

e.en: If you trust someone, you believe that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.

ex.en: "I trust you completely," he said.
ex.zh: “我完全信任你。”他说。

e.en: Your trust in someone is your belief that they are honest and sincere and will not deliberately do anything to harm you.

ex.en: He destroyed me and my trust in men.
ex.zh: 他毁了我，也毁了我对男人的信任。

ex.en: You've betrayed their trust.
ex.zh: 你辜负了他们的信任。

e.en: If you trust someone to do something, you believe that they will do it. 相信 (某人会做某事)

ex.en: That's why I must trust you to keep this secret.
ex.zh: 这就是我一定相信你会保守此秘密的原因。

e.en: If you trust someone with something important or valuable, you allow them to look after it or deal with it.

ex.en: This could make your superiors hesitate to trust you with major responsibilities.
ex.zh: 这可能会使你的上司犹豫着不愿把重大职责托付给你。

d: n. 信任，信赖；（金钱或财产的）信托，托管；受托基金机构，受托团体；代管的财物，托管的财物；公立医院（由政府资助、独立经营）；托拉斯托拉斯，垄断企业；受托，受委任；被托付的人，被赋予的职责；希望，期待
v. 信任，相信；对……有把握，信得过；坚信，信仰；希望，盼望；托交，托付；赊账
【名】 （Trust）（英）特拉斯特（人名）
n. 乌克兰（欧洲东部国家，原苏联一加盟共和国，现已独立）

e.en: If something is worth a particular amount of money, it can be sold for that amount or is considered to have that value.

ex.en: A local jeweler says the pearl is worth at least $500.
ex.zh: 一位本地珠宝商说这颗珍珠至少值$500。

ex.en: His mother inherited a business worth 15,000 dollars a year.
ex.zh: 他的母亲继承了一个每年盈利15000美元的商行。

e.tip: 与数量词结合的复合词
e.en: Worth combines with amounts of money, so that when you talk about a particular amount of money's worth of something, you mean the quantity of it that you can buy for that amount of money.

ex.en: I went and bought about six dollars' worth of potato chips.
ex.zh: 我去买了价值约六美元的土豆片。

e.en: Worth is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Gold reserves had fallen to less than $3 billion worth.
ex.zh: 黄金储备已经降价至30亿美元以下。

e.tip: 与数量词结合的复合词
e.en: Worth combines with time expressions, so you can use worth when you are saying how long an amount of something will last. For example, a week's worth of food is the amount of food that will last you for a week. 可维持 (一段时间)

ex.en: You've got three years' worth of research money to do what you want with.
ex.zh: 你有可维持3年的研究经费来做你想做的事情。

d: adj. 价值……的，值……钱的；值得的，具有……价值的；拥有……财产的；（尤指合同）毫无价值的
n. 价格，价值；重要性，作用；能用（一个星期、一个月等）的东西
prep. 价值……；值得
【名】 （Worth）沃特（人名）

e.en: Acceptable activities and situations are those that most people approve of or consider to be normal.

ex.en: It is becoming more acceptable for women to drink.
ex.zh: 女性饮酒越来越为人接受。

e.en: 可接受性

ex.en: This assumption played a considerable part in increasing the social acceptability of divorce.
ex.zh: 这种假设对增加社会对离婚的接纳起了相当大的作用。

e.en: If something is acceptable to someone, they agree to consider it, use it, or allow it to happen.

ex.en: They have thrashed out a compromise formula acceptable to Moscow.
ex.zh: 他们反复讨论确定了一个莫斯科可以接受的妥协方案。

e.en: If you describe something as acceptable, you mean that it is good enough or fairly good. 足够好的;

ex.en: On the far side of the street was a restaurant that looked acceptable.
ex.zh: 在这条街的另一头有家餐馆看起来还可以。

d: adj. 可接受的，（大多数人）认同的；合意的，令人满意的；尚可的，勉强的；可容忍的，可允许的

e.en: the first letter in the Hebrew alphabet (א) articulated as a glottal stop and transliterated with a superior comma (`) 希伯来语的第一个字母; 发音作为声门闭锁音(א)，并在音译成英语时在上方加一个逗点（`）

d: n. 希伯来语的第一个字母（א）；（数学）阿列夫数：集合论中用符号 ℵ 表示的超限基数

e.en: Your address is the number of the house or apartment and the name of the street and the town where you live or work.

ex.en: The address is 2025 M Street, NW, Washington, DC, 20036.
ex.zh: 地址是华盛顿哥伦比亚特区，华盛顿西北，M街2025号，邮编20036。

e.en: The address of a website is its location on the Internet, for example, http://www.thomson.com.

ex.en: Full details, including the website address to log on to, are at the bottom of this page.
ex.zh: 包括要登陆的网址的完整信息在本页下端。

e.en: If a letter, envelope, or parcel is addressed to you, your name and address have been written on it. 写 (收信人的)

ex.en: Applications should be addressed to: The business affairs editor.
ex.zh: 申请信应该寄给商务编辑。

e.en: If you address a group of people, you give a speech to them.

ex.en: He is due to address a conference on human rights next week.
ex.zh: 他下周要在一个人权会议上发言。

d: adj. （邮件等）写有收件人姓名地址的，有地址的
v. （address 的过去式和过去分词）在（邮件、信封、包裹等）上写收件人姓名地址；解决，处理（问题等）；向……讲话，致词，发表演说；正式向……提出（陈述、投诉等）；称呼（某人）；（高尔夫）就位击球

e.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

ex.en: Mr. Williams is a conservative who advocates fewer government controls on business.
ex.zh: 威廉斯先生是一位提倡减少政府对商业的控制的保守人士。

e.en: An advocate of a particular action or plan is someone who recommends it publicly.

ex.en: He was a strong advocate of free market policies and a multi-party system.
ex.zh: 他是自由市场政策以及多党制的坚定倡导者。

e.en: An advocate for a particular group is a person who works for the interests of that group. 为 (某团体)

ex.en: ...advocates for the homeless.
ex.zh: …为无家可归者谋利益的人。

e.en: An advocate is a lawyer who speaks in favour of someone or defends them in a court of law.

d: v. advocate 的过去式和过去分词；（正式）拥护，支持，提倡，主张：为某个观点、政策或行动提供支持或争取支持。

e.en: the first letter in the Greek alphabet (Α, α), a vowel transliterated as a
e.zh: 希腊字母中的第一个字母

d: n. 希腊字母表的第一个字母；甲，α项，α类（一系列项目、分类中的第一位，如化合物的第一种形式）；（学校考试成绩或作业）Α等 , 甲等；（人或动物特定群体中的）头领，首领；特定领域内的主导人；α测试，智力测验（alpha test）；（天文）α星（星座中第一颗星，多为最亮的星）；α衰变（或α粒子）；（无线电通信中字母 A 的代码词）Α，α；开端，最初
adj. （兽群或人群中）最有权势的；（产品）初版的，雏形的
n. 安东尼奥（男名）

e.en: Artificial objects, materials, or processes do not occur naturally and are created by human beings, often using science or technology. 人造的 (物体、材料、工艺等)

ex.en: The city is dotted with small lakes, natural and artificial.
ex.zh: 这座城市满是天然和人造的小湖泊。

ex.en: ...a wholefood diet free from artificial additives, colours and flavours.
ex.zh: …一种无人造添加剂、色素及味素的全天然食物饮食。

e.en: 人造地

ex.en: ...artificially sweetened lemonade.
ex.zh: …人工加了糖的柠檬汽水。

e.en: An artificial state or situation exists only because someone has created it, and therefore often seems unnatural or unnecessary. 人为的 (状态、状况)

ex.en: Even in the artificial environment of an office, our body rhythms continue to affect us.
ex.zh: 即便在办公室的人为环境中，我们的身体节律继续影响我们。

e.en: 人为地

ex.en: ...state subsidies that have kept retail prices artificially low.
ex.zh: …人为地将零售价格保持在低水平的国家补贴。

d: adj. 人造的，人工的；人为的；不真挚的，矫揉造作的

e.en: If something is behind a thing or person, it is on the other side of them from you, or nearer their back rather than their front.

ex.en: I put one of the cushions behind his head.
ex.zh: 我把其中一个垫子放在了他脑后。

ex.en: They were parked behind the truck.
ex.zh: 它们被停在了卡车后面。

e.en: Behind is also an adverb.

ex.en: Rising into the hills behind are 800 acres of parkland.
ex.zh: 往上延伸至后面小山的是800英亩的草木区。

e.en: If you are walking or travelling behind someone or something, you are following them. (跟随)

ex.en: Keith wandered along behind him.
ex.zh: 基思跟在他后面闲逛。

e.en: Behind is also an adverb. (跟随)

ex.en: The troopers followed behind, every muscle tensed for the sudden gunfire.
ex.zh: 骑兵们跟在后面，每一块肌肉都因突如其来的炮火而绷得紧紧的。

d: prep. 在（或向）……的后面；落后于；是……背后的原因；支持；（……的外表）之下；成为（某人的）过去；低于；在……死后
adv. 在后面；留在原地；落后（于）；拖欠，不按时
n. 屁股；（澳橄）射门得分

e.en: An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.

ex.en: ...the National Basketball Association.
ex.zh: …全国篮球协会。

e.en: Your association with a person or a thing such as an organization is the connection that you have with them. (与某人、某物的)

ex.en: ...the company's six-year association with retailer J.C. Penney Co.
ex.zh: …这家公司与零售商彭尼公司6年的业务往来。

e.en: If something has particular associations for you, it is connected in your mind with a particular memory, idea, or feeling. (与某记忆、观念、情感的)

ex.en: He has a shelf full of things, each of which has associations for him.
ex.zh: 他有一个摆满了东西的架子，每一样都与他的内心世界有关联。

e.en: If you do something in association with someone else, you do it together.

ex.en: The changes I instigated in association with the board 18 months ago were because I love this company.
ex.zh: 18个月前我联合董事会发起的这些变革是出于我爱这家公司。

d: n. 协会，社团，联盟；交往，联合；联系，因果关系；联想

e.en: Belief is a feeling of certainty that something exists, is true, or is good.

ex.en: One billion people throughout the world are Muslims, united by belief in one god.
ex.zh: 全世界有10亿人是穆斯林，因为对一位神灵的信仰而团结在一起。

e.en: Your religious or political beliefs are your views on religious or political matters. (宗教或政治的)

ex.en: He refuses to compete on Sundays because of his religious beliefs.
ex.zh: 由于他的宗教观念，他拒绝星期天进行比赛。

e.en: If it is your belief that something is the case, it is your strong opinion that it is the case.

ex.en: It is our belief that improvements in health care will lead to a stronger, more prosperous economy.
ex.zh: 我们坚定的信念是卫生保健的改善会带来更加茁壮、繁荣的经济。

e.en: You use beyond belief to emphasize that something is true to a very great degree or that it happened to a very great degree.

ex.en: We are devastated, shocked beyond belief.
ex.zh: 我们遭到了挫败，震惊得难以置信。

d: n. 相信，信心；看法，信念，观点；信仰，信条

e.en: If you believe that something is true, you think it is true, but you are not sure.

ex.en: Experts believe that the coming drought will be extensive.
ex.zh: 专家们认为即将到来的干旱将会是大面积的。

ex.en: We believe them to be hidden here in this apartment.
ex.zh: 我们认为他们藏匿在这所公寓里。

e.en: If you believe someone or if you believe what they say or write, you accept that they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He did not sound as if he believed her.
ex.zh: 听起来他似乎不相信她的话。

ex.en: Never believe anything a married man says about his wife.
ex.zh: 永远别相信一个已婚男人说的关于自己妻子的话。

e.en: If you believe in fairies, ghosts, or miracles, you are sure that they exist or happen. If you believe in a god, you are sure of the existence of that god.

ex.en: I don't believe in ghosts.
ex.zh: 我不相信有鬼。

e.en: If you believe in a way of life or an idea, you are in favour of it because you think it is good or right.

ex.en: He believed in marital fidelity.
ex.zh: 他赞成对婚姻忠实。

d: v. 相信；认为，猜想；信教

e.en: A bloc is a group of countries that have similar political aims and interests and that act together over some issues. (具有相似政治目标和利益的国家结成的)

ex.en: ...the former Soviet bloc.
ex.zh: …前苏联阵营。

d: n. 集团，阵营
【名】 （Bloc）（法、罗）布洛克（人名）

e.en: Bristles are the short hairs that grow on a man's face after he has shaved. The hairs on the top of a man's head can also be called bristles when they are cut very short. 胡子茬; (男子头顶处的)

ex.en: ...two days' growth of bristles.
ex.zh: …两天没剃长出的胡子茬儿。

e.en: The bristles of a brush are the thick hairs or hairlike pieces of plastic which are attached to it. (刷子的)

ex.en: As soon as the bristles on your toothbrush begin to wear, throw it out.
ex.zh: 牙刷毛一旦磨损就扔掉。

e.en: Bristles are thick, strong animal hairs that feel hard and rough.

ex.en: It has a short stumpy tail covered with bristles.
ex.zh: 它有一条又短又粗、长满了刚毛的尾巴。

d: v. （bristle 的过去式及过去分词）：（毛发等）竖立；（动物）竖起毛发；使（毛发等）竖起；对……发怒，被激怒；充满，密布（bristle with 的过去式）
adj. 有刚毛的；（毛发等）竖起的
v. 建造，修建；发展，建立；逐渐增强
n. 体形，体格；（尤指车辆的）造型，构造；构件

e.en: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen. 起因;

ex.en: Smoking is the biggest preventable cause of death and disease.
ex.zh: 吸烟是造成不必要疾病和死亡的最大原因。

e.en: A cause is an aim or principle which a group of people supports or is fighting for. 奋斗目标;

ex.en: Refusing to have one leader has not helped the cause.
ex.zh: 拒绝接受领导无益于该事业。

e.en: To cause something, usually something bad, means to make it happen.

ex.en: The insecticide used on some weeds can cause health problems.
ex.zh: 喷洒在野草上的杀虫剂会引发各种健康问题。

ex.en: This was a genuine mistake, but it did cause me some worry.
ex.zh: 这纯属失误，但它确实令我有些不安。

e.en: If you have cause for a particular feeling or action, you have good reasons for feeling it or doing it.

ex.en: Only a few people can find any cause for celebration.
ex.zh: 只有少数人能找到庆祝的理由。

d: v. 引起；导致；使发生（cause 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 由……引起的；由……造成的（常与 by 连用）

e.en: Certainty is the state of being definite or of having no doubts at all about something.

ex.en: I have told them with absolute certainty there'll be no change of policy.
ex.zh: 我十分确定地告诉他们政策不会有变。

e.en: Certainty is the fact that something is certain to happen.

ex.en: A general election became a certainty last week.
ex.zh: 普选上周已成必然。

ex.en: ...the certainty of more violence and bloodshed.
ex.zh: …必然会有的更多的暴力和流血事件。

e.en: Certainties are things that nobody has any doubts about.

ex.en: There are no certainties in modern Europe.
ex.zh: 现代欧洲无定事。

d: n. 确实，确定性；确实的事，必然的事

e.en: A chain consists of metal rings connected together in a line.

ex.en: His open shirt revealed a fat gold chain.
ex.zh: 他敞开的衬衣里露出一条粗大的金链子。

e.en: A chain of things is a group of them existing or arranged in a line.

ex.en: ...a chain of islands known as the Windward Islands.
ex.zh: …被称为“向风群岛”的列岛。

e.en: A chain of stores, hotels, or other businesses is a number of them owned by the same person or company.

ex.en: ...a large supermarket chain.
ex.zh: …一家大型连锁超市。

e.en: If prisoners are in chains, they have thick rings of metal around their wrists or ankles to prevent them from escaping.

ex.en: He'd spent four and a half years in windowless cells, much of the time in chains.
ex.zh: 他在无窗的牢房里呆了4年半，大部分时间是手铐脚镣。

d: n. （chain 的复数）链条，链子；一连串，一系列；镣铐，枷锁；连锁店，联营企业
v. （chain 的第三人称单数形式）用链条系住；束缚

e.en: If there is a choice of things, there are several of them and you can choose the one you want.

ex.en: It's available in a choice of colours.
ex.zh: 它有多种颜色可供选择。

ex.en: At lunchtime, there's a choice between the buffet or the set menu.
ex.zh: 午饭时，可以选择自助餐或套餐。

e.en: Your choice is someone or something that you choose from a range of things.

ex.en: Although he was only grumbling, his choice of words made Rodney angry.
ex.zh: 尽管他只是在发牢骚，但他所用的字眼却让罗德尼很生气。

e.en: Choice means of very high quality.

ex.en: ...a box of their choicest chocolates.
ex.zh: …他们的一盒上等巧克力。

e.en: If you have no choice but to do something or have little choice but to do it, you cannot avoid doing it.

ex.en: They had little choice but to agree to what he suggested.
ex.zh: 除了同意他的意见，他们别无选择。

d: n. 选择，抉择；选择的机会，选择权；选择范围，选择余地；入选者，被选中的东西；精选品
adj. 上等的，优质的；尖刻的，刻薄的；精选的

e.en: Someone who is a citizen of a particular country is legally accepted as belonging to that country.

ex.en: ...American citizens.
ex.zh: …美国公民。

e.en: The citizens of a town or city are the people who live there.

ex.en: ...the citizens of Buenos Aires.
ex.zh: …布宜诺斯艾利斯的市民。

d: n. 市民，城镇居民；公民，国民

e.en: A cocktail is an alcoholic drink which contains several ingredients.

ex.en: On arrival, guests are offered wine or a champagne cocktail.
ex.zh: 到达时，客人们可以享用葡萄酒或一份香槟鸡尾酒。

e.en: A cocktail is a mixture of a number of different things, especially ones that do not go together well. (尤指不太容易融合的几种物品的)

ex.en: The court was told she had taken a cocktail of drugs and alcohol.
ex.zh: 法庭被告知她服用了药酒混合剂。

e.en: a horse with a docked tail

d: n. 鸡尾酒（cocktail 的复数）；混合物（cocktail 的复数）；餐前开胃菜（cocktail 的复数）

e.en: Collective actions, situations, or feelings involve or are shared by every member of a group of people.

ex.en: It was a collective decision.
ex.zh: 这是集体的决定。

e.en: 集体地

ex.en: They collectively decided to recognize the changed situation.
ex.zh: 他们集体决定承认局势的变化。

e.en: A collective amount of something is the total obtained by adding together the amounts that each person or thing in a group has.

ex.en: Their collective volume wasn't very large.
ex.zh: 他们总体的数量不太大。

e.en: 总体地

ex.en: In 1968 the states collectively spent $2 billion on it.
ex.zh: 1968年各州总体为此花了20亿美元。

d: adj. 集体的，共同的；总的，集合的
n. 集体农庄，集体企业；集合名词

e.en: in Britain Central Office of Information (英国)

d: abbr. 利益冲突（conflict of interest）；（英国）中央新闻署（Central Office of Information）；（生物学）细胞色素c氧化酶亚基I（cytochrome c oxidase subunit I）基因，常用作物种鉴定DNA条形码；（通信）通信操作说明书（Communications Operating Instructions）；利益共同体（Community of Interest）
n. （Coi）人名；（法）克瓦；（意）科伊

e.en: If something is common, it is found in large numbers or it happens often.

ex.en: His name was Hansen, a common name in Norway.
ex.zh: 他叫汉森，一个在挪威很常见的名字。

ex.en: Oil pollution is the most common cause of death for seabirds.
ex.zh: 石油污染是海鸟死亡的最常见的原因。

e.en: 常见地

ex.en: Parsley is one of the most commonly used herbs.
ex.zh: 欧芹是最常用的草药之一。

e.en: If something is common to two or more people or groups, it is done, possessed, or used by them all. 共同的; 共有的;

ex.en: Moldavians and Romanians share a common language.
ex.zh: 摩尔达维亚人和罗马尼亚人使用一种共同的语言。

e.en: When there are more animals or plants of a particular species than there are of related species, then the first species is called common. (物种)

ex.en: ...the common house fly.
ex.zh: …常见的家蝇。

d: adj. 共同的，共享的；常见的，普遍的，一般的；普通的，平凡的；出于礼貌的，起码的；粗俗的，庸俗的
n. 公共用地，公地；校园公共食堂；常识；（基督教教会适用于各种场合的）普通礼拜；平民

e.en: If someone commits a crime or a sin, they do something illegal or bad. 犯 (罪); 做 (坏事)

ex.en: I have never committed any crime.
ex.zh: 我从没有犯过任何罪。

ex.en: This is a man who has committed murder.
ex.zh: 这是个犯了谋杀罪的男人。

e.en: If someone commits suicide, they deliberately kill themselves. 进行 (自杀)

ex.en: There are unconfirmed reports he tried to commit suicide.
ex.zh: 有未经证实的报道说他曾企图自杀。

e.en: If you commit money or resources to something, you decide to use them for a particular purpose. 调拨 (钱、资源)

ex.en: They called on Western nations to commit more money to the poorest nations.
ex.zh: 他们号召西方国家为最贫困国家拨更多的款。

ex.en: The company had committed thousands of dollars for a plan to reduce mercury emissions.
ex.zh: 该公司已经为了一项减少汞排放的计划调拨了数千美元。

e.en: If you commit yourself to something, you say that you will definitely do it. If you commit yourself to someone, you decide that you want to have a long-term relationship with them. 使 (自己) 致力于; 使 (自己) 承诺 (与某人的长期关系)

ex.en: I would advise people to think very carefully about committing themselves to working Sundays.
ex.zh: 我会建议人们认真考虑答应周日工作。

ex.en: I'd like a friendship that might lead to something deeper, but I wouldn't want to commit myself too soon.
ex.zh: 我想要可能发展到更深层关系的友谊，但我不想太快做出承诺。

d: adj. 尽心尽力的，忠诚的
v. 承诺；委托；干坏事（commit 的过去分词形式）

e.en: Concern is worry about a situation.

ex.en: The group has expressed concern about reports of political violence in Africa.
ex.zh: 该集团已对有关非洲政治暴力的报道表示担忧。

ex.en: The move follows growing public concern over the spread of the disease.
ex.zh: 该行动是针对公众日益增长的对该疾病传播的担忧而采取的。

e.en: If something concerns you, it worries you.

ex.en: The growing number of people seeking refuge in Thailand is beginning to concern Western aid agencies.
ex.zh: 日益增多的到泰国寻求避难的人数开始让西方援助机构感到担忧。

e.en: 感到担忧的

ex.en: Academics and employers are concerned that students are not sufficiently prepared for college courses.
ex.zh: 学术界和用人单位都担心学生们对大学课程没有做好足够准备。

e.en: If you concern yourself with something, you give it attention because you think that it is important.

ex.en: I didn't concern myself with politics.
ex.zh: 我不关心政治。

d: n. 担心，忧虑；使人担忧的事物；关心，关爱；重要的事物，关心的事；（某人）负责的事，涉及的事；公司，企业；复杂的物体
v. 有关，关于；涉及，影响；使忧虑，使担心

e.en: Competition is a situation in which two or more people or groups are trying to get something which not everyone can have. (为获取难得之物而进行的)

ex.en: There's been some fierce competition for the title.
ex.zh: 已有一些为此头衔的激烈竞争。

e.en: Competition is an activity involving two or more companies, in which each company tries to get people to buy its own goods in preference to the other companies' goods. (商业上的)

ex.en: The deal would have reduced competition in the commuter-aircraft market.
ex.zh: 该交易本可以减少通勤飞机市场的竞争。

ex.en: The farmers have been seeking higher prices as better protection from foreign competition.
ex.zh: 农场主们一直在寻求更高价格来作为对外来竞争的更好保护。

e.en: The competition is the goods or services that a rival organization is selling. 竞争产品;

ex.en: The American aerospace industry has been challenged by some stiff competition.
ex.zh: 美国航空航天工业遭到了一些强劲竞争产品的挑战。

e.en: The competition is the person or people you are competing with.

ex.en: I have to change my approach, the competition is too good now.
ex.zh: 我得改变我的方法，竞争对手现在太好了。

d: n. 竞争；比赛，竞赛；竞争者，对手

e.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

ex.en: Testing patients without their consent would constitute a professional and legal offence.
ex.zh: 未得病人同意即对其进行试验会构成职业和法律犯罪。

e.en: If a number of things or people constitute something, they are the parts or members that form it. (某数量的物或人) 构成 (某事物)

ex.en: China's ethnic minorities constitute less than 7 percent of its total population.
ex.zh: 中国的少数民族构成总人口的不到7%。

d: v. 构成，组成（constitute 的第三人称单数形式）；等于，可被视为；设立，组建，任命

e.en: If you confuse two things, you get them mixed up, so that you think one of them is the other one.

ex.en: I always confuse my left with my right.
ex.zh: 我总是混淆左右。

e.en: 混淆

ex.en: Use different colours of felt pen on your sketch to avoid confusion.
ex.zh: 在草图上使用不同颜色的毡笔以免混淆。

e.en: To confuse someone means to make it difficult for them to know exactly what is happening or what to do.

ex.en: My words surprised and confused him.
ex.zh: 我的话使他既惊讶又困惑。

e.en: To confuse a situation means to make it complicated or difficult to understand.

ex.en: To further confuse the issue, there is an enormous variation in the amount of sleep people feel happy with.
ex.zh: 使这个问题进一步复杂化的是，人们感觉愉快的睡眠时间相差很大。

d: v. confuse 的第三人称单数形式：使（某人）困惑，使（某人）迷惑或头脑混乱，无法理解或分辨；混淆，弄混，把不同的人或事物误认为另一个；使（问题、局面等）复杂化，变得难以理解。

e.en: A critic is a person who writes about and expresses opinions about things such as books, movies, music, or art.

ex.en: Mather was a film critic for many years.
ex.zh: 马瑟做过多年的电影评论家。

e.en: Someone who is a critic of a person or system disapproves of them and criticizes them publicly.

ex.en: The newspaper has been one of the most consistent critics ever of the government.
ex.zh: 该报纸是政府最坚持的批评者之一。

d: n. 批评家，评论员；批评者，反对……的人
n. 创造力，独创性
adj. deep 的比较级：更深的；更深刻的，更深入的
adv. deep 的比较级：更深；更深入地，更深刻地

e.en: Decided means clear and definite.

ex.en: They got involved in a long and exhausting struggle and were at a decided disadvantage in the afternoon.
ex.zh: 他们卷入了一场长时间的令人疲惫的斗争，下午他们处于明显的劣势。

d: adj. 明显的，明白无误的；观点鲜明的，坚决的；（案件）判决了的
v. 决定，选定；影响（或决定）……的结果；裁决，判决（decide 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

ex.en: Bolivia returned to democratic rule in 1982, after a series of military governments.
ex.zh: 玻利维亚经历了一系列军事政府统治后于1982年恢复了民主统治。

e.en: 民主地

ex.en: That June, Yeltsin became Russia's first democratically elected president.
ex.zh: 那年6月，叶利钦成为俄罗斯第一位通过民主选举产生的总统。

e.en: Something that is democratic is based on the idea that everyone should have equal rights and should be involved in making important decisions.

ex.en: Education is the basis of a democratic society.
ex.zh: 教育是民主社会的基础。

e.en: 民主精神地

ex.en: This committee will enable decisions to be made democratically.
ex.zh: 这个委员会将保证决策是民主地产生的。

d: adj. 平等的，有民主精神的；民主政体的；（美国）民主党的

e.en: Defence is action that is taken to protect someone or something against attack. 保护;

ex.en: The land was flat, giving no scope for defence.
ex.zh: 土地非常平坦，无法做防卫之用。

e.en: Defence is the organization of a country's armies and weapons, and their use to protect the country or its interests.

ex.en: Twenty-eight percent of the federal budget is spent on defence.
ex.zh: 百分之二十八的联邦预算用于国防。

ex.en: ...the Ministry of Defence.
ex.zh: ...国防部。

e.en: The defences of a country or region are all its armed forces and weapons.

ex.en: He emphasized the need to maintain Britain's defences at a level sufficient to deal with the unexpected.
ex.zh: 他强调需要将英国的防卫力量维持在足以应付突发事件的水平。

e.en: A defence is something that people or animals can use or do to protect themselves.

ex.en: Despite anything the science of medicine may have achieved, the immune system is our main defence against disease.
ex.zh: 不管医疗科学已取得了什么样的进步，免疫系统仍是我们抵抗疾病的主要防御手段。

d: n. 防御，防御物；国防；辩护，答辩；辩方，辩护律师；防守队员，后卫；卫冕
v. 防御，防守

e.en: A draft is an early version of a letter, book, or speech. 草稿;

ex.en: I rewrote his rough draft, which was published under my name.
ex.zh: 我改写了他那篇以我的名义发表了的初稿。

ex.en: I faxed a first draft of this article to him.
ex.zh: 我把这篇文章的初稿传真给他。

e.en: A draft is a written order for payment of money by a bank, especially from one bank to another.

ex.en: Payments must be made in U.S. dollars by a bank draft drawn to the order of the United Nations Postal Administration.
ex.zh: 付款必须用开给联合国邮政管理处的银行汇票，并以美元支付。

e.en: A draft is a current of air that comes into a place in an undesirable way. (钻进某处的)

ex.en: Block drafts around doors and windows.
ex.zh: 挡住门窗周围的风。

e.en: When you draft a letter, book, or speech, you write the first version of it.

ex.en: He drafted a letter to the editors.
ex.zh: 他草拟了一封给编辑的信。

d: n. 草稿，草案；汇票；通风气流，穿堂风（=draught）；征兵；（职业球队的）选拔队员制
v. 起草，草拟；选派，派遣；征召，征召……入伍；挑选，选拔（运动员）；作草图，绘样
adj. （动物）驮重物的，负重的；（啤酒）散装的；草拟的

e.en: If someone or something disrupts an event, system, or process, they cause difficulties that prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way. 妨碍;

ex.en: Anti-war protesters disrupted the debate.
ex.zh: 反战示威者们扰乱了辩论。

d: v. 中断，扰乱（disrupt 的现在分词／动名词）

e.en: Educational matters or institutions are concerned with or relate to education.

ex.en: ...the Japanese educational system.
ex.zh: …日本教育体制。

e.en: An educational experience teaches you something.

ex.en: The staff should make sure the kids have an enjoyable and educational day.
ex.zh: 教职员要确保孩子们度过愉快的、有教育意义的一天。

d: adj. 教育的；有教育意义的

e.en: The effect of one thing on another is the change that the first thing causes in the second thing.

ex.en: Parents worry about the effect of music on their adolescent's behaviour.
ex.zh: 家长们担心音乐对于其青少年子女行为的影响。

e.en: An effect is an impression that someone creates deliberately, for example in a place or in a piece of writing.

ex.en: The whole effect is cool, light, and airy.
ex.zh: 整体印象是凉爽、明亮和通风。

e.en: A person's effects are the things that they have with them at a particular time, for example when they are arrested or admitted to a hospital, or the things that they owned when they died.

ex.en: His daughters were collecting his effects.
ex.zh: 他的女儿们正在收集他的个人物品。

e.en: The effects in a film are the specially created sounds and scenery. (影片中音响或布景的)

ex.en: It's got a gripping story, great acting, superb sets, and stunning effects.
ex.zh: 电影有扣人心弦的故事情节、精湛的表演、绝妙的布景和惊人的特效。

d: n. 影响，效果，结果；个人财物，随身物品，所有物（effect 的复数）；（影视等的）特殊效果，特效
v. 引起，使发生，实现（effect 的第三人称单数）

e.en: When people elect someone, they choose that person to represent them, by voting for them.

ex.en: The people of the Philippines have voted to elect a new president.
ex.zh: 菲律宾人民已经投票选举出一位新总统。

ex.en: The University of Washington elected him dean in 1956.
ex.zh: 华盛顿大学在1956年选他为院长。

e.en: If you elect to do something, you choose to do it.

ex.en: Those electing to smoke will be seated at the rear.
ex.zh: 选择抽烟的人将坐在后面。

e.en: Elect is added after words such as "president" or "governor" to indicate that a person has been elected to the post but has not officially started to carry out the duties involved.

ex.en: ...the date when the president-elect takes office.
ex.zh: …总统当选人的就职日。

d: adj. 当选的，由选举产生的
v. 选举，推选；决定做……，选择做……（elect 的过去式和过去分词，常接不定式）
n. 埃伦（可溶性显影剂粉末）
n. （Elon）人名；（英、以）埃隆

e.en: Energy is the ability and strength to do active physical things and the feeling that you are full of physical power and life.

ex.en: He was saving his energy for next week's race in Tuscon.
ex.zh: 他正为下周在特斯康举行的比赛养精蓄锐。

e.en: Energy is determination and enthusiasm about doing things.

ex.en: You have drive and energy for those things you are interested in.
ex.zh: 你对那些你感兴趣的事情有动力、有干劲。

e.en: Your energies are the efforts and attention that you can direct toward a particular aim.

ex.en: She had started to devote her energies to teaching rather than performing.
ex.zh: 她已经开始将精力投入到教学而不是表演中。

e.en: Energy is the power from sources such as electricity and coal that makes machines work or provides heat.

ex.en: ...those who favour nuclear energy.
ex.zh: …那些拥护核能的人们。

d: n. 能力，力气；精力，活力；能源；能，能量

e.en: An emergency is an unexpected and difficult or dangerous situation, especially an accident, that happens suddenly and that requires quick action to deal with it. 突发事件;

ex.en: He deals with emergencies promptly.
ex.zh: 他迅速地应对突发事件。

e.en: An emergency action is one that is done or arranged quickly and not in the normal way, because an emergency has occurred.

ex.en: Yesterday, the centre's board held an emergency meeting.
ex.zh: 昨天，中心的董事会召开了一次紧急会议。

e.en: Emergency equipment or supplies are those intended for use in an emergency.

ex.en: The plane is carrying emergency supplies for refugees.
ex.zh: 这架飞机载着给难民的应急物资。

d: n. 突发事件，紧急情况；急症病人，急诊病人；（医院的）急诊室
adj. 紧急情况下的；应急的

e.en: Erosion is the gradual destruction and removal of rock or soil in a particular area by rivers, the sea, or the weather.

ex.en: ...erosion of the river valleys.
ex.zh: …河谷的侵蚀。

e.en: The erosion of a person's authority, rights, or confidence is the gradual destruction or removal of them.

ex.en: ...the erosion of confidence in world financial markets.
ex.zh: …对世界金融市场信心的削弱。

e.en: The erosion of support, values, or money is a gradual decrease in its level or standard.

ex.en: ...the erosion of moral standards.
ex.zh: …道德水准的逐渐降低。

d: n. 侵蚀，腐蚀；削弱，降低；糜烂

e.en: An event is something that happens, especially when it is unusual or important. You can use events to describe all the things that are happening in a particular situation. (尤指特殊、重大)

ex.en: A new inquiry into the events of the day was opened in 2002.
ex.zh: 对那天发生的事件的新一轮调查于2002年开始。

e.en: An event is a planned and organized occasion, for example a social gathering or a sports tournament. (有计划、有组织的)

ex.en: ...major sporting events.
ex.zh: …重大体育赛事。

e.en: An event is one of the races or competitions that are part of an organized occasion such as a sports tournament.

ex.en: The main events start at 1 p.m.
ex.zh: 主赛项目下午1点开始。

e.en: You use in the event of, in the event that, and in that event when you are talking about a possible future situation, especially when you are planning what to do if it occurs.

ex.en: The bank has agreed to give an immediate refund in the unlikely event of an error being made.
ex.zh: 银行已同意倘若出现不太可能的错误便立即退款。

d: n. 事件，大事；社交场合，既定活动；赛事，比赛项目；结果

e.en: If something or someone is floating in a liquid, they are in the liquid, on or just below the surface, and are being supported by it. You can also float something on a liquid.

ex.en: They noticed fifty and twenty dollar bills floating in the water.
ex.zh: 他们注意到水中漂浮着一些50和20美元的纸币。

ex.en: It's below freezing and small icebergs are floating by.
ex.zh: 气温在冰点以下，一座座小冰山正漂过。

e.en: Something that floats lies on or just below the surface of a liquid when it is put in it and does not sink. (在水面或水中)

ex.en: They will also float if you drop them in the water.
ex.zh: 如果你把它们丢进水里，它们也会浮起来。

e.en: Something that floats in or through the air hangs in it or moves slowly and gently through it. (在空中)

ex.en: The white cloud of smoke floated away.
ex.zh: 那团白色的烟雾飘走了。

e.en: If you float a project, plan, or idea, you suggest it for others to think about.

ex.en: The French had floated the idea of placing the diplomatic work in the hands of the UN.
ex.zh: 法国人提出了将外交工作交由联合国处理的意见。

d: v. float 的过去式和过去分词：（使）漂浮，飘浮；发行（股票），使（公司）上市；使（货币）自由浮动；提出（想法、计划等），散布
adj. 悬浮的，浮动的（多用于技术语境，常作定语）

e.en: A form of something is a type or kind of it.

ex.en: He contracted a rare form of cancer.
ex.zh: 他患上了一种罕见的癌症。

ex.en: I am against hunting in any form.
ex.zh: 我反对任何形式的狩猎。

e.en: When something can exist or happen in several possible ways, you can use form to refer to one particular way in which it exists or happens.

ex.en: They received a benefit in the form of a tax reduction.
ex.zh: 他们以减税的方式获得了收益。

e.en: The form of something is its shape.

ex.en: ...the form of the body.
ex.zh: …体型。

e.en: You can refer to something that you can see as a form if you cannot see it clearly, or if its outline is the clearest or most striking aspect of it.

ex.en: His form lay still under the blankets.
ex.zh: 他的身形一动不动地躺在毯子下面。

d: adj. 成形的；形成的；定型的
v. 构成；形成；创立；使成形；制作（form 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If there is friction between people, there is disagreement and argument between them. (人与人之间的)

ex.en: Sara sensed that there had been friction between her children.
ex.zh: 萨拉感觉到她的孩子们中间出现了摩擦。

e.en: Friction is the force that makes it difficult for things to move freely when they are touching each other.

ex.en: The pistons are graphite-coated to reduce friction.
ex.zh: 活塞表面涂有石墨以减少摩擦。

d: n. 不和，分歧；摩擦；摩擦力

e.en: Geopolitical means relating to or concerned with geopolitics.

ex.en: Early resolution of geopolitical issues would be beneficial.
ex.zh: 尽早解决地缘政治学议题是有益的。

d: adj. （通常作定语）地缘政治的，地理政治学的

e.en: Geography is the study of the countries of the world and of such things as the land, seas, climate, towns, and population.
The geography of a place is the way that features such as rivers, mountains, towns, or streets are arranged within it.

ex.en: ...policemen who knew the local geography.
ex.zh: …了解当地地形的警察们。

d: n. 地理，地理学；地形，地貌；地理环境

e.en: Something that is described as giant is much larger or more important than most others of its kind. 巨大的;

ex.en: ...America's giant car maker, General Motors.
ex.zh: …美国的汽车制造巨头——通用汽车公司。

ex.en: ...a giant oak table.
ex.zh: …一张巨大的栎木桌。

e.en: Giant is often used to refer to any large, successful business organization or country. 大企业;

ex.en: ...Japanese electronics giant, Sony.
ex.zh: …日本的电子业巨头——索尼公司。

e.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. (尤指古老故事中虚构的)

ex.en: ...a Nordic saga of giants.
ex.zh: …一部关于巨人的北欧传奇。

d: n. 巨人（giant 的复数形式）；巨人族（希腊神话中常与天上诸神作战的种族）；癸干忒斯

e.en: in Germany Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung; a limited company (德语)

d: abbr. 股份有限公司（Gesellschaft mit beschrankter Haftung）

e.en: A governing body or organization is one which controls a particular activity. 治理的;

ex.en: The league became the governing body for amateur fencing in the U.S.
ex.zh: 此联盟成为了美国业余击剑运动的管理机构。

d: adj. 统治的，执政的；管理的，治理的，控制的
v. 统治；支配；控制；影响；抑制（情绪）；成为……的法律（govern 的现在分词）

e.en: A harbour is an area of the sea at the coast which is partly enclosed by land or strong walls, so that boats can be left there safely.

ex.en: She led us to a room with a balcony overlooking the harbour.
ex.zh: 她领我们到一个房间，房间带一个俯瞰港口的阳台。

e.en: If you harbour an emotion, thought, or secret, you have it in your mind over a long period of time.

ex.en: He might have been murdered by a former client or someone harbouring a grudge.
ex.zh: 他可能是被一个前委托人或某个怀有积怨的人谋杀了。

e.en: If a person or country harbours someone who is wanted by the police, they let them stay in their house or country and offer them protection.

ex.en: Accusations of harbouring suspects were raised against the former Hungarian leadership.
ex.zh: 匈牙利前领导人被指控窝藏疑犯。

d: n. 港口；避难所，避风港
v. 窝藏，庇护；心怀（想法、感受等）；带有（某种疾病）的病菌；为……提供住所（或动物栖息地）
【名】 （Harbour）（英、美、加拿大）哈伯（人名）

e.en: The headquarters of an organization are its main offices.

ex.en: ...fraud squad officers from Chicago's police headquarters.
ex.zh: …来自芝加哥警察局总部的诈骗侦查组的警官们。

d: n. 总部，总公司；司令部，指挥部

e.en: Your head is the top part of your body, which has your eyes, mouth, and brain in it.

ex.en: She turned her head away from him.
ex.zh: 她扭过头，不看他。

e.en: You can use head to refer to your mind and your mental abilities.

ex.en: ...an exceptional analyst who could do complex maths in his head.
ex.zh: …一位能做复杂心算的杰出分析家。

e.en: The head of a line of people or vehicles is the front of it, or the first person or vehicle in the line. (人群或车辆的)

ex.en: He made his way to the head of the line.
ex.zh: 他来到队伍的最前端。

e.en: The head of a company or organization is the person in charge of it and in charge of the people in it. (公司、团体的)

ex.en: Heads of government from more than 100 countries gather in Geneva tomorrow.
ex.zh: 来自一百多个国家的政府首脑明天将聚集在日内瓦。

d: n. 头；头脑，智力；顶部；排头；领导人，负责人；校长，院长；人数，（动物的）头数；（植物的）叶球，头状花序；一头长，一头高；钉头，锤头；啤酒沫；（河流）源头；脓头；硬币正面（有人头像）；磁头；（短语的）中心词，主导词；水压，蒸汽压力；紧要关头；桌子的上首座位，床头；头痛；蓄水高度，水头
v. 朝（某方向）行进；领导，主管；居……之首；加标题；用头顶（球）；形成……的头或顶部；砍（植物或树木的）枝；（莴苣，卷心菜）结球，长成球状；发源
adj. 领头的，负责的；头的；在顶端的；从前方来的
adv. （硬币）有头像的一面朝上（heads）

e.en: A helping of food is the amount of it that you get in a single serving. (食物的)

ex.en: She gave them extra helpings of ice cream.
ex.zh: 她额外给了他们几份冰激淋。

e.en: You can refer to an amount of something, especially a quality, as a helping of that thing. 一些(品质、特性等);

ex.en: There are large helpings of escapism in these movies.
ex.zh: 这些电影中有大量逃避现实主义的表现。

d: n. （食物的）一份，一客；（尤指品质、特性等的）一定量，一些
v. help 的现在分词/动名词：帮助，援助；有助于；搀扶，带领；给（人）拿（食物等）；私自拿走，窃取；无法避免，忍不住；减轻（疾病的）症状

e.en: When you are talking about a crime or something wrong that has been done, you can refer to the person who did it as the culprit. 犯罪者;

ex.en: All the men were being deported even though the real culprits in the fight have not been identified.
ex.zh: 尽管那次斗殴事件的真凶未被确认，但那些男人都在被驱逐出境。

e.en: When you are talking about a problem or bad situation, you can refer to its cause as the culprit. (造成问题或麻烦的)

ex.en: About 10% of Japanese teenagers are overweight. Nutritionists say the main culprit is increasing reliance on Western fast food.
ex.zh: 约10%的日本青少年都超重。营养学家们称主要的原因是他们越来越依赖西方快餐。

d: n. 罪犯，过失者；问题的起因
adv. 完全地，彻底地

e.en: a depression in the ground surface, esp in limestone, where a surface stream disappears underground 落水洞; 尤指石灰石地面下陷，地表水消失于地下 (Also called (esp Brit) swallow hole)

d: 污水池

e.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

ex.en: Try to estimate how many steps it will take to get to a close object.
ex.zh: 估计一下需要多少步才能到达一个近距目标。

ex.en: I estimate that total cost for treatment will go from $9,000 to $12,500.
ex.zh: 我估计治疗费总额将在9千美元到1.25万美元之间。

e.en: 估计的

ex.en: There are an estimated 90,000 gangsters in the country.
ex.zh: 这个国家估计有9万名歹徒。

e.en: An estimate is an approximate calculation of a quantity or value.

ex.en: ...the official estimate of the election result.
ex.zh: …选举结果的官方估计。

e.en: An estimate is a judgment about a person or situation that you make based on the available evidence.

ex.en: I hadn't been far wrong in my estimate of his grandson's capabilities.
ex.zh: 我对他孙子能力的判断没有太离谱。

d: adj.  估计的，预计的
v. 估计，估算；判断，评价（estimate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A university is an institution where students study for degrees and where academic research is done.

ex.en: Offenbacker earned an education degree at the University of Washington and taught elementary school.
ex.zh: 奥芬巴克在华盛顿大学获得了教育学位，教了小学。

ex.en: She goes to Duke University.
ex.zh: 她上杜克大学。

d: n. 大学，综合性大学；大学校舍

e.en: Mine is the first person singular possessive pronoun. A speaker or writer uses mine to refer to something that belongs or relates to himself or herself.

ex.en: Her right hand is inches from mine.
ex.zh: 她的右手离我的几英寸远。

ex.en: That wasn't his fault, it was mine.
ex.zh: 那不是他的错，是我的错。

e.en: A mine is a place where deep holes and tunnels are dug under the ground in order to obtain a mineral such as coal, diamonds, or gold.

ex.en: ...coal mines.
ex.zh: …煤矿。

e.en: a lucrative source or abundant supply 摇钱树 ;

ex.en: she was a mine of information

e.en: When a mineral such as coal, diamonds, or gold is mined, it is obtained from the ground by digging deep holes and tunnels.

ex.en: The pit is being shut down because it no longer has enough coal that can be mined economically.
ex.zh: 那个煤矿要关闭了，因为储量不足，难以经济开采。

d: v. （动词 mine 的过去式和过去分词）开采，采掘；布雷；挖掘、搜集（数据、信息）
adj. 被开采的，已开采出来的；布有雷的，被布雷的

e.en: Someone who is old has lived for many years and is no longer young.

ex.en: ...a white-haired old man.
ex.zh: …一位白发老人。

e.en: The old are people who are old.

ex.en: ...providing a caring response for the needs of the old and the handicapped.
ex.zh: …对老年人和残疾人的需要做出一个充满关怀的回应。

e.en: You use old to talk about how many days, weeks, months, or years someone or something has lived or existed. …岁的; …

ex.en: He was abandoned by his father when he was three months old.
ex.zh: 他3个月大的时候被父亲遗弃了。

ex.en: How old are you now?
ex.zh: 你现在多大了？

e.en: Something that is old has existed for a long time.

ex.en: She loved the big old house.
ex.zh: 她喜爱那座古老的大房子。

ex.en: These books must be very old.
ex.zh: 这些书一定年头很久了。

d: adj. （人）……岁的，（事物）存在……久的；年老的，年纪大的；衰老的；古老的，历史悠久的；陈旧的；过去的，从前的；原来（属于自己的）的；结识久的；（表示亲昵）老……；（语言形式）古的，早期的；老派的，守旧的；老一套的，经历多次的
n. 老年人；某个年龄段的人；古时
【名】 （Old）（英）奥尔德（人名）
n. （打扮成 Robin Hood 等传奇人物跳的）莫理斯舞；（常大写 Morris）人名，英语姓氏及男子名，莫里斯

e.en: A politician is a person whose job is in politics, especially a member of the government. 政客 (尤指政府成员);

ex.en: They have arrested a number of leading opposition politicians.
ex.zh: 他们已经逮捕了一些主要的反对党政治家。

d: n. 政治家，政界人士，从政者（politician 的复数形式）；政客，玩弄权术者

e.en: A professor in an American or Canadian university or college is a teacher of the highest rank. (美国大学的)

ex.en: Robert Dunn is a professor of economics at George Washington University.
ex.zh: 罗伯特·邓恩是乔治·华盛顿大学的经济学教授。

e.en: A professor in a British university is the most senior teacher in a department. (英国大学的)

ex.en: ...Professor Cameron.
ex.zh: …卡梅伦主任。

d: n. 教授；（大学的）讲师，教员；信仰表示者，宣称信仰者

e.en: If you say that an idea or situation is far removed from something, you mean that it is very different from it.

ex.en: Central office was too far removed from operating decisions at the department level.
ex.zh: 总部办公室与部门级别对运行的决策大相径庭。

d: adj. （亲属关系）隔代的，隔辈的；不同的；（时间或空间上）遥远的；（对某一课题、问题、情况等）知之甚少的
