v. 移开，拿开；除去，废除；把……免职，开除（remove 的过去式和过去分词）
n.  研究人员

e.en: When you seal an envelope, you close it by folding part of it over and sticking it down, so that it cannot be opened without being torn. 封 (信封)

ex.en: He sealed the envelope and put on a stamp.
ex.zh: 他封好信封，贴了张邮票。

ex.en: Write your letter and seal it in a blank envelope.
ex.zh: 写好你的信，然后将其封入一个空信封。

e.en: If you seal a container or an opening, you cover it with something in order to prevent air, liquid, or other material from getting in or out. If you seal something in a container, you put it inside and then close the container tightly. 封 (容器、开口); 将 (某物) 封入 (某容器中)

ex.en: She filled the containers, sealed them with a cork, and stuck on labels.
ex.zh: 她装满那些容器，用塞子封了口，然后贴上了标签。

ex.en: A woman picks them up and seals them in plastic bags.
ex.zh: 一位女士拣起它们，然后把它们封入各塑料袋中。

e.en: The seal on a container or opening is the part where it has been sealed. (容器、开口等)

ex.en: When assembling the pie, wet the edges where the two crusts join, to form a seal.
ex.zh: 捏合馅饼时，弄湿两块面皮封合的边缘，以形成一个封口。

e.en: A seal is a device or a piece of material, for example, in a machine, which closes an opening tightly so that air, liquid, or other substances cannot get in or out. (机器上防止气体或液体渗入或露出的)

ex.en: Check seals on fridges and freezers regularly.
ex.zh: 定期检查冰箱和冰柜的密封装置。

d: n. 印章，图章；表示确认的事物；密封装置，密封物；密封，密封状态；水止，水封（根据排污管道深度U形管中防止臭气上升的存水）；封蜡，火漆；封蜡模（印），封铅模（印）；海豹；海豹皮；装饰性的背面涂胶水的邮票（印花）；（美国海军）海豹特种部队士兵（SEAL）
v. 封上（信封）；密封（容器）；确定，使成定局；给……涂上保护层；（给文件）加封，盖印；封锁；（为避免烹调时失去过多水分，将食物放在热油中）快速煎炸；猎捕海豹
【名】  （Seal）西尔（人名）

e.en: A section of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

ex.en: He said it was wrong to single out any section of society for AIDS testing.
ex.zh: 他说挑出社会任何一部份人做艾滋病检查都是错误的。

ex.en: ...the Georgetown section of Washington, D.C.
ex.zh: …华盛顿特区的乔治敦区。

e.en: If something is sectioned, it is divided into sections. 分 (成若干部分)

ex.en: It holds vegetables in place while they are being peeled or sectioned.
ex.zh: 它在蔬菜被去皮或切分时将他们固定。

e.en: A section is a diagram of something such as a building or a part of the body. It shows how the object would appear to you if it were cut from top to bottom and looked at from the side.

ex.en: For some buildings a vertical section is more informative than a plan.
ex.zh: 对一些建筑物来说，垂直剖面图比平面图提供的信息更多。

d: n. 部分；散件，部件；（书、报等的）节，栏；一部分人；（乐队的）组；断面图，剖面图；（手术中的）开刀，切开；（供显微镜下观察的）切片；（柑橘类水果的）一瓣；（法律文件的）款，项；地段，区域；部门，科； 建房用地；（生物）组（尤指亚属）； 一平方英里的土地
v.   强制（精神病人）入院；将……制成切片；切开，切断；分开，给……分区

e.en: If people agree with each other about something, they have the same opinion about it or say that they have the same opinion.

ex.en: Both have agreed on the need for the money.
ex.zh: 双方都同意需要那笔钱。

ex.en: So we both agree there's a problem?
ex.zh: 那么我们两个人都同意是有一个问题啦？

e.en: If people agree on something, they all decide to accept or do something.

ex.en: The warring sides have agreed on an unconditional ceasefire.
ex.zh: 交战各方已经对无条件停火达成了一致意见。

e.en: In grammar, if a word agrees with a noun or pronoun, it has a form that is appropriate to the number or gender of the noun or pronoun. For example, in "He hates it," the singular verb agrees with the singular pronoun "he."
If you agree to do something, you say that you will do it. If you agree to a proposal, you accept it. 答应;

ex.en: He agreed to pay me for the drawings.
ex.zh: 她答应为这些画付给我钱。

d: v. 同意，赞成；答应，接受；达成一致意见；商定，约定；相符，吻合；赞同；（语法）呼应；批准，认可（计划、要求等）；适合（某人）

e.en: An animal is a living creature such as a dog, lion, or rabbit, rather than a bird, fish, insect, or human being. 动物 (不包括鸟类、鱼类、昆虫和人类)

ex.en: He was attacked by wild animals.
ex.zh: 他被野兽袭击了。

e.en: Any living creature other than a human being can be referred to as an animal. 兽类; 动物 (不包括人类)

ex.en: Language is something that fundamentally distinguishes humans from animals.
ex.zh: 语言是从根本上把人类与动物区分开的事物。

e.en: Any living creature, including a human being, can be referred to as an animal. (包括人类在内的)

ex.en: Watch any young human being, or any other young animal.
ex.zh: 观察任意一个年少的人，或者任意其他幼小的动物。

e.en: Animal products come from animals rather than from plants.

ex.en: ...food high in animal fats such as red meat and dairy products.
ex.zh: …富含动物脂肪的食物，如红色肉类和奶制品。

d: n. 动物；兽类；衣冠禽兽，畜牲；某一类人或物
adj. 动物的；肉体的，肉欲的；取自动物的；（胚胎）动物极的

e.en: Anthropology is the scientific study of people, society, and culture.
人类学家

ex.en: ...an anthropologist who had been in China for three years.
ex.zh: …一位在中国呆过3年的人类学家。

d: n.  人类学

e.en: A bench is a long seat of wood or metal that two or more people can sit on.

ex.en: He sat down on a park bench.
ex.zh: 他在一条公园的长凳上坐下来。

e.en: A bench is a long, narrow table in a factory or laboratory. (工厂、实验室的)

ex.en: ...the laboratory bench.
ex.zh: …实验室工作台。

e.en: In a court of law, the bench is the judge or magistrates.

ex.en: The chairman of the bench adjourned the case until October 27.
ex.zh: 首席法官将该案延至到10月27日。

d: n. 长凳，长椅；长方形工作台；法官席（the bench）； 议员席；替补席；（砖石建筑的）壁架，（斜坡上的）平台
v. 把（场上队员）换下；（在展览会上）展览（狗）；仰卧推举；给……以席位；为……设置条凳
【名】 （Bench）（英）本奇，（德）本希，（丹）本克（人名）

e.en: Arteries are the tubes in your body that carry blood from your heart to the rest of your body. Compare .

ex.en: ...patients suffering from blocked arteries.
ex.zh: …患动脉堵塞的病人们。

e.en: You can refer to an important main route within a complex road, railway, or river system as an artery.

ex.en: ...Connecticut Ave., one of the main arteries of Washington.
ex.zh: …康涅狄格大道，华盛顿的主干道之一。

d: n. 动脉；干线，干道，干流
adj. 最大的（big 的最高级）
v. blame 的过去式和过去分词：责备，谴责；归咎于
adj. 混蛋的，该死的（damned 的委婉说法，非正式）

e.en: If something is blocked or blocked up, it is completely closed so that nothing can get through it. 封锁的; 闭塞的;

ex.en: The main drain was blocked.
ex.zh: 主下水道被堵住了。

ex.en: His arteries were blocked up again, requiring him to undergo repeat surgery.
ex.zh: 他的动脉再次栓塞，需要再做一次同样的外科手术。

d: adj. 封锁的，闭塞的， 堵住的
v.  阻塞，堵塞（道路、管道等）；遮住（视线）；封锁，挡住（去路）（block 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Your body is all your physical parts, including your head, arms, and legs.

ex.en: The largest organ in the body is the liver.
ex.zh: 体内最大的器官是肝脏。

e.en: You can also refer to the main part of your body, except for your arms, head, and legs, as your body.

ex.en: Lying flat on the floor, twist your body on to one hip and cross your upper leg over your body.
ex.zh: 平躺在地板上，躯干扭向胯一侧，将上边的腿跨过躯干。

e.en: You can refer to a person's dead body as a body.

ex.en: Officials said they had found no traces of violence on the body of the politician.
ex.zh: 官方说他们在这位政治家的尸体上没有发现任何暴力痕迹。

e.en: A body is an organized group of people who deal with something officially. 团体;

ex.en: She was elected student body president at the University of North Carolina.
ex.zh: 她当选为北卡罗莱纳大学学生社团主席。

d: n. （人或动物的）身体，躯体；尸体；团体，机构，组织；（文章、文件、车辆、建筑物等的）主体，正文，主要部分；物体（尤指天体、水体等）

e.en: the sport of climbing in and exploring caves
e.zh: 一种登高及探索岩洞的体育运动

d: n. 洞穴探险；（地质、采矿）崩落，塌落；崩落开采法（如 block caving）
v. 洞穴探险（用于 go caving）；塌陷，倒塌（cave 的现在分词）；屈服（cave in）；挖空，开凿

e.en: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen. 起因;

ex.en: Smoking is the biggest preventable cause of death and disease.
ex.zh: 吸烟是造成不必要疾病和死亡的最大原因。

e.en: A cause is an aim or principle which a group of people supports or is fighting for. 奋斗目标;

ex.en: Refusing to have one leader has not helped the cause.
ex.zh: 拒绝接受领导无益于该事业。

e.en: To cause something, usually something bad, means to make it happen.

ex.en: The insecticide used on some weeds can cause health problems.
ex.zh: 喷洒在野草上的杀虫剂会引发各种健康问题。

ex.en: This was a genuine mistake, but it did cause me some worry.
ex.zh: 这纯属失误，但它确实令我有些不安。

e.en: If you have cause for a particular feeling or action, you have good reasons for feeling it or doing it.

ex.en: Only a few people can find any cause for celebration.
ex.zh: 只有少数人能找到庆祝的理由。

d: n. 原因；事业；理由（cause 的复数）
v. 引起（cause 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.

ex.en: At one o'clock the rain had ceased.
ex.zh: 一点钟时雨已经停了。

e.en: If you cease to do something, you stop doing it. 停止; 不再 (做某事)

ex.en: He never ceases to amaze me.
ex.zh: 他总让我惊喜不断。

ex.en: The secrecy about the president's condition had ceased to matter.
ex.zh: 有关总统健康状况的秘密已经不再举足轻重了。

e.en: If you cease something, you stop it happening or working.

ex.en: The Tundra Times, a weekly newspaper in Alaska, ceased publication this week.
ex.zh: 阿拉斯加的周报——《苔原时报》于本周停刊。

d: v. 终止，结束
n. 停止

e.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He claimed that it was all a conspiracy against him.
ex.zh: 他声称这完全是一个针对他的阴谋。

ex.en: A man claiming to be a journalist threatened to reveal details about her private life.
ex.zh: 一个自称是记者的男人威胁要公开她的私生活细节。

e.en: If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth. 声称 (对某事负责或应得荣誉)

ex.en: An underground organization has claimed responsibility for the bomb explosion.
ex.zh: 一个地下组织已声称对炸弹爆炸事件负责。

e.en: If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.

ex.en: Now they are returning to claim what was theirs.
ex.zh: 现在他们回来索要原本属于他们的东西。

e.en: If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.

ex.en: Zhuang claimed the record in 54.64 seconds.
ex.zh: 庄创造了54.64秒的纪录。

d: v. 声称，宣称，断言（claim 的过去式和过去分词）；要求，索取，认领，索赔

e.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He claimed that it was all a conspiracy against him.
ex.zh: 他声称这完全是一个针对他的阴谋。

ex.en: A man claiming to be a journalist threatened to reveal details about her private life.
ex.zh: 一个自称是记者的男人威胁要公开她的私生活细节。

e.en: If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth. 声称 (对某事负责或应得荣誉)

ex.en: An underground organization has claimed responsibility for the bomb explosion.
ex.zh: 一个地下组织已声称对炸弹爆炸事件负责。

e.en: If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.

ex.en: Now they are returning to claim what was theirs.
ex.zh: 现在他们回来索要原本属于他们的东西。

e.en: If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.

ex.en: Zhuang claimed the record in 54.64 seconds.
ex.zh: 庄创造了54.64秒的纪录。

d: n. 声称，说法；要求，请求权；索赔；债权；（法）权利要求（claim 的复数形式）
v. 要求，索取，申领，索赔；声称，主张（claim 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

ex.en: A section of the Bay Bridge had collapsed.
ex.zh: 海湾大桥有一部分坍塌了。

e.en: Collapse is also a noun.

ex.en: The governor called for an inquiry into the motorway's collapse.
ex.zh: 州长要求对高速公路的坍塌进行调查。

e.en: If something, for example a system or institution, collapses, it fails or comes to an end completely and suddenly. (系统或制度等) 崩溃;

ex.en: His business empire collapsed under a massive burden of debt.
ex.zh: 他的商业帝国由于债台高筑而瓦解。

e.en: Collapse is also a noun. (系统或制度等的) 崩溃;

ex.en: The coup's collapse has speeded up the drive to independence.
ex.zh: 那次政变的失败加速推动了独立进程。

d: v. 倒塌，塌下；崩溃，瓦解；突然倒下，昏倒；瘫倒；突然贬值，暴跌；萎陷，瘪掉；折叠
n. 倒塌，塌陷；突然失败，崩溃；病倒，垮掉；突然贬值，暴跌

e.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

ex.en: A section of the Bay Bridge had collapsed.
ex.zh: 海湾大桥有一部分坍塌了。

e.en: Collapse is also a noun.

ex.en: The governor called for an inquiry into the motorway's collapse.
ex.zh: 州长要求对高速公路的坍塌进行调查。

e.en: If something, for example a system or institution, collapses, it fails or comes to an end completely and suddenly. (系统或制度等) 崩溃;

ex.en: His business empire collapsed under a massive burden of debt.
ex.zh: 他的商业帝国由于债台高筑而瓦解。

e.en: Collapse is also a noun. (系统或制度等的) 崩溃;

ex.en: The coup's collapse has speeded up the drive to independence.
ex.zh: 那次政变的失败加速推动了独立进程。

d: adj. 倒塌的，坍塌的，塌陷的；（肺等组织）萎陷的；（系统、机构、计划等）崩溃的，瓦解的；（价格、市场、数值等）暴跌的；折叠的，收拢的，收缩的
v. collapse 的过去式和过去分词：倒塌；崩溃；晕倒，倒下；价格暴跌

e.en: Control of an organization, place, or system is the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run. (对某组织机构的)

ex.en: The restructuring involves Mr. Ronson giving up control of the company.
ex.zh: 公司重组需要罗森先生放弃对公司的控制。

e.en: If something is under your control, you have the power to make all the important decisions about the way that it is run.

ex.en: All the newspapers are under government control.
ex.zh: 所有的报纸都处在政府控制之下。

e.en: If you are in control of something, you have the power to make all the important decisions about the way it is run.

ex.en: Nobody knows who is in control of the club.
ex.zh: 没有人知道谁掌管这个俱乐部。

e.en: If you have control of something or someone, you are able to make them do what you want them to do. (对某物或某人的)

ex.en: He lost control of his car.
ex.zh: 他失去了对他的车的控制。

d: adj. 限制的，控制的；受法律制约的，受规则限制的；保持冷静的，克制的
v. 控制，掌管；限制，限定；阻止蔓延（或恶化）（control 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

ex.en: The Rough Guide to Nepal is a comprehensive guide to the region.
ex.zh: 《尼泊尔概览》是介绍该地区的一本全面指南。

d: adj. 综合性的，全面的；有理解力的
n. 综合中学；专业综合测验

e.en: In many religions, creation is the making of the universe, earth, and creatures by God.

ex.en: ...the Creation of the universe as told in Genesis Chapter One.
ex.zh: …如《创世纪》第一章中讲述的上帝创造天地万物。

e.en: People sometimes refer to the whole universe as creation.

ex.en: The whole of creation is made up of energy.
ex.zh: 全宇宙是由能量构成的。

e.en: You can refer to something that someone has made as a creation, especially if it shows skill, imagination, or artistic ability.

ex.en: The bathroom is entirely my own creation.
ex.zh: 这个浴室完全是我个人的创作。

d: n. 创造，创建；作品，创作；（上帝）创造天地；宇宙，世界，天地万物；授予，册封

e.en: The cost of something is the amount of money that is needed in order to buy, do, or make it.

ex.en: The cost of a loaf of bread has increased five-fold.
ex.zh: 一块面包的价格已经涨了5倍。

ex.en: In 1989 the price of coffee fell so low that in many countries it did not even cover the cost of production.
ex.zh: 1989年咖啡的价格跌得那么低，以致在许多国家还抵不上其生产成本。

e.en: If something costs a particular amount of money, you can buy, do, or make it for that amount.

ex.en: This course is limited to 12 people and costs $150.
ex.zh: 这门课程限招12人，费用为$150。

ex.en: Painted walls look much more interesting and don't cost much.
ex.zh: 粉刷过的墙壁看上去更有趣，要价也不高。

e.en: When something that you plan to do or make is costed, the amount of money you need is calculated in advance.

ex.en: The building work has not been fully costed but runs into millions of dollars.
ex.zh: 建筑工作的费用还未完全估算出来，但要高达几百万美元。

e.en: If an event or mistake costs you something, you lose that thing as the result of it.

ex.en: ...a six-year-old boy whose life was saved by an operation that cost him his sight.
ex.zh: …一个通过手术保住生命但双目失明的6岁男孩。

d: n. 费用，成本；代价，损失；诉讼费（cost 的复数）
v. 花费，价格为；使损失（cost 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A crime is an illegal action or activity for which a person can be punished by law.

ex.en: He and Lieutenant Cassidy were checking the scene of the crime.
ex.zh: 当时他正与卡西迪中尉一起检查犯罪现场。

ex.en: ...the growing problem of organized crime.
ex.zh: …越来越严重的有组织犯罪问题。

e.en: If you say that doing something is a crime, you think it is very wrong or a serious mistake.

ex.en: It would be a crime to travel all the way to Australia and not stop in Sydney.
ex.zh: 如果千里迢迢去澳大利亚而不在悉尼停留，那就是大错特错。

d: n. 罪，罪行；犯罪，犯罪活动；可耻行为，错误
v. （尤指在军队里）指控……有罪，判……有罪

e.en: You use definitely to emphasize that something is the case, or to emphasize the strength of your intention or opinion.

ex.en: I'm definitely going to get in touch with these people.
ex.zh: 我一定要联系上这些人。

e.en: If something has been definitely decided, the decision will not be changed.

ex.en: She had definitely decided that she wanted to continue working with women in prison.
ex.zh: 她打定主意要继续与监狱里的女人一起工作。

d: adv. 肯定地，当然；明确地，确定地

e.en: A place or building that is derelict is empty and in a bad state of repair because it has not been used or lived in for a long time.

ex.en: Her body was found dumped in a derelict warehouse less than a mile from her home.
ex.zh: 她的尸体被发现丢在离她家不到一英里的一座废弃的仓库里。

e.en: A derelict is a person who has no home or job and who has to live on the streets. 无家可归者;

ex.en: I had never seen so many derelicts in one place.
ex.zh: 我从未在一个地方见到过这么多无家可归的人。

d: adj. （建筑物或土地）破旧的，弃置的；玩忽职守的，失职的
n. 无家可归者，流浪汉；废弃物（尤指废弃船只）；（因水位后退）逐渐变干的土地

e.en: If people or animals dig, they make a hole in the ground or in a pile of earth, stones, or rubbish.

ex.en: I grabbed the spade and started digging.
ex.zh: 我抓起铁锹开始挖了起来。

ex.en: Dig a large hole and drive the stake in first.
ex.zh: 先挖个大洞，把桩子打进去。

e.en: If you dig into something such as a deep container, you put your hand in it to search for something. 将手伸入… (以探寻某物)

ex.en: He dug into his coat pocket for his keys.
ex.zh: 他把手伸进大衣口袋里找钥匙。

e.en: If you dig one thing into another or if one thing digs into another, the first thing is pushed hard into the second, or presses hard into it. 刺入;

ex.en: She digs the serving spoon into the moussaka.
ex.zh: 她把分菜匙插进茄合里。

e.en: If you dig into a subject or a store of information, you study it very carefully in order to discover or check facts.

ex.en: ...as a special congressional enquiry digs deeper into the alleged financial misdeeds of his government.
ex.zh: …随着一项国会特别调查行动对其政府所谓的不当财政行为的深入调查。

ex.en: He has been digging into the local archives.
ex.zh: 他一直在仔细研究当地的档案。

d: n. 挖掘，采掘
v. 挖掘，发掘（dig 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you deliver something somewhere, you take it there.

ex.en: The Canadians plan to deliver more food to southern Somalia.
ex.zh: 加拿大人计划向索马里南部运送更多的食物。

e.en: If you deliver something that you have promised to do, make, or produce, you do, make, or produce it. 实现;

ex.en: They have yet to show that they can really deliver working technologies.
ex.zh: 他们仍需证明他们确实能够实现可用的技术。

ex.en: The question is, can he deliver?
ex.zh: 问题是他能履行吗？

e.en: If you deliver a lecture or speech, you give it in public.

ex.en: The president will deliver a speech about schools.
ex.zh: 校长将发表关于学校的演讲。

e.en: When someone delivers a baby, they help the woman who is giving birth to the baby. 给 (产妇)

ex.en: Although we'd planned to have our baby at home, we never expected to deliver her ourselves!
ex.zh: 尽管我们是打算在家生孩子，可我们从未想过要自己给她接生!

d: v. 投递，运送；履行，兑现；交付，移交；发表，宣布；接生，分娩（deliver 的过去式和过去分词）
v．去水，脱水：从物质中去除水分。

e.en: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

ex.en: The black car drove away from them and disappeared.
ex.zh: 黑色的小汽车驶离了他们便消失了。

e.en: If someone or something disappears, they go away or are taken away somewhere where nobody can find them.

ex.en: ...a Japanese woman who disappeared thirteen years ago.
ex.zh: …一位13年前失踪的日本妇女。

e.en: If something disappears, it stops existing or happening.

ex.en: The immediate threat of the past has disappeared and the security situation in Europe has significantly improved.
ex.zh: 过去的直接威胁不复存在了，欧洲的安全状况有重大改善。

d: adj. 消失的，消失了的
v. 消失，不见；失踪，丢失；不复存在，灭绝（disappear 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 被秘密逮捕（或处决）的人（常作 the disappeared）
adj. 含白云石的

e.en: When you drink a liquid, you take it into your mouth and swallow it.

ex.en: He drank his cup of tea.
ex.zh: 他喝了他那杯茶。

ex.en: He drank thirstily.
ex.zh: 他迫不及待地喝了。

e.en: To drink means to drink alcohol.

ex.en: By his own admission, he was smoking and drinking too much.
ex.zh: 他自己承认抽烟饮酒过度。

e.en: 喝酒

ex.en: She had left him because of his drinking.
ex.zh: 她离开了他，因为他酗酒。

e.en: A drink is an amount of a liquid which you drink. 一杯 (饮料)

ex.en: I'll get you a drink of water.
ex.zh: 我去给你弄杯水来。

d: v. 喝，饮；喝酒；饱览，欣赏；吸收（水分）
n. 饮料；一杯，一口，一份（饮料）；酒，酒精饮料；酒会，酒宴；一片水（the drink）

e.en: a state of melancholy or depression (esp in the phrase down in the dumps)

d: n. 废物，垃圾场（dump 的复数）；忧郁（常用于 down in the dumps）
v. 倾倒（dump 的第三人称单数形式）；倾销

e.en: An election is a process in which people vote to choose a person or group of people to hold an official position.

ex.en: ...Poland's first fully free elections for more than fifty years.
ex.zh: …五十多年来波兰首次完全自由选举。

ex.en: During his election campaign he promised to put the economy back on its feet.
ex.zh: 在竞选活动期间他承诺要重振经济。

e.en: The election of a particular person or group of people is their success in winning an election.

ex.en: ...the election of the Democrat candidate last year.
ex.zh: …去年民主党候选人的当选。

ex.en: ...Vaclav Havel's election as president of Czechoslovakia.
ex.zh: …瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔当选捷克斯洛伐克总统。

d: n. 选举；选举制；投票（election 的复数形式）
adv. 广阔地；广泛地；巨大地

e.en: To export products or raw materials means to sell them to another country.

ex.en: The nation also exports beef.
ex.zh: 该国也出口牛肉。

ex.en: They expect the antibiotic products to be exported to Southeast Asia and Africa.
ex.zh: 他们期望抗生素产品出口到东南亚和非洲。

e.en: Export is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the production and export of cheap casual wear.
ex.zh: …廉价休闲服的生产与出口。

ex.en: A lot of our land is used to grow crops for export.
ex.zh: 我们很多的土地用来种植出口作物。

e.en: Exports are goods sold to another country and sent there.

ex.en: Ghana's main export is cocoa.
ex.zh: 加纳的主要出口产品是可可。

e.en: To export something means to introduce it into another country or make it happen there.

ex.en: It has exported inflation at times.
ex.zh: 它有时将通货膨胀引入他国。

d: v. （贸易）出口，外销；输出（export 的过去式和过去分词）；（计算机）导出，输出
adj. 出口的，外销的；（计算机）导出的，输出的

e.en: Failure is a lack of success in doing or achieving something, especially in relation to a particular activity.

ex.en: This policy is doomed to failure.
ex.zh: 这项政策注定要失败。

ex.en: Three attempts on the 200-metre record ended in failure.
ex.zh: 3次向200米纪录的冲击以失败告终。

e.en: Your failure to do a particular thing is the fact that you do not do it, even though you were expected to do it.

ex.en: They see their failure to produce an heir as a curse from God.
ex.zh: 他们将自己未能生育一个后嗣看作是来自上帝的一个诅咒。

e.en: If something is a failure, it is not a success.

ex.en: The marriage was a failure and they both wanted to be free of it.
ex.zh: 这段婚姻是个失败，他们俩都想从中解放出来。

e.en: If you say that someone is a failure, you mean that they have not succeeded in a particular activity, or that they are unsuccessful at everything they do.

ex.en: Elgar received many honours and much acclaim and yet he often considered himself a failure.
ex.zh: 埃尔加获得了很多荣誉和欢呼，但是他常常把自己看成一个失败者。

d: n. 失败；失败的人（或企业、事物）；未做到；缺乏，不足；故障，衰退；公司倒闭；歉收；突然失去

e.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy. (思想、论据、理由等)荒谬的;

ex.en: Their main argument is fallacious.
ex.zh: 他们的主要论点是荒谬的。

d: adj. 谬误的，不合理的；骗人的，欺骗性的；靠不住的，渺茫的

e.en: A farm is an area of land, together with the buildings on it, that is used for growing crops or raising animals, usually in order to sell them.

ex.en: Farms in France are much smaller than those in the United States or even Britain.
ex.zh: 法国的农场比美国甚至英国的都小得多。

e.en: A mink farm or a fish farm, for example, is a place where a particular kind of animal or fish is bred and kept in large quantities in order to be sold.

ex.en: ...trout fresh from a local trout farm.
ex.zh: …来自当地一家鲑鱼养殖场的新鲜鲑鱼。

e.en: If you farm an area of land, you grow crops or keep animals on it. 耕种;

ex.en: They farmed some of the best land in the country.
ex.zh: 他们耕种着该国最好的一些土地。

ex.en: Bease has been farming for 30 years.
ex.zh: 比斯经营农场已有30年。

d: n. 农场，养殖场；农舍；生产企业
v. 耕种，养殖；（收取一定费用）将（税收）包出；承包，外包

e.en: If a bad or undesirable situation is your fault, you caused it or are responsible for it. 过错;

ex.en: There was no escaping the fact: it was all his fault.
ex.zh: 无法逃避这一事实：这都是他的错。

e.en: A fault is a mistake in what someone is doing or in what they have done.

ex.en: It is a big fault to think that you can learn how to manage people in business school.
ex.zh: 认为你能在商学院学会如何管理人是一大错误。

e.en: A fault in someone or something is a weakness in them or something that is not perfect.

ex.en: His manners had always made her blind to his faults.
ex.zh: 他的彬彬有礼总使她看不见他的缺点。

e.en: A fault is a large crack in the surface of the earth.

ex.en: ...the San Andreas Fault.
ex.zh: …圣安德烈亚斯断层。

d: n. 错误；责任，过错；缺点，故障；断层；发球失误
v. 挑剔，指责；发球失误；产生断层；犯错误，做错事

e.en: Food is what people and animals eat.

ex.en: Enjoy your food.
ex.zh: 用餐愉快。

ex.en: ...frozen foods.
ex.zh: …冷冻食品。

e.en: If you give someone food for thought, you make them think carefully about something.

ex.en: Her speech offers much food for thought.
ex.zh: 她的演讲有许多发人深思的内容。

d: n. （植物生长的）养料；食物，食品

e.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

ex.en: Best friends are the foundation of my life.
ex.zh: 良友们是我生活的基础。

ex.en: The issue strikes at the very foundation of our community.
ex.zh: 这个问题严重影响到我们社会的基础。

e.en: A foundation is an organization which provides money for a special purpose such as research or charity.

ex.en: ...the National Foundation for Educational Research.
ex.zh: …全国教育研究基金会。

e.en: The foundations of a building or other structure are the layer of bricks or concrete below the ground that it is built on.
If a story, idea, or argument has no foundation, there are no facts to prove that it is true.

ex.en: The allegations were without foundation.
ex.zh: 这些指控没有根据。

d: n. 地基，基础；基本原理，根据；基金会；建立，创办；（化妆打底用的）粉底霜

e.en: Formal speech or behaviour is very correct and serious rather than relaxed and friendly, and is used especially in official situations. 正式的 (演讲、行为)

ex.en: He wrote a very formal letter of apology to Douglas.
ex.zh: 他写了一封非常正式的道歉信给道格拉斯。

e.en: 正式地

ex.en: He took her back to Vincent Square in a taxi, saying goodnight formally on the doorstep.
ex.zh: 他打出租车将她送回文森特广场，在门阶上客气地道了晚安。

e.en: A formal action, statement, or request is an official one. 官方的; 正式的 (行为、陈述、要求等)

ex.en: UN officials said a formal request was passed to American authorities.
ex.zh: 联合国官员们称一份正式的要求已转给了美国当局。

ex.en: No formal announcement had been made.
ex.zh: 尚无官方声明。

e.en: 官方地;

ex.en: Diplomats haven't formally agreed to Anderson's plan.
ex.zh: 外交官们还没有正式同意安德森的计划。

d: adj. 庄重的，合乎礼仪的；（语言）正式的，规范的；合法的；整齐的，布置井然的；正统的，拘谨的；（教育或培训）正规的；形式上的，表面的；官方的，公开的
n. 正式的社交聚会；（女子的）正式礼服
【名】 （Formal）（法）福马尔（人名）

e.en: A gallon is a unit of measurement for liquids that is equal to eight pints or 3.785 litres. 加仑 (液体计量单位，合八品脱或3.785升)

ex.en: ...80 million gallons of water a day.
ex.zh: …一天8千万加仑水。

d: n. 加仑；大量；一加仑的容器（均为 gallon 的复数）

e.en: If you fulfil something such as a promise, dream, or hope, you do what you said or hoped you would do. 实现 (承诺、梦想、希望等)

ex.en: President Kaunda fulfilled his promise of announcing a date for the referendum.
ex.zh: 卡翁达总统实现了他的关于宣布投票公决日期的诺言。

e.en: To fulfil a task, role, or requirement means to do or be what is required, necessary, or expected. 完成 (任务、角色); 达到 (要求)

ex.en: Without them you will not be able to fulfil the tasks you have before you.
ex.zh: 没有他们你将不能完成你面前的任务。

e.en: If something fulfils you, or if you fulfil yourself, you feel happy and satisfied with what you are doing or with what you have achieved.

ex.en: The war was the biggest thing in her life and nothing after that quite fulfilled her.
ex.zh: 那场战争是她一生中最重大的事，在那之后没有什么颇使她感到满足过。

e.en: 感到满足的

ex.en: She has courageously continued to lead a fulfilled life.
ex.zh: 她已勇敢地继续过一种心满意足的生活。

d: v. 实现；达到，完成；履行，执行；使满足，使有成就感；结束（一段时间），完成（一件工作）

e.en: A gang is a group of people, especially young people, who go around together and often deliberately cause trouble. (尤指滋事的青少年的)

ex.en: During the fight with a rival gang he lashed out with his flick knife.
ex.zh: 和对立帮派群殴时，他用弹簧刀猛烈攻击。

ex.en: Gang members were behind a lot of the violence.
ex.zh: 流氓团伙暗中策划了许多暴力行为。

e.en: A gang is a group of criminals who work together to commit crimes.

ex.en: Police were hunting for a gang that had allegedly stolen fifty-five cars.
ex.zh: 警察正在追捕一个涉嫌偷窃55辆汽车的犯罪团伙。

ex.en: ...an underworld gang.
ex.zh: …一个地下犯罪团伙。

e.en: The gang is a group of friends who frequently meet. (经常聚会的)

ex.en: Come on over, we've got lots of the old gang here.
ex.zh: 过来吧，我们这里有很多老朋友。

e.en: A gang is a group of workers who do physical work together. (一) 队 (一起干体力活的工人)

ex.en: ...a gang of labourers.
ex.zh: …一群劳工。

d: n. 帮派（gang 的复数）
v. 成帮结伙；合伙行动（gang 的三单形式）

e.en: A gate is a structure like a door which is used at the entrance to a field, a garden, or the grounds of a building.

ex.en: He opened the gate and started walking up to the house.
ex.zh: 他打开大门并迈步向那房子走去。

e.en: In an airport, a gate is a place where passengers leave the airport and get on their aeroplane.

ex.en: Passengers with hand luggage can go straight to the departure gate to check in there.
ex.zh: 携带手提行李的乘客可以直接到登机口办理登机手续。

e.en: The gate  is the total amount of money that is paid by the people who go to a sports match or other event.
to provide with a gate or gates

d: n. 大门；登机口；闸门，阀门；（体育比赛的）观众人数；（体育比赛的）门票收入
comb. ……门事件（表示政治丑闻）(-gate)
【名】 （Gate）（英）盖特，（法、瑞典）加特（人名）
adv. 全球地，世界上；（多用于数学、计算机科学等）全局地，就整体而言

e.en: Geology is the study of the Earth's structure, surface, and origins.

ex.en: He was visiting professor of geology at the University of Georgia.
ex.zh: 他曾是佐治亚大学的地质学客座教授。

e.en: 地质学家

ex.en: Geologists have studied the way that heat flows from the earth.
ex.zh: 地质学家们已经研究了热量从地表流出的方式。

e.en: The geology of an area is the structure of its land, together with the types of rocks and minerals that exist within it.

ex.en: ...the geology of Asia.
ex.zh: …亚洲的地质状况。

d: n. 地质学；地质状况

e.en: Grass is a very common plant consisting of large numbers of thin, spiky, green leaves that cover the surface of the ground.

ex.en: Small things stirred in the grass around the tent.
ex.zh: 帐篷周围的草丛里有小东西在动。

e.en: If you say the grass is greener somewhere else, you mean that other people's situations always seem better or more attractive than your own, but may not really be so.

ex.en: He was very happy with us but wanted to see if the grass was greener elsewhere.
ex.zh: 他当时对我们感到很满意，但想看看有没有更好的。

d: n. 草；草地，草坪；大麻； 告密者；草地网球场；牧场
v. 在……上种草；（向警方）告发；捕（鱼）并带上河岸；将（某人）撞倒；给（牲畜）喂草
【名】 （Grass）（英、法、德、俄、瑞典）格拉斯（人名）

e.en: A group of people or things is a number of people or things that are together in one place at one time.

ex.en: The trouble involved a small group of football fans.
ex.zh: 那次骚乱涉及到一小撮足球迷。

e.en: A group is a set of people who have the same interests or aims, and who organize themselves to work or act together. 集体;

ex.en: Members of an environmental group are staging a protest inside a chemical plant.
ex.zh: 一个环保团体的成员们正在一家化工厂内进行抗议。

e.en: A group is a set of people, organizations, or things which are considered together because they have something in common. (有共同之处的)

ex.en: She is among the most promising players in her age group.
ex.zh: 在她那个年龄组中她是最有前途的选手之一。

e.en: A group is a number of separate commercial or industrial firms that all have the same owner. (企业)

ex.en: The group made a pretax profit of $1.05 million.
ex.zh: 该集团赚取了105万美元的税前利润。

d: n. 集体，团体；组，群；集团；乐团，乐队；空军大队（通常由两个或两个以上的基地组成）；（元素周期表中的）族；（系统语法中的）词组；原子团
v. （使）成组，聚集；将……分类

e.en: Hidden is the past participle of . (hide)
Hidden facts, feelings, activities, or problems are not easy to notice or discover.

ex.en: Under all the innocent fun, there are hidden dangers, especially for children.
ex.zh: 在所有无害的娱乐节目背后都有隐患，对儿童来说尤其如此。

e.en: A hidden place is difficult to find.

ex.en: As you descend, suddenly you see at last the hidden waterfall.
ex.zh: 你往下走，最终会突然发现那个隐秘的瀑布。

d: adj. 隐形的，隐秘的；不易察觉的，潜在的
v. 隐藏；躲避；遮挡（hide 的过去分词）
【名】 （Hidden）（英）希登（人名）

e.en: Held is the past tense and past participle of hold. (hold)

d: v. hold 的过去式和过去分词，可译为“抓住，托住”“按住，捂住”“拥抱”“举行”等；用于一般过去时、完成时及被动语态
adj. 被控制的，被占领的，被持有的（常作定语并用于复合词，如 enemy-held territory 敌方占领区、privately held company 私人持股公司）

e.en: Something that is high extends a long way from the bottom to the top when it is upright. You do not use high to describe people, animals, or plants. 高的 (不用于形容人、动物或植物)

ex.en: ...a house with a high wall all around it.
ex.zh: …四周围着高墙的房子。

ex.en: Mount Marcy is the highest mountain in the Adirondacks.
ex.zh: 马西山是阿迪朗达克山脉中最高的山。

e.en: High is also an adverb.

ex.en: ...wagons packed high with bureaus, bedding, and cooking pots.
ex.zh: …高高地推放着衣柜、寝具和炊具的四轮运货马车。

e.en: You use high to talk or ask about how much something upright measures from the bottom to the top.

ex.en: ...an elegant bronze horse only nine inches high.
ex.zh: …一尊高度仅为9英寸的精致的青铜马。

ex.en: The grass in the garden was a foot high.
ex.zh: 院子里的草有1英尺高。

e.en: If something is high, it is a long way above the ground, above sea level, or above a person or thing. (与地面、海平面、其他人或物相比而言)

ex.en: I looked down from the high window.
ex.zh: 我从高高的窗户往下看。

ex.en: The sun was high in the sky, blazing down on us.
ex.zh: 太阳高挂在空中，朝我们发出耀眼的光芒。

d: adj. 高的；富含……的；重要的；先进的，高级的；崇高的；高音的，声音尖锐的；兴高采烈的；喝醉了的，（吸毒后）极度兴奋的；十分赞同的，非常尊敬的；中间的，全盛的；开始变质的，开始发馊的；（宗教或政治观点）极端的，偏激的；（元音）舌位高的
n. 最高水平，最大数量；兴奋，高兴；高气压区；（毒品引致的）快感；高中，中学；强档；高音，高音符
adv. （成本、价值、音量）高，（数量）大；在高处，向高处
【名】  （High）（英）海伊（人名）

e.en: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

ex.en: She has moved to a small house and is living off her meagre savings.
ex.zh: 她搬进了一幢小房子，靠自己微薄的积蓄过日子。

e.en: You can refer to all the people who live together in a house as the house. 一家人;

ex.en: If he set his alarm clock for midnight, it would wake the whole house.
ex.zh: 如果他把闹钟设定在午夜，铃声会把全家人都吵醒。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of places where people go to eat and drink. …馆 (用于某些类型的餐馆名称中)

ex.en: ...a steak house.
ex.zh: …一家牛排馆。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of companies, especially ones which publish books, lend money, or design clothes. …公司 (用于某些类型的公司名称中，尤其是出版、贷款或服装设计等公司)

ex.en: Many of the clothes come from the world's top fashion houses.
ex.zh: 这些服装中有很多来自世界顶级时装设计公司。

d: v. house 的过去式和过去分词
adj. 被安置在…的，设在…的；封装的，装在保护性外壳/箱体内的

e.en: Haven't is the usual spoken form of "have not." (have not)

d: v. have not 的常用口语缩略形式，表示“没有”“尚未”，后接过去分词构成否定现在完成时，也可用于否定 have got、have to 等结构

e.en: A hundred or one hundred is the number 100. 100;

ex.en: According to one official more than a hundred people have been arrested.
ex.zh: 据一名官员说，已有一百多人被捕。

e.en: If you refer to hundreds of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them. 许许多多;

ex.en: Hundreds of tree species face extinction.
ex.zh: 很多树种濒临灭绝。

e.en: You can also use hundreds as a pronoun.

ex.en: Hundreds have been killed in the fighting and thousands made homeless.
ex.zh: 成百上千的人在战斗中丧生，并有成千上万的人变得无家可归。

e.en: You can use a hundred percent or one hundred percent to emphasize that you agree completely with something or that it is completely right or wrong.

ex.en: Are you a hundred percent sure it's your neighbour?
ex.zh: 你百分百肯定这是你的邻居？

d: n. 数百，成百上千，许多，大量（常与 of 连用）；（the hundreds）百位数（指 100 到 999 的数目或人数）；（the ... hundreds）某世纪的年代，如 the eighteen hundreds 指 1800—1899 年；（hundreds of thousands）数十万，成千上万；（hundreds and thousands）彩色小糖粒，彩针糖
pron. 很多人，成百上千的人（或事物）

e.en: A hunter is a person who hunts wild animals for food or as a sport.

ex.en: The hunters stalked their prey.
ex.zh: 猎人们隐伏跟踪猎物。

e.en: People who are searching for things of a particular kind are often referred to as hunters.

ex.en: ...job-hunters.
ex.zh: …求职者。

d: n. 猎人，捕猎者；搜寻者，寻找者；猎狐马；猎犬；有护盖的手表

e.en: A briefing is a meeting at which information or instructions are given to people, especially before they do something. 信息发布会;

ex.en: They're holding a press briefing tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他们明天将召开新闻发布会。

d: n. 情况介绍会；简报；详细指示，详情介绍
v. 给……指示，向……介绍情况（brief 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Security refers to all the measures that are taken to protect a place, or to ensure that only people with permission enter it or leave it. 保安措施;

ex.en: They are now under a great deal of pressure to tighten their airport security.
ex.zh: 他们目前承受着加强机场保安措施的巨大压力。

ex.en: Strict security measures are in force in the capital.
ex.zh: 严格的安全措施在首都实施。

e.en: A feeling of security is a feeling of being safe and free from worry.

ex.en: He loves the security of a happy home life.
ex.zh: 他非常喜欢幸福的家庭生活所来的那种安全感。

ex.en: If an alarm gives you that feeling of security, then it's worth carrying.
ex.zh: 如果一个报警器能给你那种安全感，那就值得携带。

e.en: If something gives you a false sense of security, it makes you believe that you are safe when you are not.
If something is security for a loan, you promise to give that thing to the person who lends you money, if you fail to pay the money back.

ex.en: The central bank will provide special loans, and the banks will pledge the land as security.
ex.zh: 中央银行将提供特别贷款,而各家银行将以土地作为抵押品。

d: n. 保护措施，安全工作；保安部门；安检处；保障，保证；安全，安全感；抵押品，保证金；证券，债券
n. 共同创立者，联合创始人

e.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

ex.en: The Democratic candidate is still leading in the polls.
ex.zh: 那名民主党候选人仍在民意测验中领先。

ex.en: He is a candidate for the office of governor.
ex.zh: 他是州长的候选人。

e.en: A candidate is someone who is studying for a degree at a college.

ex.en: He is now a candidate for a Master's degree in social work at San Francisco State University.
ex.zh: 他目前在旧金山州立大学攻读社会工作硕士学位。

e.en: A candidate is a person or thing that is regarded as being suitable for a particular purpose or as being likely to do or be a particular thing. 有望做…的人;

ex.en: Those who are overweight or indulge in high-salt diets are candidates for hypertension.
ex.zh: 那些身体超重或饮食偏咸的人属于易患高血压症的人群。

d: n. 候选人，申请者；有望体验（得到）……的人（物）；投考者，考生；攻读学位者
n. 责任，责任心，可说明性

e.en: Someone's advocacy of a particular action or plan is their act of recommending it publicly.

ex.en: I support your advocacy of free trade.
ex.zh: 我支持你的自由贸易倡议。

e.en: An advocacy group or organization is one that tries to influence the decisions of a government or other authority. 游说 (组织)

ex.en: Consumer advocacy groups are not so enthusiastic about removing restrictions on the telephone companies.
ex.zh: 各顾客游说组织对于取消对电话公司的限制不是那么热衷。

d: n. 拥护，提倡；辩护，辩护术；游说（团体或组织）；律师职业（或工作）

e.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

ex.en: Polls show that the European treaty has gained support in Denmark.
ex.zh: 民意测验显示，欧洲条约已经在丹麦获得支持。

ex.en: We are doing a weekly poll on the president, and clearly his popularity has declined.
ex.zh: 我们正在对总统进行每周一次的民意测验，很显然他的受欢迎度已经下降了。

e.en: If you are polled on something, you are asked what you think about it as part of a survey.

ex.en: More than 18,000 people were polled.
ex.zh: 18000多人接受了民意测验。

ex.en: Audiences were going to be polled on which of three pieces of contemporary music they liked best.
ex.zh: 听众将就3首现代乐曲中最喜欢哪一首接受民意调查。

e.en: The polls means an election for a country's government, or the place where people go to vote in an election. 政治大选;

ex.en: Incumbent officeholders are difficult to defeat at the polls.
ex.zh: 现任官员很难在选举中被击败。

ex.en: Voters are due to go to the polls on Sunday to elect a new president.
ex.zh: 选民们按计划将于周日前往投票站选举新总统。

e.en: If a political party or a candidate polls a particular number or percentage of votes, they get that number or percentage of votes in an election.

ex.en: The result showed he had polled enough votes to force a second ballot.
ex.zh: 结果显示他获得了足够的选票来促使第二轮选举。

d: n. 民意调查，民意测验；选举投票，计票；投票数；投票点（the polls）；头顶，头皮；无角动物（尤指无角牛）
v. 对……进行民意测验（调查）；获得（票数）；（电信，计算机）轮询，探询；截掉（动物，尤指小牛）的角；修枝
【名】 【名】（Poll）（德、匈、罗、英）波尔（人名）

e.en: An atrocity is a very cruel, shocking action.

ex.en: The killing was cold-blooded, and those who committed this atrocity should be tried and punished.
ex.zh: 这场杀戮非常残酷，那些犯下此暴行的人应该受到审判和惩罚。

d: n. 暴行（atrocity 的复数）

e.en: Something that is permanent lasts forever.

ex.en: Heavy drinking can cause permanent damage to the brain.
ex.zh: 饮酒过量可能造成永久性脑损伤。

ex.en: ...a permanent solution to the problem.
ex.zh: …一个解决该问题的永久性办法。

e.en: 永久地

ex.en: His confidence had been permanently affected by the ordeal.
ex.zh: 他的信心已永久地被这次磨难影响了。

e.en: You use permanent to describe situations or states that keep occurring or that seem to exist all the time; used especially to describe problems or difficulties. (问题或困难) 不断发生的;

ex.en: ...a permanent state of tension.
ex.zh: …长期的紧张状态。

ex.en: They feel under permanent threat.
ex.zh: 他们感觉处在持续不断的威胁之下。

e.en: (问题或困难) 不断发生地;

ex.en: ...the heavy, permanently locked gate.
ex.zh: …这扇厚重的、长年锁着的大门。

d: adj. 永久的，永恒的；（尤指问题或困难）不断出现的，一直存在的；（员工）终生的，长期的；（家庭住址）固定的
n. 烫发
n. 罗斯（姓氏）

e.en: Tuesday is the day after Monday and before Wednesday.

ex.en: He phoned on Tuesday, just before you came.
ex.zh: 他星期二打了电话，刚好在你来之前。

ex.en: Talks are likely to start next Tuesday.
ex.zh: 会谈可能在下星期二开始。

d: n. 星期二

e.en: A victim is someone who has been hurt or killed.

ex.en: Statistically our chances of being the victims of violent crime are remote.
ex.zh: 从统计上来看，我们成为暴力犯罪受害者的可能性是微乎其微的。

e.en: A victim is someone who has suffered as a result of someone else's actions or beliefs, or as a result of unpleasant circumstances.

ex.en: He was a victim of racial prejudice.
ex.zh: 他是种族偏见的一个牺牲品。

ex.en: He described himself and Altman as victims rather than participants in the scandal.
ex.zh: 他把自己和奥尔特曼描述成这一丑闻的受害者，而不是参与者。

d: n. 受害者，牺牲者，遇难者；受灾群众（victim 的复数）；受骗者，上当者

e.en: Someone's absence from a place is the fact that they are not there.

ex.en: ...a bundle of letters which had arrived for me in my absence.
ex.zh: …我不在的时候寄给我的一捆信。

e.en: The absence of something from a place is the fact that it is not there or does not exist.

ex.en: The presence or absence of clouds can have an important impact on temperature.
ex.zh: 云的有无对气温会产生重要影响。

d: n. 缺席，缺勤，不在；缺乏，没有；缺席期间，休假期间；不注意

e.en: If you watch someone or something, you look at them, usually for a period of time, and pay attention to what is happening.

ex.en: The man was standing in his doorway watching him.
ex.zh: 那个男人正站在自家门道里看着他。

ex.en: He seems to enjoy watching me work.
ex.zh: 他似乎喜欢看我干活。

e.en: If you watch something on television or an event such as a sports contest, you spend time looking at it, especially when you see it from the beginning to the end. 观看 (电视节目、比赛等)

ex.en: I'd stayed up late to watch the movie.
ex.zh: 我熬夜看了那部电影。

e.en: If you watch a situation or event, you pay attention to it or you are aware of it, but you do not influence it.

ex.en: Human rights groups have been closely watching the case.
ex.zh: 人权组织一直在密切关注着这件案子。

ex.en: He watched as nine people were swept into the crevasse.
ex.zh: 他眼看着9个人被卷入冰缝中。

e.en: If you watch people, especially children or animals, you are responsible for them, and make sure that they are not in danger.

ex.en: Parents can't be expected to watch their children 24 hours a day.
ex.zh: 不能指望父母全天24小时都照看自己的孩子。

d: v. 看，注视；观看（电视节目、比赛等）；关注；照看，守护；当心，留意；监视
n. 表，手表；观察，监视； 警卫队，治安队；警戒时间，（警卫或治安队等的）值班时间；巡夜人，巡夜队（the watch）；一群夜莺；（某人的）管理期；（官方）天气预警，天气警报

e.en: If you achieve a particular aim or effect, you succeed in doing it or causing it to happen, usually after a lot of effort.

ex.en: There are many who will work hard to achieve these goals.
ex.zh: 有很多人会努力工作来实现这些目标。

d: v. （经努力）达到，取得，实现；获得成功

e.en: An activist is a person who works to bring about political or social changes by campaigning in public or working for an organization.

ex.en: The police say they suspect the attack was carried out by animal rights activists.
ex.zh: 警方说他们怀疑这次袭击是由保护动物权利的激进分子实施的。

ex.en: Dobson blames activist judges for undermining families with favourable gay-marriage rulings.
ex.zh: 多布森责备激进派法官们通过赞成同性婚姻的裁决破坏家庭。

d: n. 积极分子，活动家
adj. 积极分子的

e.en: An affirmative word or gesture indicates that you agree with what someone has said or that the answer to a question is "yes." 肯定的 (言辞、手势)

ex.en: Haig was desperately eager for an affirmative answer.
ex.zh: 黑格极渴望得到一个肯定的回答。

e.en: In grammar, an affirmative clause is positive and does not contain a negative word. (语法中) 肯定的 (分句)
If you reply to a question in the affirmative, you say "yes" or make a gesture that means "yes." (回答问题)

ex.en: He asked me if I was ready. I answered in the affirmative.
ex.zh: 他问我是否准备好了。我肯定地回答了。

d: adj. 肯定的，同意的；（法律提案）须议会投票赞成生效的；积极的
n. 同意，赞成；陈述词，肯定词；赞成的一方
int. 同意的，赞成的

e.en: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The deaths occurred when police acted to stop widespread looting and vandalism.
ex.zh: 当警方行动起来去制止大范围的洗劫和蓄意破坏时，死亡事件发生了。

e.en: If you act on advice or information, you do what has been advised or suggested. (按照建议或信息)

ex.en: A patient will usually listen to the doctor's advice and act on it.
ex.zh: 病人通常会听从医生的建议并且按照它行动。

e.en: If someone acts in a particular way, they behave in that way.

ex.en: ...a gang of youths who were acting suspiciously.
ex.zh: …一帮表现可疑的年轻人。

ex.en: He acted as if he hadn't heard any of it.
ex.zh: 他表现得好像一点都没有听过这件事一样。

e.en: If someone or something acts as a particular thing, they have that role or function.

ex.en: Among his other duties, he acted both as the ship's surgeon and as chaplain for the men.
ex.zh: 另外，他兼任船上的外科医生以及船员们的牧师。

d: v. 行动；表现；起作用；扮演（角色）；担任；假装；代理（act的第三人称单数）
n. 行为；假装；某种行为（或常规等）；法令；判决书；会议记录；（戏剧等的）幕；表演；演出团体（act的复数）
abbr. 声控遥测系统 (Acoustic Control and Telemetry System)；声控制与遥测系统 (Acoustic Control and Telemetry System)

e.en: Someone who is armed is carrying a weapon, usually a gun.

ex.en: City police said the man was armed with a revolver.
ex.zh: 市警方说那名男子持有一支左轮手枪。

ex.en: ...a barbed-wire fence patrolled by armed guards.
ex.zh: …一个由武装卫兵巡查的带刺铁丝网围栏。

e.en: An armed attack or conflict involves people fighting with guns or carrying weapons.

ex.en: They had been found guilty of armed robbery.
ex.zh: 他们被判犯有持械抢劫罪。

d: adj. 武装的，持械的，携带武器的；使用武器的，涉及武器的（指攻击、冲突、抢劫等）；配备…的，拥有…的（armed with）；有臂的，…臂的（用于复合词）；有扶手的（指椅子等）；有防卫器官的（指动植物）
n. （Armed）人名，阿米德（科摩）

e.en: the act of taking arms or providing with arms
e.zh: 准备作战之状态或行动

d: n. 武装，装备（武器），备战；徽章
v. arm 的现在分词和动名词：武装，给…提供武器

e.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad. (质量)

ex.en: I remain to this day fluent in Hebrew, while my Arabic is atrocious.
ex.zh: 我直到今天希伯莱语仍很流利，而我的阿拉伯语则极差。

e.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or their actions as atrocious, you mean that it is unacceptable because it is extremely violent or cruel. (行为)

ex.en: The judge said he had committed atrocious crimes against women.
ex.zh: 该法官称他对妇女犯下了残暴的罪行。

d: adj. 凶恶的，残暴的；恶劣的，糟糕的

e.en: An autocratic person or organization has complete power and makes decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

ex.en: The people have grown intolerant in recent weeks of the king's autocratic ways.
ex.zh: 最近几周，民众越来越难以忍受国王的专制行径。

d: adj. 独裁的，专制的；专横的，独断专行的

e.en: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.

ex.en: Fifty civilians in Masawa were killed when government planes attacked the town.
ex.zh: 马萨瓦50名平民在政府飞机袭击该市时丧生。

ex.en: He bundled the old lady into her hallway and brutally attacked her.
ex.zh: 他把老太太推进她家门厅里，并且野蛮地袭击了她。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a campaign of air attacks on strategic targets.
ex.zh: …对战略目标的空袭行动。

e.en: If you attack a person, belief, idea, or act, you criticize them strongly.

ex.en: He publicly attacked the people who've been calling for secret ballot nominations.
ex.zh: 他公开抨击了那些一直要求秘密投票提名的人。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: The role of the state as a prime mover in planning social change has been under attack.
ex.zh: 国家作为规划社会变革发起者的角色已经遭到抨击。

d: v. 批评，抨击；侵蚀，侵害；全力应对，奋力处理；袭击，攻击；（体育比赛中）进攻
n. （疾病的）突然发作；（情感的）一阵突发；（体育运动中的）进攻；袭击，攻击；批评，抨击；进攻队员；（病虫等的）损害，伤害
【名】 （Attack）（瑞典）阿塔克（人名）
n．Avaaz是一个全球性的民间组织，成立于2007年，旨在通过网络平台动员全球公民参与解决重要的国际、地区和国内问题，如环境保护、人权、动物福利等。

e.en: A blanket is a large square or rectangular piece of thick cloth, especially one that you put on a bed to keep you warm.
A blanket of something such as snow is a continuous layer of it which hides what is below or beyond it.

ex.en: The mud disappeared under a blanket of snow.
ex.zh: 泥地在一层白雪的覆盖下消失不见了。

e.en: If something such as snow blankets an area, it covers it.

ex.en: More than a foot of snow blanketed parts of Michigan.
ex.zh: 一英尺多厚的白雪覆盖了密歇根州的部分地区。

e.en: You use blanket to describe something when you want to emphasize that it affects or refers to every person or thing in a group, without any exceptions.

ex.en: There's already a blanket ban on foreign unskilled labour in Japan.
ex.zh: 日本已经有一项禁止使用外国非熟练工人的通用禁令。

d: n. 毯子，毛毯；厚层，覆盖层；气氛，氛围；障碍，障碍物；（平版印刷的）橡皮布；（平版印刷的）橡皮
v. 覆盖，盖住，笼罩；消除（声音），使（声音）模糊不清；迎风航行抢（他船）的上风
adj. 总括的，全面的，通用的

e.en: Blatantly is used to add emphasis when you are describing states or situations that you think are bad.

ex.en: It became blatantly obvious to me that the band wasn't going to last.
ex.zh: 我看得再清楚不过，这个乐队存在不了多久。

ex.en: For years, blatantly false assertions have gone unchallenged.
ex.zh: 很多年来，极其错误的断言从未曾受到质疑。

d: adv. 公然地，露骨地，明目张胆地；（常用于 obvious 或 false 前）极其，显然，再…不过；喧闹地
n. 布鲁诺（男子名）；也用作姓氏

e.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

ex.en: The Democratic candidate is still leading in the polls.
ex.zh: 那名民主党候选人仍在民意测验中领先。

ex.en: He is a candidate for the office of governor.
ex.zh: 他是州长的候选人。

e.en: A candidate is someone who is studying for a degree at a college.

ex.en: He is now a candidate for a Master's degree in social work at San Francisco State University.
ex.zh: 他目前在旧金山州立大学攻读社会工作硕士学位。

e.en: A candidate is a person or thing that is regarded as being suitable for a particular purpose or as being likely to do or be a particular thing. 有望做…的人;

ex.en: Those who are overweight or indulge in high-salt diets are candidates for hypertension.
ex.zh: 那些身体超重或饮食偏咸的人属于易患高血压症的人群。

d: n. 候选人，申请者，应征人员（candidate 的复数）；考生，应试者；有望成为…的人或事物，适合某用途的候选对象；（美国英语）攻读学位者

e.en: If you capture someone or something, you catch them, especially in a war. 俘虏;

ex.en: The guerrillas shot down one aeroplane and captured the pilot.
ex.zh: 那些游击队员击落了一架飞机，并俘虏了飞行员。

e.en: Capture is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the final battles which led to the army's capture of the town.
ex.zh: …部队夺取该镇的最后几场战斗。

e.en: If something or someone captures a particular quality, feeling, or atmosphere, they represent or express it successfully.

ex.en: Chef Idris Caldora offers an inspired menu that captures the spirit of the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: 伊德里斯·卡尔多拉厨师的菜单很有创意，充分体现了地中海风情。

e.en: If something captures your attention or imagination, you begin to be interested or excited by it. If someone or something captures your heart, you begin to love them or like them very much.

ex.en: ...the great names of the past who usually capture the historian's attention.
ex.zh: …那些常常为史学家所关注的伟人们。

d: v. 俘获，捕获；夺取，占领；吸引，引起；记录，体现；拍摄，录制；吃掉（国际象棋棋子）；使（数据）保存于电脑中；俘获（原子，亚原子粒）；（河流）袭夺
n. 捕获，被捕获；被捕获的人（或物）；占领，攻占；夺取，抢占；（数据）存储

e.en: You use civil to describe events that happen within a country and that involve the different groups of people in it.

ex.en: ...civil unrest.
ex.zh: …民众的骚乱。

e.en: You use civil to describe people or things in a country that are not connected with its armed forces.

ex.en: ...the U.S. civil aviation industry.
ex.zh: …美国民用航空工业。

e.en: You use civil to describe things that are connected with the state rather than with a religion.

ex.en: They were married on August 9 in a civil ceremony in Venice.
ex.zh: 他们于8月9日在威尼斯通过民政仪式结了婚。

e.en: You use civil to describe the rights that people have within a society.

ex.en: ...a United Nations covenant on civil and political rights.
ex.zh: …一份关于民权和政治权利的联合国公约。

d: adj. 公民的，国民的，国内的；平民的，民用的；文明的，有礼貌的；民法的（非刑法的），民事的；习俗规定的，历法规定的
【名】 （Civil）（土）吉维尔，（法）西维尔（人名）

e.en: A crime is an illegal action or activity for which a person can be punished by law.

ex.en: He and Lieutenant Cassidy were checking the scene of the crime.
ex.zh: 当时他正与卡西迪中尉一起检查犯罪现场。

ex.en: ...the growing problem of organized crime.
ex.zh: …越来越严重的有组织犯罪问题。

e.en: If you say that doing something is a crime, you think it is very wrong or a serious mistake.

ex.en: It would be a crime to travel all the way to Australia and not stop in Sydney.
ex.zh: 如果千里迢迢去澳大利亚而不在悉尼停留，那就是大错特错。

d: n. 犯罪，罪行（crime 的复数形式）

e.en: A criminal is a person who has committed a crime.

ex.en: A group of gunmen attacked a prison and set free nine criminals.
ex.zh: 一伙持枪歹徒袭击了一所监狱并放走了9名罪犯。

e.en: Criminal means connected with crime. 犯罪的;

ex.en: Her husband faces various criminal charges.
ex.zh: 她丈夫面临多项刑事的指控。

e.en: If you describe an action as criminal, you think it is very wrong or a serious mistake.

ex.en: He said a full-scale dispute involving strikes would be criminal.
ex.zh: 他说一个卷入罢工的全面抗争将是极其错误的。

d: n. 罪犯（criminal 的复数形式）
共同执行

e.en: Criticism is the action of expressing disapproval of something or someone. A criticism is a statement that expresses disapproval. 批评;

ex.en: This policy had repeatedly come under strong criticism on Capitol Hill.
ex.zh: 这项政策在国会反复受到强烈批评。

e.en: Criticism is a serious examination and judgment of something such as a book or play.

ex.en: She has published more than 20 books including novels, poetry and literary criticism.
ex.zh: 她已出版了二十多本书，其中包括小说、诗歌和文学评论。

d: n. 批评，批判；意见；评论，评价；（对文学作品和历史文献的）考证

e.en: If someone is a defender of a particular thing or person that has been criticized, they argue or act in support of that thing or person.

ex.en: ...the most ardent defenders of conventional family values.
ex.zh: …传统家庭价值最强烈的捍卫者。

e.en: A defender in a game such as football or hockey is a player whose main task is to try and stop the other side from scoring.

ex.en: Lewis was the NFL's top defender in the 2000 season.
ex.zh: 刘易斯是2000年赛季美国国家足球联盟的最佳防守球员。

d: n. 防守队员，后卫；保护者，捍卫者；（桥牌）守方；辩护人，辩护律师；（苏格兰法律）被告

e.en: A denial of something is a statement that it is not true, does not exist, or did not happen.

ex.en: It seems clear that despite official denials, differences of opinion lay behind the ambassador's decision to quit.
ex.zh: 很清楚，尽管官方否认，人们对大使决定辞职还是有不同看法。

e.en: The denial of something to someone is the act of refusing to let them have it.

ex.en: ...the denial of visas to international relief workers.
ex.zh: …对国际救济工作人员拒发签证。

e.en: In psychology, denial is when a person cannot or will not accept an unpleasant truth. (不愉快事实的)

ex.en: With major life traumas, like losing a loved one, for instance, the mind's first reaction is denial.
ex.zh: 面对人生的重大创痛，例如失去深爱的人，心理的第一反应就是拒绝接受。

d: n．
1. 否认，拒绝承认：对某事的真实性、存在或有效性的否定。
2. 拒绝，不给予：拒绝给予某人某物或拒绝允许某人做某事。

e.en: When you deny something, you state that it is not true.

ex.en: She denied both accusations.
ex.zh: 她否认对她的两项指控。

ex.en: The government has denied that the authorities have uncovered a plot to assassinate the president.
ex.zh: 政府否认当局已经发现一个暗杀总统的阴谋。

e.en: If you deny someone something that they need or want, you refuse to let them have it.

ex.en: Two federal courts ruled that the military cannot deny prisoners access to lawyers.
ex.zh: 两联邦法院裁定军方不能拒绝让囚犯聘请律师。

d: v. deny 的第三人称单数一般现在时形式：否认，否定；拒绝，拒绝给予；（deny oneself）节制，戒除

e.en: A diplomat is a senior official who discusses affairs with another country on behalf of his or her own country, usually working as a member of an embassy.

ex.en: ...a Western diplomat with long experience in Asia.
ex.zh: …一名在亚洲有长期经验的西方外交官。

d: n. 外交官；善于打交道的人，处世圆通的人

e.en: When an employee is dismissed from their job, you can refer to their dismissal.

ex.en: ...Mr. Low's dismissal from his post at the head of the commission.
ex.zh: …洛先生被免去委员会主任的职务。

e.en: Dismissal of something means deciding or saying that it is not important.

ex.en: ...bureaucratic indifference to people's rights and needs, and high-handed dismissal of public opinion.
ex.zh: …官僚主义对民众权利和需求的冷漠，以及对公众意见的不懈一顾。

d: n. 开除，解雇；不予考虑，摒弃；驳回，不予受理；打发走，遣散；出局

e.en: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them. 文件;

ex.en: She produces legal documents for a downtown Seattle law firm.
ex.zh: 她为西雅图市区的一家法律事务所撰写法律文件。

e.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example, a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

ex.en: When you are finished typing, remember to save your document.
ex.zh: 输入完毕后，要记着保存文档。

e.en: If you document something, you make a detailed record of it in writing or on film or tape.

ex.en: He wrote a book documenting his prison experiences.
ex.zh: 他写了一本书，记录他的牢狱经历。

d: adj. 有文件证明的；有据可查的
v. document 的过去式和过去分词：记录，记载

e.en: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them. 文件;

ex.en: She produces legal documents for a downtown Seattle law firm.
ex.zh: 她为西雅图市区的一家法律事务所撰写法律文件。

e.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example, a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

ex.en: When you are finished typing, remember to save your document.
ex.zh: 输入完毕后，要记着保存文档。

e.en: If you document something, you make a detailed record of it in writing or on film or tape.

ex.en: He wrote a book documenting his prison experiences.
ex.zh: 他写了一本书，记录他的牢狱经历。

d: v. document 的现在分词：详细记录，记载；用文件或证据证明
n. document 的动名词：文件编制，文档编制

e.en: When people elect someone, they choose that person to represent them, by voting for them.

ex.en: The people of the Philippines have voted to elect a new president.
ex.zh: 菲律宾人民已经投票选举出一位新总统。

ex.en: The University of Washington elected him dean in 1956.
ex.zh: 华盛顿大学在1956年选他为院长。

e.en: If you elect to do something, you choose to do it.

ex.en: Those electing to smoke will be seated at the rear.
ex.zh: 选择抽烟的人将坐在后面。

e.en: Elect is added after words such as "president" or "governor" to indicate that a person has been elected to the post but has not officially started to carry out the duties involved.

ex.en: ...the date when the president-elect takes office.
ex.zh: …总统当选人的就职日。

d: v. elect 的现在分词和动名词：选举，推选；（正式）选择（做某事）

e.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it. 牵连;

ex.en: Such a decision would entail a huge political risk in the midst of the presidential campaign.
ex.zh: 这样的决定会在总统大选之际导致一个巨大的政治风险。

d: v. 使必要，需要；遗赠（财产），限定继承；使人承担
n. 限定继承，限嗣继承的财产

e.en: An endorsement is a statement or action that shows you support or approve of something or someone.

ex.en: This is a powerful endorsement for his softer style of government.
ex.zh: 这是对他的更温和的执政风格的强有力认可。

e.en: An endorsement for a product or company involves appearing in advertisements for it or showing support for it.

ex.en: His commercial endorsements for everything from running shoes to breakfast cereals will take his earnings to more than ten million dollars a year.
ex.zh: 他的商业代言从跑鞋到早餐麦片一应俱全，令其年收入达到一千多万美元。

d: n. 背书，票据签字；（驾驶执照上的）违章记录；（说明不予理赔或变更细节的）保险单附加条款；赞同，支持；（为某产品或服务所做的）宣传，代言

e.en: You use essentially to emphasize a quality that someone or something has, and to say that it is their most important or basic quality.

ex.en: It's been believed for centuries that great writers, composers, and scientists are essentially quite different from ordinary people.
ex.zh: 几个世纪以来人们都认为伟大的作家、作曲家和科学家本质上与常人大不相同。

e.en: You use essentially to indicate that what you are saying is mainly true, although some parts of it are wrong or more complicated than has been stated.

ex.en: His analysis of urban use of agricultural land has been proved essentially correct.
ex.zh: 他的城市对农用土地使用的分析已经被证明基本上正确。

d: adv. 本质上，根本上；大体上，基本上

e.en: Facts are pieces of information that can be discovered.

ex.en: There is so much information you can almost effortlessly find the facts for yourself.
ex.zh: 有这么多信息，你几乎能毫不费力地为自己找到实例。

ex.en: His opponent swamped him with facts and figures.
ex.zh: 他的对手用实例和数字让他难以招架。

e.en: You use the fact that after some verbs or prepositions, especially in expressions such as in view of the fact that, apart from the fact that, and despite the fact that, to link the verb or preposition with a clause. …

ex.en: His chances do not seem good in view of the fact that the Chief Prosecutor has already voiced his public disapproval.
ex.zh: 鉴于首席检察官已公开表示反对这一事实，他的机会看起来不好。

ex.en: Despite the fact that the disease is so prevalent, treatment is still far from satisfactory.
ex.zh: 尽管事实上这种疾病非常普遍，治疗却远不尽如人意。

e.en: You use the fact that instead of a simple that-clause either for emphasis or because the clause is the subject of your sentence. …

ex.en: My family now accepts the fact that I don't eat sugar or bread.
ex.zh: 我的家人现在接受了我不吃糖或面包这一事实。

e.en: You use in fact, in actual fact, or in point of fact to indicate that you are giving more detailed information about what you have just said.

ex.en: We've had a pretty bad time while you were away. In fact, we very nearly split up this time.
ex.zh: 我们在你走的那段时间过得非常糟糕。确切地说，我们这次几乎分道扬镳了。

ex.en: He apologized as soon as he realized what he had done. In actual fact he wrote a nice little note to me.
ex.zh: 他一意识到他所做的一切就道歉了。确切地说，他给我写了一张友善的小便条。

d: abbr. 设备管理控制与时间调度程序；Facilities Administration Control and Time Schedule

e.en: Something or someone that is fair is reasonable, right, and just.

ex.en: It didn't seem fair to leave out her father.
ex.zh: 将她的父亲排除在外似乎不公平。

ex.en: Do you feel they're paying their fair share?
ex.zh: 你觉得他们正支付自己应分担的那一份吗？

e.en: 公平地

ex.en: ...demonstrating concern for employees and solving their problems quickly and fairly.
ex.zh: …证实对雇员的关注以及迅速公平地解决他们的问题。

e.en: A fair amount, degree, size, or distance is quite a large amount, degree, size, or distance. 相当大的;

ex.en: My neighbours across the street travel a fair amount.
ex.zh: 我街对面的邻居们去过相当多的地方。

e.en: A fair guess or idea about something is one that is likely to be correct.

ex.en: It's a fair guess to say that the damage will be extensive.
ex.zh: 说破坏将很严重是合理的猜测。

d: adj. 公平的；合理的，公正的；相当好的；（数量、大小）相当大的；浅色的，（肤色）白皙的，（头发）金色的；晴朗的；顺风的；普通的；美丽的；界内的；（手段，方法）温和的，非暴力的；（言语，谈话，许诺）花言巧语的
adv. 公平地，公正地；非常；正面地，直接地；清楚地
n. 集市，展览会；露天游乐场；庙会；义卖会；牲畜市场；美女；职业介绍会
v. 变得晴朗；使（车辆，船舶，飞机）具有流线型

e.en: A fact-finding mission or visit is one whose purpose is to get information about a particular situation, especially for an official group.

ex.en: A UN fact-finding mission is on its way to the region.
ex.zh: 一个联合国实地调查团正在赶赴该地区的途中。

d: n. 实情调查；调解
adj. （尤指委员会及其活动）实情调查的

e.en: If you have faith in someone or something, you feel confident about their ability or goodness.

ex.en: People have lost faith in the government.
ex.zh: 人们已失去了对政府的信心。

e.en: Faith is strong religious belief in a particular God.

ex.en: Umberto Eco's loss of his own religious faith is reflected in his novels.
ex.zh: 翁贝托·埃科宗教信仰的丧失在他的小说当中得到了反映。

e.en: A faith is a particular religion, for example, Christianity, Buddhism, or Islam.

ex.en: England shifted officially from a Catholic to a Protestant faith in the 16th century.
ex.zh: 英格兰在16世纪正式从信仰天主教改信新教。

e.en: If you do something in good faith, you seriously believe that what you are doing is right, honest, or legal, even though this may not be the case.

ex.en: This report was published in good faith but we regret any confusion which may have been caused.
ex.zh: 发表这份报告出自诚意，但是我们对可能引发的任何混乱而感到遗憾。

d: n. 信任，信心，信念；宗教；宗教信仰；忠诚
int. 用以表示惊讶或强调千真万确
【名】 （Faith）（英）费思，费丝，（匈）福伊特，（瑞典）法伊特（人名）
n. 弗格森（美国密苏里州的一个城市名）；弗格森（姓氏）

e.en: The format of something is the way or order in which it is arranged and presented.

ex.en: I had met with him to explain the format of the programme and what we had in mind.
ex.zh: 我已经同他见过面，解释了这个节目的程式和我们的想法。

e.en: The format of a piece of computer software, a film or a musical recording is the type of equipment on which it is designed to be used or played. For example, possible formats for a film are DVD and video cassette. (计算机软件、电影、音乐录制品等的)

ex.en: His latest album is available on all formats.
ex.zh: 他的最新专辑有各种格式可以买到。

e.en: To format a computer disk means to run a program so that the disk can be written on. 将 (电脑磁盘)

ex.en: ...a menu that includes the choice to format a disk.
ex.zh: …一个包括格式化磁盘选项的菜单。

e.en: To format a piece of computer text or graphics means to arrange the way in which it appears when it is printed or is displayed on a screen. 设置 (电脑文本或图形的)

ex.en: When text is saved from a Web page, it is often very badly formatted with many short lines.
ex.zh: 文本从网页上另存时版式通常会变乱，出现很多短行。

d: n. 总体安排，计划，设计；（书或杂志的）开本，版式；（录像、激光唱片、磁带等的）格式
v. 为……编排格式；格式化

e.en: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. 向前 (移动、看)

ex.en: He came forward with his hand out. "Mr. and Mrs. Selby?" he said.
ex.zh: 他伸着手走上前来，“塞尔比先生和夫人吧？”他说。

ex.en: She fell forward on to her face.
ex.zh: 她脸着地向前摔倒了。

e.en: Forward means in a position near the front of something such as a building or a vehicle.

ex.en: The best seats are in the aisle and as far forward as possible.
ex.zh: 最好的座位在过道处尽可能靠前的地方。

e.en: Forward is also an adjective.

ex.en: Reinforcements were needed to allow more troops to move to forward positions.
ex.zh: 需要增援以便让更多的部队推进至前沿阵地。

e.en: If you say that someone looks forward, you approve of them because they think about what will happen in the future and plan for it. (看)

ex.en: Now the leadership wants to look forward, and to outline a strategy for the rest of the century.
ex.zh: 现在领导层想要向前看，为本世纪余下的时间勾画一个战略框架。

ex.en: People should forget and look forward.
ex.zh: 人们应当忘记过去向前看。

d: adv. 向前；在船头，朝飞机头部；按顺序地；有进展地，前进地；向将来，往后；提前；（钟表）往前（拨）；从……起，自……以来
adj. 向前的，前进的；在前部的，位于前面的；（电子）正向的；未来的，将来的；期货的，预先的；早的，早熟的；鲁莽的，冒失的；热心的，动辄就……的
n. （足球、篮球等运动的）前锋；（尤指金融市场）远期协议，远期交易
v. 转交，转寄；寄，发送；促进，推进
n. 领跑者，领先者；最有可能获胜的人（或队伍、公司等）

e.en: Genocidal means relating to genocide or carrying out genocide.

ex.en: They have been accused of genocidal crimes.
ex.zh: 他们被指控犯有种族灭绝罪。

d: adj. 集团屠杀的，种族灭绝的

e.en: Genocide is the deliberate murder of a whole community or race. 大屠杀;

ex.en: They have alleged that acts of genocide and torture were carried out.
ex.zh: 他们声称实施了大屠杀和酷刑。

d: n. 种族灭绝，大屠杀

e.en: Grew is the past tense of . (grow)

d: v. grow 的过去式：长大，成长；生长，成活；变得，逐渐成为；发展，增加，扩大；种植，栽培；grew up（grow up 的过去式）长大成人，成长

e.en: Gridlock is the situation that exists when all the roads in a particular place are so full of vehicles that none of them can move.

ex.en: The streets are wedged solid with the chaos of poorly regulated parking and near-constant traffic gridlock.
ex.zh: 由于管理不当的乱停车以及不断的交通阻塞，街道被堵得严严实实。

e.en: You can use gridlock to refer to a situation in an argument or dispute when neither side is prepared to give in, so no agreement can be reached.

ex.en: He agreed that these policies will lead to gridlock in the future.
ex.zh: 他赞同这些政策将来会导致僵局。

d: v. （交通等）堵塞（gridlock 的过去式及过去分词）
adj. 交通堵塞的；陷入僵局的

e.en: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. Each hand has four fingers and a thumb.

ex.en: I put my hand into my pocket and pulled out the letter.
ex.zh: 我把手伸进衣袋，掏出那封信。

e.en: The hand of someone or something is their influence in an event or situation.

ex.en: The hand of the military authorities can be seen in the entire electoral process.
ex.zh: 军方的影响在整个选举过程中都可以看到。

e.en: If you say that something is in a particular person's hands, you mean that they are taking care of it, own it, or are responsible for it. 照顾;

ex.en: I feel that possibly the majority of these dogs are in the wrong hands.
ex.zh: 我觉得这些狗中大多数可能没有得到适当的照顾。

ex.en: We're in safe hands.
ex.zh: 我们得到妥善的照顾。

e.en: If you ask someone for a hand with something, you are asking them to help you in what you are doing.

ex.en: Come and give me a hand in the garden.
ex.zh: 到花园里来给我搭把手。

d: n. 手；（钟表的）指针；一局牌，一手牌；帮助，援手；工人；船员，水手；支配，掌管；作用，影响；鼓掌，拍手喝彩；字迹；一手之宽（用来测量马匹的高度）；（女方的）允婚；表演艺人，制作工匠
comb. 用……手的；手工
v. 交，递；支持，搀扶；卷（帆）
【名】 （Hand）（英、瑞典）汉德（人名）

e.en: On a vehicle such as a car, the horn is the device that makes a loud noise as a signal or warning. (汽车等的)

ex.en: He sounded the car horn.
ex.zh: 他按响了汽车喇叭。

e.en: The horns of an animal such as a cow or deer are the hard pointed things that grow from its head. (牛、鹿等动物头上的)

ex.en: A mature cow has horns.
ex.zh: 成年母牛头上长有角。

e.en: A horn is a musical instrument of the brass family. It is a long circular metal tube, wide at one end, which you play by blowing. 号 (铜管乐器)

ex.en: He started playing the horn when he was eight.
ex.zh: 他8岁时就开始吹号。

e.en: A horn is a simple musical instrument consisting of a metal tube that is wide at one end and narrow at the other. You play it by blowing into it. 号 (一种以一头宽一头窄的金属管制成的简单的吹奏乐器)

ex.en: ...a hunting horn.
ex.zh: …猎号。

d: n. 角；角质；号角；喇叭；角状物
v. （动物）用角抵撞（或顶撞）；对（丈夫或妻子）不忠诚；装角于

e.en: You can describe a place as a hub of an activity when it is a very important centre for that activity.

ex.en: The island's social hub is the Cafe Sport.
ex.zh: 该岛的社交中心是“运动咖啡馆”。

e.en: The hub of a wheel is the part at the centre.
A hub or a hub airport is a large airport from which you can travel to many other airports.

ex.en: ...a campaign to secure Heathrow's place as Europe's main international hub.
ex.zh: …一场确保希思罗机场成为欧洲主要国际枢纽机场的运动。

e.en: A hub is a device for connecting computers in a network.

d: n. （活动的）中心；枢纽机场，枢纽城市；（轮）毂，（推进器、风扇等的）旋翼叶毂；（网络）集线器
【名】 （Hub）（捷）胡布（人名）

e.en: If you hide something or someone, you put them in a place where they cannot easily be seen or found.

ex.en: He hid the bicycle in the hawthorn hedge.
ex.zh: 他把自行车藏进了山楂树树丛里。

e.en: If you hide or if you hide yourself, you go somewhere where you cannot easily be seen or found.

ex.en: At their approach the little boy scurried and hid.
ex.zh: 当他们走近时，那个小男孩急忙跑开躲了起来。

e.en: If you hide your face, you press your face against something or cover your face with something, so that people cannot see it. 捂住; 把 (脸)

ex.en: She hid her face under the collar of his jacket and started to cry.
ex.zh: 她把脸埋在他的外套领子下哭了起来。

e.en: If you hide what you feel or know, you keep it a secret, so that no one knows about it.

ex.en: Lee tried to hide his excitement.
ex.zh: 李努力掩饰内心的激动。

d: v. 把……藏起来，隐藏；躲藏，躲避；遮住，遮挡；掩盖，隐瞒
n. （可观察鸟兽行动的）隐匿处，埋伏处；兽皮；（困境中的）生命，人身安全

e.en: If you describe a physical attack, accident, or injury as horrific, you mean that it is very bad, so that people are shocked when they see it or think about it.

ex.en: I have never seen such horrific injuries.
ex.zh: 我从没见过这么严重的伤。

e.en: 极其可怕地

ex.en: He had been horrifically assaulted before he died.
ex.zh: 他死之前曾遭人毒打。

e.en: If you describe something as horrific, you mean that it is so big that it is extremely unpleasant.

ex.en: ...piling up horrific extra amounts of money on top of your original debt.
ex.zh: …在你原有债务的基础上再加上数目骇人的几大笔钱。

e.en: 大得骇人地

ex.en: Opera productions are horrifically expensive.
ex.zh: 歌剧的演出花销大得吓人。

d: adj. 可怕的，令人毛骨悚然的；极其糟糕的，大得骇人的
n. （Husam）人名；（塞）胡萨姆
n. 易卜拉欣（与阿丹、努哈、穆萨、尔撒和穆罕默德并称为安拉的六大使者，亦系犹太教和基督教推崇的圣人和希伯来人的祖先）

e.en: If a country has or gains independence, it has its own government and is not ruled by any other country. (国家的)

ex.en: In 1816, Argentina declared its independence from Spain.
ex.zh: 1816年，阿根廷宣布脱离西班牙而独立。

e.en: Someone's independence is the fact that they do not rely on other people. (人的)

ex.en: He was afraid of losing his independence.
ex.zh: 他担心丧失自己的独立。

d: n. 独立，自主；（国家的）独立；（国家或地区的）政治独立日期

e.en: An incoming message or phone call is one that you receive. (短信、邮件等)

ex.en: We keep a tape of incoming calls.
ex.zh: 我们保留打进电话的录音磁带。

e.en: An incoming plane or passenger is one that is arriving at a place. (飞机、旅客等)

ex.en: The airport was closed for incoming flights.
ex.zh: 机场为正到达的飞机而关闭。

e.en: An incoming official or government is one that has just been appointed or elected.

ex.en: ...the problems confronting the incoming government.
ex.zh: …新一届政府面临的难题。

d: adj. 进来的，到来的，收到的；即将就任的，新任的
n. 进入；到来；常作 incomings 收入，收益

e.en: Informal speech or behaviour is relaxed and friendly rather than serious, very correct, or official. 非正式的 (言行)

ex.en: She is refreshingly informal.
ex.zh: 她随和得令人耳目一新。

e.en: 非正式地 (言行)

ex.en: She was always there at half past eight, chatting informally to the children.
ex.zh: 她总是八点半钟到那儿，与孩子们随意交谈。

e.en: An informal situation is one that is relaxed and friendly and not very serious or official.

ex.en: The house has an informal atmosphere.
ex.zh: 这屋子里有一种轻松随意的气氛。

e.en: 轻松随意

ex.en: She enjoyed the relative informality of island life.
ex.zh: 她喜欢相对轻松随意的岛屿生活。

d: adj. 轻松友好的，不拘礼节的；（文字或言谈）非正式的，口语体的；（服装）休闲的，家居的；（组织、团体和安排）非官方的，非正规的

e.en: A person's or animal's hearing is the sense which makes it possible for them to be aware of sounds.

ex.en: His mind still seemed clear and his hearing was excellent.
ex.zh: 他的头脑看来依然清醒，而且听力极好。

e.en: A hearing is an official meeting which is held in order to collect facts about an incident or problem.

ex.en: After more than two hours of pandemonium, the judge adjourned the hearing until next Tuesday.
ex.zh: 在两个多小时的混乱之后，法官暂时中止了听证会，将其延至下周二。

e.en: If someone gives you a fair hearing or a hearing, they listen to you when you give your opinion about something.

ex.en: Weber gave a fair hearing to anyone who held a different opinion.
ex.zh: 韦伯让任何持有不同意见的人有发言的机会。

e.en: If someone says something in your hearing or within your hearing, you can hear what they say because they are with you or near you.

ex.en: No one spoke disparagingly of her father in her hearing.
ex.zh: 没有人在她跟前说过她父亲的坏话。

d: n. 听力，听觉；审讯，听证会；解释机会，申辩机会；听力范围
v. 听到，听见；聆听，倾听；听说，得知（动词hear 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Hearing）（英）希尔林（人名）

e.en: You use fine to describe something that you admire and think is very good.

ex.en: There is a fine view of the countryside.
ex.zh: 有一幅美丽的乡村景色。

ex.en: This is a fine book.
ex.zh: 这是一本好书。

e.en: 美好地

ex.en: They are finely engineered boats.
ex.zh: 它们是设计精美的船只。

e.en: If you say that you are fine, you mean that you are in good health or reasonably happy. 健康的;

ex.en: Lina is fine and sends you her love and best wishes.
ex.zh: 莉娜很好，她向你问候并祝福你。

e.en: If you say that something is fine, you mean that it is satisfactory or acceptable.

ex.en: The skiing is fine.
ex.zh: 滑雪挺好的。

ex.en: Everything was going to be just fine.
ex.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

d: adj. 令人满意的，可以接受的；值得崇敬的；健康的，身体好的；优质的，出色的，美好的；晴朗的；纤细的，细小的；精美的，精巧的；细微的，细密的；糟糕的；矫饰的，华而不实的
adv. 很，很好；精致地，精美地；细小地
v. 罚款，处以罚金；使变纯，使澄清；使变细，使变瘦；放晴
n. 罚金，罚款；微小颗粒

e.en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

ex.en: ...football team.
ex.zh: …一支足球队。

ex.en: ...the swim team.
ex.zh: …那支游泳队。

e.en: You can refer to any group of people who work together as a team. 团队;

ex.en: Each specialist has a team of doctors under him or her.
ex.zh: 每位专家手下都有一组医生。

d: n. （游戏或体育运动的）队，小组；工作队，工作组；（套在一起拉车的）一组牲口（尤指马）
v. 协作，合作；使（颜色、布料、衣服）相配；（套在一起拉车的）一组牲口（尤指马）

e.en: A particular case is a particular situation or incident, especially one that you are using as an individual example or instance of something.

ex.en: Surgical training takes at least nine years, or 11 in the case of obstetrics.
ex.zh: 外科培训至少需要9年，产科则要11年。

ex.en: In extreme cases, insurance companies can prosecute for fraud.
ex.zh: 在极个别情况下，保险公司会起诉骗保行为。

e.en: A case is a person or their particular problem that a doctor, social worker, or other professional is dealing with.

ex.en: Dr. Thomas Bracken describes the case of a 45-year-old Catholic priest much given to prayer whose left knee became painful.
ex.zh: 托马斯·布拉肯医生描述了那个病例：一名45岁天主教牧师由于经常祈祷导致左膝疼痛。

ex.en: Some cases of arthritis respond to a gluten-free diet.
ex.zh: 不含谷蛋白的饮食对一些关节炎病例有疗效。

e.en: If you say that someone is a sad case or a hopeless case, you mean that they are in a sad situation or a hopeless situation. (处于某种状况的)

ex.en: I knew I was going to make it – that I wasn't a hopeless case.
ex.zh: 我知道自己能行–我不是无药可救的人。

e.en: A case is a crime or mystery that the police are investigating.

ex.en: The police have several suspects in the case of five murders committed in Gainesville, Florida.
ex.zh: 警方就佛罗里达州盖恩斯维尔市的5起谋杀案已经锁定了几名嫌疑人。

d: n. 具体情况，实例；病例，病案；诉讼，官司；案件，案子；容器，箱子；事实，论据；（特定处境或品性的）人；（语法的）格
v. 围绕，包盖；（盗抢前）探察，踩点儿；装入保护容器内
【名】 （Case）（英）凯斯，（西）卡塞，（法）卡斯（人名）

e.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

ex.en: Police arrested five young men in connection with one of the attacks.
ex.zh: 警方逮捕了与其中一起袭击事件有关的5名年轻男子。

e.en: Arrest is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a substantial reward for information leading to the arrest of the bombers.
ex.zh: …用于奖励为抓捕爆炸犯提供有效信息的一大笔赏金。

ex.en: Police chased the fleeing terrorists and later made two arrests.
ex.zh: 警方追赶逃窜的恐怖分子，后来逮捕了两个人。

e.en: If something or someone arrests a process, they stop it from continuing.

ex.en: The sufferer may have to make major changes in his or her life to arrest the disease.
ex.zh: 患者可能得对自身生活作大的调整以抑制病情。

d: v. 逮捕，拘留；阻止，抑制；吸引；心跳停止
n. 逮捕，拘留；停止，终止
【名】 （Arrest）（法）阿雷斯特（人名）
n. （Bahgat）人名；（阿拉伯）巴赫贾特

e.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

ex.en: I hope they continue to fight for equal justice after I'm gone.
ex.zh: 我希望我走后他们继续为司法公正而奋斗。

ex.en: Diana and Roy Jarvis are determined to continue working when they reach retirement age.
ex.zh: 戴安娜·贾维斯和罗伊·贾维斯决心到退休年龄后还继续工作。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it does not stop. 使继续;

ex.en: He insisted that the conflict would continue until conditions were met for a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 他坚持认为冲突会持续下去，直至停火条件得到满足为止。

ex.en: Outside the building people continue their vigil, huddling around bonfires.
ex.zh: 在楼外，人们围聚在篝火旁继续守夜。

e.en: If you continue something or continue with something, you start doing it again after a break or interruption. (某人在歇息或被打断后) 继续 (做某事或某事)

ex.en: I went up to my room to continue with my packing.
ex.zh: 我上我房间去继续收拾行李。

ex.en: She looked up for a minute and then continued drawing.
ex.zh: 她抬头看了一会儿，然后继续画。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it starts again after a break or interruption. (某事在停顿或被打断后)

ex.en: He denies 18 charges. The trial continues today.
ex.zh: 他否认18项指控。审判今天继续。

d: adj. 持续的，频繁的
v. （使）继续，（使）延续；继续说，接着说；移动，延伸（continue 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A lawyer is a person who is qualified to advise people about the law and represent them in court.

ex.en: Prosecution and defence lawyers are expected to deliver closing arguments next week.
ex.zh: 原告律师和被告律师下周将要作终结辩论。

d: n. 律师
v. 从事法律工作，当律师；（律师）处理法律事务
【名】 (Lawyer)（英）劳耶（人名）
abbr. 胰腺空肠端端吻合术（caudal pancreaticojejunostomy）

e.en: Legal is used to describe things that relate to the law.

ex.en: He vowed to take legal action.
ex.zh: 他发誓要诉诸法律行动。

ex.en: ...the legal system.
ex.zh: …法律制度。

e.en: 在法律上

ex.en: It could be a bit problematic, legally speaking.
ex.zh: 从法律上说，可能是有点问题。

e.en: An action or situation that is legal is allowed or required by law.

ex.en: What I did was perfectly legal.
ex.zh: 我做的事情完全合法。

d: adj. 法律允许的，合法的；与法律有关的，法律的；（与衡平法相对）普通法或成文法确认的；神学律法的，与神学律法有关的；（纸张）标准大小的
【名】 （Legal）（法）勒加尔（人名）

e.en: A margin is the difference between two amounts, especially the difference in the number of votes or points between the winner and the loser in an election or other contest.

ex.en: They could end up with a 50-point winning margin.
ex.zh: 他们最后可能会以50点的优势获胜。

e.en: The margin of a written or printed page is the empty space at the side of the page.

ex.en: She added her comments in the margin.
ex.zh: 她在页边空白处加上了她的评语。

e.en: If there is a margin for something in a situation, there is some freedom to choose what to do or decide how to do it.

ex.en: The money is collected in a straightforward way with little margin for error.
ex.zh: 这笔钱是直接募集上来的, 几乎没有出错的余地。

e.en: The margin of a place or area is the extreme edge of it.

ex.en: ...the low coastal plain along the western margin.
ex.zh: …沿着西部边缘地带的低洼海岸平原。

d: n. 页边空白；差额，幅度；盈余，利润；余地，备用的时间（或空间、金钱等）；边缘，非主体部分；保证金，押金；额外报酬
v. 给……加上边；预付定金，交押金；页边做注释或总结
【名】 （Margin）（俄、意）马尔金（人名）

e.en: An outlet is a shop or organization which sells the goods made by a particular manufacturer or at a discount price, often direct from the manufacturer. 专卖店;

ex.en: ...the largest retail outlet in the city.
ex.zh: …该市最大的零售专卖店。

ex.en: At the factory outlet you'll find discounted items at up to 75% off regular prices.
ex.zh: 在工厂的直销店里，你会找到比常规价低75%的打折商品。

e.en: If someone has an outlet for their feelings or ideas, they have a means of expressing and releasing them. (感情的) 发泄途径; (思想的)

ex.en: Her father had found an outlet for his ambition in his work.
ex.zh: 她父亲在工作中找到了施展抱负的途径。

e.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow away. 出水口;

ex.en: ...a warm air outlet.
ex.zh: …一个热气排气口。

e.en: An outlet is a place, usually in a wall, where you can connect electrical devices to the electricity supply.

d: n. （outlet 的复数）销售点（如零售店、批发点）；排水口，排气口，出口；（美国英语）电源插座；（表达情感、发挥天赋的）途径，出路；（常作 news outlets / media outlets）新闻媒体，媒体机构；（Outlets）奥特莱斯（品牌折扣购物中心，汇集众多品牌折扣店、工厂直销店）

e.en: When you move something or when it moves, its position changes and it does not remain still.

ex.en: She moved the sheaf of papers into position.
ex.zh: 她把那捆纸移到了位置上。

ex.en: A traffic policeman asked him to move his car.
ex.zh: 一位交警让他挪动一下他的车。
