e.en: When you move, you change your position or go to a different place. 移动 (位置)

ex.en: She waited for him to get up, but he didn't move.
ex.zh: 她等着他起来，可他没有动。

ex.en: He moved around the room, putting his possessions together.
ex.zh: 他在屋里走来走去，把他的东西都放在一起。

e.en: Move is also a noun.

ex.en: The doctor made a move toward the door.
ex.zh: 医生朝门口挪了一下。

e.en: If you move, you act or you begin to do something.

ex.en: Industrialists must move fast to take advantage of new opportunities in Eastern Europe.
ex.zh: 实业家们必须快速采取行动，抓住东欧的新机遇。

d: v. （move 的第三人称单数）（使）移动，（使）改变位置；搬家，搬迁；调动；（使）变换，改变；进展；采取行动，开始行动；感动，打动；促使，激励
n. （move 的复数）措施，行动；移动，活动，动作；转变，改变；搬迁；调动；（棋类、游戏、体育等中的）一步，招法
n. 组织，团体，机构（英国英语拼法，等于 organization）；组织，筹备，安排；条理，系统性

e.en: Paid is the past tense and past participle of . (pay)
Paid workers, or people who do paid work, receive money for the work that they do.

ex.en: Apart from a small team of paid staff, the organization consists of unpaid volunteers.
ex.zh: 除了一小部分有薪酬的工作人员，这个机构还包含没有薪酬的志愿者。

e.en: If you are given paid holiday, you get your wages or salary even though you are not at work. (假期)

ex.en: He agreed to hire her at slightly over minimum wage with two weeks' paid holiday.
ex.zh: 他同意以略高于最低工资的薪资雇用她，外加两周带薪假。

e.en: If you are well paid, you receive a lot of money for the work that you do. If you are badly paid, you do not receive much money. 薪水 (高或低)

ex.en: ...a well-paid accountant.
ex.zh: …一名高薪的会计师。

ex.en: Travel and tourism employees are among the worst paid in the developed world.
ex.zh: 旅行和旅游业的雇员们在发达国家属于薪酬最低的行列。

d: adj. （工作等）有偿的，付费的；有报酬的，领取薪金的；（用在复合词中）报酬……的；（休假）带薪的
v. 支付，付费；交纳，偿还；付出代价（pay 的过去式和过去分词形式）
【名】 （Paid）（美）排德（人名）

e.en: A pound is a unit of weight used mainly in the U.S., Britain and other countries where English is spoken. One pound is equal to 0.454 kilograms. A pound of something is a quantity of it that weighs one pound. 磅 (英美等国的重量单位，等于0.454公斤);

ex.en: Her weight was under ninety pounds.
ex.zh: 她的体重不足90磅。

ex.en: ...a pound of cheese.
ex.zh: …一磅奶酪。

e.en: The pound is the unit of money which is used in Britain. It is represented by the symbol £. One British pound is divided into a hundred pence. Some other countries, for example, Egypt, also have a unit of money called a pound. 英镑 (英国货币单位，等于100便士)

ex.en: ...multi-million pound profits.
ex.zh: …数百万英镑的利润。

e.en: The pound is used to refer to the British currency system, and sometimes to the currency systems of other countries which use pounds. 镑制 (英国等国的币制)

ex.en: The pound is expected to continue to increase against most other currencies.
ex.zh: 英镑对多数其他货币的汇率有望继续上升。

e.en: A pound is a place where dogs and cats found wandering in the street are taken and kept until they are claimed by their owners. (走失猫狗的)

ex.en: ...cages at the local pound.
ex.zh: …本地走失猫狗认领处的笼子。

d: n. 磅（重量单位，pound 的复数形式）；英镑，镑（货币单位，pound 的复数形式）；重击（pound 的复数形式）；（Pounds）庞兹（人名）
v. （pound 的第三人称单数）连续猛击，猛敲；捣碎；（心脏等）怦怦跳

e.en: A personal opinion, quality, or thing belongs or relates to one particular person rather than to other people. 个人的;

ex.en: He learned this lesson the hard way – from his own personal experience.
ex.zh: 他惨痛地得到了这一教训–从他自己的亲身经历中得来的。

ex.en: That's my personal opinion.
ex.zh: 这是我的个人意见。

e.en: If you give something your personal care or attention, you deal with it yourself rather than letting someone else deal with it.

ex.en: ...a business that requires a lot of personal contact.
ex.zh: …一桩需要很多亲自联络的生意。

ex.en: ...a personal letter from the president's secretary.
ex.zh: …一封来自总统秘书的亲笔信。

e.en: Personal matters relate to your feelings, relationships, and health.

ex.en: ...teaching young people about marriage and personal relationships.
ex.zh: …教导年轻人婚姻和人际关系。

ex.en: You never allow personal problems to affect your performance.
ex.zh: 绝不容许个人问题影响你的表现。

e.en: Personal comments refer to someone's appearance or character in an offensive way.

ex.en: Newspapers resorted to personal abuse.
ex.zh: 报纸搞起了人身攻击。

d: adj. 个人的，私人的；私密的，隐私的；针对个人的，人身攻击的；人身的，身体的；人际的，私交的；供个人使用的；亲自的；有人性的；（语法）人称的
n. （报纸私人广告栏内的）私人信息发布，私人广告；（报纸或杂志上的）个人启事栏，私人广告栏（the personals）

e.en: To protect someone or something means to prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

ex.en: So, what can women do to protect themselves from heart disease?
ex.zh: 那么，女性能做什么来保护自己不患心脏病呢？

ex.en: A long thin wool coat and a purple headscarf protected her against the wind.
ex.zh: 一件薄薄的羊毛长大衣和一条紫色头巾为她挡风。

e.en: If an insurance policy protects you against an event such as death, injury, fire, or theft, the insurance company will give you or your family money if that event happens.

ex.en: Many manufacturers have policies to protect themselves against blackmailers.
ex.zh: 许多制造商都有为敲诈勒索保险的保单。

d: v. 保护，防护；（制订法律）保护；投保，为……买保险；对……实行贸易保护；（计算机）保护（数据或储存库）；防守

e.en: arranged or planned according to a programme, timetable, etc (根据节目、时间表等)事先安排的;

ex.en: a scheduled meeting
a change to the scheduled programmes on TV tonight

d: adj. 预先安排的，按时刻表的；（尤指航班）定期的；（建筑，历史遗迹）列入文物保护单位的
v. 安排；将……列入计划表（或时间表等）；把（建筑物）列为文物保护单位（schedule 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way. (正式或明确的口头或书面) 陈述;

ex.en: Andrew now disowns that statement, saying he was depressed when he made it.
ex.zh: 安德鲁现在否认了那个声明，说那是自己心情沮丧时作的。

e.en: A statement is an official or formal announcement that is issued on a particular occasion. (在特定场合的官方或正式的)

ex.en: The statement by the military denied any involvement in last night's attack.
ex.zh: 军方的声明否认其与昨晚的袭击有任何关系。

e.en: You can refer to the official account of events which a suspect or a witness gives to the police as a statement. (嫌犯或证人向警方提供的) 陈述;

ex.en: The 350-page report was based on statements from witnesses to the events.
ex.zh: 这份350页的报告基于该事件目击者的证词。

e.en: If you describe an action or thing as a statement, you mean that it clearly expresses a particular opinion or idea that you have. (某观点的)

ex.en: The following recipe is a statement of another kind – food is fun!
ex.zh: 下面的食谱是另一种表述–食物就是乐趣！

d: n. statement 的复数：陈述，声明，报告；说明，说法，表态；证词；结算单，报表，财务报表；计算机程序中的语句，指令；通过行为、衣着等非言语方式作出的表达；陈述句

e.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

ex.en: New evidence showed the police lied at the trial.
ex.zh: 新的证据表明警方在审判时撒了谎。

ex.en: I have the right to a trial with a jury of my peers.
ex.zh: 我有权要求由和我一样的平民组成的陪审团参加审判。

e.en: A trial is an experiment in which you test something by using it or doing it for a period of time to see how well it works. If something is on trial, it is being tested in this way.

ex.en: They have been treated with this drug in clinical trials.
ex.zh: 他们在临床试验中一直接受这种药物的治疗。

ex.en: I took the car out for a trial on the roads.
ex.zh: 我把车开出去在公路上试了一下。

e.en: If you refer to the trials of a situation, you mean the unpleasant things that you experience in it.

ex.en: ...the trials of adolescence.
ex.zh: …青春期的磨难。

e.en: to test or make experimental use of (something)

ex.en: the idea has been trialled in several schools

d: n. 审判，审理；试验，试用；（对人的忍耐、自制力的）考验，磨练；烦人的事，惹麻烦的人；预赛，选拔赛；（检验车手技能的）摩托车障碍检验赛；（动物的）比赛，表演
v. 测试，试验；（马、狗等动物）参加比赛
adj. 试验性的
【名】 （Trial）（法）特里亚尔（人名）

e.en: In a court of law, the verdict is the decision that is given by the jury or judge at the end of a trial.

ex.en: The jury returned a unanimous guilty verdict.
ex.zh: 该陪审团作出了一份一致通过的有罪裁决。

e.en: Someone's verdict on something is their opinion of it, after thinking about it or investigating it.

ex.en: The doctor's verdict was that he was entirely healthy.
ex.zh: 这名医生的判断是他完全是健康的。

d: n. （法庭的）裁定，判决；（权威的）评判，定论；意见，决定

e.en: An agency is a business that provides a service on behalf of other businesses.

ex.en: We had to hire maids through an agency.
ex.zh: 我们得通过代理公司雇用女佣。

e.en: An agency is a government organization responsible for a certain area of administration.

ex.en: She is calling for a collaboration of local, state and federal agencies to deal with the problem.
ex.zh: 她在呼吁地方、州和联邦等各级政府通力合作来处理这个问题。

d: n. 代理，代理处，代理机构；政府机构（agency 的复数）

e.en: If something is done to you in absentia, it is done to you when you are not present.

ex.en: He was tried in absentia and sentenced to seven years in prison.
ex.zh: 他在未出庭的情况下被判七年监禁。

d: n. 缺席，不在场（多用于固定短语 in absentia，指在当事人未出庭或不在场时进行审判、判刑等）；失踪；（医学）失神
n. （Abdel）人名；（阿拉伯、哈萨、塔吉、吉尔、乌兹、阿塞、土库、乍、塞）阿卜杜勒

e.en: If people or animals are alive, they are not dead.

ex.en: She does not know if he is alive or dead.
ex.zh: 她不知道他是活还是死。

e.en: If you say that someone seems alive, you mean that they seem to be very lively and to enjoy everything that they do.

ex.en: She seemed more alive and looked forward to getting up in the morning.
ex.zh: 她似乎更有活力，并且期待着一早就起来。

e.en: If an activity, organization, or situation is alive, it continues to exist or function.

ex.en: The big factories are trying to stay alive by cutting costs.
ex.zh: 大工厂试图通过减少开支以维持生存。

e.en: If a place is alive with something, there are a lot of people or things there and it seems busy or exciting. 满是 (人或物，显得繁忙或兴奋的)

ex.en: The river was alive with birds.
ex.zh: 这条河流周围满是各种鸟类。

d: adj. 活着的；仍然存在的；活跃的，充满活力的；热闹的；尚未失败，仍有成功机会；注意到的

e.en: If a group of people ambush their enemies, they attack them after hiding and waiting for them.

ex.en: The Guatemalan army says rebels ambushed and killed 10 patrolmen.
ex.zh: 危地马拉军方称叛军伏击并杀死了10名巡逻兵。

e.en: An ambush is an attack on someone by people who have been hiding and waiting for them.

ex.en: Three civilians were killed in guerrilla ambushes.
ex.zh: 3名平民在游击队的伏击中丧生。

d: v. 伏击，埋伏（动词 ambush 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 遭伏击的，中埋伏的

e.en: If you attend a meeting or other event, you are present at it. 参加;

ex.en: Thousands of people attended the funeral.
ex.zh: 数千人参加了葬礼。

ex.en: The meeting will be attended by finance ministers from many countries.
ex.zh: 这次会议将有许多国家的财政部长出席。

e.en: If you attend an institution such as a school, college, or church, you go there regularly. 上 (学); 去 (教堂)

ex.en: They attended college together at the University of Pennsylvania.
ex.zh: 他们一起就读于宾夕法尼亚大学。

e.en: If you attend to something, you deal with it. If you attend to someone who is hurt or injured, you care for them. 处理;

ex.en: He took a short leave of absence to attend to personal business.
ex.zh: 他休了一个短假去处理私事。

d: v. （attend 的过去式和过去分词）出席，参加；随同，陪同（较正式，常用 be attended by）；经常去，定期去（学校、教堂等），亦指就读于（学校）；用于 attend to/attend on 时表示处理、照料
adj. 有人照料的；有人陪同的；（活动等）参加人数多的（常作 well attended）

e.en: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of prisoners by the state.

ex.en: Activists who were involved in crimes of violence will not automatically be granted amnesty.
ex.zh: 参与暴力犯罪的活跃分子不会被自动地给予赦免。

e.en: An amnesty is a period of time during which people can admit to a crime or give up weapons without being punished.

ex.en: The government has announced an immediate amnesty for rebel fighters.
ex.zh: 政府已经宣布了一个对叛军战士的即刻赦免时段。

d: n. 大赦，特赦，官方赦免；（违法者可自首、上缴武器或补缴欠税而不受处罚的）赦免期
vt. 对……实行大赦，赦免

e.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

ex.en: It made sense to appoint a banker to this job.
ex.zh: 任命一位银行家做这项工作是合理的。

ex.en: The president has appointed a civilian as defence secretary.
ex.zh: 总统任命了一位平民做国防部长。

d: v. 任命，委任，指派；指定，约定；装备，布置（appoint 的现在分词/动名词形式）
adj. 委任的，负责任命的（多作定语）

e.en: Avenue is sometimes used in the names of streets. The written abbreviation  is also used.

ex.en: ...the most expensive apartments on Park Avenue.
ex.zh: …派克大街上最昂贵的公寓。

e.en: An avenue is a wide, straight road, especially one with trees on either side.

d: n. 大街，大道（街道名称中常大写）；（尤指通向大宅或庄园的）林荫道，林荫大道；途径，渠道，办法（avenue 的复数）

e.en: A bar is a place where you can buy and drink alcoholic drinks.

ex.en: ...Devil's Herd, the city's most popular country and western bar.
ex.zh: …“魔鬼群”，全城最受欢迎的西部乡村酒吧。

e.en: A bar is a room in a hotel or other establishment where alcoholic drinks are served. (旅馆等的)

ex.en: Last night in the hotel there was some talk in the bar about drugs.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上，在旅馆的酒吧间里有人说起毒品了。

e.en: A bar is a counter on which alcoholic drinks are served.

ex.en: Michael was standing alone by the bar when Brian rejoined him.
ex.zh: 布赖恩回来的时候，迈克尔正独自站在吧台旁。

e.en: A bar is a long, straight, stiff piece of metal. (金属)

ex.en: ...a brick building with bars across the ground floor windows.
ex.zh: …底楼窗户有铁栅穿过的一座砖楼。

d: n. bar 的复数形式：酒吧，酒馆；吧台；长条，棒，条块；栅栏，栏杆；障碍；behind bars（在狱中，坐牢）；（音乐）小节；图表或界面中的条、栏；巴（压强单位）；马齿龈；（体操器械，如 parallel bars 双杠、uneven bars 高低杠）；monkey bars（猴架，攀架）；（Bars）人名：（匈）鲍尔什；（法、德、土）巴尔斯
v. （bar 的第三人称单数）禁止；阻挡；闩（门）
n. （Azhari）人名；（阿拉伯、伊朗）爱资哈里

e.en: The border between two countries or regions is the dividing line between them. Sometimes the border also refers to the land close to this line. 边界;

ex.en: They fled across the border.
ex.zh: 他们越过边界逃走了。

ex.en: Soldiers had temporarily closed the border between the two countries.
ex.zh: 士兵们已暂时封闭了两国的边界。

e.en: A country that borders another country, a sea, or a river is next to it.

ex.en: ...the European and Arab countries bordering the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: …地中海沿岸的欧洲国家和阿拉伯国家。

e.en: Border on means the same as .

ex.en: Both republics border on the Black Sea.
ex.zh: 这两个共和国都与黑海毗邻。

e.en: A border is a strip or band around the edge of something.

ex.en: ...pillowcases trimmed with a hand-crocheted border.
ex.zh: …镶有一道手工钩制花边的枕套。

d: n. [地理]边界；边缘地区（border 的复数）
v. 毗连；邻接；给……镶边（border 的第三人称单数）

e.en: When a wind or breeze blows, the air moves.

ex.en: A chill wind blew at the top of the hill.
ex.zh: 山顶上刮了一阵凉飕飕的风。

e.en: If the wind blows something somewhere or if it blows there, the wind moves it there. 把…吹到;

ex.en: The wind blew her hair back from her forehead.
ex.zh: 风把她额头上的头发向后吹。

ex.en: Sand blew in our eyes.
ex.zh: 沙子吹进了我们眼里。

e.en: If you blow, you send out a stream of air from your mouth.

ex.en: Danny rubbed his arms and blew on his fingers to warm them.
ex.zh: 丹尼搓着胳膊，向他的手指上呵气来暖手。

e.en: If you blow something somewhere, you move it by sending out a stream of air from your mouth. (人)

ex.en: He picked up his mug and blew off the steam.
ex.zh: 他端起杯子吹掉蒸汽。

d: v. （风）刮，吹；（用嘴）吹气；吹响，吹奏；毁掉，炸毁；（轮胎）爆开，爆裂；（保险丝）烧断，熔化；擤（鼻子）；浪费，挥霍（金钱）；出错，错失机会；泄露，暴露；迅速离开（某地）；用力投（球）；讨厌，糟糕；开花；（鲸鱼）喷水；吹制（玻璃）；（苍蝇）产卵于
n. 大风，强风；吹气，擤鼻子；猛击，一击；奋斗，努力；打击，挫折；开花，开花期；爵士乐演奏；大麻；（炼钢用语）吹炼

e.en: secure relationship; affinity (esp in the phrase a sense of belonging) 稳定关系; 归属感，尤用于短语a sense of belonging

d: n. 归属感，稳定关系（常用于 a sense of belonging）；所有物，附属物（常用复数 belongings）
v. （belong 的现在分词）属于，归……所有；属于（某团体或类别），（有资格）成为其成员；应在（某处），应归入，被适当地置于；适应，合得来；是……的合法财产，应付给；（比赛或时间）被……控制

e.en: Brotherhood is the affection and loyalty that you feel for people who you have something in common with. 兄弟情谊;

ex.en: People threw flowers into the river between the two countries as a symbolic act of brotherhood.
ex.zh: 人们把花扔进两国之间的河里，以此作为兄弟情谊的象征性的行为。

e.en: A brotherhood is an organization whose members all have the same political aims and beliefs or the same job or profession. 兄弟会;

ex.en: ...the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers.
ex.zh: …机车工程师同业会。

d: n. 兄弟关系，手足情谊；兄弟会，同业会，工会；四海之内皆兄弟的信念；同行，同业者；（Brotherhood）人名；布拉泽胡德

e.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

ex.en: The new government's first challenge is the economy.
ex.zh: 新政府面临的第一项挑战是经济。

e.en: A challenge to something is a questioning of its truth or value. A challenge to someone is a questioning of their authority.

ex.en: The demonstrators have now made a direct challenge to the authority of the government.
ex.zh: 示威者现已对该政府的权威性提出了直截了当的质疑。

e.en: If someone rises to the challenge, they act in response to a difficult situation which is new to them and are successful.

ex.en: The new Germany must rise to the challenge of its enhanced responsibilities.
ex.zh: 新德国必须奋起应对更艰巨的挑战。

e.en: If you challenge ideas or people, you question their truth, value, or authority.

ex.en: Democratic leaders have challenged the president to sign the bill.
ex.zh: 民主党领导人对总统签署这项法案存有质疑。

ex.en: The move was immediately challenged by two of the republics.
ex.zh: 这项提案立即遭到了这两个共和国的质疑。

d: n. 挑战，难题；挑战书，比赛邀请；质疑，质询；喝停盘查
v. 挑战，向……下战书；质疑，拒绝接受；盘问，查问；考验
adv. 小心地，仔细地

e.en: When you chill something or when it chills, you lower its temperature so that it becomes colder but does not freeze. 使冷却;

ex.en: Chill the fruit salad until serving time.
ex.zh: 上菜前把水果色拉冷却。

ex.en: These doughs can be rolled out while you wait for the pastry to chill.
ex.zh: 当你等待油酥面团冷却时，可以擀平这些生面团。

e.en: When cold weather or something cold chills a person or a place, it makes that person or that place feel very cold.

ex.en: The marble floor was beginning to chill me.
ex.zh: 大理石的地板开始让我感到很冷。

ex.en: Wade placed his chilled hands on the radiator and warmed them.
ex.zh: 韦德把他冰冷的双手放到散热器上取暖。

e.en: If something sends a chill through you, it gives you a sudden feeling of fear or anxiety.

ex.en: The violence used against the students sent a chill through Indonesia.
ex.zh: 对学生使用暴力使得整个印度尼西亚不寒而栗。

e.en: A chill is a mild illness which can give you a slight fever and headache.

ex.en: He caught a chill while performing at a rain-soaked open-air venue.
ex.zh: 他在一个被雨浸湿的露天场地表演时着了风寒。

d: n. 寒冷，寒意；着凉，受寒；害怕，担心；冷漠，敌意；冷模，冷模部件
v. （使）冷却，冰镇；使很冷；惊吓，使恐惧；放松；（使）沮丧，（使）扫兴
adj. 冷飕飕的；令人紧张的，令人害怕的

e.en: If a situation is charged, it is filled with emotion and therefore very tense or exciting.

ex.en: There was a highly charged atmosphere.
ex.zh: 气氛极度亢奋。

ex.en: A wedding is an emotionally charged situation.
ex.zh: 婚礼是一个激动人心的场合。

e.en: Charged particles carry an electrical charge.

ex.en: ...negatively charged ions.
ex.zh: ...负离子。

d: adj. 引起强烈感情的，气氛紧张的；充电的，带电的
v. 充电；使……承担责任；控告，指控（charge 的和过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He claimed that it was all a conspiracy against him.
ex.zh: 他声称这完全是一个针对他的阴谋。

ex.en: A man claiming to be a journalist threatened to reveal details about her private life.
ex.zh: 一个自称是记者的男人威胁要公开她的私生活细节。

e.en: If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth. 声称 (对某事负责或应得荣誉)

ex.en: An underground organization has claimed responsibility for the bomb explosion.
ex.zh: 一个地下组织已声称对炸弹爆炸事件负责。

e.en: If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.

ex.en: Now they are returning to claim what was theirs.
ex.zh: 现在他们回来索要原本属于他们的东西。

e.en: If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.

ex.en: Zhuang claimed the record in 54.64 seconds.
ex.zh: 庄创造了54.64秒的纪录。

d: v. （动词 claim 的现在分词/动名词）声称，宣称，自称；要求给予，索取；认领，领取（行李等）；索赔（赔偿等）；理应获得，赢得；（战争、疾病、事故等）夺走（生命）

e.en: The closure of a place such as a business or factory is the permanent ending of the work or activity there. 倒闭;

ex.en: ...the closure of the steel mill.
ex.zh: …这家钢厂的关闭。

ex.en: ...protests against the proposed pit closures.
ex.zh: …针对关闭矿井计划的抗议。

e.en: The closure of a road or border is the blocking of it in order to prevent people from using it. (道路、边界等的)

ex.en: Overnight storms left many streets underwater and forced the closure of road tunnels in the city.
ex.zh: 一夜的暴风雨使城市里的许多街道都淹没在水中，公路隧道被迫封闭。

e.en: If someone achieves closure, they succeed in accepting something bad that has happened to them.

ex.en: I asked McKean if the reunion was meant to achieve closure.
ex.zh: 我问迈可基恩再度联合是否意味着认栽。

d: n. （永久的）关闭，倒闭；（尤指通路、边境的）封锁；（讨论、写作、活动或事件的）结尾；（事件或一段时间的）了结，解脱感；（立法院）辩论终止提付表决；认栽；闭锁物（如帽子、领带）；（夹克等）闭合方式
v. （在立法会议上）终止（辩论，发言）；使终止

e.en: A condemned man or woman is going to be executed.

ex.en: ...prison officers who had sat with the condemned man during his last days.
ex.zh: …在那个死囚临终前的日子看管他的狱警们。

d: adj. 已被定罪（尤指被判死刑）的；受谴责的，被指责的；被官方宣布为危险而不宜使用或居住的（指建筑物、食品等）
v. condemn 的过去式和过去分词：谴责，指责；判处（刑罚）；宣告（建筑物等）不适用；be condemned to 被迫承受，注定要
n. the condemned 被判处死刑的人，死刑犯，死囚

e.en: A committee is a group of people who meet to make decisions or plans for a larger group or organization that they represent.

ex.en: ...the school yearbook committee.
ex.zh: …学校年鉴编委会。

d: n. 委员会；受托人，监护人；精神病者监护人

e.en: A courtroom is a room in which a legal court meets. 审判室;

d: n. 法庭，审判室（法院开庭审理案件的房间）

e.en: A crushing defeat, burden, or disappointment is a very great or severe one.

ex.en: ...since their crushing defeat in the local elections.
ex.zh: …自从他们在地方选举中遭到毁灭性的挫败以来。

d: adj. （强调糟糕或严重的程度）惨重的，毁坏性的，压倒性的；（评论、回答等）强烈批评的
v. （crush 的现在分词）压坏，压伤；把……挤入；压碎，捣碎；变皱，起皱；破坏，毁坏（某人的信心或幸福）
n. （不可数）压碎，粉碎；压制，镇压
adv. 现时，当前

e.en: When people such as the police detain someone, they keep them in a place under their control.

ex.en: Police have detained two suspects in connection with the attack.
ex.zh: 警方拘留了2名与该袭击事件有关的嫌疑人。

e.en: To detain someone means to delay them, for example, by talking to them.

ex.en: Millson stood up. "Thank you. We won't detain you any further, Mrs. Stebbing."
ex.zh: 米尔森站起来。“谢谢您。我们不再耽搁您了，斯特宾太太。”

d: v. 被扣留，拘留，扣留（detain 的过去式和过去分词）；耽搁，延误
adj. 被拘留的，被扣留的
v. （英国英语拼写）使不稳定，使动摇；（局势、制度等）变得不稳定

e.en: If you have a dozen things, you have twelve of them.

ex.en: You will be able to take ten dozen bottles free of duty through customs.
ex.zh: 你可以携带120瓶免税通过海关。

e.en: You can refer to a group of approximately twelve things or people as a dozen. You can refer to a group of approximately six things or people as half a dozen.

ex.en: In half a dozen words, he had explained the bond that linked them.
ex.zh: 他用五六个字解释了将他们联系在一起的那种关系。

e.en: If you refer to dozens of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are very many of them.

ex.en: ...a storm which destroyed dozens of homes and buildings.
ex.zh: …一场毁坏了许多房屋和建筑物的暴风雨。

e.en: You can also use dozens as a pronoun.

ex.en: Just as revealing are Mr. Johnson's portraits, of which there are dozens.
ex.zh: 透过约翰逊先生的许多肖像画，同样也可以了解其人。

d: n. 一打，十二个；大量，许多；十多个

e.en: You use entire when you want to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population. 全部的;

ex.en: He had spent his entire life in China as a doctor.
ex.zh: 他整个一生都在中国做医生。

ex.en: There are only 60 swimming pools in the entire country.
ex.zh: 整个国家仅有60个游泳池。

d: adj. 全部的，整个的；完全的，绝对的；（公马）未经阉割的；（叶子）全缘的，边缘光滑的
n. 未经阉割的公马，种马
【名】 （Entire）（英）恩泰尔（人名）
n. 迅速增加，上涨；升级，恶化

e.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity. 使…加剧;

ex.en: Both unions and management fear the dispute could escalate.
ex.zh: 各工会与资方都害怕争端会加剧。

ex.en: The protests escalated into five days of rioting.
ex.zh: 抗议逐渐升级为5天的暴乱。

e.en: 加剧

ex.en: The threat of nuclear escalation remains.
ex.zh: 核升级的威胁依然存在。

d: v. （使）变得严重，（使）升级；迅速增加，迅速增长；逐步增强，逐步升高
vt.对……进行事实查核（factcheck 的现在分词）
vi.进行事实查核（factcheck 的现在分词）

e.en: To eviscerate a person or animal means to remove their internal organs, such as their heart, lungs, and stomach. 取出(人或动物)

ex.en: ...strangling and eviscerating rabbits for the pot.
ex.zh: ...勒死并取出兔子的内脏以便下锅。

e.en: If you say that something will eviscerate an organization or system, you are emphasizing that it will make the organization or system much weaker or much less powerful. 重创(组织或体系)

ex.en: Democrats say the petition will eviscerate state government.
ex.zh: 民主党人说该请求将重创政府的元气。

d: n. 去内脏
v. 去内脏（eviscerate 的 ing 形式）

e.en: The expression of ideas or feelings is the showing of them through words, actions, or artistic activities.

ex.en: Laughter is one of the most infectious expressions of emotion.
ex.zh: 笑是最具感染力的感情表达方式之一。

ex.en: ...the rights of the individual to freedom of expression.
ex.zh: …个人表达自由权。

e.en: Your expression is the way that your face looks at a particular moment. It shows what you are thinking or feeling.

ex.en: Levin sat there, an expression of sadness on his face.
ex.zh: 莱文坐在那里，神情忧伤。

e.en: Expression is the showing of feeling when you are acting, singing, or playing a musical instrument. (艺术表演中的)

ex.en: I think I put more expression into my lyrics than a lot of other singers do.
ex.zh: 我认为我比许多其他歌手在歌词中注入了更多的情感表达。

e.en: An expression is a word or phrase. 字词;

ex.en: She spoke in a quiet voice but used remarkably coarse expressions.
ex.zh: 她说话声音很轻，但使用了非常粗俗的言辞。

d: n. 表达，表示；表情，神情；（表演、歌唱或演奏时的）情感表现；词语，措词；式，表达式；挤压
n. 法塔赫（巴勒斯坦武装力量）

e.en: If something is founded on a particular thing, it is based on it.

ex.en: The criticisms are founded on facts as well as on convictions.
ex.zh: 这些批评是以事实和信念为基础的。

d: adj. 有基础的
v. 建立；创立（found 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them because you want to go to the same place.

ex.en: We followed him up the steps into a large hall.
ex.zh: 我们跟他上了台阶，进入一个大厅。

ex.en: Please follow me, madam.
ex.zh: 夫人，请跟我来。

e.en: If you follow someone who is going somewhere, you move along behind them without their knowledge, in order to catch them or find out where they are going.

ex.en: She realized that the Mercedes was following her.
ex.zh: 她意识到那辆奔驰在跟踪她。

e.en: If you follow someone to a place where they have recently gone and where they are now, you go to join them there.

ex.en: He followed Janice to New York, where she was preparing an exhibition.
ex.zh: 他跟随贾妮丝去了纽约，她正在那儿准备一个展览。

e.en: An event, activity, or period of time that follows a particular thing happens or comes after that thing, at a later time. 在…后到来;

ex.en: ...the rioting and looting that followed the verdict.
ex.zh: …判决之后发生的暴乱和抢劫。

ex.en: Other problems may follow.
ex.zh: 其它问题也许会随之而来。

d: v. 跟随，跟在……后面；在……后发生，接着发生；沿（路、路线等）行进，循着（地图、标志）走；追逐，跟踪，追踪；遵守，遵循，按照（规则）执行；领会，理解，跟得上；密切注意，关注；追随，拥护，以……为榜样；是……的逻辑结果，由此得出；从事（职业）（follow 的第三人称单数）
adv. （as follows）如下，如下所述
n. 跟随；遵照（follow 的复数）；（what follows）下列所述，接下来的内容；（Follows）福洛斯（人名）

e.en: If something is frequent, it happens often.

ex.en: Bordeaux is on the main Paris-Madrid line so there are frequent trains.
ex.zh: 波尔多位于巴黎至马德里的铁路主干线上，因此有频繁的列车。

e.en: 经常地

ex.en: Iron and folic acid supplements are frequently given to pregnant women.
ex.zh: 铁和叶酸补充剂常给孕妇服用。

d: adj. 频繁的，经常性的；间隔很近的
v. 常去，常出入于

e.en: Fully means to the greatest degree or extent possible.

ex.en: She was fully aware of my thoughts.
ex.zh: 她完全了解了我的想法。

e.en: You use fully to say that a process is completely finished.

ex.en: He had still not fully recovered.
ex.zh: 他还没有彻底康复。

e.en: If you describe, answer, or deal with something fully, you leave out nothing that should be mentioned or dealt with.

ex.en: Fiers promised to testify fully and truthfully.
ex.zh: 菲尔斯承诺毫无保留地、如实地作证。

d: adv. 充分地，完全地，彻底地；（强调数量）整整，至少
【名】 （Fully）（法）菲利（人名）

e.en: Freedom is the state of being allowed to do what you want to do. Freedoms are instances of this.

ex.en: ...freedom of speech.
ex.zh: …言论自由。

ex.en: The United Nations Secretary-General has spoken of the need for individual freedoms and human rights.
ex.zh: 联合国秘书长谈到了个人自由和人权的必要性。

e.en: When prisoners or slaves are set free or escape, they gain their freedom.

ex.en: ...the agreement worked out by the UN, under which all hostages and detainees would gain their freedom.
ex.zh: …联合国制定的协议，据此所有人质和被扣押者应获得自由。

e.en: Freedom from something you do not want means not being affected by it.

ex.en: ...all the freedom from pain that medicine could provide.
ex.zh: …药物所能免除的所有痛苦。

d: n. 自由（freedom 的复数，指各项自由权）；（民航）航权，即空中自由（freedoms of the air），常概括为五大航权

e.en: A handful of people or things is a small number of them.

ex.en: He surveyed the handful of customers at the bar.
ex.zh: 他打量着吧台边仅有的几位顾客。

e.en: A handful of something is the amount of it that you can hold in your hand.

ex.en: She scooped up a handful of sand and let it trickle through her fingers.
ex.zh: 她抓了一把沙子，然后让它们从指缝间慢慢漏掉。

e.en: If you say that someone, especially a child, is a handful, you mean that they are difficult to control. 难管的人 (尤指小孩)

ex.en: Zara can be a handful sometimes.
ex.zh: 扎拉有时会很难管教。

d: n. 一把；少数，少量； 难以控制的人（或事物）

e.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

ex.en: A woman reporter complained one of them sexually harassed her in the locker room.
ex.zh: 一名女记者抱怨说，他们当中的一个在更衣室里对她进行了性骚扰。

d: v. 骚扰；不断攻击（敌人）

e.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

ex.en: A woman reporter complained one of them sexually harassed her in the locker room.
ex.zh: 一名女记者抱怨说，他们当中的一个在更衣室里对她进行了性骚扰。

d: v. harass 的现在分词/动名词：骚扰；扰乱；使烦恼
adj. 骚扰性的；令人烦扰的
n. （Hossam）人名；（阿拉伯）胡萨姆
n. 哈桑，哈山（男子名；亦用作姓氏）

e.en: Harassment is behaviour which is intended to trouble or annoy someone, for example repeated attacks on them or attempts to cause them problems.

ex.en: Another survey found that 51 percent of women had experienced some form of sexual harassment in their working lives.
ex.zh: 另一份调查显示有51%的女性在其职业生涯中曾遭遇过某种形式的性骚扰。

d: n. 骚扰

e.en: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount. 使增加;

ex.en: The population continues to increase.
ex.zh: 人口持续增长。

ex.en: Japan's industrial output increased by 2%.
ex.zh: 日本的工业产量增长了2%。

e.en: If there is an increase in the number, level, or amount of something, it becomes greater.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in productivity.
ex.zh: …生产率的急速增长。

e.en: If something is on the increase, it is happening more often or becoming greater in number or intensity.

ex.en: Crime is on the increase.
ex.zh: 犯罪活动日益猖獗。

d: v. 增长，增强，增大（increase 的现在分词）

e.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are eager and determined to do it.

ex.en: The rebels are obviously intent on keeping up the pressure.
ex.zh: 反叛分子显然决心继续施加压力。

e.en: If someone does something in an intent way, they pay great attention to what they are doing.

ex.en: She looked from one intent face to another.
ex.zh: 她看着一张张专注的面孔。

e.en: 专注地

ex.en: He listened intently, then slammed down the phone.
ex.zh: 他专注地听着，然后猛地把电话放下。

e.en: A person's intent is their intention to do something.

ex.en: The timing of this strong statement of intent on arms control is crucial.
ex.zh: 发表这项意图实施军备控制的强硬声明的时机至关重要。

d: adj. 专注的，专心致志的；坚决的；急切的
n. 目的，意图；故意

e.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem. (重要的) 法案;

ex.en: Local initiatives to help young people have been inadequate.
ex.zh: 当地对年轻人的扶助法案一直不够完善。

e.en: In a fight or contest, if you have the initiative, you are in a better position than your opponents to decide what to do next.

ex.en: We have the initiative; we intend to keep it.
ex.zh: 我们拥有主动权；我们想要保持主动权。

e.en: If you have initiative, you have the ability to decide what to do next and to do it, without needing other people to tell you what to do.

ex.en: She was disappointed by his lack of initiative.
ex.zh: 她对他缺乏主动性感到失望。

e.en: An initiative is a political procedure in which a group of citizens propose a new law or a change to the law, which all voters can then vote on.

ex.en: If they reject or ignore the initiative, the public will vote on it in November.
ex.zh: 如果他们拒绝或无视公民立法提案程序，公众将于11月对它进行投票表决。

d: n. 措施，倡议；主动性，积极性；主动权；（美国某些州的）公民立法提案程序

e.en: A jailer is a person who is in charge of a jail and the prisoners in it.

d: n．狱卒，看守犯人的人：负责看管监狱中囚犯的人。

e.en: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

ex.en: Agents will raise the issue of prize-money for next year's world championships.
ex.zh: 代理商们会提出明年世界锦标赛的奖金问题。

ex.en: A key issue for higher education in the 1990s is the need for greater diversity of courses.
ex.zh: 20世纪90年代高等教育的一个关键问题是需要使课程更加多样化。

e.en: If something is the issue, it is the thing you consider to be the most important part of a situation or discussion.

ex.en: I was earning a lot of money, but that was not the issue.
ex.zh: 我是挣着很多钱，但那不是问题的关键。

ex.en: Do not draw it on the chart, however, as this will confuse the issue.
ex.zh: 但是不要把它画在图表上，因为这将使要点模糊不清。

e.en: An issue of something such as a magazine or newspaper is the version of it that is published, for example, in a particular month or on a particular day. (杂志或报刊的)

ex.en: The growing problem is underlined in the latest issue of the Scientific American.
ex.zh: 这一日益严重的问题在最新一期的《科学美国人》上得到强调。

e.en: If you issue a statement or a warning, you make it known formally or publicly. 发表 (声明); 发出 (警告)

ex.en: Last night he issued a statement denying the allegations.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上，他发表了一项声明否认那些说法。

ex.en: The government issued a warning that the strikers should end their action or face dismissal.
ex.zh: 该政府发出了警告，罢工者们应停止他们的行动，否则将被免职。

d: v. 发布，发表，发出；发给，分发，配发；出版；发行（新的一批）；将……诉诸法律；签发（法律文书）；流出，冒出；由……产生（issue 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已发行的（股票、证券等）；已签发的（证件、文件等）

e.en: A judge is the person in a court of law who decides how the law should be applied, for example how criminals should be punished.

ex.en: The judge adjourned the hearing until next Tuesday.
ex.zh: 法官将听证延至下星期二。

e.en: A judge is a person who decides who will be the winner of a competition.

ex.en: A panel of judges is now selecting the finalists.
ex.zh: 裁判组现在正在选拔参加决赛的选手。

e.en: If you judge something such as a competition, you decide who or what is the winner.

ex.en: He was asked to judge a literary competition.
ex.zh: 他被邀请评判一场文学竞赛。

e.en: If you judge something or someone, you form an opinion about them after you have examined the evidence or thought carefully about them.

ex.en: It will take a few more years to judge the impact of these ideas.
ex.zh: 还需要再过几年才能判断这些思想的影响。

ex.en: I am ready to judge any book on its merits.
ex.zh: 我会根据每本书自身的性质来对其进行评判。

d: n. 法官，审判官；裁判员，评判员；鉴定人，行家；士师（古犹太人领袖称谓）
v. 判断，认为；裁判，评判；估计，估算（数量、距离、尺寸等）；批评，指责；审判，审理
【名】 （Judge）（英、美、爱）贾奇（人名）

e.en: conformity or harmony (esp in the phrases in or out of keeping) 一致;

d: n. 保管，监护，照管，保存；拥有；维持；保护；一致，协调
v. （keep 的现在分词／动名词）保持，维持，保存；拥有，占有；遵守；抚养；兑现；记（日记）

e.en: A lawyer is a person who is qualified to advise people about the law and represent them in court.

ex.en: Prosecution and defence lawyers are expected to deliver closing arguments next week.
ex.zh: 原告律师和被告律师下周将要作终结辩论。

d: n. 律师（lawyer 的复数）

e.en: A licence is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something. 许可;

ex.en: The judge fined the man and suspended his licence.
ex.zh: 法官罚了那个人的款，并且吊销了他的执照。

ex.en: The company has applied to the FDA for a licence to sell the drug.
ex.zh: 该公司已向美国食品及药品管理局申请了销售药物的许可证。

e.en: If you say that something gives someone licence or a licence to act in a particular way, you mean that it gives them an excuse to behave in an irresponsible or excessive way.

ex.en: Partition would give licence to other aggressors in other conflicts.
ex.zh: 分裂组织给其他侵略者提供其他冲突的借口。

d: n. 许可证，执照；许可，准许；（言论或行动的）自由，不受拘束；（做错事的）诱因，借口
v. 给……发许可证，批准；就……发许可证；按协议特许，授权
v. 举债经营；充分利用（资源、观点等）（leverage 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. （金融／商业）使用财务杠杆的，高杠杆的，举债的（常用 highly leveraged 表示高杠杆；固定搭配 leveraged buyout 指杠杆收购）

e.en: If you talk about the magnitude of something, you are talking about its great size, scale, or importance. (尺寸、规模、重要性等)

ex.en: An operation of this magnitude is going to be difficult.
ex.zh: 一个这么大的手术会很难的。

e.en: You can use order of magnitude when you are giving an approximate idea of the amount or importance of something. 重要级;

ex.en: America and Russia do not face a problem of the same order of magnitude as Japan.
ex.zh: 美俄两国没有面临与日本同样的重要级别的问题。

d: n. 巨大，重要性；震级；规模，大小；数量，数值；（恒星的）亮度，星等

e.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

ex.en: After the divorce, their father still maintained close contact with the boys.
ex.zh: 离婚后，他们的父亲仍和儿子们保持着密切联系。

e.en: If you say that someone maintains that something is true, you mean that they have stated their opinion strongly but not everyone agrees with them or believes them. 坚持说;

ex.en: He has maintained that the money was donated for international purposes.
ex.zh: 他坚持说这笔钱是出于国际目的而捐助的。

ex.en: "Not all feminism has to be like this," Jo maintains.
ex.zh: 乔坚持认为，“并非所有的女权运动都得像这样。”

e.en: If you maintain something at a particular rate or level, you keep it at that rate or level.

ex.en: The government was right to maintain interest rates at a high level.
ex.zh: 该政府将利率维持在一个高的层面是正确的。

e.en: If you maintain a road, building, vehicle, or machine, you keep it in good condition by regularly checking it and repairing it when necessary. 维修;

ex.en: The house costs a fortune to maintain.
ex.zh: 维修这房子花费巨大。

d: v. maintain 的过去式和过去分词：保持，维持；维护，维修，保养；坚持认为；供养
adj. 被保持的，被维持的；得到维护的，保养良好的

e.en: a kind of black tea from China 工夫茶;

d: n. 刚果共和国（非洲中西部国家，首都布拉柴维尔，简称刚果（布））；刚果民主共和国（非洲中部国家，首都金沙萨，简称刚果（金），旧称扎伊尔）；刚果河（非洲中部大河，流入大西洋）；（亦作 congou）中国产工夫红茶
n．布迪布吉奥：位于乌干达西部的一个地区，靠近刚果民主共和国边境。该地区以其丰富的生物多样性和自然景观而闻名。
n. 乌干达（东非内陆国家，首都坎帕拉；正式名称为乌干达共和国）

e.en: A virus is a kind of germ that can cause disease.

ex.en: There are many different strains of flu virus.
ex.zh: 有许多不同类型的流感病毒。

e.en: In computer technology, a virus is a program that introduces itself into a system, altering or destroying the information stored in the system. (计算机)

ex.en: Hackers are said to have started a computer virus.
ex.zh: 据说黑客们已开始传播一种计算机病毒。

d: n. 病毒；病毒性疾病，病毒感染；（计算机）病毒，（手机的）短信病毒；有害影响，毒害；毒液
【名】 （Virus）比鲁斯（人名）

e.en: You use confirmed to describe someone who has a particular habit or belief that they are very unlikely to change. 坚定的;

ex.en: I'm a confirmed bachelor.
ex.zh: 我是个坚定的独身主义者。

d: adj. 坚定的，根深蒂固的；已被证实的
v. 确定，确认；证实，证明；批准，认可（confirm 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 热点，热门地点（活动、兴趣或现象集中的地方）；无线热点，Wi-Fi 热点（提供无线上网接入的地点或共享上网功能）；冲突热点，动乱地区（政治动荡或潜在暴力集中的地区）；（生态学）生物多样性热点（物种丰富且受威胁程度高的地区）；（地质学）热点（火山活动集中的地点）；（物理/工程）热区（局部热量或辐射集中的点或区域）
n. 肯尼亚（东非国家）

e.en: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

ex.en: His father was a Baptist minister.
ex.zh: 他父亲是一名浸礼会牧师。

e.en: A minister is a person who officially represents their government in a foreign country and has a lower rank than an ambassador.

ex.en: He concluded a deal with the Danish minister in Washington.
ex.zh: 他在华盛顿与丹麦公使达成了一项协议。

e.en: In some countries outside the United States, a minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department.

ex.en: When the government came to power, he was named minister of culture.
ex.zh: 这届政府上台时，他被任命为了文化部长。

d: n. 部长，阁僚；（基督教，尤指新教）牧师；（外交）公使（均为 minister 的复数）
v. 伺候，照顾（minister 的第三人称单数形式）
n. （Ituri）人名；（西）伊图里

e.en: A region is a large area of land that is different from other areas of land, for example because it is one of the different parts of a country with its own customs and characteristics, or because it has a particular geographical feature.

ex.en: ...Barcelona, capital of the autonomous region of Catalonia.
ex.zh: …巴塞罗那，加泰罗尼亚自治区的首府。

e.en: You can refer to a part of your body as a region. (身体)

ex.en: ...the pelvic region.
ex.zh: …骨盆部位。

e.en: You say in the region of to indicate that an amount that you are stating is approximate. (数量)

ex.en: The plan will cost in the region of six million dollars.
ex.zh: 这项计划将花费大约六百万美元。

d: n. 地区，区域，地域；身体部位（region 的复数）；领域，范围

e.en: If you understand someone or understand what they are saying, you know what they mean. 明白 (某人的话的意思)

ex.en: I think you heard and also understand me.
ex.zh: 我想你听到了我的话，而且也明白我的意思。

ex.en: I don't understand what you are talking about.
ex.zh: 我不明白你在说什么。

e.en: If you understand a language, you know what someone is saying when they are speaking that language. 懂 (某种语言)

ex.en: I couldn't read or understand a word of Yiddish, so I asked him to translate.
ex.zh: 我完全不懂意第绪语，所以请他翻译。

e.en: To understand someone means to know how they feel and why they behave in the way that they do. 理解 (某人)

ex.en: It would be nice to have someone who really understood me, a friend.
ex.zh: 有个真正理解我的人，一个朋友，就太好啦。

ex.en: Trish had not exactly understood his feelings.
ex.zh: 特里希并没有确切地理解他的感受。

e.en: You say that you understand something when you know why or how it happens. 明白 (某事)

ex.en: They are too young to understand what is going on.
ex.zh: 他们太小，不明白在发生什么事。

ex.en: She didn't understand why the TV was kept out of reach of the patients.
ex.zh: 她那时不明白为什么不让病人看电视。

d: v. 理解，懂得；了解，明白（某事物）；谅解，体谅；得知，听说；默认，默许；领会，推断出；解释

e.en: If something affects a person or thing, it influences them or causes them to change in some way. (某事物) 影响 (某人或物)

ex.en: Nicotine adversely affects the functioning of the heart and arteries.
ex.zh: 尼古丁对心脏和动脉功能有负面影响。

ex.en: More than seven million people have been affected by drought.
ex.zh: 七百多万多人受到了干旱的影响。

e.en: If a disease affects someone, it causes them to become ill. (疾病) 困扰 (某人)

ex.en: Arthritis is a crippling disease which affects people all over the world.
ex.zh: 关节炎是一种严重影响健康、困扰全人类的疾病。

e.en: If something or someone affects you, they make you feel a strong emotion, especially sadness or pity. (某事物或人) 影响 (某人)

ex.en: If Jim had been more independent, the divorce would not have affected him as deeply.
ex.zh: 如果吉姆曾经更独立一些，离婚就不会对他有这么深的影响了。

e.en: to put on an appearance or show of; make a pretence of

ex.en: to affect ignorance

d: v. 影响；（疾病）侵袭，感染；（在感情上）深深打动，震撼； 假装，佯装
n. （尤指影响行为或行动的）情感，感情
n. 阿布贾（尼日利亚现在的首都）

e.en: Your colleagues are the people you work with, especially in a professional job.

ex.en: Without consulting his colleagues, he flew from Los Angeles to Chicago.
ex.zh: 在没有和同事商量的情况下，他从洛杉矶飞到了芝加哥。

d: n. 同事；同行（colleague 的复数）

e.en: If you say that something is complicated, you mean it has so many parts or aspects that it is difficult to understand or deal with.

ex.en: The situation in Lebanon is very complicated.
ex.zh: 黎巴嫩的形势非常复杂。

d: adj. 复杂的，难处理的
v. 使复杂化，使难以理解；引起并发症（complicate 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Contact involves meeting or communicating with someone, especially regularly.

ex.en: Opposition leaders are denying any contact with the government in Kabul.
ex.zh: 反对党领袖们在否认同喀布尔政府有任何往来。

e.en: If you come into contact with someone or something, you meet that person or thing in the course of your work or other activities. (打)

ex.en: Doctors I came into contact with voiced their concern.
ex.zh: 我打过交道的医生们表达了他们的关注。

e.en: When people or things are in contact, they are touching each other.

ex.en: They compared how these organisms behaved when left in contact with different materials.
ex.zh: 他们比较了这些有机物在接触不同材料时如何表现。

ex.en: The cry occurs when air is brought into contact with the baby's larynx.
ex.zh: 当空气接触到婴儿的喉咙时，哭声就会响起。

e.en: Your contact details or number are information such as a telephone number where you can be contacted.

ex.en: You must leave your full name and contact details when you phone.
ex.zh: 你打电话时必须留下自己的完整姓名及用于联络的详细资料。

d: n. 联系，联络；接触，触摸；联络人，熟人，社会关系；会见，往来，接触；传染病接触者；隐形眼镜；接通电，触点，接头；（无线电）通信
v. 联系，联络；接触
adj. 供联络的；接触性的，通过接触而起作用的

e.en: A disease that is contagious can be caught by touching people or things that are infected with it. Compare .

ex.en: ...a highly contagious disease of the lungs.
ex.zh: …一种高度接触传染的肺病。

e.en: A feeling or attitude that is contagious spreads quickly among a group of people.

ex.en: Laughing is contagious.
ex.zh: 笑是有感染力的。

d: adj. （疾病）接触性传染的；（情感）具有感染力的；患接触传染病的
n. 合作，协作；协助，配合

e.en: A corridor is a long passage in a building, with doors and rooms on one or both sides.

ex.en: There were doors on both sides of the corridor.
ex.zh: 走廊的两侧都有门。

e.en: A corridor is a strip of land that connects one country to another or gives it a route to the sea through another country. 走廊地带 (与另一国家相连或穿越另一国取得出海通道的狭长地带)

ex.en: East Prussia and the rest of Germany were separated, in 1919, by the Polish Corridor.
ex.zh: 1919年，波兰走廊把东普鲁士和德国其他地方分隔开了。

e.en: A corridor is an area of land between 2 large cities. (两大城市之间的)

ex.en: ...the Northeast corridor.
ex.zh: …东北走廊地带。

d: n. （建筑物或火车内的）通道，过道；（一国领土通过他国境内的）走廊；狭长地带

e.en: Computer Users' Tape System

d: n. （cut 的复数）切口，伤口，割伤；削减，缩减，裁减；份额，分成；近路，捷径；（用于 cold cuts）冷切肉，冷盘
v. （cut 的第三人称单数）切，割，剪，砍；砍倒；削减，减少；（机械）切割

e.en: A person, animal, or plant that is dead is no longer living.

ex.en: "You're a widow?"—"Yes. My husband's been dead a year now."
ex.zh: “你是个寡妇？”——“是的，我丈夫去世1年了。”

ex.en: The group had shot dead another hostage.
ex.zh: 这伙人又打死了一名人质。

e.en: The dead are people who are dead.

ex.en: Two American soldiers were among the dead.
ex.zh: 死者中有两名美军士兵。

e.en: If you describe a place or a period of time as dead, you do not like it because there is very little activity taking place in it.

ex.en: ...some dead little town where the liveliest thing is the flies.
ex.zh: …最有活力的东西是苍蝇的死气沉沉的某个小镇。

e.en: Something that is dead is no longer being used or is finished. 用尽的;

ex.en: The dead cigarette was still between his fingers.
ex.zh: 燃尽的香烟还夹在他指缝间。

d: adj. 死的，去世的；不再使用的，用尽的；（因无电力）不工作的；无生气的，死气沉沉的；过时的，不再有关的；（身体部位）无知觉的，麻木的；筋疲力尽的；神情冷漠的，漠不关心的；完全的，精确的；无生命的，无生物的；界外的；（时间段）空档的，无事可做的
adv. 恰好，精确地；完全地，全然地；非常，十分；突然，顿时
n. 死人，死者；死；深夜，隆冬
adj. 最致命的

e.en: If you declare that something is true, you say that it is true in a firm, deliberate way. You can also declare an attitude or intention. 声明;

ex.en: He declared he would not run for a second term as president.
ex.zh: 他声明不再竞选连任总统。

ex.en: He declared his intention to become the best golfer in the world.
ex.zh: 他表明了要成为世界上最佳高尔夫球手的意愿。

e.en: If you declare something, you state officially and formally that it exists or is the case.

ex.en: The government is ready to declare a permanent ceasefire.
ex.zh: 政府已经准备好宣布永久停火。

ex.en: His lawyers are confident that the judges will declare Mr. Stevens innocent.
ex.zh: 他的律师们确信法官们会宣布史蒂文斯先生无罪。

e.en: If you declare goods that you have bought in another country or money that you have earned, you say how much you have bought or earned so that you can pay tax on it. 申报 (在国外所购之物或收入等)

ex.en: Declaring the wrong income by mistake will no longer lead to an automatic fine.
ex.zh: 由于失误申报收入不符的不再予以自动罚款。

d: adj. 正式宣布的，公开声明的
v. 公布，宣告；声称，宣称；申报（declare 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Direct means moving toward a place or object, without changing direction and without stopping, for example, in a trip.

ex.en: They'd come on a direct flight from Athens.
ex.zh: 他们是从雅典乘坐直达航班来的。

e.en: Direct is also an adverb.

ex.en: You can fly direct from Seattle to Europe.
ex.zh: 你可以从西雅图直飞欧洲。

e.en: 直达地

ex.en: On arriving in New York, Dylan went directly to Greenwich Village.
ex.zh: 迪伦一到纽约就直接去了格林威治村。

e.en: If something is in direct heat or light, it is strongly affected by the heat or light, because there is nothing between it and the source of heat or light to protect it. 直接 (受热) 的; (光)

ex.en: All medicines should be stored away from moisture, direct sunlight, and heat.
ex.zh: 所有药物应避免储存在潮湿、阳光直射或者高温的地方。

d: adj. 径直的，笔直的；坦率的；直射的；直接的，亲身的；正好的；直系的
v. 把……对准；管理，指导；给……指路；指引，引导；导演；指示，命令；交予，寄至
adv. 径直地，直达地；亲自，直接

e.en: A doctor is someone who has a degree in medicine and treats people who are sick or injured.

ex.en: Do not discontinue the treatment without consulting your doctor.
ex.zh: 不要不征求医生的意见就中断治疗。

e.en: A  or  can also be called doctor. (牙医、兽医)
The doctor's is used to refer to the office where a doctor works.

ex.en: I have an appointment at the doctor's.
ex.zh: 我在诊所有个预约。

e.en: A doctor is someone who has been awarded the highest academic or honorary degree by a university.

ex.en: He is a doctor of philosophy.
ex.zh: 他是一位哲学博士。

d: n. 医生，大夫；诊所（the doctor）；博士；牙医，兽医 (Dr)；博学的人；（钓鱼用）人造蝇；凉爽海风；船上的厨师
v. 篡改，伪造；将有害物掺入（食物或饮料）中；阉割（动物）；为……治病，给……疗伤；授以博士学位；修理（机器等），修复；当医生，行医

e.en: A donor is someone who gives a part of their body or some of their blood to be used by doctors to help a person who is ill. 器官捐献者;

ex.en: Doctors removed the healthy kidney from the donor.
ex.zh: 医生从捐献者体内取出了健康的肾脏。

e.en: A donor is a person or organization who gives something, especially money, to a charity, organization, or country that needs it.

ex.en: Donor countries are becoming more choosy about which countries they are prepared to help.
ex.zh: 捐赠国对受赠国的选择变得更加慎重了。

e.en: Donor organs or parts are organs or parts of the body which people allow doctors to use to help people who are ill.

ex.en: ...the severe shortage of donor organs.
ex.zh: …捐献器官的严重匮乏。

d: n. 捐赠者，捐赠人（donor 的复数）；（医学）献血者，器官捐献者；（电子）施主

e.en: An economy is the system according to which the money, industry, and commerce of a country or region are organized.

ex.en: Zimbabwe boasts Africa's most industrialized economy.
ex.zh: 津巴布韦自夸有着非洲最为工业化的经济体制。

e.en: A country's economy is the wealth that it gets from business and industry.

ex.en: The Japanese economy grew at an annual rate of more than 10 percent.
ex.zh: 日本的经济以每年10%以上的速度增长。

e.en: Economy is the use of the minimum amount of money, time, or other resources needed to achieve something, so that nothing is wasted.

ex.en: ...improvements in the fuel economy of cars.
ex.zh: …在节省汽车燃料方面的一些改进。

e.en: Economy services such as travel are cheap and have no luxuries or extras. 经济的;

ex.en: ...the limitations that come with economy travel.
ex.zh: …伴随经济舱的一些限制。

d: n. （economy 的复数）经济；经济体制；经济体；经济状况；节约，节省

e.en: The east is the direction where the sun rises.

ex.en: ...the vast swamps that lie to the east of the River Nile.
ex.zh: …位于尼罗河以东的大片沼泽。

e.en: The east of a place, country, or region is the part which is in the east.

ex.en: ...a village in the east of the country.
ex.zh: …该国东部的一个村庄。

e.en: If you go east, you travel toward the east.

ex.en: To drive, go east on Route 9.
ex.zh: 开车的话，向东上9号路。

e.en: Something that is east of a place is positioned to the east of it.

ex.en: ...just east of the centre of town.
ex.zh: …就在城中心以东。

d: n. 东，东方（the east）；（世界或某个国家、地区或城市的）东部；东方（指亚洲南部和东部，包括印度、中国和日本）（the East）；（旧时）东欧共产主义国家（the East）；（桥牌）坐在东首位置的人（East）
adj. 近东的，面朝东的；（特定的地区、城市、国家或其居民）东部的；东风的；在教堂设有圣坛的一端的（实际上的东端）
adv. 向东，在东方
【名】 （East）（美、英、加）伊斯特（人名）

e.en: If you gain entry to a particular place, you are able to go in.

ex.en: You can gain entry to the club only through a member.
ex.zh: 你只有通过一位会员才能进入该俱乐部。

ex.en: Entry to the museum is free.
ex.zh: 这座博物馆免费参观。

e.en: No Entry is used on signs to indicate that you are not allowed to go into a particular area or go through a particular door or gate.
You can refer to someone's arrival in a place as their entry, especially when you think that they are trying to be noticed and admired. 驾到;

ex.en: He made his triumphal entry into Mexico City.
ex.zh: 他胜利进入了墨西哥城。

e.en: Someone's entry into a particular society or group is their joining of it.

ex.en: ...China's entry into the World Trade Organization.
ex.zh: …中国的入世。

d: n. 进入，加入；出场，莅临；门，入口；进入权，进入许可；参赛；参赛作品，竞赛答题；参赛人数，报名人数；登记，录入；条目，账目，记录

e.en: Equipment consists of the things that are used for a particular purpose, such as a hobby or job. 设备;

ex.en: ...computers, electronic equipment and machine tools.
ex.zh: …电脑、电子设备和机床。

d: n. 设备，用具；（对某人或某物的）装备过程；（做某事应具备的）素质，才能

e.en: The exit is the door through which you can leave a public building.

ex.en: He picked up the case and walked toward the exit.
ex.zh: 他提起箱子朝出口走去。

e.en: An exit on a motorway is a place where traffic can leave it. (公路的)

ex.en: She continued to the next exit, got off the motorway and pulled into a parking lot.
ex.zh: 她继续开到下个出口，出了公路，驶入一个停车场。

e.en: If you refer to someone's exit, you are referring to the way that they left a room or building, or the fact that they left it.

ex.en: I made a hasty exit and managed to open the gate.
ex.zh: 我匆忙离场，设法打开了大门。

e.en: If you refer to someone's exit, you are referring to the way that they left a situation or activity, or the fact that they left it. 退场;

ex.en: It's her earliest exit from Wimbledon since going out in the opening round in 1997.
ex.zh: 这是她自1997年首轮出局以来最早一次从温布尔顿网球赛出局。

d: n. 出口，通道，太平门；（车辆驶出公路的）出路；离去；退出；去世，死亡
v. 退出（电脑程序）；退场（剧本里的舞台指示）；去世，死亡；摊牌让分；离去

e.en: An extension is a new room or building that is added to an existing building or group of buildings. (已有建筑或建筑群的)

ex.en: We are thinking of having an extension built, as we now require an extra bedroom.
ex.zh: 我们正在考虑扩建房屋，因为我们现在需要多一间卧室。

e.en: An extension is a new section of a road or railway that is added to an existing road or railway. (已有公路、铁路的)

ex.en: ...a proposed extension to the No. 7 subway line.
ex.zh: …提议的地铁7号线的一段延长路段。

e.en: An extension is an extra period of time for which something lasts or is valid, usually as a result of official permission.

ex.en: He first entered the country on a six-month visa, and was given a further extension of six months.
ex.zh: 他最初凭有效期为6个月的签证进入这个国家，之后又得到了6个月的续签。

e.en: Something that is an extension of something else is a development of it that includes or affects more people, things, or activities.

ex.en: Many Filipinos see the bases as an extension of American colonial rule.
ex.zh: 许多菲律宾人把这些基地看作是美国殖民统治的延展。

d: n. 延伸，扩展；展期，延长期；扩建部分，延伸部分；（电话）分机；扩展名；（为非全日制学生开设的）进修部；牵伸（术）；外延；广延（性）

e.en: February is the second month of the year in the Western calendar. ２

ex.en: He joined the Army in February 1943.
ex.zh: 他1943年2月参军。

ex.en: His exhibition opens on February 5.
ex.zh: 他的展览2月5日开幕。

d: n. 二月

e.en: A fatal action has very undesirable effects.

ex.en: It would be fatal for the nation to overlook the urgency of the situation.
ex.zh: 国家若忽视这一局势的紧迫性，后果将会非常严重。

ex.en: He made the fatal mistake of compromising early.
ex.zh: 他犯了妥协早了的致命错误。

e.en: 后果严重地

ex.en: Failure now could fatally damage his chances in the future.
ex.zh: 现在的失败能严重地毁掉他将来的机会。

e.en: A fatal accident or illness causes someone's death. (事故、疾病)

ex.en: ...the fatal stabbing of a police sergeant.
ex.zh: …对一名警官的致命一刺。

e.en: (事故、疾病)

ex.en: The dead soldier is reported to have been fatally wounded in the chest.
ex.zh: 报道说死去的那名士兵胸部受到了致命伤。

d: adj. 致命的；导致失败的，灾难性的
【名】 （Fatal）（葡、芬）法塔尔（人名）

e.en: A fluid is a liquid.

ex.en: The blood vessels may leak fluid, which distorts vision.
ex.zh: 血管可能渗漏出液体，扰乱视觉。

ex.en: Make sure that you drink plenty of fluids.
ex.zh: 一定要饮用大量流质。

e.en: Fluid movements or lines or designs are smooth and graceful.

ex.en: His painting became less illustrational and more fluid.
ex.zh: 他的画变得更为流畅，没那么生硬了。

e.en: If you forget something or forget how to do something, you cannot think of it or think how to do it, although you knew it or knew how to do it in the past. 忘了 (某事物、如何做某事)

ex.en: She forgot where she left the car and it took us two days to find it.
ex.zh: 她忘了把车停在了哪里，我们花了两天时间才找到它。

e.en: If you forget something or forget to do it, you fail to think about it or fail to remember to do it, for example, because you are thinking about other things. 忘记 (某事物、做某事)

ex.en: She never forgets her daddy's birthday.
ex.zh: 她从不忘记她爸爸的生日。

ex.en: She forgot to lock her door one day and two men got in.
ex.zh: 她有一天忘了锁门，结果两名男子进去了。

e.en: If you forget something that you had intended to bring with you, you do not bring it because you did not think about it at the right time. 忘记带 (某物)

ex.en: Once when we were going to Paris, I forgot my passport.
ex.zh: 有一次我们去巴黎时，我忘了带护照。

e.en: If you forget something or someone, you deliberately put them out of your mind and do not think about them any more. 忘掉 (某事物、某人)

ex.en: I hope you will forget the bad experience you had today.
ex.zh: 我希望你会忘掉你今天的这次不愉快经历。

ex.en: I found it very easy to forget about Sumner.
ex.zh: 我发现要忘掉萨姆纳很容易。

d: v. 忘记，遗忘；忘做；忽略，不再关注；不再打算做，放弃；忘乎所以，举止不得体
【名】 （Forget）（法）福尔热（人名）

e.en: A funeral is the ceremony that is held when the body of someone who has died is buried or cremated.

ex.en: The funeral will be held in Joplin, Missouri.
ex.zh: 该葬礼将在密苏里州的乔普林市举行。

d: n. 葬礼，丧礼；葬礼上的布道；出殡行列，送葬队伍；需要操心的事
adj. 葬礼的，似葬礼的
adj. 地理的，地理学的

e.en: Greater is the comparative of . great
Greater is used with the name of a large city to refer to the city together with the surrounding urban and suburban area. 大的;

ex.en: ...Greater Los Angeles.
ex.zh: ...大洛杉矶地区。

e.en: Greater is used with the name of a country to refer to a larger area which includes that country and other land which used to belong to it, or which some people believe should belong to it. 大的;
e.zh: 包括该国本身的及过去属地的

ex.en: ...Greater Syria.
ex.zh: ...大叙利亚。

d: adj. 较大的，更大的（great 的比较级）；用于大城市名或国名等专有名词前，表示“大”，指包括该城市及周边地区，或包括该国及其相关属地的更大区域，首字母通常大写，如 Greater London（大伦敦）、Greater China（大中华）

e.en: If someone or something hampers you, they make it difficult for you to do what you are trying to do.

ex.en: The bad weather hampered rescue operations.
ex.zh: 恶劣的天气阻碍了救助行动。

e.en: A hamper is a basket containing food of various kinds that is given to people as a present.

ex.en: ...a luxury food hamper.
ex.zh: …一个豪华的食物礼品篮。

e.en: A hamper is a large basket with a lid, used especially for carrying food. 有盖大篮 (尤装食品)

ex.en: ...a picnic hamper.
ex.zh: …一个野炊篮子。

e.en: A hamper is a storage container for soiled laundry.

ex.en: He tossed his damp towel into the laundry hamper.
ex.zh: 他把湿毛巾抛入洗衣篮里。

d: adj. 受阻碍的，受阻的
v. 妨碍，阻碍，限制（hamper 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned. (偶然地)

ex.en: We cannot say for sure what will happen.
ex.zh: 我们说不准将会发生些什么。

e.en: If something happens, it occurs as a result of a situation or course of action. (作为结果)

ex.en: She wondered what would happen if her parents found her.
ex.zh: 她不知道如果父母发现了她会怎么样。

e.en: When something, especially something unpleasant, happens to you, it takes place and affects you. (尤指不愉快的事) 发生 (在某人身上)

ex.en: If we had been spotted at that point, I don't know what would have happened to us.
ex.zh: 如果那时我们被发现了，我不知道我们会有什么后果。

e.en: If you happen to do something, you do it by chance. If it happens that something is the case, it occurs by chance.

ex.en: We happened to discover we had a friend in common.
ex.zh: 我们碰巧发现我们有个共同的朋友。

d: v. 发生；使遭遇；碰巧
adv. 或许，大概

e.en: Your head is the top part of your body, which has your eyes, mouth, and brain in it.

ex.en: She turned her head away from him.
ex.zh: 她扭过头，不看他。

e.en: You can use head to refer to your mind and your mental abilities.

ex.en: ...an exceptional analyst who could do complex maths in his head.
ex.zh: …一位能做复杂心算的杰出分析家。

e.en: The head of a line of people or vehicles is the front of it, or the first person or vehicle in the line. (人群或车辆的)

ex.en: He made his way to the head of the line.
ex.zh: 他来到队伍的最前端。

e.en: The head of a company or organization is the person in charge of it and in charge of the people in it. (公司、团体的)

ex.en: Heads of government from more than 100 countries gather in Geneva tomorrow.
ex.zh: 来自一百多个国家的政府首脑明天将聚集在日内瓦。

d: adj. 正面朝上的
n. （Heads）人名；（英）黑兹

e.en: Highly is used before some adjectives to mean "very."

ex.en: Mr. Singh was a highly successful salesman.
ex.zh: 辛格先生曾是一位非常成功的推销员。

ex.en: It seems highly unlikely that she ever existed.
ex.zh: 看来很有可能压根儿就没有过她这么个人。

e.en: You use highly to indicate that someone has an important position in an organization or set of people.

ex.en: ...a highly placed government advisor.
ex.zh: …高级政府顾问。

e.en: If someone is highly paid, they receive a large salary.

ex.en: ...the 30 most highly paid athletes in the world.
ex.zh: …世界30位薪酬最高的运动员。

e.en: If you think highly of something or someone, you think they are extremely good.

ex.en: Daphne and Michael thought highly of the school.
ex.zh: 达夫妮和迈克尔对那所学校评价很高。

d: adv. 极其，非常；高度地，高水平地；钦佩地，赞赏地；在高处，地位高
n. 不安全，无把握

e.en: An infected place is one where germs or bacteria are causing a disease to spread among people or animals.

ex.en: In heavily infected areas, half the population become blind.
ex.zh: 在严重感染的地区，有一半人口失明了。

d: adj. （人或动物、身体部位、伤口等）受感染的，被传染的；（食品、水等）受细菌污染的；（计算机、磁盘等）受病毒感染的
v. 感染，传染（infect 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: June is the sixth month of the year in the Western calendar. 6

ex.en: He spent two and a half weeks with us in June 1986.
ex.zh: 1986年6月，他和我们呆了两个半星期。

ex.en: I am moving out on June 5th.
ex.zh: 我将于6月5日搬出去。

d: n. 六月；琼（女名）

e.en: The leading person or thing in a particular area is the one which is most important or successful.

ex.en: ...a leading member of the city's Sikh community.
ex.zh: …该市锡克教团体的一名主要成员。

e.en: The leading role in a play or film is the main role. A leading lady or man is an actor who plays this role. 主要的 (角色);

ex.en: ...an offer to play the leading role in an Arthur Miller play.
ex.zh: …一个在亚瑟·米勒的剧目中出演主角的提议。

e.en: The leading group, vehicle, or person in a race or procession is the one that is at the front.

ex.en: The leading car came to a halt.
ex.zh: 行驶在前面的车停了下来。

e.en: the spacing between lines of photocomposed or digitized type 行距 (Also called interlinear spacing)

d: adj. 主要的，最重要的；在（比赛或行列中）首位的，居前的
n. 行距；领导；（用于屋顶的）铅皮，铅板
v. 领导（lead 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A level is a point on a scale, for example, a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

ex.en: If you don't know your cholesterol level, it's a good idea to have it checked.
ex.zh: 如果你不知道自己的胆固醇水平，最好去查一下。

ex.en: We do have the lowest level of inflation for some years.
ex.zh: 我们几年来的确保持最低水平的通货膨胀。

e.en: The level of a river, lake, or ocean or the level of liquid in a container is the height of its surface.

ex.en: The water level of the Mississippi River is already 6.5 feet below normal.
ex.zh: 密西西比河的水位已经比正常水位低6.5英尺。

e.en: If something is at a particular level, it is at that height.

ex.en: Liz sank down until the water came up to her chin and the bubbles were at eye level.
ex.zh: 莉兹下沉直到水漫到她的下巴，泡沫到了她眼睛的高度。

e.en: A level of a building is one of its different storeys, which is situated above or below other storeys.

ex.en: Thurlow and Brown's rooms were on the second level, to the rear of the building.
ex.zh: 瑟洛和布朗的房间都在大楼背面的第二层。

d: n. 数量，程度；标准，水平；层次，级别；看待（或应对、理解）事物的方式；水平高度，相对高度；楼层；平地；水平仪
adj. 平坦的，水平的；相同价值的，相同地位的；比分相同的；平静的，冷静的
v. 使平整；推倒，夷平；（使）比分相同；（尤指用枪）瞄准；针对……（进行批评等）；稳定下来，达到平衡（level off）；坦诚相见；作水准测量
【名】 （Level）（法）勒韦尔（人名）

e.en: Meant is the past tense and past participle of mean. (mean)
You use meant to to say that something or someone was intended to be or do a particular thing, especially when they have failed to be or do it.

ex.en: I can't say any more, it's meant to be a big secret.
ex.zh: 我再也无可奉告了，这原本是个大秘密。

ex.en: Everything is meant to be businesslike.
ex.zh: 所有的事情原本应该是公事公办的。

e.en: If something is meant for particular people or for a particular situation, it is intended for those people or for that situation.

ex.en: Fairy tales weren't just meant for children.
ex.zh: 童话故事不单单是为孩子们写的。

ex.en: The seeds were not meant for human consumption.
ex.zh: 这些种子并不是给人吃的。

e.en: If you say that something is meant to happen, you mean that it is expected to happen or that it ought to happen.

ex.en: The peculiar thing about getting engaged is that you're meant to announce it to everyone.
ex.zh: 订婚特别要做的事是你理应该向每个人宣布你订婚了。

d: v. 意味；打算（mean 的过去式和过去分词）；表示……的意思

e.en: A lot of something or lots of it is a large amount of it. A lot of people or things, or lots of them, is a large number of them.

ex.en: A lot of our land is used to grow crops for export.
ex.zh: 我们的土地大多用来种植出口农作物。

ex.en: He drank lots of milk.
ex.zh: 他喝了许多奶。

e.en: Lot is also a pronoun.

ex.en: I personally prefer to be in a town where there's lots going on.
ex.zh: 我个人更喜欢呆在充满生机的小镇上。

ex.en: I learned a lot from him about how to run a band.
ex.zh: 我从他那里学了很多管理乐队的知识。

e.en: A lot means to a great extent or degree.

ex.en: Matthew's out quite a lot doing his research.
ex.zh: 马修经常出去做研究。

ex.en: I like you, a lot.
ex.zh: 我非常喜欢你。

e.en: If you do something a lot, you do it often or for a long time. 频繁地;

ex.en: They went out a lot, to restaurants and bars.
ex.zh: 他们经常去饭店和酒吧。

d: n. (常sing.) 一群，一批；小块土地；电影摄制场；（汽车经销处的）停车场；拍卖品；全体成员；（尤指不太好的）命运, 处境；签，阄；一群，一批
v. （拍卖前）将（商品）分成批组
pron. 大量，许多；所有，全部
adv. 很多地，非常（a lot）

e.en: The main thing is the most important one of several similar things in a particular situation. 最重要的;

ex.en: ...one of the main tourist areas of San Francisco.
ex.zh: …旧金山的主要旅游区之一。

ex.en: My main concern now is to protect the children.
ex.zh: 我现在最关心的是保护这些孩子。

e.en: If you say that something is true in the main, you mean that it is generally true, although there may be exceptions.

ex.en: Tourists are, in the main, sympathetic people.
ex.zh: 游客们大都是有同情心的人。

e.en: The mains are the pipes which supply gas or water to buildings, or which take sewage away from them.

ex.en: ...the water supply from the mains.
ex.zh: …总管道的水供应。

e.en: a throw of the dice in dice games (骰子游戏的)

d: adj. 主要的，最大的
n. 总管道，主线路；（电、气、水的）供应系统（the mains）；电源插座；海洋，公海（the main）；（主桅上的）主帆；（掷骰子游戏中，掷者在投掷前的）叫数（须是5，6，7，8，9中的任何一个数）；斗鸡比赛
【名】 （Main）（美）梅因（人名）

e.en: rock strata that are characterized by a particular type of sediment or deposit

ex.en: coal measures

d: n. 措施；层组（measure 的复数）
v. 测量（measure 的第三人称单数）
n. （Measures）梅热斯（人名）

e.en: Misinformation is wrong information which is given to someone, often in a deliberate attempt to make them believe something that is not true. (常指故意提供的)

ex.en: This was a deliberate piece of misinformation.
ex.zh: 这是一条故意提供的虚假消息。

d: n. 错误信息，虚假消息（常指故意提供）

e.en: Mistrust is the feeling that you have toward someone who you do not trust.

ex.en: There was mutual mistrust between the two men.
ex.zh: 这两人之间互不信任。

e.en: If you mistrust someone or something, you do not trust them.

ex.en: It frequently appears that Bell mistrusts all journalists.
ex.zh: 贝尔常常表露出他不信任所有的记者。

d: v. 不信任，怀疑（某人或某事）
n. 不信任，怀疑（对某人或某事的信任缺失）

e.en: You can refer to a very short period of time, for example a few seconds, as a moment or moments.

ex.en: In a moment he was gone.
ex.zh: 不一会儿他就不见了。

ex.en: In moments, I was asleep once more.
ex.zh: 很快，我又睡着了。

e.en: A particular moment is the point in time at which something happens.

ex.en: At this moment a car stopped at the house.
ex.zh: 就在此时，一辆汽车停在那座房子前。

e.en: If you say that something will or may happen at any moment or any moment now, you are emphasizing that it is likely to happen very soon.

ex.en: He'll be here to see you any moment now.
ex.zh: 他随时会来这里看你。

e.en: You use expressions such as at the moment, at this moment, and at the present moment to indicate that a particular situation exists at the time when you are speaking.

ex.en: At the moment, no one is talking to me.
ex.zh: 此刻没人和我说话。

ex.en: He's touring South America at this moment in time.
ex.zh: 他此刻正在周游南美。

d: n. 片刻，瞬间；某一时刻；现在，目前；时机，机会；（事物发展的）关头，转折点；重大，重要；力矩；矩，动差
【名】 （Moment）（英）莫门特（人名）
n. 尼日利亚（西非国家，濒临几内亚湾，是非洲人口最多的国家）

e.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

ex.en: Derartu is an outstanding athlete and deserved to win.
ex.zh: 德拉图是位杰出的运动员，他理应获胜。

e.en: Money that is outstanding has not yet been paid and is still owed to someone.

ex.en: The total debt outstanding is $70 billion.
ex.zh: 尚未偿还的总债务额是700亿美元。

e.en: Outstanding issues or problems have not yet been resolved.

ex.en: We still have some outstanding issues to resolve before we'll have a treaty that is ready to sign.
ex.zh: 我们在签署这份条约之前还有一些悬而未决的问题要解决。

e.en: Outstanding means very important or obvious.

ex.en: The company is an outstanding example of a small business that grew into a big one.
ex.zh: 该公司是小企业成长为大公司的突出例子。

d: adj. 杰出的，优秀的；显著的，突出的；未解决的，未完成的；（款项）未支付的，未结清的

e.en: A forced action is something that you do because someone else makes you do it.

ex.en: A system of forced labour was used on the cocoa plantations.
ex.zh: 一种受迫劳动制曾用于可可种植园。

e.en: A forced action is something that you do because circumstances make it necessary.

ex.en: He made a forced landing on a motorway.
ex.zh: 他迫降在了一条高速公路上。

e.en: If you describe something as forced, you mean it does not happen naturally and easily.

ex.en: ...a forced smile.
ex.zh: …一个勉强的微笑。

d: adj. 被迫的；勉强的，不自然的
v. 强迫；用力推；使发生（force 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Known is the past participle of know. (know)
You use known to describe someone or something that is clearly recognized by or familiar to all people or to a particular group of people. 众所周知的;

ex.en: ...He was a known drug dealer.
ex.zh: …他是一个臭名昭著的毒品贩子。

e.en: If someone or something is known for a particular achievement or feature, they are familiar to many people because of that achievement or feature.

ex.en: He is better known for his film and TV work.
ex.zh: 他更为著名的是影视作品。

e.en: If you let it be known that something is the case, or you let something be known, you make sure that people know it or can find out about it.

ex.en: The president has let it be known that he is against it.
ex.zh: 总统已经明确表示，他反对此事。

d: adj. 已知的，已发现的；知名的，出了名的
v. 知道（know 的过去分词形式）

e.en: If something drones, it makes a low, continuous, dull noise.

ex.en: Above him an invisible plane droned through the night sky.
ex.zh: 在他头顶上空一架隐形飞机飞过夜空，不断发出低沉单调的声音。

e.en: Drone is also a noun.

ex.en: I hear the drone of an aeroplane as it banks across the bay.
ex.zh: 飞机倾斜飞过海湾时，我听到它单调的低鸣。

e.en: If you say that someone drones, you mean that they keep talking about something in a boring way.

ex.en: Chambers' voice droned, maddening as an insect around his head.
ex.zh: 钱伯斯唠唠叨叨，那声音像一只飞虫绕着他的头打转般令人发狂。

e.en: Drone is also a noun.

ex.en: The minister's voice was a relentless drone.
ex.zh: 该大臣的声音是无休止的絮叨。

d: n. 嗡嗡叫，嗡嗡响；雄蜂，公蜂；（遥控的）无人驾驶飞机（或导弹）；单调乏味的讲话；（不劳动，依赖他人为生的）寄生虫；伴音（如风笛等发出的持续音），伴音管（或弦等）；干单调工作的人
v. 嗡嗡叫，嗡嗡响；（人）絮絮叨叨地说，喋喋不休地说；混日子
【名】  （Drone）（法）德罗纳（人名）

e.en: If you believe that something is true, you think it is true, but you are not sure.

ex.en: Experts believe that the coming drought will be extensive.
ex.zh: 专家们认为即将到来的干旱将会是大面积的。

ex.en: We believe them to be hidden here in this apartment.
ex.zh: 我们认为他们藏匿在这所公寓里。

e.en: If you believe someone or if you believe what they say or write, you accept that they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He did not sound as if he believed her.
ex.zh: 听起来他似乎不相信她的话。

ex.en: Never believe anything a married man says about his wife.
ex.zh: 永远别相信一个已婚男人说的关于自己妻子的话。

e.en: If you believe in fairies, ghosts, or miracles, you are sure that they exist or happen. If you believe in a god, you are sure of the existence of that god.

ex.en: I don't believe in ghosts.
ex.zh: 我不相信有鬼。

e.en: If you believe in a way of life or an idea, you are in favour of it because you think it is good or right.

ex.en: He believed in marital fidelity.
ex.zh: 他赞成对婚姻忠实。

d: v. 相信，信以为真；认为，猜想；信教（believe 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

ex.en: I hope they continue to fight for equal justice after I'm gone.
ex.zh: 我希望我走后他们继续为司法公正而奋斗。

ex.en: Diana and Roy Jarvis are determined to continue working when they reach retirement age.
ex.zh: 戴安娜·贾维斯和罗伊·贾维斯决心到退休年龄后还继续工作。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it does not stop. 使继续;

ex.en: He insisted that the conflict would continue until conditions were met for a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 他坚持认为冲突会持续下去，直至停火条件得到满足为止。

ex.en: Outside the building people continue their vigil, huddling around bonfires.
ex.zh: 在楼外，人们围聚在篝火旁继续守夜。

e.en: If you continue something or continue with something, you start doing it again after a break or interruption. (某人在歇息或被打断后) 继续 (做某事或某事)

ex.en: I went up to my room to continue with my packing.
ex.zh: 我上我房间去继续收拾行李。

ex.en: She looked up for a minute and then continued drawing.
ex.zh: 她抬头看了一会儿，然后继续画。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it starts again after a break or interruption. (某事在停顿或被打断后)

ex.en: He denies 18 charges. The trial continues today.
ex.zh: 他否认18项指控。审判今天继续。

d: v. 继续，持续，连续；中断后继续，接着说；保持，继续处于原有状态或职位；继续行进；延伸，扩展（continue 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A massacre is the killing of a large number of people at the same time in a violent and cruel way.

ex.en: Maria lost her 62-year-old mother in the massacre.
ex.zh: 玛丽亚在大屠杀中失去了她62岁的母亲。

e.en: If people are massacred, a large number of them are attacked and killed in a violent and cruel way.

ex.en: 300 civilians are believed to have been massacred by the rebels.
ex.zh: 据信300名平民被叛乱分子屠杀了。

d: n. 屠杀，残杀；（运动或比赛中的）惨败
v. （大规模地）屠杀，杀戮；（比赛或竞争等中）使惨败，彻底击败；笨拙地演奏（演唱）
【名】 （Massacre）（俄、泰、马、尼）马萨克尔（人名）

e.en: the first man, created by God: the progenitor of the human race (Genesis 2–3) 亚当;

d: n. 亚当

e.en: A million or one million is the number 1,000,000.

ex.en: Up to five million people a year visit the county.
ex.zh: 每年多达500万人到这个县游览。

e.en: If you talk about millions of people or things, you mean that there is a very large number of them but you do not know or do not want to say exactly how many.

ex.en: The program was viewed on television in millions of homes.
ex.zh: 无数的家庭从电视上收看了这个节目。

d: num. 一百万，一百万个
n. 百万，百万个（人或物）；许多，无数；百万英镑（或美元）
adj. 许多的，无数的
【名】 （Million）（美、法）米利翁（人名）
n. 艾哈迈德（Ahmed，阿拉伯语男性人名，亦译阿赫麦德）；也用作姓氏
adv. 据说，据宣称

e.en: having a back or backing
(in combination)

ex.en: high-backed
black-backed

d: adj. 有背的，有靠背的；（常构成复合词）具有某种背部或背面的；受支持的，有财力支持的，以…为后盾（或担保）的；（胶片）涂有防光晕背层的
v. 支持，资助（back 的过去式和过去分词）；证实（back up 的过去式和过去分词）；使后退，倒车（back 的过去式和过去分词）；（车辆、人流等）拥堵，积压（back up 的过去式和过去分词）；（用于 be backed by）背后是，背靠

e.en: A colonel is a senior officer in an army, air force, or the marines. (陆军、空军或海军的)

ex.en: This particular place was run by an ex-Army colonel.
ex.zh: 这个特别的地方归一位前陆军上校掌管。

d: n. （陆军、空军或海军陆战队）上校
【名】 （Colonel）（法、罗）科洛内尔（人名）

e.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

ex.en: Government officials visited the earthquake zone on Thursday morning to coordinate the relief effort.
ex.zh: 政府官员星期四上午视察了地震灾区以协调救灾工作。

e.en: 协调的

ex.en: Coalition forces were planning a coordinated effort to attack the drug trade.
ex.zh: 联合部队正在计划共同打击毒品买卖。

ex.en: ...a well-coordinated surprise attack.
ex.zh: …一次完美配合的突袭。

e.en: If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently to perform particular movements. 使 (身体各部位)

ex.en: You need to coordinate legs, arms, and breathing for the front crawl.
ex.zh: 匍匐前进时，你要协调双腿、胳膊和呼吸。

e.en: If you coordinate clothes or furnishings that are used together, or if they coordinate, they are similar in some way and look nice together. 搭配 (衣服、饰品)

ex.en: She'll show you how to coordinate pattern and colours.
ex.zh: 她会向你展示如何搭配款式和颜色。

ex.en: Tie it with fabric bows that coordinate with other furnishings.
ex.zh: 扎上和其他的饰品相配的布制蝴蝶结。

d: adj. 协调一致的；（色彩等）搭配协调的
v. 协调，配合；使身体协调；（使颜色、款式、风格等）搭配，配套（coordinate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you talk about developed countries or the developed world, you mean the countries or the parts of the world that are wealthy and have many industries.

ex.en: This scarcity is inevitable in less developed countries.
ex.zh: 在欠发达国家这种匮乏是不可避免的。

d: adj. 发达的，高度发展的；先进的，成熟的；人体成规定比例的
v. 发展，壮大；养成，形成；开发，研制（develop 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you feed a person or animal, you give them food to eat and sometimes actually put it in their mouths.

ex.en: We brought along pieces of old bread and fed the birds.
ex.zh: 我们带了几片陈面包来喂鸟。

e.en: 喂食

ex.en: The feeding of dairy cows has undergone a revolution.
ex.zh: 奶牛的喂食已经历了一场革命。

e.en: To feed a family or a community means to supply food for them.

ex.en: Feeding a hungry family can be expensive.
ex.zh: 为一家子饥饿的人张罗食物要花不少钱。

e.en: When an animal feeds, it eats or drinks something. (动物)

ex.en: After a few days the caterpillars stopped feeding.
ex.zh: 几天后毛虫停止了进食。

d: v. 饲养，喂养，为……提供食物；以……为食物，吃食；提供（意见或信息等），灌输；施肥；添加燃料；把……放进机器，将……塞进机器；加深，强化；使（缓慢平稳地）移动，使穿过（有限的空间）；维持，满足（习惯）；传球；流入，进入
n. 哺乳，喂养；动物的饲料，植物的肥料；（机器的）进料装置；（机器、设备的）原料供给；（卫星或网络）转播，（信号）传输；（计算机）订阅源；（给舞台演员的）提词，提白；丰盛的一餐
adj. 较少的
pron. 更少的人（或物）

e.en: Something or someone that is foreign comes from or relates to a country that is not your own.

ex.en: She was on her first foreign holiday without her parents.
ex.zh: 她首次不在父母的陪同下到国外度假。

ex.en: ...a foreign language.
ex.zh: …一门外语。

e.en: In politics and journalism, foreign is used to describe people, jobs, and activities relating to countries that are not the country of the person or government concerned.

ex.en: ...the German foreign minister.
ex.zh: …德国外交部长。

ex.en: I am the foreign correspondent in Washington of La Tribuna newspaper of Honduras.
ex.zh: 我是洪都拉斯《论坛报》驻华盛顿的记者。

e.en: A foreign object is something that has got into something else, usually by accident, and should not be there.

ex.en: The patient's immune system would reject the transplanted organ as a foreign object.
ex.zh: 该病人的免疫系统会将移植器官作为异物加以排斥。

d: adj. 外国的，来自国外的；外交的，涉外的；陌生的，不熟悉的；外来的，异质的；外地的，不属于本地区的

e.en: If you flee from something or someone, or flee a person or thing, you escape from them.

ex.en: He slammed the bedroom door behind him and fled.
ex.zh: 他砰地关上卧室的门就逃走了。

ex.en: ...refugees fleeing persecution or torture.
ex.zh: …逃避迫害或折磨的难民们。

d: v. 逃离，逃避，逃跑

e.en: A guardian is someone who has been legally appointed to take charge of the affairs of another person, for example a child or someone who is mentally ill.

ex.en: Destiny's legal guardian was her grandmother.
ex.zh: 德斯蒂妮的法定监护人是她的祖母。

e.en: The guardian of something is someone who defends and protects it.

ex.en: ...an institution acting as the guardian of democracy in Europe.
ex.zh: …一个在欧洲扮演民主捍卫者的机构。

d: n. 监护人；守卫者，保护者；（方济各会隐修院的）院长
adj. 守护的
【名】 （Guardian）（西）瓜尔迪安（人名）

e.en: Forgotten is the past participle of . (forget)

d: v. 忘记（forget 的过去分词）
adj. 被遗忘的；被忽视的；已失传的

e.en: Something that is horrendous is very unpleasant or shocking.

ex.en: He described it as the most horrendous experience of his life.
ex.zh: 他把那件事形容为他生活中最恐怖的经历。

e.en: Some people use horrendous to describe something that is so big or great that they find it extremely unpleasant. (程度大得或严重得)

ex.en: ...the usually horrendous traffic jams.
ex.zh: …通常糟糕透顶的交通堵塞。

e.en: 极其令人不快地

ex.en: The man in the photo was horrendously fat.
ex.zh: 照片里的男人胖得惊人。

d: adj. 极其可怕的，骇人的；（程度、规模）极其严重的，大得惊人的

e.en: a fit of depression or anxiety (突发的一阵)压抑;
an expression of dismay, sometimes facetious 呦(表示沮丧)

d: n. horror 的复数形式。恐怖，惊骇：由可怕的事物或事件引起的强烈恐惧或震惊（该义通常用单数 horror）；可怕的事物、经历或场面，惨状（如 the horrors of war）；恐怖片等恐怖题材作品；（俚语）the horrors：一阵压抑或焦虑，惊恐不安。
int. （非正式）哎呀！天哪！糟了！（表示沮丧、震惊或反感，有时带诙谐语气）

e.en: If one thing includes another thing, it has the other thing as one of its parts.

ex.en: The trip has been extended to include a few other events.
ex.zh: 行程已经延长以包括其他几项活动。

e.en: If someone or something is included in a large group, system, or area, they become a part of it or are considered a part of it.

ex.en: I had worked hard to be included in a project like this.
ex.zh: 为了成为这样的项目的一分子，我过去一直埋头苦干。

d: v. 包含；把……列为一部分，把……算入
n. 侯赛因（阿拉伯常见人名或姓氏）；萨达姆·侯赛因（伊拉克前总统）；约旦国王侯赛因（King Hussein）

e.en: Individual means relating to one person or thing, rather than to a large group.

ex.en: ...waiting for the group to decide rather than making individual decisions.
ex.zh: …等待集体作决定而不是作单独的决定。

e.en: 单独地

ex.en: ...individually crafted tiles.
ex.zh: …一块块单独制作的瓦片。

e.en: An individual is a person.

ex.en: ...anonymous individuals who are doing good things within our community.
ex.zh: …一些在我们社区里做好事不留名人士。

e.en: If you describe someone or something as individual, you mean that you admire them because they are very unusual and do not try to imitate other people or things.

ex.en: It was really all part of her very individual personality.
ex.zh: 那确实是她非常独特个性的全部。

d: n. 个人；个体（individual 的复数）

e.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

ex.en: A survey of retired people has indicated that most are independent and enjoying life.
ex.zh: 一项对退休人员的调查表明，他们中的大部分人生活自立而愉快。

ex.en: Our vote today indicates a change in United States policy.
ex.zh: 我们今天的投票表明了美国政策的变化。

e.en: If you indicate an opinion, an intention, or a fact, you mention it in an indirect way.

ex.en: Mr. Rivers has indicated that he may resign.
ex.zh: 里弗斯先生已经暗示他可能要辞职。

e.en: If you indicate something to someone, you show them where it is, especially by pointing to it.

ex.en: He indicated a chair. "Sit down."
ex.zh: 他指着一把椅子说，“坐下。”

e.en: If one thing indicates something else, it is a sign of that thing. 象征;

ex.en: Dreams can help indicate your true feelings.
ex.zh: 梦能代表你的真实情感。

d: v. （indicate 的现在分词形式）表明，显示，预示；暗示，示意；指示，指出，标示；说明，写明，简要陈述；（仪器）显示（量度或读数）；（驾驶时）打转向灯，打行车转向信号；（医学）有必要，适用
adj. 指示的，指示用的（常用于复合词，如 indicating lamp 指示灯）

e.en: Something or someone that is inside a place, container, or object is in it or is surrounded by it. 在…里面;

ex.en: Inside the passport was a folded slip of paper.
ex.zh: 护照里面是一张折叠的纸条。

e.en: Inside is also an adverb. 在里面;

ex.en: The couple chatted briefly on the doorstep before going inside.
ex.zh: 夫妇俩进屋前在门阶上简单地聊了几句。

e.en: Inside is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an inside wall.
ex.zh: …一面内墙。

e.en: The inside of something is the part or area that its sides surround or contain. 里面;

ex.en: The doors were locked from the inside.
ex.zh: 门从里面锁住了。

d: n. 内部，内侧；内脏，（尤指）胃；里道，内圈；（靠近路边的）慢车道
adv. 在（或向）里面；在监牢里
prep. 在（或向）……内，在（或向）……里；在……时间之内；（足球、英式橄榄球等体育运动）（比另一队员）更靠近球场中心
adj. 里面的；从内部了解到的，内线干的；（马路车道）靠近路边的，慢（道）的；（曲棍球、足球等体育运动）场地中心附近的

e.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a country or organization. 国内的;

ex.en: The country stepped up internal security.
ex.zh: 该国加强了国内安全防卫。

ex.en: ...Russia's Ministry of Internal Affairs.
ex.zh: …俄罗斯内务部。

e.en: 在国内;

ex.en: The state is not a unified and internally coherent entity.
ex.zh: 这个国家不是一个内部凝聚的统一体。
