e.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place. 体内的;

ex.en: The doctor said the internal bleeding had been massive.
ex.zh: 医生说内出血的量很大。

e.en: 在体内;

ex.en: Evening primrose oil is used on the skin as well as taken internally.
ex.zh: 夜来香油可外用在皮肤上，也可内服。

d: adj. 内部的，体内的；内政的，国内的；本身的，本质的；内心的；（大学生）本校生的
n. 内部部件，内部特征；内脏

e.en: If there is a link between two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example, because one thing causes or affects the other.

ex.en: ...the link between smoking and lung cancer.
ex.zh: …吸烟和肺癌之间的关系。

e.en: If someone or something links two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example, because one thing causes or affects the other.

ex.en: The U.N. Security Council has linked any lifting of sanctions to compliance with the ceasefire terms.
ex.zh: 联合国安全理事会将任何制裁的解除与遵守停火条款联系起来。

ex.en: The study further strengthens the evidence linking smoking with early death.
ex.zh: 这项研究进一步加强了联系吸烟与早亡的证据。

e.en: A link between two things or places is a physical connection between them.

ex.en: ...the railway link between Boston and New York.
ex.zh: …波士顿与纽约之间的铁路连接线。

ex.en: Drivers ran into a field of weeds at the state border, where no link with the neighbouring state had yet been planned.
ex.zh: 司机们闯入了州界处一块杂草丛生的原野，在那里还没有计划修建连接邻州的道路。

e.en: If two places or objects are linked or something links them, there is a physical connection between them.

ex.en: ...the Rama Road, which links the capital, Managua, with the Caribbean coast.
ex.zh: …连接首都马那瓜与加勒比海岸的拉玛公路。

ex.en: Seven miles of track were installed to link the hotel to the golf course.
ex.zh: 七英里的轨道被铺设来连接宾馆和高尔夫球场。

d: v. link 的过去式和过去分词：连接，把……连接起来；使相联系，与……相关联，与……挂钩（常用于 be linked to/with）；说明（两者间）有联系，认为……与……有关；挽住，勾住
adj. 连接的；相关联的；（计算机）链接的；（遗传学）连锁的，显示连环遗传的

e.en: If someone lives in a particular place or with a particular person, their home is in that place or with that person.

ex.en: She has lived here for 10 years.
ex.zh: 她在这里住了10年了。

ex.en: Where do you live?
ex.zh: 你住在哪里？

e.en: If you say that someone lives in particular circumstances or that they live a particular kind of life, you mean that they are in those circumstances or that they have that kind of life.

ex.en: We lived quite grandly.
ex.zh: 我们生活得相当快乐。

ex.en: Compared to people living only a few generations ago, we have greater opportunities to have a good time.
ex.zh: 与生活在仅仅几代之前的人相比，我们有更大的过得快乐的机会。

e.en: If you say that someone lives for a particular thing, you mean that it is the most important thing in their life. (为…而)

ex.en: He lived for his work.
ex.zh: 他为了工作而活。

e.en: To live means to be alive. If someone lives to a particular age, they stay alive until they are that age.

ex.en: He's got a terrible disease and will not live long.
ex.zh: 他得了一种重病，活不长了。

ex.en: He lived to be 103.
ex.zh: 他活到了103岁。

d: v. 生存，活着；生活在；居住；生长，栖息；（以某种方式）生活，过日子；为……而生活；以……为生；继续存在，铭记；过精彩的生活，享受生活；（物）搁置在（某处）；恪守（规则、信念、理想等）；（船）逃过劫难，未沉没
adj. 活的，有生命的；含乳酸菌的；现场直播的，实况转播的；现场演出的；（电线或设备等）通电的，带电的；仍可爆炸的，随时可用的；（火、煤炭或火柴）燃烧的，可燃的；（火柴）未用过的；当前所关心的，时下重大的；（球类运动中的球）处于比赛状态的；（电子链接）有效的；（机器中轮或轴）转动的
adv. 现场直播地，实况转播地
【名】 （Live）（挪、芬、印、俄、美、荷）利夫（人名）

e.en: Men is the plural of . (man)

d: n. 男人，男性（man 的复数）；人，人类（泛指）；人手，人员，员工（常与 the 连用）；（Men）人名，姓氏（如日语“面”、葡萄牙语“梅恩”、柬埔寨语“孟”）

e.en: An outage is a period of time when the electricity supply to a building or area is interrupted, for example, because of damage to the cables.

d: n. （电力或其他服务的）停止供应期，设备停开期

e.en: When children, animals, or adults play, they spend time doing enjoyable things, such as using toys and taking part in games.

ex.en: ...invite the children over to play.
ex.zh: …邀请孩子们过来玩。

ex.en: They played in the little garden.
ex.zh: 他们在小花园里玩耍。

e.en: Play is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a few hours of play until the babysitter puts them to bed.
ex.zh: …直到保姆让他们上床睡觉之前的几小时的玩耍。

e.en: When you play a sport, game, or match, you take part in it. 参加 (体育运动、游戏、比赛等)

ex.en: While the twins played cards, Leona sat reading.
ex.zh: 那对双胞胎玩牌的时候，利昂娜坐着看书。

ex.en: I used to play basketball.
ex.zh: 我过去常打篮球。

e.en: Play is also a noun. (对运动、游戏、比赛等的)

ex.en: They've got more exciting players and a more exciting style of play.
ex.zh: 他们有更精彩的选手和更精彩的比赛风格。

d: n. 比赛；参赛；演奏；（戏剧、影视中的）扮演，演出
v. play 的现在分词/动名词：（尤指儿童）玩，玩耍；参加（比赛、游戏或运动）；演奏（乐器）；扮演（角色）；捉弄，戏弄；随意摆弄，弄着玩

e.en: Prewar is used to describe things that happened, existed, or were made in the period immediately before a war, especially World War II, 1939-45. 战 (尤指第二次世界大战)

ex.en: ...Poland's prewar leader.
ex.zh: …波兰的战前领导人。

d: adj. 战前的
adv. 在战前

e.en: The population of a country or area is all the people who live in it.

ex.en: Bangladesh now has a population of about 110 million.
ex.zh: 孟加拉国现有约一亿一千万人口。

ex.en: ...the annual rate of population growth.
ex.zh: …人口年增长率。

e.en: If you refer to a particular type of population in a country or area, you are referring to all the people or animals of that type there. (某种) 人群;

ex.en: ...75.6 percent of the male population over sixteen.
ex.zh: …16岁以上男性人群的75.6％。

ex.en: ...areas with a large black population.
ex.zh: …有大批黑人群体的的各地区。

d: n. （地区、国家等的）人口，人口数量；（某领域的）生物，族群，人口；（统计）总体，母体；（天文）星族；（物理）布居数

e.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it. 执行;

ex.en: He said Japan would continue to pursue the policies laid down at the London summit.
ex.zh: 他说日本将继续贯彻伦敦峰会上确定的方针。

e.en: If you pursue a particular aim or result, you make efforts to achieve it, often over a long period of time. 追求;

ex.en: He will pursue a trade policy that protects American workers.
ex.zh: 他将努力实行保护美国工人的贸易政策。

e.en: If you pursue a particular topic, you try to find out more about it by asking questions.

ex.en: If your original request is denied, don't be afraid to pursue the matter.
ex.zh: 如果你最初的要求被拒绝了，不要害怕去追问这件事情。

e.en: If you pursue a person, vehicle, or animal, you follow them, usually in order to catch them.

ex.en: She pursued the man who had stolen a woman's bag.
ex.zh: 她追赶那个偷了一女士钱包的男子。

d: v. 追求，致力于，执行；继续探讨（或追究、从事）；追逐，跟踪，追赶；沿着……前行；追求（某人）；力劝（某人）接受聘用

e.en: If someone or something is responsible for a particular event or situation, they are the cause of it or they can be blamed for it.

ex.en: He still felt responsible for her death.
ex.zh: 他依然觉得对她的死负有责任。

e.en: If you are responsible for something, it is your job or duty to deal with it and make decisions relating to it.

ex.en: ...the cabinet member responsible for the environment.
ex.zh: …负责环境的内阁成员。

e.en: If you are responsible to a person or group, they have authority over you and you have to report to them about what you do.

ex.en: I'm responsible to my board of directors.
ex.zh: 我向我的董事会汇报。

e.en: Responsible people behave properly and sensibly, without needing to be supervised.

ex.en: He feels that the media should be more responsible in what they report.
ex.zh: 他觉得媒体应该对他们的报道更负责些。

d: adj. （对某人、某事）负责的；（对事故、错误、罪行等）负有责任的，应承担责任的；（工作或职位）重要的，责任重大的；可靠的，负责任的；作为缘由的，应受归咎的；向......负责的，向......汇报的

e.en: To reveal something means to make people aware of it. 透露;

ex.en: She has refused to reveal the whereabouts of her daughter.
ex.zh: 她已拒绝透露她女儿的行踪。

ex.en: A survey of the American diet has revealed that a growing number of people are overweight.
ex.zh: 一项有关美国人日常饮食的调查表明越来越多的人超重。

e.en: If you reveal something that has been out of sight, you uncover it so that people can see it. 使显露;

ex.en: In the principal room, a grey carpet was removed to reveal the original pine floor.
ex.zh: 在主房间里，一块灰色的地毯被挪开了，使原有的松木地板露了出来。

d: v. 揭露，透露；显示；使显露（reveal 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 显露的，被揭露的

e.en: A routine is the usual series of things that you do at a particular time. A routine is also the practice of regularly doing things in a fixed order. 惯例;

ex.en: The players had to change their daily routine and lifestyle.
ex.zh: 这些运动员不得不改变他们的每日常规和生活方式。

e.en: You use routine to describe activities that are done as a normal part of a job or process.

ex.en: ...a series of routine medical tests including X-rays and blood tests.
ex.zh: …一系列包括X光和验血在内的常规医学检查。

e.en: A routine situation, action, or event is one which seems completely ordinary, rather than interesting, exciting, or different.

ex.en: So many days are routine and uninteresting, especially in winter.
ex.zh: 太多的日子都是平淡和无趣，尤其是在冬季。

e.en: You use routine to refer to a way of life that is uninteresting and ordinary, or hardly ever changes.

ex.en: ...the mundane routine of her life.
ex.zh: …她生活的平常乏味。

d: n. 常规，惯例；生活乏味，无聊；（演出中的）一套动作，一系列笑话（等）；（为达到特定目的的）老一套，俗套；（计算机）例行程序
adj. 常规的，例行的；平常的，毫不特别的；平淡乏味的
v.  按惯例安排

e.en: The run-up to an event is the period of time just before it.

ex.en: The company believes the products will sell well in the run-up to Christmas.
ex.zh: 该公司相信这些产品在圣诞节前夕将会销得很好。

d: n. （体育）助跑；某一事件发生前的预备阶段，前夕（常作 the run-up to sth）；急剧增长（多指价格等数值）
abbr. 战略空军（Strategic Air Force）；美国林业者协会（Society of American Foresters）；超耐磨炉（super abrasion furnace）；可持续航空燃料（sustainable aviation fuel）

e.en: If someone in authority sanctions an action or practice, they officially approve of it and allow it to be done. 批准;

ex.en: He may now be ready to sanction the use of force.
ex.zh: 他或许现在正准备批准使用武力。

e.en: Sanction is also a noun. 批准;

ex.en: ...a newspaper run by citizens without the sanction of the government.
ex.zh: …未经政府许可的一家民办报纸。

e.en: Sanctions are measures taken by countries to restrict trade and official contact with a country that has broken international law.

ex.en: The continued abuse of human rights has now led the United States to impose sanctions against the regime.
ex.zh: 对人权的不断践踏现已导致美国对该政权实施国际制裁。

d: n. 制裁，国际制裁；处罚，惩罚（sanction 的复数）
v. 认可，准许；对……实施制裁，处罚（sanction 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you save someone or something, you help them to avoid harm or to escape from a dangerous or unpleasant situation. 救助;

ex.en: ...an austerity programme designed to save the country's failing economy.
ex.zh: …一个旨在拯救该国衰退的经济的紧缩计划。

ex.en: The meeting is an attempt to mobilize nations to save children from death by disease and malnutrition.
ex.zh: 该会议试图动员各国救助儿童，以免死于疾病和营养不良。

e.en: If you save, you gradually collect money by spending less than you get, usually in order to buy something that you want.

ex.en: The majority of people intend to save, but find that by the end of the month there is nothing left.
ex.zh: 大多数人都想要储蓄，但到月底的时候却发现已经一分不剩了。

ex.en: Tim and Barbara are now saving for a house in the suburbs.
ex.zh: 蒂姆和芭芭拉眼下正为郊区的一所房子攒钱。

e.en: Save up means the same as . 同(save)

ex.en: Julie wanted to put some of her money aside for holidays or save up for something special.
ex.zh: 朱莉想留出一些钱去度假或是存些钱以备专门之需。

e.en: If you save something such as time or money, you prevent the loss or waste of it.

ex.en: It saves time in the kitchen to have things you use a lot within reach.
ex.zh: 在厨房里把常用的东西放在手边可以节省时间。

ex.en: I'll try to save him the expense of a flight from Perth.
ex.zh: 我会想办法给他省下从珀斯过来的机票费用。

d: adj. 获救的；已保存的；（基督教）得救的
v. save 的过去式和过去分词：救助，挽救，抢救；储蓄，积攒；节约，节省；保留，留作备用；（计算机）保存，存盘；（体育）扑救，救球；免去，省去，避免；收集，收藏（邮票、优惠券等）

e.en: A sideline is something that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.

ex.en: It was quite a lucrative sideline.
ex.zh: 那是一份很赚钱的兼职工作。

e.en: The sidelines are the lines marking the long sides of the playing area, for example, on a football field or tennis court. (运动场地的)
If you are on the sidelines in a situation, you do not influence events at all, either because you have chosen not to be involved, or because other people have not involved you.

ex.en: France no longer wants to be left on the sidelines when critical decisions are made.
ex.zh: 法国再也不想在做出重大决定时被搁置一旁。

e.en: If someone or something is sidelined, they are made to seem unimportant and not included in what people are doing. 把…排除在外;

ex.en: For months he had been under pressure to resign and was about to be sidelined anyway.
ex.zh: 几个月以来他一直处在辞职的压力下，他无论如何都是要靠边站了。

d: v. 使靠边站，使边缘化，把…排除在外；使（运动员）因伤病等不能上场；使…持观望态度（常用被动语态；sideline 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 退出的，不能参赛的；被搁置的，被边缘化的（sideline 的过去分词形式）

e.en: If large numbers of people or animals are slaughtered, they are killed in a way that is cruel or unnecessary.

ex.en: Thirty four people were slaughtered while lining up to cast their votes.
ex.zh: 有34人在排队投票时遭屠杀。

e.en: Slaughter is also a noun.

ex.en: This was only a small part of a war where the slaughter of civilians was commonplace.
ex.zh: 这只是战争的一小部分，在战争中对平民的屠杀已司空见惯。

e.en: To slaughter animals such as cows and sheep means to kill them for their meat.

ex.en: Lack of chicken feed means that chicken farms are having to slaughter their stock.
ex.zh: 饲料不足意味着养鸡场将不得不宰杀鸡。

e.en: Slaughter is also a noun.

ex.en: More than 491,000 sheep were exported for slaughter last year.
ex.zh: 去年，超过四十九万一千只羊被出口供屠宰。

d: v. 屠杀；屠宰（slaughtered 是 slaughter 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被屠宰的；被屠杀的（分词形容词）

e.en: Starvation is extreme suffering or death, caused by lack of food. 饥饿;

ex.en: Over three hundred people have died of starvation since the beginning of the year.
ex.zh: 自那年年初开始，已有三百多人饿死了。

d: n. 饥饿，捱饿，饿死

e.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way. (正式或明确的口头或书面) 陈述;

ex.en: Andrew now disowns that statement, saying he was depressed when he made it.
ex.zh: 安德鲁现在否认了那个声明，说那是自己心情沮丧时作的。

e.en: A statement is an official or formal announcement that is issued on a particular occasion. (在特定场合的官方或正式的)

ex.en: The statement by the military denied any involvement in last night's attack.
ex.zh: 军方的声明否认其与昨晚的袭击有任何关系。

e.en: You can refer to the official account of events which a suspect or a witness gives to the police as a statement. (嫌犯或证人向警方提供的) 陈述;

ex.en: The 350-page report was based on statements from witnesses to the events.
ex.zh: 这份350页的报告基于该事件目击者的证词。

e.en: If you describe an action or thing as a statement, you mean that it clearly expresses a particular opinion or idea that you have. (某观点的)

ex.en: The following recipe is a statement of another kind – food is fun!
ex.zh: 下面的食谱是另一种表述–食物就是乐趣！

d: n. 声明，报告；说明，说法，表态；结算单，报表；（某观点的） 表达；（嫌犯或证人向警方提供的） 陈述，证词；（文字）陈述，表述；评估报告（英国地方教育主管部门针对儿童的特殊需要而提出意见）；（乐）（作品主题或旋律的）呈现；（计算机程序中的）语句
vt. 对儿童进行特殊教育评估认定

e.en: When there is a strike, workers stop doing their work for a period of time, usually in order to try to get better pay or conditions for themselves.

ex.en: Air traffic controllers have begun a three-day strike in a dispute over pay.
ex.zh: 空中交通管制员在一场薪酬纠纷中开始了为时3天的罢工。

ex.en: Staff at the hospital went on strike in protest at the incidents.
ex.zh: 这个医院的员工举行罢工，抗议这些事件。

e.en: A military strike is a military attack, especially an air attack.

ex.en: ...a punitive air strike.
ex.zh: …一次惩罚性空袭。

e.en: the act or an instance of knocking down all the pins with the first bowl of a single frame
the score thus made

d: n. 罢工；攻击，袭击（strike 的复数；军事打击尤指空袭）
v. 打，击；碰撞；攻击，袭击；罢工；（疾病、灾难等）突然发生并侵袭；使突然想到；给…留下某种印象（strike 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A takeover is the act of gaining control of a company by buying more of its shares than anyone else. (公司的)

ex.en: He lost his job in a corporate takeover.
ex.zh: 他在一次公司收购中丢掉了工作。

e.en: A takeover is the act of taking control of a country, political party, or movement by force. (用武力的)

ex.en: There's been a military takeover of some kind.
ex.zh: 曾发生过一次类似军事接管的事情。

d: n. 接管；验收

e.en: A survivor of a disaster, accident, or illness is someone who continues to live afterward in spite of coming close to death.

ex.en: Officials said there were no survivors of the plane crash.
ex.zh: 官员们说这次飞机失事中没有幸存者。

e.en: A survivor of a very unpleasant experience is a person who has had such an experience, and who is still affected by it.

ex.en: This book is written with survivors of child sexual abuse in mind.
ex.zh: 这本书写的是关于童年时经受过性虐待的人。

e.en: A person's survivors are the members of their family who continue to live after they have died. (家中)

ex.en: The compensation bill offers the miners or their survivors as much as $100,000 apiece.
ex.zh: 这笔赔偿款提供给这些矿工或其尚活着的家人每人$100000。

d: n. 幸存者（survivor 的复数），指在灾难、事故、疾病等危险事件后活下来的人；经受过创伤或不幸的人；（法律）遗属，尚在世的家人；泛指比他人活得长的人

e.en: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object. 靶; (攻击的)

ex.en: The village lies beside a main road, making it an easy target for bandits.
ex.zh: 该村位于大路边，容易成为匪徒攻击的目标。

e.en: A target is a result that you are trying to achieve. (试图达成的)

ex.en: She's won back her place too late to achieve her target of 20 goals this season.
ex.zh: 她赢回她的位置为时已晚,无法实现她本赛季打进20个球的目标。

e.en: To target a particular person or thing means to decide to attack or criticize them. 把…作为攻击目标;

ex.en: Republicans targeted her as vulnerable in her bid for reelection this year.
ex.zh: 共和党人认为她在今年的再次参选中是不堪一击的攻击目标。

e.en: Target is also a noun. (攻击、批评的)

ex.en: In the past they have been the target of racist abuse.
ex.zh: 过去他们一直是种族虐待的对象。

d: n. （营销）目标市场选择，确定目标市场；（广告／网络营销）定向，按内容、用户特征、地域或投放位置等选择目标受众
v. 把……作为目标，以……为对象，针对（target 的 ing 形式，即现在分词／动名词）

e.en: In a court of law, someone's testimony is a formal statement that they make about what they saw someone do or what they know of a situation, after having promised to tell the truth. (法庭上的)

ex.en: His testimony was an important element of the prosecution's case.
ex.zh: 他的证词是本起公诉案中的一个重要因素。

e.en: If you say that one thing is testimony to another, you mean that it shows clearly that the second thing has a particular quality.

ex.en: The environmental movement is testimony to the widespread feelings of support for nature's importance.
ex.zh: 环保运动是大自然重要性得到广泛认可的明证。

d: n. （尤指法庭上的）证词，证言；证据，证明；（宗教皈依或经历的）公开表白

e.en: If someone is tortured, another person deliberately causes them terrible pain over a period of time, in order to punish them or to make them reveal information. 拷打;

ex.en: Despite being tortured she proclaimed her innocence.
ex.zh: 尽管受到拷打，她仍声称自己是清白的。

e.en: Torture is also a noun. 拷打;

ex.en: ...alleged cases of torture and murder by the security forces.
ex.zh: …安全部队涉嫌严刑拷打与谋杀的案子。

e.en: To torture someone means to cause them to suffer mental pain or anxiety. (精神上)

ex.en: He would not torture her further by trying to argue with her.
ex.zh: 他不会通过和她争吵而进一步折磨她。

d: n. 拷打，拷问，酷刑逼供；折磨，煎熬；变形
v. 拷打，拷问，严刑逼供；造成精神上的巨大痛苦，使忧虑；扭曲
adj. 未加解释的；未包括在某数目中的；（人）行踪不明的
adj. 总的，全部的；完全的，绝对的
v. 总数达，总计；把……加起来；彻底毁坏（汽车）；杀死，严重伤害（某人）
n. 总数，合计
【名】 （Total）（法、德）托塔尔（人名）

e.en: If something is unlawful, the law does not allow you to do it.

ex.en: ...employees who believe their dismissal was unlawful.
ex.zh: …认为其被解雇不合法的雇员们。

e.en: 不合法地

ex.en: The government acted unlawfully in imposing the restrictions.
ex.zh: 政府不合法地采取行动强加制约。

d: adj. 非法的，违法的；（旧）私生的，非婚生的

e.en: Women is the plural of . (woman)

d: n. 女人，女性，妇女（woman 的复数）

e.en: A set of things is a number of things that belong together or that are thought of as a group. 套;

ex.en: There must be one set of laws for the whole of the country.
ex.zh: 必须有一套适用于全国的法律。

ex.en: The mattress and base are normally bought as a set.
ex.zh: 床垫和床基通常成套购买。

e.en: In tennis, a set is one of the groups of six or more games that form part of a match. (网球赛的)

ex.en: Graf was leading 5-1 in the first set.
ex.zh: 格拉夫在首盘比赛中以5-1领先。

e.en: In mathematics, a set is a group of mathematical quantities that have some characteristic in common.

ex.en: ...the field of set theory.
ex.zh: …集合论领域。

e.en: The set for a play, movie, or television show is the furniture and scenery that is on the stage when the play is being performed or in the studio where filming takes place. (话剧的) 布景; (电影的) 摄影棚;

ex.en: From the first moment he got on the set, he wanted to be a director too.
ex.zh: 从踏进摄影棚的第一刻起，他就也想成为一名导演。

ex.en: He achieved fame for his stage sets for the Folies Bergeres.
ex.zh: 他因为为《疯狂的藤椅》设计舞台布景而一举成名。

d: v. 放，置；使开始；把故事情节安排在；设置；摆放餐具；镶嵌；安排；树立；布置；凝固；使现出坚定的表情；固定发型；把（断骨）复位；排版；为……谱曲；落（下）；布置（戏剧、电影或电视节目的布景）；（断骨）愈合
n. 一组（类似的东西）；一组（配套使用的东西）；一伙（或一帮、一群）人；电视机；布景 ；舞台；（网球、排球比赛等的）盘；集；一组歌曲（或乐曲）；（在某学科上能力相当的）一批学生 ；（尤指坚定的）姿势；头发的定型；凝固；兽穴；（供移植的）秧苗
adj. 位于（或处于）……的；安排好的；固定的；套（餐）；有可能的；不自然的
【名】 （Set）（瑞、以）塞特（人名）
n. 催泪性毒气
vt. 用催泪瓦斯袭击

e.en: A cannon is a large gun, usually on wheels, which used to be used in battles.

ex.en: The cannons boom, the band plays.
ex.zh: 炮声隆隆，鼓乐齐鸣。

e.en: A cannon is a heavy automatic gun, especially one that is fired from an aircraft.

ex.en: Others carried huge cannons plundered from Russian aircraft.
ex.zh: 其他人扛着从俄国飞机上抢来的巨型机关炮。

e.en: If someone is a loose cannon, they do whatever they want and nobody can predict what they are going to do.

ex.en: Max is a loose cannon politically.
ex.zh: 马克斯是个在政治上随心所欲的人。

d: n. 加农炮，大炮；自动机关炮
v. 猛撞，碰撞；炮轰
【名】 （Cannon）（英、葡）坎农（人名）

e.en: When something disperses or when you disperse it, it spreads over a wide area. 使分散;

ex.en: The oil appeared to be dispersing.
ex.zh: 油看上去正在扩散。

e.en: When a group of people disperses or when someone disperses them, the group splits up and the people leave in different directions. 驱散;

ex.en: Police fired shots and used tear gas to disperse the demonstrators.
ex.zh: 警察开枪并使用了催泪瓦斯来驱散示威人群。

d: v. 分散，散布；疏散，驱散；使（光）色散
adj. 分散的

e.en: Demonstrators are people who are marching or gathering somewhere to show their opposition to something or their support for something. 游行者;

ex.en: I saw the police using tear gas to try and break up a crowd of demonstrators.
ex.zh: 我看到警察使用催泪瓦斯试图驱散示威人群。

e.en: A demonstrator is a person who shows people how something works or how to do something.

ex.en: ...a demonstrator in a department store.
ex.zh: …一名百货商场的产品展示员。

d: n. 游行示威者；示范者（demonstrator 的名词复数）

e.en: A projectile is an object that is fired from a gun or other weapon. (枪炮或其他武器的)

d: n. projectile 的复数形式：射弹，投射物；（物理）抛射体。

e.en: To deploy troops or military resources means to organize or position them so that they are ready to be used.

ex.en: The president said he had no intention of deploying ground troops.
ex.zh: 总统说他无意调遣地面部队。

d: v. 部署，调遣，展开；运用，采用（手段、方法、资源等）；（计算机）部署，上线（软件、系统、服务等）（均为 deploy 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已部署的，展开的（部队、设备、软件、系统、服务等）

e.en: When people clash, they fight, argue, or disagree with each other. 发生冲突;

ex.en: A group of 400 demonstrators ripped down the front gate and clashed with police.
ex.zh: 400名示威者推倒前面的大前门，与警察发生了冲突。

ex.en: Behind the scenes, Parsons clashed with almost everyone on the show.
ex.zh: 幕后，帕森斯几乎跟每个参与演出的人都产生过矛盾。

e.en: Clash is also a noun.

ex.en: There have been a number of clashes between police in riot gear and demonstrators.
ex.zh: 穿防暴服的警察和示威者之间发生过多次冲突。

e.en: Beliefs, ideas, or qualities that clash with each other are very different from each other and therefore are opposed. (因信仰、观点或质量不同而)

ex.en: Don't make any policy decisions which clash with official company thinking.
ex.zh: 不要做与公司官方理念有分歧的任何政策性决定。

e.en: Clash is also a noun.

ex.en: Inside government, there was a clash of views.
ex.zh: 政府内部有意见分歧。

d: n. （clash 的复数）冲突，打斗；意见分歧，对立；铿锵声，碰撞声；（颜色、风格的）不协调
v. （clash 的第三人称单数）发生冲突，产生矛盾；（信仰、观点等）抵触，相矛盾；时间上冲突，撞期；（颜色、风格）不协调

e.en: a show in which large numbers of fireworks are let off simultaneously (大量烟火同时燃放的)

d: n. 烟火，烟花，焰火（firework 的复数形式）；烟花表演，焰火表演；激烈争论

e.en: If you hurl something, you throw it violently and with a lot of force.

ex.en: Groups of angry youths hurled stones at police.
ex.zh: 一群群愤怒的年轻人朝着警察猛掷石块。

ex.en: Simon caught the grenade and hurled it back.
ex.zh: 西蒙接住手榴弹，把它掷了回去。

e.en: If you hurl abuse or insults at someone, you shout insults at them aggressively.

ex.en: How would you handle being locked in the back of a cab while the driver hurled abuse at you?
ex.zh: 如果你被锁在出租车后座又遭司机谩骂，你会怎么办？

d: v. （hurl 的过去式和过去分词）猛力投掷，用力抛出；大声辱骂，厉声叫骂（多用于 hurl abuse/insults at 某人）
adv. 更大声地，大声一点（loud 作副词时的比较级）
adj. 更响亮的，更大声的（loud 的比较级）

e.en: When soldiers march somewhere, or when a commanding officer marches them somewhere, they walk there with very regular steps, as a group. 使齐步走;

ex.en: A U.S. infantry battalion was marching down the street.
ex.zh: 一个美军步兵营沿着街道行进。

ex.en: Captain Ramirez called them to attention and marched them off to the main camp.
ex.zh: 拉米雷斯上校命令他们立正，然后让他们向主营地行进。

e.en: March is also a noun.

ex.en: After a short march, the column entered the village.
ex.zh: 短途行军之后，队伍进入了村子。

e.en: a frontier, border, or boundary or the land lying along it, often of disputed ownership (所有权常有争议的)边界; 边疆; 边地 (Also called marchland)
When a large group of people march for a cause, they walk somewhere together in order to express their ideas or to protest about something.

ex.en: The demonstrators then marched through the capital chanting slogans and demanding free elections.
ex.zh: 示威者然后穿越首都游行，反复喊着口号，要求进行自由选举。

d: v. march 的过去式和过去分词：行进，行军，按照一定的节奏或步伐向前移动（通常用于军队或游行队伍）；游行，示威游行；（因愤怒等）坚定地快步走；迫使（某人）同行，押送

e.en: You use mostly to indicate that a statement is generally true, for example true about the majority of a group of things or people, true most of the time, or true in most respects. 主要地;

ex.en: I am working with mostly highly motivated people.
ex.zh: 我正与大多都积极性很高的人们共事。

ex.en: Cars are mostly metal.
ex.zh: 汽车大多是金属制成的。

d: adv. 多半，主要地；几乎全部，几乎所有

e.en: Protesters are people who protest publicly about an issue.

ex.en: The protesters say the government is corrupt and inefficient.
ex.zh: 抗议者指责政府腐败无能。

d: n. 抗议者，示威者；持异议者，反对者

e.en: A recent event or period of time happened only a short while ago.

ex.en: In the most recent attack, one man was shot dead and two others were wounded.
ex.zh: 在最近的这次袭击中有1人被打死，另2人受伤。

d: adj. 最近的，最新的；（地质）全新世的 （Recent）
n. 暴徒；暴民；骚乱者

e.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party.

ex.en: About three thousand people held a rally to mark international human rights day.
ex.zh: 大约三千人举行集会以纪念国际人权日。

e.en: When people rally to something or when something rallies them, they unite to support it. 一致支持;

ex.en: Her cabinet colleagues have continued to rally to her support.
ex.zh: 她的内阁同僚们继续团结一致地支持她。

e.en: to bring (a group, unit, etc) into order, as after dispersal, or (of such a group) to reform and come to order 重整;

ex.en: the troops rallied for a final assault

e.en: When someone or something rallies, they begin to recover or improve after having been weak. 恢复健康;

ex.en: He rallied enough to thank his doctors.
ex.zh: 他身体恢复得能向医生们道谢了。

d: n. rally 的复数：集会；价格回升，反弹；公路汽车赛；（网球、羽毛球、壁球等的）连续对打
v. rally 的第三人称单数：集合，召集；团结起来；恢复，好转；（行情、价格）回升

e.en: You can refer to people in general, or to all the people in a particular country or community, as the public.

ex.en: The park is now open to the public.
ex.zh: 那公园现在对公众开放了。

ex.en: Pure alcohol is not for sale to the general public.
ex.zh: 纯酒精是不对大众销售的。

e.en: You can refer to a set of people in a country who share a common interest, activity, or characteristic as a particular kind of public.

ex.en: Market research showed that 93% of the viewing public wanted a hit movie channel.
ex.zh: 市场调查显示，93%的收视群体希望有一个热门电影频道。

e.en: Public means relating to all the people in a country or community.

ex.en: The president is attempting to drum up public support for his economic programme.
ex.zh: 总统正试图为他的经济计划争取公众的支持。

e.en: Public means relating to the government or state, or things that are done for the people by the state.

ex.en: The social services account for a substantial part of public spending.
ex.zh: 社会服务性事业占政府开支的相当大的一部分。

d: adj. 公众的，大众的；公共的，公用的；政府的，公众事务的； 大学的，为大学的；（声明、事件等）公开的，公诸于众的；公开场合的，大庭广众的；上市的；众所周知的，广为人知的
n. 公众，大众（the public）；志趣相投（或从事同一类活动、具有共同特征）的群体；（对某个艺术家、作家或表演家感兴趣的）读者，观众（one's public）；（酒馆中的）低价吧台（=public bar），酒吧（=public house）；公共场所
【名】  （Public）（英）帕布利克（人名）

e.en: We're is the usual spoken form of "we are." (we are)

ex.en: I'm married, but we're separated.
ex.zh: 我已婚，但是我们分居了。

d: abbr. 我们是（we are）

e.en: You use yes to give a positive response to a question. 是的 (用以对问题作肯定回答)

ex.en: "Are you a friend of Nick's?"—"Yes."
ex.zh: “你是尼克的朋友吗？”—“是的。”

ex.en: "You actually wrote it down, didn't you?"—"Yes."
ex.zh: “你实际上把它写下来了，不是吗？”—“是的。”

e.en: You use yes to accept an offer or request, or to give permission. 好的 (用以接受提议、要求或给予许可)

ex.en: "More wine?"—"Yes please."
ex.zh: “再要点儿葡萄酒？”—“好的，请来点。”

ex.en: "Will you take me there?"—"Yes, I will."
ex.zh: “你带我去那儿吗？”—“好的，我会的。”

e.en: You use yes to tell someone that what they have said is correct. 对 (用以告诉某人他所说的是正确的)

ex.en: "Well I suppose it is based on the old lunar months, isn't it?"—"Yes, that's right."
ex.zh: “嗯，我想它是基于旧的阴历月份的，不是吗？”—“对，是那样的。”

e.en: You use yes to show that you are ready or willing to speak to the person who wants to speak to you, for example when you are answering a telephone or a knock at your door. 请讲; 请进 (用于表示准备好或愿意跟想跟自己说话的人说话)

ex.en: He pushed a button on the intercom. "Yes?" came a voice.
ex.zh: 他按了对讲机的一个按钮。“什么事？”传来一个声音。

d: adv. 是，是的，对；是吗？（升调，表示疑问或请对方继续说）
n. 是（表示肯定），肯定答复；赞成票

e.en: When you approach something, you get closer to it.

ex.en: He didn't approach the front door at once.
ex.zh: 他没有立即走近前门。

ex.en: When I approached, they grew silent.
ex.zh: 当我走近时，他们变得沉默了。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: At their approach the little boy ran away and hid.
ex.zh: 当他们走近时，那个小男孩跑开了并藏了起来。

e.en: If you approach someone about something, you speak to them about it for the first time, often making an offer or request.

ex.en: When Brown approached me about the job, my first reaction was of disbelief.
ex.zh: 当布朗为这份工作找我时，我的第一反应是不相信。

ex.en: He approached me to create and design the restaurant.
ex.zh: 他来找我创办并设计那家餐馆。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: There had already been approaches from buyers interested in the whole of the group.
ex.zh: 已经有一些对整个集团感兴趣的买主来接洽了。

d: v. approach 的过去式和过去分词：接近，走近；临近（指时间或事件）；与…接洽，就某事找某人谈；处理，应对（任务、问题或情况）；几乎达到（某水平或状态）

e.en: Something that is ablaze is burning very fiercely.

ex.en: Stores, houses, and vehicles were set ablaze.
ex.zh: 商店、房子和车辆被大火烧着了。

e.en: If a place is ablaze with lights or colours, it is very bright because of them.

ex.en: The chamber was ablaze with light.
ex.zh: 该大厅当时灯火辉煌。

d: adj. （通常作表语）着火的，熊熊燃烧的；闪耀的，光亮的；激昂的，兴奋的，愤怒的

e.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

ex.en: You can remain anonymous if you wish.
ex.zh: 如果你愿意你可以保持匿名。

ex.en: An anonymous benefactor stepped in to provide the prize money.
ex.zh: 一位匿名捐助人参与进来提供了奖金。

e.en: 匿名

ex.en: Both mother and daughter, who have requested anonymity, are doing fine.
ex.zh: 要求匿名的母女情况都好。

e.en: Something that is anonymous does not reveal who you are.

ex.en: Of course, that would have to be by anonymous vote.
ex.zh: 当然，那得是通过不记名投票。

e.en: 不记名

ex.en: He claims many more people would support him in the anonymity of a voting booth.
ex.zh: 他声称在投票站不记名的情况下更多的人会支持他。

d: adj. 匿名的，不知名的；不记名的，不具名的；无特色的

e.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

ex.en: We all have to stay alert.
ex.zh: 我们都必须保持警觉。

e.en: 警觉性

ex.en: The drug improved mental alertness.
ex.zh: 这种药物提高了大脑的灵敏度。

e.en: If you are alert to something, you are fully aware of it.

ex.en: The bank is alert to the danger.
ex.zh: 该银行对这种危险有警觉。

e.en: An alert is a situation in which people prepare themselves for something dangerous that might happen soon.

ex.en: There has been criticism of how his administration handled last week's terrorism alert.
ex.zh: 对他的政府对待上周恐怖主义戒备状态的方式有批评之辞。

d: adj. 警惕的，警觉的；机敏的，敏捷的；意识到，注意到（alert to）
v. 向……报警，使警觉；提示，提醒（某人）
n. 警报，警示；警戒，警惕；（电子设备的）提示信号；警戒期
【名】 （Alert）（美、德、俄、西、印）阿莱尔特（人名）

e.en: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.

ex.en: Fifty civilians in Masawa were killed when government planes attacked the town.
ex.zh: 马萨瓦50名平民在政府飞机袭击该市时丧生。

ex.en: He bundled the old lady into her hallway and brutally attacked her.
ex.zh: 他把老太太推进她家门厅里，并且野蛮地袭击了她。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a campaign of air attacks on strategic targets.
ex.zh: …对战略目标的空袭行动。

e.en: If you attack a person, belief, idea, or act, you criticize them strongly.

ex.en: He publicly attacked the people who've been calling for secret ballot nominations.
ex.zh: 他公开抨击了那些一直要求秘密投票提名的人。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: The role of the state as a prime mover in planning social change has been under attack.
ex.zh: 国家作为规划社会变革发起者的角色已经遭到抨击。

d: v. attack 的现在分词：攻击，进攻，袭击；抨击；（疾病、化学物质、昆虫等）侵害，损害；（球类运动）攻球
adj. 攻击性的，进攻型的

e.en: If you avoid something unpleasant that might happen, you take action in order to prevent it from happening. 避免 (坏事的发生)

ex.en: The pilots had to take emergency action to avoid a disaster.
ex.zh: 飞行员们不得不采取紧急措施以避免灾难的发生。

e.en: If you avoid doing something, you choose not to do it, or you put yourself in a situation where you do not have to do it.

ex.en: By borrowing from dozens of banks, he managed to avoid giving any of them an overall picture of what he was up to.
ex.zh: 通过向几十家银行借钱，他得以避免让任何一家了解他要做事情的全貌。

e.en: If you avoid a person or thing, you keep away from them. When talking to someone, if you avoid the subject, you keep the conversation away from a particular topic.

ex.en: She eventually had to lock herself in the women's restroom to avoid him.
ex.zh: 她最后不得不把自己锁在女厕所里避开他。

e.en: If a person or vehicle avoids someone or something, they change the direction they are moving in, so that they do not hit them. (人或车)

ex.en: The driver had ample time to brake or swerve and avoid the woman.
ex.zh: 该司机有足够的时间刹车或急转来避让那女子。

d: v. avoid 的现在分词；避免，防止；回避，避开；避免（做某事），逃避（做某事）；（法律）撤销，使无效

e.en: If something is done badly or goes badly, it is not very successful or effective.

ex.en: I was angry because I played so badly.
ex.zh: 我生气因为我弹得这么糟。

ex.en: The whole project was badly managed.
ex.zh: 整个项目管理得差劲。

e.en: If someone or something is badly hurt or badly affected, they are severely hurt or affected.

ex.en: The bomb destroyed a police station and badly damaged a church.
ex.zh: 炸弹炸毁了一个警察局，还严重毁坏了一座教堂。

ex.en: One man was killed and another badly injured.
ex.zh: 一男子死亡，另一个受重伤。

e.en: If you want or need something badly, you want or need it very much.

ex.en: Why do you want to go so badly?
ex.zh: 你为什么要这么急着走？

e.en: If someone behaves badly or treats other people badly, they act in an unkind, unpleasant, or unacceptable way. 不友善地; (待人)

ex.en: They have both behaved very badly and I am very hurt.
ex.zh: 他们俩都表现得极不友善，这令我很伤心。

d: adv. 严重地；差，拙劣地；很，非常；不友好地，恶劣地；不利地，负面地；（支付薪水）低地

e.en: A baton is a light, thin stick used by a conductor to conduct an orchestra or a choir. (乐队)

ex.en: The maestro raises his baton.
ex.zh: 大师举起他的指挥棒。

e.en: In track and field or track events, a baton is a short stick that is passed from one runner to another in a relay race.

ex.en: ...their biggest relay outing since dropping the baton in Edmonton last August.
ex.zh: …自去年8月在埃德蒙顿丢棒以来他们参加的最大的接力赛。

e.en: A baton is a short heavy stick which is sometimes used as a weapon by the police.

d: n. 指挥棒；接力棒（常用于 pass the baton，比喻移交职责）；警棍；权杖，司令棒；（Baton）人名（法）巴东，（阿尔巴）巴唐
n. 巴塞罗纳（西班牙）

e.en: A barricade is a line of vehicles or other objects placed across a road or open space to stop people from getting past, for example, during street fighting or as a protest. 街垒;

ex.en: Large areas of the city have been closed off by barricades set up by the demonstrators.
ex.zh: 城里的大部分地区都被示威者设置的路障给封锁了。

e.en: If you barricade something such as a road or an entrance, you place a barricade or barrier across it, usually to stop someone from getting in.

ex.en: The rioters barricaded streets with piles of blazing tyres.
ex.zh: 闹事者用成堆燃烧着的轮胎挡住了街道。

e.en: If you barricade yourself inside a room or building, you place barriers across the door or entrance so that other people cannot get in.

ex.en: The students have barricaded themselves into their dormitory building.
ex.zh: 学生们将自己堵在宿舍楼里。

d: n. 路障；隔板；障碍物；争论之处（barricade 的复数）
v. 设路障于；阻挡（barricade 的三单形式）

e.en: If a situation is bleak, it is bad, and seems unlikely to improve.

ex.en: The immediate outlook remains bleak.
ex.zh: 最近的前景依然很黯淡。

e.en: 黯淡

ex.en: The continued bleakness of the American job market was blamed.
ex.zh: 美国就业市场的持续低迷被认为是其根源。

e.en: If you describe a place as bleak, you mean that it looks cold, empty, and unattractive.

ex.en: The island's pretty bleak.
ex.zh: 这个岛很荒凉。

e.en: When the weather is bleak, it is cold, dull, and unpleasant.

ex.en: The weather can be quite bleak on the coast.
ex.zh: 沿海一带的天气可能会十分阴冷。

d: adj. 不乐观的，无望的；无遮掩的，荒凉的；阴冷的，寒冷的；沮丧的，阴郁的；（人或其表情）冷漠的，冷峻的
n. 欧鲌
n. 德国报纸《图片报》

e.en: A blockade of a place is an action that is taken to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving it.

ex.en: It's not yet clear who will actually enforce the blockade.
ex.zh: 目前还不清楚到底谁会来执行封锁。

e.en: If a group of people blockade a place, they stop goods or people from reaching that place. If they blockade a road or a port, they stop people from using that road or port.

ex.en: About 50,000 people are trapped in the town, which has been blockaded for more than 40 days.
ex.zh: 约有五万人被困在这个已经被封锁了40多天的小镇里。

d: n．封锁（复数）：阻止人员、物资进出某地区的行动，通常用于战争或紧急情况。
v．封锁（复数）：设立封锁线，阻止人员、物资进出某地区。

e.en: A bottle is a glass or plastic container in which drinks and other liquids are kept. Bottles are usually round with straight sides and a narrow top.

ex.en: There were two empty beer bottles on the table.
ex.zh: 桌上有两个空啤酒瓶。

ex.en: He was pulling the cork from a bottle of wine.
ex.zh: 他在拔一瓶葡萄酒的瓶塞。

e.en: You can use bottle to refer to a bottle and its contents, or to the contents only.

ex.en: She had drunk half a bottle of whisky.
ex.zh: 她已经喝了半瓶威士忌。

e.en: nerve; courage (esp in the phrase lose one's bottle) 胆量;
To bottle a drink or other liquid means to put it into bottles after it has been made.

ex.en: This is a large truck which has equipment to automatically bottle the wine.
ex.zh: 这是辆有葡萄酒自动装瓶设备的大卡车。

d: n. 瓶子（bottle 的复数）；瓶（指瓶中所盛之物或一瓶之量）；奶瓶
v. 装瓶，把…装入瓶中（bottle 的第三人称单数现在时）

e.en: Bologna is a type of large smoked sausage, usually made of beef, veal, or pork.

ex.en: ...a bologna sandwich.
ex.zh: …一个波隆那熏肠三明治。

d: n. 博洛尼亚大红肠（一种大腊肠）
n. 卡米尔（女子名）

e.en: A boulevard is a wide street in a city, usually with trees along each side.

ex.en: ...Lenton Boulevard.
ex.zh: …伦特林荫大道。

d: n. 林荫大道，城市中的宽阔大街；大马路
adj. 娱乐性的（尤指轻松通俗的戏剧、娱乐）
vt. 给…提供林荫大道；把…建成林荫大道

e.en: The centre of something is the middle of it.

ex.en: A large, wooden table dominates the centre of the room.
ex.zh: 一张大木桌占据了房间的中央。

e.en: A centre is a building where people have meetings, take part in a particular activity, or get help of some kind. (会议、活动、援助的)

ex.en: She now also does pottery classes at a community centre.
ex.zh: 她现在还在社区中心上陶艺课。

e.en: If an area or town is a centre for an industry or activity, that industry or activity is very important there. (行业、活动的) 中心;

ex.en: New York is also a major international financial centre.
ex.zh: 纽约也是一个重要的国际金融中心。

e.en: The centre of a town or city is the part where there are the most stores and businesses and where a lot of people come from other areas to work or shop. (镇、市的)

ex.en: ...the city centre.
ex.zh: …市中心。

d: n. （地理位置）中间，中心点；（机构，组织）活动中心；关注点，焦点；中间派，中间立场；中锋
v. 把……放在中央；（使）以……为中心，（使）注意力集中于；（使）主要发生在，（使）集中于
【名】 （Centre）（澳、印、肯尼亚）森特尔（人名）

e.en: If you charge someone an amount of money, you ask them to pay that amount for something that you have sold to them or done for them. 要价;

ex.en: Even local nurseries charge $150 a week.
ex.zh: 即便当地的托儿所每周也要收$150的费用。

ex.en: Some banks charge if you access your account to determine your balance.
ex.zh: 如果你进入自己的账户查看余额，有些银行要收费。

e.en: To charge something to a person or organization means to tell the people providing it to send the bill to that person or organization. To charge something to someone's account means to add it to their account so they can pay for it later. 开帐单;

ex.en: Go out and buy a pair of glasses, and charge it to us.
ex.zh: 出去买一副眼镜，记在我们的账上。

e.en: When the police charge someone, they formally accuse them of having done something illegal.

ex.en: They have the evidence to charge him.
ex.zh: 他们有证据来指控他。

e.en: If you charge toward someone or something, you move quickly and aggressively toward them.

ex.en: He charged through the door to my mother's office.
ex.zh: 他破门而入，进了我母亲的办公室。

ex.en: He ordered us to charge.
ex.zh: 他命令我们冲锋。

d: n. （常作复数）费用，手续费，运费；（法律）指控，罪名；（物理／化学）电荷
v. （charge 的第三人称单数）要价，收费；指控，控告；充电；命令，指派

e.en: A cent is a small unit of money worth one hundredth of some currencies, for example the dollar and the euro. 分 (如美元、欧元等基本货币单位的1%)

ex.en: A cup of rice which cost thirty cents a few weeks ago is now being sold for up to one dollar.
ex.zh: 几周前价值30美分的1杯米如今卖到了1美元。

d: n. cent 的复数形式：分，美分；一分硬币。
n. 沙伦顿（美国地名）

e.en: If you talk about the condition of a person or thing, you are talking about the state that they are in, especially how good or bad their physical state is. (尤指健康)

ex.en: He remains in a critical condition in a California hospital.
ex.zh: 他在加利福尼亚的一家医院里，仍处于危急的状况。

ex.en: I received several compliments on the condition of my skin.
ex.zh: 我得到好几次有关我皮肤的状况的夸赞。

e.en: The conditions under which something is done or happens are all the factors or circumstances which directly affect it. (某事完成或发生的)

ex.en: It's easy to make a wrong turn here even under ideal weather conditions.
ex.zh: 即使在非常理想的天气条件下，也很容易在这里拐错弯。

e.en: The conditions in which people live or work are the factors which affect their comfort, safety, or health. (生活或工作的)

ex.en: People are living in appalling conditions.
ex.zh: 人们生活在极其恶劣的环境中。

ex.en: I could not work in these conditions any longer.
ex.zh: 我再也不能在这样的环境中工作了。

e.en: A condition is something which must happen or be done in order for something else to be possible, especially when this is written into a contract or law. (尤指写进合同或法律中的某事发生的)

ex.en: Argentina failed to hit the economic targets set as a condition for loan payments.
ex.zh: 阿根廷没能达到作为贷款偿还条件而设的的经济目标。

ex.en: ...terms and conditions of employment.
ex.zh: …雇用条款和条件。

d: n. 条件，情况，环境，状况；疾病，健康问题；条款，条件（condition 的复数）
v. 训练，使习惯于；控制，制约，影响；护理，保养；规定，以……为条件（condition 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A cocktail is an alcoholic drink which contains several ingredients.

ex.en: On arrival, guests are offered wine or a champagne cocktail.
ex.zh: 到达时，客人们可以享用葡萄酒或一份香槟鸡尾酒。

e.en: A cocktail is a mixture of a number of different things, especially ones that do not go together well. (尤指不太容易融合的几种物品的)

ex.en: The court was told she had taken a cocktail of drugs and alcohol.
ex.zh: 法庭被告知她服用了药酒混合剂。

e.en: a horse with a docked tail

d: n. 鸡尾酒；混合物；杂锦冷盘
adj. 鸡尾酒的
v. 喝鸡尾酒

e.en: The destination of someone or something is the place to which they are going or being sent.

ex.en: Ellis Island has become one of America's most popular tourist destinations.
ex.zh: 埃利斯岛已经成为美国最受欢迎的游览地之一。

d: n. 目的地，终点，目标
adj. 作为目的地的

e.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

ex.en: There are fears that the situation might deteriorate into full-scale war.
ex.zh: 人们担心局势会恶化为全面战争。

e.en: 恶化

ex.en: ...concern about the rapid deterioration in relations between the two countries.
ex.zh: …对两国关系迅速恶化的担忧。

d: v. 退化，恶化（deteriorate 的现在分词形式）
adj. 恶化的，变坏的，日益恶化的

e.en: A dress is a piece of clothing worn by a woman or girl. It covers her body and part of her legs.

ex.en: She was wearing a black dress.
ex.zh: 她穿着一套黑色连衣裙。

e.en: You can refer to clothes worn by men or women as dress.

ex.en: He wore formal evening dress.
ex.zh: 他穿了正式的晚礼服。

e.en: When you dress or dress yourself, you put on clothes.

ex.en: He told Sarah to wait while he dressed.
ex.zh: 他让莎拉等着他穿好衣服。

e.en: If you dress someone, for example, a child, you put clothes on them.

ex.en: She bathed her and dressed her in clean clothes.
ex.zh: 她给她洗了澡并穿上干净衣服。

d: n. 连衣裙，套裙；（特定种类的）服装，衣服；（统指）服装；（上下连身的）女装，童装
v. 穿衣；给……穿衣服；穿正式服装；清洗包扎（伤口）；调制；加工，处理（食材、材料等）；整队；布置，装饰；为……制作或挑选衣服；做头发
【名】 （Dress）（美、巴）德雷斯（人名）

e.en: If you are in disguise, you are not wearing your usual clothes or you have altered your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.

ex.en: You'll have to travel in disguise.
ex.zh: 你将不得不乔装出行。

e.en: If you disguise yourself, you put on clothes which make you look like someone else or alter your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.

ex.en: She disguised herself as a man so she could fight on the battlefield.
ex.zh: 她女扮男装以便能上战场打仗。

e.en: 乔装的

ex.en: The extremists entered the building disguised as medical workers.
ex.zh: 极端分子们假扮成医务人员，进入了大楼。

e.en: To disguise something means to hide it or make it appear different so that people will not know about it or will not recognize it.

ex.en: He made no attempt to disguise his agitation.
ex.zh: 他无意掩饰他的不安。

d: adj. 伪装的，乔装的，假扮的；掩饰的，隐蔽的，变相的
v. 伪装，乔装，掩饰，掩盖（disguise 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Drew is the past tense of draw. (draw)

d: v. draw 的过去式：牵引，拖，拉；画，描绘；起草，拟定；朝某方向移动，如靠近、离开。
n. (Drew)（美）德鲁（人名），英语男子名或姓氏，常作 Andrew 的昵称。

e.en: Education involves teaching people various subjects, usually at a school or college, or being taught.

ex.en: They're cutting funds for education.
ex.zh: 他们正在削减教育经费。

e.en: Education of a particular kind involves teaching the public about a particular issue.

ex.en: ...better health education.
ex.zh: …更好的健康教育。

d: n. （尤指学校）教育；培养，训练；教育机构，教育界人士；教育学；有教益的经历

e.en: An egg is an oval object that is produced by a female bird and contains a baby bird. Other animals such as reptiles and fish also lay eggs. 蛋;

ex.en: ...a baby bird hatching from its egg.
ex.zh: …一只从蛋壳里孵出来的雏鸟。

e.en: In many countries, eggs often means hen's eggs, eaten as food.

ex.en: Break the eggs into a shallow bowl and beat them lightly.
ex.zh: 把鸡蛋打在一个浅碗里并且稍微搅打。

e.en: Egg is used to refer to an object in the shape of a hen's egg.

ex.en: ...a chocolate egg.
ex.zh: …一个巧克力蛋。

e.en: An egg is a cell that is produced in the bodies of female animals and humans. If it is fertilized by a sperm, a baby develops from it.

ex.en: It only takes one sperm to fertilize an egg.
ex.zh: 只需一个精子就可以使卵受精。

d: n. [禽]蛋（egg 的复数形式）；鸡蛋

e.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

ex.en: ...a government comprised mainly of the elite.
ex.zh: …主要由精英组成的政府。

e.en: Elite people or organizations are considered to be the best of their kind.

ex.en: ...the elite troops of the president's bodyguard.
ex.zh: …总统卫队中的精英部队。

d: n. 权力集团，上层人士；尖子，精英
adj. 出类拔萃的，精锐的

e.en: Elsewhere means in other places or to another place. 在别处地;

ex.en: Almost 80 percent of the state's residents were born elsewhere.
ex.zh: 这个州几乎百分之八十的居民是在其他地方出生的。

ex.en: They were living well, in comparison with people elsewhere in the world.
ex.zh: 和世界上其他地方的人们比起来，他们过着舒适的生活。

d: adv. 在别处，去别处
pron. 别处，别的地方
n. 以马内利（耶稣基督的别称）；伊曼纽尔（男子名，等于 Immanuel）

e.en: Fell is the past tense of . (fall)
If trees are felled, they are cut down.

ex.en: Badly infected trees should be felled and burned.
ex.zh: 严重感染的树木应该被砍掉并焚烧。

e.en: cruel or fierce; terrible 凶残的;
an animal skin or hide

d: n. （尤指英格兰北部的）山（冈），丘陵，高沼地；采伐的木材数量；兽皮，生皮
v. 砍伐；击倒；把（接缝的边）缝平； 掉下，跌落（fall 的过去式形式）
adj. 凶恶的，残暴的；和丘陵、小山有关的
【名】 （Fell）（美、英、德、法）费尔（人名）

e.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, for example because it has a lot of decoration.

ex.en: The magazine was packaged in a fancy plastic case with attractive graphics.
ex.zh: 这本杂志装在一个带有漂亮图纹的别致塑料盒子里。

e.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is very expensive or of very high quality, and you often dislike it because of this.

ex.en: My parents sent me to a fancy private school.
ex.zh: 我父母把我送到了一所阔气的私立学校。

e.en: If you fancy yourself as a particular kind of person or fancy yourself doing a particular thing, you like the idea of being that kind of person or doing that thing. 认为 (自己)

ex.en: So you fancy yourself as the boss someday?
ex.zh: 那么你认为自己有一天会成老板？

e.en: If you say that someone fancies themselves as a particular kind of person, you mean that they think, often wrongly, that they have the good qualities which that kind of person has. (自)

ex.en: She fancies herself a bohemian.
ex.zh: 她自命为一个放荡不羁的艺术家。

d: v.  喜欢，想要； 爱恋，爱慕； 认为……会成功（赢）； 认为，想象；自负，自命不凡（fancy oneself）； （表示惊奇或震惊）真想不到，竟然；爱恋，爱慕（常用于英式口语中）； 喜欢，想要（常用于英式口语中）；爱恋，爱慕（常用于英式口语中）；认为……会成功（赢）
n. 喜欢，想要；想象，想象力，想象的事物； （无根据的）想法，空想；花色小蛋糕；（赛马或其他体育比赛中）最被看好的人（或动物）； 喜爱的人（或事物）；（16和17世纪音乐用语）幻想曲；（无根据的）想法，空想
adj. 时髦的，奢华的；华丽的，花哨的；复杂的，高难度的；（食品）特级的，优质的；娴熟的，巧妙的；（花）杂色的；（动物）供观赏的；（画，雕塑）凭想像创作的，想像出来的
【名】 （Fancy）范茜（人名）

e.en: fly

d: v. 飞，飞翔（fly 的过去式）
n. （Flew）（英、美）弗卢（人名）

e.en: Fireworks are small objects that are lit to entertain people on special occasions. They contain chemicals and burn brightly or attractively, often with a loud noise, when you light them.

ex.en: They drank champagne, set off fireworks and tooted their car horns.
ex.zh: 他们喝香槟、放烟花，还按他们的车喇叭。

d: n. 烟火，烟花；焰火表演（fireworks）；（愤怒等情绪的）爆发，（才智、活力的）展现（fireworks）；精彩难忘的演出（或作品）（fireworks）

e.en: A gathering is a group of people meeting together for a particular purpose.

ex.en: ...the twenty-second annual gathering of the South Pacific Forum.
ex.zh: …第22届南太平洋论坛年会。

e.en: If there is gathering darkness, the light is gradually decreasing, usually because it is nearly night. 逐渐 (进入黑夜)

ex.en: The lighthouse beam was quite distinct in the gathering dusk.
ex.zh: 灯塔的光柱在渐暗的黄昏中相当清楚。

d: n. 聚会，集会（gathering 的复数）

e.en: A gendarme is a member of the French police force. (法国)

d: n. 宪兵（gendarme 的复数）

e.en: A grenade or a hand grenade is a small bomb that can be thrown by hand.

ex.en: A hand grenade was thrown at an army patrol.
ex.zh: 一颗手榴弹被扔向陆军巡逻队。

d: n. 手榴弹；榴弹（grenade 的复数）
v. 用（手）榴弹攻击；向……投掷榴弹（grenade 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: a waist- or hip-length garment, usually sleeveless, fastening up the front; sometimes made from a quilted fabric, and designed to be worn over a blouse, shirt, etc

d: n. 马甲，背心（通常无袖、长度及腰或及臀的上衣）；吉莱（法语姓氏 Gilet）

e.en: When a person or a vehicle halts or when something halts them, they stop moving in the direction they were going and stand still. 使停住;

ex.en: They halted at a short distance from the house.
ex.zh: 他们停在离房子不远处。

e.en: When something such as growth, development, or activity halts or when you halt it, it stops completely. 使完全停止;

ex.en: Striking workers halted production at the auto plant yesterday.
ex.zh: 昨天，汽车厂的罢工工人完全停止了生产。

e.en: (esp of logic or verse) to falter or be defective (尤指逻辑或诗韵)有缺陷;
an interruption or end to activity, movement, or progress (活动、运动或进展的)中止;

d: v. 停止，停顿；使停止（halt 的过去式和过去分词）
n. system halted（计算机）系统停止运行（或崩溃）的提示，死机

e.en: A hammer is a tool that consists of a heavy piece of metal at the end of a handle. It is used, for example, to hit nails into a piece of wood or a wall, or to break things into pieces.

ex.en: He used a hammer and chisel to chip away at the wall.
ex.zh: 他用锤子和凿子将墙壁一点点凿掉。

e.en: If you hammer an object such as a nail, you hit it with a hammer.

ex.en: To avoid damaging the tree, hammer a wooden peg into the hole.
ex.zh: 为了避免毁坏这棵树，把一只木钉敲进那个洞里。

e.en: If you hammer on a surface, you hit it several times in order to make a noise, or to emphasize something you are saying when you are angry.

ex.en: We had to hammer and shout before they would open up.
ex.zh: 我们不得不砰砰敲打并大喊大叫，他们才会开门。

ex.en: A crowd of reporters was hammering on the door.
ex.zh: 一群记者在砰砰敲那扇门。

e.en: If you hammer something such as an idea into people or you hammer at it, you keep repeating it forcefully so that it will have an effect on people.

ex.en: He hammered it into me that I had not suddenly become a rotten goalkeeper.
ex.zh: 他反复向我灌输，我并没有突然变成一个糟糕的守门员。

d: n. 锤子（hammer 的复数）；（Hammers）人名，亦为德语姓氏，译作哈默斯；（The Hammers）铁锤帮（西汉姆联队绰号）
v. 锤击；反复敲打；（比喻义）猛烈抨击，严厉批评；彻底击败，使惨败（hammer 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned. (偶然地)

ex.en: We cannot say for sure what will happen.
ex.zh: 我们说不准将会发生些什么。

e.en: If something happens, it occurs as a result of a situation or course of action. (作为结果)

ex.en: She wondered what would happen if her parents found her.
ex.zh: 她不知道如果父母发现了她会怎么样。

e.en: When something, especially something unpleasant, happens to you, it takes place and affects you. (尤指不愉快的事) 发生 (在某人身上)

ex.en: If we had been spotted at that point, I don't know what would have happened to us.
ex.zh: 如果那时我们被发现了，我不知道我们会有什么后果。

e.en: If you happen to do something, you do it by chance. If it happens that something is the case, it occurs by chance.

ex.en: We happened to discover we had a friend in common.
ex.zh: 我们碰巧发现我们有个共同的朋友。

d: v. （happen 的第三人称单数现在时）发生；（尤指不愉快的事）发生在某人身上（happen to sb）；碰巧，偶然（用于 happen to do sth、it happens that ...、as it happens 等结构）；偶然遇到或发现（happen on/upon）

e.en: a style of rock music characterized by short fast numbers with minimal melody and aggressive delivery

d: adj. 硬核的，铁杆的，激烈不妥协的；赤裸裸描写性行为的，露骨的
n. 硬核音乐，硬核摇滚乐；铁杆核心成员，中坚分子；（建筑）硬底层，碎砖垫层

e.en: A helicopter is an aircraft with long blades on top that go around very fast. It is able to stay still in the air and to move straight upward or downward.

d: n. 直升机
v. 用直升机运送；乘直升机飞至（某地）

e.en: If you hurl something, you throw it violently and with a lot of force.

ex.en: Groups of angry youths hurled stones at police.
ex.zh: 一群群愤怒的年轻人朝着警察猛掷石块。

ex.en: Simon caught the grenade and hurled it back.
ex.zh: 西蒙接住手榴弹，把它掷了回去。

e.en: If you hurl abuse or insults at someone, you shout insults at them aggressively.

ex.en: How would you handle being locked in the back of a cab while the driver hurled abuse at you?
ex.zh: 如果你被锁在出租车后座又遭司机谩骂，你会怎么办？

d: v. 猛扔，猛摔；大声说出（辱骂或斥责等）；呕吐
n. 乘车，搭便车；猛投，投掷

e.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly. 无能的;

ex.en: He wants the power to fire incompetent employees.
ex.zh: 他希望有权解雇不称职的雇员。

e.en: An incompetent is someone who is incompetent. 无能的人;

ex.en: The president turned furiously on his staff. "I'm surrounded by incompetents!"
ex.zh: 董事长愤怒地指责其职员，“我身边全是些没用的人！”

d: n．无能力者，不称职者：指在某方面缺乏能力或技能的人。
n. 意大利（欧洲南部国家）

e.en: Inequality is the difference in social status, wealth, or opportunity between people or groups. 不平等;

ex.en: People are concerned about corruption and social inequality.
ex.zh: 人们对腐败和社会不公感到担忧。

d: n. 不平等，不均等，不平衡（多用于社会、经济等语境）；（数学）不等式；不平坦，不平整（inequality 的复数形式）

e.en: Incendiary weapons or attacks are ones that cause large fires.

ex.en: Five incendiary devices were found in her house.
ex.zh: 5个燃烧装置在她家里被发现了。

e.en: An incendiary is an incendiary bomb.

ex.en: A shower of incendiaries struck the Opera House.
ex.zh: 阵雨般的燃烧弹击中了歌剧院。

e.en: If you accuse someone of saying or doing incendiary things, you mean that what they say or do is likely to make people react very angrily.

ex.en: ...incendiary slogans such as "Hospital closures kill more than car bombs."
ex.zh: …诸如“关闭医院比汽车炸弹杀人更多”之类的煽动性标语。

d: adj. 纵火的，引火的；煽动性的，激起愤怒的；能引起燃烧的；非常辣的
n. 燃烧弹（燃烧装置）；纵火者，纵火犯；煽动者；易燃物，引火物，燃烧剂
n. 黄色
adj. 黄色的

e.en: If one person joins another, they move or go to the same place, for example, so that both of them can do something together.

ex.en: His wife and children moved to join him in their new home.
ex.zh: 他的妻子和孩子们搬来和他一起住在新家。

e.en: If you join an organization, you become a member of it or start work as an employee of it. 参加 (组织)

ex.en: He joined the Army five years ago.
ex.zh: 他５年前参了军。

e.en: If you join an activity that other people are doing, you take part in it or become involved with it. 参加 (活动)

ex.en: The United States joined the war in April 1917.
ex.zh: 美国于1917年4月参战。

ex.en: The pastor requested the women present to join him in prayer.
ex.zh: 该牧师请在场的妇女和他一起祈祷。

e.en: If you join a line, you stand at the end of it so that you are part of it. 加入 (队列)

ex.en: It is advised that fans seeking autographs join the line before practice starts.
ex.zh: 建议寻求亲笔签名的影迷们在活动开始前排好队。

d: v. （join 的过去式和过去分词）加入，参加；连接，接合；汇合；（计）（数据库）连接
adj. 连接在一起的，联合的，结合的

e.en: If you juggle lots of different things, such as your work and your family, you try to give enough time or attention to all of them.

ex.en: The management team meets several times a week to juggle budgets and resources.
ex.zh: 管理团队一周开几次会，力图兼顾预算和资源。

e.en: If you juggle, you entertain people by throwing things into the air, catching each one, and throwing it up again so that there are several of them in the air at the same time. 用…玩抛接杂耍;

ex.en: Soon she was juggling five eggs.
ex.zh: 很快她就在抛接5个鸡蛋了。

e.en: 抛接杂耍

ex.en: He can perform an astonishing variety of acts, including mime and juggling.
ex.zh: 他会表演的节目种类多得惊人，包括哑剧和抛接杂耍。

d: v. 玩杂耍（连续向空中抛接多个物体）；力图使平衡，尽力应付；歪曲，篡改；有效地组织，有效利用（信息、数字、开支等）
n. 手技杂耍；平衡；虚报，谎报

e.en: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it. 保持 (特定状态)

ex.en: The noise kept him awake.
ex.zh: 噪音使他一直醒着。

ex.en: People had to burn these trees to keep warm during harsh winters.
ex.zh: 在寒冷的冬天，人们得靠烧这些树保暖。

e.en: If you keep or you are kept in a particular position or place, you remain in it.

ex.en: Keep away from the doors while the train is moving.
ex.zh: 列车运行时请远离车门。

ex.en: He kept his head down, hiding his features.
ex.zh: 他一直低着头藏住脸。

e.en: If you keep off something or keep away from it, you avoid it. If you keep out of something, you avoid getting involved in it.

ex.en: I managed to stick to the diet and keep off sweet foods.
ex.zh: 我设法坚持节食，不吃甜食。

e.en: If you keep doing something, you do it repeatedly or continue to do it.

ex.en: I keep forgetting it's December.
ex.zh: 我总是忘了现在是12月份。

d: v. （使）保持，（使）留在；继续，重复；耽搁，延误；保有，留下；存放，储存；经营，管理；保鲜；保守（秘密）；遵守；记录，记载；饲养；供养；保护；（按规定）纪念，庆祝；守门；尊重（法律或习俗）
n. 生活必需品，生活费用；城堡主楼
【名】 （Keep）（英）基普（人名）

e.en: If you have integrity, you are honest and firm in your moral principles. 正直;

ex.en: I have always regarded him as a man of integrity.
ex.zh: 我一直把他当作一个正直诚实的人。

e.en: The integrity of something such as a group of people or a text is its state of being a united whole.

ex.en: Separatist movements are a threat to the integrity of the nation.
ex.zh: 分裂活动是对国家领土完整的威胁。

d: n. 正直，诚实；完整，完全；职业操守；（电子数据的）集成度

e.en: A midterm election is an election that takes place approximately halfway through a president's or a government's term of office.

ex.en: Bush's Republican Party faces a tough challenge in midterm congressional elections in November.
ex.zh: 布什的共和党在11月中期国会选举中面临艰难的挑战。

e.en: A midterm or a midterm exam is a test which a student takes in the middle of a school or college term.

ex.en: She was about to walk into a midterm exam for a subject she knew very little about.
ex.zh: 她马上就要参加一个她知之甚少的科目的期中考试了。

d: n. 期中考试；中期
adj. 中期的；学期中间的

e.en: Administration is the range of activities connected with organizing and supervising the way that an organization or institution functions. 行政工作;

ex.en: Too much time is spent on administration.
ex.zh: 太多的时间花在了管理工作上。

e.en: The administration of something is the process of organizing and supervising it.

ex.en: Standards in the administration of justice have degenerated.
ex.zh: 司法监管的标准已退化了。

e.en: The administration of a company or institution is the group of people who organize and supervise it. 管理层;

ex.en: They would like the college administration to exert more control over the fraternity.
ex.zh: 他们希望该学院行政部门加大对该兄弟会的控制力度。

e.en: You can refer to a country's government as the administration; used especially in the United States. 政府 (尤用于美国)

ex.en: O'Leary served in federal energy posts in both the Ford and Carter administrations.
ex.zh: 奥利里在福特政府和卡特政府期间都任过联邦政府能源部门的职位。

d: n. 管理，行政；管理部门，行政部门；（某一任期的）政府；执行，监管；（药的）服用，配给；遗产管理，（债务人、其他个人或破产公司的）资产管理

e.en: A vote is a choice made by a particular person or group in a meeting or an election.

ex.en: He walked to the local polling place to cast his vote.
ex.zh: 他走到当地的投票点去投票。

ex.en: Mr. Reynolds was re-elected by 102 votes to 60.
ex.zh: 雷诺兹先生以102票对60票再次当选。

e.en: A vote is an occasion when a group of people make a decision by each person indicating his or her choice. The choice that most people support is accepted by the group.

ex.en: Why do you think we should have a vote on that?
ex.zh: 你为什么认为我们应该对那件事进行投票表决？

e.en: The vote is the total number of votes or voters in an election, or the number of votes received or cast by a particular group. 投票总数;

ex.en: Opposition parties won about fifty-five percent of the vote.
ex.zh: 反对党赢得大约55％的选票。

e.en: If you have the vote in an election, or have a vote in a meeting, you have the legal right to indicate your choice.

ex.en: Before that, women did not have a vote at all.
ex.zh: 在那之前，妇女根本就没有选举权。

d: n. 投票，选举，表决
v. 投票，选举，表决（vote 的现在分词/动名词）
adj. 有投票权的；与投票、表决有关的

e.en: In a game of cards, trumps is the suit which is chosen to have the highest value in one particular game. (牌戏中的)

ex.en: Hearts are trumps.
ex.zh: 红桃牌是王牌。

e.en: In a game of cards, a trump is a playing card which belongs to the suit which has been chosen as trumps. (一张)

ex.en: He played a trump.
ex.zh: 他打了一张王牌。

e.en: a trumpet or the sound produced by one 小号;
If you trump what someone has said or done, you beat it by saying or doing something else that seems better. (因说或做得更好而)

ex.en: The Republicans tried to trump this with their slogan.
ex.zh: 共和党人试图用他们的口号来胜出。

d: n. （牌戏中的一张）王牌，将牌；（牌戏中的）一套王牌，一套将牌（trumps）；（塔罗牌）有典型象征意义的人物和场景的一张；（喻）（尤指出奇制胜的）有效手段，王牌；喇叭，喇叭声
v. 出王牌赢（牌）；赢，胜过，打败；比……更重要；出声放屁；吹喇叭
【名】 （Trump）（英）特朗普（人名）
n. 米切尔（男子名，等于 Michael）；米切尔（英语姓氏）

e.en: Something that is ahead is in front of you. If you look ahead, you look directly in front of you. 在前面地;

ex.en: Brett looked straight ahead.
ex.zh: 布瑞特向前直视。

ex.en: The road ahead was now blocked solid.
ex.zh: 前方道路现在被堵死了。

e.en: You use ahead with verbs such as "push," "move," and "forge" to indicate that a plan, programme, or organization is making fast progress.

ex.en: Western countries were moving ahead with plans to send financial aid to all of the former Soviet republics.
ex.zh: 西方国家正推行对所有前苏联国家提供经济援助的计划。

e.en: If you are ahead in your work or achievements, you have made more progress than you expected to and are performing well.

ex.en: First half profits have charged ahead from $127.6m to $134.2m.
ex.zh: 上半年利润已经提前从1.276亿美元提升到了1.342亿美元。

e.en: If a person or a team is ahead in a competition, they are winning.

ex.en: Australia was ahead throughout the game.
ex.zh: 澳大利亚队在整场比赛中一直领先。

ex.en: The Communists are comfortably ahead in the opinion polls.
ex.zh: 共产党在民意调查中遥遥领先。

d: adv. 在前面，朝前面；领先，占优势；提前，预先；在将来，今后；（数量或价值上）更多，更高；取得进步，获得成功；超出预期地，超前地
adj. 在前的，提前的

e.en: Voters are people who have the legal right to vote in elections, or people who are voting in a particular election.

ex.en: The turnout was at least 62 percent of registered voters.
ex.zh: 至少有62%的登记选民参加了投票。

d: n. 选民，选举人，投票人；有投票权者

e.en: An appointee is someone who has been chosen for a particular job or position of responsibility.

ex.en: ...Becket, a recent appointee to the Supreme Court.
ex.zh: ...贝克特，一个最近刚被任命在最高法院工作的人。

d: n．被任命者，被委派者：被任命或委派担任职务的人。
n. 非公民（noncitizen 的复数形式）
n. 克拉克（Clark，英语姓氏，亦为多国语言人名音译）；克拉克（Clark，英语男子名）

e.en: Information that is confidential is meant to be kept secret or private.

ex.en: She accused them of leaking confidential information about her private life.
ex.zh: 她指责他们泄露了有关她的私生活的保密信息。

e.en: 保密地

ex.en: People can phone in, knowing that any information they give will be treated confidentially.
ex.zh: 人们可以打电话进来，他们知道他们所提供的一切信息都会被保密。

e.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

ex.en: "Look," he said in a confidential tone, "I want you to know that me and Joey are cops."
ex.zh: “喂，”他悄声说，“我想要你知道我和乔伊都是警察。”

e.en: 悄悄地

ex.en: Nash hadn't raised his voice, still spoke rather softly, confidentially.
ex.zh: 纳什没有提高嗓门，仍然很轻地、悄悄地说。

d: adj. 机密的，保密的；（言谈举止）神秘的，隐秘的；受信任的，委以机密的

e.en: Someone who is conservative has views that are toward the political right. In the U.S. the Republicans are more conservative than the Democrats, who are more liberal.

ex.en: ...counties whose citizens invariably support the most conservative candidate in any election.
ex.zh: …公民们在任何选举中都千篇一律地支持最保守的候选人的县。

e.en: Conservative is also a noun.

ex.en: The new judge is 50-year-old David Suitor who's regarded as a conservative.
ex.zh: 这名新法官是50岁的、被视为右倾人士的戴维·休特。

e.en: Someone who is conservative or has conservative ideas is unwilling to accept changes and new ideas. (观点)

ex.en: People tend to be more liberal when they're young and more conservative as they get older.
ex.zh: 人们在年轻时常常更开放，年纪越大就越保守。

e.en: If someone dresses in a conservative way, their clothes are conventional in style. (衣着)

ex.en: The girl was well dressed, as usual, though in a more conservative style.
ex.zh: 这个女孩像平常一样穿着得体，但式样则更守旧。

d: adj. 保守的；保守派的，保守主义的（认为政府应该实行政治保守主义）；（衣着）守旧的，传统的；低估的；保守党的；不愿冒险的，谨慎的
n. 保守者，因循守旧者；保守党党员，保守党支持者
abbr. （美）司法部（Department of Justice）；反不正当竞争部门（department of justice）

e.en: (in Canada) district high school (加拿大)

d: 数据处理系数（Data Handing System）；癸二酸二己酯

e.en: If someone or something exerts influence, authority, or pressure, they use it in a strong or determined way, especially in order to produce a particular effect. 施加 (影响、压力); 运用 (权威)

ex.en: He exerted considerable influence on the thinking of the scientific community on these issues.
ex.zh: 他对科学界在这些问题上的思考施加了相当大的影响。

e.en: If you exert yourself, you make a great physical or mental effort, or work hard to do something. 耗费 (自己的精力)

ex.en: Do not exert yourself unnecessarily.
ex.zh: 不要无谓地耗费自己的精力。

e.en: 耗费

ex.en: He clearly found the physical exertion exhilarating.
ex.zh: 他明显发现体力消耗令人愉悦。

d: v. 运用，施加（影响）；努力，尽力（exert oneself）

e.en: If you describe someone or something as focused, you approve of the fact that they have a clear and definite purpose.

ex.en: I spent the next year just wandering. I wasn't focused.
ex.zh: 接下来的一年我一直在闲逛。我没有什么明确的目标。

d: adj. 专注的，目标明确的；（声音或图像）清晰的
v. 集中，关注；聚焦，调焦；以（句子的一部分）为焦点（或重心）（focus 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: The grassroots of an organization or movement are the ordinary people who form the main part of it, rather than its leaders. (组织、运动的)

ex.en: You have to join the party at grassroots level from what I understand.
ex.zh: 据我的了解，你得由基层组织入党。

d: adj. （常用作定语）基层的，草根的，民间的；根本的，基础的
n. （常作复数）基层群众，草根阶层，草根；基础

e.en: Your homeland is your native country.

ex.en: Many are planning to return to their homeland.
ex.zh: 很多人正计划回到自己的祖国去。

e.en: The homelands were regions within South Africa in which black South Africans had a limited form of self-government. (过去南非种族隔离制度下的)

d: n. 祖国，家乡；（某一特殊群体居住的）大片定居地

e.en: Interference by a person or group is their unwanted or unnecessary involvement in something.

ex.en: Airlines will be able to set cheap fares without further interference from the government.
ex.zh: 如果不受政府更多的干预，各航空公司将能够把票价定得很低。

e.en: When there is interference, a radio signal is affected by other radio waves or electrical activity so that it cannot be received properly.

ex.en: ...electrical interference.
ex.zh: …电子干扰。

d: n. 干涉，干预；（收音机或电视机受到的）干扰信号；犯规阻挡；抵触，冲突

e.en: A key is a specially shaped piece of metal that you place in a lock and turn in order to open or lock a door, or to start or stop the engine of a vehicle.

ex.en: They put the key in the door and entered.
ex.zh: 他们用钥匙开了门然后走了进去。

e.en: The keys on a computer keyboard or typewriter are the buttons that you press in order to operate it.

ex.en: Finally, press the Delete key.
ex.zh: 最后，按删除键。

e.en: The keys of a piano or organ are the long narrow pieces of wood or plastic that you press in order to play it.

ex.en: ...the black and white keys on a piano keyboard.
ex.zh: …一架钢琴键盘上的黑白琴键。

e.en: In music, a key is a scale of musical notes that starts on one specific note.

ex.en: ...the key of A minor.
ex.zh: …A小调。

d: n. 钥匙；（电脑、打字机或乐器的）键；关键，要诀；答案；音调，声调；图例，符号说明；低岛，礁；扳手；销子，楔；（文章、形势等）主调，基调；（梣树、枫树或无花果树的）翼果；板条间首层灰泥；（有助于石膏等黏附的）粗糙表面；罚球区
v. 键入；成为（获胜）的关键；用钥匙划坏（汽车）；用别针（或楔子、栓）固定；将……的表面处理好；给（广告）加识别编码
adj. 关键的，主要的
【名】 （Key）（美）基（人名）
邮递抗议

e.en: A movement is a group of people who share the same beliefs, ideas, or aims. 运动 (指具有共同信仰、思想或目标的团体)

ex.en: It's part of a broader nationalist movement that's gaining strength throughout the country.
ex.zh: 这是一场正在全国范围内日益壮大的更为广泛的民族主义运动的一部分。

e.en: Movement involves changing position or going from one place to another.

ex.en: They actually monitor the movement of the fish going up river.
ex.zh: 他们实际上在观测鱼向上游的迁移活动。

ex.en: There was movement behind the window in the back door.
ex.zh: 后门窗户的后面有动静。

e.en: A movement is a planned change in position that an army makes during a battle or military exercise. (军队作战或演习时的)

ex.en: There are reports of fresh troop movements across the border.
ex.zh: 有报道称新近有部队越过边境。

e.en: Movement is a gradual development or change of an attitude, opinion, or policy. (态度、观点、政策等的)

ex.en: ...the movement toward democracy in Latin America.
ex.zh: …拉丁美洲民主的渐进。

d: n. 移动，转移；（具有共同思想或目标的）运动；军队有计划的移动；行踪；乐章；改进，发展；量的变化；（活动）机件；排便；（飞机）抵达，起飞
n. 非公民，非居民

e.en: When children, animals, or adults play, they spend time doing enjoyable things, such as using toys and taking part in games.

ex.en: ...invite the children over to play.
ex.zh: …邀请孩子们过来玩。

ex.en: They played in the little garden.
ex.zh: 他们在小花园里玩耍。

e.en: Play is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a few hours of play until the babysitter puts them to bed.
ex.zh: …直到保姆让他们上床睡觉之前的几小时的玩耍。

e.en: When you play a sport, game, or match, you take part in it. 参加 (体育运动、游戏、比赛等)

ex.en: While the twins played cards, Leona sat reading.
ex.zh: 那对双胞胎玩牌的时候，利昂娜坐着看书。

ex.en: I used to play basketball.
ex.zh: 我过去常打篮球。

e.en: Play is also a noun. (对运动、游戏、比赛等的)

ex.en: They've got more exciting players and a more exciting style of play.
ex.zh: 他们有更精彩的选手和更精彩的比赛风格。

d: v. 演奏；播放；玩耍；参加竞赛（play 的过去分词）
adj. 比赛的

e.en: Paper is a material that you write on or wrap things with. The pages of this book are made of paper.

ex.en: He wrote his name down on a piece of paper for me.
ex.zh: 他把他的名字写在一张纸上给我。

ex.en: ...a paper bag.
ex.zh: …一个纸袋。

e.en: A paper is a newspaper.

ex.en: I might get a paper in the town.
ex.zh: 我或许能在城里买到一份报纸。

e.en: You can refer to newspapers in general as the paper or the papers. (总称)

ex.en: You can't believe everything you read in the paper.
ex.zh: 你不能相信在报纸上读到的所有内容。

e.en: Your papers are sheets of paper with information on them that you might keep in a safe place at home.

ex.en: After her death, her papers – including unpublished articles and correspondence – were deposited at the library.
ex.zh: 她死后，她的资料–包括未发表的文章和信函–都被存放在图书馆里。

d: n. 纸；报纸；（工作、学习或个人的）资料，文件（papers）；证明，证件（如护照、身份证等）（papers）；政府报告，官方政策文件；考试，答卷；（研究）论文，（学术）讲话；（学校课程的）学期论文；墙纸，壁纸；有价证券；手纸，卫生纸；（剧院等娱乐场所的）免费入场券
v. 用墙纸裱糊（墙壁）；用墙纸覆盖（洞，污点）（paper sth. over）；掩盖（尴尬问题）（paper sth. over）；发免费入场券使（剧院）满座
adj. 纸做的，纸质的；书面的，印刷的；纸上的，有名无实的
【名】 （Paper）（俄）帕佩尔（人名）

e.en: A podcast is an audio file similar to a radio broadcast, that can be downloaded and listened to on a computer or iPod.

ex.en: Now there are thousands of podcasts available daily.
ex.zh: 现在每天有数千个播客可供下载。

d: n. 播客
v. 将……做成播客

e.en: Postal is used to describe things or people connected with the public service of carrying letters and packages from one place to another.

ex.en: Compensation for lost or damaged mail will be handled by the postal service.
ex.zh: 丢失或损坏邮件的赔偿事宜将由邮政部门处理。

e.en: Postal is used to describe activities that involve sending things by mail.

ex.en: ...free postal delivery.
ex.zh: …免费邮递。

d: adj. 邮政的，邮递的；邮寄的，以邮递方式进行的
n. 明信片

e.en: Presidential activities or things relate or belong to a president.

ex.en: ...campaigning for Peru's presidential election.
ex.zh: …秘鲁总统选举竞选活动。

d: adj. 与总统有关的；总统似的，像总统的（尤指貌似自信大方、经验老到的）

e.en: When something rolls or when you roll it, it moves along a surface, turning over many times.

ex.en: The ball rolled into the net.
ex.zh: 球滚进了网。

e.en: If you roll somewhere, you move on a surface while lying down, turning your body over and over, so that you are sometimes on your back, sometimes on your side, and sometimes on your front.

ex.en: When I was a little kid I rolled down a hill and broke my leg.
ex.zh: 我小的时候曾滚下山摔断了腿。

e.en: When vehicles roll along, they move along slowly. (车辆)

ex.en: The truck quietly rolled forward and demolished all the old wooden fencing.
ex.zh: 卡车静静地缓慢前行，毁了所有旧木栅栏。

e.en: If a machine rolls, it is operating. (机器)

ex.en: He slipped and fell on the step as the cameras rolled.
ex.zh: 在相机拍摄时，他滑倒在了台阶上。

d: n. 滚动（roll 的复数）；面包卷；捆；卷轴；辊碎机
v. 滚动；行驶；盘旋；辗；使左右摇晃；运转（roll 的三单形式）

e.en: If you save someone or something, you help them to avoid harm or to escape from a dangerous or unpleasant situation. 救助;

ex.en: ...an austerity programme designed to save the country's failing economy.
ex.zh: …一个旨在拯救该国衰退的经济的紧缩计划。

ex.en: The meeting is an attempt to mobilize nations to save children from death by disease and malnutrition.
ex.zh: 该会议试图动员各国救助儿童，以免死于疾病和营养不良。

e.en: If you save, you gradually collect money by spending less than you get, usually in order to buy something that you want.

ex.en: The majority of people intend to save, but find that by the end of the month there is nothing left.
ex.zh: 大多数人都想要储蓄，但到月底的时候却发现已经一分不剩了。

ex.en: Tim and Barbara are now saving for a house in the suburbs.
ex.zh: 蒂姆和芭芭拉眼下正为郊区的一所房子攒钱。

e.en: Save up means the same as . 同(save)

ex.en: Julie wanted to put some of her money aside for holidays or save up for something special.
ex.zh: 朱莉想留出一些钱去度假或是存些钱以备专门之需。

e.en: If you save something such as time or money, you prevent the loss or waste of it.

ex.en: It saves time in the kitchen to have things you use a lot within reach.
ex.zh: 在厨房里把常用的东西放在手边可以节省时间。

ex.en: I'll try to save him the expense of a flight from Perth.
ex.zh: 我会想办法给他省下从珀斯过来的机票费用。

d: v. 救助，搭救；避免，减少；积攒，储蓄；节省（钱、时间或其他资源）；保存，保留；收集；（为某人）保留；（计算机）保存（数据）；使健康长寿，护佑；（足球等）救球，防止对方进球；（棒球）（替补投手） 保持（其他投手取得的领先地位）；（基督教）拯救（某人），使摆脱罪孽
n. （足球等守门员的）救球；（棒球）（替补投手） 保持（其他投手取得的领先地位）；（计算机）存储数据
prep.  除……之外
【名】 （Save）（法）萨夫，（意、保、西、罗、塞、瑞典）萨薇 （女名），萨韦（人名）

e.en: Australian Rules

d: n. 规章，条例，规定；（语言、科学等的）规则，法则，规律；行事准则，指导方针，惯例（以上为 rule 的复数）
v. 统治，管辖；支配，控制；占优势，占首要地位，盛行；（尤指对法律问题）判定，裁定（以上为 rule 的第三人称单数）

e.en: When you send someone something, you arrange for it to be taken and delivered to them, for example, by mail. 邮寄;

ex.en: Myra Cunningham sent me a note thanking me for dinner.
ex.zh: 迈拉·坎宁安寄给了我一封短信，感谢我请她吃饭。

ex.en: I sent a copy to the school principal.
ex.zh: 我寄了一份复印件给校长。

e.en: If you send someone somewhere, you tell them to go there. 派遣;

ex.en: Inspector Banbury came up to see her, but she sent him away.
ex.zh: 班伯里警官过来看她，但她却把他打发走了。

ex.en: ...the government's decision to send troops to the region.
ex.zh: …政府向该地区派遣军队的决定。

e.en: If you send someone to an institution such as a school or a prison, you arrange for them to stay there for a period of time. 把…送进 (学校、监狱等)

ex.en: It's his parents' choice to send him to a boarding school, rather than a convenient day school.
ex.zh: 把他送到寄宿学校而不是去附近的走读学校，是他父母的决定。

e.en: To send a signal means to cause it to go to a place by means of radio waves or electricity. (通过电波或电) 发送 (信号)

ex.en: The transmitters will send a signal automatically to a local base station.
ex.zh: 发射台会自动将信号发送到地方基站。

d: v. 邮寄，发送；传达，告知；派遣，打发，安排去；使快速（或猛然）移动；使作出（某种反应），使表现出（某种行为）；排放，排出（烟或化学反应的产生物等）； 使着迷，使入迷
n.  波浪的推力，波浪引起的水位上升（=scend）
【名】 （Send）（德）森德

e.en: A service is something that the public needs, such as transportation, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body. 公共服务机构;

ex.en: The postal service has been trying to cut costs.
ex.zh: 邮政系统一直在试图削减成本。

ex.en: We have started a campaign for better nursery and school services.
ex.zh: 我们已开展了一场运动，以改善幼儿园和学校的服务。

e.en: You can sometimes refer to an organization or private company as a particular service when it provides something for the public or acts on behalf of the government. 官方机构;

ex.en: The Agriculture Department has ultimate control over the Forest Service.
ex.zh: 农业部对林务局有最终控制权。

e.en: If an organization or company provides a particular service, they can do a particular job or a type of work for you. 服务;

ex.en: The kitchen maintains a twenty-four hour service and can be contacted via reception.
ex.zh: 厨房提供24小时服务，可通过接待处联系。

e.en: Services are activities such as tourism, banking, and selling things which are part of a country's economy, but are not concerned with producing or manufacturing goods. 服务性工作;

ex.en: Mining rose by 9.1%, manufacturing by 9.4% and services by 4.3%.
ex.zh: 采矿业增长了9.1%，制造业增长了9.4%，服务业增长了4.3%。

d: n. 公共服务系统，公共事业；（服务性行业或机构所提供的）服务；（对顾客的）接待，招待；工作，效劳；服务费；政府机构，公务部门；兵役，军队；（机器的）使用；仆人，佣人； 服务站；宗教仪式；检修，保养；整套餐具；发球，发球方式；班车，车次；（法律文件的）送达
v. 维修，检修；支付（债务）利息；为……提供服务；（雄性动物）与（雌性动物）交配
adj. 员工专用的； 部队的；提供服务的
【名】 （Service）（英）瑟维斯（人名）

e.en: You can refer to countries as states, particularly when you are discussing politics. (政治上所指的)

ex.en: Mexico is a secular state and does not have diplomatic relations with the Vatican.
ex.zh: 墨西哥是个非宗教国家，和梵蒂冈没有外交关系。

e.en: Some large countries such as the U.S. are divided into smaller areas called states. (美国等大国的)

ex.en: Leaders of the Southern states are meeting in Louisville.
ex.zh: 南部各州的领导人们正在路易斯维尔会晤。

e.en: The U.S. is sometimes referred to as the States.

ex.en: She bought it last year in the States.
ex.zh: 她去年在美国买了它。

e.en: You can refer to the government of a country as the state.

ex.en: The state does not collect enough revenue to cover its expenditure.
ex.zh: 政府没有征到足够的税来支付它的费用。

d: n. 状态，状况；紧张，焦虑；政府；国家；州，邦；美国（the States）；国事礼仪，隆重仪式；（物质的）形态，态；（物理学）量子态；泽西、根西和奥尔德尼三岛的立法机关（the States）；压印，印图；受公众瞻仰和吊唁
adj. 州的；国事的，国事礼仪的；国家提供（或控制）的
v. 陈述，说明；规定，公布；表现（主题，旋律）
【名】 （State）（罗、瑞典）斯塔特，（英）斯泰特（人名）

e.en: Supreme is used in the title of a person or an official group to indicate that they are at the highest level in a particular organization or system.

ex.en: MacArthur was Supreme Commander for the allied powers in the Pacific.
ex.zh: 麦克阿瑟是太平洋盟军的最高司令官。

ex.en: ...the Supreme Court.
ex.zh: …最高法院。

e.en: You use supreme to emphasize that a quality or thing is very great.

ex.en: Her approval was of supreme importance.
ex.zh: 她的认可是极其重要的。

e.en: 极其地

ex.en: She does her job supremely well.
ex.zh: 她工作得极其出色。

d: adj. 最高的，至高无上的；（政府、司法或军事机构）拥有最高权力的；极大的，极度的；（处罚，牺牲）涉及死的；杰出的
n. 奶油沙司
v. 用工具处理水果（尤指柑橘类）以达到最佳效果

e.en: A trail is a rough path across open country or through forests. (乡间或林中的)

ex.en: He was following a trail through the trees.
ex.zh: 他正沿着一条崎岖小路穿过树林。

e.en: A trail is a route along a series of paths or roads, often one that has been planned and marked out for a particular purpose. (有特定目的的) 路线;

ex.en: ...a large area of woodland with hiking and walking trails.
ex.zh: …有徒步旅行和散步路线的大片林区。

e.en: A trail is a series of marks or other signs of movement or other activities left by someone or something.

ex.en: Everywhere in the house was a sticky trail of orange juice.
ex.zh: 房子里到处都是粘乎乎的橙汁印迹。

e.en: If you trail someone or something, you follow them secretly, often by finding the marks or signs that they have left.

ex.en: Two detectives were trailing him.
ex.zh: 两个侦探正在跟踪他。

d: n. 痕迹，踪迹；（人或动物的）足迹，嗅迹；（乡间的）小路，小径；（特定）路线，路径；一系列（坏事或有害事件）；（尤指细长）一缕，一串；滑雪坡，滑雪道，越野滑雪路线；电影或广播的预告片；（炮架的）架尾
v. 拖，拉；没精打采地走，拖沓地走；（在竞赛或选举中）落后，输；跟踪，追踪；蔓生，蔓延，被搁置；垂下；慢慢移动，缓缓流动；（声音，喇叭）渐弱；事先宣传，预告（影片，节目等）；喷注（泥釉）
【名】 （Trail）（美）特雷尔（人名）

e.en: If you try to do something, you want to do it, and you take action which you hope will help you to do it.

ex.en: He secretly tried to help her at work.
ex.zh: 他试图悄悄地在工作上帮助她。

ex.en: Does it annoy you if others don't seem to try hard enough?
ex.zh: 如果其他人做得似乎不够努力，这会使你烦恼吗？

e.en: Try is also a noun.

ex.en: It wasn't that she'd really expected to get any money out of him; it had just seemed worth a try.
ex.zh: 并非是她真的期望从他那里弄到一些钱；只是似乎值得一试。

e.en: To try and do something means to try to do it.

ex.en: I must try and see him.
ex.zh: 我必须设法见到他。

e.en: If you try for something, you make an effort to get it or achieve it. 试图 (获得)

ex.en: My partner and I have been trying for a baby for two years.
ex.zh: 我和我的配偶两年来一直试着生个孩子。

d: v. 试图，努力；试用，试做，试验；品尝；考验，磨炼；到（某处）试试，找一找；试着打开（门、窗等）；审理，审判；用刨子刨平（木头粗糙面）；加热以提取（油，脂肪），熬（油）
n. 试图，努力；试用，试验；（橄榄球）持球触地得分
【名】 （Try）（英、印尼）特里，（柬）德里（人名）

e.en: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction. 转动 (身体);

ex.en: He turned abruptly and walked away.
ex.zh: 他突然转身走开了。

ex.en: He sighed, turning away and surveying the sea.
ex.zh: 他叹了口气，转过身去，眺望着大海。

e.en: Turn around means the same as turn.

ex.en: I felt a tapping on my shoulder and I turned around.
ex.zh: 我感到有人拍了一下我的肩膀，于是转过身去。

e.en: When you turn something, you move it so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction, or is in a very different position.

ex.en: They turned their telescopes toward other nearby galaxies.
ex.zh: 他们把望远镜转向附近的其他星系。

ex.en: She had turned the bedside chair to face the door.
ex.zh: 她已经把那张床边的椅子转过来对着门。

e.en: When something such as a wheel turns, or when you turn it, it continually moves around in a particular direction.

ex.en: As the wheel turned, the potter shaped the clay.
