ex.zh: 随着轮子的转动，制陶工人给黏土塑形。

d: v. 旋转，转动；转身，扭转（身体部位）；翻转；旋动，拧动；翻动（书页）；转向，拐（弯）；（路或河流）转弯；对准；（潮）涨落；（使）松开，释放；表演，做；（使）扭转局势；（使）变成，成为；转移（思考、处理、观察等的对象）；求助于，求教于；达到（一定年龄或时间）；（使）反胃，（使）恶心；车削；获得（利益）；扭伤（脚踝）；造（句），组（词）；（印刷）倒排，倒空；包抄（敌军）
n. 转动，旋转；转向；（道路的）转弯处；轮到的机会；（情况的）变化，转变；交替时刻；短小节目；短小节目表演者；散步，转一圈；（疾病的）一阵发作，不适；（影响他人的）举止，行为；吓唬，惊吓；（股票等的）买卖差价；（板球）（球）弹地转向；（一卷绳子等的）一圈；涨潮或落潮；（乐）回音
【名】 （Turn）（德、匈）图恩（人名）

e.en: You're is the usual spoken form of "you are." (you are)

ex.en: Go to him, tell him you're sorry.
ex.zh: 去找他，告诉他你很抱歉。

d: abbr. 你是，你们是（you are 的缩略形式）
int. 不客气，不用谢（回应感谢的固定用语 you're welcome）

e.en: Something that is white is the colour of snow or milk.

ex.en: He had nice square white teeth.
ex.zh: 他有整齐洁白的漂亮牙齿。

ex.en: Issa's white beach hat gleamed in the harsh lights.
ex.zh: 伊萨的白色沙滩帽在刺目的灯光下闪闪发光。

e.en: A white person has a pale skin and belongs to a race of European origin.

ex.en: Working with white people hasn't been a problem for me or for them.
ex.zh: 和白种人在一起工作对我或对他们来说一直都不是个问题。

e.en: Whites are white people.

ex.en: It's a school that's brought blacks and whites and Hispanics together.
ex.zh: 这是一所让黑人、白种人和西班牙裔人走到了一起的学校。

e.en: White wine is pale yellow in colour.

ex.en: Gregory poured another glass of white wine and went back to his bedroom.
ex.zh: 格雷戈里又倒了一杯白葡萄酒，回卧室去了。

d: adj. 白色的；白种人的，白肤色的；苍白的；加牛奶（或奶油）的；（葡萄酒）白的，淡黄色的；（面粉）精白的；空白的；树皮淡色的；（玻璃）透明的，无色的；完全公正的，非常诚实的；（魔法）善意的；（血细胞）白的；（政治）反动的；纯洁的
n. 白色，白颜料；白种人，白人；白葡萄酒；眼白；蛋清，蛋白；白色运动服（whites）；要洗涤的白色织物（whites）；白衣服；执白棋者，白方；白色的东西，白球；白粉蝶
v. 把……漆成白色，使变白
【名】 （White）怀特（人名）

e.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

ex.en: Mr. Williams is a conservative who advocates fewer government controls on business.
ex.zh: 威廉斯先生是一位提倡减少政府对商业的控制的保守人士。

e.en: An advocate of a particular action or plan is someone who recommends it publicly.

ex.en: He was a strong advocate of free market policies and a multi-party system.
ex.zh: 他是自由市场政策以及多党制的坚定倡导者。

e.en: An advocate for a particular group is a person who works for the interests of that group. 为 (某团体)

ex.en: ...advocates for the homeless.
ex.zh: …为无家可归者谋利益的人。

e.en: An advocate is a lawyer who speaks in favour of someone or defends them in a court of law.

d: vt. 主张，提倡（advocate 的第三人称单数）
n. 拥护者，提倡者，倡导者；辩护律师（advocate 的复数）

e.en: An alleged fact has been stated but has not been proved to be true.

ex.en: They have begun a hunger strike in protest at the alleged beating.
ex.zh: 他们已经开始了绝食以抗议所指称的打人事件。

e.en: 指称地

ex.en: His van allegedly struck the two as they were crossing a street.
ex.zh: 据称，他的货车在这两个人过马路时撞上了他们。

d: adj. （未经证实而）声称的，所谓的；（在证据不足的情况下）被指控的
v. (未经证实地）宣称，指控（allege 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 美国；美洲（包括北美和南美洲）

e.en: Analysis is the process of considering something carefully or using statistical methods in order to understand it or explain it.

ex.en: Sporting greatness defies analysis – but we know it when we see it.
ex.zh: 运动的伟大无法进行分析–但是我们一看就知道。

e.en: Analysis is the scientific process of examining something in order to find out what it consists of.

ex.en: They collect blood samples for analysis at a national laboratory.
ex.zh: 他们收集血样以在一个国家实验室做化验分析。

e.en: An analysis is an explanation or description that results from considering something carefully.

ex.en: Coming up after the newscast, an analysis of the president's domestic policy.
ex.zh: 在新闻广播之后是一个对总统国内政策的分析报告。

d: n. 分析；化验分析；心理分析，精神分析；分析报告
n. 安纳托利亚（亚洲西南部的半岛）；WASP-52（位于飞马座的一颗主序星）

e.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them.

ex.en: He appealed to voters to go to the polls tomorrow.
ex.zh: 他呼吁选民们明天去投票站。

ex.en: He will appeal to the state for an extension of unemployment benefits.
ex.zh: 他将呼吁国家延长失业救济。

e.en: If you appeal a decision to someone in authority, you formally ask them to change it.

ex.en: We intend to appeal the verdict.
ex.zh: 我们打算对此裁决提出申诉。

e.en: If something appeals to you, you find it attractive or interesting.

ex.en: On the other hand, the idea appealed to him.
ex.zh: 另一方面，这个主意对他有吸引力。

e.en: An appeal is a serious and urgent request.

ex.en: He has a message from King Fahd, believed to be an appeal for Arab unity.
ex.zh: 他有个来自法赫德国王的口信，相信是对阿拉伯团结的呼吁。

d: n. （appeal 的复数）恳求，呼吁；募捐呼吁；（法）上诉
v. （appeal 的第三人称单数）有吸引力；呼吁，恳求；（法）对……提出上诉，申诉

e.en: If something happens at the appointed time, it happens at the time that was decided in advance.

ex.en: The appointed hour of the ceremony was drawing nearer.
ex.zh: 该仪式的指定时间正在临近。

d: v. （appoint 的过去式及过去分词）任命，委派（某人担任某职）；约定，确定（时间、地点、日期等）；（旧用或正式）命令，规定；（法律）受权处置（财产）
adj. 指定的，约定的，预先确定的；被任命的，被委派的，由任命产生的；法定的；（建筑、房间）按一定方式（或标准）陈设（或布置）的

e.en: April is the fourth month of the year in the Western calendar. 4

ex.en: The changes will be introduced in April.
ex.zh: 这些变更将于4月实施。

d: n. 四月

e.en: If you associate someone or something with another thing, the two are connected in your mind. 将 (…和…)

ex.en: Through science we've got the idea of associating progress with the future.
ex.zh: 通过科学我们已有了将进步与未来联系起来的观念。

e.en: If you are associated with a particular organization, cause, or point of view, or if you associate yourself with it, you support it publicly. 使 (某人与某组织、事业、观点等)

ex.en: I haven't been associated with the project over the last year.
ex.zh: 我过去一年不曾跟这个项目有关联。

e.en: If you say that someone is associating with another person or group of people, you mean they are spending a lot of time in the company of people you do not approve of. (与某个或某群人)

ex.en: What would they think if they knew that they were associating with a murderer?
ex.zh: 如果他们知道了他们正与一个杀人犯打成一片，他们会怎么想？

e.en: Your associates are the people you are closely connected with, especially at work. (尤指工作中的)

ex.en: ...the restaurant owner's business associates.
ex.zh: …该餐馆老板的商业伙伴们。

d: n. 同伴，合作人，同事；联合公司，联营公司（associate 的复数形式；亦见于公司、事务所等名称）
v. 联合；把……联系起来，联想到；交往，来往（associate 的第三人称单数形式，常与 with 连用）

e.en: In the United States, an attorney or attorney-at-law is a lawyer.

ex.en: ...a prosecuting attorney.
ex.zh: …一位公诉律师。

ex.en: At the hearing, her attorney did not enter a plea.
ex.zh: 在听证会上，她的律师没有提出申诉。

d: n. 律师（attorney 的复数形式）

e.en: The authorities are the people who have the power to make decisions and to make sure that laws are obeyed.

ex.en: This provided a pretext for the authorities to cancel the elections.
ex.zh: 这给当局提供了一个取消选举的借口。

e.en: An authority is an official organization or government department that has the power to make decisions.

ex.en: ...the Philadelphia Parking Authority.
ex.zh: …费城停车管理局。

e.en: Someone who is an authority on a particular subject knows a lot about it. (某一学科的)

ex.en: He's universally recognized as an authority on Russian affairs.
ex.zh: 他被公认为是俄罗斯事务的权威。

e.en: Authority is the right to command and control other people.

ex.en: A family member in a family business has a position of authority and power.
ex.zh: 家庭成员在家族企业中都有职有权。

d: n. 专家，权威人士；行政管理机构；权力，权限；权威，威信；许可，授权；当局，官方

e.en: A ballot is a secret vote in which people select a candidate in an election, or express their opinion about something.

ex.en: The result of the ballot will not be known for two weeks.
ex.zh: 本次无记名投票的结果将在两周后才会揭晓。

e.en: A ballot is a piece of paper on which you indicate your choice or opinion in a secret vote.

ex.en: Election boards will count the ballots by hand.
ex.zh: 选举委员会将手工清点选票。

e.en: If you ballot a group of people, you find out what they think about a subject by organizing a secret vote.

ex.en: The union said they will ballot members on whether to strike.
ex.zh: 工会称他们将组织会员们秘密投票表决是否罢工。

d: n. 选举，无记名投票，投票表决；不记名票，选票，投票用纸（ballot 的复数）
v. 投票，进行无记名投票；组织…进行无记名投票表决（ballot 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A bill is a written statement of money that you owe for goods or services.

ex.en: They couldn't afford to pay the bills.
ex.zh: 他们付不起账。

ex.en: He paid his bill for the newspapers promptly.
ex.zh: 他立刻付了报纸的帐单。

e.en: If you bill someone for goods or services you have provided them with, you give or send them a bill stating how much money they owe you for these goods or services.

ex.en: Are you going to bill me for this?
ex.zh: 你会为这开帐单给我吗？

e.en: A bill is a piece of paper money.

ex.en: The case contained a large quantity of U.S. dollar bills.
ex.zh: 盒子里装有大量美钞。

e.en: In government, a bill is a formal statement of a proposed new law that is discussed and then voted on.

ex.en: This is the toughest crime bill that Congress has passed in a decade.
ex.zh: 这是十年来国会通过的最强硬的有关犯罪的议案。

d: n. （商品、服务或餐馆的）账单；议案，法案；纸币，钞票；演出人员名单；广告，传单；票据，汇票；单子，清单；喙
v. 开账单；把……宣传为；宣布（某人）将参加演出
n. 博克啤酒（一种烈性黑啤酒，传统德国烈性拉格）；一杯（或一客）博克啤酒；（Bock）人名，译作“博克”（英、德、西、葡、罗、捷、瑞典、匈）或“木”（东南亚国家华语）

e.en: Columbia Broadcasting System

d: abbr. 哥伦比亚广播公司（Columbia Broadcasting System）；共电式振铃设备（Central Battery Signalling）

e.en: If you have citizenship of a country, you are legally accepted as belonging to it.

ex.en: After 15 years in the U.S., he has finally decided to apply for American citizenship.
ex.zh: 在美国住了15年后，他最终决定申请美国的公民身份。

e.en: Citizenship is the fact of belonging to a community because you live in it, and the duties and responsibilities that this brings.

ex.en: Their German peers had a more developed sense of citizenship.
ex.zh: 他们的德国同龄人对于公民的义务和责任有更成熟的认识。

d: n. 公民资格，公民身份；公民义务，公民责任感

e.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

ex.en: He claimed that it was all a conspiracy against him.
ex.zh: 他声称这完全是一个针对他的阴谋。

ex.en: A man claiming to be a journalist threatened to reveal details about her private life.
ex.zh: 一个自称是记者的男人威胁要公开她的私生活细节。

e.en: If you say that someone claims responsibility or credit for something, you mean they say that they are responsible for it, but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth. 声称 (对某事负责或应得荣誉)

ex.en: An underground organization has claimed responsibility for the bomb explosion.
ex.zh: 一个地下组织已声称对炸弹爆炸事件负责。

e.en: If you claim something, you try to get it because you think you have a right to it.

ex.en: Now they are returning to claim what was theirs.
ex.zh: 现在他们回来索要原本属于他们的东西。

e.en: If someone claims a record, title, or prize, they gain or win it.

ex.en: Zhuang claimed the record in 54.64 seconds.
ex.zh: 庄创造了54.64秒的纪录。

d: v. 声称，断言；索取，索要（钱）；要求（拥有），认领；使丧生，致命；赢得，获得；值得，需要（花时间或精力）
n. 声称，断言；索要，索赔；权利，所有权；要求得到的土地使用权；专利新特征申明
n. 克勒塔（希腊神话中登场的美惠女神卡里忒斯之一）；（美、菲、巴西）克勒塔（人名）

e.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

ex.en: ...the introduction of legislation to compel cyclists to wear a helmet.
ex.zh: …强制骑车人戴头盔的法律的引入。

e.en: If you feel compelled to do something, you feel that you must do it, because it is the right thing to do. 感到必须 (做某事)

ex.en: Dickens felt compelled to return to the stage for a final goodbye.
ex.zh: 狄更斯感到必须返回舞台作最后的告别。

d: v. 强迫，迫使；使发生，促使；驱赶
【名】 （Compel）（法）孔佩尔（人名）

e.en: If you consider a person or thing to be something, you have the opinion that this is what they are.

ex.en: We don't consider our customers to be mere consumers; we consider them to be our friends.
ex.zh: 我们没有视我们的顾客为纯粹的消费者；我们视他们为我们的朋友。

ex.en: I had always considered myself a strong, competent woman.
ex.zh: 我曾一直以为自己是个坚强能干的女人。

e.en: If you consider something, you think about it carefully. 仔细考虑 (某事物)

ex.en: The administration continues to consider ways to resolve the situation.
ex.zh: 政府继续仔细考虑解决这种情况的办法。

ex.en: You do have to consider the feelings of those around you.
ex.zh: 你真的得仔细考虑你身边那些人的感受。

e.en: If you are considering doing something, you intend to do it, but have not yet made a final decision whether to do it. 考虑 (做某事)

ex.en: I had seriously considered telling the story from the point of view of the wives.
ex.zh: 我曾认真考虑过从妻子们的角度来讲述这个故事。

d: v. 考虑，斟酌；认为，视为；体贴，顾及；细看，端详；探讨，讨论

e.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

ex.en: The envelope contained a Christmas card.
ex.zh: 该信封里装有一张圣诞贺卡。

ex.en: The first two floors of the building contain retail space and a restaurant.
ex.zh: 该大楼最底下两层有零售空间和一家餐馆。

e.en: If a substance contains something, that thing is a part of it.

ex.en: Watermelon contains vitamins and also potassium.
ex.zh: 西瓜含有维生素也有钾。

e.en: If writing, speech, or film contains particular information, ideas, or images, it includes them. (文章、演讲、电影) 包含 (某些信息、观点、图像等)

ex.en: This sheet contained a list of problems a patient might like to raise with the doctor.
ex.zh: 这张纸写有一个病人可能想向医生提出的问题清单。

e.en: If a group or organization contains a certain number of people, those are the people that are in it. (团体、组织等) 包括 (某数量的成员)

ex.en: The committee contains 11 Democrats and nine Republicans.
ex.zh: 该委员会包括11名民主党人和9名共和党人。

d: v. 包含，容纳；遏制，防止……蔓延；抑制（感情）

e.en: Ideas, attitudes, or reactions that are contrary to each other are completely different from each other. (观点、态度、反应)

ex.en: This view is contrary to the aims of critical social research for a number of reasons.
ex.zh: 许多原因证明这种观点与批判性社会研究的目的截然相反。

e.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

ex.en: Contrary to popular belief, moderate exercise actually decreases your appetite.
ex.zh: 与大部分人的想法相反，适度的运动实际上会降低食欲。

e.en: You use on the contrary when you have just said or implied that something is not true and are going to say that the opposite is true.

ex.en: It is not an idea around which the community can unite. On the contrary, I see it as one that will divide us.
ex.zh: 这不是一个可以让我们的组织团结起来的主意。恰恰相反，我看它会分裂我们。

e.en: You can use on the contrary when you are disagreeing strongly with something that has just been said or implied, or are making a strong negative reply. 相反 (用于否定对方意见)

ex.en: "People just don't do things like that."—"On the contrary, they do them all the time."
ex.zh: “人们根本就不像那样做事。” —“然而，他们却一直在那么做。”

d: adj. 相反的，相对的；乖戾的，好与人作对的；逆向的，逆行的
n. 相反的事实（或事情、情况）；对立命题，反对命题
adv. 相反地

e.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it.

ex.en: Government officials visited the earthquake zone on Thursday morning to coordinate the relief effort.
ex.zh: 政府官员星期四上午视察了地震灾区以协调救灾工作。

e.en: 协调的

ex.en: Coalition forces were planning a coordinated effort to attack the drug trade.
ex.zh: 联合部队正在计划共同打击毒品买卖。

ex.en: ...a well-coordinated surprise attack.
ex.zh: …一次完美配合的突袭。

e.en: If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently to perform particular movements. 使 (身体各部位)

ex.en: You need to coordinate legs, arms, and breathing for the front crawl.
ex.zh: 匍匐前进时，你要协调双腿、胳膊和呼吸。

e.en: If you coordinate clothes or furnishings that are used together, or if they coordinate, they are similar in some way and look nice together. 搭配 (衣服、饰品)

ex.en: She'll show you how to coordinate pattern and colours.
ex.zh: 她会向你展示如何搭配款式和颜色。

ex.en: Tie it with fabric bows that coordinate with other furnishings.
ex.zh: 扎上和其他的饰品相配的布制蝴蝶结。

d: v. （使）协调，调节，配合；协同动作，使（身体部位）协调；搭配（衣服、饰品等）；（化学）与……形成配位键（coordinate 的现在分词）
adj. 协调的，统筹的；（语法）并列的，对等的，同位的

e.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

ex.en: At this rate, we could find ourselves in the divorce courts!
ex.zh: 照这样下去，我们可能会在离婚法庭上对簿公堂！

ex.en: ...a county court judge.
ex.zh: …一名县法院的法官。

e.en: You can refer to the people in a court, especially the judge, jury, or magistrates, as a court. (一次开庭的)

ex.en: A court at Tampa, Florida has convicted five officials on charges of handling millions of dollars earned from illegal drug deals.
ex.zh: 佛罗里达州坦帕市的一个法庭宣布被指控通过非法毒品买卖获取上百万美元的5名官员罪名成立。

e.en: A court is an area in which you play a game such as tennis, basketball, badminton, or squash.

ex.en: The hotel has several tennis and squash courts.
ex.zh: 该旅馆有几个网球场和壁球场。

e.en: The court of a king or queen is the place where he or she lives and carries out ceremonial or administrative duties.

ex.en: She came to visit England, where she was presented at the court of James I.
ex.zh: 她来访问英格兰，在詹姆斯一世的王宫受到了接见。

d: n. 法院，法庭（court 的复数）；球场，运动场地（court 的复数）；（Courts）人名；（英）考茨
v. 讨好，献殷勤，取悦；设法获得；招致；（旧）求爱，谈恋爱（court 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Someone's contention is the idea or opinion that they are expressing in an argument or discussion. (辩论或讨论中表达的)

ex.en: It is my contention that death and murder always lurk as potentials in violent relationships.
ex.zh: 我的观点是，在暴力关系中总是潜伏着死亡和谋杀的可能。

e.en: If something is a cause of contention, it is a cause of disagreement or argument.

ex.en: His case has become a source of contention between civil liberties activists and the government.
ex.zh: 他的案子已变成了公民自由活动家们和政府之间的争论缘由。

d: n. 看法，观点；争论，争吵；争夺，竞争

e.en: A covering is a layer of something that protects or hides something else. 保护层;

ex.en: Leave a thin covering of fat.
ex.zh: 留下一层薄脂肪层。

d: n. 遮盖物，覆盖层
v. 遮盖，覆盖（cover 的现在分词）；（与 for 连用）顶替，代班

e.en: To create something means to cause it to happen or exist. 创造;

ex.en: We set business free to create more jobs.
ex.zh: 我们让企业自由以创造更多的就业机会。

ex.en: She could create a fight out of anything.
ex.zh: 她可以为了任何事制造争斗。

e.en: 创造

ex.en: These businesses stimulate the creation of local jobs.
ex.zh: 这些企业刺激了当地就业机会的产生。

e.en: When someone creates a new product or process, they invent it or design it. 创造;

ex.en: It is really great for a radio producer to create a show like this.
ex.zh: 一个电台节目制作人能设计出这样的节目真是太了不起了。

d: v. 创造，创建；设计，创作；造成，引起；授予，册封；大惊小怪，抱怨

e.en: A cutting from a plant is a part of the plant that you have cut off so that you can grow a new plant from it.

ex.en: Take cuttings from it in July or August.
ex.zh: 在7月或8月从它上面剪下插枝。

ex.en: Take cuttings from suitable garden tomatoes in late summer.
ex.zh: 夏末从合适的园栽西红柿剪下插枝。

e.en: A cutting remark is unkind and likely to hurt someone's feelings.

ex.en: People make cutting remarks to help themselves feel superior or powerful.
ex.zh: 人们说尖刻的话来帮自己感觉优越或强势。

e.en: A cutting is a piece of writing which has been cut from a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: ...notice boards crowded with newspaper cuttings.
ex.zh: …贴满了剪报的布告栏。

e.en: A cutting is a narrow valley which has been cut through a hill so that a road or railway line can pass through. (山中开出的)

d: n. 切割，切断；剪报；插枝，插条；狭窄通道，路堑；割下的东西；（Cutting）卡廷（人名）
adj. 尖酸刻薄的；严寒的，刺骨的；切割用的；锋利的
v. 切割；凿成；剪短；把……切碎；划破；削减（cut 的现在分词）

e.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is. 曝光; 揭露...

ex.en: Historian Michael Beschloss debunks a few myths.
ex.zh: 历史学家迈克尔·贝斯切罗斯揭露了一些神话的真相。

d: v. debunk 的过去式和过去分词：揭穿，拆穿（谎言、神话、误解等）
adj. 被揭穿的，被拆穿的（指已被证明不实的信念、说法、神话或理论等）

e.en: If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.

ex.en: She decided to take a course in philosophy.
ex.zh: 她决定修一门哲学课。

ex.en: Think about it very carefully before you decide.
ex.zh: 在你决定之前慎重地考虑。

e.en: If a person or group of people decides something, they choose what something should be like or how a particular problem should be solved.

ex.en: She was still young, he said, and that would be taken into account when deciding her sentence.
ex.zh: 她还年轻，他说，这一点对裁定关于她的判决时要考虑进去。

e.en: If an event or fact decides something, it makes it certain that a particular choice will be made or that there will be a particular result.

ex.en: What happens next could decide their destiny.
ex.zh: 接下来发生的事可能会决定他们的命运。

ex.en: The election will decide if either party controls both houses of Congress.
ex.zh: 这次选举将决定是否由任一党控制国会两院。

e.en: If you decide that something is true, you form that opinion about it after considering the facts.

ex.en: He decided Franklin must be suffering from a bad cold.
ex.zh: 他断定富兰克林肯定是得了重感冒。

d: adj. 决定性的，关键的；无疑的
v. 决定；裁决；断定（decide 的现在分词／动名词）

e.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

ex.en: The number of staff has declined from 217,000 to 114,000.
ex.zh: 员工人数已从217000人减少到114000人。

ex.en: Hourly output by workers declined 1.3% in the first quarter.
ex.zh: 工人每小时的产量在第1季度下降了1.3%。

e.en: If you decline something or decline to do something, you politely refuse to accept it or do it.

ex.en: He declined their invitation.
ex.zh: 他谢绝了他们的邀请。

ex.en: He offered the boys some coffee. They declined politely.
ex.zh: 他要给男孩们来些咖啡。他们礼貌地拒绝了。

e.en: If there is a decline in something, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or quality.

ex.en: Official figures show a sharp decline in the number of foreign tourists.
ex.zh: 官方数字显示外国游客数量骤降。

e.en: If something is in decline or on the decline, it is gradually decreasing in importance, quality, or power.

ex.en: Thankfully the smoking of cigarettes is on the decline.
ex.zh: 感谢的是吸烟正在减少。

d: v. 下降；拒绝；衰退（decline 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you demand something such as information or action, you ask for it in a very forceful way.

ex.en: Human rights groups are demanding an investigation into the shooting.
ex.zh: 人权组织正强烈要求对这一枪击案进行调查。

ex.en: Russia demanded that UNITA send a delegation to the peace talks.
ex.zh: 俄罗斯强烈要求安哥拉彻底独立全国同盟派遣一个代表团参加和谈。

e.en: If one thing demands another, the first needs the second in order to happen or be dealt with successfully.

ex.en: He said the task of reconstruction would demand much patience, hard work, and sacrifice.
ex.zh: 他说重建工作会需要高度坚韧、勤劳和奉献。

e.en: A demand is a firm request for something.

ex.en: There have been demands for services from tenants up there.
ex.zh: 那边的房客们有服务的明确要求。

e.en: If you refer to demand, or to the demand for something, you are referring to how many people want to have it, do it, or buy it.

ex.en: Another flight would be arranged on Saturday if sufficient demand arose.
ex.zh: 如果有足够的需求量，周六就会安排另一个航班。

d: v．要求，需求：强烈要求或需要某物。

e.en: A Democrat is a member or supporter of a particular political party which has the word "democrat" or "democratic" in its title, for example, the Democratic Party in the United States.

ex.en: Murray has joined other Senate Democrats in blocking the legislation.
ex.zh: 默里已经加入其他民主党参议员反对这项立法了。

e.en: A democrat is a person who believes in the ideals of democracy, personal freedom, and equality.

ex.en: This is the time for democrats and not dictators.
ex.zh: 这是民主主义者而不是独裁者的时代。

d: n. 民主党员（democrat 的复数）；民主主义者

e.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely.

ex.en: A storm moved directly over the island, demolishing buildings and flooding streets.
ex.zh: 一场暴风雨直扫这个岛屿，彻底摧毁了房屋，淹没了街道。

e.en: If you demolish someone's ideas or arguments, you prove that they are completely wrong or unreasonable.

ex.en: Our intention was quite the opposite – to demolish rumours that have surrounded him since he took office.
ex.zh: 我们的意图恰恰相反–要粉碎自他就职以来就缠着他的谣言。

d: v. （demolish 的过去式和过去分词）拆毁，摧毁，破坏；驳倒，推翻；彻底击败，大胜；狼吞虎咽地吃光，一扫而光
adj. 被拆毁的，被拆除的

e.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university. A department is also one of the sections in a large shop. (政府、企业等机构的) 部; (大学的) 系; (大型商店的)

ex.en: ...the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
ex.zh: …美国健康和公共事业部。

ex.en: He moved to the sales department.
ex.zh: 他调到了销售部。

d: n. 部，［管理］部门；（大学的）系，教学单位；（医院的）科室；（法国等国家的）省，行政区（department 的复数形式）

e.en: A detailed report or plan contains a lot of details.

ex.en: Yesterday's letter contains a detailed account of the decisions.
ex.zh: 昨天的信里有对那些决定的详细说明。

d: adj. 详尽的，详细的；（装饰）精细的，细致的
v. 详细说明，详述；彻底清洗（汽车）；（尤指军队中）派遣，选派（detail 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The details of something are its individual features or elements.

ex.en: The details of the plan are still being worked out.
ex.zh: 计划的细节还在制定中。

ex.en: No details of the discussions have been given.
ex.zh: 会谈的细节尚未透露。

e.en: A detail is a minor point or aspect of something, as opposed to the central ones.

ex.en: Only minor details now remain to be settled.
ex.zh: 只有细枝末节还没确定。

e.en: Details about someone or something are facts or pieces of information about them.

ex.en: See the bottom of this page for details of how to apply for this exciting offer.
ex.zh: 关于如何申请这个令人激动的机会，详情请参看本页末。

e.en: You can refer to the small features of something which are often not noticed as detail.

ex.en: We like his attention to detail and his enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 我们喜欢他对细微之处的关注，以及他的热情。

d: n. （建筑、服装等的）装饰细部，细部设计；（汽车的）彻底清洗、抛光等精细美容养护
v. （detail 的现在分词）详细说明，详述；彻底清洗（汽车）；（尤指军队中）派遣，选派

e.en: reduced or lessened; made smaller 减少的;
denoting any minor or perfect interval reduced by a semitone
denoting a triad consisting of the root plus a minor third and a diminished fifth

d: v. 减少，降低，削弱；贬低，轻视（diminish 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 减少的，减弱的，缩小的；被贬低的，受轻视的；（音乐）减音程、减和弦的；（法律）限定责任能力的（用于 diminished responsibility）

e.en: If you discard something, you get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

ex.en: Read the manufacturer's guidelines before discarding the box.
ex.zh: 先阅读制造商的说明书再把盒子丢掉。

d: adj. 丢弃的，废弃的
v. 丢弃（discard 的过去式和过去分词）；（牌戏）垫牌，打出（不用的牌）

e.en: If you dismiss something, you decide or say that it is not important enough for you to think about or consider.

ex.en: Mr. Wakeham dismissed the reports as speculation.
ex.zh: 韦克厄姆先生把这些报道当作臆测而不予理会。

e.en: If you dismiss something from your mind, you stop thinking about it.

ex.en: I dismissed the problem from my mind.
ex.zh: 我从心中摒除了这个问题。

e.en: When an employer dismisses an employee, the employer tells the employee that they are no longer needed to do the job that they have been doing.

ex.en: ...the power to dismiss civil servants who refuse to work.
ex.zh: …解雇拒绝工作的公务员们的权力。

e.en: If you are dismissed by someone in authority, they tell you that you can go away from them.

ex.en: Two more witnesses were called, heard, and dismissed.
ex.zh: 又有两名证人被传讯后获准离开了。

d: v. dismiss 的过去式和过去分词：解雇，开除；不考虑，不理会，摒弃；驳回，不受理；让……离开，解散
adj. 被解雇的，被开除的

e.en: If a group of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

ex.en: The building houses a wide and diverse variety of antiques.
ex.zh: 这栋楼里摆放着大量各式各样的古董。

e.en: Diverse people or things are very different from each other.

ex.en: Albert Jones' new style will inevitably put him in touch with a much more diverse and perhaps younger audience.
ex.zh: 艾伯特·琼斯的新风格无疑将使他接触更多形形色色的、或许更年轻的观众。

d: adj. 不同的，各式各样的
n. 唐纳德（男子名）
n. 道格（男子名，常作 Douglas（道格拉斯）的昵称或简称）
n. （Elkind）人名；（英）埃尔金德

e.en: To emphasize something means to indicate that it is particularly important or true, or to draw special attention to it.

ex.en: But it's also been emphasized that no major policy changes can be expected to come out of the meeting.
ex.zh: 但是也强调，这次会议预期不会做出重大政策改变。

d: v. 强调，着重；重读（单词或短语）；使突出（或明显）（emphasize 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If someone is empowered to do something, they have the authority or power to do it.

ex.en: The army is now empowered to operate on a shoot-to-kill basis.
ex.zh: 军队现在被授权依据“杀无赦”原则行动。

e.en: To empower someone means to give them the means to achieve something, for example, to become stronger or more successful.

ex.en: You must delegate effectively and empower people to carry out their roles with your full support.
ex.zh: 你们必须有效地下放权力，使人们能够在你们的全力支持下履行他们的职责。

d: adj. 获得授权的，被赋予权力的；有自主能力的，有信心的
v. 授权；给予（某人）权力，使自主（empower 的过去式和过去分词）
v. 努力，奋力（endeavor 的第三人称单数）
n. 努力，尝试；事业（endeavor 的复数）

e.en: To ensure something, or to ensure that something happens, means to make certain that it happens.

ex.en: We must ensure that all patients have access to high quality care.
ex.zh: 我们必须确保所有的病人都能够得到高质量的护理。

d: v. 确保，保证；保护，使安全（ensure 的现在分词）

e.en: If someone carries out the enforcement of an act or rule, they enforce it.

ex.en: The doctors want stricter enforcement of existing laws.
ex.zh: 医生们希望现行法律的执行能更严格。

d: n. 执行，实施

e.en: Carbon is a chemical element that diamonds and coal are made up of. (化学元素)

d: n. 碳；复写纸；炭精棒；碳纤维
adj. 碳的，碳处理的
【名】 （Carbon）（英）卡本，（西）卡尔翁，（法）卡尔邦（人名）

e.en: A drill is a tool or machine that you use for making holes.

ex.en: ...a dentist's drill.
ex.zh: …一把牙钻。

e.en: A drill is a routine exercise or activity, in which people practise what they should do in dangerous situations.

ex.en: ...a fire drill.
ex.zh: …一场消防演习。

e.en: When you drill into something or drill a hole in something, you make a hole in it using a drill. 钻 (孔); 打 (眼)

ex.en: He drilled into the wall of Lili's bedroom.
ex.zh: 他在丽莉卧室的墙上打孔。

e.en: When people drill for oil or water, they search for it by drilling deep holes in the ground or in the bottom of the sea. 钻探 (石油或地下水源)

ex.en: There have been proposals to drill for more oil.
ex.zh: 有人提出了钻探更多石油的建议。

d: adj. 钻过孔的，由钻孔形成的；受过反复操练的，训练有素的
v. 钻（孔）；钻探；训练（drill 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: You use cc when referring to the volume or capacity of something such as the size of a car engine. cc is an abbreviation for "cubic centimetres."

ex.en: ...1,500 cc sports cars.
ex.zh: …气缸容量为1500立方厘米的跑车。

e.en: cc is used in e-mail headers or at the end of a business letter to indicate that a copy is being sent to another person. (电子邮件或业务信函的)

ex.en: ...cc j.jones@harpercollins.co.uk
ex.zh: …转发到j.jones@harpercollins.co.uk。

ex.en: ...cc J. Chater, S. Cooper.
ex.zh: …转发给J.蔡特与S.库珀。

e.en: Cocos Islands

d: abbr. 通信学会理事会（Council of Communication Societies）；联合参谋部（combined chiefs of staff）

e.en: A fossil is the hard remains of a prehistoric animal or plant that are found inside a rock.

d: n. 化石；思想僵化的人；僵化的事物
adj. 化石的，从地下采掘出的；不变的，古老的

e.en: If you report something that has happened, you tell people about it. 报告;

ex.en: I reported the theft to the police.
ex.zh: 我向警察报告了这起盗窃案。

ex.en: The officials also reported that two more ships were apparently heading for Malta.
ex.zh: 官员们也报告说另有两艘船显然正朝马耳他驶去。

e.en: If you report on an event or subject, you tell people about it, because it is your job or duty to do so. 报道; (工作或职责上)

ex.en: Many journalists based outside of Sudan have been refused visas to enter the country to report on political affairs.
ex.zh: 很多驻在苏丹境外的记者遭到拒签，无法进入该国报道政治事件。

e.en: A report is a news article or broadcast which gives information about something that has just happened. (报刊或广播电视上的)

ex.en: According to a report in the newspaper, he still has control over the remaining shares.
ex.zh: 根据报纸上的报道，他依然控制着剩余的股份。

e.en: A report is an official document which a group of people issue after investigating a situation or event. (调查)

ex.en: The education committee will today publish its report on the supply of teachers for the next decade.
ex.zh: 教育委员会今天将公布关于今后十年师资储备的报告。

d: n. 报告，汇报；新闻报道；官方文件，调查报告；传闻，传说；（学生）成绩报告单；案情报告；下属；爆炸声，枪声；谣言，流传；名誉，名声
v. 报道；据说，传闻；述说，报告；公告，公布；举报（罪案）， 报告（事故）；报到；描述（感情、病情等）；（议会委员会主席）正式宣布委员会已讨论（法案）；（议会委员会）将法案交还给议会表决；对（上级或监督者）负责，由......领导；告发，检举
【名】 （Report）（匈）雷波特（人名）

e.en: Fuel is a substance such as coal, oil, or petrol that is burned to provide heat or power.

ex.en: They ran out of fuel.
ex.zh: 他们用完了燃料。

e.en: To fuel a situation means to make it become worse or more intense.

ex.en: The result will inevitably fuel speculation about the prime minister's future.
ex.zh: 该结果将不可避免地加剧人们对首相前途的猜测。

d: n. 燃料（fuel 的复数形式）
v. 供给燃料；使（情绪、争论等）加剧（fuel 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: The author of a piece of writing is the person who wrote it.

ex.en: ...Jill Phillips, author of the book "Give Your Child Music."
ex.zh: …吉尔·菲利浦斯，《把音乐给你的孩子》一书的作者。

e.en: An author is a person whose job is writing books.

ex.en: Haruki Murakami is Japan's best-selling author.
ex.zh: 村上春树是日本的畅销书作家。

d: n. 作者，著者；作家（author 的复数）
v. 撰写，写作（author 的第三人称单数）
n. 梅茨（法国东北部城市）

e.en: Technology refers to methods, systems, and devices which are the result of scientific knowledge being used for practical purposes.

ex.en: Technology is changing fast.
ex.zh: 技术日新月异。

ex.en: They should be allowed to wait for cheaper technologies to be developed.
ex.zh: 他们应该被允许等待更廉价的技术开发出来。

d: n. 科技，技术；技术设备，先进机器；技术学，工艺学；术语
n. 班森，本森（男子名）；班森，本森（英语姓氏）；本森（美国、英国等地地名）
n. 奥维耶多（西班牙西北部一城市）

e.en: a Spanish sparkling wine produced by a method similar to that used for champagne
e.zh: 用与制香槟相似的方法酿成的一种西班牙气泡酒

d: n. 卡瓦（一种西班牙起泡酒，主要产于加泰罗尼亚，用类似香槟的方法酿造，常写作 Cava）；腔静脉（解剖学术语，多用于 vena cava 等固定搭配）

e.en: A chapter is one of the parts that a book is divided into. Each chapter has a number, and sometimes a title.

ex.en: Chromium supplements were used successfully in the treatment of diabetes (see Chapter 4).
ex.zh: 铬补充剂成功地用在了糖尿病的治疗上(参见第4章)。

e.en: A chapter in someone's life or in history is a period of time during which a major event or series of related events takes place. (事件发生的)

ex.en: This had been a particularly difficult chapter in Lebanon's recent history.
ex.zh: 这是黎巴嫩近代史上的一个特别困难的时期。

d: n. 章，回，篇；阶段，时期；分会，分部；议会法案；一系列，一连串（a chapter of）；全体教士；宗教团体理事会
v. 把……分成章节

e.en: Something that is hard is very firm and stiff to touch and is not easily bent, cut, or broken.

ex.en: He shuffled his feet on the hard wooden floor.
ex.zh: 他拖着脚走在坚硬的木地板上。

e.en: 坚硬

ex.en: He felt the hardness of the iron railing press against his spine.
ex.zh: 他感觉到硬梆梆的铁栏杆抵住了他的脊梁骨。

e.en: Something that is hard is very difficult to do or deal with.

ex.en: It's hard to tell what effect this latest move will have.
ex.zh: 很难说最近的这次行动将会有什么样的影响。

ex.en: That's a very hard question.
ex.zh: 那是个很难的问题。

e.en: If you work hard doing something, you are very active or work intensely, with a lot of effort.

ex.en: I'll work hard. I don't want to let him down.
ex.zh: 我会努力工作。我不想让他失望。

d: adj. 硬的，坚固的；困难的；困苦的，艰苦的；费力的，努力的；坚强的，勇敢的；猛烈的，用力的；冷酷的，严厉的；寒冷的，凛冽的；可证实的，确凿的；刺眼的，（感觉上）难受的；（水）硬的；烈性的，强烈的；（酒）苦涩的；仔细的，认真的；严肃的；强壮的；（政治上）极端的；发硬音的
adv. 努力地，费力地；用力地，猛烈地；仔细地，认真地；沉重地，大量地；变硬；在最大程度上
n. 海滩路
【名】 （Hard）（英、芬、瑞典）哈德（人名）

e.en: To inject a substance such as a medicine into someone means to put it into their body using a device with a needle called a syringe.

ex.en: His son was injected with strong drugs.
ex.zh: 他的儿子被注射了强效的药。

ex.en: The technique consists of injecting healthy cells into the weakened muscles.
ex.zh: 这项技术包括把健康细胞注射进衰弱的肌肉里。

e.en: If you inject a new, exciting, or interesting quality into a situation, you add it. 注入;

ex.en: She kept trying to inject a little fun into their relationship.
ex.zh: 她一直设法给他们的关系增添一点情趣。

e.en: If you inject money or resources into a business or organization, you provide more money or resources for it. 注入 (资金或资源)

ex.en: The insurance fund would inject $750 into the banks.
ex.zh: 该保险基金将向银行投入750美元。

d: adj. 注入的；注射的；充血的，布满血丝的（多指眼睛）
v. inject 的过去式和过去分词
n. 基思（男子名）

e.en: Novels, plays, and poetry are referred to as literature, especially when they are considered to be good or important.

ex.en: ...classic works of literature.
ex.zh: …古典文学作品。

ex.en: I have spent my life getting to know diverse literatures of different epochs.
ex.zh: 我花费一生时间来逐渐了解不同时代形形色色的文学。

e.en: The literature on a particular subject of study is all the books and articles that have been published about it.

ex.en: ...the literature on immigration policy.
ex.zh: …关于外来移民政策的文献。

e.en: Literature is written information produced by people who want to sell you something or give you advice.

ex.en: I am sending you literature from two other companies that provide a similar service.
ex.zh: 我在给你邮寄来自另外两家提供类似服务的公司的宣传单。

d: n. 文学，文学作品；（某一学科的）文献，著述；印刷品，宣传品

e.en: The making of something is the act or process of producing or creating it. 制作;

ex.en: ...Salamon's book about the making of this film.
ex.zh: 萨拉蒙的关于制作这部影片的书。

e.en: If you describe a person or thing as something in the making, you mean that they are going to become known or recognized as that thing.

ex.en: Her drama teacher is confident Julie is a star in the making.
ex.zh: 她的戏剧老师相信朱莉是未来的明星。

e.en: If something is the making of a person or thing, it is the reason that they become successful or become very much better than they used to be. 是某人/

ex.en: This discovery may yet be the making of him.
ex.zh: 这一发现也许成为他成功的因素。

e.en: If you say that a person or thing has the makings of something, you mean it seems possible or likely that they will become that thing, as they have the necessary qualities.

ex.en: Godfrey had the makings of a successful journalist.
ex.zh: 戈弗雷具备一个成功记者的素质。

d: n. 制作，生产；素质，潜在能力；材料，原料；使……成功的因素；（自己动手卷烟用）纸和烟叶
v. 使得；进行；布置，准备，整理；制造（make 的现在分词形式）

e.en: You use potential to say that someone or something is capable of developing into the particular kind of person or thing mentioned.

ex.en: The company has identified 60 potential customers.
ex.zh: 该公司已确定了60位潜在的客户。

ex.en: We are aware of the potential problems and have taken every precaution.
ex.zh: 我们意识到了潜在的问题，已经采取了一切防范措施。

e.en: 潜在地

ex.en: Clearly this is a potentially dangerous situation.
ex.zh: 显然这是一种具有潜在危险的局势。

e.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future. 潜力;

ex.en: The boy has great potential.
ex.zh: 这个男孩有很大的潜力。

ex.en: The school strives to treat students as individuals and to help each one to achieve their full potential.
ex.zh: 学校力图因材施教，并帮助每位学生发挥他们的全部潜能。

e.en: If you say that someone or something has potential for doing a particular thing, you mean that it is possible they may do it. If there is the potential for something, it may happen.

ex.en: John seemed as horrified as I about his potential for violence.
ex.zh: 和我一样，约翰对他的暴力倾向感到恐惧。

ex.en: The meeting has the potential to be a watershed event.
ex.zh: 这次会议有可能成为一次分水岭事件。

d: adj. 潜在的，可能的
n. （事物的）潜力，可能性；（人的）潜能，潜力；电势，电位，电压

e.en: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

ex.en: We have been accused of exaggerating before, but unfortunately all our reports proved to be true.
ex.zh: 我们曾被指责夸大其词，但遗憾的是，我们所有的报告都证明是真实的。

ex.en: In the past this process of transition has often proven difficult.
ex.zh: 在过去，这种转变过程常证明是艰难的。

e.en: If you prove that something is true, you show by means of argument or evidence that it is definitely true.

ex.en: You brought this charge. You prove it!
ex.zh: 你提出了这一指控。你来证明它！

ex.en: The results prove that regulation of the salmon farming industry is inadequate.
ex.zh: 结果证明，大马哈鱼养殖业的管理是失当的。

e.en: If you prove yourself to have a certain good quality, you show by your actions that you have it. 显示 (优点)

ex.en: Margie proved herself to be a good mother.
ex.zh: 玛吉显示了自己是个好母亲。

ex.en: As a composer he proved himself adept at large dramatic forms.
ex.zh: 作为一名作曲家，他显示出自己擅长创作大型的戏剧体裁。

d: n. 证明；检验，检查；校对
v. 证明，证实；证明是，结果是，显示出；检验，试验，检查；校对；使发酵，醒发（prove 的现在分词）

e.en: Research is work that involves studying something and trying to discover facts about it.

ex.en: Sixty-five percent of the 1987 budget went for nuclear weapons research and production.
ex.zh: 1987年预算的65%用在了核武器的研制上。

e.en: If you research something, you try to discover facts about it.

ex.en: She spent two years in South Florida researching and filming her documentary.
ex.zh: 她在南佛罗里达花了两年的时间研究和拍摄纪录片。

e.en: 研究员

ex.en: He chose to join the company as a market researcher.
ex.zh: 他选择加入这家公司当一名市场研究员。

d: n. （尤指大学或科研机构进行的）研究，探讨；研究工作，调查工作
v. 研究，探索；为……收集资料，调查
n. 研究人员，研究者（researcher 的复数）

e.en: Saudi or Saudi Arabian means belonging or relating to Saudi Arabia or to its people, language, or culture. 沙特(人)的; 沙特语的;

ex.en: Saudi officials have dismissed such reports as rumours.
ex.zh: 沙特官员已经将此类报告驳斥为谣言。

e.en: The Saudis or Saudi Arabians are the people who come from Saudi Arabia.

d: adj. 沙特阿拉伯的，沙特人的
n. 沙特阿拉伯人，沙特人；（Saudi）（阿、埃、美、英、印、肯）沙特（人名）

e.en: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other. 一连串;

ex.en: ...a series of meetings with students and political leaders.
ex.zh: …与学生和政治领袖们的一连串会晤。

e.en: A radio or television series is a set of programs of a particular kind which have the same title. (广播或电视的)

ex.en: ...Captain Kirk's chair from the TV series "Star Trek."
ex.zh: …电视系列片《星际迷航》中柯克船长的椅子。

d: n. 连续，一系列（事件）；（电视、广播等的）系列片，系列节目；丛书，系列出版物；（两队之间的）系列比赛；（电路的）串联；（同时发行的）一套邮票（或货币、硬币）；（由某一公司推出的）系列产品，（尤指）汽车系列；（年代地层学用语）统；（元素的）系；级数，序列项的总和；有共同特征的一组语音，系列（音）；音列

e.en: (esp of a sum) determined by agreement; fixed (尤指总额)确定的;

d: adj. 正式表明的；（尤指总额）确定的，固定的；定期的
v. 陈述，说明；规定，公布；详述（案情）（state 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people. 显示;

ex.en: Research shows that young people still look to parents as their main source for health information.
ex.zh: 研究表明年轻人仍然指望父母作为他们主要的健康信息来源。

ex.en: These figures show an increase of over one million in unemployment.
ex.zh: 这些数据表明失业人数增长超过100万。

e.en: If a picture, chart, movie, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it. (图画、图表、文章等)

ex.en: Figure 4.1 shows the respiratory system.
ex.zh: 图4.1所示的是呼吸系统。

ex.en: The cushions, shown left, measure 20 x 12 inches and cost $39.95.
ex.zh: 左边展示的垫子尺寸是20 x 12英寸，价格为$39.95。

e.en: If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to. 拿给…看;

ex.en: Cut out this article and show it to your boss.
ex.zh: 把这篇文章剪下来拿给你的老板看。

ex.en: He showed me the apartment he shares with Esther.
ex.zh: 他指给我看他和埃斯特合住的公寓。

e.en: If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.

ex.en: It was very good of you to come. Let me show you to my study.
ex.zh: 你能来真是太好了。让我带你看我的书房。

ex.en: Milton was shown into the office.
ex.zh: 米尔顿被领进了办公室。

d: v. 显示，表明；给……看，出示；演示，教；带领，引领；表露出，显示出；（对某人）表现出，对待；容易显出，容易看到；标示，标明；描绘，描述；放映，播出；展示，展出；露面，出现；证明，证实；替（动物）报名参加比赛； （妇女）已显出身孕；获得第三名（或前三名）
n. 演出，歌舞表演；（电视或广播）节目；展览，展览会；表现，行为；假象，假装；景象；事情，场面；动物比赛；（分娩或月经时的）见红；（做某事的）机会
【名】 （Show）（美、巴西）肖（人名）

e.en: If you carry out a survey, you try to find out detailed information about a lot of different people or things, usually by asking people a series of questions.

ex.en: The council conducted a survey of the uses to which farm buildings are put.
ex.zh: 该委员会对农场建筑的用途进行了一个调查。

e.en: If you survey a number of people, companies, or organizations, you try to find out information about their opinions or behaviour, usually by asking them a series of questions.

ex.en: Business Development Advisers surveyed 211 companies for the report.
ex.zh: 企业发展顾问为这份报告调查了211家公司。

e.en: If you survey something, you look at or consider the whole of it carefully.

ex.en: He pushed himself to his feet and surveyed the room.
ex.zh: 他站起来审视这个房间。

e.en: If someone carries out a survey of an area of land, they examine it and measure it, usually in order to make a map of it.

ex.en: ...the organizer of the geological survey of India.
ex.zh: …印度地质勘测的组织者。

d: n. 民意调查，民意测验；考察，调查；（对课题或情况的）全面考察，概述；测量，勘测；测绘图，勘测记录；测量部门； （尤指为欲购房者所做的）房屋鉴定；查勘报告
v. 做民意测验，做民意调查；（尤指认真地）审视，检查；测量，勘测； （尤指为可能的买家）查勘，检视（建筑物的状况）；全面评述，概述

e.en: When you test something, you try it, for example, by touching it or using it for a short time, in order to find out what it is, what condition it is in, or how well it works.

ex.en: Either measure the temperature with a thermometer or test the water with your wrist.
ex.zh: 要么用温度计测量水温，要么用你的手腕来试水温。

e.en: A test is a deliberate action or experiment to find out how well something works.

ex.en: ...the banning of nuclear tests.
ex.zh: …对核试验的禁止。

e.en: If you test someone, you ask them questions or tell them to perform certain actions in order to find out how much they know about a subject or how well they are able to do something.

ex.en: There was a time when each teacher spent an hour, one day a week, testing students in every subject.
ex.zh: 曾有一段时间，每个老师每周都花一小时来测验学生的各门功课。

e.en: A test is a series of questions that you must answer or actions that you must perform in order to show how much you know about a subject or how well you are able to do something.

ex.en: Out of a total of 25 students only 15 passed the test.
ex.zh: 所有25个学生中只有15个通过了测试。

d: adj. 经受过考验的，经检验证明可靠的
v. test 的过去式和过去分词：测试，测验；考验；检测呈阳性

e.en: If you warn someone about something such as a possible danger or problem, you tell them about it so that they are aware of it. 警告;

ex.en: When I had my first baby friends warned me that children were expensive.
ex.zh: 当我有了第一个孩子时，朋友们提醒我说养小孩是很花钱的。

ex.en: They warned him of the dangers of sailing alone.
ex.zh: 他们警告他独自航行的重重危险。

e.en: If you warn someone not to do something, you advise them not to do it so that they can avoid possible danger or punishment.

ex.en: Mrs. Blount warned me not to interfere.
ex.zh: 布朗特太太告诫我不要插手。

ex.en: "Don't do anything yet," he warned. "Too risky."
ex.zh: “先别行动，”他警告道，“太冒险了。”

d: adj. 已警告的，已受到警告的
v. 警告（warn 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Writing is something that has been written or printed.

ex.en: If you have a complaint about your holiday, please inform us in writing.
ex.zh: 如果你对你的假期有意见，请以书面形式告知我们。

e.en: You can refer to any piece of written work as writing, especially when you are considering the style of language used in it.

ex.en: The writing is brutally tough and savagely humorous.
ex.zh: 该作品文笔痛快地犀利和极端地幽默。

e.en: Writing is the activity of writing, especially of writing books for money.

ex.en: She had begun to be a little bored with novel writing.
ex.zh: 她已经开始对小说写作有点厌倦了。

e.en: Your writing is the way that you write with a pen or pencil, which can usually be recognized as belonging to you.

ex.en: It was a little difficult to read your writing.
ex.zh: 辨认你的笔迹有点难。

d: n. 写作，著书；作品，著作；写，书写；字迹；（书写或印刷的）文字；（某作家或专题的）著作，作品（writings）
v. 写字；写作；写信（write 的现在分词）

e.en: If you have an account with a bank or a similar organization, you have an arrangement to leave your money there and take some out when you need it.

ex.en: Some banks make it difficult to open an account.
ex.zh: 有些银行使开一个账户困难重重。

e.en: In business, a regular customer of a company can be referred to as an account, especially when the customer is another company.

ex.en: All three Internet agencies boast they've won major accounts.
ex.zh: 所有的三家网络代理公司都夸口说他们已赢得了大客户。

e.en: Accounts are detailed records of all the money that a person or business receives and spends.

ex.en: He kept detailed accounts.
ex.zh: 他保存了详细的账目。

e.en: An account is a written or spoken report of something that has happened.

ex.en: He gave a detailed account of what happened on the fateful night.
ex.zh: 他对那个决定命运的夜晚所发生的事情做了一个详细的报道。

d: n. 账户，户头；客户，老主顾；网络账号；描述，报道；账目；账单；赊购账，赊购；理由，解释；重要性；（定期结付的）交易合同；演奏（音乐）；账期交易期
v. 把……视作，认为；解释，说明（account for）；占（一定数量或比例）（account for）；报账

e.en: Your address is the number of the house or apartment and the name of the street and the town where you live or work.

ex.en: The address is 2025 M Street, NW, Washington, DC, 20036.
ex.zh: 地址是华盛顿哥伦比亚特区，华盛顿西北，M街2025号，邮编20036。

e.en: The address of a website is its location on the Internet, for example, http://www.thomson.com.

ex.en: Full details, including the website address to log on to, are at the bottom of this page.
ex.zh: 包括要登陆的网址的完整信息在本页下端。

e.en: If a letter, envelope, or parcel is addressed to you, your name and address have been written on it. 写 (收信人的)

ex.en: Applications should be addressed to: The business affairs editor.
ex.zh: 申请信应该寄给商务编辑。

e.en: If you address a group of people, you give a speech to them.

ex.en: He is due to address a conference on human rights next week.
ex.zh: 他下周要在一个人权会议上发言。

d: n. 地址，住址；网址；电子邮箱地址；演讲，演说；（电子表格中某个单元格的）位置；（对他人的）谈吐；谦恭（或脉脉含情）的方式；机敏，迅速；位置存储编码
v. 演说，演讲；处理，设法解决；在（信封、包裹等）上写姓名和地址，致函； 向……讲话；称呼；（向某人）提出（陈述、投诉等）；（高尔夫）就位击（球）

e.en: If you give someone advice, you tell them what you think they should do in a particular situation.

ex.en: Don't be afraid to ask for advice about ordering the meal.
ex.zh: 别怕就点餐寻求建议。

ex.en: Take my advice and stay away from him!
ex.zh: 听我的忠告，离他远点！

d: n. 忠告，劝告，建议；（金融交易）正式通知；消息

e.en: If you do something or if something happens afterward, you do it or it happens after a particular event or time that has already been mentioned. (某事件、某时间)

ex.en: Shortly afterward, police arrested four suspects.
ex.zh: 之后不久，警方逮捕了４名嫌疑犯。

d: adv. 以后，后来，其后

e.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

ex.en: The children are allowed to watch TV after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们被允许在放学后看电视。

ex.en: Smoking will not be allowed.
ex.zh: 吸烟将被禁止。

e.en: If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.

ex.en: Gifts like chocolates or flowers are allowed.
ex.zh: 像巧克力或者花这样的礼物是准许的。

e.en: If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.

ex.en: He won't allow himself to fail.
ex.zh: 他不容许自己失败。

e.en: If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen. 使能够 (发生)

ex.en: The compromise will allow him to continue his free market reforms.
ex.zh: 这个妥协将使他得以继续他的自由市场改革。

ex.en: ...an attempt to allow the Muslim majority a greater share of power.
ex.zh: …使穆斯林多数派分享更多权力的一种尝试。

d: v. 允许（allow 的现在分词/动名词）；容许；使能够（发生）；allowing for：考虑到，虑及

e.en: Air is the mixture of gases that forms the Earth's atmosphere and that we breathe.

ex.en: Draughts help to circulate air.
ex.zh: 通风有助于循环空气。

ex.en: Keith opened the window and leaned out into the cold air.
ex.zh: 基斯打开窗户，探出身到冷风中。

e.en: Air is used to refer to travel in aircraft.

ex.en: Air travel will continue to grow at about 6% per year.
ex.zh: 乘飞机旅行的人数将以每年大约6%的速度持续增加。

e.en: The air is the space around things or above the ground.

ex.en: Government troops broke up the protest by firing their guns in the air.
ex.zh: 政府军通过朝天鸣枪驱散了这场抗议示威。

e.en: If a broadcasting company airs a television or radio programme, they show it on television or broadcast it on the radio.

ex.en: Tonight PBS will air a documentary called "Democracy In Action".
ex.zh: 今晚PBS电台将播放一部名为《民主进行时》的纪录片。

d: n. 大气，空气；空中，天空；乘坐飞机，航空；神态，氛围；曲调，旋律；装腔作势，做作；空气媒质；气，风
v. 使公开，宣扬；（使）通风；（使）晾干，（使）烘干；播送，播放；出去透气；炫耀，夸示
abbr. 沙特阿美石油公司（Arabian-American Oil Company）

e.en: When you assess a person, thing, or situation, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them.

ex.en: The test was to assess aptitude rather than academic achievement.
ex.zh: 该测试将评估能力而不是学业成绩。

ex.en: It would be a matter of assessing whether she was well enough to travel.
ex.zh: 这将是个评估她是否身体好到可以旅行的问题。

e.en: When you assess the amount of money that something is worth or should be paid, you calculate or estimate it. 计算;

ex.en: Ask them to send you information on how to assess the value of your belongings.
ex.zh: 叫他们把如何估算你的财产价值的资料寄给你。

d: v. 评价，评定；估价，估计；征税，处以罚金

e.en: If you are astonished by something, you are very surprised about it.

ex.en: They were astonished to find the driver was a six-year-old boy.
ex.zh: 他们当时很感意外，发现司机是个６岁的男孩。

d: adj. 十分震惊的，非常惊讶的
v. 使吃惊，使惊讶（astonish 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 澳大利亚，澳洲

e.en: A bed is a piece of furniture that you lie on when you sleep.

ex.en: We finally went to bed at about 4am.
ex.zh: 我们最后在凌晨四点左右上了床。

ex.en: By the time we got back from dinner, Nona was already in bed.
ex.zh: 等我们吃完饭回来，诺娜已经上床了。

e.en: If a place such as a hospital or a hotel has a particular number of beds, it is able to hold that number of patients or guests. (医院、旅馆等的)
A bed in a garden or park is an area of ground that has been specially prepared so that plants can be grown in it.

ex.en: ...beds of strawberries and rhubarb.
ex.zh: …草莓与大黄的苗床。

e.en: A bed of shellfish or plants is an area in the sea or in a lake where a particular type of shellfish or plant is found in large quantities. (某种贝类生物或植物密集的)

ex.en: The whole lake was rimmed with thick beds of reeds.
ex.zh: 整个湖边长满了厚厚的芦苇丛。

d: n. 床，床铺，床位；底部，基座；花坛，苗圃；海底，河床；岩层；（车辆的）拖斗
v. 把……固定，嵌入；与（某人）上床

e.en: If you are based in a particular place, that is the place where you live or do most of your work. See also . 基地 (或总部)

ex.en: Both firms are based in Kent.
ex.zh: 这两家公司的总部都位于肯特郡。

d: adj. （以某事）为基础的，为根据的；在……居住（或工作）的，基地（或总部）在……的
v. 以……为基础；把基地设在……（base 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 伯特（男子名，等于 Burt）
n. 伯克利（美国加利福尼亚州西部港市，位于旧金山湾东岸）；伯克利（加州大学伯克利分校的简称，也作 UC Berkeley）；贝克莱（George Berkeley，爱尔兰哲学家及圣公会主教）；伯克利（英语姓氏）

e.en: the red wood obtained from various tropical leguminous trees of the genus Caesalpinia, such as C. echinata of America: used for cabinetwork 巴西苏木 (Also called brazil wood)

d: n. 巴西木；巴西坚果（同 brazil nut）；从木材中提取的红色或紫色染料；（Brazil）巴西（拉丁美洲国家）

e.en: If you bring someone or something with you when you come to a place, they come with you or you have them with you.

ex.en: Remember to bring an apron or an old shirt to protect your clothes.
ex.zh: 记着带一条围裙或一件旧衬衫来保护你的衣服。

ex.en: Someone went upstairs and brought down a huge kettle.
ex.zh: 有人上楼拿下来一个巨大的水壶。

e.en: If you bring something somewhere, you move it there.

ex.en: Reaching into her pocket, she brought out a cigarette.
ex.zh: 她把手伸进口袋，拿出一根香烟。

e.en: If you bring something that someone wants or needs, you get it for them or carry it to them.

ex.en: He went and poured a brandy for Dena and brought it to her.
ex.zh: 他去给德娜倒了杯白兰地并拿给了她。

e.en: To bring something or someone to a place or position means to cause them to come to the place or move into that position.

ex.en: I told you about what brought me here.
ex.zh: 我告诉过你是什么把我引到这里来的。

ex.en: The shock of her husband's arrival brought her to her feet.
ex.zh: 丈夫的到来惊得她不由自主地站了起来。

d: v. 拿来，带来； 使……转入（新的话题）；移动；使处于某种状况；导致，引起；起诉；提供；强迫（自己）做；标价，售价为
【名】 （Bring）（英、瑞典）布林（人名）

e.en: Something that is broad is wide.

ex.en: His shoulders were broad and his waist narrow.
ex.zh: 他肩宽腰细。

ex.en: The hills rise green and sheer above the broad river.
ex.zh: 群山青翠，陡然屹立于宽阔的大河之上。

e.en: A broad smile is one in which your mouth is stretched very wide because you are very pleased or amused. 咧开大嘴的 (笑)

ex.en: He greeted them with a wave and a broad smile.
ex.zh: 他咧嘴笑着挥手和他们打招呼。

e.en: 咧开大嘴地

ex.en: Charles grinned broadly.
ex.zh: 查尔斯咧大嘴笑。

e.en: You use broad to describe something that includes a large number of different things or people.

ex.en: A broad range of issues was discussed.
ex.zh: 广泛的问题得到了讨论。

d: adj. 宽广的，宽阔的；……宽；咧开嘴的；广泛的，普遍的；大致的，概括的；明确的，明显的；粗俗滑稽的；口音重的
n. 对女人的粗俗称呼；宽阔部分
adv. 宽阔地
【名】 （Broad）（英、德）布罗德（人名）

e.en: You use burning to describe something that is extremely hot.

ex.en: ...the burning desert of central Asia.
ex.zh: …中亚地区炙热的沙漠。

e.en: Burning is also an adverb.
火热地

ex.en: He touched the boy's forehead. It was burning hot.
ex.zh: 他摸了摸男孩的前额，热得发烫。

e.en: If you have a burning interest in something or a burning desire to do something, you are extremely interested in it or want to do it very much.

ex.en: I had a burning ambition to become a journalist.
ex.zh: 我有强烈的愿望要成为一名记者。

d: adj. 燃烧的，着火的；强烈的，热切的；炙热的，明亮的；疼痛的，火辣辣的；事关紧要的
adv.  炙热地，火热地
n. 灼热，烧毁
v. 燃烧，消耗；烧坏，烧毁；火辣辣地发痛，发烫（burn 的现在分词）

e.en: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a fire or flame burning there.

ex.en: Fires were burning out of control in the centre of the city.
ex.zh: 火在市中心燃烧着,失去了控制。

ex.en: There was a fire burning in the fireplace.
ex.zh: 壁炉里有火正燃着。

e.en: If something is burning, it is on fire.

ex.en: When I arrived one of the vehicles was still burning.
ex.zh: 我到达时，其中的一辆车还在燃烧。

ex.en: The building housed 1,500 refugees and it burned for hours.
ex.zh: 这栋楼住着1500个难民，它烧了好几个小时。

e.en: 燃烧

ex.en: When we arrived in our village there was a terrible smell of burning.
ex.zh: 我们到达村子的时候，那里有一股难闻的燃烧的味道。

e.en: If you burn something, you destroy or damage it with fire.

ex.en: Protesters set cars on fire and burned a building.
ex.zh: 抗议者们焚烧汽车，烧毁了一栋建筑。

ex.en: Incineration plants should be built to burn household waste.
ex.zh: 应该建焚化厂来焚烧生活垃圾。

d: v. 燃烧，消耗；烧坏，烧毁，烧焦；晒伤，晒黑；火辣辣地发痛，发烫；发光，发亮；激怒；刻录；渴望；迅速移动
n. 灼伤，烧伤，烧痕；肌肉酸痛感；小溪
【名】 （Burn）（英）伯恩（人名）

e.en: To bury something means to put it into a hole in the ground and cover it up with earth.

ex.en: They make the charcoal by burying wood in the ground and then slowly burning it.
ex.zh: 他们制作木炭时要把木头埋进地里，然后让它慢慢燃烧。

ex.en: ...squirrels who bury nuts and seeds.
ex.zh: …将坚果和种子埋起来的松鼠。

e.en: To bury a dead person means to put their body into a grave and cover it with earth.

ex.en: Soldiers helped to bury the dead in large communal graves.
ex.zh: 士兵们协助将死者埋葬在大型公共墓地里。

ex.en: I was horrified that people would think I was dead and bury me alive.
ex.zh: 人们会以为我死了而将我活埋的想法让我极度恐惧。

e.en: If someone says they have buried one of their relatives, they mean that one of their relatives has died. 丧失 (亲人)

ex.en: He had buried his wife some two years before he retired.
ex.zh: 他大约在退休前两年丧妻。

e.en: If you bury something under a large quantity of things, you put it there, often in order to hide it.

ex.en: She buried it under some leaves.
ex.zh: 她把它埋藏在一些树叶下。

d: v. 埋，埋葬（bury 的 ing 形式）；掩藏
n. 埋，埋葬
adj. 埋葬的，用于埋葬的

e.en: A casting is an object or piece of machinery which has been made by pouring a liquid such as hot metal into a container, so that when it hardens it has the required shape. 铸件;

d: n. 角色分配，演员挑选；铸件，铸造物
v. 投射（光，影）；将（视线，目光）投向；浇铸（金属等）（cast 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A ceiling is the horizontal surface that forms the top part or roof inside a room.

ex.en: The rooms were spacious, with tall windows and high ceilings.
ex.zh: 房间很宽敞，且窗户和屋顶都很高。

e.en: A ceiling on something such as prices or wages is an official upper limit that cannot be broken. (价格、工资等的)

ex.en: ...an informal agreement to put a ceiling on salaries.
ex.zh: …一项规定工资上限的非正式协议。

d: n. 天花板，吊顶；上限，最高限度；最高飞行限度，升限

e.en: A celebration is a special enjoyable event that people organize because something pleasant has happened or because it is someone's birthday or anniversary.

ex.en: I can tell you, there was a celebration in our house that night.
ex.zh: 跟你说吧，那天晚上我们在家里搞了个庆祝活动。

e.en: The celebration of something is praise and appreciation which is given to it.

ex.en: This was not a memorial service but a celebration of his life.
ex.zh: 这仪式不是追悼会，而是对他的生平的颂扬。

d: n. 庆典，庆祝活动；庆祝，颂扬；宗教仪式的举行

e.en: If you celebrate an occasion or if you celebrate, you do something enjoyable because of a special occasion or to mark someone's success.

ex.en: I was in a mood to celebrate.
ex.zh: 我很想庆祝一番。

ex.en: Dick celebrated his 60th birthday Monday.
ex.zh: 迪克星期一庆祝了他的60岁生日。

e.en: If an organization or country is celebrating an anniversary, it has existed for that length of time and is doing something special because of it. 庆祝 (周年纪念日)

ex.en: The society is celebrating its tenth anniversary this year.
ex.zh: 该学会今年将举行10周年年庆。

e.en: When priests celebrate Holy Communion or Mass, they officially perform the actions and ceremonies that are involved. 主持 (圣餐或弥撒等宗教仪式)

ex.en: Pope John Paul celebrated mass today in a city in central Poland.
ex.zh: 约翰·保罗教皇今天在位于波兰中心的一个城市主持了弥撒。

d: v. 庆祝，庆贺；赞扬，赞美；主持（宗教仪式）

e.en: A chevron is a V shape. V

ex.en: The chevron or arrow road sign indicates a sharp bend to the left or right.
ex.zh: V形或箭头交通标志表示左方或右方有急转弯。

d: n. V 形线条、V 形图案；提示急弯的 V 形或箭头交通标志；军人、警察制服上表示军衔或警衔的 V 形标志；（Chevron）雪佛龙公司（美国跨国能源公司）；（Chevron）（法语姓氏）谢弗龙
n. 克里斯（男子名）；克莉丝（女子名）

e.en: When people clash, they fight, argue, or disagree with each other. 发生冲突;

ex.en: A group of 400 demonstrators ripped down the front gate and clashed with police.
ex.zh: 400名示威者推倒前面的大前门，与警察发生了冲突。

ex.en: Behind the scenes, Parsons clashed with almost everyone on the show.
ex.zh: 幕后，帕森斯几乎跟每个参与演出的人都产生过矛盾。

e.en: Clash is also a noun.

ex.en: There have been a number of clashes between police in riot gear and demonstrators.
ex.zh: 穿防暴服的警察和示威者之间发生过多次冲突。

e.en: Beliefs, ideas, or qualities that clash with each other are very different from each other and therefore are opposed. (因信仰、观点或质量不同而)

ex.en: Don't make any policy decisions which clash with official company thinking.
ex.zh: 不要做与公司官方理念有分歧的任何政策性决定。

e.en: Clash is also a noun.

ex.en: Inside government, there was a clash of views.
ex.zh: 政府内部有意见分歧。

d: v．
1. 冲突，抵触：指两个或多个事物、观点、意见等相互冲突或抵触。
2. 发生冲突，交锋：指两个或多个人或团体在某个问题上发生冲突或交锋。

e.en: If you cite something, you quote it or mention it, especially as an example or proof of what you are saying.

ex.en: She cites a favourite poem by George Herbert.
ex.zh: 她引用了一首她所喜爱的乔治·赫伯特的诗。

ex.en: Domestic interest rates are often cited as a major factor affecting exchange rates.
ex.zh: 国内利率常常被援引为影响汇率的一个主要因素。

e.en: To cite a person means to officially name them in a legal case. To cite a reason or cause means to state it as the official reason for your case.

ex.en: They cited Alex's refusal to return to the marital home.
ex.zh: 他们援引了亚历克斯拒绝重返婚后住所这一事实为证。

e.en: If someone is cited, they are officially ordered to appear before a court.

ex.en: He is the owner of a restaurant chain that was cited for violations of child labour laws.
ex.zh: 他是那个因违反童工法而被传讯的餐饮连锁店的业主。

e.en: If a judge cites someone, he or she officially names them in a critical way in court.

ex.en: The judge ruled a mistrial and cited the prosecutors for outrageous misconduct.
ex.zh: 法官裁定判决无效并且指控控方有极其不端的行为。

d: v. 引用，援引（cite 的过去式和过去分词）；（法律）被传讯；被指控；因杰出成就等受到表彰
adj. 被引用的，被援引的（常作定语）
adj．共同领导的：指两个或多个人或团体共同担任领导角色。

e.en: Coal is a hard, black substance that is extracted from the ground and burned as fuel.

ex.en: Gas is cheaper than coal.
ex.zh: 煤气比煤便宜。

e.en: Coals are burning pieces of coal.

ex.en: The iron teakettle was hissing splendidly over live coals.
ex.zh: 铁茶壶在熊熊燃烧着的煤块上“嘶嘶”作响。

d: n. 煤；煤炭工业；（尤指燃烧着的）煤块
v. 供煤；采煤，提炼煤
n. 完成，结束；成功前传；（房地产等）完成交易，完成交割

e.en: A concentrated liquid has been increased in strength by having water removed from it.

ex.en: Sweeten dishes sparingly with honey, or concentrated apple or pear juice.
ex.zh: 用少许蜂蜜或浓缩苹果汁或梨汁使菜肴变甜。

e.en: A concentrated activity is directed with great intensity in one place.

ex.en: ...a more concentrated effort to reach out to troubled kids.
ex.zh: …更集中的帮助问题儿童的努力。

d: adj.  集中的；全神贯注的，全力以赴的；浓缩的
v. 集中注意力，聚精会神；使集中，聚集；（使）浓缩（concentrate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Concentration on something involves giving all your attention to it.

ex.en: Neal kept interrupting, breaking my concentration.
ex.zh: 尼尔不断打扰，打断我的注意力。

e.en: A concentration of something is a large amount of it or large numbers of it in a small area.

ex.en: The area has one of the world's greatest concentrations of wildlife.
ex.zh: 该地区有世界上野生生物最集中的区域之一。

e.en: The concentration of a substance is the proportion of essential ingredients or substances in it.

ex.en: pH is a measure of the concentration of free hydrogen atoms in a solution.
ex.zh: pH值是溶液中游离氢原子浓度的计量单位。

d: n. concentration 的复数：浓度，含量；集中，聚集；（大学）专业方向，专修领域；关注点；（土壤）浓聚物

e.en: When you conduct an activity or task, you organize it and do it.

ex.en: I decided to conduct an experiment.
ex.zh: 我决定做一项实验。

e.en: If you conduct yourself in a particular way, you behave in that way. (以某种方式)

ex.en: The way he conducts himself reflects on the family.
ex.zh: 他的行为方式折射出他的家庭。

e.en: When someone conducts an orchestra or choir, they stand in front of it and direct its performance. 指挥 (交响乐、合唱等)

ex.en: Dennis had recently begun a successful career conducting opera.
ex.zh: 丹尼斯最近成功地开始了指挥歌剧的生涯。

ex.en: Solti continued to conduct here and abroad.
ex.zh: 佐尔蒂继续在国内外指挥。

e.en: If something conducts heat or electricity, it allows heat or electricity to pass through it or along it. 传导 (热、电)

ex.en: Water conducts heat faster than air.
ex.zh: 水比空气导热快。

d: v. 实施，进行；指挥；带领，引导；举止，表现；传导
n. 行为，举止；经营方式，管理方法

e.en: A contingent of police, soldiers, or military vehicles is a group of them. (警察、士兵、军车)

ex.en: Nigeria provided a large contingent of troops to the West African Peacekeeping Force.
ex.zh: 尼日利亚向西非维和部队派出了一大批部队。

e.en: A contingent is a group of people representing a country or organization at a meeting or other event.

ex.en: The American contingent will stay overnight in London.
ex.zh: 美国代表团将在伦敦留宿。

d: n. （军队的）分遣队；代表团
adj. 附带的，依情况而定的；偶然（发生）的，可能的

e.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. You can also say that people convene or that a meeting convenes. 召集 (会议);

ex.en: Last August he convened a meeting of his closest advisers at Camp David.
ex.zh: 去年8月份，他在戴维营召集他最亲近的顾问开了一次会。

d: v. 召集，召开（会议）；集合，聚集（开会）（convene 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

ex.en: An intense debate is going on within the Israeli government.
ex.zh: 一场激烈的争论正在以色列政府内部进行。

ex.en: There has been a lot of debate among scholars about this.
ex.zh: 在学者中有很多关于此问题的辩论。

e.en: A debate is a formal discussion, for example, in a parliament or institution, in which people express different opinions about a particular subject and then vote on it. (议会投票前的)

ex.en: He is expected to force a debate in Congress on his immigration reform.
ex.zh: 他预期会推动一个关于他的移民改革的正式讨论。

e.en: If people debate a topic, they discuss it fairly formally, putting forward different views. You can also say that one person debates a topic with another person.

ex.en: The United Nations Security Council will debate the issue today.
ex.zh: 联合国安理会今天将辩论该问题。

ex.en: Scientists were debating whether an asteroid was about to hit the Earth.
ex.zh: 科学家们在争论一颗小行星是否要撞上地球。

e.en: If you debate whether to do something or what to do, you think or talk about possible courses of action before deciding exactly what you are going to do.

ex.en: Taggart debated whether to have yet another double vodka.
ex.zh: 塔格特考虑着是否要再来一杯双份伏特加。

d: n. 讨论，辩论
v. 反复思考，斟酌；讨论，辩论

e.en: If something is deemed to have a particular quality or to do a particular thing, it is considered to have that quality or do that thing. 认为;

ex.en: French and German were deemed essential.
ex.zh: 法语和德语被认为是必需的。

ex.en: He says he would support the use of force if the UN deemed it necessary.
ex.zh: 他说如果联合国认为有必要，他就支持动用武力。

d: v. 认为，视为，相信（deem 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that is definitive provides a firm conclusion that cannot be questioned.

ex.en: No one has come up with a definitive answer as to why this should be so.
ex.zh: 至于为什么该这样，还没有人给出明确的答复。

e.en: 确定地

ex.en: Law enforcement officials had definitively identified Blanco as a potential suspect.
ex.zh: 执法官员明确认为布兰科是个可能的嫌疑犯。

e.en: A definitive book or performance is thought to be the best of its kind that has ever been done or that will ever be done.

ex.en: ...Ian Macdonald's definitive book on The Beatles.
ex.zh: …伊恩·麦克唐纳写的有关甲壳虫乐队的最权威的书。

d: adj. 最终的，确定的；最好的，最权威的；（邮票）普通标准型的
n. 普通邮票；限定词

e.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them. (权力、责任)

ex.en: ...the need to decentralize and devolve power to regional governments.
ex.zh: …把权力分散下放到地方政府的需要。

ex.en: The best companies are those that devolve responsibility as far as they can.
ex.zh: 最好的公司是那些尽可能把责任下放的公司。

d: v. devolve 的过去式和过去分词：把（权力、责任等）移交、下放给下级或地方机构，常与 to 连用；（正式）（财产、权利等）依法转移给他人或继承人，常与 to/upon 连用；（正式）逐步恶化、演变为（较差局面），常与 into 连用。
adj. 被移交的，下放的（指权力、职责等已下放给地方或下级机构）。
n. 二氧化物

e.en: Diplomatic means relating to diplomacy and diplomats.

ex.en: ...before the two countries resume full diplomatic relations.
ex.zh: …在两国全面恢复外交关系之前。

e.en: 外交地

ex.en: ...a growing sense of doubt that the conflict can be resolved diplomatically.
ex.zh: …对该冲突能用外交手段得以解决的不断增加的怀疑。

e.en: Someone who is diplomatic is careful to say or do things without offending people.

ex.en: She is very direct. I tend to be more diplomatic, I suppose.
ex.zh: 她很直率。我觉得我更圆通些。

e.en: 圆通得体地

ex.en: "I really like their sound, although I'm not crazy about their lyrics," he says, diplomatically.
ex.zh: “我非常喜欢他们的声音，但不太喜欢他们的歌词，”他很圆滑地说。

d: adj. 外交的，从事外交的；有手腕的，灵活变通的；（版本，副本）仿真的，和原件完全一致的

e.en: If something distracts you or your attention from something, it takes your attention away from it. 分散 (注意力);

ex.en: Tom admits that playing video games sometimes distracts him from his homework.
ex.zh: 汤姆承认玩电子游戏有时让他做家庭作业时分心。

ex.en: Don't let yourself be distracted by fashionable theories.
ex.zh: 别让自己被新潮的理论给分心了。

d: v. 使分心，使转移注意力；使困惑，使迷惑

e.en: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them. 文件;

ex.en: She produces legal documents for a downtown Seattle law firm.
ex.zh: 她为西雅图市区的一家法律事务所撰写法律文件。

e.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example, a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

ex.en: When you are finished typing, remember to save your document.
ex.zh: 输入完毕后，要记着保存文档。

e.en: If you document something, you make a detailed record of it in writing or on film or tape.

ex.en: He wrote a book documenting his prison experiences.
ex.zh: 他写了一本书，记录他的牢狱经历。

d: n. 文件，公文，文献；证件，单据；（计算机）文件，文档
v. 记录，记载（详情）

e.en: A document is one or more official pieces of paper with writing on them. 文件;

ex.en: She produces legal documents for a downtown Seattle law firm.
ex.zh: 她为西雅图市区的一家法律事务所撰写法律文件。

e.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example, a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

ex.en: When you are finished typing, remember to save your document.
ex.zh: 输入完毕后，要记着保存文档。

e.en: If you document something, you make a detailed record of it in writing or on film or tape.

ex.en: He wrote a book documenting his prison experiences.
ex.zh: 他写了一本书，记录他的牢狱经历。

d: n. 文件，公文，文献；证件，单据（document 的复数）
v. 记录，记载（详情）；用文献证明，为……提供文献依据（document 的第三人称单数）

e.en: An editor is the person who is in charge of a newspaper or magazine and who decides what will be published in each edition of it.

ex.en: Her father was the former editor of the Saturday Review.
ex.zh: 她的父亲是《星期六评论》的前任主编。

e.en: An editor is a journalist who is responsible for a particular section of a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: Mike later became the sports editor for The Beacon.
ex.zh: 迈克后来成为《烽火》的体育栏目编辑。

e.en: An editor is a person who checks and corrects texts before they are published.

ex.en: Your role as editor is important, for you can look at a piece of writing objectively.
ex.zh: 你作为编辑的角色是重要的，因为你可以客观地看一篇文字。

e.en: An editor is a radio or television journalist who reports on a particular type of news.

ex.en: ...our economics editor, Tom Goldberg.
ex.zh: …我们的经济节目记者，汤姆·戈德堡。

d: n. 编辑（editor 的复数形式）；编辑器（editor 的复数形式，指用于创建、修改文本或数据的计算机程序）；剪辑师（editor 的复数形式，指从事电影、电视或广播节目剪辑的人员）

e.en: Someone who is educated has a high standard of learning.

ex.en: The new CEO is an educated, amiable, and decent man.
ex.zh: 新的首席执行官是一位受过良好教育、亲切、正派的人。

d: adj. 受过教育的；有教养的；有根据的（用于 educated guess，指基于知识或经验而非凭空猜测）
v. （在学校）教育，培养；教导，训练；使（孩子）受学校教育（educate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: You use effectively with a statement or opinion to indicate that it is not accurate in every detail, but that you feel it is a reasonable description or summary of a particular situation.

ex.en: The region was effectively independent.
ex.zh: 该地区实际上是独立的。

d: adv. 有效地；实际上

e.en: Someone's ego is their sense of their own worth. For example, if someone has a large ego, they think they are very important and valuable.

ex.en: He had a massive ego, never would he admit he was wrong.
ex.zh: 他有极强的自我价值感，从来不会承认他错了。

d: n. 自我（ego 的复数）
n. 引出，诱出，启发；抽出

e.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity to do it.

ex.en: The new test should enable doctors to detect the disease early.
ex.zh: 新的检验使医生能在早期发现该种疾病。

e.en: To enable something to happen means to make it possible for it to happen.

ex.en: The hot sun enables the grapes to reach optimum ripeness.
ex.zh: 炙热的阳光使葡萄能达到最佳成熟状态。

e.en: To enable someone to do something means to give them permission or the right to do it.

ex.en: ...legislation which enables young people to do a form of alternative service.
ex.zh: …允许年轻人通过一种替代性服务来服刑的立法。

d: v. 使能够，使可能；激活，启动；准许，授权

e.en: Eventually means in the end, especially after a lot of delays, problems, or arguments.

ex.en: Eventually, the army caught up with him in Latvia.
ex.zh: 部队终于在拉脱维亚追上了他。

e.en: Eventually means at the end of a situation or process or as the final result of it.

ex.en: Eventually your child will leave home to lead her own life as a fully independent adult.
ex.zh: 你的孩子最终会离开家，作为完全独立的成年人过她自己的日子。

d: adv. 最终，结果

e.en: An exception is a particular thing, person, or situation that is not included in a general statement, judgment, or rule.

ex.en: Few guitarists can sing as well as they can play; Eddie, however, is an exception.
ex.zh: 很少有吉他手唱歌能唱得跟弹得一样好，而艾迪是个例外。

ex.en: The law makes no exceptions.
ex.zh: 法律不搞例外。

e.en: If you make a general statement, and then say that something or someone is no exception, you are emphasizing that they are included in that statement. 不例外;

ex.en: Marketing is applied to everything these days, and books are no exception.
ex.zh: 现在市场营销用于任何事物，图书也不例外。

e.en: If you take exception to something, you feel offended or annoyed by it, usually with the result that you complain about it. 厌恶;

ex.en: He also took exception to having been spied on.
ex.zh: 他也厌恶被暗中监视。

e.en: You use with the exception of to introduce a thing or person that is not included in a general statement that you are making.

ex.en: Yesterday was a day off for everybody, with the exception of Lorenzo.
ex.zh: 昨天每个人休一天假，洛伦佐除外。

d: n. 例外，例外的人、事物或情况（exception 的复数形式）；（法律、合同、保险等）免责条款，除外责任；（计算机）异常

e.en: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

ex.en: He thought that if he couldn't see something, it didn't exist.
ex.zh: 他认为如果他看不见某种东西，它就不存在。

ex.en: Research opportunities exist in a wide range of areas.
ex.zh: 研究机会存在于广泛的领域中。

e.en: To exist means to live, especially under difficult conditions or with very little food or money. (尤指在困境中)

ex.en: I was barely existing.
ex.zh: 我几乎活不下去了。

ex.en: Some people exist on melons or coconuts for weeks at a time.
ex.zh: 有些人一度数周靠各种瓜与椰子生存。

d: v. exist 的过去式和过去分词：存在，有；生存，过活（尤指在困境中，常与 on 连用）

e.en: If something exists, it is present in the world as a real thing.

ex.en: He thought that if he couldn't see something, it didn't exist.
ex.zh: 他认为如果他看不见某种东西，它就不存在。

ex.en: Research opportunities exist in a wide range of areas.
ex.zh: 研究机会存在于广泛的领域中。

e.en: To exist means to live, especially under difficult conditions or with very little food or money. (尤指在困境中)

ex.en: I was barely existing.
ex.zh: 我几乎活不下去了。

ex.en: Some people exist on melons or coconuts for weeks at a time.
ex.zh: 有些人一度数周靠各种瓜与椰子生存。

d: n. 存在量词（exist 的复数）
v. 存在；出现；活着（exist 的三单形式）

e.en: An expert is a person who is very skilled at doing something or who knows a lot about a particular subject. 专家;

ex.en: ...a yoga expert.
ex.zh: …一位瑜伽专家。

e.en: Someone who is expert at doing something is very skilled at it.

ex.en: The Japanese are expert at lowering manufacturing costs.
ex.zh: 日本人在降低生产成本方面很在行。

e.en: 在行地

ex.en: Shopkeepers expertly rolled spices up in bay leaves.
ex.zh: 店主在行地把各种香料卷进了月桂叶中。

e.en: If you say that someone has expert hands or an expert eye, you mean that they are very skilful or experienced in using their hands or eyes for a particular purpose.

ex.en: Harvey cured the pain with his own expert hands.
ex.zh: 哈维用他那行家之手治愈了那病痛。

d: n. 专家，能手，权威
adj. 专业的，熟练的
v. 当专家
【名】 （Expert）（法、印、俄、罗、巴、荷）埃克斯佩（人名）

e.en: Feet is the plural of foot. (foot)

d: n. 脚（foot 的复数形式）；尺，英尺；音步（诗律用语）

e.en: A field is an area of grass, for example, in a park or on a farm. A field is also an area of land on which a crop is grown. 草地;

ex.en: ...a field of wheat.
ex.zh: …一片麦田。

e.en: A sports field is an area of grass where sports are played.
A field is an area of land or sea bed under which large amounts of a particular mineral have been found.

ex.en: ...an extensive natural gas field in Alaska.
ex.zh: …阿拉斯加的一个巨大的天然气田。

e.en: A magnetic, gravitational, or electric field is the area in which that particular force is strong enough to have an effect.

ex.en: Some people are worried that electromagnetic fields from electric power lines could increase the risk of cancer.
ex.zh: 一些人担心电源线的电磁场可能增加患癌症的风险。

d: n. 田地，田野；专业，领域；现场，实地；体育场；全体参赛者；矿场，油田；战场；视野；（物理）场；信息栏，字段；外场员，防守队；盾面，底
v. 组建，派出；担任守方；接（球），守（球）；处理，应付（问题或电话）
adj. 实地的，野外的；（军事装备）轻便机动的，战役用的；（比赛）田赛的
【名】 （Field）（英、法、德、葡）菲尔德（人名）

e.en: When you finish doing or dealing with something, you do or deal with the last part of it, so that there is no more for you to do or deal with.

ex.en: As soon as he'd finished eating, he excused himself.
ex.zh: 他一吃完就借口离开了。

ex.en: Mr. Gould was given a standing ovation and loud cheers when he finished his speech.
ex.zh: 古尔德先生结束他的演讲时观众起立为他鼓掌并大声欢呼。

e.en: Finish up means the same as .

ex.en: We waited a few minutes outside his office while he finished up his meeting.
ex.zh: 我们在他办公室外面等了几分钟，这时他结束了他的会议。

e.en: When you finish something that you are making or producing, you reach the end of making or producing it, so that it is complete.

ex.en: The consultants had been working to finish a report this week.
ex.zh: 顾问们一直在争取于本周完成一份报告。

e.en: Finish off and finish up mean the same as .

ex.en: Now she is busy finishing off a biography of Queen Caroline.
ex.zh: 现在她正忙于完成卡罗琳女王的传记。

d: v. 完成，做好；（使）结束；消耗尽（所剩之物）；（比赛中）获得（名次）；（英式足球用语）进球；对（物件）做最后加工；杀死，歼灭；使精疲力竭；为（少女）进入上流社会做好准备；使精疲力竭
n. 结尾，结局；（赛跑、比赛的）终点；最后精细加工；饰面，饰面材料；（葡萄酒或啤酒的）余味

e.en: If a liquid, gas, or electrical current flows somewhere, it moves there steadily and continuously.

ex.en: A stream flowed gently down into the valley.
ex.zh: 一条小溪缓缓地流进山谷。

ex.en: The current flows into electric motors that drive the wheels.
ex.zh: 电流流进电机，驱动轮子。

e.en: Flow is also a noun.

ex.en: It works only in the veins, where the blood flow is slower.
ex.zh: 它只在血液流动较缓的静脉中起作用。

e.en: If a number of people or things flow from one place to another, they move there steadily in large groups, usually without stopping. (大量人或物)

ex.en: Large numbers of refugees continue to flow from the troubled region into the no-man's land.
ex.zh: 大批的难民持续从骚乱地区涌进无人区。

e.en: Flow is also a noun.

ex.en: She watched the frantic flow of cars and buses along the street.
ex.zh: 她注视着街道上川流不息的小车和巴士。

d: v. 流动，流淌；（人，物）涌向，涌进；（车辆）畅通无阻；持续抵达，持续供应；（信息）传播，（资金）流通；飘垂，飘拂；强烈感到；（说话或思想）流畅；引发，来自；充满，满是；畅饮；涨潮；永久性变形；来月经
n. 流，流动；持续生产，不断供应；车流，人流；（语言、思路等的）连贯；流速，流率；流动物；流量；涨潮；湿地，沼泽；形变；月经；大量
【名】 （Flow）（美）弗洛（人名）

e.en: Gambling is the act or activity of betting money, for example in card games or on horse racing.

ex.en: Gambling is a form of entertainment.
ex.zh: 赌博是一种娱乐形式。

d: n. 赌博；投机，冒险
v. 赌博；投机，冒险（gamble 的现在分词）
【名】 （Gambling）（英）甘布林（人名）

e.en: Gaming means the same as .

ex.en: ...offences connected with vice, gaming, and drugs.
ex.zh: …与恶行、赌博、吸毒相关的犯罪行为。

d: n. 游戏活动，尤指电子（视频或电脑）游戏；（正式或法律用语）赌博、赌胜负
v. game 的现在分词：玩视频（或电视、电脑）游戏；赌博；（尤指为谋取利益）操纵规则或制度

e.en: A board is a flat, thin, rectangular piece of wood or plastic which is used for a particular purpose. (木头的或塑料的)

ex.en: ...a cutting board.
ex.zh: …一块砧板。

e.en: A board is a square piece of wood or stiff cardboard that you use for playing games such as chess. (棋)

ex.en: ...a chequers board.
ex.zh: …一个跳棋盘。

e.en: You can refer to a blackboard or a bulletin board as a board. 黑板;

ex.en: He wrote a few more notes on the board.
ex.zh: 他在黑板上多写了几条笔记。

e.en: Boards are long flat pieces of wood which are used, for example, to make floors or walls. (建筑用的)

ex.en: The floor was draughty bare boards.
ex.zh: 地板是有缝隙的裸板。

d: n. 板，木板；黑板，告示牌；董事会，理事会；膳食，伙食，膳食费用；局；舞台；（冰球场周围的）界墙；（美国大学的）入学考试
v.  登上（火车、轮船或飞机）；让乘客登机（或上船等）；寄宿；（在学校）住校；将（宠物）暂时寄养在他处；用木板覆盖
【名】 （Board）（英、西）博德（人名）

e.en: If you say the betting is that something will happen or is true, you are suggesting that it is very likely to happen or to be true.

ex.en: The betting is that the experience will make Japan more competitive still.
ex.zh: 这场经历很可能会让日本更具竞争力。

d: n. 打赌，赌博，下注；（the betting）某事发生的可能性；赛马赌注登记人提供的投注赔率
v. 打赌，赌博，下注；（非正式）敢说，断言（bet 的现在分词）
adj. 好赌的，爱打赌的（多作定语）

e.en: relating to, concerned with, or used in sports (关于)运动的;

ex.en: sports equipment

d: adj. 体育运动的，与运动有关的
n. 运动会；（某项）体育运动（sport 的复数）
v. （引人注目地）穿戴，展示；嬉戏，玩耍（sport 的第三人称单数）
n. 美国路易斯安那州

e.en: A user is a person or thing that uses something such as a place, facility, product, or machine. 使用者;

ex.en: Beach users have complained that the bikes are noisy.
ex.zh: 去海滩的人已在抱怨那些自行车太吵。

ex.en: ...a regular user of the subway.
ex.zh: …一个定期乘坐地铁的人。

d: n. 使用者；受限用户（user 的复数）

e.en: An amendment is a section that is added to a law or rule in order to change it.

ex.en: ...an amendment to the defence bill.
ex.zh: …对辩护法案的一条修正案。

e.en: An amendment is a change that is made to a piece of writing.

d: n. 修正，修订之处；美国宪法修正案（Amendment）；（土壤结构或肥力的）改善；（对文件或计划的）修改

e.en: A tool is any instrument or simple piece of equipment that you hold in your hands and use to do a particular kind of work. For example, spades, hammers, and knives are all tools.

ex.en: I find the best tool for the purpose is a pair of shears.
ex.zh: 我发现达到这一目的的最好工具是一把大剪刀。

e.en: You can refer to anything that you use for a particular purpose as a particular type of tool.

ex.en: Writing is a good tool for expressing feelings.
ex.zh: 写作是表达情感的一种好方法。

d: n. 工具（tool 的复数形式）；方法，手段（比喻用法）；工具菜单或工具栏选项（软件界面，常写作 Tools）
v. 用工具加工；给……装配工具（tool 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not. 对…下注;

ex.en: Jockeys are forbidden to bet on the outcome of races.
ex.zh: 职业赛马骑师们被禁止对比赛结果下注。
