ex.en: I bet $20 on a horse called Premonition.
ex.zh: 我在那匹名叫“预言”的赛马身上下了$20的赌注。

e.en: Bet is also a noun.

ex.en: Do you always have a bet on the Kentucky Derby?
ex.zh: 你总是在肯塔基赛马大会上赌马吗？

e.en: 赌注

ex.en: ...his thousand-dollar fine for illegal betting.
ex.zh: …他因非法赌博而受的千元罚款。

e.en: A bet is a sum of money which you give to someone when you bet.

ex.en: You can put a bet on almost anything these days.
ex.zh: 如今，你几乎可以就任何事下赌注。

d: v. 打赌，赌博；敢肯定
n. 下注；赌金；预计，猜想；有可能成功的人选（或备选行动）
abbr. 在……之间（between）
【名】 （Bet）（美）贝特（人名）

e.en: If you propose something such as a plan or an idea, you suggest it for people to think about and decide upon.

ex.en: Hamilton proposed a change in the traditional debating format.
ex.zh: 汉密尔顿建议对传统的辩论形式作一个改变。

e.en: If you propose to do something, you intend to do it.

ex.en: It's still far from clear what action the government proposes to take over the affair.
ex.zh: 尚不清楚政府打算采取什么行动接手这件事。

e.en: If you propose a motion for debate, or a candidate for election, you begin the debate or the election procedure by formally stating your support for that motion or candidate. 提出;

ex.en: He has proposed a resolution limiting the role of U.S. troops.
ex.zh: 他提出了一项限制美军作用的决议。

e.en: If you propose to someone, or propose marriage to them, you ask them to marry you.

ex.en: He proposed to his girlfriend over a public-address system.
ex.zh: 他在有线广播系统上向女友求婚。

d: adj. 被提议的，建议的，拟议中的
v. 提议，建议；计划，打算；求婚（propose 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A reporter is someone who writes news articles or who broadcasts news reports.

ex.en: ...a TV reporter.
ex.zh: …一名电视台记者。

d: n. 记者，通讯员

e.en: If you opt for something, or opt to do something, you choose it or decide to do it in preference to anything else.

ex.en: Depending on your circumstances you can opt for one method or the other.
ex.zh: 根据自己的情况，你可以选择这种或那种方法。

d: v. 选择，做出抉择（opt 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you have an account with a bank or a similar organization, you have an arrangement to leave your money there and take some out when you need it.

ex.en: Some banks make it difficult to open an account.
ex.zh: 有些银行使开一个账户困难重重。

e.en: In business, a regular customer of a company can be referred to as an account, especially when the customer is another company.

ex.en: All three Internet agencies boast they've won major accounts.
ex.zh: 所有的三家网络代理公司都夸口说他们已赢得了大客户。

e.en: Accounts are detailed records of all the money that a person or business receives and spends.

ex.en: He kept detailed accounts.
ex.zh: 他保存了详细的账目。

e.en: An account is a written or spoken report of something that has happened.

ex.en: He gave a detailed account of what happened on the fateful night.
ex.zh: 他对那个决定命运的夜晚所发生的事情做了一个详细的报道。

d: n. 账目，账簿，会计账簿（account 的复数）；银行账户，户头；账号，用户账户；叙述，报道，描述；商业客户，客户关系
v. 把…归因于，解释，说明（用于 accounts for）；占（比例），构成（用于 accounts for）；以为，认为，把…视为（account 的第三人称单数）
n. （Kalani）人名；（阿拉伯）盖拉尼；（芬）卡拉尼

e.en: application program

d: n. 应用程序，应用软件；应用服务
n．下注者，赌徒：在赛事或游戏中投注的人。

e.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

ex.en: He has also had managerial experience on every level.
ex.zh: 他还具备各层次的管理经验。

e.en: Experience is used to refer to the past events, knowledge, and feelings that make up someone's life or character.

ex.en: I should not be in any danger here, but experience has taught me caution.
ex.zh: 我在这里应该没有任何危险，但阅历已教会我谨慎。

e.en: An experience is something that you do or that happens to you, especially something important that affects you.

ex.en: His only experience of gardening so far proved immensely satisfying.
ex.zh: 他仅有的园艺经历到目前为止非常令人满意。

e.en: If you experience a particular situation, you are in that situation or it happens to you.

ex.en: We had never experienced this kind of holiday before and had no idea what to expect.
ex.zh: 我们以前从未经历过这种假期，不知道有什么可期待的。

d: n. 经历，往事；经验，阅历；传统
v. 经历，遭遇；体会到，感受到

e.en: A gambler is someone who gambles regularly, for example in card games or on horse racing.

ex.en: There was a fellow in that casino tonight who's a very heavy gambler.
ex.zh: 今晚那家赌场有个家伙是个嗜赌成性的赌棍。

e.en: If you describe someone as a gambler, you mean that they are ready to take risks in order to gain advantages or success.

ex.en: He had never been afraid of failure: he was a gambler, ready to go off somewhere else and start all over again.
ex.zh: 他从不害怕失败：他是个冒险家，随时准备去别的地方重新开始。

d: n. 赌徒；投机者（gambler 的复数）

e.en: Information about someone or something consists of facts about them. 消息;

ex.en: Pat refused to give her any information about Sarah.
ex.zh: 帕特拒绝向她提供任何有关萨拉的消息。

ex.en: Each centre would provide information on technology and training.
ex.zh: 每个中心都将提供有关技术与培训的资料。

e.en: Information consists of the facts and figures that are stored and used by a computer program. (电脑中储存和使用的)

ex.en: Pictures are scanned into a form of digital information that computers can recognize.
ex.zh: 图片被扫描成一种计算机能识别的数字化资料。

e.en: Information is a service that you can telephone to find out someone's telephone number.

ex.en: He called information, and they gave him the number.
ex.zh: 他打电话给信息台，他们便给了他电话号码。

d: n. 消息，资料，情报；（计算机程序储存和使用的）数据，信息；问讯处，信息台；（向治安法院提起的）控告，起诉；知识
赫伯特（人名）

e.en: Intelligence is the quality of being intelligent or clever.

ex.en: She's a woman of exceptional intelligence.
ex.zh: 她是个格外聪明的女人。

e.en: Intelligence is the ability to think, reason, and understand instead of doing things automatically or by instinct.

ex.en: Nerve cells, after all, do not have intelligence of their own.
ex.zh: 神经元本身毕竟不具备智能。

e.en: Intelligence is information that is gathered by the government or the army about their country's enemies and their activities.

ex.en: Why was military intelligence so lacking?
ex.zh: 为什么军事情报如此缺乏？

d: n. 智力，才智；智能；情报，谍报；情报机构

e.en: A lawmaker is someone such as a politician who is responsible for proposing and passing new laws.

d: n. 立法者，议员（lawmaker 的复数）

e.en: A limit is the greatest amount, extent, or degree of something that is possible.

ex.en: Her love for him was being tested to its limits.
ex.zh: 她对他的爱正在考验着极限。

ex.en: There is no limit to how much fresh fruit you can eat in a day.
ex.zh: 你一天内能吃多少新鲜水果并无上限。

e.en: A limit of a particular kind is the largest or smallest amount of something such as time or money that is allowed because of a rule, law, or decision.

ex.en: The three month time limit will be up in mid-June.
ex.zh: 3个月的时间限制将于6月中旬到期。

e.en: The limit of an area is its boundary or edge.

ex.en: ...the city limits of Baghdad.
ex.zh: …巴格达的城市边界。

e.en: The limits of a situation are the facts involved in it which make only some actions or results possible.

ex.en: She has to work within the limits of a fairly tight budget.
ex.zh: 她不得不在一个相当紧张的预算范围内工作。

d: n. 限度，限制；极限，限量；（区域的）界限，边界；（法律允许的机动车驾驶员血液的）最高酒精浓度；（可能行动或结果的）范围
v. 限制，限定；制约（某人的发展等）；减少

e.en: unprofitable; failing 无利可图的;

ex.en: the business was a losing concern

d: n. 失败，失利；损失，丧失
adj. 输的，失败的；亏损的；导致失败的
v. 失去；损失（lose 的 ing 形式）；错过；输掉

e.en: A number is a word such as "two," "nine," or "twelve," or a symbol such as 1, 3, or 47. You use numbers to say how many things you are referring to or where something comes in a series. 数字;

ex.en: No, I don't know the room number.
ex.zh: 不，我不知道房间号。

ex.en: Stan Laurel was born at number 3, Argyll Street.
ex.zh: 斯坦·劳雷尔出生于阿盖尔街3号。

e.en: You use number with words such as "large" or "small" to say approximately how many things or people there are.

ex.en: Quite a considerable number of interviews are going on.
ex.zh: 许许多多的面试正在进行。

ex.en: I have had an enormous number of letters from single parents.
ex.zh: 我收到了大量单亲家长的来信。

e.en: If there are a number of things or people, there are several of them. If there are any number of things or people, there is a large quantity of them. 几个;

ex.en: I seem to remember that Sam told a number of lies.
ex.zh: 我记得好像萨姆撒过一些谎。

e.en: You can refer to someone's or something's position in a list of the most successful or most popular of a particular type of thing as, for example, number one or number two. (排名)

ex.en: Martin now faces the world number one, Jansher Khan of Pakistan.
ex.zh: 马丁现在面对的是世界头号选手，巴基斯坦的詹舍尔汉。

ex.en: Before you knew it, the single was at number 90 in the U.S. singles charts.
ex.zh: 转眼间这张单曲唱片在美国单曲唱片排行榜上排第90位了。

d: n. 数字；编号，序数；电话号码；总量，数量；大量（numbers）；一群人；（杂志的）期，号；（演出中的）一首歌，一段舞蹈；有吸引力的人（或事物）；数，单复数；历史数据（numbers）；数字彩票（numbers）；钱数（numbers）；具有……特征的人；常说的事
v. 标号，编号；总计；包括，列入（某类）；计算，数
n. 俄亥俄州（美国中北部一州）；俄亥俄河（美国东部河流，源出宾夕法尼亚州西部，流入密西西比河）

e.en: An operation is a highly organized activity that involves many people doing different things.

ex.en: The rescue operation began on Friday afternoon.
ex.zh: 营救行动星期五下午展开。

ex.en: The soldiers were engaged in a military operation close to the Ugandan border.
ex.zh: 士兵们在靠近乌干达边界的地区开展军事行动。

e.en: A business or company can be referred to as an operation.

ex.en: Thorn's electronics operation employs around 5,000 people.
ex.zh: 索恩的电子公司雇佣了大约五千名员工。

e.en: When a patient has an operation, a surgeon cuts open their body in order to remove, replace, or repair a diseased or damaged part.

ex.en: Charles was at the clinic recovering from an operation on his arm.
ex.zh: 查尔斯在诊所，进行手臂的术后恢复。

e.en: If a system is in operation, it is being used.

ex.en: ...the free banking system that has been in operation since the early eighties.
ex.zh: …从80年代初就开始实施的自由银行制度。

d: n. 有组织的行动，活动；运营，运作，业务操作（operation 的复数）；公司，企业，业务单位；（医学）手术；（数学、计算机）运算，操作；（金融）交易操作，证券交易业务

e.en: If you are given promotion or a promotion in your job, you are given a more important job or rank in the organization that you work for.

ex.en: Consider changing jobs or trying for promotion.
ex.zh: 考虑换工作或者争取晋升。

e.en: A promotion is an attempt to make a product or event popular or successful, especially by advertising. 促销;

ex.en: Advertising and promotion are what American business does best.
ex.zh: 打广告和促销是美国企业做得最好的事情。

d: n. 促销，推广活动；升职，晋升（promotion 复数）

e.en: If you raise something, you move it so that it is in a higher position.

ex.en: He raised his hand to wave.
ex.zh: 他举起手来挥动。

ex.en: Milton raised the glass to his lips.
ex.zh: 米尔顿举起杯子放到嘴唇边。

e.en: If you raise a flag, you display it by moving it up a pole or into a high place where it can be seen.

ex.en: They had raised the white flag in surrender.
ex.zh: 他们已经升起白旗投降。

e.en: If you raise yourself, you lift your body so that you are standing up straight, or so that you are no longer lying flat. 站立;

ex.en: He raised himself into a sitting position.
ex.zh: 他起身坐了起来。

e.en: If you raise the rate or level of something, you increase it.

ex.en: The Federal Reserve Board is expected to raise interest rates.
ex.zh: 联邦储备委员会预计将增加利率。

d: adj. （地方）抬高的，凸起的；（身体部位）抬起的；（温度、声音、力气等）升高的，提高的；浮雕的
v. 举起，使升高；提高，增加；筹集，募集（raise 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Rules are instructions that tell you what you are allowed to do and what you are not allowed to do.

ex.en: ...a thirty-two-page pamphlet explaining the rules of basketball.
ex.zh: …一本说明篮球规则的32页的小册子。

e.en: A rule is a statement telling people what they should do in order to achieve success or a benefit of some kind. 原则;

ex.en: An important rule is to drink plenty of water during any flight.
ex.zh: 一条重要的原则是在任何一次飞行中都要喝大量的水。

e.en: The rules of something such as a language or a science are statements that describe the way that things usually happen in a particular situation. 规律;

ex.en: ...according to the rules of quantum theory.
ex.zh: …根据量子论的法则。

e.en: If something is the rule, it is the normal state of affairs. 常规;

ex.en: However, for many Americans today, weekend work has unfortunately become the rule rather than the exception.
ex.zh: 然而，如今对许多美国人而言，周末工作已不幸成为惯例而不是特例。

d: n. 规章，条例；（语言、科学等的）规则，法则；行事准则，指导方针；常规，惯常做法；统治，管辖；尺，直尺；铅线印出的线，破折号； 澳大利亚式橄榄球规则（两队各18人参赛）
v. 统治，管辖；支配，控制；占首要地位；（尤指对法律问题）判定，裁定；（用尺等）划（线）； 好极了，非常棒；（行星）对（黄道十二宫图的宫，房子，生活等）有影响；（价格或贸易商品的价格）普遍处于某一水平（或坚挺趋势）
【名】 （Rule）（西）鲁莱（人名）

e.en: A story is a description of imaginary people and events, which is written or told in order to entertain. (虚构的)

ex.en: The second story in the book is titled "The Scholar."
ex.zh: 这本书中的第2个故事标题为《学者》。

ex.en: I shall tell you a story about four little rabbits.
ex.zh: 我将给你讲个关于4只小兔子的故事。

e.en: A story is a description of an event or something that happened to someone, especially a spoken description of it. (尤指口头的)

ex.en: The parents all shared interesting stories about their children.
ex.zh: 那些家长们都会互相讲起有关自己孩子的趣事。

e.en: The story of something is a description of all the important things that have happened to it since it began.

ex.en: ...the story of the women's movement.
ex.zh: …妇女运动的史话。

e.en: If someone invents a story, they give a false explanation or account of something.

ex.en: He invented some story about a cousin.
ex.zh: 他们编造了一些关于一位表亲的谎话。

d: n. （story 的复数）故事，叙述；新闻报道；谎言，虚假的借口；楼层；（社交媒体）动态，快拍
v. 讲述，叙述；用历史故事画装饰（story 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A target is something at which someone is aiming a weapon or other object. 靶; (攻击的)

ex.en: The village lies beside a main road, making it an easy target for bandits.
ex.zh: 该村位于大路边，容易成为匪徒攻击的目标。

e.en: A target is a result that you are trying to achieve. (试图达成的)

ex.en: She's won back her place too late to achieve her target of 20 goals this season.
ex.zh: 她赢回她的位置为时已晚,无法实现她本赛季打进20个球的目标。

e.en: To target a particular person or thing means to decide to attack or criticize them. 把…作为攻击目标;

ex.en: Republicans targeted her as vulnerable in her bid for reelection this year.
ex.zh: 共和党人认为她在今年的再次参选中是不堪一击的攻击目标。

e.en: Target is also a noun. (攻击、批评的)

ex.en: In the past they have been the target of racist abuse.
ex.zh: 过去他们一直是种族虐待的对象。

d: n. 目标，指标；（攻击的）目标；（批评、嘲笑等的）对象；靶子；目标受众，受影响的人（或群体）； 圆形小盾；（语音）目标
v. 把……作为攻击目标，把……作为批评的对象；面向，把……对准（某群体）；将（钱款或援助）用于

e.en: A tool is any instrument or simple piece of equipment that you hold in your hands and use to do a particular kind of work. For example, spades, hammers, and knives are all tools.

ex.en: I find the best tool for the purpose is a pair of shears.
ex.zh: 我发现达到这一目的的最好工具是一把大剪刀。

e.en: You can refer to anything that you use for a particular purpose as a particular type of tool.

ex.en: Writing is a good tool for expressing feelings.
ex.zh: 写作是表达情感的一种好方法。

d: n. （尤指手用）工具；（完成工作或达到目标的）工具，手段；受人利用的人，工具；阴茎；容易被利用（或欺骗）的人，蠢人；（计算机）工具；（书籍装订时的）压印图案
v. 驱车兜风，驾车到处跑；（用工具）制作，在（皮革，尤指书籍的皮革封面）上压印图案；（为生产而）配置设备；凿刻（石头）；（尤指为犯罪活动而）武装

e.en: If you use something, you do something with it in order to do a job or to achieve a particular result or effect.

ex.en: Trim off the excess pastry using a sharp knife.
ex.zh: 用一把锋利刀削掉过多的油酥面团。

ex.en: The U.S. has used ships to bring most of its heavy material, like tanks, to the region.
ex.zh: 美国已用船把坦克等大多数重型物资运到了该地区。

e.en: If you use a supply of something, you finish it so that none of it is left.

ex.en: You used all the ice cubes and didn't put the ice trays back.
ex.zh: 你用光了所有的冰块，也没有把冰格盘放回去。

e.en: Use up means the same as use.

ex.en: It isn't animals who use up the world's resources.
ex.zh: 不是动物耗尽了世界资源。

e.en: If someone uses drugs, they take drugs regularly, especially illegal ones. 服; 吸食 (药、毒品)

ex.en: He denied he had used drugs.
ex.zh: 他否认吸食过毒品。

d: v. 使用，利用（use 的现在分词形式）
n. 使用，利用

e.en: Addiction is the condition of taking harmful drugs and being unable to stop taking them. (毒品)

ex.en: She helped him fight his drug addiction.
ex.zh: 她帮助了他对抗自己的毒瘾。

e.en: An addiction to something is a very strong desire or need for it.

ex.en: He needed money to feed his addiction to gambling.
ex.zh: 他需要钱来满足他的赌瘾。

d: n. 瘾；入迷，嗜好

e.en: An ad is an advertisement.

ex.en: She replied to a lonely hearts ad she spotted in the New York Times.
ex.zh: 她回复了在《纽约时报》上看到的一则求友广告。

e.en: advantage的缩写 (Brit equivalent van)
Andorra

d: abbr. 弹药分配系统（Ammunition Delivery System）；可调式避震系统（Adaptive Damping System）

e.en: the daughter of Cassiopeia and wife of Perseus, who saved her from a sea monster 安德梅达;
e.zh: 仙女座之女，宙斯之子珀尔修斯的妻子，把丈夫从海怪手里救出

e.en: a constellation in the N hemisphere lying between Cassiopeia and Pegasus, the three brightest stars being of the second magnitude. It contains the Andromeda Galaxy a spiral galaxy 2.2 million light years away

d: n. [天] 仙女座；安德洛墨达（希腊神话中的埃塞俄比亚公主）

e.en: application program

d: abbr. （计算机）应用程序，应用软件；开胃菜
【名】  （App）（美、德、巴）阿普（人名）；（App）（美、德、巴）阿普（人名）

e.en: An article is a piece of writing that is published in a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: ...a newspaper article.
ex.zh: …一篇报上的文章。

ex.en: According to an article in Newsweek the drug could have side effects.
ex.zh: 据一篇《新闻周刊》上的文章，这种药物可能有副作用。

e.en: You can refer to objects as articles of some kind.

ex.en: ...articles of clothing.
ex.zh: …衣物。

ex.en: He had stripped the house of all articles of value.
ex.zh: 他已把那所房子里值钱的东西洗劫一空。

e.en: An article of a formal agreement or document is a section of it that deals with a particular point.

ex.en: The country appears to be violating several articles of the convention.
ex.zh: 该国看来正在违反该公约中的数个条款。

e.en: In grammar, an article is a kind of determiner. In English, "a" and "an" are called the indefinite article, and "the" is called the definite article.

d: n. （article 的复数）文章；物品，物件；（法律或正式文件中的）条款，条文；（语法）冠词；（法律/职业）见习契约或培训期
v. （article 的第三人称单数）使受协议条款的约束；按条款提出指控

e.en: A bar is a place where you can buy and drink alcoholic drinks.

ex.en: ...Devil's Herd, the city's most popular country and western bar.
ex.zh: …“魔鬼群”，全城最受欢迎的西部乡村酒吧。

e.en: A bar is a room in a hotel or other establishment where alcoholic drinks are served. (旅馆等的)

ex.en: Last night in the hotel there was some talk in the bar about drugs.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上，在旅馆的酒吧间里有人说起毒品了。

e.en: A bar is a counter on which alcoholic drinks are served.

ex.en: Michael was standing alone by the bar when Brian rejoined him.
ex.zh: 布赖恩回来的时候，迈克尔正独自站在吧台旁。

e.en: A bar is a long, straight, stiff piece of metal. (金属)

ex.en: ...a brick building with bars across the ground floor windows.
ex.zh: …底楼窗户有铁栅穿过的一座砖楼。

d: n. 酒吧；吧台；小吃店；块，棒；（金属）条，栏杆；球门横梁；障碍；小节；条纹，带；功能条；律师职业；（法庭中的）围栏，被告席；电热棒；沙洲，暗礁；军阶杠；巴（气压单位）
v. 封，堵；阻挡，拦住；阻止，禁止；做条纹标记
prep. 除……外
【名】 （Bar）（德、法、俄、罗、捷、波、葡、以、阿拉伯）巴尔（人名）

e.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

ex.en: The United States bestowed honorary citizenship upon England's World War II prime minister, Sir Winston Churchill.
ex.zh: 美国授予了二战期间的英国首相温斯顿·丘吉尔爵士荣誉公民的称号。

d: v．
1. 赠予，授予：将某物或某种荣誉、权力等给予某人。
2. 安置，安顿：将某人或某物放置在某个地方。

e.en: When a wind or breeze blows, the air moves.

ex.en: A chill wind blew at the top of the hill.
ex.zh: 山顶上刮了一阵凉飕飕的风。

e.en: If the wind blows something somewhere or if it blows there, the wind moves it there. 把…吹到;

ex.en: The wind blew her hair back from her forehead.
ex.zh: 风把她额头上的头发向后吹。

ex.en: Sand blew in our eyes.
ex.zh: 沙子吹进了我们眼里。

e.en: If you blow, you send out a stream of air from your mouth.

ex.en: Danny rubbed his arms and blew on his fingers to warm them.
ex.zh: 丹尼搓着胳膊，向他的手指上呵气来暖手。

e.en: If you blow something somewhere, you move it by sending out a stream of air from your mouth. (人)

ex.en: He picked up his mug and blew off the steam.
ex.zh: 他端起杯子吹掉蒸汽。

d: v. 吹，刮；吹气；吹奏；充气；被吹走；鼓风，送风；离开（blow 的现在分词）
n. 吹制；吹气法
n. （Blumenthal）人名；（法）布吕芒塔尔；（英）布卢门撒尔；（德、芬、罗、捷、瑞典）布卢门塔尔

e.en: A browser is a piece of computer software that you use to search for information on the Internet, especially on the World Wide Web.

ex.en: You need an up-to-date Web browser.
ex.zh: 你需要一个最新的网络浏览器。

d: n. 浏览器；逛商店的人，浏览书报者；吃高处草木的动物

e.en: A casino is a building or room where people play gambling games such as roulette.

d: n. 赌场
【名】 （Casino）（西、法）卡西诺（人名）

e.en: Caution is great care which you take in order to avoid possible danger.

ex.en: Extreme caution should be exercised when buying used tyres.
ex.zh: 买二手轮胎时一定要极其谨慎。

e.en: If someone cautions you, they warn you about problems or danger. 警告;

ex.en: Tony cautioned against misrepresenting the situation.
ex.zh: 托尼告诫说不要歪曲事实。

ex.en: The statement clearly was intended to caution Seoul against attempting to block the council's action again.
ex.zh: 很显然，这份声明用意在于警告首尔别再试图阻止委员会的行动。

e.en: Caution is also a noun. 警告;

ex.en: There was a note of caution for the treasury in the figures.
ex.zh: 这些数据向财政部亮出了一个警告。

d: v. （caution 的过去式和过去分词）警告，告诫：提醒某人注意潜在的危险或问题；（英国警方，常用被动语态）对违法者予以正式警告，训诫。

e.en: You use certainly to emphasize what you are saying when you are making a statement. 的确;

ex.en: The public is certainly getting tired of hearing about it.
ex.zh: 公众无疑厌倦了听这方面的事。

ex.en: The bombs are almost certainly part of a much bigger conspiracy.
ex.zh: 几乎可以确定这些炸弹是一个更大阴谋的一部分。

e.en: You use certainly when you are agreeing with what someone has said.

ex.en: "In any case you remained friends."—"Certainly."
ex.zh: “不管怎样，你们还是朋友。”—“那当然。”

e.en: You say certainly not to say "no" in a strong way.

ex.en: "Perhaps it would be better if I withdrew altogether."—"Certainly not!"
ex.zh: “我完全退出的话情况或许会好些。” — “当然不是。”

d: adv. 无疑，确定；当然，行（用于回答）

e.en: A chair is a piece of furniture for one person to sit on, with a back and four legs.

ex.en: He rose from his chair and walked to the window.
ex.zh: 他从椅子上站起来走到窗户旁。

e.en: At a university, a chair is the position or job of professor.

ex.en: He has been appointed to the chair of sociology.
ex.zh: 他受命任职社会学教授。

e.en: The person who is the chair of a committee or meeting is the person in charge of it.

ex.en: She is the chair of the Defense Advisory Committee on Women in the Military.
ex.zh: 她是军队女兵国防顾问委员会的主席。

e.en: If you chair a meeting or a committee, you are the person in charge of it. 担任 (会议、委员会)

ex.en: He was about to chair a meeting in Venice of E.U. foreign ministers.
ex.zh: 他将担任威尼斯欧盟外交部长会议的主席 。

d: n. 椅子；主席，委员长；电椅；大学教授的职位
v. 主席，主持；用椅子把某人高高抬起；使……入座；使就任要职
【名】 （Chair）（法）谢尔 （人名）

e.en: At an airport, a check-in is the counter or desk where you check in.

ex.en: The line at the check-in was already dispersing.
ex.zh: 在登机手续办理处排的队已在散开了。

d: n. （机场、酒店等处）办理登机、入住等手续，报到，登记；登机手续办理处，报到处，登记处
n. 克里斯托弗，克里斯多夫（男子名）；圣克里斯托弗（Saint Christopher，相传为 3 世纪的基督教殉道者、旅行者的主保圣人）

e.en: If there is a choice of things, there are several of them and you can choose the one you want.

ex.en: It's available in a choice of colours.
ex.zh: 它有多种颜色可供选择。

ex.en: At lunchtime, there's a choice between the buffet or the set menu.
ex.zh: 午饭时，可以选择自助餐或套餐。

e.en: Your choice is someone or something that you choose from a range of things.

ex.en: Although he was only grumbling, his choice of words made Rodney angry.
ex.zh: 尽管他只是在发牢骚，但他所用的字眼却让罗德尼很生气。

e.en: Choice means of very high quality.

ex.en: ...a box of their choicest chocolates.
ex.zh: …他们的一盒上等巧克力。

e.en: If you have no choice but to do something or have little choice but to do it, you cannot avoid doing it.

ex.en: They had little choice but to agree to what he suggested.
ex.zh: 除了同意他的意见，他们别无选择。

d: n. 选择（choice 的复数）；选项，可供选择的事物；所选择的人或事物，入选者

e.en: When you close something such as a door or lid or when it closes, it moves so that a hole, gap, or opening is covered. 关闭;

ex.en: If you are cold, close the window.
ex.zh: 如果你冷就关上窗户。

ex.en: Zacharias heard the door close.
ex.zh: 札哈里亚斯听到门关上了。

e.en: When you close something such as an open book or umbrella, you move the different parts of it together. 把 (书、伞等)

ex.en: Slowly he closed the book.
ex.zh: 慢慢地他把书合上了。

e.en: If you close something such as a computer file or window, you give the computer an instruction to remove it from the screen. 关闭 (计算机文件、窗口)

ex.en: To close your document, press CTRL+W on your keyboard.
ex.zh: 要关闭你的文件同时按下键盘上的CTRL和W键。

e.en: When you close your eyes or your eyes close, your eyelids move downward, so that you can no longer see.

ex.en: Bess closed her eyes and fell asleep.
ex.zh: 贝丝闭上眼睛，睡着了。

d: v. （close 的第三人称单数）关闭，合上，闭上；（商店、工厂、机构等）停业，倒闭；（事件、会议、故事等）结束，终止
n. （close 的复数）围场，院子；（英国英语）死胡同
v. co-found 的过去式和过去分词：共同建立，共同成立，共同创办

e.en: If you comment on something, you give your opinion about it or you give an explanation for it. 评论;

ex.en: So far, Mr. Cook has not commented on these reports.
ex.zh: 到目前为止，库克先生还未对这些报告进行过评论。

ex.en: You really can't comment until you know the facts.
ex.zh: 你的确不能在你知道事实之前进行评论。

e.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it. 评论;

ex.en: He made his comments at a news conference in Amsterdam.
ex.zh: 他在阿姆斯特丹的一次记者招待会上做了评论。

ex.en: There's been no comment so far from police about the allegations.
ex.zh: 到目前为止还没有来自警方的对那些指控的任何解释。

e.en: People say "no comment" as a way of refusing to answer a question, usually when it is asked by a journalist.

ex.en: No comment. I don't know anything.
ex.zh: 无可奉告。我什么也不知道。

d: n. 评论，意见；注解，注释（comment 的复数）
v. 评论，发表意见；解释，说明（comment 的第三人称单数）
n. 公司的

e.en: When you come to a conclusion, you decide that something is true after you have thought about it carefully and have considered all the relevant facts.

ex.en: Over the years I've come to the conclusion that she's a very great musician.
ex.zh: 这些年我得出的结论是，她是位非常伟大的音乐家。

e.en: The conclusion of something is its ending. 结束;

ex.en: At the conclusion of the programme, I asked the children if they had any questions they wanted to ask me.
ex.zh: 节目结束时我问孩子们是否有要问我的问题。

e.en: The conclusion of a treaty or a business deal is the act of arranging it or agreeing on it. (条约、交易等的)

ex.en: ...the expected conclusion of a free-trade agreement between Mexico and the United States.
ex.zh: …墨西哥和美国之间自由贸易协议的如期达成。

e.en: You say "in conclusion" to indicate that what you are about to say is the last thing that you want to say. 最后 (用以表明讲话即将结束)

ex.en: In conclusion, walking is a cheap, safe, enjoyable, and readily available form of exercise.
ex.zh: 综上所述，散步是一种廉价、安全、有趣而又随时可以开展的运动形式。

d: n. conclusion 的复数；结论，判断；决定；总结，结论部分
n. 美国康乃迪克州（位于美国东北部）

e.en: Something that consists of particular things or people is formed from them. (以…)

ex.en: My diet consisted almost exclusively of chocolate-covered cookies and glasses of milk.
ex.zh: 我的饮食几乎只包含裹上巧克力的曲奇饼和一杯杯牛奶。

e.en: Something that consists in something else has that thing as its main or only part. (以…)

ex.en: His work as a consultant consisted in advising foreign companies on the siting of new factories.
ex.zh: 他做顾问的工作主要包括就新工厂选址为外国公司提出意见。

d: v. consist 的第三人称单数形式：由……组成，由……构成（常与 of 连用）；在于，以……为主要（或唯一）部分（常与 in 连用）；（正式）与……一致，符合（常与 with 连用）

e.en: If you consult an expert or someone senior to you or consult with them, you ask them for their opinion, advice, or permission.

ex.en: Consult your doctor about how much exercise you should get.
ex.zh: 咨询你的医生你应做多少运动。

ex.en: He needed to consult with an attorney.
ex.zh: 他需要和律师咨询。

e.en: If you consult a book or a map, you look in it or look at it in order to find some information.

ex.en: Consult the chart on page 44 for the correct cooking times.
ex.zh: 查阅第44页的图表找正确的烹调时间。

e.en: If a person or group of people consults with other people or consults them, or if two people or groups consult, they talk and exchange ideas and opinions about what they might decide to do.

ex.en: After consulting with her daughter and manager, she decided to take on the part, on her terms.
ex.zh: 同她的女儿兼经纪人商量之后，她决定按她的要求接受那个角色。

ex.en: The two countries will have to consult their allies.
ex.zh: 两国得同各自的盟友协商。

d: v. consult 的第三人称单数形式：咨询，请教；查阅，参看；商量，协商；以顾问身份提供专业意见（常与 for 连用）。

e.en: A consumer is a person who buys things or uses services.

ex.en: ...claims that tobacco companies failed to warn consumers about the dangers of smoking.
ex.zh: …声称烟草公司没有就吸烟的种种危险警告消费者。

d: n. consumer 的复数：消费者，顾客，用户；消耗者；（生态学）消费者（异养生物）

e.en: If someone or something cools off, or if you cool them off, they become cooler after having been hot. 变凉;

ex.en: Maybe he's trying to cool off out there in the rain.
ex.zh: 可能他是想在外面的雨中凉快一下。

ex.en: She made a fanning motion, pretending to cool herself off.
ex.zh: 她做了一个扇扇子的动作，假装使自己凉快一些。

e.en: If someone cools off, they become less angry than they were.

ex.en: We've got to give him some time to cool off.
ex.zh: 我们必须给他时间让他冷静下来。

d: 冷却

e.en: If you have a conversation with someone, you talk with them, usually in an informal situation. (非正式的)

ex.en: He's a talkative guy, and I struck up a conversation with him.
ex.zh: 他是一个健谈的人，我和他聊了起来。

d: n. 会话，交谈（conversation 的复数）
adv. 故意地；从容不迫地，小心翼翼地

e.en: A demanding job or task requires a lot of your time, energy, or attention. 费力的;

ex.en: He tried to return to work, but found he could no longer cope with his demanding job.
ex.zh: 他试图回去工作，但发现自己不再能适应这项费时的工作。

e.en: People who are demanding are not easily satisfied or pleased.

ex.en: Ricky was a very demanding child.
ex.zh: 里基是个非常苛求的孩子。

d: adj. 费时费力的；苛刻的，难以满足的
v. 强烈要求；需要，需求（demand 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Dialogue is communication or discussion between people or groups of people such as governments or political parties.

ex.en: People of all social standings should be given equal opportunities for dialogue.
ex.zh: 社会各阶层的人都应该被给予平等对话的机会。

e.en: A dialogue is a conversation between two people in a book, film, or play. (书籍、影视、戏剧中的)

ex.en: Although the dialogue is sharp, the actors move too awkwardly around the stage.
ex.zh: 尽管对白很清晰，但演员们在舞台上的动作却太不自然。

d: n. 对白；对话，交换意见
v. （为解决问题而）参加对话，进行讨论；为（电影、戏剧）配上对白

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it.

ex.en: The initial deposit required to open an account is a minimum 100 dollars.
ex.zh: 开户需要的首笔存入额是至少100美元。

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is in a bank account or savings account, especially a sum which will be left there for some time.
A deposit is an amount of a substance that has been left somewhere as a result of a chemical or geological process. 沉积物;

ex.en: ...underground deposits of gold and diamonds.
ex.zh: …黄金和钻石的地下矿床。

e.en: A deposit is a sum of money which you pay when you start renting something. The money is returned to you if you do not damage what you have rented.

ex.en: I put down a $500 security deposit for another apartment.
ex.zh: 我为另一套公寓支付了$500押金。

d: v. 放下，放置；储蓄；存放，寄存；沉积，沉淀；支付（押金、订金或预缴费用）
n. 沉积物，沉积层；订金；押金；存款；竞选保证金

e.en: If something is directly above, below, or in front of something, it is in exactly that position.

ex.en: The second rainbow will be bigger than the first, and directly above it.
ex.zh: 第二道彩虹将比第一道更大，并位于第一道的正上方。

e.en: If you do one action directly after another, you do the second action as soon as the first one is finished.

ex.en: Most guests left directly after the wake.
ex.zh: 守灵仪式一结束，大部分客人就立刻走了。

d: adv. 直接地，径直地；坦率地；恰好，正好；立即，很快地
conj. 一……就……
vt. 挫伤积极性，使失去激励

e.en: A disorder is a problem or illness which affects someone's mind or body.

ex.en: ...a rare nerve disorder that can cause paralysis of the arms.
ex.zh: …一种罕见的能导致手臂瘫痪的神经紊乱疾病。

e.en: Disorder is violence or rioting in public.

ex.en: Six months ago America's worst civil disorder in more than 100 years erupted in the city of Los Angeles.
ex.zh: 6个月前，美国100多年来最严重的市民骚乱在洛杉矶市爆发了。

e.en: Disorder is a state of being untidy, badly prepared, or badly organized.

ex.en: The emergency room was in disorder.
ex.zh: 急救室一片混乱。

d: n. 混乱，杂乱；骚乱，动乱；紊乱，疾病
v. 打乱，使紊乱

e.en: To download data means to transfer it to or from a computer along a line such as a telephone line, a radio link, or a computer network.

ex.en: Users can download their material to a desktop PC back in the office.
ex.zh: 用户们可以将他们的资料下载到办公室的台式计算机上。

d: v. 下载
n. 下载，下载的文件或程序

e.en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

ex.en: When things aren't going well, he encourages me, telling me not to give up.
ex.zh: 当事情不顺利的时候，他鼓励我，告诉我不要放弃。

e.en: If someone is encouraged by something that happens, it gives them hope or confidence.

ex.en: Investors were encouraged by the news.
ex.zh: 投资者被这条消息所鼓舞。

e.en: 受到鼓舞的

ex.en: We were very encouraged after over 17,000 pictures were submitted.
ex.zh: 我们深受鼓舞，17000多张照片已被提交了。

e.en: If you encourage someone to do something, you try to persuade them to do it, for example, by telling them that it would be a pleasant thing to do, or by trying to make it easier for them to do it. You can also encourage an activity.

ex.en: Herbie Hancock was encouraged by his family to learn music at a young age.
ex.zh: 赫比·汉考克小时候受到家人鼓励去学音乐。

d: v. 鼓励（encourage 的过去式和过去分词）；支持；促进；鼓动
adj. （常作表语）受到鼓舞的

e.en: If you enjoy something, you find pleasure and satisfaction in doing it or experiencing it.

ex.en: Ross had always enjoyed the company of women.
ex.zh: 罗斯一直都很享受女人的陪伴。

ex.en: He was a guy who enjoyed life to the full.
ex.zh: 他是个尽情享受生活乐趣的人。

e.en: If you enjoy yourself, you do something that you like doing or you take pleasure in the situation that you are in. (自)

ex.en: I am really enjoying myself at the moment.
ex.zh: 我此刻很是自得其乐。

e.en: If you enjoy something such as a right, benefit, or privilege, you have it.

ex.en: The average German will enjoy 40 days' paid holiday this year.
ex.zh: 德国人今年平均将享有40天带薪假期。

d: v. 享受，欣赏，喜爱；过得愉快，玩得开心（enjoy oneself）；享有，拥有；请尽情享用； 请尽情享用

e.en: If you engage in an activity, you do it or are actively involved with it.

ex.en: I have never engaged in drug trafficking.
ex.zh: 我从来没有从事过贩毒。

e.en: If something engages you or your attention or interest, it keeps you interested in it and thinking about it.

ex.en: They never learned skills to engage the attention of the others.
ex.zh: 他们从来没有学过吸引别人注意的技巧。

e.en: If you engage someone in conversation, you have a conversation with them.

ex.en: They tried to engage him in conversation.
ex.zh: 他们试图使他加入谈话。

e.en: If you engage with something or with a group of people, you get involved with that thing or group and feel that you are connected with it or have real contact with it.

ex.en: She found it hard to engage with office life.
ex.zh: 她发现难以融入办公室生活。

d: v. 雇用，聘请；参加，从事；吸引，引起；与……交战，开战；（使）（机器）啮合，接合；预定（膳食，地方等）；适应，与……有密切关系；允诺，签约保证；（运动员或击剑手）使（兵器）交结在一起；占用

e.en: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

ex.en: He examined her passport and stamped it.
ex.zh: 他仔细检查了她的护照，然后在上面盖了章。

e.en: 仔细检查

ex.en: The navy is to carry out an examination of the wreck tomorrow.
ex.zh: 海军明天将会对失事船只作仔细检查。

e.en: If a doctor examines you, he or she looks at your body, feels it, or does simple tests in order to check how healthy you are.

ex.en: Another doctor examined her and could still find nothing wrong.
ex.zh: 另一个医生对她进行了检查，仍然找不出任何毛病。

e.en: 诊察

ex.en: He was later discharged after an examination at the hospital.
ex.zh: 后来他在医院做过检查后就出院了。

d: v. 检查，调查；考核，测验；（医生）诊察；（尤指在法庭上）审问，查问

e.en: An executive is someone who is employed by a business at a senior level. Executives decide what the business should do, and ensure that it is done.

ex.en: ...an advertising executive.
ex.zh: …一位广告执行总监。

e.en: The executive sections and tasks of an organization are concerned with the making of decisions and with ensuring that decisions are carried out.

ex.en: A successful job search needs to be as well organized as any other executive task.
ex.zh: 一次成功的寻职要像任何其他执行任务一样精心安排。

e.en: Executive goods are expensive products designed or intended for executives and other people at a similar social or economic level.

ex.en: ...an executive briefcase.
ex.zh: …一个高级公文包。

e.en: The executive committee or board of an organization is a committee within that organization that has the authority to make decisions and ensures that these decisions are carried out.

ex.en: They opted to put an executive committee in charge of the project rather than a single person.
ex.zh: 他们选择由一个执行委员会而非个人来负责这个项目。

d: n. 高管，主管（executive 的复数）

e.en: Fairly means to quite a large degree. For example, if you say that something is fairly old, you mean that it is old but not very old.

ex.en: We did fairly well but only fairly well.
ex.zh: 我们做得尚可，但仅仅是尚可。

e.en: You use fairly instead of "very" to add emphasis to an adjective or adverb without making it sound too forceful.

ex.en: Were you always fairly bright at school?
ex.zh: 你上学时一直挺聪明吧？

ex.en: You've got to be fairly single-minded about it.
ex.zh: 你必须对此事专心一些。

d: adv. 相当地，颇；公平地，公正地；（用以强调）完全，简直；令人愉快地，让人喜欢地
【名】 （Fairly）（英）费尔利（人名）

e.en: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

ex.en: He rolled down his window and stuck his face out.
ex.zh: 他摇下窗户，探出脸来。

ex.en: He was going red in the face and breathing with difficulty.
ex.zh: 他脸面发红，费力地喘着气。

e.en: If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.

ex.en: He was walking around with a sad face.
ex.zh: 他四处走着，面带哀伤。

e.en: The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it. (悬崖、山、建筑物的)

ex.en: Harrer was one of the first to climb the north face of the Eiger.
ex.zh: 哈勒是第一批登上艾格尔山北坡的人之一。

e.en: The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time. 钟面;

ex.en: It was too dark to see the face of my watch.
ex.zh: 天太黑了，以致看不见我表盘上的时间。

d: n. 脸，面孔（face 的复数）；面部表情，脸色；鬼脸（用于 make faces）；脸面，面子；表面，面
v. 面对，面临，正视；向，面向，朝向；转向（face 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A file is a box or a folded piece of heavy paper or plastic in which letters or documents are kept. 文件盒;

ex.en: ...a file of insurance papers.
ex.zh: …一个保险单文件夹。

e.en: A file is a collection of information about a particular person or thing.

ex.en: We already have files on people's tax details.
ex.zh: 我们已经有了人们付税详情的卷宗。

e.en: In computing, a file is a set of related data that has its own name.

ex.en: Be sure to save the revised version of the file under a new filename.
ex.zh: 确保将改过的文件版本另存在一个新的文件名下。

e.en: A file is a hand tool which is used for rubbing hard objects to make them smooth, shape them, or cut through them.

d: n. file 的复数：文件，文档；档案，卷宗；锉刀；行列，纵队
v. file 的第三人称单数：提出，提交（诉讼、申请、报告等），发送（报道等）；把……归档，存档，汇订；用锉刀锉，锉平，锉光；排成单行行进

e.en: Someone's findings are the information they get or the conclusions they come to as the result of an investigation or some research. 调查结果;

ex.en: One of the main findings of the survey was the confusion about the facilities already in place.
ex.zh: 该调查的主要发现之一是对已安装到位的设备的混淆。

e.en: The findings of a court are the decisions that it reaches after a trial or an investigation.

ex.en: The government hopes the court will announce its findings before the end of the month.
ex.zh: 政府希望该法院能在月底前宣布判决。

d: n.  结果，发现；判决，裁决；（制作服装、鞋子或首饰用的）一应小物件（或小工具）
v. 找到，感到（find 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Someone's findings are the information they get or the conclusions they come to as the result of an investigation or some research. 调查结果;

ex.en: One of the main findings of the survey was the confusion about the facilities already in place.
ex.zh: 该调查的主要发现之一是对已安装到位的设备的混淆。

e.en: The findings of a court are the decisions that it reaches after a trial or an investigation.

ex.en: The government hopes the court will announce its findings before the end of the month.
ex.zh: 政府希望该法院能在月底前宣布判决。

d: n. （通常用复数）发现，调查结果，研究结论；（检验、检查中）发现的情况；（法律）法庭等审理或调查后作出的裁决，判决，认定；（制鞋、首饰加工、服装制作等行业用的）材料、辅料、小配件或工具

e.en: A gambler is someone who gambles regularly, for example in card games or on horse racing.

ex.en: There was a fellow in that casino tonight who's a very heavy gambler.
ex.zh: 今晚那家赌场有个家伙是个嗜赌成性的赌棍。

e.en: If you describe someone as a gambler, you mean that they are ready to take risks in order to gain advantages or success.

ex.en: He had never been afraid of failure: he was a gambler, ready to go off somewhere else and start all over again.
ex.zh: 他从不害怕失败：他是个冒险家，随时准备去别的地方重新开始。

d: n. 赌徒，赌客；冒险家，投机者，投机商人
n. 盖提（姓氏）
n. 波兰（欧洲国家）

e.en: The law is a system of rules that a society or government develops in order to deal with crime, business agreements, and social relationships. You can also use the law to refer to the people who work in this system. 法律;

ex.en: Obscene and threatening phone calls are against the law.
ex.zh: 猥亵电话和恐吓电话是违法的。

ex.en: They are beginning criminal proceedings against him for breaking the law on financing political parties.
ex.zh: 他们正开始对他进行刑事诉讼，因为他违反了政党资助法。

e.en: Law is used to refer to a particular branch of the law, such as criminal law or business law. (某一类)

ex.en: He was a professor of criminal law at Harvard University law school.
ex.zh: 他曾是哈佛大学法学院的刑法教授。

ex.en: Under international law, diplomats living in foreign countries are exempt from criminal prosecution.
ex.zh: 按照国际法，驻外外交官免受刑事诉讼。

e.en: A law is one of the rules in a system of law which deals with a particular type of agreement, relationship, or crime. (特定的)

ex.en: ...the country's liberal political asylum law.
ex.zh: …该国的自由政治避难法。

e.en: The laws of an organization or activity are its rules, which are used to organize and control it. 戒律;

ex.en: ...the laws of the Catholic Church.
ex.zh: …天主教会的戒律。

d: n. 法律（体系）；法令，法规；规律，法则，定律；法学，法律学；司法界，律师业；（道德或宗教上的）准则，守则；警方，警察
v. 起诉，控告
【名】 （Law）（英、缅、柬）劳（人名）

e.en: the book of the Old Testament recounting the history of Israel under the warrior champions and national leaders known as judges from the death of Joshua to the birth of Samuel (《旧约》)士师记;
e.zh: 其中记录了从约书亚去世到撒母耳出生期间武士为尊和国家领导人充当法官的历史

d: n. 士师记（又译《民长记》，旧约全书之一卷）

e.en: The tusks of an elephant, wild boar, or walrus are its two very long, curved, pointed teeth. (大象等的)

d: n. 长牙，獠牙，（大象的）象牙；尖头，尖形物，似长牙的突出物；（Tusk）人名；（波）图斯克
vt. 以牙刺戳；以长牙掘

e.en: Constitutional means relating to the constitution of a particular country or organization. 有关宪法的;

ex.en: The issue is one of constitutional and civil rights.
ex.zh: 这问题涉及宪法的和民事的权利。

d: adj. 宪法的；宪法规定的，合乎宪法的；体质的，体格的；本性的，天性的
n. 保健散步

e.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties. 宪法;

ex.en: The king was forced to adopt a new constitution which reduced his powers.
ex.zh: 国王被迫通过了削减其权力的新宪法。

e.en: Your constitution is your health.

ex.en: He must have an extremely strong constitution.
ex.zh: 他必有极为强健的体格。

d: n. 宪法，章程；体质，体格；组成，结构

e.en: Polish is a substance that you put on the surface of an object in order to clean it, protect it, and make it shine. 抛光剂;

ex.en: The still air smelled faintly of furniture polish.
ex.zh: 久未流通的空气中有股淡淡的家具漆的气味。

e.en: If you polish something, you put polish on it or rub it with a cloth to make it shine. (用抛光剂等)

ex.en: Each morning he shaved and polished his shoes.
ex.zh: 每天早晨他都刮胡子、擦皮鞋。

e.en: Polish is also a noun. 擦亮;

ex.en: He gave his counter a polish with a soft duster.
ex.zh: 他用柔软的抹布将柜台擦得亮亮的。

e.en: 擦亮的;

ex.en: ...a highly polished floor.
ex.zh: …一块擦得很亮的地板。

d: v. 擦亮，磨光；改进，使完美，给……润色；涂指甲油
n. 上光剂，亮光剂；抛光，擦亮；擦光的面，打磨光亮的面；（表演或作品的）完美，优美；文雅，礼貌
n. （Polish）波兰人；波兰语
adj. （Polish）波兰的

e.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law. 司法的;

ex.en: ...an independent judicial system.
ex.zh: …一个独立的司法体系。

ex.en: ...efforts to manipulate the judicial process.
ex.zh: …操纵审判程序的努力。

e.en: 司法地;

ex.en: Even if the amendment is passed it can be defeated judicially.
ex.zh: 即使这项修正案获得了通过，它也有可能通过司法程序被否决。

d: adj. 法庭的，司法的；公正的，明断的

e.en: A tribunal is a special court or committee that is appointed to deal with particular problems. 特别法庭;

ex.en: His case comes before an industrial tribunal in March.
ex.zh: 他的案子将于3月在产业法庭审判。

d: n. 法庭，特别法庭，审裁处；法官席，审判席

e.en: If someone or something highlights a point or problem, they emphasize it or make you think about it. 强调;

ex.en: Last year Collins wrote a moving ballad which highlighted the plight of the homeless.
ex.zh: 去年柯林斯写了一首感人的叙事诗，突出描写了无家可归者的苦境。

e.en: To highlight a piece of text means to mark it in a different colour, either with a special type of pen or on a computer screen. (用不同颜色) 标出; (在电脑屏幕上)

ex.en: Highlight the chosen area by clicking and holding down the left mouse button.
ex.zh: 通过点击鼠标左键并摁住以突出显示所选区域。

e.en: The highlights of an event, activity, or period of time are the most interesting or exciting parts of it.

ex.en: ...a match that is likely to prove one of the highlights of the tournament.
ex.zh: …可能是本届锦标赛最精彩的赛事之一。

d: v. 突出，强调；用亮色标出，高亮显示；挑染（highlight 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 突出的；被强调的；高亮显示的

e.en: The parliament of some countries is the group of people who make or change its laws, and decide what policies the country should follow.

ex.en: The Bangladesh Parliament today approved the policy, but it has not yet become law.
ex.zh: 孟加拉共和国议会今天批准了这项政策，但它还没有成为法律。

e.en: A particular parliament is a particular period of time in which a parliament is doing its work, between two elections or between two periods of holiday. 一届议会的任期; (两次大选之间的)

ex.en: The legislation is expected to be passed in the next parliament.
ex.zh: 这项法规有望在下届议会中通过。

d: n. 议会，国会；英国议会（包括下议院和上议院）（Parliament）；一届议会（会期）

e.en: Pi is a number, approximately 3.14, which is equal to the distance around a circle divided by its width. It is usually represented by the Greek letter π.
the 16th letter in the Greek alphabet (Π, π), a consonant, transliterated as p 希腊字母(Π, π)
a jumbled pile of printer's type
to spill and mix (set type) indiscriminately 使(活字等)

d: n. 圆周率；希腊字母 π（pis 是 pi 的复数）；捣实粘土（用作建筑材料）；（印刷）混杂的活字；（Pis）皮斯（姓氏）
v. 使（活字等）混杂（pis 是 pi 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Opposition is strong, angry, or violent disagreement and disapproval.

ex.en: There is bitter opposition from local business to the plan.
ex.zh: 有来自当地企业对此计划的强烈反对。

e.en: The opposition is the political parties or groups that are opposed to a government.

ex.en: The main opposition parties boycotted the election, saying it would not be conducted fairly.
ex.zh: 主要的反对党抵制了选举，声称选举不会公平进行。

e.en: In countries with a parliament, such as Britain, the opposition refers to the politicians or political parties that form part of the parliament, but are not the government.

ex.en: ...the Leader of the Opposition.
ex.zh: …在野党领袖。

e.en: The opposition is the person or team you are competing against in a sports event.

ex.en: The coach says his team is not underestimating the opposition.
ex.zh: 教练说他的队没在低估对手。

d: n. （强烈的） 反对，反抗；对手，竞争者（the opposition）；反对党，在野党（ the Opposition）；对立，对立的事物；（天文，占星）冲

e.en: When there is a riot, a crowd of people behave violently in a public place, for example they fight, throw stones, or damage buildings and vehicles.

ex.en: Twelve inmates have been killed during a riot at the prison.
ex.zh: 十二名囚犯在该监狱里的一次暴乱中丧生。

e.en: If people riot, they behave violently in a public place.

ex.en: Last year 600 inmates rioted, starting fires and building barricades.
ex.zh: 去年600名囚犯闹事，放火并制造路障。

e.en: 闹事者

ex.en: The militia dispersed the rioters.
ex.zh: 民兵驱散了闹事者。

e.en: If you say that there is a riot of something pleasant such as colour, you mean that there is a large amount of various types of it. (颜色等)

ex.en: It would be a riot of colour, of poppies and irises and flowers of every kind.
ex.zh: 那将会是五彩斑斓的颜色，由罂粟花、鸢尾花以及各种花卉组成。

d: n. 暴乱，骚乱；纷呈，丰富多彩；非常有趣的人（或事物）；纵情欢闹，狂欢；骚动；（感情的）爆发，宣泄
v. （人群）发生骚乱，聚众闹事；放纵，恣意；浪费，挥霍
【名】 （Riot）（法）里奥，（西）里奥特（人名）

e.en: Procedural means involving a formal procedure.

ex.en: A Spanish judge rejected the suit on procedural grounds.
ex.zh: 一名西班牙法官以程序理由驳回了该起诉。

d: adj. 程序上的，程序性的；（法学）程序法的，诉讼程序上的；（计算机）过程式的，程序化的
n. （影视、文学）以专业人员按程序展开调查或办案过程为主线的作品

e.en: If something is done in accordance with a particular rule or system, it is done in the way that the rule or system says that it should be done.

ex.en: Entries which are illegible or otherwise not in accordance with the rules will be disqualified.
ex.zh: 难以辨认的或不符合这些规定的参赛作品将被取消资格。

d: n. 按照，依据，与……一致（in accordance with）

e.en: If you look at someone with an accusing expression or speak to them in an accusing tone of voice, you are showing that you think they have done something wrong. 指责的;

ex.en: The accusing look in her eyes conveyed her sense of betrayal.
ex.zh: 她眼中谴责的目光表达了她被出卖的感受。

d: adj. （多形容目光、语气等）指责的，非难的，归咎的
v. 指责，指控，归咎于（accuse 的现在分词）

e.en: If you say that something appears to be the way you describe it, you are reporting what you believe or what you have been told, though you cannot be sure it is true.

ex.en: There appears to be increasing support for the leadership to take a more aggressive stance.
ex.zh: 似乎有不断增长的对领导层采取更强立场的支持。

e.en: If someone or something appears to have a particular quality or characteristic, they give the impression of having that quality or characteristic.

ex.en: She did her best to appear more self-assured than she felt.
ex.zh: 她竭力表现得比她感觉的更为自信。

ex.en: He is anxious to appear a gentleman.
ex.zh: 他急于表现得像一位绅士。

e.en: When someone or something appears, they move into a position where you can see them.

ex.en: A woman appeared at the far end of the street.
ex.zh: 一个女人在街那端出现了。

e.en: When something new appears, it begins to exist or reaches a stage of development where its existence can be noticed.

ex.en: ...small white flowers which appear in early summer.
ex.zh: …在初夏出现的小白花。

d: v. 出现，显得，表现得（appear 的现在分词）；也可表示显现、露面、出版、出庭等
n. （印刷）版面高度

e.en: Adverse decisions, conditions, or effects are unfavourable to you.

ex.en: The police said Mr. Hadfield's decision would have no adverse effect on the progress of the investigation.
ex.zh: 警方说哈德菲尔德先生的决定对于调查进展不会有任何不利的影响。

e.en: 不利地

ex.en: Price changes must not adversely affect the living standards of the people.
ex.zh: 价格变化一定不能负面地影响人们的生活水平。

d: adj. 不利的，有害的；相反的；敌对的

e.en: An apparent situation, quality, or feeling seems to exist, although you cannot be certain that it does exist.

ex.en: I was a bit depressed by our apparent lack of progress.
ex.zh: 我对我们表面上的缺乏进展感到有点沮丧。

e.en: If something is apparent to you, it is clear and obvious to you.

ex.en: It has been apparent that in other areas standards have held up well.
ex.zh: 显然在其他领域标准保持得良好。

e.en: If you say that something happens for no apparent reason, you cannot understand why it happens.

ex.en: The person may become dizzy for no apparent reason.
ex.zh: 此人可能会莫名其妙地变得头晕目眩。

d: adj. 显而易见的，易懂的；貌似的，表面上的

e.en: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

ex.en: Not everyone approves of the festival.
ex.zh: 不是每个人都喜欢这个节日。

e.en: If you approve of someone or something, you like and admire them.

ex.en: You've never approved of Henry, have you?
ex.zh: 你从未赞赏过亨利，是吧？

e.en: to improve or increase the value of (waste or common land), as by enclosure 使(废品或公共土地)

d: v. 同意，赞成；批准，通过；核准；喜欢，赞赏；证明，显示；使（废品或公共土地）升值

e.en: A country's ally is another country that has an agreement to support it, especially in war.

ex.en: Washington would not take such a step without its allies' approval.
ex.zh: 没有其同盟国的赞同，华盛顿不会迈出这样的一步。

e.en: If you describe someone as your ally, you mean that they help and support you, especially when other people are opposing you.

ex.en: He is a close ally of the president.
ex.zh: 他是总统的一位亲密盟友。

e.en: The Allies were the armed forces that fought against Germany and Japan in World War II. (二战时的)

ex.en: ...Germany's surrender to the Allies.
ex.zh: …德国向同盟国的投降。

e.en: If you ally yourself with someone or something, you give your support to them.

ex.en: He will have no choice but to ally himself with the new movement.
ex.zh: 他将别无选择，只能与这个新运动结盟。

d: n. 同盟国；盟友，支持者；辅助物，助手
v. 与……结盟，与……联合
【名】 （Ally）（英）艾丽，（法）阿利，（巴基）阿利，（尼日利）阿利（人名）

e.en: An aide is an assistant to someone who has an important job, especially in government or in the armed forces.

ex.en: A close aide to the prime minister repeated that Israel would never accept it.
ex.zh: 首相身边的一个助手重申了以色列绝不会接受。

d: n. 助理，助手；随从武官
【名】 （Aide）（葡）艾德（人名）

e.en: An attempted crime or unlawful action is an unsuccessful effort to commit the crime or action. (犯罪或非法行为)

ex.en: ...a case of attempted murder.
ex.zh: …一起谋杀未遂案件。

d: adj. 未遂的，企图的（多作定语）
v. 企图，试图，尝试（attempt 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Caught is the past tense and past participle of catch. (catch)

d: v. catch 的过去式和过去分词（表示抓住、捕捉、赶上、听到、染上（疾病）、发现（某人做某事）等）；被抓住、被捕获、被捕（用于 be caught / get caught 等被动结构）；陷入、遭遇、被困住（用于 be caught in / get caught in 等搭配）；被卷入、被牵涉（用于 be caught up in / get caught up in 等搭配）

e.en: If something is done on a particular basis, it is done according to that method, system, or principle. 按…原则;

ex.en: We're going to be meeting there on a regular basis.
ex.zh: 我们将定期在那儿会面。

ex.en: They want all groups to be treated on an equal basis.
ex.zh: 他们要求所有的群体都能得到平等的对待。

e.en: If you say that you are acting on the basis of something, you are giving that as the reason for your action.

ex.en: McGregor must remain confined, on the basis of the medical reports we have received.
ex.zh: 基于我们所收到的医疗报告，麦格雷戈必须继续卧床休息。

e.en: The basis of something is its starting point or an important part of it from which it can be further developed.

ex.en: Both factions have broadly agreed that the U.N. plan is a possible basis for negotiation.
ex.zh: 两派已大致同意该联合国计划是谈判的可能基础。

e.en: The basis for something is a fact or argument that you can use to prove or justify it.

ex.en: ...Japan's attempt to secure the legal basis to send troops overseas.
ex.zh: …日本取得派遣军队的法律依据的企图。

d: n. 基础，要素；基准，方式；理由，根据；主要成分（或部分）

e.en: A breakthrough is an important development or achievement.

ex.en: The company looks poised to make a significant breakthrough in China.
ex.zh: 该公司看上去稳将在中国实现一次重大突破。

d: n. 突破，重大进展
n. （Bogucki）人名；（法、波）博古茨基

e.en: A battle is a violent fight between groups of people, especially one between military forces during a war.

ex.en: ...the victory of King William III at the Battle of the Boyne.
ex.zh: …威廉三世国王在博因河战役中所取得的胜利。

ex.en: ...a gun battle between police and drug traffickers.
ex.zh: …警察和毒品贩子之间的一场枪战。

e.en: A battle is a conflict in which different people or groups compete in order to achieve success or control. 斗争;

ex.en: ...an unfolding political battle over jobs and the economy.
ex.zh: …一场正在展开的关于就业和经济的政治较量。

ex.en: ...the eternal battle between good and evil in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上善恶之间永无休止的较量。

e.en: You can use battle to refer to someone's efforts to achieve something in spite of very difficult circumstances.

ex.en: ...the battle against crime.
ex.zh: …制止犯罪的斗争。

ex.en: She has fought a constant battle with her weight.
ex.zh: 她一直在和自己的体重作斗争。

e.en: To battle with an opposing group means to take part in a fight or contest against them. You can also say that one group or person is battling another. 与…搏斗;

ex.en: In one town thousands of people battled with police and several were reportedly wounded.
ex.zh: 在一个镇子里，成千上万的人同警察展开搏斗，据报道有几人受伤。

ex.en: The sides must battle again for a quarter-final place on December 16.
ex.zh: 两队必须于12月16日再战一次，来争夺1/4决赛的位置。

d: n. 战役，战争；争论，斗争；竞赛，较量；拼搏，奋斗
v. 与……作战，和……斗争；搏斗，奋斗；争吵，争论；阻止，打败
【名】 （Battle）（英）巴特尔，（法）巴特勒，（西）巴特莱（人名）
中右的（指支持资本主义并接受某些社会改革的）
中右翼（指支持资本主义并接受某些社会改革的）

e.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

ex.en: Mr. Berry said the timing was a coincidence and that his decision was unrelated to Mr. Roman's departure.
ex.zh: 贝里先生说时间的安排是个巧合，而且他的决策与罗曼先生的离去毫无关系。

d: n. 巧合，同时发生；相符，一致；符合

e.en: If you are certain about something, you firmly believe it is true and have no doubt about it. If you are not certain about something, you do not have definite knowledge about it.

ex.en: She's absolutely certain she's going to make it in the world.
ex.zh: 她确信自己将享誉全球。

ex.en: We are not certain whether the appendix had already burst or not.
ex.zh: 我们不能确定阑尾破了没有。

e.en: If you say that something is certain to happen, you mean that it will definitely happen. 肯定的;

ex.en: However, the scheme is certain to meet opposition from fishermen's leaders.
ex.zh: 不过这个计划肯定会遭到渔夫头领们的反对。

ex.en: It's not certain they'll accept that candidate if he wins.
ex.zh: 如果那位候选人胜出，无法肯定他们是否会接受他。

e.en: If you say that something is certain, you firmly believe that it is true, or have definite knowledge about it.

ex.en: One thing is certain, both have the utmost respect for each other.
ex.zh: 有一点是确定无疑的，即两人对彼此都非常敬重。

e.en: If you know something for certain, you have no doubt at all about it.

ex.en: She couldn't know what time he'd go, or even for certain that he'd go at all.
ex.zh: 她不知道他何时要走，甚至于还不能确定他究竟要不要走。

d: adj. 必然的，必定的；确定的，无疑的；某个，特定的；某位，一位叫……的；一定程度上的，有点儿
pron. 某些，某几个
n. （Certain）（美、法）塞尔坦（人名）

e.en: A compromise is a situation in which people accept something slightly different from what they really want, because of circumstances or because they are considering the wishes of other people.

ex.en: Encourage your child to reach a compromise between what he wants and what you want.
ex.zh: 鼓励你的孩子在他想要的和你想要的之间折衷。

e.en: If you compromise with someone, you reach an agreement with them in which you both give up something that you originally wanted. You can also say that two people or groups compromise.

ex.en: The government has compromised with its critics over monetary policies.
ex.zh: 政府已经在货币政策上与其批评者们有了妥协。

ex.en: "Nine," I said. "Nine thirty," he replied. We compromised on 9:15.
ex.zh: “9点，”我说。“9：30，”他回答道。我们各让一步定在9:15。

e.en: If someone compromises themselves or compromises their beliefs, they do something which damages their reputation for honesty, loyalty, or high moral principles. 使 (自己、自己的信念)

ex.en: ...members of the government who have compromised themselves by accepting bribes.
ex.zh: 收受贿赂而使其声誉受损的政府成员们。

d: n. 折中，妥协；妥协方案，折中办法
v. 妥协，让步；危及，损害

e.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct. (常指不情愿地)

ex.en: Bess finally conceded that Nancy was right.
ex.zh: 贝丝最终承认南希是对的。

ex.en: "Well," he conceded, "I do sometimes mumble a bit."
ex.zh: “嗯，”他承认道，“我有时说话确实有点儿含糊。”

e.en: If you concede something to someone, you allow them to have it as a right or privilege. 给予 (权利或特权)

ex.en: Poland's Communist government conceded the right to establish independent trade unions.
ex.zh: 波兰共产党政府给予了建立独立工会的权力。

e.en: If you concede something, you give it to the person who has been trying to get it from you.

ex.en: The strike by bank employees ended after employers conceded some of their demands.
ex.zh: 银行雇员的罢工在雇主们答应了他们的一些要求之后停止了。

e.en: If you concede a game, contest, or argument, you end it by admitting that you can no longer win. (通过认输而) 使 (比赛、竞赛、争论等)

ex.en: Reiner, 56, has all but conceded the race to his rival.
ex.zh: 56岁的赖纳差一点就向他的对手认输而使比赛结束。

d: v. （通常指不情愿地）承认；认（输），承认（失败）；授予，让与；让对手得分

e.en: A contest is a competition or game that people try to win. 竞赛;

ex.en: Few contests in the recent history of boxing have been as thrilling.
ex.zh: 在近期拳击史上没有几场比赛曾如此惊心动魄。

e.en: A contest is a struggle to win power or control.

ex.en: The state election in November will be the last such ballot before next year's presidential contest.
ex.zh: 11月的州选举将是明年的总统竞选前最后一轮这类投票。

e.en: If you contest a statement or decision, you object to it formally because you think it is wrong or unreasonable.

ex.en: Your former employer has to reply within 14 days in order to contest the case.
ex.zh: 你的前雇主得在14天内做出答复以对本案提出抗辩。

e.en: If someone contests an election or competition, they take part in it and try to win it. 参加 (竞选或比赛)

ex.en: He quickly won his party's nomination to contest the elections.
ex.zh: 他迅速赢得了其党派的提名来参加竞选。

d: adj. 有争议的，受争议的：指某事物或观点存在不同意见或争论。
v. contest 的过去式和过去分词：争夺，角逐（职位、领导权等）；对……提出异议，对……提出抗辩（决定、声明、案件等）。

e.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct. (常指不情愿地)

ex.en: Bess finally conceded that Nancy was right.
ex.zh: 贝丝最终承认南希是对的。

ex.en: "Well," he conceded, "I do sometimes mumble a bit."
ex.zh: “嗯，”他承认道，“我有时说话确实有点儿含糊。”

e.en: If you concede something to someone, you allow them to have it as a right or privilege. 给予 (权利或特权)

ex.en: Poland's Communist government conceded the right to establish independent trade unions.
ex.zh: 波兰共产党政府给予了建立独立工会的权力。

e.en: If you concede something, you give it to the person who has been trying to get it from you.

ex.en: The strike by bank employees ended after employers conceded some of their demands.
ex.zh: 银行雇员的罢工在雇主们答应了他们的一些要求之后停止了。

e.en: If you concede a game, contest, or argument, you end it by admitting that you can no longer win. (通过认输而) 使 (比赛、竞赛、争论等)

ex.en: Reiner, 56, has all but conceded the race to his rival.
ex.zh: 56岁的赖纳差一点就向他的对手认输而使比赛结束。

d: v. concede 的过去式和过去分词：承认，认可（常指不情愿地）；让步，勉强同意；给予（权利、特权等）；认输，承认失败；（体育）失球、失分。

e.en: Someone who is conservative has views that are toward the political right. In the U.S. the Republicans are more conservative than the Democrats, who are more liberal.

ex.en: ...counties whose citizens invariably support the most conservative candidate in any election.
ex.zh: …公民们在任何选举中都千篇一律地支持最保守的候选人的县。

e.en: Conservative is also a noun.

ex.en: The new judge is 50-year-old David Suitor who's regarded as a conservative.
ex.zh: 这名新法官是50岁的、被视为右倾人士的戴维·休特。

e.en: Someone who is conservative or has conservative ideas is unwilling to accept changes and new ideas. (观点)

ex.en: People tend to be more liberal when they're young and more conservative as they get older.
ex.zh: 人们在年轻时常常更开放，年纪越大就越保守。

e.en: If someone dresses in a conservative way, their clothes are conventional in style. (衣着)

ex.en: The girl was well dressed, as usual, though in a more conservative style.
ex.zh: 这个女孩像平常一样穿着得体，但式样则更守旧。

d: n. 保守派，保守主义者；（the Conservatives）保守党；保守党人

e.en: A confrontation is a dispute, fight, or battle between two groups of people. 争执;

ex.en: The commission remains so weak that it will continue to avoid confrontation with governments.
ex.zh: 该委员会依然如此弱小以致它将继续避免和各政府的冲突。

d: n. 对抗，冲突；战斗，战役

e.en: If you declare that something is true, you say that it is true in a firm, deliberate way. You can also declare an attitude or intention. 声明;

ex.en: He declared he would not run for a second term as president.
ex.zh: 他声明不再竞选连任总统。

ex.en: He declared his intention to become the best golfer in the world.
ex.zh: 他表明了要成为世界上最佳高尔夫球手的意愿。

e.en: If you declare something, you state officially and formally that it exists or is the case.

ex.en: The government is ready to declare a permanent ceasefire.
ex.zh: 政府已经准备好宣布永久停火。

ex.en: His lawyers are confident that the judges will declare Mr. Stevens innocent.
ex.zh: 他的律师们确信法官们会宣布史蒂文斯先生无罪。

e.en: If you declare goods that you have bought in another country or money that you have earned, you say how much you have bought or earned so that you can pay tax on it. 申报 (在国外所购之物或收入等)

ex.en: Declaring the wrong income by mistake will no longer lead to an automatic fine.
ex.zh: 由于失误申报收入不符的不再予以自动罚款。

d: v. 宣布，声明；断言，宣称；申报（declare 的现在分词）；（计算机）声明（变量、函数等）

e.en: A person with a physical disability or a serious permanent injury is sometimes referred to as a cripple. 残疾人;

ex.en: She has gone from being a healthy, fit, and sporty young woman to being a cripple.
ex.zh: 她从一个健康、强壮、爱好体育运动的年轻姑娘变成了一个残疾人。

e.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again.

ex.en: Mr. Easton was crippled in an accident and had to leave his job.
ex.zh: 伊斯顿先生在一场事故中受伤致残，不得不离开了工作。

ex.en: He had been warned that another bad fall could cripple him for life.
ex.zh: 他被警告说再一次严重摔跤会使他终身残疾。

d: adj. 肢体残疾的，跛的（用于人时可能含冒犯意味或已过时）；严重受损的，无法正常运转的（多用于飞机、经济等）
v. 使跛足，使残疾，使伤残；严重毁坏或损害，给……造成严重问题（cripple 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: denoting interaction between two or more political parties
e.zh: 代表多党派交叉利益的

ex.en: a cross-party group

d: 跨党派

e.en: If you defend someone or something, you take action in order to protect them.

ex.en: His courage in defending religious and civil rights inspired many outside the church.
ex.zh: 他捍卫宗教权和公民权的勇气鼓舞了许多非教会人士。

e.en: If you defend someone or something when they have been criticized, you argue in support of them.

ex.en: He defended his administration's response to the disaster against critics who charge the federal government is moving too slowly.
ex.zh: 他为他的行政部门对灾难的反应做了争辩，反驳批评人士指控联邦政府行动过于迟缓。

e.en: When a lawyer defends a person who has been accused of something, the lawyer argues on their behalf in a court of law that the charges are not true.

ex.en: ...a lawyer who defended political prisoners during the military regime.
ex.zh: …一位在军权时期为政治犯进行辩护的律师。

ex.en: He has hired a lawyer to defend him against the allegation.
ex.zh: 他已聘请一位律师为他所受的指控辩护。

e.en: When a sports player plays in the tournament which they won the previous time it was held, you can say that they are defending their title.

ex.en: Torrence expects to defend her title successfully in the next Olympics.
ex.zh: 托伦斯希望下届奥运会能成功卫冕。

d: adj. 防御中的，防守型的，防守的
v. 防护，防卫；为……辩护；防守（defend 的现在分词）；卫冕，竞赛中保护（头衔）
vt. 批评；评论；评判（criticize 的英式拼写）
vi. 批评；评论（criticize 的英式拼写）

e.en: When there is a coup, a group of people seize power in a country.

ex.en: ...a military coup.
ex.zh: …一次军事政变。

e.en: A coup is an achievement which is thought to be especially good because it was very difficult.

ex.en: The sale is a big coup for the auction house.
ex.zh: 这次拍卖额对该拍卖行而言是极为难得的成就。

d: n. 政变；成功之举，妙计；突然的一击，漂亮的一击；主球径自入袋；（北美印第安人中）触碰敌人（以示勇气），抢先触碰敌人的物品（以示占有）
v. 使……颠倒，使……倾斜
【名】 （Coup）（法）库普（人名）
n. 德米特里（俄罗斯钢琴家）

e.en: If you say that someone is defiant, you mean they show aggression or independence by refusing to obey someone. 挑战的;

ex.en: The players are in a defiant mood as they prepare for tomorrow's game.
ex.zh: 在准备明天的比赛时，球员们态度挑衅。

e.en: 挑战地;

ex.en: They defiantly rejected any talk of a compromise.
ex.zh: 他们轻蔑地拒绝了任何妥协谈判。

d: adj. 违抗的，反叛的，蔑视的

e.en: A deputy is the second most important person in an organization such as a business or government department. Someone's deputy often acts on their behalf when they are not there.

ex.en: ...Jack Lang, France's minister for culture, and his deputy, Catherine Tasca.
ex.zh: …法国文化部长杰克·朗和他的副手凯瑟琳·塔斯卡。

e.en: In some legislatures, the elected members are called deputies.

ex.en: The president appealed to deputies to approve the plan quickly.
ex.zh: 总统呼吁议员们迅速通过该方案。

e.en: A deputy is a police officer.

ex.en: Robyn asked the deputy on duty if she could speak with Sheriff Adkins.
ex.zh: 萝宾问值班警官她能否跟县治安官阿德金斯谈话。

e.en: A deputy is a person appointed to act on another person's behalf.

ex.en: His brother was acting as his deputy in America.
ex.zh: 他的兄弟充当他在美洲的代理人。

d: n. 代理人，副手，副职；代表，议员；（美国协助地方治安官办案的）警官
adj. 副的；代理的

e.en: Democracy is a system of government in which people choose their rulers by voting for them in elections.

ex.en: The spread of democracy in Eastern Europe appears to have had negative as well as positive consequences.
ex.zh: 东欧民主政体的蔓延看来既有消极也有积极的影响。

e.en: A democracy is a country in which the people choose their government by voting for it.

ex.en: The new democracies face tough challenges.
ex.zh: 新生的民主国家面临严峻的挑战。

d: n. 民主政体；民主国家；民主，民主精神

e.en: A draft is an early version of a letter, book, or speech. 草稿;

ex.en: I rewrote his rough draft, which was published under my name.
ex.zh: 我改写了他那篇以我的名义发表了的初稿。

ex.en: I faxed a first draft of this article to him.
ex.zh: 我把这篇文章的初稿传真给他。

e.en: A draft is a written order for payment of money by a bank, especially from one bank to another.

ex.en: Payments must be made in U.S. dollars by a bank draft drawn to the order of the United Nations Postal Administration.
ex.zh: 付款必须用开给联合国邮政管理处的银行汇票，并以美元支付。

e.en: A draft is a current of air that comes into a place in an undesirable way. (钻进某处的)

ex.en: Block drafts around doors and windows.
ex.zh: 挡住门窗周围的风。

e.en: When you draft a letter, book, or speech, you write the first version of it.

ex.en: He drafted a letter to the editors.
ex.zh: 他草拟了一封给编辑的信。

d: v. 草拟，起草；征召；选派；挑选；设计，绘制草图（draft 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: To destroy something means to cause so much damage to it that it is completely ruined or does not exist any more.

ex.en: That's a sure recipe for destroying the economy and creating chaos.
ex.zh: 那是一个摧毁经济、制造混乱的注定因素。

e.en: To destroy someone means to ruin their life or to make their situation impossible to bear.

ex.en: If I was younger or more naive, the criticism would have destroyed me.
ex.zh: 要是我年轻点儿或幼稚点儿，这批评可能已经把我毁了。

e.en: If an animal is destroyed, it is killed, either because it is ill or because it is dangerous.

ex.en: Lindsay was unhurt but the horse had to be destroyed.
ex.zh: 林赛没被伤着，但那匹马不得不被宰掉。

d: v. 破坏，毁灭；杀死，人道毁灭（受伤、生病或危险的动物）；彻底打败，击溃；毁掉……的生活，使垮掉

e.en: Duty is work that you have to do for your job.

ex.en: Staff must report for duty at their normal place of work.
ex.zh: 职员必须到他们平常的岗位报到上班。

e.en: Your duties are tasks which you have to do because they are part of your job.

ex.en: I carried out my duties conscientiously.
ex.zh: 我认真执行了我的各项职责。

e.en: If you say that something is your duty, you believe that you ought to do it because it is your responsibility.

ex.en: I consider it my duty to write to you and thank you.
ex.zh: 我觉得我有责任给你写信表示感谢。

e.en: Duties are taxes which you pay to the government on goods that you buy.

ex.en: Import duties still average 30%.
ex.zh: 进口关税平均仍为30%。

d: n. 关税；责任，义务，职责（duty 的复数）

e.en: You use elderly as a polite way of saying that someone is old.

ex.en: There was an elderly couple on the terrace.
ex.zh: 露台上有一对上年纪的老人。

e.en: The elderly are people who are old.

ex.en: The elderly are a formidable force in any election.
ex.zh: 老年人在任何选举中都是一股强大的力量。

d: adj. 上了年纪的；老掉牙的
n. 老人（the elderly）

e.en: If you exercise something such as your authority, your rights, or a good quality, you use it or put it into effect. 行使;

ex.en: They are merely exercising their right to free speech.
ex.zh: 他们仅仅是在行使言论自由的权利。

e.en: Exercise is also a noun. 行使;

ex.en: Social structures are maintained through the exercise of political and economic power.
ex.zh: 社会结构是通过政治和经济权力的运用来维护的。

e.en: When you exercise, you move your body energetically in order to get in shape and to remain healthy.

ex.en: She exercises two or three times a week.
ex.zh: 她一周锻炼两三次。

e.en: Exercise is also a noun.

ex.en: Lack of exercise can lead to feelings of depression and exhaustion.
ex.zh: 锻炼的缺乏会导致抑郁和疲倦感。

d: n. 运动，锻炼；（一套）动作，体操；练习，演练；运用；活动，任务；典礼；宗教仪式，礼拜
v. 运动，锻炼；运用，行使；使担忧，使烦恼；驯，遛

e.en: Flared skirts or trousers are wider at the bottom or at the end of the legs than at the top. (裙子或裤子)

ex.en: In the 1970s they all had flared trousers.
ex.zh: 20世纪70年代，他们都有喇叭裤。

d: adj. （裙、裤等）向外展开的，喇叭形的；（鼻孔、管口等）张开的，扩口的
v. 闪光，闪亮；突然爆发；向外张开（flare 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that is extensive covers or includes a large physical area.

ex.en: ...an extensive tour of Latin America.
ex.zh: …在拉丁美洲的一次大范围的观光。

e.en: 广阔地

ex.en: Mark, however, needs to travel extensively with his varied business interests.
ex.zh: 然而，马克因各种各样的商业利益而需要四处旅行。

e.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide range of details, ideas, or items.

ex.en: She recently completed an extensive study of elected officials who began their political careers before the age of 35.
ex.zh: 她最近完成了一项对35岁前开始政治生涯的当选的官员的广泛研究。

e.en: 广泛地

ex.en: All these issues have been extensively researched in recent years.
ex.zh: 所有这些问题近年来都得到广泛地研究。

d: adj. 广阔的；广泛的；巨大的，大量的；（农业）粗放（经营）的

e.en: If someone forces you to do something, they make you do it even though you do not want to, for example, by threatening you.

ex.en: He took two women hostage and forced them to drive away from the area.
ex.zh: 他劫持了两名女人质并强迫她们开车离开这个地区。

ex.en: They were grabbed by three men who appeared to force them into a car.
ex.zh: 他们被三名男子抓住，这些人看上去强使他们进入了一辆汽车。

e.en: If a situation or event forces you to do something, it makes it necessary for you to do something that you would not otherwise have done.

ex.en: A back injury forced her to withdraw from Wimbledon.
ex.zh: 一处背伤迫使她退出了温布尔登网球赛。

ex.en: He turned right, down a dirt road that forced him into four-wheel drive.
ex.zh: 他向右转弯，开上了一条土路，这迫使他开始四轮驱动行驶。

e.en: If someone forces something on or upon you, they make you accept or use it when you would prefer not to.

ex.en: To force this agreement on the nation is wrong.
ex.zh: 把这项协议强加于这个国家是错误的。

e.en: If you force something into a particular position, you use a lot of strength to make it move there.

ex.en: They were forcing her head under the icy waters, drowning her.
ex.zh: 他们在用力把她的头按到冰冷的水中，淹她。

d: adj. （桥牌）逼叫的
v. 强迫，迫使（force 的现在分词/动名词）；强行通过，强行打开；用力推进；用强迫手段获得；竭力推；使发生；强作（笑颜）；（园艺/农业）人工催熟，促成栽培；将（跑垒员）封杀出局

e.en: Following a particular event means after that event.

ex.en: In the centuries following Christ's death, Christians genuinely believed the world was about to end.
ex.zh: 在耶稣死后的几个世纪里，基督徒们真地认为世界将要消亡。

e.en: The following day, week, or year is the day, week, or year after the one you have just mentioned. 其后的 (日、月、年等)

ex.en: The following day the picture appeared on the front pages of every newspaper in the world.
ex.zh: 次日，照片出现在世界各地报纸的头版。

ex.en: We went to dinner the following Monday evening.
ex.zh: 在接下来的那个周一晚上我们一起共进晚餐。

e.en: You use following to refer to something that you are about to mention.

ex.en: Write down the following information: name of product, type, date purchased and price.
ex.zh: 写下以下信息：产品名称、型号、购买日期和价格。

e.en: The following refers to the thing or things that you are about to mention.

ex.en: The following is a paraphrase of what was said.
ex.zh: 以下是对所说内容的解释。

d: adj. 之后的，接下来的；下列的，以下的；顺风的
n. 追随者，拥护者
prep. 在……之后，紧接着
v. 跟随；沿行；（时间、顺序）排在……之后（follow 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to do anything about the problems it creates.

ex.en: These questions frustrated me.
ex.zh: 这些问题使我懊丧。

e.en: 懊丧的

ex.en: Roberta felt frustrated and angry.
ex.zh: 罗伯塔感到又懊丧又生气。

e.en: If someone or something frustrates a plan or attempt to do something, they prevent it from succeeding.

ex.en: The government has deliberately frustrated his efforts to gain work permits for his foreign staff.
ex.zh: 政府蓄意挫败了他为其外国员工取得工作许可证的努力。

d: adj. 懊恼的，沮丧的，失望的；失意的，不得志的；无效的，没有得到满足的；（在性方面）受挫的，压抑的
v. 使懊恼，使沮丧；挫败，阻挠；受挫（frustrate 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A gambit is an action or set of actions which you carry out in order to try to gain an advantage in a situation or game.

ex.en: He sees the proposal as more of a diplomatic gambit than a serious defence proposal.
ex.zh: 他认为与其说这是一项严肃的防御计划，不如说是一种抢占先机的外交策略。

ex.en: Campaign strategists are calling the plan a clever political gambit.
ex.zh: 竞选战略家们把这项计划称作一个狡猾的政治策略。

e.en: A gambit is a remark which you make to someone in order to start or continue a conversation with them.

ex.en: His favourite opening gambit is: "You are so beautiful, will you be my next wife?"
ex.zh: 他最喜欢的开场白是：“你真漂亮。愿意做我的下一任妻子吗？”

ex.en: Bernard made no response to Tom's conversational gambits.
ex.zh: 伯纳德没有回应汤姆对话的开场白。

d: n. （国际象棋）以取得优势的开局棋法，常指主动牺牲兵或其他棋子；为抢占先机而采取的策略，占先的一着；为开始或延续交谈而说的开场白；（首字母大写）漫威漫画中的超级英雄，中文常译作“金牌手”“牌皇”“牌王”
政府支持的
政府担保的

e.en: Genuine is used to describe people and things that are exactly what they appear to be, and are not false or an imitation.

ex.en: There was a risk of genuine refugees being returned to Vietnam.
ex.zh: 有把真正的难民遣送回越南的风险。

ex.en: ...genuine leather.
ex.zh: …真皮。

e.en: Genuine refers to things such as emotions that are real and not pretended.

ex.en: If this offer is genuine, I will gladly accept it.
ex.zh: 如果这份帮助是真诚的，我将愉快地接受它。

e.en: 真诚地

ex.en: He was genuinely surprised.
ex.zh: 他真得吃了一惊。

e.en: If you describe a person as genuine, you approve of them because they are honest, truthful, and sincere in the way they live and in their relationships with other people.

ex.en: She is very caring and very genuine.
ex.zh: 她很有同情心，也非常诚实可靠。

d: adj. 真正的，非伪造的；真诚的，真心的

e.en: A handbag is a small bag which a woman uses to carry things such as her money and keys in when she goes out.

d: n. 手提包；手袋（通常指女式）
v. （英式，非正式）抨击；严厉批评
n. 赫尔辛基（芬兰首都）

e.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

ex.en: Further investigation was hindered by the loss of all documentation on the case.
ex.zh: 由于有关此案的材料全部丢失，进一步的调查受到了阻碍。

e.en: If something hinders your movement, it makes it difficult for you to move forward or move around.

ex.en: A thigh injury increasingly hindered her mobility.
ex.zh: 大腿上的伤愈发束缚了她的活动自由。

e.en: situated at or further towards the back or rear; posterior 后面的;

ex.en: the hinder parts

d: v. hinder 的现在分词/动名词；妨碍，阻碍
adj. 阻碍的，妨碍的

e.en: A hound is a type of dog that is often used for hunting or racing. 猎犬;

ex.en: Rainey's chief interest in life is hunting with hounds.
ex.zh: 雷尼一生中的主要嗜好是带着猎犬去打猎。

e.en: (in combination)

ex.en: an otterhound
a deerhound

e.en: either of a pair of horizontal bars that reinforce the running gear of a horse-drawn vehicle
If someone hounds you, they constantly disturb or speak to you in an annoying or upsetting way. (不断地)

ex.en: Newcomers are constantly hounding them for advice.
ex.zh: 新来的人老是缠着他们问这问那的。

d: v. 追捕；纠缠，骚扰（hound 的现在分词）
n. 追逼，纠缠（动词 hound 的动名词用法）；（海事）桅肩

e.en: If you impose something on people, you use your authority to force them to accept it.

ex.en: Fines are imposed on retailers who sell tobacco to minors.
ex.zh: 向未成年人销售烟草制品的零售商要被强制罚款。

ex.en: A third of companies reviewing pay since last August have imposed a pay freeze of up to a year.
ex.zh: 自去年8月以来，在审检工资发放的公司中，有三分之一已经强行实施工资冻结长达1年。

e.en: 强制实行

ex.en: ...the imposition of sanctions against Pakistan.
ex.zh: …对巴基斯坦制裁的强制实行。

e.en: If you impose your opinions or beliefs on other people, you try and make people accept them as a rule or as a model to copy. 把 (观点、信仰等)

ex.en: Parents should beware of imposing their own tastes on their children.
ex.zh: 父母应该提防把自己的兴趣强加给孩子。

e.en: If something imposes strain, pressure, or suffering on someone, it causes them to experience it. 使承受 (令人不快之事物)

ex.en: The filming imposed an additional strain on her.
ex.zh: 影片拍摄使她承受了额外的压力。

d: v. 强制实行；把……强加于；征收（impose 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 强加的；强制规定的

e.en: If you insist that something should be done, you say so very firmly and refuse to give in about it. If you insist on something, you say firmly that it must be done or provided. 坚持认为;

ex.en: My family insisted that I should not give in, but stay and fight.
ex.zh: 我家人坚持认为我不应该屈服，而应该留下来斗争。

ex.en: She insisted on being present at all the interviews.
ex.zh: 她坚决要求出席所有的采访。

e.en: If you insist that something is the case, you say so very firmly and refuse to say otherwise, even though other people do not believe you.

ex.en: The president insisted that he was acting out of compassion, not political opportunism.
ex.zh: 总统坚持说他这么做是出于同情而不是政治投机。

ex.en: "It's not that difficult," she insists.
ex.zh: “事情并没有像想的那么难，”她坚持说。

d: v. insist 的过去式和过去分词；坚持；坚称，坚决认为（某事属实）；执意要求，坚决要求（某事必须做到或提供）

e.en: If you intend to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

ex.en: Maybe he intends to leave her.
ex.zh: 也许他打算离开她。

ex.en: What do you intend doing when you get to this place?
ex.zh: 你打算到这里干什么？

e.en: If something is intended for a particular purpose, it has been planned to fulfil that purpose. If something is intended for a particular person, it has been planned to be used by that person or to affect them in some way. 被用于 (某目的或某人)

ex.en: This money is intended for the development of the tourist industry.
ex.zh: 这笔钱是准备用于发展旅游业的。

ex.en: Columns are usually intended in architecture to add grandeur and status.
ex.zh: 柱子被用于建筑通常是为了增添宏伟和高贵。

e.en: If you intend a particular idea or feeling in something that you say or do, you want to express it or want it to be understood.

ex.en: He didn't intend any sarcasm.
ex.zh: 他没有任何讽刺的意思。

ex.en: Barzun's response seemed a little patronizing, though he undoubtedly hadn't intended it that way.
ex.zh: 巴曾的反应好像显得有点屈尊俯就，但无疑他不是想要那样。

d: v. 打算，想要；意指，意思是；准备，预留（作某种用途或给某人用）

e.en: Interim is used to describe something that is intended to be used until something permanent is done or established.

ex.en: She was sworn in as head of an interim government in March.
ex.zh: 她3月份宣誓出任临时政府首脑。

e.en: In the interim means until a particular thing happens or until a particular thing happened.

ex.en: But, in the interim, we obviously have a duty to maintain law and order.
ex.zh: 但是，在过渡时期我们显然有责任维持法律与秩序。

d: adj. 暂时的，过渡期间的，间歇的；决算前的，中间时期的
n. 过渡期，中间期；中期利润，阶段性成果

e.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

ex.en: The situation calmed down when police intervened.
ex.zh: 警察干预后，局势平静了下来。

e.en: If you intervene, you interrupt a conversation in order to add something to it.

ex.en: Hernandez intervened and told me to stop it.
ex.zh: 贺尔南德兹插话，不让我再说下去。

e.en: If an event intervenes, it happens suddenly in a way that stops, delays, or prevents something from happening.

ex.en: The mailboat arrived on Friday mornings unless bad weather intervened.
ex.zh: 除非受到恶劣天气的干扰，邮船于星期五上午到达。

d: v. 干预，干涉；插话，打岔；干扰，阻挠；发生于其间，介于中间；调停，斡旋

e.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do. 恐吓;

ex.en: Jones had set out to intimidate and dominate Paul.
ex.zh: 琼斯曾试图威胁并控制保罗。

e.en: 威胁

ex.en: ...an inquiry into allegations of intimidation during last week's vote.
ex.zh: …一项对上周选举期间恐吓指控的调查。

d: v. 恫吓，威胁

e.en: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

ex.en: Agents will raise the issue of prize-money for next year's world championships.
ex.zh: 代理商们会提出明年世界锦标赛的奖金问题。
