ex.zh: 一些鸟类可能彼此紧挨着筑巢。

e.en: A nest is a home that a group of insects or other creatures make in order to live in and give birth to their young in. (昆虫或其他动物的)

ex.en: Some solitary bees make their nests in burrows in the soil.
ex.zh: 一些独居的蜜蜂将它们的巢筑在土壤中的洞穴里。

d: n. 窝，巢，穴；舒适的居所，安乐窝；（套叠的）一套物件，一组物件；藏匿处，秘密窝点
v. （鸟类）筑巢，做窝；（一套物件）逐个套叠；嵌套（信息）；找鸟巢
【名】 （Nest）（英）内丝特，（德）内丝特（人名）

e.en: In the armed forces, an officer is a person in a position of authority.

ex.en: ...a retired army officer.
ex.zh: …一位退役陆军军官。

e.en: Members of the police force can be referred to as officers. 警察;

ex.en: The officer saw no obvious signs of a break-in.
ex.zh: 那个警察没看到任何闯入的明显痕迹。

ex.en: Officer Montoya was first on the scene.
ex.zh: 蒙托亚警官是第一个到达现场的人。

e.en: An officer is a person who has a responsible position in an organization, especially a government organization. (尤指政府部门的)

ex.en: ...a local authority education officer.
ex.zh: …一名地方政府教育官员。

d: n. 军官；（政府或大机构的）官员，高级职员；警察，警官；船长；某一荣誉等级中的一分子（如英帝国勋位中四等勋爵士以下的级别）
v. 配备军官；指挥
【名】 （Officer）（英）奥菲瑟（人名）

e.en: Something that is oily is covered with oil or contains oil. 涂满油的;

ex.en: He was wiping his hands on an oily rag.
ex.zh: 他在一块油乎乎的抹布上擦着双手。

e.en: Oily means looking, feeling, tasting, or smelling like oil. 油状的;

ex.en: ...traces of an oily substance.
ex.zh: …一种油状物质的痕迹。

d: adj. 含油的，涂油的；（食物）含油多的，富含脂肪的；（头发或皮肤）油质的，油性的；（质地、味道、气味、形态）像油的；（人，行为）油滑的，讨好的

e.en: If something is pale, it is very light in colour or almost white. 浅色的;

ex.en: Migrating birds filled the pale sky.
ex.zh: 迁徙的鸟布满了灰白的天空。

ex.en: As we age, our skin becomes paler.
ex.zh: 随着我们变老，我们的皮肤变得更加苍白。

e.en: Pale is also a combining form. (用于构成合成词)

ex.en: ...a pale blue sailor dress.
ex.zh: …一件浅蓝色的水手服。

e.en: If someone looks pale, their face looks a lighter colour than usual, usually because they are ill, frightened, or shocked. (脸色)

ex.en: She looked pale and tired.
ex.zh: 她看起来苍白而疲惫。

e.en: to make or become pale or paler; blanch

d: adj. （脸色）苍白的；（颜色）浅的，淡的；（光线）暗淡的，微弱的；较差的，逊色的
v. （脸色）变苍白；（颜色）变淡，变浅；使褪色；显得逊色，相形见绌；用板条围
n. （做桩篱用的）板条，尖桩；（喻）界限，范围；（纹章）（盾形中部的）垂直宽条；（俄国）犹太人居住区
【名】 （Pale）（塞）帕莱（人名）

e.en: a wooden construction around an opening in a deck, as to support a mast (支撑船桅的)
e.zh: 围着甲板周边空旷地区的木质建筑

d: n. 伙伴，搭档（partner 的复数形式）；伴侣，配偶；合作伙伴，贸易伙伴；合伙人（法律、商业）
v. 合伙；成为…的搭档，合作（partner 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

ex.en: This ability to persevere despite obstacles and setbacks is the quality people most admire in others.
ex.zh: 这种不管障碍和挫折的锲而不舍的能力是人们最为钦佩的品质。

ex.en: ...a school with a reputation for persevering with difficult and disruptive children.
ex.zh: …一所因坚持不懈地教诲难管捣蛋的学生而闻名的学校。

d: adj. 坚忍的，不屈不挠的
v. 坚持，锲而不舍（persevere 的现在分词和动名词）

e.en: A plain object, surface, or fabric is entirely in one colour and has no pattern, design, or writing on it.

ex.en: In general, a plain carpet makes a room look bigger.
ex.zh: 一般来讲，纯色的地毯使房间显得更大。

ex.en: He placed the paper in a plain envelope.
ex.zh: 他把论文放在一个空白信封里。

e.en: Something that is plain is very simple in style.

ex.en: It was a plain, grey stone house.
ex.zh: 这是一座简朴的灰色石头房子。

e.en: 朴素地

ex.en: He was very tall and plainly dressed.
ex.zh: 他个子很高，穿着朴素。

e.en: If a fact, situation, or statement is plain, it is easy to recognize or understand.

ex.en: It was plain to him that I was having a nervous breakdown.
ex.zh: 我那时神经衰弱，他是清楚的。

d: adj. 无装饰的，朴素的；单色的，无花纹的；单纯的，不掺杂的；显而易见的；（书面或口头用法）表达清楚的；直截了当的，坦率的；相貌平平的；普通的；直呼其名的；完全的；（编织）平针的
adv. 完全地，简直；明白地，不含糊地
n. （大）平原；（编织的）平针；朴实无华的东西
【名】 （Plain）（英）普莱恩，（法）普兰（人名）

e.en: Pollen is a fine powder produced by flowers. It fertilizes other flowers of the same species so that they produce seeds.

d: n.  花粉
【名】 （Pollen）波伦（人名）

e.en: The population of a country or area is all the people who live in it.

ex.en: Bangladesh now has a population of about 110 million.
ex.zh: 孟加拉国现有约一亿一千万人口。

ex.en: ...the annual rate of population growth.
ex.zh: …人口年增长率。

e.en: If you refer to a particular type of population in a country or area, you are referring to all the people or animals of that type there. (某种) 人群;

ex.en: ...75.6 percent of the male population over sixteen.
ex.zh: …16岁以上男性人群的75.6％。

ex.en: ...areas with a large black population.
ex.zh: …有大批黑人群体的的各地区。

d: n. 人口，总人口，全体居民（population 的复数形式，常指多个地区或群体的人口）；（某类）人群，群体（常与 urban、aging 等形容词连用）；（生物学、农业科学）种群；（统计学）总体，母体

e.en: A programme of actions or events is a series of actions or events that are planned to be done.

ex.en: The nation's largest training and education programme for adults.
ex.zh: 该国最大的成人培训与教育计划。

e.en: A television or radio programme is something that is broadcast on television or radio. (电视、广播)

ex.en: ...a network television programme.
ex.zh: …一个网络电视节目。

e.en: A theatre or concert programme is a small book or sheet of paper that gives information about the play or concert you are attending. (戏剧、音乐会的)

ex.en: When you go to concerts, it's helpful to read the programme.
ex.zh: 去音乐会的时候，看看节目单是有帮助的。

d: n. 计划，方案；（电视或广播的）节目；（戏剧或音乐会等演出的）说明书，节目单；（活动的）计划表，程序单；课程；（计算机等的）程序，程序设计
v. （给计算机）编写程序，设计程序；调好，设置（机器使之按某种方式运作）；使……有倾向，使按某种方式行事；计划，安排

e.en: a rule that moves a constituent from an embedded clause into the main clause 提升;
e.zh: 将嵌入句成分移到主句中的语法规则

d: n. 增加，提高
v. 提升，举起；（使）直立，站立；建造，树立（纪念碑等）（raise 的现在分词）

e.en: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind. (同类事物的)

ex.en: A wide range of colours and patterns are available.
ex.zh: 一系列各种各样的颜色和图案都有。

e.en: A range is the complete group that is included between two points on a scale of measurement or quality.

ex.en: The average age range is between 35 and 55.
ex.zh: 平均年龄范围是35至55岁。

e.en: The range of something is the maximum area in which it can reach things or detect things. (能够到达或探知的)

ex.en: The 120mm mortar has a range of 18,000 yards.
ex.zh: 口径120毫米的迫击炮的射程是1.8万码。

e.en: If things range between two points or range from one point to another, they vary within these points on a scale of measurement or quality. (在一定幅度内)

ex.en: They range in price from $3 to $15.
ex.zh: 它们的价格在$3到$15之间变化。

ex.en: ...offering merchandise ranging from the everyday to the esoteric.
ex.zh: …出售的商品包括日常用品到少数人使用的特别物品。

d: n. （变动或浮动的）范围，界限；视觉（或听觉）范围；射程，射击距离；一系列；成套产品，系列商品；山脉；牧场，牧区；靶场，射击场，炸弹试验场；（尤指旧时的）炉灶；一排建筑物；方向，走向；（飞机等交通工具的）续航距离
v. （在一定的范围内）变化，变动；（按一定位置或顺序）排列，排序；徘徊，四处移动；（文章或讲话）涉及，包括 ；（枪、炮、射击后校准）测距，（用雷达或激光）测距；支持，反对；自然生长，分布；与……联合起来，加入……行列
adj. （生活方式）有秩序的，安定的

e.en: If a sick person makes a recovery, he or she becomes well again.

ex.en: He made a remarkable recovery from a shin injury.
ex.zh: 他胫骨伤恢复得相当好。

e.en: When there is a recovery in a country's economy, it improves. 好转;

ex.en: Interest-rate cuts have failed to bring about economic recovery.
ex.zh: 利率的降低未能带来经济的复苏。

e.en: You talk about the recovery of something when you get it back after it has been lost or stolen.

ex.en: A substantial reward is being offered for the recovery of a painting by Turner.
ex.zh: 一笔巨额悬赏正被用来找回特纳的一幅油画。

e.en: You talk about the recovery of someone's physical or mental state when they return to this state. 复原;

ex.en: ...the abrupt loss and recovery of consciousness.
ex.zh: …意识的突然失去和恢复。

d: n. 康复，痊愈；戒除；恢复，复苏；（供刚做完手术的病人使用的）监护室；（被拿走或失去的东西的）复得，找回；收回的物品（资金）；（破损车辆或坠毁飞机）回收修理；（高尔夫）挽回败局之击，复原之击（击回球道或球穴区）；（美橄）重新获球；（划船，自行车赛，游泳）还原至预备姿势（如回桨等）；回收利用（能源、化工品等）

e.en: If someone is ready, they are properly prepared for something. If something is ready, it has been properly prepared and is now able to be used.

ex.en: It took her a long time to get ready for church.
ex.zh: 她花了很长时间才准备好去教堂。

ex.en: Are you ready to board, Mr. Daly?
ex.zh: 准备好上飞机了吗，戴利先生？

e.en: If you are ready for something or ready to do something, you have enough experience to do it or you are old enough and sensible enough to do it. 胜任的;

ex.en: She says she's not ready for marriage.
ex.zh: 她说她还没有准备好结婚。

e.en: If you are ready to do something, you are willing to do it.

ex.en: They were ready to die for their beliefs.
ex.zh: 他们愿意为信仰而献身。

e.en: If you are ready for something, you need it or want it.

ex.en: I don't know about you, but I'm ready for bed.
ex.zh: 我不知道你怎样，但我想去睡了。

d: adj. （某人）准备好（做某事）的；预先备好的，可供使用的；乐意的；方便使用的，现成的；迅速的，敏捷的；即将……的；需要的，想要的
n. 现款（the ready/readies）；预备好的状态
adv. 已做完，已完成
v. 做好……的准备

e.en: If two or more things are related, there is a connection between them.

ex.en: The philosophical problems of chance and of free will are closely related.
ex.zh: 关于偶然性和自由意志的哲学问题是紧密相联的。

e.en: People who are related belong to the same family.

ex.en: The children, although not related to us by blood, had become as dear to us as our own.
ex.zh: 这些孩子，虽然和我们没有血缘上的亲属关系，也变得像我们亲生的一样亲了。

e.en: If you say that different types of things, such as languages, are related, you mean that they developed from the same language. (语言)

ex.en: He recognized that Sanskrit, the language of India, was related very closely to Latin, Greek, and the Germanic and Celtic languages.
ex.zh: 他认识到梵语，即印度的语言，与拉丁语、希腊语、日尔曼语和凯尔特语密切同源。

d: adj. 相关的，有联系的；有亲戚关系的；（动植物、语言等）同类的，同族的；讲述的，叙述的
v. 联系，有关联；叙述，讲述；认同，理解（relate 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you rely on someone or something, you need them and depend on them in order to live or work properly. 依赖;

ex.en: They relied heavily on the advice of their professional advisers.
ex.zh: 他们非常依赖专业顾问的建议。

e.en: If you can rely on someone to work well or to behave as you want them to, you can trust them to do this. 信任;

ex.en: I know I can rely on you to sort it out.
ex.zh: 我知道我可以信赖你来处理此事。

d: v. 相信，信赖；依靠，依赖（rely 的第三人称单数，常与 on/upon 连用）

e.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid, it produces it.

ex.en: The sweat glands secrete water.
ex.zh: 汗腺分泌汗液。

e.en: If you secrete something somewhere, you hide it there so that nobody will find it.

ex.en: She secreted the gun in the kitchen cabinet.
ex.zh: 她把枪藏在了厨房的橱柜里。

d: v. （动植物或其细胞）分泌；隐藏，藏匿（小物件）
n. 索尔兹伯里市（津巴布韦，原罗得西亚首都）

e.en: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example, whether they are round, square, curved, or fat. 外形;

ex.en: Each mirror is made to order and can be designed to almost any shape or size.
ex.zh: 每面镜子都是定制做的，而且能设计成几乎任何形状或规格。

ex.en: ...little pens in the shape of baseball bats.
ex.zh: …棒球球棒形状的小钢笔。

e.en: You can refer to something that you can see as a shape if you cannot see it clearly, or if its outline is the clearest or most striking aspect of it. (模糊的)

ex.en: The great grey shape of a tank rolled out of the village.
ex.zh: 一个坦克状的巨大灰影从村子里开了出来。

e.en: A shape is a space enclosed by an outline, for example, a circle, a square, or a triangle.

ex.en: Imagine a sort of a kidney shape.
ex.zh: 想像一种类似肾脏的形状。

e.en: The shape of something that is planned or organized is its structure and character. (计划或组织的)

ex.en: The last two weeks have seen a lot of talk about the future shape of Europe.
ex.zh: 在过去的两周里有许多关于欧洲的未来格局的讨论。

d: n. 形状，外形；形态，特征；状况，身体状况；健壮；（朦胧的）影像；（事物平常或本来的）样子；有序的排列，条理清楚；伪装，假装；特定形状的东西，模型；身材
vt. 形成，影响；使成形，塑造；计划，思考出；产生（声音，词）；使适合，使符合；（运动员）摆姿势，做动作
【名】 （Shape）（瑞典）沙佩（人名）

e.en: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment. 股份;

ex.en: People in China are eager to buy shares in new businesses.
ex.zh: 中国民众热衷于购买新企业的股票。

e.en: If you share something with another person, you both have it, use it, or occupy it. You can also say that two people share something. 共有; 共用;

ex.en: ...the small income he had shared with his brother from his father's estate.
ex.zh: …他和他兄弟分享从他父亲的地产中得来的一小笔收入。

ex.en: Two Americans will share this year's Nobel Prize for Medicine.
ex.zh: 两位美国人将共同摘得今年的诺贝尔医学奖。

e.en: If you share a task, duty, or responsibility with someone, you each carry out or accept part of it. You can also say that two people share something. 共同承担;

ex.en: You can find out whether they are prepared to share the cost of the flowers with you.
ex.zh: 你会发现他们是否准备与你分摊鲜花的费用。

e.en: If you share an experience with someone, you have the same experience, often because you are with them at the time. You can also say that two people share something. 共享 (经历)

ex.en: Yes, I want to share my life with you.
ex.zh: 是的，我想和你共享生活。

d: v. 共享，合用；分享；分配；分担（责任），分摊（费用）；共同拥有（看法、特质或经历）；倾诉，吐露
n. 股份，股票；（共有财产的）部分所有权；责任，贡献；份额；（某物的）一个合理（或正常）的量
【名】 （Share）（美）沙雷（人名）

e.en: A shrill sound is high-pitched and unpleasant. (声音)

ex.en: Shrill cries and startled oaths flew up around us as pandemonium broke out.
ex.zh: 骚乱爆发时，我们周围充斥着尖厉的哭喊声和难听的咒骂声。

ex.en: ...the shrill whistle of the engine.
ex.zh: …那发动机的尖啸声。

d: adj. （声音）尖锐的，刺耳的；（引申，多含贬义）尖刻激烈的，咄咄逼人的
vi. 尖声喊叫；发出尖锐刺耳的声音
vt. 尖声喊出，尖声说出（话、警告等）
n. 尖叫声；尖锐刺耳的声音

e.en: A sighting of something, especially something unusual or unexpected is an occasion on which it is seen.

ex.en: ...the sighting of a rare sea bird at Lundy island.
ex.zh: …在隆地岛见到一种珍稀海鸟。

d: n. 目击，看见（尤指看到罕见或意外的事物）；（技术）瞄准，照准
v. 看见；瞄准（均为 sight 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: If one thing is similar to another, or if two things are similar, they have features that are the same.

ex.en: ...a savoury cake with a texture similar to that of carrot cake.
ex.zh: …一块口感跟胡萝卜饼差不多的咸味饼。

ex.en: The accident was similar to one that happened in 1973.
ex.zh: 这起事故跟1973年发生的那起相似。

d: adj. 相像的，类似的；（几何图形）相似的
n. 相似之人（或物）；顺势药物（指疗效与某些疾病症状相似的药物，为顺势疗法的基础）

e.en: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens. 场地;

ex.en: I was working as a foreman on a building site.
ex.zh: 我在一个建筑工地当工头。

e.en: The site of an important event is the place where it happened. (事件发生的) 现场;

ex.en: Scientists have described the Aral sea as the site of the worst ecological disaster on earth.
ex.zh: 科学家们把咸海描绘成地球上生态环境最差的地方。

e.en: A site is a piece of ground where something such as a statue or building stands or used to stand. 地点; 遗址;

ex.en: ...the site of Moses' tomb.
ex.zh: …摩西墓遗址。

e.en: A site is the same as a .

d: n. 地点，位置；场所；网站，站点；遗址，古迹（site 的复数）
v. 为……选址，使坐落于（site 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A snag is a small problem or disadvantage. 小问题;

ex.en: A police clampdown on car thieves hit a snag when villains stole one of their cars.
ex.zh: 匪徒偷走了警方一辆汽车后，警方打击盗车贼的行动遇到了一点儿小挫折。

e.en: If you snag part of your clothing on a sharp or rough object or if it snags, it gets caught on the object and tears.

ex.en: She snagged a heel on a root and tumbled to the ground.
ex.zh: 她的鞋后跟绊在树根上，跌倒在地。

ex.en: Brambles snagged his suit.
ex.zh: 刺藤钩破了他的西服。

d: n. 障碍、意外障碍、小问题；尖利突出物、钩挂物；（衣物上的）钩破处、抽丝处；枯立木
v. （使）钩住、钩破、挂住；被绊住；抓住机会、抢先弄到；造成阻碍、形成障碍、使受阻；清除（河道等中的）障碍物

e.en: A substance is a solid, powder, liquid, or gas with particular properties.

ex.en: There's absolutely no regulation of cigarettes to make sure that they don't include poisonous substances.
ex.zh: 绝对没有确保香烟不含有毒物质的规定。

e.en: Substance is the quality of being important or significant.

ex.en: It's questionable whether anything of substance has been achieved.
ex.zh: 是否已取得任何实质性的进展值得质疑。

e.en: The substance of what someone says or writes is the main thing that they are trying to say.

ex.en: The substance of his discussions doesn't really matter.
ex.zh: 他讨论的要旨实际并不重要。

e.en: If you say that something has no substance, you mean that it is not true.

ex.en: There is no substance in any of these allegations.
ex.zh: 这些指控没有一个是正确的。

d: n. 物质，材料；主旨，主要内容；重要性；真实性，可信性；毒品；财富，财产；实质，（实在的）东西； 实体；可靠，稳定；（哲）实体

e.en: An object that is stubby is shorter and thicker than usual.

ex.en: He pointed a stubby finger at a wooden chair opposite him.
ex.zh: 他用粗短的手指指了指他对面的一把木椅。

d: adj. 短而粗的，粗短的；短而钝的；断株样的

e.en: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

ex.en: He suggested a link between class size and test results of seven-year-olds.
ex.zh: 他建议把7岁儿童的班级大小和考试结果相关联。

ex.en: I suggest you ask him some specific questions about his past.
ex.zh: 我建议你问问他有关他的过去的一些具体问题。

e.en: If you suggest the name of a person or place, you recommend them to someone.

ex.en: Could you suggest someone to advise me how to do this?
ex.zh: 你能推荐一个人来建议我怎么做这件事吗？

e.en: If you suggest that something is the case, you say something which you believe is the case.

ex.en: I'm not suggesting that is what is happening.
ex.zh: 我并不是说那就是所发生的情况。

ex.en: It is wrong to suggest that there are easy alternatives.
ex.zh: 认为有容易的选择是错误的。

e.en: If one thing suggests another, it implies it or makes you think that it might be the case.

ex.en: Earlier reports suggested that a meeting would take place on Sunday.
ex.zh: 早期的报道暗示了一次会议将在周日举行。

d: v. 提议，建议；推荐，举荐；显示，表明；暗示，暗指；使人想到，使人联想到

e.en: Someone or something that is suitable for a particular purpose or occasion is right or acceptable for it.

ex.en: Employers usually decide within five minutes whether someone is suitable for the job.
ex.zh: 雇主们通常在5分钟内判断出某人是否适合那份工作。

e.en: 适合

ex.en: ...information on the suitability of a product for use in the home.
ex.zh: …有关一项产品家庭适用性的信息。

d: adj. 适宜的，合适的

e.en: If you carry out a survey, you try to find out detailed information about a lot of different people or things, usually by asking people a series of questions.

ex.en: The council conducted a survey of the uses to which farm buildings are put.
ex.zh: 该委员会对农场建筑的用途进行了一个调查。

e.en: If you survey a number of people, companies, or organizations, you try to find out information about their opinions or behaviour, usually by asking them a series of questions.

ex.en: Business Development Advisers surveyed 211 companies for the report.
ex.zh: 企业发展顾问为这份报告调查了211家公司。

e.en: If you survey something, you look at or consider the whole of it carefully.

ex.en: He pushed himself to his feet and surveyed the room.
ex.zh: 他站起来审视这个房间。

e.en: If someone carries out a survey of an area of land, they examine it and measure it, usually in order to make a map of it.

ex.en: ...the organizer of the geological survey of India.
ex.zh: …印度地质勘测的组织者。

d: n. （survey 的复数）调查；勘测，测量
v. （survey 的第三人称单数）调查；审视；勘测

e.en: Something that is thick has a large distance between its two opposite sides.

ex.en: For breakfast I had a thick slice of bread and butter.
ex.zh: 早餐我吃了一片厚厚的黄油面包。

ex.en: He wore thick glasses.
ex.zh: 他戴着厚厚的眼镜。

e.en: 厚厚地

ex.en: Slice the meat thickly.
ex.zh: 把肉切成厚片。

e.en: You can use thick to talk or ask about how wide or deep something is.

ex.en: The folder was two inches thick.
ex.zh: 那个文件夹有两英寸厚。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: Thick is also a combining form.

ex.en: His life was saved by a quarter-inch-thick bullet-proof vest.
ex.zh: 他被0.25英寸厚的防弹背心救了一命。

d: adj. 厚的，粗的；有……厚的；（衣服）厚重的，暖和的 ；（字体）粗体的；茂密的，繁茂的；（毛发）浓密的；（烟、云、雾等）浑浊的，能见度低的；（液体）稠的，浓的； 愚钝的，笨的；（尤指由于疾病、酗酒而使头脑）隐痛的，思路不清的；充满的，弥漫的；（因为难过等而嗓音）沙哑的，低沉的；（口音）重的，难听懂的；亲密无间的，交情厚的
n. 在……最激烈时，在……最紧张的时刻（the thick）
adv. 厚地，浓密地；大量地
【名】 （Thick）（美、英、加）西克（人名）

e.en: If someone or something thrives, they do well and are successful, healthy, or strong. 兴旺发达;

ex.en: He appears to be thriving.
ex.zh: 他看起来兴旺发达蒸蒸日上。

ex.en: Today her company continues to thrive.
ex.zh: 如今，她的公司继续蓬勃发展。

e.en: If you say that someone thrives on a particular situation, you mean that they enjoy it or that they can deal with it very well, especially when other people find it unpleasant or difficult. 喜欢; 从容应对 (尤指别人不喜欢或认为困难的事)

ex.en: Many people thrive on a stressful lifestyle.
ex.zh: 许多人喜欢有压力的生活方式。

d: v. 兴盛，繁荣，茁壮成长（thrive 的过去式和过去分词形式）；（thrive on 的过去式）喜欢，善于应对（尤指别人觉得困难或不快的事）

e.en: If something happens until a particular time, it happens during the period before that time and stops at that time.

ex.en: Until 2004, she lived in Canada.
ex.zh: 到2004年为止，她一直住在加拿大。

e.en: Until is also a conjunction.

ex.en: I waited until it got dark.
ex.zh: 我一直等到天黑。

e.en: You use until with a negative to emphasize the moment in time after which the rest of your statement becomes true, or the condition which would make it true.

ex.en: The traffic laws don't take effect until the end of the year.
ex.zh: 交通法要到年底才生效。

e.en: Until is also a conjunction.

ex.en: The government said that it has suspended all aid to Haiti until that country's legitimate government is restored.
ex.zh: 政府说它已经暂停对海地的所有援助，直到海地恢复合法政府为止。

d: conj.  到……时，直到……为止
prep.  到……时，直到……为止；直到（某处）

e.en: If something is unusual, it does not happen very often or you do not see it or hear it very often. 不寻常的;

ex.en: They have replanted many areas with rare and unusual plants.
ex.zh: 他们在很多地方重新种上了稀有罕见的植物。

e.en: If you describe someone as unusual, you think that they are interesting and different from other people.

ex.en: He was an unusual man with great business talents.
ex.zh: 他是一个与众不同的人，极具高超的商业才能。

d: adj. 不寻常的，罕见的；与众不同的，独特的

e.en: Plants, trees, and flowers can be referred to as vegetation.

ex.en: The inn has a garden of semi-tropical vegetation.
ex.zh: 这家小旅馆拥有一个亚热带植物园。

d: n. （总称）植物，植被；（植物的）生长；呆板单调的生活
n. 生存能力，发育能力，活力；可行性，可持续性

e.en: A violet is a small plant that has purple or white flowers in the spring.
Something that is violet is a bluish-purple colour.

ex.en: The light was beginning to drain from a violet sky.
ex.zh: 光线正开始从紫罗兰色的天空中渐渐消失。

e.en: If you say that someone is no shrinking violet, you mean that they are not at all shy.

ex.en: When it comes to expressing himself he is no shrinking violet.
ex.zh: 他表达自己看法时一点都不羞涩。

d: n. 紫罗兰，堇菜；蓝紫色，紫罗兰色
adj. 紫色的，紫罗兰色的
【名】 （Violet）（印、匈、英）维奥莱特，（西）比奥莱特，（法）维奥莱（人名）

e.en: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, because they want to do it.

ex.en: She now helps in a local school as a volunteer three days a week.
ex.zh: 她现在作为一名志愿者每周3天在当地一所学校帮忙。

e.en: A volunteer is someone who offers to do a particular task or job without being forced to do it.

ex.en: Right. What I want now is two volunteers to come down to the front.
ex.zh: 对了。我现在需要的就是两个自告奋勇者到前面来。

e.en: If you volunteer to do something, you offer to do it without being forced to do it.

ex.en: Aunt Mary volunteered to clean up the kitchen.
ex.zh: 玛丽姨妈主动要求打扫厨房。

ex.en: He volunteered for the army in 1939.
ex.zh: 他在1939年自愿参军。

e.en: If you volunteer information, you tell someone something without being asked. 主动提供 (信息)

ex.en: The room was quiet; no one volunteered any further information.
ex.zh: 房间里很安静；没有人主动提供更多的信息。

ex.en: "They were both great supporters of Franco," Ryle volunteered.
ex.zh: “他们俩都是佛朗哥的坚定支持者，”赖尔主动说道。

d: n. 志愿者（volunteer 的复数）；自告奋勇者
v. 志愿（volunteer 的三单形式）；主动提供（信息）

e.en: A warning is something said or written to tell people of a possible danger, problem, or other unpleasant thing that might happen. 警告;

ex.en: The minister gave a warning that if war broke out, it would be catastrophic.
ex.zh: 大臣警告说战争一旦爆发，将会是灾难性的。

ex.en: He was killed because he ignored a warning to put stronger cords on his parachute.
ex.zh: 他死了，因为他忽视了要给降落伞装上更结实的绳索的警告。

e.en: A warning is an advance notice of something that will happen, often something unpleasant or dangerous.

ex.en: The soldiers opened fire without warning.
ex.zh: 士兵们未发警告就开了火。

e.en: Warning actions or signs give a warning.

ex.en: She ignored the warning signals and did not check the patient's medical notes.
ex.zh: 她忽视了一些先兆症状，也没有检查病人的病历。

d: n. 警示，提醒，告诫；（对不良行为的）警告；预告，预兆
adj. 表示警告的，告诫的
v. 提醒注意（可能发生的事），使警惕；劝告（使有所防备），告诫；警告（warn 的现在分词）
【名】 （Warning）（德）瓦宁（人名）
黄橙色的

e.en: An autonomous country, organization, or group governs or controls itself rather than being controlled by anyone else.

ex.en: They proudly declared themselves part of a new autonomous province.
ex.zh: 他们自豪地宣布自己是新自治省的一部分。

e.en: An autonomous person makes their own decisions rather than being influenced by someone else.

ex.en: He treated us as autonomous individuals who had to learn to make up our own minds about issues.
ex.zh: 他视我们为独立个体，必须学会自主处理问题。

d: adj. 自治的，有自治权的；自主的，有自主权的；自动的

e.en: A vehicle is a machine with an engine, such as a bus, car, or truck, that carries people or things from place to place.

ex.en: ...a vehicle that was somewhere between a tractor and a truck.
ex.zh: …一辆介于拖拉机和卡车之间的机动车。

e.en: You can use vehicle to refer to something that you use in order to achieve a particular purpose.

ex.en: Her art became a vehicle for her political beliefs.
ex.zh: 她的艺术成了她政治信仰的媒介。

d: n. vehicle 的复数：车辆，交通工具；引申指媒介，手段，载体
n. 自动驾驶出租车（robotaxi 的复数）

e.en: A car is a motor vehicle with room for a small number of passengers.

ex.en: He had left his tickets in his car.
ex.zh: 他把票落在自己的小汽车里了。

e.en: A car is the same as a .
The separate sections of a train are called cars when they are used for a particular purpose. (有特殊用途的)

ex.en: He made his way into the dining car for breakfast.
ex.zh: 他挤进餐车吃早点。

d: n. 汽车，车辆（car 的复数）；（美式）火车车厢，列车车厢；（大写 Cars）美国皮克斯/迪士尼动画电影系列《赛车总动员》（亦译《汽车总动员》）；（Cars）人名（法语：卡尔，罗马尼亚语、瑞典语：卡尔斯）

abbr. （医学/心理学）（大写 CARS）儿童孤独症评定量表（Childhood Autism Rating Scale）；中美洲研究站（Central America Research Station）；计算机化自动额定值系统（computerized automatic rating system）；汽车收据结账证书（Certificates for Automobile Receivables）

e.en: The driver of a vehicle is the person who is driving it.

ex.en: The driver got out of his van.
ex.zh: 司机从货车里下来。

e.en: A driver is a computer program that controls a device such as a printer.

ex.en: Printer driver software includes standard features such as print layout and fit-to-page printing.
ex.zh: 打印机驱动程序软件包含标准功能，比如打印版面设定和符合纸张大小的打印。

d: n. 司机，驾驶员；驱动程序；推动力；驱赶某种动物的人；传动装置，主动轮；（电子）激励器；高尔夫球棒
【名】 （Driver）（英）德赖弗，（德）德里弗（人名）

e.en: (formerly) a title borne by medieval Chinese emperors and Mongol and Turkic rulers: usually added to a name (旧时)汗;
e.zh: 中古时期对中国帝王以及蒙古、土耳其对君主的尊称

ex.en: Kublai Khan

e.en: such a ruler
e.zh: 中古时期中国帝王以及蒙古、土耳的君主

e.en: an inn in Turkey, certain Arab countries, etc; caravanserai 小客栈;
e.zh: 位于土耳其与阿拉伯国家

d: n. 可汗（旧时对蒙古、突厥等亚洲统治者或君主的尊称）；商队客店；（Khan）人名（姓氏，常译作汗，瑞典译作卡恩，老挝、柬埔寨译作坎）
n. 来福车（美国网约车公司及同名打车应用）
abbr. 伦敦交通局（Transport for London）
n. Uber，优步（美国一家科技公司）；Uber，人名：（德）乌贝尔，（英）尤伯

e.en: An automated factory, office, or industrial process uses machines to do the work instead of people.

ex.en: The equipment was made on highly automated production lines.
ex.zh: 该设备是在高度自动化的生产线上制造的。

d: adj. 自动化的
v. 使自动化（automate 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A cap is a soft, flat hat with a curved part at the front which is called a visor. 软扁帽;

ex.en: ...a dark blue baseball cap.
ex.zh: …一顶深蓝色的棒球帽。

e.en: A cap is a special hat which is worn as part of a uniform.

ex.en: ...a border guard in olive grey uniform and a cap.
ex.zh: …一个穿橄榄绿军服、戴军帽的边防卫士。

e.en: The cap of a bottle is its lid.

ex.en: She unscrewed the cap of her water bottle and gave him a drink.
ex.zh: 她拧开水瓶盖，给他喝了一口水。

e.en: If someone says that a good or bad event caps a series of events, they mean it is the final event in the series, and the other events were also good or bad.

ex.en: The unrest capped a weekend of right-wing attacks on foreigners.
ex.zh: 整个周末右翼分子对外国人的袭击最终发展成为骚乱。

d: n. 帽子；（对物件起保护作用的）罩，盖，套；最高限额；国家队队员
v. 覆盖；限额收取（或支出）；选入国家队；给（牙齿）上牙套；胜过，超过；脱帽致意
【名】 （Cap）（法、德、罗）卡普，（塞、捷）察普（人名）
adj. （指车辆、列车等）无人驾驶的，无需驾驶员操作即可自动行驶的
abbr. there is 的缩约形式，表示“有、存在”；there has 的缩约形式，多用于 there's been 等现在完成时结构
n. 百度（全球最大的中文搜索引擎）

e.en: If there is congestion in a place, the place is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

ex.en: The problems of traffic congestion will not disappear in a hurry.
ex.zh: 交通堵塞问题不会很快消失。

e.en: Congestion in a part of the body is a medical condition in which the part becomes blocked. (身体部位的)

ex.en: ...nasal congestion.
ex.zh: …鼻塞

d: n. （交通）拥塞，塞车；充血，淤血

e.en: Something that is Chinese relates or belongs to China or its languages or people. 中国的; 中文的;
The Chinese are the people who come from China.
The languages that are spoken in China, especially Mandarin, are often referred to as Chinese.

d: adj. （Chinese）中国的；中国人的；汉语的
n. （Chinese）中国人，华人；汉语；中餐，中餐馆
n. （Chinese）（美、印、澳、巴）奇内斯（人名）
n. 弗朗西斯科（男子名，等于 Francis）

e.en: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

ex.en: Sixteen of the contestants have hired lawyers and are suing the organizers.
ex.zh: 参赛者中有16人已经聘了律师，正在起诉主办方。

ex.en: He will be in charge of all hiring and firing at PHA.
ex.zh: 他将负责公众房产管理局里的一切人事任免事务。

e.en: If you hire something, you pay money to the owner so that you can use it for a period of time.
You use hire to refer to the activity or business of hiring something.
If something is for hire, it is available for you to hire.

ex.en: Helmets will be available for hire at all Vail Resort ski areas.
ex.zh: 在韦尔度假村的所有滑雪场里都有头盔供出租。

d: v. 租用，租借；聘用，录用
n. 租借，租金；被雇用的人
【名】 （Hire）（美、印）希尔（人名）

e.en: If someone has power, they have a lot of control over people and activities.

ex.en: In a democracy, power must be divided.
ex.zh: 在民主政体中，权力必须被分散。

e.en: Your power to do something is your ability to do it.

ex.en: Human societies have the power to solve the problems confronting them.
ex.zh: 人类社会有能力解决他们面临的问题。

ex.en: Fathers have the power to dominate children and young people.
ex.zh: 父辈们有控制孩子们和年轻人的能力。

e.en: If it is in or within your power to do something, you are able to do it or you have the resources to deal with it.

ex.en: Your debt situation is only temporary, and it is within your power to resolve it.
ex.zh: 你的债务状况只是暂时的，解决它在你的能力范围里。

e.en: If someone in authority has the power to do something, they have the legal right to do it. (法律赋予的)

ex.en: The police have the power of arrest.
ex.zh: 警察有逮捕权。

d: n. 力量（power 的复数形式）；权力，权势，权限；能力，本领；强国，列强；（数学）幂，乘方
v. 为…提供动力，驱动（power 的第三人称单数现在时）
n. 无人驾驶出租车，自动驾驶出租车

e.en: The purpose of something is the reason for which it is made or done. 目的;

ex.en: The purpose of the occasion was to raise money for medical supplies.
ex.zh: 此次活动的目的是为医疗用品筹款。

ex.en: ...the use of nuclear energy for military purposes.
ex.zh: …军事用途的核能的使用。

e.en: Your purpose is the thing that you want to achieve.

ex.en: They might well be prepared to do you harm in order to achieve their purpose.
ex.zh: 他们很可能有备而来伤害你，以实现其目标。

e.en: Purpose is the feeling of having a definite aim and of being determined to achieve it.

ex.en: The teachers are enthusiastic and have a sense of purpose.
ex.zh: 教师们热情高涨，感到很有奔头。

e.en: If you do something on purpose, you do it intentionally.

ex.en: Was it an accident or did David do it on purpose?
ex.zh: 这是个意外呢，还是戴维故意干的？

d: n. 目的，意图；目标，计划；（达到生活中目标的）决心，毅力；（情势等的）需要，用意（purposes）；重要意义，有价值的意义
v. 有意，打算

e.en: The pace of something is the speed at which it happens or is done. 速度;

ex.en: Many people were not satisfied with the pace of change.
ex.zh: 许多人都不满意变化的速度。

ex.en: They could not stand the pace or the workload.
ex.zh: 他们受不了工作的节奏和负荷。

e.en: Your pace is the speed at which you walk.

ex.en: He moved at a brisk pace down the rue St. Antoine.
ex.zh: 他沿着圣安托万街轻快地走着。

e.en: A pace is the distance that you move when you take one step.

ex.en: He'd only gone a few paces before he stopped again.
ex.zh: 他只走了几步就又停了下来。

e.en: If you pace a small area, you keep walking up and down it, because you are anxious or impatient. (因焦虑或不耐烦)

ex.en: As they waited, Kravis paced the room nervously.
ex.zh: 在他们等着时，克拉维斯在房间里紧张不安地走来走去。

ex.en: He found John pacing around the house, unable to sleep.
ex.zh: 他发现约翰正在房子里四下踱步，无法入眠。

d: n. 步速，（移动的）速度；（发生、进展、发展的）速度，节奏；一步，一步之距；（马行走或奔跑的）步法；步态；快节奏；快跑的能力；（板球）（影响球速的）两个三柱门之间的场地状况
v. （因担忧、紧张或不耐烦而）踱步，踱步于；（在赛跑中）为……定速度；为……领跑；为（书、电影等中的故事）设定节奏；调整自己的工作（或活动）节奏；步测；（马）走侧对步（主见于专门饲养或训练的马）
prep.  （用于人名前，委婉提出不同意见）请……原谅
【名】 （Pace）（捷）帕采，（英）佩斯，（法）帕斯，（罗）帕切（人名）
n. 推出，推广，部署（新产品、服务、系统或政策，常指分阶段或大范围展开）；首次展示；（航）滑跑（飞机着陆时在跑道上滑跑减速的阶段）

e.en: sanatorium

d: abbr. 疗养院（sanatorium 的缩写）
n. （San）圣（西班牙语、意大利语等罗曼语中相当于 Saint，用于人名和地名）
suffix. （日语敬称“さん”的罗马字，加在姓名后）先生，女士
adj. （用于车辆）自动驾驶的；无人驾驶的；（用于旅行、租车等）自驾的；自己驾驶的

e.en: A seat is an object that you can sit on, for example, a chair.

ex.en: Stephen returned to his seat.
ex.zh: 斯蒂芬回到了他的座位上。

e.en: The seat of a chair is the part that you sit on. (椅子的)

ex.en: The stool had a torn, red plastic seat.
ex.zh: 这条无靠背凳子有一个破了的、红色的塑料坐部。

e.en: If you seat yourself somewhere, you sit down. 使 (自己)

ex.en: He waved toward a chair, and seated himself at the desk.
ex.zh: 他朝一把椅子一挥手，在桌旁坐了下来。

e.en: A building or vehicle that seats a particular number of people has enough seats for that number. (建筑物、车等) 提供 (一定数量的)

ex.en: The theatre seats 570.
ex.zh: 这家剧院可容纳570名观众。

d: n. 座位；（椅子等的）座部；（机器的）基座；（议会、委员会、法庭等的）席位，职位； 议会议员选区；（组织或重大活动的）所在地；（大户人家在乡间的）别墅，宅邸；（裙子或裤子的）臀部，后裆；屁股；（骑马的）骑姿
v. 使坐下，使就座；容纳，坐得下；使就职；固定，安装

e.en: When you test something, you try it, for example, by touching it or using it for a short time, in order to find out what it is, what condition it is in, or how well it works.

ex.en: Either measure the temperature with a thermometer or test the water with your wrist.
ex.zh: 要么用温度计测量水温，要么用你的手腕来试水温。

e.en: A test is a deliberate action or experiment to find out how well something works.

ex.en: ...the banning of nuclear tests.
ex.zh: …对核试验的禁止。

e.en: If you test someone, you ask them questions or tell them to perform certain actions in order to find out how much they know about a subject or how well they are able to do something.

ex.en: There was a time when each teacher spent an hour, one day a week, testing students in every subject.
ex.zh: 曾有一段时间，每个老师每周都花一小时来测验学生的各门功课。

e.en: A test is a series of questions that you must answer or actions that you must perform in order to show how much you know about a subject or how well you are able to do something.

ex.en: Out of a total of 25 students only 15 passed the test.
ex.zh: 所有25个学生中只有15个通过了测试。

d: n. （书面或口头的）测验，考试；（医疗上的）检查，化验，检验；（对机器或武器等的）试验，检验；（对水、土壤、空气等的）检测，检验；（衡量能力或技能等的）测试，考验；医疗检查设备；化验结果；（常指板球、橄榄球的）国际锦标赛（Test）；准则，标准；（冶）烤钵，灰皿；（一些无脊椎动物和原生动物的）甲壳
v. 试验，测试；测验，考查（熟练程度，知识）；检测，检验（质量或含量）；检查（身体），（用试剂）化验；考验；尝，（触）试

e.en: A service is something that the public needs, such as transportation, communications facilities, hospitals, or energy supplies, which is provided in a planned and organized way by the government or an official body. 公共服务机构;

ex.en: The postal service has been trying to cut costs.
ex.zh: 邮政系统一直在试图削减成本。

ex.en: We have started a campaign for better nursery and school services.
ex.zh: 我们已开展了一场运动，以改善幼儿园和学校的服务。

e.en: You can sometimes refer to an organization or private company as a particular service when it provides something for the public or acts on behalf of the government. 官方机构;

ex.en: The Agriculture Department has ultimate control over the Forest Service.
ex.zh: 农业部对林务局有最终控制权。

e.en: If an organization or company provides a particular service, they can do a particular job or a type of work for you. 服务;

ex.en: The kitchen maintains a twenty-four hour service and can be contacted via reception.
ex.zh: 厨房提供24小时服务，可通过接待处联系。

e.en: Services are activities such as tourism, banking, and selling things which are part of a country's economy, but are not concerned with producing or manufacturing goods. 服务性工作;

ex.en: Mining rose by 9.1%, manufacturing by 9.4% and services by 4.3%.
ex.zh: 采矿业增长了9.1%，制造业增长了9.4%，服务业增长了4.3%。

d: n. 服务，服务项目，劳务；维修，保养；服务业，服务性行业；公共服务，公共事业，公共设施；the services 军队，武装力量；（宗教）礼拜，仪式（均为 service 的复数）
v. 服务；检修，保养（service 的第三人称单数）

e.en: We've is the usual spoken form of "we have," especially when "have" is an auxiliary verb. (we have)的常用口语形式，尤当(have)

ex.en: It's the first time we've been to the cinema together as a family.
ex.zh: 这是我们一家人第一次一起去看电影。

d: abbr. 我们已，我们有（we have）
一家研发自动驾驶汽车的公司，为Alphabet公司（Google母公司）旗下的子公司

e.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

ex.en: The children are allowed to watch TV after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们被允许在放学后看电视。

ex.en: Smoking will not be allowed.
ex.zh: 吸烟将被禁止。

e.en: If you are allowed something, you are given permission to have it or are given it.

ex.en: Gifts like chocolates or flowers are allowed.
ex.zh: 像巧克力或者花这样的礼物是准许的。

e.en: If you allow something to happen, you do not prevent it.

ex.en: He won't allow himself to fail.
ex.zh: 他不容许自己失败。

e.en: If one thing allows another thing to happen, the first thing creates the opportunity for the second thing to happen. 使能够 (发生)

ex.en: The compromise will allow him to continue his free market reforms.
ex.zh: 这个妥协将使他得以继续他的自由市场改革。

ex.en: ...an attempt to allow the Muslim majority a greater share of power.
ex.zh: …使穆斯林多数派分享更多权力的一种尝试。

d: v. 允许，准许；使有可能；任凭；接受，认可；促使；（特地）酌留；承认，同意；让对方得分

e.en: If the process or rate of something accelerates or if something accelerates it, it gets faster and faster. 使加速;

ex.en: Growth will accelerate to 2.9 percent next year.
ex.zh: 增长明年将加快到2.9%。

e.en: When a moving vehicle accelerates, it goes faster and faster.

ex.en: Suddenly the car accelerated.
ex.zh: 突然车加速了。

d: v. （使）加快，促进；（车辆或驾驶者）加速

e.en: When you answer someone who has asked you something, you say something back to them. (口头)

ex.en: Just answer the question.
ex.zh: 只回答这个问题。

ex.en: He paused before answering.
ex.zh: 他在回答前停了下来。

e.en: If you answer a letter or advertisement, you write to the person who wrote it.

ex.en: Did he answer your letter?
ex.zh: 他回复你的信了吗？

e.en: When you answer the telephone, you pick it up when it rings. When you answer the door, you open it when you hear a knock or the bell.

ex.en: She answered her phone on the first ring.
ex.zh: 她在响第一声铃时就接了电话。

e.en: Answer is also a noun.

ex.en: I knocked at the front door and there was no answer.
ex.zh: 我敲了前门，没有应答。

d: v. 回答；回复；应答（answer 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: a strikingly handsome youth
a handsome Eurasian mountain butterfly, Parnassius apollo, with palish wings and prominent red ocelli
e.zh: 产于欧亚山区的美丽蝴蝶

d: n. 阿波罗（古希腊神话中的光明之神、文艺之神，古罗马神话中的太阳神）；（美、意、菲、肯、巴西、英、印）阿波罗（人名）；（apollo）美男子

e.en: If you say that something appears to be the way you describe it, you are reporting what you believe or what you have been told, though you cannot be sure it is true.

ex.en: There appears to be increasing support for the leadership to take a more aggressive stance.
ex.zh: 似乎有不断增长的对领导层采取更强立场的支持。

e.en: If someone or something appears to have a particular quality or characteristic, they give the impression of having that quality or characteristic.

ex.en: She did her best to appear more self-assured than she felt.
ex.zh: 她竭力表现得比她感觉的更为自信。

ex.en: He is anxious to appear a gentleman.
ex.zh: 他急于表现得像一位绅士。

e.en: When someone or something appears, they move into a position where you can see them.

ex.en: A woman appeared at the far end of the street.
ex.zh: 一个女人在街那端出现了。

e.en: When something new appears, it begins to exist or reaches a stage of development where its existence can be noticed.

ex.en: ...small white flowers which appear in early summer.
ex.zh: …在初夏出现的小白花。

d: v. 似乎，看来，显得；出现，显现；发表，出版；（在戏剧、影视、节目等中）出场，演出；（在法庭或官方委员会等）出庭，出席；appear 的过去式和过去分词

e.en: (in the Jewish calendar) the fifth month of the year according to biblical reckoning and the eleventh month in the civil year, usually falling within July and August (历法)阿布月; 即犹太教历五月和非宗教日历的每年第11

d: abbr. 数字音视频编解码技术标准（Audio Video Standard）

e.en: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion. (突然的)

ex.en: I heard four or five loud bangs.
ex.zh: 我听到四五声巨响。

ex.en: She slammed the door with a bang.
ex.zh: 她砰地一声关上门。

e.en: If something bangs, it makes a sudden loud noise, once or several times.

ex.en: The engine spat and banged.
ex.zh: 引擎发出劈啪声和砰砰巨响。

e.en: If you bang a door or if it bangs, it closes suddenly with a loud noise.

ex.en: ...the sound of doors banging.
ex.zh: …砰砰的关门声。

ex.en: All up and down the street the windows bang shut.
ex.zh: 整条街的窗户都砰砰关上了。

e.en: If you bang on something or if you bang it, you hit it hard, making a loud noise.

ex.en: We could bang on the desks and shout till they let us out.
ex.zh: 我们会大声猛拍桌子，大声喊叫，直到他们放我们出去。

d: n. 突然的巨响；重击，猛撞；刘海（bangs）
v. 猛敲，砰然重击；猛摔；很响地使劲关上；（意外地）撞击；与……性交；砰砰作响
adv. 恰好，正好；完全，彻底；突然，猛然
int. 砰；突然，猛然

e.en: A beep is a short, loud sound like that made by a car horn or a telephone answering machine.
If something such as a horn beeps, or you beep it, it makes a short, harsh sound.

ex.en: My cell phone beeped.
ex.zh: 我的手机嘟嘟响了。

ex.en: He beeped the horn.
ex.zh: 他按响了喇叭。

d: v. beep 的过去式和过去分词：发出短促、尖锐的哔哔声（或蜂鸣声），通常表示警告或通知；按响（喇叭）。

e.en: A borough is a town, or a district within a large city, which has its own council, government, or local services. 自治市; (大城市中的)

ex.en: ...the New York City borough of Brooklyn.
ex.zh: …纽约市的布鲁克林自治区。

d: n. 自治市，自治市镇；（美国大城市中的）行政区；（美国阿拉斯加州的）行政区；（Borough）人名，伯勒

e.en: a minibus used to transport workers from the townships to the city centres  黑色出租车;
e.zh: 将工人从小镇运往市中心的小型公共汽车

d: 黑车

e.en: A cab is a taxi.

ex.en: Could I use your phone to call a cab?
ex.zh: 我能用你的电话叫一辆出租车吗？

e.en: The cab of a truck or train is the front part in which the driver sits. (卡车或列车的)

ex.en: The van has additional load space over the driver's cab.
ex.zh: 该货车在驾驶室上方有额外的载货空间。

e.en: an ancient Hebrew measure equal to about 2.3 litres (4 pints) 古希伯来计量单位，相当于2.3

d: n. cab 的复数：出租车，出租汽车；（卡车、火车等的）驾驶室
abbr. 大写 CABS 是下列全称的缩写：北美华人生物医药协会（Chinese-American BioPharmaceutical Society）；生物多样性应用科学中心（Center for Applied Biodiversity Science）；儿童适应行为评定量表（Children Adaptive Behaviour Scale）

e.en: Built-in devices or features are included in something as a part of it, rather than being separate.

ex.en: ...modern cameras with built-in flash units.
ex.zh: …有内置闪光灯的新式照相机。

d: adj. 内置的，嵌入的，固定的；内在的，固有的
n. 内置物，内嵌装置，固定式设备

e.en: If you give your consent to something, you give someone permission to do it.

ex.en: At approximately 11:30 p.m., Pollard finally gave his consent to the search.
ex.zh: 大约晚上11:30的时候，波拉德终于对搜查予以同意。

e.en: If you consent to something, you agree to do it or to allow it to be done.

ex.en: He finally consented to go.
ex.zh: 他最终同意去。

ex.en: He asked Ginny if she would consent to a small celebration after the christening.
ex.zh: 他问金尼她是否同意在洗礼仪式后来个小庆祝。

d: n. 许可，允许；同意，赞同；正式批准文件，批文
v. 赞同，准许，同意
【名】 （Consent）（美、法、荷）孔桑（人名）

e.en: the hand (used esp when addressing children) (昵称)

d: n. 手（尤用于与幼儿说话时）；侦察用车

e.en: If one thing displaces another, it forces the other thing out of its place, position, or role, and then occupies that place, position, or role itself.

ex.en: These factories have displaced tourism as the country's largest source of foreign exchange.
ex.zh: 这些工厂已经取代了旅游业而成为该国最大的外汇来源。

e.en: If a person or group of people is displaced, they are forced to move away from the area where they live.

ex.en: More than 600,000 people were displaced by the tsunami.
ex.zh: 超过60万人被海啸搞得背井离乡。

d: adj. （常作定语，指人，displaced person 为固定搭配）被迫离开家园的，流离失所的，无家可归的；位移的，错位的；被取代的，被替换的，被撤换的
n. 无家可归者，流离失所者（the displaced）
v. displace 的过去式和过去分词：迫使离开家园；取代；移动……的位置；撤换

e.en: A depot is a bus station or train station. 公共汽车站;

ex.en: She was reunited with her boyfriend in the bus depot of Ozark, Alabama.
ex.zh: 她和她的男朋友在亚拉巴马州的奥扎克汽车站重新团聚了。

e.en: A depot is a place where large amounts of raw materials, equipment, arms, or other supplies are kept until they are needed. 仓库;

ex.en: ...food depots.
ex.zh: …食物储藏室。

d: n. 仓库，库房；公共汽车站，火车站，航空站；车库，修车厂
【名】 （Depot）（刚（布））德波特（人名）

e.en: When you drive somewhere, you operate a car or other vehicle and control its movement and direction.

ex.en: I drove into town and went to a restaurant for dinner.
ex.zh: 我开车进城到一家餐馆用餐。

ex.en: She never learned to drive.
ex.zh: 她从未学过开车。

e.en: 驾驶

ex.en: ...a qualified driving instructor.
ex.zh: …一名合格的驾驶教练。

e.en: If you drive someone somewhere, you take them there in a car or other vehicle. 开车送 (某人去某处)

ex.en: His daughter Carly drove him to the train station.
ex.zh: 她的女儿卡莉开车送他去火车站。

e.en: If something drives a machine, it supplies the power that makes it work.

ex.en: The current flows into electric motors that drive the wheels.
ex.zh: 电流流入驱动轮子的电动机。

d: v. 驾车送（人）；迫使，驱使；驱赶；敲，击；猛踢，猛击（球）；驱动；吹，刮；凿，挖掘；开车，驾驶
n. 驱车出行；强烈欲望，本能需求；私人车道；有组织的努力，运动；干劲，驱动力；驱动器；猛踢，猛击；驱赶，围歼；（用于路名）路，大道；（有组织的）惠斯特牌戏等的比赛；（有自动传动装置的汽车的）自动挡；（从球座上）发球

e.en: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

ex.en: The company employs 18 workers.
ex.zh: 该公司雇用18位职工。

ex.en: More than 3,000 local workers are employed in the tourism industry.
ex.zh: 超过3000名本地工人受雇于旅游业。

e.en: If you employ certain methods, materials, or expressions, you use them.

ex.en: The group will employ a mix of tactics to achieve its aim.
ex.zh: 该团体将运用混合策略来实现其目标。

e.en: If your time is employed in doing something, you are using the time you have to do that thing.

ex.en: Your time could be usefully employed in attending night classes.
ex.zh: 你的时间可以被有效地利用来上夜课。

d: adj. 被雇用的
vt. 雇佣；使用（employ 的过去式与过去分词）

e.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk. 热衷的;

ex.en: Tom was very enthusiastic about the place.
ex.zh: 汤姆曾非常热衷于那个地方。

e.en: 热衷地;

ex.en: The announcement was greeted enthusiastically.
ex.zh: 这则通告受到了热烈的欢迎。

d: adj. 热心的，热情的

e.en: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

ex.en: Physical activity is an important factor in maintaining fitness.
ex.zh: 体育活动是保持健康的一个重要因素。

e.en: If an amount increases by a factor of two, for example, or by a factor of eight, then it becomes two times bigger or eight times bigger.

ex.en: The cost of butter quadrupled and bread prices increased by a factor of five.
ex.zh: 黄油的价格是原来的4倍，面包的价格上涨了5倍。

e.en: You can use factor to refer to a particular level on a scale of measurement.

ex.en: A sunscreen with a protection factor of 30 allows you to stay in the sun without burning.
ex.zh: 一种防护系数为30的防晒霜使你能够待在太阳底下而不被晒伤。

d: n. 因素，要素；等级，系数；因数，因子；遗传因子，基因；（血液中的）凝血因子；代理公司，代理商；地产管理人，管家；测量水平
v. 把……作为因素计入，把……包括在内（factor in）；把……作为因素排除，不把……包括在内（factor out）；将……分解为因子；代理经营，（代管）产业；做代理商
【名】 （Factor）（英）法克特（人名）

e.en: Fear is the unpleasant feeling you have when you think that you are in danger.

ex.en: I was sitting on the floor shivering with fear because a bullet had been fired through a window.
ex.zh: 我坐在地板上吓得浑身发抖，因为有一颗子弹射穿窗户打了进来。

e.en: A fear is a thought that something unpleasant might happen or might have happened.

ex.en: These youngsters are motivated by fear of failure.
ex.zh: 这些年轻人因担心失败而被激发。

ex.en: Then one day his worst fears were confirmed.
ex.zh: 后来有一天，他最大的担心被证实了。

e.en: If you say that there is a fear that something unpleasant or undesirable will happen, you mean that you think it is possible or likely. (发生坏事的)

ex.en: There is a fear that the freeze on bank accounts could prove a lasting deterrent to investors.
ex.zh: 冻结银行帐户很可能对投资者是一个长期的威慑因素。

e.en: If you have fears for someone or something, you are very worried because you think that they might be in danger.

ex.en: He also spoke of his fears for the future of his country's culture.
ex.zh: 他也谈及了他对祖国文化前景的担忧。

d: v. 害怕，畏惧；担心，担忧（fear 的现在分词/动名词）
adj. 敬畏神的，虔诚的（用于 God-fearing 等复合词）

e.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

ex.en: The research effort has focused on tracing the effects of growing levels of five compounds.
ex.zh: 研究集中跟踪5种化合物水平上升带来的影响。

ex.en: Today he was able to focus his message exclusively on the economy.
ex.zh: 今天他能够将重点聚焦在经济方面。

e.en: If you focus your eyes or if your eyes focus, your eyes adjust so that you can clearly see the thing that you want to look at. If you focus a camera, telescope, or other instrument, you adjust it so that you can see clearly through it. 使 (眼睛、相机、望远镜或其它仪器) 对焦;

ex.en: Kelly couldn't focus his eyes well enough to tell if the figure was male or female.
ex.zh: 凯利无法看清那个人影是男的还是女的。

ex.en: His eyes slowly began to focus on what looked like a small dark ball.
ex.zh: 他的眼睛开始慢慢聚焦到那个小黑球似的东西上。

e.en: If you focus rays of light on a particular point, you pass them through a lens or reflect them from a mirror so that they meet at that point. 把 (光线)

ex.en: Magnetic coils focus the electron beams into fine spots.
ex.zh: 磁线圈将电子束聚焦成细小的点。

e.en: The focus of something is the main topic or main thing that it is concerned with.

ex.en: The UN's role in promoting peace is increasingly the focus of international attention.
ex.zh: 联合国在促进和平方面的作用越来越成为国际关注的焦点。

ex.en: The new system is the focus of controversy.
ex.zh: 新系统是争议的焦点。

d: v. 集中，专注，关注；注视；使聚焦，调焦，对焦（focus 的现在分词和动名词）
n. 注意力的集中，专注

e.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

ex.en: ...within the framework of federal regulations.
ex.zh: …在联邦法规的体系内。

e.en: A framework is a structure that forms a support or frame for something.

ex.en: ...wooden shelves on a steel framework.
ex.zh: …在钢架上的木搁板。

d: n. (建筑物或物体的）构架，结构；参照标准，准则；(社会、法律、政治等）框架

e.en: The front of something is the part of it that faces you, or that faces forward, or that you normally see or use.

ex.en: One man sat in an armchair, and the other sat on the front of the desk.
ex.zh: 一个男人坐在扶手椅上，另一个坐在桌前。

ex.en: Stand at the front of the line.
ex.zh: 站在队伍的前面。

e.en: The front of a building is the side or part of it that faces the street.

ex.en: Attached to the front of the house, there was a large veranda.
ex.zh: 连着房子的临街面有一个大阳台。

e.en: In a war, the front is a line where two opposing armies are facing each other.

ex.en: Sonja's husband is fighting at the front.
ex.zh: 索妮亚的丈夫正在前线打仗。

e.en: If you say that something is happening on a particular front, you mean that it is happening with regard to a particular situation or field of activity.

ex.en: ...research across a wide academic front.
ex.zh: …跨多个学术领域的研究。

d: n. 前面，正面；前线，前方；方面，领域；掩护；锋；海滨，湖畔；封面，头版；建筑物的面；（装出的）样子；（政治组织名称）阵线；胆大，自信；胸部；（人的）脸，前额
adj. 前面的，正面的；（足球等）踢前锋的；（元音）舌前位的；起掩护作用的；（18穴高尔夫球场的）前9穴的
v. 领导（机构、乐队）；主持（电视节目）；面向；用……覆盖正面；提供资金；面临，对抗；露面，到达；以舌前位发（元音）；（语言学）将（句子成分）前置；为……作掩护
【名】 （Front）（法）弗龙（人名）

e.en: If you grasp something, you take it in your hand and hold it very firmly.

ex.en: He grasped both my hands.
ex.zh: 他紧紧地抓住我的双手。

e.en: A grasp is a very firm hold or grip.

ex.en: His hand was taken in a warm, firm grasp.
ex.zh: 他的手被热情地、紧紧地握住了。

e.en: If you say that something is in someone's grasp, you disapprove of the fact that they possess or control it. If something slips from your grasp, you lose it or lose control of it.

ex.en: The people in your grasp are not guests, they are hostages.
ex.zh: 在你控制之下的这些人并非宾客，而是人质。

ex.en: She allowed victory to slip from her grasp.
ex.zh: 她听任胜利从手中溜走。

e.en: If you grasp something that is complicated or difficult to understand, you understand it.

ex.en: The government has not yet grasped the seriousness of the crisis.
ex.zh: 政府还不明白这场危机的严重性。

d: v. 抓牢，握紧；理解，领会；抓住（机会）
n. 紧抓，紧握；理解（力），领会；能力所及，伸手可及的距离；控制，权力

e.en: A handle is a small round object or a lever that is attached to a door and is used for opening and closing it.

ex.en: I turned the handle and found the door was open.
ex.zh: 我转动把手，发现门是开着的。

e.en: A handle is the part of an object such as a tool, bag, or cup that you hold in order to be able to pick up and use the object. 柄;

ex.en: ...a broom handle.
ex.zh: …一个扫帚柄

e.en: If you say that someone can handle a problem or situation, you mean that they have the ability to deal with it successfully. (成功地)

ex.en: To tell the truth, I don't know if I can handle the job.
ex.zh: 说实话，我不知道我能否做好这份工作。

e.en: If you talk about the way that someone handles a problem or situation, you mention whether or not they are successful in achieving the result they want.

ex.en: I think I would handle a meeting with Mr. Siegel very badly.
ex.zh: 我觉得我可能应付不了与西格尔先生的会谈。

d: n. 处理，应对，对待；（货物、物料等的）搬运，装卸，操作；（车辆、机械等的）操纵性能，操控性
v. handle 的现在分词；拿；处理；应付；操纵；操作；负责

e.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

ex.en: She had decided she must go on as usual, follow her normal routine, and hope and pray.
ex.zh: 她已决定自己必须一如既往地过下去，遵循自己的日常生活规律，同时心存希望并祈祷。

ex.en: He hesitates before leaving, almost as though he had been hoping for conversation.
ex.zh: 他离开前有些犹豫，好像希望跟人说些什么。

e.en: If you say that you cannot hope for something, or if you talk about the only thing that you can hope to get, you mean that you are in a bad situation, and there is very little chance of improving it.

ex.en: Things aren't ideal, but that's the best you can hope for.
ex.zh: 事情并不理想，但你只能指望这些了。

e.en: Hope is also a noun.

ex.en: The only hope for underdeveloped countries is to become, as far as possible, self-reliant.
ex.zh: 欠发达国家的惟一指望就是尽可能地做到自力更生。

e.en: Hope is a feeling of desire and expectation that things will go well in the future.

ex.en: Now that he has become president, many people once again have hope for genuine changes in the system.
ex.zh: 既然他已成为总统，许多人又一次寄期望于体制的真正改革。

ex.en: But Kevin hasn't given up hope of getting in shape.
ex.zh: 但是凯文仍没有放弃康复的希望。

d: v. 希望（hope 的现在分词／动名词）

e.en: If you grasp something, you take it in your hand and hold it very firmly.

ex.en: He grasped both my hands.
ex.zh: 他紧紧地抓住我的双手。

e.en: A grasp is a very firm hold or grip.

ex.en: His hand was taken in a warm, firm grasp.
ex.zh: 他的手被热情地、紧紧地握住了。

e.en: If you say that something is in someone's grasp, you disapprove of the fact that they possess or control it. If something slips from your grasp, you lose it or lose control of it.

ex.en: The people in your grasp are not guests, they are hostages.
ex.zh: 在你控制之下的这些人并非宾客，而是人质。

ex.en: She allowed victory to slip from her grasp.
ex.zh: 她听任胜利从手中溜走。

e.en: If you grasp something that is complicated or difficult to understand, you understand it.

ex.en: The government has not yet grasped the seriousness of the crisis.
ex.zh: 政府还不明白这场危机的严重性。

d: v. grasp 的过去式和过去分词：1. 抓住，握紧，用手紧紧抓住某物；2. 理解，领悟，对某个概念、想法或信息有清晰的认识。

e.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

ex.en: She said her husband ignored her.
ex.zh: 她说她丈夫对她置之不理。

e.en: If you say that an argument or theory ignores an important aspect of a situation, you are criticizing it because it fails to consider that aspect or to take it into account. (某论断或理论)

ex.en: Such arguments ignore the question of where ultimate responsibility lay.
ex.zh: 此类争论忽视了最终责任何在的问题。

d: v. 佯装未见，不理睬；忽视，对……不予理会；（因证据不足）驳回（诉讼）

e.en: The impact that something has on a situation, process, or person is a sudden and powerful effect that it has on them.

ex.en: They say they expect the meeting to have a marked impact on the future of the country.
ex.zh: 他们说期望这次会议对国家的未来产生显著的影响。

e.en: An impact is the action of one object hitting another, or the force with which one object hits another. 撞击;

ex.en: The plane is destroyed, a complete wreck: the pilot must have died on impact.
ex.zh: 飞机被毁，完全成了一堆残骸：飞行员一定在撞击中丧生了。

e.en: To impact a situation, process, or person means to affect them. 对…造成影响;

ex.en: Such schemes mean little unless they impact people.
ex.zh: 除非能对人们造成影响，否则这样的计划意义不大。

e.en: If one object impacts on another, it hits it with great force.

ex.en: ...the sharp tinkle of metal impacting on stone.
ex.zh: …金属撞击石头的刺耳叮当声。

d: n. 撞击，冲击力；巨大影响，强大作用
v. 冲击，撞击；挤入，压紧；（对……）产生影响

e.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

ex.en: The new cars will incorporate a number of major improvements.
ex.zh: 这种新型汽车将包含许多重大的改进。

e.en: If someone or something is incorporated into a large group, system, or area, they become a part of it.

ex.en: The agreement would allow the rebels to be incorporated into a new national police force.
ex.zh: 该协议将允许叛军并入一支新的国家警察部队。

d: v. 包含，合并；组成公司；掺和，混合（成分）；使具体化，体现
adj. 合成一体的，合并的；具体化的；组成公司（或社团）的

e.en: Incremental is used to describe something that increases in value or worth, often by a regular amount.

ex.en: ...our ability to add production capacity at relatively low incremental cost.
ex.zh: ...我们以比原成本稍微高出一点但又相对较低的成本增加产量的能力。

d: adj. 增加的，递增的；逐渐的，逐步的

e.en: An innovation is a new thing or a new method of doing something. 新事物;

ex.en: They produced the first vegetarian beanburger – an innovation which was rapidly exported.
ex.zh: 他们制造出第一个素式豆堡包–一种被迅速销往国外的新食品。

e.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things. 创新;

ex.en: We must promote originality, inspire creativity and encourage innovation.
ex.zh: 我们必须提倡独创性，激发创造力，鼓励创新。

d: n. 新事物，新方法；革新，创新

e.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example, by putting it in a bank, or buying securities or property. 投 (资);

ex.en: Many people don't like to invest in stocks.
ex.zh: 许多人不喜欢投资股票。

ex.en: I'm tired of watching you invest our money in insane projects.
ex.zh: 我看够了你将我们的钱投到一些荒唐的项目上。

e.en: If you invest in something useful, you buy it, because it will help you to do something more efficiently or more cheaply.

ex.en: The company has invested a six-figure sum in an electronic order-control system which is used to keep stores stocked.
ex.zh: 这家公司已经耗资6位数购买了电子定单控制系统来为商店进货。

e.en: When a government or organization invests in something, it gives or lends money for a purpose that it considers useful or profitable. (政府或机构)

ex.en: ...the need to invest in new technology.
ex.zh: …这种投资于新技术的需要。

ex.en: Government agencies must invest more funds in training and development programmes.
ex.zh: 政府机构必须将更多的资金投入到培训和开发项目中。

e.en: If you invest time or energy in something, you spend a lot of time or energy on it because you think it will be useful or successful. 投入 (时间、精力)

ex.en: I would rather invest time in Rebecca than in the kitchen.
ex.zh: 我宁愿把时间花在丽贝卡身上，也不愿花在厨房里。

d: v. 投资；投入（时间或精力）；赋予，授予；给……穿衣；包围，围攻
n. 爱尔兰（西欧国家，中文常称爱尔兰共和国，正式英文国名为 Ireland，占爱尔兰岛大部）；爱尔兰岛（欧洲西北部大西洋上的岛屿，包括爱尔兰共和国与北爱尔兰）；爱尔兰国家队（体育用语）

e.en: Iron is an element that usually takes the form of a hard, dark grey metal. It is used to make steel, and also forms part of many tools, buildings, and vehicles. Very small amounts of iron occur in your blood and in food.

ex.en: The huge, iron gate was locked.
ex.zh: 那扇巨大的铁门被锁上了。

ex.en: ...the highest grade iron ore deposits in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上最优质的铁矿床。

e.en: An iron is an electrical device with a flat metal base. You heat it until the base is hot, then rub it over clothes to remove creases.
If you iron clothes, you remove the creases from them using an iron.

ex.en: She used to iron his shirts.
ex.zh: 她过去常给他熨衬衫。

e.en: 熨烫

ex.en: I managed to get all the ironing done this morning.
ex.zh: 今天上午我设法把所有的衣物都熨了。

d: v. 熨烫，熨平（iron 的过去式和过去分词）：用熨斗将衣物等加热压平，使其平整无皱；解决，消除（iron out 的过去式和过去分词）：消除困难、解决分歧或处理细节问题。
adj. 熨平的，熨烫过的（iron 的过去分词作形容词）：经过熨烫而平整无皱的，多指衣物、布料等。

e.en: A large thing or person is greater in size than usual or average.

ex.en: The pike lives mainly in large rivers and lakes.
ex.zh: 梭鱼主要生活在大的江河湖泊里。

ex.en: In the largest room about a dozen children and seven adults are sitting on the carpet.
ex.zh: 在最大的那个房间里，十几个孩子和七个大人正坐在地毯上。

e.en: A large amount or number of people or things is more than the average amount or number.

ex.en: The gang finally fled with a large amount of cash and jewellery.
ex.zh: 那帮歹徒最终带着大量的现金和珠宝逃走了。

ex.en: There are a large number of centres where you can take full-time courses.
ex.zh: 这里有很多你可以上全日制课程的培训中心。

e.en: Large is used to indicate that a problem or issue which is being discussed is very important or serious. 重要的;

ex.en: ...the already large problem of under-age drinking.
ex.zh: …已颇为严重的未成年人酗酒问题。

e.en: You use at large to indicate that you are talking in a general way about most of the people mentioned.

ex.en: I think the chances of getting reforms accepted by the community at large remain extremely remote.
ex.zh: 我认为，让该团体的大部分人都接受改革的希望仍然极其渺茫。

d: adj. （尺寸、范围、容量）大的；广泛的，重要的；身材高大的；（公司或组织）大规模的
n. 大号，同类中最大者
v. （尤指跳舞和饮酒）作乐，狂欢
adv. 夸大地；大大地

e.en: To launch a rocket, missile, or satellite means to send it into the air or into space.

ex.en: NASA plans to launch a satellite to study cosmic rays.
ex.zh: 美国国家航空航天局计划发射一颗卫星来研究宇宙射线。

e.en: Launch is also a noun.

ex.en: This morning's launch of the space shuttle Columbia has been delayed.
ex.zh: 定于今天上午哥伦比亚号航天飞机的发射已经被推迟了。

e.en: To launch a ship or a boat means to put it into water, often for the first time after it has been built. 使 (新船等)

ex.en: There was no time to launch the lifeboats because the ferry capsized with such alarming speed.
ex.zh: 因为渡船倾斜的速度如此之快，根本没有时间把救生艇放下水。

e.en: Launch is also a noun.

ex.en: The launch of a ship was a big occasion.
ex.zh: 船下水曾是一件大事。

d: v. 发动，发起；上市，发行；使（船或舰）下水；发射（武器或宇宙飞船）；启动（计算机程序）；投出，用力扔出；使投身于（事业等）；起飞，出海
n. （航天器的）发射；（产品的）上市；（事件的）发起；汽艇，游艇；（新产品，出版物）发布会，推介会

e.en: To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

ex.en: ...a proposal that would require the state to license guns the way it does cars.
ex.zh: …提案要求政府像发驾驶证一样发放枪支许可证。

d: n. （美国英语）执照，许可证，特许证；特许（同 licence）；破格，自由（如 poetic license、artistic license）
vt. 许可，特许，发许可证给

e.en: Something that is limited is not very great in amount, range, or degree.

ex.en: They may only have a limited amount of time to get their points across.
ex.zh: 他们可能只有有限的时间来阐述清楚他们的观点。

e.en: A limited company is one whose owners are legally responsible for only a part of any money that it may owe if it goes bankrupt. 有限责任的 (公司)

d: adj. 有限的；受限的；受宪法限制的；（公司）有限责任的 (=Ltd)
n. 高级快车
v. 限制（limit 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: To license a person or activity means to give official permission for the person to do something or for the activity to take place.

ex.en: ...a proposal that would require the state to license guns the way it does cars.
ex.zh: …提案要求政府像发驾驶证一样发放枪支许可证。

d: n. 许可，授权，许可证发放
v. 许可，批准（license 的现在分词）

e.en: Your livelihood is the job or other source of income that gives you the money to buy the things you need.

ex.en: ...fishermen who depend on the seas for their livelihood.
ex.zh: …依靠大海谋生的渔夫。

d: n. 生计，营生

e.en: If you lobby someone such as a member of a government or council, you try to persuade them that a particular law should be changed or that a particular thing should be done.

ex.en: The Wilderness Society lobbied Congress to authorize the Endangered Species Act.
ex.zh: 荒野协会游说国会批准《濒危物种法》。

e.en: A lobby is a group of people who represent a particular organization or campaign, and try to persuade a government or council to help or support them.

ex.en: Agricultural interests are some of the most powerful lobbies in Washington.
ex.zh: 农业利益集团是华盛顿最有影响力的游说团体中的一部分。

e.en: In a hotel or other large building, the lobby is the area near the entrance that usually has corridors and staircases leading off it.

ex.en: I met her in the lobby of the museum.
ex.zh: 我在博物馆大厅遇到了她。

d: v. 游说（政治家或政府）
n. 游说团体，活动集团；大堂，大厅；（旨在对政治家施加影响的）游说；（英国议会的）接见厅，表决厅

e.en: If you lobby someone such as a member of a government or council, you try to persuade them that a particular law should be changed or that a particular thing should be done.

ex.en: The Wilderness Society lobbied Congress to authorize the Endangered Species Act.
ex.zh: 荒野协会游说国会批准《濒危物种法》。

e.en: A lobby is a group of people who represent a particular organization or campaign, and try to persuade a government or council to help or support them.

ex.en: Agricultural interests are some of the most powerful lobbies in Washington.
ex.zh: 农业利益集团是华盛顿最有影响力的游说团体中的一部分。

e.en: In a hotel or other large building, the lobby is the area near the entrance that usually has corridors and staircases leading off it.

ex.en: I met her in the lobby of the museum.
ex.zh: 我在博物馆大厅遇到了她。

d: n. 游说，游说活动，院外活动
v. 进行游说（lobby 的现在分词）
adj. 游说的，从事游说的（作定语）

e.en: A manager is a person who is responsible for running part of or the whole of a business organization.

ex.en: The chef, staff, and managers are all Chinese.
ex.zh: 厨师、工作人员和经理都是中国人。

e.en: The manager of a pop star or other entertainer is the person who takes care of their business interests. (明星等艺人的)

ex.en: ...the star's manager and agent, Anne Chudleigh.
ex.zh: …那位明星的经纪人兼代理人安妮·查德利。

e.en: The manager of a sports team is the person responsible for training the players and organizing the way they play. (棒球队)

ex.en: The team expects to have a new manager before spring training.
ex.zh: 队员们期待着春训前能有一位新的教练。

d: n. （公司、部门等的）经理；（艺人或运动员的）经纪人；（运动队的）管理人，主教练；管理某物的人；（计算机）管理程序

e.en: If you manage an organization, business, or system, or the people who work in it, you are responsible for controlling them. 管理; 经营 (机构、企业、系统等)

ex.en: Within two years he was managing the shop.
ex.zh: 两年内他经营着该商店。

ex.en: There is a lack of confidence in the government's ability to manage the economy.
ex.zh: 对政府管理经济的能力缺乏信心。

e.en: If you manage time, money, or other resources, you deal with them carefully and do not waste them. 管理 (时间、金钱等)

ex.en: In a busy world, managing your time is increasingly important.
ex.zh: 在一个忙碌的世界里，管理好你的时间越来越重要。

e.en: If you manage to do something, especially something difficult, you succeed in doing it. 设法 (做成某事)

ex.en: Somehow, he'd managed to persuade Kay to buy one for him.
ex.zh: 不管怎么说，他已设法说服了凯给他买一个。

ex.en: I managed to pull myself up onto a wet, sloping ledge.
ex.zh: 我设法爬上了一个潮湿的倾斜岩脊。

e.en: If you manage, you succeed in coping with a difficult situation.

ex.en: She had managed perfectly well without medication for three years.
ex.zh: 她3年没用药，却成功地挺了过来。

d: v. 管理，处理；操纵，控制；设法做到，勉力完成；腾出时间参加；凑合着活下去，支撑；调教（人或动物）；竟搞得，竟做出

e.en: household linen or cotton goods, such as sheets and towels (家用)

d: n. 曼彻斯特（英格兰西北部一大城市）；曼彻斯特（美国新罕布什尔州最大城市）；家用棉织品或亚麻制品（如床单、毛巾等）

e.en: The mayor of a town or city is the person who has been elected for a fixed period of time to run its government.

ex.en: ...the new mayor of New York.
ex.zh: …新任纽约市长。

d: n. （英格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰由议员选举产生的）镇长，市长；（美国、加拿大等国家公众选举的）市长
【名】 （Mayor）（英）梅厄，（法、西、俄）马约尔（人名）

e.en: Massage is the action of squeezing and rubbing someone's body, as a way of making them relax or reducing their pain.

ex.en: Alex asked me if I wanted a massage.
ex.zh: 亚历克斯问我是否需要一次按摩。

e.en: If you massage someone or a part of their body, you squeeze and rub their body, in order to make them relax or reduce their pain.

ex.en: She continued massaging her right foot, which was bruised and aching.
ex.zh: 她继续按摩她的右脚，那只脚又肿又疼。

e.en: If you say that someone massages statistics, figures, or evidence, you are criticizing them for changing or presenting the facts in a way that misleads people.

ex.en: Their governments have no reason to "massage" the statistics.
ex.zh: 他们的政府没有理由“窜改”这些数据。

d: n. 按摩，推拿
v. 按摩，推拿；窜改；用………揉擦（皮肤、头发等）

e.en: Something that is narrow measures a very small distance from one side to the other, especially compared to its length or height.

ex.en: ...through the town's narrow streets.
ex.zh: …穿过小镇狭窄的街道。

ex.en: She had long, narrow feet.
ex.zh: 她有一双瘦长的脚。

e.en: 狭窄

ex.en: ...the narrowness of the river mouth.
ex.zh: …河口的狭窄。

e.en: If something narrows, it becomes less wide.

ex.en: The wide track narrows before crossing another stream.
ex.zh: 宽宽的路径在穿越另一条小溪前变窄了。

e.en: If your eyes narrow or if you narrow your eyes, you almost close them, for example because you are angry or because you are trying to concentrate on something.

ex.en: Coggins' eyes narrowed angrily. "You think I'd tell you?"
ex.zh: 科金斯愤怒地眯起双眼说，“你以为我会告诉你？”

d: adj. 狭窄的，狭小的；（想法、态度或信仰）狭隘的；勉强的，（成败）差距很小的；（种类或数目）有限的，范围小的；严格的，精确的；（标音）严式的；（语音）窄的
v. （人的眼睛）眯起来；使缩小，压缩；使变窄，变窄
n. 海峡；狭窄部分

e.en: financial statistics

ex.en: let's look at last year's numbers

d: n. [数] 数字（number的复数）；算术
n. （Numbers）Numbers表格

e.en: If you remember people or events from the past, you still have an idea of them in your mind and you are able to think about them.

ex.en: You wouldn't remember me. I was in another group.
ex.zh: 你不会记得我的，我当时在另一个组。

ex.en: I remembered that we had made the last of the coffee the day before.
ex.zh: 我记得我们前一天刚煮完了最后一点咖啡。

e.en: If you remember that something is the case, you become aware of it again after a time when you did not think about it. 忆起;

ex.en: She remembered that she was going to the club that evening.
ex.zh: 她回想起那天晚上她要去俱乐部。

e.en: If you cannot remember something, you are not able to bring it back into your mind when you make an effort to do so.

ex.en: If you can't remember your number, write it in code in an appointment book.
ex.zh: 如果你记不住你的号码，就用密码把它写在预约本里。

ex.en: I can't remember what I said.
ex.zh: 我记不起我说过什么了。

e.en: If you remember to do something, you do it when you intend to. 记住 (做某事)

ex.en: Please remember to enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope when writing.
ex.zh: 请记住写信的时候附上一个贴好邮票、写好自己姓名地址的信封。

d: v. 回想起，记得；记起，忆起（某事物）；记牢，不忘记；纪念，缅怀；（祈祷时）为......祝福；送钱，送礼（给某人）；代（某人）问候（某人）；（失态后）检点，补救

e.en: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them. 注意到;

ex.en: He stressed that people should not hesitate to contact the police if they've noticed any strangers recently.
ex.zh: 他强调人们最近如果注意到任何陌生人，要马上与警方联系。

ex.en: I noticed that most academics were writing papers during the summer.
ex.zh: 我注意到大部分学者那个暑期都在撰写论文。

e.en: A notice is a written announcement in a place where everyone can read it.

ex.en: Notices in the waiting room requested that you neither smoke nor spit.
ex.zh: 等候室的告示要求人们不要吸烟也不要随地吐痰。

ex.en: A few guest houses had "No Vacancies" notices in their windows.
ex.zh: 几家旅社在他们的窗户上贴出了“客满”的告示。

e.en: If you give notice about something that is going to happen, you give a warning in advance that it is going to happen.

ex.en: Interest is paid monthly. Three months' notice is required for withdrawals.
ex.zh: 利息按月给付。提款要求提前三个月通知。

ex.en: The insured must be given at least 10 days' notice of cancellation.
ex.zh: 取消保险必须给被保险人至少十天的事先通知。

e.en: A notice is a formal announcement in a newspaper or magazine about something that has happened or is going to happen.

ex.en: I spotted a notice in a local newspaper.
ex.zh: 我在当地一家报纸上看到了一则启事。

d: v. 注意到，察觉；重视，认可；评论，提及（notice 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被注意到的；受到注意的

e.en: If you describe something or someone as extraordinary, you mean that they have some extremely good or special quality.

ex.en: We've made extraordinary progress as a society in that regard.
ex.zh: 我们社会在那方面已经取得了巨大进步。

ex.en: The task requires extraordinary patience and endurance.
ex.zh: 这项工作需要非凡的耐心和毅力。

e.en: 非凡地

ex.en: She's extraordinarily disciplined.
ex.zh: 她特别遵守纪律。

e.en: If you describe something as extraordinary, you mean that it is very unusual or surprising.

ex.en: What an extraordinary thing to happen!
ex.zh: 发生了多么非同寻常的事啊！

e.en: 非同寻常地

ex.en: Apart from the hair, he looked extraordinarily unchanged.
ex.zh: 除了头发，他看上去真是一点也没变。

d: adj. 异乎寻常的，令人惊奇的；非凡的，卓越的；特别的，临时的；特大（或多）的；特派的，特命的
n. （公司正常业务活动之外的）非常账目，特支款项

e.en: Your colleagues are the people you work with, especially in a professional job.

ex.en: Without consulting his colleagues, he flew from Los Angeles to Chicago.
ex.zh: 在没有和同事商量的情况下，他从洛杉矶飞到了芝加哥。

d: n. 同事，同僚
adv. 难以置信地；非常地

e.en: Taught is the past tense and past participle of . (teach)

d: v. 教，教授（teach 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Curiosity is a desire to know about something.

ex.en: Ryle accepted more out of curiosity than anything else.
ex.zh: 赖尔接受更多是出于好奇心而不是别的原因。

ex.en: ...enthusiasm and genuine curiosity about the past.
ex.zh: …对过去的热情和真正的好奇。

e.en: A curiosity is something that is unusual, interesting, and fairly rare.

ex.en: There is much to see in the way of castles, curiosities, and museums.
ex.zh: 那里有许多可看的城堡、奇珍异宝和博物馆。

d: n. 好奇心，求知欲；珍品，奇事

e.en: A film consists of moving pictures that have been recorded so that they can be shown in a theatre or on television. A film tells a story, or shows a real situation.

ex.en: Everything about the film was good. Good acting, good story, good fun.
ex.zh: 这部电影样样都好：演技好，故事好，非常有趣。

e.en: A film of powder, liquid, or oil is a very thin layer of it.

ex.en: The sea is coated with a film of raw sewage.
ex.zh: 海上覆盖着薄薄一层未经处理的污水。

e.en: If you film something, you use a camera to take moving pictures which can be shown on a screen or on television.

ex.en: He had filmed her life story.
ex.zh: 他已经把她的人生故事拍成了电影。

e.en: Film of something is moving pictures of a real event that are shown on television or on a screen.

ex.en: He likes to look at film of old-time players.
ex.zh: 他喜欢看那些以前运动员的影片。

d: n. 电影，影片；电影艺术，电影业；胶卷，底片；薄膜，薄层；纪实镜头，记录画面；细丝
v. 录制，拍摄电影；（似）被覆盖上一薄层东西，变得朦胧；在……上覆以薄膜

e.en: If you enjoy something, you find pleasure and satisfaction in doing it or experiencing it.

ex.en: Ross had always enjoyed the company of women.
ex.zh: 罗斯一直都很享受女人的陪伴。

ex.en: He was a guy who enjoyed life to the full.
ex.zh: 他是个尽情享受生活乐趣的人。

e.en: If you enjoy yourself, you do something that you like doing or you take pleasure in the situation that you are in. (自)

ex.en: I am really enjoying myself at the moment.
ex.zh: 我此刻很是自得其乐。

e.en: If you enjoy something such as a right, benefit, or privilege, you have it.

ex.en: The average German will enjoy 40 days' paid holiday this year.
ex.zh: 德国人今年平均将享有40天带薪假期。

d: v. （enjoy 的过去式和过去分词）享受，欣赏，喜爱；过得愉快，玩得开心（用于 enjoy oneself）；享有（权利、利益、好处等）

e.en: A film consists of moving pictures that have been recorded so that they can be shown in a theatre or on television. A film tells a story, or shows a real situation.

ex.en: Everything about the film was good. Good acting, good story, good fun.
ex.zh: 这部电影样样都好：演技好，故事好，非常有趣。

e.en: A film of powder, liquid, or oil is a very thin layer of it.

ex.en: The sea is coated with a film of raw sewage.
ex.zh: 海上覆盖着薄薄一层未经处理的污水。

e.en: If you film something, you use a camera to take moving pictures which can be shown on a screen or on television.

ex.en: He had filmed her life story.
ex.zh: 他已经把她的人生故事拍成了电影。

e.en: Film of something is moving pictures of a real event that are shown on television or on a screen.

ex.en: He likes to look at film of old-time players.
ex.zh: 他喜欢看那些以前运动员的影片。

d: n. （film 的复数）电影，影片；薄膜，薄层，膜；（摄影）胶片，胶卷；电影艺术，电影业
v. （film 的第三人称单数）拍摄；以薄膜覆盖

e.en: Joy is a feeling of great happiness.

ex.en: Salter shouted with joy.
ex.zh: 索尔特高兴地叫起来。

e.en: A joy is something or someone that makes you feel happy or gives you great pleasure. 使人高兴的事;

ex.en: Spending evenings outside is one of the joys of summer.
ex.zh: 在户外消磨晚间时光是夏天的乐事之一。

e.en: If you say that someone is jumping for joy, you mean that they are very pleased or happy about something.

ex.en: He jumped for joy on being told the news.
ex.zh: 听到这个消息他兴高采烈。

d: n. 欢欣，高兴；使人高兴的人（或物），乐趣；成功，满足
v. 感到高兴，感到欣喜

e.en: If you love someone, you feel romantically or sexually attracted to them, and they are very important to you.

ex.en: Oh, Amy, I love you.
ex.zh: 啊，埃米，我爱你。

e.en: Love is a very strong feeling of affection toward someone who you are romantically or sexually attracted to.

ex.en: Our love for each other has been increased by what we've been through together.
ex.zh: 我们对彼此的爱因我们共同经历的一切而增强。

ex.en: ...an old fashioned love story.
ex.zh: …一个老套的爱情故事。

e.en: You say that you love someone when their happiness is very important to you, so that you behave in a kind and caring way toward them.

ex.en: You'll never love anyone the way you love your baby.
ex.zh: 你永远不会像疼爱你的孩子那样爱任何人。

e.en: Love is the feeling that a person's happiness is very important to you, and the way you show this feeling in your behaviour toward them.

ex.en: My love for all my children is unconditional.
ex.zh: 我对我所有孩子的疼爱是无条件的。

d: n. （对家庭成员或挚友的）喜爱，关爱；爱情，恋爱；喜好，喜爱；（昵称）亲爱的；（用于信尾署名前）爱你的；心爱之人，心爱之物；（网球、软式墙网球和其他运动）零分；（用于表示对某人的亲切好感）宝贝（a love）；仁慈的人，乐于助人的人；爱神（Love）
v. 爱恋（某人）；关爱（尤指家庭成员或密友）；喜欢（某物或某事）；热爱（国家、组织等）；很愿意；感到好笑；适于（某些特定的条件）
【名】 （Love）（英、菲、瑞、美）洛夫（人名）

e.en: A man is an adult male human being. 男子;

ex.en: He had not expected the young man to reappear before evening.
ex.zh: 他没想到那个年轻男子傍晚前会再次出现。

ex.en: I have always regarded him as a man of integrity.
ex.zh: 我一直把他看作个正直的男人。

e.en: Man and men are sometimes used to refer to all human beings, including both males and females. Some people dislike this use. 人 (用以泛指)

ex.en: The chick initially has no fear of man.
ex.zh: 小鸡最初不怕人。

e.en: If you say that a man is, for example, a gambling man or an outdoors man, you mean that he likes gambling or outdoor activities. (有某嗜好的)

ex.en: Are you a gambling man, Mr. Graham?
ex.zh: 你是个赌徒吗，格雷勒姆先生?

e.en: If you say that a man is, for example, a Harvard man or a Yale man, you mean that he went to that university. (属某院校的)

ex.en: Stewart, a Yale man, was invited to stay on and write the script.
ex.zh: 斯图尔特，一个耶鲁人，应邀留下来写该剧本。

d: n. 成年男子，男人；人类；（不论性别的）人；（来自某地、从事某种工作的）人；（喜欢某事的）人 ； （支持某组织或为其工作的）人；士兵，（男性）工人 ；上门服务的人；伙计，哥儿们；（表示不耐烦或生气）你这家伙；丈夫，男友；男子汉，大丈夫；棋子；头头，老板，警察（the Man）
v. 负责，操控（某物）
int. （表示惊奇、气愤等）嘿，天哪
【名】 （Man）（俄）马恩，（英、葡、意、罗、捷、尼、老、缅、柬）曼，（日）万（人名）
n. 密歇根（美国中西部州）；密歇根湖（北美五大湖之一）

e.en: Mischief is playing harmless tricks on people or doing things you are not supposed to do. It can also refer to the desire to do this. 恶作剧;

ex.en: The little boy was a real handful. He was always up to mischief.
ex.zh: 这个小男孩真是难管教。他总是在搞恶作剧。

e.en: Mischief is behaviour that is intended to cause trouble for people. It can also refer to the trouble that is caused.

ex.en: The more sinister explanation is that he is about to make mischief in the Middle East again.
ex.zh: 更为险恶的解释是他又要在中东制造事端。

d: n. 恶作剧，捣乱，胡闹；顽皮，淘气；伤害，麻烦，不和；（律）造成损害的行为

e.en: If something is moving, it makes you feel an emotion such as sadness, pity, or sympathy very strongly.

ex.en: It is very moving to see how much strangers can care for each other.
ex.zh: 令人非常感动的是看到陌生人能够如此互相关心。

e.en: 感人地

ex.en: You write very movingly of your sister Amy's suicide.
ex.zh: 你把你妹妹埃米的自杀写得非常令人感伤。

e.en: A moving model or part of a machine moves or is able to move. (模型或机器部件) 活动的;

ex.en: It also means there are no moving parts to break down.
ex.zh: 这也意味着没有活动零部件可拆卸。

d: adj. 动人的，感人的；活动的，移动的；促使某人采取行动的；搬家的，调动的
v. （使）改变位置，（使）移动；搬家，搬迁；（使）变换，调动（move 的现在分词）
【名】 （Moving）（英、印、丹、挪、以、阿、加拿大）穆文英（人名）

e.en: If something is missing or has gone missing, it is not in its usual place, and you cannot find it.

ex.en: It was only an hour or so later that I discovered that my gun was missing.
ex.zh: 也就是一个小时左右后，我发现自己的枪不见了。

e.en: If a part of something is missing, it has been removed or has come off, and has not been replaced.

ex.en: Three buttons were missing from his shirt.
ex.zh: 他的衬衫少了3颗纽扣。

e.en: If you say that something is missing, you mean that it has not been included, and you think that it should have been.

ex.en: She had given me an incomplete list. One name was missing from it.
ex.zh: 她给了我一份不全的名单，上面漏掉了一个名字。

e.en: Someone who is missing cannot be found, and it is not known whether they are alive or dead. (人)

ex.en: Five people died in the explosion and more than one thousand were injured. One person is still missing.
ex.zh: 爆炸中5人丧生，一千多人受伤，还有1人失踪。

d: adj. 找不到的，丢失的；缺少的，缺损的；（人）失踪的，下落不明的；遗漏的，未被包括在内的
v. 未击中，未抓住；未做，错过；思念，怀念（miss 的现在分词）
【名】 （Missing）（德）米辛（人名）

e.en: If you sneak somewhere, you go there very quietly on foot, trying to avoid being seen or heard.

ex.en: Sometimes he would sneak out of his house late at night to be with me.
ex.zh: 有时候他会在深夜偷偷溜出他的家来陪伴我。

e.en: If you sneak something somewhere, you take it there secretly.

ex.en: He smuggled papers out each day, photocopied them, and snuck them back.
ex.zh: 他每天都把文件偷带出来，复印后又偷偷送回去。

e.en: If you sneak a look at someone or something, you secretly have a quick look at them.

ex.en: You sneak a look at your watch to see how long you've got to wait.
ex.zh: 你偷偷看一眼手表，看还要等多久。

d: v. 偷偷地走，潜行；偷带，私运；偷走（不重要的或小的东西）；偷偷地做（或获得）；（尤作儿童用语）打小报告，告密
n. 打小报告的人，告状者（尤指儿童）；鬼鬼祟祟的人；四分卫快速带球切入；旅游鞋，软帮运动鞋；偷偷摸摸的行为
adj. 出其不意的，偷偷摸摸的

e.en: When you sneeze, you suddenly take in your breath and then blow it down your nose noisily without being able to stop yourself, for example, because you have a cold.

ex.en: What exactly happens when we sneeze?
ex.zh: 我们打喷嚏究竟是怎么回事？

e.en: Sneeze is also a noun.

ex.en: Coughs and sneezes spread infections.
ex.zh: 咳嗽和打喷嚏会传播传染病。

e.en: If you say that something is not to be sneezed at, you mean that it is worth having.

ex.en: The money's not to be sneezed at.
ex.zh: 这笔钱可不容小视。

d: v. 打喷嚏
n. 打喷嚏，喷嚏声

e.en: When you sneeze, you suddenly take in your breath and then blow it down your nose noisily without being able to stop yourself, for example, because you have a cold.

ex.en: What exactly happens when we sneeze?
ex.zh: 我们打喷嚏究竟是怎么回事？

e.en: Sneeze is also a noun.

ex.en: Coughs and sneezes spread infections.
ex.zh: 咳嗽和打喷嚏会传播传染病。

e.en: If you say that something is not to be sneezed at, you mean that it is worth having.

ex.en: The money's not to be sneezed at.
ex.zh: 这笔钱可不容小视。

d: n. 打喷嚏
v. 打喷嚏
不容小视

e.en: You use someone or somebody to refer to a person without saying exactly who you mean.

ex.en: Her father was shot by someone trying to rob his small retail shop.
ex.zh: 她父亲被某个试图抢劫他的小零售店的人开枪打中了。

ex.en: I need someone to help me.
ex.zh: 我需要有人帮我。

e.en: If you say that a person is someone or somebody in a particular kind of work or in a particular place, you mean that they are considered to be important in that kind of work or in that place.

ex.en: "Before she came around," she says, "I was somebody in this town."
ex.zh: “她来这之前，”她说，“我在这个镇上是个人物。”

d: pron. 有人，某人；重要人物
