e.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

ex.en: That's absurd.
ex.zh: 那是荒谬的。

ex.en: It's absurd to suggest that they knew what was going on but did nothing.
ex.zh: 暗示说他们知道怎么回事但却袖手旁观是荒谬的。

e.en: The absurd is something that is absurd.

ex.en: Connie had a sharp eye for the absurd.
ex.zh: 康妮对荒谬之事有敏锐的眼光。

e.en: 荒谬地

ex.en: Prices were still absurdly low, in his opinion.
ex.zh: 在他看来，价格依然低得荒谬。

d: adj. 愚蠢的，荒谬的；滑稽可笑的；荒诞派的
n. 荒诞，荒诞的事物 （the absurd）

e.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

ex.en: He claimed that his parents had abandoned him.
ex.zh: 他声称他的父母抛弃了他。

e.en: If you abandon an activity or piece of work, you stop doing it before it is finished.

ex.en: The authorities have abandoned any attempt to distribute food in an orderly fashion.
ex.zh: 当局中途放弃了任何有序地分发食品的尝试。

e.en: If you abandon an idea or way of thinking, you stop having that idea or thinking in that way. 放弃 (想法或思想方式)

ex.en: Logic had prevailed and he had abandoned the idea.
ex.zh: 理性占了上风，他放弃了该想法。

e.en: If you say that someone does something with abandon, you mean that they behave in a wild, uncontrolled way and do not think or care about how they should behave.

ex.en: He approached life with reckless abandon–I don't think he himself knew what he was going to do next.
ex.zh: 他以不计后果的放纵态度对待生活–我想他自己都不知道他接下来要做什么。

d: v. 抛弃，遗弃；（因危险）离开，舍弃；中止，不再有；放弃（信念、信仰或看法）；陷入，沉湎于（某种情感）
n. 放任，放纵

e.en: Admiration is a feeling of great liking and respect for a person or thing.

ex.en: I have always had the greatest admiration for him.
ex.zh: 我对他一直怀有最大的钦佩。

d: n. 钦佩，赞美，欣赏；赞美对象

e.en: If you regard someone or something with affection, you like them and are fond of them.

ex.en: She thought of him with affection.
ex.zh: 她怀着喜爱想起了他。

e.en: Your affections are your feelings of love or fondness for someone.

ex.en: Caroline is the object of his affections.
ex.zh: 卡罗琳是他感情的归属。

d: n. 喜爱，关爱；爱恋，爱慕之情；精神状况，感情；疾患，病；影响

e.en: If people agree with each other about something, they have the same opinion about it or say that they have the same opinion.

ex.en: Both have agreed on the need for the money.
ex.zh: 双方都同意需要那笔钱。

ex.en: So we both agree there's a problem?
ex.zh: 那么我们两个人都同意是有一个问题啦？

e.en: If people agree on something, they all decide to accept or do something.

ex.en: The warring sides have agreed on an unconditional ceasefire.
ex.zh: 交战各方已经对无条件停火达成了一致意见。

e.en: In grammar, if a word agrees with a noun or pronoun, it has a form that is appropriate to the number or gender of the noun or pronoun. For example, in "He hates it," the singular verb agrees with the singular pronoun "he."
If you agree to do something, you say that you will do it. If you agree to a proposal, you accept it. 答应;

ex.en: He agreed to pay me for the drawings.
ex.zh: 她答应为这些画付给我钱。

d: v. 同意（agree 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: Alien means belonging to a different country, race, or group, usually one you do not like or are frightened of.

ex.en: He said they were opposed to what he described as the presence of alien forces in the region.
ex.zh: 他说他们反对他所描述的在该地区有外国军队的存在。

e.en: If something is alien to you or to your normal feelings or behaviour, it is not the way you would normally feel or behave.

ex.en: Such an attitude is alien to most businessmen.
ex.zh: 这种态度对大多数商人都很陌生。

e.en: An alien is someone who is not a legal citizen of the country in which they live.

ex.en: Both women had hired illegal aliens for child care.
ex.zh: 这两个女人都雇佣了非法入境者来照看孩子。

e.en: In science fiction, an alien is a creature from outer space.

ex.en: ...aliens from another planet.
ex.zh: …从另一个行星来的外星人。

d: adj. 陌生的；外国的，异域的；与外星人有关的，与地球外有关的；（植物或动物种类）外来的；不相容的，格格不入的 （alien to）
n. 外国人，侨民；外星人（或生物）；（植物或动物种类）外国引进品种
v. 让渡，转让
【名】 （Alien）（法）阿利安（人名）
一胎中最小的猪仔
n. 安东尼（男子名）
adv. 不具名地，匿名地；化名地

e.en: When you approach something, you get closer to it.

ex.en: He didn't approach the front door at once.
ex.zh: 他没有立即走近前门。

ex.en: When I approached, they grew silent.
ex.zh: 当我走近时，他们变得沉默了。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: At their approach the little boy ran away and hid.
ex.zh: 当他们走近时，那个小男孩跑开了并藏了起来。

e.en: If you approach someone about something, you speak to them about it for the first time, often making an offer or request.

ex.en: When Brown approached me about the job, my first reaction was of disbelief.
ex.zh: 当布朗为这份工作找我时，我的第一反应是不相信。

ex.en: He approached me to create and design the restaurant.
ex.zh: 他来找我创办并设计那家餐馆。

e.en: Approach is also a noun.

ex.en: There had already been approaches from buyers interested in the whole of the group.
ex.zh: 已经有一些对整个集团感兴趣的买主来接洽了。

d: v. 接近，靠近，临近（approach 的 ing 形式）；（航空）进场，进近
adj. 正在接近的，临近的，即将到来的

e.en: If two or more things are alike, they are similar in some way.

ex.en: We looked very alike.
ex.zh: 我们长得很相像。

e.en: Alike means in a similar way.

ex.en: They even dressed alike.
ex.zh: 他们甚至连穿着都相像。

d: adj. 相似的，相像的
adv. 相似地，相同地；两者都，同样地
【名】 （Alike）（美、印）艾立凯（人名）

e.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

ex.en: ...a long, hot and arduous trip.
ex.zh: …一段漫长、灼热、艰难的旅程。

d: adj. 艰辛的，困难的

e.en: An artist is someone who draws or paints pictures or creates sculptures as a job or a hobby.

ex.en: ...the studio of a great artist.
ex.zh: …一位伟大美术家的工作室。

ex.en: Each poster is signed by the artist.
ex.zh: 每张海报都由这位美术家签了名。

e.en: An artist is a person who creates novels, poems, films, or other things which can be considered as works of art.

ex.en: His books are enormously easy to read, yet he is a serious artist.
ex.zh: 他的书极易读，然而他却是一位严肃的文学艺术家。

e.en: An artist is a performer such as a musician, actor, or dancer.

ex.en: ...a popular artist who has sold millions of records.
ex.zh: …一位卖了上百万张唱片的、受人欢迎的表演艺术家。

d: n. 艺术家，美术家；表演艺术家；大师，行家

e.en: A band is a small group of musicians who play popular music such as jazz, rock, or pop. (演奏流行音乐的)

ex.en: He was a drummer in a rock band.
ex.zh: 他曾是一支摇滚乐队里的鼓手。

e.en: A band is a group of musicians who play brass and percussion instruments. (演奏管乐和打击乐的)

ex.en: Bands played German marches.
ex.zh: 管乐队演奏了德国的进行曲。

e.en: A band of people is a group of people who have joined together because they share an interest or belief. (趣味相投的)

ex.en: Bands of government soldiers, rebels and just plain criminals have been roaming some neighbourhoods.
ex.zh: 一群群政府士兵、叛乱分子和纯属一般的罪犯一直在一些街区里游荡。

e.en: A band is a flat, narrow strip of cloth which you wear around your head or wrists, or which forms part of a piece of clothing. (指服饰)

ex.en: Almost all hospitals use a wrist-band of some kind with your name and details on it.
ex.zh: 几乎所有医院都使用某种腕带，上面有你的名字和详细信息。

d: n. 乐队；一伙，一群；范围，段；带，箍；带状物，条纹；波段，频带；戒指
v. 给……分级，把……分段；用带绑扎；加彩条
n. 注意力，专注；体贴，周到

e.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

ex.en: The man's bald head was beaded with sweat.
ex.zh: 这位男子的秃头上满是汗珠。

e.en: 秃顶

ex.en: He wears a cap to cover a spot of baldness.
ex.zh: 他戴一顶帽子来遮住一小块秃顶。

e.en: If a tyre is bald, its surface has worn down and it is no longer safe to use. (轮胎表面)
A bald statement is in plain language and contains no extra explanation or information. (陈述等)

ex.en: The bald truth is he's just not happy.
ex.zh: 明摆着的事实是他就是不高兴。

d: adj. 秃头的；光秃的，磨光的，掉光的；不加修饰的，直截了当的
【名】 （Bald）（英）鲍尔德，（德、法、波）巴尔德（人名）

e.en: mad; crazy
(intensifier)

ex.en: barking mad

d: adj. （英，非正式）疯狂的，精神错乱的
adv. 作强调成分
n. 狗叫声；（木）剥皮，去皮；（Barking）（德、美）巴尔金（人名）
v. 吠；咆哮，厉声说出；擦破（或蹭掉）……的皮（bark的现在分词）

e.en: Baseball is a game played by two teams of nine players. Each player from one team hits a ball with a bat and then tries to run around three bases and get to home plate before the other team can get the ball back. Compare .
A baseball is a small hard ball which is used in the game of baseball.

d: n. 棒球运动；棒球（比赛用的小硬球）

e.en: The way that you behave is the way that you do and say things, and the things that you do and say. 行为;

ex.en: I couldn't believe these people were behaving in this way.
ex.zh: 我无法相信这些人竟这样行事。

e.en: If you behave or behave yourself, you act in the way that people think is correct and proper. 使…规矩;

ex.en: You have to behave.
ex.zh: 你得守规矩。

e.en: In science, the way that something behaves is the things that it does. (科学领域)

ex.en: Under certain conditions, electrons can behave like waves rather than particles.
ex.zh: 在某些条件下，电子能像波而不是粒子那样运动。

d: v. behave 的现在分词：行为，表现；（科学/技术）起反应，起作用；守规矩，举止得体

e.en: The breadth of something is the distance between its two sides.

ex.en: The breadth of the whole camp was 400 paces.
ex.zh: 整个营地的宽度为400步。

e.en: The breadth of something is its quality of consisting of or involving many different things.

ex.en: Older people have a tremendous breadth of experience.
ex.zh: 年长的人们有极其广泛的经验。

d: n. 宽度，幅度；广度，广泛性

e.en: If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.

ex.en: Both are blessed with an uncommon ability to fix things.
ex.zh: 俩人都有幸具有不寻常的修理东西的能力。

e.en: You use blessed to describe something that you think is wonderful, and that you are grateful for or relieved about.

ex.en: The birth of a live healthy baby is a truly blessed event.
ex.zh: 生一个活泼健康的孩子确实是一件幸运的事。

e.en: 幸运地

ex.en: ...a wall still blessedly warm from the day's sun.
ex.zh: …一堵受到了日间阳光照晒依然温暖的墙。

d: adj. 受祝福的，受上帝保佑的；神圣的，尊敬的；有福的，幸运的；带来幸福的，带来好运的；令人愉快安宁的；有幸具有的，赋有…的（常用于 be blessed with）；该死的，表示恼怒的
v. 祝福，保佑，求神赐福；祝圣，使神圣化；称颂上帝（bless 的过去式和过去分词）
adv. 大胆地；冒失地；显眼地

e.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful. 极有才智的;

ex.en: She had a brilliant mind.
ex.zh: 她有极聪明的头脑。

e.en: 极有才智地;

ex.en: It is a very high quality production, brilliantly written and acted.
ex.zh: 这是一部非常高质量的演出,绝妙地编写而成并被表演出来。

e.en: A brilliant career or success is very successful.

ex.en: He served four years in prison, emerging to find his brilliant career in ruins.
ex.zh: 他在监狱服了4年刑,出狱后发现他的辉煌事业已经毁了。

e.en: 非常成功地

ex.en: The strategy worked brilliantly.
ex.zh: 这项策略非常成功。

d: adj. 巧妙的，使人印象深的；成功的，辉煌的；聪颖的，技艺高超的；明亮的，鲜艳的

e.en: If something buzzes or buzzes somewhere, it makes a long continuous sound, like the noise a bee makes when it is flying.

ex.en: The intercom buzzed and he pressed down the appropriate switch.
ex.zh: 对讲机嗡嗡地响起来，他按下了相应的开关。

e.en: Buzz is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the irritating buzz of an insect.
ex.zh: …一只昆虫的烦人的嗡嗡声。

e.en: If people are buzzing around, they are moving around quickly and busily.

ex.en: A few tourists were buzzing around.
ex.zh: 几名游客在匆忙地跑来跑去。

e.en: If questions or ideas are buzzing around your head, or if your head is buzzing with questions or ideas, you are thinking about a lot of things, often in a confused way.

ex.en: Many more questions were buzzing around in my head.
ex.zh: 更多的问题在我头脑中翻腾。

d: v. buzz 的现在分词；发出嗡嗡声；（耳朵）充满嗡嗡声；用蜂鸣器发信号；给……打电话；迅速（或匆忙）地移动；低空掠过；（地方）喧闹；（头脑）兴奋（或混乱）；猛掷
n. 嗡嗡声；嘈杂声
adj. 嗡嗡响的；热闹的，充满活力的，繁忙的

e.en: If you carry something, you take it with you, holding it so that it does not touch the ground. 提;

ex.en: He was carrying a briefcase.
ex.zh: 他提着公文包。

ex.en: She carried her son to the car.
ex.zh: 她抱着儿子向车走去。

e.en: If you carry something, you have it with you wherever you go.

ex.en: You have to carry a pager so that they can call you in at any time.
ex.zh: 你得带个传呼机，以便他们随时可以联系到你。

e.en: If something carries a person or thing somewhere, it takes them there.

ex.en: Flowers are designed to attract insects which then carry the pollen from plant to plant.
ex.zh: 花儿天生就能吸引昆虫，昆虫则在植物之间传递花粉。

ex.en: The delegation was carrying a message of thanks to President Mubarak.
ex.zh: 代表团向穆巴拉克总统传达谢意。

e.en: If a person or animal is carrying a disease, they are infected with it and can pass it on to other people or animals. 携带 (病毒)

ex.en: The test could be used to screen healthy people to see if they are carrying the virus.
ex.zh: 这项测试可以用来检查健康人群，看他们是否携带该病毒。

d: v. 提，扛，背；携带，佩戴；运送，载运；传输（水、电等）；传播（疾病）；能记住，能回想起；支撑，承载；承担（责任）；推动，发展；具有（某种特质）；带有，导致；被判处（某种刑罚）；传得远；扔（或踢）到……距离；以多数同意批准（提议）；赢得……的支持；赢得（州或地区的）选举；标有，贴有；刊登，广播；出售；怀（胎）；保持姿态；（加法）进位；准确地唱；超重，超载
n. 搬运；带球跑；掷（击）球距离，（枪的）射程；随身携带（尤指枪）；（财政）转记，结转；水上运输的地方或路线；进位
【名】 （Carry）（英）卡里（人名）

e.en: Chemistry is the scientific study of the structure of substances and of the way that they react with other substances.
The chemistry of an organism or a material is the chemical substances that make it up and the chemical reactions that go on inside it. 化学成分;

ex.en: We have literally altered the chemistry of our planet's atmosphere.
ex.zh: 我们实际上改变了地球大气层的化学成分。

e.en: If you say that there is chemistry between two people, you mean that it is obvious they are attracted to each other or like each other very much. (彼此间的)

ex.en: ...the extraordinary chemistry between Ingrid and Bogart.
ex.zh: …英格丽德和博加特之间强烈的相互吸引。

d: n. 化学；化学成分，化学反应；（彼此间的）吸引

e.en: A child is a human being who is not yet an adult.

ex.en: When I was a child I lived in a country village.
ex.zh: 小时候我住在乡村里。

ex.en: ...a child of six.
ex.zh: …一个6岁的小孩。

e.en: Someone's children are their sons and daughters of any age.

ex.en: How are the children?
ex.zh: 孩子们好吗？

ex.en: His children have left home.
ex.zh: 他的儿女们已经离开家了。

d: n. 儿童，小孩；子女；深受（某时期思想）影响的人；孩子气的人，幼稚的人；缺乏经验的人
n. 契诃夫（俄国著名作家）

e.en: If you describe someone as clueless, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they do not know anything about a particular subject or that they are incapable of doing a particular thing properly.

ex.en: I came into adult life clueless about a lot of things that most people take for granted.
ex.zh: 我成年后，发现自己对大多数人认为是理所当然之事知之甚少。

d: adj. 一无所知的，毫无头绪的（常与 about 连用）；愚蠢的，无能的（非正式，含贬义）

e.en: a yellow butterfly, Gonepteryx cleopatra, the male of which has its wings flushed with orange

d: n. 克利欧佩特拉（女子名）；《埃及艳后》（电影名）

e.en: You use complete to emphasize that something is as great in extent, degree, or amount as it possibly can be.

ex.en: The house is a complete mess.
ex.zh: 这房子实在太乱了。

ex.en: The rebels had taken complete control.
ex.zh: 叛乱者已经取得了完全的控制。

e.en: 完全地

ex.en: Dozens of homes had been completely destroyed.
ex.zh: 数十家房屋已被完全毁坏了。

ex.en: Make sure that you defrost it completely.
ex.zh: 确保将其彻底除霜。

e.en: You can use complete to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something and not just part of it.

ex.en: A complete apartment complex was burned to the ground.
ex.zh: 整座公寓大楼被烧成平地。

e.en: If something is complete, it contains all the parts that it should contain.

ex.en: The list may not be complete.
ex.zh: 这份清单可能不完整。

ex.en: ...a complete dinner service.
ex.zh: …一整套餐具。

d: adj. 完全的，彻底的；全部的，完整的；完成的，结束的；技能全面的，技术娴熟的；向前传球成功的
v. 使完整，使完美；填写（表格）；完成，结束

e.en: A conspirator is a person who joins a conspiracy.

ex.en: Julius Caesar was murdered by a group of conspirators famously headed by Marcus Junius Brutus.
ex.zh: 尤利乌斯·凯撒被以人所共知的马库斯·朱尼厄斯·布鲁特斯为首脑的一伙谋反者谋杀了。

d: n. 共谋者，同谋者，阴谋者

e.en: If you have a conversation with someone, you talk with them, usually in an informal situation. (非正式的)

ex.en: He's a talkative guy, and I struck up a conversation with him.
ex.zh: 他是一个健谈的人，我和他聊了起来。

d: n. （非正式的）谈话，交谈；社交，交际

e.en: Courage is the quality shown by someone who decides to do something difficult or dangerous, even though they may be afraid.

ex.en: General Lewis Mackenzie has impressed everyone with his authority and personal courage.
ex.zh: 刘易斯·麦肯齐将军以其权威和个人勇气给每个人留下了深刻印象。

d: n. 勇气，胆量
【名】 （Courage）（英）卡里奇，（法）库拉热（人名）
n. 《达芙妮》（歌剧名）；（墨、美、巴西、以、意、印、秘）达夫内（人名）

e.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

ex.en: We asked her to describe what kind of things she did in her spare time.
ex.zh: 我们请她描述她在闲暇时做些什么。

ex.en: She read a poem by Carver which describes their life together.
ex.zh: 她读了一首卡弗描写他们在一起生活的诗。

e.en: If a person describes someone or something as a particular thing, he or she believes that they are that thing and says so. 讲成;

ex.en: He described it as an extraordinarily tangled and complicated tale.
ex.zh: 他把它讲成了一个格外错综复杂的故事。

ex.en: Even his closest allies describe him as forceful, aggressive, and determined.
ex.zh: 甚至他最亲密的同盟者们都说他强势、好斗且坚决。

d: v. 描述，形容；做……运动，形成……形状

e.en: If you are in disguise, you are not wearing your usual clothes or you have altered your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.

ex.en: You'll have to travel in disguise.
ex.zh: 你将不得不乔装出行。

e.en: If you disguise yourself, you put on clothes which make you look like someone else or alter your appearance in other ways, so that people will not recognize you.

ex.en: She disguised herself as a man so she could fight on the battlefield.
ex.zh: 她女扮男装以便能上战场打仗。

e.en: 乔装的

ex.en: The extremists entered the building disguised as medical workers.
ex.zh: 极端分子们假扮成医务人员，进入了大楼。

e.en: To disguise something means to hide it or make it appear different so that people will not know about it or will not recognize it.

ex.en: He made no attempt to disguise his agitation.
ex.zh: 他无意掩饰他的不安。

d: v. 假扮，伪装；掩饰，隐瞒
n. 伪装物，伪装

e.en: If you earn money, you receive money in return for work that you do. 挣 (钱)

ex.en: What a lovely way to earn a living.
ex.zh: 一个多好的谋生方式啊！

e.en: If something earns money, it produces money as profit or interest. 赢 (利)

ex.en: ...a bank account that earns little or no interest.
ex.zh: …一个很少或不生利息的银行账户。

e.en: If you earn something such as praise, you get it because you deserve it.

ex.en: Companies must earn a reputation for honesty.
ex.zh: 公司必须赢得诚信。

d: adj. 挣得的；应得的；凭努力获得的
v. earn 的过去式和过去分词：赚得，挣得；赢得，博得；引起，招致；产生（利息或收益）
n. earned income：劳动收入，劳动所得；已获收益

e.en: If you are ecstatic, you feel very happy and full of excitement.

ex.en: His wife gave birth to their first child, and he was ecstatic about it.
ex.zh: 他的妻子生下了他们的第一个孩子，他对此欣喜若狂。

e.en: 欣喜若狂地

ex.en: We are both ecstatically happy.
ex.zh: 我们俩都欣喜若狂。

e.en: You can use ecstatic to describe reactions that are very enthusiastic and excited. For example, if someone receives an ecstatic reception or an ecstatic welcome, they are greeted with great enthusiasm and excitement.

ex.en: They gave an ecstatic reception to the speech.
ex.zh: 他们给该演讲以热烈的欢迎。

d: adj. 狂喜的；出神的，入迷的；（反应）热情的，兴奋的
n. 心醉神迷的人

e.en: Something that is encouraging gives people hope or confidence.

ex.en: There are encouraging signs of an artistic revival.
ex.zh: 有了鼓舞人心的艺术复兴的迹象。

ex.en: The results have been encouraging.
ex.zh: 这些结果是鼓舞人心的。

e.en: 鼓舞人心地

ex.en: The people at the next table watched me eat and smiled encouragingly.
ex.zh: 邻桌的人们看着我吃，鼓励地微笑着。

d: adj. 鼓舞人心的，鼓励的
v. 鼓励，激励；鼓动，怂恿，支持；刺激，促进（encourage 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If a place is exposed, it has no natural protection against bad weather or enemies, for example, because it has no trees or is on very high ground. 暴露的;

ex.en: ...an exposed hillside in Connecticut.
ex.zh: ...康涅狄格一块暴露的山坡。

d: adj. 暴露的，无遮蔽的；无保护的，易受攻击的；风险高的，很可能遭受经济损失的
v. 暴露，使显露；使面临，使遭受（危险或不快）；揭露，揭发（expose 的过去分词形式）

e.en: If you describe an event or a period of time as eventful, you mean that a lot of interesting, exciting, or important things have happened during it. 充满 (有趣、重要)

ex.en: This has been an eventful year for Tom, both professionally and personally.
ex.zh: 不论在事业方面还是在个人方面，对汤姆来说这一年都是有着许多重大变化的一年。

d: adj. 充满大事的，多变故的；重大的，重要的

e.en: Equally means in sections, amounts, or spaces that are the same size as each other.

ex.en: Try to get into the habit of eating at least three small meals a day, at equally spaced intervals.
ex.zh: 试着养成每天隔相等的时间吃至少3小餐的习惯。

e.en: Equally means to the same degree or extent.

ex.en: All these techniques are equally effective.
ex.zh: 所有这些方法都同等有效。

e.en: Equally is used to introduce another comment on the same topic, that balances or contrasts with the previous comment. 同样地 (用于引出同一话题的另议)

ex.en: Subscribers should be allowed call-blocking services, but equally, they should be able to choose whether to accept calls from blocked numbers.
ex.zh: 用户应当被允许使用拒收来电服务，但同样地，他们也应能够选择是否接听被阻拦号码的来电。

d: adv. （程度）相当地，同样地；平均地，相等地；（用于补充观点）同样（重要）地

e.en: If someone or something is familiar to you, you recognize them or know them well.

ex.en: He talked of other cultures as if they were more familiar to him than his own.
ex.zh: 他谈起其他文化就像它们对于他比他自己的文化还熟悉。

ex.en: They are already familiar faces on our TV screens.
ex.zh: 他们已经是我们电视屏幕上熟悉的面孔了。

e.en: 熟悉

ex.en: Tony was unnerved by the uncanny familiarity of her face.
ex.zh: 托尼被她不寻常的熟悉面孔弄得心烦意乱。

e.en: If you are familiar with something, you know or understand it well.

ex.en: Most people are familiar with this figure from Wagner's opera.
ex.zh: 多数人对瓦格纳歌剧中的这个人物是熟悉的。

e.en: 熟悉

ex.en: The enemy would always have the advantage of familiarity with the rugged terrain.
ex.zh: 敌人会一直在对崎岖地形的熟悉上占有优势。

d: adj. 熟悉的；常见的，普通的；非正式的，随和的；过分亲密的，随便的
n. （与女巫共居的）妖精；知交，密友；（在教皇或主教家服务的）仆人
【名】 （Familiar）（西）法米利亚尔（人名）

e.en: Someone or something that is famous is very well known.

ex.en: ...one of Kentucky's most famous landmarks.
ex.zh: …肯塔基州最有名的标志之一。

d: adj. 著名的，出名的；极好的，了不起的

e.en: If you say that something is fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

ex.en: I have a fantastic social life.
ex.zh: 我有着极好的社交生活。

e.en: A fantastic amount or quantity is an extremely large one. 极大的 (量)

ex.en: ...fantastic amounts of money.
ex.zh: …几笔巨款。

e.en: 极其

ex.en: ...a fantastically expensive restaurant.
ex.zh: …一家极其昂贵的餐馆。

d: adj. 极好的，非常棒的；极大的，极高的；不切实际的，异想天开的；奇异的，怪诞的

e.en: Fast means happening, moving, or doing something at great speed. You also use fast in questions or statements about speed.

ex.en: ...fast cars with flashing lights and sirens.
ex.zh: …闪灯、鸣笛、快速行驶的汽车。

ex.en: The only question is how fast the process will be.
ex.zh: 惟一的问题是这个过程会有多快。

e.en: Fast is also an adverb.

ex.en: They work terrifically fast.
ex.zh: 他们工作极快。

ex.en: It would be nice to go faster and break the world record.
ex.zh: 再快一些，打破世界纪录就好了。

e.en: If a watch or clock is fast, it is showing a time that is later than the real time. (钟表)

ex.en: That clock's an hour fast.
ex.zh: 那个钟快了一个小时。

e.en: If colours or dyes are fast, they do not come out of the fabrics they are used on when they get wet.

ex.en: The fabric was ironed to make the colours fast.
ex.zh: 这布被熨烫过以使其不褪色。

d: adj. 快的，迅速的；系牢的，紧缚的；寻欢作乐的；不褪色的；忠实的，可靠的
adv. 快速地；坚定地，牢固地
v. 斋戒，禁食
n. 斋戒，斋戒期

e.en: The gears on a machine or vehicle are a device for changing the rate at which energy is changed into motion.

ex.en: On hills, he must use low gears.
ex.zh: 在山上，他必须用低速挡。

ex.en: The car was in fourth gear.
ex.zh: 那辆汽车处于第4挡。

e.en: The gear involved in a particular activity is the equipment or special clothing that you use. (用于特定活动的)

ex.en: About 100 officers in riot gear were needed to break up the fight.
ex.zh: 大约需要100名配备防暴装备的警官来结束那场斗殴。

ex.en: ...fishing gear.
ex.zh: …钓鱼用具。

e.en: Gear means clothing.

ex.en: I used to wear trendy gear but it just looked ridiculous.
ex.zh: 我过去常穿时髦服装，但那看起来简直滑稽。

e.en: If someone or something is geared to or toward a particular purpose, they are organized or designed in order to achieve that purpose.

ex.en: Colleges are not always geared to the needs of mature students.
ex.zh: 大学并不总是去适应成年学生的需要。

ex.en: My training was geared toward winning gold.
ex.zh: 我的训练是为赢得金牌去规划的。

d: n. 排挡，齿轮；（用于特定目的的）装备，服装；（做事的）速度，努力；（特定用途的）器械，装置；毒品；所有物，财物
v. 使变速，使调挡
【名】 （Gear）（英）吉尔（人名）

e.en: If you say that something will happen or continue forever, you mean that it will always happen or continue.

ex.en: I think that we will live together forever.
ex.zh: 我想我们会永远生活在一起。

e.en: If something has gone or changed forever, it has gone or changed completely and permanently. 永久地;

ex.en: The old social order was gone forever.
ex.zh: 旧的社会秩序一去不复返了。

e.en: If you say that something takes forever or lasts forever, you are emphasizing that it takes or lasts a very long time, or that it seems to. 很长久地;

ex.en: The drive seemed to take forever.
ex.zh: 这车好像永远也开不到头似的。

d: adv. 永远；完全地，永恒地；长久地；老是，没完没了地；万岁（用在物或人名后，表示支持的口号）
n. 极长的时间，永恒
adj. 长期的，永久的

e.en: If you refer to someone's generosity, you mean that they are generous, especially in doing or giving more than is usual or expected.

ex.en: There are stories about his generosity, the massive amounts of money he gave to charities.
ex.zh: 关于他的慷慨有些传闻，说他向慈善机构捐献巨款。

d: n. 慷慨，大方

e.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

ex.en: Dietler is generous with his time and money.
ex.zh: 迪特勒在他的时间和金钱方面慷慨大方。

e.en: 慷慨地

ex.en: We would like to thank all the judges who gave so generously of their time.
ex.zh: 我们想感谢所有慷慨地付出时间的裁判们。

e.en: A generous person is friendly, helpful, and willing to see the good qualities in someone or something.

ex.en: He was always generous in sharing his enormous knowledge.
ex.zh: 他一直不吝分享自己丰富的知识。

e.en: 宽厚地

ex.en: The students generously gave them instruction in social responsibility.
ex.zh: 学生们欣然为他们讲解了社会责任。

d: adj. 慷慨的，大方的；大量的，丰富的；宽宏大量的
adv. 慷慨地，大方地；宽厚地，宽大地；丰盛地，大量地

e.en: Someone who is gifted has a natural ability to do something well.

ex.en: ...one of the most gifted players in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上最有天赋的运动员之一。

e.en: A gifted child is much more intelligent or talented than average. (儿童)

ex.en: ...a state programme for gifted children.
ex.zh: …一项培养天才儿童的国家计划。

d: adj. 有天赋的，有才华的；聪慧的，有特长的
v. 赠送；（无意中）让（对手）获得（gift 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If something such as a building or a piece of scenery has grandeur, it is impressive because of its size, its beauty, or its power.

ex.en: Venezuela is the ideal starting point to explore the grandeur and natural beauty of South America.
ex.zh: 委内瑞拉是探索南美的宏伟壮观与自然美景的理想出发点。

e.en: Someone's grandeur is the great importance and social status that they have, or think they have. 高贵;

ex.en: He is wholly concerned with his own grandeur.
ex.zh: 他只关心他自己的显赫地位。

d: n. 壮丽，雄伟；（社会地位的）高贵

e.en: A grown-up is an adult.

ex.en: Jan was almost a grown-up.
ex.zh: 简几乎是个大人了。

e.en: Someone who is grown-up is physically and mentally mature and no longer depends on their parents or another adult.

ex.en: I seem to have everything anyone could want–a good husband, a lovely home, grown-up children who're doing well.
ex.zh: 我似乎拥有任何人想要的一切–好丈夫,可爱的家和已长大成人、有出息的子女。

e.en: If you say that someone is grown-up, you mean that they behave in an adult way, often when they are in fact still a child.

ex.en: She's very grown-up.
ex.zh: 她非常成人化。

e.en: Grown-up things seem suitable for or typical of adults.

ex.en: Her songs tackle grown-up subjects.
ex.zh: 她的歌曲以成人题材为主题。

d: adj. 成年的，成熟的；适于成人的，成年人特有的；似成人的，成熟的
n. （尤指用于对儿童说话时）大人，成年人

e.en: Halftime is the short period of time between the two parts of a sports event such as a football, rugby, or basketball game, when the players take a short rest. (球赛的)

ex.en: The game started in brilliant sunshine but during halftime fog closed in.
ex.zh: 比赛在灿烂的阳光中开始，但在中场休息时却起雾了。

d: n. 中场休息；半日工作
adj. 正常时间一半的
n. 哈里特（女子名）

e.en: Something that happens occurs or is done without being planned. (偶然地)

ex.en: We cannot say for sure what will happen.
ex.zh: 我们说不准将会发生些什么。

e.en: If something happens, it occurs as a result of a situation or course of action. (作为结果)

ex.en: She wondered what would happen if her parents found her.
ex.zh: 她不知道如果父母发现了她会怎么样。

e.en: When something, especially something unpleasant, happens to you, it takes place and affects you. (尤指不愉快的事) 发生 (在某人身上)

ex.en: If we had been spotted at that point, I don't know what would have happened to us.
ex.zh: 如果那时我们被发现了，我不知道我们会有什么后果。

e.en: If you happen to do something, you do it by chance. If it happens that something is the case, it occurs by chance.

ex.en: We happened to discover we had a friend in common.
ex.zh: 我们碰巧发现我们有个共同的朋友。

d: vi. 发生（happen 的过去式及过去分词）；碰巧，恰好（happened to do something）

e.en: When a baby bird, insect, or other animal hatches, or when it is hatched, it comes out of its egg by breaking the shell. 使孵出;

ex.en: The young disappeared soon after they were hatched.
ex.zh: 幼崽孵出后不久就不见了。

e.en: When an egg hatches or when a bird, insect, or other animal hatches an egg, the egg breaks open and a baby comes out.

ex.en: The eggs hatch after a week or ten days.
ex.zh: 这些蛋1周或10天后孵化。

e.en: If you hatch a plot or a scheme, you think of it and work it out.

ex.en: He has accused opposition parties of hatching a plot to assassinate the pope.
ex.zh: 他曾指责各反对党阴谋策划暗杀教皇。

e.en: to mark (a figure, shade, etc) with fine parallel or crossed lines to indicate shading 在(图形、投影等上)

d: n. 孵化，孵出；（制图、美术）剖面线，画影线
v. 孵化，孵出；（绘画、制图）给……加影线；策划，密谋（hatch 的 ing 形式）
adj. 孵化的；孵化用的（多作定语）

e.en: A haven is a place where people or animals feel safe, secure, and happy.

ex.en: ...Lake Baringo, a freshwater haven for a mixed variety of birds.
ex.zh: …百瑞高湖，一个适合各种鸟类的淡水栖息地。

d: n. 安全地，避难所；港口，港湾
v. 为……提供避难所
【名】 （Haven）（美）黑文（人名）

e.en: Your heart is the organ in your chest that pumps the blood around your body. People also use heart to refer to the area of their chest that is closest to their heart. 心脏;

ex.en: The bullet had passed less than an inch from Andrea's heart.
ex.zh: 子弹从距安德烈亚心脏不到一英寸处穿过。

e.en: You can refer to someone's heart when you are talking about their deep feelings and beliefs.

ex.en: Alik's words filled her heart with pride.
ex.zh: 亚历克的话让她的内心充满骄傲。

e.en: You use heart when you are talking about someone's character and attitude toward other people, especially when they are kind and generous.

ex.en: She loved his brilliance and his generous heart.
ex.zh: 她爱他的才华横溢和心地宽厚。

e.en: The heart of something is the most central and important part of it.

ex.en: The heart of the problem is supply and demand.
ex.zh: 问题的核心是供给和需求。

d: n. 心，心脏；内心，感情；胸前；重点，核心；中心，中央；信心，勇气；（表示爱的）心形物；红桃牌，红心牌；菜心；同情，怜悯；爱情，情爱；（土地的）肥力
v. 喜爱，深爱
【名】 （Heart）（英）哈特（人名）

e.en: You can refer to the amusing things that people say as their humour.

ex.en: Her humour and determination were a source of inspiration to others.
ex.zh: 她的幽默与坚毅对其他人来说是一种鼓舞。

e.en: Humour is a quality in something that makes you laugh, for example in a situation, in someone's words or actions, or in a book or film. 幽默性;

ex.en: She felt sorry for the man but couldn't ignore the humour of the situation.
ex.zh: 她很同情这个男人，但面对此情此景又不禁觉得好笑。

e.en: If you are in a good humour, you feel cheerful and happy, and are pleasant to people. If you are in a bad humour, you feel bad tempered and unhappy, and are unpleasant to people.

ex.en: Christina was still not clear why he had been in such ill humour.
ex.zh: 克里斯蒂娜仍不明白为什么他的心情一直这么糟。

e.en: If you do something with good humour, you do it cheerfully and pleasantly.

ex.en: Hugo bore his illness with great courage and good humour.
ex.zh: 雨果以巨大的勇气和良好的精神状态面对疾病。

d: n. 幽默，幽默感；感觉，心情；体液； 古怪念头，想入非非
v. 迁就，迎合
n. 易卜生（姓氏）；易卜生（挪威戏剧作家）

e.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. 传授;

ex.en: The ability to impart knowledge and command respect is the essential qualification for teachers.
ex.zh: 传授知识并博得尊敬的能力对老师们来说是基本的条件。

e.en: To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality. 给予 (特定品质)

ex.en: She managed to impart great elegance to the unpretentious dress she was wearing.
ex.zh: 她努力为自己朴素的衣着增添几分优雅。

d: v. impart 的过去式和过去分词：传授（知识等），告知；给予，赋予（品质等）。
adj. 给予的，授予的，被传授的。

e.en: Something that is impossible cannot be done or cannot happen.

ex.en: It was impossible for anyone to get in because no one knew the password.
ex.zh: 任何人都不可能进得去，因为没人知道口令。

ex.en: He thinks the tax is impossible to administer.
ex.zh: 他认为治税是不可能的。

e.en: The impossible is something that is impossible.

ex.en: They were expected to do the impossible.
ex.zh: 他们被要求去做不可能的事。

e.en: 不可能地

ex.en: Mathematical physics is an almost impossibly difficult subject.
ex.zh: 数学物理学是一门难得难以想像的学科。

e.en: An impossible situation or an impossible position is one that is very difficult to deal with.

ex.en: I think he was in an impossible position.
ex.zh: 我想他当时处于一个极难应付的境地。

d: adj. 不可能的，办不到的；（境况）极其艰难的；（人）难以对付的
n. 不可能的事（the impossible）

e.en: If there is an inexhaustible supply of something, there is so much of it that it cannot all be used up. 取之不尽的;

ex.en: She has an inexhaustible supply of enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 她拥有无穷无尽的热情。

d: adj. 取之不尽的，用不完的，无穷无尽的；不知疲倦的

e.en: You use included to emphasize that a person or thing is part of the group of people or things that you are talking about.

ex.en: Many runners, myself included, are loners.
ex.zh: 包括我本人在内的许多赛跑选手都是喜欢独来独往的人。

d: adj. 包括在内的，包含在内的；（费用等）已包括的
v. include 的过去式及过去分词：包括，包含；（使）成为……的一部分；允许（某人）加入活动（或同享特权）

e.en: If you are inexperienced, you have little knowledge or experience of a particular situation or activity.

ex.en: Routine tasks are often delegated to inexperienced young doctors.
ex.zh: 例行的差事经常交给缺乏经验的年轻医生们去做。

d: adj. 无经验的，缺乏经验的，不熟练的

e.en: Injustice is a lack of fairness in a situation.

ex.en: They'll continue to fight injustice.
ex.zh: 他们将继续与不公正的现象抗争。

e.en: An injustice is an action or statement in which someone judges you or treats you unfairly. 不公正的行为;

ex.en: Calling them a bunch of capricious kids with half-formed ideas does them an injustice.
ex.zh: 把他们称作一群懵懂无知、喜怒无常的孩子是冤枉了他们。

d: n. 不公正，无道义；非正义行为，不公正事件

e.en: You use inimitable to describe someone, especially a performer, when you like or admire them because of their special qualities.

ex.en: He makes his own point in his own inimitable way.
ex.zh: 他以他独有的的方式阐述了自己的观点。

d: adj.  独特的，无比的，无法仿效的

e.en: An instinctive feeling, idea, or action is one that you have or do without thinking or reasoning.

ex.en: It's an instinctive reaction – if a child falls you pick it up.
ex.zh: 这是一种本能的反应–如果小孩摔倒了你会扶他起来。

e.en: 本能地

ex.en: Jane instinctively knew all was not well with her 10-month old son.
ex.zh: 简本能地知道她10个月大的儿子不太对劲。

d: adj. 本能的，直觉的；天生的

e.en: A remake is a movie that has the same story, and often the same title, as a movie that was made earlier.

ex.en: ...a 1953 remake of the thirties musical "Roberta."
ex.zh: ...1953年对30年代音乐剧《罗伯塔》的一次翻拍。

e.en: If a movie is remade, a new movie is made that has the same story, and often the same title, as a movie that was made earlier. 重拍; 翻拍(电影)

ex.en: Originally released in 1957, the film was remade as "The Magnificent Seven."
ex.zh: 这部电影最早在1957年上映，后被翻拍为《七侠荡寇志》。

e.en: If you have something remade, you ask someone to make it again, especially in a way that is better than before. 重新做;

ex.en: He had all the window frames in the room remade.
ex.zh: 他让人把屋子里所有的窗框都翻新了。

d: n. （电影或歌曲的）新版，改编版，翻拍版；重做；重制物
vt. 重新制作，改编，翻拍（电影或歌曲等）；重做，改造

e.en: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand. 计划;

ex.en: The three leaders had worked out a peace plan.
ex.zh: 这3位领导人已制定出了一份和平计划。

ex.en: He maintains that everything is going according to plan.
ex.zh: 他坚持说一切都在按计划进行。

e.en: If you plan what you are going to do, you decide in detail what you are going to do, and you intend to do it.

ex.en: If you plan what you're going to eat, you reduce your chances of overeating.
ex.zh: 如果你对要吃的东西加以计划，饮食过度的几率就会减少。

ex.en: He planned to leave Baghdad on Monday.
ex.zh: 他计划星期一离开巴格达。

e.en: If you have plans, you are intending to do a particular thing. (具体)

ex.en: "I'm sorry," she said. "I have plans for tonight.".
ex.zh: “抱歉，”她说。“我今晚有安排。”

e.en: When you plan something that you are going to make, build, or create, you decide what the main parts of it will be and do a drawing of how it should be made.

ex.en: It is no use trying to plan an 18-hole golf course on a 120-acre site if you have to ruin the environment to do it.
ex.zh: 要规划一个占地120公顷、拥有18洞的高尔夫球场如果必须破坏环境才能做到，那就毫无益处了。

d: n. 计划，打算（plan 的复数）；详细规划；（养老金、储蓄、保险）方案；（具体）安排
v. 计划，筹划；打算；设计；期望，预料（plan 的第三人称单数，多用于 plan on 结构）

e.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

ex.en: The dispute culminated last week in a lawsuit against the government.
ex.zh: 这场针对政府诉讼案的争论在上星期达到了高潮。

d: n. 诉讼，诉讼案

e.en: A battle is a violent fight between groups of people, especially one between military forces during a war.

ex.en: ...the victory of King William III at the Battle of the Boyne.
ex.zh: …威廉三世国王在博因河战役中所取得的胜利。

ex.en: ...a gun battle between police and drug traffickers.
ex.zh: …警察和毒品贩子之间的一场枪战。

e.en: A battle is a conflict in which different people or groups compete in order to achieve success or control. 斗争;

ex.en: ...an unfolding political battle over jobs and the economy.
ex.zh: …一场正在展开的关于就业和经济的政治较量。

ex.en: ...the eternal battle between good and evil in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上善恶之间永无休止的较量。

e.en: You can use battle to refer to someone's efforts to achieve something in spite of very difficult circumstances.

ex.en: ...the battle against crime.
ex.zh: …制止犯罪的斗争。

ex.en: She has fought a constant battle with her weight.
ex.zh: 她一直在和自己的体重作斗争。

e.en: To battle with an opposing group means to take part in a fight or contest against them. You can also say that one group or person is battling another. 与…搏斗;

ex.en: In one town thousands of people battled with police and several were reportedly wounded.
ex.zh: 在一个镇子里，成千上万的人同警察展开搏斗，据报道有几人受伤。

ex.en: The sides must battle again for a quarter-final place on December 16.
ex.zh: 两队必须于12月16日再战一次，来争夺1/4决赛的位置。

d: n. 战争，战斗，战役；竞争，较量（battle 的复数）
v. 战斗，搏斗，斗争；竞争（battle 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you add one thing to another, you put it in or on the other thing, to increase, complete, or improve it.

ex.en: Add the grated cheese to the sauce.
ex.zh: 把磨碎的奶酪加进那种酱中。

ex.en: Since 1908, chlorine has been added to drinking water.
ex.zh: 自从1908年起，氯就被添加到饮用水当中了。

e.en: If you add numbers or amounts together, you calculate their total.

ex.en: Banks add all the interest and other charges together.
ex.zh: 银行把所有利息和其他费用加在一起。

e.en: If one thing adds to another, it makes the other thing greater in degree or amount.

ex.en: This latest incident will add to the pressure on the White House.
ex.zh: 最近的这起事件会给白宫增加更多的压力。

e.en: To add a particular quality to something means to cause it to have that quality. 增添 (某种特性)

ex.en: The generous amount of garlic adds flavour.
ex.zh: 大量的蒜会增添滋味。

d: v. add 的第三人称单数现在时：加，添加；增加，增添；补充说；adds up 合计，加起来；（口语）说得通
abbr. ADDS 的缩写：高级数据显示系统（Advanced Data Display System）；美国陆军数据分发系统；应用数字数据系统（Applied Digital Data System）
n. 华盛顿（美国州名，美国城市名，美国第一任总统，姓氏）

e.en: A crocodile is a large reptile with a long body and strong jaws. Crocodiles live in rivers and eat meat.

d: n. 鳄鱼，鳄类（crocodile 的复数形式）

e.en: The sphinx is a large ancient statue of a creature with a human head and a lion's body that stands near the pyramids in Egypt. In mythology, sphinxes gave people puzzles to solve, and so a person who is mysterious or puzzling is sometimes referred to as a sphinx.

d: n. （古埃及）狮身人面像；难于理解的人；天蛾

e.en: a large fish-eating Indian crocodilian, Gavialis gangeticus, with a very long slender snout: family Gavialidae

d: n. 印度食鱼鳄（等于 gharial）

e.en: The Mediterranean is the sea between southern Europe and North Africa.

ex.en: You have the choice of night fishing in the Mediterranean, or windsurfing on a lake in Switzerland.
ex.zh: 你可选择在地中海夜间垂钓，或是在瑞士的湖上玩帆板。

e.en: The Mediterranean refers to the southern part of Europe, which is next to the Mediterranean Sea.

ex.en: Barcelona has become one of the most dynamic and prosperous cities in the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: 巴塞罗那已经成为地中海地区最具活力、最为繁荣的城市之一。

d: n. （Mediterranean）地中海地区；地中海沿岸国家居民
adj. （Mediterranean）地中海的，地中海沿岸的；地中海沿岸国家居民的；（肤色）浅黑的
n. （Mediterranean）（美、巴、埃、澳）梅迪特拉内安（人名）

e.en: A crocodile is a large reptile with a long body and strong jaws. Crocodiles live in rivers and eat meat.

d: n. 鳄鱼；鳄鱼皮（皮革）；（短语 crocodile tears）鳄鱼的眼泪，假慈悲

e.en: The ocean is the sea.

ex.en: There were few sights as beautiful as the calm ocean on a warm night.
ex.zh: 很少有景色像温暖夜晚的平静大海那样美丽。

e.en: An ocean is one of the five very large areas of sea on the Earth's surface.

ex.en: They spent many days cruising the northern Pacific Ocean.
ex.zh: 他们花了很多天巡游北太平洋。

e.en: If you say that there is an ocean of something, you are emphasizing that there is a very large amount of it.

ex.en: I had cried oceans of tears.
ex.zh: 我已哭得泪流成河。

e.en: If you say that something is a drop in the ocean, you mean that it is a very small amount which is unimportant compared to the cost of other things or is so small that it has very little effect on something.

ex.en: His fee is a drop in the ocean compared with the real cost of broadcasting.
ex.zh: 他的费用与广播的实际成本相比是沧海一粟。

d: n. 海洋，大海（the ocean）；（五大洋之一的）洋；许多，大量（an ocean of/oceans of）
【名】 （Ocean）（罗）奥切安（人名）

e.en: A species of animal or plant that is extinct no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

ex.en: At the current rate of decline, many of the rain forest animals could become extinct in less than 10 years.
ex.zh: 按照目前的下降速度，许多雨林动物不到十年就会绝种。

e.en: If a particular kind of worker, way of life, or type of activity is extinct, it no longer exists, because of changes in society.

ex.en: Herbalism had become an all but extinct skill in the Western world.
ex.zh: 草药医术在西方世界几乎已成了一项绝迹的技术。

e.en: An extinct volcano is one that does not erupt or is not expected to erupt anymore. 死的 (火山)

ex.en: Its tallest volcano, long extinct, is Olympus Mons.
ex.zh: 它最高的火山是已死很久的奥林匹斯山。

d: adj. 灭绝的；消亡的；（火山）死的；（贵族称号）无合法继承人的；熄灭了的

e.en: A region is a large area of land that is different from other areas of land, for example because it is one of the different parts of a country with its own customs and characteristics, or because it has a particular geographical feature.

ex.en: ...Barcelona, capital of the autonomous region of Catalonia.
ex.zh: …巴塞罗那，加泰罗尼亚自治区的首府。

e.en: You can refer to a part of your body as a region. (身体)

ex.en: ...the pelvic region.
ex.zh: …骨盆部位。

e.en: You say in the region of to indicate that an amount that you are stating is approximate. (数量)

ex.en: The plan will cost in the region of six million dollars.
ex.zh: 这项计划将花费大约六百万美元。

d: n. 地区，区域；行政区；（首都以外的）地方（the regions）；身体部位；领域，界

e.en: A fossil is the hard remains of a prehistoric animal or plant that are found inside a rock.

d: n. （古生物学）化石（fossil 的复数形式）

e.en: a large fish-eating Indian crocodilian, Gavialis gangeticus, with a very long slender snout: family Gavialidae

d: n. 印度食鱼鳄（等于 gharial）

e.en: The sea is the salty water that covers about three-quarters of the Earth's surface.

ex.en: Most of the kids have never seen the sea.
ex.zh: 这些孩子中的大多数从没见过大海。

e.en: You use seas when you are describing the sea at a particular time or in a particular area. (某时、某区域的)

ex.en: He drowned after 30 minutes in the rough seas.
ex.zh: 他在波涛汹涌的海里挣扎了30分钟后溺死了。

e.en: A sea is a large area of salty water that is part of an ocean or is surrounded by land. (作为海洋的一部分的或陆地围起来的)

ex.en: ...the North Sea.
ex.zh: …北海。

e.en: At sea means on or under the sea, far away from land. 在海上;

ex.en: The boats remain at sea for an average of ten days at a time.
ex.zh: 这些船平均每次在海上呆10天。

d: n. 海洋；内海；海（指月球或火星表面的一片广阔平原）；海面情况，海浪状况；大量，茫茫一片；（用于海名）海（Sea）；巨浪（seas）
n. 吉萨（埃及北部城市）；吉萨金字塔群；吉萨棉

e.en: high
in Scotland the advanced level of the Scottish Certificate of Education (苏格兰)
in Scotland (as modifier)

ex.en: Higher Latin

d: adj. 更高的，较高的（high 的比较级）；高等的，高级的（用于 higher education、higher mathematics 等搭配）
adv. 更高地，较高地（high 的比较级）
n. 高级水平教育证书（通常写作 Higher，可作定语）

e.en: A marine is a member of an armed force, for example the U.S. Marine Corps or the Royal Marines, who is specially trained for military duties at sea as well as on land.

ex.en: A small number of Marines were wounded.
ex.zh: 几名海军陆战队士兵受了伤。

e.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the animals and plants that live in the sea.

ex.en: ...breeding grounds for marine life.
ex.zh: …海洋生物的繁殖地。

e.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to ships and their movement at sea.

ex.en: ...a lawyer specializing in marine law.
ex.zh: …一名专攻海事法的律师。

d: adj. 海洋的，海产的；海运的，海事的
n. 水兵，海军陆战队士兵；（一个国家的）船舶
【名】 （Marine）（英）马林，（西）马里内（人名）

e.en: The ocean is the sea.

ex.en: There were few sights as beautiful as the calm ocean on a warm night.
ex.zh: 很少有景色像温暖夜晚的平静大海那样美丽。

e.en: An ocean is one of the five very large areas of sea on the Earth's surface.

ex.en: They spent many days cruising the northern Pacific Ocean.
ex.zh: 他们花了很多天巡游北太平洋。

e.en: If you say that there is an ocean of something, you are emphasizing that there is a very large amount of it.

ex.en: I had cried oceans of tears.
ex.zh: 我已哭得泪流成河。

e.en: If you say that something is a drop in the ocean, you mean that it is a very small amount which is unimportant compared to the cost of other things or is so small that it has very little effect on something.

ex.en: His fee is a drop in the ocean compared with the real cost of broadcasting.
ex.zh: 他的费用与广播的实际成本相比是沧海一粟。

d: n. 海洋，大洋（ocean 的复数形式）

e.en: Saltwater is water, especially from the ocean, which has salt in it.
Saltwater fish live in water which is salty. Saltwater lakes contain salty water.

ex.en: ...useful information for owners of saltwater fish.
ex.zh: ...对咸水鱼所有者有用的信息。

d: n. 咸水，尤指海水；（Saltwater）（日、澳、巴）桑乐特华特尔（人名）
adj. （多作定语）咸水的，盐水的，海产的；贮有咸水的

e.en: Anatomical means relating to the structure of the bodies of people and animals.

ex.en: ...minute anatomical differences between insects.
ex.zh: …昆虫之间微小的身体结构上的区别。

d: adj. 解剖的，解剖学的，结构上的

e.en: If someone or something is absent from a place or situation where they should be or where they usually are, they are not there.

ex.en: He has been absent from his desk for two weeks.
ex.zh: 他已经两个星期没来了。

ex.en: The pictures, too, were absent from the walls.
ex.zh: 那些照片也不在那些墙上了。

e.en: If someone appears absent, they are not paying attention because they are thinking about something else.

ex.en: "Nothing," Rosie said in an absent way.
ex.zh: “没什么，”罗茜心不在焉地说。

e.en: 心不在焉地

ex.en: He nodded absently.
ex.zh: 他心不在焉地点了点头。

e.en: An absent parent does not live with his or her children.

ex.en: ...absent fathers who fail to pay toward the costs of looking after their children.
ex.zh: …未能支付抚养费的不与孩子同住的父亲们。

d: adj. 缺勤的，缺席的；不存在的，缺乏的；心不在焉的，出神的；不与子女一起住的
prep. 缺乏，没有
v. 缺席，离开

e.en: If you carve an object, you make it by cutting it out of a substance such as wood or stone. If you carve something such as wood or stone into an object, you make the object by cutting it out.

ex.en: One of the prisoners has carved a beautiful wooden chess set.
ex.zh: 有名囚犯雕刻了一副精美的木制国际象棋。

ex.en: I picked up a piece of wood and started carving.
ex.zh: 我捡起一块木头，刻了起来。

e.en: If you carve writing or a design on an object, you cut it into the surface of the object.

ex.en: He carved his name on his desk.
ex.zh: 他在书桌上刻了自己的名字。

e.en: If you carve a piece of cooked meat, you cut slices from it so that you can eat it.

ex.en: Andrew began to carve the chicken.
ex.zh: 安德鲁动手切鸡肉。

d: v. 雕，刻；切下，割下；开创，赢得（carve out）；铺（路），修（路）；侵蚀，冲刷；减少，削减
【名】 （Carve）（西、瑞典）卡韦（人名）

e.en: Dinosaurs were large reptiles which lived in prehistoric times.
If you refer to an organization as a dinosaur, you mean that it is large, inefficient, and out of date.
e.zh: 庞大、低效且落后的机构

ex.en: ...industrial dinosaurs.
ex.zh: …庞大臃肿的工业企业。

d: n. [古生]恐龙（dinosaur 的复数形式）；恐龙类

e.en: The distribution of things involves giving or delivering them to a number of people or places.

ex.en: ...the council which controls the distribution of foreign aid.
ex.zh: …掌管分发国外援助的委员会。

e.en: The distribution of something is how much of it there is in each place or at each time, or how much of it each person has. 分配;

ex.en: Mr. Roh's economic planners sought to achieve a more equitable distribution of wealth.
ex.zh: 罗欧先生的经济规划者们努力实现更公平的财富分配。

d: n. 分发；分销，配送；（电影在各院线的）发行，上映；分配，分布

e.en: The diversity of something is the fact that it contains many very different elements.

ex.en: ...the cultural diversity of Latin America.
ex.zh: …拉丁美洲文化的多样性。

e.en: A diversity of things is a range of things which are very different from each other.

ex.en: Forslan's object is to gather as great a diversity of genetic material as possible.
ex.zh: 福斯兰的目标是尽可能收集各种不同的基因物质。

d: n. 多样性，多样化；不同，差异

e.en: Someone's environment is all the circumstances, people, things, and events around them that influence their life.

ex.en: Students in our schools are taught in a safe, secure environment.
ex.zh: 我校学生在安全无忧的环境中接受教育。

ex.en: The moral characters of men are formed not by heredity but by environment.
ex.zh: 人的品德不是由遗传而是由环境形成的。

e.en: Your environment consists of the particular natural surroundings in which you live or exist, considered in relation to their physical characteristics or weather conditions.

ex.en: ...a safe environment for marine mammals.
ex.zh: …一个适合海洋哺乳动物的安全环境。

e.en: The environment is the natural world of land, sea, air, plants, and animals.

ex.en: ...persuading people to respect the environment.
ex.zh: …劝人们重视自然环境。

d: n. 环境；生态环境；（计算机系统运行的）环境（environment 的复数）

e.en: A level is a point on a scale, for example, a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

ex.en: If you don't know your cholesterol level, it's a good idea to have it checked.
ex.zh: 如果你不知道自己的胆固醇水平，最好去查一下。

ex.en: We do have the lowest level of inflation for some years.
ex.zh: 我们几年来的确保持最低水平的通货膨胀。

e.en: The level of a river, lake, or ocean or the level of liquid in a container is the height of its surface.

ex.en: The water level of the Mississippi River is already 6.5 feet below normal.
ex.zh: 密西西比河的水位已经比正常水位低6.5英尺。

e.en: If something is at a particular level, it is at that height.

ex.en: Liz sank down until the water came up to her chin and the bubbles were at eye level.
ex.zh: 莉兹下沉直到水漫到她的下巴，泡沫到了她眼睛的高度。

e.en: A level of a building is one of its different storeys, which is situated above or below other storeys.

ex.en: Thurlow and Brown's rooms were on the second level, to the rear of the building.
ex.zh: 瑟洛和布朗的房间都在大楼背面的第二层。

d: n. 数量，程度；标准，水平；层次，级别；层，楼层；水位；高度（level 的复数形式）
v. 使平整；推倒，夷平；（使）比分相同，拉平（level 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If someone lives in a particular place or with a particular person, their home is in that place or with that person.

ex.en: She has lived here for 10 years.
ex.zh: 她在这里住了10年了。

ex.en: Where do you live?
ex.zh: 你住在哪里？

e.en: If you say that someone lives in particular circumstances or that they live a particular kind of life, you mean that they are in those circumstances or that they have that kind of life.

ex.en: We lived quite grandly.
ex.zh: 我们生活得相当快乐。

ex.en: Compared to people living only a few generations ago, we have greater opportunities to have a good time.
ex.zh: 与生活在仅仅几代之前的人相比，我们有更大的过得快乐的机会。

e.en: If you say that someone lives for a particular thing, you mean that it is the most important thing in their life. (为…而)

ex.en: He lived for his work.
ex.zh: 他为了工作而活。

e.en: To live means to be alive. If someone lives to a particular age, they stay alive until they are that age.

ex.en: He's got a terrible disease and will not live long.
ex.zh: 他得了一种重病，活不长了。

ex.en: He lived to be 103.
ex.zh: 他活到了103岁。

d: v. 居住（live 的过去式和过去分词）；活着；生活；度过；以……为生；经历（常作 lived through）
adj. 有生命的；（用于复合词）寿命或持续时间……的，如 long-lived 长寿的、short-lived 短暂的；亲身经历的（如 lived experience 生活经验）
n．穆卡塔姆：位于埃及开罗市东南部的一座山丘，也是一个居民区。
墨西拿

e.en: Rock is the hard substance which the earth is made of.

ex.en: The hills above the valley are bare rock.
ex.zh: 河谷上面的山是光秃秃的岩石。

e.en: A rock is a large piece of rock that sticks up out of the ground or the sea, or that has broken away from a mountain or a cliff.

ex.en: She sat cross-legged on the rock.
ex.zh: 她盘着腿坐在那块巨石上。

e.en: A rock is a piece of rock that is small enough for you to pick up.

ex.en: She bent down, picked up a rock, and threw it into the trees.
ex.zh: 她弯下腰，拣起一块小石头，把它扔进树林里。

e.en: When something rocks or when you rock it, it moves slowly and regularly backward and forward or from side to side. 使摇晃;

ex.en: His body rocked from side to side with the train.
ex.zh: 他的身体随着火车左右晃动着。

d: n. [岩]岩石，岩礁；岩石礁石（rock 复数形式）；（Rocks）人名；（英、德）罗克斯
v. 轻轻摇摆；发抖；演唱摇滚乐（rock 的第三人称单数形式）
n. 盐度，盐分，盐性

e.en: Your skull is the bony part of your head which encloses your brain. 颅骨;

ex.en: Her husband was later treated for a fractured skull.
ex.zh: 她丈夫后来因颅骨碎裂而接受治疗。

d: n. 颅骨，头骨；脑袋，头脑
v. 击中（某人的）头

e.en: A shallow container, hole, or area of water measures only a short distance from the top to the bottom.

ex.en: Put the milk in a shallow dish.
ex.zh: 把牛奶倒进一个浅盘里。

e.en: If you describe a person, piece of work, or idea as shallow, you disapprove of them because they do not show or involve any serious or careful thought. (人、作品、主意等)

ex.en: I think he is shallow, vain and untrustworthy.
ex.zh: 我认为他浅薄、虚荣、不可信。

e.en: If your breathing is shallow, you take only a very small amount of air into your lungs at each breath. (呼吸)

ex.en: She began to hear her own taut, shallow breathing.
ex.zh: 她开始听到自己紧张、短促的呼吸。

d: adj. 浅的，不深的；肤浅的，浅薄的；（呼吸）浅的，微弱的；平缓的；靠近内线的
n. （海、湖或河的）浅水处，浅滩（shallows）
v. （使）变浅
【名】 （Shallow）（英）沙洛（人名）

e.en: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

ex.en: ...a relaxed and happy atmosphere that will allow you to study to your full potential.
ex.zh: …一个将使你学习到充分发挥潜能的轻松又愉快的氛围。

ex.en: He studied History and Economics.
ex.zh: 他学过历史和经济学。

e.en: Study is the activity of studying.

ex.en: ...the use of maps and visual evidence in the study of local history.
ex.zh: …在当地历史的学习中地图和图像证据的使用。

e.en: A study of a subject is a piece of research on it.

ex.en: Recent studies suggest that as many as 5 in 1,000 new mothers are likely to have this problem.
ex.zh: 最近的研究表明，1000个新妈妈中有多达5个可能有这个问题。

e.en: You can refer to educational subjects or courses that contain several elements as studies of a particular kind.

ex.en: ...a centre for Islamic studies.
ex.zh: …一个伊斯兰教学科中心。

d: v. 学习，攻读；研究，仔细察看（study 的现在分词及动名词形式）

e.en: If you achieve a particular aim or effect, you succeed in doing it or causing it to happen, usually after a lot of effort.

ex.en: There are many who will work hard to achieve these goals.
ex.zh: 有很多人会努力工作来实现这些目标。

d: v. （经努力）达到，取得，实现；获得成功（achieve 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The tip of something long and narrow is the end of it.

ex.en: The sleeves covered his hands to the tips of his fingers.
ex.zh: 衣袖遮住了他的手，一直盖到他的手指尖。

e.en: If you tip an object or part of your body or if it tips, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

ex.en: He leaned away from her, and she had to tip her head back to see him.
ex.zh: 他侧身避开她，她只得向后侧过头来看他。

e.en: If you tip something somewhere, you pour it there.

ex.en: Tip the vegetables into a bowl.
ex.zh: 把这些蔬菜倒进一个碗里。

e.en: If you tip someone such as a waiter in a restaurant, you give them some money in order to thank them for their services.

ex.en: We usually tip 18-20%.
ex.zh: 我们通常付18-20%的小费。

d: v. （使）倾斜，（使）斜侧；给小费；扔掉，倒掉（垃圾）；倾倒，倒出；打翻；（用液体、颜色等）覆盖……的尖端；预言……获胜；轻触，轻碰；密报，透露消息，告诫
n. 指点，诀窍，建议；小费；末梢，尖端；垃圾场；脏乱的地方；（对赛马、比赛结果的）预测，内幕消息；顶端附加物；（尤指给警方的）密报；（对运动的球或冰球的）轻碰，轻击；手触帽檐，脱帽（致敬、问好或道别的动作）；擦棒球
【名】 （Tip）（美、俄）蒂普（人名）

e.en: An adaptation of a book or play is a film or a television programme that is based on it.

ex.en: Branagh won two awards for his screen adaptation of Shakespeare's Henry the Fifth.
ex.zh: 布拉纳因他对莎士比亚的《亨利五世》的荧幕改编而获了两次奖。

e.en: Adaptation is the act of changing something or changing your behaviour to make it suitable for a new purpose or situation.

ex.en: Most living creatures are capable of adaptation when compelled to do so.
ex.zh: 大多数生物在为情势所迫时都能适应。

d: n. 适应，调整；改编作品；生物的适应性特征（均为 adaptation 的复数）

e.en: Aid is money, equipment, or services that are provided for people, countries, or organizations who need them but cannot provide them for themselves.

ex.en: ...regular flights carrying humanitarian aid to Cambodia.
ex.zh: …向柬埔寨运送人道主义援助的定期班机。

ex.en: They have already pledged billions of dollars in aid.
ex.zh: 他们已经承诺了数十亿美元的援助。

e.en: If you perform a task with the aid of something, you need or use that thing to perform that task.

ex.en: He succeeded with the aid of a completely new method he discovered.
ex.zh: 借助于一个他所发现的全新方法，他取得了成功。

e.en: To aid a country, organization, or person means to provide them with money, equipment, or services that they need.

ex.en: ...U.S. efforts to aid Kurdish refugees.
ex.zh: …美国援助库尔德难民的努力。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: 援助的

ex.en: ...government-aided research.
ex.zh: …政府援助的研究。

d: adj. 辅助的；（自）半自动的
v. 帮助；援助；有助于（aid 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: When you alternate two things, you keep using one then the other. When one thing alternates with another, the first regularly occurs after the other.

ex.en: Her aggressive moods alternated with gentle or more cooperative states.
ex.zh: 她的挑衅情绪与温和或更为合作的情绪互相交替。

ex.en: Now you just alternate layers of that mixture and eggplant.
ex.zh: 现在你只用把那种混合物与茄子一层层交叠起来。

e.en: Alternate actions, events, or processes regularly occur after each other.

ex.en: They were streaked with alternate bands of colour.
ex.zh: 他们都带有色彩交替相间的条纹。

e.en: 交替地

ex.en: He could alternately bully and charm people.
ex.zh: 他能时而欺负人，时而吸引人。

e.en: If something happens on alternate days, it happens on one day, then happens on every second day after that. In the same way, something can happen in alternate weeks, years, or other periods of time.

ex.en: Lesley had agreed to Jim going skiing in alternate years.
ex.zh: 莱斯丽已经同意了吉姆隔年去滑雪。

d: adj. 交替的，交互的，轮流的，交变的，交流的（用于 alternating current 等）
v. 使交替，使轮流；依次（alternate 的 ing 形式）

e.en: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the bodies of people or animals.

ex.en: ...a course in anatomy.
ex.zh: …一门解剖学课程。

e.en: You can refer to your body as your anatomy.

ex.en: The ball hit him in the most sensitive part of his anatomy.
ex.zh: 这个球打中了他身体的最敏感部位。

d: n. 解剖学；（动植物的）组成结构，解剖构造；人体；剖析，详细分析；原因，成因；骨骼
干旱化
adv. 大约，大概
n. 亚洲

e.en: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

ex.en: Climate and weather affect every aspect of our lives.
ex.zh: 气候和天气影响我们生活的每个方面。

ex.en: He was interested in all aspects of the work here.
ex.zh: 他对这里工作的各方面都感兴趣。

e.en: The aspect of a building or window is the direction in which it faces. (建筑物或窗子的)

ex.en: The house had a southwest aspect.
ex.zh: 这房子为西南朝向。

d: n. 方面，层面（aspect 的复数）；（建筑物、窗户等的）朝向，方位；外观，面貌；（语言学）体，动词的体
n. （Atlantic）（美）艾克朗提克（人名）

e.en: Biology is the science which is concerned with the study of living things.
生物学家

ex.en: ...biologists studying the fruit fly.
ex.zh: …研究果蝇的生物学家。

e.en: The biology of a living thing is the way in which its body or cells behave. (机体、细胞的)

ex.en: The biology of these diseases is terribly complicated.
ex.zh: 这些疾病的作用方式极其复杂。

d: n. 生物学；生命机理，作用方式；生理习性；（某个地区的）生物

e.en: to murder in such a way as to leave no marks on the body, usually by suffocation （
e.zh: 通常用窒息方式）秘密谋杀

d: v. （通常用窒息方式）秘密谋杀；压制，封杀（问题、言论等）
n. （Burke）伯克（英语姓氏，也用作人名）

e.en: Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

ex.en: Her father died of a brain tumour.
ex.zh: 他的父亲死于脑瘤。

e.en: Your brain is your mind and the way that you think.

ex.en: Once you stop using your brain you soon go stale.
ex.zh: 一旦你停止动脑筋,你很快就会变迟钝。

e.en: If someone has brains or a good brain, they have the ability to learn and understand things quickly, to solve problems, and to make good decisions.

ex.en: They were not the only ones to have brains and ambition.
ex.zh: 他们并非仅有的有头脑、有抱负的人。

e.en: If someone is the brains behind an idea or an organization, he or she had that idea or makes the important decisions about how that organization is managed.

ex.en: Mr. White was the brains behind the scheme.
ex.zh: 怀特先生是这项计划后面的智囊。

d: n. 智力，头脑，脑筋；大脑，脑髓（brain 的复数）；智囊，主脑，策划者（非正式，常作 the brains）

e.en: A century is a period of a hundred years that is used when stating a date. For example, the 19th century was the period from 1801 to 1900.

ex.en: The material position of the Church had been declining since the late eighteenth century.
ex.zh: 自18世纪晚期以来，教堂的世俗地位一直在下降。

e.en: A century is any period of a hundred years.

ex.en: The drought there is the worst in a century.
ex.zh: 那里的旱情百年不遇。

d: n. century 的复数：世纪；一百年；（板球运动）击球手所得的一百分（或一百多分）

e.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

ex.en: The exhibition coincides with the 50th anniversary of his death.
ex.zh: 展会与他50周年忌辰同日。

e.en: If the ideas or interests of two or more people coincide, they are the same. (观点或兴趣)

ex.en: The kids' views on life don't always coincide, but they're not afraid of voicing their opinions.
ex.zh: 孩子们的生活观未必总是一致，但是他们不怕表达自己的观点。

d: v. （coincide 的第三人称单数，常与 with 连用）两件或更多的事情同时发生；相符，一致；重合，位置相同

e.en: An author's collected works or letters are all their works or letters published in one book or in a set of books.

ex.en: ...the collected works of Rudyard Kipling.
ex.zh: ...拉吉亚德·吉卜林的作品集。

e.en: If you say that someone is collected, you mean that they are very calm and self-controlled, especially when they are in a difficult or serious situation. 镇定自若的;

ex.en: Police say she was cool and collected during her interrogation.
ex.zh: 警方说她在接受审讯时冷静而又镇定自若。

d: v. collect 的过去式和过去分词：收集，收藏；聚集，聚积；去领取，领取（工资等）；接；募捐；赢得；（使）集中；推断；（使）马以受衔姿势跑；（非正式）和……互撞
adj. 镇静的，泰然自若的；汇编成集的，全集/文集的，合订的；（马奔跑时）步态稳健的，收拢步法的

e.en: A cooler is a container for keeping things cool, especially drinks.

d: n. 冷却器，散热器；冷藏箱，冰袋；电冰箱，冷藏柜；空气调节器；清凉饮料，冰镇饮料，高杯饮料；（俚语）监狱，禁闭室
adj. 更凉的，更凉快的，更令人凉爽的；更冷静的，更镇定的；更放松的；更满不在乎的；更冷漠的；更绝妙的，更酷的

e.en: If you cope with a problem or task, you deal with it successfully. (妥善地)

ex.en: It was amazing how my mother coped with bringing up three children on less than thirty dollars a week.
ex.zh: 让人惊叹的是我妈妈怎样以每周不到30美元的开销养大了3个孩子。

e.en: If you have to cope with an unpleasant situation, you have to accept it or bear it. 应付 (困难局面)

ex.en: Never before has the industry had to cope with war and recession at the same time.
ex.zh: 企业以前从来没有同时应付过战争和经济衰退。

e.en: If a machine or a system can cope with something, it is large enough or complex enough to deal with it satisfactorily. (用机器)

ex.en: A giant washing machine copes with the mountain of laundry created by their nine boys and five girls.
ex.zh: 一台大容量洗衣机能够清洗他们9个男孩和5个女孩换下的堆积如山的脏衣服。

e.en: a large ceremonial cloak worn at solemn liturgical functions by priests of certain Christian sects (基督教教士的)

d: v. 对付，处理
n. 长袍，法衣
【名】 （Cope）（英）科普，（西）科佩（人名）

e.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

ex.en: ...a cosmopolitan city.
ex.zh: …一个国际化都市。

e.en: Someone who is cosmopolitan has had a lot of contact with people and things from many different countries and as a result is very open to different ideas and ways of doing things.

ex.en: The family is rich, and extremely sophisticated and cosmopolitan.
ex.zh: 这个家庭殷实富足，深谙世故，又见多识广。

d: adj. 世界主义的，四海为家的；国际性的，国际化的；见过世面的，见识广的；广布的，遍生的
n. 四海为家的人，周游世界的人

e.en: If you cross something such as a room, a road, or an area of land or water, you move or travel to the other side of it. If you cross to a place, you move or travel over a room, road, or area of land or water in order to reach that place. 穿过;

ex.en: She was partly to blame for failing to look as she crossed the road.
ex.zh: 她横穿马路时没有看车，应承担部分责任。

ex.en: Egan crossed to the drinks cabinet and poured a Scotch.
ex.zh: 伊根穿过去，来到酒柜旁，倒了一杯苏格兰威士忌。

e.en: A road, railway, or bridge that crosses an area of land or water passes over it.

ex.en: The road crosses the river half a mile outside the town.
ex.zh: 这条路横跨城外半英里处的那条河。

e.en: If someone or something crosses a limit or boundary, for example, the limit of acceptable behaviour, they go beyond it. 越过 (可以被容忍的限度)

ex.en: I normally never write into magazines but Mr. Stubbs has finally crossed the line.
ex.zh: 我通常是从不给杂志写信的，但斯塔布斯先生最后太出格了。

e.en: If an expression crosses someone's face, it appears briefly on their face.

ex.en: Berg tilts his head and a mischievous look crosses his face.
ex.zh: 伯格歪着脑袋，一种淘气的表情在他的脸上一闪而过。

d: v. 反对；杂交；在（支票）上划线（表示只能转入银行帐户）；超过，超出（极限或范围）；（表情）掠过，闪过；（基督教徒）画十字；横传；（两封来往的信）相互错过，相互交错；做斗鸡眼；穿越，横渡；交叉
n. 十字标记，十字形（或叉形）物；杂交，混合物；十字架；苦难；横传；（拳击中的）钩拳迎击
adj. 恼怒的；脾气坏的，易怒的；（街道）交叉的，十字的

e.en: A covered area is an area that has a roof. 建筑面积;

ex.en: There are 40 shops and restaurants in a covered mall.
ex.zh: 一个室内大卖场里共有40家商店和饭店。

d: adj. 有顶的；有一层覆盖物的；投过保的，在保险范围内的
v. 覆盖；包括；掩护（cover 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death. 终止;

ex.en: ...the demise of the reform movement.
ex.zh: …改良运动的告终。

d: n. 倒闭，败落；死亡，逝世；（律）（财产或所有权的）转让，遗赠
v. （律）遗赠，转让（产业）；正式放弃，禅让（最高统治者的头衔）

e.en: The depth of something such as a river or hole is the distance downward from its top surface, or between its upper and lower surfaces.

ex.en: The depth of the shaft is 520 yards.
ex.zh: 这个通道的深度是520码。

ex.en: The smaller lake ranges from five to fourteen feet in depth.
ex.zh: 这个较小的湖的深度在5至14英尺之间。

e.en: The depth of something such as a wardrobe or drawer is the distance between its front surface and its back.
If an emotion is very strongly or intensely felt, you can talk about its depth. (感情的)

ex.en: I am well aware of the depth of feeling that exists in Ontario.
ex.zh: 我深知安大略人情感的深厚。

e.en: The depth of a situation is its extent and seriousness.

ex.en: The country's leadership had underestimated the depth of the crisis.
ex.zh: 这个国家的领导层低估了这次危机的严重程度。

d: n. 深处，深渊；深度；深渊，低谷，最糟的状态

e.en: If two or more things differ, they are unlike each other in some way.

ex.en: The story he told police differed from the one he told his mother.
ex.zh: 他告诉警察的话和告诉他母亲的不同。

e.en: If people differ about something, they do not agree with each other about it.

ex.en: The two leaders had differed on the issue of sanctions.
ex.zh: 就制裁问题两位领导持不同意见。

ex.en: That is where we differ.
ex.zh: 那就是我们的分歧所在。

d: v. differ 的过去式和过去分词：不同，有区别（常与 from、in 连用）；意见不同，有分歧（常与 on、about、over 连用）。

e.en: If you describe something as devastating, you are emphasizing that it is very harmful or damaging.

ex.en: Affairs do have a devastating effect on marriages.
ex.zh: 外遇着实对婚姻有极具破坏性的影响。

e.en: You can use devastating to emphasize that something is very shocking, upsetting, or terrible.

ex.en: The diagnosis was devastating. She had cancer.
ex.zh: 诊断结果令人震惊。她得了癌症。

e.en: You can use devastating to emphasize that something or someone is very impressive.

ex.en: He returned to his best with a devastating display of galloping and jumping.
ex.zh: 他骑马飞驰和跳跃的精彩展示，说明他恢复到了最佳状态。

d: adj. 毁灭性的，极具破坏力的；令人极为震惊的；令人印象深刻的，吸引人的；极有效的，强有力的
v. 毁灭，破坏；使极度震惊，使伤心欲绝（devastate 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If someone makes a discovery, they become aware of something that they did not know about before.

ex.en: I felt I'd made an incredible discovery.
ex.zh: 我感到自己有了一个惊人的发现。

e.en: If someone makes a discovery, they are the first person to find or become aware of a place, substance, or scientific fact that no one knew about before.

ex.en: In that year, two momentous discoveries were made.
ex.zh: 那年有2项重大的新发现。

e.en: When the discovery of people or objects happens, someone finds them, either by accident or as a result of looking for them.

ex.en: ...the discovery and destruction by soldiers of millions of marijuana plants.
ex.zh: …士兵们对数百万株大麻的发现和摧毁。

d: n. 发现，被发现的事物；（法律）强制性透露

e.en: If you differentiate between things or if you differentiate one thing from another, you recognize or show the difference between them.

ex.en: A child may not differentiate between his imagination and the real world.
ex.zh: 孩子也许无法区分想像与真实世界的差别。

e.en: A quality or feature that differentiates one thing from another makes the two things different.

ex.en: ...distinctive policies that differentiate them from the other parties.
ex.zh: …使他们与其他政党区别开来的独特政策。

e.en: 差别

ex.en: For about six or seven weeks after conception, there is no differentiation between male and female.
ex.zh: 在受精后大约六七个星期时，男性和女性胚胎之间没有什么差别。

d: v. 使不同；求……的微分；区别

e.en: Dried food or milk has had all the water removed from it so that it will last for a long time. (食物或牛奶)

ex.en: ...an infusion which may be prepared from the fresh plant or the dried herb.
ex.zh: …可以用新鲜植物或干的草本植物制备的一种泡剂。

d: adj. （食物、花等）干的，脱水的，经干燥处理以便保存的
v. 使变干；变干（dry 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Your ears are the two parts of your body, one on each side of your head, with which you hear sounds.

ex.en: He whispered something in her ear.
ex.zh: 他在她耳边低声说了些什么。

e.en: If you have an ear for music or language, you are able to hear its sounds accurately and to interpret them or reproduce them well.

ex.en: Moby certainly has a fine ear for a tune.
ex.zh: 莫比对音调的分辨能力一定很强。

e.en: Ear is often used to refer to people's willingness to listen to what someone is saying.

ex.en: What would cause the masses to give him a far more sympathetic ear?
ex.zh: 什么能使大众更富同情心地听他诉说呢？

e.en: The ears of a cereal plant such as corn or barley are the parts at the top of the stem that contain the seeds or grains.

ex.en: American farmers use machines to pick the ears of corn from the plants.
ex.zh: 美国农民使用机器收割谷穗。

d: n. 耳朵；灵敏的听力；倾听；穗；耳状物
【名】 （Ear）（柬）伊（人名）

e.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between plants, animals, people, and their environment, and the balances between these relationships.

ex.en: ...a professor in ecology.
ex.zh: …一位生态学教授。

e.en: When you talk about the ecology of a place, you are referring to the pattern and balance of relationships between plants, animals, people, and the environment in that place.

ex.en: ...the ecology of the rocky Negev desert in Israel.
ex.zh: …以色列内盖夫的多岩石沙漠生态。

d: n. 生态学；生态；生态保护运动

e.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity to do it.

ex.en: The new test should enable doctors to detect the disease early.
ex.zh: 新的检验使医生能在早期发现该种疾病。

e.en: To enable something to happen means to make it possible for it to happen.

ex.en: The hot sun enables the grapes to reach optimum ripeness.
ex.zh: 炙热的阳光使葡萄能达到最佳成熟状态。

e.en: To enable someone to do something means to give them permission or the right to do it.

ex.en: ...legislation which enables young people to do a form of alternative service.
ex.zh: …允许年轻人通过一种替代性服务来服刑的立法。

d: v. 使能够，使成为可能；授权，允许，批准；（计）启动，激活（enable 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 启用的，激活的；（常用于复合词）由…支持或实现的
n. 蒸发

e.en: An example of something is a particular situation, object, or person that shows that what is being claimed is true.

ex.en: The doctors gave numerous examples of patients being expelled from the hospital.
ex.zh: 医生给出了大量病人被逐出医院的实例。

e.en: An example of a particular class of objects or styles is something that has many of the typical features of such a class or style, and that you consider clearly represents it.

ex.en: Symphonies 103 and 104 stand as perfect examples of early symphonic construction.
ex.zh: 第103和104号交响曲是早期交响乐谱曲的完美范本。

e.en: If you refer to a person or their behaviour as an example to other people, you mean that he or she behaves in a good or correct way that other people should copy.

ex.en: He is a model professional and an example to the younger boys.
ex.zh: 他是个模范的专业人员，是年轻人的榜样。

e.en: You use for example to introduce and emphasize something that shows that something is true.

ex.en: Take, for example, the simple sentence: "The man climbed up the hill."
ex.zh: 以这个简单句为例：“那个人爬上了山坡。”

d: n. 例子，例证；榜样，楷模；典型，范例；例句，例题；警戒，受罚（以示警告）者
v. 得到说明，可加以举例说明

e.en: Evolution is a process of gradual change that takes place over many generations, during which species of animals, plants, or insects slowly change some of their physical characteristics.

ex.en: ...the evolution of plants and animals.
ex.zh: …动植物的进化。

e.en: Evolution is a process of gradual development in a particular situation or thing over a period of time. 演化;

ex.en: ...a crucial period in the evolution of modern physics.
ex.zh: …现代物理学发展过程中的一个关键时期。

d: n. 进化（论）；演变，发展；（气体的）释放，（热量的）散发；队形变换，位置变换；开方

e.en: Extreme means very great in degree or intensity.

ex.en: The girls were afraid of snakes and picked their way along with extreme caution.
ex.zh: 那些女孩们害怕蛇，一路极其谨慎地看好每一步走。

ex.en: ...people living in extreme poverty.
ex.zh: …活在极度贫穷中的人们。

e.en: You use extreme to describe situations and behaviour that are much more severe or unusual than you would expect, especially when you disapprove of them because of this.

ex.en: The extreme case was Poland, where 29 parties won seats.
ex.zh: 过激的案例是波兰，那里有29个政党获得席位。

ex.en: It is hard to imagine Jesse capable of anything so extreme.
ex.zh: 很难想像杰西能做这样过激的事情。

e.en: You use extreme to describe opinions, beliefs, or political movements that you disapprove of because they are very different from those that most people would accept as reasonable or normal.

ex.en: This extreme view hasn't captured popular opinion.
ex.zh: 这种偏激的观点还没有赢得大众的认同。

e.en: You can use extremes to refer to situations or types of behaviour that have opposite qualities to each other, especially when each situation or type of behaviour has such a quality to the greatest degree possible.

ex.en: ...a "middle way" between the extremes of success and failure, wealth and poverty.
ex.zh: …成功与失败、富裕与贫穷两个极端之间的“中道”。

d: adj. 极大的，极度的；极端的，严重的；过分的，偏激的；尽头的，末端的；极限的，从事极限运动的
n. （观点或行为方式的）极端；（事物的）极度；端顶，端词

e.en: Your eyes are the parts of your body with which you see.

ex.en: I opened my eyes and looked.
ex.zh: 我睁开眼睛看了看。

ex.en: ...a tall, thin white-haired lady with piercing dark brown eyes.
ex.zh: …有一双深邃的深棕色眼睛的一位瘦高个白发女士。

e.en: If you eye someone or something in a particular way, you look at them carefully in that way.

ex.en: Sally eyed Claire with interest.
ex.zh: 萨莉饶有兴味地注视着克莱尔。

ex.en: We eyed each other thoughtfully.
ex.zh: 我们若有所思地看了看彼此。

e.en: to look at in a manner indicating sexual interest; ogle 色迷迷地看; 送秋波 (Also eye up)
You use eye when you are talking about a person's ability to judge things or about the way in which they are considering or dealing with things.

ex.en: William was a man of discernment, with an eye for quality.
ex.zh: 威廉是个有鉴赏力的人，对于品质的优劣很有眼力。

ex.en: He first learned to fish under the watchful eye of his grandmother.
ex.zh: 他最初在祖母留心的眼光下学习钓鱼。

d: n. 眼睛；目光，所看之处；眼力，鉴赏力；眼光，视角；观点，态度；（钩）环，扣眼；（马铃薯上的）芽眼，芽；（飓风等风暴的）风眼；拍摄对象，取景器；（电）眼，（红外）眼，眼状探测装置；针眼，针鼻儿
v. 注视，仔细打量
【名】 （Eye）（英）艾，（德）艾厄（人名）

e.en: You use famously to refer to a fact that is well known, usually because it is remarkable or extreme.

ex.en: Authors are famously ignorant about the realities of publishing.
ex.zh: 作者们对出版业的实际情况出了名地无知。

d: adv. 著名地；极好地（多与 get on/along 连用）

e.en: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.

ex.en: Body temperature can fluctuate if you are ill.
ex.zh: 如果你病了，体温会波动。

e.en: 波动

ex.en: Don't worry about tiny fluctuations in your weight.
ex.zh: 不用担心你体重的轻微波动。

d: v. （fluctuate 的过去式和过去分词）波动，起伏；（在希望、意见、情绪等之间）摇摆不定，犹豫

e.en: A freshwater lake contains water that is not salty, usually in contrast to the sea. Freshwater creatures live in water that is not salty.

ex.en: ...Lake Balaton, the largest freshwater lake in Europe.
ex.zh: …巴拉顿湖，欧洲最大的淡水湖。

d: adj. 淡水的；淡水中生长的；位于偏僻地方的，地方性的（较旧或非正式，较少见）；无经验的（较旧或非正式，较少见）
n. 淡水；淡水水域；（Freshwater，首字母大写）（美）弗雷什沃特（人名）

e.en: You can refer to the world as the globe when you are emphasizing how big it is or that something happens in many different parts of it.

ex.en: ...bottles of beer from every corner of the globe.
ex.zh: …一瓶瓶来自全球各个角落的啤酒。

ex.en: 70% of our globe's surface is water.
ex.zh: 我们地球表面的70%是水。

e.en: A globe is a ball-shaped object with a map of the world on it. It is usually fixed on a stand.

ex.en: Three large globes stand on the floor.
ex.zh: 地板上立着三个大地球仪。

e.en: Any ball-shaped object can be referred to as a globe.

ex.en: The overhead light was covered now with a white globe.
ex.zh: 顶灯现在被一个白色的球状物罩了起来。

d: n. 地球，世界；地球仪；球体，球状物
v. （使）成球状

e.en: The name God is given to the spirit or being who is worshipped as the creator and ruler of the world, especially by Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

ex.en: He believes in God.
ex.zh: 他信奉上帝。

e.en: People sometimes use God in exclamations to emphasize something that they are saying, or to express surprise, fear, or excitement. This use could cause offence.

ex.en: Oh my God, he's shot somebody.
ex.zh: 噢，我的天哪，他向人开了枪。

ex.en: Good God, it's Mr. Harper!
ex.zh: 天哪，是哈珀先生！

e.en: In many religions, a god is one of the spirits or beings that are believed to have power over a particular part of the world or nature.

ex.en: ...Zeus, king of the gods.
ex.zh: …宙斯，众神之王。

e.en: Someone who is admired very much by a person or group of people, and who influences them a lot, can be referred to as a god.

ex.en: To his followers he was a god.
ex.zh: 对他的追随者们来说，他是个神一般的人物。

d: n. 神；上帝，天主， 真主（God）；受崇敬的人，偶像；（某一领域的）要人，权威；至为重要的事物；（剧场中的）顶层楼座（the gods）
v. 膜拜，崇拜
int. （用以表示吃惊、愤怒或悲痛等）天哪（God）
【名】 （God）（索、阿拉伯）古德（人名）

e.en: When you go somewhere, you move or travel there. 去;

ex.en: We went to Rome.
ex.zh: 我们去了罗马。

ex.en: I went home for the weekend.
ex.zh: 我回家过周末了。

e.en: When you go, you leave the place where you are.

ex.en: Let's go.
ex.zh: 我们走吧。

e.en: You use go to say that someone leaves the place where they are and does an activity, often a leisure activity. 去 (从事某活动)

ex.en: We went swimming very early.
ex.zh: 我们很早就去游泳了。

ex.en: Maybe they've just gone shopping.
ex.zh: 或许他们刚刚去买东西了。

e.en: When you go do something, you move to a place in order to do it and you do it. You can also go and do something, but you always say that someone went and did something. 去 (做某事)

ex.en: I have to go see the doctor.
ex.zh: 我得去看医生。

ex.en: I finished my beer, then went and got another.
ex.zh: 我喝完了自己的啤酒，然后又去拿了一瓶。

d: vi. go 的第三人称单数现在时形式：去，行走，前进，离开（词义随搭配而定）。
n. go 的复数形式：尝试，机会，轮到的机会；大写 Goes 可作人名，译写作约斯（瑞典）、格斯（法、德）、胡斯（荷）；也指荷兰泽兰省的一个市镇。
abbr. GOES：地球静止业务环境卫星（Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites）的缩写。
集团旗下

e.en: If something heightens a feeling or if the feeling heightens, the feeling increases in degree or intensity.

ex.en: The move has heightened tension in the state.
ex.zh: 这一举动加剧了该州的紧张局势。

ex.en: Cross's interest heightened.
ex.zh: 克罗斯的兴趣增强了。

d: v. 提高，升高（heighten 的过去式和过去分词）；加剧，增强；使（感觉、意识等）更加敏锐
adj. 增强的，加剧的，提高的；加高的；（感官等）更敏锐的

e.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.

ex.en: He has helped to raise a lot of money.
ex.zh: 他帮着筹到了很多钱。

ex.en: You can of course help by giving them a donation directly.
ex.zh: 你当然可以通过直接给他们一笔捐赠来帮助他们。

e.en: Help is also a noun.

ex.en: Thanks very much for your help.
ex.zh: 非常感谢你的帮助。

e.en: If you say that something helps, you mean that it makes something easier to do or get, or that it improves a situation to some extent.

ex.en: The right style of swimsuit can help to hide, minimize, or emphasize what you want it to.
ex.zh: 款式得当的泳衣有助于按你的意愿掩饰、缩小或突出某些部位。

ex.en: Building more bypasses will help the environment by reducing pollution and traffic jams in towns and cities.
ex.zh: 修建更多的支路将减少城镇中的污染和交通堵塞，从而改善环境。

e.en: If you help someone go somewhere or move in some way, you give them support so that they can move more easily.

ex.en: Martin helped Tanya over the rail.
ex.zh: 马丁扶着塔尼娅翻过栏杆。

d: abbr. 高端激光打印解决方案（High-End Laser Printing Solutions）
n. （Helps）人名；（英）赫尔普斯
n. （Heru）毛利人的传统装饰梳；人名，通常写作 Heru；（日）平流（姓）
adv. 从历史角度说，从历史观点上说；在历史上，过去。

e.en: a solar god of Egyptian mythology, usually depicted with a falcon's head 何露斯;
e.zh: 埃及神话中的太阳神，通常被绘以鹰头

d: n. 荷鲁斯（古埃及神话中的鹰首太阳神，奥西里斯与伊西斯之子；亦译“何露斯”）

e.en: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment. (聚会的)

ex.en: Apart from my host, I didn't know a single person there.
ex.zh: 除了主人，那儿的人我一个也不认识。

e.en: If someone hosts a party, dinner, or other function, they have invited the guests and provide the food, drink, or entertainment. 主办 (聚会、宴会或其他集会)

ex.en: Tonight she hosts a ball for 300 guests.
ex.zh: 今晚她做东办一场有300名来宾参加的舞会。

e.en: A country, city, or organization that is the host of an event provides the facilities for that event to take place. (举办某活动的)

ex.en: Atlanta was chosen to be host of the 1996 Olympic games.
ex.zh: 亚特兰大被选为1996年奥运会的东道主。

e.en: If a country, city, or organization hosts an event, they provide the facilities for the event to take place.

ex.en: New Bedford hosts a number of lively festivals throughout the summer months.
ex.zh: 新贝德福德整个夏天举办了许多个欢快有趣的艺术节。

d: v. 主办，做……的东道主；做节目主持人；作为主人组织（聚会），做东（host 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: An iconic image or thing is important or impressive because it seems to be a symbol of something. 偶像的; 图符的;

ex.en: The ads helped Nike to achieve iconic status.
ex.zh: 这些广告帮助耐克公司成就了偶像地位。

d: adj. 偶像的，图符的，象征性的；（古典希腊雕像）以传统风格刻画得胜运动员的

e.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

ex.en: There are a number of distinguishing characteristics by which you can identify a Hollywood epic.
ex.zh: 通过其诸多与众不同的特点,你可以识别出好莱坞的史诗影片。

e.en: If you identify someone or something, you name them or say who or what they are.

ex.en: Police have already identified 10 murder suspects.
ex.zh: 警方已经确认了10名谋杀嫌疑犯。
