e.en: If you identify something, you discover or notice its existence. 发现;

ex.en: Scientists claim to have identified chemicals produced by certain plants which have powerful cancer-fighting properties.
ex.zh: 科学家们声称已经发现某些植物产生的化学物质有强大的抗癌功能。

e.en: If a particular thing identifies someone or something, it makes them easy to recognize, by making them different in some way. 是…的标志;

ex.en: She wore a little nurse's hat on her head to identify her.
ex.zh: 她头上戴了一顶小护士帽，这使她易于辨认。

d: v. 认出，识别；查明，确认；发现；证明（身份），表明；认同，理解；认为……和……一致；和（某人）打成一片

e.en: If you have a role in a situation or in society, you have a particular position and function in it. 功能;

ex.en: Until now scientists had very little clear evidence about the drug's role in preventing more serious effects of infection.
ex.zh: 到目前为止，科学家们几乎没有该药物在防止更严重的感染后果的功能的明确证据。

e.en: A role is one of the characters that an actor or singer can play in a movie, play, or opera.

ex.en: She has just landed the lead role in their latest production.
ex.zh: 她刚在他们最新的作品中取得了主角。

d: n. 任务，作用（role 的复数形式）；角色，人物；（计算机／信息技术）权限角色

e.en: A screen is a flat vertical surface on which pictures or words are shown. Television sets and computers have screens, and movies are shown on a screen in movie theatres. (电视、电脑、影院等的)
You can refer to movies or television as the screen.

ex.en: Many viewers have strong opinions about violence on the screen.
ex.zh: 许多观众对影视暴力有强烈意见。

e.en: When a movie or a television programme is screened, it is shown in the movie theatre or broadcast on television. 上映 (影片); 播放 (电视节目)

ex.en: The series is likely to be screened in January.
ex.zh: 这部系列剧可能在1月份播放。

e.en: 放映;

ex.en: The film-makers will be present at the screenings to introduce their works.
ex.zh: 电影制作人将在放映时到场介绍他们的作品。

d: n. 屏幕，荧光屏；银幕；电影（总称）；屏风，隔板；掩蔽物，屏障；纱窗，纱门；（医疗）化验，检查；（机动车的）挡风玻璃；（篮球、冰球等运动的）掩护；掩护部队，护航舰队；大筛子，滤网；（纱门或纱窗的）金属丝，塑料线；（印刷）网屏，网版；屏蔽器
v. 隐藏，遮蔽；庇护，包庇；检查，筛查；审查，甄别；筛选，检查排除；防止（或免受）电磁干扰；放映（影片），播放（电视节目）；分析，评估；加网印刷
【名】 （Screen）斯克林（人名）

e.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically.

ex.en: The restaurant has been widely acclaimed for its excellent French cuisine.
ex.zh: 这个餐馆因出众的法式烹调而受到广泛赞扬。

ex.en: He was acclaimed as America's greatest filmmaker.
ex.zh: 他被赞誉为美国最伟大的电影制片人。

e.en: 受到高度赞扬的

ex.en: She has published six highly acclaimed novels.
ex.zh: 她已经出版了6本受到高度赞扬的小说。

e.en: Acclaim is public praise for someone or something.

ex.en: Angela Bassett has won critical acclaim for her excellent performance.
ex.zh: 安杰拉·巴西特因她出色的表演而赢得了评论界的赞扬。

d: adj. 受到赞扬的，备受推崇的，广受欢迎的
v. 称赞，推崇；为……欢呼喝彩（acclaim 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A theatre is a building with a stage in it, on which plays, shows, and other performances take place.

ex.en: They brought her to the theatre where their new musical was in production.
ex.zh: 他们带她到正编排新音乐剧的剧院。

e.en: You can refer to work in the theatre such as acting or writing plays as the theatre.

ex.en: The story of her career in the theatre is told in a new biography.
ex.zh: 她的戏剧生涯故事记载在新的传记中。

e.en: Theatre is entertainment that involves the performance of plays.

ex.en: ...American musical theatre.
ex.zh: …美国的音乐剧表演。

e.en: A theatre is a room in a hospital where surgeons operate on their patients.

d: n. 剧场，戏院；电影院；戏剧；戏剧表演，戏剧演出；手术室；战场，战区；（事件发生的）场所；做戏，夸张做作；戏剧效果；阶梯式讲堂（或教室）；手术室

e.en: A mutant is an animal or plant that is physically different from others of the same species because of a change in its genes.

ex.en: New species are merely mutants of earlier ones.
ex.zh: 新物种不过是早先物种的突变体。

d: adj. 突变的，因基因变异而不同的，由突变产生的
n. （生物学、遗传学）突变体，突变型，突变株；（科幻、漫画、影视等中的）变异生物，变种人，突变异体怪物；（非正式，贬义）令人讨厌（或可怕）的事物，怪胎

e.en: A television or television set is a piece of electrical equipment consisting of a box with a glass screen on it on which you can watch programmes with pictures and sounds.

ex.en: She turned the television on and flicked around between news programmes.
ex.zh: 她打开电视机，不停地在新闻节目间切换。

e.en: Television is the system of sending pictures and sounds by electrical signals over a distance so that people can receive them on a television in their home.

ex.en: Toy manufacturers began promoting some of their products on television.
ex.zh: 玩具制造商们开始在电视上促销他们的一些产品。

e.en: Television refers to all the programmes that you can watch.

ex.en: I don't have much time to watch very much television.
ex.zh: 我没有很多时间看很多电视节目。

e.en: Television is the business or industry concerned with making programmes and broadcasting them on television.

ex.en: I'd like a job in television.
ex.zh: 我想有份电视行业的工作。

d: n. 电视（电视广播系统）；电视机（电视接收机）；电视节目；电视业
n. 英格兰

e.en: The Internet is the network that allows computer users to connect with computers all over the world, and that carries e-mail.

d: n. 互联网，因特网（=the Internet）

e.en: An enterprise is a company or business. 公司;

ex.en: There are plenty of small industrial enterprises.
ex.zh: 有很多小型的工业企业。

e.en: An enterprise is something new, difficult, or important that you do or try to do.

ex.en: Horse breeding is indeed a risky enterprise.
ex.zh: 养马的确是一项有风险的事业。

e.en: Enterprise is the activity of managing companies and businesses and starting new ones.

ex.en: He is still involved in voluntary work promoting local enterprise.
ex.zh: 他仍从事志愿工作推动当地创业。

e.en: Enterprise is the ability to think of new and effective things to do, together with an eagerness to do them. 开创力;

ex.en: ...the spirit of enterprise worthy of a free and industrious people.
ex.zh: …与一个自由勤劳的民族相称的开拓精神。

d: n. 企业，事业单位；事业心，进取心；事业；创业，企业经营

e.en: The leader of a group of people or an organization is the person who is in control of it or in charge of it.

ex.en: We now need a new leader of the party and a new style of leadership.
ex.zh: 我们现在需要一个新的政党领导人和一种新的领导风格。

e.en: The leader at a particular point in a race or competition is the person who is winning at that point.

ex.en: The leaders came in two minutes clear of the field.
ex.zh: 领先的选手们早两分钟到达终点。

e.en: The leader of an orchestra is the most senior violin player, who acts as a deputy to the conductor. (交响乐团的)
A leader in a newspaper is a piece of writing which gives the editor's opinion on an important news item. (报纸上的)

d: n. 领导者，首领；领先者，佼佼者；首席小提琴手；指挥；社论；（报纸的）要闻，头条；（胶卷，磁带的）空白段；（渔线）接钩绳；（植物的）顶枝；（尤指表格中的）指向符
【名】 （Leader）（英）利德（人名）

e.en: A servant's master is the man that he or she works for.

ex.en: My master ordered me not to deliver the message except in private.
ex.zh: 主人命令我不能传送信息，除非在私下里。

e.en: If you say that someone is a master of a particular activity, you mean that they are extremely skilled at it.

ex.en: She was a master of the English language.
ex.zh: 她曾是一名英语语言专家。

e.en: Master is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...a master craftsman.
ex.zh: …一名手艺高超的工匠。

e.en: If you are master of a situation, you have complete control over it.

ex.en: Jackson remained calm and always master of his passions.
ex.zh: 杰克逊保持着平静，始终是自己情感的掌控者。

d: n. 雇主，主子；主宰者，控制者；大师，能手；硕士；原版，母带；男教师；（动物的）主人；少爷；（英国）校长，院长；船长；著名画家；主控机件；国业公会主管，共济会地方分会会长；最高法院官员；（子爵或男爵的）长子
v. 精通，掌握；控制，掌控；制作……母版
adj. 熟练的，精通的；最重要的，主要的；原版的
【名】 （Master）马斯特（人名）

e.en: A performance involves entertaining an audience by doing something such as singing, dancing, or acting.

ex.en: Inside the theatre, they were giving a performance of Bizet's Carmen.
ex.zh: 他们正在剧院里演出比才的《卡门》。

ex.en: ...her performance as the betrayed Medea.
ex.zh: …她出演被出卖的美狄亚。

e.en: Someone's or something's performance is how successful they are or how well they do something. 业绩;

ex.en: That study looked at the performance of 18 surgeons.
ex.zh: 那项研究着眼于18位外科医生的业绩。

ex.en: The poor performance has been blamed on the recession and cheaper sports car imports.
ex.zh: 业绩惨淡归咎于经济衰退和更便宜跑车的进口。

e.en: The performance of a task is the fact or action of doing it. 执行;

ex.en: He devoted in excess of seventy hours a week to the performance of his duties.
ex.zh: 他每周在自己职责的执行上投入超过70个小时。

d: n. 表演，演出；工作情况，表现（performance 的复数）
赖克（人名）

e.en: People sometimes say sir as a polite way of addressing a man whose name they do not know, or an older man. For example, a shop assistant might address a male customer as sir. 先生 (对男性的客气称呼)

ex.en: Excuse me sir, but would you mind telling me what sort of car that is?
ex.zh: 对不起，先生，您能告诉我那是什么样的汽车吗？

e.en: Sir is the title used in front of the name of a knight or baronet. (爵士或从男爵名字前的头衔)

ex.en: She introduced me to Sir Tobias and Lady Clarke.
ex.zh: 她把我介绍给托拜厄斯爵士和克拉克夫人。

e.en: You use the expression Dear Sir at the beginning of a formal letter or a business letter when you are writing to a man. 敬启者 (常用于正式函件或商务函件)

ex.en: Dear Sir, Enclosed is a copy of my résumé for your consideration.
ex.zh: 敬启者，兹附上我的简历一份，请予以考虑。

d: n. 先生，长官（尤指对上级的尊称）；老师（学生对男教师的称呼）；先生，阁下（正式或商业信函开头的称呼）（Dear Sir）；爵士（用于爵士或准男爵名字之前）（Sir）；决不，的确（no/yes sir）（同 siree）
【名】 （苏丹、德）西尔（人名）

e.en: If you remember people or events from the past, you still have an idea of them in your mind and you are able to think about them.

ex.en: You wouldn't remember me. I was in another group.
ex.zh: 你不会记得我的，我当时在另一个组。

ex.en: I remembered that we had made the last of the coffee the day before.
ex.zh: 我记得我们前一天刚煮完了最后一点咖啡。

e.en: If you remember that something is the case, you become aware of it again after a time when you did not think about it. 忆起;

ex.en: She remembered that she was going to the club that evening.
ex.zh: 她回想起那天晚上她要去俱乐部。

e.en: If you cannot remember something, you are not able to bring it back into your mind when you make an effort to do so.

ex.en: If you can't remember your number, write it in code in an appointment book.
ex.zh: 如果你记不住你的号码，就用密码把它写在预约本里。

ex.en: I can't remember what I said.
ex.zh: 我记不起我说过什么了。

e.en: If you remember to do something, you do it when you intend to. 记住 (做某事)

ex.en: Please remember to enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope when writing.
ex.zh: 请记住写信的时候附上一个贴好邮票、写好自己姓名地址的信封。

d: v. remember 的过去式和过去分词：记得，回忆起。
adj. 被记住的，被铭记的，被纪念的（常作 be remembered as，意为“作为……被铭记”）。
《X战警》（电影名）
X战警（漫威漫画的超级英雄团体）

e.en: United States Senate

d: abbr. 美国军舰（United States Ship，美国海军舰名前缀）；美国参议院（United States Senate）；（计算机）UNIX 系统服务（UNIX System Services）；美国标准（United States Standard）；美国船舶（United States Steamship）

e.en: When you act, you do something for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The deaths occurred when police acted to stop widespread looting and vandalism.
ex.zh: 当警方行动起来去制止大范围的洗劫和蓄意破坏时，死亡事件发生了。

e.en: If you act on advice or information, you do what has been advised or suggested. (按照建议或信息)

ex.en: A patient will usually listen to the doctor's advice and act on it.
ex.zh: 病人通常会听从医生的建议并且按照它行动。

e.en: If someone acts in a particular way, they behave in that way.

ex.en: ...a gang of youths who were acting suspiciously.
ex.zh: …一帮表现可疑的年轻人。

ex.en: He acted as if he hadn't heard any of it.
ex.zh: 他表现得好像一点都没有听过这件事一样。

e.en: If someone or something acts as a particular thing, they have that role or function.

ex.en: Among his other duties, he acted both as the ship's surgeon and as chaplain for the men.
ex.zh: 另外，他兼任船上的外科医生以及船员们的牧师。

d: v. 行动，做事（act 的过去式和过去分词）；表演，扮演（角色）；表现，行事；担任，充当（某角色）；行使……职能；代理

e.en: An adaptation of a book or play is a film or a television programme that is based on it.

ex.en: Branagh won two awards for his screen adaptation of Shakespeare's Henry the Fifth.
ex.zh: 布拉纳因他对莎士比亚的《亨利五世》的荧幕改编而获了两次奖。

e.en: Adaptation is the act of changing something or changing your behaviour to make it suitable for a new purpose or situation.

ex.en: Most living creatures are capable of adaptation when compelled to do so.
ex.zh: 大多数生物在为情势所迫时都能适应。

d: n. 改编本，改写本；适应，改变；适应（性），适应力；适应性变化

e.en: An admiral is a very senior officer who commands a navy.

ex.en: ...Admiral Hodges.
ex.zh: …霍奇斯海军上将。

d: n. 海军上将，海军将军；舰队司令；海军上将蛱蝶；（Admiral）（美、俄、加）阿德米拉尔（人名）

e.en: If you advise someone to do something, you tell them what you think they should do.

ex.en: The minister advised him to leave as soon as possible.
ex.zh: 部长建议他尽快离开。

ex.en: I would strongly advise against it.
ex.zh: 我会强烈建议不要这样做。

e.en: If an expert advises people on a particular subject, he or she gives them help and information on that subject. (就某话题向某人)

ex.en: ...an officer who advises undergraduates from the University on money matters.
ex.zh: …一位在钱的问题上向该大学本科生提供咨询的官员。

d: v. 劝告，建议（advise 的现在分词）；通知，告知
n. 咨询，辅导；建议（advise 的动名词）
n. 盟友关系，同盟状态；（社会正义、包容等语境中）亦指掌握权力或优势的人作为盟友，以持续行动支持、声援弱势或被边缘化群体的做法

e.en: Your antagonist is your opponent or enemy.

ex.en: Spassky had never previously lost to his antagonist.
ex.zh: 斯帕斯基以前从未败给过他的敌手。

d: n. 对手，敌手，对立者；拮抗物；拮抗肌

e.en: If you say that something appears to be the way you describe it, you are reporting what you believe or what you have been told, though you cannot be sure it is true.

ex.en: There appears to be increasing support for the leadership to take a more aggressive stance.
ex.zh: 似乎有不断增长的对领导层采取更强立场的支持。

e.en: If someone or something appears to have a particular quality or characteristic, they give the impression of having that quality or characteristic.

ex.en: She did her best to appear more self-assured than she felt.
ex.zh: 她竭力表现得比她感觉的更为自信。

ex.en: He is anxious to appear a gentleman.
ex.zh: 他急于表现得像一位绅士。

e.en: When someone or something appears, they move into a position where you can see them.

ex.en: A woman appeared at the far end of the street.
ex.zh: 一个女人在街那端出现了。

e.en: When something new appears, it begins to exist or reaches a stage of development where its existence can be noticed.

ex.en: ...small white flowers which appear in early summer.
ex.zh: …在初夏出现的小白花。

d: v. 出现，呈现；首次使用，起源；出庭；演出，出场；出版，发表；记载，提及；看来，似乎；表现得……；到达
n. 有声读物，有声书（将书籍等文字内容朗读并录制而成的音频制品）

e.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them. 大量;

ex.en: As the deadline approached she experienced a bewildering array of emotions.
ex.zh: 随着最后期限的临近，她心绪变得纷繁复杂起来。

e.en: An array of objects is a collection of them that is displayed or arranged in a particular way.

ex.en: We visited the local markets and saw wonderful arrays of fruit and vegetables.
ex.zh: 我们参观了当地的市场，看到了漂亮地摆放着的水果蔬菜。

d: n. 一系列，大量；数组，阵列；盛装
v. 布置，排列；配置（兵力）；穿戴，打扮
n. 亚崔迪家族（《沙丘》中虚构的贵族家庭）；希腊神话人物阿特雷斯的后代；（英、美、俄、印尼、比、墨、加）亚崔迪（姓氏）
n. 复仇者（avenger 的复数）

e.en: The beginning of an event or process is the first part of it. (事情、过程的)

ex.en: This was also the beginning of her recording career.
ex.zh: 这也是她灌片生涯的开始。

e.en: The beginnings of something are the signs or events which form the first part of it.

ex.en: The discussions were the beginnings of a dialogue with Moscow.
ex.zh: 这些会谈是与莫斯科对话的序曲。

e.en: The beginning of a period of time is the time at which it starts. (某时段的)

ex.en: The wedding will be at the beginning of March.
ex.zh: 婚礼将于3月初举行。

e.en: The beginning of a piece of written material is the first words or sentences of it. (文章的)

ex.en: ...the question that was raised at the beginning of this chapter.
ex.zh: …本章开头提出的问题。

d: n. 开始，开端（beginning 的复数）；初期迹象，早期阶段（the beginnings of something）；出身，背景（如 humble beginnings）

e.en: A beloved person, thing, or place is one that you feel great affection for.

ex.en: He lost his beloved wife last year.
ex.zh: 他去年痛失爱妻。

d: adj. 钟爱的，深受爱戴的
n. 心爱的人

e.en: When a baby is born, it comes out of its mother's body at the beginning of its life. In formal English, if you say that someone is born of someone or to someone, you mean that person is their parent.

ex.en: She was born in Milan on April 29, 1923.
ex.zh: 她1923年4月29日生于米兰。

ex.en: He was born of German parents and lived most of his life abroad.
ex.zh: 他的父母是德国人，他一生大部分时间生活在国外。

e.en: If someone is born with a particular disease, problem, or characteristic, they have it from the time they are born.

ex.en: He was born with only one lung.
ex.zh: 他生下来就只有一个肺。

ex.en: Some people are born brainy.
ex.zh: 有些人生来就聪明。

e.en: You can use be born in front of a particular name to show that a person was given this name at birth, although they may be better known by another name.

ex.en: She was born Jenny Harvey on June 11, 1946.
ex.zh: 1946年6月11日她出生时取名珍妮·哈维。

e.en: You use born to describe someone who has a natural ability to do a particular activity or job. For example, if you are a born cook, you have a natural ability to cook well.

ex.en: Jack was a born teacher.
ex.zh: 杰克是个天生的教师。

d: adj. 天生的，生来就有的；出生的；产生的，（机构、想法等）问世的
comb. 以……的顺序（或方式、地点等）出生的
v. 忍受；承担；具有（bear 的过去分词形式）
【名】 （Born）（英、美、德、爱、丹）博恩（人名）

e.en: A book is a number of pieces of paper, usually with words printed on them, which are fastened together and fixed inside a cover of stronger paper or cardboard. Books contain information, stories, or poetry, for example.

ex.en: His eighth book came out earlier this year and was an instant best-seller.
ex.zh: 他的第8本书今年早些时候出版了，并很快成为了一本畅销书。

ex.en: ...the author of a book on politics.
ex.zh: …一本政治书的作者。

e.en: A book of something such as stamps, matches, or tickets is a small number of them fastened together between thin cardboard covers. (邮票) 册; (火柴) 纸板; (票)

ex.en: Can I have a book of first class stamps please?
ex.zh: 请给我一版一等邮票，好吗？

e.en: When you book something such as a hotel room or a ticket, you arrange to have it or use it at a particular time.

ex.en: American officials have booked hotel rooms for the women and children.
ex.zh: 美国官员已经为这些妇女和儿童预订了宾馆房间。

ex.en: Laurie booked herself a flight home.
ex.zh: 劳里为自己预订了回家的机票。

e.en: A company's or organization's books are its records of money that has been spent and earned or of the names of people who belong to it. (公司或机构的) 帐簿;

ex.en: For the most part he left the books to his managers and accountants.
ex.zh: 他大多把账簿留给他的经理和会计们处理。

d: n. 书，书籍，图书（book 的复数）；账簿，账目记录，（机构）名册
v. 预订；把……记录在案，登记（book 的第三人称单数）
n. 布里斯托尔（英国西部的港口城市）

e.en: If you describe someone as calculating, you disapprove of the fact that they deliberately plan to get what they want, often by hurting or harming other people. 精明的;

ex.en: Northbridge is a cool, calculating, and clever criminal who could strike again.
ex.zh: 诺思布里奇是个冷静、精明、机灵的罪犯，他有可能再犯。

d: adj. 精明的，精于算计的
v. 计算；预测（calculate 的现在分词形式）

e.en: In the army, navy, and some other armed forces, a captain is an officer of middle rank. (陆军、海军及其他军种的)

ex.en: ...Captain Mark Phillips.
ex.zh: …马克·菲利普斯上尉。

ex.en: ...a captain in the army.
ex.zh: …一名陆军上尉。

e.en: The captain of a sports team is the player in charge of it. (体育运动队)

ex.en: ...Mickey Thomas, the captain of the tennis team.
ex.zh: …米奇·托马斯，这支网球队的队长。

e.en: The captain of a ship is the sailor in charge of it.

ex.en: ...the captain of an excursion boat.
ex.zh: …一艘游船的船长。

e.en: The captain of an aeroplane is the pilot in charge of it.

d: v．担任队长，担任船长：在团队、船只或其他组织中担任领导角色。

e.en: A channel is a television station.

ex.en: ...the only serious current affairs programme on either channel.
ex.zh: …任一频道上惟一严肃的时事节目。

ex.en: ...the proliferating number of television channels in America.
ex.zh: …美国电视频道的激增数量。

e.en: A channel is a band of radio waves on which radio messages can be sent and received.

ex.en: The radio channels were filled with the excited, jabbering voices of men going to war.
ex.zh: 收音机各波段满是即将参战的男人们激动喧哗的声音。

e.en: If you do something through a particular channel, or particular channels, that is the system or organization that you use to achieve your aims or to communicate. 渠道;

ex.en: The government will surely use the diplomatic channels available.
ex.zh: 政府肯定会采用现有的外交途径。

ex.en: The Americans recognize that the U.N. can be the channel for greater diplomatic activity.
ex.zh: 美国人承认联合国可以是更重要的外交活动的渠道。

e.en: A channel is a passage along which water flows.

ex.en: Keep the drainage channel clear.
ex.zh: 保持排水管渠道畅通。

d: n. 频道，电视频道；管道，通道，航道；渠道，手段；沟渠，沟槽；河床；海峡；信道；电子沟道；输液道
v. 引导，把……用于；输送，传送；通灵；努力赶上，受启发；形成凹槽
【名】 （Channel）（美）沙内乐（人名）

e.en: The CIA is the government organization in the United States that collects secret information about other countries. CIA is an abbreviation for "Central Intelligence Agency." (美国)

d: abbr. 中央情报局（Central Intelligence Agency）；美国烹饪学院（Culinary Institute of America）

e.en: If you cherish something such as a hope or a pleasant memory, you keep it in your mind for a long period of time. 珍藏 (希望、记忆等)

ex.en: The president will cherish the memory of this visit to Ohio.
ex.zh: 总统将铭记这次对俄亥俄州的访问。

e.en: (对希望、记忆等)

ex.en: ...the cherished dream of a world without wars.
ex.zh: …久藏心中的梦想：一个没有战争的世界。

e.en: If you cherish someone or something, you take good care of them because you love them.

ex.en: He genuinely loved and cherished her.
ex.zh: 他真爱并珍惜过她。

e.en: 珍爱的

ex.en: He described the picture as his most cherished possession.
ex.zh: 他说这张照片是他最珍爱的财产。

d: v. 珍视，珍爱；怀念（过去），抱有（希望）

e.en: If you make a copy of something, you produce something that looks like the original thing.

ex.en: The reporter apparently obtained a copy of Steve's resignation letter.
ex.zh: 记者显然得到了史蒂夫辞职信的复件。

e.en: A copy of a book, newspaper, or CD is one of many that are exactly the same. 一份 (书籍、报纸、CD等)

ex.en: I bought a copy of "USA Today" from a street-corner machine.
ex.zh: 我从售货机上买了一份《今日美国》。

e.en: If you copy something, you produce something that looks like the original thing.

ex.en: ...lawsuits against companies who have unlawfully copied computer programs.
ex.zh: …对非法复制计算机程序的公司的诉讼。

ex.en: He copied the chart from a book.
ex.zh: 他从书上复制了表格。

e.en: If you copy, or copy a piece of writing, you write it again exactly.

ex.en: He copied the data into a notebook.
ex.zh: 他把资料抄在了笔记本上。

ex.en: We're copying from textbooks because we don't have enough to go round.
ex.zh: 我们在抄写课本，因为不够每人一本。

d: v. 抄写，誊写；模仿，效法；作弊，抄袭；听见（或明白）无线电收发报机中讲话人的话；复制，拷贝
n. 一本，一册，一份；复印件，副本；原稿，素材；广告文字

e.en: A coronation is the ceremony at which a king or queen is crowned. (国王或女王的)

d: n. 加冕礼，加冕仪式

e.en: A crash is an accident in which a moving vehicle hits something and is damaged or destroyed. 撞车;

ex.en: His elder son was killed in a car crash a few years ago.
ex.zh: 他大儿子几年前死于一次车祸。

e.en: A crash is a sudden, loud noise.

ex.en: Two people recalled hearing a loud crash about 1:30 a.m.
ex.zh: 两人回忆说大约凌晨1：30时听到一声巨响。

e.en: If a moving vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed. 使…撞毁;

ex.en: The plane crashed mysteriously near the island of Ustica.
ex.zh: 飞机在乌斯蒂卡岛附近神秘地坠毁了。

ex.en: Her car crashed into the rear of a van.
ex.zh: 她的汽车撞毁了一辆面包车的尾部。

e.en: If something crashes somewhere, it moves and hits something else violently, making a loud noise. (发出巨响的)

ex.en: The door swung inwards to crash against a chest of drawers behind it.
ex.zh: 门摆向里面，砰的一声猛力撞上了门后的五斗橱。

ex.en: My words were lost as the walls above us crashed down, filling the cellar with brick dust.
ex.zh: 随着上面的墙体轰隆一声倒塌下来，地窖里充满砖灰，我吓得说不出话来。

d: v. 碰撞，撞毁，坠毁，坠落；（企业、金融市场）破产，崩溃，垮台，暴跌；（计算机、系统）死机，崩溃（crash 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 失事的，已撞毁的

e.en: A cult is a fairly small religious group, especially one which is considered strange.

ex.en: The teenager may have been abducted by a religious cult.
ex.zh: 这位少年可能被某个异教团体绑架了。

e.en: The cult of something is a situation in which people regard that thing as very important or special.

ex.en: ...the cult of youth that recently gripped publishing.
ex.zh: …近期吸引了出版界的年青人的狂热。

e.en: Cult is used to describe things that are very popular or fashionable among a particular group of people.

ex.en: Since her death, she has become a cult figure.
ex.zh: 她死后已成为人们顶礼膜拜的人物。

e.en: Someone or something that is a cult has become very popular or fashionable among a particular group of people.

ex.en: Violence has become a cult among some young men.
ex.zh: 暴力已成为一些年轻人追逐的时尚。

d: n. 异教，异教组织；狂热崇拜，迷信；（特定群体的）偶像，时尚；崇拜者，信徒；宗教信仰，宗教习俗
adj. 受崇拜的，热门的

e.en: December is the twelfth and last month of the year in the Western calendar. 12

ex.en: ...a bright morning in mid-December.
ex.zh: …12月中旬一个晴朗的早晨。

d: n. 十二月，公历（西方历法）中的第十二个月，也是一年的最后一个月

e.en: If you describe something or someone as delightful, you mean they are very pleasant.

ex.en: It was the most delightful garden I had ever seen.
ex.zh: 这是我见过的最讨人喜欢的花园。

e.en: 令人愉快地

ex.en: This delightfully refreshing cologne can be splashed on liberally.
ex.zh: 这种清爽怡人的古龙香水可以尽情喷洒。

d: adj. 令人愉快的，宜人的

e.en: A designer is a person whose job is to design things by making drawings of them.

ex.en: Carolyne is a fashion designer.
ex.zh: 卡罗琳是位时装设计师。

e.en: Designer clothes or designer labels are expensive, fashionable clothes made by a famous designer, rather than being made in large quantities in a factory.

ex.en: He wears designer clothes and drives an antique car.
ex.zh: 他穿着名师设计的服装，开着一辆老爷车。

e.en: You can use designer to describe things that are worn or bought because they are fashionable.

ex.en: She sat up and removed her designer sunglasses.
ex.zh: 她坐起来，摘掉她的时尚墨镜。

d: n. 设计师，设计者；谋划者
adj. 由著名设计师设计的，标有设计师姓名的；时尚的，时髦的

e.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

ex.en: ...a distinguished academic family.
ex.zh: …一个卓越的学术之家。

e.en: If you describe someone as distinguished, you mean that they look very noble and respectable.

ex.en: His suit was immaculately cut and he looked very distinguished.
ex.zh: 他的西服剪裁完美，人显得十分高贵。

d: adj. 卓越的，杰出的；高贵的，尊贵的
v. 区别，分清；使有别于；看清，认出（distinguish 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 同伴，伴侣；（受雇照料老人或病人的）陪护；成对的物品之一；同甘共苦的伙伴；（用于书名）指南，手册；伴星；最低级爵士
v. 陪伴
【名】 （Companion）（英）康帕宁（人名）

e.en: Domestic political activities, events, and situations happen or exist within one particular country.

ex.en: ...over 100 domestic flights a day to 30 leading U.S. destinations.
ex.zh: …每天飞往美国30个主要目的地的100多个国内航班。

e.en: Domestic duties and activities are concerned with the running of a home and family.

ex.en: ...a plan for sharing domestic chores.
ex.zh: …一份分担家务的计划。

e.en: Domestic items and services are intended to be used in people's homes rather than in factories or offices.

ex.en: ...domestic appliances.
ex.zh: …家用电器。

e.en: A domestic situation or atmosphere is one which involves a family and their home.

ex.en: It was a scene of such domestic bliss.
ex.zh: 这是一幕家庭美满的场景。

d: adj. 国内的，本国的；家用的，家庭的；喜爱家庭生活的，乐于操持家务的；非野生的，驯养的
n. 家庭纠纷，家庭矛盾；佣人，家仆；国货，本地产品

e.en: Doomsday is a day or time when you expect something terrible or unpleasant is going to happen.

ex.en: ...the doomsday scenario of civil war between the two factions.
ex.zh: ...两派系间内战可能导致的灾难情景。

e.en: In the Christian religion, Doomsday is the last day of the world, on which God will judge everyone. (基督教)

d: n. 世界末日；灾难时刻；（基督教）最后的审判日

e.en: a dramatist, esp one associated with a particular company or theatre 剧作家 (Also called dramaturgist)

d: n. 剧作家（等于 dramatist, dramaturgist）；剧团的文艺顾问（等于 dramaturg）

e.en: To embody an idea or quality means to be a symbol or expression of that idea or quality. 体现;

ex.en: Jack Kennedy embodied all the hopes of the 1960s.
ex.zh: 杰克•肯尼迪体现了20世纪60年代的全部希望。

ex.en: For twenty-nine years, Checkpoint Charlie embodied the Cold War.
ex.zh: 29年来，查理检查站具体象征了冷战。

e.en: If something is embodied in a particular thing, the second thing contains or consists of the first. 包含;

ex.en: The proposal has been embodied in a draft resolution.
ex.zh: 这项提议已经被包含在一份决议草案中。

d: v. 体现，使具体化，具体表达（embody 的过去式和过去分词）；用于 be embodied in 时表示被包含、被收录或被具体体现
adj. （认知科学中）具身的；有形体的，具体化的

e.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as endearing, you mean that it causes you to feel very fond of them.

ex.en: She has such an endearing personality.
ex.zh: 她有个如此招人喜爱的个性。

d: adj. 可爱的，讨人喜欢的，惹人喜爱的

e.en: Someone who is empathetic has the ability to share another person's feelings or emotions as if they were their own. 体恤别人感受的;

ex.en: ...Clinton's skills as an empathetic listener.
ex.zh: ...克林顿作为一位感同身受倾听者的本领。

d: adj. 移情作用的，有同理心的，善解人意的，同感的（等于 empathic）

e.en: English is the language spoken by people who live in Great Britain and Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, and many other countries.

English means belonging or relating to England, or to its people or language. It is also often used to mean belonging or relating to Great Britain, although many people object to this. 英格兰 (人) 的; 英国 (人) 的;

ex.en: ...the English way of life.
ex.zh: …英格兰人的生活方式。

e.en: The English are English people.

ex.en: It is often said that the English are reserved.
ex.zh: 人们常说英格兰人保守。

d: adj. 英国的；英国人的；英语的，英文的
n. 英语，英文；英语（学科）；（总称）英国人，英格兰人；（台球等的）侧旋
vt. 把……译成英语，把……译成英文

e.en: An exemplar is someone or something that is considered to be so good that they should be copied or imitated.

ex.en: They viewed their new building as an exemplar of taste.
ex.zh: 他们将自己的新建筑视为一个品味的典范。

e.en: An exemplar is a typical example of a group or class of things.

ex.en: One of the wittiest exemplars of the technique was M. C. Escher.
ex.zh: 该技术最巧妙的代表之一是埃舍尔。

d: n. 模范，榜样，典范；典型例子，范例；标本，样本，样例

e.en: Someone or something that is enigmatic is mysterious and difficult to understand.

ex.en: She starred in one of Welles's most enigmatic films.
ex.zh: 她主演了威尔斯最神秘的电影当中的一部。

e.en: 神秘难解地

ex.en: "Corbiere didn't deserve this," she said enigmatically.
ex.zh: “科比埃尔不应获得这个，”她高深莫测地说。

d: adj. 神秘的，高深莫测的，谜一般的

e.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

ex.en: He has also had managerial experience on every level.
ex.zh: 他还具备各层次的管理经验。

e.en: Experience is used to refer to the past events, knowledge, and feelings that make up someone's life or character.

ex.en: I should not be in any danger here, but experience has taught me caution.
ex.zh: 我在这里应该没有任何危险，但阅历已教会我谨慎。

e.en: An experience is something that you do or that happens to you, especially something important that affects you.

ex.en: His only experience of gardening so far proved immensely satisfying.
ex.zh: 他仅有的园艺经历到目前为止非常令人满意。

e.en: If you experience a particular situation, you are in that situation or it happens to you.

ex.en: We had never experienced this kind of holiday before and had no idea what to expect.
ex.zh: 我们以前从未经历过这种假期，不知道有什么可期待的。

d: n. 经历，体验（experience 的复数）
v. 经历；体验到，感受到（experience 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Firefighters are people whose job is to put out fires.

d: n. 消防队员

e.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

ex.en: I still love him and I would never forsake him.
ex.zh: 我仍然爱他，我永远不会离弃他。

e.en: If you forsake something, you stop doing it, using it, or having it.

ex.en: He doubted their claim to have forsaken military solutions to the civil war.
ex.zh: 他对他们声称已经放弃以军事手段解决内战的说法有怀疑。

d: v. 抛弃，离开（尤指不履行责任)；摒弃，离开（尤指喜爱的事物）；离开，告别（某地）

e.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting. 耀眼的;

ex.en: Freddie Mercury was a flamboyant star of the hard rock scene.
ex.zh: 弗雷迪·默丘里曾是硬摇滚乐舞台上一颗耀眼的明星。

e.en: 耀眼;

ex.en: Campese was his usual mixture of flamboyance and flair.
ex.zh: 坎皮斯仍像平时那样，既有派，又有才。

d: adj. 艳丽的，艳丽夺目的；华丽张扬的，炫耀的；火焰似的；（建筑）火焰式的
n. 凤凰木

e.en: If you describe someone as foul-mouthed, you disapprove of them because they use offensive words or say very rude things.

d: adj. 说话下流的；满嘴脏话的

e.en: A franchise is an authority that is given by an organization to someone, allowing them to sell its goods or services or to take part in an activity which the organization controls. (公司授予某人的)

ex.en: ...fast-food franchises.
ex.zh: …快餐特许经营权。

ex.en: ...the franchise to build and operate the tunnel.
ex.zh: …建造、运营隧道的特许权。

e.en: If a company franchises its business, it sells franchises to other companies, allowing them to sell its goods or services.

ex.en: She has recently franchised her business.
ex.zh: 她最近已出售了其公司的特许经营权。

e.en: Franchise is the right to vote in an election.

ex.en: ...the introduction of universal franchise.
ex.zh: …普选权的采用。

d: n. 特许经营权；获特许经营权的企业（商店）；公民权，选举权；职业运动队；（由运动联合会授予的）会员运动队拥有权；特许经营品牌（或创意）；在相关故事中出现相同角色的一组电影
v. 给予特许经销权；给予……公民权（或选举权）

e.en: A friend is someone who you know well and like, but who is not related to you.

ex.en: I had a long talk about this with my best friend.
ex.zh: 我和我最好的朋友就此进行了长谈。

ex.en: She never was a close friend of mine.
ex.zh: 她从来就不是我的密友。

e.en: If one country refers to another as a friend, they mean that the other country is not an enemy of theirs.

ex.en: The president said that Japan is now a friend and international partner.
ex.zh: 总统说日本现在是盟国和国际伙伴。

e.en: If you are friends with someone, you are their friend and they are yours. (与…是)

ex.en: I still wanted to be friends with Alison.
ex.zh: 我仍然希望同艾莉森做朋友。

ex.en: We remained good friends.
ex.zh: 我们一直是好朋友。

e.en: The friends of a country, cause, organization, or a famous politician are the people and organizations who help and support them.

ex.en: ...the friends of Israel.
ex.zh: …以色列的支持者。

d: n. 朋友，友人；（社交网站上的）好友；（与……是） 朋友，朋友关系（friends）；（组织或政治运动等的）支持者，（尤指）赞助者；自己人，同盟者；熟悉（或有帮助）的事物；相识的人，（偶然遇见的）陌生人（常作礼貌称呼语或讽刺用语）；友好国家；（议员间或律师间的一种称呼）朋友，阁下，同人；（基督教）公谊会教友，贵格会成员，教友派信徒（Friend）
v. （在社交网站上） 把（某人）加为好友；与……为友，帮助
【名】 （Friend）（英）弗兰德（人名）

e.en: A friendship is a relationship between two or more friends.

ex.en: Giving advice when it's not called for is the quickest way to end a good friendship.
ex.zh: 在不需要时给予建议是了结一段友谊的最快方式。

ex.en: She struck up a close friendship with Desiree during the week of rehearsals.
ex.zh: 她在那一周的排练中和德西蕾建立起亲密的友谊。

e.en: Friendship is a relationship between two countries in which they help and support each other.

ex.en: The president set the targets for the future to promote friendship with East Europe.
ex.zh: 总统确定了与东欧增进友好关系的未来目标。

e.en: You use friendship to refer in a general way to the state of being friends, or the feelings that friends have for each other.

ex.en: ...a hobby which led to a whole new world of friendship and adventure.
ex.zh: …一个通向友情和冒险的一个全新世界的爱好。

d: n. 友谊，朋友关系；友情，友好；（国家或政府之间的）友好关系
【名】 （Friendship）（英）弗兰德希普（人名）

e.en: To harm a person or animal means to cause them physical injury, usually on purpose. (故意地)

ex.en: The hijackers seemed anxious not to harm anyone.
ex.zh: 劫机犯们似乎并不急于伤害任何人。

e.en: Harm is physical injury to a person or an animal which is usually caused on purpose. (故意的)

ex.en: All dogs are capable of doing harm to human beings.
ex.zh: 所有的狗都能对人造成伤害。

e.en: To harm a thing, or sometimes a person, means to damage them or make them less effective or successful than they were.

ex.en: ...a warning that the product may harm the environment.
ex.zh: …一则该产品可能会破坏环境的警告。

e.en: Harm is the damage to something which is caused by a particular course of action.

ex.en: The abuse of your powers does harm to all other officers who do their job properly.
ex.zh: 你滥用权力有损于所有其他好好工作的政府官员。

d: v. harm 的过去式和过去分词：伤害；损害
adj. 受到伤害的，受损的（the harmed 可指受害者、被侵害者）

e.en: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment. (聚会的)

ex.en: Apart from my host, I didn't know a single person there.
ex.zh: 除了主人，那儿的人我一个也不认识。

e.en: If someone hosts a party, dinner, or other function, they have invited the guests and provide the food, drink, or entertainment. 主办 (聚会、宴会或其他集会)

ex.en: Tonight she hosts a ball for 300 guests.
ex.zh: 今晚她做东办一场有300名来宾参加的舞会。

e.en: A country, city, or organization that is the host of an event provides the facilities for that event to take place. (举办某活动的)

ex.en: Atlanta was chosen to be host of the 1996 Olympic games.
ex.zh: 亚特兰大被选为1996年奥运会的东道主。

e.en: If a country, city, or organization hosts an event, they provide the facilities for the event to take place.

ex.en: New Bedford hosts a number of lively festivals throughout the summer months.
ex.zh: 新贝德福德整个夏天举办了许多个欢快有趣的艺术节。

d: n. 主人；主持人；主办者，东道主；寄主，宿主；接受移植组织（或器官）的受体；主机；（某种特别生物的）生存地；许多人（或物）；军队；（圣餐仪式中的）圣饼，圣体
v. 主办，做……的东道主；做节目主持人；作为主人组织（聚会），做东；（通常收费在与互联网连接的计算机上）存储网站

e.en: A humble person is not proud and does not believe that they are better than other people. 谦卑的;

ex.en: He gave a great performance, but he was very humble.
ex.zh: 他的表演很精彩，但他却很谦逊。

e.en: 谦卑地;

ex.en: "I'm a lucky man, undeservedly lucky," he said humbly.
ex.zh: “我是个幸运的人，不该这么幸运，”他谦虚地说。

e.en: People with low social status are sometimes described as humble. (社会地位)

ex.en: Spyros Latsis started his career as a humble fisherman in the Aegean.
ex.zh: 斯派罗斯·拉齐斯最初的职业是爱琴海的一名地位低微的渔夫。

e.en: A humble place or thing is ordinary and not special in any way.

ex.en: There are restaurants, both humble and expensive, that specialize in noodles.
ex.zh: 既有普通的也有昂贵的专营面条的餐馆。

d: adj. 谦虚的，谦卑的；（级别或地位）低下的，卑微的；简陋的，没有特别之处的
v. 使谦卑，使感到自惭；（轻易）击败（强敌）

e.en: If you describe someone as an illustrious person, you mean that they are extremely well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive. (人)

ex.en: ...the most illustrious scientists of the century.
ex.zh: …本世纪最著名的科学家们。

d: adj. 著名的，杰出的，显赫的；辉煌的，卓越的，光荣的

e.en: If you describe a group or organization as inclusive, you mean that it allows all kinds of people to belong to it, rather than just one kind of person.

ex.en: The academy is far more inclusive now than it used to be.
ex.zh: 该学院如今比过去更为兼收并蓄。

e.en: After stating the first and last item in a set of things, you can add inclusive to make it clear that the items stated are included in the set.

ex.en: You are also invited to join us on our prayer days (this year, June 6 to June 14 inclusive).
ex.zh: 你也受邀加入我们的祷告日（今年从6月6日（含）至6月14日（含））。

e.en: If a price is inclusive, it includes all the charges connected with the goods or services offered. If a price is inclusive of shipping and handling, it includes the charge for this.

ex.en: ...all prices are inclusive of delivery.
ex.zh: …所有价格包括运费。

e.en: Inclusive is also an adverb.

ex.en: The outpatient programme costs $105 per day, all inclusive.
ex.zh: 门诊病人方案收费每人每天105美元，一切费用包括在内。

d: adj. 包容广阔的；包括一切费用在内的；包括的，包含的；无性别歧视的；对外开放的

e.en: Infamous people or things are well-known because of something bad.

ex.en: He was infamous for his anti-feminist attitudes.
ex.zh: 他因为他的反女权主义姿态而臭名昭著。

d: adj. 声名狼藉的，臭名昭著的；邪恶的，无耻的，不名誉的
adv. 不可磨灭地，无法消除地

e.en: You use initial to describe something that happens at the beginning of a process.

ex.en: The initial reaction has been excellent.
ex.zh: 最初的反应极好。

e.en: Initials are the capital letters that begin each word of a name. For example, if your full name is Michael Dennis Stocks, your initials are M.D.S. (姓名的)

ex.en: ...a silver Porsche with her initials JB on the side.
ex.zh: …一辆银色保时捷汽车，侧面有她的姓名首字母JB。

e.en: If someone initials an official document, they write their initials on it, to show that they have seen it or that they accept or agree with it.

ex.en: Would you mind initialling this voucher?
ex.zh: 请您在这张单子上签上姓名的首字母，好吗？

d: adj. 开始的，最初的；（字母）位于词首的
n. （姓名的）首字母
v. 用姓名的首字母作标记（或签名）于

e.en: Intellect is the ability to understand or deal with ideas and information.

ex.en: Do the emotions develop in parallel with the intellect?
ex.zh: 情感与智力同步发展吗？

e.en: Intellect is the quality of being intelligent.

ex.en: She is famed for her intellect.
ex.zh: 她因才智而出名。

d: n. 智力，思维能力；才智出众者

e.en: If two or more things are intertwined or intertwine, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

ex.en: Their destinies are intertwined.
ex.zh: 他们的命运交织在一起。

ex.en: Three major narratives intertwine within Foucault's text, "Madness and Civilization."
ex.zh: 福考特的文章《疯狂与文明》中交织着三种主要的叙述。

e.en: If two things intertwine, they are twisted together or go over and under each other.

ex.en: Trees, undergrowth and creepers intertwined, blocking our way.
ex.zh: 树木、灌木和攀藤植物相互缠绕，挡了我们的路。

ex.en: The towels were embroidered with their intertwined initials.
ex.zh: 这些毛巾上绣着他们缠绕着的第一个字母。

d: adj. 缠绕的；错综复杂的，交织的
v. 使缠结，缠绕，使交织（intertwine 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: You use ironically to draw attention to a situation that is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast.

ex.en: Ironically, for a man who hated war, he would have made a superb war cameraman.
ex.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，他这样一个憎恨战争的人曾经可能成为一名优秀的战地摄影师。

e.en: If you say something ironically, you say the opposite of what you really mean, as a joke.

ex.en: Classmates at West Point had ironically dubbed him Beauty.
ex.zh: 西点军校的同学们曾经讽刺地给他起了一个绰号——“美人”。

d: adv. 具有讽刺意味的是；反讽地，讽刺地

e.en: a variety of red apple that ripens in early autumn
the son of Saul and David's close friend, who was killed in battle (I Samuel 31; II Samuel 1:19–26) 约拿单;
e.zh: 扫罗之子，大卫的密友，在战斗中牺牲

d: n. 乔纳森（男子名）

e.en: If you describe someone as irreverent, you mean that they do not show respect for people or things that are generally respected.

ex.en: Taylor combined great knowledge with an irreverent attitude to history.
ex.zh: 泰勒知识渊博，但对历史却持不尊重态度。

e.en: 不尊敬

ex.en: His irreverence for authority marks him out as a troublemaker.
ex.zh: 他对权威的蔑视表明他是个惹事的人。

d: adj. 不敬的，无礼的，不尊敬的（常含调侃或赞赏意味）

e.en: When you make a journey, you travel from one place to another.

ex.en: There is an express service from Paris that completes the journey to Bordeaux in under 4 hours.
ex.zh: 有一趟从巴黎开出的快车，到波尔多全程不到4小时。

e.en: You can refer to a person's experience of changing or developing from one state of mind to another as a journey. (心路)

ex.en: My films try to describe a journey of discovery, both for myself and the viewer.
ex.zh: 我的影片力图为我自己和观众描述一段自我发现的心路历程。

e.en: If you journey somewhere, you travel there.

ex.en: In February 1935, Naomi journeyed to the United States for the first time.
ex.zh: 1935年2月，内奥米第一次踏入美国。

d: n. 旅行，旅程；历程，过程
v. 旅行
【名】 （Journey）（英）朱尼，朱妮（人名）

e.en: If you describe something as kaleidoscopic, you mean that it consists of a lot of very different parts, such as different colours, patterns, or shapes. 由多种不同部分组成的(如不同颜色、图案或形状)

ex.en: ...a kaleidoscopic study of the shifting ideas and symbols of nationhood.
ex.zh: ...一种对不断变化的民族主义思想及象征的多角度研究。

d: adj. 千变万化的；万花筒似的
adj. 眼光锐利的

e.en: A king is a man who is the most important member of the royal family of his country, and who is considered to be the head of state of that country. 君主;

ex.en: ...the king and queen of Spain.
ex.zh: …西班牙国王和王后。

e.en: If you describe a man as the king of something, you mean that he is the most important person doing that thing or he is the best at doing it. 首屈一指的男性;

ex.en: He was the king of the cowboys.
ex.zh: 他是牛仔之王。

e.en: A king is a playing card with a picture of a king on it. (扑克牌的) 老(K)

ex.en: ...the king of diamonds.
ex.zh: …方片。

e.en: In chess, the king is the most important piece. When you are in a position to capture your opponent's king, you win the game. (国际象棋的)

d: n. 君主，国王；某物之王，首屈一指者；（国际象棋中的）王；极具影响；（纸牌中的）老K；（英国）男性国王在位时使用的国歌
v. 立……为王
【名】 （King）（德、英、葡、捷、西）金，（中）金（普通话·威妥玛），（泰）京，（东南亚国家华语）京（人名）

e.en: Immigration is the coming of people into a country in order to live and work there.

ex.en: The government has decided to tighten its immigration policy.
ex.zh: 政府已决定收紧其移民政策。

e.en: Immigration or immigration control is the place at a port, airport, or international border where officials check the passports of people who wish to come into the country.

ex.en: First, you have to go through immigration and customs.
ex.zh: 首先你必须通过移民局和海关的检查。

d: n. 移民（入境）；移民人数；移民局入境检查，移民局入境检查处

e.en: attracting attention; striking

d: adj. 醒目的，引人注意的，显著的
v. 逮捕，拘留；扣留（船只）；阻止，抑制，中止；拦住，抓住；吸引（某人的）注意（均为 arrest 的现在分词）

e.en: An agent is a person who looks after someone else's business affairs or does business on their behalf.

ex.en: You are buying direct, rather than through an agent.
ex.zh: 你在直接购买，而不是通过代理商购买。

e.en: An agent in the arts world is a person who gets work for an actor or musician, or who sells the work of a writer to publishers. (艺术界的)

ex.en: My literary agent thinks it is not unreasonable to expect $500,000 in total.
ex.zh: 我的文学经纪人认为预期总共50万美元并非不合情理。

e.en: An agent is a person who works for a country's secret service.

ex.en: All these years he's been an agent for the East.
ex.zh: 这些年来他一直为东方国家做间谍。

e.en: A chemical that has a particular effect or is used for a particular purpose can be referred to as a particular kind of agent.

ex.en: ...the bleaching agent in white flour.
ex.zh: …白面粉中的漂白剂。

d: n. （人工智能领域）智能体；代理人，代理商；（艺术界的）经纪人；间谍，特工；原动力，动因；剂；（语法）施动者；（美国某些政府部门的）官员
【名】 （Agent）（罗）阿真特（人名）

e.en: If something is below something else, it is in a lower position.

ex.en: He appeared from the apartment directly below Leonard's.
ex.zh: 他从伦纳德家正下方的公寓里走了出来。

ex.en: The sun had already sunk below the horizon.
ex.zh: 太阳已沉下地平线。

e.en: Below is also an adverb.

ex.en: We climbed rather perilously down a rope-ladder to the boat below.
ex.zh: 我们冒着危险沿着绳梯爬到了下边的小船上。

ex.en: ...a view to the street below.
ex.zh: …楼下街景。

e.en: If something is below ground or below the ground, it is in the ground.

ex.en: They have designed a system which pumps up water from nearly 1,000 feet below ground.
ex.zh: 他们设计了一个能从地表以下1000英尺处抽水的系统。

e.en: You use below in a piece of writing to refer to something that is mentioned later.

ex.en: Please write to me at the address below.
ex.zh: 请按以下地址给我写信。

d: prep. （位置）在……下面； （数、量、水平等）在……以下；（职位、官衔等）低于
adv. 在下面；（数字或级别）在……以下；在下文中；在下层甲板
【名】 （Below）（英、德、芬、瑞、丹、加）贝洛（人名）

e.en: An agent is a person who looks after someone else's business affairs or does business on their behalf.

ex.en: You are buying direct, rather than through an agent.
ex.zh: 你在直接购买，而不是通过代理商购买。

e.en: An agent in the arts world is a person who gets work for an actor or musician, or who sells the work of a writer to publishers. (艺术界的)

ex.en: My literary agent thinks it is not unreasonable to expect $500,000 in total.
ex.zh: 我的文学经纪人认为预期总共50万美元并非不合情理。

e.en: An agent is a person who works for a country's secret service.

ex.en: All these years he's been an agent for the East.
ex.zh: 这些年来他一直为东方国家做间谍。

e.en: A chemical that has a particular effect or is used for a particular purpose can be referred to as a particular kind of agent.

ex.en: ...the bleaching agent in white flour.
ex.zh: …白面粉中的漂白剂。

d: n. agent 的复数；代理人，代理商，经纪人；特工，间谍，探员；媒介，动因；药剂，制剂；（计算机）代理程序，智能体
v. 将……编入目录；系统记录，登记（catalog 的过去式/过去分词）
adj. 编入目录的

e.en: A criminal is a person who has committed a crime.

ex.en: A group of gunmen attacked a prison and set free nine criminals.
ex.zh: 一伙持枪歹徒袭击了一所监狱并放走了9名罪犯。

e.en: Criminal means connected with crime. 犯罪的;

ex.en: Her husband faces various criminal charges.
ex.zh: 她丈夫面临多项刑事的指控。

e.en: If you describe an action as criminal, you think it is very wrong or a serious mistake.

ex.en: He said a full-scale dispute involving strikes would be criminal.
ex.zh: 他说一个卷入罢工的全面抗争将是极其错误的。

d: n. 罪犯
adj. 犯法的，犯罪的；刑事的；应受责备的，可耻的；罪犯的，犯人的；（行为或情形）令人遗憾的，令人震惊的

e.en: When you compile something such as a report, book, or programme, you produce it by collecting and putting together many pieces of information. 汇编;

ex.en: The book took 10 years to compile.
ex.zh: 这本书花了10年编写。

d: v. 汇编，编纂；收集，搜集（信息、资料）；编译（计算机程序）（compile 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: An immigrant is a person who has come to live in a country from some other country. Compare . (外来)

ex.en: ...illegal immigrants.
ex.zh: …非法移民。

d: n. 移民（immigrant 的复数）

e.en: When people such as the police detain someone, they keep them in a place under their control.

ex.en: Police have detained two suspects in connection with the attack.
ex.zh: 警方拘留了2名与该袭击事件有关的嫌疑人。

e.en: To detain someone means to delay them, for example, by talking to them.

ex.en: Millson stood up. "Thank you. We won't detain you any further, Mrs. Stebbing."
ex.zh: 米尔森站起来。“谢谢您。我们不再耽搁您了，斯特宾太太。”

d: v. （正式）拘留，扣留：暂时限制某人的自由，或依法扣留货物、财物，通常是为了进一步调查或等待法律程序；（正式）耽搁，使耽误：使某人停留或延迟，通常是因为某种原因。

e.en: Done is the past participle of . (do)
A task or activity that is done has been completed successfully.

ex.en: When her deal is done, the client emerges with her purchase.
ex.zh: 交易完成后，顾客拿着购买的东西出来了。

e.en: When something that you are cooking is done, it has been cooked long enough and is ready. (饭菜)

ex.en: As soon as the cake is done, remove it from the oven.
ex.zh: 蛋糕一烤好，就把它从烤箱里拿出来。

e.en: You say "Done" when you are accepting a deal, arrangement, or bet that someone has offered to make with you. 行; 好 (表示接受建议或条件)

ex.en: "You lead and we'll look for it."—"Done."
ex.zh: “你带路，我们来找!”—“好的！”

d: adj. 完成的；煮熟的；不再发生的；为社会所接受的，得体的；上当受骗的；筋疲力尽的
int. 行，好
v. 做（do 的过去分词形式）
【名】 （Done）（美、英、罗马尼亚）多恩（人名）

e.en: A dragnet is a method used by police to catch suspected criminals. A large number of police officers search a specific area, in the hope that they will eventually find the person they are looking for.

ex.en: ...a massive police dragnet for two suspected terrorists.
ex.zh: ...警方为抓捕两名恐怖嫌疑人而展开的一场大规模拉网式搜查。

d: n. 拖网；搜索网，拉网式搜查，法网；收集装置（等于 drawnet）
n. 就职典礼；开幕式；开创

e.en: If something will inevitably happen, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

ex.en: Technological changes will inevitably lead to unemployment.
ex.zh: 技术变革将必然导致失业。

d: adv. 不可避免地，必然地；意料之中

e.en: If you post notices, signs, or other pieces of information somewhere, you attach them to a wall or board so that everyone can see them.

ex.en: Officials began posting warning notices.
ex.zh: 官员们开始张贴警示布告。

e.en: Post up means the same as . 同post

ex.en: He has posted a sign up that says "No Fishing."
ex.zh: 他已经张贴了一个标牌，写着“禁止钓鱼。”

e.en: If you post information on the Internet, you make the information available to other people on the Internet. (在互联网上)

ex.en: A consultation paper has been posted on the Internet inviting input from users.
ex.zh: 一份咨询文件已经贴上了互联网，恳请用户们提供信息。

e.en: If you keep someone posted, you keep giving them the latest information about a situation that they are interested in. 让 (某人)

ex.en: Keep me posted on your progress.
ex.zh: 让我及时知道你的进展。

d: n. 邮政，邮递；邮件，包裹；收集（或投递）邮件，邮班；职位，要职；岗位，哨所；柱，杆，桩；（赛马的）终点；球门柱；邮报（用于某些报纸名称中）；帖子，在线留言板上的信息；篮球场上篮筐附近的区域；策应位置；退伍军人协会地方分会
v. 邮寄；把……放入（或塞入）；派驻，委派；使驻守，设置（岗哨等）；张贴，公布；发布，发帖子；交付（保释金）；（运动员，参赛队）取得（成绩），创造（纪录）；（记账用语）将……入账
prep. 在……之后
【名】 （Post）（英、西、捷、瑞典、荷）波斯特（人名）
abbr. 十月（October）

e.en: You use reality to refer to real things or the real nature of things rather than imagined, invented, or theoretical ideas.

ex.en: Fiction and reality were increasingly blurred.
ex.zh: 小说与现实越来越混淆难分。

e.en: The reality of a situation is the truth about it, especially when it is unpleasant or difficult to deal with. (尤指令人不快或难对付的)

ex.en: ...the harsh reality of top international competition.
ex.zh: …顶级的国际竞争的残酷现实。

e.en: You say that something has become a reality when it actually exists or is actually happening. 事实存在;

ex.en: ...the whole procedure that made this book become a reality.
ex.zh: …使这本书的出版成为现实的整个过程。

e.en: You can use in reality to introduce a statement about the real nature of something, when it contrasts with something incorrect that has just been described. 事实上;

ex.en: He came across as streetwise, but in reality he was not.
ex.zh: 他看似适应都市的生活，但事实上他不是。

d: n. 真实，现实；实际经历，见到的事物；真实感，逼真性；存在；（哲学）实在，实在性
adj. 真人秀节目的

e.en: A receipt is a piece of paper that you get from someone as proof that they have received money or goods from you.

ex.en: I wrote her a receipt for the money.
ex.zh: 我为那笔钱给她开了张收据。

e.en: Receipts are the amount of money received during a particular period, for example by a shop or theatre.

ex.en: He was tallying the day's receipts.
ex.zh: 他正在结算当天的收入。

e.en: The receipt of something is the act of receiving it.

ex.en: Goods should be supplied within 28 days after the receipt of your order.
ex.zh: 收到你的订单28天内供货。

e.en: If you are in receipt of something, you have received it or you receive it regularly. 已收到;

ex.en: We are taking action, having been in receipt of a letter from him.
ex.zh: 收到他的信之后，我们正采取行动。

d: n. 收据，收条（receipt 的复数形式）；收入，进款（商店、企业、银行等在一定时期内收到的款项）

e.en: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later. 记录;

ex.en: Keep a record of all the payments.
ex.zh: 对所有付款做一个记录。

ex.en: There's no record of any marriage or children.
ex.zh: 没有任何有关结婚或子女的记录。

e.en: If you record a piece of information or an event, you write it down, photograph it, or put it into a computer so that in the future people can refer to it. 记录;

ex.en: Her letters record the domestic and social details of diplomatic life in China.
ex.zh: 她的信件记录了在中国的外交生活中家庭和社会活动的细节。

e.en: If you record something such as a speech or performance, you put it on tape or film so that it can be heard or seen again later. 录音;

ex.en: There is nothing to stop viewers from recording the films on videotape.
ex.zh: 没有办法阻止观众用录像带录下电影。

e.en: If a musician or performer records a piece of music or a television or radio show, they perform it so that it can be put onto CD, tape, or film.

ex.en: It took the musicians two and a half days to record their soundtrack for the film.
ex.zh: 音乐家们花了两天半的时间录制电影的配乐。

d: n. （record 的复数）记录，记载，档案；某人或某物过去的记录，经历，履历；（尤指体育或竞赛中的）最佳纪录，最好成绩；唱片
v. （record 的第三人称单数）记录，记载；录制；（仪器）显示，标示；（尤指体育上）获得（好成绩）

e.en: Relations between people, groups, or countries are contacts between them and the way in which they behave toward each other.

ex.en: Greece has established full diplomatic relations with Israel.
ex.zh: 希腊已经和以色列建立了全面的外交关系。

e.en: If you talk about the relation of one thing to another, you are talking about the ways in which they are connected.

ex.en: It is a question of the relation of ethics to economics.
ex.zh: 这是个道德和经济之间关系的问题。

e.en: Your relations are the members of your family.

ex.en: ...visits to friends and relations.
ex.zh: …对亲友的拜访。

e.en: You can talk about something in relation to something else when you want to compare the size, condition, or position of the two things.

ex.en: The money he'd been ordered to pay was minimal in relation to his salary.
ex.zh: 他被要求支付的钱与他的薪水相比是少的。

d: n. （人或物间的）联系；（国家、公司、组织等之间的）（正式）关系； 性关系；亲戚，亲属；讲述，叙述

e.en: If you do something repeatedly, you do it many times. 反复地;

ex.en: Both men have repeatedly denied the allegations.
ex.zh: 两个人都再三地否认这些指控。

d: adv. 重复地，再三地

e.en: If you say that something is reportedly true, you mean that someone has said that it is true, but you have no direct evidence of it. 据报道;

ex.en: More than two hundred people have reportedly been killed in the past week's fighting.
ex.zh: 据报道有两百多人在上周的战斗中丧生。

d: adv. 据报道，据传闻，据说

e.en: If you scour something such as a place or a book, you make a thorough search of it to try to find what you are looking for.

ex.en: Rescue crews had scoured an area of 30 square miles.
ex.zh: 救援人员已经搜遍了30平方英里的范围。

e.en: If you scour something such as a sink, floor, or pan, you clean its surface by rubbing it hard with something rough. (费力地)

ex.en: He decided to scour the sink.
ex.zh: 他决定把水池擦洗干净。

e.en: the act of scouring

d: v. scour 的现在分词：擦洗，擦亮；（彻底地）搜查；冲刷出，冲蚀；（兽医、畜牧）给……服强烈泻药；（家畜）患腹泻；（尤指搜寻追捕时）快速行走
n. 擦洗，刷洗；搜查，搜寻；（水利、地质）冲刷，冲蚀（作用）；牲畜排便，尤指腹泻

e.en: A result is something that happens or exists because of something else that has happened.

ex.en: Compensation is available for people who have developed asthma as a direct result of their work.
ex.zh: 直接因工作原因患哮喘的人会获得赔偿。

e.en: If something results in a particular situation or event, it causes that situation or event to happen.

ex.en: Fifty percent of road accidents result in head injuries.
ex.zh: 50%的公路交通事故致使头部受伤。

e.en: If something results from a particular event or action, it is caused by that event or action.

ex.en: Many hair problems result from what you eat.
ex.zh: 很多头发问题是由你吃的东西引起的。

e.en: A result is the situation that exists at the end of a contest.

ex.en: The final election results will be announced on Friday.
ex.zh: 最终选举结果将在周五被公布。

d: n. 结果，后果；（比赛或选举的）结果；（通过调查、研究、计算而获得的）结果； 考试成绩；成效，成果（results）；经营业绩（results）；（体育比赛中）胜局，获胜
v. 发生，产生；导致，造成（注明的结局或结果）
int.  成功了！（Result!）

e.en: If you search for something or someone, you look carefully for them.

ex.en: The Turkish security forces have started searching for the missing men.
ex.zh: 土耳其安全部队已经开始搜寻失踪人员。

ex.en: They searched for a spot where they could sit on the floor.
ex.zh: 他们在地板上寻找一个能够坐下的地方。

e.en: If you search a place, you look carefully for something or someone there. 在 (某地) 搜寻; 搜查 (某地)

ex.en: Armed troops searched the hospital yesterday.
ex.zh: 武装部队昨天搜查了这家医院。

ex.en: She searched her desk for the necessary information.
ex.zh: 她在她的书桌里搜寻必要的资料。

e.en: A search is an attempt to find something or someone by looking for them carefully.

ex.en: There was no chance of him being found alive and the search was abandoned.
ex.zh: 没有他活着被找到的可能了，于是放弃了搜寻。

e.en: If a police officer or someone else in authority searches you, they look carefully to see whether you have something hidden on you. 搜 (某人)

ex.en: The man took her suitcase from her and then searched her.
ex.zh: 那个人从她手上拿走了她的手提箱然后搜了她的身。

d: v. 搜查，搜寻；搜查（地方，车辆），搜……的身；思索，细想（问题答案等）；细察，细查；（用计算机）搜索，检索
n. 搜寻，搜查；探索，寻求；（计算机的）搜索，检索；调查地产负担
【名】 （Search）（印、美）瑟奇（人名）

e.en: If you search for something or someone, you look carefully for them.

ex.en: The Turkish security forces have started searching for the missing men.
ex.zh: 土耳其安全部队已经开始搜寻失踪人员。

ex.en: They searched for a spot where they could sit on the floor.
ex.zh: 他们在地板上寻找一个能够坐下的地方。

e.en: If you search a place, you look carefully for something or someone there. 在 (某地) 搜寻; 搜查 (某地)

ex.en: Armed troops searched the hospital yesterday.
ex.zh: 武装部队昨天搜查了这家医院。

ex.en: She searched her desk for the necessary information.
ex.zh: 她在她的书桌里搜寻必要的资料。

e.en: A search is an attempt to find something or someone by looking for them carefully.

ex.en: There was no chance of him being found alive and the search was abandoned.
ex.zh: 没有他活着被找到的可能了，于是放弃了搜寻。

e.en: If a police officer or someone else in authority searches you, they look carefully to see whether you have something hidden on you. 搜 (某人)

ex.en: The man took her suitcase from her and then searched her.
ex.zh: 那个人从她手上拿走了她的手提箱然后搜了她的身。

d: v. 搜索，搜寻；搜身；思索，细想（问题答案等）（search 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: a presentation, exhibition, or display 展览;

d: n. 放映，放映场次；表演；展示，展览，陈列；表现，成绩
v. 展示，显示（show 的现在分词和动名词形式）；炫耀，显耀（show off 的现在分词/动名词形式）

e.en: The source of something is the person, place, or thing which you get it from.

ex.en: ...over 40 percent of adults use television as their major source of information about the arts.
ex.zh: …超过40%的成年人利用电视作为他们了解艺术信息的主要来源。

ex.en: Renewable sources of energy must be used.
ex.zh: 可再生的能源必须利用。

e.en: In business, if a person or firm sources a product or a raw material, they find someone who will supply it.

ex.en: Together they travel the world, sourcing clothes for the small, privately owned company.
ex.zh: 他们一起环游世界，为那家小私营公司寻找服装货源。

e.en: A source is a person or book that provides information for a news story or for a piece of research.

ex.en: Military sources say the boat was heading south at high speed.
ex.zh: 军方的消息来源说船正向南方快速驶去。

e.en: The source of a difficulty is its cause.

ex.en: This gave me a clue as to the source of the problem.
ex.zh: 这给了我一个关于问题根源的线索。

d: n. 来源，出处；消息来源；起源，根源；发源地（source 的复数）
v. 从（某地）获取；寻找……的来源（source 的第三人称单数）
v. 少计（尤指人口统计数）
n. 少计（额）

e.en: A tally is a record of amounts or numbers which you keep changing and adding to as the activity which affects it progresses.

ex.en: They do not keep a tally of visitors to the palace, but it is very popular.
ex.zh: 他们没有对来宫殿的游客作一个记录，不过这个地方非常受欢迎的。

e.en: If one number or statement tallies with another, they agree with each other or are exactly the same. You can also say that two numbers or statements tally.

ex.en: Its own estimate of three hundred tallies with that of another survey.
ex.zh: 它自己估计的300与另一项调查的结果相吻合。

d: v. tally 的过去式和过去分词：（使）符合，（使）一致；计算总数，统计；（在比赛或游戏中）得分，或记录（比分、成绩）

e.en: Won't is the usual spoken form of "will not." (will not)

ex.en: The space shuttle won't lift off the launch pad until Sunday at the earliest.
ex.zh: 这架航天飞机最早要到星期天才会发射升空。

d: contr. 不会，将不（等于 will not）

e.en: If you watch someone or something, you look at them, usually for a period of time, and pay attention to what is happening.

ex.en: The man was standing in his doorway watching him.
ex.zh: 那个男人正站在自家门道里看着他。

ex.en: He seems to enjoy watching me work.
ex.zh: 他似乎喜欢看我干活。

e.en: If you watch something on television or an event such as a sports contest, you spend time looking at it, especially when you see it from the beginning to the end. 观看 (电视节目、比赛等)

ex.en: I'd stayed up late to watch the movie.
ex.zh: 我熬夜看了那部电影。

e.en: If you watch a situation or event, you pay attention to it or you are aware of it, but you do not influence it.

ex.en: Human rights groups have been closely watching the case.
ex.zh: 人权组织一直在密切关注着这件案子。

ex.en: He watched as nine people were swept into the crevasse.
ex.zh: 他眼看着9个人被卷入冰缝中。

e.en: If you watch people, especially children or animals, you are responsible for them, and make sure that they are not in danger.

ex.en: Parents can't be expected to watch their children 24 hours a day.
ex.zh: 不能指望父母全天24小时都照看自己的孩子。

d: v. 观察；注视；看守；警戒（watch的过去式）

e.en: The contents of a container such as a bottle, box, or room are the things that are inside it. (瓶子、盒子或房间的)

ex.en: Empty the contents of the pan into the sieve.
ex.zh: 将平锅里的东西全部倒入漏勺。

e.en: The contents of a book are its different chapters and sections, usually shown in a list at the beginning of the book. (书的)

ex.en: There is no Table of Contents.
ex.zh: 没有目录。

e.en: If you refer to the content or contents of something such as a book, television programme, or website, you are referring to the subject that it deals with, the story that it tells, or the ideas that it expresses. (书、电视节目或网站等的)

ex.en: She is reluctant to discuss the content of the play.
ex.zh: 她不愿讨论这部话剧的内容。

ex.en: Stricter controls were placed on the content of videos.
ex.zh: 对录像的内容有了更严格的控制。

e.en: The content of something such as an educational course or a programme of action is the elements that it consists of. (课程或计划的)

ex.en: Previous students have had nothing but praise for the course content and staff.
ex.zh: 以前的学生们对该课程的内容和教师只有称赞。

d: adj. 满足的，满意的，甘愿的
n. 目录；所含物，容纳的东西；（书、文章、演讲、电影等的）内容；含量；满足，满意；投赞成票的贵族院议员；网上信息，电子信息
v. 使满意，使满足
【名】 （Content）（法）孔唐（人名）

e.en: Porn is the same as .

ex.en: ...a porn cinema.
ex.zh: …色情影院。

d: n. 色情作品（同 pornography）；淫秽（或过度关注某话题）的电视节目（或书籍等）
adj. 色情（或淫秽）作品
【名】 （Porn）（泰、柬）蓬（人名）

e.en: Strangulation is the act of killing someone by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe. 勒死;

ex.en: He is charged with the strangulation of two students.
ex.zh: 他被指控勒死了两名学生。

d: n. 勒杀，扼死，勒颈；窒息；（医学）绞窄；钳制，扼制

e.en: You can refer to an event or a short period of time as an episode if you want to suggest that it is important or unusual, or has some particular quality. 事件;

ex.en: This episode is bound to be a deep embarrassment for Washington.
ex.zh: 这一事件必然使华盛顿大为尴尬。

e.en: An episode of something such as a series on television or a story in a magazine is one of the separate parts in which it is broadcast or published. (电视连续剧的) 集; (连载小说的)

ex.en: The final episode will be shown next Sunday.
ex.zh: 最后一集将于下周日播放。

d: n. 一段经历，一段时期；（电视剧或广播剧的）集，一集；疾病的发作，发病；插句，插段；（希腊悲剧中）两段合唱之间的部分

e.en: A weekly event or publication happens or appears once a week or every week. 一周一次的;

ex.en: Each course comprises 10-12 informal weekly meetings.
ex.zh: 每门课程包括10至12次每周1次的非正式见面会。

ex.en: We go and do the weekly shopping every Thursday.
ex.zh: 我们每星期四采购一次。

e.en: Weekly is also an adverb.

ex.en: The group meets weekly.
ex.zh: 小组每周见面一次。

e.en: Weekly quantities or rates relate to a period of one week.

ex.en: Of course, in addition to my weekly pay, I got a lot of tips.
ex.zh: 当然，除了周薪外，我还得到很多小费。

e.en: A weekly is a newspaper or magazine that is published once a week. 周报;

ex.en: Two of the four national daily papers are to become weeklies.
ex.zh: 4家全国性的日报中有2家要改为周报。

d: adj. 每周的，一周一次的；持续一周的，按周计算的；周刊的
n. 周报，周刊
adv. 每周，每星期

e.en: An algorithm is a series of mathematical steps, especially in a computer program, which will give you the answer to a particular kind of problem or question. (尤指计算机程序中的)

d: n. 算法（algorithm 的复数，亦译“算法式”）
n. 艾什，埃利什（人名）
n. 克莱尔（女子名）
n. 霍华德（男子名）

e.en: Incest is the crime of two members of the same family having sexual intercourse, such as a father and daughter, or a brother and sister.

ex.en: Oedipus, according to ancient Greek legend, killed his father and committed incest with his mother.
ex.zh: 据古希腊传说，俄狄浦斯杀死了父亲并与母亲乱伦。

d: n. 乱伦；近亲通婚

e.en: If you listen to someone who is talking or to a sound, you give your attention to them or it.

ex.en: He spent his time listening to the radio.
ex.zh: 他把时间花在了听收音机上。

e.en: 听者

ex.en: One or two listeners had fallen asleep while the president was speaking.
ex.zh: 总统讲话时，有一两个听众睡着了。

e.en: If you listen for a sound, you keep alert and are ready to hear it if it occurs.

ex.en: We listen for footsteps approaching.
ex.zh: 我们侧耳倾听脚步声靠近。

e.en: If you listen to someone, you do what they advise you to do, or you believe them.

ex.en: Anne, you need to listen to me this time.
ex.zh: 安妮，这次你要听我的。

d: v. 听，倾听；听从，听信；努力听，留神地听（listen for/listen out for）；听着
n. 听，倾听

e.en: Something that is problematic involves problems and difficulties.

ex.en: Some places are more problematic than others for women travelling alone.
ex.zh: 对独自旅行的妇女来说，有些地方比其他地方更容易出问题。

d: adj. 成问题的，有困难的；未确定的
n. 成问题之事

e.en: If there is a risk of something unpleasant, there is a possibility that it will happen.

ex.en: There is a small risk of brain damage from the procedure.
ex.zh: 存在该手术导致脑损伤的小风险。

e.en: If something that you do is a risk, it might have unpleasant or undesirable results.

ex.en: You're taking a big risk showing this to Kravis.
ex.zh: 你在冒很大的危险把这给克拉维斯看。

e.en: If you say that something or someone is a risk, you mean they are likely to cause harm.

ex.en: It's being obese that constitutes a health risk.
ex.zh: 是痴肥构成的健康风险。

e.en: If you are considered a good risk, a bank or shop thinks that it is safe to lend you money or let you have goods without paying for them at the time. (风险大或小的)

ex.en: Before providing the cash, they will have to decide whether you are a good or bad risk.
ex.zh: 提供资金之前，他们得确定你是风险小还是大的信贷对象。

d: n. 危险，风险；危险的人（或事物），隐患；（按风险大小评估的）被保险对象，受贷者；（保险业承保的）险；金融风险
v. 使遭受（失去、毁坏或伤害的）危险；冒......的危险，担......的风险；冒险做，（明知结果而）大胆做
【名】 （Risk）（英、阿拉伯）里斯克（人名）

e.en: The two sexes are the two groups, male and female, into which people and animals are divided according to the function they have in producing young. (雌、雄、男、女)

ex.en: ...a movie star who appeals to all ages and both sexes.
ex.zh: …一个吸引男女老少的电影明星。

e.en: The sex of a person or animal is their characteristic of being either male or female.

ex.en: She continually failed to gain promotion because of her sex.
ex.zh: 由于性别的原因，她频频得不到升职。

ex.en: The new technique has been used to identify the sex of fetuses.
ex.zh: 这项新技术已被用来鉴定胎儿的性别。

e.en: Sex is the physical activity by which people can produce young.

ex.en: He was very open in his attitudes about sex.
ex.zh: 他对性的态度很开放。

ex.en: The entire film revolves around drugs, sex and violence.
ex.zh: 整部电影都围绕着毒品、色情和暴力展开。

e.en: If two people have sex, they perform the act of sex.

ex.en: Have you ever thought about having sex with someone other than your husband?
ex.zh: 你想过与丈夫之外的人发生性关系吗？

d: n. 性行为，性交；性，性别；雄性，雌性；性器官（用于小说中避免更粗俗或更露骨的措词）
v. 辨别......的性别，辨识......的雌雄； 引起……的性欲

e.en: A searching question or look is intended to discover the truth about something. 探寻的 (问题、目光)

ex.en: They asked her some searching questions on moral philosophy and logic.
ex.zh: 他们就道德哲学和逻辑学问了她一些探寻性的问题。

d: adj. 搜索的；彻查的，透彻的；探寻性的（问题等）
v. 搜寻，查找；搜身，搜查；思索，细想（问题）；（在计算机或网络上）搜索（search 的现在分词）

e.en: Stern words or actions are very severe. (话语或行为)

ex.en: Mr. Monroe issued a stern warning to those who persist in violence.
ex.zh: 门罗先生向那些顽守暴力之徒发出严厉警告。

e.en: 严厉地

ex.en: "We will take the necessary steps," she said sternly.
ex.zh: “我们将采取必要措施，”她严厉地说道。

e.en: Someone who is stern is very serious and strict.

ex.en: Her father was stern and hard to please.
ex.zh: 她父亲苛刻，不易讨好。

e.en: the rear or after part of a vessel, opposite the bow or stem 船尾;

d: adj. （人或其态度）严厉的，认真的；（工作等）严峻的，棘手的；不屈从的，不动摇的
n. 船尾，艉部
【名】 （Stern）（英、以、法、瑞典、西）斯特恩（人名）

e.en: If you study, you spend time learning about a particular subject or subjects.

ex.en: ...a relaxed and happy atmosphere that will allow you to study to your full potential.
ex.zh: …一个将使你学习到充分发挥潜能的轻松又愉快的氛围。

ex.en: He studied History and Economics.
ex.zh: 他学过历史和经济学。

e.en: Study is the activity of studying.

ex.en: ...the use of maps and visual evidence in the study of local history.
ex.zh: …在当地历史的学习中地图和图像证据的使用。

e.en: A study of a subject is a piece of research on it.

ex.en: Recent studies suggest that as many as 5 in 1,000 new mothers are likely to have this problem.
ex.zh: 最近的研究表明，1000个新妈妈中有多达5个可能有这个问题。

e.en: You can refer to educational subjects or courses that contain several elements as studies of a particular kind.

ex.en: ...a centre for Islamic studies.
ex.zh: …一个伊斯兰教学科中心。

d: n. 研究；研究报告；学习；学业（study 的复数）；学科；课程；…研究（如 business studies、gender studies）
v. 学习；研究；仔细观察（study 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If someone is violent, or if they do something that is violent, they use physical force or weapons to hurt, injure, or kill other people.

ex.en: A quarter of current inmates have committed violent crimes.
ex.zh: 四分之一的在押囚犯实施过暴力犯罪。

ex.en: ...violent anti-government demonstrations.
ex.zh: …反政府的暴力示威。

e.en: 暴力地

ex.en: Some opposition activists have been violently attacked.
ex.zh: 一些反对派激进分子遭到了暴力袭击。

e.en: A violent event happens suddenly and with great force.

ex.en: A violent impact hurtled her forward.
ex.zh: 一股剧烈的冲击力将她猛地向前抛了出去。

e.en: 剧烈地

ex.en: A nearby volcano erupted violently, sending out a hail of molten rock and boiling mud.
ex.zh: 一座附近的火山猛烈爆发，喷出大量熔岩和沸腾的泥浆。

d: adj. 暴力的；（人）有暴力倾向的；含暴力行为的；剧烈的；（风、暴风雨或爆炸）强烈的，猛烈的；带有强烈愤怒情绪的，激烈的；（颜色的）鲜艳的

e.en: Written is the past participle of . (write)
A written test or piece of work is one that involves writing rather than doing something practical or giving spoken answers.

ex.en: ...knowledge that can be assessed in a short written test.
ex.zh: …用简短的书面测试可以评估的知识。

e.en: A written agreement, rule, or law has been officially written down. 正式写成的 (协议、规定、法律)

ex.en: The newspaper broke a written agreement not to sell certain photographs.
ex.zh: 该报纸违反了不出售某些摄影作品的书面协议。

d: adj. 书面的，（协议、规定、法律等）成文的，（测验、工作等）书面的
v. 书写；写作；写信（write 的过去分词形式）

e.en: Someone who is abusive behaves in a cruel and violent way toward other people.

ex.en: He became violent and abusive toward Ben's mother.
ex.zh: 他对待本的妈妈变得粗暴而又残酷。

e.en: Abusive language is extremely rude and insulting.

ex.en: I did not use any foul or abusive language.
ex.zh: 我没有使用过任何粗话或侮辱性的语言。

d: adj. 辱骂的，侮辱的；凌辱的，虐待的；受虐待的；舞弊的，不法的；滥用的

e.en: An abundance of something is a large quantity of it.

ex.en: This area of Mexico has an abundance of safe beaches and a pleasing climate.
ex.zh: 墨西哥的这个地区有大量的安全沙滩与宜人的气候。

d: n. 大量，丰富；繁荣，富裕；数量，丰度；（纸牌惠斯特用语）独得九墩

e.en: Someone who is addicted to a harmful drug cannot stop taking it. (吸食毒品)

ex.en: Many of the women are addicted to heroin and cocaine.
ex.zh: 这些妇女中的很多吸食海洛因和可卡因成瘾。

e.en: If you say that someone is addicted to something, you mean that they like it very much and want to spend as much time doing it as possible.

ex.en: She had become addicted to golf.
ex.zh: 她已经对高尔夫球入迷了。

d: adj. （吸毒）成瘾的，上瘾的；入迷的，着迷的
v. 使上瘾，使沉迷（addict 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: The appointment of a person to a particular job is the choice of that person to do it.

ex.en: His appointment to the cabinet would please the right wing.
ex.zh: 他进入内阁的任命会令右翼高兴。

e.en: An appointment is a job or position of responsibility. 职务;

ex.en: Mr. Fay is to take up an appointment as a researcher.
ex.zh: 费伊先生将担任研究员的职务。

e.en: If you have an appointment with someone, you have arranged to see them at a particular time, usually in connection with their work or for a serious purpose.

ex.en: She has an appointment with her accountant.
ex.zh: 她和她的会计师有个约会。

e.en: If something can be done by appointment, people can arrange in advance to do it at a particular time.

ex.en: Viewing is by appointment only.
ex.zh: 参观须预约。

d: n. 约会，约定；任命，委派；职务，职位；家具，陈设

e.en: If one group has an affiliation with another group, it has a close or official connection with it. 紧密联系;

ex.en: The kidnappers had no affiliation with any militant group.
ex.zh: 这些绑架者与任何军事组织都没有紧密联系。

d: n. 从属关系，隶属关系；联盟；所属机构，附属机构；加入（affiliation 的复数）

e.en: The benefit of something is the help that you get from it or the advantage that results from it. 益处;

ex.en: Each family farms individually and reaps the benefit of its labour.
ex.zh: 每个家庭独立耕作，收获各自的劳动成果。

ex.en: I'm a great believer in the benefits of this form of therapy.
ex.zh: 我对这种疗法的益处深信不疑。

e.en: If something is to your benefit or is of benefit to you, it helps you or improves your life.

ex.en: This could now work to Albania's benefit.
ex.zh: 这可能现在对阿尔巴尼亚有利。

e.en: If you benefit from something or if it benefits you, it helps you or improves your life. 有益于;

ex.en: Both sides have benefited from the talks.
ex.zh: 双方都从会谈中获益。

e.en: If you have the benefit of some information, knowledge, or equipment, you are able to use it so that you can achieve something.

ex.en: Steve didn't have the benefit of a formal college education.
ex.zh: 史蒂夫没有接受过正规大学教育的优势。

d: n. 好处，益处；救济金，补助金；额外奖励，保险金；慈善活动
v. 对（某人）有用，使受益；得益于，得利于

e.en: The base of something is its lowest edge or part. 底边;

ex.en: There was a bike path running along this side of the wall, right at its base.
ex.zh: 沿着墙的这一边，就在墙脚下，有一条自行车道。

e.en: The base of something is the lowest part of it, where it is attached to something else.

ex.en: The surgeon placed catheters through the veins and arteries near the base of the head.
ex.zh: 外科医生把导管插入靠近大脑底部附近的血管和动脉。

e.en: The base of an object such as a box or vase is the lower surface of it that touches the surface it rests on. (箱或瓶等器皿的)

ex.en: Remove from the heat and plunge the base of the pan into a bowl of very cold water.
ex.zh: 把烤盘从高温中取出，把盘的底部浸泡在一盆极冷的水中。

e.en: The base of an object that has several sections and that rests on a surface is the lower section of it.

ex.en: The mattress is best on a solid bed base.
ex.zh: 床垫最好放在结实的床座上。

d: n. 根基，底部；基础；基地；基础成分；（数字进位制中的）基数；（棒球）垒；碱，盐基；（晶体管的）基极；词根
v. 以……为基础；把基地设在……
adj. 卑鄙的，下流的；低劣的
【名】 （Base）（英、美、爱尔兰）马濑（人名）
n. 比利（女子名）

e.en: If something clicks or if you click it, it makes a short, sharp sound. 使发咔嚓声;

ex.en: The applause rose to a crescendo and cameras clicked.
ex.zh: 掌声越来越来响，照相机咔嚓咔嚓地响。

ex.en: He clicked off the radio.
ex.zh: 他咔嗒一声关上了收音机。

e.en: Click is also a noun.

ex.en: The telephone rang three times before I heard a click and then her recorded voice.
ex.zh: 电话响了3次后我听到了咔嗒一声响，然后是她的录音留言。

e.en: If you click on an area of a computer screen, you point the cursor at that area and press one of the buttons on the mouse in order to make something happen. (用鼠标)

ex.en: I clicked on a link and recent reviews of the production came up.
ex.zh: 我点击了一个链接，最近的演出评论就出来了。

ex.en: Click the link and see what happens.
ex.zh: 点击那个链接，看看会发生什么。

e.en: Click is also a noun.

ex.en: You can check your e-mail with a click of your mouse.
ex.zh: 通过鼠标的一点你就能查电子邮件。

d: v. 点击（click 的现在分词或动名词）；发出咔嗒声，滴答声，咔嚓声
n. 咔嗒声，滴答声，咔嚓声
adj. 发出咔嗒声的，咔嗒作响的

e.en: A boy is a child who will grow up to be a man.

ex.en: He was still just a boy.
ex.zh: 他还只是个男孩。

e.en: You can refer to a young man as a boy, especially when talking about relationships between boys and girls.

ex.en: ...the age when girls get interested in boys.
ex.zh: …女孩儿开始对小伙子感兴趣的年纪。

e.en: Someone's boy is their son.

ex.en: Eric was my cousin Edward's boy.
ex.zh: 埃里克是我堂兄爱德华的儿子。

e.en: You can refer to a man as a boy, especially when you are talking about him in an affectionate way.

ex.en: ...the local boy who made president.
ex.zh: …那个当上总统的本地小伙儿。

d: n. 男孩子们；小伙子们（boy 的复数）；（Boys）人名；（西）博伊斯；（法）布瓦；（英）博伊斯

e.en: If you consult an expert or someone senior to you or consult with them, you ask them for their opinion, advice, or permission.

ex.en: Consult your doctor about how much exercise you should get.
ex.zh: 咨询你的医生你应做多少运动。

ex.en: He needed to consult with an attorney.
ex.zh: 他需要和律师咨询。

e.en: If you consult a book or a map, you look in it or look at it in order to find some information.

ex.en: Consult the chart on page 44 for the correct cooking times.
ex.zh: 查阅第44页的图表找正确的烹调时间。

e.en: If a person or group of people consults with other people or consults them, or if two people or groups consult, they talk and exchange ideas and opinions about what they might decide to do.

ex.en: After consulting with her daughter and manager, she decided to take on the part, on her terms.
ex.zh: 同她的女儿兼经纪人商量之后，她决定按她的要求接受那个角色。

ex.en: The two countries will have to consult their allies.
ex.zh: 两国得同各自的盟友协商。

d: v. 咨询，请教；商量，商讨；查询，查阅；当顾问

e.en: If you are given credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

ex.en: The group can't get credit to buy farming machinery.
ex.zh: 该集团无法以赊购方式购买农业机械。

e.en: If you get the credit for something good, people praise you because you are responsible for it, or are thought to be responsible for it.

ex.en: We don't mind who gets the credit so long as we don't get the blame.
ex.zh: 只要我们不挨批评，谁受到表扬我们都不在乎。

ex.en: It would be wrong for us to take all the credit.
ex.zh: 我们把所有的功劳都揽到自己身上就不对了。

e.en: When a sum of money is credited to an account, the bank adds that sum of money to the total in the account.

ex.en: She noticed that only $80,000 had been credited to her account.
ex.zh: 她注意到只有$80000存入了她的账户。

ex.en: Midland decided to change the way it credited payments to accounts.
ex.zh: 米德兰公司决定改变将所付款项存入账户的方式。

e.en: If people credit someone with an achievement or if it is credited to them, people say or believe that they were responsible for it.

ex.en: The staff are crediting him with having saved Hythe's life.
ex.zh: 海斯能得救全体人员都归功于他。

ex.en: The 74-year-old mayor is credited with helping make Los Angeles the financial capital of the West Coast.
ex.zh: 74岁的市长被归功为帮助洛杉矶成为西海岸金融中心的人。

d: n. 学分（credit 的复数）；（金融）信用；信贷；贷方记录；（影视、唱片等作品的）演职员名单（the credits；含工作人员名单及片头或片尾字幕）；税收抵免或碳信用额
v. 相信；把…归因于，归功于；认为（某人）有（某种品质或能力）；将（钱款）记入账户贷方（均为 credit 的第三人称单数）

e.en: a youth who was taken into the household of Nebuchadnezzar, received guidance and apocalyptic visions from God, and was given divine protection when thrown into the lions' den 丹尼尔;
e.zh: 在尼布甲尼撒的家中，得到上帝保护和指引，并在被抛入狮穴时得到神护的青年

e.en: the book that recounts these experiences and visions (in full The Book of the Prophet Daniel) 《

d: n. 丹尼尔（男子名）；但以理（《圣经》中的先知）；《但以理书》（《旧约》经卷）

e.en: If you disclose new or secret information, you tell people about it.

ex.en: Neither side would disclose details of the transaction.
ex.zh: 双方都不会透露交易的细节。

d: vt. 揭露，透露，披露（disclose 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 已披露的；已公开的；显露出的

e.en: Disclosure is the act of giving people new or secret information.

ex.en: ...insufficient disclosure of negative information about the company.
ex.zh: …有关该公司负面信息的不充分公开。

d: n. 披露，泄密；透露的秘闻，公开的事情

e.en: The dollar is the unit of money used in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and some other countries. It is represented by the symbol $, the dollar sign. A dollar is divided into one hundred smaller units called cents. 元 (美国、加拿大、澳大利亚以及其他一些国家的货币单位)

ex.en: She gets paid seven dollars an hour.
ex.zh: 她的报酬是每小时7元。

e.en: The dollar is also used to refer to the American currency system.

ex.en: In early trading in Tokyo, the dollar fell sharply against the yen.
ex.zh: 在东京的早盘交易中，美元对日元的汇率急剧下跌。

d: n. 美元；元（美国、加拿大、澳大利亚等许多国家的货币单位，1 dollar = 100 cents）；一美元纸币或硬币；（比喻）金钱、商业主义或贪婪的象征；（Dollar）人名（英：多拉尔）
n. 达拉谟（英格兰一郡及其首府名）；一种产自该地的有短角肉牛

e.en: Someone who is engaged in a particular activity is doing that thing.

ex.en: ...the various projects he was engaged in.
ex.zh: …他从事过的不同项目。

e.en: When two people are engaged, they have agreed to marry each other.

ex.en: We got engaged on my eighteenth birthday.
ex.zh: 我们在我18岁生日那天订婚了。

e.en: If a telephone or a telephone line is engaged, it is already being used by someone else so that you are unable to speak to the person you are phoning.

ex.en: I tried to reach him, but the line was engaged.
ex.zh: 我试过联系他，但电话占线。

e.en: If a public toilet is engaged, it is already being used by someone else.

d: adj. 已订婚的；从事……的，忙于……的；电话占线的；（公用卫生间）被占用的；（圆柱）附墙的，部分砌在墙内的
v. 雇用，聘请；参加，从事；吸引，引起；与……交战，开战（engage 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 剥削，压榨；开发，开采；（出于私利、不公正的）利用

e.en: If something is free, you can have it or use it without paying for it.

ex.en: The seminars are free, with lunch provided.
ex.zh: 研讨会是免费的，还提供午餐。

e.en: Someone or something that is free is not restricted, controlled, or limited, for example, by rules, customs, or other people. 自由的;

ex.en: The government will be free to pursue its economic policies.
ex.zh: 政府将自由实行其经济政策。

ex.en: The elections were free and fair.
ex.zh: 选举是自由公正的。

e.en: 自由地

ex.en: They cast their votes freely and without coercion on election day.
ex.zh: 他们在选举日自由地投票，不受强迫。

e.en: Someone who is free is no longer a prisoner or a slave.

ex.en: He walked from the court house a free man.
ex.zh: 他走出法庭，重获自由。

d: adj. 免费的；自由的；随心所欲的；不含……的；免于，不遭受；空闲的；未使用的，空着的；无阻碍的；不拘泥于原文的；游离的；不吝惜的；干净整洁的；（风）顺的
adv. 自由地；免费地；帆脚索被松开地
v. 释放；使解脱出来；使免于；使可用于；使能腾出时间
n. 自由转会
