e.en: To harm a person or animal means to cause them physical injury, usually on purpose. (故意地)

ex.en: The hijackers seemed anxious not to harm anyone.
ex.zh: 劫机犯们似乎并不急于伤害任何人。

e.en: Harm is physical injury to a person or an animal which is usually caused on purpose. (故意的)

ex.en: All dogs are capable of doing harm to human beings.
ex.zh: 所有的狗都能对人造成伤害。

e.en: To harm a thing, or sometimes a person, means to damage them or make them less effective or successful than they were.

ex.en: ...a warning that the product may harm the environment.
ex.zh: …一则该产品可能会破坏环境的警告。

e.en: Harm is the damage to something which is caused by a particular course of action.

ex.en: The abuse of your powers does harm to all other officers who do their job properly.
ex.zh: 你滥用权力有损于所有其他好好工作的政府官员。

d: vt. 伤害；危害；损害（harm 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: You use hardly to modify a statement when you want to emphasize that it is only a small amount or detail which makes it true, and that therefore it is best to consider the opposite statement as being true.

ex.en: I hardly know you.
ex.zh: 我几乎不了解你。

ex.en: I've hardly slept in three days.
ex.zh: 我3天之中几乎没睡。

e.en: You use hardly in expressions such as hardly ever, hardly any, and hardly anyone to mean almost never, almost none, or almost no one. (后接)(ever)(,)(any)(,)(anyone)(等表示)

ex.en: We hardly ever eat fish.
ex.zh: 我们几乎从不吃鱼。

ex.en: Most of the others were so young they had hardly any experience.
ex.zh: 其他人中的大部分都太年轻，几乎没任何经验。

e.en: You use hardly before a negative statement in order to emphasize that something is usually true or usually happens. 几乎没有 (后接否定，表肯定)

ex.en: Hardly a day goes by without a visit from someone.
ex.zh: 几乎没有哪一天没有来访者。

e.en: When you say you can hardly do something, you are emphasizing that it is very difficult for you to do it.

ex.en: My garden was covered with so many butterflies that I could hardly see the flowers.
ex.zh: 我的花园里飞满了太多的蝴蝶，我几乎看不到花了。

d: adv. 几乎不，几乎没有；刚刚，才；几乎无法；差不多，大约；严厉的，苛刻的

e.en: a small asexual reproductive structure in liverworts, mosses, etc, that becomes detached from the parent and develops into a new individual

d: n. （生物）胞芽，芽孢

e.en: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount. 使增加;

ex.en: The population continues to increase.
ex.zh: 人口持续增长。

ex.en: Japan's industrial output increased by 2%.
ex.zh: 日本的工业产量增长了2%。

e.en: If there is an increase in the number, level, or amount of something, it becomes greater.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in productivity.
ex.zh: …生产率的急速增长。

e.en: If something is on the increase, it is happening more often or becoming greater in number or intensity.

ex.en: Crime is on the increase.
ex.zh: 犯罪活动日益猖獗。

d: v. 增长，增强，增大（increase 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 增加的，增多的，增强的

e.en: Something or someone that is huge is extremely large in size. (尺寸)

ex.en: ...a tiny little woman with huge black glasses.
ex.zh: …一位个子很小的戴着硕大黑色眼镜的女人。

e.en: Something that is huge is extremely large in amount or degree. (数量或程度)

ex.en: I have a huge number of ties because I never throw them away.
ex.zh: 我有非常多的领带，因为我从不扔掉它们。

e.en: (数量或程度)

ex.en: In summer this hotel is a hugely popular venue for wedding receptions.
ex.zh: 夏天，这家饭店是非常受欢迎的婚宴场所。

e.en: Something that is huge exists or happens on a very large scale, and involves a lot of different people or things. (规模上)

ex.en: Another team is looking at the huge problem of debts between companies.
ex.zh: 另一组人正在研究公司间债务这个大问题。

d: adj. 庞大的，极大的；很受欢迎的，著名的
【名】 （Huge）（英）休奇（人名）

e.en: Instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

ex.en: I didn't have as strong a maternal instinct as some other mothers.
ex.zh: 我不像其他一些母亲那样有那么强烈的母性本能。

e.en: If you have an instinct for something, you are naturally good at it or able to do it.

ex.en: He seems to have an instinct for smart advertising and marketing.
ex.zh: 他好像在广告和营销方面有天分。

e.en: If it is your instinct to do something, you feel that it is right to do it.

ex.en: I should've gone with my first instinct, which was not to do the interview.
ex.zh: 我应该凭我的本能反应行事，那就是，不去面试。

e.en: Instinct is a feeling, rather than an opinion or idea based on facts, that something is the case.

ex.en: There is scientific evidence to support our instinct that being surrounded by plants is good for health.
ex.zh: 有科学证据表明我们的直觉是正确的，即被植物环绕着有益健康。

d: n. 本能，天性；直觉，本能的反应

e.en: a greyish-yellow colour
(as adjective) 灰黄色的 (See also Isabelline)

ex.en: an Isabella mohair coat

d: n. 伊莎贝拉（意、英女子名，常大写为 Isabella；亦作 Isabel）；灰黄色，浅黄褐色
adj. 灰黄色的（亦作 Isabel）

e.en: in Britain Independent Television (英国)

d: abbr. （英）独立电视台（Independent Television）；工业电视（Industrial Television）；教学电视（Instructional Television）

e.en: A list of things such as names or addresses is a set of them which all belong to a particular category, written down one below the other.

ex.en: We are making a list of the top ten men we would not want to be married to.
ex.zh: 我们正在列一个我们最不想嫁的10种男人的名单。

ex.en: There were six names on the list.
ex.zh: 单子上有6个名字。

e.en: A list of things is a set of them that you think of as being in a particular order. (按一定顺序排列的)

ex.en: High on the list of public demands is to end military control of broadcasting.
ex.zh: 高居公众要求事项前列的是结束对广播的军事控制。

ex.en: The criminal judicial system always comes up at the top of the list of voters' concerns in focus groups.
ex.zh: 刑事司法制度总是出现在焦点小组中投票者关注事项之首。

e.en: To list several things such as reasons or names means to write or say them one after another, usually in a particular order.

ex.en: The pupils were asked to list the sports they loved most and hated most.
ex.zh: 学生们被要求列出他们最喜欢的和最讨厌的运动。

e.en: To list something in a particular way means to include it in that way in a list or report. 把…列入 (表、报告)

ex.en: A medical examiner has listed the deaths as homicides.
ex.zh: 验尸官已将这些死亡列为他杀案件。

d: adj. （建筑）列入文物保护名录的；与（伦敦）股票交易所主板市场（有关）的；上市的；在表列的，已登录的
v. 列出（list 的过去式和过去分词）；登记

e.en: A material is a solid substance.

ex.en: ...electrons in a conducting material such as a metal.
ex.zh: …金属等导电物质中的电子。

e.en: Material is cloth.

ex.en: ...the thick material of her skirt.
ex.zh: …她裙子的厚布料。

e.en: Materials are the things that you need for a particular activity.

ex.en: The builders ran out of materials.
ex.zh: 建筑商用完了材料。

e.en: Ideas or information that are used as a basis for a book, play, or film can be referred to as material.

ex.en: In my version of the story, I added some new material.
ex.zh: 在我这个版本的故事中，我添加了一些新素材。

d: n. 衣料，布料；材料，原料；素材；节目，剧目；（有指明特征的）人才；（某一活动所需的）材料
adj. 物质的，非精神上的；重要的，需予以考虑的；和推理内容有关的
【名】 （Material）（美、意）妈特力娅丽（人名）
n. （McGhee）人名；（英）麦吉

e.en: People, activities, or ideas that are part of the mainstream are regarded as the most typical, normal, and conventional because they belong to the same group or system as most others of their kind.

ex.en: ...people outside the economic mainstream.
ex.zh: …经济主流之外的人们。

d: n. 主流
adj. 主流的；（学校，班级）为无特殊需求学生开设的，普通的
v. 使主流化，使成为主流；（把有特殊教育需求的孩子）编入普通班级

e.en: Misogynistic means the same as . 同misogynist

d: adj. 厌恶女人的，歧视女性的

e.en: A model of an object is a physical representation that shows what it looks like or how it works. The model is often smaller than the object it represents.

ex.en: ...an architect's model of a wooden house.
ex.zh: …一名建筑师的木屋模型。

ex.en: I made a model out of paper and glue.
ex.zh: 我用纸和胶水做了一个模型。

e.en: Model is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...a model railway.
ex.zh: …一个铁路模型。

e.en: A model is a system that is being used and that people might want to copy in order to achieve similar results.

ex.en: ...the Chinese model of economic reform.
ex.zh: …中国经济改革的模式。

e.en: A model of a system or process is a theoretical description that can help you understand how the system or process works, or how it might work.

ex.en: Darwin eventually put forward a model of biological evolution.
ex.zh: 达尔文最终提出了一套生物进化的理论模式。

d: n. 模型；模式；（机器等的）型号；模范，典型；模特儿；样本，范例；（小说中人物或地点的）原型；（著名设计师设计的）款式
v. （为艺术家）当模特儿；模特儿展示（服装）；（用黏土、木头等）做……的模型，塑造；（用计算机）做出（情景、事件）的模型；使仿效，使模仿
adj. 模范的，榜样的；模型的
【名】 （Model）（英、德、俄）莫德尔 (人名)

e.en: If two substances mix or if you mix one substance with another, you stir or shake them together, or combine them in some other way, so that they become a single substance.

ex.en: Oil and water don't mix.
ex.zh: 油与水无法混合。

ex.en: A quick stir will mix them thoroughly.
ex.zh: 快速搅拌会使它们完全混合。

e.en: If you mix something, you prepare it by mixing other things together.

ex.en: He had spent several hours mixing cement.
ex.zh: 他用了几个小时的时间来搅拌水泥。

e.en: A mix is a powder containing all the substances that you need in order to make something such as a cake or a sauce. When you want to use it, you add liquid. (制作蛋糕或调味汁等的)

ex.en: For speed we used packets of pizza dough mix.
ex.zh: 为了赶速度，我们用了几包做比萨饼的混合面粉。

e.en: A mix of different things or people is two or more of them together.

ex.en: The story is a magical mix of fantasy and reality.
ex.zh: 这个故事是一个幻想与现实的奇妙组合。

d: v. mix 的现在分词：（使）混合；（使）相结合；搅拌；（不同物质或事物）能相混合，相容；配制，调制；交往；混音，混录，混成（声音信号）
n. mix 的动名词：混合；混音，混录
数百万

e.en: Music is the pattern of sounds produced by people singing or playing instruments.

ex.en: ...classical music.
ex.zh: …古典音乐。

e.en: Music is the art of creating or performing music. 音乐创作;

ex.en: He went on to study music, specializing in the clarinet.
ex.zh: 他继续学习音乐，专攻单簧管。

e.en: Music is the symbols written on paper which represent musical sounds.

ex.en: He's never been able to read music.
ex.zh: 他从来就不识乐谱。

e.en: If something that you hear is music to your ears, it makes you feel very happy.

ex.en: Popular support – it's music to the ears of any politician.
ex.zh: 公众的支持–这对任何政客都是佳音。

d: n. 音乐，乐曲；乐谱；悦耳的声音；音乐（学），音乐创作（或演奏）技能

e.en: A speaker or writer uses myself to refer to himself or herself. Myself is used as the object of a verb or preposition when the subject refers to the same person.

ex.en: I asked myself what I would have done in such a situation.
ex.zh: 我问过自己在这样一种情况下我会做什么。

e.en: You use myself to emphasize a first person singular subject. In more formal English, myself is sometimes used instead of "me" as the object of a verb or preposition, for emphasis. 我自己 (用于强调第一人称单数主语)

ex.en: I myself enjoy movies, poetry, eating out, and long walks.
ex.zh: 我本人喜欢电影、诗歌、外出就餐和远足。

e.en: If you say something such as "I did it myself," you are emphasizing that you did it, rather than anyone else.

ex.en: "Where did you get that embroidery?"—"I made it myself."
ex.zh: “你从哪儿得到那件刺绣的？”“我自己做的。”

d: pron. 我自己（反身代词，作动词或介词宾语）；我本人，我亲自（用于强调）；我的正常健康状况或正常情绪（用于 be/feel (not) myself 等）；by myself 独自一人；独立完成

e.en: If you say that something is not necessarily the case, you mean that it may not be the case or is not always the case.

ex.en: Anger is not necessarily the most useful or acceptable reaction to such events.
ex.zh: 生气未必是对待此类事件最有用或最适合的反应。

e.en: If you reply "Not necessarily," you mean that what has just been said or suggested may not be true.

ex.en: "He was lying, of course."—"Not necessarily."
ex.zh: “他当然是在撒谎。”—“不一定。”

e.en: If you say that something necessarily happens or is the case, you mean that it has to happen or be the case and cannot be any different.

ex.en: Brookman & Langdon were said to manufacture the most desirable pens and these necessarily command astonishingly high prices.
ex.zh: 据说布鲁克曼兰登公司制造的钢笔最令人满意，而这必然地导致高得惊人的价格。

d: adv. 必定，必然；必要地
n．Neeta是一个印度女性名字，来源于梵文，意为“有规律的”或“有秩序的”。
n. 新闻剪辑：指从不同的新闻源收集和编辑的短视频或音频片段。

e.en: A nightmare is a very frightening dream.

ex.en: All the victims still suffered nightmares.
ex.zh: 所有的受害者仍为恶梦所扰。

e.en: If you refer to a situation as a nightmare, you mean that it is very frightening and unpleasant. 噩梦 (指可怕处境)

ex.en: The years in prison were a nightmare.
ex.zh: 数年的铁窗生涯是一场噩梦。

e.en: If you refer to a situation as a nightmare, you are saying in a very emphatic way that it is irritating because it causes you a lot of trouble. 噩梦 (指恼人的情况)

ex.en: Taking my son Peter to a restaurant was a nightmare.
ex.zh: 带我儿子彼得去饭店吃饭真是一场噩梦。

d: n. 梦魇，恶梦（nightmare 的复数形式）；令人恐惧、不快或烦恼的经历或处境

e.en: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

ex.en: He opened the window and looked out.
ex.zh: 他打开窗户往外看。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open window.
ex.zh: …一扇开着的窗户。

e.en: If you open something such as a bottle, box, parcel, or envelope, you move, remove, or cut part of it so you can take out what is inside.

ex.en: I opened the letter.
ex.zh: 我拆开了那封信。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open bottle of milk.
ex.zh: …一瓶打开的牛奶。

d: v. open 的过去式和过去分词形式：打开，开启，张开，睁开；开始，开业，开通，开放等
adj. 开着的，打开的；已开封的；已开通或已开放的
v. （使）正常化；废止种族隔离；（使）正规化；（浮点表示法）使用标准格式表示；（使）邦交正常化（normalise 的现在分词，normalise 等于 normalize）
n. 组织，团体，机构（英国英语拼法，等于 organization）；组织，筹备，安排；条理，系统性

e.en: A platform is a flat raised structure, usually made of wood, that people stand on when they make speeches or give a performance. 讲台;

ex.en: Nick finished what he was saying and jumped down from the platform.
ex.zh: 尼克讲完话，从讲台上跳了下来。

e.en: A platform is a flat raised structure or area, usually one that something can stand on or land on. (用于放置物品或着陆的)

ex.en: They found a spot on a rocky platform where they could pitch their tents.
ex.zh: 他们在一个岩石平台上找到了一处可以搭帐篷的地方。

e.en: A platform is a structure built for people to work and live on when drilling for oil or gas at sea, or when extracting it. (在海上为钻探石油或天然气而建的)

ex.en: The platform began to produce oil in 1994.
ex.zh: 1994年，这个钻井平台开始产油。

e.en: A platform in a train or subway station is the area beside the tracks where you wait for or get off a train. (火车或地铁站的)

ex.en: The train was about to leave and I was not even on the platform.
ex.zh: 火车就要开了，而我甚至还没有赶到站台上。

d: n. 平台；讲台，舞台；讲台上的人（the platform）；（火车站的）月台；（公共汽车上供乘客上下车的）踏脚台；发言机会，论坛；契机；（政党的）纲领；厚底鞋；计算机平台；（海上）钻井平台；（供人上下小船的）水上平台；（火箭或导弹的）卫星发射平台

e.en: You use particularly to indicate that what you are saying applies especially to one thing or situation.

ex.en: Keep your office space looking good, particularly your desk.
ex.zh: 保持你办公的地方整洁美观，特别是办公桌。

ex.en: More local employment will be created, particularly in service industries.
ex.zh: 更多的面向当地的就业将被创造出来，尤其是在服务业。

e.en: Particularly means more than usual or more than other things. 格外;

ex.en: Progress has been particularly disappointing.
ex.zh: 进展一直格外令人失望。

d: adv. 非常，尤其；特别是；清楚地，明确地

e.en: A platform is a flat raised structure, usually made of wood, that people stand on when they make speeches or give a performance. 讲台;

ex.en: Nick finished what he was saying and jumped down from the platform.
ex.zh: 尼克讲完话，从讲台上跳了下来。

e.en: A platform is a flat raised structure or area, usually one that something can stand on or land on. (用于放置物品或着陆的)

ex.en: They found a spot on a rocky platform where they could pitch their tents.
ex.zh: 他们在一个岩石平台上找到了一处可以搭帐篷的地方。

e.en: A platform is a structure built for people to work and live on when drilling for oil or gas at sea, or when extracting it. (在海上为钻探石油或天然气而建的)

ex.en: The platform began to produce oil in 1994.
ex.zh: 1994年，这个钻井平台开始产油。

e.en: A platform in a train or subway station is the area beside the tracks where you wait for or get off a train. (火车或地铁站的)

ex.en: The train was about to leave and I was not even on the platform.
ex.zh: 火车就要开了，而我甚至还没有赶到站台上。

d: n. （platform 的复数）平台，讲台，舞台；站台，月台；（计算机、互联网、商业、矿业等）平台；（海上石油、天然气开采的）钻井平台；党纲，施政纲领；发表意见的机会；厚底鞋，松糕鞋
v. （platform 的第三人称单数）把……放在台上；在台上演讲
n. 播客（podcast 的复数形式）
v. 制作并发布播客（podcast 的第三人称单数现在时形式）
v. （使）两极化；（使）偏振；（使）极化（polarise 的现在分词，polarise 等于 polarize）
adj. 造成（舆论或人群）两极分化的；极具争议的

e.en: To produce something means to cause it to happen.

ex.en: The drug is known to produce side-effects in women.
ex.zh: 众所周知，这种药会在女性身上产生各种副作用。

e.en: If you produce something, you make or create it.

ex.en: The company produced circuitry for communications systems.
ex.zh: 这家公司为通讯系统生产电路系统。

e.en: When things or people produce something, it comes from them or slowly forms from them, especially as the result of a biological or chemical process. 生长出;

ex.en: These plants are then pollinated and allowed to mature and produce seed.
ex.zh: 这些植物之后被授粉，使其成熟、结籽。

e.en: If you produce evidence or an argument, you show it or explain it to people in order to make them agree with you. 给出 (证据、论据等)

ex.en: They challenged him to produce evidence to support his allegations.
ex.zh: 他们要求他给出证据来支撑他的断言。

d: v. produce 的过去式和过去分词：引起，造成；（自然地）生产，产生；（尤指用机器）生产，制造；制作，创作，出品；出示，拿出，提出
adj. 由……产生的/造成的；经生产/制造而成的（常作后置定语或表语）

e.en: If you are in possession of something, you have it, because you have obtained it or because it belongs to you.

ex.en: Those documents are now in the possession of the Washington Post.
ex.zh: 那些文件现在归《华盛顿邮报》所有。

ex.en: He was also charged with illegal possession of firearms.
ex.zh: 他还被指控非法拥有火器。

e.en: Your possessions are the things that you own or have with you at a particular time. 财产;

ex.en: People had lost their homes and all their possessions.
ex.zh: 人们已失去了家园和所有的财产。

d: n.  拥有，持有；个人财产，所有物；持有违禁物，私藏毒品（或武器）；（对球的）控制，球权；进攻；领地，殖民地；鬼魂附体，着魔；（观点或情感的）支配，控制

e.en: The publication of a book or magazine is the act of printing it and sending it to stores to be sold.

ex.en: The guide is being translated into several languages for publication near Christmas.
ex.zh: 这本指南正被翻译成好几种语言，准备在圣诞节前后出版。

e.en: A publication is a book or magazine that has been published.

ex.en: They have started legal proceedings against two publications which spoke of an affair.
ex.zh: 他们已开始对提及一件绯闻的两本出版物进行法律诉讼。

e.en: The publication of something such as information is the act of making it known to the public, for example, by informing journalists or by publishing a government document.

ex.en: A spokesman said: "We have no comment regarding the publication of these photographs."
ex.zh: 一位发言人说: “关于这些照片的公开，我们无可奉告。”

d: n. 出版，发行；出版物，发行物；（信息的） 刊登，公布

e.en: If you say that someone is pushing a particular age, you mean that they are nearly that age. 接近(某个年龄)

ex.en: Pushing 40, he was an aging rock star.
ex.zh: 快40岁的他是个慢慢老去的摇滚明星。

d: prep. 接近（某个年龄）
adj. 奋斗的，富有进取心的；莽撞的
v. 推，推动；按下（按钮、开关等）；鼓励，逼迫（push 的现在分词）

e.en: If you describe people, things, or behaviour as racist, you mean that they are influenced by the belief that some people are inferior because they belong to a particular race.

ex.en: You have to acknowledge that we live in a racist society.
ex.zh: 你不得不承认我们生活在一个有种族歧视的社会。

e.en: A racist is someone who is racist.

ex.en: He has a hard core of support among white racists.
ex.zh: 他得到了白人种族主义分子强有力的支持。

d: n. 种族主义者
adj. 种族主义的

e.en: When you receive something, you get it after someone gives it to you or sends it to you. 接到;

ex.en: They will receive their awards at a ceremony in Stockholm.
ex.zh: 他们将在斯德哥尔摩的典礼上接受给他们的奖励。

e.en: You can use receive to say that certain kinds of things happen to someone. For example if they are injured, you can say that they received an injury. 受到;

ex.en: He received more of the blame than anyone when the plan failed to work.
ex.zh: 当计划失败之后他受到的指责比任何人都多。

e.en: When you receive a visitor or a guest, you greet them. 接待;

ex.en: The following evening the hotel was again receiving guests.
ex.zh: 第二天晚上饭店又接待起客人来。

e.en: If you say that something is received in a particular way, you mean that people react to it in that way. (用某种特定方式)

ex.en: The resolution had been received with great disappointment within the PLO.
ex.zh: 巴勒斯坦解放组织内部对此决议感到极其失望。

d: v. 得到，收到；遭受，经受（特定待遇）；对……作出反应；接待，招待；接收（某人为成员）；接收，收听（信号）；（通过无线电）听到；购买，窝藏（赃物）；接（球）；领受（圣餐面包或葡萄酒）；接受（治疗）；形成（看法，印象）；容纳，承接

e.en: If something rises, it moves upward. 上升;

ex.en: Wilson's ice-cold eyes watched the smoke rise from his cigarette.
ex.zh: 威尔逊那双冰冷的眼睛注视着烟雾从他的香烟中冒出。

e.en: Rise up means the same as . 上升;

ex.en: Spray rose up from the surface of the water.
ex.zh: 水花从水面上溅起来。

e.en: When you rise, you stand up.

ex.en: Luther rose slowly from the chair.
ex.zh: 卢瑟慢慢从椅子上站起身来。

e.en: Rise up means the same as .

ex.en: The only thing I wanted was to rise up from the table and leave this house.
ex.zh: 我惟一想做的是从餐桌旁站起身来，离开这所房子。

d: v. （数字、 数量、价值）增加；升高，上升；起身，站起；（权力或地位）提高；耸立，隆起；（声音）变响，变大；（太阳、月亮）升起；（感情或情绪） 变得强烈；（面包、蛋糕等）发酵；起床；复活，再生；休会，休庭；（风力）加强，增强；（河流）发源；起义，反抗；脸红，涨红；（毛发）竖起；（胃）感到恶心；接近（某个年龄）
n. （数量或水平的）增加，改善；加薪；（地位的）升高，增强；上升，升起；小山丘，斜坡；（声音或声调的）提高；源头，起源；兴起，高涨

e.en: Rich Site Summary: a way of allowing web users to receive news headlines and updates on their browser from selected websites as soon as they are published
(as modifier)

ex.en: an RSS newsfeed

d: abbr. 和的平方根（root-sum square）；英国皇家学会会员（Regiae Societatis Socius，等于 Fellow of the Royal Society）；残差平方和（residual sum of squares）；简易信息聚合（really simple syndication）；网站聚合内容摘要（Rich Site Summary）
abbr. （法）有限责任公司（Société à responsabilité limitée）
n. （Sarl）人名；（土）萨勒

e.en: You use seem to say that someone or something gives the impression of having a particular quality, or of happening in the way you describe. 似乎;

ex.en: The explosions seemed quite close by.
ex.zh: 爆炸似乎就在近旁。

ex.en: To everyone who knew them, they seemed an ideal couple.
ex.zh: 在每个认识他们的人看来，他们似乎是一对佳偶。

e.en: You use seem when you are describing your own feelings or thoughts, or describing something that has happened to you, in order to make your statement less forceful.

ex.en: I seem to have lost all my self-confidence.
ex.zh: 我好像已经丧失了所有的自信。

ex.en: I seem to remember giving you very precise instructions.
ex.zh: 我好像记得曾给过你非常明确的指示。

e.en: If you say that you cannot seem or could not seem to do something, you mean that you have tried to do it and were unable to.

ex.en: No matter how hard I try I cannot seem to catch up on all the bills.
ex.zh: 不管我怎么努力，我好像总也无法付清所有的账单。

d: v. seem 的第三人称单数现在时形式：似乎，好像，看起来，表示凭外表或感觉得出的印象，但不一定是事实；用于 it seems that/as if/like 等句型时表示“看来，好像”；用于委婉陈述自己的感受或经历时表示“感觉好像”；也用于 cannot/could not seem to do sth，表示“好像总也无法做到”。
n. （美、以、埃）塞莫（人名）

e.en: When you send someone something, you arrange for it to be taken and delivered to them, for example, by mail. 邮寄;

ex.en: Myra Cunningham sent me a note thanking me for dinner.
ex.zh: 迈拉·坎宁安寄给了我一封短信，感谢我请她吃饭。

ex.en: I sent a copy to the school principal.
ex.zh: 我寄了一份复印件给校长。

e.en: If you send someone somewhere, you tell them to go there. 派遣;

ex.en: Inspector Banbury came up to see her, but she sent him away.
ex.zh: 班伯里警官过来看她，但她却把他打发走了。

ex.en: ...the government's decision to send troops to the region.
ex.zh: …政府向该地区派遣军队的决定。

e.en: If you send someone to an institution such as a school or a prison, you arrange for them to stay there for a period of time. 把…送进 (学校、监狱等)

ex.en: It's his parents' choice to send him to a boarding school, rather than a convenient day school.
ex.zh: 把他送到寄宿学校而不是去附近的走读学校，是他父母的决定。

e.en: To send a signal means to cause it to go to a place by means of radio waves or electricity. (通过电波或电) 发送 (信号)

ex.en: The transmitters will send a signal automatically to a local base station.
ex.zh: 发射台会自动将信号发送到地方基站。

d: vt. 发送（send 第三人称单数）；派遣，打发；使（向某方向）移动；使进入（某种状态）

e.en: The shape of an object, a person, or an area is the appearance of their outside edges or surfaces, for example, whether they are round, square, curved, or fat. 外形;

ex.en: Each mirror is made to order and can be designed to almost any shape or size.
ex.zh: 每面镜子都是定制做的，而且能设计成几乎任何形状或规格。

ex.en: ...little pens in the shape of baseball bats.
ex.zh: …棒球球棒形状的小钢笔。

e.en: You can refer to something that you can see as a shape if you cannot see it clearly, or if its outline is the clearest or most striking aspect of it. (模糊的)

ex.en: The great grey shape of a tank rolled out of the village.
ex.zh: 一个坦克状的巨大灰影从村子里开了出来。

e.en: A shape is a space enclosed by an outline, for example, a circle, a square, or a triangle.

ex.en: Imagine a sort of a kidney shape.
ex.zh: 想像一种类似肾脏的形状。

e.en: The shape of something that is planned or organized is its structure and character. (计划或组织的)

ex.en: The last two weeks have seen a lot of talk about the future shape of Europe.
ex.zh: 在过去的两周里有许多关于欧洲的未来格局的讨论。

d: n. 塑造；成形
adj. 塑造的，成形的
v. 塑造（shape 的 ing 形式）；（使）成形

e.en: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment. 股份;

ex.en: People in China are eager to buy shares in new businesses.
ex.zh: 中国民众热衷于购买新企业的股票。

e.en: If you share something with another person, you both have it, use it, or occupy it. You can also say that two people share something. 共有; 共用;

ex.en: ...the small income he had shared with his brother from his father's estate.
ex.zh: …他和他兄弟分享从他父亲的地产中得来的一小笔收入。

ex.en: Two Americans will share this year's Nobel Prize for Medicine.
ex.zh: 两位美国人将共同摘得今年的诺贝尔医学奖。

e.en: If you share a task, duty, or responsibility with someone, you each carry out or accept part of it. You can also say that two people share something. 共同承担;

ex.en: You can find out whether they are prepared to share the cost of the flowers with you.
ex.zh: 你会发现他们是否准备与你分摊鲜花的费用。

e.en: If you share an experience with someone, you have the same experience, often because you are with them at the time. You can also say that two people share something. 共享 (经历)

ex.en: Yes, I want to share my life with you.
ex.zh: 是的，我想和你共享生活。

d: n. （金融）股份，股票；一份，份额（share 的复数形式）
v. 分享，共享，共有；分担，分配（share 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: You can say that something is shocking if you think that it is very bad.

ex.en: The media coverage was shocking.
ex.zh: 媒体的报道糟透了。

e.en: 极坏地

ex.en: His memory was becoming shockingly bad.
ex.zh: 他的记忆力正变得很糟。

e.en: You can say that something is shocking if you think that it is morally wrong. 令人震惊的;

ex.en: It is shocking that nothing was said.
ex.zh: 令人震惊的是，什么都没说。

e.en: 令人震惊地;

ex.en: Shockingly, this useless and dangerous surgery did not end until the 1930s.
ex.zh: 令人震惊地，这种毫无作用又危险的外科手术直到20世纪30年代才结束。

d: adj. 令人震惊的；骇人听闻的，令人愤慨的，令人厌恶的；糟糕的，极坏的
v. shock 的现在分词/动名词，表示使震惊、震动、感到震惊等

e.en: A singer is a person who sings, especially as a job. 歌手;

ex.en: My mother was a singer in a dance band.
ex.zh: 我妈妈是一个舞蹈团的歌手。

d: n. 歌手，歌唱家；Singer（英语姓氏或人名，译名有“桑热”，常见“辛格”）

e.en: Society is people in general, thought of as a large organized group. 社会 (指社会中所有的人)

ex.en: This reflects attitudes and values prevailing in society.
ex.zh: 这反映出社会上普遍流行的态度和价值观。

e.en: A society is the people who live in a country or region, their organizations, and their way of life. 社会; (生活于某个地区、有自己生活方式的)

ex.en: We live in a capitalist society.
ex.zh: 我们生活在资本主义社会。

e.en: A society is an organization for people who have the same interest or aim. 社团;

ex.en: ...the Atlanta Horticultural Society.
ex.zh: …亚特兰大园艺协会。

e.en: Society is the rich, fashionable people in a particular place who meet on social occasions.

ex.en: The couple quickly became a fixture in society.
ex.zh: 这对夫妇很快就成为上流社会的常客。

d: n. 社会（以群体形式生活在一起的人的总称）；社群（某国家、地区、时期等的群体组织）；社团，协会；上层社会；交往，相伴；阶层，界；植物的群落，动物的群体
n. 底特律（美国一座城市）

e.en: A crown is a circular ornament, usually made of gold and jewels, which a king or queen wears on their head at official ceremonies. You can also use crown to refer to anything circular that is worn on someone's head. 王冠;

ex.en: ...a crown of flowers.
ex.zh: …一个花冠。

e.en: Your crown is the top part of your head, at the back.

ex.en: He laid his hand gently on the crown of her head.
ex.zh: 他把手轻轻地放在她的头顶后部。

e.en: A crown is an artificial top piece fixed over a broken or decayed tooth.

ex.en: How long does it take to have crowns fitted?
ex.zh: 镶齿冠需要多长时间？

e.en: The government of a country that has a king or queen is sometimes referred to as the Crown.

ex.en: She says the sovereignty of the Crown must be preserved.
ex.zh: 她说君主政权必须予以保留。

ex.en: ...a minister of the Crown.
ex.zh: …王国政府的一位大臣。

d: n. 王冠，冕；王位，王权（the crown）；王国政府，王国（the Crown）；冠军宝座，桂冠；头顶，帽顶；顶部；5先令的英国旧币；（受损牙齿的）人造冠
v. 为……加冕，立……为王；形成……顶部，给……加顶；使圆满，使完美；（在牙齿上）镶人造冠；打……的头部；（分娩时胎儿的头）露顶
【名】 （Crown）（英）克朗（人名）
n. 街区，社区（城镇中人们居住的地区）；附近，邻近地区；街坊，邻里（居住在同一地区的人们）；接近，大约（用于 in the neighborhood of，表示数量、价格等的约数）；邻域（数学、计算机科学中指一点附近的点集）
n. 克隆那斯（等于 Cronus）；二氧化钛

e.en: A plant is a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.

ex.en: Water each plant as often as required.
ex.zh: 按要求经常给每棵植物浇水。

e.en: When you plant a seed, plant, or young tree, you put it into the ground so that it will grow there.

ex.en: He says he plans to plant fruit trees and vegetables.
ex.zh: 他说他计划栽种果树和蔬菜。

e.en: 栽种

ex.en: Extensive flooding in the country has delayed planting and many crops are still under water.
ex.zh: 该国大范围的洪水已经延误了栽种，许多庄稼现在还泡在水中。

e.en: When someone plants land with a particular type of plant or crop, they put plants, seeds, or young trees into the land to grow them there. 将 (土地) 种植 (植被)

ex.en: They plan to plant the area with grass and trees.
ex.zh: 他们计划在这个地区植树种草。

ex.en: Recently much of their energy has gone into planting a large vegetable garden.
ex.zh: 最近，他们的大部分精力已经花在种植一个大型蔬菜园上。

d: n. 植物；工厂，发电厂；房屋，设施；重型机械，机械设备；栽赃物品；密探，卧底；（斯诺克）击接触球犯规
v. 栽种，种植；灌输（思想）；栽赃；安放（炸弹），（秘密）放置；安插（眼线、密探等）；把……牢牢插进，稳固地放置……；（通常出于不可告人的目的）发布，散布；移栽，移植（室外）；埋葬（人）；创建，建立（殖民地，城市，社区）；（在河流或湖泊中）放养（鱼苗、鱼卵、牡蛎等）
【名】 （Plant）（英、西、意）普兰特，（法）普朗（人名）
n. 凯迪拉克（亦作卡迪拉克，美国通用汽车公司旗下的豪华汽车品牌，也指该品牌生产的汽车）；〈非正式〉 the Cadillac of something：同类中最佳者，极品；卡迪拉克（法国北美殖民地总督，底特律的创立者）

e.en: The height of a person or thing is their size or length from the bottom to the top.

ex.en: Her weight is about normal for her height.
ex.zh: 按她的身高，她的体重大体正常。

ex.en: I am 5'6'' in height.
ex.zh: 我的身高是5英尺6英寸。

e.en: Height is the quality of being tall.

ex.en: She admits that her height is intimidating for some men.
ex.zh: 她承认自己的高个儿对一些男人而言是吓人的。

e.en: A particular height is the distance that something is above the ground or above something else mentioned.

ex.en: At the speed and height at which he was moving, he was never more than half a second from disaster.
ex.zh: 以这样的速度在这么高的地方移动，他离灾难永远只有半步之遥。

e.en: A height is a high position or place above the ground.

ex.en: I'm not afraid of heights.
ex.zh: 我不恐高。

d: n. 高处，高地，高空（复数名词，指高于周围的地面或位置）；高度（height 的复数，指多个高度值）；极点，高峰，顶点（比喻用法，指程度、强度或水平达到最高）

e.en: The recommendations of a person or a committee are their suggestions or advice on what is the best thing to do. 建议;

ex.en: The committee's recommendations are unlikely to be made public.
ex.zh: 委员会的建议很可能不会公之于众。

e.en: A recommendation of something is the suggestion that someone should have or use it because it is good.

ex.en: The best way of finding a lawyer is through personal recommendation.
ex.zh: 找律师的最好方法是通过个人推荐。

d: n. 正式建议，提议；推荐，介绍；推荐信

e.en: great numbers or quantities

ex.en: lots of people
to eat lots

e.en: a great deal

d: n. 大量，许多（常与 of 连用）；一堆，一批；地块；拍卖品；签，阄（用于 draw lots、cast lots，即抽签、抓阄）；命运（lot 的复数，较少用）
adv. 很，非常
v. 把（土地等）划分成块；把…分组；分配（lot 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: The residents of a house or area are the people who live there.

ex.en: The archbishop called on the government to build more low cost homes for local residents.
ex.zh: 这位大主教呼吁该政府为当地居民建更多的廉价住宅。

e.en: Someone who is resident in a country or a town lives there.

ex.en: He moved to the United States in 1990 to live with his son, who had been resident in Baltimore since 1967.
ex.zh: 他1990年移居美国去和从1967年就住在巴尔的摩的儿子一起住。

e.en: A resident or a resident doctor is a doctor who is receiving a period of specialized training in a hospital after completing his or her internship.

ex.en: Many resident doctors complain that they are assigned too many duties that are usually not performed by physicians.
ex.zh: 很多住院医师抱怨他们被指派了太多通常不由内科医生完成的职责。

d: n. 居民；房客；住院医生，（美国的）高级专科住院实习医生；（美）寄宿制学校学生；（英国派驻半独立国家的）特派代表；驻外特工（resident 的复数）

e.en: A zone is an area that has particular features or characteristics. (有某些特征或特点的)

ex.en: Many people have stayed behind in the potential war zone.
ex.zh: 许多人留在了可能交战的地带。

ex.en: The area has been declared a disaster zone.
ex.zh: 该地区已被宣布为灾难带。

e.en: If an area of land is zoned, it is formally set aside for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The land was not zoned for commercial purposes.
ex.zh: 这块地未被划为商业用地。

e.en: 分区制

ex.en: ...the use of zoning to preserve agricultural land.
ex.zh: …使用分区制以保留农业用地。

d: n. （城市规划、土地管理）分区制，区划，都市的区域划分；（信息技术、存储网络）分区，即将节点、设备或存储资源划分为相互隔离的逻辑区

e.en: If you say that you need or have a great deal of or a good deal of a particular thing, you are emphasizing that you need or have a lot of it.

ex.en: ...a great deal of money.
ex.zh: …许多钱。

e.en: Deal is also an adverb.

ex.en: As a relationship becomes more established, it also becomes a good deal more complex.
ex.zh: 当一段关系固定下来以后，它也会变得复杂得多。

e.en: Deal is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Although he had never met Geoffrey Hardcastle, he knew a good deal about him.
ex.zh: 尽管他从未见过杰弗里·哈德卡斯尔，他还是十分了解他。

e.en: If you make a deal, do a deal, or cut a deal, you complete an agreement or an arrangement with someone, especially in business. 达成协议;

ex.en: He made a deal to testify against the others and wasn't charged.
ex.zh: 他达成了协议出庭指证别人，因而未获指控。

ex.en: Japan will have to do a deal with the U.S. on rice imports.
ex.zh: 日本将不得不就水稻进口问题和美国达成协议。

d: n. 大量；交易；坏运气，不公平的对待；发牌；冷衫木；优惠的价格，划算的价格；牌戏的一局；一手牌
v. 应对（难缠的人，困难局面）（deal with）；（以某种方式）对付，对待（deal with）；论及，讨论（deal with）；买卖，交易；给予；贩卖（毒品、艺术品等）；与……有关；发牌
【名】 （Deal）（美）迪尔（人名）

e.en: If there is an improvement in something, it becomes better. If you make improvements to something, you make it better.

ex.en: ...the dramatic improvements in organ transplantation in recent years.
ex.zh: …近几年器官移植上令人瞩目的改进。

e.en: If you say that something is an improvement on a previous thing or situation, you mean that it is better than that thing. 改进的事物;

ex.en: The new governor is an improvement on his predecessor.
ex.zh: 新任总督胜过他的前任。

d: n. 提高，改进（improvement 的复数）；具体的改进之处、改善措施，尤指设施、房屋等的改建工程（常作复数，用于 improvements to something）

e.en: You use industrial to describe things that relate to or are used in industry.

ex.en: ...industrial machinery and equipment.
ex.zh: …工业机械及设备。

e.en: An industrial city or country is one in which industry is important or highly developed.

ex.en: ...leading western industrial countries.
ex.zh: …主要的西方工业发达国家。

d: adj. 工业的，产业的；有很多产业的，工业发达的；工业用的，用于工业的；（与）工业摇滚（有关）的；因勤劳而得到的
n. 从事工业的公司；工业股票；工业工人

e.en: An operation is a highly organized activity that involves many people doing different things.

ex.en: The rescue operation began on Friday afternoon.
ex.zh: 营救行动星期五下午展开。

ex.en: The soldiers were engaged in a military operation close to the Ugandan border.
ex.zh: 士兵们在靠近乌干达边界的地区开展军事行动。

e.en: A business or company can be referred to as an operation.

ex.en: Thorn's electronics operation employs around 5,000 people.
ex.zh: 索恩的电子公司雇佣了大约五千名员工。

e.en: When a patient has an operation, a surgeon cuts open their body in order to remove, replace, or repair a diseased or damaged part.

ex.en: Charles was at the clinic recovering from an operation on his arm.
ex.zh: 查尔斯在诊所，进行手臂的术后恢复。

e.en: If a system is in operation, it is being used.

ex.en: ...the free banking system that has been in operation since the early eighties.
ex.zh: …从80年代初就开始实施的自由银行制度。

d: n. 运作，实施；运转，操作；手术；（有组织的）活动，行动；军事行动；企业，公司；业务，经营 ；（数学）运算

e.en: A parcel is something wrapped in paper, in a bag or large envelope, or in a box, usually so that it can be sent to someone by mail. 包裹;

ex.en: They also sent parcels of food and clothing.
ex.zh: 他们还寄送了成包的食物和衣物。

e.en: If you say that something is part and parcel of something else, you are emphasizing that it is involved or included in it.

ex.en: Learning about life in a new culture is part and parcel of what newcomers to America face.
ex.zh: 学习在一种新的文化中生活是每一个新来美国的人要面对的事情中的重要部分。

d: n. parcel 的复数：包裹、邮包；地块、宗地（常作 parcels of land）
vt. parcel 的第三人称单数：打包、包扎；分配，把…分成几份（常作 parcels out）
v. 再分区规划；重新区划（rezone 的 ing 形式）
n. 水虫，水虿
n. （Dobson）人名；（英）多布森

e.en: Dust is very small dry particles of earth or sand.

ex.en: Tanks raise huge trails of dust when they move.
ex.zh: 坦克移动时掀起滚滚的尘土。

e.en: Dust is the very small pieces of dirt which you find inside buildings, for example, on furniture, floors, or lights.

ex.en: I could see a thick layer of dust on the stairs.
ex.zh: 我能看见楼梯上厚厚的一层灰尘。

e.en: Dust is a fine powder which consists of very small particles of a substance such as gold, wood, or coal.

ex.en: The air is so black with diesel fumes and coal dust, I can barely see.
ex.zh: 天空由于充满柴油机的浓烟和煤灰而如此黑，我几乎看不见。

e.en: When you dust something such as furniture, you remove dust from it, usually using a cloth.

ex.en: I vacuumed and dusted and polished the living room.
ex.zh: 我把起居室吸了尘、掸了灰并且擦亮了。

d: n. 沙尘；灰尘；粉末；尘雾；除尘，掸灰；尸骨，遗骸；凡身，肉体
v. 擦去……的灰尘；把粉末撒于；狠揍，杀死（某人）
【名】 （Dust）（德、俄）杜斯特（人名）

e.en: An enterprise is a company or business. 公司;

ex.en: There are plenty of small industrial enterprises.
ex.zh: 有很多小型的工业企业。

e.en: An enterprise is something new, difficult, or important that you do or try to do.

ex.en: Horse breeding is indeed a risky enterprise.
ex.zh: 养马的确是一项有风险的事业。

e.en: Enterprise is the activity of managing companies and businesses and starting new ones.

ex.en: He is still involved in voluntary work promoting local enterprise.
ex.zh: 他仍从事志愿工作推动当地创业。

e.en: Enterprise is the ability to think of new and effective things to do, together with an eagerness to do them. 开创力;

ex.en: ...the spirit of enterprise worthy of a free and industrious people.
ex.zh: …与一个自由勤劳的民族相称的开拓精神。

d: n. （经）企业，公司（enterprise 的复数）；事业，艰巨或重要的活动、项目（enterprise 的复数）

e.en: Something that is heavy weighs a lot.

ex.en: These scissors are awfully heavy.
ex.zh: 这些剪刀非常重。

e.en: 沉重

ex.en: ...a sensation of warmth and heaviness in the muscles.
ex.zh: …一种肌肉的温暖和沉重感。

e.en: You use heavy to ask or talk about how much someone or something weighs.

ex.en: How heavy are you?
ex.zh: 你有多重？

e.en: Heavy means great in amount, degree, or intensity. 大量的; 过度的;

ex.en: Heavy fighting has been going on.
ex.zh: 激战一直在进行。

ex.en: He worried about her heavy drinking.
ex.zh: 他为她的酗酒感到担忧。

d: adj. 重的，沉的；大量的，严重的；大而结实的，不精致的；厚实的；充满（某物）（heavy with）；重型的，大型的；繁忙的；辛苦的，费力的；用力的，重重的；难消化的；难懂的，艰涩的；危险的，汹涌的；闷热的，沉闷的；浓郁的；（土壤）黏重的；苛刻的，严厉的；认真的，严肃的；（声音）粗重的；（身体部位）沉重的；（心情）忧伤的
n. 保镖，打手；（电影或戏剧中的）反派；重要人物； 严肃报纸（heavies）；烈性啤酒
adv. 浓浓地，沉重地；使不安，使担忧

e.en: If you help someone, you make it easier for them to do something, for example by doing part of the work for them or by giving them advice or money.

ex.en: He has helped to raise a lot of money.
ex.zh: 他帮着筹到了很多钱。

ex.en: You can of course help by giving them a donation directly.
ex.zh: 你当然可以通过直接给他们一笔捐赠来帮助他们。

e.en: Help is also a noun.

ex.en: Thanks very much for your help.
ex.zh: 非常感谢你的帮助。

e.en: If you say that something helps, you mean that it makes something easier to do or get, or that it improves a situation to some extent.

ex.en: The right style of swimsuit can help to hide, minimize, or emphasize what you want it to.
ex.zh: 款式得当的泳衣有助于按你的意愿掩饰、缩小或突出某些部位。

ex.en: Building more bypasses will help the environment by reducing pollution and traffic jams in towns and cities.
ex.zh: 修建更多的支路将减少城镇中的污染和交通堵塞，从而改善环境。

e.en: If you help someone go somewhere or move in some way, you give them support so that they can move more easily.

ex.en: Martin helped Tanya over the rail.
ex.zh: 马丁扶着塔尼娅翻过栏杆。

d: v. 帮助（help 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: An issue is an important subject that people are arguing about or discussing.

ex.en: Agents will raise the issue of prize-money for next year's world championships.
ex.zh: 代理商们会提出明年世界锦标赛的奖金问题。

ex.en: A key issue for higher education in the 1990s is the need for greater diversity of courses.
ex.zh: 20世纪90年代高等教育的一个关键问题是需要使课程更加多样化。

e.en: If something is the issue, it is the thing you consider to be the most important part of a situation or discussion.

ex.en: I was earning a lot of money, but that was not the issue.
ex.zh: 我是挣着很多钱，但那不是问题的关键。

ex.en: Do not draw it on the chart, however, as this will confuse the issue.
ex.zh: 但是不要把它画在图表上，因为这将使要点模糊不清。

e.en: An issue of something such as a magazine or newspaper is the version of it that is published, for example, in a particular month or on a particular day. (杂志或报刊的)

ex.en: The growing problem is underlined in the latest issue of the Scientific American.
ex.zh: 这一日益严重的问题在最新一期的《科学美国人》上得到强调。

e.en: If you issue a statement or a warning, you make it known formally or publicly. 发表 (声明); 发出 (警告)

ex.en: Last night he issued a statement denying the allegations.
ex.zh: 昨天晚上，他发表了一项声明否认那些说法。

ex.en: The government issued a warning that the strikers should end their action or face dismissal.
ex.zh: 该政府发出了警告，罢工者们应停止他们的行动，否则将被免职。

d: n. 议题，问题；问题，困扰（委婉，常用 have issues with…）；争点；债券，证券；（股票、债券等的）发行；（报刊的）期，期号
v. 发行；分发，配发；签发（证件、执照等）；发表，发布（声明、警告等）；流出，冒出

e.en: To obtain something means to get it or achieve it.

ex.en: Evans was trying to obtain a false passport and other documents.
ex.zh: 埃文斯当时正试图获取假护照和其他文件。

d: v. obtain 的过去式和过去分词：（尤指通过艰难的过程）得到，获得；（规则或情况）存在，适用，通用

e.en: A pizza is a flat, round piece of dough covered with tomatoes, cheese, and other toppings, and then baked in an oven.

ex.en: ...the last piece of pizza.
ex.zh: …最后一块比萨饼。

d: n. 比萨饼，披萨（一种意大利烤饼，用扁平的面饼铺上番茄酱、奶酪及其他配料烤制而成）；（Pizza）皮扎（意大利人名）

e.en: A plan is a method of achieving something that you have worked out in detail beforehand. 计划;

ex.en: The three leaders had worked out a peace plan.
ex.zh: 这3位领导人已制定出了一份和平计划。

ex.en: He maintains that everything is going according to plan.
ex.zh: 他坚持说一切都在按计划进行。

e.en: If you plan what you are going to do, you decide in detail what you are going to do, and you intend to do it.

ex.en: If you plan what you're going to eat, you reduce your chances of overeating.
ex.zh: 如果你对要吃的东西加以计划，饮食过度的几率就会减少。

ex.en: He planned to leave Baghdad on Monday.
ex.zh: 他计划星期一离开巴格达。

e.en: If you have plans, you are intending to do a particular thing. (具体)

ex.en: "I'm sorry," she said. "I have plans for tonight.".
ex.zh: “抱歉，”她说。“我今晚有安排。”

e.en: When you plan something that you are going to make, build, or create, you decide what the main parts of it will be and do a drawing of how it should be made.

ex.en: It is no use trying to plan an 18-hole golf course on a 120-acre site if you have to ruin the environment to do it.
ex.zh: 要规划一个占地120公顷、拥有18洞的高尔夫球场如果必须破坏环境才能做到，那就毫无益处了。

d: n. （详细）规划；（养老金、储蓄、保险）方案；计划，打算；平面图，详图；分布图，示意图；（卫理公会教堂）巡回传教士名单；（手机流量、话费等）套餐
v. 计划，筹划；打算；设计；期望，预料
【名】 （Plan）（瑞典）普兰，（法）普朗（人名）

e.en: A residential area contains houses rather than offices or factories.

ex.en: ...a posh residential area 20 minutes from the White House.
ex.zh: …距离白宫20分钟路程的一个豪华住宅区。

e.en: A residential institution is one where people live while they are studying there or being cared for there.

ex.en: Training involves a two-year residential course.
ex.zh: 培训包括两年的住校课程。

d: adj. 住宅区的，居民区的 ；家庭的，住宅的；（为工作、学习或受人照料而）住宿（在某地）的

e.en: If a person or thing is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

ex.en: The small churchyard was surrounded by a rusted wrought-iron fence.
ex.zh: 这个小墓地被一道生锈的锻铁栅栏围着。

ex.en: The shell surrounding the egg has many important functions.
ex.zh: 包着蛋的外壳有很多重要功能。

e.en: If you are surrounded by soldiers or police, they spread out so that they are in positions all the way around you.

ex.en: When the car stopped in the town square it was surrounded by soldiers and militiamen.
ex.zh: 当这辆车在城镇广场停下时，它被战士和民兵们包围了。

e.en: The circumstances, feelings, or ideas which surround something are those that are closely associated with it.

ex.en: The decision had been agreed in principle before today's meeting, but some controversy surrounded it.
ex.zh: 在今天的会议之前该决定原则上已获同意，但围绕这项决定还存在一些争议。

e.en: If you surround yourself with certain people or things, you make sure that you have a lot of them near you all the time.

ex.en: He had made it his business to surround himself with a hand-picked group of bright young officers.
ex.zh: 他把确保身边有自己亲手挑选的一群聪明的年轻军官当作自己的职责。

d: adj. 周围的，附近的
n. 周围环境（surroundings）
v. 围绕，环绕；包围，围住；与……紧密相连（或相关）（surround 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A zone is an area that has particular features or characteristics. (有某些特征或特点的)

ex.en: Many people have stayed behind in the potential war zone.
ex.zh: 许多人留在了可能交战的地带。

ex.en: The area has been declared a disaster zone.
ex.zh: 该地区已被宣布为灾难带。

e.en: If an area of land is zoned, it is formally set aside for a particular purpose.

ex.en: The land was not zoned for commercial purposes.
ex.zh: 这块地未被划为商业用地。

e.en: 分区制

ex.en: ...the use of zoning to preserve agricultural land.
ex.zh: …使用分区制以保留农业用地。

d: adj. 划成区域的、分区的；（土地、区域等）被划定或规划为特定用途的；（旧义）束带的
v. 将（土地等）划分成区；将（土地等）划定为特定用途区域（zone 的过去式和过去分词）；（旧义）环绕

e.en: If the process or rate of something accelerates or if something accelerates it, it gets faster and faster. 使加速;

ex.en: Growth will accelerate to 2.9 percent next year.
ex.zh: 增长明年将加快到2.9%。

e.en: When a moving vehicle accelerates, it goes faster and faster.

ex.en: Suddenly the car accelerated.
ex.zh: 突然车加速了。

d: adj. 加速的，加快的；（教育）速成的，跳级的。
v. accelerate 的过去式和过去分词；（使）加速，加快，促进。

e.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

ex.en: General Motors acquired a 50% stake in Saab for about $400m.
ex.zh: 通用汽车公司以大约4亿美元获得了萨博50%的股份。

e.en: If you acquire something such as a skill or a habit, you learn it, or develop it through your daily life or experience.

ex.en: I've never acquired a taste for wine.
ex.zh: 我从未养成对葡萄酒的爱好。

e.en: If someone or something acquires a certain reputation, they start to have that reputation. 获得 (名声)

ex.en: During her film career, she acquired a reputation as a strong-willed, outspoken woman.
ex.zh: 在她的银幕生涯中，她获得了一个意志坚定、坦率直言的名声。

d: v. 获得，得到；学到，习得；患上（疾病）；逐渐具有，开始学会

e.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

ex.en: General Motors acquired a 50% stake in Saab for about $400m.
ex.zh: 通用汽车公司以大约4亿美元获得了萨博50%的股份。

e.en: If you acquire something such as a skill or a habit, you learn it, or develop it through your daily life or experience.

ex.en: I've never acquired a taste for wine.
ex.zh: 我从未养成对葡萄酒的爱好。

e.en: If someone or something acquires a certain reputation, they start to have that reputation. 获得 (名声)

ex.en: During her film career, she acquired a reputation as a strong-willed, outspoken woman.
ex.zh: 在她的银幕生涯中，她获得了一个意志坚定、坦率直言的名声。

d: v. 获得，取得，购买；习得，养成，学到（acquire 的现在分词）
n. 获得，取得（的行为）

e.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, the two things are next to each other.

ex.en: He sat in an adjacent room and waited.
ex.zh: 他坐在一间相邻的房间里等。

ex.en: The schools were adjacent but there were separate doors.
ex.zh: 这些学校相邻，但是有各自的门。

d: adj. 邻近的，毗连的；（几何）（两个角）相邻的

e.en: Additional things are extra things apart from the ones already present.

ex.en: The U.S. is sending additional troops to the region.
ex.zh: 美国正在往该地区派遣额外的部队。

d: adj. 附加的，额外的

e.en: An adjustment is a small change that is made to something such as a machine or a way of doing something. (对机器、做事方法等的)

ex.en: Compensation could be made by adjustments to taxation.
ex.zh: 补偿可由调税实现。

ex.en: Investment is up by 5.7% after adjustment for inflation.
ex.zh: 投资在通货膨胀调整之后增长了5.7%。

e.en: An adjustment is a change in a person's behaviour or thinking. (对行为、思想等的)

ex.en: He will have to make major adjustments to his thinking if he is to survive in office.
ex.zh: 他要想继续任职的话，就得对他的思维方式作大的调整。

d: n. 调整，校正；（行为、思想的）调节，适应；调节器
n. 阿尔坎塔拉（地名，位于意大利的西西岛）

e.en: An approving reaction or remark shows support for something, or satisfaction with it. 满意的;

ex.en: His mother leaned forward and gave him an approving look.
ex.zh: 他妈妈向前探身并对他投出赞许的目光。

d: adj. 赞成的，赞许的，满意的
v. 赞成，同意；批准，通过；认可，核准（approve 的现在分词）

e.en: An assessor is a person who is employed to calculate the value of something, or the amount of money that should be paid, for example, in tax.

d: n. 评估员，评审员；评税员，财产估价员；保险公估人，估损人；（法律、技术等领域的）顾问

e.en: An automaker is a company that manufactures cars.

ex.en: ...General Motors Corp., the world's largest automaker.
ex.zh: ...通用汽车公司，世界最大的汽车制造商。

d: n. 汽车制造商

e.en: If you backtrack on a statement or decision you have made, you do or say something that shows that you no longer agree with it or support it.

ex.en: The committee backtracked by scrapping the controversial bonus system.
ex.zh: 该委员会改变主意，废除充满争议性的奖金系统。

ex.en: His arrest sparked fears that the country was backtracking on market reforms.
ex.zh: 他被捕一事引起恐慌，国家有关市场改革政策可能会有变动。

e.en: If you backtrack, you go back along a path or route you have just used.

ex.en: Leonard jumped in his car and started backtracking.
ex.zh: 里欧纳德跳上车，原路返回。

ex.en: We had to backtrack to the corner and cross the street.
ex.zh: 我们必须退回转角，然后过马路。

e.en: If you backtrack in an account or explanation, you talk about things which happened before the ones you were previously talking about.

ex.en: Can we just backtrack a little bit and look at your primary and secondary education?
ex.zh: 我们能否稍微回顾一下刚刚提及的你的中小学教育背景？

d: v. 原路返回，折回；出尔反尔，变卦；回到先前的话题，回头讲述（backtrack 的现在分词）
n. （计算机）回溯法，回溯

e.en: In the United States, an attorney or attorney-at-law is a lawyer.

ex.en: ...a prosecuting attorney.
ex.zh: …一位公诉律师。

ex.en: At the hearing, her attorney did not enter a plea.
ex.zh: 在听证会上，她的律师没有提出申诉。

d: n. 律师；代理人

e.en: A barren landscape is dry and bare, and has very few plants and no trees.

ex.en: ...the Tibetan landscape of high barren mountains.
ex.zh: …西藏荒芜的高山景观。

e.en: Barren land consists of soil that is so poor that plants cannot grow in it.

ex.en: He wants to use the water to irrigate barren desert land.
ex.zh: 他想用该水来灌溉贫瘠的沙漠土地。

e.en: If you describe something such as an activity or a period of your life as barren, you mean that you achieve no success during it or that it has no useful results. 无成就的;

ex.en: ...an empty exercise barren of utility.
ex.zh: …一项毫无效用的无聊训练。

e.en: If you describe a room or a place as barren, you do not like it because it has almost no furniture or other objects in it.

ex.en: The room was austere, nearly barren of furniture or decoration.
ex.zh: 这个房间很简朴，几乎没有什么家具或装饰。

d: adj. 贫瘠的，不毛的；不结果实的；不育的；不出成绩的，无效果的；沉闷无趣的，没有吸引力的
n. 瘠地
【名】 （Barren）（英、西）巴伦（人名）

e.en: A bike is a bicycle.

ex.en: When you ride a bike, you exercise all of the leg muscles.
ex.zh: 骑自行车时，你可以锻炼腿部的全部肌肉。

e.en: A bike is a motorcycle.

ex.en: She parked her bike in the alley.
ex.zh: 她把摩托车停在巷子里。

e.en: a promiscuous woman

ex.en: the town bike

e.en: To bike somewhere means to go there on a bicycle.

ex.en: I biked home from the beach.
ex.zh: 我从海滩骑自行车回家。

d: n. 骑自行车，骑单车，骑车（指骑行活动）
v. 骑自行车（bike 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Your birthplace is the place where you were born.

ex.en: ...Bob Marley's birthplace in the village of Nine Mile.
ex.zh: …在九里村鲍勃·马利的出生地。

e.en: The birthplace of something is the place where it began.

ex.en: ...Athens, the birthplace of the ancient Olympics.
ex.zh: …雅典，古代奥林匹克运动的发祥地。

d: n. 出生地；发源地

e.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that prevents two things from harming each other.

ex.en: Keep savings as a buffer against unexpected cash needs.
ex.zh: 备有存款来作为急需现金时的缓冲。

e.en: If something is buffered, it is protected from harm.

ex.en: The company is buffered by long-term contracts with growers.
ex.zh: 这家公司受到了与种植者签订长期合同的保护。

e.en: one of a pair of spring-loaded steel pads attached at both ends of railway vehicles and at the end of a railway track to reduce shock due to contact (铁路)
A buffer is an area in a computer's memory where information can be stored for a short time.

d: n. 起缓冲作用的人（物）；老家伙，老头；缓冲存储器，缓存；（铁路机车头尾的）缓冲器，减震器；（用于擦亮表面的）抛光工具
v. 保护（某物）；缓解，缓冲；存储，缓存（数据等）

e.en: If you describe a woman as butch, you mean that she behaves or dresses in a masculine way. This use could cause offence. (指女人)
If you describe a man as butch, you mean that he behaves in an extremely masculine way.

d: adj. （女子外表、举止、穿着）男性化的，男人腔的；（男子）高大的
n. 充当男性角色的女同性恋者；粗鲁的男人或男孩

e.en: Commercial means involving or relating to the buying and selling of goods.

ex.en: Baltimore in its heyday was a major centre of industrial and commercial activity.
ex.zh: 巴尔的摩在其鼎盛时期曾是工商业活动的主要中心。

e.en: Commercial organizations and activities are concerned with making money or profits, rather than, for example, with scientific research or providing a public service.

ex.en: The company has indeed become more commercial over the past decade.
ex.zh: 这个公司在过去的十年里确实已变得越来越商业化了。

ex.en: Conservationists in Chile are concerned over the effect of commercial exploitation of forests.
ex.zh: 智利的自然保护者对森林商业化开发的后果感到担忧。

e.en: 商业化地

ex.en: The plane will be commercially viable if 400 can be sold.
ex.zh: 这飞机若能售出400架从商业上看就可行。

e.en: A commercial product is made to be sold to the public.

ex.en: They are the leading manufacturer in both defence and commercial products.
ex.zh: 他们在防御性和商业性的产品方面都是领先的制造商。

d: adj. 商业的，商务的；商业化的，以获利为目的的；由广告商支付的；（化学制品）大量供应且纯度不高的
n. 电视广告，电台广告

e.en: A commissioner is an important official in a government department or other organization. (政府部门等的)

ex.en: ...Alaska's commissioner of education.
ex.zh: …阿拉斯加州的教育要员。

d: n.  （政府部门的）首长，长官；（委员会的）委员，专员；警察局局长；〈北美〉体育组织的行政管理人，干事

e.en: A commissioner is an important official in a government department or other organization. (政府部门等的)

ex.en: ...Alaska's commissioner of education.
ex.zh: …阿拉斯加州的教育要员。

d: n. 委员，委员会成员；政府或机构中的重要官员，如专员、特派员、地方长官（commissioner 的复数形式）

e.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a situation. 怨言;

ex.en: There's been a record number of complaints about the standard of service.
ex.zh: 已有对服务水准的创纪录数量的投诉。

ex.en: People have been reluctant to make formal complaints to the police.
ex.zh: 人们一直不愿正式向警方投诉。

e.en: A complaint is a reason for complaining.

ex.en: My main complaint is that we can't go out on the racecourse anymore.
ex.zh: 我抱怨的主要缘由是我们无法再去外面的赛道了。

e.en: You can refer to an illness as a complaint, especially if it is not very serious. (尤指不严重的)

ex.en: Eczema is a common skin complaint which often runs in families.
ex.zh: 湿疹是一种常见的皮肤病，常会遗传。

d: n. 投诉，申诉，抱怨（complaint 的复数）；抱怨的缘由，不满之处；（医学）（尤指不严重的）疾病，不适

e.en: If you decide to do something, you choose to do it, usually after you have thought carefully about the other possibilities.

ex.en: She decided to take a course in philosophy.
ex.zh: 她决定修一门哲学课。

ex.en: Think about it very carefully before you decide.
ex.zh: 在你决定之前慎重地考虑。

e.en: If a person or group of people decides something, they choose what something should be like or how a particular problem should be solved.

ex.en: She was still young, he said, and that would be taken into account when deciding her sentence.
ex.zh: 她还年轻，他说，这一点对裁定关于她的判决时要考虑进去。

e.en: If an event or fact decides something, it makes it certain that a particular choice will be made or that there will be a particular result.

ex.en: What happens next could decide their destiny.
ex.zh: 接下来发生的事可能会决定他们的命运。

ex.en: The election will decide if either party controls both houses of Congress.
ex.zh: 这次选举将决定是否由任一党控制国会两院。

e.en: If you decide that something is true, you form that opinion about it after considering the facts.

ex.en: He decided Franklin must be suffering from a bad cold.
ex.zh: 他断定富兰克林肯定是得了重感冒。

d: v. 影响（或决定）……的结果；断定，判定；使下决心；决定，选定；裁决，判决

e.en: A deed is something that is done, especially something that is very good or very bad.

ex.en: The perpetrators of this evil deed must be brought to justice.
ex.zh: 这件恶行的凶手必须接受法律的制裁。

e.en: A deed is a document containing the terms of an agreement, especially an agreement concerning the ownership of land or a building. 契约;

ex.en: He asked if I had the deeds to his father's property.
ex.zh: 他问我是否有他父亲财产的各种证书。

d: n. 行为，行动；事迹，功绩；契约，证书（deed 的复数）；（Deeds）迪兹（姓氏）
v. 立契转让（deed 的第三人称单数）

e.en: To devalue something means to cause it to be thought less impressive or less deserving of respect.

ex.en: They spread tales about her in an attempt to devalue her work.
ex.zh: 他们散布关于她的传闻，企图贬低她的工作。

e.en: To devalue the currency of a country means to reduce its value in relation to other currencies.

ex.en: India has devalued the rupee by about eleven percent.
ex.zh: 印度已经使卢比贬值约11%。

e.en: 贬值

ex.en: It will lead to devaluation of a number of currencies.
ex.zh: 这将导致多种货币的贬值。

d: vt. 使贬值，降低……的价值；贬低，降低……的重要性
vi. （货币、资产等）贬值

e.en: If you are disappointed, you are sad because something has not happened or because something is not as good as you had hoped.

ex.en: Adamski says he was very disappointed with the mayor's decision.
ex.zh: 阿达姆斯基说他对市长的决定非常失望。

ex.en: I was disappointed that John was not there.
ex.zh: 我很失望约翰不在那儿。

e.en: If you are disappointed in someone, you are sad because they have not behaved as well as you expected them to. 对 (某人)

ex.en: You should have accepted that. I'm disappointed in you.
ex.zh: 你本该接受的。我对你感到失望。

d: adj. 失望的，沮丧的；（希望、期待）破灭的
v. 使失望；使破灭，使落空（disappoint 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: An estate is a large area of land in the country which is owned by a person, family, or organization.

ex.en: He spent holidays at the 300-acre estate of his aunt and uncle.
ex.zh: 他在叔叔和婶婶的300英亩庄园里度过许多假日。

e.en: Someone's estate is all the money and property that they leave behind when they die.

ex.en: His estate was valued at $150,000.
ex.zh: 他的遗产价值为15万美元。

d: n. 财产，遗产；大片私有土地，庄园；住宅区，工业区；社会阶层；（生活）状况，条件
adj. 更简单；容易些（easy 的比较级形式）；较早的

e.en: If you exclude someone from a place or activity, you prevent them from entering it or taking part in it. 拒 (某人) 于 (某地、活动) 之外;

ex.en: Many of the youngsters feel excluded.
ex.zh: 很多年轻人感觉受排挤。

e.en: If you exclude something that has some connection with what you are doing, you deliberately do not use it or consider it. 故意不用;

ex.en: In some schools, Christmas carols are being modified to exclude any reference to Christ.
ex.zh: 在有些学校，圣诞颂歌正在被修改以去掉任何涉及基督的内容。

e.en: To exclude a possibility means to decide or prove that it is wrong and not worth considering. 排除 (某种可能性)

ex.en: I cannot entirely exclude the possibility that some form of pressure was applied to the neck.
ex.zh: 我不能完全排除有些压力作用到了颈部的可能性。

e.en: To exclude something such as the sun's rays or harmful germs means to prevent them physically from reaching or entering a particular place.

ex.en: This was intended to exclude the direct rays of the sun.
ex.zh: 这是用来阻挡太阳直射光线的。

d: vt. （故意）不包括，把……排除在外；认为……不可能，排除……的可能；阻挡；开除（学生）；防止……的发生
n. 评价，评估

e.en: If you exclude someone from a place or activity, you prevent them from entering it or taking part in it. 拒 (某人) 于 (某地、活动) 之外;

ex.en: Many of the youngsters feel excluded.
ex.zh: 很多年轻人感觉受排挤。

e.en: If you exclude something that has some connection with what you are doing, you deliberately do not use it or consider it. 故意不用;

ex.en: In some schools, Christmas carols are being modified to exclude any reference to Christ.
ex.zh: 在有些学校，圣诞颂歌正在被修改以去掉任何涉及基督的内容。

e.en: To exclude a possibility means to decide or prove that it is wrong and not worth considering. 排除 (某种可能性)

ex.en: I cannot entirely exclude the possibility that some form of pressure was applied to the neck.
ex.zh: 我不能完全排除有些压力作用到了颈部的可能性。

e.en: To exclude something such as the sun's rays or harmful germs means to prevent them physically from reaching or entering a particular place.

ex.en: This was intended to exclude the direct rays of the sun.
ex.zh: 这是用来阻挡太阳直射光线的。

d: v. （exclude 的第三人称单数）排除，不包括；排斥，拒绝…进入或参加；排除（可能性）或故意不考虑；阻挡，隔绝

e.en: If something expands or is expanded, it becomes larger. 扩大;

ex.en: Engineers noticed that the pipes were not expanding as expected.
ex.zh: 工程师们注意到管子并未像预期的那样膨胀。

ex.en: We have to expand the size of the image.
ex.zh: 我们不得不扩大图像的尺寸。

e.en: If something such as a business, organization, or service expands, or if you expand it, it becomes bigger and includes more people, goods, or activities. 使…发展;

ex.en: The popular ceramics industry expanded toward the middle of the 19th century.
ex.zh: 大众陶瓷业在19世纪中叶得到了发展。

d: adj. 扩大的，扩展的，膨胀的
v. expand 的现在分词/动名词：扩大，增大；扩展（业务）；详述；（宇宙、气体等）膨胀；变得开朗

e.en: When you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

ex.en: He expressed grave concern at American attitudes.
ex.zh: 他对美国的态度表达了严肃关注。

e.en: If an idea or feeling expresses itself in some way, it can be clearly seen in someone's actions or in its effects on a situation. (想法、情感) 流露;

ex.en: The anxiety of the separation often expresses itself as anger toward the child for getting lost.
ex.zh: 对失散的焦虑常常表现成对孩子走失的愤怒。

e.en: An express command or order is one that is clearly and deliberately stated. 明确陈述的 (命令、指令)

ex.en: This mighty electricity-generating power station was built on the express orders of the president.
ex.zh: 这一大型电力发电站是按照总统的明确指令修建的。

e.en: 明确陈述地

ex.en: He has expressly forbidden her to go out on her own.
ex.zh: 他已明确禁止她独自外出。

d: v. 表达，表露；表现，体现；（用数学方法）表示；压榨，挤压出（空气或液体）；特快发运
n. 快车；快递；初速大的猎枪；专使；捷运公司
adj. 快递的，特快的；明确的；特意的
adv. 用快递寄送

e.en: A file is a box or a folded piece of heavy paper or plastic in which letters or documents are kept. 文件盒;

ex.en: ...a file of insurance papers.
ex.zh: …一个保险单文件夹。

e.en: A file is a collection of information about a particular person or thing.

ex.en: We already have files on people's tax details.
ex.zh: 我们已经有了人们付税详情的卷宗。

e.en: In computing, a file is a set of related data that has its own name.

ex.en: Be sure to save the revised version of the file under a new filename.
ex.zh: 确保将改过的文件版本另存在一个新的文件名下。

e.en: A file is a hand tool which is used for rubbing hard objects to make them smooth, shape them, or cut through them.

d: n. 存档，归档；存档档案，归档记录；锉屑；（法院的）立案
v. 把（文件等）归档；提出（诉讼），提出（申请），送交（备案）；发送（报道给报社）（file 的现在分词形式）

e.en: A firm is an organization which sells or produces something or which provides a service which people pay for.

ex.en: The firm's employees were expecting large bonuses.
ex.zh: 这家公司的雇员们正期待着大笔的奖金。

ex.en: ...a legal assistant at a Chicago law firm.
ex.zh: …一家芝加哥律师事务所的一名法律助理。

e.en: If something is firm, it does not change much in shape when it is pressed but is not completely hard.

ex.en: Fruit should be firm and in excellent condition.
ex.zh: 水果应该硬实且完好无损。

e.en: If someone's grip is firm or if they perform a physical action in a firm way, they do it with quite a lot of force or pressure but also in a controlled way.

ex.en: The quick handshake was firm and cool.
ex.zh: 那次迅速的握手有力而冷静。

e.en: 强有力地

ex.en: She held me firmly by the elbow and led me to my aisle seat.
ex.zh: 她使劲抓着我的胳膊肘，把我领到靠过道的座位上。

d: n. 公司，商行；（以顾问医师为首的）医务小组；（敌视敌对球队球迷的）球迷俱乐部，球迷联盟
adj. 结实的，坚硬的；牢固的，稳固的；坚定的，坚决的；强有力的；牢牢掌控的；坚挺的；确切的，可靠的；严厉的，强硬的
v. 使强壮，使坚实；坚挺，稳步上涨；敲定
adv. 坚定地，坚决地

e.en: You use fine to describe something that you admire and think is very good.

ex.en: There is a fine view of the countryside.
ex.zh: 有一幅美丽的乡村景色。

ex.en: This is a fine book.
ex.zh: 这是一本好书。

e.en: 美好地

ex.en: They are finely engineered boats.
ex.zh: 它们是设计精美的船只。

e.en: If you say that you are fine, you mean that you are in good health or reasonably happy. 健康的;

ex.en: Lina is fine and sends you her love and best wishes.
ex.zh: 莉娜很好，她向你问候并祝福你。

e.en: If you say that something is fine, you mean that it is satisfactory or acceptable.

ex.en: The skiing is fine.
ex.zh: 滑雪挺好的。

ex.en: Everything was going to be just fine.
ex.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

d: n. 罚款，罚金（fine 的复数）；细粉，粉末；细骨料
v. 对……处以罚款，处……以罚金（fine 的第三人称单数）；使精细；变好；澄清（fine 的第三人称单数）
adj. 同类首创的，同类首例的，史无前例的
n. 弗雷德（Fred），英语国家常见男子名，常作 Frederick（弗雷德里克）的昵称或简称
abbr. 快速随机询问显示（FRED, Fast Random Enquiry Display）

e.en: A foothold is a strong or favourable position from which further advances or progress may be made.

ex.en: Businesses are investing millions of dollars to gain a foothold in this new market.
ex.zh: 商家们正投资数百万美元以求在新市场中赢得立足点。

e.en: A foothold is a place such as a small hole or area of rock where you can safely put your foot when climbing. (攀登时的)

ex.en: He lowered his legs until he felt he had a solid foothold on the rockface beneath him.
ex.zh: 他往下探腿，直到感觉双脚稳稳地踩住了岩石。

d: n. 立足点；立足处；据点

e.en: If something changes or is done gradually, it changes or is done in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

ex.en: Electricity lines to 30,000 homes were gradually being restored yesterday.
ex.zh: 通向3万户人家的电线昨日被逐步修复。

d: adv. 逐渐地，逐步地

e.en: If you are glad about something, you are happy and pleased about it.

ex.en: The people seem genuinely glad to see you.
ex.zh: 人们看到你似乎真得很高兴。

ex.en: I'd be glad if the boys slept a little longer so I could do some ironing.
ex.zh: 如果男孩子们多睡一会儿我就高兴了，可以熨熨衣服。

e.en: 高兴地

ex.en: Malcolm gladly accepted the invitation.
ex.zh: 马尔科姆欣然接受了邀请。

e.en: If you say that you will be glad to do something, usually for someone else, you mean that you are willing and eager to do it.

ex.en: I'll be glad to show you everything.
ex.zh: 我将乐意向你展示每样东西。

e.en: 乐意地

ex.en: The counsellors will gladly baby-sit during their free time.
ex.zh: 咨询员在空闲时也会乐意照看一下孩子。

d: adj. 高兴的；感激的；乐意的，非常愿意的；令人愉快的，充满欢乐的
v. 取悦，使高兴
n. 唐菖蒲属植物，唐菖蒲
【名】 （Glad） （英）格莱德，（塞、瑞典）格拉德，（法、挪）格拉（人名）

e.en: a corridor of protected open space that is maintained for conservation, recreation, and non-motorized transportation

d: n. 园林路；林荫道路
n. （Greenway）人名；（英）格林韦
v. 修理，维修；确定（时间、地点、价格等）；安排，组织；处理，解决（问题等）；固定，安装；使（目光、注意力或思想）集中于；牢记，铭记；把（枪、相机、雷达）瞄准；操纵，作弊；梳洗，整理；整容，矫正（牙齿）；提供，准备（饮食等）；惩罚，收拾；固着（颜色），定（影）；阉割（动物）；介绍对象；注射毒品
n. 解决方案（或措施）；窘境，困境；（毒品或致瘾物的）一次用量；方位确定，定位；理解，了解；受操纵的事，勾当
【名】 （Fix）（美）菲克斯（人名）

e.en: Ethics are moral beliefs and rules about right and wrong.

ex.en: Refugee workers said such action was a violation of medical ethics.
ex.zh: 难民工作者称这种行为违背了医学道德。

e.en: Someone's ethics are the moral principles about right and wrong behaviour that they believe in.

ex.en: He told the police that he had thought honestly about the ethics of what he was doing.
ex.zh: 他告诉警察他曾真诚地考虑过他所作所为依据的行为准则。

e.en: Ethics is the study of questions about what is morally right and wrong.

ex.en: ...the teaching of ethics and moral philosophy.
ex.zh: …伦理学和道德哲学的教学。

e.en: An ethic of a particular kind is an idea or moral belief that influences the behaviour, attitudes, and philosophy of a group of people.

ex.en: ...the ethic of public service.
ex.zh: …公共服务的道德观念。

d: n. 行为准则，道德原则；伦理学，道德学
abbr. 卫生和福利部（Health and Human Services）

e.en: A question is something that you say or write in order to ask a person about something.

ex.en: They asked a lot of questions about China.
ex.zh: 他们问了许多有关中国的问题。

e.en: If you question someone, you ask them a lot of questions about something.

ex.en: This led the therapist to question Jim about his parents and their marriage.
ex.zh: 这让治疗师询问起吉姆关于其父母以及他们的婚姻情况。

e.en: 询问

ex.en: The police have detained thirty-two people for questioning.
ex.zh: 警方拘留了32个人进行审问。

e.en: If you question something, you have or express doubts about whether it is true, reasonable, or worthwhile.

ex.en: It never occurs to them to question the doctor's decisions.
ex.zh: 他们从来没有想到去怀疑那个医生的决定。

d: n. 问题，疑问（question 的复数）
v. 质疑，询问（question 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Disclosure is the act of giving people new or secret information.

ex.en: ...insufficient disclosure of negative information about the company.
ex.zh: …有关该公司负面信息的不充分公开。

d: n. disclosure 的复数形式；公开，披露（指公开或透露信息、秘密等的行为）；披露的信息，披露事项（常用于财务、法律、隐私等正式语境）

e.en: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

ex.en: There has been a lively interest in the elections in the last two weeks.
ex.zh: 过去两周人们对选举一直有强烈的兴趣。

ex.en: She'd liked him at first, but soon lost interest.
ex.zh: 最初她喜欢过他，但很快就失去了兴趣。

e.en: Your interests are the things that you enjoy doing.

ex.en: Encourage your child in her interests and hobbies.
ex.zh: 鼓励你的孩子发展她的兴趣和爱好。

e.en: If something interests you, it attracts your attention so that you want to learn or hear more about it or continue doing it.

ex.en: Your financial problems do not interest me.
ex.zh: 我对你的财务问题不感兴趣。

e.en: If you are trying to persuade someone to buy or do something, you can say that you are trying to interest them in it. 引起 (购买或做某事)

ex.en: Can I interest you in a new car?
ex.zh: 我给你介绍一下新车，你感兴趣吗？

d: n. 兴趣，关注；吸引力，趣味；爱好；利息；利益，好处；权益，股权；利害关系，重要影响；利益集团，利益相关者
v. 使感兴趣，引起……的关注；劝说（某人）做（或参与）

e.en: The received opinion about something or the received way of doing something is generally accepted by people as being correct. 被广为接受的;

ex.en: He was among the first to question the received wisdom of the time.
ex.zh: 他是那个时代首先质疑当时被广为接受的处世之道的人之一。

d: adj.  广为接受的，公认的
v. 得到，收到；遭受，经受（特定待遇）；对……作出反应（receive 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A waiver is when a person, government, or organization agrees to give up a right or says that people do not have to obey a particular rule or law.

ex.en: ...a waiver of constitutional rights.
ex.zh: …一位放弃宪法权利者。

d: n. （对权利或要求的）放弃；弃权声明书

e.en: Investment is the activity of investing money.

ex.en: He said the government must introduce tax incentives to encourage investment.
ex.zh: 他说，政府必须通过给予税收利益来鼓励投资。

e.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest, or the thing that you invest it in.

ex.en: ...an investment of twenty-eight million dollars.
ex.zh: …2800万美元的投资额。

e.en: If you describe something you buy as an investment, you mean that it will be useful, especially because it will help you to do a task more cheaply or efficiently.

ex.en: When selecting boots, fine, quality leather will be a wise investment.
ex.zh: 在挑选靴子时，买精致、质量上乘的皮靴会是明智的。

e.en: Investment of time or effort is the spending of time or effort on something in order to make it a success.

ex.en: I worry about this big investment of time not working.
ex.zh: 我担心这么多的时间投入不起作用。

d: n. （经）投资；投资额或所投资的资产、项目（investment 的复数形式）

e.en: If you leave a place or person, you go away from that place or person.

ex.en: He would not be allowed to leave the country.
ex.zh: 他不准离开这个国家。

ex.en: My flight leaves in less than an hour.
ex.zh: 我的航班一小时内起飞。

e.en: If you leave an institution, group, or job, you permanently stop attending that institution, being a member of that group, or doing that job. 离开 (机构、团体或工作)

ex.en: He left school with no qualifications.
ex.zh: 他离开学校时没有拿到证书。

ex.en: I am leaving to concentrate on writing fiction.
ex.zh: 我要离开去专心写小说。

e.en: If you leave your husband, wife, or some other person with whom you have had a close relationship, you stop living with them or you end the relationship. 与…脱离关系; 离开 (某人)

ex.en: He'll never leave you. You needn't worry.
ex.zh: 他永远都不会离开你的，你不必担心。

e.en: If you leave something or someone in a particular place, you let them remain there when you go away. If you leave something or someone with a person, you let them remain with that person so they are safe while you are away.

ex.en: I left my bags in the car.
ex.zh: 我把包留在车里。

ex.en: From the moment that Philippe had left her in the bedroom at the hotel, she had heard nothing of him.
ex.zh: 自从菲利普把她遗弃在旅店房间的那一刻起，她就再没有他的任何消息。

d: v. 离开（某人或某处）；离开居住地点（或群体、工作单位等）；与……脱离关系， 离开（某人）；不立刻做，不马上处理；使保留，让……处于（某种状态、某地等）；给……留下（不愉快的东西）；留下（信息或答复）；遗留，遗忘；剩下（食物或饮料）；遗下（家人）；（去世时）遗赠，遗留；把……留交，交托；递送，递交；留（空隙或空白）；留给（指有限的机会）；不再谈论；（数学）剩余，余下
n. 假期，休假；准许，许可；（斯努克、槌球等）收盘球势，（球被击后）停留的位置

e.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing. 先进的 (系统、方法、设计等)

ex.en: ...a superpower equipped with the most advanced military technology in the world.
ex.zh: …一个拥有世界上最先进的军事技术的超级大国。

e.en: A country that is advanced has reached a high level of industrial or technological development. (国家)

ex.en: Agricultural productivity remained low by comparison with advanced countries like the United States.
ex.zh: 与美国等发达国家相比，农业生产率仍很低。

e.en: An advanced student has already learned the basic facts of a subject and is doing more difficult work. An advanced course of study is designed for such students. 高阶的 (学生、课程)

ex.en: The course is suitable for beginners and advanced students.
ex.zh: 该课程适合初学者和高阶学生。

e.en: Something that is at an advanced stage or level is at a late stage of development.

ex.en: Medicare is available to victims of advanced kidney disease.
ex.zh: 晚期肾病患者可获得医疗保障。

d: adj. 先进的；高级的，高等的；晚期的，状况不佳的；高龄的；新提出（尚未被广泛接受）的
v. 行进；发展，进步；预付（advance 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 艾丽西娅
n. 彭博社；彭博资讯

e.en: A box is a square or rectangular container with hard or stiff sides. Boxes often have lids. 盒子;

ex.en: He reached into the cardboard box beside him.
ex.zh: 他把手伸进他旁边的纸板箱。

ex.en: They sat on wooden boxes.
ex.zh: 他们坐在木箱上。

e.en: You can use box to refer to a box and its contents, or to the contents only.

ex.en: She ate two boxes of chocolates.
ex.zh: 她吃了两盒巧克力。

e.en: A box is a square or rectangle that is printed or drawn on a piece of paper, a road, or on some other surface.

ex.en: For more information, just check the box and send us the form.
ex.zh: 若需更多信息，在方框内打勾，然后把表格寄给我们。

e.en: A box is a small separate area in a theatre or at a sports arena or stadium, where a small number of people can sit to watch the performance or game.

ex.en: Jim watched the game from a private box.
ex.zh: 吉姆在私人包厢里观看比赛。

d: n. 盒，箱，匣；（戏院的）包厢，（法庭的）专席；小亭，岗亭；方框，方格；邮箱；（运动场上的）区，特定区域；电视（the box）；耳光；黄杨；（运动员的）下体护身
v. 把……装箱；（与……）斗拳，参加拳击比赛；（非同群牲畜）混杂，混群（box sheep up）
【名】 （Box）（英、法、西）博克斯（人名）

e.en: A bush is a large plant which is smaller than a tree and has a lot of branches.

ex.en: Trees and bushes grew down to the water's edge.
ex.zh: 树和灌木丛一直向下长到了水边。

e.en: The wild, uncultivated parts of some hot countries are referred to as the bush.

ex.en: They walked through the dense Mozambican bush for thirty-six hours.
ex.zh: 他们步行穿过茂密的莫桑比克灌木丛区，走了36个小时。

e.en: a thin metal sleeve or tubular lining serving as a bearing or guide 轴衬; 套管 (Also called (esp US and Canadian) bushing)
to fit a bush to (a casing, bearing, etc)

d: n. 灌木，灌木丛；荒野，丛林地带；衬套；绝缘套管；浓密的头发
v. 蓬松；伸展，丛生；以灌木装饰
adj. 如灌木般长得低矮的；粗野的；低劣的，便宜的
【名】 （Bush）布什（人名)

e.en: When a horse canters, it moves at a speed that is slower than a gallop but faster than a trot.

ex.en: The competitors cantered into the arena to conclude the closing ceremony.
ex.zh: 赛手们慢跑进入比赛场地，结束了闭幕式。

e.en: Canter is also a noun.

ex.en: Carnac set off at a canter.
ex.zh: 卡纳克以慢步小跑出发了。

d: n. （马术）慢跑，慢步小跑（马介于快步与飞奔之间的三拍步态）；〈旧〉流浪汉；（Canter）人名（姓氏），常译“坎特”，西班牙语、意大利语、瑞典语中亦译“坎特尔”
vi. （马术）（马）慢跑，以慢步小跑行进；（骑手）骑马慢跑
vt. 使（马）慢跑，策马慢跑
adv. at a canter / in a canter：轻松地，轻易地

e.en: A drug is a chemical which is given to people in order to treat or prevent an illness or disease.

ex.en: The drug will be useful to hundreds of thousands of infected people.
ex.zh: 这种药物将会对成千上万感染者有用。

e.en: Drugs are substances that some people take because of their pleasant effects, but which are usually illegal.

ex.en: His mother was on drugs, on cocaine.
ex.zh: 他的母亲吸毒，吸可卡因。

ex.en: She was sure Leo was taking drugs.
ex.zh: 她肯定利奥在吸毒。

e.en: If you drug a person or animal, you give them a chemical substance in order to make them sleepy or unconscious.

ex.en: She was drugged and robbed.
ex.zh: 她被下了迷药，遭到抢劫。

e.en: If food or drink is drugged, a chemical substance is added to it in order to make someone sleepy or unconscious when they eat or drink it. 下麻醉药于 (食物或饮料)

ex.en: I wonder now if that drink had been drugged.
ex.zh: 我现在怀疑那饮料是否已被人下了麻醉药。

d: n. 毒品，[药] 药物

e.en: When someone finances something such as a project or a purchase, they provide the money that is needed to pay for them.

ex.en: The fund has been used largely to finance the construction of federal prisons.
ex.zh: 该基金大部分已用于资助联邦监狱的建造。

e.en: Finance is also a noun.

ex.en: A United States delegation is in Japan seeking finance for a major scientific project.
ex.zh: 1个美国代表团正在日本为一个重大科研项目寻求资助。

e.en: Finance is the commercial or government activity of managing money, debt, credit, and investment. 金融;

ex.en: ...a major player in the world of high finance.
ex.zh: …高层金融界的大腕。

ex.en: The report recommends an overhaul of public finances.
ex.zh: 这份报告建议对公共财政进行彻底检视。

e.en: You can refer to the amount of money that you have and how well it is organized as your finances.

ex.en: Be prepared for unexpected news concerning your finances.
ex.zh: 对关于你财务状况的意外消息要做好准备。

d: n. 资金，财源，资产；财务状况

e.en: the automatic pilot in an aircraft (飞机的)

d: n. 乔治（男子名）；自动操纵装置；英国最高勋爵勋章上的圣乔治诛龙图

e.en: A hormone is a chemical, usually occurring naturally in your body, that makes an organ of your body do something.

ex.en: ...the male sex hormone testosterone.
ex.zh: …男性性激素睾酮。

d: n. 激素，荷尔蒙；人造激素；性激素（hormones）

e.en: An inspector is a person, usually employed by a government agency, whose job is to find out whether people are obeying official regulations. 检查员;

ex.en: The mill was finally shut down by state safety inspectors.
ex.zh: 这家工厂最终被州安全检查官关闭了。

e.en: An inspector is an officer in the police who is next in rank to a superintendent or police chief. 巡官 (官阶仅次于警长或警察局长的警官)

ex.en: ...San Francisco police inspector Tony Camileri.
ex.zh: …旧金山市巡官托尼·卡米勒瑞。

d: n. 检查员，督察员；（警察）巡官；（英国公共汽车或火车上的）查票员

e.en: To launch a rocket, missile, or satellite means to send it into the air or into space.

ex.en: NASA plans to launch a satellite to study cosmic rays.
ex.zh: 美国国家航空航天局计划发射一颗卫星来研究宇宙射线。

e.en: Launch is also a noun.

ex.en: This morning's launch of the space shuttle Columbia has been delayed.
ex.zh: 定于今天上午哥伦比亚号航天飞机的发射已经被推迟了。

e.en: To launch a ship or a boat means to put it into water, often for the first time after it has been built. 使 (新船等)

ex.en: There was no time to launch the lifeboats because the ferry capsized with such alarming speed.
ex.zh: 因为渡船倾斜的速度如此之快，根本没有时间把救生艇放下水。

e.en: Launch is also a noun.

ex.en: The launch of a ship was a big occasion.
ex.zh: 船下水曾是一件大事。

d: v. 启动，开始；推出，发布；发射（火箭、导弹、卫星等）；发起，开展（运动、调查、攻击等）；使（船）下水（launch 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The law is a system of rules that a society or government develops in order to deal with crime, business agreements, and social relationships. You can also use the law to refer to the people who work in this system. 法律;

ex.en: Obscene and threatening phone calls are against the law.
ex.zh: 猥亵电话和恐吓电话是违法的。

ex.en: They are beginning criminal proceedings against him for breaking the law on financing political parties.
ex.zh: 他们正开始对他进行刑事诉讼，因为他违反了政党资助法。

e.en: Law is used to refer to a particular branch of the law, such as criminal law or business law. (某一类)

ex.en: He was a professor of criminal law at Harvard University law school.
ex.zh: 他曾是哈佛大学法学院的刑法教授。

ex.en: Under international law, diplomats living in foreign countries are exempt from criminal prosecution.
ex.zh: 按照国际法，驻外外交官免受刑事诉讼。

e.en: A law is one of the rules in a system of law which deals with a particular type of agreement, relationship, or crime. (特定的)

ex.en: ...the country's liberal political asylum law.
ex.zh: …该国的自由政治避难法。

e.en: The laws of an organization or activity are its rules, which are used to organize and control it. 戒律;

ex.en: ...the laws of the Catholic Church.
ex.zh: …天主教会的戒律。

d: n. 法律，法规，法令；规章（law 的复数），守则，准则；规律，定律；（Laws，英语姓氏）劳斯

e.en: Medical means relating to illness and injuries and to their treatment or prevention. 医学的;

ex.en: Several police officers received medical treatment for cuts and bruises.
ex.zh: 几位警官接受了割伤和瘀伤的治疗。

e.en: 医学上地;

ex.en: Therapists cannot prescribe drugs as they are not necessarily medically qualified.
ex.zh: 治疗师们不能开药方，因为他们不一定具备医疗资格。

e.en: A medical is a thorough examination of your body by a doctor, for example before you start a new job.

d: adj. 医学的，医疗的；内科的
n. 体格检查，健康检查

e.en: A glacier is an extremely large mass of ice which moves very slowly, often down a mountain valley.

d: n. （地理／水文）冰川，冰河（glacier 的复数）

e.en: A glacier is an extremely large mass of ice which moves very slowly, often down a mountain valley.

d: n. 冰河，冰川

e.en: Ice is frozen water.

ex.en: Glaciers are moving rivers of ice.
ex.zh: 冰川是流动成河的冰。

e.en: If you ice a cake, you cover it with icing. 在 (糕饼)

ex.en: I've made the cake. I've iced and decorated it.
ex.zh: 我做了蛋糕，给它裹上了糖霜并进行了装饰。

e.en: If you break the ice at a party or meeting, or in a new situation, you say or do something to make people feel relaxed and comfortable.

ex.en: That sort of approach should go a long way toward breaking the ice.
ex.zh: 那种方法应该对打破僵局大有帮助。

e.en: If you say that something cuts no ice with you, you mean that you are not impressed or influenced by it.

ex.en: That sort of romantic attitude cuts no ice with moneymen.
ex.zh: 那种罗曼蒂克的态度对金融家们不起作用。

d: n. 冰；冰块；冰冻甜食，刨冰；溜冰场；钻石，珠宝；（态度，表情）冰冷；一份冰淇淋
v. 在（糕饼上）加糖霜；冷却，冰镇；确保（胜利等）；杀死；结冰；长射（冰球）过全场越过对方球门线
adj. 冰的
【名】 （Ice）（英）艾斯，（法）伊斯（人名）

e.en: Heating is the process of heating a building or room, considered especially from the point of view of how much this costs.

ex.en: We wanted to reduce the cost of heating and air-conditioning.
ex.zh: 我们想减少供暖与空调的开支。

e.en: Heating is the system and equipment that is used to heat a building.

ex.en: I wish I knew how to turn on the heating.
ex.zh: 要是我知道如何打开暖气装置就好了。

d: n. （尤指从经济角度考虑的）供暖，暖气供应；供暖系统，暖气设备
v. 加热，使变暖；激起，使激动（heat 的现在分词形式）
n. 冰冻圈，冰雪圈，冰冻层（地球表面水以固态形式存在的圈层，包括海冰、冰川、积雪、冻土等）

e.en: Something that is warm has some heat but not enough to be hot.

ex.en: Wheat is grown in places which have cold winters and warm, dry summers.
ex.zh: 小麦生长在冬季寒冷、夏季温暖干燥的地方。

ex.en: Because it was warm, David wore only a white cotton shirt.
ex.zh: 因为天气暖和，戴维只穿了一件白色棉衫。
