e.en: Warm clothes and blankets are made of a material such as wool that protects you from the cold.

ex.en: They have been forced to sleep in the open without food or warm clothing.
ex.zh: 他们被迫睡在露天里，没有食物也没有保暖的衣服。

e.en: 保暖地

ex.en: Remember to wrap up warmly on cold days.
ex.zh: 记得天冷时穿暖和些。

e.en: Warm colours have red or yellow in them rather than blue or green, and make you feel comfortable and relaxed. 暖色调的;

ex.en: The basement hallway is painted a warm yellow.
ex.zh: 地下室的走廊被涂成暖色调的黄色。

d: n. 加温，变暖，气温升高（常构成 global warming，即全球变暖）；（关系）升温，缓和；（Warming）（丹、瑞、美）瓦明（人名）
adj. 让人感到温暖的，给人温暖感的
v. （使）变暖，加温（常与 up 连用：warming up，预热、加热）；（使关系）升温，变友好；（对某人）产生好感，（对某事）开始感兴趣（warm 的现在分词）

e.en: If you overshoot a place that you want to get to, you go past it by mistake.

ex.en: The plane apparently overshot the runway after landing.
ex.zh: 飞机在着陆后明显越过了跑道。

e.en: If a government or organization overshoots its budget, it spends more than it had planned to.

ex.en: The government usually overshot its original spending target.
ex.zh: 该政府经常超过它原本的支出目标。

e.en: Overshoot is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the 100 million dollar overshoot in the cost of building the hospital.
ex.zh: ...该医院建设成本中1亿美元的超支。

d: vt. 超越，超过，突破（目标、限额、预算等）；越过，冲过（目标、地点等）；打过头；把……做过头
vi. 射击越标；（飞机）滑出跑道；行动过火，做得过头
n. 超出部分，超额量；超越目标；行动过火；（工程、电子）超调量，过冲

e.en: A sheet is a large rectangular piece of cotton or other cloth that you sleep on or cover yourself with in a bed. 床单;

ex.en: Once a week, a maid changes the sheets.
ex.zh: 女仆每个星期换一次床单。

e.en: A sheet of paper is a rectangular piece of paper. (一) 张 (纸)

ex.en: ...a sheet of newspaper.
ex.zh: …一张报纸。

e.en: You can use sheet to refer to a piece of paper which gives information about something. (一份)

ex.en: ...information sheets on each country in the world.
ex.zh: …有关世界各国的情报资料。

e.en: A sheet of glass, metal, or wood is a large, flat, thin piece of it. (一) 块 (玻璃、金属或木头等)

ex.en: ...a cracked sheet of glass.
ex.zh: …一块裂开的玻璃。

ex.en: Overhead cranes were lifting giant sheets of steel.
ex.zh: 高架起重机正吊起一块块巨大的钢材。

d: n. 床单，被单（纺）；片材，板片（材）；纸张；覆盖层（以上均为 sheet 的复数）；（Sheets）希茨（英语姓氏）
v. 覆盖；铺床单；使成大片；（雨、雪等）倾泻而下（以上均为 sheet 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: When a solid substance melts or when you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated. 使融化;

ex.en: The snow had melted, but the lake was still frozen solid.
ex.zh: 雪已经融化了，但湖面仍然冻得结结实实。

ex.en: Meanwhile, melt the white chocolate in a bowl suspended over simmering water.
ex.zh: 同时，把碗架在快烧开的水上，融化碗里的白巧克力。

e.en: If something such as your feelings melt, they suddenly disappear and you no longer feel them.

ex.en: His anxiety about the outcome melted, only to return later.
ex.zh: 他对结果的焦虑消失了，但过后又来了。

e.en: Melt away means the same as . 同(melt)

ex.en: When he heard these words, Scot felt his inner doubts melt away.
ex.zh: 听到这些话，斯科特觉得内心的疑虑消失了。

e.en: If a person or thing melts into something such as darkness or a crowd of people, they become difficult to see, for example because they are moving away from you or are the same colour as the background. 消失 (在黑暗、人群等中)

ex.en: The youths dispersed and melted into the darkness.
ex.zh: 年轻人们散开了，消失在夜色中。

d: adj. 令人爱怜的，让人同情的
v. （使）融化，（使）熔化；消散，消失；使心软，使同情（melt 的现在分词）

e.en: An emission of something such as gas or radiation is the release of it into the atmosphere.

ex.en: The emission of gases such as carbon dioxide should be stabilized at their present level.
ex.zh: 二氧化碳之类气体的排放应该被控制在目前的水平上。

d: n. 排放；排放物；辐射；发行（emission 的复数）

e.en: The temperature of something is a measure of how hot or cold it is.

ex.en: Winter closes in and the temperature drops below freezing.
ex.zh: 冬天来临，气温降至冰点以下。

e.en: Your temperature is the temperature of your body. A normal temperature is about 98.6° Fahrenheit.

ex.en: His temperature continued to rise and the cough worsened until Tania finally persuaded him to see a doctor.
ex.zh: 他的体温持续升高且咳嗽加重，直到塔妮娅最终说服了他去看医生。

e.en: You can use temperature to talk about the feelings and emotions that people have in particular situations. (特定场合的)

ex.en: There's also been a noticeable rise in the political temperature.
ex.zh: 政治气氛也明显升温。

e.en: If you are running a temperature or if you have a temperature, your temperature is higher than it should be.

ex.en: He began to run an extremely high temperature.
ex.zh: 他开始发严重高烧。

d: n. 温度，气温（temperature 的复数）

e.en: Polar means near the North or South Poles.

ex.en: ...the rigours of life in the polar regions.
ex.zh: …极地的艰苦生活。

ex.en: There was a period of excessive warmth which melted some of the polar ice.
ex.zh: 有段时期温度过高，融化了极地的部分冰层。

e.en: Polar is used to describe things that are completely opposite in character, quality, or type. (性格、质量或类型)

ex.en: The nomads' lifestyle was the polar opposite of collectivization.
ex.zh: 游牧民的生活方式同集体化的生活方式刚好相反。

d: adj. 极地的，来自极地的；截然不同的；磁极的；（天体）极性的，极地的；（细胞，器官，身体部分）极的；（液体，尤指溶剂）由偶极矩分子组成的；（固体）离子的；（几何）（球体）轴极的
n. （几何）极线；极光双子星
【名】 （Polar）（德、西）波拉尔（人名）

e.en: Permafrost is land that is permanently frozen to a great depth.

d: n. （地质、地理）多年冻土，永久冻土，永冻土

e.en: Something that is long-term has continued for a long time or will continue for a long time in the future.

ex.en: They want their parents to have access to affordable long-term care.
ex.zh: 他们希望他们的父母可以得到负担得起的长期看护。

e.en: When you talk about what happens in the long term, you are talking about what happens over a long period of time, either in the future or after a particular event.

ex.en: In the long term the company hopes to open in Moscow and other major cities.
ex.zh: 从长远来看，该公司希望能在莫斯科和其它主要城市开展业务。

d: adj. 长期的，长远的
n. （the long term）长期，长远（in the long term 从长远来看）
n. （Kirkham）人名；（英）柯卡姆

e.en: A policy is a set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions, especially in politics, economics, or business.

ex.en: ...plans that include changes in foreign policy and economic reforms.
ex.zh: …包括外交政策调整和经济改革的计划。

e.en: An official organization's policy on a particular issue or toward a country is their attitude and actions regarding that issue or country.

ex.en: ...the organization's future policy toward South Africa.
ex.zh: …该组织未来的南非政策。

ex.en: ...the government's policy on repatriation.
ex.zh: …该政府的遣返政策。

e.en: An insurance policy is a document that shows the agreement that you have made with an insurance company.

ex.en: You are advised to read the small print of homeowner and car insurance policies.
ex.zh: 建议你读一下房主保险单和汽车保险单上的小号印刷字。

d: n. 政策，方针，策略；保险单（policy 的复数）；封闭的庭院

e.en: Snow consists of a lot of soft white pieces of frozen water that fall from the sky in cold weather.

ex.en: Six inches of snow blocked roads.
ex.zh: 六英寸的大雪阻塞了道路。

e.en: When it snows, snow falls from the sky.

ex.en: It had been snowing all night.
ex.zh: 整个晚上一直在下雪。

d: n. 雪，积雪；降雪，一场雪；下雪天；（因信号差出现在电视屏幕的）“雪花”干扰；似雪的菜肴；似雪的冷冻气体；可卡因
v. 下雪，飘雪；（用花言巧语）蒙骗，使相信；使洒落；使变白
【名】 （Snow）斯诺（人名）

e.en: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly. 破坏;

ex.en: He maliciously damaged a car with a baseball bat.
ex.zh: 他用棒球棍恶意地损坏了一辆汽车。

e.en: To damage something means to cause it to become less good, pleasant, or successful. 损害;

ex.en: ...the electoral chaos that damaged Florida's reputation.
ex.zh: …损害佛罗里达州声誉的选举骚乱。

e.en: 有损害性的

ex.en: The weakened currency could have damaging effects for the economy.
ex.zh: 货币贬值可能会对经济造成破坏性的影响。

e.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to an object. 破坏;

ex.en: The blast had serious effects with quite extensive damage to the house.
ex.zh: 爆炸影响严重，对房屋造成了大面积破坏。

d: n. （有形的）损坏，损失；损害，伤害；损害赔偿金；费用，代价
v. 损坏，损害；对……造成坏影响

e.en: a game in which each player writes down a part of a story, folds over the paper, and passes it on to another player who continues the story. After several stages, the resulting (nonsensical) stories are read out 连环叙事游戏; 每位玩家写下故事的一部分,将纸对折,传给下一位玩家继续叙写故事,

d: n. 后果，结果，影响（consequence 的复数）；（英国英语）连环叙事游戏（每人写故事的一部分，将纸折起传给下一位续写，最后朗读合写的故事）

e.en: If a change is irreversible, things cannot be changed back to the way they were before.

ex.en: She could suffer irreversible brain damage if she is not treated within seven days.
ex.zh: 如果在7天内得不到治疗，她的大脑有可能会受到不可恢复的损害。

d: adj. 不可挽回的，无法逆转的；不能治愈的，不能挽救的
n. 格陵兰（北美东北的一大岛名，属丹麦）

e.en: The temperature of something is a measure of how hot or cold it is.

ex.en: Winter closes in and the temperature drops below freezing.
ex.zh: 冬天来临，气温降至冰点以下。

e.en: Your temperature is the temperature of your body. A normal temperature is about 98.6° Fahrenheit.

ex.en: His temperature continued to rise and the cough worsened until Tania finally persuaded him to see a doctor.
ex.zh: 他的体温持续升高且咳嗽加重，直到塔妮娅最终说服了他去看医生。

e.en: You can use temperature to talk about the feelings and emotions that people have in particular situations. (特定场合的)

ex.en: There's also been a noticeable rise in the political temperature.
ex.zh: 政治气氛也明显升温。

e.en: If you are running a temperature or if you have a temperature, your temperature is higher than it should be.

ex.en: He began to run an extremely high temperature.
ex.zh: 他开始发严重高烧。

d: n. 温度，气温；体温；发烧；热烈程度，情绪激烈程度

e.en: A period is a length of time.

ex.en: This crisis might last for a long period of time.
ex.zh: 此次危机可能会持续很长一段时间。

ex.en: ...a period of a few months.
ex.zh: …几个月的时间。

e.en: A period in the life of a person, organization, or society is a length of time that is remembered for a particular situation or activity. (个人、组织或社会的)

ex.en: ...a period of economic good health and expansion.
ex.zh: …一段经济健康发展和扩张时期。

ex.en: He went through a period of wanting to be accepted.
ex.zh: 他经历了一段渴望得到接受的时期。

e.en: A particular length of time in history is sometimes called a period. For example, you can talk about the Civil War period or the Prohibition period in the U.S. (历史)

ex.en: The novel is set in the Roman period.
ex.zh: 该小说的背景是罗马时期。

ex.en: No reference to their existence appears in any literature of the period.
ex.zh: 该时期的任何文献中都没有提及他们的存在。

e.en: Period costumes, furniture, and instruments were made at an earlier time in history, or look as if they were made then.
e.zh: 具特定历史时期特点的

ex.en: The characters were dressed in full period costume.
ex.zh: 剧中人物全都身着具有时代特色的服装。

d: n. 一段时间，时期；（人生或国家历史的）阶段，时代；（地质年代划分的）纪；课时，节；（练习、训练或学习的）时段；（妇女的）月经，经期；（体育比赛的）局；句号，句点；（物理）（振动或循环的）周期；（天文）自转（或公转）周期；（数学）（周期函数的）周期；（化学）周期元素；（修辞）完整句；（乐）乐段，乐节
adj. 具有某个时代特征的
adv. 到此为止，不再说了

e.en: an insurrection or rebellion; revolt
increasing in rank, status, or reputation (级别、地位或声誉的)

ex.en: a rising young politician

e.en: approaching the age of; nearly 接近于某一年龄地;

ex.en: she's rising 40

d: adj. （级别、地位或声誉）提高的；升起的，增加的，向上斜的；接近（某一年龄）的；（占星）星位的，运星的；（纹章）（鸟）展翅欲飞状的
n. 造反，起义；上升
prep. 接近，将近，即将
v. （数字、 数量、价值）增加，（质量）提高；升起，达到较高水平（或位置）；（尤指从坐姿）起身，站起（rise 的现在分词）

e.en: When ice, snow, or something else that is frozen thaws, it melts. (冰雪等)

ex.en: It's so cold the snow doesn't get a chance to thaw.
ex.zh: 天气太冷了，积雪都没机会融化。

e.en: A thaw is a period of warmer weather when snow and ice melt, usually at the end of winter. (通常指冬末的)

ex.en: We slogged through the mud of an early spring thaw.
ex.zh: 我们在初春解冻期的泥泞里艰难跋涉。

e.en: When you thaw frozen food or when it thaws, you leave it in a place where it can reach room temperature so that it is ready for use.

ex.en: Always thaw pastry thoroughly.
ex.zh: 一定要让油酥面团完全解冻。

e.en: Thaw out means the same as .

ex.en: Thaw it out completely before reheating in a saucepan.
ex.zh: 将之完全解冻后，放到平底锅里重新加热。

d: v. （使）（冰雪）融化；（使）（冷冻食品）解冻；使（身体等）变得暖起来；变得友好，变得缓和
n. 解冻时期，融化季节；（敌对国家之间）关系缓和
【名】 （Thaw）（美）陶（人名）

e.en: If you overshoot a place that you want to get to, you go past it by mistake.

ex.en: The plane apparently overshot the runway after landing.
ex.zh: 飞机在着陆后明显越过了跑道。

e.en: If a government or organization overshoots its budget, it spends more than it had planned to.

ex.en: The government usually overshot its original spending target.
ex.zh: 该政府经常超过它原本的支出目标。

e.en: Overshoot is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the 100 million dollar overshoot in the cost of building the hospital.
ex.zh: ...该医院建设成本中1亿美元的超支。

d: v. overshoot 的现在分词：越过，驶过（港口、跑道等）
n. 超出规定，超支；（经济学、金融学、控制工程、电子学等）超调，过冲

e.en: You can describe someone's behaviour as threatening when you think that they are trying to harm you. (行为)

ex.en: People who engage in threatening behaviour should expect to be arrested.
ex.zh: 有威胁行为的人应该被逮捕。

d: adj. 威胁（性）的，恐吓（性）的；（天气状况）险恶的，（海）险恶的；凶兆的
v. 威胁，恐吓；危及，对……构成威胁；预示凶兆，有……危险（threaten 的现在分词）

e.en: You use possibly to indicate that you are not sure whether something is true or might happen. 可能地 (表示没把握)

ex.en: Exercise will not only lower blood pressure but possibly protect against heart attacks.
ex.zh: 运动不仅会降低血压，而且能防止心脏病发作。

ex.en: They were casually dressed; possibly students.
ex.zh: 他们穿着随意，可能是学生。

e.en: You use possibly to emphasize that you are surprised, puzzled, or shocked by something that you have seen or heard. 可能地 (强调惊讶、迷惑或震惊)

ex.en: It was the most unexpected piece of news one could possibly imagine.
ex.zh: 可以想像，这是最出人意料的一则消息。

e.en: You use possibly to emphasize that someone has tried their hardest to do something, or has done it as well as they can. (最大)

ex.en: They've done everything they can possibly think of.
ex.zh: 凡是可能想得到的，他们都已经做了。

e.en: You use possibly to emphasize that something definitely cannot happen or definitely cannot be done. (完全不)

ex.en: No I really can't possibly answer that!
ex.zh: 不，我真地根本不可能回答那个问题。

d: adv. 可能，或许；（用于强调惊讶或震惊）怎么，究竟；怎么可能，绝不可能（用于否定句，表强调）；能不能，能否（用于礼貌地请求）；尽量，尽可能

e.en: The tip of something long and narrow is the end of it.

ex.en: The sleeves covered his hands to the tips of his fingers.
ex.zh: 衣袖遮住了他的手，一直盖到他的手指尖。

e.en: If you tip an object or part of your body or if it tips, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

ex.en: He leaned away from her, and she had to tip her head back to see him.
ex.zh: 他侧身避开她，她只得向后侧过头来看他。

e.en: If you tip something somewhere, you pour it there.

ex.en: Tip the vegetables into a bowl.
ex.zh: 把这些蔬菜倒进一个碗里。

e.en: If you tip someone such as a waiter in a restaurant, you give them some money in order to thank them for their services.

ex.en: We usually tip 18-20%.
ex.zh: 我们通常付18-20%的小费。

d: n. 倾斜；倾倒；（英国英语）倒垃圾；给小费（的做法）；tipping point（临界点，引爆点）；Tipping（蒂平，人名）
v. （使）倾斜；倾倒；轻触；给小费（tip 的现在分词）

e.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

ex.en: There is widespread support for the new proposals.
ex.zh: 这些新提案得到广泛的支持。

d: adj. 普遍的，广泛的

e.en: If something exists or happens worldwide, it exists or happens throughout the world.

ex.en: His books have sold more than 20 million copies worldwide.
ex.zh: 他的书在全世界卖出了两千多万本。

e.en: Worldwide is also an adjective.

ex.en: Today, doctors are fearing a worldwide epidemic.
ex.zh: 如今，医生们在担心一次世界性的流行。

d: adj. 世界范围的，全世界的
adv. 在全世界，在世界各地

e.en: An abrupt change or action is very sudden, often in a way that is unpleasant.

ex.en: Rosie's idyllic world came to an abrupt end when her parents' marriage broke up.
ex.zh: 当她的父母婚姻破裂后，罗茜的田园诗一般的世界骤然结束了。

e.en: 骤然地

ex.en: He stopped abruptly and looked my way.
ex.zh: 他突然停住，向我看了过来。

e.en: Someone who is abrupt speaks in a rude, unfriendly way.

ex.en: He was abrupt to the point of rudeness.
ex.zh: 他唐突到了无礼的地步。

e.en: 唐突地

ex.en: "Good night, then," she said abruptly.
ex.zh: “那么，晚安”，她唐突地说道。

d: adj. 突然的，意外的；粗鲁的，唐突的，（言语）生硬的；险峻的，陡峭的；（讲话或写作风格）不流畅的，不连贯的
abbr. 联合国环境规划署（United Nations Environment Programme）

e.en: If the process or rate of something accelerates or if something accelerates it, it gets faster and faster. 使加速;

ex.en: Growth will accelerate to 2.9 percent next year.
ex.zh: 增长明年将加快到2.9%。

e.en: When a moving vehicle accelerates, it goes faster and faster.

ex.en: Suddenly the car accelerated.
ex.zh: 突然车加速了。

d: adj. 加速的，促进的；催化的
v. accelerate 的现在分词或动名词；加速，促进

e.en: to convert into or become acid 使酸化;

d: adj. 酸化的
v. [化学]酸化；使酸化（acidify 的 ing 形式）
n. 酸化，成酸性；使……发酸
n. 数据分析，分析；（化学，数）分析学，解析学

e.en: (in the European Alps) an area of pasture above the valley bottom but below the mountain peaks (欧洲阿尔卑斯山中)

d: n. 阿尔卑斯山脉；alp 的复数形式，指高山或阿尔卑斯山区的山地牧场
n. 适应性，适应能力；可变性；适合性

e.en: The Antarctic is the area around the South Pole.

d: n. (the Antarctic) 南极洲，南极地区
adj. 南极的，南极地带的

e.en: A planet's atmosphere is the layer of air or other gases around it. (行星的)

ex.en: The shuttle Columbia will re-enter Earth's atmosphere tomorrow morning.
ex.zh: 哥伦比亚号航天飞机将在明天上午重进地球大气层。

e.en: The atmosphere of a place is the air that you breathe there. (某地的)

ex.en: These gases pollute the atmosphere of towns and cities.
ex.zh: 这些气体污染城镇的空气。

e.en: The atmosphere of a place is the general impression that you get of it.

ex.en: There's still an atmosphere of great hostility and tension in the city.
ex.zh: 在这座城市里依然有一种极其敌对和紧张的气氛。

e.en: If a place or an event has atmosphere, it is interesting.

ex.en: The old harbour is still full of atmosphere and well worth visiting.
ex.zh: 旧港口依然充满神韵，很值得参观。

d: n. （包围地球或其他行星的）大气，大气层；（房间或其他场所内的）空气；气氛，环境；情调，感染力

e.en: The author of a piece of writing is the person who wrote it.

ex.en: ...Jill Phillips, author of the book "Give Your Child Music."
ex.zh: …吉尔·菲利浦斯，《把音乐给你的孩子》一书的作者。

e.en: An author is a person whose job is writing books.

ex.en: Haruki Murakami is Japan's best-selling author.
ex.zh: 村上春树是日本的畅销书作家。

d: n. 作者，著者；作家；发起者，创始人；作品
v. 撰写，写作；发起，创造

e.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow that falls down the side of a mountain.

d: n. （水文、地理）雪崩（avalanche 的名词复数）；（比喻义）雪崩般突然大量涌现的事物（常作 avalanches of）
v. （水文、地理）发生雪崩；如雪崩般崩落或大量涌来（avalanche 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Something that is brief lasts for only a short time.

ex.en: She once made a brief appearance on television.
ex.zh: 她曾在电视上短暂露面。

e.en: A brief speech or piece of writing does not contain too many words or details. (讲话、文章)

ex.en: In a brief statement, he concentrated entirely on international affairs.
ex.zh: 在一个简短的陈述中,他完全集中在了国际事务上。

e.en: If you are brief, you say what you want to say in as few words as possible. (说话)

ex.en: Now please be brief – my time is valuable.
ex.zh: 现在请长话短说–我的时间很宝贵。

e.en: You can describe a period of time as brief if you want to emphasize that it is very short.

ex.en: For a few brief minutes we forgot the anxiety and anguish.
ex.zh: 短短的几分钟,我们忘却了忧伤和痛苦。

d: adj. 短暂的；简短的；（衣服）很短的
v. 给……指示，向……介绍情况；向（辩护律师）提供案情摘要
n. 指示，任务简介；摘要，概要；短内裤（briefs）；辩护状；辩护律师；委托辩护
【名】 （Brief）（英）布里夫（人名）

e.en: The border between two countries or regions is the dividing line between them. Sometimes the border also refers to the land close to this line. 边界;

ex.en: They fled across the border.
ex.zh: 他们越过边界逃走了。

ex.en: Soldiers had temporarily closed the border between the two countries.
ex.zh: 士兵们已暂时封闭了两国的边界。

e.en: A country that borders another country, a sea, or a river is next to it.

ex.en: ...the European and Arab countries bordering the Mediterranean.
ex.zh: …地中海沿岸的欧洲国家和阿拉伯国家。

e.en: Border on means the same as .

ex.en: Both republics border on the Black Sea.
ex.zh: 这两个共和国都与黑海毗邻。

e.en: A border is a strip or band around the edge of something.

ex.en: ...pillowcases trimmed with a hand-crocheted border.
ex.zh: …镶有一道手工钩制花边的枕套。

d: n. 国境，边界；镶边，包边；狭长花坛，花带
v. 接壤，毗邻；环绕，沿……的边缘；近似，相像
【名】 （Border）（英）博德（人名）

e.en: The cause of an event, usually a bad event, is the thing that makes it happen. 起因;

ex.en: Smoking is the biggest preventable cause of death and disease.
ex.zh: 吸烟是造成不必要疾病和死亡的最大原因。

e.en: A cause is an aim or principle which a group of people supports or is fighting for. 奋斗目标;

ex.en: Refusing to have one leader has not helped the cause.
ex.zh: 拒绝接受领导无益于该事业。

e.en: To cause something, usually something bad, means to make it happen.

ex.en: The insecticide used on some weeds can cause health problems.
ex.zh: 喷洒在野草上的杀虫剂会引发各种健康问题。

ex.en: This was a genuine mistake, but it did cause me some worry.
ex.zh: 这纯属失误，但它确实令我有些不安。

e.en: If you have cause for a particular feeling or action, you have good reasons for feeling it or doing it.

ex.en: Only a few people can find any cause for celebration.
ex.zh: 只有少数人能找到庆祝的理由。

d: n. 原因；事业；理由
v. 引起

e.en: The circulation of a newspaper or magazine is the number of copies that are sold each time it is produced.

ex.en: The Daily News once had the highest circulation of any daily in the country.
ex.zh: 《每日新闻报》一度在该国所有日报中拥有最高发行量。

e.en: Your circulation is the movement of blood through your body.

ex.en: Anyone with heart, lung, or circulation problems should seek medical advice before flying.
ex.zh: 任何有心、肺或血液循环问题的人都应该在飞行前寻求医生建议。

e.en: If something such as money is in circulation, it is being used by the public. If something is out of circulation or has been withdrawn from circulation, it is no longer available for use by the public. 流通/

ex.en: The supply of money in circulation was drastically reduced overnight.
ex.zh: 一夜之间流通货币的供应就急剧减少了。

ex.en: ...a society like America, with perhaps 180 million guns in circulation.
ex.zh: …像美国这样的社会里，可能有1.8亿支枪在流通之中。

d: n. 发行量，销售量；血液循环；流传，流通；参加社交活动，交际；环流，循环；（图书的）借出

e.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

ex.en: Larry had concluded that he had no choice but to accept Paul's words as the truth.
ex.zh: 拉里断定他别无选择，只能相信保罗所说为实。

ex.en: So what can we conclude from this debate?
ex.zh: 那么从这场辩论中我们能推断出什么呢？

e.en: When you conclude, you say the last thing that you are going to say. 结束 (说话)

ex.en: "It's a waste of time," he concluded.
ex.zh: “这是浪费时间，”他最后说道。

e.en: When something concludes, or when you conclude it, you end it. 使…结束;

ex.en: The evening concluded with dinner and speeches.
ex.zh: 这个夜晚以晚宴和演讲告一段落。

e.en: If one person or group concludes an agreement, such as a treaty or business deal, with another, they arrange it. You can also say that two people or groups conclude an agreement. 达成 (协议)

ex.en: Mexico and the Philippines have both concluded agreements with their commercial bank creditors.
ex.zh: 墨西哥和菲律宾双方都与他们的商业银行债权人达成了协议。

d: v. 断定，推断出；结束，终止；达成，做成，完成；决定

e.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

ex.en: ...advertisements aimed at curbing the spread of AIDS.
ex.zh: …旨在抑制爱滋病蔓延的广告。

e.en: Curb is also a noun. 控制;

ex.en: He called for much stricter curbs on immigration.
ex.zh: 他呼吁对移民实行更为严格的限制。

e.en: If you curb an emotion or your behaviour, you keep it under control. 控制 (脾气、行为等)

ex.en: He curbed his temper.
ex.zh: 他控制住了自己的脾气。

e.en: a swelling on the leg of a horse, below the point of the hock, usually caused by a sprain (马腿上由扭伤导致的)

d: v. 控制，抑制；勒住（马）
n. 控制，抑制；路缘，马路牙子；（马的跗关节后部因扭伤韧带引起的）硬瘤

e.en: If people or vehicles converge on a place, they move toward it from different directions. (人或车辆等)

ex.en: Hundreds of tractors will converge on the capital.
ex.zh: 成百上千的拖拉机将向首都聚集。

e.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place. (道路、江河等)

ex.en: As they flow south, the five rivers converge.
ex.zh: 这5条河向南流，最终汇合在一起。

d: v. （使）汇聚，集中；（观点、目标）趋同；（数）收敛

e.en: If you cross something such as a room, a road, or an area of land or water, you move or travel to the other side of it. If you cross to a place, you move or travel over a room, road, or area of land or water in order to reach that place. 穿过;

ex.en: She was partly to blame for failing to look as she crossed the road.
ex.zh: 她横穿马路时没有看车，应承担部分责任。

ex.en: Egan crossed to the drinks cabinet and poured a Scotch.
ex.zh: 伊根穿过去，来到酒柜旁，倒了一杯苏格兰威士忌。

e.en: A road, railway, or bridge that crosses an area of land or water passes over it.

ex.en: The road crosses the river half a mile outside the town.
ex.zh: 这条路横跨城外半英里处的那条河。

e.en: If someone or something crosses a limit or boundary, for example, the limit of acceptable behaviour, they go beyond it. 越过 (可以被容忍的限度)

ex.en: I normally never write into magazines but Mr. Stubbs has finally crossed the line.
ex.zh: 我通常是从不给杂志写信的，但斯塔布斯先生最后太出格了。

e.en: If an expression crosses someone's face, it appears briefly on their face.

ex.en: Berg tilts his head and a mischievous look crosses his face.
ex.zh: 伯格歪着脑袋，一种淘气的表情在他的脸上一闪而过。

d: adj. 交叉的；划掉的；十字形的；（支票）划线的
v. 交叉；越过（cross 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: CEO is an abbreviation for .

d: abbr. 首席执行官；执行总裁（chief executive officer）

e.en: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly. 破坏;

ex.en: He maliciously damaged a car with a baseball bat.
ex.zh: 他用棒球棍恶意地损坏了一辆汽车。

e.en: To damage something means to cause it to become less good, pleasant, or successful. 损害;

ex.en: ...the electoral chaos that damaged Florida's reputation.
ex.zh: …损害佛罗里达州声誉的选举骚乱。

e.en: 有损害性的

ex.en: The weakened currency could have damaging effects for the economy.
ex.zh: 货币贬值可能会对经济造成破坏性的影响。

e.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to an object. 破坏;

ex.en: The blast had serious effects with quite extensive damage to the house.
ex.zh: 爆炸影响严重，对房屋造成了大面积破坏。

d: adj. 被损坏的
v. 损害；伤害；破坏（damage 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you cut something, you use a knife or a similar tool to divide it into pieces, or to mark it or damage it. If you cut a shape or a hole in something, you make the shape or hole by using a knife or similar tool. 切;

ex.en: Mrs. Haines stood nearby, holding scissors to cut a ribbon.
ex.zh: 海恩斯太太站在旁边，拿着剪刀剪缎带。

ex.en: Cut the tomatoes in half vertically.
ex.zh: 把西红柿竖着切成两半。

e.en: Cut is also a noun.

ex.en: Carefully make a cut in the shell with a small serrated knife.
ex.zh: 用有锯齿的小刀小心地在壳上切个口。

e.en: If you cut yourself or cut a part of your body, you accidentally injure yourself on a sharp object so that you bleed.

ex.en: Johnson cut himself shaving.
ex.zh: 约翰逊刮胡子时割伤了自己。

ex.en: I started to cry because I cut my finger.
ex.zh: 因为割破了自己的手指，我哭了起来。

e.en: Cut is also a noun.

ex.en: He had sustained a cut on his left eyebrow.
ex.zh: 他的左眉留下了一处伤口。

d: v. 切，割，剪；削减，缩减；删节，删减；停止，切断；抄近路，穿过；切（牌），倒（牌）；灌制（唱片），录制（讲话）；划伤，割伤；剪裁；开始长（新牙）；逃学，逃课；停止做不好的事情；切下；切开，把……切碎；凿，挖，刻；剪短，修剪；（割断束缚物）使脱身，使松开；可用于切割；能被切割；剪切（计算机文档）； 剪辑，剪接；停止拍片（或录音、录像）；切换画面；（从感情上）伤害；（与另一条线）相交；冲淡，稀释；划分（区域）；砍（植物）；开除，除名；快速行进；突然转向；插队；（直截了当地）处理；去除（污垢、油污等）；削（球）；符合要求（cut it）
n. 切下的肉块；份额，一份利润；（开出的）通道；伤口，划口；开口，破口；（数量或尺寸上的）削减；理发，发型；款式，式样；删剪，删节；剪辑；（录制的）乐曲；精简，淘汰（如参赛人员）；切，割，削；不理睬，伤人的话（或举动）
adj. 缩减的；割下的；雕过的；阉割过的

e.en: To damage an object means to break it, spoil it physically, or stop it from working properly. 破坏;

ex.en: He maliciously damaged a car with a baseball bat.
ex.zh: 他用棒球棍恶意地损坏了一辆汽车。

e.en: To damage something means to cause it to become less good, pleasant, or successful. 损害;

ex.en: ...the electoral chaos that damaged Florida's reputation.
ex.zh: …损害佛罗里达州声誉的选举骚乱。

e.en: 有损害性的

ex.en: The weakened currency could have damaging effects for the economy.
ex.zh: 货币贬值可能会对经济造成破坏性的影响。

e.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to an object. 破坏;

ex.en: The blast had serious effects with quite extensive damage to the house.
ex.zh: 爆炸影响严重，对房屋造成了大面积破坏。

d: n. （法律）损害赔偿金，赔偿金；伤害，损伤（damage 的复数）
v. 损害，伤害；毁坏（damage 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If something is dangerous, it is able or likely to hurt or harm you.

ex.en: It's a dangerous stretch of road.
ex.zh: 这是一截危险路段。

ex.en: ...dangerous drugs.
ex.zh: …危险的药品。

e.en: 危险地

ex.en: He is dangerously ill.
ex.zh: 他病得很重。

d: adj. 危险的，有威胁的

e.en: If something is deadly, it is likely or able to cause someone's death, or has already caused someone's death. 致命的;

ex.en: He was acquitted on charges of assault with a deadly weapon.
ex.zh: 他用凶器伤人的罪名不成立。

ex.en: ...a deadly disease currently affecting dolphins.
ex.zh: …目前影响海豚的一种致命疾病。

e.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as deadly, you mean that they will do or say anything to get what they want, without caring about other people. 不择手段的;

ex.en: The Duchess levelled a deadly look at Nikko.
ex.zh: 公爵夫人无所顾忌地瞪了尼克一眼。

e.en: A deadly situation has unpleasant or dangerous consequences.

ex.en: ...the deadly combination of low expectations and low achievement.
ex.zh: …低期望值和低成就的不良结合。

e.en: You can use deadly to emphasize that something has a particular quality, especially an unpleasant or undesirable quality.

ex.en: Broadcast news was accurate and reliable but deadly dull.
ex.zh: 新闻广播准确、可靠，但极其枯燥。

d: adj. 致命的；极度的；乏味枯燥的；死一般的；阴险毒辣的，冷酷无情的；极有害的，破坏性的；（运动员或其动作）极富技巧性的，极难防御的；极好的，卓越的
adv. 极其；死一般

e.en: You use degree to indicate the extent to which something happens or is the case, or the amount which something is felt.

ex.en: These man-made barriers will ensure a very high degree of protection for several hundred years.
ex.zh: 这些人造屏障将会确保几百年的高度保护。

ex.en: Recent presidents have used television, as well as radio, with varying degrees of success.
ex.zh: 新近的总统们已经利用了电视和收音机，取得了不同程度的成功。

e.en: If something has a degree of a particular quality, it has a small but significant amount of that quality.
A degree is a unit of measurement that is used to measure temperatures. It is often written as °, for example, 23°. (指温度)

ex.en: It's over 80 degrees outside.
ex.zh: 外面超过80度。

e.en: A degree is a unit of measurement that is used to measure angles, and also longitude and latitude. It is often written as °, for example, 23°. (指角度、经纬度)

ex.en: It was pointing outward at an angle of 45 degrees.
ex.zh: 它以45度角指向外侧。

d: n. 度，度数（温度单位）；（角的）度，度数；学位课程，学位；程度；音级；次，次数；（形容词或副词的）级；共济会职务；社会地位，官衔

e.en: When there is disruption of an event, system, or process, it is prevented from continuing or operating in a normal way. 妨碍;

ex.en: The plan was designed to ensure disruption to business was kept to a minimum.
ex.zh: 该计划旨在确保对业务的妨碍保持在最低限度。

d: n. 扰乱，中断

e.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same. 等量物;

ex.en: Mr. Li's pay is the equivalent of about $80 a month.
ex.zh: 李先生的报酬大约等于每月80美元。

e.en: Equivalent is also an adjective. 等量的;

ex.en: If they want to change an item in the budget, they will have to propose equivalent cuts elsewhere.
ex.zh: 如果他们想要改变预算中的一个款项，必须得提出其他等值的削减。

e.en: The equivalent of someone or something is a person or thing that has the same function in a different place, time, or system.

ex.en: ...the Red Cross emblem, and its equivalent in Muslim countries, the Red Crescent.
ex.zh: …红十字徽章、及其在穆斯林国家对应物的红新月。

e.en: Equivalent is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...a decrease of 10% in property investment compared with the equivalent period in 1991.
ex.zh: …房产投资相比1991年同期10％的降幅。

d: adj. 等同的，等效的
n. 对等的人（或事物），对应的人（或事物）；当量（equivalent weight）

e.en: If you say that someone or something disappears, you mean that you can no longer see them, usually because you or they have changed position.

ex.en: The black car drove away from them and disappeared.
ex.zh: 黑色的小汽车驶离了他们便消失了。

e.en: If someone or something disappears, they go away or are taken away somewhere where nobody can find them.

ex.en: ...a Japanese woman who disappeared thirteen years ago.
ex.zh: …一位13年前失踪的日本妇女。

e.en: If something disappears, it stops existing or happening.

ex.en: The immediate threat of the past has disappeared and the security situation in Europe has significantly improved.
ex.zh: 过去的直接威胁不复存在了，欧洲的安全状况有重大改善。

d: v. 消失，不见；失踪（disappear 的现在分词，与 be 连用构成进行时或作分词短语）
adj. 正在消失的，消逝中的，渐隐的（常用作定语）

e.en: Fuel is a substance such as coal, oil, or petrol that is burned to provide heat or power.

ex.en: They ran out of fuel.
ex.zh: 他们用完了燃料。

e.en: To fuel a situation means to make it become worse or more intense.

ex.en: The result will inevitably fuel speculation about the prime minister's future.
ex.zh: 该结果将不可避免地加剧人们对首相前途的猜测。

d: n. 燃料，燃烧剂；刺激因素，刺激性言行；（为身体提供能量的）食物，饮料，药剂
v. （给……）提供燃料，加油；刺激，加剧
【名】 （Fuel）（美）傅爱乐（人名）

e.en: To expose something that is usually hidden means to uncover it so that it can be seen.

ex.en: Lowered sea levels exposed the shallow continental shelf beneath the Bering Sea.
ex.zh: 下降了的海平面使白令海底的浅大陆架露了出来。

e.en: To expose a person or situation means to reveal that they are bad or immoral in some way.

ex.en: ...the story of how the press helped expose the truth about the Nixon administration.
ex.zh: …关于新闻界如何协助揭露尼克松政府真相的报道。

e.en: If someone is exposed to something dangerous or unpleasant, they are put in a situation in which it might affect them. 使暴露于 (危险或令人不快的境地)

ex.en: They had not been exposed to most diseases common to urban populations.
ex.zh: 他们未曾遭遇城市人口常得的大多数疾病。

ex.en: A wise mother never exposes her children to the slightest possibility of danger.
ex.zh: 一个明智的母亲从不会置其孩子于丝毫可能的危险中。

e.en: If someone is exposed to an idea or feeling, usually a new one, they are given experience of it, or introduced to it. 使体验 (观念、情感); 引入 (观念、情感)

ex.en: ...local people who've not been exposed to glimpses of Western life before.
ex.zh: …以前从未领略过西方生活方式的当地人。

d: v. 暴露，使显露；使面临，使遭受（危险或不快）；揭露，揭发；接触，体验；露出，显露（感情）；使（胶卷）曝光；弃（婴孩）于户外让其死去
n. 揭露，曝光

e.en: A fraction of something is a tiny amount or proportion of it.

ex.en: She hesitated for a fraction of a second before responding.
ex.zh: 她犹豫了一下才回应。

ex.en: Here's how to eat like the stars, at a fraction of the cost.
ex.zh: 这就是如何花少量钱却能像明星一样吃喝的方法。

e.en: A fraction is a number that can be expressed as a proportion of two whole numbers. For example, 1/2 and 1/3 are both fractions.

ex.en: The students had a grasp of decimals, percentages and fractions.
ex.zh: 学生们掌握了小数、百分数和分数。

d: n. 分数，小数；小部分，微量；持不同意见的小集团；分离；（基督教用语）分切圣餐面包

e.en: Your face is the front part of your head from your chin to the top of your forehead, where your mouth, eyes, nose, and other features are.

ex.en: He rolled down his window and stuck his face out.
ex.zh: 他摇下窗户，探出脸来。

ex.en: He was going red in the face and breathing with difficulty.
ex.zh: 他脸面发红，费力地喘着气。

e.en: If your face is happy, sad, or serious, for example, the expression on your face shows that you are happy, sad, or serious.

ex.en: He was walking around with a sad face.
ex.zh: 他四处走着，面带哀伤。

e.en: The face of a cliff, mountain, or building is a vertical surface or side of it. (悬崖、山、建筑物的)

ex.en: Harrer was one of the first to climb the north face of the Eiger.
ex.zh: 哈勒是第一批登上艾格尔山北坡的人之一。

e.en: The face of a clock or watch is the surface with the numbers or hands on it, which shows the time. 钟面;

ex.en: It was too dark to see the face of my watch.
ex.zh: 天太黑了，以致看不见我表盘上的时间。

d: n. 脸，面部；面部表情，脸色；人；初看，初听；尊严，威信；面貌；（物体的）正面，表面；斜坡，山坡；钟面，表盘；采掘面，工作面；（球拍的）拍面；（尤指足球的）球门
v. 面临，遭遇；正视，面对；与……交往，与……交谈；面向，面朝；迎战，对阵；抹盖，覆盖；接受，容忍
【名】 （Face）（法）法斯，（意）法切（人名）

e.en: In economics, a country's GDP is the total value of goods and services produced within a country in a year, not including its income from investments in other countries. GDP is an abbreviation for . Compare .

d: abbr. 国内生产总值（Gross Domestic Product）；辉光放电聚合物（Glow Discharge Polymer）

e.en: You use fundamentally for emphasis when you are stating an opinion, or when you are making an important or general statement about something.

ex.en: Fundamentally, women like him for his sensitivity and charming vulnerability.
ex.zh: 从根本上说，女人们因他的敏感和迷人的脆弱而喜欢他。

e.en: You use fundamentally to indicate that something affects or relates to the deep, basic nature of something.

ex.en: He disagreed fundamentally with the president's judgment.
ex.zh: 他从根本上不同意总统的判断。

ex.en: Environmentalists say the treaty is fundamentally flawed.
ex.zh: 环境保护主义者称那个条约从根本上是有缺陷的。

d: adv. 根本地，基础地；（用来加强语气）从根本上说

e.en: A heated discussion or quarrel is one where the people involved are angry and excited.

ex.en: It was a very heated argument and they were shouting at each other.
ex.zh: 这是一场非常激烈的争论，他们彼此冲着对方大喊大叫。

e.en: If someone gets heated about something, they get angry and excited about it.

ex.en: You will understand that people get a bit heated about issues such as these.
ex.zh: 你会理解人们对诸如此类的问题有些愤怒。

e.en: 激烈地

ex.en: The crowd continued to argue heatedly about the best way to tackle the problem.
ex.zh: 这群人继续激烈地争论着解决该问题的最好方式。

d: adj. 加热的，有供暖系统的；激烈的，愤怒的
v. 加热，使变暖；激起，使激动（heat 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A greenhouse is a glass building in which you grow plants that need to be protected from bad weather.
Greenhouse means relating to or causing the greenhouse effect. 温室的;

ex.en: ...controls on greenhouse emissions.
ex.zh: …对温室气体排放量的控制。

d: n. 温室，暖房
adj. 温室效应的

e.en: A hare is an animal like a rabbit but larger with long ears, long legs, and a small tail.

d: n. 野兔；（跑狗比赛中的用电力驱动在跑道上奔跑的）电兔（=electric hare）
v. 飞跑，疾走
【名】 （Hare）（印）哈雷，（英）黑尔，（法）阿尔（人名）
n. 冰川学家

e.en: A heatwave is a period of time during which the weather is much hotter than usual. 酷暑期;

d: n. 热浪，酷暑期，奇热时期

e.en: A Hindu is a person who believes in Hinduism and follows its teachings.
Hindu is used to describe things that belong or relate to Hinduism.

ex.en: ...a Hindu temple.
ex.zh: …一座印度教寺庙。

d: adj. （Hindu）印度教的；印度的
n. （Hindu）印度教徒；印度人；（印、美、英、俄、加）欣杜（人名）
n. 冰岛（北大西洋中的欧洲岛国，靠近北极圈）；又指该岛国所在的同名大西洋火山岛
n. 喜马拉雅山脉

e.en: If you say that ideally a particular thing should happen or be done, you mean that this is what you would like to happen or be done, but you know that this may not be possible or practical.

ex.en: People should, ideally, be persuaded to eat a diet with much less fat or oil.
ex.zh: 理想的做法是应该说服人们吃更低脂肪或更低油脂的食品。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is ideally suited, ideally located, or ideally qualified, you mean that they are as well suited, located, or qualified as they could possibly be.

ex.en: They were an extremely happy couple, ideally suited.
ex.zh: 他们是极其幸福、天造地设的一对。

d: adv. 理想地，完美地；按理想来说，理想情况下；观念上地

e.en: If you describe something as icy or icy cold, you mean that it is extremely cold.

ex.en: An icy wind blew hard across the open spaces.
ex.zh: 一阵寒风猛烈地吹过开阔的空地。

e.en: An icy road has ice on it.

ex.en: The roads were icy.
ex.zh: 道路都结冰了。

e.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as icy, you mean that they are not affectionate or friendly, and they show their dislike or anger in a quiet, controlled way.

ex.en: His response was icy.
ex.zh: 他的反应很冷漠。

d: adj. 冰冷的；结冰的；不友好的，冷漠的

e.en: Historical people, situations, or things existed in the past and are considered to be a part of history.

ex.en: ...an important historical figure.
ex.zh: …一位重要的历史人物。

ex.en: ...the historical impact of Western capitalism on the world.
ex.zh: …西方资本主义对全世界的历史影响。

e.en: 在历史上

ex.en: Historically, royal marriages have been cold, calculating affairs.
ex.zh: 从历史上来看，王室婚姻一直都是冷酷、精心策划的结合。

e.en: Historical books, movies, or pictures describe or represent people, situations, or things that existed in the past.

ex.en: He is writing a historical novel about nineteenth-century France.
ex.zh: 他正在写一部关于19世纪的法国的历史小说。

e.en: Historical information, research, and discussion is related to the study of history.

ex.en: ...historical records.
ex.zh: …史学记录。

d: adj. （有关）历史的；历史学的；（书籍、电影或图片）描述历史的，基于史实的；按历史顺序排列的
adv. 不可逆转地，不可阻挡地；无情地，冷酷地

e.en: The impact that something has on a situation, process, or person is a sudden and powerful effect that it has on them.

ex.en: They say they expect the meeting to have a marked impact on the future of the country.
ex.zh: 他们说期望这次会议对国家的未来产生显著的影响。

e.en: An impact is the action of one object hitting another, or the force with which one object hits another. 撞击;

ex.en: The plane is destroyed, a complete wreck: the pilot must have died on impact.
ex.zh: 飞机被毁，完全成了一堆残骸：飞行员一定在撞击中丧生了。

e.en: To impact a situation, process, or person means to affect them. 对…造成影响;

ex.en: Such schemes mean little unless they impact people.
ex.zh: 除非能对人们造成影响，否则这样的计划意义不大。

e.en: If one object impacts on another, it hits it with great force.

ex.en: ...the sharp tinkle of metal impacting on stone.
ex.zh: …金属撞击石头的刺耳叮当声。

d: n. 影响（impact 的复数）；冲击，撞击
v. 影响，对……产生影响（impact 的第三人称单数形式）；撞击，冲撞；压紧，压实

e.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. You can also use institute to refer to the building the organization occupies. 协会;

ex.en: ...the National Cancer Institute.
ex.zh: …国家癌症研究所。

e.en: If you institute a system, rule, or course of action, you start it. 制定 (规章、制度);

ex.en: We will institute a number of measures to better safeguard the public.
ex.zh: 我们将制定许多措施更好地保护公众。

d: n. 研究所，学院，协会；（尤指与法律相关的）注释，论述
v. 制定（制度、规则等）；提出（诉讼）；任命，授予……职位（尤指圣职）

e.en: Climbing is the activity of climbing rocks or mountains. 攀岩运动;

ex.en: I had done no skiing, no climbing, and no hiking.
ex.zh: 我从未滑过雪、攀过岩和徒步旅行过。

d: n. 登山，攀岩
adj. （植物）攀缘的；和登山、攀岩运动有关的
v. 攀登，攀爬；升高；升值（climb 的现在分词形式）

e.en: An interactive computer program or electronic device is one that allows direct communication between the user and the machine.

ex.en: This will make computer games more interactive than ever.
ex.zh: 这将使电脑游戏比以前更具交互性。

e.en: 交互性

ex.en: ...digital television, with more channels and interactivity.
ex.zh: …有更多频道和交互功能的数字电视。

e.en: If you describe a group of people or their activities as interactive, you mean that the people communicate with each other.

ex.en: There is little evidence that this encouraged flexible, interactive teaching in the classroom.
ex.zh: 几乎没有证据表明这促进灵活互动的课堂教学。

d: adj. 交互式的，人机对话的；相互交流的，互动的

e.en: Inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services in a country.

ex.en: ...rising unemployment and high inflation.
ex.zh: …上涨的失业率和高通胀。

d: n. 通货膨胀，通胀率；充气，膨胀，增大；（宇宙论某些理论）暴涨；夸张，自命不凡

e.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something. 花销;

ex.en: Policies of tax reduction must lead to reduced public expenditure.
ex.zh: 减税政策必然导致公共开支减少。

d: n. 经费，支出额；（时间、金钱、精力等的）消耗，花费
n. （Bartos）人名；（匈）鲍尔托什；（英、德、西）巴托斯

e.en: Parliamentary is used to describe things that are connected with a parliament or with members of parliament. 议会的;

ex.en: He used his influence to make sure she was not selected as a parliamentary candidate.
ex.zh: 他利用自己的影响来确保她不会被选为议员候选人。

d: adj. 议会的，国会的，设有议会的

e.en: When you spend money, you pay money for things that you want or need. 花 (钱)

ex.en: By the end of the holiday I had spent all my money.
ex.zh: 到那个假期结束时我已经花光了我所有的钱。

ex.en: Businessmen spend enormous amounts advertising their products.
ex.zh: 商人们花巨额资金为他们的产品做广告。

e.en: If you spend time or energy doing something, you use your time or effort doing it. 花 (时间、精力)

ex.en: Engineers spend much time and energy developing brilliant solutions.
ex.zh: 工程师们花大量时间和精力开发出色的解决方案。

e.en: If you spend a period of time in a place, you stay there for a period of time. 度过 (一段时间)

ex.en: We spent the night in a hotel.
ex.zh: 我们在一家宾馆过了夜。

d: n. （尤指政府或组织的）支出，开销，花费
v. 用，花（钱）；花（时间），度过；花费，消耗，用尽（精力等）（spend的现在分词形式）；花费，消耗，用尽（精力等）（spend 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Accounting is the activity of keeping detailed records of the amounts of money a business or person receives and spends.

ex.en: ...the accounting firm of Leventhal & Horwath.
ex.zh: …利文撒尔与霍瓦特会计事务所。

d: n. 会计，会计学；会计工作，会计职业（=accountancy）；账单
v. 解释，说明；占（一定数量或比例）（account 的现在分词形式）
abbr. （计算机）网络驱动程序接口规范（Network Driver Interface Specification，Microsoft Windows 中网卡驱动程序和协议驱动程序使用的接口标准；亦作“网络驱动器接口标准”）；（澳大利亚）国家残障保险计划（National Disability Insurance Scheme，澳大利亚政府为符合条件的残障人士提供支持与资金的计划）
n. 斯蒂芬（男子名）

e.en: If you jump, you bend your knees, push against the ground with your feet, and move quickly upward into the air.

ex.en: I jumped over the fence.
ex.zh: 我从篱笆上跳了过去。

ex.en: I'd jumped seventeen feet six in the long jump, which was a school record.
ex.zh: 我跳远曾跳了17.6英尺，这是个校纪录。

e.en: Jump is also a noun.

ex.en: The longest jumps by a man and a woman were witnessed in Sestriere, Italy, yesterday.
ex.zh: 男女跳远项目最远的一跳都于昨天在意大利的塞斯特雷得以见证。

e.en: If you jump from something above the ground, you deliberately push yourself into the air so that you drop toward the ground.

ex.en: I jumped the last six feet down to the deck.
ex.zh: 我跳下最后6英尺，到了甲板上。

ex.en: He jumped out of a third-floor window.
ex.zh: 他从3楼的一个窗口跳了出去。

e.en: If you jump something such as a fence, you move quickly up and through the air over or across it.

ex.en: He jumped the first fence beautifully.
ex.zh: 他漂亮地跃过了第一道篱笆。

d: v. 跳跃（jump 的过去分词）

e.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists. 承认 (事实或情况)

ex.en: Naylor acknowledged, in a letter to the judge, that he was a drug addict.
ex.zh: 在一封写给法官的信中，内勒承认他是一个吸毒者。

ex.en: Belatedly, the government has acknowledged the problem.
ex.zh: 政府过晚地承认了这个问题。

e.en: If someone's achievements, status, or qualities are acknowledged, they are known about and recognized by a lot of people, or by a particular group of people. 认可 (某人的成就、地位或品质)

ex.en: He is also acknowledged as an excellent goalkeeper.
ex.zh: 他还被认可为一名优秀的守门员。

e.en: If you acknowledge a message or letter, you write to the person who sent it in order to say that you have received it.

ex.en: The army sent me a postcard acknowledging my request.
ex.zh: 军方寄给我一张明信片以确认收到了我的请求。

e.en: If you acknowledge someone, for example, by moving your head or smiling, you show that you have seen and recognized them. (点头或微笑)

ex.en: He saw her but refused to even acknowledge her.
ex.zh: 他看到了她，但甚至都拒绝向她致意。

d: v. 承认；认可； 跟……打招呼，理会；告知收到；（公开）感谢
n. 安格斯（男子名）；安格斯牛，源自苏格兰的黑色无角肉牛品种，亦作 Aberdeen Angus 或 black Angus；安格斯，凯尔特神话中的爱与美之神，亦作 Aengus、Oengus

e.en: Aren't is the usual spoken form of "are not." (are not)
Aren't is the form of "am not" that is used in questions or tags in spoken English. 口语中疑问句或附加疑问句里(am not)

d: abbr. are not 的缩略形式，表示“不是”；口语疑问句或附加疑问句中可代替 am not（如 Aren't I?）

e.en: An argument is a statement or set of statements that you use in order to try to convince people that your opinion about something is correct.

ex.en: There's a strong argument for lowering the price.
ex.zh: 有一个支持降低价格的有力论据。

ex.en: The doctors have set out their arguments against the proposals.
ex.zh: 医生们已经说明了反对这些提案的理由。

e.en: An argument is a discussion or debate in which a number of people put forward different or opposing opinions. 讨论;

ex.en: The incident has triggered fresh arguments about the role of the extreme right in U.S. politics.
ex.zh: 该事件引发了有关美国政治中极右势力角色的新讨论。

e.en: An argument is a conversation in which people disagree with each other angrily or noisily.

ex.en: Anny described how she got into an argument with one of the marchers.
ex.zh: 安妮描述了她是如何与游行者中的一个人争吵起来的。

e.en: If you accept something without argument, you do not question it or disagree with it.

ex.en: He complied without argument.
ex.zh: 他没有争辩就服从了。

d: n. 争论，争吵；论据，理由；辩论，讨论；自变数；主词，受词；书的内容提要

e.en: If one thing is associated with another, the two things are connected with each other. (与…)

ex.en: These symptoms are particularly associated with migraine headaches.
ex.zh: 这些症状尤其与偏头痛相关联。

e.en: Associated is used in the name of a company that is made up of a number of smaller companies that have joined together. 联合的 (用于由若干小公司组成的公司名称中)

ex.en: ...the Associated Press.
ex.zh: …联合通讯社。

d: adj. 有关联的，相关的；联合的，联营的
v. 联想，联系；支持；交往（associate 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

ex.en: The committee is concerned about players' behaviour, especially arguing with referees.
ex.zh: 该委员会担心运动员的表现，尤其担心他们与裁判争吵。

e.en: If you argue with someone about something, you discuss it with them, with each of you giving your different opinions.

ex.en: He was arguing with the king about the need to maintain the cavalry at full strength.
ex.zh: 他在和国王讨论保留骑兵全部兵力的必要性。

ex.en: They are arguing over foreign policy.
ex.zh: 他们在讨论外交政策。

e.en: If you tell someone not to argue with you, you want them to do or believe what you say without protest or disagreement.

ex.en: Don't argue with me.
ex.zh: 不要和我争辩。

e.en: If you argue that something is true, you state it and give the reasons why you think it is true.

ex.en: His lawyers are arguing that he is unfit to stand trial.
ex.zh: 他的律师们在辩称他不适宜受审。

d: v. argue 的第三人称单数现在时形式：争吵，吵架；讨论，争论；主张，辩称，论证；表明，显示
n. Argues 人名，阿尔古埃斯（土耳其语）

e.en: Something that is Australian belongs or relates to Australia, or to its people or culture. 澳大利亚的; 澳大利亚人的;

ex.en: She went solo backpacking for eight months in the Australian outback.
ex.zh: 她在澳大利亚内陆独自背包旅行了八个月。

e.en: An Australian is someone who comes from Australia.

d: n. 澳大利亚人（Australian 的复数）

e.en: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, or if you blame something bad on somebody, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it. 指责;

ex.en: The commission is expected to blame the army for many of the atrocities.
ex.zh: 该委员会预计会将大量暴行归咎于军队。

ex.en: Ms. Carey appeared to blame her breakdown on EMI's punishing work schedule.
ex.zh: 凯丽女士看来是将自己的崩溃归咎于百代公司紧张的工作安排。

e.en: Blame is also a noun.

ex.en: Nothing could relieve my terrible sense of blame.
ex.zh: 没什么能把我从极度自责中解脱出来。

e.en: The blame for something bad that has happened is the responsibility for causing it or letting it happen. (事故、过失等的)

ex.en: I'm not going to sit around and take the blame for a mistake he made.
ex.zh: 我不会闲坐着，为他犯的错误承担责任。

e.en: If you say that you do not blame someone for doing something, you mean that you consider it was a reasonable thing to do in the circumstances.

ex.en: I do not blame them for trying to make some money.
ex.zh: 我不怪他们想要挣些钱。

d: v. 责怪，归咎于；怨，怪
n. 责备，过错，罪责

e.en: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, or if you blame something bad on somebody, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it. 指责;

ex.en: The commission is expected to blame the army for many of the atrocities.
ex.zh: 该委员会预计会将大量暴行归咎于军队。

ex.en: Ms. Carey appeared to blame her breakdown on EMI's punishing work schedule.
ex.zh: 凯丽女士看来是将自己的崩溃归咎于百代公司紧张的工作安排。

e.en: Blame is also a noun.

ex.en: Nothing could relieve my terrible sense of blame.
ex.zh: 没什么能把我从极度自责中解脱出来。

e.en: The blame for something bad that has happened is the responsibility for causing it or letting it happen. (事故、过失等的)

ex.en: I'm not going to sit around and take the blame for a mistake he made.
ex.zh: 我不会闲坐着，为他犯的错误承担责任。

e.en: If you say that you do not blame someone for doing something, you mean that you consider it was a reasonable thing to do in the circumstances.

ex.en: I do not blame them for trying to make some money.
ex.zh: 我不怪他们想要挣些钱。

d: v. blame 的现在分词/动名词：责备；归咎；谴责

e.en: Your budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend. The budget for something is the amount of money that a person, organization, or country has available to spend on it.

ex.en: She will design a fantastic new kitchen for you – and all within your budget.
ex.zh: 她将为你设计一个崭新的漂亮厨房–所有的花费都将在你的预算之内。

ex.en: Someone had furnished the place on a tight budget.
ex.zh: 有人用不多的钱把那个地方布置了一下。

e.en: The budget of an organization or country is its financial situation, considered as the difference between the money it receives and the money it spends. (机构、政府等的)

ex.en: The hospital obviously needs to balance the budget each year.
ex.zh: 该医院显然每年都需要平衡其财务收支。

e.en: If you budget certain amounts of money for particular things, you decide that you can afford to spend those amounts on those things. 安排开支;

ex.en: The company has budgeted $10 million for advertising.
ex.zh: 公司已经安排了1千万美元的广告预算。

ex.en: The film is only budgeted at $10 million.
ex.zh: 这部电影的预算只有1千万美元。

e.en: 预算

ex.en: We have continued to exercise caution in our budgeting for the current year.
ex.zh: 在今年的预算方面，我们继续小心谨慎。

d: n. 编制预算，预算编制
v. 做预算（budget 的现在分词/动名词）
adv. 非常，相当多地

e.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

ex.en: I hope they continue to fight for equal justice after I'm gone.
ex.zh: 我希望我走后他们继续为司法公正而奋斗。

ex.en: Diana and Roy Jarvis are determined to continue working when they reach retirement age.
ex.zh: 戴安娜·贾维斯和罗伊·贾维斯决心到退休年龄后还继续工作。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it does not stop. 使继续;

ex.en: He insisted that the conflict would continue until conditions were met for a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 他坚持认为冲突会持续下去，直至停火条件得到满足为止。

ex.en: Outside the building people continue their vigil, huddling around bonfires.
ex.zh: 在楼外，人们围聚在篝火旁继续守夜。

e.en: If you continue something or continue with something, you start doing it again after a break or interruption. (某人在歇息或被打断后) 继续 (做某事或某事)

ex.en: I went up to my room to continue with my packing.
ex.zh: 我上我房间去继续收拾行李。

ex.en: She looked up for a minute and then continued drawing.
ex.zh: 她抬头看了一会儿，然后继续画。

e.en: If something continues or if you continue it, it starts again after a break or interruption. (某事在停顿或被打断后)

ex.en: He denies 18 charges. The trial continues today.
ex.zh: 他否认18项指控。审判今天继续。

d: adj. 继续的；持续的；连续的
v. continue 的现在分词和动名词形式
n. 查尔莫斯港（新西兰港口）；查尔默斯（姓氏）

e.en: If you buy something, you obtain it by paying money for it.

ex.en: He could not afford to buy a house.
ex.zh: 他买不起房子。

ex.en: Lizzie bought herself a mountain bike.
ex.zh: 莉齐给自己买了一辆山地自行车。

e.en: If you talk about the quantity or standard of goods an amount of money buys, you are referring to the price of the goods or the value of the money.

ex.en: About $70,000 buys a habitable house.
ex.zh: 大约七万美元才买得到一栋适合居住的房子。

e.en: If you buy something like time, freedom, or victory, you obtain it but only by offering or giving up something in return.

ex.en: It was a risky operation, but might buy more time.
ex.zh: 这是一项冒险的举动，但也许能换得更多的时间。

e.en: If you say that a person can be bought, you are criticizing the fact that they will give their help or loyalty to someone in return for money.

ex.en: Any number of our military and government officials can be bought.
ex.zh: 我们的军官和政府官员中有许多可以被收买。

d: v. 购买；获得；收买（buy 的现在分词和动名词形式）
n. 购买，买进，采购（buy 的动名词形式）
n. 堪培拉（澳大利亚的首都）

e.en: If you say that you need or have a great deal of or a good deal of a particular thing, you are emphasizing that you need or have a lot of it.

ex.en: ...a great deal of money.
ex.zh: …许多钱。

e.en: Deal is also an adverb.

ex.en: As a relationship becomes more established, it also becomes a good deal more complex.
ex.zh: 当一段关系固定下来以后，它也会变得复杂得多。

e.en: Deal is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Although he had never met Geoffrey Hardcastle, he knew a good deal about him.
ex.zh: 尽管他从未见过杰弗里·哈德卡斯尔，他还是十分了解他。

e.en: If you make a deal, do a deal, or cut a deal, you complete an agreement or an arrangement with someone, especially in business. 达成协议;

ex.en: He made a deal to testify against the others and wasn't charged.
ex.zh: 他达成了协议出庭指证别人，因而未获指控。

ex.en: Japan will have to do a deal with the U.S. on rice imports.
ex.zh: 日本将不得不就水稻进口问题和美国达成协议。

d: n. （deal 的复数）交易，买卖；协议，协定，协约
v. （deal 的第三人称单数）处理，应对，对待（常与 with 连用）；经营，买卖（常与 in 连用）；贩卖（毒品）；涉及，论述；分配，分发；发牌；给以（打击）（用于 deal a blow）

e.en: Diesel or diesel oil is the heavy fuel used in a diesel engine.
A diesel is a vehicle which has a diesel engine.

ex.en: I keep hearing that diesels are better now than ever before.
ex.zh: 我总听说现在的柴油车比以往的都好。

d: n. 柴油；内燃机，柴油车
【名】  (Diesel）（德）狄塞耳（人名）
n. 德勤（全球性专业服务机构，四大会计师事务所之一）

e.en: A disability is a permanent injury, illness, or physical or mental condition that tends to restrict the way that someone can live their life. (身体或精神方面的)

ex.en: Facilities for people with disabilities are still insufficient.
ex.zh: 供残疾人使用的设施仍然不足。

e.en: Disability is the state of being disabled.

ex.en: Disability can make extra demands on financial resources because the disabled need extra care.
ex.zh: 残疾会增加额外经济需求，因为残疾人需要特别护理。

d: n. 残疾，缺陷；无能力，障碍；残疾补贴

e.en: The fifth item in a series is the one that you count as number five. 第5

ex.en: Joe has recently returned from his fifth trip to Australia.
ex.zh: 乔最近从他第5次澳大利亚之旅返回。

e.en: A fifth is one of five equal parts of something. 1/5

ex.en: India spends over a fifth of its budget on defence.
ex.zh: 印度在国防上支出预算的五分之一以上。

e.en: If you take or plead the fifth, you take the . 《
e.zh: 美国宪法修正案》第五条

d: adj. 第五的；五分之一的
n. 第五；五分之一；（某月的）五日；the Fifth《美国宪法第五修正案》（常用于 take/plead the Fifth）
num. 第五

e.en: Expense is the money that something costs you or that you need to spend in order to do something.

ex.en: He's bought a big TV at vast expense so that everyone can see properly.
ex.zh: 他花了很多钱买了台大电视，这样人人都可以看清楚了。

e.en: Expenses are amounts of money that you spend while doing something in the course of your work, which will be paid back to you afterwards. (由雇主报销的工作)

ex.en: Her airfare and hotel expenses were paid by the committee.
ex.zh: 她乘飞机及住酒店的费用由该委员会支付了。

e.en: If you do something at someone's expense, they provide the money for it.

ex.en: Should architects continue to be trained for five years at public expense?
ex.zh: 建筑师继续受训5年应由公众付费吗？

e.en: If someone laughs or makes a joke at your expense, they do it to make you seem foolish. 捉弄 (某人)

ex.en: I think he's having fun at our expense.
ex.zh: 我看他是在拿咱们寻开心。

d: n. 费用，开支，花费；（可报销的）业务费用；（会计）费用项目，支出；代价（expense 的复数）
v. 把……记入费用账户；向……收取费用；被花掉（expense 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A figure is a particular amount expressed as a number, especially a statistic.

ex.en: It would be very nice if we had a true figure of how many people in this country haven't got a job.
ex.zh: 要是我们有一个确切的数字反映这个国家到底有多少人没有工作就好了。

ex.en: It will not be long before the inflation figure starts to fall.
ex.zh: 过不了多久，通货膨胀的数字就会开始下降。

e.en: A figure is any of the ten written symbols from 0 to 9 that are used to represent a number.

ex.en: ...the glowing red figures on the radio alarm clock which read 4:22 a.m.
ex.zh: …收音机闹钟上闪闪发光的红色数字显示凌晨4点22分。

e.en: You refer to someone that you can see as a figure when you cannot see them clearly or when you are describing them.

ex.en: Ernie saw the dim figure of Rose in the chair.
ex.zh: 厄尼看到了罗斯坐在椅子里的模糊身影。

e.en: In art, a figure is a person in a drawing or a painting, or a statue of a person.

ex.en: ...a life-size bronze figure of a brooding, hooded woman.
ex.zh: …一个真人大小、戴着头巾、正在沉思的女铜像。

d: n. 数字，数目，数值；数字符号，位数；身材，体型；（远处的）人影；（重要的）人物；（绘画或模型中）人像；（书中的）图、表；（数学）图形；价格，金额
v. （以重要地位）出现；认为，估计；理解，弄懂；计算；用图画（或图形等）描绘，想象

e.en: If a situation or action is fraught with problems or risks, it is filled with them. 充满 (问题或风险)

ex.en: The earliest operations employing this technique were fraught with dangers.
ex.zh: 最早采用这一技术的手术充满了危险。

e.en: If you say that a situation or action is fraught, you mean that it is worrisome or difficult.

ex.en: It has been a somewhat fraught day.
ex.zh: 这是令人颇为担忧的一天。

d: adj. 充满（糟糕或令人讨厌的事物）；造成忧虑（或紧张）的，受忧虑（或压力）影响的；充满的
n. 货物
v. 装载

e.en: Drove is the past tense of . (drive)
a herd of livestock being driven together (被驱赶着一起前进的)
to drive (a group of livestock), usually for a considerable distance 驱赶(畜群)
to be employed as a drover

d: n. （移动的）人群，畜群
v. 驱赶（牲口），使（家畜）迁徙
v. 开车；驾车送人；迫使，促使（drive 的过去式形式）

e.en: When you halve something or when it halves, it is reduced to half its previous size or amount. 使减半;

ex.en: Dr. Lee believes that men who exercise can halve their risk of colon cancer.
ex.zh: 李医生认为，男人坚持锻炼，可以使他们患结肠癌的风险减半。

e.en: If you halve something, you divide it into two equal parts.

ex.en: Halve the pineapple and scoop out the inside.
ex.zh: 把菠萝对半切开，并取出内瓤。

e.en: Halves is the plural of . (half)

d: v. （使）减半；把……分成两半，对半分；均摊；（高尔夫）与对手以相同杆数打完（一穴或一场比赛）；半嵌接，槽舌接，合缺接（两块木料）
【名】 （Halve）（芬）哈尔韦（人名）

e.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page. (尤指报纸头版的)

ex.en: The Sydney Morning Herald carried the headline: "Sorry Ma'am, Most Australians Want a Republic."
ex.zh: 《悉尼先驱晨报》有这样一则头版标题：“对不起，夫人，大多数澳大利亚人想要一个共和国。”

e.en: The headlines are the main points of the news which are read on radio or television.

ex.en: I'm Claudia Polley with the news headlines.
ex.zh: 我是克劳迪娅•波莉，以下是新闻提要。

e.en: If a newspaper or magazine article is headlined a particular thing, that is the headline that introduces it.

ex.en: The article was headlined "Tell us the truth."
ex.zh: 该文章题为“告诉我们真相。”

e.en: Someone or something that hits the headlines or grabs the headlines gets a lot of publicity from the media.

ex.en: El Salvador first hit the world headlines at the beginning of the 1980s.
ex.zh: 萨尔瓦多首度成为国际媒体的焦点是在20世纪80年代初。

d: n. （报纸的）标题，大字标题；（广播或电视里的）新闻提要，头条新闻
v. 给（报道、文章）加标题；在（演出）中担任主演；大肆宣传

e.en: A herculean task or ability is one that requires extremely great strength or effort. 艰巨的;

ex.en: ...his herculean efforts to bring peace to our troubled island.
ex.zh: ...他为给我们纷争不断的岛屿带来和平所付出的艰辛努力。

d: adj. 力大无比的；极为困难的，艰巨的；赫拉克勒斯的（首字母常大写）

e.en: A hospital is a place where people who are ill are cared for by nurses and doctors.

ex.en: ...a children's hospital with 120 beds.
ex.zh: …一个有120张床位的儿童医院。

d: n. 医院；青年教育慈善机构；（尤指僧侣骑士团所办的）慈善招待所
【名】 （Hospital）（英）霍斯皮特尔（人名）

e.en: When people, animals, and plants grow, they increase in size and change physically over a period of time.

ex.en: We stop growing at maturity.
ex.zh: 我们在成熟后就停止成长了。

e.en: If a plant or tree grows in a particular place, it is alive there.

ex.en: The station had roses growing at each end of the platform.
ex.zh: 车站月台两端生长着玫瑰。

e.en: If you grow a particular type of plant, you put seeds or young plants in the ground and take care of them as they develop.

ex.en: Lettuce was grown by the ancient Romans.
ex.zh: 莴苣是由古罗马人种植的。

e.en: When someone's hair grows, it gradually becomes longer. Your nails also grow. (毛发、指甲等)

ex.en: Then the hair began to grow again and I felt terrific.
ex.zh: 接着头发又长起来了，我感觉棒极了。

d: v. 长大，成长；成活，生长；发展，增加；逐渐变得；产生，形成；栽种，种植；留长，蓄；变长
【名】 （Grow）（英）格罗（人名）

e.en: If you are inclined to behave in a particular way, you often behave in that way, or you want to do so. 常表现出…的;

ex.en: Nobody felt inclined to argue with Smith.
ex.zh: 没人想和史密斯争论。

ex.en: He was inclined to self-pity.
ex.zh: 他总是自哀自怜。

e.en: If you say that you are inclined to have a particular opinion, you mean that you hold this opinion but you are not expressing it strongly.

ex.en: I am inclined to agree with Alan.
ex.zh: 我倾向于同意艾伦的看法。

e.en: Someone who is mathematically inclined or artistically inclined, for example, has a natural talent for mathematics or art.

ex.en: ...the needs of academically inclined pupils.
ex.zh: …有学术天赋的学生的需求。

d: adj. 有……意向，倾向于……；对……有兴趣的，有天赋的；倾斜的，有坡度的
v. 点头；（使）倾向于；（使）倾斜（incline 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If something increases or you increase it, it becomes greater in number, level, or amount. 使增加;

ex.en: The population continues to increase.
ex.zh: 人口持续增长。

ex.en: Japan's industrial output increased by 2%.
ex.zh: 日本的工业产量增长了2%。

e.en: If there is an increase in the number, level, or amount of something, it becomes greater.

ex.en: ...a sharp increase in productivity.
ex.zh: …生产率的急速增长。

e.en: If something is on the increase, it is happening more often or becoming greater in number or intensity.

ex.en: Crime is on the increase.
ex.zh: 犯罪活动日益猖獗。

d: v. 增长，增强，增大（increase 的第三人称单数）
n. 增长；增长量（increase 的复数）

e.en: A hike is a long walk in the country, especially one that you go on for pleasure.

ex.en: The site is reached by a 30-minute hike through dense forest.
ex.zh: 要花30分钟徒步穿过密林才能到达那个地方。

e.en: If you hike, you go for a long walk in the country.

ex.en: You could hike through the Fish River Canyon – it's entirely up to you.
ex.zh: 你可以远足穿越菲什干河大峡谷–这全由你自己决定。

e.en: 远足

ex.en: ...some harder, more strenuous hiking on cliff pathways.
ex.zh: …在悬崖峭壁的小路上进行的更艰难、更费力的长途行走。

e.en: A hike is a sudden or large increase in prices, rates, taxes, or quantities.

ex.en: ...a sudden 1.75 percent hike in interest rates.

d: n. 徒步旅行，远足；（价格、花费等的）大幅度提高，猛增
v. 远足，徒步旅行；突然增加，突然提高；拉起，提起（尤指衣物）；后传（发球）给四分卫
【名】 （Hike）（美、俄）海克（人名）
n. 吉姆（人名）

e.en: Meanwhile means while a particular thing is happening.

ex.en: Brush the eggplant with oil, add salt and pepper, and bake till soft. Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan.
ex.zh: 给茄子刷好油，加盐和胡椒粉，烤到软。同时，加热厚底锅中剩余的油。

e.en: Meanwhile means in the period of time between two events.

ex.en: You needn't worry; I'll be ready to greet them. Meanwhile, I'm off to discuss the Fowler's party with Felix.
ex.zh: 你不用担心；我会做好准备迎接他们的。在此期间，我会去和费利克斯商量在福勒家聚会的事情。

e.en: You use meanwhile to introduce a different aspect of a particular situation, especially one that is completely opposite to the one previously mentioned.

ex.en: He had always found his wife's mother a bit annoying. The mother-daughter relationship, meanwhile, was close.
ex.zh: 他总是觉得他的岳母有点烦人。另一方面，她们母女之间的关系很亲近。

d: adv. 与此同时；在此期间；另一方面
n. 其间，其时

e.en: If you measure the quality, value, or effect of something, you discover or judge how great it is.

ex.en: I continued to measure his progress against the charts in the doctor's office.
ex.zh: 我继续根据医生办公室里的图表来估量他的进展。

e.en: If you measure a quantity that can be expressed in numbers, such as the length of something, you discover it using a particular instrument or device, for example a ruler.

ex.en: Measure the length and width of the gap.
ex.zh: 测量一下这个裂口的长度和宽度。

e.en: If something measures a particular length, width, or amount, that is its size or intensity, expressed in numbers. (长度、宽度、数量的)

ex.en: It measures 20 yards from side to side.
ex.zh: 从这边到那边的距离为20码。

e.en: A measure of a particular quality, feeling, or activity is a fairly large amount of it. 一定数量;

ex.en: With the exception of Juan, each attained a measure of success.
ex.zh: 除了胡安，每个人都取得了一定的成功。

d: n. 措施，办法；适量，适度；判断，衡量；度量单位，计量标准；（酒的）标准量；小节，拍子；象征，迹象；议案，法案；格律单位；计量工具，量器；（尤指庄重或肃穆的）舞蹈，舞步；岩层；（数）除数；（印刷）行宽，页宽
v. 测量；（指尺寸、长短、数量等）量度为；估量，判定（重要性、价值或影响等）；走过；显示，记录；用作……的量器

e.en: If you kick someone or something, you hit them forcefully with your foot.

ex.en: He kicked the door hard.
ex.zh: 他用力踢门。

ex.en: He threw me to the ground and started to kick.
ex.zh: 他把我摔在地上开始踢我。

e.en: Kick is also a noun.

ex.en: He suffered a kick to the knee.
ex.zh: 他的膝盖被踢了一脚。

e.en: When you kick a ball or other object, you hit it with your foot so that it moves through the air.

ex.en: I went to kick the ball and I completely missed it.
ex.zh: 我去踢球却踢空了。

ex.en: He kicked the ball away.
ex.zh: 他把球踢开了。

e.en: Kick is also a noun.

ex.en: He missed an easy kick.
ex.zh: 他错失很容易的一脚球。

d: n. 踢腿；反撞
adj. 活泼热烈的；激动人心的；令人兴奋的
v. 踢；反冲；加速；活跃（kick 的现在分词）

e.en: Your partner is the person you are married to or are having a romantic or sexual relationship with. 配偶; 情人;

ex.en: Wanting other friends doesn't mean you don't love your partner.
ex.zh: 需要其他朋友并不意味着你不爱你的伴侣。

e.en: Your partner is the person you are doing something with, for example, dancing with or playing with in a game against two other people.

ex.en: ...to dance with a partner.
ex.zh: …与一名搭档跳舞。

ex.en: Her partner for the game was Venus Williams.
ex.zh: 她的比赛搭挡是维纳斯•威廉姆斯。

e.en: The partners in a firm or business are the people who share the ownership of it.

ex.en: He's a partner in a Chicago law firm.
ex.zh: 他是芝加哥一家律师事务所的合伙人。

e.en: The partner of a country or organization is another country or organization with which they work or do business.

ex.en: Spain has been one of Cuba's major trading partners.
ex.zh: 西班牙一直是古巴的主要贸易伙伴之一。

d: n. （跳舞、玩游戏等的）搭档，同伴；（合伙企业的）合伙人；（生意、组织或国家的）伙伴；配偶，（同居的）伴侣，情人
v. 成为搭档，合伙
【名】 （Partner）（英、德）帕特纳（人名）

e.en: Petrol is the fuel which is used to drive motor vehicles.

d: n. 汽油；深蓝绿色
adj. 失控

e.en: Pharmaceutical means connected with the industrial production of medicines.

ex.en: ...a Swiss pharmaceutical company.
ex.zh: …一家瑞士制药公司。

e.en: Pharmaceuticals are medicines.

ex.en: Antibiotics were of no use, neither were other pharmaceuticals.
ex.zh: 抗生素没有用，其他药物也没有用。

d: adj. 制药的
n. 药物；制药公司股票（pharmaceuticals）

e.en: Outlay is the amount of money that you have to spend in order to buy something or start a project. (必要的)

ex.en: Apart from the capital outlay of buying the machine, dishwashers can actually save you money.
ex.zh: 抛开购买的费用不讲，洗碗机实际上能给你省钱。

d: n. （outlay 的复数形式）花费，支出费用
v. 花费（outlay 的第三人称单数）
adv. 快速地，迅速地

e.en: A payment is an amount of money that is paid to someone, or the act of paying this money. 支付的款项;
Payment is the act of paying money to someone or of being paid.

ex.en: He had sought to obtain payment of a sum which he had claimed was owed to him.
ex.zh: 他曾试图获得一笔他声称是欠他的钱。

d: n. 多笔款项；支付，付款（payment 的复数形式）

e.en: If something happens regardless of something else, it is not affected or influenced at all by that other thing. 不管;

ex.en: It takes in anybody regardless of religion, colour, or creed.
ex.zh: 这个组织接纳任何人，不管其宗教、肤色或信仰。

e.en: If you say that someone did something regardless, you mean that they did it even though there were problems or factors that could have stopped them, or perhaps should have stopped them.

ex.en: Despite her recent surgery she has been carrying on regardless.
ex.zh: 尽管她最近动了手术，她却一直在不顾一切地继续工作。

d: adv. 不顾，不加理会；不管怎样，无论如何
adj. 不管的，不注意的

e.en: A quarterly event happens four times a year, at intervals of three months. 一年四次的;

ex.en: ...the latest Bank of Japan quarterly survey of 5,000 companies.
ex.zh: …日本银行对5000家公司最新的季度调查。

e.en: Quarterly is also an adverb. 一年四次地;

ex.en: It makes no difference whether dividends are paid quarterly or annually.
ex.zh: 红利是按季度还是按年度支付没有区别。

e.en: A quarterly is a magazine that is published four times a year, at intervals of three months.

ex.en: The quarterly had been a forum for sound academic debate.
ex.zh: 这份季刊曾经是正统学术辩论的论坛。

d: adj. 季度的，每季的；（盾，图记）纵横划成四（或更多）部分的
adv. 一季一次地，按季度；（纹章）在盾的四分之一部分（或对角两部分）上
n. 季刊
【名】 （Quarterly）（英）夸特利（人名）

e.en: In a tool or machine, a ratchet is a wheel or bar with sloping teeth, which can move only in one direction, because a piece of metal stops the teeth from moving backward. (防倒转的)棘齿;

ex.en: The chair has a ratchet below it to adjust the height.
ex.zh: 这把椅子下面有一个棘轮来调整高度。

e.en: If a tool or machine ratchets or if you ratchet it, it makes a clicking noise as it operates, because it has a ratchet in it. 使(工具或机器)发出嗒嗒声; (工具或机器)

ex.en: The rod bent double, the reel shrieked and ratcheted.
ex.zh: 该操作杆加倍弯曲，线轴发出刺耳的嗒嗒声。

ex.en: She took up a sheet and ratcheted it into the typewriter.
ex.zh: 她拿起一张纸，把它塞入打字机，发出一阵“嗒嗒”的声音。

d: v．逐步升高或降低：通过一系列的小步骤逐渐改变某物的水平或位置。

e.en: If something is reserved for a particular person or purpose, it is kept specially for that person or purpose.

ex.en: A double room with a balcony overlooking the sea had been reserved for him.
ex.zh: 一个带一座阳台的海景双人间已被预留给他了。

e.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept specially for you, rather than sold or given to someone else.

ex.en: I'll reserve a table for five.
ex.zh: 我要预订一个5人的餐位。

e.en: A reserve is a supply of something that is available for use when it is needed.

ex.en: The Persian Gulf has 65 percent of the world's oil reserves.
ex.zh: 波斯湾拥有全世界石油储备的65%。

e.en: A nature reserve is an area of land where the animals, birds, and plants are officially protected.

d: v. 预订；保留，预留；拥有，保留（某种权利）；留作，用于（特定场合）；保留（意见），推迟作出（决定或判断）；贮存，贮藏；（教会用语）弥撒仪式后保留部分圣餐

n.  储备（量），储藏（量）；含蓄，寡言；保留意见，异议；（野生生物）保护区；替补队员，后备队员；后备队，替补队（the reserves）；预备役部队，后备部队；（尤指拍卖时的）底价，最低价；（美洲土著居民的）居留地；（陶瓷装饰或纺织品印染中保留原色的）防染本色区
；（陶瓷装饰或纺织品印染中保留原色的）防染本色区
【名】  （Reserve）（挪、美、法、俄、墨）勒塞尔夫（人名）

e.en: When you respond to something that is done or said, you react to it by doing or saying something yourself.

ex.en: They are likely to respond positively to the president's request for aid.
ex.zh: 他们有可能积极地回应该总统的援助请求。

ex.en: The army responded with gunfire and tear gas.
ex.zh: 军方以炮火和催泪弹回应。

e.en: When you respond to a need, crisis, or challenge, you take the necessary or appropriate action.

ex.en: This modest group size allows our teachers to respond to the needs of each student.
ex.zh: 这个适中的小组规模使得我们的老师们可以应对每个学生的需要。

e.en: If a patient or their injury or illness is responding to treatment, the treatment is working and they are getting better.

ex.en: I'm pleased to say that he is now doing well and responding to treatment.
ex.zh: 我很高兴地说他现在正在顺利恢复，治疗是有效果的。

d: v. （口头或书面）回答，回应；作出反应，回应；（对某种治疗）有良好反应；（桥牌）（对同伴的叫牌）作应叫；（会众对牧师）应答，唱和；承担责任
n. （教堂用语）应答，唱和；（建筑）壁联（与墙相连支承拱的半柱或半墩，尤指在拱廊两端）
n. 速度，速率；比率，率；费用，价格；费率；（英国）地方税，房地产税（rates）；等级
v. 评价，评定；被认为，被列为； 看好； 对（影片、视频游戏等）分级；划分等级，分等；值得，应得；给（财产）核定应缴地方税款；（机器、发动机等的）额定功率（极限）为；受器重，受青睐（rate with）
【名】 （Rate）（法、塞）拉特（人名）

e.en: If you describe something as simple, you mean that it is not complicated, and is therefore easy to understand. 简单的;

ex.en: ...simple pictures and diagrams.
ex.zh: …简明的图片和图表。

ex.en: ...pages of simple advice on filling in your tax form.
ex.zh: …几页有关填写纳税表格的简单建议。

e.en: 简单地

ex.en: When applying for a visa extension state simply and clearly the reasons why you need an extension.
ex.zh: 申请签证续签时，简单明了地陈述你需要延期的理由。

e.en: If you describe people or things as simple, you mean that they have all the basic or necessary things they require, but nothing extra. 简朴的;

ex.en: He ate a simple dinner of rice and beans.
ex.zh: 他吃了一顿米饭加豆子的简单晚餐。

ex.en: ...the simple pleasures of childhood.
ex.zh: …童年纯朴的快乐。

e.en: 简朴地;

ex.en: The living room is furnished simply with white wicker furniture and blue-and-white fabrics.
ex.zh: 起居室朴素地摆放着白柳条家具和蓝白相间的织物。

d: adj. 简单的，简明的；简朴的，朴素的；纯粹的，完全的；结构单一的，简易的；普通的，平凡的；愚笨的，迟钝的；（动词时态）简单的；（数）简单的；（叶、茎）没有分杈的；（镜头、显微镜等）单镜头的；（利息）单利的；（句子）无从句的
n.  草药，药草；出身低微者；笨蛋
【名】  （Simple）（法）桑普勒（人名）

e.en: A small person, thing, or amount of something is not large in physical size. (体积或规模等)

ex.en: She is small for her age.
ex.zh: 相对她的年龄而言，她个子小了。

ex.en: Stick them on using a small amount of glue.
ex.zh: 用少量胶水把它们粘上。

e.en: A small group or quantity consists of only a few people or things. (规模)

ex.en: A small group of students meets regularly to learn Japanese.
ex.zh: 一个小组的学生定期聚在一起学日语。

e.en: A small child is a very young child.

ex.en: I have a wife and two small children.
ex.zh: 我有妻子和两个年幼的孩子。

e.en: You use small to describe something that is not significant or great in degree. (程度上)

ex.en: It's quite easy to make quite small changes to the way that you work.
ex.zh: 对你的工作方式做些相当细微的调整是很容易的。

ex.en: No detail was too small to escape her attention.
ex.zh: 最微小的细节也逃不过她的注意。

d: adj. 小型的；（数量）少的；小规模的；无关紧要的，不重要的；幼小的，年幼的；（字母）小写的；（嗓音）微弱的，轻柔的；一般的，非极端的；出丑的，羞愧的
n. 小件衣服（尤指内衣）（smalls）；后腰（the small of the/sb.'s back）；小费，小额礼金（smalls）；小件物品；矮小的人
adv. 成小块地；小小地
【名】 （Small）（英）斯莫尔（人名）

e.en: If you remove something from a place, you take it away.

ex.en: As soon as the cake is done, remove it from the oven.
ex.zh: 蛋糕一烤好，就把它从烤箱里移出来。

e.en: If you remove clothing, you take it off. 脱下;

ex.en: He removed his jacket.
ex.zh: 他脱掉了夹克。

e.en: If you remove a stain from something, you make the stain disappear by treating it with a chemical or by washing it. 去除 (痕迹); 洗掉 (污渍)

ex.en: This treatment removes the most stubborn stains.
ex.zh: 这个处理方法能洗掉最顽固的污渍。

e.en: If people remove someone from power or from something such as a committee, they stop them from being in power or being a member of the committee.

ex.en: The student senate voted to remove Fuller from office.
ex.zh: 大学评议会投票将富勒免职了。

d: v. remove 的现在分词，表示移动、去除、清除等
n. 去除，消除；拆除，拆迁（remove 的动名词形式）

e.en: a person who works in metal, esp one who shapes metal by hammering
(in combination) (结合中)

ex.en: a silversmith

d: n. 铁匠；锻工；制作者
vt. 锻制
vi. 锻打金属；当锻工

e.en: If the amount, value, level, or volume of something soars, it quickly increases by a great deal.

ex.en: Insurance claims are expected to soar.
ex.zh: 预计保险索赔会急剧增加。

ex.en: Shares soared on the New York stock exchange.
ex.zh: 纽约证券交易所股票暴涨。

e.en: If something such as a bird soars into the air, it goes quickly up into the air.

ex.en: If you're lucky, a splendid golden eagle may soar into view.
ex.zh: 幸运的话，一只金色雄鹰会跃入视线。

d: adj. 翱翔的，高飞的；猛增的，飞涨的；高耸的，高入云霄的；（情绪等）高涨的
n. 高飞，翱翔；（航空）滑翔；高耸；猛增，飞涨
v. 高飞，翱翔；猛增，飞涨；高耸；（情绪等）高涨（soar 的现在分词）

e.en: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people. 显示;

ex.en: Research shows that young people still look to parents as their main source for health information.
ex.zh: 研究表明年轻人仍然指望父母作为他们主要的健康信息来源。

ex.en: These figures show an increase of over one million in unemployment.
ex.zh: 这些数据表明失业人数增长超过100万。

e.en: If a picture, chart, movie, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it. (图画、图表、文章等)

ex.en: Figure 4.1 shows the respiratory system.
ex.zh: 图4.1所示的是呼吸系统。

ex.en: The cushions, shown left, measure 20 x 12 inches and cost $39.95.
ex.zh: 左边展示的垫子尺寸是20 x 12英寸，价格为$39.95。

e.en: If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to. 拿给…看;

ex.en: Cut out this article and show it to your boss.
ex.zh: 把这篇文章剪下来拿给你的老板看。

ex.en: He showed me the apartment he shares with Esther.
ex.zh: 他指给我看他和埃斯特合住的公寓。

e.en: If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.

ex.en: It was very good of you to come. Let me show you to my study.
ex.zh: 你能来真是太好了。让我带你看我的书房。

ex.en: Milton was shown into the office.
ex.zh: 米尔顿被领进了办公室。

d: v. 显示；表现；展示（show 的过去式）
adv. 成功地，顺利地，圆满地

e.en: Reparations are sums of money that are paid after a war by the defeated country for the damage and injuries it caused in other countries. (战败国须支付的)

ex.en: Israel accepted billions of dollars in war reparations.
ex.zh: 以色列得到了几十亿美元的战争赔款。

e.en: Reparation is help or payment that someone gives you for damage, loss, or suffering that they have caused you. 补偿;

ex.en: There is a clear demand among victims for some sort of reparation from offenders.
ex.zh: 受害者明确要求责任人给予一定的赔偿。

d: n. 战争赔款；赔偿，补偿

e.en: The commonwealth is an organization consisting of the United Kingdom and most of the countries that were previously under its rule.

ex.en: ...the Asian, Caribbean and African members of the commonwealth.
ex.zh: …英联邦在亚洲、加勒比海和非洲的成员国。

e.en: Commonwealth is used in the official names of some countries, groups of countries, or parts of countries.

ex.en: ...the Commonwealth of Australia.
ex.zh: …澳大利亚联邦。

d: n. 国家，独立的政治共同体（尤指民主共和国）；英联邦（the Commonwealth）；界，组织；（自愿加入美国的）自治政区，自治政体（如波多黎各）；（美国的）州（尤指肯塔基、马萨诸塞、宾夕法尼亚和弗吉尼亚）；（澳大利亚）联邦；公益

e.en: having a distinct physical shape or form, often provided by an internal structure (构造)

d: adj. 有结构的，有组织的，有条理的；（计算机）结构化的；（金融）结构性的
v. 组织；安排；构成；建造（structure 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The Caribbean is the sea which is between the West Indies, Central America and the north coast of South America.
Caribbean means belonging or relating to the Caribbean Sea and its islands, or to its people. 加勒比海的;

ex.en: ...the Caribbean island of St. Thomas.
ex.zh: …加勒比海上的圣·托马斯岛。

e.en: A Caribbean is a person from a Caribbean island.

d: adj. 加勒比海的；加勒比人的；加勒比语的
n. 加勒比海
abbr. 英联邦政府首脑会议（Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting）
n．一个姓氏，起源于葡萄牙和西班牙。
n. 印度（南亚国家）

e.en: The position of someone or something is the place where they are in relation to other things.

ex.en: The ship was identified, and its name and position were reported to the Coast Guard.
ex.zh: 该轮船的身份已得到确认，其名称和位置已报告给了海岸警卫队。

e.en: When someone or something is in a particular position, they are sitting, lying, or arranged in that way.

ex.en: It is crucial that the upper back and neck are held in an erect position to give support for the head.
ex.zh: 重要的是：上背和颈部要挺直以支撑头部，这一点很重要。

ex.en: Mr. Dambar had raised himself to a sitting position.
ex.zh: 丹巴先生已坐了起来。

e.en: If you position something somewhere, you put it there carefully, so that it is in the right place or position.

ex.en: Position the cursor where you want the new margins to begin.
ex.zh: 将光标放在你所要的新页边空白开端。

e.en: Your position in society is the role and the importance that you have in it. (社会)

ex.en: Adjustment to their changing role and position in society can be painful for some old people.
ex.zh: 对有些老年人适应他们在社会中不断变化的角色和地位可能是痛苦的。

d: n. 位置，方位；姿势，安置方式；处境，状况；观点，立场；地位，身份；职务，职位；名次；（队员的）职责，角色；恰当位置；阵地；持有状态；（逻辑）命题，主张
v. 安置，使处于；为（产品）定位
adj. 赔偿的；修缮的；弥补的

e.en: Slavery is the system by which people are owned by other people as slaves.

ex.en: My people have survived 400 years of slavery.
ex.zh: 我的民族历经400年的奴隶制度后幸存了下来。

d: n. 奴隶制，蓄奴；奴隶身份，奴役；过分依赖，过分投入
adv. 正式地；按传统（礼仪或规则）；形式上，理论上
n. 阿里

e.en: An apology is something that you say or write in order to tell someone that you are sorry that you have hurt them or caused trouble for them.

ex.en: I didn't get an apology.
ex.zh: 我没有得到道歉之词。

ex.en: We received a letter of apology.
ex.zh: 我们收到了一封致歉信。

e.en: If you offer or make your apologies, you apologize. (表达)

ex.en: When Mary finally appeared, she made her apologies to Mrs. Velasquez.
ex.zh: 当玛丽最终露面时，她向委拉斯开兹夫人道了歉。

d: n. 道歉；（因不能赴会的）道歉信；辩护，辩解；勉强（或不适当的）替代物；糟糕的例子

e.en: If you welcome someone, you greet them in a friendly way when they arrive somewhere.

ex.en: Several people came by to welcome me.
ex.zh: 几个人走过来欢迎我。

ex.en: She was there to welcome him home from war.
ex.zh: 她在那里欢迎他从战场回家。

e.en: Welcome is also a noun.

ex.en: There would be a fantastic welcome awaiting him back here.
ex.zh: 会有一场热烈的欢迎仪式迎接他回来。

e.en: You use welcome in expressions such as welcome home, welcome to Boston, and welcome back when you are greeting someone who has just arrived somewhere.

ex.en: Welcome to Washington.
ex.zh: 欢迎来到华盛顿。

e.en: If you welcome an action, decision, or situation, you approve of it and are pleased that it has occurred.

ex.en: She welcomed this move but said that overall the changes didn't go far enough.
ex.zh: 她欣然接受了这一举措，但又说总体上改变还不彻底。

d: v. welcome 的过去式和过去分词：欢迎，迎接；欣然接受，赞成（行动、决定等）；（被动语态）受到欢迎，被热情接纳。
adj. 受欢迎的，被欣然接受的。
