e.en: If you rid yourself of something you do not want, you take action so that you no longer have it or are no longer affected by it. 使 (自己)

ex.en: Why couldn't he ever rid himself of those thoughts, those worries?
ex.zh: 为什么他始终摆脱不了那些想法、那些担忧呢？

d: v. 使……去掉，使……去除；摆脱，消除
adj. 得到解脱的
【名】 （Rid）（俄、德、英、美）里德（人名）

e.en: A scroll is a long roll of paper or a similar material with writing on it. (写有文字的)

ex.en: Ancient scrolls were found in caves by the Dead Sea.
ex.zh: 在死海边的洞穴里发现了古代的卷轴。

e.en: A scroll is a painted or carved decoration made to look like a scroll.

ex.en: ...a handsome suite of chairs incised with Grecian scrolls.
ex.zh: …一套漂亮的刻有古希腊式卷轴形装饰的椅子。

e.en: If you scroll through text on a computer screen, you move the text up or down to find the information that you need. (在计算机屏幕上的文本中)

ex.en: I scrolled down to find "United States of America."
ex.zh: 我向下滚动以寻找。

d: n. 滚动，卷动
v. 滚动，卷动（scroll 的现在分词/动名词）；浏览，刷（社交媒体内容）
adj. 滚动的，卷动的

e.en: If people promote something, they help or encourage it to happen, increase, or spread.

ex.en: You don't have to sacrifice environmental protection to promote economic growth.
ex.zh: 你们没有必要牺牲环保来促进经济增长。

e.en: 促进

ex.en: The government has pledged to give the promotion of democracy higher priority.
ex.zh: 政府已承诺要给民主的促进以更高的优先级。

e.en: If a firm promotes a product, it tries to increase the sales or popularity of that product.

ex.en: ...a tour to promote his second solo album.
ex.zh: …一场促销他第二张个人专辑的巡回演出。

e.en: If someone is promoted, they are given a more important job or rank in the organization that they work for.

ex.en: I was promoted to editor and then editorial director.
ex.zh: 我晋升为编辑，之后又晋升为编辑部主任。

d: v. 促进，推动，发扬；推销，推广，促销；晋升，提拔，职位提升（promote 的现在分词）

e.en: Spots are small, round, coloured areas on a surface.

ex.en: The leaves have yellow areas on the top and underneath are powdery orange spots.
ex.zh: 叶子上端有黄色斑块，下方有粉状橙色斑点。

e.en: Spots on a person's skin are small lumps or marks. (皮肤上的) 小疙瘩;

ex.en: My brother's face was covered with spots.
ex.zh: 我弟弟曾满脸疙瘩。

e.en: You can refer to a particular place as a spot.

ex.en: They stayed at several of the island's top tourist spots.
ex.zh: 他们在岛上几个最好的旅游景点呆过。

e.en: A spot in a television or radio show is a part of it that is regularly reserved for a particular performer or type of entertainment.

ex.en: Unsuccessful at screen writing, he got a spot on a CNN show.
ex.zh: 电影剧本创作方面未能成功，之后他在CNN得到了一个固定节目档。

d: n. 地点，场所；点，斑点；污点，污渍；丘疹，疱疹；某演员的固定节目；排名位置； 少量，一点；几滴，少许（液体）；困境，窘境；现货交易，现金交易；聚光灯（spotlight 的简称）；（多米诺牌、纸牌或骰子上的）点；调灰泥板，调石膏板；（特定面值的）钞票；（英足）点球点
v. 看见，注意到；让分，让步；飘了几滴雨；借（钱）给；使有斑点，使有污迹；稀疏地点缀；在场监护（运动员）；（军）确定敌人的位置；将（球）放在适当位置
adj. 现货交易的，立即支付的

e.en: You can use stuff to refer to things such as a substance, a collection of things, events, or ideas, or the contents of something in a general way without mentioning the thing itself by name.

ex.en: I'd like some coffee, and I don't object to the powdered stuff if it's all you've got.
ex.zh: 我想要点咖啡，如果你们只有粉状的东西，我也不反对。

ex.en: He pointed to a duffle bag. "That's my stuff."
ex.zh: 他指着一个旅行袋。“那是我的东西。”

e.en: If you stuff something somewhere, you push it there quickly and roughly.

ex.en: I stuffed my hands in my pockets.
ex.zh: 我把双手塞进了我的口袋里。

e.en: If you stuff a container or space with something, you fill it with something or with a quantity of things until it is full.

ex.en: He grabbed my purse, opened it and stuffed it full, then gave it back to me.
ex.zh: 他抢走我的钱包，打开并把它装得满满的，然后还给了我。

e.en: If you stuff yourself, you eat a lot of food.

ex.en: I could stuff myself with ten chocolate bars and half an hour later eat a big meal.
ex.zh: 我可以给自己塞下10块巧克力，并在半小时后再大吃一顿。

d: n. 东西，物品；基本特征，特质，根本；（某人从事的）活动，事情；原材料；投球能力；作品，乐曲，艺术；胡说八道，废话，荒谬的想法；饮料，毒品；毛料，呢绒
v. 塞进，填进；填满，装满；填作料，填馅；制作（动物）标本；（使）吃撑，吃足；不稀罕，不在乎；把同样的印刷品装进（信封）；把伪造选票投入（票箱）；性交（一个男人和一个女人性交）

e.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you do not trust them, and are careful when dealing with them.

ex.en: He was rightly suspicious of meeting me until I reassured him I was not writing about him.
ex.zh: 他对于见我充满疑虑，直到我向他再次保证我不是在写有关他的东西。

e.en: 怀疑地

ex.en: "What is it you want me to do?" Adams asked suspiciously.
ex.zh: “你要我去干的是什么？”亚当斯怀疑地问道。

e.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you believe that they are probably involved in a crime or some dishonest activity.

ex.en: Two officers on patrol became suspicious of two men in a car.
ex.zh: 两位巡警对一辆小汽车内的两名男子起了疑心。

e.en: If you describe someone or something as suspicious, you mean that there is some aspect of them which makes you think that they are involved in a crime or a dishonest activity.

ex.en: He reported that two suspicious-looking characters had approached Callendar.
ex.zh: 他报告说两名看似可疑的人曾靠近过卡兰德。

d: adj. 感觉可疑的，怀疑的；不信任的，持怀疑态度的；令人怀疑的，引起怀疑的

e.en: A user is a person or thing that uses something such as a place, facility, product, or machine. 使用者;

ex.en: Beach users have complained that the bikes are noisy.
ex.zh: 去海滩的人已在抱怨那些自行车太吵。

ex.en: ...a regular user of the subway.
ex.zh: …一个定期乘坐地铁的人。

d: n. 用户，使用者；（User）（土）乌塞尔（人名）

e.en: If you visit someone, you go to see them and spend time with them.

ex.en: He wanted to visit his brother in Worcester.
ex.zh: 他想去拜访住在伍斯特的兄弟。

ex.en: In the evenings, friends would visit.
ex.zh: 晚上朋友们会来拜访。

e.en: Visit is also a noun.

ex.en: Helen had recently paid him a visit.
ex.zh: 海伦最近拜访了他。

e.en: If you visit a place, you go there for a short time.

ex.en: He'll be visiting four cities including Cagliari in Sardinia.
ex.zh: 他将访问4座城市，包括撒丁岛的卡利亚里。

ex.en: ...a visiting family from Texas.
ex.zh: …一个从得克萨斯来访的家庭。

e.en: Visit is also a noun.

ex.en: ...the pope's visit to Canada.
ex.zh: …教皇对加拿大的访问。

d: v. 参观，游览；拜访，作客；浏览（网页）；视察，巡视；找（医生或律师）咨询；闲谈；（多作圣经用语）（上帝）救助（某人），降临（某地）；使某人遭受（有害或不快之事）
n. 参观，游览；拜访，作客；（政治领导人或公务员的）访问，视察；（到网站的）访问；（在宾馆或汽车旅馆等的）住宿，逗留；就诊，咨询（律师等）；会面，闲聊
【名】 （Visit）（泰）威实（人名）

e.en: When you walk, you move forward by putting one foot in front of the other in a regular way. 行走;

ex.en: Rosanna and Forbes walked in silence.
ex.zh: 罗莎娜与福布斯默默地走着。

ex.en: We walked into the foyer.
ex.zh: 我们走进前厅。

e.en: A walk is a trip that you make by walking, usually for pleasure.

ex.en: I went for a walk.
ex.zh: 我去散步了。

e.en: A walk of a particular distance is the distance that a person has to walk to get somewhere.

ex.en: It was only a three-mile walk to Kabul from there.
ex.zh: 从那里到喀布尔只有3英里的步行路程。

e.en: A walk is a route suitable for walking along for pleasure. (适宜散步的)

ex.en: ...a 2-mile coastal walk.
ex.zh: …一条2英里长的海边人行道。

d: v. 走，步行；徒步旅行，散步；陪（某人）走，护送（某人）；带（宠物）散步，遛；把（某物）移走，使（某物）移动；消失，被偷；轻易做成（某事）；放弃，突然退出；出现，显灵；（使）上一垒；被无罪释放，未获刑罚；（击球手不等裁判指示）离开球场；生活
n. 步行，散步；徒步旅行；散步的小路，步行的路径；步态；步行的距离（或时间）；步行速度；（棒球）自由上垒；（护林人的）管辖林区；斗鸡场；小猎犬驯养场；（邮递员的）投递路线；一群沙锥
【名】 （Walk）（美）沃克（人名）

e.en: The wheels of a vehicle are the circular objects that are attached underneath it and that enable it to move along the ground.

ex.en: The car wheels spun and slipped on some oil on the road.
ex.zh: 小汽车的车轮在路面的油迹上空转打了滑。

e.en: A wheel is a circular object that forms a part of a machine, usually a moving part.

ex.en: The wheels are usually fairly large.
ex.zh: 该机轮通常相当大。

e.en: The wheel of a car or other vehicle is the circular object that is used to steer it. The wheel is used in expressions to talk about who is driving a vehicle. For example, if someone is at the wheel or behind the wheel of a car, they are driving it.

ex.en: My co-pilot suddenly grabbed the wheel.
ex.zh: 我的副驾驶突然抢过了方向盘。

ex.en: Curtis got behind the wheel and they started back toward the cottage.
ex.zh: 柯蒂斯开车，他们启程返回小屋。

e.en: If you wheel an object that has wheels somewhere, you push it along. 推 (带轮子的物体)

ex.en: He wheeled his bike into the alley at the side of the house.
ex.zh: 他把自行车推进了房屋一侧的胡同里。

d: n. 轮子，车轮；汽车（wheels）；机轮，齿轮，传动轮；（汽车、轮船等的）方向盘，转向盘；系统，机构；轮状物；轮盘（一种旋转的赌具）；轮；重要人物，大亨；轮式机械（或器具）；旋转，回旋；（诗歌等的）叠句；（用于牵拉或分裂肢体的）轮式刑车（the wheel）
v. 推，拉（带轮运输工具）；用有轮之物推动（或拉动、移动）……；（鸟或飞机）盘旋；（使）迅速转身，猛然转身

e.en: You've is the usual spoken form of "you have," when "have" is an auxiliary verb. (you have)的常用口语形式，其中(have)

ex.en: You've got to see it to believe it.
ex.zh: 你要看见了才能相信。

d: abbr. you have 的缩略形式（口语中常见，尤用于 have 作助动词时）：你已，你有

e.en: Someone who is wealthy has a large amount of money, property, or valuable possessions.

ex.en: ...a wealthy international businessman.
ex.zh: …一个富有的跨国商人。

e.en: The wealthy are people who are wealthy.

ex.en: The best education should not be available only to the wealthy.
ex.zh: 不应该只有富人才能得到最好的教育。

d: adj. 富有的，丰富的
n. 富人（the wealthy）

e.en: Your bones are the hard parts inside your body that together form your skeleton.

ex.en: Many passengers suffered broken bones.
ex.zh: 许多乘客骨折了。

ex.en: The body is made up primarily of bone, muscle, and fat.
ex.zh: 人体主要由骨、肌肉和脂肪组成。

e.en: If you bone a piece of meat or fish, you remove the bones from it before cooking it. 去 (肉、鱼)

ex.en: Make sure that you do not pierce the skin when boning the chicken thighs.
ex.zh: 给鸡腿去骨时，确保不要刺破皮。

e.en: A bone tool or ornament is made of bone.

ex.en: ...a small, expensive pocketknife with a bone handle.
ex.zh: …一把昂贵的、带骨制刀把的小刀。

e.en: The bare bones of something are its most basic parts or details.

ex.en: There are not even the bare bones of a garden here – I've got nothing.
ex.zh: 这儿连花园的最基本的东西都没有–我一无所获。

d: n. 骨骼，骨头（bone 的复数）；身体（bone 的复数）；争议点（bone 的复数）；the bare bones of something：基本要素，梗概；（音乐）响板（一种打击乐器）；（Bones）人名；（英）博恩斯；（德）博内斯
v. 剔去……的骨，去骨（bone 的第三人称单数）；bone up (on) 的第三人称单数 bones up：专心致志地学习，钻研（科目）

e.en: If someone forages for something, they search for it in a busy way.

ex.en: They were forced to forage for clothing and fuel.
ex.zh: 他们被迫匆忙搜寻衣物和燃料。

e.en: When animals forage, they search for food. (动物)

ex.en: We disturbed a wild boar that had been foraging by the roadside.
ex.zh: 我们惊动了一只在路边觅食的野公猪。

d: v. 觅食；用手搜寻东西；搜得（食物）；从（某地）搜到食物；给……提供食物（forage 的现在分词）
n. 觅食行为
n. 马拉维（非洲中南部内陆国家）

e.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it. 碎片;

ex.en: The only reminder of the shooting is a few fragments of metal in my shoulder.
ex.zh: 惟一使我记起那次枪击的，是我肩膀里的一些金属碎片。

ex.en: She read everything, digesting every fragment of news.
ex.zh: 她什么都读，对新闻的每一个片段都细细品味。

e.en: If something fragments or is fragmented, it breaks or separates into small pieces or parts.

ex.en: The clouds fragmented and out came the sun.
ex.zh: 云开日出。

e.en: 分裂

ex.en: ...the extraordinary fragmentation of styles on the music scene.
ex.zh: …音乐界各种风格的不寻常分化。

d: n. 碎片（fragment 的复数）；片断；（计）分段
v. 破碎，打碎（fragment 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, especially to the period in history before the end of the Roman Empire.

ex.en: They believed ancient Greece and Rome were vital sources of learning.
ex.zh: 他们认为古希腊和古罗马是至关重要的知识来源。

e.en: Ancient means very old, or having existed for a long time.

ex.en: ...ancient Jewish tradition.
ex.zh: …古老的犹太传统。

e.en: a member of a civilized nation in the ancient world, esp a Greek, Roman, or Hebrew 古(希腊、罗马或希伯来)
a flag or other banner; standard 旗帜;

d: adj. 古代的，远古的；古老的，年代久远的；老的，老掉牙的
n. （尤指埃及、希腊和罗马的）古代人；老头

e.en: a traditional Israeli or Romanian circle dance (以色列或罗马尼亚传统)

d: n. 霍拉舞（一种传统式圆舞）；（Hora）人名；（尼、捷、罗）霍拉；（法、西、葡）奥拉

e.en: Northern means in or from the north of a region, state, or country. 在北部的;

ex.en: Their two children were immigrants to Northern Ireland from Pennsylvania.
ex.zh: 他们的两个孩子是从宾夕法尼亚到北爱尔兰的移民。

d: adj. 北方的，向北的，北部的；生活在北方的，源自北方的；（风）北方吹来的
n. （美国）北部方言（Northern）

e.en: personal abilities or talents 个人能力;

ex.en: a man of many parts

d: n. 部分；（动植物的）器官，部位；部件，零件；（世界、国家或城镇等的）区域，地区；（在活动或事件中的）作用（part 的复数）
v. （使）分开，（使）分离；放弃，移交；给（头发）分缝（part 的第三人称单数）
n. （Parts）帕茨（姓氏）

e.en: Your teeth are the hard white objects in your mouth, which you use for biting and chewing.

ex.en: She had very pretty straight teeth.
ex.zh: 她有非常漂亮整齐的牙齿。

e.en: The teeth of something such as a comb, saw, cog, or zipper are the parts that stick out in a row on its edge. (梳子、锯子、齿轮或拉链等物的)

ex.en: The front cog has 44 teeth.
ex.zh: 前齿轮有44个齿。

e.en: If you have a sweet tooth, you like sweet food very much.

ex.en: Add more honey if you have a sweet tooth.
ex.zh: 如果你嗜好甜食就多加些蜂蜜。

d: n. 牙，齿；（工具边缘、梳子、锯、拉链等的）齿状物，齿；（官方组织、法律等的）威力，效力（teeth）；口味，爱好；粗糙面（颜料、胶水能黏附于上）
v. 给……装齿；啮合
【名】 （Tooth）（英）图思（人名）

e.en: Territory is land which is controlled by a particular country or ruler.

ex.en: The government denies that any of its territory is under rebel control.
ex.zh: 该政府否认有任何领土被叛乱者控制。

ex.en: ...the view that the US should use military force only when our borders or US territories are attacked.
ex.zh: …那种观点认为只有我们的边界或美国领土受到袭击时美国才应该使用武力。

e.en: A territory is a country or region that is controlled by another country.

ex.en: He toured some of the disputed territories now under UN control.
ex.zh: 他巡访过一些现归联合国管辖的有争议的属地。

e.en: You can use territory to refer to an area of knowledge or experience.

ex.en: Following the futuristic "The Handmaid's Tale," Margaret Atwood's seventh novel, "Cat's Eye," returns to more familiar territory.
ex.zh: 在推出具有未来主义色彩的《女仆的故事》之后，玛格丽特·阿特伍德的第7部小说《猫眼》返回了更为熟悉的领域。

e.en: An animal's territory is an area which it regards as its own and which it defends when other animals try to enter it. (动物的)

ex.en: The territory of a cat only remains fixed for as long as the cat dominates the area.
ex.zh: 猫的地盘只在它占据那个地方的时候才保持稳定不变。

d: n. 领土，版图，领地；（美国、加拿大等的）准州；（某些国家划分的）地区；（某一动物或人想控制的）领地，地盘；（某人负责的）区域，地区；（具有某种特性的）地区，地方；（知识等的）领域，范围；（体育运动中的）防守区

e.en: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

ex.en: He suggested a link between class size and test results of seven-year-olds.
ex.zh: 他建议把7岁儿童的班级大小和考试结果相关联。

ex.en: I suggest you ask him some specific questions about his past.
ex.zh: 我建议你问问他有关他的过去的一些具体问题。

e.en: If you suggest the name of a person or place, you recommend them to someone.

ex.en: Could you suggest someone to advise me how to do this?
ex.zh: 你能推荐一个人来建议我怎么做这件事吗？

e.en: If you suggest that something is the case, you say something which you believe is the case.

ex.en: I'm not suggesting that is what is happening.
ex.zh: 我并不是说那就是所发生的情况。

ex.en: It is wrong to suggest that there are easy alternatives.
ex.zh: 认为有容易的选择是错误的。

e.en: If one thing suggests another, it implies it or makes you think that it might be the case.

ex.en: Earlier reports suggested that a meeting would take place on Sunday.
ex.zh: 早期的报道暗示了一次会议将在周日举行。

d: v. 暗示，建议（suggest的suggest的第三人称单数）
adj. 考古学的，考古的
n. 可用性，可得性；空闲，闲暇；未婚，单身

e.en: Broken is the past participle of break. (break)
A broken line is not continuous but has gaps or spaces in it. 虚的 (线)

ex.en: A broken blue line means the course of a waterless valley.
ex.zh: 蓝色虚线代表无水流过的山谷走向。

e.en: You can use broken to describe a marriage that has ended in divorce, or a home in which the parents of the family are divorced, when you think this is a sad or bad thing. (婚姻)

ex.en: She spoke for the first time about the traumas of a broken marriage.
ex.zh: 她第一次说起婚姻破裂之痛。

e.en: If someone talks in broken English, for example, or in broken French, they speak slowly and make a lot of mistakes because they do not know the language very well.

ex.en: Eric could only respond in broken English.
ex.zh: 埃里克只能用蹩脚的英语应答。

d: adj. 损坏的，破碎的；衰弱的，颓丧的；间断的，不连续的；破裂的，终止的；违背的，未遵守的；蹩脚的，不流利的；凹凸不平的，坎坷的
v. 打碎；弄坏；违反（break 的过去分词形式）

e.en: The boundary of an area of land is an imaginary line that separates it from other areas.

ex.en: The Bow Brook forms the western boundary of the wood.
ex.zh: 鲍溪成了树林的西边界。

e.en: The boundaries of something such as a subject or activity are the limits that people think that it has.

ex.en: The boundaries between history and storytelling are always being blurred and muddled.
ex.zh: 历史与故事的界限一直模糊不清。

d: n. 边界，分界线；界限，限度；（板球）将球击过边界线得分（boundary 的复数）

e.en: Your fingers are the long thin parts at the end of each hand, sometimes also including the thumb.

ex.en: She suddenly held up a small, bony finger and pointed across the room.
ex.zh: 她突然举起一根瘦小的手指指向房间的另一头。

ex.en: She ran her fingers through her hair.
ex.zh: 她用手指捋了捋头发。

e.en: The fingers of a glove are the parts that a person's fingers fit into. (手套的)

ex.en: He bit the fingers of his right glove and pulled it off.
ex.zh: 他咬住右手手套的指套，把它扯了下来。

e.en: A finger of something such as smoke or land is an amount of it that is shaped rather like a finger.

ex.en: ...a thin finger of land that separates Pakistan from the former Soviet Union.
ex.zh: …一片分隔巴基斯坦和前苏联的狭长地带。

e.en: If you finger something, you touch or feel it with your fingers.

ex.en: He fingered the few coins in his pocket.
ex.zh: 他用手指摸了摸他兜里的几枚硬币。

d: n. 手指；（手套的）手指部分；（酒在杯中的深度）一指宽；指状物；竖中指；指针
v. 用手指触摸；告发，告密；拨弄（乐器）；用某种指法演奏（乐曲）；给（乐谱）标明指法符号
【名】 （Finger）（英、德、捷）芬格，（俄）芬格尔（人名）
n. 搜寻食物（或给养）的人或动物，觅食者；四处寻找的人，到处搜寻者
n. 切尔西（英国伦敦西部的一个地区，曾为文艺界人士聚居地）；切尔西队（英格兰足球俱乐部，位于伦敦）；切尔西（英语女子名）；切尔西区（美国纽约曼哈顿的一个街区）

e.en: Chemical means involving or resulting from a reaction between two or more substances, or relating to the substances that something consists of.

ex.en: ...chemical reactions that cause ozone destruction.
ex.zh: …导致臭氧破坏的化学反应。

ex.en: ...the chemical composition of the ocean.
ex.zh: …海洋的化学成分。

e.en: 经化学方式

ex.en: ...chemically treated foods.
ex.zh: …经化学方式处理过的食品。

e.en: Chemicals are substances that are used in a chemical process or made by a chemical process. 化学物;

ex.en: The whole food chain is affected by the overuse of chemicals in agriculture.
ex.zh: 整个食物链受到了化学物质在农业中过度使用的影响。

ex.en: ...a chemical company.
ex.zh: …一家化学制品公司。

d: adj. 化学的，与化学有关的
n. 化学品，化学制品；成瘾的药物

e.en: Hunting is the chasing and killing of wild animals by people or other animals, for food or as a sport. 狩猎;

ex.en: He'd gone deer hunting with his cousins.
ex.zh: 他已和堂兄弟们猎鹿去了。

e.en: Hunting is the activity of searching for a particular thing.

ex.en: Job hunting should be approached as a job in itself.
ex.zh: 找工作本身就应当被看作是一种工作。

e.tip: 与非可数名词结合的复合词
e.en: Hunting is also a combining form. 寻求… (用于构词成分)

ex.en: Make job-hunting a full-time job until you find one.
ex.zh: 在你找到工作之前，把求职当作一项全职工作。

d: n. 打猎，狩猎；搜寻，寻找；摆动，不规则振荡
adj. 打猎的
v. 打猎，猎取；搜寻，搜索；追踪，追捕（hunt 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Hunting）（英）亨廷（人名）

e.en: A meal is an occasion when people sit down and eat, usually at a regular time.

ex.en: She sat next to him throughout the meal.
ex.zh: 她在这一顿饭的时间里坐在他旁边。

e.en: A meal is the food you eat during a meal. (一餐所吃的)

ex.en: The waiter offered him red wine or white wine with his meal.
ex.zh: 那位侍者为他的餐配了红葡萄酒或白葡萄酒。

e.en: the edible part of a grain or pulse (excluding wheat) ground to a coarse powder, used chiefly as animal food
If you have a square meal, you have a large, healthy meal.

ex.en: The troops are very tired. They haven't had a square meal for four or five days.
ex.zh: 这些部队非常疲惫。他们已经四五天没有丰盛食物了。

d: n. 一餐，进餐（时间）；一餐所吃的食物；磨成粗粉的东西
v. 进餐

e.en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

ex.en: We had a long talk about the problem of materialism in modern society.
ex.zh: 我们就现代社会中的实利主义问题进行了一次长谈。

e.en: Something that is modern is new and involves the latest ideas or equipment.

ex.en: In many ways, it was a very modern school for its time.
ex.zh: 从多方面看，这是当时很现代化的一所学校。

e.en: People are sometimes described as modern when they have opinions or ways of behaving that have not yet been accepted by most people in a society.

ex.en: She is very modern in outlook.
ex.zh: 她的看法很时髦。

e.en: Modern is used to describe styles of art, dance, music, and architecture that have developed in recent times, in contrast to classical styles. (艺术、舞蹈、音乐和建筑)

ex.en: She'd been a dancer with a modern dance company in New York.
ex.zh: 她过去一直是纽约一家现代舞公司的舞蹈演员。

d: adj. 近代的，现代的；当代风格的，现代派的；现代化的，新式的；摩登的，时髦的
n. 现代人；现代派艺术家；主张现代风格的人，宣扬现代价值观的人

e.en: A mountain is a very high area of land with steep sides.

ex.en: Mt. McKinley, in Alaska, is the highest mountain in North America.
ex.zh: 位于阿拉斯加的麦金利山是北美最高的山。

e.en: If you talk about a mountain of something, or mountains of something, you are emphasizing that there is a large amount of it.

ex.en: They are faced with a mountain of bureaucracy.
ex.zh: 他们面临着一大堆的官僚制度。

e.en: If you say that someone has a mountain to climb, you mean that it will be difficult for them to achieve what they want to achieve.

ex.en: "We had a mountain to climb after the second goal went in," said Crosby.
ex.zh: 克罗斯比说:“第2个球进了后，我们面临着很大的困难。”

d: n. 山，高山；许多，大量（a mountain/mountains of）；（食物的）过剩，积压
【名】 （Mountain）（英）芒廷（人名）
n. 宫（粤语姓氏）；龚

e.en: harassed and worn

ex.en: he has a hunted look

d: adj. 被追捕的，被捕猎的，受迫害的；（多指目光或神情）惶恐不安的，惴惴不安的；疲惫的，疲惫不堪的
v. hunt 的过去式和过去分词（狩猎、追捕、搜寻）

e.en: You use present to describe things and people that exist now, rather than those that existed in the past or those that may exist in the future.

ex.en: He has brought much of the present crisis on himself.
ex.zh: 他目前的危机大多是他自己造成的。

ex.en: ...the government's present economic difficulties.
ex.zh: …政府目前的经济困难。

e.en: The present is the period of time that we are in now and the things that are happening now.

ex.en: ...his struggle to reconcile the past with the present.
ex.zh: …他将过去和现在调和的斗争。

ex.en: ...continuing right up to the present.
ex.zh: …一直持续到现在。

e.en: A situation that exists at present exists now, although it may change.

ex.en: There is no way at present of predicting which individuals will develop the disease.
ex.zh: 目前还没有办法预言哪些人会患这种病。

e.en: The present day is the period of history that we are in now.

ex.en: ...Western European art from the period of Giotto to the present day.
ex.zh: …从乔托时代到现代的西欧艺术。

d: adj. （人）在场的，出席的；（事物）存在的；现在的，目前的；考虑中的，正在讨论的；（语法）现在时（态）的；历历在目的
n. 现在，目前；礼物，赠品；（语法）现在时；（举枪的）瞄准（姿势）
v. 颁发，赠送；出示（护照等供检查）；正式提交（支票，账单）； 正式引见，介绍；正式出席，到场；引起，造成；表达（歉意等）；提出，陈述；上映，播出；展示，表现； 主持（广播或电视节目）；把……对准；（病人）呈现症状
n. 奥凯克人

e.en: A creature's prey are the creatures that it hunts and eats in order to live.

ex.en: Electric rays stun their prey with huge electrical discharges.
ex.zh: 电鳐释放大量的电荷将他们的猎物击昏。

e.en: A creature that preys on other creatures lives by catching and eating them.

ex.en: The effect was to disrupt the food chain, starving many animals and those that preyed on them.
ex.zh: 后果是打断食物链，使许多动物和捕食它们的动物饿死。

e.en: You can refer to the people who someone tries to harm or trick as their prey. (某人的)

ex.en: Police officers lie in wait for the gangs who stalk their prey at night.
ex.zh: 警官们埋伏起来等待捉拿那些夜间悄悄追踪作案对象的黑帮成员。

e.en: If someone preys on other people, especially people who are unable to protect themselves, they take advantage of them or harm them in some way.

ex.en: Pam had never learned that there were men who preyed on young runaways.
ex.zh: 帕姆从未了解到有些人专门坑害那些年轻的离家出走者。

d: n. 猎物，捕获物；受害者，受骗者；掠夺品
v. 捕食；欺凌，坑害（尤指弱者）；不断困扰，折磨
【名】 （Prey）（美、德、爱）普赖（人名）

e.en: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later. 记录;

ex.en: Keep a record of all the payments.
ex.zh: 对所有付款做一个记录。

ex.en: There's no record of any marriage or children.
ex.zh: 没有任何有关结婚或子女的记录。

e.en: If you record a piece of information or an event, you write it down, photograph it, or put it into a computer so that in the future people can refer to it. 记录;

ex.en: Her letters record the domestic and social details of diplomatic life in China.
ex.zh: 她的信件记录了在中国的外交生活中家庭和社会活动的细节。

e.en: If you record something such as a speech or performance, you put it on tape or film so that it can be heard or seen again later. 录音;

ex.en: There is nothing to stop viewers from recording the films on videotape.
ex.zh: 没有办法阻止观众用录像带录下电影。

e.en: If a musician or performer records a piece of music or a television or radio show, they perform it so that it can be put onto CD, tape, or film.

ex.en: It took the musicians two and a half days to record their soundtrack for the film.
ex.zh: 音乐家们花了两天半的时间录制电影的配乐。

d: v. record 的过去式和过去分词：记录，记载；录制；（仪器）显示，标示；（尤指体育等）获得（成绩）
adj. 记录下来的；已登记的；（音乐、影像等）已录制的
adj. 最小的（small 的最高级）

e.en: If you say that an event is predictable, you mean that it is obvious in advance that it will happen.

ex.en: This was a predictable reaction, given the bitter hostility between the two countries.
ex.zh: 考虑到两国之间的强烈敌意，这种反应是可以预见的。

e.en: 可预见地

ex.en: His article is, predictably, a scathing attack on capitalism.
ex.zh: 可以预见，他的文章会是对资本主义的猛烈抨击。

d: adj. 可预测的，可预料的；老套乏味的，墨守成规的

e.en: Teeth is the plural of . (tooth)

d: n. 牙齿（tooth 的复数）；（机械、工具等的）齿，齿状物

e.en: Stone is a hard solid substance found in the ground and often used for building houses.

ex.en: He could not tell whether the floor was wood or stone.
ex.zh: 他分不清这地板是木头的还是石头的。

ex.en: People often don't appreciate that marble is a natural stone.
ex.zh: 人们往往不了解大理石是一种天然石头。

e.en: A stone is a small piece of rock that is found on the ground.

ex.en: He removed a stone from his shoe.
ex.zh: 他清除了鞋中的一粒石子。

e.en: A stone is a large piece of stone put somewhere in memory of a person or event, or as a religious symbol.

ex.en: The monument consists of a circle of gigantic stones.
ex.zh: 该纪念碑由一圈巨大的石碑组成。

e.en: Stone is used in expressions such as set in stone and tablets of stone to suggest that an idea or rule is firm and fixed, and cannot be changed. (思想或规则)

ex.en: He is merely throwing the idea forward for discussion, it is not cast in stone.
ex.zh: 他只是抛出个想法供讨论，不是固定不变的。

d: n. 石头，石料；石块；宝石；果核；结石； 英石（英国重量单位,相当于6.35千克或14磅）；纪念碑，石碑；（指重量或缺少感情、表情或动作）像石头一样；（天文）陨石；CURLING STONE的简称；（桌游中的）棋子，筹码；排版用石台，石印台；（表示观念或规则固定而不可改变）板上钉钉；石头色，石青色
v. 向……扔石头；去核；用石头建（或铺）
adj. 石的，石制的
adv. 完全地，全部地

e.en: If you trace the origin or development of something, you find out or describe how it started or developed.

ex.en: The exhibition traces the history of graphic design in America from the 19th century to the present.
ex.zh: 这个展览会追溯了从19世纪到现在美国平面设计的历史。

e.en: Trace back means the same as .

ex.en: ...Bronx residents who trace their families back to Dutch settlers.
ex.zh: …将自己的家族追溯到荷兰移民者们的布朗克斯居民。

e.en: If you trace someone or something, you find them after looking for them.

ex.en: Police are anxious to trace two men seen leaving the house just before 8am.
ex.zh: 警察急切想找到在接近早晨8点前被人看到离开那幢房子的两名男子。

e.en: If you trace something such as a pattern or a shape, for example, with your finger or toe, you mark its outline on a surface. 勾画出 (轮廓)

ex.en: I traced the course of the river on the map spread out on my briefcase.
ex.zh: 我在自己公文包上铺展开的地图中勾画出了这条河的流向。

d: n. 痕迹，踪迹，遗迹（均为 trace 的复数）；微量，少许（常与 of 搭配）
v. （trace 的第三人称单数形式）追溯；找到，查出；描摹，摹写；勾画……的轮廓；（计算机／电子）跟踪，追踪

e.en: A valley is a low stretch of land between hills, especially one that has a river flowing through it.

ex.en: ...a wooded valley set against the backdrop of Monte Rosa.
ex.zh: …罗莎峰前一个林木繁茂的山谷。

d: n. 山谷，溪谷，谷地；流域，河谷地区；（Valley）人名；瓦利；瓦莱

e.en: A wildebeest is a large African antelope that has a hairy tail, short curved horns, and long hair under its neck. Wildebeest usually live in large groups.

d: n. 牛羚，角马（一种大型非洲羚羊，产于非洲，头形似牛，有短弯角和长尾毛）

e.en: Your age is the number of years that you have lived. (人的)

ex.en: She has a nephew who is just ten years of age.
ex.zh: 她有个才满10岁的侄子。

ex.en: At the age of sixteen he qualified for a place at the University of North Carolina.
ex.zh: 16岁时他取得了北卡罗来纳大学的入学资格。

e.en: The age of a thing is the number of years since it was made. (物的)

ex.en: Everything in the room looks in keeping with the age of the building.
ex.zh: 该房间里的一切看起来都和该楼的年代相符。

e.en: Age is the state of being old or the process of becoming older. 年长;

ex.en: Perhaps he has grown wiser with age.
ex.zh: 或许他已经随着年龄的增长变得更睿智了。

ex.en: This cologne, like wine, improves with age.
ex.zh: 这种科隆香水像葡萄酒一样越陈越香。

e.en: When someone ages, or when something ages them, they seem much older and less strong or less alert. 使显老;

ex.en: He had always looked so young, but he seemed to have aged in the last few months.
ex.zh: 他曾一直显得很年轻，但是在过去的几个月里他似乎显得老了。

d: n. 年龄，年龄段，年龄范围（age 的复数形式）；很长时间，很久（非正式，常用于 for ages、ages ago、in ages 等）；时代，年代，历史时期（age 的复数形式，常用于 through the ages、the Middle Ages 等）
vi. 变老，衰老；年龄增长；（酒、奶酪等）陈化，成熟（age 的第三人称单数）
vt. 使变老，使显老；使（酒、奶酪等）陈化，成熟；测定，鉴定（马、化石、文物等）的年龄（age 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The amount of something is how much there is, or how much you have, need, or get.

ex.en: He needs that amount of money to survive.
ex.zh: 他需要那笔钱来维持生活。

ex.en: I still do a certain amount of work for them.
ex.zh: 我仍旧为他们做一定数量的工作。

e.en: If something amounts to a particular total, all the parts of it add up to that total.

ex.en: Consumer spending on sports-related items amounted to $9.75 billion.
ex.zh: 消费者在体育相关用品上的消费总共达到了97.5亿美元。

d: n. 数量，总额（amount 的复数）；大量（常用于 amounts of 结构）
v. 总计，合计；等于，相当于（amount 的第三人称单数形式，常用于 amount to 结构）
n. 考古学家（archaeologist 的复数）

e.en: Ate is the past tense of . (eat)

d: v. 吃（eat 的过去式）

e.en: Arid land is so dry that very few plants can grow on it.

ex.en: ...new strains of crops that can withstand arid conditions.
ex.zh: …能经受干旱条件的新品种作物。

d: adj. （土地或气候）干燥的，干旱的；枯燥的，乏味的；不成功的，无结果的

e.en: An antelope is an animal like a deer, with long legs and horns, that lives in Africa or Asia. Antelopes are graceful and can run fast. There are many different types of antelope.

d: n. 羚羊（antelope 的复数）；羚羊皮革

e.en: An average is the result that you get when you add two or more numbers together and divide the total by the number of numbers you added together.

ex.en: Take the average of those ratios and multiply by a hundred.
ex.zh: 取那些比例的平均数再乘以100。

e.en: Average is also an adjective.

ex.en: The average price of goods rose by just 2.2%.
ex.zh: 商品的平均价格仅上涨了2.2%。

e.en: You use average to refer to a number or size that varies but is always approximately the same.

ex.en: It takes an average of ten weeks for a house sale to be completed.
ex.zh: 平均需要10周的时间才能完成一幢房子的销售。

e.en: An amount or quality that is the average is the normal amount or quality for a particular group of things or people.

ex.en: 35% of staff time was being spent on repeating work, about the average for a service industry.
ex.zh: 员工35%的时间花费在重复劳动上，大约是服务业的一般水平。

d: n. 平均水平，一般标准；平均数，平均值；（海损的）平均分担；（按保单规定应付赔偿额的）降减，均减
adj. 普通的，平常的；不好不坏的；平均（数）的；中等的，适中的
v. 平均为，平均达到；计算平均值；将……平均分配；（行情下跌时）买进更多的证券（或商品）以降低平均进价

e.en: If you apply for something such as a job or membership of an organization, you write a letter or fill out a form in order to ask formally for it.

ex.en: I am continuing to apply for jobs.
ex.zh: 我在继续申请工作。

ex.en: They may apply to join the organization.
ex.zh: 他们可能申请加入该组织。

e.en: If you apply yourself to something or apply your mind to something, you concentrate hard on doing it or on thinking about it.

ex.en: Scymanski has applied himself to this task with considerable energy.
ex.zh: 赛曼斯基已经花了相当多的精力致力于这项任务。

e.en: If something such as a rule or a remark applies to a person or in a situation, it is relevant to the person or the situation. (对…)

ex.en: The convention does not apply to us.
ex.zh: 该协定对我们不适用。

ex.en: The rule applies where a person owns stock in a corporation.
ex.zh: 该规定对于在公司里拥有股份的人适用。

e.en: If you apply something such as a rule, system, or skill, you use it in a situation or activity.

ex.en: The government appears to be applying the same principle.
ex.zh: 政府似乎在运用同样的原则。

d: v. 申请；涂，敷，施用；施加，实施；应用，运用（apply 的现在分词/动名词）；适用；致力于，专心于（apply oneself to 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: If something belongs to you, you own it.

ex.en: The house had belonged to her family for three or four generations.
ex.zh: 这座房子属于她家已有三四代了。

e.en: You say that something belongs to a particular person when you are guessing, discovering, or explaining that it was produced by or is part of that person. (某人) 所做;

ex.en: The handwriting belongs to a male.
ex.zh: 这笔迹出自一名男子之手。

e.en: If someone belongs to a particular group, they are a member of that group.

ex.en: I used to belong to a youth club.
ex.zh: 我曾是一个青年俱乐部的成员。

e.en: If something or someone belongs in or to a particular category, type, or group, they are of that category, type, or group. 属 (某一类别、类型、群)

ex.en: The judges could not decide which category it belonged in.
ex.zh: 法官们无法决定它属于哪一类别。

d: v. belong 的过去式和过去分词；属于；归……所有；是……的成员；应归入；适合（某地或环境）

e.en: You can refer to something that is provided in large amounts as bounty.

ex.en: ...autumn's bounty of fruits, seeds and berries.
ex.zh: …秋天丰收的水果、种子和浆果。

e.en: A bounty is money that is offered as a reward for doing something, especially for finding or killing a particular person. 奖金 (尤用于寻人或杀人)

ex.en: A bounty of $50,000 was put on Dr. Alvarez's head.
ex.zh: 一笔5万美元的赏金用以悬赏阿尔瓦雷斯博士的人头。

d: n. 慷慨；丰富；奖励金；赠款
vt. 发给……奖金等；为……而发给赏金
vi. 以赏金等形式发放

e.en: The boundary of an area of land is an imaginary line that separates it from other areas.

ex.en: The Bow Brook forms the western boundary of the wood.
ex.zh: 鲍溪成了树林的西边界。

e.en: The boundaries of something such as a subject or activity are the limits that people think that it has.

ex.en: The boundaries between history and storytelling are always being blurred and muddled.
ex.zh: 历史与故事的界限一直模糊不清。

d: n. 分界线，边界；界限，范围；（板球）击球超过边界线得分

e.en: A burial is the act or ceremony of putting a dead body into a grave in the ground. 埋葬;

ex.en: The priest prepared the body for burial.
ex.zh: 牧师为尸体做好了下葬的准备。

d: n．埋葬，葬礼（burial的复数形式）：将死者遗体安置在墓地或其他指定地点的仪式。

e.en: A carcass is the body of a dead animal.

ex.en: A cluster of vultures crouched on the carcass of a dead buffalo.
ex.zh: 一群秃鹫伏在一头水牛的尸体上啄食。

d: n. 动物尸体，（尤指供食用的）畜体；（人的）身躯，躯体；（汽车、建筑等的）残骸；（建筑、船或家具的）构架；（被抛弃、肢解或无价值的）空壳

e.en: If there is a chance of something happening, it is possible that it will happen.

ex.en: Do you think they have a chance of beating Australia?
ex.zh: 你认为他们有可能击败澳大利亚队吗?

ex.en: There was really very little chance that Ben would ever have led a normal life.
ex.zh: 那时本几乎不可能过上正常的生活。

e.en: If you have a chance to do something, you have the opportunity to do it.

ex.en: The electoral council announced that all eligible people would get a chance to vote.
ex.zh: 选举委员会曾宣布所有符合条件者都将获得投票机会。

ex.en: Most refugee doctors never get the chance to practise medicine in our hospitals.
ex.zh: 绝大部分难民医生在我们的医院里从未得到行医的机会。

e.en: A chance meeting or event is one that is not planned or expected.

ex.en: ...a chance meeting.
ex.zh: …一次邂逅。

e.en: Chance is also a noun. 偶然;

ex.en: ...a victim of chance and circumstance.
ex.zh: …一个时运不济的倒霉者。

d: n. 机会；[数]机遇（chance 的复数形式）；可能性
vi. 偶然发生，碰巧（chance 的三单形式）
vt. 冒……的险（chance 的三单形式）

e.en: If you chase someone, or chase after them, you run after them or follow them quickly in order to catch or reach them.

ex.en: She chased the thief for 100 yards.
ex.zh: 她追了小偷100码远。

e.en: Chase is also a noun.

ex.en: He was reluctant to give up the chase.
ex.zh: 他不愿意放弃追逐。

e.en: If you are chasing something you want, such as work or money, or are chasing after it, you are trying hard to get it. 追求 (事业、金钱等)

ex.en: In some areas, 14 people are chasing every job.
ex.zh: 在某些地区，14个人角逐每一个岗位。

ex.en: There are too many schools chasing after too few students.
ex.zh: 有太多的学校争抢太少的学生。

e.en: Chase is also a noun. (对事业、金钱等的)

ex.en: They took an invincible lead in the chase for the championship.
ex.zh: 他们在冠军角逐中遥遥领先。

d: v. 追逐，追赶；匆忙赶往，急奔；追求，努力争取；求爱；驱逐，赶走；撤职；催促；镂刻，雕刻
n. 追赶，追逐；争取，努力获得；狩猎，猎捕；越野赛马，障碍赛马
【名】 （Chase）（英）蔡斯，（法）沙斯（人名）

e.en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have. 挑选;

ex.en: They will be able to choose their own leaders in democratic elections.
ex.zh: 在民主选举中他们将可以选出他们自己的领导人。

ex.en: There are several patchwork cushions to choose from.
ex.zh: 有几种拼布工艺垫子可供选择。

e.en: If you choose to do something, you do it because you want to or because you feel that it is right. 情愿; 觉得应该 (做某事)

ex.en: They knew that discrimination was going on, but chose to ignore it.
ex.zh: 他们知道歧视仍然存在，但他们情愿不去理会。

ex.en: You have the right to remain silent if you choose.
ex.zh: 如果你愿意，你有权保持沉默。

d: v. 选择，挑选；情愿，决定

e.en: When you chew food, you use your teeth to break it up in your mouth so that it becomes easier to swallow.

ex.en: Be certain to eat slowly and chew your food extremely well.
ex.zh: 一定要慢慢吃，特别细地咀嚼食物。

ex.en: Daniel leaned back on the sofa, still chewing on his apple.
ex.zh: 丹尼尔仰靠在沙发上，还在嚼着苹果。

e.en: If you chew gum or tobacco, you keep biting it and moving it around your mouth to taste the flavour of it. You do not swallow it. 嚼 (口香糖、烟)

ex.en: One girl was chewing gum.
ex.zh: 一个女孩在嚼口香糖。

e.en: If you chew your lips or your fingernails, you keep biting them because you are nervous. 咬 (嘴唇、手指)

ex.en: He chewed his lower lip nervously.
ex.zh: 他紧张地咬着下唇。

e.en: If a person or animal chews an object or chews on it, they bite it with their teeth.

ex.en: They pause and chew their pencils.
ex.zh: 他们停了下来，咬着铅笔。

ex.en: She chewed through the tape that bound her.
ex.zh: 她咬断了捆绑她的带子。

d: v. （chew 的过去式和过去分词）咀嚼，嚼碎（食物）；嚼（口香糖、烟草等）；因紧张而咬（嘴唇、指甲等）
adj. 被嚼过的，嚼碎的（chew 的过去分词作定语）

e.en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have. 挑选;

ex.en: They will be able to choose their own leaders in democratic elections.
ex.zh: 在民主选举中他们将可以选出他们自己的领导人。

ex.en: There are several patchwork cushions to choose from.
ex.zh: 有几种拼布工艺垫子可供选择。

e.en: If you choose to do something, you do it because you want to or because you feel that it is right. 情愿; 觉得应该 (做某事)

ex.en: They knew that discrimination was going on, but chose to ignore it.
ex.zh: 他们知道歧视仍然存在，但他们情愿不去理会。

ex.en: You have the right to remain silent if you choose.
ex.zh: 如果你愿意，你有权保持沉默。

d: v. 选择，挑选；情愿，决定（choose 的现在分词）

e.en: A clue to a problem or mystery is something that helps you to find the answer to it. (解决问题或疑团时的)

ex.en: Geneticists in Canada have discovered a clue to the puzzle of why our cells get old and die.
ex.zh: 加拿大的遗传学家已经发现了解开我们细胞衰老死亡之迷的线索。

e.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps someone solve a crime. (破案中的)

ex.en: The vital clue to the killer's identity was his nickname, Peanuts.
ex.zh: 关于杀手身份的重大线索是他的绰号——花生。

e.en: A clue in a crossword or game is information which is given to help you to find the answer to a question. (纵横字谜或游戏中的)

ex.en: Give me a clue. What's it begin with?
ex.zh: 给我点提示。是什么开头？

e.en: If you haven't a clue about something, you do not know anything about it or you have no idea what to do about it.

ex.en: I haven't a clue what I'll give Carl for his birthday next year.
ex.zh: 对于明年该送什么生日礼物给卡尔我毫无头绪。

d: n. 线索，蛛丝马迹（clue 的复数）
v. 提示（clue 的第三人称单数）；暗示

e.en: If people or things are clustered somewhere, there is a group of them close together there. 群集的;

ex.en: Officials were clustered at every open office door, talking excitedly.
ex.zh: 官员们聚集在每一个门面大开的办公室前，兴奋地谈论着。

d: adj. 成群的，聚集成群的；丛生的；（计算机）集群的，聚簇的
v. 聚集，聚合（cluster 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Coastal is used to refer to things that are in the sea or on the land near a coast.

ex.en: Local radio stations serving coastal areas often broadcast forecasts for yachtsmen.
ex.zh: 服务沿海地区的地方电台经常向驾驶快艇者播放天气预报。

d: adj. 近海的，沿海的

e.en: Communal means relating to particular groups in a country or society.

ex.en: Communal violence broke out in different parts of the country.
ex.zh: 团体暴力冲突在该国不同地区爆发了。

e.en: You use communal to describe something that is shared by a group of people.

ex.en: The inmates ate in a communal dining room.
ex.zh: 同狱室的人在一个公共饭厅吃饭。

d: adj.  公共的；群体的，团体的；种族间的，教派间的；（与他人）同做的，共事的
【名】 （Communal）（法）科米纳尔（人名）

e.en: When you compare things, you consider them and discover the differences or similarities between them.

ex.en: Compare the two illustrations in Figure 60.
ex.zh: 比较一下图60中的两个图示。

ex.en: Managers analyse their company's data and compare it with data on their competitors.
ex.zh: 经理们分析他们公司的数据并与其竞争者的数据进行比较。

e.en: If you compare one person or thing to another, you say that they are like the other person or thing.

ex.en: Some commentators compared his work to that of James Joyce.
ex.zh: 一些评论员认为他的作品像詹姆士·乔伊斯的作品。

e.en: If you say that something does not compare with something else, you mean that it is much worse.

ex.en: The flowers here do not compare with those at home.
ex.zh: 这儿的花比不上家里的花。

e.en: If one thing compares favourably with another, it is better than the other thing. If it compares unfavourably, it is worse than the other thing. (与…) 比起来 (好、差)

ex.en: Our road safety record compares favourably with that of other countries.
ex.zh: 我们的道路安全纪录比其他国家的好。

d: n. 比较，对照
v. 比较，对照（compare 的 ing 形式）

e.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them. (巨大的)

ex.en: ...the contrast between town and country.
ex.zh: …城乡差别。

ex.en: The two visitors provided a startling contrast in appearance.
ex.zh: 两位来访者的外貌有惊人的不同。

e.en: You say by contrast or in contrast, or in contrast to something, to show that you are mentioning a very different situation from the one you have just mentioned.

ex.en: The private sector, by contrast, has plenty of money to spend.
ex.zh: 私营部门相比之下有很多钱可花。

ex.en: In contrast, the lives of girls in well-to-do families were often very sheltered.
ex.zh: 相比之下，富裕家庭的女孩子们通常都过着养尊处优的生活。

e.en: If one thing is in contrast to another, it is very different from it.

ex.en: His public statements have always been in marked contrast to those of his son.
ex.zh: 他在公共场合的发言总是和他儿子的话截然不同。

e.en: If you contrast one thing with another, you point out or consider the differences between those things. 对比 (事物以指出不同点)

ex.en: She contrasted the situation then with the present crisis.
ex.zh: 她把过去的情况与现在的危机进行了对比。

ex.en: Contrast that approach with what goes on in most organizations.
ex.zh: 对比这个方法与大多数组织运用的方法的不同之处。

d: n. 差异，对比；对照物，明显不同的事物；（摄影或绘画中的）颜色反差，明暗对比；（电视屏幕的）图像明暗对比度，反差
v. 对比，对照；显出明显的差异，形成对比

e.en: When you cook a meal, you prepare food for eating by heating it.

ex.en: I have to go and cook dinner.
ex.zh: 我要去做饭了。

ex.en: Chefs at the restaurant once cooked for President Kennedy.
ex.zh: 这家饭店的厨师曾经给肯尼迪总统做过饭。

e.en: 烹饪

ex.en: Her hobbies include music, dancing, sport, and cooking.
ex.zh: 她的爱好包括音乐、跳舞、运动和烹饪。

e.en: When you cook food, or when food cooks, it is heated until it is ready to be eaten.

ex.en: ...some basic instructions on how to cook a turkey.
ex.zh: ...火鸡的一些基本做法。

ex.en: Let the vegetables cook gently for about 10 minutes.
ex.zh: 把蔬菜小火煮约十分钟。

e.en: A cook is a person whose job is to prepare and cook food, especially in someone's home or in an institution. (职业)

ex.en: They had a butler, a cook, and a maid.
ex.zh: 他们有一位管家、一位厨师和一位女仆。

d: v. 烹饪；被烧煮；篡改；伪造；干得起劲，干得好（cook 的过去式及过去分词）
adj. 煮熟的，烧熟的

e.en: Something that is coloured a particular colour is that colour.

ex.en: The illustration shows a cluster of five roses coloured apricot orange.
ex.zh: 插图上展示了一簇杏黄色的5朵玫瑰。

e.en: Something that is coloured is a particular colour or combination of colours, rather than being just white, black, or the colour that it is naturally.

ex.en: You can often choose between plain white or coloured and patterned scarves.
ex.zh: 你通常可在原白色或彩色带图案的围巾中进行选择。

e.en: A coloured person belongs to a race of people with dark skins.

d: adj. 有色的，着色的；彩色的（常用于构成复合词，表示“呈……色的”）；有色人种的，混血种的（旧用法，常被认为冒犯）；带主观感情色彩的；有偏见的，受影响的
n. 有色人种的人，混血人（旧用法，常被认为冒犯）；（南非，常大写为 Coloured）混血种族群体成员；有色服装，有色衣物（尤指洗衣时需与白色衣物分开洗涤的）
v. 给……着色，染色；（因尴尬等而）脸红；（负面地）影响，扭曲；使生动，使鲜明；colour 的过去式和过去分词
adv. 集体地，共同地

e.en: Coordination means organizing the activities of two or more groups so that they work together efficiently and know what the others are doing.

ex.en: ...the lack of coordination between the civilian and military authorities.
ex.zh: …民事机关和军事机关缺少协作。

ex.en: ...the coordination of economic policy.
ex.zh: …经济政策的协作。

e.en: If you do something in coordination with someone else, you both organize your activities so that you work together efficiently.
Coordination is the ability to use the different parts of your body together efficiently. (身体各部位的)

ex.en: ...clumsiness and lack of coordination.
ex.zh: …笨手笨脚，缺乏协调能力。

d: n. 协调，配合；身体的协调性；配位；同一等级（或类别）

e.en: You can refer to any living thing that is not a plant as a creature, especially when it is of an unknown or unfamiliar kind. People also refer to imaginary animals and beings as creatures. (尤指不明的或想像中的) 生物;

ex.en: Alaskan Eskimos believe that every living creature possesses a spirit.
ex.zh: 阿拉斯加的爱斯基摩人认为每个活着的动物都有灵魂。

d: n. 动物，生物；（想象出来的）怪物，奇幻生物；……的人（creature 的复数）
adv. 关键地，至关重要地；重要的是，关键的是

e.en: Cultural means relating to a particular society and its ideas, customs, and art.

ex.en: ...a deep sense of personal honour which was part of his cultural heritage.
ex.zh: …成为他文化遗产中一部分的强烈的个人荣誉感。

e.en: 文化上地

ex.en: ...an informed guide to culturally and historically significant sites.
ex.zh: …一份介绍文化和历史名胜内容丰富的指南。

e.en: Cultural means involving or concerning the arts.

ex.en: ...the sponsorship of sports and cultural events by tobacco companies.
ex.zh: …烟草公司对体育和文艺活动的赞助。

e.en: 文化艺术上地

ex.en: ...one of our better-governed, culturally active regional centres.
ex.zh: …管理较好、文化艺术活动活跃的地区中心之一。

d: adj. 文化的，与文化有关的；艺术的，文艺的

e.en: If you defend someone or something, you take action in order to protect them.

ex.en: His courage in defending religious and civil rights inspired many outside the church.
ex.zh: 他捍卫宗教权和公民权的勇气鼓舞了许多非教会人士。

e.en: If you defend someone or something when they have been criticized, you argue in support of them.

ex.en: He defended his administration's response to the disaster against critics who charge the federal government is moving too slowly.
ex.zh: 他为他的行政部门对灾难的反应做了争辩，反驳批评人士指控联邦政府行动过于迟缓。

e.en: When a lawyer defends a person who has been accused of something, the lawyer argues on their behalf in a court of law that the charges are not true.

ex.en: ...a lawyer who defended political prisoners during the military regime.
ex.zh: …一位在军权时期为政治犯进行辩护的律师。

ex.en: He has hired a lawyer to defend him against the allegation.
ex.zh: 他已聘请一位律师为他所受的指控辩护。

e.en: When a sports player plays in the tournament which they won the previous time it was held, you can say that they are defending their title.

ex.en: Torrence expects to defend her title successfully in the next Olympics.
ex.zh: 托伦斯希望下届奥运会能成功卫冕。

d: v. 保卫，防御；捍卫，维护；（在比赛中）防守，防卫；参加卫冕赛，蝉联；做……的辩护律师，为……辩解

e.en: If you defend someone or something, you take action in order to protect them.

ex.en: His courage in defending religious and civil rights inspired many outside the church.
ex.zh: 他捍卫宗教权和公民权的勇气鼓舞了许多非教会人士。

e.en: If you defend someone or something when they have been criticized, you argue in support of them.

ex.en: He defended his administration's response to the disaster against critics who charge the federal government is moving too slowly.
ex.zh: 他为他的行政部门对灾难的反应做了争辩，反驳批评人士指控联邦政府行动过于迟缓。

e.en: When a lawyer defends a person who has been accused of something, the lawyer argues on their behalf in a court of law that the charges are not true.

ex.en: ...a lawyer who defended political prisoners during the military regime.
ex.zh: …一位在军权时期为政治犯进行辩护的律师。

ex.en: He has hired a lawyer to defend him against the allegation.
ex.zh: 他已聘请一位律师为他所受的指控辩护。

e.en: When a sports player plays in the tournament which they won the previous time it was held, you can say that they are defending their title.

ex.en: Torrence expects to defend her title successfully in the next Olympics.
ex.zh: 托伦斯希望下届奥运会能成功卫冕。

d: v. defend 的过去式和过去分词；保护，保卫，抵御；为…争辩，捍卫；（法律）为（被告）辩护；（体育）卫冕
adv. 密集地，稠密地；难懂地，费解地；愚笨地，迟钝地

e.en: A desert is a large area of land, usually in a hot region, where there is almost no water, rain, trees, or plants.

ex.en: ...the Sahara Desert.
ex.zh: …撒哈拉沙漠。

e.en: If people or animals desert a place, they leave it and it becomes empty.

ex.en: Poor farmers are deserting their parched farm fields and coming here looking for jobs.
ex.zh: 贫穷的农民丢下干旱的农田，来这里寻找工作。

e.en: 被遗弃的

ex.en: She led them into a deserted sidestreet.
ex.zh: 她领他们来到一条废弃的小巷。

e.en: If someone deserts you, they go away and leave you, and no longer help or support you.

ex.en: Mrs. Roding's husband deserted her years ago.
ex.zh: 罗丁太太的丈夫数年前抛弃了她。

d: n. 沙漠，荒漠；荒凉的地方；应得的赏罚
v. 离弃，舍弃（某地）；抛弃，遗弃（某人）；背弃，放弃；擅离，开小差；突然丧失
adj. 无人居住的，荒凉的；像沙漠的

e.en: When you drive somewhere, you operate a car or other vehicle and control its movement and direction.

ex.en: I drove into town and went to a restaurant for dinner.
ex.zh: 我开车进城到一家餐馆用餐。

ex.en: She never learned to drive.
ex.zh: 她从未学过开车。

e.en: 驾驶

ex.en: ...a qualified driving instructor.
ex.zh: …一名合格的驾驶教练。

e.en: If you drive someone somewhere, you take them there in a car or other vehicle. 开车送 (某人去某处)

ex.en: His daughter Carly drove him to the train station.
ex.zh: 她的女儿卡莉开车送他去火车站。

e.en: If something drives a machine, it supplies the power that makes it work.

ex.en: The current flows into electric motors that drive the wheels.
ex.zh: 电流流入驱动轮子的电动机。

d: n. drive 的复数形式：驱动器；驱动力，推动力；干劲；驾车出行，乘车兜风；运动，宣传活动。
v. drive 的第三人称单数形式：驾驶，开车；驱动，推动，促使；强迫，迫使；努力争取，力求达成。

e.en: To emerge means to come out from an enclosed or dark space such as a room or a vehicle, or from a position where you could not be seen. (从视线以外的地方) 出现;

ex.en: Richard was waiting outside the door as she emerged.
ex.zh: 当她出现的时候，理查德正等候在门外。

ex.en: She then emerged from the courthouse to thank her supporters.
ex.zh: 于是她从法院大楼出来向支持者们表示感谢。

e.en: If you emerge from a difficult or bad experience, you come to the end of it.

ex.en: There is growing evidence that the economy is at last emerging from recession.
ex.zh: 有越来越多的迹象表明经济将最终摆脱萧条。

e.en: If a fact or result emerges from a period of thought, discussion, or investigation, it becomes known as a result of it. 显露 (事实、结果)

ex.en: ...the growing corruption that has emerged in the past few years.
ex.zh: …过去几年中暴露出来的日趋严重的腐败。

ex.en: It soon emerged that neither the July nor August mortgage payment had been collected.
ex.zh: 很快显示的是7月和8月的抵押款都没有被收取。

e.en: If someone or something emerges as a particular thing, they become recognized as that thing.

ex.en: Vietnam has emerged as the world's third-biggest rice exporter.
ex.zh: 越南已立足成为世界第三大稻米出口国。

d: v. （emerge 的第三人称单数形式）出现，显现（从某个状态、地点或物体中出来，变得可见或可知）；暴露，显露，变得明显或显著；走出，摆脱（困境、衰退等）；显示出，被认定是，脱颖而出；兴起，产生，成立

e.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

ex.en: Every day of our lives we encounter major and minor stresses of one kind or another.
ex.zh: 生活中的每一天，我们会遇到或大或小的这样那样的压力。

e.en: If you encounter someone, you meet them, usually unexpectedly.

ex.en: Did you encounter anyone in the building?
ex.zh: 你在那栋大楼里偶然遇到什么人了吗？

e.en: An encounter with someone is a meeting with them, particularly one that is unexpected or significant.

ex.en: The author tells of a remarkable encounter with a group of South Vietnamese soldiers.
ex.zh: 作者讲述了他与一群南越士兵的惊人邂逅。

e.en: An encounter is a particular type of experience.

ex.en: ...a sexual encounter.
ex.zh: …一次性经历。

d: v. 遭遇；偶遇，邂逅
n. 偶遇，邂逅；经历，体验；冲突；比赛，交锋

e.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

ex.en: Every day of our lives we encounter major and minor stresses of one kind or another.
ex.zh: 生活中的每一天，我们会遇到或大或小的这样那样的压力。

e.en: If you encounter someone, you meet them, usually unexpectedly.

ex.en: Did you encounter anyone in the building?
ex.zh: 你在那栋大楼里偶然遇到什么人了吗？

e.en: An encounter with someone is a meeting with them, particularly one that is unexpected or significant.

ex.en: The author tells of a remarkable encounter with a group of South Vietnamese soldiers.
ex.zh: 作者讲述了他与一群南越士兵的惊人邂逅。

e.en: An encounter is a particular type of experience.

ex.en: ...a sexual encounter.
ex.zh: …一次性经历。

d: v. 遭遇，遇到；邂逅（encounter 的第三人称单数）
n. 相遇，相见，邂逅；遭遇；遭遇战；冲突（encounter 的复数）

e.en: When archaeologists or other people excavate a piece of land, they remove earth carefully from it and look for things such as pots, bones, or buildings that are buried there, in order to discover information about the past. 挖掘 (古物)

ex.en: A new Danish expedition is again excavating the site in annual summer digs.
ex.zh: 一支新的丹麦考察队又在对那个地方进行年度的夏季挖掘。

e.en: 挖掘

ex.en: She worked on the excavation of a Mayan archaeological site.
ex.zh: 她那时从事一个玛雅考古遗址的挖掘工作。

e.en: To excavate means to dig a hole in the ground, for example, in order to build there. 挖;

ex.en: A contractor was hired to drain the reservoir and to excavate soil from one area for replacement with clay.
ex.zh: 一个承包商被雇来排干蓄水池里的水，然后挖出其中一块地方的泥土，换上粘土。

e.en: 挖;

ex.en: ...the excavation of canals.
ex.zh: …运河的开凿。

d: v. 挖掘；开凿；发掘（excavate 的现在分词/动名词）

e.en: Farming is the activity of growing crops or keeping animals on a farm. 耕种;

ex.en: ...a career in farming.
ex.zh: …务农生涯。

d: n. 农业，农场经营
v. 耕种，养殖；（收取一定费用）将（税收）包出；承包，外包（farm 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Fatty food contains a lot of fat. (食物)

ex.en: Don't eat fatty food or chocolates.
ex.zh: 不要吃高脂肪的食物或巧克力。

e.en: Fatty acids or fatty tissues, for example, contain or consist of fat. 含脂肪的;

ex.en: ...fatty acids.
ex.zh: …多种脂肪酸。

d: adj. 脂肪的，含脂肪的，由脂肪组成的；多脂肪的，脂肪过多的；肥胖的
n. （可能含贬义）胖子

e.en: When archaeologists or other people excavate a piece of land, they remove earth carefully from it and look for things such as pots, bones, or buildings that are buried there, in order to discover information about the past. 挖掘 (古物)

ex.en: A new Danish expedition is again excavating the site in annual summer digs.
ex.zh: 一支新的丹麦考察队又在对那个地方进行年度的夏季挖掘。

e.en: 挖掘

ex.en: She worked on the excavation of a Mayan archaeological site.
ex.zh: 她那时从事一个玛雅考古遗址的挖掘工作。

e.en: To excavate means to dig a hole in the ground, for example, in order to build there. 挖;

ex.en: A contractor was hired to drain the reservoir and to excavate soil from one area for replacement with clay.
ex.zh: 一个承包商被雇来排干蓄水池里的水，然后挖出其中一块地方的泥土，换上粘土。

e.en: 挖;

ex.en: ...the excavation of canals.
ex.zh: …运河的开凿。

d: v. （考古）发掘；挖掘，挖（excavate 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 出土的，被发掘出来的（常作定语）

e.en: If you find someone or something, you see them or learn where they are. 发现;

ex.en: The police also found a pistol.
ex.zh: 警察还发现了一把手枪。

ex.en: They have spent ages looking at the map and can't find a trace of anywhere called Darrowby.
ex.zh: 他们已花了很长时间察看地图，却怎么也找不到一个叫“达罗比”的地方。

e.en: If you find something that you need or want, you succeed in achieving or obtaining it.

ex.en: Many people here cannot find work.
ex.zh: 这里很多人找不到工作。

ex.en: He has to apply for a permit and we have to find him a job.
ex.zh: 他得申请一个许可证，而我们得给他找一份工作。

e.en: If you find someone or something in a particular situation, they are in that situation when you see them or come into contact with them. 发现 (某人或某物处于某种状态)

ex.en: They found her walking alone and depressed on the beach.
ex.zh: 他们发现她独自一人、神情沮丧地走在海滩上。

ex.en: She returned to her home to find her back door forced open.
ex.zh: 她回到家中，发现后门被强行打开了。

e.en: If you find yourself doing something, you are doing it without deciding or intending to do it. 意识到 (自己无意中的动作)

ex.en: It's not the first time that you've found yourself in this situation.
ex.zh: 这已经不是你第一次意识到自己处于这种情形了。

ex.en: I found myself having more fun than I had had in years.
ex.zh: 我发现自己多年来从未玩得这样开心过。

d: v. 找到，找回；发现，发觉；（经过研究）找出，查明；觉得，认为（find 的第三人称单数）
n. 被发现的人，发现物（尤指有价值的人或物）；发现狐狸（find 的复数）

e.en: The upside of an unpleasant situation is the aspect of it that is more pleasant or positive.

ex.en: Residents said the only upside would be a boost to the island's economy.
ex.zh: 居民们说惟一好的方面会是对该岛经济的促进。

d: n. 好的一面，优势；（股票价格）上涨
prep. 对着……一侧

e.en: If you are sitting or standing upright, you are sitting or standing with your back straight, rather than bending or lying down.

ex.en: Helen sat upright in her chair.
ex.zh: 海伦笔直地坐在椅子上。

ex.en: He moved into an upright position.
ex.zh: 他换成了一个挺直的姿势。

e.en: An upright vacuum cleaner or freezer is tall rather than wide. 立式的 (吸尘器或冰箱)
An upright chair has a straight back and no arms. 有靠背无扶手的 (椅子)

ex.en: He was sitting on an upright chair beside his bed, reading.
ex.zh: 他正坐在床边一把有靠背无扶手的椅子上阅读。

e.en: You can refer to vertical posts or the vertical parts of an object as uprights.

ex.en: ...the uprights of a canopy bed.
ex.zh: …一张顶篷床的立柱。

d: adj. （人）直立的，挺直的；直立的，垂直的，立式的；正直的，诚实的；（椅子）直靠背的，没有扶手的
adv. 笔直地，直立地，垂直地；平稳地
n. （起支撑作用的）直柱，立柱，直立部分；球门柱；立式钢琴
n. 物化，客体化（把人当作物品、工具或性对象来对待）；客观化，对象化（将抽象事物或内在状态表现为客观对象）

e.en: A photo is the same as a .

ex.en: Let's take a photo!
ex.zh: 我们拍张照片吧！

d: n. 照片（photo 的复数）
v. 拍照（photo 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Your brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

ex.en: Her father died of a brain tumour.
ex.zh: 他的父亲死于脑瘤。

e.en: Your brain is your mind and the way that you think.

ex.en: Once you stop using your brain you soon go stale.
ex.zh: 一旦你停止动脑筋,你很快就会变迟钝。

e.en: If someone has brains or a good brain, they have the ability to learn and understand things quickly, to solve problems, and to make good decisions.

ex.en: They were not the only ones to have brains and ambition.
ex.zh: 他们并非仅有的有头脑、有抱负的人。

e.en: If someone is the brains behind an idea or an organization, he or she had that idea or makes the important decisions about how that organization is managed.

ex.en: Mr. White was the brains behind the scheme.
ex.zh: 怀特先生是这项计划后面的智囊。

d: n. 脑；智力，智慧；聪明的人，智者；电脑；（供食用的）动物脑髓
v. 猛击……的头部
【名】 （Brain）（英）布雷恩（人名）
v. 使有性特征；使性感；给与性别角色（sexualise 的过去式和过去分词，sexualise 同 sexualize）
n. 刺激，激励，兴奋作用
vt. （英国英语拼写；亦作 recognize）认出，辨认出；识别，辨别；承认，认可；认识到，意识到

e.en: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

ex.en: All three attacks followed the same pattern.
ex.zh: 3次袭击都依照同一模式。

e.en: A pattern is an arrangement of lines or shapes, especially a design in which the same shape is repeated at regular intervals over a surface.

ex.en: ...a golden robe embroidered with red and purple thread stitched into a pattern of flames.
ex.zh: …一件用红紫相间的线镶了火焰图案的边的金色长袍。

e.en: A pattern is a diagram or shape that you can use as a guide when you are making something such as a model or a piece of clothing.

ex.en: ...cutting out a pattern for slacks.
ex.zh: …剪出一个便裤的纸样。

ex.en: Send for our free patterns to knit yourself.
ex.zh: 索取我们免费的参照图形以便自己织。

e.en: to model

d: n. 模式，方式；图案，花样；模范，典范；模型，底样；（布或墙纸的）样品；样式；（声音或词汇有规则排列的）模式
v. 用图案装饰，给……加上花样；仿照，模仿；赋予……以固定（或易辨认）的形式；使形成，促成（某行为模式）

e.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief.

ex.en: No one really has any illusions about winning the war.
ex.zh: 事实上没有人对打赢这场战争抱任何幻想。

e.en: An illusion is something that appears to exist or be a particular thing but does not actually exist or is in reality something else.

ex.en: Floor-to-ceiling windows can look stunning, giving the illusion of extra height.
ex.zh: 从地板直抵天花板的窗户看上去非常漂亮，有增加高度的假象。

d: n. 错觉，幻觉；幻想，错误的观念

e.en: An advantage is something that puts you in a better position than other people.

ex.en: They are breaking the law in order to obtain an advantage over their competitors.
ex.zh: 他们为了获得超越其竞争对手的有力条件在违犯法律。

e.en: An advantage is a way in which one thing is better than another.

ex.en: The great advantage of home-grown oranges is their magnificent flavour.
ex.zh: 自产橙子的巨大优势是其极好的味道。

e.en: Advantage is the state of being in a better position than others who are competing against you.

ex.en: Men have created a social and economic position of advantage for themselves over women.
ex.zh: 男性创造了相对于女性的社会和经济上的优势地位。

e.en: If you take advantage of something, you make good use of it while you can. 利用 (某事物)

ex.en: I intend to take full advantage of this trip to buy the things we need.
ex.zh: 我打算充分利用这次旅行来购买我们需要的物品。

d: n. 有利条件，优势；优点；利益；（局末平分后）占先，优势分
v. 有利于，有助于

e.en: A photo is the same as a .

ex.en: Let's take a photo!
ex.zh: 我们拍张照片吧！

d: n. 照片，相片
v. 拍照；给……拍照

e.en: Someone who is powerless is unable to control or influence events.

ex.en: If you don't have money, you're powerless.
ex.zh: 如果你没有钱，你就无能为力。

e.en: 无能为力

ex.en: If we can't bring our problems under control, feelings of powerlessness and despair often ensue.
ex.zh: 如果我们不能将我们的问题控制住，无能为力和绝望感往往就会随之而来。

e.en: If you are powerless to do something, you are completely unable to do it.

ex.en: People are being murdered every day and I am powerless to stop it.
ex.zh: 每天都有人被杀害，而我却无力制止。

d: adj. 无力的；无能力的，无权的（常接不定式或 against、in 等介词短语）；（机器、飞行器等）无动力的，失去动力的
n. （the powerless）无权无势者；弱势群体

e.en: If someone is weak, they are not healthy or do not have good muscles, so that they cannot move quickly or carry heavy things.

ex.en: I was too weak to move or think or speak.
ex.zh: 我太虚弱了，不能动、不能思维、不能说话。

e.en: 虚弱地

ex.en: "I'm all right," Max said weakly, but his breathing came in jagged gasps.
ex.zh: “我没事，”马克斯虚弱地说，但是他呼吸艰难，长短不均。

e.en: If someone has an organ or sense that is weak, it is not very effective or powerful, or is likely to fail. (人的器官、感官)

ex.en: She tired easily and had a weak heart.
ex.zh: 她容易疲劳，心脏也比较弱。

e.en: If you describe someone as weak, you mean that they are not very confident or determined, so that they are often frightened or worried, or easily influenced by other people.

ex.en: He was a nice doctor, but a weak man who wasn't going to stick his neck out.
ex.zh: 他是个好医生，但为人懦弱，遇事不敢出头。

d: adj. 虚弱的，无力的；不牢固的；懦弱的，无判断力的；无影响力的，无权力的；疲软的，萧条的；不擅长的；无说服力的；力量微弱的，无强度的；（光、热或声音）微弱的；无活力的，无生气的；（饮品）稀的；（脸的部分）瘦小的，（容貌）不突出的；（受强烈情感影响而）腿发软的；无效力的，没有吸引力的；（动词）弱的，规则的；非重读的；弱电解的，弱电解质的
n. 穷人，弱者，病人（the weak）

e.en: Bias is a tendency to prefer one person or thing to another, and to favour that person or thing.

ex.en: ...his desire to avoid the appearance of bias in favour of one candidate or another.
ex.zh: …他想避免表现出对这个或那个候选人有偏好。

e.en: To bias someone means to influence them in favour of a particular choice. (影响某人) 使偏心;

ex.en: We mustn't allow it to bias our teaching.
ex.zh: 我们不允许它使我们的教学产生偏见。

d: n. 偏见，成见；偏好，天赋；倾向，趋势；斜纹；（统计）偏差，偏倚；偏重心球形；偏压，偏统
v. 使有偏见，使偏心；加偏压（或偏流）于
adj. 偏斜的
adv. 偏斜地

e.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

ex.en: Patriotic songs have long been a feature of Kuwaiti life.
ex.zh: 爱国歌曲长期以来一直是科威特人生活的一个特点。

ex.en: The spacious gardens are a special feature of this property.
ex.zh: 宽敞的花园是这处房产的一大特色。

e.en: A feature is a special article in a newspaper or magazine, or a special programme on radio or television. (报纸、杂志的) 特写; (广播、电视的)

ex.en: We are delighted to see the Sunday Times running a long feature on breast cancer.
ex.zh: 我们高兴地看到《星期日泰晤士报》刊登了关于乳腺癌的一篇长长的特写。

e.en: A feature or a feature film or movie is a full-length film about a fictional situation, as opposed to a short film or a documentary. 正片;

ex.en: ...the first feature-length cartoon, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
ex.zh: …第一部故事片长度的卡通片《白雪公主和七个小矮人》。

e.en: A geographical feature is something noticeable in a particular area of country, for example, a hill, river, or valley. (地理)

ex.en: ...one of the area's oddest geographical features - an eight-mile bank of pebbles shelving abruptly into the sea.
ex.zh: …这个地区最奇怪的地理特征之一，一条8英里长的鹅卵石堤岸陡然倾斜伸到海里。

d: n. 产品特点，特征，特性；容貌，面容，面部特征；特写、专题报道、（广播、电视的）特别节目；正片，故事片；嘴脸
v. 以……为特色，由……主演，使突出；在……中占重要位置（feature 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Your mouth is the area of your face where your lips are, or the space behind your lips where your teeth and tongue are.

ex.en: She clamped her hand against her mouth.
ex.zh: 她用手紧紧捂住嘴。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: (用于构成复合形容词)

ex.en: He straightened up and looked at me, open-mouthed.
ex.zh: 他直起身子看着我，嘴大张着。

e.en: You can say that someone has a particular kind of mouth to indicate that they speak in a particular kind of way or that they say particular kinds of things. 说话 (方式或内容)

ex.en: I've always had a loud mouth, I refuse to be silenced.
ex.zh: 我总是有话就讲，我拒绝保持沉默。

e.tip: 与形容词结合的复合词
e.en: (用于构成复合形容词)

ex.en: ...Sam, their smart-mouthed teenage son.
ex.zh: …萨姆，他们十几岁的伶牙俐齿的儿子。

d: n. 嘴，口腔；需要供养的人，食客；入口，开口；入海口，河口；讲话方式，言谈；饶舌，出言不逊；（受嚼子控制的）马口；（葡萄酒的不同于气味的）口感
v. 不出声地说，用口型默示；言不由衷地说，（自己并不明白却）信口开河；（清晰明确地）说，发……的音；吃，用嘴触碰；训练（马）使之习惯于服从嚼子
comb. 有……嘴的，……口的(-mouthed)；言谈……的，口齿……的(-mouthed)

e.en: An object is anything that has a fixed shape or form, that you can touch or see, and that is not alive.

ex.en: He squinted his eyes as though he were studying an object on the horizon.
ex.zh: 他眯着眼睛，好像在研究地平线上的某个物体。

ex.en: ...an object the shape of a coconut.
ex.zh: …一个椰子状的物体。

e.en: The object of what someone is doing is their aim or purpose.

ex.en: The object of the exercise is to raise money for the charity.
ex.zh: 此项活动的目的是为慈善筹款。

e.en: The object of a particular feeling or reaction is the person or thing it is directed toward or that causes it. (某情感或反应的)

ex.en: The object of her hatred was 24-year-old model Ros French.
ex.zh: 她憎恨的对象是24岁的模特罗斯·弗伦奇。

ex.en: The object of great interest at the temple was a large marble tower built in memory of Buddha.
ex.zh: 那庙里使人极感兴趣的东西是一座为纪念佛陀而修建的大理石巨塔。

e.en: In grammar, the object of a verb or a preposition is the word or phrase which completes the structure begun by the verb or preposition.

d: n. 物体，物品（object 的复数）；目标，目的（object 的复数）；宾语（object 的复数）；对象（object 的复数，指情感或行为所指向的人或事物）；对象（object 的复数，计算机科学中指程序实体）
v. 反对，不赞成（object 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you pick a particular person or thing, you choose that one.

ex.en: Mr. Nowell had picked ten people to interview for six sales jobs in Dallas.
ex.zh: 诺埃尔先生为在达拉斯的六个销售职位挑选了十人进行面试。

e.en: You can refer to the best things or people in a particular group as the pick of that group. 精华;

ex.en: The boys here are the pick of the high school's football players.
ex.zh: 这儿的男孩都是该中学足球队的精英。

e.en: When you pick flowers, fruit, or leaves, you break them off the plant or tree and collect them.

ex.en: She used to pick flowers in the Adirondacks.
ex.zh: 她以前常去阿迪朗达克山采花。

e.en: If you pick something from a place, you remove it from there with your fingers or your hand.

ex.en: He picked the napkin from his lap and placed it alongside his plate.
ex.zh: 他从腿上拿起餐巾，放在他的盘子旁边。

d: v. 采，摘（花、果）；（用手指）弄掉；找茬；捡，抱起；选择；弹，拨（弦）；撬开（锁），扒窃……中的东西；小心走路（~ one's way）；（反复地）拔，拉，撕，扯；没胃口地吃；（高尔夫）拾球（尤指认输的拾球）（~ up）；采，摘（花、果等）
n. 精华（the pick of）；选择，选择权；被选中的人（或事物）；鹤嘴锄；（吉他的）拨子；（尖状的）挖撬工具；（篮球）掩护
【名】 （Pick）（英、法、德、捷、匈、瑞典）皮克（人名）

e.en: A psychologist is a person who studies the human mind and tries to explain why people behave in the way that they do.

d: n. （心理）心理学家（psychologist 的复数形式）

e.en: A placebo is a substance with no chemical effects that a doctor gives to a patient instead of a drug. Placebos are used when testing new drugs or sometimes when a patient has imagined their illness. (无药用效果的)

d: n. 安慰剂，无效对照剂；使人宽慰的事，安抚话；为死者所颂的晚祷词

e.en: Recognition is the act of recognizing someone or identifying something when you see it. 认出;

ex.en: He searched for a sign of recognition on her face, but there was none.
ex.zh: 他在她的脸上搜寻她认出来的迹象，但没有。

e.en: Recognition of something is an understanding and acceptance of it. 认可;

ex.en: Recognition of the importance of career development is increasing.
ex.zh: 对职业发展重要性的认可在不断增加。

e.en: When a government gives diplomatic recognition to another country, they officially accept that its status is valid. (国际上的)

ex.en: His government did not receive full recognition by the United States until July.
ex.zh: 他的政府直到7月才得到美国的完全承认。

e.en: When a person receives recognition for the things that they have done, people acknowledge the value or skill of their work. 赞赏;

ex.en: At last, her father's work has received popular recognition.
ex.zh: 最终，她父亲的工作得到了大家的普遍赞赏。

d: n. 承认，接受；表彰，赞誉；认出，识别；（政府对他国的）外交认可
adj. 较小的，更小的（small 的比较级）

e.en: If you tell someone something, you give them information. 告诉 (某人某事)

ex.en: In the evening I returned to tell Phyllis I got the job.
ex.zh: 晚上我回来告诉菲莉丝我得到了那份工作。

ex.en: I called Andie to tell her how spectacular the stuff looked.
ex.zh: 我打电话给安迪告诉她那东西看上去多么壮观。

e.en: If you tell something such as a joke, a story, or your personal experiences, you communicate it to other people using speech. 讲述 (笑话、故事、个人经历等)

ex.en: His friends say he was always quick to tell a joke.
ex.zh: 他的朋友们说他以前总是张口就能讲笑话。

ex.en: He told his story to The L.A. Times and produced photographs.
ex.zh: 他向《洛杉机时报》叙述了自己的故事，并提供了一些照片。

e.en: If you tell someone to do something, you order or advise them to do it. 命令; 建议 (某人做某事)

ex.en: He said officers told him to get out of his car and lean against it.
ex.zh: 他说警官们命令他从他的车里出来并靠在车上。

e.en: If you tell yourself something, you put it into words in your own mind because you need to encourage or persuade yourself about something. 叮嘱 (自己)

ex.en: "Come on," she told herself.
ex.zh: “加油，”她叮嘱自己。

d: v. 告诉，告知；说，讲述；吐露，显示；看出，确切地判断；辨别，区别；命令，吩咐；告诉自己，暗自叮嘱；表明，说明；（不快的或令人疲倦的经历）产生效果，产生影响；泄密；数，计算；（通常指小孩）告状；警告，告诫；（某种因素）影响，起作用
n. （尤作纸牌用语）（泄露试图作弊的）不经意动作；（中东）台形（土墩）遗址（由远古人村落遗迹堆积而成的）
【名】 （Tell）泰尔（人名）

e.en: If something tends to happen, it usually happens or it often happens. 倾向于;

ex.en: A problem for manufacturers is that lighter cars tend to be noisy.
ex.zh: 制造商遇到的一个问题是重量较轻的汽车往往噪音大。

e.en: If you tend toward a particular characteristic, you often display that characteristic.

ex.en: Artistic and intellectual people tend toward left-wing views.
ex.zh: 艺术人士和知识分子趋向左翼观点。

e.en: You can say that you tend to think something when you want to give your opinion, but do not want it to seem too forceful or definite. 倾向于 (认为)

ex.en: I tend to think that our Representatives by and large do a good job.
ex.zh: 我倾向于认为我们的众议员们总体上干得不错。

e.en: to attend (to) 照顾;

ex.en: to tend to someone's needs

d: v. 倾向于，往往会；照顾，护理；走向，趋向；招待，照料（商店、酒吧等的顾客）

e.en: If you take a particular turning, you go along a road which leads away from the side of another road.

d: n. 转弯处，岔路口；转向，旋转；车削，车工工艺；车削下脚，削屑（turnings）
v. 使旋转，使转动；转身，扭转（身体部位）；翻动，翻转（turn 的现在分词）

e.en: Underwear is items of clothing that you wear next to your skin and under your other clothes.

ex.en: For Christmas my brother and I got new underwear, one toy and one book.
ex.zh: 作为圣诞礼物，我弟弟和我得到了新内衣、一件玩具和一本书。

d: n. 内衣，衬衣

e.en: Your views on something are the beliefs or opinions that you have about it, for example,whether you think it is good, bad, right, or wrong.

ex.en: Washington and Moscow are believed to have similar views on Kashmir.
ex.zh: 华盛顿和莫斯科被认为在克什米尔问题上持有相似的观点。

ex.en: You should also make your views known to your congressperson.
ex.zh: 你们的观点也应该让国会议员们知道。

e.en: Your view of a particular subject is the way that you understand and think about it.

ex.en: The whole point was to get away from a Christian-centered view of religion.
ex.zh: 整个核心问题是要摆脱以基督教为中心的宗教观。

e.en: If you view something in a particular way, you think of it in that way.

ex.en: First-generation Americans view the United States as a land of golden opportunity.
ex.zh: 第一代美国人把美国看成一个充满良机的大陆。

ex.en: Abigail's mother Linda views her daughter's talent with a mixture of pride and worry.
ex.zh: 阿比盖尔的母亲琳达看待女儿的天赋时既骄傲又担忧。

e.en: The view from a window or high place is everything that can be seen from that place, especially when it is considered to be beautiful.

ex.en: The view from our window was one of beautiful green countryside.
ex.zh: 从我们窗口可以看到一片绿色乡村的美景。

d: n. 观点，看法；（理解或思维的）方法，方式；景象，视野；风景，景色；风景画，风景照；图像，视图；（一次）观看，一睹，一览；（文本或图表在计算机屏幕上的）显示方式
v. 看待，考虑；观看；查看，观察；（在计算机屏幕上）阅读，看；看见（狐狸）离开隐藏处

e.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in. 吸收 (液体、气体等)

ex.en: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air and moisture from the soil.
ex.zh: 植物从空气中吸收二氧化碳，从泥土中吸收水分。

e.en: If something absorbs light, heat, or another form of energy, it takes it in. 吸取 (光、热等能量)

ex.en: A household radiator absorbs energy in the form of electric current and releases it in the form of heat.
ex.zh: 家用暖气以电流的形式吸收能量，然后以热量的形式将其释放出去。

e.en: If a group is absorbed into a larger group, it becomes part of the larger group.

ex.en: City schools were absorbed into the countywide school district.
ex.zh: 市立学校被并入了郡学区。

e.en: If something absorbs a force or shock, it reduces its effect.

ex.en: ...footwear which does not absorb the impact of the foot striking the ground.
ex.zh: …不能缓冲脚踏在地面上所产生的冲击力的鞋子。

d: v. 吸收；使并入，纳入；同化，汲取；消减，缓冲（外力、震动等）；理解，掌握（信息）；使全神贯注，使专心；承受（变革、影响等），承担（费用等）；花掉（大量金钱），耗费

e.en: A thatcher is a person whose job is making roofs from straw or reeds.

d: n. 盖茅草屋顶的人
n. （Thatcher）（美、英）撒切尔（人名）

e.en: If you attempt to do something, especially something difficult, you try to do it. 试图 (尤指做困难的事)

ex.en: The only time that we attempted to do something like that was in the city of Philadelphia.
ex.zh: 我们惟一一次试图做那样的事是在费城。

e.en: If you make an attempt to do something, you try to do it, often without success. (常指不成功的)

ex.en: ...a deliberate attempt to destabilize the defence.
ex.zh: …蓄意削弱防御的企图。

e.en: An attempt on someone's life is an attempt to kill them. (杀人)

ex.en: ...an attempt on the life of the former Iranian prime minister.
ex.zh: …刺杀伊朗前总理的企图。

d: n. 尝试，试图，企图（attempt 的复数形式）
v. 试图，努力去做（attempt 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you give someone or something your attention, you look at it, listen to it, or think about it carefully.

ex.en: You have my undivided attention.
ex.zh: 我全部的注意力都在你身上。

ex.en: Later he turned his attention to the desperate state of housing in the city.
ex.zh: 后来他把注意力转向了该市极为严重的住房状况。

e.en: Attention is great interest that is shown in someone or something, particularly by the general public. (尤指公众的)

ex.en: Volume Two, subtitled "The Lawyers," will also attract considerable attention.
ex.zh: 副标题为《律师》的第2卷也将会引起极大的关注。

e.en: If someone or something is getting attention, they are being dealt with or cared for.

ex.en: Each year more than two million household injuries need medical attention.
ex.zh: 每年有二百多万起在家受伤、需要医疗救治的案例。

e.en: If you bring something to someone's attention or draw their attention to it, you tell them about it or make them notice it. (引起某人)

ex.en: If we don't keep bringing this to the attention of the people, nothing will be done.
ex.zh: 如果我们无法让公众保持对此事的关注，那就将一事无成。

d: n. 注意；注意力；照料；兴趣；立正；殷勤，关心

e.en: A blur is a shape or area which you cannot see clearly because it has no distinct outline or because it is moving very fast.

ex.en: Out of the corner of my eye I saw a blur of movement on the other side of the glass.
ex.zh: 从眼角我看见了玻璃窗另一边一个移动的模糊身影。

e.en: When a thing blurs or when something blurs it, you cannot see it clearly because its edges are no longer distinct. 使变模糊;

ex.en: This creates a spectrum of colours at the edges of objects which blurs the image.
ex.zh: 这在物体的边缘产生了一系列颜色，使图像变得模糊不清。

e.en: 模糊不清的

ex.en: ...blurred black and white photographs.
ex.zh: …模糊的黑白照片。

e.en: If something blurs an idea or a distinction between things, that idea or distinction no longer seems clear.

ex.en: ...her belief that scientists are trying to blur the distinction between "how" and "why" questions.
ex.zh: …她认为科学家们正试图模糊“如何”与“为什么”问题之间的区别的想法。

d: v. （使）变得模糊不清；（使）视线模糊；（使）难以区分（blur 的现在分词）
n. 模糊；变得模糊不清的过程或状态；（图像处理）模糊化

e.en: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

ex.en: The ambassador appealed for a change in U.S. policy.
ex.zh: 该大使呼吁美国政策的变革。

ex.en: There are going to have to be some drastic changes.
ex.zh: 一定得有些重大变革。

e.en: If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.

ex.en: It is a complex system, but it certainly makes a change.
ex.zh: 这是个复杂系统，但肯定有所改进。

e.en: If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.

ex.en: His physician modified the dosage but did not change to a different medication.
ex.zh: 他的医生调整了剂量，但没有改换成别的药方。

e.en: When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different. 改变;

ex.en: We are trying to detect and understand how the climates change.
ex.zh: 我们在努力探测并了解气候是怎样变化的。

ex.en: In the union office, the mood gradually changed from resignation to rage.
ex.zh: 在工会办公室，情绪渐渐由依从变成了愤怒。

d: adj. 经过改变的，变化了的
v. 改变，变化；更换，替换；换乘（change 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Your chest is the top part of the front of your body where your ribs, lungs, and heart are.

ex.en: He crossed his arms over his chest.
ex.zh: 他在胸前交叉双臂。

ex.en: He was shot in the chest.
ex.zh: 他胸部中弹。

e.en: A chest is a large, heavy box used for storing things.

ex.en: At the very bottom of the chest were his carving tools.
ex.zh: 在储物箱的最底部有他的雕刻工具。

ex.en: ...a treasure chest.
ex.zh: …一个珍宝箱。

d: n. （解剖）胸，胸膛，胸腔；大箱子，储物箱，宝箱；带抽屉的衣柜，五斗柜（chest of drawers）

e.en: The circumstances of a particular situation are the conditions which affect what happens.

ex.en: Recent opinion polls show that 60 percent favour abortion under certain circumstances.
ex.zh: 最近的民意调查显示60%的人赞同特定情况下的流产。

ex.en: The strategy was too dangerous in the explosive circumstances of the times.
ex.zh: 在当时爆炸性的形势下，这一战略太危险了。

e.en: The circumstances of an event are the way it happened or the causes of it. 详情;

ex.en: I'm making inquiries about the circumstances of Mary Dean's murder.
ex.zh: 我正在调查玛丽·迪安谋杀案的原委。

e.en: Your circumstances are the conditions of your life, especially the amount of money that you have. 境况 (尤指经济状况)

ex.en: ...help and support for the single mother, whatever her circumstances.
ex.zh: …提供给单身母亲的帮助和支持，无论她们的境况如何。

e.en: Events and situations which cannot be controlled are sometimes referred to as circumstance. 命运;

ex.en: There are those, you know, who, by circumstance, end up homeless.
ex.zh: 你知道，有些人由于命运的原因最终变得无家可归。

d: n. 情况，环境，状况；（尤指经济上的）境况；原委，详情

e.en: Someone who is competent is efficient and effective.

ex.en: He was a loyal, distinguished and very competent civil servant.
ex.zh: 他是一个忠诚、出色、很有能力的公务员。

e.en: 有能力地

ex.en: The government performed competently in the face of multiple challenges.
ex.zh: 政府在面临多重挑战时表现得很出色。

e.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

ex.en: Most adults do not feel competent to deal with a medical emergency involving a child.
ex.zh: 多数成年人感到难以应付小孩医疗突发事件。

d: adj. 能干的，能胜任的；合格的，过得去的；精神正常的，智力无缺陷的；有决定权的；有法定资格的；活性的，（处于）感受态的

e.en: Your attitude to something is the way that you think and feel about it, especially when this shows in the way you behave.

ex.en: ...the general change in attitude toward handicapped people.
ex.zh: …对残疾人态度的普遍转变。

ex.en: Being unemployed produces negative attitudes to work.
ex.zh: 失业会对工作产生消极态度。

d: n. 态度，看法；姿势，姿态（attitude 的复数）

e.en: If doctors or medical treatments cure an illness or injury, they cause it to end or disappear. 治愈 (疾病、损伤)

ex.en: An operation finally cured his shin injury.
ex.zh: 手术最终治愈了他的胫骨损伤。

e.en: If doctors or medical treatments cure a person, they make the person well again after an illness or injury. 治愈 (病人)

ex.en: It is an effective treatment and could cure all the leprosy sufferers worldwide.
ex.zh: 那是一种有效的疗法，可以治愈全世界的麻疯病患者。

ex.en: Almost overnight I was cured.
ex.zh: 几乎在一夜之间我被治愈了。

e.en: If someone or something cures a problem, they bring it to an end.

ex.en: Private firms are willing to make large scale investments to help cure Russia's economic troubles.
ex.zh: 私有公司愿意进行大规模投资来帮助解决俄罗斯的经济困难。

e.en: When food, tobacco, or animal skin is cured, it is dried, smoked, or salted so that it will last for a long time. 加工处理 (食物、烟草、动物皮等)

ex.en: Legs of pork were cured and smoked over the fire.
ex.zh: 猪腿在火上经过了烟熏处理。

d: n. 药物，疗法；对策，措施；治愈，治疗；（对橡胶、塑料或其他材料的）熟化；（基督教牧师的）牧师责任（或责任区）；教区
v. 治愈（病人），治好（疾病）；解决；控制，消除（不良的习惯、情感或态度）；加工贮藏；变干硬
【名】 （Cure）（美、法）楚雷（人名）

e.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

ex.en: An intense debate is going on within the Israeli government.
ex.zh: 一场激烈的争论正在以色列政府内部进行。

ex.en: There has been a lot of debate among scholars about this.
ex.zh: 在学者中有很多关于此问题的辩论。

e.en: A debate is a formal discussion, for example, in a parliament or institution, in which people express different opinions about a particular subject and then vote on it. (议会投票前的)

ex.en: He is expected to force a debate in Congress on his immigration reform.
ex.zh: 他预期会推动一个关于他的移民改革的正式讨论。

e.en: If people debate a topic, they discuss it fairly formally, putting forward different views. You can also say that one person debates a topic with another person.

ex.en: The United Nations Security Council will debate the issue today.
ex.zh: 联合国安理会今天将辩论该问题。

ex.en: Scientists were debating whether an asteroid was about to hit the Earth.
ex.zh: 科学家们在争论一颗小行星是否要撞上地球。

e.en: If you debate whether to do something or what to do, you think or talk about possible courses of action before deciding exactly what you are going to do.

ex.en: Taggart debated whether to have yet another double vodka.
ex.zh: 塔格特考虑着是否要再来一杯双份伏特加。

d: v. 辩论，争论，讨论（debate 的过去式及过去分词形式）；考虑，斟酌（多后接 whether/how 等从句）
adj. 有争议的，争论中的（分词形容词，常作定语）

e.en: If you display something that you want people to see, you put it in a particular place, so that people can see it easily. 陈列;

ex.en: Among the protesters and war veterans proudly displaying their medals was Aubrey Rose.
ex.zh: 在抗议人群和自豪地展示勋章的退伍军人中的是奥布里∙罗斯。

e.en: Display is also a noun. 陈列;

ex.en: Most of the other artists whose work is on display were his pupils or colleagues.
ex.zh: 其他有作品展出的艺术家大多数是他的学生或同事。

e.en: If you display something, you show it to people.

ex.en: She displayed her wound to the twelve gentlemen of the jury.
ex.zh: 她向陪审团的12位男士展示她的伤痕。
