e.en: If you display a characteristic, quality, or emotion, you behave in a way which shows that you have it. 表露 (特点、素质、情感)

ex.en: It was unlike Gordon to display his feelings.
ex.zh: 表露自己的感情这点可不像戈登。

d: v. 展示，陈列；显露，表现；（计算机）显示；（为求偶）作炫耀行为
n. 展览，陈列；表演；（计算机屏幕上的）显示，显示器；流露，表现；炫耀行为

e.en: You use either in front of the first of two or more alternatives, when you are stating the only possibilities or choices that there are. The other alternatives are introduced by "or." 与(or)
e.zh: 连用，表示几个可选项中只能选其一

ex.en: Sightseeing is best done either by tour bus or by bicycles.
ex.zh: 观光最好要么乘游览巴士，要么骑自行车。

ex.en: The former president was demanding that he should be either put on trial or set free.
ex.zh: 前总统一直要求要么对他进行审判，要么就无罪释放。

e.en: You use either in a negative statement in front of the first of two alternatives to indicate that the negative statement refers to both the alternatives.
e.zh: 用于否定句中，表示“两者都不”

ex.en: There had been no indication of either breathlessness or any loss of mental faculties right until his death.
ex.zh: 直到去世，他既没有出现呼吸困难也没有脑功能丧失的迹象。

e.en: You can use either to refer to one of two things, people, or situations, when you want to say that they are both possible and it does not matter which one is chosen or considered.
e.zh: 用于表示“两者中的任一个”

ex.en: There were glasses of iced champagne and cigars. Unfortunately not many of either were consumed.
ex.zh: 有很多杯冰镇香槟和雪茄。可惜两样东西中哪一样都没被受用多少。

e.en: Either is also a quantifier.

ex.en: Do either of you smoke or drink heavily?
ex.zh: 你们俩当中有谁抽烟、喝酒凶吗？

d: conj. 或者，要么；两者都（不），既（不）
pron. （两者之中）任意一个；两者都（不）
adv. 也（不），亦（不）；而且，还
det. （两者中的）每个，各方

e.en: Electrical goods, equipment, or appliances work by means of electricity.

ex.en: ...shipments of electrical equipment.
ex.zh: …电器设备的运输。

e.en: 电力地

ex.en: ...electrically powered vehicles.
ex.zh: …电动车。

e.en: Electrical systems or parts supply or use electricity.

ex.en: ...lighting and other electrical systems on the new runway.
ex.zh: …新跑道上的照明和其他电力系统。

e.en: Electrical energy is energy in the form of electricity.

ex.en: ...brief pulses of electrical energy.
ex.zh: …短暂的电能脉冲。

d: adj. 电的，与电有关的；生产或销售电器的
n. 电气设备，电路；电器公司发行的股票

e.en: If you use established to describe something such as an organization, you mean that it is well known because it has existed for a long time.

ex.en: These range from established companies to start-ups.
ex.zh: 这些包括老牌公司和新兴公司。

d: adj. 确立已久的，早已投入使用的；资深的，知名的；（植物）已生根的，长势良好的；已被认可的，已被接受的（尤指英国国教）
v. 建立，设立；证实，确定；发现，找出（establish 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

ex.en: We asked her to describe what kind of things she did in her spare time.
ex.zh: 我们请她描述她在闲暇时做些什么。

ex.en: She read a poem by Carver which describes their life together.
ex.zh: 她读了一首卡弗描写他们在一起生活的诗。

e.en: If a person describes someone or something as a particular thing, he or she believes that they are that thing and says so. 讲成;

ex.en: He described it as an extraordinarily tangled and complicated tale.
ex.zh: 他把它讲成了一个格外错综复杂的故事。

ex.en: Even his closest allies describe him as forceful, aggressive, and determined.
ex.zh: 甚至他最亲密的同盟者们都说他强势、好斗且坚决。

d: v. 描述，叙述，描写；表示（describe 的 ing 形式）
adj. 描述的，起描述作用的（常用于复合词）

e.en: If you give an explanation of something that has happened, you give people reasons for it, especially in an attempt to justify it. 解释 (原因)

ex.en: She told the court she would give a full explanation of the prosecution's decision on Monday.
ex.zh: 她告诉法庭她将在星期一就控方的决定做出详尽的解释。

e.en: If you say there is an explanation for something, you mean that there is a reason for it.

ex.en: The deputy airport manager said there was no apparent explanation for the crash.
ex.zh: 机场副经理称那次飞机坠毁没有明显的原因。

e.en: If you give an explanation of something, you give details about it or describe it so that it can be understood.

ex.en: He has given a very clear explanation of his remarks and the context in which they were made.
ex.zh: 他对他的评论以及作出那些评论的情境已经作了非常清楚详细的说明。

d: n. 解释，说明；解释性说法，说明性文字；理由，原因

e.en: Exposure to something dangerous means being in a situation where it might affect you.

ex.en: Exposure to lead is known to damage the brains of young children.
ex.zh: 已知接触铅会损害幼童的大脑。

e.en: Exposure is the harmful effect on your body caused by very cold weather.

ex.en: He was suffering from exposure and shock but his condition was said to be stable.
ex.zh: 他受冻休克，但他的状态据说很稳定。

e.en: The exposure of a well-known person is the revealing of the fact that they are bad or immoral in some way.

ex.en: He undertook increasingly dangerous assignments until his exposure as a spy.
ex.zh: 在间谍身份暴露之前他一直从事日益危险的任务。

e.en: Exposure is publicity that a person, company, or product receives.

ex.en: All the candidates have been getting an enormous amount of exposure on television and in the press.
ex.zh: 所有候选人都在争取大量的电视和新闻媒体宣传。

d: n. 暴露，接触；曝光，揭发；报道，宣传；单张胶片；曝光时间，曝光量；受冻；朝向

e.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

ex.en: Patriotic songs have long been a feature of Kuwaiti life.
ex.zh: 爱国歌曲长期以来一直是科威特人生活的一个特点。

ex.en: The spacious gardens are a special feature of this property.
ex.zh: 宽敞的花园是这处房产的一大特色。

e.en: A feature is a special article in a newspaper or magazine, or a special programme on radio or television. (报纸、杂志的) 特写; (广播、电视的)

ex.en: We are delighted to see the Sunday Times running a long feature on breast cancer.
ex.zh: 我们高兴地看到《星期日泰晤士报》刊登了关于乳腺癌的一篇长长的特写。

e.en: A feature or a feature film or movie is a full-length film about a fictional situation, as opposed to a short film or a documentary. 正片;

ex.en: ...the first feature-length cartoon, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
ex.zh: …第一部故事片长度的卡通片《白雪公主和七个小矮人》。

e.en: A geographical feature is something noticeable in a particular area of country, for example, a hill, river, or valley. (地理)

ex.en: ...one of the area's oddest geographical features - an eight-mile bank of pebbles shelving abruptly into the sea.
ex.zh: …这个地区最奇怪的地理特征之一，一条8英里长的鹅卵石堤岸陡然倾斜伸到海里。

d: n. 特点，特征；五官，面貌（特征）；地貌；特写，专题节目；正片； 特点，特征
v. 以……为特色，以……为主要组成；起重要作用，占重要地位；放映，上演；担任主演

e.en: A feeling is an emotion, such as anger or happiness.

ex.en: It gave me a feeling of satisfaction.
ex.zh: 它给了我一种满足感。

ex.en: He was unable to contain his own destructive feelings.
ex.zh: 他无法克制自己的消极情绪。

e.en: If you have a feeling of hunger, tiredness, or other physical sensation, you experience it.

ex.en: I also had a strange feeling in my neck.
ex.zh: 我的脖子也有一种奇怪的感觉。

ex.en: Focus on the feeling of relaxation.
ex.zh: 专注于放松的感觉。

e.en: If you have a feeling that something is the case or that something is going to happen, you think that is probably the case or that it is probably going to happen.

ex.en: I have a feeling that everything will be all right.
ex.zh: 我有种预感一切都会好起来的。

e.en: Your feelings about something are the things that you think and feel about it, or your attitude toward it. 看法;

ex.en: She has strong feelings about the alleged growth in violence against female officers.
ex.zh: 她对据称的女性军官遭遇暴力事件的增多有强烈的看法。

ex.en: I think that sums up the feelings of most discerning and intelligent Indians.
ex.zh: 我认为那综合了最有眼力和智慧的印第安人的观点。

d: n. 感觉，感触；预感；看法，态度；情感，情绪；理解力，领悟力；好感，同情；知觉；氛围；品质，特点
adj. 多愁善感的，多情的
v. 感受到，体会到；觉得，相信；使人感觉……(feel 的现在分词形式)

e.en: Someone who is female is a woman or a girl.

ex.en: ...a sixteen-piece dance band with a female singer.
ex.zh: …一支有一名女歌手的16人伴舞乐队。

e.en: Female matters and things relate to, belong to, or affect women rather than men.

ex.en: ...female infertility.
ex.zh: …女性不孕症。

e.en: Women and girls are sometimes referred to as females when they are being considered as a type.

ex.en: Hay fever affects males more than females.
ex.zh: 男性感染花粉热多于女性。

e.en: You can refer to any creature that can lay eggs or produce babies from its body as a female.

ex.en: Each female will lay just one egg in April or May.
ex.zh: 每只雌性在4月或5月份将只产一颗卵。

d: adj. 女性的，妇女的；女性特有的；由女性组成的；内孔的；雌性的，母的；雌蕊的
n. 雌性动物，雌性植物；女子

e.en: You use fixed to describe something which stays the same and does not or cannot vary.

ex.en: They issue a fixed number of shares that trade publicly.
ex.zh: 他们发行了固定数量可公开交易的股票。

ex.en: Many restaurants offer fixed-price menus.
ex.zh: 很多餐馆提供固定价格的菜单。

e.en: If you say that someone has fixed ideas or opinions, you mean that they do not often change their ideas and opinions, although perhaps they should.

ex.en: ...people who have fixed ideas about things.
ex.zh: …固执己见的人。

e.en: If someone has a fixed smile on their face, they are smiling even though they do not feel happy or pleased. (笑容)

ex.en: I had to go through the rest of the evening with a fixed smile on my face.
ex.zh: 我不得不带着一脸僵硬的笑容度过那晚余下的时间。

e.en: Someone who is of no fixed address does not have a permanent place to live.

ex.en: They are not able to get a job interview because they have no fixed address.
ex.zh: 他们无法获得工作面试的机会，因为他们居无定所。

d: adj. 固定的；（神情）僵硬的；确定的，不变的；顽固的，固执的；（比赛、选举等）被操纵的；（经济上）处境……的；不易挥发的，形成化合物的
v. 修理（fix 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: If you flip a device on or off, or if you flip a switch, you turn it on or off by pressing the switch quickly. 快速地按动 (装置或开关)

ex.en: He didn't flip on the headlights until he was two blocks away.
ex.zh: 直到过了两个街区后，他才打开前灯。

ex.en: Then he walked out, flipping the lights off.
ex.zh: 接着他走了出去，随手把灯关掉。

e.en: If you flip through the pages of a book, for example, you quickly turn over the pages in order to find a particular one or to get an idea of the contents.

ex.en: He was flipping through a magazine in the living room.
ex.zh: 他在起居室里快速翻阅一本杂志。

e.en: If something flips over, or if you flip it over or into a different position, it moves or is moved into a different position.

ex.en: The plane then flipped over and burst into flames.
ex.zh: 这时飞机翻了个个儿，接着就燃烧了起来。

e.en: If you flip something, especially a coin, you use your thumb to make it turn over and over, as it goes through the air. 投掷 (尤指硬币)

ex.en: I pulled a coin from my pocket and flipped it.
ex.zh: 我从口袋里掏出一枚硬币，把它投掷出去。

d: v. （flip 的过去式和过去分词形式）翻转，翻倒，翻过来；快速翻阅，翻动
vt. （flip 的过去式和过去分词形式）打开（开关）；掷，丢，轻抛（尤指硬币）；倒卖（房产）
vi. （flip 的过去式和过去分词形式）蹦跳；（情况、位置、状态等的）突然变化，反转；（口语，常作 flipped out）失控，发疯
adj. （课堂）翻转的（一种新教学方式）

e.en: Your forehead is the area at the front of your head between your eyebrows and your hair.

ex.en: ...the lines on her forehead.
ex.zh: …她前额上的皱纹。

d: n. 前额

e.en: A person's gender is the fact that they are male or female.

ex.en: Women are sometimes denied opportunities solely because of their gender.
ex.zh: 女性有时仅仅因为她们的性别而被剥夺机会。

e.en: You can refer to all male people or all female people as a particular gender.

ex.en: While her observations may be true about some men, they could hardly apply to the entire gender.
ex.zh: 她的观察对某些男人可能是对的，但并不适用于所有男性。

e.en: In grammar, the gender of a noun, pronoun, or adjective is whether it is masculine, feminine, or neuter. A word's gender can affect its form and behaviour. In English, only personal pronouns such as "she," reflexive pronouns such as "itself," and possessive determiners such as "his" have gender. (语法上的)

ex.en: In both Welsh and Irish the word for "moon" is of feminine gender.
ex.zh: 在威尔士语和爱尔兰语中，“月亮”这个单词都是阴性。

d: n. 性别；（语法中的）性；（总称）男性，女性

e.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

ex.en: I managed to grab her hand.
ex.zh: 我设法抓住了她的手。

e.en: If you grab at something, you try to grab it. (设法)

ex.en: He was clumsily trying to grab at Alfred's arms.
ex.zh: 他正笨手笨脚地试图抓住艾尔弗雷德的手臂。

e.en: Grab is also a noun.

ex.en: I made a grab for the knife.
ex.zh: 我伸手去抓那把刀。

e.en: If you grab someone who is walking past, you succeed in getting their attention.

ex.en: Grab that waiter, Mary Ann.
ex.zh: 玛丽•安，叫住那个服务生。

d: v. 攫取，抓住；（尤指匆忙地）取，吃，喝；霸占，强夺；利用，抓住（机会）；引人注意，吸引
n. 攫取，赚取；抓具，抓斗；抓取（或截获、采集）的图像

e.en: A graduate is a student who has successfully completed a course at a high school, college, or university.

ex.en: The top one-third of all high school graduates are entitled to an education at California State University.
ex.zh: 全部高中毕业生当中排名前三分之一的有资格到加利福尼亚州立大学学习。

e.en: When a student graduates, they complete their studies successfully and leave their school or university.

ex.en: When the boys graduated from high school, Ann moved to a small town in Vermont.
ex.zh: 男孩们中学毕业后安迁到了佛蒙特州的一座小镇。

e.en: If you graduate from one thing to another, you go from a less important job or position to a more important one.

ex.en: Bruce graduated to chef at the Bear Hotel.
ex.zh: 布鲁斯晋升为大熊酒店的厨师长。

d: v. 获得学位（尤指学士），大学毕业；毕业（尤指中学）；（学校等）准予……毕业，授予……学位；（从……）进步到，升级到（graduate 的第三人称单数）
n. 毕业生（graduate 的复数）；大学毕业生，学士学位获得者

e.en: You say that something is grotesque when it is so unnatural, unpleasant, and exaggerated that it upsets or shocks you.

ex.en: ...the grotesque disparities between the wealthy few and nearly everyone else.
ex.zh: …少数富人和几乎所有其他人之间荒唐的差异。

e.en: 荒唐地

ex.en: He called it the most grotesquely tragic experience he's ever had.
ex.zh: 他称之为他所经历的最荒诞不经的悲惨经历。

e.en: If someone or something is grotesque, they are very ugly.

ex.en: They tried to avoid looking at his grotesque face and his crippled body.
ex.zh: 他们尽量不去看他那丑陋的面庞和残疾的身躯。

e.en: 丑陋地

ex.en: ...grotesquely deformed beggars.
ex.zh: …面目丑陋、身体畸形的乞丐们。

d: adj. 怪诞的，奇怪的，荒唐的；丑陋奇异的，奇形怪状的
n. （尤指书画中的）奇形怪状的人（或物）；奇异风格；（印刷）畸形字体

e.en: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.

ex.en: He has an endearing habit of licking his lips when he's nervous.
ex.zh: 他有个紧张时舔嘴唇的可爱习惯。

ex.en: Many people add salt to their food out of habit, without even tasting it first.
ex.zh: 许多人出于习惯往他们的食物中加盐，甚至都不先品尝一下。

e.en: A habit is an action considered bad that someone does repeatedly and finds it difficult to stop doing.

ex.en: A good way to break the habit of eating too quickly is to put your knife and fork down after each mouthful.
ex.zh: 一个改掉吃饭太快的坏习惯的好方法是每吃一口后放下刀叉。

e.en: A drug habit is an addiction to a drug such as heroin or cocaine.

ex.en: She became a prostitute in order to pay for her cocaine habit.
ex.zh: 她为花钱过可卡因毒瘾而成了一名妓女。

e.en: If you say that someone is a creature of habit, you mean that they usually do the same thing at the same time each day, rather than doing new and different things.

ex.en: Jesse is a creature of habit and always eats breakfast.
ex.zh: 杰西是按习惯行事的人，每天都吃早餐。

d: n. 习惯；（吸毒、喝酒、抽烟的）瘾；道袍，道服；体质，体型
v. 给……穿衣

e.en: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.

ex.en: He has an endearing habit of licking his lips when he's nervous.
ex.zh: 他有个紧张时舔嘴唇的可爱习惯。

ex.en: Many people add salt to their food out of habit, without even tasting it first.
ex.zh: 许多人出于习惯往他们的食物中加盐，甚至都不先品尝一下。

e.en: A habit is an action considered bad that someone does repeatedly and finds it difficult to stop doing.

ex.en: A good way to break the habit of eating too quickly is to put your knife and fork down after each mouthful.
ex.zh: 一个改掉吃饭太快的坏习惯的好方法是每吃一口后放下刀叉。

e.en: A drug habit is an addiction to a drug such as heroin or cocaine.

ex.en: She became a prostitute in order to pay for her cocaine habit.
ex.zh: 她为花钱过可卡因毒瘾而成了一名妓女。

e.en: If you say that someone is a creature of habit, you mean that they usually do the same thing at the same time each day, rather than doing new and different things.

ex.en: Jesse is a creature of habit and always eats breakfast.
ex.zh: 杰西是按习惯行事的人，每天都吃早餐。

d: n. 习惯（habit 的复数）；（生物）习性；（Habits）人名；（匈）豪比奇

e.en: Your groin is the front part of your body between your legs.

ex.en: I underwent an operation on my groin once.
ex.zh: 我的腹股沟部位曾动过一次手术。

d: 丁坝

e.en: A house is a building in which people live, usually the people belonging to one family.

ex.en: She has moved to a small house and is living off her meagre savings.
ex.zh: 她搬进了一幢小房子，靠自己微薄的积蓄过日子。

e.en: You can refer to all the people who live together in a house as the house. 一家人;

ex.en: If he set his alarm clock for midnight, it would wake the whole house.
ex.zh: 如果他把闹钟设定在午夜，铃声会把全家人都吵醒。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of places where people go to eat and drink. …馆 (用于某些类型的餐馆名称中)

ex.en: ...a steak house.
ex.zh: …一家牛排馆。

e.en: House is used in the names of types of companies, especially ones which publish books, lend money, or design clothes. …公司 (用于某些类型的公司名称中，尤其是出版、贷款或服装设计等公司)

ex.en: Many of the clothes come from the world's top fashion houses.
ex.zh: 这些服装中有很多来自世界顶级时装设计公司。

d: n. 住宅；家园；洋房（house 的复数）；房子的总称

e.en: If you hurt yourself or hurt a part of your body, you feel pain because you have injured yourself.

ex.en: Yasin had seriously hurt himself while trying to escape from the police.
ex.zh: 亚辛在企图从警方手中逃脱时把自己伤得很厉害。

e.en: If a part of your body hurts, you feel pain there.

ex.en: His collar bone only hurt when he lifted his arm.
ex.zh: 他的锁骨只是在举起手臂时才感觉疼痛。

e.en: If you are hurt, you have been injured.

ex.en: His comrades asked him if he was hurt.
ex.zh: 他的伙伴们问他是否受伤了。

e.en: If you hurt someone, you cause them to feel pain.

ex.en: I didn't mean to hurt her, only to keep her still.
ex.zh: 我没想把她弄痛，只是想让她别动。

ex.en: That hurts!
ex.zh: 好痛呀！

d: v. 动词 hurt 的第三人称单数：（身体部位）感到疼痛；弄痛，使受伤；使伤心，伤害感情；损害，对…产生不良影响
n. 名词 hurt 的复数：痛痒；创伤，痛苦

e.en: An immediate result, action, or reaction happens or is done without any delay.

ex.en: These tragic incidents have had an immediate effect.
ex.zh: 这些悲惨事件已经有了立杆见影的结果。

e.en: Immediate needs and concerns exist at the present time and must be dealt with quickly.

ex.en: Relief agencies say the immediate problem is not a lack of food, but transportation.
ex.zh: 救援机构称当务之急不是食品匮乏，而是交通运输不足。

e.en: The immediate person or thing comes just before or just after another person or thing in a sequence.

ex.en: In the immediate aftermath of the riots, a mood of hope and reconciliation sprang up.
ex.zh: 暴乱之后紧接的是一股希望与和解情绪的产生。

e.en: You use immediate to describe an area or position that is next to or very near a particular place or person.

ex.en: Only a handful had returned to work in the immediate vicinity.
ex.zh: 只有少数几个人回到附近地区工作。

d: adj. 立刻的，即时的；目前的，紧迫的；附近的，紧接的；（关系或级别）最接近的，直系的；（两者间）直接的；（感知，反应）直觉的

e.en: A hardwired part of a computer forms part of its hardware. (计算机系统)
If an ability, approach, or type of activity is hardwired into the brain, it is a basic one and cannot be changed. (能力、方法、活动类型等)

ex.en: Others think that the rules for what is "musical" are hardwired in our brains to some degree.
ex.zh: 其他人认为，我们的大脑对什么东西是“悦耳的”在某种程度上有其内在的标准。

d: adj. [计] 硬连线的，硬接线的；天生的，固有的
硬接线：指在电子设备或系统中使用物理电路连接，而非通过软件或程序控制。

e.en: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

ex.en: Within a month, both the texture and condition of your hair should improve.
ex.zh: 不出一个月，你头发的质地和状况应该都会改善。

e.en: If a skill you have improves or you improve a skill, you get better at it.

ex.en: Their French has improved enormously.
ex.zh: 他们的法语水平提高了很多。

e.en: If you improve after an illness or an injury, your health gets better or you get stronger.

ex.en: He had improved so much the doctor had cut his dosage.
ex.zh: 他康复了很多，医生减少了他的用药量。

e.en: If you improve on a previous achievement of your own or of someone else, you achieve a better standard or result.

ex.en: We need to improve on our performance against Nabisco.
ex.zh: 我们需根据纳贝斯克公司标准来提高我们的业绩。

d: adj. 改良的，改进过的，改善的；（土地等）已开发整理并具备设施的
v. improve 的过去式和过去分词：改进，改善，提高；增加；变得更好

e.en: A lab is the same as a .

d: n. 实验室 (=laboratory)；实验课
abbr. 工党 (Lab)；工党；拉布拉多寻回犬

e.en: If you learn something, you obtain knowledge or a skill through studying or training.

ex.en: Their children were going to learn English.
ex.zh: 他们的孩子们打算学英语。

ex.en: He is learning to play the piano.
ex.zh: 他正在学弹钢琴。

e.en: 学习

ex.en: ...a bilingual approach to the learning of English.
ex.zh: …英语学习的双语法。

e.en: If you learn of something, you find out about it.

ex.en: It was only after his death that she learned of his affair with Betty.
ex.zh: 是在他去世之后她才得知他和贝蒂的风流事。

ex.en: It didn't come as a shock to learn that the fuel and cooling systems are the most common causes of breakdown.
ex.zh: 不足为怪的是，燃料和冷却系统是故障的最常见原因。

e.en: If people learn to behave or react in a particular way, they gradually start to behave in that way as a result of a change in attitudes.

ex.en: You have to learn to face your problem.
ex.zh: 你得学会面对自己的问题。

d: v. 学习，学会；得知，获悉；背熟，熟记；认识到，（从……）吸取教训；教导（某人）

e.en: If there is a link between two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example, because one thing causes or affects the other.

ex.en: ...the link between smoking and lung cancer.
ex.zh: …吸烟和肺癌之间的关系。

e.en: If someone or something links two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example, because one thing causes or affects the other.

ex.en: The U.N. Security Council has linked any lifting of sanctions to compliance with the ceasefire terms.
ex.zh: 联合国安全理事会将任何制裁的解除与遵守停火条款联系起来。

ex.en: The study further strengthens the evidence linking smoking with early death.
ex.zh: 这项研究进一步加强了联系吸烟与早亡的证据。

e.en: A link between two things or places is a physical connection between them.

ex.en: ...the railway link between Boston and New York.
ex.zh: …波士顿与纽约之间的铁路连接线。

ex.en: Drivers ran into a field of weeds at the state border, where no link with the neighbouring state had yet been planned.
ex.zh: 司机们闯入了州界处一块杂草丛生的原野，在那里还没有计划修建连接邻州的道路。

e.en: If two places or objects are linked or something links them, there is a physical connection between them.

ex.en: ...the Rama Road, which links the capital, Managua, with the Caribbean coast.
ex.zh: …连接首都马那瓜与加勒比海岸的拉玛公路。

ex.en: Seven miles of track were installed to link the hotel to the golf course.
ex.zh: 七英里的轨道被铺设来连接宾馆和高尔夫球场。

d: v. 连接；与……有关联；挽住，钩住
n. （事物间的）联系，关系；（交通上的）联系；（链状物的）环，节；（超文本）链接；一节香肠；令（长度单位，1令等于1测链的百分之一，即7.92英寸）；（行路时照明用）沥青和麻屑火把
【名】 （Link）（英、德、塞、捷、匈、瑞典）林克（人名）

e.en: You use mainly when mentioning the main reason or thing involved in something.

ex.en: The stock market scandal is refusing to go away, mainly because there's still no consensus over how it should be dealt with.
ex.zh: 此次股市丑闻历久不散，主要是因为在此事如何处理上尚无共识。

e.en: You use mainly when you are referring to a group and stating something that is true of most of it.

ex.en: The African half of the audience was mainly from Senegal or Mali.
ex.zh: 观众中的一半非洲人主要来自塞内加尔或马里。

d: adv. 主要地，首要地；大部分，大多

e.en: Someone who is male is a man or a boy.

ex.en: Many women achievers appear to pose a threat to their male colleagues.
ex.zh: 许多女性成功者似乎对她们的男同事造成一种威胁。

ex.en: The company has engaged two male dancers from the Bolshoi.
ex.zh: 该公司聘了两名来自波修瓦剧院的男舞蹈演员。

e.en: Men and boys are sometimes referred to as males when they are being considered as a type.

ex.en: ...the remains of a Caucasian male, aged 65-70.
ex.zh: …一个年龄在65至70岁之间的高加索男子的遗骸。

e.en: Male means relating to, belonging to, or affecting men rather than women.

ex.en: Massive male unemployment has diminished the status of men in the family.
ex.zh: 大量男性失业已经降低了男人在家庭中的地位。

ex.en: ...male violence.
ex.zh: …男性暴力。

e.en: You can refer to any creature that belongs to the sex that cannot lay eggs or have babies as a male.

ex.en: Males and females take turns brooding the eggs.
ex.zh: 雌雄轮流孵卵。

d: adj. 男性的；（动物）公的，雄性的；只有雄蕊的；全由男性组成的；（工具部件等）凸形的，阳的；男性特有的
n. 男子，男孩；雄性动物；雄性植物
【名】 （Male）（英）梅尔，（柬）马尔，（意、西、塞）马莱（人名）

e.en: A matter is a task, situation, or event which you have to deal with or think about, especially one that involves problems.

ex.en: It was clear that she wanted to discuss some private matter.
ex.zh: 很明显她想讨论一些私事。

ex.en: Business matters drew him to Louisville.
ex.zh: 生意上的事情吸引他去路易斯维尔。

e.en: You use matters to refer to the situation you are talking about, especially when something is affecting the situation in some way.

ex.en: We have no objection to this change, but doubt that it will significantly improve matters.
ex.zh: 我们不反对这种变化，但怀疑这是否将明显地改善事态。

ex.en: If it would facilitate matters, I would be happy to come to New York.
ex.zh: 如果这有利于事态，我将乐意来纽约。

e.en: If you say that a situation is a matter of a particular thing, you mean that that is the most important thing to be done or considered when you are involved in the situation or explaining it.

ex.en: History is always a matter of interpretation.
ex.zh: 历史总是一个诠释的问题。

ex.en: Observance of the law is a matter of principle for us.
ex.zh: 遵守法律对于我们是一个原则问题。

e.en: Printed matter consists of books, newspapers, and other texts that are printed. Reading matter consists of things that are suitable for reading, such as books and newspapers. (印刷或阅读的)

ex.en: ...the government's plans to place a tax on printed matter.
ex.zh: …政府对印刷品征税的计划。

d: n. 事项，事务，情事（matter 的复数）；事件；事态；（Matters）马特斯（人名）
v. 有重大影响，事关紧要（matter 的第三人称单数）
vt. 记住，背熟，记忆（memorize 的英式拼写）

e.en: If you learn something, you obtain knowledge or a skill through studying or training.

ex.en: Their children were going to learn English.
ex.zh: 他们的孩子们打算学英语。

ex.en: He is learning to play the piano.
ex.zh: 他正在学弹钢琴。

e.en: 学习

ex.en: ...a bilingual approach to the learning of English.
ex.zh: …英语学习的双语法。

e.en: If you learn of something, you find out about it.

ex.en: It was only after his death that she learned of his affair with Betty.
ex.zh: 是在他去世之后她才得知他和贝蒂的风流事。

ex.en: It didn't come as a shock to learn that the fuel and cooling systems are the most common causes of breakdown.
ex.zh: 不足为怪的是，燃料和冷却系统是故障的最常见原因。

e.en: If people learn to behave or react in a particular way, they gradually start to behave in that way as a result of a change in attitudes.

ex.en: You have to learn to face your problem.
ex.zh: 你得学会面对自己的问题。

d: v. （learn 的第三人称单数）学习，学会；得知，获悉；背熟，熟记；认识到，（从……）吸取教训

e.en: Your memory is your ability to remember things.

ex.en: All the details of the meeting are fresh in my memory.
ex.zh: 会议的所有细节我都记忆犹新。

ex.en: But locals with long memories thought this was fair revenge for the injustice of 1961.
ex.zh: 但是记忆力好的当地人认为这是对1961年那起不公正事件的合理报复。

e.en: A memory is something that you remember from the past.

ex.en: She cannot bear to watch the film because of the bad memories it brings back.
ex.zh: 由于这部电影勾起的糟糕回忆，她不能忍受观看它。

ex.en: Her earliest memory is of singing at the age of four to wounded soldiers.
ex.zh: 她最早的记忆是在4岁时为受伤的士兵唱歌。

e.en: A computer's memory is the part of the computer where information is stored, especially for a short time before it is transferred to disks or magnetic tapes.

ex.en: The data are stored in the computer's memory.
ex.zh: 这些数据存储在计算机的内存中。

e.en: If you talk about the memory of someone who has died, especially someone who was loved or respected, you are referring to the thoughts, actions, and ceremonies by which they are remembered.

ex.en: She remained devoted to his memory.
ex.zh: 她依然对他十分怀念。

d: n. 记忆力，记性；记忆，回忆；（计算机存储器的）存储量；（计算机的）存储器；对死者的记忆；记忆所及的时间（或范围）
【名】 （Memory）（英）梅默里（人名）

e.en: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.

ex.en: ...the Grand Union Canal.
ex.zh: …大联盟运河。

e.en: A canal is a narrow tube inside your body for carrying food, air, or other substances. (体内的)

ex.en: ...delaying its progress through the alimentary canal.
ex.zh: …通过消化道延迟它的作用。

d: n. 运河，灌溉渠，水道；（体内的）管，道
v. 在……开凿运河
【名】 （Canal）（英、法、西、意、葡）卡纳尔，（土）贾纳尔（人名）
n. 苏伊士（埃及东北部港市）；苏伊士运河（通常作 Suez Canal）；苏伊士集团（法国公用事业与环境服务企业集团）
n. 以色列（亚洲国家）；犹太人，以色列人

e.en: Something that is cold has a very low temperature or a lower temperature than is normal or acceptable.

ex.en: Rinse the vegetables under cold running water.
ex.zh: 用冷自来水冲洗蔬菜。

ex.en: He likes his tea neither too hot nor too cold.
ex.zh: 他喜欢茶不太烫也不太凉。

e.en: 冷

ex.en: She complained about the coldness of his hands.
ex.zh: 她抱怨他的那双手冷冰冰的。

e.en: If it is cold, or if a place is cold, the temperature of the air is very low.

ex.en: It was bitterly cold.
ex.zh: 天气冷得刺骨。

ex.en: The house is cold because I can't afford to turn the heat on.
ex.zh: 屋子冷冰冰的，因为我开不起暖气。

e.en: 寒冷

ex.en: Within a quarter of an hour, the coldness of the night had gone.
ex.zh: 一刻钟之内，夜晚的寒冷就消退了。

d: adj. 冷的，凉的；冷淡的，冷漠的；冷色调的；已变淡的；失去知觉的；真实的，客观的；扫兴的，灰蒙蒙的；远未猜中的
n. 感冒，伤风；寒冷，低温
adv. 突然地，彻底地；毫无准备地

e.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

ex.en: The port is vital to supply relief to millions of drought victims.
ex.zh: 这个港口至关重要，给数百万旱灾民提供救济物资。

ex.en: It is vital that parents give children clear and consistent messages about drugs.
ex.zh: 至关重要的是，父母们给子女提供关于毒品明确一致的观点。

e.en: 至关重要地

ex.en: Lesley's career in the church is vitally important to her.
ex.zh: 莱斯利的教会生涯对于她而言至关重要。

d: adj. 至关重要的，必不可少的；生机勃勃的，充满活力的；生命的，维持生命所必需的
n. 身体的重要内脏，维持生命的重要器官（vitals）
【名】 （Vital）维塔尔（人名）
n. 霍尔木兹海峡（在伊朗和阿拉伯半岛之间）

e.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

ex.en: The number of staff has declined from 217,000 to 114,000.
ex.zh: 员工人数已从217000人减少到114000人。

ex.en: Hourly output by workers declined 1.3% in the first quarter.
ex.zh: 工人每小时的产量在第1季度下降了1.3%。

e.en: If you decline something or decline to do something, you politely refuse to accept it or do it.

ex.en: He declined their invitation.
ex.zh: 他谢绝了他们的邀请。

ex.en: He offered the boys some coffee. They declined politely.
ex.zh: 他要给男孩们来些咖啡。他们礼貌地拒绝了。

e.en: If there is a decline in something, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or quality.

ex.en: Official figures show a sharp decline in the number of foreign tourists.
ex.zh: 官方数字显示外国游客数量骤降。

e.en: If something is in decline or on the decline, it is gradually decreasing in importance, quality, or power.

ex.en: Thankfully the smoking of cigarettes is on the decline.
ex.zh: 感谢的是吸烟正在减少。

d: v. 下降，衰退；拒绝，谢绝；变格，词形变化
n. 减少，衰退

e.en: Your arms are the two long parts of your body that are attached to your shoulders and that have your hands at the end.

ex.en: She stretched her arms out.
ex.zh: 她伸开了双臂。

e.en: The arm of a chair is the part on which you rest your arm when you are sitting down. (椅子的)

ex.en: Mack gripped the arms of the chair.
ex.zh: 麦克抓紧了那把椅子的一对扶手。

e.en: An arm of an object is a long thin part of it that sticks out from the main part. (物体的)

ex.en: ...the lever arm of the machine.
ex.zh: …该机器的杠杆臂。

e.en: An arm of land or water is a long thin area of it that is joined to a broader area. (陆地、水域的)

ex.en: ...a small area of woodland between two arms of a small stream.
ex.zh: …一条小溪的两条支流之间的一小块林地。

d: n. 手臂，胳膊（arm 的复数）；（军事）武器，军械；纹章，徽记
v. 武装，配备（arm 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A fox is a wild animal which looks like a dog and has reddish-brown fur, a pointed face and ears, and a thick tail. Foxes eat smaller animals.

d: n. 狐狸；狐裘；狡猾的人； 妖精，性感的人；福克斯族，福克斯族语；妖精，性感的人
v. 欺骗，耍弄；把……难住，使……猜不透
【名】  （Fox） （英、美、德、丹、爱）福克斯（人名）

e.en: If your opinion or your reaction is favourable to something, you agree with it and approve of it.

ex.en: The president's convention speech received favourable reviews.
ex.zh: 总统的大会发言受到了好评。

e.en: Favourable conditions make something more likely to succeed or seem more attractive.

ex.en: It's believed the conditions in which the elections are being held are too favourable to the government.
ex.zh: 人们认为正在进行选举的条件对政府过于有利。

e.en: If you make a favourable comparison between two things, you say that the first is better than or as good as the second. 更优的;

ex.en: The film bears favourable technical comparison with Hollywood productions costing 10 times as much.
ex.zh: 这部电影与耗资为其10倍的好莱坞作品相比在技术上毫不逊色。

d: adj. 有利的，适宜的；称赞的，赞成的；（价格）优惠的，合理的；有吉兆的，前景乐观的；（风）朝着行进方向吹的
v. （使）国有化；（使）有民簇特点（或风格）；承认（外国人）为公民（nationalise 的过去式及过去分词，nationalise 等于 nationalize）
n. 伊朗（亚洲西部国家）；（美国、巴基斯坦）伊朗（人名）

e.en: You use major when you want to describe something that is more important, serious, or significant than other things in a group or situation. 主要的;

ex.en: The major factor in the decision to stay or to leave was usually professional.
ex.zh: 决定去留的主要因素通常与职业相关。

ex.en: Drug abuse has long been a major problem for the authorities there.
ex.zh: 毒品滥用长期以来一直是那里的当局的一大难题。

e.en: A major is an officer who is one rank above captain in the United States Army, Air Force, or Marines.

ex.en: I was a major in the war, you know.
ex.zh: 你知道，我在那场战争期间是个少校。

e.en: At a university or college in the United States, a student's major is the main subject that they are studying.

ex.en: English majors would be asked to explore the roots of language.
ex.zh: 英语专业的学生会被要求探究语言的根源。

e.en: At a university or college in the United States, if a student is, for example, a geology major, geology is the main subject they are studying. …

ex.en: She was a history major at the University of Oklahoma.
ex.zh: 她曾是俄克拉何马大学历史专业的学生。

d: adj. 重大的，主要的；严重的；大调的，大音阶的； （公立学校中置于学生姓氏后，表示两兄弟中）大的，年长的；主修的；大（项）的
n. 主修科目，专业；陆军少校，（美国）空军少校；（某专业的）主修学生；职业棒球大联盟；大型公司，重要企业；成年人，已达到法定年龄者；（军乐队中主管某一乐器部的）乐器长；大调，大音程； 大项，大前提；主要世界性组织（或公司、比赛）
v. （在美国大学）主修，专攻
【名】  (Major) （英）梅杰，（西）马霍尔，（法）马若尔，（捷、德、塞、瑞典）马约尔（人名）
杰马勒（地名）

e.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has. (某人、某团体拥有的)

ex.en: The Russian Federation has issued a decree abolishing special privileges for government officials.
ex.zh: 俄罗斯联邦已颁布了一条取消政府官员特权的法令。

e.en: If you talk about privilege, you are talking about the power and advantage that only a small group of people have, usually because of their wealth or their connections with powerful people. (一小部分人因其财富或与有权人的关系而拥有的)

ex.en: Pironi was the son of privilege and wealth, and it showed.
ex.zh: 皮罗尼是富贵人家的子弟，这一点明摆着。

e.en: You can use privilege in expressions such as be a privilege or have the privilege when you want to show your appreciation of someone or something, or to show your respect.

ex.en: It must be a privilege to know such a man.
ex.zh: 认识这样一个人必是一种荣幸。

d: n. 特权，特殊待遇；荣幸，光荣；（富人或上层阶级的）权势；（律师、医生及其他专业人士的）保密权；言行免责权（尤指议员的权利）；（授予个人，公司，某地的）特许经营权；（生活）优越
v.  给予特权，特别优待；特免，免除（某人）

e.en: Regional is used to describe things which relate to a particular area of a country or of the world.

ex.en: The Garden's menu is based on Hawaiian regional cuisine.
ex.zh: 花园饭店的菜肴以夏威夷地区的烹饪风格为基础。

d: adj. 地区的，区域的；（与）首都以外各地（有关）的
n. （邮票、报纸等）地方版；地区性体育竞赛
n. 国有化（将私有企业、产业或资产收归国家所有，由国家接管或控制的行动或过程）

e.en: If you report something that has happened, you tell people about it. 报告;

ex.en: I reported the theft to the police.
ex.zh: 我向警察报告了这起盗窃案。

ex.en: The officials also reported that two more ships were apparently heading for Malta.
ex.zh: 官员们也报告说另有两艘船显然正朝马耳他驶去。

e.en: If you report on an event or subject, you tell people about it, because it is your job or duty to do so. 报道; (工作或职责上)

ex.en: Many journalists based outside of Sudan have been refused visas to enter the country to report on political affairs.
ex.zh: 很多驻在苏丹境外的记者遭到拒签，无法进入该国报道政治事件。

e.en: A report is a news article or broadcast which gives information about something that has just happened. (报刊或广播电视上的)

ex.en: According to a report in the newspaper, he still has control over the remaining shares.
ex.zh: 根据报纸上的报道，他依然控制着剩余的股份。

e.en: A report is an official document which a group of people issue after investigating a situation or event. (调查)

ex.en: The education committee will today publish its report on the supply of teachers for the next decade.
ex.zh: 教育委员会今天将公布关于今后十年师资储备的报告。

d: n. 报告，报道；（统计、财务等）报表（report 的复数）
v. 报告，告知；报道；传达；记录；举报，告发；报到；向…汇报，受…领导，隶属（report 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Soviet is used to describe something that belonged or related to the former Soviet Union.

ex.en: ...the former Soviet empire.
ex.zh: ...前苏联帝国。

e.en: The Soviets were the people of the former Soviet Union.

ex.en: In 1957, the Soviets launched Sputnik 1 into outer space.
ex.zh: 前苏联于1957年发射了“伴侣1号”人造外星到了外太空。

e.en: A soviet was an elected local, regional, or national council in the former Soviet Union. (前苏联地方、区域或国家)

d: n. 苏维埃；苏联人民（Soviets/the Soviets）；（1917年前俄国工人、农民组成）地方革命委员会
adj. 苏联的，苏联人民的（Soviet）

e.en: A spark is a tiny bright piece of burning material that flies up from something that is burning.

ex.en: The fire gradually got bigger and bigger. Sparks flew off in all directions.
ex.zh: 火势逐渐变得越来越大。火花四处飞溅。

e.en: A spark is a flash of light caused by electricity. It often makes a loud sound.

ex.en: He passed an electric spark through a mixture of gases.
ex.zh: 他使一束电火花穿过一团气体混合物。

e.en: If something sparks, sparks of fire or light come from it.

ex.en: The wires were sparking above me.
ex.zh: 电线正在我头顶上方冒火花。

e.en: If a burning object or electricity sparks a fire, it causes a fire. 引发 (一场火)

ex.en: A dropped cigarette may have sparked the fire.
ex.zh: 一支丢弃的香烟可能引发了这场火灾。

d: n. 发火花；点火
v. 发出火星，冒火花；导致，引发，触发；激发（兴趣等），使大感兴趣

e.en: You can refer to a narrow strip of sea which joins two large areas of sea as a strait or the straits.

ex.en: An estimated 1,600 vessels pass through the strait annually.
ex.zh: 估计每年有1600艘船经过这个海峡。

e.en: If someone is in dire or desperate straits, they are in a very difficult situation, usually because they do not have much money. (常指缺钱造成的)

ex.en: The company's closure has left many small businessmen in desperate financial straits.
ex.zh: 该公司的关闭使得许多小商人陷入经济困境。

d: n. 海峡，狭窄水道；（尤指财务问题导致的）窘境，困境（straits）
adj. 严格的，精确的；（地方）空间有限的，狭窄的；苦恼的
adv. 严格地，精确地
【名】 （Strait）（美）斯特雷特（人名）
adj. 更宽的，更广阔的，更广泛的（wide 的比较级）
n. （Wider）（德）维德（人名）

e.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists. 承认 (事实或情况)

ex.en: Naylor acknowledged, in a letter to the judge, that he was a drug addict.
ex.zh: 在一封写给法官的信中，内勒承认他是一个吸毒者。

ex.en: Belatedly, the government has acknowledged the problem.
ex.zh: 政府过晚地承认了这个问题。

e.en: If someone's achievements, status, or qualities are acknowledged, they are known about and recognized by a lot of people, or by a particular group of people. 认可 (某人的成就、地位或品质)

ex.en: He is also acknowledged as an excellent goalkeeper.
ex.zh: 他还被认可为一名优秀的守门员。

e.en: If you acknowledge a message or letter, you write to the person who sent it in order to say that you have received it.

ex.en: The army sent me a postcard acknowledging my request.
ex.zh: 军方寄给我一张明信片以确认收到了我的请求。

e.en: If you acknowledge someone, for example, by moving your head or smiling, you show that you have seen and recognized them. (点头或微笑)

ex.en: He saw her but refused to even acknowledge her.
ex.zh: 他看到了她，但甚至都拒绝向她致意。

d: adj. 公认的，被普遍认可的
v. （acknowledge 的过去式和过去分词）承认，认可；确认收到，告知已收到；向……致意，搭理；答谢，感谢
n. 安东尼（英语男子名）；安东尼（英语姓氏）

e.en: You can use arguably when you are stating your opinion or belief, as a way of giving more authority to it.

ex.en: They are arguably the most important band since The Rolling Stones.
ex.zh: 他们可以说是自滚石以来最重要的乐队。

d: adv. 可论证地，按理

e.en: A superpower is a very powerful and influential country, usually one that is rich and has nuclear weapons.

ex.en: The United States could claim to be both a military and an economic superpower.
ex.zh: 美国可以声称既是军事上也是经济上的一个超级大国。

d: n. 超级大国；超能力（superpower 的复数形式）；超级强权

e.en: A waterway is a canal, river, or narrow channel of sea which ships or boats can sail along.

ex.en: There are more than 400 miles of waterways to explore in the area.
ex.zh: 此地有400多英里的航道有待勘察。

d: n. 航道，水路，水道；水沟，排水沟
n. 暗杀，行刺

e.en: If you assume that something is true, you imagine that it is true, sometimes wrongly.

ex.en: It is a misconception to assume that the two continents are similar.
ex.zh: 假设这两块大陆类似是种错误概念。

ex.en: If mistakes occurred, they were assumed to be the fault of the commander on the spot.
ex.zh: 如果出现了错误，它们就被以为是现场指挥官的错。

e.en: If someone assumes power or responsibility, they take power or responsibility. 接受 (权利、责任)

ex.en: Mr. Cross will assume the role of CEO with a team of four directors.
ex.zh: 克罗斯先生将担任由４位执行官组成的一个团队的首席执行官一职。

e.en: If you assume a particular expression or way of behaving, you start to look or behave in this way. 做出 (某表情); 采取 (某行为方式)

ex.en: He managed to assume an air of calm.
ex.zh: 他设法表现出一幅平静的样子。

d: adj.  假定的，假设的；篡夺的
v. 假定，假设，认为；装出，作出；承担，就职（assume 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If you bear something somewhere, you carry it there or take it there.

ex.en: They bore the oblong hardwood box into the kitchen and put it on the table.
ex.zh: 他们把那个长方形的硬木箱抬进了厨房，放在了餐桌上。

e.en: If you bear something such as a weapon, you hold it or carry it with you.

ex.en: ...the constitutional right to bear arms.
ex.zh: …携带武器的宪法权。

e.en: If one thing bears the weight of something else, it supports the weight of that thing. 承受;

ex.en: The ice was not thick enough to bear the weight of marching men.
ex.zh: 冰的厚度不足以支撑行军队伍的重量。

e.en: If something bears a particular mark or characteristic, it has that mark or characteristic. 带有 (标记或特征)

ex.en: The houses bear the marks of bullet holes and the streets are practically deserted.
ex.zh: 房屋带有子弹的痕迹，街道几乎是被废弃了。

ex.en: ...notepaper bearing the presidential seal.
ex.zh: …盖有总统印章的信笺。

d: v. 手持，携带；（车，船）运输，运送；写有，刻有；以（姓名，头衔）相称；见证，作证；承担，担负（责任）；经得起；承受，容忍；生育（孩子）；（树，植物）结（果实），长出（花）；拐弯
n. 熊；粗暴无礼的人，没教养的人；体格笨重的男人，行动迟缓的男人；（股票）卖空者，做空头者；麻烦事，棘手之事；“北极熊”（俄国的外号）
【名】 （Bear）（美）贝尔（人名）

e.en: If you balance something somewhere, or if it balances there, it remains steady and does not fall. 使平衡;

ex.en: I balanced on the ledge.
ex.zh: 我在岩脊上站稳。

e.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up.

ex.en: The medicines you are currently taking could be affecting your balance.
ex.zh: 你现在吃的药可能会影响你的平衡能力。

e.en: If you balance one thing with something different, each of the things has the same strength or importance.

ex.en: Balance spicy dishes with mild ones.
ex.zh: 使辛辣的菜和清淡的菜均衡。

ex.en: The government has to find some way to balance these two needs.
ex.zh: 政府得找到某种方法来平衡这两种需求。

e.en: 均衡的

ex.en: This book is a well balanced biography.
ex.zh: 这是一本很公正的传记。

d: n. 平衡，均衡，均势；平衡能力；账户余额，结存；结欠，余款；天平，秤；（乐器）平衡器
v. 保持平衡；权衡，斟酌；使收支平衡；均衡，抵消
【名】  (Balance) （西）巴兰赛（人名）

e.en: If something has a bearing on a situation or event, it is relevant to it.

ex.en: Experts generally agree that diet has an important bearing on your general health.
ex.zh: 专家们普遍认可饮食与你的总体健康有着重要关系。

e.en: Someone's bearing is the way in which they move or stand.

ex.en: She later wrote warmly of his bearing and behaviour.
ex.zh: 稍后她热情地写到了他的风度与举止。

e.en: If you get your bearings or find your bearings, you find out where you are or what you should do next. If you lose your bearings, you do not know where you are or what you should do next.

ex.en: A sightseeing tour of the city is included to help you get your bearings.
ex.zh: 城市观光游包括在内，以帮助你们弄清方向。

d: n. 举止，仪态；与……有关，对……有影响；（对坏事的）宽容，容忍；轴承，支轴；方位，方向角；（用罗盘）定向，测位；（盾形纹章面上的）图案
v. 写有，刻有；手持，携带；承担（bear 的现在分词形式）
n. 阿斯旺（埃及一城市）
n. 本杰明（男子名）；受宠爱的幼子

e.en: Chose is the past tense of . (choose)
an article of personal property

d: v. 选择，挑选（choose 的过去式）
n. （法律）物体，动产；（Chose）（法）肖兹（人名）

e.en: Calculus is a branch of advanced mathematics which deals with variable quantities.

d: n. 微积分；（数，逻）演算（法），计算（法）；（医）（尤指肾或胆囊的）结石，石

e.en: A coin is a small piece of metal which is used as money.

ex.en: ...a few loose coins.
ex.zh: …几枚零钱。

e.en: If you coin a word or a phrase, you are the first person to say it. 创造 (新词语)

ex.en: Jaron Lanier coined the term "virtual reality" and pioneered its early development.
ex.zh: 加隆·雷尼尔首创“虚拟现实”一词，并率先进行早期开发。

e.en: You say "to coin a phrase" to show that you realize you are making a pun or using a cliché. 套用一个双关语;

ex.en: Fifty local musicians have, to coin a phrase, banded together to form the Jazz Umbrella.
ex.zh: 套用一句老话，５０位当地的音乐家们联合在一起组成了爵士伞乐队。

e.en: You use the other side of the coin to mention a different aspect of a situation.

ex.en: On the other side of the coin, there'll be tax incentives for small businesses.
ex.zh: 另一方面，会有税收政策激励小型经营者。

d: v. 创造（新词等）；铸造（硬币）（coin 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The benefit of something is the help that you get from it or the advantage that results from it. 益处;

ex.en: Each family farms individually and reaps the benefit of its labour.
ex.zh: 每个家庭独立耕作，收获各自的劳动成果。

ex.en: I'm a great believer in the benefits of this form of therapy.
ex.zh: 我对这种疗法的益处深信不疑。

e.en: If something is to your benefit or is of benefit to you, it helps you or improves your life.

ex.en: This could now work to Albania's benefit.
ex.zh: 这可能现在对阿尔巴尼亚有利。

e.en: If you benefit from something or if it benefits you, it helps you or improves your life. 有益于;

ex.en: Both sides have benefited from the talks.
ex.zh: 双方都从会谈中获益。

e.en: If you have the benefit of some information, knowledge, or equipment, you are able to use it so that you can achieve something.

ex.en: Steve didn't have the benefit of a formal college education.
ex.zh: 史蒂夫没有接受过正规大学教育的优势。

d: v. 受益（benefit 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 受益的

e.en: Communications are the systems and processes that are used to communicate or broadcast information, especially by means of electricity or radio waves.

ex.en: ...a communications satellite.
ex.zh: …一颗通信卫星。

e.en: A communication is a message.

ex.en: The ambassador has brought with him a communication from the president.
ex.zh: 该大使从总统那里带来了一则信息。

d: n. 表达，交流，交际；信息，书信，电话；通讯，交通联系；传播学

e.en: A conduit is a small tunnel, pipe, or channel through which water or electrical wires go. 导管;
A conduit is a person or country that links two or more other people or countries. 渠道;

ex.en: Pakistan became a conduit for drugs produced in Afghanistan.
ex.zh: 巴基斯坦成了阿富汗制造的毒品的贩运通道。

d: n. （水或电线的）管道，导管；渠道，通道；（保护线路的）导线管，电缆沟

e.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

ex.en: We are doing this work in the context of reforms in the economic, social and cultural spheres.
ex.zh: 我们正在经济、社会和文化领域改革的背景下从事这项工作。

ex.en: It helps to understand the historical context in which Chaucer wrote.
ex.zh: 这有助于理解乔叟创作时的历史背景。

e.en: The context of a word, sentence, or text consists of the words, sentences, or text before and after it which help to make its meaning clear.

ex.en: Without a context, I would have assumed it was written by a man.
ex.zh: 如果没有一个语境，我会以为这是由一个男人写的。

e.en: If something is seen in context or if it is put into context, it is considered together with all the factors that relate to it.

ex.en: Taxation is not popular in principle, merely acceptable in context.
ex.zh: 征税原则上不受大众欢迎，只是联系背景看是可接受的。

e.en: If a statement or remark is quoted out of context, the circumstances in which it was said are not correctly reported, so that it seems to mean something different from the meaning that was intended.

ex.en: Thomas says that he has been quoted out of context.
ex.zh: 托马斯说，他的话被断章取义了。

d: n. 背景，环境；上下文，语境

e.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

ex.en: Natural disasters have obviously contributed to the continent's economic crisis.
ex.zh: 自然灾害显然促使了该大陆的经济危机。

ex.en: ...someone to turn to in moments of crisis.
ex.zh: …在危机时刻可以向其求助的人。

d: n. （crisis 的复数形式）危机，紧要关头；危险期，转折点；（医学）危象

e.en: The connotations of a particular word or name are the ideas or qualities which it makes you think of.

ex.en: It's just one of those words that's got so many negative connotations.
ex.zh: 它只是那些有很多负面内涵意义的词之一。

d: n. 内涵，含蓄，隐含意义（connotation 的复数）；（逻辑学/语义学）内涵（与“外延”相对）

e.en: The money used in a particular country is referred to as its currency.

ex.en: Tourism is the country's top earner of foreign currency.
ex.zh: 旅游业是该国外汇收入最高的行业。

ex.en: More people favour a single European currency than oppose it.
ex.zh: 支持欧洲单一货币的人比反对的多。

d: n. 通货，货币；通用，流行；现时性

e.en: If you contribute to something, you say or do things to help to make it successful. 贡献;

ex.en: The three sons also contribute to the family business.
ex.zh: 3个儿子也为家族企业做贡献。

ex.en: I believe that each of us can contribute to the future of the world.
ex.zh: 我相信我们每一个人都能为世界的未来做出贡献。

e.en: To contribute money or resources to something means to give money or resources to help pay for something or to help achieve a particular purpose.

ex.en: The U.S. is contributing $4 billion in loans, credits, and grants.
ex.zh: 美国以信贷和赠与的方式捐助了40亿美元。

ex.en: Local businesses have agreed to contribute.
ex.zh: 当地的公司已经同意捐助了。

e.en: 捐助者

ex.en: Candidates for Congress received 53 percent of their funds from individual contributors.
ex.zh: 国会候选人接受的捐款中有53%来自个人捐助者。

e.en: If something contributes to an event or situation, it is one of the causes of it. 是 (造成某情况)

ex.en: The report says design faults in both the vessels contributed to the tragedy.
ex.zh: 报道称两艘船在设计上的缺陷是造成悲剧的原因。

d: v. 捐赠，捐助；（为……）做贡献；促成，是……的原因之一；撰稿，投稿；提供（报道）（contribute 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. （会计/金融）已缴入的，实缴的

e.en: A dam is a wall that is built across a river in order to stop the water from flowing and to make a lake.

ex.en: Before the dam was built, Campbell River used to flood in the spring.
ex.zh: 大坝建好之前，坎贝尔河常在春季发大水。

e.en: a reservoir of water created by such a barrier
to obstruct or restrict by or as if by a dam
decametre(s)

d: n. 堤，坝；母兽，母畜；水库；（牙科手术中的）橡皮障
v. （在河上）筑坝；阻止，抑制
【名】 （Dam）（美）丹（人名）

e.en: If something is clearly defined or strongly defined, its outline is clear or strong.

ex.en: A clearly defined track now leads down to the valley.
ex.zh: 如今一条轮廓清晰的小径通向峡谷。

d: adj. 轮廓分明的，外形清晰的
vt. 给……下定义，解释；阐明，使清楚；标明……界限，明确显出……轮廓（define 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Your dependence on something or someone is your need for them in order to succeed or be able to survive.

ex.en: ...the city's traditional dependence on tourism.
ex.zh: …这个城市对旅游业的传统依赖。

e.en: If you talk about drug dependence or alcohol dependence, you are referring to a situation where someone is addicted to drugs or is an alcoholic. (毒、酒)

ex.en: French doctors tend to regard drug dependence as a form of deep-rooted psychological disorder.
ex.zh: 法国医生倾向于将毒瘾看作是一种根深蒂固的心理疾病。

e.en: You talk about the dependence of one thing on another when the first thing will be affected or determined by the second.

ex.en: ...the dependence of politicians on rich donors to fund their increasingly expensive campaigns.
ex.zh: …政客们为资助他们日益昂贵的竞选活动而对富有的捐赠人的依赖。

d: n. 依赖，依靠；（对毒品或酒精的）瘾，癖

e.en: A dictator is a ruler who has complete power in a country, especially power which was obtained by force and is used unfairly or cruelly.

ex.en: ...foreign dictators who contravene humanitarian conventions.
ex.zh: …违反人道主义公约的外国独裁者们。

d: n. 独裁者；专横的人

e.en: A difficulty is a problem.

ex.en: ...the difficulty of getting accurate information.
ex.zh: …获得准确信息的困难。

e.en: If you have difficulty doing something, you are not able to do it easily.

ex.en: Do you have difficulty getting up?
ex.zh: 你起床有困难吗？

e.en: If someone or something is in difficulty, they are having a lot of problems.

ex.en: The city's film industry is in difficulty.
ex.zh: 该市的电影业举步维艰。

d: n. 困难，磨难（difficulty 的复数）；困境，财务困难（常用于 in difficulties、financial difficulties 等搭配）

e.en: If someone or something disrupts an event, system, or process, they cause difficulties that prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way. 妨碍;

ex.en: Anti-war protesters disrupted the debate.
ex.zh: 反战示威者们扰乱了辩论。

d: v. 中断，扰乱；彻底改变（某物）的结构，使（某物）的结构破裂；使瓦解，使分裂

e.en: The dominance of a particular person or thing is the fact that they are more powerful, successful, or important than other people or things. 优势;

ex.en: The latest fighting appears to be an attempt by each group to establish dominance over the other.
ex.zh: 最近的战斗似乎是冲突各方在试图争夺控制权。

d: n. 优势，支配地位

e.en: If someone condones behaviour that is morally wrong, they accept it and allow it to happen.

ex.en: I have never encouraged nor condoned violence.
ex.zh: 我从来没有鼓励或纵容过暴力行为。

d: v. condone 的现在分词/动名词：宽恕，饶恕；纵容，包容，容忍；（勉强地）同意，批准

e.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

ex.en: ...a change which would maintain his party's dominant position in Scotland.
ex.zh: …巩固他的政党在苏格兰支配地位的一场变革。

d: adj. 占支配地位的，占优势的；（基因）显性的
n. 显性（性状），显性基因

e.en: Drawn is the past participle of draw. (draw)
If someone or their face looks drawn, their face is thin and they look very tired, ill, worried, or unhappy.

ex.en: She looked drawn and tired when she turned toward me.
ex.zh: 她转向我时，看上去既憔悴又疲惫。

d: adj. （因身体不适、疲倦或忧虑）憔悴的，苍白的
v. 画，绘制；拖，拉；拔出；排出（液体）（draw 的过去分词）
n. 德怀特（男子名）

e.en: You use easily to emphasize that something is very likely to happen, or is very likely to be true.

ex.en: It could easily be another year before the economy starts to show some improvement.
ex.zh: 很可能再过一年经济才会开始有所好转。

e.en: You use easily to say that something happens more quickly or more often than is usual or normal.

ex.en: He had always cried very easily.
ex.zh: 他总是动不动就哭。

d: adv. 容易地；很可能，多半；无疑；轻松自如地；更快，更经常

e.en: An echo is a sound caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

ex.en: He listened and heard nothing but the echoes of his own voice in the cave.
ex.zh: 他听了听，除了自己声音在山洞里的回响什么都没听见。

e.en: If a sound echoes, it is reflected off a surface and can be heard again after the original sound has stopped.

ex.en: His feet echoed on the hardwood floor.
ex.zh: 他的脚步声在硬木地板上回响着。

e.en: In a place that echoes, a sound is reflected off a surface, and is repeated after the original sound has stopped.

ex.en: The room echoed.
ex.zh: 房间发出了回声。

ex.en: The corridor echoed with the barking of a dozen dogs.
ex.zh: 走廊里回荡着十几条狗的吠声。

e.en: If you echo someone's words, you repeat them or express agreement with their attitude or opinion.

ex.en: Their views often echo each other.
ex.zh: 他们的见解常常彼此附和。

d: n. （echo 的复数）回声，回响，回波；重复，附和，共鸣；相似之处，再现
v. （echo 的第三人称单数）回响，发出回声，回荡；重复，附和；呼应，再现，反映

e.en: the garden in which Adam and Eve were placed at the Creation 伊甸园 (Also called Garden of Eden)

d: n. 伊甸园（《圣经》中亚当和夏娃最初居住的地方）；乐园，乐土
n. 艾森豪威尔（美国第三十四任总统）

e.en: An economist is a person who studies, teaches, or writes about economics.

d: n. 经济学者，经济学家（economist 的复数形式）

e.en: An epic is a long book, poem, or film whose story extends over a long period of time or tells of great events. 史诗;

ex.en: ...the Middle High German epic, "Nibelungenlied," written about 1200.
ex.zh: …大约写于1200年的中古高地德语史诗《尼贝龙根之歌》。

e.en: Epic is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...epic narrative poems.
ex.zh: …那些史诗般的叙事诗。

e.en: Something that is epic is very large and impressive. 伟大的;

ex.en: ...Columbus's epic voyage of discovery.
ex.zh: …哥伦布的伟大发现之旅。

d: n. （讲述英雄冒险经历的）叙事诗，史诗；史诗般的书籍（或电影等）；壮举，惊人之举；特别耗时费力的事（或活动）
adj. 史诗般的；漫长而艰难的；宏大的，壮丽的

e.en: Existential means relating to human existence and experience.

ex.en: Existential questions requiring religious answers still persist.
ex.zh: 需要宗教解答的生命问题持续存在着。

e.en: You use existential to describe fear, anxiety, and other feelings that are caused by thinking about human existence and death. 因思考人类存亡而引起的(恐惧、忧虑等感觉)

ex.en: "What if there's nothing left at all?" he cried, lost in some intense existential angst.
ex.zh: “要是什么都没了会怎样？”他大叫起来，迷失在某种强烈的攸关人类存亡的痛苦中。

d: adj. 有关存在的，关乎人类存在与生存的；存在主义的；（逻辑学）存在判断的，涉及存在量化的；（语言学）存在句的，表示存在的

e.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be. (价格、费用)

ex.en: Exorbitant housing prices have created an acute shortage of affordable housing for the poor.
ex.zh: 过高的房价使穷人负担得起的房源严重短缺。

d: adj. （价格、要求等）过分的，离谱的

e.en: If you define something, you show, describe, or state clearly what it is and what its limits are, or what it is like. 给…下定义;

ex.en: The Convention Against Torture defines torture as any act that inflicts severe pain or suffering, physical or mental.
ex.zh: 《反酷刑条约》把酷刑定义为任何造成严重身心疼痛和受苦的行为。

d: v. 定义（常与 as 连用）；规定；详述；表明…的特征（define 的第三人称单数现在时形式）

e.en: When someone finances something such as a project or a purchase, they provide the money that is needed to pay for them.

ex.en: The fund has been used largely to finance the construction of federal prisons.
ex.zh: 该基金大部分已用于资助联邦监狱的建造。

e.en: Finance is also a noun.

ex.en: A United States delegation is in Japan seeking finance for a major scientific project.
ex.zh: 1个美国代表团正在日本为一个重大科研项目寻求资助。

e.en: Finance is the commercial or government activity of managing money, debt, credit, and investment. 金融;

ex.en: ...a major player in the world of high finance.
ex.zh: …高层金融界的大腕。

ex.en: The report recommends an overhaul of public finances.
ex.zh: 这份报告建议对公共财政进行彻底检视。

e.en: You can refer to the amount of money that you have and how well it is organized as your finances.

ex.en: Be prepared for unexpected news concerning your finances.
ex.zh: 对关于你财务状况的意外消息要做好准备。

d: n. 融资，筹资，资金筹措；融资款项，筹集到的资金
v. 为…提供资金，资助，筹措资金（finance 的现在分词或动名词）

e.en: Menopause is the time during which a woman gradually stops menstruating, usually when she is about fifty years old. (女性的)

ex.en: ...alternative therapies to fight the symptoms of menopause.
ex.zh: …对抗更年期症状的替代疗法。

e.en: 更年期的

ex.en: A menopausal woman of average build and height requires 1600 – 2400 calories daily.
ex.zh: 一位一般体形和身高的更年期女性每天需要1600–2400卡的热量。

d: n. （女性的）绝经；绝经期；更年期；活动终止期

e.en: Sought is the past tense and past participle of . (seek)

d: v. 寻找；寻求；谋求；试图，设法（seek 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被寻找的；广受欢迎的（常与 after 连用，即 sought-after）

e.en: A memo is a short official note that is sent by one person to another within the same company or organization.

ex.en: He sent out a memo expressing his disagreement with their decisions.
ex.zh: 他发出一份简报表达他对他们的决定的不赞同。

d: n. 备忘录
【名】 （Memo）（土、意）梅莫（人名）

e.en: The staff of an organization are the people who work for it.

ex.en: The staff were very good.
ex.zh: 员工们都很棒。

ex.en: The outpatient programme has a staff of six people.
ex.zh: 这个门诊部有6名员工。

e.en: People who are part of a particular staff are often referred to as staff.

ex.en: 10 staff were allocated to the task.
ex.zh: 10名员工被分派做这项任务。

e.en: If an organization is staffed by particular people, they are the people who work for it. 担当 (某机构的)

ex.en: They are staffed by volunteers.
ex.zh: 他们的员工都是志愿者。

e.en: 配备了职员的

ex.en: The house allocated to them was pleasant and spacious, and well staffed.
ex.zh: 分给他们的房子既舒适又宽敞，员工也配备良好。

d: n. 全体员工，全体雇员；（大、中、小学的）管理人员，行政人员；（军队的）全体参谋人员；陆军上士；手杖，拐杖；权杖，笏；旗杆；（测绘）标杆，标尺；（钟表的）小轴杆；（铁路的）路签；五线谱
adj. 职员的
v. 为……配备员工；是……的职员
【名】 （Staff）（德、匈）施塔夫，（瑞典、英）斯塔夫（人名）

e.en: If you require something or if something is required, you need it or it is necessary.

ex.en: If you require further information, you should consult the registrar.
ex.zh: 如果你需要进一步的信息，你应该向注册主任咨询。

ex.en: This isn't the kind of crisis that requires us to drop everything else.
ex.zh: 这不是需要我们抛下其他一切的那种危机。

e.en: If a law or rule requires you to do something, you have to do it.

ex.en: The rules also require employers to provide safety training.
ex.zh: 这些规定也要求雇主们提供安全训练。

ex.en: At least 35 manufacturers have flouted a law requiring prompt reporting of such malfunctions.
ex.zh: 至少有三十五位制造商已经对要求即刻汇报这类故障的规定嗤之以鼻了。

d: adj. 必需的，规定的；理想的
v. 需要；要求做（某事），规定（require 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Stocks are shares in the ownership of a company, or investments on which a fixed amount of interest will be paid. 股票;

ex.en: ...the buying and selling of stocks and shares.
ex.zh: …证券和股票的买卖。

e.en: A company's stock is the amount of money which the company has through selling shares. (公司的)

ex.en: Two years later, when Compaq went public, their stock was valued at $38 million.
ex.zh: 两年后康柏公司上市时，他们的股票价值为3800万美元。

e.en: If a shop stocks particular products, it keeps a supply of them to sell.

ex.en: The shop stocks everything from cigarettes to recycled paper.
ex.zh: 该商店的存货包括香烟和再生纸等各种商品。

e.en: A shop's stock is the total amount of goods which it has available to sell.

ex.en: When a nearby shop burned down, our stock was ruined by smoke.
ex.zh: 附近一家商店被烧成灰烬，我们的存货也被浓烟熏坏了。

d: n. 现货，存货；储备物，备用物；股本，资本；股份，股票；公债，公债券；家畜，牲畜；种族，家系；高汤，原汤；手足枷（stocks）；柄，枪托；名声，声望；紫罗兰；接穗，砧木；根茎，根状茎；保留剧目轮演剧团；信任，相信；铁路上使用的所有车辆；（胶卷）原片；发剩下的牌；（商品的）原材料；锚杆；主轴台，主轴箱（headstock 的简写）；尾架，尾座（tailstock 的简写）；白色领结，白色领带；（牧师衣领下系的）黑色领带；船台（stocks）
v. 备有，存有；摆满，供应；为（枪等火器）装枪托；出新芽
adj. 老一套的，陈腐的；（商店）库存的，常备的；（有关）电影资料镜头的
【名】 （Stock）（德、匈、捷）施托克，（英、法、葡、瑞典）斯托克（人名）

e.en: A symptom of an illness is something wrong with your body or mind that is a sign of the illness.

ex.en: One of the most common symptoms of schizophrenia is hearing imaginary voices.
ex.zh: 精神分裂症最常见的症状之一是幻听。

ex.en: ...patients with flu symptoms.
ex.zh: …有流感症状的病人。

e.en: A symptom of a bad situation is something that happens which is considered to be a sign of this situation.

ex.en: Your problem with keeping boyfriends is just a symptom of a larger problem: making and keeping friends.
ex.zh: 你无法留住男友的问题只是一个更大的问题的征兆：结交朋友并与其维持关系。

d: n. 症状；症候；病征（symptom 的复数）；征兆，迹象（引申指问题或不良状况的标志）

e.en: If something is unclear, it is not known or not certain. 未知的;

ex.en: It is unclear how much popular support they have among the island's population.
ex.zh: 不知道他们在该岛居民中有多少民众支持。

ex.en: Just what the soldier was doing there is unclear.
ex.zh: 那个士兵在那儿到底在干什么不得而知。

e.en: If you are unclear about something, you do not understand it well or are not sure about it. 不明白的;

ex.en: He is still unclear about his own future.
ex.zh: 他对自己的未来仍不清楚。

d: adj. （指事实、原因等）不清楚的、不确定的、不易了解的；（指人）对……不清楚的、不明白的

e.en: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.

ex.en: Money will also go into local development projects in Vietnam.
ex.zh: 资金也会流入越南本地开发项目。

ex.en: ...an international science project.
ex.zh: …一个国际科研项目。

e.en: A project is a detailed study of a subject by a student. (学生研究的)

ex.en: Students complete projects for a personal tutor, working at home at their own pace.
ex.zh: 学生们为个人导师完成课题研究，在家里按自己的速度工作。

e.en: If something is projected, it is planned or expected. 计划;

ex.en: 13% of Americans are over 65; this number is projected to reach 22% by the year 2030.
ex.zh: 13%的美国人在65岁以上；这个数字预计到2030年会达到22%。

ex.en: The government had been projecting a 5% consumer price increase for the entire year.
ex.zh: 政府一直在预计全年5%的消费价格增长。

e.en: If you project someone or something in a particular way, you try to make people see them in that way. If you project a particular feeling or quality, you show it in your behaviour. (以某方式)

ex.en: Bradley projects a natural warmth and sincerity.
ex.zh: 布拉德利表现出一种自然的热情和真诚。

ex.en: He just hasn't been able to project himself as the strong leader.
ex.zh: 他只是还没能把自己表现得是个强有力的领导。

d: n. （project 的复数）项目，计划，工程；（学校的）课题，研究项目；政府出资建造的低收入住宅区（常作 the projects 或 housing projects）
v. （project 的第三人称单数）预计，推算；计划，规划；投射，投映；表现；传达；伸出，突出

e.en: If you tie two things together or tie them, you fasten them together with a knot. 系;

ex.en: He tied the ends of the plastic bag together.
ex.zh: 他把塑料袋的两头系在一起。

e.en: If you tie something or someone in a particular place or position, you put them there and fasten them using rope or string. (用绳索) 捆绑;

ex.en: He had tied the dog to one of the trees near the canal.
ex.zh: 他已经把狗拴在运河边的一棵树上。

e.en: If you tie a piece of string or cloth around something or tie something with a piece of string or cloth, you put the piece of string or cloth around it and fasten the ends together. (用绳子或布条)

ex.en: She tied her scarf over her head.
ex.zh: 她把围巾围在头上。

ex.en: Roll the meat and tie it with string.
ex.zh: 把肉卷起来用线捆好。

e.en: If you tie a knot or bow in something or tie something in a knot or bow, you fasten the ends together. 打 (结); 把…打成 (结)

ex.en: He took a short length of rope and swiftly tied a slip knot.
ex.zh: 他拿了一小段绳子迅速打了个活结。

ex.en: She tied a knot in a cherry stem.
ex.zh: 她在樱桃梗上打了个结。

d: n. （tie 的复数）关系，联系，纽带（常用复数）；领带；结；（体育/竞赛）平局，平分；扎带，束线带（常用于 cable ties）
v. （tie 的第三人称单数）系，绑，捆扎；连接，联系；（体育/竞赛）打成平局

e.en: If you add one thing to another, you put it in or on the other thing, to increase, complete, or improve it.

ex.en: Add the grated cheese to the sauce.
ex.zh: 把磨碎的奶酪加进那种酱中。

ex.en: Since 1908, chlorine has been added to drinking water.
ex.zh: 自从1908年起，氯就被添加到饮用水当中了。

e.en: If you add numbers or amounts together, you calculate their total.

ex.en: Banks add all the interest and other charges together.
ex.zh: 银行把所有利息和其他费用加在一起。

e.en: If one thing adds to another, it makes the other thing greater in degree or amount.

ex.en: This latest incident will add to the pressure on the White House.
ex.zh: 最近的这起事件会给白宫增加更多的压力。

e.en: To add a particular quality to something means to cause it to have that quality. 增添 (某种特性)

ex.en: The generous amount of garlic adds flavour.
ex.zh: 大量的蒜会增添滋味。

d: v. 添加，掺入；（使）相加，加；增加；增添（某种特性）；把……计算在内，包括；补充说，继续说
abbr. 注意力缺陷障碍，多动症（ADD）

e.en: Administrative work involves organizing and supervising an organization or institution. 行政的;

ex.en: Other industries have had to sack managers to reduce administrative costs.
ex.zh: 其他行业已不得不解雇管理人员来减少管理成本。

d: adj. 管理的，行政的

e.en: If something adorns a place or an object, it makes it look more beautiful.

ex.en: His watercolour designs adorn a wide range of books.
ex.zh: 他的水彩设计装饰着各种各样的书籍。

d: adj. 被装饰的，装饰过的，被修饰的
v. adorn 的过去式和过去分词（用于完成时或被动语态）

e.en: Something that is alarming makes you feel afraid or anxious that something unpleasant or dangerous might happen.

ex.en: The disease has spread at an alarming rate.
ex.zh: 这种疾病已经以惊人的速度传播开来。

e.en: 令人惊恐地

ex.en: ...the alarmingly high rate of heart disease.
ex.zh: …高得惊人的心脏病发病率。

d: adj. 令人担忧的，令人恐惧的
v. 使不安，使恐慌；给（门等）安装警报器（alarm 的现在分词）

e.en: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard, but you are not certain that it is true.

ex.en: Apparently the girls are not at all amused by the whole business.
ex.zh: 据说这些女孩们完全不觉得这整件事好笑。

e.en: You use apparently to refer to something that seems to be true, although you are not sure whether it is or not.

ex.en: The recent deterioration has been caused by an apparently endless recession.
ex.zh: 最近的恶化是由貌似没完没了的萧条造成的。

d: adv. 据说，显然；似乎，好像
n. 巴拉克（男子名）

e.en: Something that is beneficial helps people or improves their lives.

ex.en: ...vitamins that are beneficial to our health.
ex.zh: …有益我们健康的维生素。

d: adj. 有益的，有利的；（与）权益（有关）的，有财产使用权的

e.en: A bureaucracy is an administrative system operated by a large number of officials.

ex.en: State bureaucracies can tend to stifle enterprise and initiative.
ex.zh: 国家官僚体制会压抑人的进取心和积极性。

e.en: Bureaucracy refers to all the rules and procedures followed by government departments and similar organizations, especially when you think that these are complicated and cause long delays.

ex.en: People usually complain about too much bureaucracy.
ex.zh: 人们通常会抱怨过多的官僚作风。

d: n. 官僚制度，官僚机构，官僚作风；官僚，政府官员

e.en: If you aim for something or aim to do something, you plan or hope to achieve it.

ex.en: He said he would aim for the 100 metre world record at the world championships in August.
ex.zh: 他说他将以在8月举行的世界锦标赛上打破100米世界纪录为目标。

ex.en: Businesses will have to aim at long-term growth.
ex.zh: 企业必须以长期增长为目标。

e.en: If you aim to do something, you decide or want to do it.

ex.en: I didn't aim to get caught.
ex.zh: 我并不想被抓到。

e.en: If your actions or remarks are aimed at a particular person or group, you intend that the person or group should notice them and be influenced by them.

ex.en: His message was aimed at the undecided middle ground of Israeli politics.
ex.zh: 他所传达的信息针对的是以色列政坛中尚未表态的中间派。

e.en: If you aim a weapon or object at something or someone, you point it toward them before firing or throwing it.

ex.en: When he appeared again, he was aiming the rifle at Wade.
ex.zh: 他再次出现时，他正将步枪瞄准维德。

ex.en: ...a missile aimed at the arms factory.
ex.zh: …一枚瞄准了军工厂的导弹。

d: v. aim 的现在分词/动名词：瞄准，对准；旨在，致力于；针对，指向。
n. （地理位置）中间，中心点；（机构，组织）活动中心；关注点，焦点；中间派，中间立场；中锋
v. 把……放在中央；（使）以……为中心，（使）注意力集中于；（使）主要发生在，（使）集中于
n. （Center）森特（人名）

e.en: holding or guaranteed by a certificate

d: adj. 有合格证书的，获得资格的；（经官方批准为）合格的，达到标准的；真正的，名副其实的；（经官方批准为）合格的，达到标准的；真正的，名副其实的
v. 证明，证实；给……颁发合格证书；证明（某人）患有精神病（certify 的过去分词）

e.en: A capitalist country or system supports or is based on the principles of capitalism.

ex.en: China has pledged to retain Hong Kong's capitalist system for 50 years.
ex.zh: 中国政府已保证维持香港的资本主义制度50年。

e.en: A capitalist is someone who believes in and supports the principles of capitalism. 资本主义者;

ex.en: Lenin had hoped to even have a working relationship with the capitalists.
ex.zh: 列宁甚至曾希望能与资本主义者建立合作关系。

e.en: A capitalist is someone who owns a business which they run in order to make a profit for themselves.

ex.en: They argue that only private capitalists can remake Poland's economy.
ex.zh: 他们争辩说只有个体资本家才能重振波兰的经济。

d: n. 资本主义者；资本家
adj. 资本主义的

e.en: If you comment on something, you give your opinion about it or you give an explanation for it. 评论;

ex.en: So far, Mr. Cook has not commented on these reports.
ex.zh: 到目前为止，库克先生还未对这些报告进行过评论。

ex.en: You really can't comment until you know the facts.
ex.zh: 你的确不能在你知道事实之前进行评论。

e.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it. 评论;

ex.en: He made his comments at a news conference in Amsterdam.
ex.zh: 他在阿姆斯特丹的一次记者招待会上做了评论。

ex.en: There's been no comment so far from police about the allegations.
ex.zh: 到目前为止还没有来自警方的对那些指控的任何解释。

e.en: People say "no comment" as a way of refusing to answer a question, usually when it is asked by a journalist.

ex.en: No comment. I don't know anything.
ex.zh: 无可奉告。我什么也不知道。

d: n. 评论，意见；批评，指责；说明，写照；解说，注释；（计算机）注解
v. 评论，发表意见；（计算机）注解，把（部分程序）转成注解
【名】 （Comment）（美、瑞、法）科门特（人名）

e.en: Compliance with something, for example a law, treaty, or agreement, means doing what you are required or expected to do.

ex.en: Inspectors were sent to visit nuclear sites and verify compliance with the treaty.
ex.zh: 监察员被派去参观核址并核实条约的遵守情况。

d: n. 服从，遵守；屈从，迁就；可塑性，柔量
n. 克林顿
v. 证明，证实；给……颁发合格证书；证明（某人）患有精神病；保证

e.en: If someone or something complies with an order or set of rules, they do what is required or expected.

ex.en: The commander said that the army would comply with the ceasefire.
ex.zh: 指挥官说过部队会遵从停火协议。

ex.en: Some beaches had failed to comply with environmental regulations.
ex.zh: 一些海滩没能遵守环保规定。

d: v. 遵从，服从；（商品）符合特定标准

e.en: Conflict is serious disagreement and argument about something important. If two people or groups are in conflict, they have had a serious disagreement or argument and have not yet reached agreement. 争执;

ex.en: Try to keep any conflict between you and your ex-partner to a minimum.
ex.zh: 尽量把你和前合伙人之间的争执控制到最少。

e.en: Conflict is a state of mind in which you find it impossible to make a decision.

ex.en: ...the anguish of his own inner conflict.
ex.zh: …他自己内心矛盾的痛苦。

e.en: Conflict is fighting between countries or groups of people. (国家或团体之间的)

ex.en: ...talks aimed at ending four decades of conflict.
ex.zh: …旨在结束40年冲突的会谈。

e.en: A conflict is a serious difference between two or more beliefs, ideas, or interests. If two beliefs, ideas, or interests are in conflict, they are very different. (信念、观点、利益之间的)

ex.en: There is a conflict between what they are doing and what you want.
ex.zh: 他们在做的和你想要的之间存在冲突。

d: n. 冲突，矛盾（conflict 的复数）
v. 冲突，抵触（conflict 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If someone or something complies with an order or set of rules, they do what is required or expected.

ex.en: The commander said that the army would comply with the ceasefire.
ex.zh: 指挥官说过部队会遵从停火协议。

ex.en: Some beaches had failed to comply with environmental regulations.
ex.zh: 一些海滩没能遵守环保规定。

d: v. 遵从，服从；遵守（规则、法律、要求等，常与 with 连用）；（商品、企业等）符合特定标准或规定；comply 的现在分词或动名词

e.en: The details of something are its individual features or elements.

ex.en: The details of the plan are still being worked out.
ex.zh: 计划的细节还在制定中。

ex.en: No details of the discussions have been given.
ex.zh: 会谈的细节尚未透露。

e.en: A detail is a minor point or aspect of something, as opposed to the central ones.

ex.en: Only minor details now remain to be settled.
ex.zh: 只有细枝末节还没确定。

e.en: Details about someone or something are facts or pieces of information about them.

ex.en: See the bottom of this page for details of how to apply for this exciting offer.
ex.zh: 关于如何申请这个令人激动的机会，详情请参看本页末。

e.en: You can refer to the small features of something which are often not noticed as detail.

ex.en: We like his attention to detail and his enthusiasm.
ex.zh: 我们喜欢他对细微之处的关注，以及他的热情。

d: n. 细节，细微之处；详情，资料；（军队中的）任务，特遣队
v. 详细说明，详述；彻底清洗（汽车）；（尤指军队中）派遣，选派

e.en: If something or someone connects one thing to another, or if one thing connects to another, or if two things connect, the two things are joined together. (某物、某人) 连接 (某物); (一物与另一物)

ex.en: You can connect the speakers to your CD player.
ex.zh: 你可以将这些扬声器与你的激光唱机连接起来。

ex.en: I connected the wires for the transformer.
ex.zh: 我给变压器接上了电线。

e.en: If two things or places connect or if something connects them, they are joined and people or things can pass between them. (两物或两地)

ex.en: ...the long hallway that connects the rooms.
ex.zh: …连接这些房间的长长的过道。

ex.en: A pedestrian bridge now connects the parking garage with the mall.
ex.zh: 现在一座人行桥连通车库和购物中心。

e.en: If one train or plane, for example, connects with another, it arrives at a time which allows passengers to change to the other one in order to continue their trip. (与火车、飞机等)

ex.en: ...a train connecting with a ferry to Ireland.
ex.zh: …一列与通往爱尔兰的渡船联运的火车。

e.en: If a piece of equipment or a place is connected to a source of power or water, it is joined to that source so that it has power or water. 将 (设备、某地与水源、电源等)

ex.en: These appliances should not be connected to power supplies.
ex.zh: 这些装置不应该接通电源。

d: v. （使）连接；（使）相通；使接通（电源、水源等）；与……有关系；把……联系起来；（火车、航班等）衔接，联运；与……建立联系，沟通（connect 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If a particular factor determines the nature of a thing or event, it causes it to be of a particular kind.

ex.en: The size of the chicken pieces will determine the cooking time.
ex.zh: 鸡块的大小决定烹饪时间。

e.en: 决定

ex.en: ...the gene which is responsible for male sex determination.
ex.zh: …决定男性性别的基因。

e.en: To determine a fact means to discover it as a result of investigation.

ex.en: The investigation will determine what really happened.
ex.zh: 该调查将查明真相。

ex.en: Experts say testing needs to be done on each contaminant to determine the long-term effects on humans.
ex.zh: 专家说需要对每种污染物进行测试，以查明对人类的长期影响。

e.en: If you determine something, you decide about it or settle it.

ex.en: The Baltic people have a right to determine their own future.
ex.zh: 波罗的海人民有权决定他们自己的未来。

d: v. 决定，控制，起决定作用；查明，确定，测定；下定决心（determine 的现在分词）
adj. 决定性的，有决定作用的

e.en: If a level or amount drops or if someone or something drops it, it quickly becomes less. 使迅速下降;

ex.en: Temperatures can drop to freezing at night.
ex.zh: 晚上气温能陡降到零度以下。

ex.en: His blood pressure had dropped severely.
ex.zh: 他的血压严重地迅速下降。

e.en: Drop is also a noun.

ex.en: He was prepared to take a drop in wages.
ex.zh: 他准备好了接受一次工资的快速下调。

e.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

ex.en: I dropped my glasses and broke them.
ex.zh: 我不小心掉了眼镜，把它摔破了。

e.en: If something drops onto something else, it falls onto that thing. If something drops from somewhere, it falls from that place.

ex.en: He felt hot tears dropping onto his fingers.
ex.zh: 他感到热泪滴在他的手指上。

d: n. 掉落；空投；滴落物
v. 落下，滴下；下降，减少；放弃；停止；退出（学校、活动等）；投下；垂下（头、眼睛等）；（用车）送到某处；中途卸客；累垮（drop 的现在分词）

e.en: Elimination is the process of getting rid of waste products from your body by going to the bathroom.

ex.en: Breast-feeding is as natural as sex or elimination or any other bodily function.
ex.zh: 母乳哺养是天生的，就像性交、排泄或者其他任何身体功能一样。

d: n. 消除，排除；淘汰；消灭，铲除；排泄

e.en: A bill is a written statement of money that you owe for goods or services.

ex.en: They couldn't afford to pay the bills.
ex.zh: 他们付不起账。

ex.en: He paid his bill for the newspapers promptly.
ex.zh: 他立刻付了报纸的帐单。

e.en: If you bill someone for goods or services you have provided them with, you give or send them a bill stating how much money they owe you for these goods or services.

ex.en: Are you going to bill me for this?
ex.zh: 你会为这开帐单给我吗？

e.en: A bill is a piece of paper money.

ex.en: The case contained a large quantity of U.S. dollar bills.
ex.zh: 盒子里装有大量美钞。

e.en: In government, a bill is a formal statement of a proposed new law that is discussed and then voted on.

ex.en: This is the toughest crime bill that Congress has passed in a decade.
ex.zh: 这是十年来国会通过的最强硬的有关犯罪的议案。

d: n. 账单；议案，法案；（美国英语）纸币，钞票；（金融）票据，如汇票、提单、国库券等（以上均为 bill 的复数）；（Bills，首字母大写）人名，比尔斯（英、德姓氏）
v. 开账单（bill 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.

ex.en: Try to get the best product at the lowest price.
ex.zh: 尽力以最低的价格买到最好的产品。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is a product of a situation or process, you mean that the situation or process has had a significant effect in making them what they are.

ex.en: We are all products of our time.
ex.zh: 我们都是我们时代的产物。

e.en: a substance formed in a chemical reaction (化学反应)

d: n. 产品，商品（product 的复数）；产物；（化学）生成物；（数学）积

e.en: Plastic is a material that is produced from oil by a chemical process and that is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

ex.en: ...a wooden crate, sheltered from rain by sheets of plastic.
ex.zh: …一只板条木箱，用塑料膜盖着遮雨。

ex.en: A lot of the plastics that carmakers are using cannot be recycled.
ex.zh: 汽车制造商们正在使用的很多塑料制品是无法回收再用的。

e.en: If you describe something as plastic, you mean that you think it looks or tastes unnatural or not real. (样子或味道)

ex.en: You wanted proper home-cooked meals, you said you had enough plastic hotel food and airline food.
ex.zh: 你想吃地道的家常饭菜，你说你吃够了宾馆里和航班上味道不纯的食品。

e.en: If you use plastic or plastic money to pay for something, you pay for it with a credit card instead of using cash.

ex.en: Using plastic to pay for an order is simplicity itself.
ex.zh: 使用信用卡支付订单本身就很简单。

e.en: Something that is plastic is soft and can easily be made into different shapes.

ex.en: You can also enjoy mud packs with the natural mud, smooth, grey, soft, and plastic as butter.
ex.zh: 你还可以享受天然泥制面膜，灰色的泥，光滑、柔软, 像黄油一样易塑。

d: n. 塑料；信用卡；塑胶制造业（plastics）；塑料学（plastics）
adj. 塑料制的；人造的，不自然的；可塑的；（艺术用语）造型的，塑造的；（科技用语）范性的，塑性的；适应环境多样性的

e.en: If you recycle things that have already been used, such as bottles or sheets of paper, you process them so that they can be used again. 回收利用;

ex.en: The objective would be to recycle 98 percent of domestic waste.
ex.zh: 该目标是循环使用98%的生活垃圾。

e.en: 回收利用;

ex.en: ...a recycling plan.
ex.zh: …一项回收利用计划。

d: n. 回收利用；回收利用物
v. 回收利用，再利用；（将可回收物品）送入回收加工厂；再次应用，重新使用（观念、文章等）（recycle 的现在分词）

e.en: If you recycle things that have already been used, such as bottles or sheets of paper, you process them so that they can be used again. 回收利用;

ex.en: The objective would be to recycle 98 percent of domestic waste.
ex.zh: 该目标是循环使用98%的生活垃圾。

e.en: 回收利用;

ex.en: ...a recycling plan.
ex.zh: …一项回收利用计划。

d: adj. 回收利用的；再生的；用再生材料制成的（常作定语）
v. recycle 的过去式和过去分词：回收利用（废品），使再循环，重新使用（内容、材料等）

e.en: Plastic is a material that is produced from oil by a chemical process and that is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

ex.en: ...a wooden crate, sheltered from rain by sheets of plastic.
ex.zh: …一只板条木箱，用塑料膜盖着遮雨。

ex.en: A lot of the plastics that carmakers are using cannot be recycled.
ex.zh: 汽车制造商们正在使用的很多塑料制品是无法回收再用的。

e.en: If you describe something as plastic, you mean that you think it looks or tastes unnatural or not real. (样子或味道)

ex.en: You wanted proper home-cooked meals, you said you had enough plastic hotel food and airline food.
ex.zh: 你想吃地道的家常饭菜，你说你吃够了宾馆里和航班上味道不纯的食品。

e.en: If you use plastic or plastic money to pay for something, you pay for it with a credit card instead of using cash.

ex.en: Using plastic to pay for an order is simplicity itself.
ex.zh: 使用信用卡支付订单本身就很简单。

e.en: Something that is plastic is soft and can easily be made into different shapes.

ex.en: You can also enjoy mud packs with the natural mud, smooth, grey, soft, and plastic as butter.
ex.zh: 你还可以享受天然泥制面膜，灰色的泥，光滑、柔软, 像黄油一样易塑。

d: n. 塑料；塑料制品；整形外科，整形手术（旧译“外科修补术”）；塑料工业，塑料工艺

e.en: If you chase someone, or chase after them, you run after them or follow them quickly in order to catch or reach them.

ex.en: She chased the thief for 100 yards.
ex.zh: 她追了小偷100码远。

e.en: Chase is also a noun.

ex.en: He was reluctant to give up the chase.
ex.zh: 他不愿意放弃追逐。

e.en: If you are chasing something you want, such as work or money, or are chasing after it, you are trying hard to get it. 追求 (事业、金钱等)

ex.en: In some areas, 14 people are chasing every job.
ex.zh: 在某些地区，14个人角逐每一个岗位。

ex.en: There are too many schools chasing after too few students.
ex.zh: 有太多的学校争抢太少的学生。

e.en: Chase is also a noun. (对事业、金钱等的)

ex.en: They took an invincible lead in the chase for the championship.
ex.zh: 他们在冠军角逐中遥遥领先。

d: v. 追赶，追逐；追求（chase 的现在分词形式）
n. 雕镂术，金属錾花；车螺纹，车螺丝雕镂；铸件最后抛光；（Chasing）（英）蔡辛（人名）

e.en: If you waste something such as time, money, or energy, you use too much of it doing something that is not important or necessary, or is unlikely to succeed.

ex.en: There could be many reasons and he was not going to waste time speculating on them.
ex.zh: 原因可能很多，而他不打算浪费时间猜测这些原因。

ex.en: I resolved not to waste money on a hotel.
ex.zh: 我决定不把钱白白浪费在旅馆住宿上。

e.en: Waste is also a noun. (时间、金钱等的)

ex.en: It is a waste of time going to the doctor with most mild complaints.
ex.zh: 为了种种小毛病去看医生是浪费时间。

e.en: Waste is the use of money or other resources on things that do not need it.

ex.en: The packets are measured to reduce waste.
ex.zh: 测量包裹尺寸以减少浪费。
