e.en: Waste is material that has been used and is no longer wanted, for example, because the valuable or useful part of it has been taken out. 废物;

ex.en: Congress passed a law that regulates the disposal of waste.
ex.zh: 国会通过了一条管理废物处理的法律。

ex.en: ...the dangers posed by toxic waste.
ex.zh: …有毒废弃物造成的危险。

d: n. 浪费，滥用；废物，废弃物（同 wastes）；荒地，荒原（wastes）；（尤指因租借人的行为或疏忽而导致的）不动产的损坏，产业损伤；粪便，尿液
v. 浪费，滥用；未能充分利用，没有物尽其用；杀害，谋杀（某人）；（使）（人，身体部位）逐渐变虚弱，变消瘦；破坏，毁坏（地方）；（时间）流逝，被花掉
adj. （通常指城市中的某地）荒芜的，荒废的；（材料、物质等）废弃的，无用的

e.en: A consumer is a person who buys things or uses services.

ex.en: ...claims that tobacco companies failed to warn consumers about the dangers of smoking.
ex.zh: …声称烟草公司没有就吸烟的种种危险警告消费者。

d: n. 消费者，顾客，用户；食用者，使用者，消耗者

e.en: to treat or prepare (something) by a special method again 用特殊方式再次处理(某事); 用特殊方式再次准备(某事)

d: adj. 再经过加工的
v. 再加工（reprocess 的过去式）
共同发起人

e.en: A solution to a problem or difficult situation is a way of dealing with it so that the difficulty is removed.

ex.en: Although he has sought to find a peaceful solution, he is facing pressure to use greater military force.
ex.zh: 虽然他已设法寻找一个和平的解决办法，但他正面临着使用更大军事力量的压力。

e.en: The solution to a puzzle is the answer to it.

ex.en: We invited readers who completed the puzzle to send in their solutions.
ex.zh: 我们邀请解完谜的读者交出谜底。

e.en: A solution is a liquid in which a solid substance has been dissolved.

ex.en: ...a warm solution of liquid detergent.
ex.zh: …液体洗洁精的温热稀释溶液。

d: n. （问题、困难等的）解决办法；（练习或竞赛的）解答，答案；溶液；溶解过程，溶解状态；（满足特定需要的）产品（或服务）（solutions）

e.en: A congress is a large meeting that is held to discuss ideas and policies.

ex.en: A lot has changed after the party congress.
ex.zh: 该党代表大会后很多都变了。

d: n. 国会，议会；代表大会；美国国会（Congress）

e.en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

ex.en: When things aren't going well, he encourages me, telling me not to give up.
ex.zh: 当事情不顺利的时候，他鼓励我，告诉我不要放弃。

e.en: If someone is encouraged by something that happens, it gives them hope or confidence.

ex.en: Investors were encouraged by the news.
ex.zh: 投资者被这条消息所鼓舞。

e.en: 受到鼓舞的

ex.en: We were very encouraged after over 17,000 pictures were submitted.
ex.zh: 我们深受鼓舞，17000多张照片已被提交了。

e.en: If you encourage someone to do something, you try to persuade them to do it, for example, by telling them that it would be a pleasant thing to do, or by trying to make it easier for them to do it. You can also encourage an activity.

ex.en: Herbie Hancock was encouraged by his family to learn music at a young age.
ex.zh: 赫比·汉考克小时候受到家人鼓励去学音乐。

d: v. 鼓励，激励；鼓动，怂恿；刺激，促进
n. 贝城（美国城市）
n. 箭头

e.en: A label is a piece of paper or plastic that is attached to an object in order to give information about it.

ex.en: He peered at the label on the bottle.
ex.zh: 他注视着瓶子上的标签。

e.en: If something is labelled, a label is attached to it giving information about it.

ex.en: It requires foreign frozen-food imports to be clearly labelled.
ex.zh: 它要求外国进口冷冻食品要粘贴明确的标签。

ex.en: The produce was labelled "Made in China."
ex.zh: 该产品上贴有“中国制造”的标签。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is labelled as a particular thing, you mean that people generally describe them that way and you think that this is unfair.

ex.en: It won't be labelled in any way as a military expedition.
ex.zh: 它无论如何也称不上是一次军事远征。

ex.en: It does not matter whether these duties are labelled "duties" or "tasks".
ex.zh: 这些义务被称作“义务”还是“任务”都无关紧要。

d: n. 标签，标牌；称号，绰号；商标，品牌；唱片公司；（计算机）标记；示踪剂；带垂饰的横带
v. 贴标签；把……不公正地称为；用示踪剂使（物质等）示踪
【名】 （Label）（美、法、巴）拉贝尔（人名）

e.en: An item is one of a collection or list of objects.

ex.en: The most valuable item on show will be a Picasso drawing.
ex.zh: 展览中最有价值的作品将是毕加索的一幅画。

e.en: An item is one of a list of things for someone to do, deal with, or talk about.

ex.en: The other item on the agenda is the tour.
ex.zh: 另一项议程是旅行。

e.en: An item is a report or article in a newspaper or magazine, or on television or radio. (报刊、电视或广播中的)

ex.en: There was an item in the paper about him.
ex.zh: 报纸上有一篇关于他的报道。

e.en: If you say that two people are an item, you mean that they are having a romantic or sexual relationship. (在恋爱或有性关系的)

ex.en: She and Gino were an item.
ex.zh: 她和吉诺曾是一对。

d: n. item 的复数：物品，物件；项目，条目，事项；报纸、电视或广播上的一条新闻，一则报道
v. （古）逐条记载（item 的第三人称单数）
n. 埃克森美孚国际公司（美国大型跨国石油天然气公司）

e.en: A label is a piece of paper or plastic that is attached to an object in order to give information about it.

ex.en: He peered at the label on the bottle.
ex.zh: 他注视着瓶子上的标签。

e.en: If something is labelled, a label is attached to it giving information about it.

ex.en: It requires foreign frozen-food imports to be clearly labelled.
ex.zh: 它要求外国进口冷冻食品要粘贴明确的标签。

ex.en: The produce was labelled "Made in China."
ex.zh: 该产品上贴有“中国制造”的标签。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is labelled as a particular thing, you mean that people generally describe them that way and you think that this is unfair.

ex.en: It won't be labelled in any way as a military expedition.
ex.zh: 它无论如何也称不上是一次军事远征。

ex.en: It does not matter whether these duties are labelled "duties" or "tasks".
ex.zh: 这些义务被称作“义务”还是“任务”都无关紧要。

d: n. 标签，标牌，标记；（常指不恰当的）称谓，称号；唱片公司；时装公司等的品牌（或商标）；（词典、计算机等中的）标识，标注；带垂饰的横带；滴水石（label 的复数）
v. 贴标签于，给……加标签；（尤指不公正地）把……称为，将……归类为；用示踪剂标记（物质等）以便研究（label 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Packaging is the container or covering that something is sold in.

ex.en: It is selling very well, in part because the packaging is so attractive.
ex.zh: 它卖得非常好，部分原因在于包装很吸引人。

d: n. 包装材料，外包装；包装工作；包装，美化
v. 把……打包，把……装箱（以便出售）；包装（产品或想法等）；配套销售（商品）（package 的现在分词）

e.en: If you describe something as misleading, you mean that it gives you a wrong idea or impression.

ex.en: It would be misleading to say that we were friends.
ex.zh: 说我们是朋友会对别人产生误导。

e.en: 误导性地

ex.en: The data had been presented misleadingly.
ex.zh: 数据被以一种令人误解的方式表达出来。

d: adj. 误导的，引入歧途的
v. 误导，将……引入歧途（mislead 的现在分词形式）

e.en: Pollution is the process of polluting water, air, or land, especially with poisonous chemicals.

ex.en: The fine was for the company's pollution of the air near its plants.
ex.zh: 公司被罚款是因为它的工厂污染了周围的空气。

e.en: Pollution is poisonous or dirty substances that are polluting the water, air, or land somewhere.

ex.en: The level of pollution in the river was falling.
ex.zh: 该河流受污染的程度其时正在降低。

d: n. 污染；污染物；噪音污染，（夜间扰人的）强烈灯光

e.en: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.

ex.en: Try to get the best product at the lowest price.
ex.zh: 尽力以最低的价格买到最好的产品。

e.en: If you say that someone or something is a product of a situation or process, you mean that the situation or process has had a significant effect in making them what they are.

ex.en: We are all products of our time.
ex.zh: 我们都是我们时代的产物。

e.en: a substance formed in a chemical reaction (化学反应)

d: n. 产品，制品；（自然、化学或工业过程的）生成物；（特定行动、影响或事件的）结局；（受某种环境或经历影响而形成的）产物；积，乘积；总称（商业性）音乐制品

e.en: A manufacturer is a business or company which makes goods in large quantities to sell.

ex.en: ...the world's largest doll manufacturer.
ex.zh: …世界上最大的玩偶生产商。

d: n. manufacturer 的复数形式：（经）制造商，厂商，生产商

e.en: A proposal is a plan or an idea, often a formal or written one, which is suggested for people to think about and decide upon. (常为正式书面的)

ex.en: The president is to put forward new proposals for resolving the country's constitutional crisis.
ex.zh: 总统将提出解决国家宪法危机的新议案。

ex.en: ...the governor's proposal to restrict cigarette sales.
ex.zh: …州长关于限制香烟销售的提案。

e.en: A proposal is the act of asking someone to marry you.

ex.en: After a three-weekend courtship, Pam accepted Randy's proposal of marriage.
ex.zh: 经过一段为期3个周末的恋爱，帕姆接受了兰迪的求婚。

d: n. （proposal 的复数）建议，提议，提案；求婚；建议书

e.en: To give or be protection against something unpleasant means to prevent people or things from being harmed or damaged by it.

ex.en: Such a diet is widely believed to offer protection against a number of cancers.
ex.zh: 这样的日常饮食被广泛认为可以预防多种癌症。

ex.en: It is clear that the primary duty of parents is to provide protection for our children.
ex.zh: 很明显，父母的首要职责就是为孩子提供保护。

e.en: If an insurance policy gives you protection against an event such as death, injury, fire, or theft, the insurance company will give you or your family money if that event happens. (保险单提供的)

ex.en: Insurance can be purchased to provide protection against such risks.
ex.zh: 买保险可以应对此类风险。

e.en: If a government has a policy of protection, it helps its own industries by putting a tax on imported goods or by restricting imports in some other way.

ex.en: Over the same period trade protection has increased in the rich countries.
ex.zh: 在同一时期，富国的贸易保护增强了。

d: n. 保护，防护；保护物，护身符；保险；避孕（措施）；保护费；贸易保护，关税保护制；保护条例，保护措施；（登山）安全保护器材数量与质量

e.en: If something has a sheen, it has a smooth and gentle brightness on its surface.

ex.en: The carpet had a silvery sheen to it.
ex.zh: 地毯有种银色的光泽。

d: n. 光泽，光辉，光彩；（英语姓氏）希恩
adj. 光辉的，有光泽的；华丽的
vi. 闪耀，发光

e.en: Technical means involving the sorts of machines, processes, and materials that are used in industry, transportation, and communications. 技术的;

ex.en: In order to reach this limit a number of technical problems will have to be solved.
ex.zh: 为了达到这个限度，有许多技术问题得解决。

e.en: 技术上地;

ex.en: ...the largest and most technically advanced furnace company in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上规模最大、技术最先进的锅炉公司。

e.en: You use technical to describe the practical skills and methods used to do an activity such as an art, a craft, or a sport.

ex.en: Their technical ability is exceptional.
ex.zh: 他们的技能是非凡的。

e.en: 技巧上地

ex.en: While Sade's voice isn't technically brilliant it has a quality which is unmistakable.
ex.zh: 虽然萨德的嗓音从技巧上讲不是很出色，但它有一种独特的音质。

d: adj. 工艺的，技术的；专业的，专门的；严格按照法律意义的，严格按字面解释的；（尤指体育或艺术等活动）技巧（上）的；与机器（或系统）运行相关的，技术性的
n. （车后架设有机枪的）小卡车
n. （Texas）德克萨斯州（美国州名）
n. （Texas）（美、俄、印、巴、墨）台萨（人名）

e.en: Technology refers to methods, systems, and devices which are the result of scientific knowledge being used for practical purposes.

ex.en: Technology is changing fast.
ex.zh: 技术日新月异。

ex.en: They should be allowed to wait for cheaper technologies to be developed.
ex.zh: 他们应该被允许等待更廉价的技术开发出来。

d: n. 技术，科技（technology 的复数）
n. 可回收性，可回收利用性，再循环能力

e.en: A type of something is a group of those things that have particular features in common. 类型;

ex.en: ...several types of lettuce.
ex.zh: …生菜的几个品种。

ex.en: There are various types of the disease.
ex.zh: 该疾病有各种类型。

e.en: If you refer to a particular thing or person as a type of something more general, you are considering that thing or person as an example of that more general group. 某类 (人或事物)

ex.en: Have you done this type of work before?
ex.zh: 你以前做过这种工作吗？

ex.en: Rates of interest for this type of borrowing can be high.
ex.zh: 这种贷款的利率可能会很高。

e.en: If you refer to a person as a particular type, you mean that they have that particular appearance, character, or type of behaviour.

ex.en: It's the first time I, a fair-skinned, freckly type, have sailed in the sun without burning.
ex.zh: 这是第一次，我这样一个皮肤白皙、有雀斑的人，顶着太阳航海而没有晒伤。

e.en: If you type something, you use a typewriter or computer keyboard to write it.

ex.en: I can type your essays for you.
ex.zh: 我可以为你打文章。

ex.en: I had never really learned to type properly.
ex.zh: 我从未真正地学会正确地打字。

d: n. 类型，种类；具有某种特征的人，典型；（印刷的）文字，字体；（印刷）铅字，活字；象征；（艺术的）典型，榜样；（宗教学）预兆；（植，动）型，模式标本；（奖章或硬币）图案；（语言学）类型，型
v. （用计算机或打字机）打字；测定……的类型，分型
【名】 （Type）（英）泰普（人名）

e.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job. 为…做广告;

ex.en: The company is spending heavily to advertise its strongest brands.
ex.zh: 该公司在花重金为其最强势的品牌做广告。

ex.en: In 1991, the house was advertised for sale at $49,000.
ex.zh: 在1991年，这所房子登出以4.9万美元出售的广告。

e.en: If you advertise for someone to do something for you, for example, to work for you or share your accommodation, you announce it in a newspaper, on television, or on a bulletin board. 登广告 (寻求职员、合住者等)

ex.en: We advertised for staff in a local newspaper.
ex.zh: 我们在一份地方报纸上登了广告招聘员工。

e.en: If you do not advertise the fact that something is the case, you try not to let other people know about it.

ex.en: There is no need to advertise the fact that you are a single woman.
ex.zh: 没必要宣传你是个单身女性这一事实。

d: adj. 广告的，被广告宣传的
v. 做广告，登广告，宣传（advertise 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: any of various tropical American parrots of the genus Amazona, such as A. farinosa (green amazon), having a short tail and mainly green plumage

d: 亚马逊；古希腊女战士

e.en: An arrow is a long thin weapon that is sharp and pointed at one end and that often has feathers at the other end. An arrow is shot from a bow.

ex.en: Warriors armed with bows and arrows and spears have invaded their villages.
ex.zh: 佩有弓箭和长矛的武士们已入侵了他们的村庄。

e.en: An arrow is a written or printed sign that consists of a straight line with another line bent at a sharp angle at one end. This is a printed arrow: →. The arrow points in a particular direction to indicate where something is.

ex.en: A series of arrows points the way to the modest grave of Andrei Sakharov.
ex.zh: 一系列箭头指示着通往简朴的安德烈·萨哈罗夫之墓的路。

d: n. 箭，矢；箭头，箭号
【名】 （Arrow）（英）阿罗（人名）
n. 认识，意识；感悟能力

e.en: a lot; a great deal
an indication of the desire to do, be, or have something 表示想做、想成为、想拥有的欲望 (See also bags I)

d: n. 包，袋，手提包、旅行袋等（bag 的复数形式）；大量，许多（非正式，英国英语，用于 bags of）；（口语）眼袋，肿眼泡（bags under the eyes）
v. 把……装入袋中，装袋；（狩猎中）捕获（猎物）（bag 的第三人称单数形式）
int. （英国英语，儿童口语）表示想做、想要或想得到某事物，常作“我先来”（用于 bags I ...）
adj. 反消费主义的：反对过度消费、消费主义文化的。
n. 禁令（ban的复数）；结婚预告（等于banns）
n. （Bans）人名；（西）班斯；（法）邦斯

e.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

ex.en: Duties and taxes are the most obvious barrier to free trade.
ex.zh: 关税及其他各种税是自由贸易最明显的障碍。

e.en: A barrier is a problem that prevents two people or groups from agreeing, communicating, or working with each other. 障碍;

ex.en: There is no reason why love shouldn't cross the age barrier.
ex.zh: 爱情没有理由不应跨越年龄障碍。

ex.en: She had been waiting for Simon to break down the barrier between them.
ex.zh: 她一直在等着西蒙来破除他们之间的隔阂。

e.en: A barrier is something such as a fence or wall that is put in place to prevent people from moving easily from one area to another. 栅栏;

ex.en: The demonstrators broke through heavy police barriers.
ex.zh: 示威者们冲破了警方的重重关卡。

e.en: A barrier is an object or layer that physically prevents something from moving from one place to another.

ex.en: A severe storm destroyed a natural barrier between the house and the lake.
ex.zh: 一场猛烈的暴风雨摧毁了房屋和湖泊之间的天然屏障。

d: n. 障碍，隔阂；栅栏，障碍物；（经济学）贸易壁垒、进入壁垒、退出壁垒（barrier 的复数）
v. 假定，假设，认为；装出，做出；承担，就职；呈现，具有；夺取，篡夺

e.en: A bin is a container that you keep or store things in.

ex.en: ...big steel storage bins.
ex.zh: …钢制大贮藏箱。

e.en: A bin is a container that you put waste or rubbish in.

d: n. 垃圾桶；储物箱；瓶酒搁架；统计堆栈
v. 把……扔进垃圾箱；摒弃，拒绝；把……放（或贮藏）在箱（或仓）中；把（酒等）放进搁架；把（数据）归入统计堆
【名】 （Bin）（美、意）本（人名）

e.en: Bipartisan means concerning or involving two different political parties or groups. 两党的;

ex.en: ...a bipartisan approach to educational reform.
ex.zh: ...教育改革的一种两党合作模式。

d: adj. 两党连立的，代表两党的，得到两党支持的

e.en: When an object breaks or when you break it, it suddenly separates into two or more pieces, often because it has been hit or dropped. 打碎;

ex.en: He fell through the window, breaking the glass.
ex.zh: 他打破玻璃，从窗口摔了出去。

ex.en: The plate broke.
ex.zh: 盘子碎了。

e.en: If you break a part of your body such as your leg, your arm, or your nose, or if a bone breaks, you are injured because a bone cracks or splits. 弄折 (骨头);

ex.en: She broke a leg in a skiing accident.
ex.zh: 她在一次滑雪事故中摔断了一条腿。

ex.en: Old bones break easily.
ex.zh: 老骨头容易骨折。

e.en: Break is also a noun.

ex.en: It has caused a bad break to Gabriella's leg.
ex.zh: 这导致了加布里埃拉的一条腿严重骨折。

e.en: If a surface, cover, or seal breaks or if something breaks it, a hole or tear is made in it, so that a substance can pass through. 拆裂;

ex.en: Once you've broken the seal of a bottle there's no way you can put it back together again.
ex.zh: 一旦你撕开瓶子的封口,就没法将它重新合上。

ex.en: The bandage must be put on when the blister breaks.
ex.zh: 水疱破口后必须包扎上绷带。

d: v. 打破，折断；（使）破裂，撕开；弄破，使流血；（使）骨折；破纪录；打断，中断；终止；断绝（联系）；损坏；违反，违背；使……放弃习惯；休息；稍停，暂留；突破，挣脱；（被）摧毁，削弱；使心碎；透露，传开；告诉（坏消息）；驯化，驯服；得分（低于或高于规定总分）；超过；（云）散开；开始，（风暴）发作；拍岸，迸溅；（男孩嗓音）变粗；（因激动）变调；破解，破译；兑开（纸币）；减缓；（网球中）破发球；（球）转向，曲线飞行；（股价）暴跌；猛冲，开始快跑；发生，发展；（热度）降低，退烧
n. 间歇，小憩；课间休息；停顿，暂停；（电台或电视节目）插播广告的间隙；短假；机会，机遇；结束，断绝；逃跑（尤指越狱）；裂缝，缺口；骨折；（因情感作用）嗓音突变；黎明，破晓；天气突变；接发球得分；接连击中；（球的）弧线飞行；（尤指球员或球队）进攻；有帮助的事物；芽，蓓蕾；双轮驱马大车（breaking cart 的原称）；敞篷四轮马车（同 brake）
n. 拜登（姓氏）；乔·拜登（美国民主党政治家，第 46 任总统，曾任副总统，常被单称）

e.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

ex.en: The new government's first challenge is the economy.
ex.zh: 新政府面临的第一项挑战是经济。

e.en: A challenge to something is a questioning of its truth or value. A challenge to someone is a questioning of their authority.

ex.en: The demonstrators have now made a direct challenge to the authority of the government.
ex.zh: 示威者现已对该政府的权威性提出了直截了当的质疑。

e.en: If someone rises to the challenge, they act in response to a difficult situation which is new to them and are successful.

ex.en: The new Germany must rise to the challenge of its enhanced responsibilities.
ex.zh: 新德国必须奋起应对更艰巨的挑战。

e.en: If you challenge ideas or people, you question their truth, value, or authority.

ex.en: Democratic leaders have challenged the president to sign the bill.
ex.zh: 民主党领导人对总统签署这项法案存有质疑。

ex.en: The move was immediately challenged by two of the republics.
ex.zh: 这项提案立即遭到了这两个共和国的质疑。

d: n. 挑战，艰巨任务；质疑；比赛（或争斗）邀约（challenge 的复数形式）
v. 质疑，质问；向……挑战（challenge 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A champion is someone who has won the first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

ex.en: ...a former Olympic champion.
ex.zh: …一位前奥运冠军。

ex.en: Kasparov became world champion.
ex.zh: 卡斯帕罗夫成了世界冠军。

e.en: If you are a champion of a person, a cause, or a principle, you support or defend them. 拥护者;

ex.en: He received acclaim as a champion of the oppressed.
ex.zh: 他作为被压迫者的捍卫者而受到了赞誉。

e.en: If you champion a person, a cause, or a principle, you support or defend them. 拥护;

ex.en: He passionately championed the poor.
ex.zh: 他曾热情地捍卫穷人。

d: v．支持，捍卫，拥护：为某个观点、原则或人物提供支持，尤指在公共场合。

e.en: If there is a change in something, it becomes different.

ex.en: The ambassador appealed for a change in U.S. policy.
ex.zh: 该大使呼吁美国政策的变革。

ex.en: There are going to have to be some drastic changes.
ex.zh: 一定得有些重大变革。

e.en: If you say that something is a change or makes a change, you mean that it is enjoyable because it is different from what you are used to.

ex.en: It is a complex system, but it certainly makes a change.
ex.zh: 这是个复杂系统，但肯定有所改进。

e.en: If you change from one thing to another, you stop using or doing the first one and start using or doing the second.

ex.en: His physician modified the dosage but did not change to a different medication.
ex.zh: 他的医生调整了剂量，但没有改换成别的药方。

e.en: When something changes or when you change it, it becomes different. 改变;

ex.en: We are trying to detect and understand how the climates change.
ex.zh: 我们在努力探测并了解气候是怎样变化的。

ex.en: In the union office, the mood gradually changed from resignation to rage.
ex.zh: 在工会办公室，情绪渐渐由依从变成了愤怒。

d: adj. 变化中的，改变中的
v. 改变，变化；更换，替换；换乘（change 的现在分词）

e.en: Cheese is a solid food made from milk. It is usually white or yellow.

ex.en: ...bread and cheese.
ex.zh: …面包和奶酪

ex.en: ...delicious French cheeses.
ex.zh: …美味的法式奶酪。

d: n. 干酪，奶酪；（拍照时让人微笑的用语）笑一笑；大人物，大亨；截然不同；（表示不同情）抱歉啦，真倒霉；带皮的乳酪块；（黏稠度像乳酪的）膏，酱；原装乳酪样的扁圆物（如九柱戏等游戏中使用的木圆盘）；过分的温情
v. 激怒，使厌烦；停止
adv. 用化学，以化学方法；在化学上，从化学角度

e.en: Chemical means involving or resulting from a reaction between two or more substances, or relating to the substances that something consists of.

ex.en: ...chemical reactions that cause ozone destruction.
ex.zh: …导致臭氧破坏的化学反应。

ex.en: ...the chemical composition of the ocean.
ex.zh: …海洋的化学成分。

e.en: 经化学方式

ex.en: ...chemically treated foods.
ex.zh: …经化学方式处理过的食品。

e.en: Chemicals are substances that are used in a chemical process or made by a chemical process. 化学物;

ex.en: The whole food chain is affected by the overuse of chemicals in agriculture.
ex.zh: 整个食物链受到了化学物质在农业中过度使用的影响。

ex.en: ...a chemical company.
ex.zh: …一家化学制品公司。

d: n. 化学品，化学制品，化学药品，化工产品（chemical 的复数）
n. 圆度，圆形，环状；（逻辑）循环性，循环论证

e.en: The clarity of something such as a book or argument is its quality of being well explained and easy to understand. 明晰;

ex.en: ...the ease and clarity with which the author explains difficult technical and scientific subjects.
ex.zh: …该作者用于解释难懂的科技主题的轻松与明晰。

e.en: Clarity is the ability to think clearly. (思路的)

ex.en: In business circles he is noted for his flair and clarity of vision.
ex.zh: 在商界，他以其风度与犀利的眼光而闻名。

e.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear in outline or sound. (指轮廓、声音等)

ex.en: This remarkable technology provides far greater clarity than conventional x-rays.
ex.zh: 这一非凡技术提供了比传统的X光要高得多的清晰度。

d: n. 清晰易懂；思路清晰；（画面或声音的）清晰，清楚；清澈，明净
【名】 （Clarity）（英）克拉里蒂（人名）

e.en: Commerce is the activities and procedures involved in buying and selling things.

ex.en: They have made their fortunes from industry and commerce.
ex.zh: 他们从工商业中发了财。

d: n. 贸易，商业；社交，交往；性交

e.en: A concept is an idea or abstract principle. 概念;

ex.en: She added that the concept of arranged marriages is misunderstood in the west.
ex.zh: 她补充说包办婚姻的概念在西方被误解了。

d: n. 概念，观念
adj. （围绕）某主题的；为表达一种想法而创造的
v. 想象，设想

e.en: A compound is an enclosed area of land that is used for a particular purpose.

ex.en: They took refuge in the embassy compound.
ex.zh: 他们在大使馆围区内避难。

ex.en: ...a military compound.
ex.zh: …一个军事管辖区。

e.en: In chemistry, a compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements.

ex.en: Organic compounds contain carbon in their molecules.
ex.zh: 有机化合物的分子里含碳。

e.en: If something is a compound of different things, it consists of those things.

ex.en: Honey is basically a compound of water, two types of sugar, vitamins and enzymes.
ex.zh: 蜂蜜主要是水、两种糖、维生素和酶的混合物。

e.en: Compound is used to indicate that something consists of two or more parts or things.

ex.en: ...the big compound eyes of dragonflies.
ex.zh: …蜻蜓的大复眼。

d: n. 化合物；混合物；复合词；大院，有围墙的场地（以上均为 compound 的复数）
vt. 使加重，使恶化；合成，混合；以复利计算支付；和解，私了（以上均为 compound 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you are confused, you do not know exactly what is happening or what to do.

ex.en: A survey showed people were confused about what they should eat to stay healthy.
ex.zh: 一项调查表明人们对于保持健康该吃什么很困惑。

e.en: Something that is confused does not have any order or pattern and is difficult to understand.

ex.en: The situation remains confused as both sides claim success.
ex.zh: 由于双方都声称自己获胜，形势依然混乱。

d: adj. 困惑的，糊涂的；混乱的，难懂的
v. 使糊涂，使迷惑；混淆，弄错；使复杂化（confuse 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: Something that is clear is easy to understand, see, or hear. 清楚的;

ex.en: The book is clear, readable, and adequately illustrated.
ex.zh: 这本书易懂易读，而且图解充足。

ex.en: The space telescope has taken the clearest pictures ever of Pluto.
ex.zh: 太空望远镜拍下了有史以来最清晰的冥王星的照片。

e.en: 清楚地;

ex.en: Whales journey up the coast of California, clearly visible from the beach.
ex.zh: 鲸鱼们朝着加利福尼亚海岸游过来，从海滩就能清楚地看见。

e.en: Something that is clear is obvious and impossible to be mistaken about.

ex.en: It was a clear case of homicide.
ex.zh: 这是一起确信无疑的谋杀案。

ex.en: It became clear that I hadn't been able to convince Mike.
ex.zh: 显然我没能说服迈克。

e.en: 显然无疑地

ex.en: Clearly, the police cannot break the law in order to enforce it.
ex.zh: 显然地，警察不能为了执法而违法。

d: vt. 使干净；证明......无罪；清除；批准，通过（clear的过去式和过去分词）
vi. 放晴；变清澈；通过（clear的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

ex.en: The envelope contained a Christmas card.
ex.zh: 该信封里装有一张圣诞贺卡。

ex.en: The first two floors of the building contain retail space and a restaurant.
ex.zh: 该大楼最底下两层有零售空间和一家餐馆。

e.en: If a substance contains something, that thing is a part of it.

ex.en: Watermelon contains vitamins and also potassium.
ex.zh: 西瓜含有维生素也有钾。

e.en: If writing, speech, or film contains particular information, ideas, or images, it includes them. (文章、演讲、电影) 包含 (某些信息、观点、图像等)

ex.en: This sheet contained a list of problems a patient might like to raise with the doctor.
ex.zh: 这张纸写有一个病人可能想向医生提出的问题清单。

e.en: If a group or organization contains a certain number of people, those are the people that are in it. (团体、组织等) 包括 (某数量的成员)

ex.en: The committee contains 11 Democrats and nine Republicans.
ex.zh: 该委员会包括11名民主党人和9名共和党人。

d: v. 包含，容纳，含有；遏制，防止……蔓延；抑制（感情）（contain 的现在分词）

e.en: A container is something such as a box or bottle that is used to hold or store things in.

ex.en: ...the plastic containers in which fish are stored and sold.
ex.zh: …储藏和出售鱼的塑料容器。

e.en: A container is a very large metal or wooden box used for transporting goods so that they can be loaded easily onto ships and trucks.

ex.en: The train, carrying loaded containers on flatcars, was 1.2 miles long.
ex.zh: 那列在平车上载着装得满满的集装箱的火车长1.2英里。

d: n. 容器；集装箱

e.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

ex.en: The envelope contained a Christmas card.
ex.zh: 该信封里装有一张圣诞贺卡。

ex.en: The first two floors of the building contain retail space and a restaurant.
ex.zh: 该大楼最底下两层有零售空间和一家餐馆。

e.en: If a substance contains something, that thing is a part of it.

ex.en: Watermelon contains vitamins and also potassium.
ex.zh: 西瓜含有维生素也有钾。

e.en: If writing, speech, or film contains particular information, ideas, or images, it includes them. (文章、演讲、电影) 包含 (某些信息、观点、图像等)

ex.en: This sheet contained a list of problems a patient might like to raise with the doctor.
ex.zh: 这张纸写有一个病人可能想向医生提出的问题清单。

e.en: If a group or organization contains a certain number of people, those are the people that are in it. (团体、组织等) 包括 (某数量的成员)

ex.en: The committee contains 11 Democrats and nine Republicans.
ex.zh: 该委员会包括11名民主党人和9名共和党人。

d: v. 包含，容纳，含有；控制，遏制，防止……蔓延；抑制（感情）（contain 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

ex.en: Immigration is a controversial issue in many countries.
ex.zh: 移民在很多国家都是一个有争议的问题。

d: adj. 有争议的，引发争论的

e.en: If you describe someone or something as convincing, you mean that they make you believe that a particular thing is true, correct, or genuine.

ex.en: Scientists say there is no convincing evidence that power lines have anything to do with cancer.
ex.zh: 科学家称没有有力证据证明电线能致癌。

e.en: 有说服力地

ex.en: He argued forcefully and convincingly that they were likely to bankrupt the budget.
ex.zh: 他强有力地证明了他们的花费可能会超出预算。

d: adj. 令人信服的，有说服力的；（胜利）轻松的，确定无疑的
v. 使确信，使信服；说服，劝服（convince 的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you say that something is costly, you mean that it costs a lot of money, often more than you would want to pay.

ex.en: Having professionally made curtains can be costly, so why not make your own?
ex.zh: 买专业制造的窗帘可能很贵，你为什么不自己做呢？

d: adj. 昂贵的，值钱的；造成严重损失的，代价大的
【名】 （Costly）（英）科斯特利（人名）

e.en: If you are given credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

ex.en: The group can't get credit to buy farming machinery.
ex.zh: 该集团无法以赊购方式购买农业机械。

e.en: If you get the credit for something good, people praise you because you are responsible for it, or are thought to be responsible for it.

ex.en: We don't mind who gets the credit so long as we don't get the blame.
ex.zh: 只要我们不挨批评，谁受到表扬我们都不在乎。

ex.en: It would be wrong for us to take all the credit.
ex.zh: 我们把所有的功劳都揽到自己身上就不对了。

e.en: When a sum of money is credited to an account, the bank adds that sum of money to the total in the account.

ex.en: She noticed that only $80,000 had been credited to her account.
ex.zh: 她注意到只有$80000存入了她的账户。

ex.en: Midland decided to change the way it credited payments to accounts.
ex.zh: 米德兰公司决定改变将所付款项存入账户的方式。

e.en: If people credit someone with an achievement or if it is credited to them, people say or believe that they were responsible for it.

ex.en: The staff are crediting him with having saved Hythe's life.
ex.zh: 海斯能得救全体人员都归功于他。

ex.en: The 74-year-old mayor is credited with helping make Los Angeles the financial capital of the West Coast.
ex.zh: 74岁的市长被归功为帮助洛杉矶成为西海岸金融中心的人。

d: n. 信用，信贷，赊购；赞扬，信誉，声望；存款金额，余额；补助；退税，抵免；学分；带来荣耀的人（或事）；作品（指影片、电视节目、戏剧等）；信任，相信
v. 把（钱）记入总账，把钱存入（账户）；相信，信任；认为是……的功劳，给予承认；认为……有特定品质（或效果）
n. 路边；靠近路缘的人行道部分
adj. 路边的；在路边进行的
adv. 在路边；在靠近路缘的一侧

e.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

ex.en: Johnston isn't tired of Las Vegas yet, it seems, but appearances can be deceptive.
ex.zh: 似乎，约翰斯顿还没有厌倦拉斯韦加斯，但表象可能是骗人的。

e.en: 骗人地

ex.en: The storyline is deceptively simple.
ex.zh: 故事情节看似简单。

d: adj. 欺骗性的，造成假象的
adv. 看似，不像看上去那么，比实际更显得

e.en: A Democrat is a member or supporter of a particular political party which has the word "democrat" or "democratic" in its title, for example, the Democratic Party in the United States.

ex.en: Murray has joined other Senate Democrats in blocking the legislation.
ex.zh: 默里已经加入其他民主党参议员反对这项立法了。

e.en: A democrat is a person who believes in the ideals of democracy, personal freedom, and equality.

ex.en: This is the time for democrats and not dictators.
ex.zh: 这是民主主义者而不是独裁者的时代。

d: n. （美国）民主党党员；民主主义者

e.en: To demonstrate a fact means to make it clear to people.

ex.en: The study also demonstrated a direct link between obesity and mortality.
ex.zh: 这项研究也证明了肥胖和死亡率之间的直接关系。

ex.en: They are anxious to demonstrate to the voters that they have practical policies.
ex.zh: 他们急于向选民证明他们有切实可行的政策。

e.en: If you demonstrate a particular skill, quality, or feeling, you show by your actions that you have it. 展现 (才能、品质、感情)

ex.en: Have they, for example, demonstrated a commitment to democracy?
ex.zh: 例如，他们展现了对民主的奉献吗？

e.en: When people demonstrate, they march or gather somewhere to show their opposition to something or their support for something.

ex.en: Some 30,000 angry farmers arrived in Brussels yesterday to demonstrate against possible cuts in subsidies.
ex.zh: 昨天大约三万名愤怒的农民到布鲁塞尔游行示威，反对可能的补贴削减。

ex.en: In the cities vast crowds have been demonstrating for change.
ex.zh: 在各城市，已经有大量的群众举行示威游行要求变革。

e.en: If you demonstrate something, you show people how it works or how to do it.

ex.en: A selection of cosmetic companies will be there to demonstrate their new products.
ex.zh: 一些化妆品公司会在那里展示他们的新产品。

d: v. 证明；示范，演示；表露；游行，示威

e.en: If a liquid is diluted or dilutes, it is added to or mixes with water or another liquid, and becomes weaker. 稀释;

ex.en: If you give your baby juice, dilute it well with cooled, boiled water.
ex.zh: 喂婴儿果汁要用凉开水充分稀释。

ex.en: The liquid is then diluted.
ex.zh: 然后液体就变稀了。

e.en: If someone or something dilutes a belief, quality, or value, they make it weaker and less effective.

ex.en: There was a clear intention to dilute black voting power.
ex.zh: 削弱黑人选举权的意图是显而易见的。

e.en: A dilute liquid is very thin and weak, usually because it has had water added to it.

ex.en: ...a dilute solution of bleach.
ex.zh: …稀释了的漂白液。

d: adj. 稀释的，冲淡的；削弱的，无力的；（金融）摊薄的，稀释后的
v. dilute 的过去分词，表示被稀释，变稀；使减低（效果），削弱
n. 柯蒂斯（男子名）；柯蒂斯（姓氏）

e.en: The end of something such as a period of time, an event, a book, or a film is the last part of it or the final point in it.

ex.en: The report is expected by the end of the year.
ex.zh: 这份报告预期年底前出台。

ex.en: ...families who settled in the region at the end of the 17th century.
ex.zh: …于17世纪末定居该地区的家庭。

e.en: An end to something or the end of it is the act or result of stopping it so that it does not continue any longer.

ex.en: The government today called for an end to the violence.
ex.zh: 政府今天呼吁结束暴力。

ex.en: I was worried she would walk out or bring the interview to an end.
ex.zh: 我担心她会突然退席或者终止采访。

e.en: The two ends of something long and narrow are the two points or parts of it that are farthest away from each other.

ex.en: The company is planning to place surveillance equipment at both ends of the tunnel.
ex.zh: 该公司计划在隧道的两端安装监视设备。

e.en: The end of a long, narrow object such as a finger or a pencil is the tip or smallest edge of it, usually the part that is furthest away from you.

ex.en: He tapped the ends of his fingers together.
ex.zh: 他用手指尖相互轻叩。

d: v. 结束，终止（end 的过去式和过去分词）；最终处于某种状态，最终到达某处或结果做了某事（end up 的过去式/过去分词）
adj. 已结束的，完结的

e.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them. 公开支持;

ex.en: I can endorse their opinion wholeheartedly.
ex.zh: 我可以全心全意地支持他们的观点。

e.en: If you endorse a product or company, you appear in advertisements for it.

ex.en: The twins endorsed a line of household cleaning products.
ex.zh: 这对双胞胎为一系列的家庭清洁产品代言过。

d: v. （公开）赞同，认可；（在广告中对某种产品）宣传，吹捧；（尤指在支票背面）签名，背书；(在驾驶执照上)记录违章事项

e.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them. 公开支持;

ex.en: I can endorse their opinion wholeheartedly.
ex.zh: 我可以全心全意地支持他们的观点。

e.en: If you endorse a product or company, you appear in advertisements for it.

ex.en: The twins endorsed a line of household cleaning products.
ex.zh: 这对双胞胎为一系列的家庭清洁产品代言过。

d: v. （endorse 的第三人称单数）（公开）赞同，支持，认可；（在广告中）为某种产品、品牌等做宣传、代言；（尤指在支票等票据背面）签名，背书

e.en: eicosapentaenoic acid: a fatty acid, found in certain fish oils, that can reduce blood cholesterol

d: abbr. 美国环境保护署（Environmental Protection Agency，亦作环境保护局）；（生物化学）二十碳五烯酸（eicosapentaenoic acid）

e.en: Journalism is the job of collecting news and writing about it for newspapers, magazines, television, or radio.

ex.en: He began a career in journalism, working for the Rocky Mountain News.
ex.zh: 他开始从事新闻事业，供职于落基山新闻报。

d: n. 新闻业，新闻工作；报刊杂志，新闻报道

e.en: Investigative work, especially journalism, involves investigating things.

ex.en: ...an investigative reporter.
ex.zh: …一位新闻调查记者。

d: adj. 调查的，调查性的；研究的，探究的；好调查的；（法律）侦查的

e.en: Courtesy is politeness, respect, and consideration for others.

ex.en: ...a gentleman who behaves with the utmost courtesy towards ladies.
ex.zh: …一位对女士极为彬彬有礼的绅士。

e.en: If you refer to the courtesy of doing something, you are referring to a polite action.

ex.en: By extending the courtesy of a phone call to my clients, I was building a personal relationship with them.
ex.zh: 通过给客户打电话这样有礼的行为，我渐渐和他们建立起私交。

e.en: Courtesy is used to describe services that are provided free of charge by an organization to its customers, or to the general public.

ex.en: A courtesy shuttle bus operates between the hotel and the town.
ex.zh: 一辆免费运送班车在旅馆和小镇之间往返。

e.en: A courtesy call or a courtesy visit is a formal visit that you pay someone as a way of showing them politeness or respect.

ex.en: The president paid a courtesy call on Emperor Akihito.
ex.zh: 总统礼节性地拜访了明仁天皇。

d: n. 礼貌，彬彬有礼；礼貌的行为（言语）；屈膝礼
adj. 免费提供的；礼节性的

e.en: A newsroom is an office in a newspaper, radio, or television organization where news reports are prepared before they are printed or broadcast. (报社、广播台或电视台的)

d: n. 新闻编辑室，新闻编辑部；（新闻机构的）编辑部人员，新闻采编人员；报刊阅览室
n. 杰西卡（女子名）

e.en: If someone is interned, they are put in prison or in a prison camp for political reasons.

ex.en: He was interned as an enemy alien at the outbreak of the Second World War.
ex.zh: 他在第二次世界大战爆发时被作为敌国侨民扣押了。

e.en: An intern is an advanced student or a recent graduate, especially in medicine, who is being given practical training under supervision. 实习生;

ex.en: ...a medical intern.
ex.zh: …一位实习医生。

d: v. intern 的过去式和过去分词：拘留，扣押（常用于被动语态，尤指战时或出于政治、安全原因）；实习，做实习生
adj. 被拘禁的，被扣押的；被拘禁人（interned person）；（计算机）驻留的（指字符串被放入字符串驻留池）

e.en: Thai means belonging or relating to Thailand, or to its people, language, or culture. 泰国(人)的 ; 泰国语的;
A Thai is a citizen of Thailand, or a person of Thai origin.
Thai is the language spoken in Thailand.

d: n. （Thai）泰国人；泰语
adj. （Thai）泰国的；泰国人的；泰语的
n. （Thai）（美）泰（人名）

e.en: If someone is interned, they are put in prison or in a prison camp for political reasons.

ex.en: He was interned as an enemy alien at the outbreak of the Second World War.
ex.zh: 他在第二次世界大战爆发时被作为敌国侨民扣押了。

e.en: An intern is an advanced student or a recent graduate, especially in medicine, who is being given practical training under supervision. 实习生;

ex.en: ...a medical intern.
ex.zh: …一位实习医生。

d: v. （由于政治原因或战时）拘留，扣押；做实习医生（或实习生）
n. 实习医生；实习生

e.en: If you hope that something is true, or if you hope for something, you want it to be true or to happen, and you usually believe that it is possible or likely.

ex.en: She had decided she must go on as usual, follow her normal routine, and hope and pray.
ex.zh: 她已决定自己必须一如既往地过下去，遵循自己的日常生活规律，同时心存希望并祈祷。

ex.en: He hesitates before leaving, almost as though he had been hoping for conversation.
ex.zh: 他离开前有些犹豫，好像希望跟人说些什么。

e.en: If you say that you cannot hope for something, or if you talk about the only thing that you can hope to get, you mean that you are in a bad situation, and there is very little chance of improving it.

ex.en: Things aren't ideal, but that's the best you can hope for.
ex.zh: 事情并不理想，但你只能指望这些了。

e.en: Hope is also a noun.

ex.en: The only hope for underdeveloped countries is to become, as far as possible, self-reliant.
ex.zh: 欠发达国家的惟一指望就是尽可能地做到自力更生。

e.en: Hope is a feeling of desire and expectation that things will go well in the future.

ex.en: Now that he has become president, many people once again have hope for genuine changes in the system.
ex.zh: 既然他已成为总统，许多人又一次寄期望于体制的真正改革。

ex.en: But Kevin hasn't given up hope of getting in shape.
ex.zh: 但是凯文仍没有放弃康复的希望。

d: v. 希望（hope 的第三人称单数）
n. 希望（hope 的复数形式）
prep. in hopes of：怀着……的希望，希望能……（后接名词或动名词）
n. 内布拉斯加州（美国中西部一州）
n. 阿尔弗雷德（亦译艾尔弗雷德，英、法、捷克、德男子名）；阿尔弗雷德大帝（九世纪威塞克斯国王，曾抵御丹麦入侵并鼓励英语写作）

e.en: An editor is the person who is in charge of a newspaper or magazine and who decides what will be published in each edition of it.

ex.en: Her father was the former editor of the Saturday Review.
ex.zh: 她的父亲是《星期六评论》的前任主编。

e.en: An editor is a journalist who is responsible for a particular section of a newspaper or magazine.

ex.en: Mike later became the sports editor for The Beacon.
ex.zh: 迈克后来成为《烽火》的体育栏目编辑。

e.en: An editor is a person who checks and corrects texts before they are published.

ex.en: Your role as editor is important, for you can look at a piece of writing objectively.
ex.zh: 你作为编辑的角色是重要的，因为你可以客观地看一篇文字。

e.en: An editor is a radio or television journalist who reports on a particular type of news.

ex.en: ...our economics editor, Tom Goldberg.
ex.zh: …我们的经济节目记者，汤姆·戈德堡。

d: n. 编辑；记者；剪辑师；编辑程序

e.en: to bowl or try to bowl (a batsman) by pitching the ball under or just beyond the bat 向(击球员)

d: n. 约克郡；约克王朝
n. （Meza）人名；（罗）梅扎；（西）梅萨

e.en: A campus is an area of land that contains the main buildings of a university or college. (大学的)

ex.en: ...during a rally at the campus.
ex.zh: …在一次校园集会时。

d: n. （大学或学院的）校园；大学生活；大学（学校、医院等机构的）场地
【名】 （Campus）（英）坎帕斯，（意、罗）坎普斯，（法）康皮斯（人名）

e.en: A career is the job or profession that someone does for a long period of their life.

ex.en: She is now concentrating on a career as a fashion designer.
ex.zh: 她现在专注于时装设计这一行。

ex.en: ...a career in journalism.
ex.zh: …新闻职业。

e.en: Your career is the part of your life that you spend working.

ex.en: During his career, he wrote more than fifty plays.
ex.zh: 在他的创作生涯里，他共写了五十多部剧作。

e.en: Career advice or guidance consists of information about different jobs and help with deciding what kind of job you want to do.

ex.en: She received very little career guidance when young.
ex.zh: 她年轻时没受过什么就业指导。

e.en: If a person or vehicle careers somewhere, they move fast and in an uncontrolled way.

ex.en: His car careered into a river.
ex.zh: 他的车猛地冲进了河里。

d: n. 职业，事业，职业生涯（career 的复数）；职业的，就业的（用于名词前作定语）
v. （不加控制地）猛冲，全速前进（career 的第三人称单数）

e.en: A class is a group of students who are taught together.

ex.en: He had to spend about six months in a class with younger students.
ex.zh: 他不得不在一个比他小的学生的班上呆了大约六个月。

e.en: A class is a course of teaching in a particular subject.

ex.en: He acquired a law degree by taking classes at night.
ex.zh: 他通过上晚上的课获得了法律学位。

e.en: A class of things is a group of them with similar characteristics.

ex.en: Harbour staff noticed that measurements given for the same class of boats often varied.
ex.zh: 港口员工们注意到对同一类小船所给出的尺寸经常不同。

e.en: If you do something in class, you do it during a lesson in school.

ex.en: There is lots of reading in class.
ex.zh: 课上有大量阅读。

d: n. 班级；（一节）课，上课时间；（某一科目的）课程；阶级，阶层；等级划分，等级制度；（货物、服务或人的）等级，类别；（飞机、火车等的）舱位等级，车厢等级；品味；同届毕业生；（英国大学的）学位等级；（生物）（植物或动物分类的）纲；（比赛的）组别
v. 把……归类，把……看作；把……编入某一班级；属于……类（或等级），被列为某类（或某级）
adj. 优秀的，出色的
【名】 （Class）（英、德）克拉斯（人名）
n. （Zahra）人名；（伊朗、阿拉伯）扎赫拉

e.en: If something happens daily, it happens every day.

ex.en: Cathay Pacific flies daily nonstop to Hong Kong.
ex.zh: 国泰航空的航班每天直飞香港。

e.en: Daily is also an adjective.

ex.en: They held daily press briefings.
ex.zh: 他们召开了每日例行的新闻发布会。

e.en: Daily quantities or rates relate to a period of one day.

ex.en: ...a diet containing adequate daily amounts of fresh fruit.
ex.zh: …包含一天足量新鲜水果的饮食。

e.en: Your daily life is the things that you do every day as part of your normal life.

ex.en: All of us in our daily life react favourably to people who take us and our views seriously.
ex.zh: 日常生活中，对于那些认真对待我们和我们的意见的人，我们都会与之交好。

d: adj. 每日的，日常的；一天的，按天计算的
adv. 每日，每天；日常地
n. 日报；日工，女佣；（每天拍摄的）电影样片
【名】 （Daily）（英）戴利（人名）
n. 休斯顿（美国得克萨斯州港市）
n. 爱荷华州（美国中西部一州，亦译艾奥瓦州、衣阿华州）；艾奥瓦人（北美苏安语系原住民，亦称 Ioway）；艾奥瓦语（艾奥瓦人使用的奇韦雷语方言，亦称 Ioway）

e.en: To marginalize a group of people means to make them feel isolated and unimportant. 使边缘化;

ex.en: We've always been marginalized, exploited, and constantly threatened.
ex.zh: 我们总是遭到排挤、剥削和不断的恐吓。

d: adj. 被边缘化的，受排斥的
v. 使边缘化；排斥；忽略（marginalize 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: The Midwest is the region in the central part of the United States and north of Texas. (美国)

ex.en: ...farmers in the Midwest.
ex.zh: …中西部的农场主们。

ex.en: ...the Midwest states.
ex.zh: …中西部各州。

d: n. （Midwest）美国的中西部
n. （Midwest）（美）密德维史特（人名）

e.en: Occasional means happening sometimes, but not regularly or often.

ex.en: I've had occasional mild headaches all my life.
ex.zh: 我此生一直有偶尔的轻微头疼。

e.en: 偶尔地

ex.en: He still misbehaves occasionally.
ex.zh: 他仍偶尔行为不乖。

d: adj. 偶尔的，不经常的；（家具）特定场合才使用的； （文章、演讲或宗教仪式等）在特殊场合所作的，为特殊场合所准备的；非定时的，临时的

e.en: Politics are the actions or activities concerned with achieving and using power in a country or society. The verb that follows politics may be either singular or plural.

ex.en: Many people think Nixon transformed American politics.
ex.zh: 许多人认为尼克松改变了美国的政治。

ex.en: He quickly involved himself in local politics.
ex.zh: 他很快就参与到地方政治活动中去了。

e.en: Your politics are your beliefs about how a country ought to be governed.

ex.en: My politics are well to the left of centre.
ex.zh: 我的政治观点很靠左翼。

e.en: Politics is the study of the ways in which countries are governed.

ex.en: He began studying politics and medieval history.
ex.zh: 他开始学习政治学和中世纪史。

e.en: Politics can be used to talk about the ways that power is shared in an organization and the ways it is affected by personal relationships between people who work together. The verb that follows politics may be either singular or plural.

ex.en: You need to understand how office politics influence the working environment.
ex.zh: 你需要明白办公室权术怎样影响工作环境。

d: n. 政治，政治活动（事务）；政治事业；政治学；(某团体、组织等内的）争权活动，权术；政治信仰，政治观点；（尤指跟社会权力和地位有关的领域、理论或活动的）主张，观（念）；政治思想体系，政治局势

e.en: The publication of a book or magazine is the act of printing it and sending it to stores to be sold.

ex.en: The guide is being translated into several languages for publication near Christmas.
ex.zh: 这本指南正被翻译成好几种语言，准备在圣诞节前后出版。

e.en: A publication is a book or magazine that has been published.

ex.en: They have started legal proceedings against two publications which spoke of an affair.
ex.zh: 他们已开始对提及一件绯闻的两本出版物进行法律诉讼。

e.en: The publication of something such as information is the act of making it known to the public, for example, by informing journalists or by publishing a government document.

ex.en: A spokesman said: "We have no comment regarding the publication of these photographs."
ex.zh: 一位发言人说: “关于这些照片的公开，我们无可奉告。”

d: n. 出版物，刊物（publication 的复数）

e.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it. 执行;

ex.en: He said Japan would continue to pursue the policies laid down at the London summit.
ex.zh: 他说日本将继续贯彻伦敦峰会上确定的方针。

e.en: If you pursue a particular aim or result, you make efforts to achieve it, often over a long period of time. 追求;

ex.en: He will pursue a trade policy that protects American workers.
ex.zh: 他将努力实行保护美国工人的贸易政策。

e.en: If you pursue a particular topic, you try to find out more about it by asking questions.

ex.en: If your original request is denied, don't be afraid to pursue the matter.
ex.zh: 如果你最初的要求被拒绝了，不要害怕去追问这件事情。

e.en: If you pursue a person, vehicle, or animal, you follow them, usually in order to catch them.

ex.en: She pursued the man who had stolen a woman's bag.
ex.zh: 她追赶那个偷了一女士钱包的男子。

d: v. pursue 的现在分词：追求；追赶，追逐；从事
n. pursue 的动名词/名词性用法：追求；追赶，追逐
adj. 追赶的，追捕的，追踪的

e.en: Summer is the season between spring and fall. In the summer the weather is usually warm or hot.

ex.en: I escaped the heatwave in Washington earlier this summer and flew to Maine.
ex.zh: 我今年初夏躲避了华盛顿的热浪，飞到了缅因州。

ex.en: It was a perfect summer's day.
ex.zh: 那是个完美的夏日。

e.en: to spend the summer (at a place) (在某地)
a large horizontal beam or girder, esp one that supports floor joists (建筑)大梁 (Also called summer tree)

d: n. 夏天，夏季；年，岁；（建筑）大梁；（天文）从夏至到秋分这段时期；全盛期
v. （在某地）避暑，过夏；夏天放牧（牛）
【名】 （Summer）（德）祖默，（英）萨默（人名）

e.en: Training is the process of learning the skills that you need for a particular job or activity.

ex.en: He called for much higher spending on education and training.
ex.zh: 他呼吁在教育和培训上投入更多的资金。

ex.en: Kennedy had no formal training as a decorator.
ex.zh: 肯尼迪没有接受过油漆工的正式培训。

e.en: Training is physical exercise that you do regularly in order to keep fit or to prepare for an activity such as a race. (体育) 锻炼; (为参加赛跑等的)

ex.en: The emphasis is on developing fitness through exercises and training.
ex.zh: 重点放在通过运动和锻炼来促进健康。

d: n. 训练，培训；体育训练，锻炼
v. 锻炼，培养（某一素质或能力）；培训，训练；（为准备体育赛事而）操练（train的现在分词形式）

e.en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

ex.en: I want a drink.
ex.zh: 我想要点喝的。

ex.en: People wanted to know who this talented designer was.
ex.zh: 人们想知道这位天才的设计者是谁。

e.en: You can say that you want to say something to indicate that you are about to say it. 想要 (说)

ex.en: I want to say how delighted I am that you're having a baby.
ex.zh: 我想要说，你怀孕了我是多么高兴啊。

e.en: If you say to someone that you want something, or ask them if they want to do it, you are firmly telling them what you want or what you want them to do. 想要得到;

ex.en: I want an explanation from you, Jeremy.
ex.zh: 我要你给我一个解释，杰里米。

ex.en: Do you want to tell me what all this is about?
ex.zh: 你是否想告诉我这究竟是怎么回事？

e.en: If you tell someone that they want to do a particular thing, you are advising them to do it.

ex.en: You want to be very careful not to have a man like Crevecoeur for an enemy.
ex.zh: 你必须非常小心，不要与像克雷弗克那样的人为敌。

d: n. 需求；欲望；必需品
v. 想要（want 的第三人称单数）；渴望

e.en: People who work have a job, usually one which they are paid to do.

ex.en: I started working in a recording studio.
ex.zh: 我开始在一个录音棚里工作。

ex.en: He worked as a teacher for 50 years.
ex.zh: 他从事教师工作50年了。

e.en: When you work, you do the things that you are paid or required to do in your job.

ex.en: I can't talk to you right now – I'm working.
ex.zh: 我这会儿不能和你说话–我正在工作。

ex.en: He was working at his desk.
ex.zh: 他正在伏案工作。

e.en: When you work, you spend time and effort doing a task that needs to be done or trying to achieve something.

ex.en: Linda spends all her time working on the garden.
ex.zh: 琳达用所有的时间在那座花园里劳作。

ex.en: The government expressed hope that all the sides will work toward a political solution.
ex.zh: 该政府希望所有各方致力于一个政治解决方案。

e.en: If someone is working on a particular subject or question, they are studying or researching it.

ex.en: Professor Bonnet has been working for many years on molecules of this type.
ex.zh: 博内特教授多年来一直在研究这类分子。

d: n. 作品，著作（work 的复数）；工厂，制造厂；工程，工程设施；（the works）全套东西，所有东西；（机器等的）机件，内部机构；善行，功德；（Works）沃克斯（人名）
v. 工作，干活儿；从事体力（或脑力）劳动；从事……工作，在……工作；（机器）运转；（计划、方法等）奏效（work 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Abuse of someone is cruel and violent treatment of them.

ex.en: ...investigation of alleged child abuse.
ex.zh: …对涉嫌虐待儿童的调查。

ex.en: ...victims of sexual and physical abuse.
ex.zh: …性虐待和肉体摧残的受害者们。

e.en: Abuse is extremely rude and insulting things that people say when they are angry.

ex.en: I was left shouting abuse as the car sped off.
ex.zh: 当车加速离去时，我在那里破口大骂。

e.en: Abuse of something is the use of it in a wrong way or for a bad purpose.

ex.en: What went on here was an abuse of power.
ex.zh: 这里发生的情况是职权的滥用。

e.en: If someone is abused, they are treated cruelly and violently.

ex.en: Janet had been abused by her father since she was eleven.
ex.zh: 詹妮特自从11岁起就被她的父亲虐待。

ex.en: ...parents who feel they cannot cope or might abuse their children.
ex.zh: …感到自己不能应付或可能虐待孩子的家长们。

d: v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂（abuse 的第三人称单数）
n. 滥用行为，弊端；虐待行为，暴行（abuse 的复数）

e.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach. (地方) 易于进入的; (物品)

ex.en: The centre is easily accessible to the general public.
ex.zh: 该中心对于广大公众来讲很便利。

e.en: (地方) 易于进入性; (物品)

ex.en: ...the easy accessibility of the area.
ex.zh: …该地区的交通便利性。

e.en: If something is accessible to people, they can easily use it or obtain it. 易使用的;

ex.en: The aim of any reform of legal aid should be to make the system accessible to more people.
ex.zh: 任何法律援助改革的目标都应该是让该体系服务于更多的人。

e.en: 易使用性;

ex.en: ...growing public concern about the cost, quality and accessibility of health care.
ex.zh: …公众对医疗保健的费用、质量与可及性的日益关注。

d: adj. 可到达的，可进入的；易得到的，可使用的；可以理解的，易懂的；平易近人的，随和的；易受影响的

e.en: To advance means to move forward, often in order to attack someone. (常指为攻击而)

ex.en: Reports from Chad suggest that rebel forces are advancing on the capital.
ex.zh: 来自乍得的报导指出叛军正在向首都挺进。

ex.en: According to one report, the water is advancing at a rate of between 8 and 10 inches a day.
ex.zh: 根据一份报告，大水在以每天8至10英寸的速度逼近。

e.en: To advance means to make progress, especially in your knowledge of something. (尤指知识)

ex.en: Medical technology has advanced considerably.
ex.zh: 医学技术已大大发展了。

e.en: If you advance someone a sum of money, you lend it to them, or pay it to them earlier than arranged. 提前借 (一笔钱给某人); 提前付 (一笔钱给某人)

ex.en: I advanced him some money, which he would repay on our way home.
ex.zh: 我先借了些钱给他，他会在回家的路上还给我。

e.en: To advance an event, or the time or date of an event, means to bring it forward to an earlier time or date.

ex.en: Too much protein in the diet may advance the aging process.
ex.zh: 饮食中过多的蛋白质会使衰老的过程提前。

d: v. （使）前进，（使）向前移动；发展，进步；预付；提前，提早；促进，推动；提出（想法或理论）；上涨，增加；提拔，晋升
n. 前进；进步，进展；改善；预付款；勾引，追求；（价格、价值的）上涨；贷款
adj. 预先的，事先的；先行的，先遣的

e.en: If you amplify a sound, you make it louder, usually by using electronic equipment. 扩大 (声音)

ex.en: This landscape seemed to trap and amplify sounds.
ex.zh: 这种地形好像能聚拢和扩大声音。

ex.en: The music was amplified with microphones.
ex.zh: 那音乐被麦克风扩大了。

e.en: 扩音

ex.en: ...a voice that needed no amplification.
ex.zh: …一个不需要扩音的嗓门。

e.en: To amplify something means to increase its strength or intensity.

ex.en: The mist had been replaced by a kind of haze that seemed to amplify the heat.
ex.zh: 这薄雾已经被一种热汽代替了，这似乎加重了炎热的程度。

d: v. 放大，扩大（声音）；增强，加强；详述，进一步阐明；扩增（基因，DNA序列）

e.en: Appreciation of something is the recognition and enjoyment of its good qualities.

ex.en: ...an investigation into children's understanding and appreciation of art.
ex.zh: …关于孩子对艺术的理解与欣赏的一个调查。

e.en: Your appreciation for something that someone does for you is your gratitude for it.

ex.en: He expressed his appreciation for what he called Saudi Arabia's moderate and realistic oil policies.
ex.zh: 他表达了对他所称的沙特阿拉伯温和而务实的石油政策的感激。

e.en: An appreciation of a situation or problem is an understanding of what it involves.

ex.en: They have a stronger appreciation of the importance of economic incentives.
ex.zh: 他们对经济激励的重要性有了更深的了解。

e.en: Appreciation in the value of something is an increase in its value over a period of time.

ex.en: You have to take capital appreciation of the property into account.
ex.zh: 你得将那个房产的资本增值考虑进来。

d: n. 欣赏，鉴赏；感激，感谢；理解，领会；升值，增值；（赞赏性的）演讲，文字

e.en: Art consists of paintings, sculpture, and other pictures or objects that are created for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.

ex.en: ...the first exhibition of such art in the West.
ex.zh: …这种艺术品在西方的初次展出。

ex.en: ...contemporary and modern American art.
ex.zh: …美国当代与现代的艺术品。

e.en: Art is the activity or educational subject that consists of creating paintings, sculptures, and other pictures or objects for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.

ex.en: ...a painter, content to be left alone with her all-absorbing art.
ex.zh: …一个乐于独自沉浸在她的迷人艺术中的画家。

ex.en: ...Savannah College of Art and Design.
ex.zh: …萨瓦纳艺术设计学院。

e.en: The arts are activities such as music, painting, literature, film, and dance, which people can take part in for enjoyment, or to create works that express certain meanings or ideas of beauty.

ex.en: Catherine the Great was a patron of the arts and sciences.
ex.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜大帝是艺术和科学活动的赞助人。

e.en: At a university or college, arts are subjects such as history, literature, or languages in contrast to scientific subjects.

ex.en: ...arts and social science graduates.
ex.zh: …人文与社会科学的毕业生们。

d: n. 技艺（art 的复数）；艺术，艺术活动（通常用 the arts）；人文科学，文科

e.en: Someone or something that is Asian comes from or is associated with Asia. Americans use this term especially to refer to China, Korea, Thailand, Japan, or Vietnam. British people use this term especially to refer to India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

ex.en: ...Asian music.
ex.zh: …亚洲音乐。

e.en: An Asian is a person who comes from or is associated with a country or region in Asia.

ex.en: Many of the shops were run by Asians.
ex.zh: 这些商店中有许多是由亚洲人经营的。

d: n. 亚洲人，亚裔人士
adj. 亚洲的，亚洲人的

e.en: Audio equipment is used for recording and reproducing sound.

ex.en: The software was the first to offer access to audio and video files.
ex.zh: 这是第一种可以访问音视频文件的软件。

d: adj. 声音的，音频的
n. 声音，音频

e.en: To chronicle a series of events means to write about them or show them in broadcasts in the order in which they happened.
e.zh: 按发生时间顺序编写或播放

ex.en: The series chronicles the everyday adventures of two eternal bachelors.
ex.zh: 这部丛书按时间顺序记载了两个终生未婚男子每天的奇遇。

e.en: A chronicle is an account or record of a series of events.

ex.en: ...this vast chronicle of Napoleonic times.
ex.zh: …这本关于拿破仑时期的大部头编年史。

e.en: Chronicle is sometimes used as part of the name of a newspaper. …

ex.en: ...the San Francisco Chronicle.
ex.zh: …旧金山报。

d: n. 编年史，大事记；（报纸名称）记事报；记事，叙述
v. 把……载入编年史，按事件顺序记载；翔实记载

e.en: Concentration on something involves giving all your attention to it.

ex.en: Neal kept interrupting, breaking my concentration.
ex.zh: 尼尔不断打扰，打断我的注意力。

e.en: A concentration of something is a large amount of it or large numbers of it in a small area.

ex.en: The area has one of the world's greatest concentrations of wildlife.
ex.zh: 该地区有世界上野生生物最集中的区域之一。

e.en: The concentration of a substance is the proportion of essential ingredients or substances in it.

ex.en: pH is a measure of the concentration of free hydrogen atoms in a solution.
ex.zh: pH值是溶液中游离氢原子浓度的计量单位。

d: n. 专心，专注；关注，重视；集中，聚集；含量，浓度

e.en: A connection is a relationship between two things, people, or groups.

ex.en: There was no evidence of a connection between BSE and the brain diseases recently confirmed in cats.
ex.zh: 没有有关疯牛病和最近证实的猫类脑部疾病之间的关系的证据。

ex.en: I felt a strong connection between us.
ex.zh: 我感觉到了我们之间的强烈关系。

e.en: A connection is a joint where two wires or pipes are joined together.

ex.en: Check all radiators for small leaks, especially round pipework connections.
ex.zh: 检查所有的暖气设备，尤其是圆形管道的接头处，看是否有小裂缝。

e.en: If a place has good road, rail, or air connections, many places can be directly reached from there by car, train, or plane. (道路、轨道、航道)

ex.en: Mexico City has excellent air and rail connections to the rest of the country.
ex.zh: 墨西哥城有很好的空运和铁路连接全国各地。

e.en: If you get a connection at a station or airport, you catch a train, bus, or plane, after getting off another train, bus, or plane, in order to continue your trip. (火车、轮船、飞机等的)

ex.en: My flight was late and I missed the connection.
ex.zh: 我乘坐的航班晚点了，因此我错过了联运航班。

d: n. 连接，联系，关系（connection 的复数形式）；人脉，人际关系，关系学；交通连接，联运，接驳；（网络、电气、管道等的）连接，接头，接口

e.en: a card game for four, played with two packs (四人玩两套牌的)

d: n. 波士顿（美国城市）

e.en: A consortium is a group of people or firms who have agreed to cooperate with each other.

ex.en: The consortium includes some of the biggest building contractors in North America.
ex.zh: 该联盟包括北美一些最大的建筑承包商。

d: n. 联合企业，财团；配偶的相互权利；联合

e.en: Corporate means relating to business corporations or to a particular business corporation.

ex.en: ...top U.S. corporate executives.
ex.zh: …美国公司的高层管理人员。

ex.en: ...a corporate lawyer.
ex.zh: …一名公司律师。

d: adj. 公司的；法人的；共同的，全体的
n. 公司，集团

e.en: A corps is a part of the army which has special duties.

ex.en: ...the Army Medical Corps.
ex.zh: …陆军医疗部队。

e.en: The Corps is the United States Marine Corps.

ex.en: ...seventy-five men, all combat veterans, all members of The Corps' most exclusive unit.
ex.zh: …75名士兵，全都是作战老手、海军陆战队最精锐部队的成员。

e.en: A corps is a small group of people who do a special job.

ex.en: ...the diplomatic corps.
ex.zh: …外交使团。

d: n. 特种部队；（从事某工作或活动的）一群人；（美国）海军陆战队；（由两个或两个以上师组成的）军，兵团
【名】 （Corps）（西、德）科尔普斯（人名）

e.en: Counsel is advice.

ex.en: He had always been able to count on her wise counsel.
ex.zh: 他总是能够指望她明智的忠告。

e.en: If you counsel someone to take a course of action, or if you counsel a course of action, you advise that course of action. 建议;

ex.en: My advisers counselled me to do nothing.
ex.zh: 我的顾问建议我不要做任何事情。

e.en: If you counsel people, you give them advice about their problems.

ex.en: ...a psychologist who counsels people with eating disorders.
ex.zh: …一名向饮食紊乱症患者提供咨询的心理医生。

e.en: Someone's counsel is the lawyer who gives them advice on a legal case and speaks on their behalf in court.

ex.en: Singleton's counsel said after the trial that he would appeal.
ex.zh: 庭审之后辛格尔顿的辩护律师说他会上诉。

d: n. 忠告，建议；辩护律师；咨询，磋商
v. 建议，劝告（做……）；为……提供咨询，给……提供建议；商讨，提出忠告

e.en: A dairy is a company that sells milk and food made from milk, such as butter, cream, and cheese.

ex.en: In my childhood, local dairies bought milk from local farmers.
ex.zh: 在我小时候，本地的乳品公司向当地农场主收购牛奶。

e.en: Dairy is used to refer to foods such as butter and cheese that are made from milk.

ex.en: He avoids all meat and dairy products.
ex.zh: 他不吃任何肉类和奶制品。

e.en: Dairy is used to refer to the use of cattle to produce milk rather than meat.

ex.en: ...a small vegetable and dairy farm.
ex.zh: …一个种菜、养奶牛的小农场。

d: adj. 奶制的，乳品的；乳品业的，生产乳品的
n. 乳品公司，乳品店；乳制品；牛奶场，乳品场；地方小店；乳牛

e.en: A dedication is a message which is written at the beginning of a book, or a short announcement which is sometimes made before a play or piece of music is performed, as a sign of affection or respect for someone.

d: n. 献身，奉献；献辞；落成典礼

e.en: in Britain Department of Education and Science (英国)

d: abbr. 数据加密标准（data encryption standard）；教育和科学部（Department of Education and Science）；目的港交货（Delivered Ex Ship）；微分方程解算器（differential equation solver）
n. （Des）人名；（西）德斯；（英）德斯（男子教名Desmond的简称）；（泰）德；（匈）德什
n. 美国陶氏；美国陶氏化学；道琼斯平均指数
n. （Dow）人名；（英）道；（东南亚国家华语）涛
n. 渴望，热心

e.en: Editorial means involved in preparing a newspaper, magazine, or book for publication.

ex.en: I went to the editorial board meetings when I had the time.
ex.zh: 我当时有空儿就去参加编辑委员会的会议。

e.en: Editorial means involving the attitudes, opinions, and contents of something such as a newspaper, magazine, or television programme.

ex.en: We are not about to change our editorial policy.
ex.zh: 我们不打算改变我们的社论方针。

e.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper that gives the opinion of the editor or owner on a topic or item of news.

ex.en: In an editorial, The New York Times suggests the victory could turn nasty.
ex.zh: 在一篇社论中，《纽约时报》认为该胜利会转成恶梦。

d: adj. 编辑的，主编的；社论的
n. 社论，社评；（报刊的）由编辑撰写的部分，非广告部分

e.en: Emphasis is special or extra importance that is given to an activity or to a part or aspect of something.

ex.en: Too much emphasis is placed on research.
ex.zh: 把重点过多地放在研究上。

e.en: Emphasis is extra force that you put on a syllable, word, or phrase when you are speaking in order to make it seem more important.

ex.en: The emphasis is on the first syllable of the last word.
ex.zh: 重音是在最末一个单词的第一个音节上。

d: n. 重要性，重点强调；重读，强调；（表达的）强有力

e.en: Entertainment consists of performances of plays and movies, and activities such as reading and watching television, that give people pleasure.

ex.en: ...the world of entertainment and international stardom.
ex.zh: …国际娱乐界及明星界。

d: n. 娱乐，娱乐表演；招待，款待

e.en: You use exceptional to describe someone or something that has a particular quality, usually a good quality, to an unusually high degree.

ex.en: ...children with exceptional ability.
ex.zh: …能力非凡的孩子们。

e.en: 非凡地

ex.en: He's an exceptionally talented dancer and needs to practise several hours every day.
ex.zh: 他是位非凡有天赋的的舞蹈家，每天需要练几小时。

e.en: Exceptional situations and incidents are unusual and only likely to happen infrequently.

ex.en: A review panel concluded that there were no exceptional circumstances that would warrant a lesser penalty for him.
ex.zh: 一个评估小组作出结论：没有什么例外情况可使他获得从轻惩罚。

e.en: 例外地

ex.en: Exceptionally, in times of emergency, we may send a team of experts.
ex.zh: 紧急情况下我们可以破例派遣一个专家队。

d: adj. 卓越的，杰出的；不寻常的，罕见的；（心理或身体上）有缺陷的
n. （公司账目上的）异常项目

e.en: An organization is an official group of people, for example, a political party, a business, a charity, or a club. 组织 (指团体机构等)

ex.en: Most of the food for the homeless is provided by voluntary organizations.
ex.zh: 给无家可归者的大部分食物是由志愿组织提供的。

e.en: The organization of an event or activity involves making all the necessary arrangements for it. (活动的)

ex.en: ...the exceptional attention to detail that goes into the organization of this event.
ex.zh: …对此项活动组织细节的格外关注。

e.en: The organization of something is the way in which its different parts are arranged or relate to each other.

ex.en: I am aware that the organization of the book leaves something to be desired.
ex.zh: 我知道这本书的结构还有待完善。

d: n. 组织，机构；组织工作，筹备工作；编排，配置，结构；条理，逻辑性；机化（医学术语）

e.en: If someone asserts a fact or belief, they state it firmly.

ex.en: Mr. Helm plans to assert that the bill violates the First Amendment.
ex.zh: 赫尔姆先生计划坚定地陈述该法案有违《第一修正案》。

ex.en: The defendants, who continue to assert their innocence, are expected to appeal.
ex.zh: 那些继续宣称其清白的被告预计会上诉。

e.en: 断言

ex.en: There is no concrete evidence to support assertions that the recession is truly over.
ex.zh: 没有任何确凿的证据支持经济衰退已真正结束的断言。

e.en: If you assert your authority, you make it clear by your behaviour that you have authority. 显示 (权威)

ex.en: After the war, the army made an attempt to assert its authority in the south of the country.
ex.zh: 战后，军队试图在该国南部显示其权威。

e.en: (权威的)

ex.en: The decision is seen as an assertion of his authority within the company.
ex.zh: 这一决定被看作是公司内他的权威的显示。

d: v. 坚称，断言；维护，坚持（权利或权威）；坚持自己的主张，表现坚定；生效，起作用

e.en: A bid for something or a bid to do something is an attempt to obtain it or do it.

ex.en: ...Sydney's successful bid for the 2000 Olympic Games.
ex.zh: …悉尼对2000年奥林匹克运动会成功的申办。

e.en: A bid is an offer to pay a particular amount of money for something that is being sold.

ex.en: Hanson made an agreed takeover bid of $351 million.
ex.zh: 汉森按约定出价3.51亿美元进行收购。

e.en: If you bid for something or bid to do something, you try to obtain it or do it. 力求获得;

ex.en: Singapore Airlines is rumoured to be bidding for a management contract to run both airports.
ex.zh: 据传，新加坡航空公司正在努力争取这两个机场的管理合约。

e.en: If you bid for something that is being sold, you offer to pay a particular amount of money for it.

ex.en: She wanted to bid for it.
ex.zh: 她想出价买下它。

ex.en: The bank announced its intention to bid.
ex.zh: 银行宣布了其投标意向。

d: v. 出价；投标，竞标；努力争取；（纸牌戏中的）叫牌；命令，吩咐；打招呼，示意；邀请
n. 出价，喊价；投标；努力，尝试；（纸牌戏中的）叫牌
【名】 （Bid）（美）比德（人名）
abbr. 设备安装通知；欧洲情报网（European Internet Network）
n. （Ein）人名；（芬）埃因；（英）艾因

e.en: Speech is the ability to speak or the act of speaking. 言语能力;

ex.en: ...the development of speech in children.
ex.zh: …孩子言语能力的发展。

ex.en: Intoxication interferes with speech and coordination.
ex.zh: 醉酒影响言语能力和协调性。

e.en: Your speech is the way in which you speak.

ex.en: His speech became increasingly thick and nasal.
ex.zh: 他说话变得越来越带口音且鼻音越来越重。

e.en: Speech is spoken language.

ex.en: He could imitate in speech or writing most of those he admired.
ex.zh: 他能在口语或书写中模仿大多数他崇拜的人。

e.en: A speech is a formal talk which someone gives to an audience.

ex.en: She is due to make a speech on the economy next week.
ex.zh: 她将在下周作有关经济的演说。

ex.en: He delivered his speech in French.
ex.zh: 他用法语作的演讲。

d: n. 演说，发言，谈话；说话的能力；说话方式；口语，言语；（戏剧中的）台词；（该词常用于使某人感到自己所说的话很愚蠢）长篇大论

e.en: July is the seventh month of the year in the Western calendar. 7

ex.en: In July 1969, Neil Armstrong walked on the moon.
ex.zh: 1969年7月，尼尔·阿姆斯特朗踏上了月球。

d: n. 七月

e.en: Someone who is devoted to a person loves that person very much.

ex.en: ...a loving and devoted husband.
ex.zh: …一个忠爱的丈夫。

e.en: If you are devoted to something, you care about it a lot and are very enthusiastic about it.

ex.en: I have personally been devoted to this cause for many years.
ex.zh: 我个人多年来一直热衷于这项事业。

e.en: Something that is devoted to a particular thing deals only with that thing or contains only that thing.

ex.en: A large part of the Internet is now devoted to weblogs.
ex.zh: 因特网的很大一部分如今都专用于网络博客。

d: adj. 挚爱的，忠诚的；热衷的；专用于……的
v. 献身，致力；用于（devote 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: She's is the usual spoken form of "she is." (she is)

ex.en: She's an exceptionally good cook.
ex.zh: 她是一个特别好的厨师。

e.en: She's is a spoken form of "she has," especially when "has" is an auxiliary verb. (she has)的口语形式 (尤其当)(has)(是助动词时)

ex.en: She's been married for seven years and has two daughters.
ex.zh: 她已结婚7年并有两个女儿。

d: abbr. she is 的缩合形式，即“她是”；she has 的缩合形式（has 作助动词时尤其常用），即“她有”

e.en: Something that is restrictive prevents people from doing what they want to do, or from moving freely.

ex.en: The state will adopt a more restrictive policy on arms sales.
ex.zh: 这个州将对武器销售采取一项更具约束性的政策。

d: adj. 限制（性）的，约束（性）的；（语法）  限定性的

e.en: A strategist is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to gain an advantage or to achieve success, especially in war.

ex.en: Military strategists had devised a plan that guaranteed a series of stunning victories.
ex.zh: 军事战略家们设计了一个保证了一系列惊人胜利的计划。

d: n. 战略家，军事家；策略师，战略顾问

e.en: A theory is a formal idea or set of ideas that is intended to explain something.

ex.en: Marx produced a new theory about historical change based upon conflict between competing groups.
ex.zh: 马克思提出了一个新理论，认为历史变革是由于对立集团的冲突而产生的。

e.en: If you have a theory about something, you have your own opinion about it which you cannot prove but which you think is true.

ex.en: There was a theory that he wanted to marry her.
ex.zh: 有种观点认为他想娶她。

e.en: The theory of a practical subject or skill is the set of rules and principles that form the basis of it.

ex.en: He taught us music theory.
ex.zh: 他教我们乐理。

e.en: You use in theory to say that although something is supposed to be true or to happen in the way stated, it may not in fact be true or happen in that way.

ex.en: Achieving these goals is relatively easy in theory, yet quite difficult in practice.
ex.zh: 实现这些目标从理论上说比较容易，但在实践上却相当困难。

d: n. 理论、学说（theory 的复数形式）；亦指未经证实的个人观点或看法

e.en: You use other to refer to an additional thing or person of the same type as one that has been mentioned or is known about. 其他的 (指属于同一类别的)

ex.en: They were just like any other young couple.
ex.zh: 他们那时就和其他任何年轻夫妇一样。

e.en: Other is also a pronoun.

ex.en: Four crewmen were killed, one other was injured.
ex.zh: 四名船员被杀，另外一个受了伤。

e.en: You use other to indicate that a thing or person is not the one already mentioned, but a different one. 别的 (指属于不同类型的)

ex.en: The authorities insist that the discussions must not be linked to any other issue.
ex.zh: 官方坚持这些讨论绝不能和任何别的问题联系起来。

ex.en: He would have to accept it; there was no other way.
ex.zh: 他不得不接受它，没有别的办法。

e.en: Other is also a pronoun.

ex.en: This issue, more than any other, has divided her cabinet.
ex.zh: 正是这个问题，而不是任何别的问题，使她的内阁产生了分裂。

d: pron. 其他人

e.en: If you win something such as a competition, battle, or argument, you defeat those people you are competing or fighting against, or you do better than everyone else involved. 赢得 (比赛、战争或辩论等);

ex.en: He does not have any realistic chance of winning the election.
ex.zh: 他没有任何赢得这次选举的实际机会。

ex.en: The top four teams all won.
ex.zh: 排名最靠前的4支队伍都赢了。

e.en: Win is also a noun.

ex.en: The voters gave a narrow win to Vargas Llosa.
ex.zh: 选民们使瓦尔加斯·略萨取得险胜。

e.en: If something wins you something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, it causes you to defeat the people competing with you or fighting you, or to do better than everyone else involved. 使…赢得 (选举、比赛、战争或辩论等)

ex.en: The Democrats had found a message that could win them the White House.
ex.zh: 民主党人已找到了一条可以使他们赢得总统选举的口号。

e.en: If you win something such as a prize or medal, you get it because you have defeated everyone else in something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, or have done very well in it. 赢得 (奖或奖牌)

ex.en: Trent Dimas won gold in the final men's gymnastic event.
ex.zh: 特伦特·迪马斯在男子体操决赛中赢得了金牌。

d: v. （在战斗、比赛、游戏等中）赢，获胜；赢得（奖品等）；通过努力得到（某物）；为……赢得，使……获得；采（矿）；晾（干草）
n. （在比赛、竞赛等中的）胜利
【名】 （Win）（德、荷、缅）温，（英）温（女子教名 Winifred 的昵称）（人名）

e.en: If someone rewrites a piece of writing such as a book, an article, or a law, they write it in a different way in order to improve it.

ex.en: Following this critique, students rewrite their papers and submit them for final evaluation.
ex.zh: 遵照这一评语，学生们重写他们的论文并交上去以接受终审。

e.en: If you accuse someone such as a government of rewriting history, you are criticizing them for selecting and presenting particular historical events in a way that suits their own purposes. 篡改 (历史)

ex.en: We have always been an independent people, no matter how they rewrite history.
ex.zh: 无论他们如何篡改历史，我们一直都是一个独立的民族。

d: v. 重写；篡改（历史）；修改（写过的东西）（rewrite 的现在分词）
n. 重写，改写

e.en: An acolyte is a follower or assistant of an important person.

ex.en: To his acolytes, he is known simply as "the Boss."
ex.zh: 对于他的助手来说，他就只是“老板”。

d: n. 助手；侍僧；党羽（acolyte 的复数）

e.en: An adviser is an expert whose job is to give advice to another person or to a group of people.

ex.en: In Washington, the president and his advisers spent the day in meetings.
ex.zh: 在华盛顿，总统和他的顾问们开了一天的会。

d: n. 顾问，指导者

e.en: An acknowledgment is a statement or action which recognizes that something exists or is true. (对某物存在或属实的)

ex.en: The president's resignation appears to be an acknowledgment that he has lost all hope of keeping the country together.
ex.zh: 该总统的辞职看起来是对他已经放弃将国家团结起来的所有希望的一种承认。

e.en: The acknowledgments in a book are the section in which the author thanks all the people who have helped him or her.

ex.en: ...two whole pages of acknowledgments.
ex.zh: …整整两页的致谢辞。

e.en: A gesture of acknowledgment, such as a smile, shows someone that you have seen and recognized them.

ex.en: Farling smiled in acknowledgment and gave a bow.
ex.zh: 法林微笑致意并鞠了一躬。

d: n. 承认，认可；感谢，致谢（书中致谢部分常用复数 acknowledgments）；致意，示意；确认，回执，确认书，承认书；（计算机）确认信号，应答（ACK）

e.en: An allegation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong.

ex.en: The company has denied the allegations.
ex.zh: 该公司否认了这些指控。

d: n．指控，指责：对某人或某事的未经证实的指控或指责。
n. （Bannon）人名；（英）班农
n. 信仰，信念（belief 的复数）
adj. 商定的，一致同意的

e.en: Besides something or beside something means in addition to it.

ex.en: I think she has many good qualities besides being very beautiful.
ex.zh: 我觉得她除了非常漂亮之外，还有许多好的品质。

e.en: Besides is also an adverb.

ex.en: You get to sample lots of baked things and take home masses of cookies besides.
ex.zh: 你可以品尝许多烘烤食品，此外还能带许多饼干回家。

e.en: Besides is used to emphasize an additional point that you are making, especially one that you consider to be important.

ex.en: The house was out of our price range and too big anyway. Besides, I'd grown fond of our little rented house.
ex.zh: 反正这个房子超出了我们的预算范围，而且也太大了。再说，我已经渐渐喜欢上我们租的小房子了。

d: prep. 除……之外（还）
adv. 而且，再说；此外，也

e.en: Clung is the past tense and past participle of . (cling)

d: v. cling 的过去式及过去分词：抓紧，紧抱；粘住，紧贴；（尤指情感上）依恋；坚持不放。

e.en: A collection of things is a group of similar things that you have deliberately acquired, usually over a period of time.

ex.en: Robert's collection of prints and paintings has been bought over the years.
ex.zh: 罗伯特的印刷收藏品和藏画是多年来花钱买的。

ex.en: The Art Gallery of Ontario has the world's largest collection of sculptures by Henry Moore.
ex.zh: 安大略美术馆关于亨利•摩尔的雕塑收藏品居世界之最。

e.en: A collection of stories, poems, or articles is a number of them published in one book. (作品)

ex.en: Two years ago he published a collection of short stories called "Facing The Music."
ex.zh: 两年前，他出版了一本题为《愿赌服输》的短篇小说集。

e.en: A collection of things is a group of things.

ex.en: ...a collection of modern glass office buildings.
ex.zh: …一组玻璃幕墙的现代办公楼群。

e.en: A fashion designer's new collection consists of the new clothes they have designed for the next season.

ex.en: Her spring/summer collection for this year deliberately uses both simple and rich fabrics.
ex.zh: 她今年的春／夏装系列故意使用了既简单又华贵的材质。

d: n. 收藏品，收集物；募捐；一堆（东西），一群（人）；系列时装；专辑，作品集；领取，收取；收集，采集；收账，收债；（尤指牛津大学的）学院期初（或期末）考试

e.en: Combat is fighting that takes place in a war.

ex.en: Over 16 million men had died in combat.
ex.zh: 一千六百多万人在战斗中阵亡。

ex.en: Yesterday saw hand-to-hand combat in the city.
ex.zh: 昨天那座城里发生了肉搏战。

e.en: A combat is a battle, or a fight between two people.

ex.en: It was the end of a long combat.
ex.zh: 那是一场长时间搏斗的结束。

e.en: If people in authority combat something, they try to stop it from happening.

ex.en: Congress has criticized new government measures to combat crime.
ex.zh: 国会批评了新政府防止犯罪的措施。

d: n. 战斗，搏斗；争论，反对
v. 与……作斗争；防止，减轻
adj. 战斗的；为……斗争的
【名】 （Comb）（法）孔巴（人名）

e.en: A compendium is a short but detailed collection of information, usually in a book.

ex.en: The Roman Catholic Church has issued a compendium of its teachings.
ex.zh: 罗马天主教会已经发行了一份其教义的概略。

d: n. 纲要，概略，摘要；汇编，选集

e.en: Consequential means the same as . 同consequent。

ex.en: The estimate for extra staff and consequential costs such as accommodation was an annual $9.18 million.
ex.zh: 额外员工引起的如住宿成本等估计每年为918万美元。

e.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant.

ex.en: From a medical standpoint a week is usually not a consequential delay.
ex.zh: 从医学观点看，一周通常不被视为是严重的拖延。

d: adj. 随之而来的，作为结果的；间接发生的，间接引起的；重要的，意义重大的

e.en: Conservatism is a political philosophy which believes that if changes need to be made to society, they should be made gradually. You can also refer to the political beliefs of a conservative party in a particular country as conservatism. (政治) 保守主义; (特指某国)

ex.en: ...the philosophy of modern conservatism.
ex.zh: …现代保守主义哲学。

e.en: Conservatism is unwillingness to accept changes and new ideas.

ex.en: The conservatism of the literary establishment in this country is astounding.
ex.zh: 这个国家文学界的守旧态度令人震惊。

d: n. 保守主义；守旧性，保守态度；（会计学）稳健性，谨慎性原则

e.en: When you count, you say all the numbers one after another up to a particular number.

ex.en: He was counting slowly under his breath.
ex.zh: 他在低声慢慢地数数。

e.en: If you count all the things in a group, you add them up in order to find how many there are.

ex.en: I counted the money. It was more than five hundred dollars.
ex.zh: 我数了数钱，有五百多美元。

ex.en: I counted 34 wild goats grazing.
ex.zh: 我数了有34只野山羊在吃草。

e.en: Count up means the same as .

ex.en: Couldn't we just count up our ballots and bring them to the courthouse?
ex.zh: 我们不能就数好我们的选票然后把它们送到法院吗？

e.en: If something or someone counts for something or counts, they are important or valuable. 有价值;

ex.en: Surely it doesn't matter where charities get their money from: what counts is what they do with it.
ex.zh: 当然，慈善组织从哪里得到钱并不重要，重要的是他们用这些钱做什么。

d: v. count 的过去式和过去分词：数，计算；认为，视为，算作；把……计算在内；指望，依靠（on/upon）

e.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

ex.en: He had administrators under him but made the crucial decisions himself.
ex.zh: 尽管他手下有许多官员，但重要的决定还是他自己做。

e.en: 至关重要地

ex.en: Chewing properly is crucially important.
ex.zh: 正确地咀嚼是至关重要的。

d: adj. 至关重要的，决定性的；极好的
adv. 很，非常；深刻地，深沉地；至深处

e.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

ex.en: Mr. Ying is one of those happy people who derive pleasure from helping others.
ex.zh: 英先生是那种助人为乐的快活人。

e.en: If you say that something such as a word or feeling derives or is derived from something else, you mean that it comes from that thing.

ex.en: The name Anastasia is derived from a Greek word meaning "of the resurrection."
ex.zh: 阿纳斯塔西娅这个名字是从一个意为“复活”的希腊词语衍生而来的。

d: v. derive 的第三人称单数现在时；源于，来自（常与 from 连用）；得自，获得（常与 from 连用）；推断，导出

e.en: You use double to indicate that something includes or is made of two things of the same kind.

ex.en: ...a pair of double doors into the room from the new entrance hall.
ex.zh: …一道从新门廊进入房间的双扇门。

e.en: You use double before a singular noun to refer to two things of the same type that occur together, or that are connected in some way.

ex.en: ...an extremely nasty double murder.
ex.zh: …一起极残忍的双人谋杀案。

e.en: You use double to describe something which is twice the normal size or can hold twice the normal quantity of something.

ex.en: ...a double helping of ice cream.
ex.zh: …双份冰激凌。

e.en: A double room is a room intended for two people, usually a couple, to stay or live in.

ex.en: ...bed and breakfast for $180 for two people in a double room.
ex.zh: …给两个人共用一个双人间的价格为$180的住宿加早餐。

d: v. （使）变为两倍，翻倍，成倍增加；加倍努力；快步走；（与 over/up 连用）因疼痛、大笑等而弯腰，蜷缩（double 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 加倍的，成倍的，双倍的（double 的过去分词）

e.en: A dove is a bird that looks like a pigeon but is smaller and lighter in colour. Doves are often used as a symbol of peace.
In politics, you can refer to people who support the use of peaceful methods to solve difficult situations as doves. Compare .

ex.en: A clear split over tactics appears to be emerging between doves and hawks in the party.
ex.zh: 一个明显的战术上的分歧似乎正出现在党内主和派和主战派之间。

e.en: Dove is sometimes used as the past tense of . (dive)

d: n. 鸽子；鸽派人士，主和派人士
n. （Dove）（基督教艺术作品和诗歌中的）圣灵
v. 跳水；潜水；突然大幅贬值，暴跌（dive 的过去式和过去分词）
【名】 （Dove）（美）达夫（人名）

e.en: If you embrace someone, you put your arms around them and hold them tightly, usually in order to show your love or affection for them. You can also say that two people embrace.

ex.en: Penelope came forward and embraced her sister.
ex.zh: 佩内洛普走上前来拥抱了她的妹妹。

ex.en: At first people were sort of crying for joy and embracing each other.
ex.zh: 开始时人们有点喜极而泣，互相拥抱。

e.en: Embrace is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a young couple locked in an embrace.
ex.zh: …紧紧相拥的年轻一对。

e.en: If you embrace a change, political system, or idea, you accept it and start supporting it or believing in it. 欣然接受;

ex.en: He embraces the new information age.
ex.zh: 他欢迎新的信息时代。

e.en: Embrace is also a noun. 欣然接受;

ex.en: The marriage signalled James's embrace of the Catholic faith.
ex.zh: 这场婚姻标志着詹姆士对天主教的信奉。

d: v. 拥抱；欣然接受，乐意采纳；包括，涉及；围绕，环绕
n. 拥抱；接受，信奉

e.en: When a government or authority enacts a proposal, they make it into a law.

ex.en: The authorities have failed so far to enact a law allowing unrestricted emigration.
ex.zh: 当局到目前为止还未能通过一项允许自由移民出境的法律。

e.en: If people enact a story or play, they perform it by acting. 表演.

ex.en: She often enacted the stories told to her by her father.
ex.zh: 她经常把父亲讲给她的故事表演出来。

e.en: If a particular event or situation is enacted, it happens; used especially to talk about something that has happened before. 发生 (尤指过去已发生的事件或情况)

ex.en: It was a scene enacted month after month for eight years.
ex.zh: 这是8年来月复一月出现的场景。

d: v. 制定，通过，颁布（法令）；扮演，表演；使发生，付诸实际

e.en: If someone is your enemy, they hate you or want to harm you.

ex.en: Imagine loving your enemy and doing good to those who hated you.
ex.zh: 想像着爱你的敌人，为仇人做好事。

e.en: If someone is your enemy, they are opposed to you and to what you think or do.

ex.en: Her political enemies were quick to pick up on this series of disasters.
ex.zh: 她的政敌很快注意到这一系列的灾难。
