e.en: The enemy is an army or other force that is opposed to you in a war, or a country with which your country is at war.

ex.en: The enemy were pursued for two miles.
ex.zh: 敌军被追赶了两英里。

e.en: If one thing is the enemy of another thing, the second thing cannot happen or succeed because of the first thing.

ex.en: Reform, as we know, is the enemy of revolution.
ex.zh: 革新，如我们所知，是革命的敌对面。

d: n. 敌人，仇敌，对某种主张、事业等怀有敌意的人（enemy 的复数形式）；敌军，敌方武装人员；大敌，对某种事业、目标等有害或起阻碍作用的人或事物

e.en: If one thing is entwined with another thing, or if you entwine two things, the two things are twisted around each other. (使)

ex.en: His dazed eyes stare at the eels, which still writhe and entwine.
ex.zh: 他茫然地盯着那些仍在扭动缠绕的鳗鱼。

ex.en: Facing each other, the giraffes entwine their necks in the most astonishing manner.
ex.zh: 长颈鹿面对面地站着，以令人无比惊骇的姿势将脖子缠绕到了一起。

e.en: If two things entwine or are entwined, they closely resemble or are linked to each other, and they are difficult to separate or identify. (使)纠缠; (使)

ex.en: The book entwines the personal and the political to chart the history of four generations of the family.
ex.zh: 这本书交织描述了这个家族四代人的个人及政治的历史。

ex.en: Once, years ago, he told me our lives should entwine.
ex.zh: 多年前他曾跟我说，我们的生命应该交织在一起。

d: adj. 缠绕的，盘绕的（常与 with、around 等介词连用）；紧密相连的，交织的（常用 be entwined with）
v. 缠绕，交织（entwine 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 劝告，劝导，劝勉；训词，告诫性讲话，讲道词

e.en: Extremism is the behaviour or beliefs of extremists.

ex.en: Greater demands were being placed on the police by growing violence and left and right-wing extremism.
ex.zh: 不断增加的暴行和左翼右翼极端主义使得需要更多警力。

d: n. 极端主义（尤指政治上的极右或极左）；极端性；过激主义

e.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

ex.en: He was jailed for two years for fraud and deception.
ex.zh: 他因诈骗与欺诈被监禁了两年。

e.en: A fraud is something or someone that deceives people in a way that is illegal or dishonest. 骗人的东西;

ex.en: He's a fraud and a cheat.
ex.zh: 他是一个骗子。

d: n. 欺诈，骗局，诡计；骗子；伪劣品，冒牌货
【名】 （Fraud）（法）弗罗（人名）

e.en: A fringe is a decoration attached to clothes, or other objects such as curtains, consisting of a row of hanging strips or threads.

ex.en: The jacket had leather fringes.
ex.zh: 这件上衣饰有皮流苏。

e.en: To be on the fringe or the fringes of a place means to be on the outside edge of it, or to be in one of the parts that are farthest from its centre.

ex.en: ...black townships located on the fringes of the city.
ex.zh: …位于该城市边缘的黑人居住区。

e.en: The fringe or the fringes of an activity or organization are its less important, least typical, or most extreme parts, rather than its main and central part. 次要部分;

ex.en: The party remained on the fringe of the political scene until last year.
ex.zh: 直到去年该党还一直处于政治舞台的外围。

e.en: A fringe is hair which is cut so that it hangs over your forehead. (头发的)

ex.en: My fringe was cut short, but the rest of my hair was long.
ex.zh: 我的刘海剪得短,但其余的头发长。

d: n. 穗，流苏；刘海儿；（地区、组织或活动范围的）边缘，外围；偏激的人，极端的活动；干扰条纹，散乱边纹；（动物的）缘缨，（植物的）毛缘；（工资外的）补贴，附加福利
v. 在……上装以缘饰，加穗于；形成……的边缘
adj. 次要的，非主流的

e.en: In some systems of government, a governor is a person who is in charge of the political administration of a state, colony, or region. 州长;

ex.en: He was governor of Iowa in the late 1970s.
ex.zh: 他是20世纪70年代末爱荷华州的州长。

e.en: A governor is a member of a committee which controls an organization such as a university or a hospital. (学校、医院等的)

ex.en: Wayne Hansen was added to the board of governors at City University, Bellevue.
ex.zh: 韦恩•汉森已被增补为贝尔维尤城市大学的董事会成员。

e.en: The governor of a prison is the person in charge of it. 监狱长;

ex.en: A new governor took over the prison.
ex.zh: 新一任狱长接管了这所监狱。

d: n. 州长，总督（governor 的复数）；理事，董事（governor 的复数，常作 board of governors）；（英国英语）监狱长，看守长（governor 的复数）；（机械）调速器（governor 的复数）

e.en: The groundwork for something is the early work on it which forms the basis for further work.

ex.en: Yesterday's meeting was to lay the groundwork for the task ahead.
ex.zh: 昨天的会议为后面的任务打下了基础。

d: n. 基础，根基；准备工作，初步工作；地基；地基工程

e.en: You use hers to indicate that something belongs or relates to a woman, girl, or female animal. 她的 (东西)

ex.en: His hand as it shook hers was warm and firm.
ex.zh: 当他握住她的手时，他的手温暖而有力。

ex.en: Professor Camm was a great friend of hers.
ex.zh: 卡姆教授是她的一位挚友。

e.en: In written English, hers is sometimes used to refer to a person without saying whether that person is a man or a woman. Some people dislike this use and prefer to use "his or hers" or "theirs." (书面英语中泛指人) 她的;

ex.en: The author can report other people's results which more or less agree with hers.
ex.zh: 作者可以报道与自己的观点或多或少一致的别人的成果。

d: pron. （上文提过的女性）她的，属于她的
n. （Hers）（法、美、英）埃尔（人名）

e.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

ex.en: Next week they will swap places and will repeat the switch weekly.
ex.zh: 下周他们将互换位置，以后将每周换一次。

ex.en: I know a sculptor who swaps her pieces for drawings by a well-known artist.
ex.zh: 我知道有个雕塑家用她自己的作品去换一位著名画家的画作。

e.en: Swap is also a noun.

ex.en: Over the long term, a swap of some kind is clearly in the public interest.
ex.zh: 从长远看，有点交换显然是为了公共利益。

e.en: If you swap one thing for another, you remove the first thing and replace it with the second, or you stop doing the first thing and start doing the second.

ex.en: Despite the heat, he'd swapped his overalls for a suit and tie.
ex.zh: 尽管天气炎热，他还是把他的工装裤换成了西装和领带。

ex.en: He has swapped his hectic rock star's lifestyle for that of a country gentleman.
ex.zh: 他已放弃紧张忙碌的摇滚明星的生活，改做乡村绅士。

d: n. swap 的复数形式：交换，互换；交换来的东西；（金融）掉期，互换合约（亦译“互惠信贷”）
v. swap 的第三人称单数形式：交换，互换；调换

e.en: A disaster is a very bad accident such as an earthquake or a plane crash, especially one in which a lot of people are killed.

ex.en: It was the second air disaster in the region in less than two months.
ex.zh: 这是不到两个月内该地区内的第2起空难。

e.en: If you refer to something as a disaster, you are emphasizing that you think it is extremely bad or unacceptable. 极为糟糕的事;

ex.en: The whole production was just a disaster!
ex.zh: 整部作品简直是一团糟！

e.en: Disaster is something which has very bad consequences for you.

ex.en: The government brought itself to the brink of fiscal disaster.
ex.zh: 该政府把自己带到了财政灾难的边缘。

e.en: If you say that something is a recipe for disaster, you mean that it is very likely to have unpleasant consequences.

ex.en: You give them a gun, and it's a recipe for disaster.
ex.zh: 你给他们一把枪，那就是祸端。

d: n. 灾难，灾害；祸患，灾难性事物；彻底的失败

e.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying some money or doing a piece of work before a particular time, they fail to do it. 不履行 (义务);

ex.en: The credit card business is down, and more borrowers are defaulting on loans.
ex.zh: 信用卡生意正在走下坡路，更多的借贷人不履行还贷责任。

e.en: Default is also a noun. 不履行;

ex.en: The corporation may be charged with default on its contract with the government.
ex.zh: 该公司可能会被指控违反了与政府签订的合同。

e.en: A default situation is what exists or happens unless someone or something changes it.

ex.en: He appeared unimpressed; but then, unimpressed was his default state.
ex.zh: 他看似不为所动，但是，不为所动就是他的原样。

e.en: In computing, the default is a particular set of instructions which the computer always uses unless the person using the computer gives other instructions.

ex.en: The default setting on Windows Explorer will not show these files.
ex.zh: 视窗浏览器上的默认系统设定不显示这些文档。

d: n. 不履行，违约；默认，系统设定值；缺席，弃权
v. 违约，不履行义务；默认，预设；弃权，未到场
adj. 默认的

e.en: If there is a vogue for something, it is very popular and fashionable.

ex.en: Despite the vogue for so-called health teas, there is no evidence that they are any healthier.
ex.zh: 尽管所谓的保健茶成了时尚，但并没有证据表明这种茶更有益于健康。

e.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable. If it comes into vogue, it becomes very popular and fashionable. 正在流行;

ex.en: Pale colours are much more in vogue than autumnal bronzes and coppers.
ex.zh: 浅色比秋季的古铜色和紫铜色更为流行。

d: n. 流行，时髦
adj. 时髦的，流行的
v. （模仿模特在 T 形台上的姿态）随音乐跳舞
【名】 （Vogue）（葡）沃格（人名）

e.en: A prison is a building where criminals are kept as punishment.

ex.en: The prison's inmates are being kept in their cells.
ex.zh: 监狱里的囚犯们被关在各自的牢房里。

d: n. 监狱，牢房；监禁，监狱制度；难以脱身的地方（或处境），牢笼
v. 禁锢，关押
【名】 （Prison）（德）普里松（人名）

e.en: When you speak, you use your voice in order to say something.

ex.en: He tried to speak, but for once, his voice had left him.
ex.zh: 他试图说话，但这一次，他已说不出声。

ex.en: I rang the hotel and spoke to Louie.
ex.zh: 我打电话给宾馆，跟路易通了话。

e.en: 口头的

ex.en: ...a marked decline in the standards of written and spoken English.
ex.zh: …书面和口头英语标准的明显下降。

e.en: When someone speaks to a group of people, they make a speech. 演讲;

ex.en: When speaking to the seminar Mr. Franklin spoke of his experience, gained on a recent visit to Trinidad.
ex.zh: 在研讨会上发言时，富兰克林先生谈到了他最近一次在特立尼达访问时所获得的经验。

ex.en: He's determined to speak at the Democratic Convention.
ex.zh: 他决心在民主党大会上发言。

e.en: If you speak for a group of people, you make their views and demands known, or represent them. 为…说话;

ex.en: He said it was the job of the Church to speak for the underprivileged.
ex.zh: 他说为弱势群体说话是教会的职责。

ex.en: I speak for all 7,000 members of our organization.
ex.zh: 我代表我们组织的全体7000名成员发言。

d: n. （Speaks）人名；（英）斯皮克斯

e.en: An economist is a person who studies, teaches, or writes about economics.

d: n. 经济学家
n. 秘密赞同者；密码学（同 cryptography）；加密货币（同 cryptocurrency）
adj. 秘密的，隐蔽的；加密的，关于暗号的，用密码写的（同 cryptographic）

e.en: A tycoon is a person who is successful in business and so has become rich and powerful. (工商界的)

ex.en: ...a self-made Irish-American property tycoon.
ex.zh: …一个靠自己奋斗成功的爱尔兰裔美国房地产大亨。

d: n. 企业界大亨，巨头；巨富

e.en: Iranian means belonging or relating to Iran, or to its people or culture. 伊朗的; 伊朗人的;
An Iranian is an Iranian citizen, or a person of Iranian origin. 伊朗人;

d: adj. 伊朗的；伊朗人的；伊朗语的
n. 伊朗人；伊朗语

e.en: A sound is something that you hear.

ex.en: Peter heard the sound of gunfire.
ex.zh: 彼得听见了枪炮声。

ex.en: Liza was so frightened she couldn't make a sound.
ex.zh: 莉莎惊吓得发不出任何声音。

e.en: a relatively narrow channel between two larger areas of sea or between an island and the mainland
Sound is energy that travels in waves through air, water, or other substances, and can be heard.

ex.en: The aeroplane will travel at twice the speed of sound.
ex.zh: 飞机将以两倍于音速的速度飞行。

e.en: The sound on a television, radio, or CD player is what you hear coming from the machine. Its loudness can be controlled. (可调大小声的)

ex.en: She went and turned the sound down.
ex.zh: 她过去把声音调小。

d: n. 声音，声响；听力范围，听距；乐音；（音乐演出、电影等的）音响录制和播出，音响制作；无线电广播；声音，音响；（个人或乐队的）音乐特色，音乐风格；流行音乐（sounds）；海峡，海湾；厄勒海峡（the Sound）；印象，感觉；（检查体腔的）医用探子
v. （使）发声，（使）作响；发出（警告等），（以……语调）发表；测量（水体）的深度；试探，探询；听起来像；（从嗓音中）听起来；（用于谈论印象或观点）听起来，似乎；发音；听诊（肺或其他体腔）；（医）用探子检查（人的膀胱或其他内腔）；（尤指鲸鱼）向深海潜入
adj. 无损伤的，健康的，坚实的；合理的，明智的，可靠的；全面的，透彻的；酣睡的，沉睡的；（惩罚）严厉的；不错的，实实在在的；资金充实的
adv. 酣畅地

e.en: An island is a piece of land that is completely surrounded by water.

ex.en: ...the Canary Islands.
ex.zh: …加那利群岛。

d: n. 岛，岛屿；岛状物，孤立体；脑岛，胰岛
v. 使成岛（状），使孤立
【名】 （Island）（英）艾兰（人名）

e.en: The eve of a particular event or occasion is the day before it, or the period of time just before it. 前一天;

ex.en: ...on the eve of his 27th birthday.
ex.zh: …在他27岁生日的前夕。

d: n. 前夕，前一天；傍晚，黄昏

e.en: To attack a person or place means to try to hurt or damage them using physical violence.

ex.en: Fifty civilians in Masawa were killed when government planes attacked the town.
ex.zh: 马萨瓦50名平民在政府飞机袭击该市时丧生。

ex.en: He bundled the old lady into her hallway and brutally attacked her.
ex.zh: 他把老太太推进她家门厅里，并且野蛮地袭击了她。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a campaign of air attacks on strategic targets.
ex.zh: …对战略目标的空袭行动。

e.en: If you attack a person, belief, idea, or act, you criticize them strongly.

ex.en: He publicly attacked the people who've been calling for secret ballot nominations.
ex.zh: 他公开抨击了那些一直要求秘密投票提名的人。

e.en: Attack is also a noun.

ex.en: The role of the state as a prime mover in planning social change has been under attack.
ex.zh: 国家作为规划社会变革发起者的角色已经遭到抨击。

d: v. 袭击，攻击；批评，抨击；侵害，侵蚀（attack 的第三人称单数）
n. 袭击，攻击；批评，抨击；（疾病等的）发作；（病虫、化学物质等的）损害，伤害或侵蚀（attack 的复数）

e.en: A hospital is a place where people who are ill are cared for by nurses and doctors.

ex.en: ...a children's hospital with 120 beds.
ex.zh: …一个有120张床位的儿童医院。

d: n. [医]医院（hospital 的复数）
adj. （与）网络（有关）的

e.en: If you expect something to happen, you believe that it will happen.

ex.en: ...a workman who expects to lose his job in the next few weeks.
ex.zh: …一个预料会在接下来几周里失业的工人。

ex.en: The talks are expected to continue until tomorrow.
ex.zh: 会谈预料将持续到明天。

e.en: If you are expecting something or someone, you believe that they will be delivered to you or come to you soon, often because this has been arranged earlier. (常指因已安排而)

ex.en: I wasn't expecting a visitor.
ex.zh: 我没有预期会有访客。

e.en: If you expect something, or expect a person to do something, you believe that it is your right to have that thing, or the person's duty to do it for you.

ex.en: He wasn't expecting our hospitality.
ex.zh: 他没有期待我们的热情款待。

ex.en: I do expect to have some time to myself in the evenings.
ex.zh: 我真期待晚上能有点儿自己的时间。

e.en: If you tell someone not to expect something, you mean that the thing is unlikely to happen as they have planned or imagined, and they should not hope that it will.

ex.en: Don't expect an instant cure.
ex.zh: 别指望会有立竿见影的疗效。

ex.en: You cannot expect to like all the people you will work with.
ex.zh: 你不能指望喜欢所有和你一起工作的人。

d: v. expect 的第三人称单数一般现在时形式；期待，预期，预料：认为某事会发生或某人会做某事，或等待某人或某事物的到来；要求，指望：认为某人应该做某事；（用于 be expecting）怀孕，怀胎；（口语，用于 I expect）我想，料想。

e.en: An airport is a place where aircraft land and take off, and that has buildings and facilities for passengers.

ex.en: ...Heathrow Airport, the busiest international airport in the world.
ex.zh: …希斯罗飞机场——世界上最繁忙的国际机场。

d: n. （航）机场，航空港（airport 的复数形式）

e.en: A rail is a horizontal bar attached to posts or around the edge of something as a fence or support.

ex.en: They had to walk across an emergency footbridge, holding onto a rope that served as a rail.
ex.zh: 他们不得不抓着当作栏杆用的绳子，走过一架应急人行桥。

e.en: A rail is a horizontal bar that you hang things on. (挂物用的)

ex.en: This pair of curtains will fit a rail up to 7 ft 6 in wide.
ex.zh: 这副窗帘适合安装在宽度为7英尺6英寸的横杆上。

e.en: Rails are the steel bars which trains run on.

ex.en: The train left the rails but somehow forced its way back onto the line.
ex.zh: 火车偏离了铁轨，但又设法回到了原来的轨道上。

e.en: If you travel or send something by rail, you travel or send it on a train. 乘火车; 用火车 (运送)

ex.en: The president travelled by rail to his home town.
ex.zh: 总统乘火车回到了家乡。

d: v. rail 的过去式和过去分词：抱怨，责骂（常与 against/at 连用，表示对某人或某事强烈不满或愤怒）；用栏杆把……围住或隔开，给……装上栏杆

e.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents. (选举中)

ex.en: He won last month's presidential election by a landslide.
ex.zh: 他以绝对优势赢得了上个月的总统选举。

e.en: A landslide is a large amount of earth and rocks falling down a cliff or the side of a mountain.

ex.en: The storm caused landslides and flooding in Savona.
ex.zh: 暴风雨引发了萨沃纳的山崩和水灾。

d: n. （地质）山崩，滑坡，山体滑坡；（选举中的）压倒性胜利，大胜利
vi. 发生山崩，发生滑坡；以压倒优势获胜

e.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

ex.en: Polls show that the European treaty has gained support in Denmark.
ex.zh: 民意测验显示，欧洲条约已经在丹麦获得支持。

ex.en: We are doing a weekly poll on the president, and clearly his popularity has declined.
ex.zh: 我们正在对总统进行每周一次的民意测验，很显然他的受欢迎度已经下降了。

e.en: If you are polled on something, you are asked what you think about it as part of a survey.

ex.en: More than 18,000 people were polled.
ex.zh: 18000多人接受了民意测验。

ex.en: Audiences were going to be polled on which of three pieces of contemporary music they liked best.
ex.zh: 听众将就3首现代乐曲中最喜欢哪一首接受民意调查。

e.en: The polls means an election for a country's government, or the place where people go to vote in an election. 政治大选;

ex.en: Incumbent officeholders are difficult to defeat at the polls.
ex.zh: 现任官员很难在选举中被击败。

ex.en: Voters are due to go to the polls on Sunday to elect a new president.
ex.zh: 选民们按计划将于周日前往投票站选举新总统。

e.en: If a political party or a candidate polls a particular number or percentage of votes, they get that number or percentage of votes in an election.

ex.en: The result showed he had polled enough votes to force a second ballot.
ex.zh: 结果显示他获得了足够的选票来促使第二轮选举。

d: n. 民意调查，民意测验；投票（the polls 指选举或投票站）；投票模块（poll 的复数形式）
v. 对……进行民意测验；获得（选票）（poll 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Supporters are people who support someone or something, for example a political leader or a sports team.

ex.en: Attacks against opposition supporters are continuing at levels higher than before the election.
ex.zh: 对反对派支持者的攻击依然持续，程度比竞选前更猛烈。

d: n. supporter 的复数：支持者，拥护者；球迷；支持单位，协办单位。

e.en: If you have to contend with a problem or difficulty, you have to deal with it or overcome it.

ex.en: It is time, once again, to contend with racism.
ex.zh: 又是对付种族主义的时候了。

e.en: If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

ex.en: The government contends that he is fundamentalist.
ex.zh: 政府辩称他是原教旨主义者。

e.en: If you contend with someone for something such as power, you compete with them to try to get it. 争夺 (权力等)

ex.en: ...the two main groups contending for power.
ex.zh: …争夺权力的两大主要集团。

ex.en: Small-market clubs such as the Kansas City Royals have had trouble contending with richer teams for championships.
ex.zh: 像堪萨斯城皇家队这样市场规模较小的俱乐部一直难以同财力更雄厚的球队争夺冠军。

d: v. contend 的过去式和过去分词：1. 竞争，争夺（常与 for 连用）；2. 主张，声称，辩称（正式，常接 that 从句）；3. 对付，处理，克服（contend with 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: a complex red organic pigment containing ferrous iron, present in haemoglobin

d: n. （生物化学）血红素，亚铁血红素（血红蛋白、肌红蛋白等中的含铁卟啉辅基，亦作 haem）

e.en: Your bones are the hard parts inside your body that together form your skeleton.

ex.en: Many passengers suffered broken bones.
ex.zh: 许多乘客骨折了。

ex.en: The body is made up primarily of bone, muscle, and fat.
ex.zh: 人体主要由骨、肌肉和脂肪组成。

e.en: If you bone a piece of meat or fish, you remove the bones from it before cooking it. 去 (肉、鱼)

ex.en: Make sure that you do not pierce the skin when boning the chicken thighs.
ex.zh: 给鸡腿去骨时，确保不要刺破皮。

e.en: A bone tool or ornament is made of bone.

ex.en: ...a small, expensive pocketknife with a bone handle.
ex.zh: …一把昂贵的、带骨制刀把的小刀。

e.en: The bare bones of something are its most basic parts or details.

ex.en: There are not even the bare bones of a garden here – I've got nothing.
ex.zh: 这儿连花园的最基本的东西都没有–我一无所获。

d: n. 骨，骨头；骨质；基本结构，基本（bones）
v. 挑刺，剔骨头；施骨肥于；（与某人）性交；（为应付考试）临时突击
adv. 非常，完全地
【名】 （Bone）（英）博恩，（法、西、罗、塞）博内，（老）奔（人名）

e.en: A compound is an enclosed area of land that is used for a particular purpose.

ex.en: They took refuge in the embassy compound.
ex.zh: 他们在大使馆围区内避难。

ex.en: ...a military compound.
ex.zh: …一个军事管辖区。

e.en: In chemistry, a compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements.

ex.en: Organic compounds contain carbon in their molecules.
ex.zh: 有机化合物的分子里含碳。

e.en: If something is a compound of different things, it consists of those things.

ex.en: Honey is basically a compound of water, two types of sugar, vitamins and enzymes.
ex.zh: 蜂蜜主要是水、两种糖、维生素和酶的混合物。

e.en: Compound is used to indicate that something consists of two or more parts or things.

ex.en: ...the big compound eyes of dragonflies.
ex.zh: …蜻蜓的大复眼。

d: n. 混合物，化合物；复合词；大院，有围墙的场地
adj. 复合的，混合的；以复利计算的
v. 使加重，使恶化；合成，混合；以复利计算支付；和解，私了

e.en: Organic methods of farming and gardening do not use pesticides, chemical fertilizers, growth hormones, or antibiotics, so that the food produced does not contain toxic chemicals.

ex.en: Organic farming is expanding everywhere.
ex.zh: 有机农业在各处发展。

e.en: 有机地

ex.en: ...organically grown vegetables.
ex.zh: …有机种植的蔬菜。

e.en: Organic substances are produced by or found in living things.

ex.en: Incorporating organic material into chalky soils will reduce the alkalinity.
ex.zh: 将有机物质掺入白垩质土壤中将会降低碱性。

e.en: Organic change or development happens gradually and naturally rather than suddenly.

ex.en: ...to manage the company and supervise its organic growth.
ex.zh: …管理公司并指导其逐步发展。

d: adj. 有机的，绿色的；有机物的，生物的；构成有机整体的，不可分割的；（发生、发展过程）自然的，演进的；器官的，器质性的；仿自然形态的
n. 有机物质；有机食品
炎生龙属
n. 血红蛋白；血色素（hemoglobin 的英式拼写；红细胞内一种含铁的携氧蛋白质，使血液呈红色，主要功能是将氧气从肺部输送到全身组织）

e.en: Oxygen is a colourless gas that exists in large quantities in the air. All plants and animals need oxygen in order to live.

ex.en: The human brain needs to be without oxygen for only four minutes before permanent damage occurs.
ex.zh: 人脑缺氧只需4分钟就会造成永久性损伤。

d: n. 氧，氧气
adj. 鲜为人知的
n. （拉丁语 caput 的复数）头；人；（用于 per capita）每人、人均；（Capita）人名，西、意语音译卡皮塔

e.en: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

ex.en: For sentimental reasons I wanted to delay my departure until June 1980.
ex.zh: 由于感情上的原因，我想把启程时间推迟到1980年6月。

ex.en: They had delayed having children, for the usual reason, to establish their careers.
ex.zh: 他们推迟了要孩子，为了要建立事业这个通常的理由。

e.en: To delay someone or something means to make them late or to slow them down. 延误;

ex.en: Can you delay him in some way?
ex.zh: 你能用什么办法耽搁他一下吗？

ex.en: Various setbacks and problems delayed production.
ex.zh: 各种各样的挫折和问题延误了生产。

e.en: If you delay, you deliberately take longer than necessary to do something.

ex.en: If he delayed any longer, the sun would be up.
ex.zh: 如果他再拖延下去，太阳就要升起来了。

e.en: If there is a delay, something does not happen until later than planned or expected.

ex.en: They claimed that such a delay wouldn't hurt anyone.
ex.zh: 他们声称这样的耽搁不会伤害任何人。

d: n. 延迟；延期；延误（delay 的复数）
v. 延误；推迟；拖延（delay 的第三人称单数）

e.en: digital compact cassette

d: abbr. 数据通信信道（Data Communication Channel）；更改设计委员会（Design Change Committee）；袖珍数字磁带（Digital Compact Cassette）

e.en: The handover of something is when possession or control of it is given by one person or group of people to another.

ex.en: The handover is expected to be completed in the next ten years.
ex.zh: 移交预计在下个10年内完成。

d: n. 移交，交接；（电信）切换，越区切换

e.en: A mark is a small area of something such as dirt that has accidentally got onto a surface or piece of clothing.

ex.en: The dogs are always rubbing against the wall and making dirty marks.
ex.zh: 这些狗总是往墙上蹭，留下了点点污斑。

e.en: If something marks a surface, or if the surface marks, the surface is damaged by marks or a mark. 玷污;

ex.en: Leather overshoes were put on the horses' hooves to stop them from marking the turf.
ex.zh: 皮套子被套在了马蹄上，防止它们弄脏了跑马场。

e.en: A mark is a written or printed symbol, for example a letter of the alphabet.

ex.en: He made marks with a pencil.
ex.zh: 他用铅笔作了记号。

e.en: If you mark something with a particular word or symbol, you write that word or symbol on it.

ex.en: The bank marks the cheque "certified."
ex.zh: 银行在支票上标有“保付”的字样。

ex.en: Mark them with a symbol.
ex.zh: 用个记号把他们标出来。

d: n. （mark 的复数）标记，记号，符号；痕迹，污点；引号；分数，成绩；标志，特征，指标；唛头，装运标记；商标，牌号；（台球）台面标志；（Marks）人名：（英、德、意、瑞典、西、捷）马克斯，（俄）马克思
v. （mark 的第三人称单数）标志，表示，纪念；作记号，标示；给…打分，批改；留下痕迹，弄脏

e.en: You can describe someone who is clever or intelligent as smart. 聪明的;

ex.en: He thinks he's smarter than Sarah is.
ex.zh: 他认为他比萨拉更聪明。

e.en: Smart people and things are pleasantly neat and clean in appearance.

ex.en: He was smart and well groomed but not good looking.
ex.zh: 他时髦而且打扮整齐，但是长得不帅。

ex.en: I was dressed in a smart navy blue suit.
ex.zh: 我穿一身整洁的海军蓝制服。

e.en: 整洁地

ex.en: He dressed very smartly, which was important in those days.
ex.zh: 他穿得非常整洁，这在当时很重要。

e.en: A smart place or event is connected with wealthy and fashionable people.

ex.en: ...smart dinner parties.
ex.zh: …时髦的宴会。

d: adj. 聪明的，明智的；（人）衣着得体的；整洁而漂亮的，光鲜的；耍小聪明的，不恭的；时髦的，高档的；迅速有力的，迅猛的；智能的
v. （身体部位）感到刺痛；（因批评、失败等）难过，烦恼
n. 剧痛，刺痛；痛苦，苦恼；聪明，敏锐（smarts）
adv. 机敏地，整洁地，潇洒地

e.en: A subsidiary or a subsidiary company is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

ex.en: WM Financial Services is a subsidiary of Washington Mutual.
ex.zh: 华盛顿互惠银行金融服务公司是华盛顿互惠银行的子公司。

e.en: If something is subsidiary, it is less important than something else with which it is connected.

ex.en: The marketing department has always played a subsidiary role to the sales department.
ex.zh: 营销部一直都扮演着销售部的辅助角色。

d: n. 子公司，附属公司；辅助者
adj. 次要的，附属的；子公司的
v. 螺旋形运动；（价格、成本、债务、失业率等）急剧增长或失控恶化（spiral 的现在分词）；使……成螺旋形
adj. （多作定语）急剧上升的

e.en: A farmer is a person who owns or manages a farm.

d: n. 农民；农场主（farmer 的复数）

e.en: When you talk, you use spoken language to express your thoughts, ideas, or feelings.

ex.en: He was too distressed to talk.
ex.zh: 他伤心得说不出话来。

ex.en: The boys all began to talk at once.
ex.zh: 男孩们都马上开始说话了。

e.en: Talk is also a noun.

ex.en: That's not the kind of talk one usually hears from accountants.
ex.zh: 那不是人们通常从会计人员那里听到的那种话。

e.en: If you talk to someone, you have a conversation with them. You can also say that two people talk.

ex.en: We talked and laughed a lot.
ex.zh: 我们畅怀说笑。

ex.en: I talked to him yesterday.
ex.zh: 我昨天和他谈过。

e.en: Talk is also a noun.

ex.en: We had a long talk about her father, Tony, who was a friend of mine.
ex.zh: 关于她父亲托尼我们进行了一次长时间的交谈，托尼是我的一个朋友。

d: n. （talk 的复数）会谈，谈判；谈话，交谈；讲话，讲座；语言；谣言
v. （talk 的第三人称单数）说话，讲话；交谈；谈论，讨论；协商

e.en: A path is a long strip of ground that people walk along to get from one place to another.

ex.en: We followed the path along the clifftops.
ex.zh: 我们沿着悬崖顶的小径行进。

ex.en: Feet had worn a path in the rock.
ex.zh: 脚步已在岩石里踏出一条小径。

e.en: Your path is the space ahead of you as you move along. (前面的)

ex.en: A group of reporters blocked his path.
ex.zh: 一群记者堵住了他的路。

e.en: The path of something is the line that it moves along in a particular direction. 路线;

ex.en: He stepped without looking into the path of a reversing car.
ex.zh: 他一步迈了出去，连看都没看一眼一辆正在倒车的汽车。

ex.en: ...people who live near airports or under the flight path of aeroplanes.
ex.zh: …住在机场附近或者飞机的飞行线路下面的人们。

e.en: A path that you take is a particular course of action or way of achieving something. 行动路线;

ex.en: They appear to have chosen the path of cooperation rather than confrontation.
ex.zh: 他们好像选择了合作而不是对抗的行动路线。

d: n. 小径，小道；（开出的）通道；（事物或人移动的）路线，轨迹；（有助于实现某事的）道路，途径；通勤火车时刻表；（计算机）路径

e.en: If you demand something such as information or action, you ask for it in a very forceful way.

ex.en: Human rights groups are demanding an investigation into the shooting.
ex.zh: 人权组织正强烈要求对这一枪击案进行调查。

ex.en: Russia demanded that UNITA send a delegation to the peace talks.
ex.zh: 俄罗斯强烈要求安哥拉彻底独立全国同盟派遣一个代表团参加和谈。

e.en: If one thing demands another, the first needs the second in order to happen or be dealt with successfully.

ex.en: He said the task of reconstruction would demand much patience, hard work, and sacrifice.
ex.zh: 他说重建工作会需要高度坚韧、勤劳和奉献。

e.en: A demand is a firm request for something.

ex.en: There have been demands for services from tenants up there.
ex.zh: 那边的房客们有服务的明确要求。

e.en: If you refer to demand, or to the demand for something, you are referring to how many people want to have it, do it, or buy it.

ex.en: Another flight would be arranged on Saturday if sufficient demand arose.
ex.zh: 如果有足够的需求量，周六就会安排另一个航班。

d: v. 强烈要求；需要，需求
n. 坚决的要求；需求，需求量；（困难的）要求
【名】 （Demand）（德）德曼德（人名）

e.en: The third item in a series is the one that you count as number three. 第3

ex.en: I sleep on the third floor.
ex.zh: 我睡在3楼。

e.en: A third is one of three equal parts of something. 1/3

ex.en: A third of the cost went into technology and services.
ex.zh: 1/3的成本用于技术和服务。

e.en: You say third when you want to make a third point or give a third reason for something. 第三 (点)

ex.en: First, interest rates may take longer to fall than is hoped. Second, lending may fall. Third, bad loans could wipe out much of any improvement.
ex.zh: 首先，利率下调可能比预期的时间要久。第二，贷款可能下降。第三，坏帐可能抵消大部分的成效。

e.en: A third is the lowest honours degree that can be obtained from a British university. 三等学位 (英国大学的最低荣誉学位)

ex.en: ...Ms. Hodge, who graduated in 2002 with a third in economics.
ex.zh: …霍奇小姐，2002年毕业并获得经济学三等学位。

d: num. 第三
n. 三分之一；（机动车变速器的）第三档；（音乐）三度音；三等学位（英国大学中低于平均水平的学位）
adj. 第三的；三分之一的
adv. 第三（点）

e.en: huge or excessive 巨大的;

ex.en: a thumping loss

d: v. （thump 的现在分词）捶击；猛力地移动；重步走；怦怦直跳；（非正式）彻底击垮
adj. （非正式）巨大的，极多的；发出重击声的；捶击的；（音乐）节奏有力、声音响亮的
n. 重击声；砰的一声

e.en: A quarter is one of four equal parts of something. 1/4

ex.en: A quarter of the residents are over 55 years old.
ex.zh: 1/4的居民在55岁以上。

ex.en: Prices have fallen by a quarter since January.
ex.zh: 自1月份以来，物价下降了1/4。

e.en: Quarter is also a predeterminer.

ex.en: The largest asteroid is Ceres, which is about a quarter the size of the moon.
ex.zh: 最大的小行星是谷神星，其体积大约是月球的四分之一。

e.en: Quarter is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...the past quarter century.
ex.zh: …过去的四分之一世纪。

e.en: A quarter is an American or Canadian coin that is worth 25 cents. (美国或加拿大) 25

ex.en: I dropped a quarter into the slot of the pay phone.
ex.zh: 我往付费电话的投币口里投了一枚25分的硬币。

d: n. 四分之一；一刻钟，十五分钟；季度，三个月；学季，四分之一学年；（城镇中的）区；个人，群体；（士兵、服务人员等的）营房；上弦（或下弦）月；（美式足球的）一节；（美国和加拿大的）二十五分硬币；四分之一磅；（对败者的）宽恕，仁慈；四分之一畜体（或鸟身）；（马的）腰腿，臀部及后腿（quarters）；（罗盘上四个点之一所指的）方向；船侧后部；盾的四分之一
v. 将……四等分；把……降至原先的四分之一；提供食宿；在（某处）来回走动；移动，斜向行进；展示，炫耀（盾的四分之一部位上的不同纹章）
adj. 四分之一的

e.en: Your expectations are your strong hopes or beliefs that something will happen or that you will get something that you want.

ex.en: Their hope, and their expectation, was that she was going to be found safe and that she would be returned to her family.
ex.zh: 他们的希望和期盼是她被找到时安全无恙并被送回她家。

e.en: A person's expectations are strong beliefs they have about the proper way someone should behave or something should happen.

ex.en: Stephen Chase had determined to live up to the expectations of the company.
ex.zh: 斯蒂芬·蔡斯已决心不辜负公司的期望。

d: n. 期望，预期；（数学、统计学）期望值（expectation 的复数）
n. 伊布斯托克（英国地名）

e.en: A bull is a male animal of the cow family.
Some other male animals, including elephants and whales, are called bulls.

ex.en: Suddenly a massive bull elephant with huge tusks charged us.
ex.zh: 突然，一只体形壮硕、长着巨型象牙的雄象朝我们冲了过来。

e.en: In the stock market, bulls are people who buy shares in expectation of a price rise, in order to make a profit by selling the shares again after a short time. Compare bear. (股票市场上)

ex.en: The bulls argue stock prices are low and there are bargains to be had.
ex.zh: 那些买空者认为股价很低，有些便宜股可以买进。

e.en: In the Roman Catholic church, a papal bull is an official statement on a particular subject that is issued by the pope.

d: n. 公牛；雄性大型动物；买空者，多头；教皇诏书，教皇训谕；废话，胡说八道；靶心
v. 用力推，猛推；（母牛）发情
【名】 （Bull）（英、葡、瑞典、芬、挪、德）布尔（人名）
n. 埃塞俄比亚（非洲东北部内陆国家，首都亚的斯亚贝巴）

e.en: Same-sex people are the same sex as each other, or the same sex as a particular person.

ex.en: ...women's same-sex friends.
ex.zh: ...女人们的同性朋友。

d: adj. 同性的

e.en: A donkey is an animal which is like a horse but which is smaller and has longer ears.

d: n. 驴；蠢人，傻瓜；发动机；（尤指在艺术学校中供艺术家跨坐的）低凳；（儿童玩的）换牌纸牌戏

e.en: If someone or something disrupts an event, system, or process, they cause difficulties that prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way. 妨碍;

ex.en: Anti-war protesters disrupted the debate.
ex.zh: 反战示威者们扰乱了辩论。

d: v. 中断，扰乱；使瓦解，使分裂，彻底改变（某物）的结构；（商业/科技）颠覆（行业、领域），彻底变革（disrupt 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 中断的，有间断的

e.en: Chaos is a state of complete disorder and confusion.

ex.en: The world's first transatlantic balloon race ended in chaos last night.
ex.zh: 世界首次横渡大西洋的气球比赛昨晚在混乱中结束了。

d: n. 混乱，无秩序状态；混沌
【名】 （Chaos）（西）查奥斯（人名）

e.en: If you refer to a way of doing something, you are referring to how you can do it, for example, the action you can take or the method you can use to achieve it. 方式;

ex.en: Freezing isn't a bad way of preserving food.
ex.zh: 冷冻不失为保存食品的一种好方法。

ex.en: I worked myself into a frenzy plotting ways to make him jealous.
ex.zh: 我绞尽脑汁，处心积虑，就是为了让他嫉妒。

e.en: If you talk about the way someone does something, you are talking about the qualities their action has. 态度;

ex.en: She smiled in a friendly way.
ex.zh: 她友好地笑了笑。

ex.en: He had a strange way of talking.
ex.zh: 他说话的样子很奇怪。

e.en: If a general statement or description is true in a particular way, this is the form of it that is true in a particular case. 形式;

ex.en: Computerized reservation systems help airline profits in several ways.
ex.zh: 电子订票系统让航空公司在好几个方面获利。

ex.en: She was afraid in a way that was quite new to her.
ex.zh: 她感到害怕，而这种害怕是以前不曾有过的。

e.en: You use way in expressions such as in some ways, in many ways, and in every way to indicate the degree or extent to which a statement is true. 某方面;

ex.en: In some ways, the official opening is a formality.
ex.zh: 从某些方面来说，官方开幕仪式是个形式而已。

d: n. 方法，方式，途径（way 的复数）；方面（常用于 in many ways、in some ways 等短语）；习俗，习惯，惯常行为方式；（造船）滑道，滑路；（Ways）人名，瓦伊斯（音译）

e.en: If you disturb someone, you interrupt what they are doing and upset them.

ex.en: Did you sleep well? I didn't want to disturb you. You looked so peaceful.
ex.zh: 你睡得好吗？我不想打扰你。你看起来如此平静。

e.en: If something disturbs you, it makes you feel upset or worried. 使不安;

ex.en: I dream about him, dreams so vivid that they disturb me for days.
ex.zh: 我梦到他了，梦是那么栩栩如生以至于困扰了我好几天。

e.en: If something is disturbed, its position or shape is changed.

ex.en: He'd placed his notes in the brown envelope. They hadn't been disturbed.
ex.zh: 他已把票据放在那个棕色信封里了。票据没有被动过。

e.en: If something disturbs a situation or atmosphere, it spoils it or causes trouble.

ex.en: What could possibly disturb such tranquillity?
ex.zh: 有什么能破坏这种宁静？

d: v. 打扰，妨碍；使焦虑，使烦恼；移动，弄乱

e.en: A wall is one of the vertical sides of a building or room. 墙;

ex.en: Kathryn leaned against the wall of the church.
ex.zh: 凯瑟琳倚靠在教堂的墙壁上。

ex.en: The bedroom walls would be papered with chintz.
ex.zh: 卧室的墙上将会贴上印花棉布。

e.en: A wall is a long narrow vertical structure made of stone or brick that surrounds or divides an area of land.

ex.en: He sat on the wall in the sun.
ex.zh: 他坐在围墙上晒太阳。

e.en: The wall of something that is hollow is its side. (中空物体的)

ex.en: He ran his fingers along the inside walls of the box.
ex.zh: 他用手摸了摸箱子的内壁。

e.en: If you say that something or someone is driving you up the wall, you are emphasizing that they annoy and irritate you.

ex.en: The heat is driving me up the wall.
ex.zh: 我热得快疯了。

d: n. 城墙，围墙；墙，壁，墙壁；屏障，壁垒；（感情或行为的）障碍，隔阂；人墙，隔离墙；（身体器官或动植物细胞等的）外壁；（盒子或管道等空心物的）内壁；堆得像墙一样的大量东西；柏林墙（the Wall）；防波堤，防洪堤；（尤指宏大的）峭立面；围住矿脉（或矿层）的岩石；梅戈拉毛眼蝶（同 wall brown）
v. 用墙围住（一区域）；砌墙封闭，砌墙堵住（wall sth. up）；把……关起来，禁闭（wall sb./sth. in/up）
adj. 墙壁的
【名】 （Wall）（英）沃尔，（德、芬、捷、瑞典）瓦尔（人名）

e.en: If someone or something remains in a particular state or condition, they stay in that state or condition and do not change. 继续;

ex.en: The three men remained silent.
ex.zh: 这3个人保持沉默。

ex.en: The government remained in control.
ex.zh: 政府继续控制着局势。

e.en: If you remain in a place, you stay there and do not move away. 留在;

ex.en: They have asked the residents to remain in their homes.
ex.zh: 他们已经要求居民待在自己家里。

e.en: You can say that something remains when it still exists. 继续存在;

ex.en: The wider problem remains.
ex.zh: 更广泛的问题依然存在。

e.en: If something remains to be done, it has not yet been done and still needs to be done. 剩下; 余留;

ex.en: Major questions remain to be answered about his work.
ex.zh: 关于他工作的主要问题仍有待回答。

d: n. 剩余物，残留物；遗体，遗骸；古迹，遗迹
v. 仍然是，保持不变；逗留，留下；剩余，余留（remain 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Your native country or area is the country or area where you were born and brought up. 出生并从小长大的 (国家或地方)

ex.en: It was his first visit to his native country since 1948.
ex.zh: 这是1948年以来他首次访问祖国。

e.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region. 本国人;

ex.en: Dr. Aubin is a native of St. Louis.
ex.zh: 奥宾医生是圣路易斯人。

e.en: Native is also an adjective. 本国的;

ex.en: Joshua Halpern is a native Northern Californian.
ex.zh: 乔舒亚·哈尔彭是土生土长的北加州人。

e.en: Some European people use native to refer to a person living in a non-Western country who belongs to the race or tribe that the majority of people there belong to. This use could cause offence.

ex.en: They used force to banish the natives from the more fertile land.
ex.zh: 他们用武力将土著人驱逐出更加肥沃的土地。

d: adj. 本地出生的，出生地的；天生的，天赋的；原产于某地的，土产的；母语的；土著的，土著人的； （动、植物）像外地物种的；（金属或其他矿物）天然的，呈天然纯态的；（计算机）本机器码
n. 土生土长者，本地人；当地居民；土著人；土生植物（或动物）

e.en: Tribal is used to describe things relating to or belonging to tribes and the way that they are organized.

ex.en: ...tribal warfare.
ex.zh: …部落战争。

ex.en: ...the Navajo Tribal Council.
ex.zh: …纳瓦霍人的部落会。

d: adj.  部落的，部族的；；有组成集团倾向的，集团意识强的； 部落的，部族的
n. （尤指印度次大陆的）部落成员（tribals）
【名】 （Tribal）（法）特里巴尔（人名）

e.en: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them. 注意到;

ex.en: He stressed that people should not hesitate to contact the police if they've noticed any strangers recently.
ex.zh: 他强调人们最近如果注意到任何陌生人，要马上与警方联系。

ex.en: I noticed that most academics were writing papers during the summer.
ex.zh: 我注意到大部分学者那个暑期都在撰写论文。

e.en: A notice is a written announcement in a place where everyone can read it.

ex.en: Notices in the waiting room requested that you neither smoke nor spit.
ex.zh: 等候室的告示要求人们不要吸烟也不要随地吐痰。

ex.en: A few guest houses had "No Vacancies" notices in their windows.
ex.zh: 几家旅社在他们的窗户上贴出了“客满”的告示。

e.en: If you give notice about something that is going to happen, you give a warning in advance that it is going to happen.

ex.en: Interest is paid monthly. Three months' notice is required for withdrawals.
ex.zh: 利息按月给付。提款要求提前三个月通知。

ex.en: The insured must be given at least 10 days' notice of cancellation.
ex.zh: 取消保险必须给被保险人至少十天的事先通知。

e.en: A notice is a formal announcement in a newspaper or magazine about something that has happened or is going to happen.

ex.en: I spotted a notice in a local newspaper.
ex.zh: 我在当地一家报纸上看到了一则启事。

d: n. 注意，察觉；通告，布告；公告牌，警示牌；通知；事先声明，警告；预先通知期；剧评，书评；辞职信，搬迁通知；（报纸、杂志上的）小型广告，简短通告；警告书，说明书
v. 意识，注意；留意；正式通知；简评；客气对待；提到，谈到

e.en: Corruption is dishonesty and illegal behaviour by people in positions of authority or power.

ex.en: The president faces 54 charges of corruption and tax evasion.
ex.zh: 总统面临着54项腐败和逃税的指控。

d: n. 贪污，腐败；堕落，腐蚀；（电脑上资讯的）破坏，损坏；（语言）变体；腐坏，腐烂

e.en: Something that is vast is extremely large.

ex.en: ...Afrikaner farmers who own vast stretches of land.
ex.zh: …拥有广阔土地的南非白人农场主们。

d: adj. 巨大的，广大的
n. 广阔空间
【名】 （Vast）（法）瓦斯特（人名）

e.en: The majority of people or things in a group is more than half of them.

ex.en: The majority of my patients come to me from out of town.
ex.zh: 我的多数病人来自市区外。

e.en: If a group is in a majority or in the majority, they form more than half of a larger group.

ex.en: Surveys indicate that supporters of the treaty are still in the majority.
ex.zh: 调查显示该条约的支持者仍占多数。

e.en: A majority is the difference between the number of votes or seats in a legislature or parliament that the winner gets in an election, and the number of votes or seats that the next person or party gets. 多得的票数;

ex.en: Members of parliament approved the move by a majority of ninety-nine.
ex.zh: 国会议员们以99票的多数批准了该提案。

e.en: Majority is used to describe opinions, decisions, and systems of government that are supported by more than half the people involved.

ex.en: ...her continuing disagreement with the majority view.
ex.zh: …她与多数人观点的持续不一致。

d: n. 大多数；多数票；成年的法定年龄；多数党；少校军衔，少校职位
adj. 多数人的

e.en: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

ex.en: All three attacks followed the same pattern.
ex.zh: 3次袭击都依照同一模式。

e.en: A pattern is an arrangement of lines or shapes, especially a design in which the same shape is repeated at regular intervals over a surface.

ex.en: ...a golden robe embroidered with red and purple thread stitched into a pattern of flames.
ex.zh: …一件用红紫相间的线镶了火焰图案的边的金色长袍。

e.en: A pattern is a diagram or shape that you can use as a guide when you are making something such as a model or a piece of clothing.

ex.en: ...cutting out a pattern for slacks.
ex.zh: …剪出一个便裤的纸样。

ex.en: Send for our free patterns to knit yourself.
ex.zh: 索取我们免费的参照图形以便自己织。

e.en: to model

d: n. 模式，方式，规律（pattern 的复数形式）；图案，花纹，花样（pattern 的复数形式）；图样，纸样，样板（pattern 的复数形式）
v. 仿制，摹制，复写（pattern 的第三人称单数形式）；用图案装饰（pattern 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A language is a system of communication which consists of a set of sounds and written symbols which are used by the people of a particular country or region for talking or writing.

ex.en: ...the English language.
ex.zh: …英语。

ex.en: Students are expected to master a second language.
ex.zh: 学生们应该掌握一门第二语言。

e.en: Language is the use of a system of communication which consists of a set of sounds or written symbols.

ex.en: Students examined how children acquire language.
ex.zh: 学生们调查了儿童是怎样学习语言的。

e.en: You can refer to the words used in connection with a particular subject as the language of that subject.

ex.en: ...the language of business.
ex.zh: …商业用语。

e.en: You can refer to someone's use of rude words or swearing as bad language when you find it offensive.

ex.en: Television companies tend to censor bad language in feature films.
ex.zh: 电视公司往往把故事片中的粗话删掉。

d: n. language 的复数形式；语言，语种，语言文字；（尤指作为学科或技能的）外语；（语言学，与语系、语族名称连用）该语系或语族下的诸语言（如 Romance languages）

e.en: A company's shares are the many equal parts into which its ownership is divided. Shares can be bought by people as an investment. 股份;

ex.en: People in China are eager to buy shares in new businesses.
ex.zh: 中国民众热衷于购买新企业的股票。

e.en: If you share something with another person, you both have it, use it, or occupy it. You can also say that two people share something. 共有; 共用;

ex.en: ...the small income he had shared with his brother from his father's estate.
ex.zh: …他和他兄弟分享从他父亲的地产中得来的一小笔收入。

ex.en: Two Americans will share this year's Nobel Prize for Medicine.
ex.zh: 两位美国人将共同摘得今年的诺贝尔医学奖。

e.en: If you share a task, duty, or responsibility with someone, you each carry out or accept part of it. You can also say that two people share something. 共同承担;

ex.en: You can find out whether they are prepared to share the cost of the flowers with you.
ex.zh: 你会发现他们是否准备与你分摊鲜花的费用。

e.en: If you share an experience with someone, you have the same experience, often because you are with them at the time. You can also say that two people share something. 共享 (经历)

ex.en: Yes, I want to share my life with you.
ex.zh: 是的，我想和你共享生活。

d: adj. 分享的，共有的
v. 共享，合用；分配；共同拥有（某种看法、特质或经历）（share 的过去式和过去分词形式）

e.en: A bird is a creature with feathers and wings. Female birds lay eggs. Most birds can fly.
If you refer to two people as birds of a feather, you mean that they have the same interests or are very similar.

ex.en: We're birds of a feather, you and me, Mr. Plimpton.
ex.zh: 我们志趣相投，我和你，普林顿先生。

e.en: A bird in the hand is something that you already have and do not want to risk losing by trying to get something else.

ex.en: Another temporary discount may not be what you want, but at least it is a bird in the hand.
ex.zh: 再一次临时打折可能达不到你所希望的，但至少这是已经到手的东西。

e.en: If you say that a little bird told you about something, you mean that someone has told you about it, but you do not want to say who it was.

ex.en: Incidentally, a little bird tells me that your birthday's coming up.
ex.zh: 顺便提一句，有个消息灵通的人告诉我你的生日快到了。

d: n. 鸟；年轻女子，姑娘；人，家伙；飞机，飞船，卫星；供捕猎（或食用）的鸟；羽毛球；监狱，服刑期（doing bird）；喝倒彩，起哄（give sb. the bird）
【名】 （Bird）（英、西）伯德（人名）

e.en: An acoustic guitar or other instrument is one whose sound is produced without any electrical equipment.
If you refer to the acoustics of a space, you are referring to the structural features which determine how well you can hear music or speech in it.

ex.en: In this performance, Rattle had the acoustics of the Symphony Hall on his side.
ex.zh: 在这场演出中，拉特尔有着交响音乐厅传声效果的翼助。

e.en: Acoustics is the scientific study of sound.

ex.en: ...his work in acoustics.
ex.zh: …他在声学方面的工作。

d: adj. 声音的，听觉的；（乐器）原声的，不加电子设备传声的；（音乐）原声的，不经过电声设备放大的；（建筑材料）隔音的，修饰声音的；（装置，系统）利用声能运作的；（爆破性水雷或其他武器）能为声波引爆的
n. （房间或建筑物的）音响效果，音质；声学（acoustics）；原声吉他（acoustic guitar）

e.en: A song is words and music sung together.

ex.en: ...a voice singing a Spanish song.
ex.zh: …一个唱着西班牙歌曲的嗓音。

e.en: Song is the art of singing.

ex.en: ...dance, music, mime, and song.
ex.zh: …舞蹈、音乐、哑剧和歌唱。

e.en: A bird's song is the pleasant, musical sounds that it makes.

ex.en: It's been a long time since I heard a blackbird's song in the evening.
ex.zh: 我已经好长时间没在晚上听到黑鹂的鸣叫声了。

e.en: If someone bursts into song or breaks into song, they start singing.

ex.en: I feel as if I should break into song.
ex.zh: 我感觉我似乎应该开始歌唱。

d: n. 歌，歌曲；歌唱，声乐；（鸟的）鸣啭，啼啭；押韵的诗歌
【名】 （Song）（英）桑，（汉语）宋（人名）

e.en: A song is words and music sung together.

ex.en: ...a voice singing a Spanish song.
ex.zh: …一个唱着西班牙歌曲的嗓音。

e.en: Song is the art of singing.

ex.en: ...dance, music, mime, and song.
ex.zh: …舞蹈、音乐、哑剧和歌唱。

e.en: A bird's song is the pleasant, musical sounds that it makes.

ex.en: It's been a long time since I heard a blackbird's song in the evening.
ex.zh: 我已经好长时间没在晚上听到黑鹂的鸣叫声了。

e.en: If someone bursts into song or breaks into song, they start singing.

ex.en: I feel as if I should break into song.
ex.zh: 我感觉我似乎应该开始歌唱。

d: n. 歌曲，歌集（song 的复数）

e.en: When you compare things, you consider them and discover the differences or similarities between them.

ex.en: Compare the two illustrations in Figure 60.
ex.zh: 比较一下图60中的两个图示。

ex.en: Managers analyse their company's data and compare it with data on their competitors.
ex.zh: 经理们分析他们公司的数据并与其竞争者的数据进行比较。

e.en: If you compare one person or thing to another, you say that they are like the other person or thing.

ex.en: Some commentators compared his work to that of James Joyce.
ex.zh: 一些评论员认为他的作品像詹姆士·乔伊斯的作品。

e.en: If you say that something does not compare with something else, you mean that it is much worse.

ex.en: The flowers here do not compare with those at home.
ex.zh: 这儿的花比不上家里的花。

e.en: If one thing compares favourably with another, it is better than the other thing. If it compares unfavourably, it is worse than the other thing. (与…) 比起来 (好、差)

ex.en: Our road safety record compares favourably with that of other countries.
ex.zh: 我们的道路安全纪录比其他国家的好。

d: v. （compare 的第三人称单数）比较，对照；把…比作，认为…相似；比得上，可与…相比

e.en: Someone or something that is influential has a lot of influence over people or events. 有影响力的;

ex.en: It helps to have influential friends.
ex.zh: 交上几个有权势的朋友很有好处。

ex.en: He had been influential in shaping economic policy.
ex.zh: 他在制定经济政策方面曾起过很大作用。

d: adj. 有影响力的，有势力的
n. 有影响力的人

e.en: The Almighty is another name for God. You can also refer to Almighty God.

ex.en: Adam sought guidance from the Almighty.
ex.zh: 亚当向上帝寻求指导。

e.en: People sometimes say God Almighty or Christ Almighty to express their surprise, anger, or horror. These expressions could cause offence.

d: adj. 全能的；有无限权力的，有强大力量的；巨大的，极度的；（表示惊奇或愤怒）上帝呀
n. 全能者（指上帝）
abbr. 计算机虚拟化领域缩略词，即虚拟输入输出（Virtual input/output），常指虚拟 I/O 服务器或虚拟 I/O 资源
n. 人名，常见于意大利语和罗马尼亚语，音译为维奥

e.en: Your stomach is the organ inside your body where food is digested before it moves into the intestines.

ex.en: He had an upset stomach.
ex.zh: 他胃部不适。

e.en: You can refer to the front part of your body below your waist as your stomach.

ex.en: The children lay down on their stomachs.
ex.zh: 孩子们俯身趴着。

e.en: If the front part of your body below your waist feels uncomfortable because you are feeling worried or frightened, you can refer to it as your stomach.

ex.en: His stomach was in knots.
ex.zh: 他的心揪得紧紧的。

e.en: If you say that someone has a strong stomach, you mean that they are not disgusted by things that disgust most other people.

ex.en: Surgery often demands actual physical strength, as well as the possession of a strong stomach.
ex.zh: 外科手术常常要求有实际体力，也要有很强的忍耐力。

d: n. 胃；腹部；（低级动物的）类胃器官；（反刍动物的）四胃之一；心窝，内脏； 食欲，胃口；（对有冲突、困难或不快之事的）欲望，倾向；（做困难或不愉快的事所需的）意愿，勇气，决心；（对令人反胃的东西的）承受能力
v. 忍受，承受；吃得下
n. 卢拉（男子名）

e.en: You use neither in front of the first of two or more words or expressions when you are linking two or more things which are not true or do not happen. The other thing is introduced by "nor." 既不… (也不…)

ex.en: Professor Hisamatsu spoke neither English nor German.
ex.zh: 久松教授既不讲英语，也不讲德语。

e.en: You use neither to refer to each of two things or people, when you are making a negative statement that includes both of them.

ex.en: At first, neither man could speak.
ex.zh: 开始两个人都不能说。

e.en: Neither is also a quantifier.

ex.en: Neither of us felt like going out.
ex.zh: 我们两个都不愿意出去。

e.en: Neither is also a pronoun.

ex.en: They both smiled; neither seemed likely to be aware of my absence for long.
ex.zh: 他们两个人都笑了，看来都没意识到我离开了很长时间。

d: det. 两者都不
pron. （两者中）无一个
conj. 既不……（也不……）；也不（用于否定句后，表示前句适用于所有提到的人或物）；也不（用于否定句后，强调要引出另一否定句）
adv. （否定的陈述同样适用于其他人或物）也不；（否定的陈述适用于两方面）既不……也不……
n.博索纳罗（人名）

e.en: If something is done properly, it is done in a correct and satisfactory way.

ex.en: You're too thin. You're not eating properly.
ex.zh: 你太瘦了。你没有好好吃饭。

e.en: If someone behaves properly, they behave in a way that is considered acceptable and not rude.

ex.en: He's a spoiled brat and it's about time he learned to behave properly.
ex.zh: 他是个被宠坏的顽劣孩子，该是他学着行为得当的时候了。

d: adv. 正确地，适当地；得体地，恰当地；实际上，严格地说；彻底地，完全地

e.en: A submarine is a type of ship that can travel both above and below the surface of the sea. The abbreviation  is also used.

ex.en: ...a nuclear submarine.
ex.zh: …一艘核潜艇。

d: n. 潜艇，潜水艇；潜艇三明治，长卷三明治；海底生物
adj. 海面下的，海底的
v. 用潜水艇攻击；在下疾行，在下滑动

e.en: A strategy is a general plan or set of plans intended to achieve something, especially over a long period.

ex.en: The energy secretary will present the strategy tomorrow afternoon.
ex.zh: 能源部长将于明天下午提出该策略。

e.en: Strategy is the art of planning the best way to gain an advantage or achieve success, especially in war.

ex.en: I've just been explaining the basic principles of strategy to my generals.
ex.zh: 我刚才一直在向我的将军们解释战略的基本原则。

d: n. （尤指为获得某物制定长期的）策略，行动计划；战略，战略学
n. 澳英美安全伙伴关系（Australia, United Kingdom, and United States Security Partnership）：是澳大利亚、英国和美国三国于2021年9月成立的一个新的防务合作伙伴关系，旨在加强三国在印度洋-太平洋地区的安全合作。

e.en: a tall fizzy iced drink made with gin, vodka, rum, etc, mixed with fruit juice, soda water, and sugar 柯林斯酒;

d: n. 柯林斯（姓氏名）；柯林斯酒

e.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

ex.en: The latest opinion polls are predicting a very close contest.
ex.zh: 最新的民意测验预言将是一场势均力敌的竞赛。

ex.en: He predicted that my hair would grow back "in no time."
ex.zh: 他预言我的头发会“马上”再长出来。

d: v. 预测，预言，预报（predict 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 预计的，被预测的，事先预料到的（常作定语）

e.en: If you want to know what a word, code, signal, or gesture means, you want to know what it refers to or what its message is.

ex.en: "Credible" means "believable."
ex.zh: 的意思是。

ex.en: What does "evidence" mean?
ex.zh: 是什么意思？

e.en: If you ask someone what they mean, you are asking them to explain exactly what or who they are referring to or what they are intending to say.

ex.en: Do you mean me?
ex.zh: 你指我吗？

ex.en: Let me illustrate what I mean with an old story.
ex.zh: 让我用一个老故事来说明我指的是什么吧。

e.en: If something means something to you, it is important to you in some way. (对某人)

ex.en: The idea that she witnessed this shameful incident meant nothing to him.
ex.zh: 他知道她目击了这可耻的一幕，但这对他来说并不重要。

e.en: If one thing means another, it shows that the second thing exists or is true. 表明…的存在;

ex.en: An enlarged prostate does not necessarily mean cancer.
ex.zh: 肿大的前列腺并不一定表明癌症的存在。

d: v. 意味着；表示……的意思，作……的解释；打算，意欲；使专门用于；导致，结果是；十分熟识；当真，说到做到；对某人重要
adj. 吝啬的，小气的；不善良的，刻薄的；要发怒的；熟练的，出色的；平均的；简陋的，破旧的；微薄的；出身卑贱的，社会地位低下的；中庸的，中等的；凶狠的，好斗的
n. 中庸，折衷；平均数，中数；中间点
【名】 （Mean）（柬）棉（人名）

e.en: If you win something such as a competition, battle, or argument, you defeat those people you are competing or fighting against, or you do better than everyone else involved. 赢得 (比赛、战争或辩论等);

ex.en: He does not have any realistic chance of winning the election.
ex.zh: 他没有任何赢得这次选举的实际机会。

ex.en: The top four teams all won.
ex.zh: 排名最靠前的4支队伍都赢了。

e.en: Win is also a noun.

ex.en: The voters gave a narrow win to Vargas Llosa.
ex.zh: 选民们使瓦尔加斯·略萨取得险胜。

e.en: If something wins you something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, it causes you to defeat the people competing with you or fighting you, or to do better than everyone else involved. 使…赢得 (选举、比赛、战争或辩论等)

ex.en: The Democrats had found a message that could win them the White House.
ex.zh: 民主党人已找到了一条可以使他们赢得总统选举的口号。

e.en: If you win something such as a prize or medal, you get it because you have defeated everyone else in something such as an election, competition, battle, or argument, or have done very well in it. 赢得 (奖或奖牌)

ex.en: Trent Dimas won gold in the final men's gymnastic event.
ex.zh: 特伦特·迪马斯在男子体操决赛中赢得了金牌。

d: v. （在战斗、比赛、游戏等中）赢，获胜；赢得（奖品等）；通过努力得到（某物）；使…赢得（选举、比赛、支持等）（win 的第三人称单数）
n. 胜利，获胜场次（win 的复数）；（Wins）（德、印）温斯（人名）

e.en: If an activity is underway, it has already started. If an activity gets underway, it starts.

ex.en: An investigation is underway to find out how the disaster happened.
ex.zh: 一项调查正在进行，以查明这场灾难是如何发生的。

ex.en: It was a cold evening, winter well underway.
ex.zh: 那是个寒冷的夜晚，冬天早已来临。

d: adj. 在进行中的；（船、火车等）在行进中的

e.en: A week is a period of seven days. Some people consider that a week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.

ex.en: I had a letter from my mother last week.
ex.zh: 我上星期收到了母亲的一封信。

ex.en: This has been on my mind all week.
ex.zh: 我整个星期都在想这件事。

e.en: A week is a period of about seven days.

ex.en: Her mother stayed for another two weeks.
ex.zh: 她母亲又呆了两周时间。

ex.en: Only 12 weeks ago he underwent major heart transplant surgery.
ex.zh: 仅仅12周之前，他接受了一次心脏移植的大手术。

e.en: Your working week is the hours that you spend at work during a week. 工作周 (指一周的工作时数)

ex.en: It is not unusual for women to work a 40-hour week.
ex.zh: 女性1周工作40小时并不少见。

e.en: The week is the part of the week that does not include Saturday and Sunday. (除星期六和星期日以外的)

ex.en: ...the hard work of looking after the children during the week.
ex.zh: …除周末外每天都照看孩子的辛苦活。

d: n. 周，星期（week 的复数）；（Weeks）威克斯（人名）

e.en: If you supply someone with something that they want or need, you give them a quantity of it.

ex.en: ...an agreement not to produce or supply chemical weapons.
ex.zh: …一份不生产或不供应化学武器的协议。

ex.en: ...a pipeline which will supply the major Greek cities with Russian natural gas.
ex.zh: …一条将为希腊各主要城市供应俄罗斯天然气的管道。

e.en: You can use supplies to refer to food, equipment, and other essential things that people need, especially when these are provided in large quantities.

ex.en: What happens when food and petrol supplies run low?
ex.zh: 食物和汽油这些补给品减少时会发生什么情况呢？

e.en: A supply of something is an amount of it which someone has or which is available for them to use.

ex.en: The brain requires a constant supply of oxygen.
ex.zh: 大脑需要持续的供氧。

e.en: Supply is the quantity of goods and services that can be made available for people to buy.

ex.en: Prices change according to supply and demand.
ex.zh: 价格根据供应量和需求量而变化。

d: n. 供给量，储备；（商品、服务的）供应量；供应，补给；生活必需品，日用品（supplies）；供应（的）；临时替代者（尤指代课教师）；议会拨给政府作开支的款项（supplies）
v. 供应，提供，供给；补充，填充；满足要求（或需要）；提供援助；替代

e.en: If you catch a person or animal, you capture them after chasing them, or by using a trap, net, or other device. 捉住;

ex.en: Police say they are confident of catching the gunman.
ex.zh: 警方说他们有信心抓获枪手。

ex.en: Where did you catch the fish?
ex.zh: 你在哪儿捕到了这条鱼？

e.en: If you catch an object that is moving through the air, you seize it with your hands.

ex.en: I jumped up to catch a ball and fell over.
ex.zh: 我跳起来接球，结果摔倒了。

e.en: Catch is also a noun.

ex.en: He missed the catch and the game was lost.
ex.zh: 他没接住球，输了这场比赛。

e.en: If you catch a part of someone's body, you take or seize it with your hand, often in order to stop them from going somewhere. 抓住;

ex.en: Liz caught his arm.
ex.zh: 利兹抓住了他的胳膊。

ex.en: He knelt beside her and caught her hand in both of his.
ex.zh: 他跪在她旁边，双手握住她的手。

d: v. catch 的第三人称单数形式：接住；抓住，握住；逮住，捕获；赶上；感染（疾病）；发觉，撞见
n. catch 的复数形式：接（球等）的动作；（鱼的）捕获量，捕获物

e.en: technical college

d: n. 技校，技术学院；技术（学），工艺（学），工业技术；技术员，技师
【名】 （Tech）（柬）德（人名）

e.en: Something that is popular is enjoyed or liked by a lot of people. (物)

ex.en: Chocolate sauce is always popular with youngsters.
ex.zh: 巧克力酱总是受年轻人喜爱。

e.en: (物的)

ex.en: ...the growing popularity of Australian wines among consumers.
ex.zh: …澳大利亚葡萄酒越来越受消费者青睐。

e.en: Someone who is popular is liked by most people, or by most people in a particular group. (人)

ex.en: He remained the most popular politician in Arkansas.
ex.zh: 他仍是阿肯色州最广受喜爱的政治家。

e.en: (人的)

ex.en: It is his popularity with ordinary people that sets him apart.
ex.zh: 他深受普通群众的喜爱，正是这一点使他与众不同。

d: adj. 受大众喜爱的，受欢迎的；（想法、情绪或态度）普遍的；通俗的，大众化的；民众的，百姓的

e.en: the medieval Schoolmen collectively
e.zh: 中世纪经院哲学家的集体称谓

d: n. （中、小）学校；学派，流派；（大学的）学院；专业学校；鱼群（school 的复数）
v. 送……上学，使受教育；训练，使学会；教育，培养；训练（马）在平地上比赛；（鱼）成群（school 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The gears on a machine or vehicle are a device for changing the rate at which energy is changed into motion.

ex.en: On hills, he must use low gears.
ex.zh: 在山上，他必须用低速挡。

ex.en: The car was in fourth gear.
ex.zh: 那辆汽车处于第4挡。

e.en: The gear involved in a particular activity is the equipment or special clothing that you use. (用于特定活动的)

ex.en: About 100 officers in riot gear were needed to break up the fight.
ex.zh: 大约需要100名配备防暴装备的警官来结束那场斗殴。

ex.en: ...fishing gear.
ex.zh: …钓鱼用具。

e.en: Gear means clothing.

ex.en: I used to wear trendy gear but it just looked ridiculous.
ex.zh: 我过去常穿时髦服装，但那看起来简直滑稽。

e.en: If someone or something is geared to or toward a particular purpose, they are organized or designed in order to achieve that purpose.

ex.en: Colleges are not always geared to the needs of mature students.
ex.zh: 大学并不总是去适应成年学生的需要。

ex.en: My training was geared toward winning gold.
ex.zh: 我的训练是为赢得金牌去规划的。

d: adj. 齿轮传动的，装有齿轮的，用齿轮连接的；变速螺旋桨的；（英）（公司）有一定股本债务比的，负债经营的
v. gear 的过去式和过去分词：使与……相适应，为……设计，针对……调整（be geared to/toward sth）；为……准备好（be geared up to do sth）；使变速，使调档；用齿轮连接；给…装上齿轮；挂档开动机器

e.en: If something shows that a state of affairs exists, it gives information that proves it or makes it clear to people. 显示;

ex.en: Research shows that young people still look to parents as their main source for health information.
ex.zh: 研究表明年轻人仍然指望父母作为他们主要的健康信息来源。

ex.en: These figures show an increase of over one million in unemployment.
ex.zh: 这些数据表明失业人数增长超过100万。

e.en: If a picture, chart, movie, or piece of writing shows something, it represents it or gives information about it. (图画、图表、文章等)

ex.en: Figure 4.1 shows the respiratory system.
ex.zh: 图4.1所示的是呼吸系统。

ex.en: The cushions, shown left, measure 20 x 12 inches and cost $39.95.
ex.zh: 左边展示的垫子尺寸是20 x 12英寸，价格为$39.95。

e.en: If you show someone something, you give it to them, take them to it, or point to it, so that they can see it or know what you are referring to. 拿给…看;

ex.en: Cut out this article and show it to your boss.
ex.zh: 把这篇文章剪下来拿给你的老板看。

ex.en: He showed me the apartment he shares with Esther.
ex.zh: 他指给我看他和埃斯特合住的公寓。

e.en: If you show someone to a room or seat, you lead them there.

ex.en: It was very good of you to come. Let me show you to my study.
ex.zh: 你能来真是太好了。让我带你看我的书房。

ex.en: Milton was shown into the office.
ex.zh: 米尔顿被领进了办公室。

d: v. 显示，表明；给……看，出示；演示，教（show 的第三人称单数）
n. 演出，歌舞表演；（电视或广播）节目；展览，展览会（show 的复数）

e.en: A swift event or process happens very quickly or without delay.

ex.en: Our task is to challenge the U.N. to make a swift decision.
ex.zh: 我们的任务是敦促联合国做出迅速的决定。

e.en: 迅速地

ex.en: Wall Street reacted swiftly to yesterday's verdict.
ex.zh: 华尔街对昨天的裁决迅速地做出了反应。

e.en: Something that is swift moves very quickly.

ex.en: With a swift movement, Matthew Jerrold sat upright.
ex.zh: 马修·杰罗德迅速地坐直了。

e.en: 快速移动地

ex.en: Lenny moved swiftly and silently across the front lawn.
ex.zh: 兰尼快速并且无声地穿过前面的草坪。

d: adj. 迅速的，立刻的；快速移动的，速度非常快的；机灵的，聪明的
n. 雨燕；蝙蝠蛾；绷架
adv.  （在组合形式以外为诗歌或文学用于）迅速
【名】 （Swift）斯威夫特（人名）

e.en: Wednesday is the day after Tuesday and before Thursday.

ex.en: Come and have supper with us on Wednesday, if you're free.
ex.zh: 星期三过来和我们一起吃晚饭，如果有空的话。

ex.en: Did you happen to see her leave last Wednesday?
ex.zh: 上星期三你正好碰巧看见她离开？

d: n. 星期三

e.en: If you re-enter a place, organization, or area of activity that you have left, you return to it.

ex.en: Ten minutes later he re-entered the hotel.
ex.zh: 十分钟后，他重新返回了酒店。

d: v. 重新进入，重返（曾离开的地方、国家、组织或活动领域）；重新输入（密码、数据等）；（航天器、卫星等）再入地球大气层
n．盖瑞尔斯（Gehrels）：一位荷兰裔美国天文学家，名叫汤姆·盖瑞尔斯（Tom Gehrels），他在小行星和彗星研究领域做出了重要贡献。
n. 尼尔（男子名，也作姓氏）

e.en: An observatory is a building with a large telescope from which scientists study things such as the planets by watching them.

d: n. 天文台，气象台；视野开阔的位置（或建筑物）

e.en: A heading is the title of a piece of writing, which is written or printed at the top of the page.

ex.en: ...helpful chapter headings.
ex.zh: …有用的章节标题。

d: n. 标题，题目；类名，条目；方向，航向；（为筑隧道作准备而造的）横向巷道；顶幔
v. 朝（某方向）行进；领导；位于排行之首（动词head 的现在分词形式）
【名】 （Heading）（美）黑丁（人名）

e.en: A ballot is a secret vote in which people select a candidate in an election, or express their opinion about something.

ex.en: The result of the ballot will not be known for two weeks.
ex.zh: 本次无记名投票的结果将在两周后才会揭晓。

e.en: A ballot is a piece of paper on which you indicate your choice or opinion in a secret vote.

ex.en: Election boards will count the ballots by hand.
ex.zh: 选举委员会将手工清点选票。

e.en: If you ballot a group of people, you find out what they think about a subject by organizing a secret vote.

ex.en: The union said they will ballot members on whether to strike.
ex.zh: 工会称他们将组织会员们秘密投票表决是否罢工。

d: n. （无记名）投票选举，投票表决；选票；投票总数（the ballot）
v. 要求（某人）投票；（为……）投票；抽签决定
【名】 （Ballot）（英）巴洛特，（法）巴洛（人名）

e.en: A public library is a building where things such as books, newspapers, videos, and music are kept for people to read, use, or borrow.

ex.en: ...the local library.
ex.zh: …当地的图书馆。

e.en: A private library is a collection of things such as books or music, that is normally only used with the permission of the owner.

ex.en: The company owns a very diverse library of Arabic music.
ex.zh: 公司收藏有多种多样的阿拉伯音乐。

e.en: A library is a public building or a room, for example in a school or hospital, where things such as books, newspapers, videos, and music are kept for people to read, use, or borrow. 图书馆;
In some large houses the library is the room where most of the books are kept.

ex.en: Guests were rarely entertained in the library.
ex.zh: 很少会在书房招待客人。

d: n. 图书馆，藏书楼；（书、激光唱片等的）私人收藏；书房，书斋；文库，系列丛书（激光唱片集，成套录像等）；软件库

e.en: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal meetings.

ex.en: We are going to be in the council chamber every time he speaks.
ex.zh: 我们每次都在会议厅听他讲话。

e.en: You can refer to a country's legislature or to one section of it as a chamber.

ex.en: More than 80 parties are contesting seats in the two-chamber parliament.
ex.zh: 80多个政党在竞争该议会两院的席位。

e.en: A chamber is a room designed and equipped for a particular purpose. (作特殊用途的)

ex.en: For many, the dentist's office remains a torture chamber.
ex.zh: 对许多人来说，牙科诊室仍是一间行刑室。

d: n. 房间，室；会议厅，会所；议院；腔，膛；洞穴；卧室；法官办公室，律师事务所（chambers）
v. 把子弹送入弹膛；把……关在房间里
adj. 室内的；私人的，秘密的
【名】 （Chamber）（英）钱伯（人名）

e.en: A cooper is a person who makes barrels.

d: n. 制桶工人，修桶匠
v. 箍桶，制桶
n. （Cooper）（英、美、加、澳）库珀（人名）

e.en: a trendy Australian male

d: n. 罗伊（男子名）

e.en: If you seek something such as a job or a place to live, you try to find one.

ex.en: They have had to seek work as labourers.
ex.zh: 他们只好找体力活来做。

ex.en: Four people who sought refuge in the Italian embassy have left voluntarily.
ex.zh: 到意大利大使馆寻求避难的四个人已经自愿离开了。

e.en: When someone seeks something, they try to obtain it.

ex.en: The prosecutors have warned they will seek the death penalty.
ex.zh: 原告已警告说他们会努力争取死刑。

e.en: If you seek someone's help or advice, you contact them in order to ask for it. 请求;

ex.en: Always seek professional legal advice before entering into any agreement.
ex.zh: 在签订任何协议之前，一定要征求法律专家的意见。

ex.en: On important issues, they seek a second opinion.
ex.zh: 在重要问题上，他们都征求别人的意见。

e.en: If you seek to do something, you try to do it. 力图;

ex.en: He also denied that he would seek to annex the country.
ex.zh: 他还否认了他企图并吞该国。

d: v．（seek 的第三人称单数）
1. 寻找，寻求：试图找到或得到某物或某人。
· He seeks a solution to the problem.
他寻求解决问题的方法。

e.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. 拿回;

ex.en: In 1986, they got the right to reclaim South African citizenship.
ex.zh: 1986年，他们得到了恢复南非公民身份的权利。

e.en: If you reclaim an amount of money, for example tax that you have paid, you claim it back.

ex.en: The good news for the industry was that investors don't seem to be in any hurry to reclaim their money.
ex.zh: 对该行业来说，好消息是投资者们似乎不急于要求收回他们的钱。

e.en: When people reclaim land, they make it suitable for a purpose such as farming or building, for example by draining it or by building a barrier against the sea. 开垦;

ex.en: The Netherlands has been reclaiming farmland from water.
ex.zh: 荷兰一直在围海造田。

e.en: If a piece of land that was used for farming or building is reclaimed by a desert, forest, or the sea, it turns back into desert, forest, or sea. 重新变成 (沙漠、森林、海洋)

ex.en: The diamond towns are gradually being reclaimed by the desert.
ex.zh: 那些开采钻石的小镇逐渐被沙漠重新吞噬了。

d: v. 要求归还；利用，改造（荒地）；回收（废品中有用的东西）；感化，使纠正
n. 归还要求（或主张）

e.en: a monetary unit of Brunei, worth one hundredth of a dollar, Cambodia, worth one hundredth of a riel, Indonesia, worth one hundredth of a rupiah, Malaysia, worth one hundredth of a ringgit, and formerly of Japan (where it is still used as a unit of account) (文莱货币单位)分; (日本货币单位)

d: n. 仙（印度尼西亚等的辅币单位）；钱（日本硬币，等于1/100日元）
n. （Sen）人名；（东南亚国家华语）生；（中）沈（普通话·威妥玛）；（中）冼（广东话·威妥玛）；（英、印、柬、孟、波、罗、不丹）森

e.en: You use upper to describe something that is above something else.

ex.en: There is a good restaurant on the upper floor.
ex.zh: 楼上有一家很好的餐馆。

e.en: You use upper to describe the higher part of something. 较高的 (部位)

ex.en: ...the upper part of the foot.
ex.zh: …脚面。

ex.en: ...the muscles of the upper back and chest.
ex.zh: …上背部和胸部的肌肉。

e.en: If you have the upper hand in a situation, you have an advantage over the other people involved, for example because you have more power or success.

ex.en: The home team was beginning to gain the upper hand.
ex.zh: 主队正开始占上风。

d: adj. 上面的，上层的，较高的；顶部的，上部的；（在机构、体系等中）较高级的，上级的；上游的，北部的；（地质，考古）晚期的，较近期的
n. 鞋面，鞋帮；兴奋剂（尤指安非他明）
【名】 （Upper）（英）厄珀（人名）

e.en: Won is the past tense and past participle of . (win)
the standard monetary unit of North Korea, divided into 100 chon 圆; 北朝鲜货币单位，合100
the standard monetary unit of South Korea, divided into 100 chon 圆; 南韩货币单位，合100

d: n. 韩圆（韩国货币单位，一圆合一百钱）；朝鲜圆（朝鲜货币单位，一圆合一百钱）
v. （win 的过去式和过去分词）（在战斗、比赛、游戏等中）赢，获胜；赢得（奖品等）；通过努力得到（某物）

e.en: If you vacate a place or a job, you leave it or give it up, making it available for other people. 离开;

ex.en: He quickly vacated the gym after the workout.
ex.zh: 锻炼完他很快离开了健身房。

d: v. vacate 的过去式和过去分词：空出，腾出（房屋、座位等）；离开，撤离；辞去，让出（职位、职务）；（法律）取消，撤销，废止（判决、裁决、命令等）。

e.en: Markings are coloured lines, shapes, or patterns on the surface of something, which help to identify it.

ex.en: A plane with Danish markings was over-flying his vessel.
ex.zh: 一架带有丹麦标志的飞机正从他的轮船上空飞过。

d: v. 做记号；留下痕迹；（使）有污点；标明方位；庆贺；表明；打分；记录；赋予特征；留意；在（羔羊）耳朵上做记号；分隔；标志；（钟表）指示；接球（mark 的现在分词）
n. 作标记，标出位置，划线；物体表面的斑纹、标识、标线（如兽类、鸟类或树木的斑纹，道路或车辆上的标线）；批改（作业），评分；盯人防守，钉人防守；乐谱说明符、记号及演奏说明；Marking 马金（人名）
n. 托姆（法国数学家）

e.en: Late-night is used to describe events, especially entertainments, that happen late in the evening or late at night. (尤指娱乐节目)深夜的;

ex.en: He used to make late-night phone calls to his wife back home.
ex.zh: 他过去经常在午夜给家里的妻子打电话。

ex.en: ...late-night drinking parties.
ex.zh: ...深夜饮酒聚会。

e.en: Late-night is used to describe services that are available late at night and do not close when most commercial activities finish.

ex.en: Saturday night was a late-night shopping night.
ex.zh: 周六晚上购物可以持续到深夜。

ex.en: ...late-night trains.
ex.zh: ...午夜列车。

d: adj. 深夜的，午夜的（指活动、节目等发生在深夜）；营业到深夜的，深夜仍运行（或开放）的（指商店、公共交通、服务机构等）

e.en: The host at a party is the person who has invited the guests and provides the food, drink, or entertainment. (聚会的)

ex.en: Apart from my host, I didn't know a single person there.
ex.zh: 除了主人，那儿的人我一个也不认识。

e.en: If someone hosts a party, dinner, or other function, they have invited the guests and provide the food, drink, or entertainment. 主办 (聚会、宴会或其他集会)

ex.en: Tonight she hosts a ball for 300 guests.
ex.zh: 今晚她做东办一场有300名来宾参加的舞会。

e.en: A country, city, or organization that is the host of an event provides the facilities for that event to take place. (举办某活动的)

ex.en: Atlanta was chosen to be host of the 1996 Olympic games.
ex.zh: 亚特兰大被选为1996年奥运会的东道主。

e.en: If a country, city, or organization hosts an event, they provide the facilities for the event to take place.

ex.en: New Bedford hosts a number of lively festivals throughout the summer months.
ex.zh: 新贝德福德整个夏天举办了许多个欢快有趣的艺术节。

d: n. 主人；主持人；东道主，主办者；寄主，宿主（host 的复数）；（计算机）主机
v. 主办（活动、赛事），做……的东道主；作为主人组织（聚会），做东（host 的第三人称单数）；主持（节目）

e.en: If something reflects an attitude or situation, it shows that the attitude or situation exists or it shows what it is like. 反映; 表现;

ex.en: A newspaper report seems to reflect the view of most members of Congress.
ex.zh: 报纸的一篇报导似乎反映了国会多数议员的观点。

e.en: When light, heat, or other rays reflect off a surface or when a surface reflects them, they are sent back from the surface and do not pass through it.

ex.en: The sun reflected off the snow-covered mountains.
ex.zh: 阳光从被雪覆盖的山峦反射回来。

e.en: When something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

ex.en: His image was reflected many times in the mirror.
ex.zh: 他的影像在那面镜子里映出了很多个。

e.en: When you reflect on something, you think deeply about it.

ex.en: We should all give ourselves time to reflect.
ex.zh: 我们都应该给自己时间来深思。

d: v. 反射（光、热或声音）；反映，照出（影像）；显示，表明；深思，反省（reflect 的现在分词）
adj. 反光的，反射的

e.en: When you put something in a particular place or position, you move it into that place or position.

ex.en: Leaphorn put the photograph on the desk.
ex.zh: 利普霍恩把那张照片放在桌子上。

ex.en: She hesitated, then put her hand on Grace's arm.
ex.zh: 她犹豫了一下，然后把手搭在格雷斯的臂膀上。

e.en: If you put someone somewhere, you cause them to go there and to stay there for a period of time.

ex.en: Rather than put him in the hospital, she had been caring for him at home.
ex.zh: 她没有把他送进医院，而是一直在家里照料他。

e.en: To put someone or something in a particular state or situation means to cause them to be in that state or situation. 致使 (…处于某种状态)

ex.en: This is going to put them out of business.
ex.zh: 这将使他们歇业。

ex.en: He was putting himself at risk.
ex.zh: 他在把自己置于危险境地。

e.en: To put something on people or things means to cause them to have it, or to cause them to be affected by it. 把…施加给;

ex.en: He didn't put any pressure on her.
ex.zh: 他并没有给她施加任何压力。

ex.en: Be aware of the terrible strain it can put on a child when you expect the best grades.
ex.zh: 当你期盼最佳成绩时，要意识到这可能给孩子带来的可怕压力。

d: n. 投掷；（高尔夫球）打球入洞，指用推杆轻击球入洞
v. （put 的现在分词／动名词形式）放置；安置，使……前往；（沿某个方向）行驶；写上，印上；说，表达；流向；使处于某状态；把……施加给；把……寄托在；把……用在；指定……价值；估计……为；投入（资金）；提出（问题）；解释；（putt 的现在分词／动名词形式）轻击球，使球入洞

e.en: You use severe to indicate that something bad or undesirable is great or intense.

ex.en: ...a business with severe cash flow problems.
ex.zh: …一个有严重现金流转问题的企业。

ex.en: Shortages of professional staff are very severe in some places.
ex.zh: 专业人员的短缺在一些地方十分严重。

e.en: 严重地

ex.en: The UN wants to send food aid to 10 countries in Africa severely affected by the drought.
ex.zh: 联合国想给予10个受旱灾严重影响的非洲国家食品援助。

ex.en: An aircraft overshot the runway and was severely damaged.
ex.zh: 一架飞机冲出了跑道后严重受损。

e.en: Severe punishments or criticisms are very strong or harsh. (惩罚、批评)

ex.en: This was a dreadful crime and a severe sentence is necessary.
ex.zh: 这是一种骇人听闻的罪行，重判是必要的。

e.en: 严厉地

ex.en: ...a campaign to try to change the law to punish dangerous drivers more severely.
ex.zh: …一场试图修改法律以更加严厉地惩罚危险驾车者的运动。

d: adj. 十分严重的，极为恶劣的；艰巨的，严峻的；（惩罚、批评）严厉的，重的；严厉的，苛刻的；不加装饰的，朴素的

e.en: If you stress a point in a discussion, you put extra emphasis on it because you think it is important.

ex.en: The spokesman stressed that the measures did not amount to an overall ban.
ex.zh: 发言人强调说，这些措施并不等于全面禁止。

ex.en: China's leaders have stressed the need for increased co-operation between Third World countries.
ex.zh: 中国领导人已经强调了增进第三世界国家之间合作的需要。

e.en: Stress is also a noun.

ex.en: Japanese car makers are laying ever more stress on overseas sales.
ex.zh: 日本的汽车制造商们把更多的重点放在海外销售上。

e.en: If you feel under stress, you feel worried and tense because of difficulties in your life.

ex.en: Katy could think clearly when not under stress.
ex.zh: 凯泰在没有精神压力时能够清晰地思考。

e.en: If you stress a word or part of a word when you say it, you put emphasis on it so that it sounds slightly louder.

ex.en: She stresses the syllables as though teaching a child.
ex.zh: 她重读这些音节，像教小孩似的。

d: n. 精神压力，紧张；压力，应力；强调，重要性；（单词）重音，重读，（音乐）加强音；压强；环境恶劣引起的疾病
v. 强调，着重；重读；焦虑，紧张；使受压力，使受重压
【名】 （Stress）（意）斯特雷斯 （人名）

e.en: A surge is a sudden large increase in something that has previously been steady, or has only increased or developed slowly.

ex.en: Specialists see various reasons for the recent surge in inflation.
ex.zh: 专家认为最近通货膨胀加剧有各种原因。

e.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after being steady or developing only slowly.

ex.en: The Freedom Party's electoral support surged from just under 10 percent to nearly 17 percent.
ex.zh: 自由党的选举支持率从只有不到10%剧增到近17%。

e.en: If a crowd of people surge forward, they suddenly move forward together.

ex.en: The photographers and cameramen surged forward.
ex.zh: 那些摄影和摄像师们涌向前去。

e.en: A surge is a sudden powerful movement of a physical force such as wind or water. (风、水等)

ex.en: The whole car shuddered with an almost frightening surge of power.
ex.zh: 整辆车因受到一股几乎令人惊骇的冲力而颤动。

d: n. 激增，猛增；（风、水等的）奔涌，汹涌；（情感的）涌起，翻涌；（人群的）蜂拥；电流急冲，电涌；增兵，增援
v. 急剧上升，激增；（人群，自然力）汹涌，奔腾；（感情）涌起，涌现；（电压，电流）猛增，浪涌；（绳子，缆索，绞盘）突然松开，突然滑脱

e.en: If you tell someone something, you give them information. 告诉 (某人某事)

ex.en: In the evening I returned to tell Phyllis I got the job.
ex.zh: 晚上我回来告诉菲莉丝我得到了那份工作。

ex.en: I called Andie to tell her how spectacular the stuff looked.
ex.zh: 我打电话给安迪告诉她那东西看上去多么壮观。

e.en: If you tell something such as a joke, a story, or your personal experiences, you communicate it to other people using speech. 讲述 (笑话、故事、个人经历等)

ex.en: His friends say he was always quick to tell a joke.
ex.zh: 他的朋友们说他以前总是张口就能讲笑话。

ex.en: He told his story to The L.A. Times and produced photographs.
ex.zh: 他向《洛杉机时报》叙述了自己的故事，并提供了一些照片。

e.en: If you tell someone to do something, you order or advise them to do it. 命令; 建议 (某人做某事)

ex.en: He said officers told him to get out of his car and lean against it.
ex.zh: 他说警官们命令他从他的车里出来并靠在车上。

e.en: If you tell yourself something, you put it into words in your own mind because you need to encourage or persuade yourself about something. 叮嘱 (自己)

ex.en: "Come on," she told herself.
ex.zh: “加油，”她叮嘱自己。

d: v. 告诉；说；讲述（tell 的第三人称单数形式）
n. （牌戏用语）泄底，玄机，马脚（tell 的复数形式）

e.en: Veterinary is used to describe the work of a person whose job is to treat sick or injured animals, or to describe the medical treatment of animals.

ex.en: It was decided that our veterinary screening of horses at events should be continued.
ex.zh: 已经决定，我们对参赛马匹的疾病检查将继续进行。

d: adj. 兽医的
n. 兽医

e.en: Member of the Pharmaceutical Society

d: abbr. （英国）医药学会会员（Member of the Pharmaceutical Society）；（英国）语文学会会员（Member of the Philological Society）；（英国）物理学会会员（Member of the Physical Society）；每秒米数, 米/秒（metres per second 或 meters per second）；微处理器系统（microprocessor system）；单核吞噬细胞系统（mononuclear phygocyte system）；移动编程系统（mobile programming system）

e.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it. (灾难性大事件的)

ex.en: In the aftermath of the coup, the troops opened fire on the demonstrators.
ex.zh: 在那次政变的余波之中，军队向示威者开了枪。

d: n. （战争、风暴、事故的）后果，余波；再萌草，再生草

e.en: If flooding occurs, an area of land that is usually dry is covered with water after heavy rain or after a river or lake flows over its banks.

ex.en: The flooding, caused by three days of torrential rain, is the worst in sixty-five years.
ex.zh: 由3天暴雨引发的这场洪水泛滥是65年来最为严重的。

d: n. 洪水泛滥；（医学）子宫大量出血，尤指产后出血；（心理学）满灌疗法，冲击疗法；（计算机网络）泛洪

e.en: Rain is water that falls from the clouds in small drops.

ex.en: I hope you didn't get soaked standing out in the rain.
ex.zh: 我希望你站在外面雨里没淋得浑身透湿。

e.en: In countries where rain only falls in certain seasons, this rain is referred to as the rains.

ex.en: ...the spring, when the rains came.
ex.zh: …春天，雨季来临时。

e.en: When rain falls, you can say that it is raining.

ex.en: It was raining hard, and she didn't have an umbrella.
ex.zh: 雨下得很大，而她没有带伞。

e.en: If someone rains blows, kicks, or bombs on a person or place, the person or place is attacked by many blows, kicks, or bombs. You can also say that blows, kicks, or bombs rain on a person or place. 使像雨点般落下;

ex.en: The police, raining blows on rioters and spectators alike, cleared the park.
ex.zh: 警察对暴乱者和旁观者都一阵猛打，清空了公园。

d: adj. 下雨的，如雨般落下的
v. 下雨，降雨；倾泻，大量降落（rain 的现在分词）
n. 稳定（性），稳固（性）；坚定，恒心

e.en: To reveal something means to make people aware of it. 透露;

ex.en: She has refused to reveal the whereabouts of her daughter.
ex.zh: 她已拒绝透露她女儿的行踪。

ex.en: A survey of the American diet has revealed that a growing number of people are overweight.
ex.zh: 一项有关美国人日常饮食的调查表明越来越多的人超重。

e.en: If you reveal something that has been out of sight, you uncover it so that people can see it. 使显露;

ex.en: In the principal room, a grey carpet was removed to reveal the original pine floor.
ex.zh: 在主房间里，一块灰色的地毯被挪开了，使原有的松木地板露了出来。

d: v. （reveal 的第三人称单数）揭露，透露，披露；使显露，展示，暴露
n. （reveal 的复数）揭示，披露，展示

e.en: A prolonged event or situation continues for a long time, or for longer than expected. 长期的;

ex.en: ...a prolonged period of low interest rates.
ex.zh: …一段很长的低利率期。

d: adj. 长期的，持续很久的
v. 拉长，拖长（感觉或活动）；延长（prolong 的过去式和过去分词）
n. 奇异；不快

e.en: People sometimes say "goodness" or "my goodness" to express surprise. (表示惊讶)

ex.en: Goodness, I wonder if he knows.
ex.zh: 天哪，我不清楚他知不知道。

e.en: Goodness is the quality of being kind, helpful, and honest.

ex.en: He retains a faith in human goodness.
ex.zh: 他依然相信人性的善。

d: n. 善良，美德；（尤指食物中的）营养，精华
int. 天哪，啊呀（用作“上帝”的替代语，表示吃惊或愤怒等）

e.en: A place that is packed is very crowded.

ex.en: The place is packed at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 这个地方在午餐时间非常拥挤。

ex.en: ...a packed meeting in Detroit.
ex.zh: …一个在底特律召开的座无虚席的会议。

e.en: Something that is packed with things contains a very large number of them.

ex.en: The encyclopedia is packed with clear illustrations and over 250 recipes.
ex.zh: 这本百科全书充满了清晰的插图，还有二百五十多个食谱。

d: adj. 挤满人的，非常拥挤的；充满的，装满的；收拾妥当的，收拾好了的；（雪、糖或土壤）压成硬块的
v. 把……打包；包装，包裹；挤满，塞满；（pack 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: A drama is a serious play for the theatre, television, or radio, or a serious film.

ex.en: He acted in radio dramas.
ex.zh: 他演过广播剧。

ex.en: The film is a drama about a woman searching for her children.
ex.zh: 这部电影是关于一个女人寻找她孩子的戏。

e.en: You use drama to refer to plays in general or to work that is connected with plays and the theatre, such as acting or producing. 戏剧;

ex.en: He knew nothing of Greek drama.
ex.zh: 他对希腊戏剧一无所知。

e.en: You can refer to a real situation which is exciting or distressing as drama.

ex.en: There was none of the drama and relief of a hostage release.
ex.zh: 丝毫没有人质释放的戏剧性场面和放松。

d: n. 剧本，戏剧；戏剧研究，戏剧艺术；戏剧性场面，戏剧性事件；激动，刺激
【名】 （Drama）（刚(金)）德拉马（人名）

e.en: If someone is on a shortlist, for example, for a job or a prize, they are one of a small group of people who have been chosen from a larger group. The successful person is then chosen from the small group. (工作或获奖的)

ex.en: If you've been asked for an interview you are probably on a shortlist of no more than six.
ex.zh: 如果你已经被要求参加面试，你很可能在不超过6人的候选名单上。

e.en: If someone or something is shortlisted for a job or a prize, they are put on a shortlist.

ex.en: He was shortlisted for the Nobel Prize for literature several times.
ex.zh: 他曾数次获得诺贝尔文学奖提名。

d: n. 最终候选名单，决选名单
v. 把……列入决选的名单

e.en: Comedy consists of types of entertainment, such as plays and film, or particular scenes in them, that are intended to make people laugh.

ex.en: Actor Dom Deluise talks about his career in comedy.
ex.zh: 演员多姆·德卢斯谈论他的喜剧事业。

e.en: A comedy is a play, film, or television programme that is intended to make people laugh.

ex.en: The movie is a romantic comedy.
ex.zh: 这部电影是一个浪漫喜剧。

d: n. 喜剧，喜剧片；滑稽的事物，搞笑的东西；滑稽，诙谐

e.en: If something rarely happens, it does not happen very often.

ex.en: They battled against other Indian tribes, but rarely fought with the whites.
ex.zh: 他们与其他印第安部落交战，但很少与白人作战。

d: adv. 罕有，很少；异乎寻常地，极度

e.en: A guide is a book that gives you information or instructions to help you do or understand something.

ex.en: Our 10-page guide will help you to change your life for the better.
ex.zh: 我们这本10页的指南将会帮助改善你们的生活。
