e.en: A guide is a book that gives tourists information about a town, area, or country.

ex.en: The Rough Guide to Paris lists accommodations for as little as $35 a night.
ex.zh: 《巴黎旅游简明指南》列出了价格低至每晚$35的住宿。

e.en: A guide is someone who shows tourists around places such as museums or cities.

ex.en: We've arranged a walking tour of the city with your guide.
ex.zh: 我们已经和你的导游安排了一个城市步行游览。

e.en: If you guide someone around a city, museum, or building, you show it to them and explain points of interest.

ex.en: ...a young Egyptologist who guided us through tombs and temples with enthusiasm.
ex.zh: …一位热心地领着我们参观陵墓和寺庙的年轻的埃及学家。

d: n. 指南，手册；导游，向导；指导原则，参照标准；（图像处理、排版软件）参考线，辅助线（guide 的复数）
v. 指导，引导，影响；带路，领路（guide 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: Sand is a substance that looks like powder, and consists of extremely small pieces of stone. Some deserts and many beaches are made up of sand.

ex.en: They all walked barefoot across the damp sand to the water's edge.
ex.zh: 他们都光着脚走过潮湿的沙地来到了水边。

e.en: Sands are a large area of sand, for example, a beach.

ex.en: ...miles of golden sands.
ex.zh: …数英里的金色沙滩。

e.en: If you sand a wood or metal surface, you rub sandpaper over it in order to make it smooth or clean.

ex.en: Sand the surface softly and carefully.
ex.zh: 轻轻地、小心地用砂纸打磨表面。

e.en: Sand down means the same as . 同(sand)

ex.en: I was going to sand down the chairs and repaint them.
ex.zh: 我打算用砂纸打磨这些椅子然后重新刷漆。

d: n. 沙，沙子；沙堆，沙地；沙滩，沙漠（sands）；沙石层，沙层；（尤指大于0.06毫米的沙粒构成的）沉积沙土；沙土色，浅黄灰色；坚定，刚毅
v. （用砂纸或打磨机）磨光；撒沙于，铺沙于；使撒沙似地布满；给……掺沙子
【名】 （Sand）（英、德、意、芬、罗、捷、挪、瑞典）桑德，（法）桑（人名）

e.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

ex.en: The terrain changed quickly from arable land to desert.
ex.zh: 这里的地形很快由耕地变为沙漠。

d: n. 地形，地势；领域

e.en: European means belonging or relating to, or coming from Europe.

ex.en: ...in some other European countries.
ex.zh: …在其他一些欧洲国家。

e.en: A European is a person who comes from Europe.

ex.en: Three-quarters of working-age Americans work, compared with roughly 60% of Europeans.
ex.zh: 3/4处于工作年龄的美国人在工作，相比之下欧洲约为60%。

d: n. 欧洲人（European 的复数）

e.en: To punish someone means to make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

ex.en: I don't believe that George ever had to punish the children.
ex.zh: 我不相信乔治曾不得不惩罚这些孩子。

ex.en: According to present law, the authorities can only punish smugglers with small fines.
ex.zh: 根据现行法律，当局只能对走私者处以小额罚款。

e.en: To punish a crime means to punish anyone who commits that crime.

ex.en: ...federal laws to punish crimes such as murder and assault.
ex.zh: …惩处诸如谋杀和强奸等罪的联邦法律。

d: adj. 被惩罚的，被处罚的
v. punish 的过去式和过去分词
n. 美国俄克拉荷马州
n. violation 的复数形式；违反，违背；侵犯，侵害；（体育比赛中的）违例；违规或不雅行为

e.en: Republican means relating to a republic. In republican systems of government, power is held by the people or the representatives that they elect.

ex.en: ...the nations that had adopted the republican form of government.
ex.zh: …采用了共和制政体的国家。

e.en: If someone is Republican, they belong to or support the Republican Party.

ex.en: Lower taxes made Republican voters happier with their party.
ex.zh: 更低的税率使共和党选民对该党更加满意。

e.en: A Republican is someone who supports or belongs to the Republican Party.

ex.en: What made you decide to become a Republican, as opposed to a Democrat?
ex.zh: 是什么使你决定成为共和党人，而不是民主党人呢？

d: adj. 共和政体的，共和国的；拥护共和政体的，共和主义的；（美国）共和党的，支持共和党的（Republican）；北爱尔兰共和主义者的，支持北爱尔兰共和主义者的（Republican）
n. 共和主义者，拥护共和政体者；（美国）共和党人，共和党支持者（Republican）；（主张北爱尔兰应脱离英国成为爱尔兰共和国一部分的）北爱尔兰共和主义者（Republican）

e.en: If you keep a record of something, you keep a written account or photographs of it so that it can be referred to later. 记录;

ex.en: Keep a record of all the payments.
ex.zh: 对所有付款做一个记录。

ex.en: There's no record of any marriage or children.
ex.zh: 没有任何有关结婚或子女的记录。

e.en: If you record a piece of information or an event, you write it down, photograph it, or put it into a computer so that in the future people can refer to it. 记录;

ex.en: Her letters record the domestic and social details of diplomatic life in China.
ex.zh: 她的信件记录了在中国的外交生活中家庭和社会活动的细节。

e.en: If you record something such as a speech or performance, you put it on tape or film so that it can be heard or seen again later. 录音;

ex.en: There is nothing to stop viewers from recording the films on videotape.
ex.zh: 没有办法阻止观众用录像带录下电影。

e.en: If a musician or performer records a piece of music or a television or radio show, they perform it so that it can be put onto CD, tape, or film.

ex.en: It took the musicians two and a half days to record their soundtrack for the film.
ex.zh: 音乐家们花了两天半的时间录制电影的配乐。

d: n. 记录，记载；（某人或某物过去的）记录，经历；（尤指体育运动中的）最佳纪录，最好成绩；唱片；前科，犯罪记录；唱片乐曲；（计算机）记录（指作为一个单位处理的一批相关信息）
v. 记录，记载；录制；（仪器）显示，标示；（尤指体育上）获得（好成绩）；发表正式（或法律方面的）声明，申明；演奏音乐供录制
adj. 创纪录的
【名】 （Record）（美）勒科尔（人名）

e.en: A billionaire is an extremely rich person who has money or property worth at least a thousand million dollars.

d: n. 亿万富翁

e.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change. (有计划的) 活动;

ex.en: During his election campaign he promised to put the economy back on its feet.
ex.zh: 竞选活动期间，他许诺要致力于恢复经济。

ex.en: ...a campaign to improve the training of staff.
ex.zh: …改进员工培训的一个活动。

e.en: In a war, a campaign is a series of planned movements carried out by armed forces. 一系列军事行动;

ex.en: The allies are intensifying their air campaign.
ex.zh: 盟军在加强他们的空中军事活动。

e.en: If someone campaigns for something, they carry out a planned set of activities over a period of time in order to achieve their aim.

ex.en: We are campaigning for law reform.
ex.zh: 我们正从事法律改革运动。

d: n. （有计划的）活动，运动；战役（campaign 的复数）
v. 参加（进行）运动，从事竞选活动（campaign 的第三人称单数）

e.en: If you pour a liquid or other substance, you make it flow steadily out of a container by holding the container at an angle. 倒 (液体等)

ex.en: Pour a pool of sauce on two plates and arrange the meat neatly.
ex.zh: 倒一些酱到两个盘子里，然后把肉摆放整齐。

ex.en: Don poured a generous measure of scotch into a fresh glass.
ex.zh: 唐往新杯子里倒了很多苏格兰威士忌。

e.en: If you pour someone a drink, you put some of the drink in a cup or glass so that they can drink it. (给某人) 倒 (一杯饮料)

ex.en: He got up and poured himself another drink.
ex.zh: 他站起身来，给自己又倒了一杯。

ex.en: She asked Tillie to pour her a cup of coffee.
ex.zh: 她叫蒂莉给她倒一杯咖啡。

e.en: When a liquid or other substance pours somewhere, for example, through a hole, it flows quickly and in large quantities.

ex.en: Blood was pouring from his broken nose.
ex.zh: 血正从他破了的鼻子里喷涌而出。

ex.en: Tears poured down both our faces.
ex.zh: 眼泪在我们两人脸上哗哗地流。

e.en: When it rains very heavily, you can say that it is pouring. (雨)

ex.en: It was still pouring outside.
ex.zh: 外面依旧大雨倾盆。

ex.en: The rain was pouring down.
ex.zh: 雨在倾盆而下。

d: v. pour 的过去式和过去分词。倾倒，倒出，斟（饮料）：将液体或松散物质从容器中倒出；涌出，涌流，倾泻：大量涌出或流出；（雨）倾盆而下；（人群、信息等）大量涌至；大量投入（金钱、资源等）；pour out：倾吐，诉说。

e.en: in the US Grand Old Party (美国)

d: abbr. 大老党（美国共和党的别称）（Grand Old Party）；图像组（视频编码中的 Group of Pictures）；地面观测站（Ground Observation Post）
n. （Colom）人名；（西）科洛姆；（法）科隆

e.en: A razor-thin majority or profit is a very small one. (多数地位)微弱的; (利润)

ex.en: There is a razor-thin Democratic majority of one seat in the Senate.
ex.zh: 民主党在参议院中只占一席的微弱多数。

ex.en: ...the consumer retail arena, where profits are razor-thin.
ex.zh: ...只有微薄利润的消费者零售领域。

d: adj. 极微弱的；极薄的
n. 斯科特（英语姓氏或男子名）；沃尔特·斯科特（苏格兰历史小说家、诗人）；罗伯特·福尔肯·斯科特（英国海军军官和南极探险家）；德雷德·斯科特（美国黑奴、美国最高法院斯科特案当事人）

e.en: A challenger is someone who competes with you for a position or title that you already have, for example being a sports champion or a political leader.

ex.en: The strongest challenger, Texas Democrat Martin Frost, has withdrawn from the race.
ex.zh: 最强劲的挑战者，德克萨斯州的民主党人马丁·弗罗斯特已经退出了竞选。

d: n. 挑战者，竞争者（与他人争夺职位、头衔或地位的人，尤指与现任者竞争的人）；市场挑战者（指挑战市场领导者的公司或品牌）；（Challenger）挑战者号（美国国家航空航天局的航天飞机，1986 年发射后失事）；（Challenger，英）查林杰（姓氏）
n. 辛迪（女子名, Cynthia 的昵称）

e.en: A map is a drawing of a particular area such as a city, a country, or a continent, showing its main features as they would appear if you looked at them from above.

ex.en: He unfolded the map and set it on the floor.
ex.zh: 他展开地图，把它放在了地板上。

e.en: To map an area means to make a map of it.

ex.en: ...a spacecraft which is using radar to map the surface of Venus.
ex.zh: …一艘利用雷达绘制金星表面地图的航天器。

d: n. 地图；分布图；（基因）图谱，染色体图；天体图；映射；脸，面孔
v. 绘制……的地图；了解信息；详细安排；映射；与……有关，与……有联系；使（基因）在染色体上定位
【名】 （Map）（美）马普（人名）

e.en: A sweeping curve is a long wide curve.

ex.en: ...the long sweeping curve of Rio's Guanabara Bay.
ex.zh: …连绵曲折的里约热内卢瓜纳巴拉海湾。

e.en: If someone makes a sweeping statement or generalization, they make a statement which applies to all things of a particular kind, although they have not considered all the relevant facts carefully.

ex.en: It is far too early to make sweeping statements about gene therapy.
ex.zh: 对基因疗法进行概括地说明还为时尚早。

e.en: Sweeping changes are large and very important or significant. (改变)

ex.en: The new government has started to make sweeping changes in the economy.
ex.zh: 新一届政府已经开始在经济领域进行意义深远的变革。

d: adj. 范围广的，影响大的；过于笼统的；弧线的，弯曲的；包含丰富信息的；（投票等中的）大胜
n. 打扫，清扫；扫集的尘土（或垃圾）（sweepings）
v. 打扫，清除；（目光）扫视，（灯光）掠过；（快速地）带走，卷走（sweep 的现在分词）

e.en: A victory is a success in a struggle, war, or competition.

ex.en: Union leaders are heading for victory in their battle over workplace rights.
ex.zh: 工会领袖们在争取工作场所权利的斗争中正迈向胜利。

e.en: If you say that someone has won a moral victory, you mean that although they have officially lost a contest or dispute, they have succeeded in showing they are right about something.

ex.en: She said her party had won a moral victory.
ex.zh: 她说她的党已赢得了精神上的胜利。

d: n. 胜利，成功，获胜
【名】 （Victory）（西）维多利，（英）维克托里（人名）

e.en: The presidency of a country or organization is the position of being the president or the period of time during which someone is president. (某国、某组织的) 最高职位;

ex.en: He is a candidate for the presidency of the organization.
ex.zh: 他是该组织最高职位候选人。

d: n. 总统（主席，校长）的职位（任期）；（基督教）（牧师或司铎）圣餐主持；监督，主管

e.en: To fortify a place means to make it stronger and more difficult to attack, often by building a wall or ditch round it. (常通过筑墙、挖沟等) 巩固 (某地)

ex.en: ...soldiers working to fortify an airbase in Bahrain.
ex.zh: …在巩固一个在巴林的空军基地的士兵们。

e.en: If food or drink is fortified, another substance is added to it to make it healthier or stronger. (通过添加另一种物质而) 强化 (食品或饮料)

ex.en: Choose margarine or butter fortified with vitamin D.
ex.zh: 选择人造黄油或用维生素D强化了的黄油。

ex.en: All sherry is made from wine fortified with brandy.
ex.zh: 所有雪利酒都是由用白兰地强化了的葡萄酒制成的。

d: adj. 加强的；防御的，设防的；增加营养的，添加营养素强化的；（酒类）加烈的，提高酒精含量的
v. fortify 的过去式和过去分词：筑防于，设要塞于；提高（食品）营养价值；使增强体质，使振奋精神

e.en: Someone who is vegan never eats meat or any animal products such as milk, butter, or cheese.

ex.en: The menu changes weekly and usually includes a vegan option.
ex.zh: 这份菜单每周变化，而且通常包括纯素菜肴供选择。

e.en: A vegan is someone who is vegan.

ex.en: ...vegetarians and vegans.
ex.zh: …素食者和严格的素食主义者。

d: n. 纯素食者，严格的素食主义者
adj. 严格素食的，不吃肉的

e.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

ex.en: I remembered a particular story about a mailman who was a murderer.
ex.zh: 我记得一个故事，关于一个邮递员是杀人犯。

ex.en: I have to know exactly why it is I'm doing a particular job.
ex.zh: 我必须确切地知道我为什么做某项工作。

e.en: If a person or thing has a particular quality or possession, it is distinct and belongs only to them.

ex.en: I have a particular responsibility to ensure I make the right decision.
ex.zh: 我有特别责任要确保做出正确的决定。

e.en: You can use particular to emphasize that something is greater or more intense than usual.

ex.en: Particular emphasis will be placed on oral language training.
ex.zh: 口语训练将给予非同寻常的重视。

e.en: If you say that someone is particular, you mean that they choose things and do things very carefully, and are not easily satisfied.

ex.en: Ted was very particular about the colours he used.
ex.zh: 特德对于他使用的颜色是非常挑剔的。

d: adj. 特定的，某一的；格外的，特别的；讲究的，挑剔的；特殊的，独特的；详细的，详尽的
n. 一点，一个细节； 详细资料，详情（particulars）；（哲学）（与普遍性相对的）特殊性

e.en: Iodine is a dark-coloured substance used in medicine and photography.

d: n. 碘；碘酒

e.en: If someone or something is in jeopardy, they are in a dangerous situation where they might fail, be lost, or be destroyed.

ex.en: A series of setbacks have put the whole project in jeopardy.
ex.zh: 一系列的挫折已经使整个项目陷入险境。

d: n. 危险，风险；（刑事案件中被告的）危险处境

e.en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than before.

ex.en: ...loss of sight.
ex.zh: …失明。

ex.en: ...hair loss.
ex.zh: …脱发。

e.en: Loss of life occurs when people die.

ex.en: ...a terrible loss of human life.
ex.zh: …人员死亡惨重。

e.en: The loss of a relative or friend is their death. (亲人、朋友的)

ex.en: They took the time to talk about the loss of Thomas and how their grief was affecting them.
ex.zh: 他们花时间来谈论托马斯的去世以及悲伤给他们带来的影响。

e.en: Loss is the feeling of sadness you experience when someone or something you like is taken away from you.

ex.en: Talk to others about your feelings of loss and grief.
ex.zh: 和别人说说你失落和悲伤。

d: n. 损失；损耗（loss 的复数）

e.en: The outer parts of something are the parts which contain or enclose the other parts, and which are furthest from the centre.

ex.en: He heard a voice in the outer room.
ex.zh: 他听到外屋有人声。

d: adj. 外面的，外部的；远离中心的，外围的；客观外界的，非主观的；（尤用于地名）更远的
n. 外衣，穿在外面的服饰的一部分；靶子的外圈，外圈命中；货箱，转运箱；跑马场围栏外部

e.en: A store is a building or part of a building where things are sold.

ex.en: They are selling them for $10 apiece at a few stores in Texas and Oklahoma.
ex.zh: 得克萨斯和俄克拉何马的一些商店正以每个$10的价钱出售它们。

ex.en: ...grocery stores.
ex.zh: …杂货店。

e.en: When you store things, you put them in a container or other place and leave them there until they are needed.

ex.en: Store the cookies in an airtight tin.
ex.zh: 把曲奇饼干存放在一个密封罐中。

e.en: Store away means the same as .

ex.en: He simply stored the tapes away.
ex.zh: 他只是把那些磁带存放起来。

e.en: When you store information, you keep it in your memory, in a file, or in a computer. 存储 (信息)

ex.en: Where in the brain do we store information about colours?
ex.zh: 我们在大脑的哪个地方存储有关颜色的信息？

d: n. 商店；仓库，储存处；（事物的）储存，储备；大量，丰富；储存的物品（stores）；军需品，补给品（stores）；（计算机的）存储器；重视，注重；待育肥的小羊（或小公牛、小母牛、小猪）
v. 贮存，储藏；（在头脑或计算机中）储存（事实或信息）
【名】 （Store）（德）施托雷（人名）

e.en: A steep slope rises at a very sharp angle and is difficult to go up.

ex.en: San Francisco is built on 40 hills and some are very steep.
ex.zh: 旧金山建在40座山丘上，其中有些非常陡峭。

e.en: 陡峭地

ex.en: The road climbs steeply, with good views of Orvieto through the trees.
ex.zh: 这条路陡直地向上延伸，透过树丛可以一览奥维多的景色。

ex.en: ...steeply terraced valleys.
ex.zh: …陡峭的梯形山谷。

e.en: A steep increase or decrease in something is a very big increase or decrease.

ex.en: Consumers are rebelling at steep price increases.
ex.zh: 消费者们正在抗议急剧的物价上涨。

e.en: 急剧地

ex.en: Unemployment is rising steeply.
ex.zh: 失业率正在急剧上升。

d: adj. （路、山等）陡峭的；（价格，需求）难以接受的，过高的；（增加或减少）急剧的，大幅度的
v. 浸泡（食物）；使沉浸，使沉湎
n. 悬崖，陡坡；用于浸泡的溶液

e.en: Someone who is vulnerable is weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

ex.en: Old people are particularly vulnerable members of our society.
ex.zh: 老人是我们社会中特别容易受到伤害的成员。

e.en: 脆弱

ex.en: David accepts his own vulnerability.
ex.zh: 戴维承认自己的脆弱。

e.en: If a person, animal, or plant is vulnerable to a disease, they are more likely to get it than other people, animals, or plants.

ex.en: People with high blood pressure are especially vulnerable to diabetes.
ex.zh: 血压高的人尤其容易患糖尿病。

e.en: 患病的可能性

ex.en: Taking long-term courses of certain medicines may increase vulnerability to infection.
ex.zh: 长期服用某些药物可能会增加受感染的几率。

d: adj. （身体或精神）脆弱的，易受伤的；（事物、人或地方）易受攻击的，易受伤害的；易患病的；（桥牌）有局方的，有身价的

e.en: A location is the place where something happens or is situated.

ex.en: The first thing he looked at was his office's location.
ex.zh: 他首先看的是他办公室的位置。

e.en: The location of someone or something is their exact position.

ex.en: She knew the exact location of The Eagle's headquarters.
ex.zh: 她知道“飞鹰”总部的准确位置。

e.en: A location is a place away from a studio where a film or part of a film is made.

ex.en: ...an art film with dozens of exotic locations.
ex.zh: …一部含有许多异国外景的艺术电影。

d: n. 位置；地点；（影视）外景拍摄地（location 的复数）

e.en: Suburban means relating to a suburb.

ex.en: ...a comfortable suburban home.
ex.zh: …一个舒适的位于郊区的家。

d: adj. 郊区的，城郊的；平淡乏味的，乡气的，平庸的
n. 郊区居民

e.en: A strategist is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to gain an advantage or to achieve success, especially in war.

ex.en: Military strategists had devised a plan that guaranteed a series of stunning victories.
ex.zh: 军事战略家们设计了一个保证了一系列惊人胜利的计划。

d: n. 战略家，军事家；策略师，战略顾问

e.en: If something proves to be true or to have a particular quality, it becomes clear after a period of time that it is true or has that quality.

ex.en: We have been accused of exaggerating before, but unfortunately all our reports proved to be true.
ex.zh: 我们曾被指责夸大其词，但遗憾的是，我们所有的报告都证明是真实的。

ex.en: In the past this process of transition has often proven difficult.
ex.zh: 在过去，这种转变过程常证明是艰难的。

e.en: If you prove that something is true, you show by means of argument or evidence that it is definitely true.

ex.en: You brought this charge. You prove it!
ex.zh: 你提出了这一指控。你来证明它！

ex.en: The results prove that regulation of the salmon farming industry is inadequate.
ex.zh: 结果证明，大马哈鱼养殖业的管理是失当的。

e.en: If you prove yourself to have a certain good quality, you show by your actions that you have it. 显示 (优点)

ex.en: Margie proved herself to be a good mother.
ex.zh: 玛吉显示了自己是个好母亲。

ex.en: As a composer he proved himself adept at large dramatic forms.
ex.zh: 作为一名作曲家，他显示出自己擅长创作大型的戏剧体裁。

d: adj. 证实的，被证明的
v. prove 的过去式和过去分词：证明，证实；检验；表现出；钻探

e.en: A pivotal role, point, or figure in something is one that is very important and affects the success of that thing.

ex.en: The elections may prove to be pivotal in Colombia's political history.
ex.zh: 这些选举也许会证明其在哥伦比亚政治史上是至关重要的。

d: adj. 中枢的，关键的；有枢轴的，像枢轴的
n. 颜色，色彩；肤色；有色人种（常用于 people of color 等短语）；颜料；脸色，气色；生动，趣味，地方色彩
vt. 给……着色，涂颜色；影响，左右；歪曲，粉饰
vi. 变色，呈现颜色
adj. 彩色的，能产生彩色的（用于名词前）

e.en: If you describe something or someone as swinging, you mean that they are lively and fashionable.

ex.en: The stuffy '50s gave way to the swinging '60s.
ex.zh: 古板乏味的 50 年代被时髦活跃的60年代所取代。

d: v. 摆动；纵身跃向；（使）弧线运动；（使）突然转向；（挥动某物）朝……打去；（使）改变意见（或情绪）；（有时略微不正当地）获得；（音乐）节奏感强；热闹（swing 的现在分词）
adj. （非正式）（人）活泼的；（地方）令人激动的；（生活方式）赶时髦的；乱交的；摇摆的
n. 性乱交

e.en: A race is a competition to see who is the fastest, for example in running, swimming, or driving. (速度的)

ex.en: The women's race was won by the only American in the field, Patti Sue Plumer.
ex.zh: 女子赛跑被田赛场上惟一的一名美国人帕蒂·休·普卢默赢得了。

e.en: If you race, you take part in a race. 参赛;

ex.en: In the 10 years I raced in Europe, 30 drivers were killed.
ex.zh: 我在欧洲参赛的10年间，有30名车手身亡。

ex.en: We raced them to the summit.
ex.zh: 我们和他们一路赛跑到最高点。

e.en: The races are a series of horse races that are held in a particular place on a particular day. People go to watch and to bet on which horse will win.

ex.en: The high point of this trip was a day at the races.
ex.zh: 这次旅行的高潮是在赛马会上度过的一天。

e.en: A race is a situation in which people or organizations compete with each other for power or control.

ex.en: The race for the White House begins in earnest today.
ex.zh: 为入主白宫而展开的竞选今天正式开始。

d: n. 竞赛（race 的复数形式）；赛马会
v. 和……竞赛；参加竞赛；急行（race 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: If you yawn, you open your mouth very wide and breathe in more air than usual, often when you are tired or when you are not interested in something.

ex.en: She yawned, and stretched lazily.
ex.zh: 她打了个哈欠，伸了个懒腰。

e.en: Yawn is also a noun.

ex.en: Rosanna stifled a huge yawn.
ex.zh: 罗莎娜忍住了一个大哈欠。

d: v. 打哈欠；（开口、洞穴等）豁开，裂开
n. 哈欠；乏味的事物（或人）

e.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort. 胜利;

ex.en: The championships proved to be a personal triumph for the coach, Dave Donovan.
ex.zh: 那些冠军称号证明了教练戴夫·多诺万的个人成就。

e.en: Triumph is a feeling of great satisfaction and pride resulting from a success or victory. (成功或胜利的)

ex.en: Her sense of triumph was short-lived.
ex.zh: 她喜悦的感觉是短暂的。

e.en: If someone or something triumphs, they gain complete success, control, or victory, often after a long or difficult struggle. 成功;

ex.en: All her life, Kelly had stuck with difficult tasks and challenges, and triumphed.
ex.zh: 凯利在一生中遭遇了种种艰巨任务与挑战，但成功了。

d: n. 巨大成功，重大胜利；（胜利或成功的）喜悦，狂喜；（成功的）典范，楷模；古罗马凯旋式
v. 获胜，成功；（因胜利或成功而）欣喜，欢跃；（古罗马将军）凯旋而归

e.en: Complacency is being complacent about a situation.

ex.en: ...a worrying level of complacency about the risks of infection from AIDS.
ex.zh: …对艾滋病感染危险的令人担忧的自满程度。

d: n. 自满，自鸣得意

e.en: The fourth item in a series is the one that you count as number four. 第4

ex.en: Last year's winner Greg Lemond of the United States is in fourth place.
ex.zh: 去年的获胜者美国的格雷格·莱蒙德现在排名第4。

e.en: A fourth is one of four equal parts of something. 1/4

ex.en: Three-fourths of the public say they favour a national referendum on the issue.
ex.zh: 3/4的公众说他们赞成就此问题举行全民公投。

d: adj. 第四的，第四个的；四分之一的
n. 第四；四分之一；某月的第四日；七月四日（美国独立日）
num. 第四
adv. 第四，在第四位（用于列举）

e.en: If someone such as an entertainer or sports personality makes a comeback, they return to their profession or sport after a period away.

ex.en: Sixties singing star Petula Clark is making a comeback.
ex.zh: 60年代的歌星佩图拉·克拉克要复出了。

e.en: If something makes a comeback, it becomes fashionable again.

ex.en: Tight fitting T-shirts are making a comeback.
ex.zh: 紧身短袖圆领T恤衫再度流行起来。

d: n. 复出，重返，东山再起，恢复（常作 make/stage a comeback）；再度流行，重新流行；在体育比赛等中反败为胜，逆转，翻盘；迅速反驳，妙答，回嘴；（英式，非正式）追索权，追责途径（多用于 have no comeback，即无从追究责任）；（畜牧/毛纺业）回交羊（其毛称回交羊毛）

e.en: If something happens all year round, it happens throughout the year.

ex.en: Many of these plants are evergreen, so you can enjoy them all year round.
ex.zh: 这些植物中有许多都是四季常青的，所以可以全年观赏。

e.en: A round of events is a series of related events, especially one which comes after or before a similar series of events. (一)

ex.en: It was agreed that another round of preliminary talks would be held in Beijing.
ex.zh: 商定了又一轮预备会谈将在北京举行。

e.en: In sports, a round is a series of games in a competition. The winners of these games go on to play in the next round, and so on, until only one player or team is left. (运动比赛的) 一轮;

ex.en: ...in the third round of the Ryder Cup.
ex.zh: …莱德杯高尔夫球赛的第三轮。

e.en: In a boxing or wrestling match, a round is one of the periods during which the boxers or wrestlers fight. (拳击或摔跤比赛的)

ex.en: He was declared the victor in the 11th round.
ex.zh: 他在第11个回合被宣布为获胜者。

d: adj. 圆形的，球形的；弧形的；微胖的，丰满的；（声音）圆润的；整数的；（钱）大量的；耿直的
adv. 旋转，环绕；周长；在周围，围绕；到处，四处；朝反方向，转过来；绕弯，向另一侧；逐一，挨个；到某地，在某地；大约；闲着；从头至尾
prep. 环绕，围绕；绕过，在另一侧；解决（问题）；在……周围，包围；在……各处；在……整个期间；适应，以……为中心
n. 轮次；（比赛的）局，场；一系列常规活动；（固定的）递送路线；巡防，巡诊；一巡（饮料）；一阵（掌声）；轮唱曲；一次射击，一发子弹；圆形物； 一片（面包），一个（三明治）

e.en: To resolve a problem, argument, or difficulty means to find a solution to it.

ex.en: We must find a way to resolve these problems before it's too late.
ex.zh: 我们必须找到一个办法去解决这些问题,不然就太晚了。

e.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

ex.en: She resolved to report the matter to the hospital's nursing supervisor.
ex.zh: 她决心把这件事向该医院的护士长汇报。

e.en: Resolve is determination to do what you have decided to do.

ex.en: So you're saying this will strengthen the American public's resolve to go to war if necessary?
ex.zh: 那么你是说，这将会坚定美国公众在必要时参战的决心？

d: v. 解决（问题或困难）；决定，下定决心；作出决议，表决；分解，转化；（使）（症状、病情）消散，消退；解析，解离；分析；（不协和音）转向协和；（当远处物体看得更清楚时）变成；（光学仪器等）分辨；辨析（图表或光谱峰值）
n. 决心，坚定的信念；正式决定，决议；决定要做的事

e.en: Structural means relating to or affecting the structure of something.

ex.en: The explosion caused little structural damage to the office towers themselves.
ex.zh: 这次爆炸对办公大楼本身几乎没有造成结构上的破坏。

e.en: 在结构上

ex.en: When we bought the house, it was structurally sound, but I decided to redecorate throughout.
ex.zh: 我们买下这个房子时，它在结构上很完好，但我决定全部重新装修。

d: adj. 建筑结构的；建筑用的；结构（或构造）上的

e.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. (精神上的)

ex.en: Smiling and laughing has actually been shown to relieve tension and stress.
ex.zh: 微笑和大笑确实已证明能缓解紧张和压力。

e.en: Tension is the feeling that is produced in a situation when people are anxious and do not trust each other, and when there is a possibility of sudden violence or conflict.

ex.en: The tension between the two countries is likely to remain.
ex.zh: 两国之间的紧张局面可能持续。

e.en: If there is a tension between forces, arguments, or influences, there are differences between them that cause difficulties.

ex.en: The film explored the tension between public duty and personal affections.
ex.zh: 该片探讨了公共义务和个人情感之间的冲突。

e.en: The tension in something such as a rope or wire is the extent to which it is stretched tight.

ex.en: As the cable wraps itself around the wheel, there is provision for adjusting the tension of the cable.
ex.zh: 缆绳绕在轮子上时就留了调整缆绳松紧的余地。

d: n. （tension 的复数形式）紧张关系，紧张局势；紧张，焦虑；冲突，矛盾；张力，拉力，拉紧程度

e.en: Lifelong means existing or happening for the whole of a person's life.

ex.en: ...her lifelong friendship with Naomi.
ex.zh: …她与娜奥米的终生友谊。

d: adj. 终身的，毕生的，终生的

e.en: Passion is strong sexual feelings toward someone.

ex.en: ...my passion for a dark-haired, slender boy named Josh.
ex.zh: …我对一个黑头发、身材修长名叫乔希的男孩的强烈的情欲。

ex.en: ...the expression of love and passion.
ex.zh: …爱与情欲的表白。

e.en: Passion is a very strong feeling about something or a strong belief in something. 强烈的感情;

ex.en: He spoke with great passion.
ex.zh: 他激情洋溢地讲话。

e.en: If you have a passion for something, you have a very strong interest in it and like it very much.

ex.en: She had a passion for gardening.
ex.zh: 她对于园艺有一份热爱。

d: n. 爱恋，情欲；激情，热情；酷爱，热衷的爱好（或活动等）；盛怒，激愤；耶稣的受难（the Passion）

e.en: Someone or something that is special is better or more important than other people or things.

ex.en: You're very special to me, darling.
ex.zh: 你对我来说很特别，亲爱的。

ex.en: My special guest will be Jerry Seinfeld.
ex.zh: 我的特邀嘉宾将是杰瑞•塞菲尔德。

e.en: Special means different from normal.

ex.en: In special cases, a husband can deduct the travel expenses of his wife who accompanies him on a business trip.
ex.zh: 在特殊情况下，丈夫可以扣除差旅中随行妻子的旅费。

ex.en: So you didn't notice anything special about him?
ex.zh: 这么说你没有注意到他的特别之处？

e.en: You use special to describe someone who is officially appointed or who has a particular position specially created for them.

ex.en: Due to his wife's illness, he returned to the State Department as special adviser to the president.
ex.zh: 由于妻子的病，他返回国务院做了总统的特派顾问。

e.en: You use special to describe something that relates to one particular person, group, or place.

ex.en: Every anxious person will have his or her own special problems or fears.
ex.zh: 每个焦虑的人都将有他/她自己特有的问题或担心。

d: adj. 特殊的，特别的；格外看重的，特别要好的；专门的，特设的；特有的，独具特色的；格外的，分外的；（主题）研究深入的；（数）特殊（矩阵）的
n. 特色菜；特别节目；特价商品，折扣商品；特派员，临时警察，特约记者；专车
【名】 （Special）（印、美、俄）史派西娅乐（人名）

e.en: Someone who is strong is healthy with good muscles and can move or carry heavy things, or do hard physical work.

ex.en: I'm not strong enough to carry him.
ex.zh: 我不够强壮，抱不动他。

e.en: Someone who is strong is confident and determined, and is not easily influenced or worried by other people.

ex.en: He is sharp and manipulative with a strong personality.
ex.zh: 他机灵且善于摆布别人，有着很强的个性。

ex.en: It's up to managers to be strong and do what they believe is right.
ex.zh: 立场坚定并做他们认为正确的事情是经理们的责任。

e.en: Strong objects or materials are not easily broken and can support a lot of weight or resist a lot of strain.

ex.en: The vacuum flask has a strong casing, which won't crack or chip.
ex.zh: 这个真空瓶有一个坚固的外壳，不会破裂。

ex.en: Glue the mirror in with a strong adhesive.
ex.zh: 用牢固的粘合剂把这面镜子粘上。

e.en: 坚固地

ex.en: The fence was very strongly built, with very large posts.
ex.zh: 这个栅栏用粗大的木桩建得非常坚固。

d: adj. 强壮的，健壮的；坚固的，结实的；坚强的，有主见的；坚定的，强烈的；有影响的，深刻的；（关系）稳固的，持久的；强有力的，有说服力的；实力强的，厉害的；有望成功的，可能性大的；精通的，擅长的；健康的；味重的；浓的；强效的；明显的，显著的；（货币）坚挺的，（行业）景气的；强劲的，高速移动的；大量的，众多的；多达……的，计有……的；强硬的，冒犯的；（语法）（动词）强变化的，强变格的；（语音学）强读式的，重读的；（物理）强，强相互作用的
adv. 强劲地，猛烈地
n. 强势群体（the strong）
【名】 （Strong）（英）斯特朗（人名）

e.en: Cash is money in the form of bills and coins rather than cheques.

ex.en: ...two thousand dollars in cash.
ex.zh: …2000美元现金。

e.en: Cash means the same as money, especially money which is immediately available.

ex.en: ...a state-owned financial-services group with plenty of cash.
ex.zh: …一家有大量现钱的国有金融机构。

e.en: any of various Chinese, Indonesian, or Indian coins of low value (中国、印度尼西亚或印度等国的)
If you cash a cheque, you exchange it at a bank for the amount of money that it is worth.

ex.en: There are similar charges if you want to cash a cheque or withdraw money at a branch other than your own.
ex.zh: 如果你在其他银行兑现支票或支取现金，将会产生差不多的手续费。

d: n. 现款，现金；金钱，资金
v. 兑现（支票）；支付现款
【名】 （Cash）（英）卡什（人名）

e.en: Cocoa is a brown powder made from the seeds of a tropical tree. It is used in making chocolate.

ex.en: The Ivory Coast became the world's leading cocoa producer.
ex.zh: 象牙海岸成了世界上领先的可可粉生产地。

e.en: Cocoa is a hot drink made from cocoa powder and milk or water.

ex.en: ...a cup of cocoa.
ex.zh: …一杯热巧克力。

d: n. 可可粉；可可豆；可可饮料；深褐色

e.en: An insect is a small animal that has six legs. Most insects have wings. Ants, flies, butterflies, and beetles are all insects.

d: n. 昆虫；类似昆虫的小动物（如蜘蛛）；卑鄙的人（insect 的复数）

e.en: Crops are plants such as wheat and potatoes that are grown in large quantities for food.

ex.en: Rice farmers here still plant and harvest their crops by hand.
ex.zh: 这里的稻农仍然用手工种植和收割庄稼。

e.en: The plants or fruits that are collected at harvest time are referred to as a crop.

ex.en: Each year it produces a fine crop of fruit.
ex.zh: 每年这里的水果收成都不错。

ex.en: The U.S. government says that this year's corn crop should be about 8 percent more than last year.
ex.zh: 美国政府称今年的玉米产量应该比去年增长约8﹪。

e.en: A crop is a short hairstyle.

ex.en: She had her long hair cut into a boyish crop.
ex.zh: 她让人把她的长发剪成了像男孩子的短发。

e.en: You can refer to a group of people or things that have appeared together as a crop of people or things. 一群 (人); 一堆 (物)

ex.en: The present crop of books and documentaries about Marilyn Monroe exploit the thirtieth anniversary of her death.
ex.zh: 现在这批有关玛丽莲·梦露的书籍和记录片是借她去世三十周年纪念之机而发行的。

d: n. 农作物（crop 的复数）；收成；（冶）切头
v. 种植（crop 的三单形式）；收割；修剪；产庄稼；裁切（照片）；突然出现（crop up）

e.en: Tropical means belonging to or typical of the tropics.

ex.en: ...tropical diseases.
ex.zh: …热带疾病。

e.en: Tropical weather is hot and damp weather typical of the tropics.

ex.en: The cool, sweet milk is just what you need in the tropical heat.
ex.zh: 清凉的甜牛奶正是你在湿热的高温中所需要的。

d: adj. 热带的，热带地区的；（天气）湿热的
n. 昆虫学家，昆虫学者

e.en: Coffee is a hot drink made with water and ground or powdered coffee beans.

ex.en: Would you like some coffee?
ex.zh: 你想喝点咖啡吗？

e.en: A coffee is a cup of coffee.

ex.en: I made a coffee.
ex.zh: 我冲了一杯咖啡。

e.en: Coffee is the roasted beans or powder from which the drink is made. 咖啡豆;

ex.en: Brazil harvested 28 million bags of coffee in 1991, the biggest crop for four years.
ex.zh: 1991年巴西收获了2800万袋咖啡豆，这是4年来的最大收成。

d: n. 咖啡（饮品）；一杯咖啡；咖啡豆或咖啡粉；咖啡色；咖啡树；（Coffee）人名，（英）科菲
n. 清除，清理，清扫工作；（棒球）第四棒，第四击球位置；暴利
adj. （棒球）第四位击球员的

e.en: If you say that something is supposed to happen, you mean that it is planned or expected. Sometimes this use suggests that the thing does not really happen in this way. 应该 (表示按计划或期望)

ex.en: He produced a hand-written list of nine men he was supposed to kill.
ex.zh: 他手写列出一份他应该杀的9个男子的名单。

e.en: If something was supposed to happen, it was planned or intended to happen, but did not in fact happen.

ex.en: He was supposed to go back to Bergen on the last bus, but of course the accident prevented him.
ex.zh: 他本应坐最后一班公共汽车回卑尔根，但当然，这场意外拦住了他。

e.en: If you say that something is supposed to be true, you mean that people say it is true but you do not know for certain that it is true.

ex.en: "The Whipping Block" has never been published, but it's supposed to be a really good poem.
ex.zh: 《鞭笞刑具》从未发表，但据说它是一首相当好的诗。

e.en: You can use "be supposed to" to express annoyance at someone's ideas, or because something is not happening in the right way. 还 (表示恼火或失望)

ex.en: You're supposed to be my friend!
ex.zh: 你还是我的朋友呢！

d: adj. 假定的，据说的；应当的；预期的；被允许的；坚信的
v. 预期，推断；假定；认为（suppose 的过去式和过去分词形式）
n. 佛蒙特州（美国州名，略作 VT）
n. 山普伦（法国探险家 Samuel de Champlain）

e.en: A lake is a large area of fresh water, surrounded by land.

ex.en: They can go fishing in the lake.
ex.zh: 他们可以去湖里钓鱼。

e.en: a bright pigment used in textile dyeing and printing inks, produced by the combination of an organic colouring matter with an inorganic compound, usually a metallic salt, oxide, or hydroxide 色淀;

d: n. 湖，湖泊；大量的液体；（液体）一滩；沉淀色料；胭脂红
v. （使）血球溶解
【名】 （Lake）（德、塞、瑞典）拉克，（英）莱克（人名）

e.en: Slime is a thick, wet substance which covers a surface or comes from the bodies of animals such as snails. (动物体表分泌的) 黏液;

ex.en: He swam down and retrieved his glasses from the muck and slime at the bottom of the pond.
ex.zh: 他潜下水去，从池塘底部的烂泥污物中找回了眼镜。

d: n. 黏液；烂泥；史莱姆（游戏、奇幻中的黏胶状虚构生物）
vt. 涂泥，用黏液或烂泥涂抹、弄脏
vi. 变粘滑，变得黏滑

e.en: A billion is a thousand million. 10

ex.en: The Ethiopian foreign debt stands at 3 billion dollars.
ex.zh: 埃塞俄比亚的外债达30亿美元。

e.en: If you talk about billions of people or things, you mean that there is a very large number of them but you do not know or do not want to say exactly how many.

ex.en: Biological systems have been doing this for billions of years.
ex.zh: 生物系统亿万年来都在这样做。

e.en: You can also use billions as a pronoun.

ex.en: He thought that it must be worth billions.
ex.zh: 他认为它一定值亿万元。

d: num. 十亿；万亿
n. 十亿；亿万，大量（billions）
【名】 （Billion）（法）比利翁（人名）

e.en: Something that is clean is free from dirt or unwanted marks.

ex.en: The subway is efficient and spotlessly clean.
ex.zh: 地铁快，而且一尘不染。

ex.en: Tiled kitchen floors are easy to keep clean.
ex.zh: 铺了地砖的厨房地面容易保持清洁。

e.en: You say that people or animals are clean when they keep themselves or their surroundings clean.

ex.en: We like pigs, they're very clean.
ex.zh: 我们喜欢猪，它们很爱干净。

e.en: A clean fuel or chemical process does not create many harmful or polluting substances.

ex.en: Fans of electric cars say they are clean, quiet, and economical.
ex.zh: 电动车爱好者说电动车无污染，无噪音，而且经济。

e.en: If you describe something such as a book, joke, or lifestyle as clean, you think that they are not sexually immoral or offensive. 纯洁的;

ex.en: They're trying to show clean, wholesome, decent movies.
ex.zh: 他们在努力放纯洁、健康、正派的电影。

ex.en: Flirting is good clean fun.
ex.zh: 调情是谑而不虐。

d: adj. 洁净的，干净的；讲卫生的，爱干净的；无有害物的，无污染的；清醇的，清新的；无污点的，清白的；公正的，遵守规则的；不私藏违禁品的；没吸毒的，没喝酒的；纯洁的，正派的；文明的，无色情的；平滑的，平整的；迅速彻底的；（行动）干净利落的；空白的，未写过的；（文件）无错误的；（木材）无树节的
v. （使）清洁，清理；变干净；清扫，做清洁工；干洗；（烹饪前）清除（动物）内脏
n. 清洁，清扫，打扫
adv. 彻底地，完全地；干净地，纯洁地

e.en: If someone keeps or is kept in a particular state, they remain in it. 保持 (特定状态)

ex.en: The noise kept him awake.
ex.zh: 噪音使他一直醒着。

ex.en: People had to burn these trees to keep warm during harsh winters.
ex.zh: 在寒冷的冬天，人们得靠烧这些树保暖。

e.en: If you keep or you are kept in a particular position or place, you remain in it.

ex.en: Keep away from the doors while the train is moving.
ex.zh: 列车运行时请远离车门。

ex.en: He kept his head down, hiding his features.
ex.zh: 他一直低着头藏住脸。

e.en: If you keep off something or keep away from it, you avoid it. If you keep out of something, you avoid getting involved in it.

ex.en: I managed to stick to the diet and keep off sweet foods.
ex.zh: 我设法坚持节食，不吃甜食。

e.en: If you keep doing something, you do it repeatedly or continue to do it.

ex.en: I keep forgetting it's December.
ex.zh: 我总是忘了现在是12月份。

d: v. （keep 的第三人称单数）保留；维持；存放；（keeps doing sth.）继续，不断，老是做某事
n. （keep 的复数形式）城堡主楼；监狱牢房；（矿井）罐笼座；盖子

e.en: Algae are plants with no stems or leaves that grow in water or on damp surfaces.

ex.en: ...an effort to control toxic algae in Green Lake.
ex.zh: …控制绿湖里有毒水藻的努力。

d: n. 水藻，海藻

e.en: A bloom is the flower on a plant.

ex.en: The sweet fragrance of the white blooms makes this climber a favourite.
ex.zh: 白色花朵散发出的甜香使这株藤蔓成了宠儿。

e.en: A plant or tree that is in bloom has flowers on it.

ex.en: ...a pink climbing rose in full bloom.
ex.zh: …一朵盛开的粉色攀缘玫瑰。

e.en: When a plant or tree blooms, it produces flowers. When a flower blooms, it opens. 开花; (花)

ex.en: This plant blooms between May and June.
ex.zh: 这种植物在五六月间开花。

e.en: If someone or something blooms, they develop good, attractive, or successful qualities.

ex.en: Not many economies bloomed in 1990, least of all gold exporters like Australia.
ex.zh: 没有几个国家的经济在1990年蓬勃发展，尤其是像澳大利亚这样的金矿出口国。

d: n. （常指供观赏的）花（bloom 的复数）；水华，藻华（藻类等浮游生物大量繁殖形成的生态现象，常作 algal blooms 或 water blooms）
v. （bloom 的第三人称单数）开花；变得健康；焕发光彩；发亮，发光；繁荣，蓬勃发展；给（透镜）敷膜；把（金属）轧成坯块

e.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

ex.en: They're still investigating the accident.
ex.zh: 他们还在调查这个事故。

e.en: 调查

ex.en: He ordered an investigation into the affair.
ex.zh: 他下令对此事进行调查。

d: v. 侦察（某事）；调查（某人）；研究

e.en: A legacy is money or property which someone leaves to you when they die.

ex.en: You could make a real difference to someone's life by leaving them a generous legacy.
ex.zh: 你留给某人一大笔遗产就可以真正改变他的生活。

e.en: A legacy of an event or period of history is something which is a direct result of it and which continues to exist after it is over.

ex.en: ...a programme to overcome the legacy of inequality and injustice created by Apartheid.
ex.zh: …解决种族隔离引起的不平等和不公正等遗留问题的一个计划。

d: n. 遗产，遗赠物；遗留问题，后遗症
adj. （软件或硬件）已过时但因使用范围广而难以替代的

e.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behaviour. 反对的;

ex.en: Many people felt he would be hostile to the idea of foreign intervention.
ex.zh: 许多人觉得他会反对外来干预。

ex.en: The West has gradually relaxed its hostile attitude to this influential state.
ex.zh: 西方对这个有影响力的国家的敌对态度已趋缓和。

e.en: Someone who is hostile is unfriendly and aggressive.

ex.en: Drinking may make a person feel relaxed and happy, or it may make her hostile, violent, or depressed.
ex.zh: 喝酒可以使一个人感到放松和愉快，也可以让人变得不友善、粗暴或沮丧。

e.en: Hostile situations and conditions make it difficult for you to achieve something. (环境和条件等)

ex.en: ...some of the most hostile climatic conditions in the world.
ex.zh: …世界上最不利的一些气候条件。

e.en: A hostile takeover bid is one that is opposed by the company that is being bid for. (收购投标)

ex.en: Soon after he arrived, Kingfisher launched a hostile bid for Dixons.
ex.zh: 金费希尔到任之后不久就开始了对迪克森斯公司的恶意收购投标。

d: adj. 敌对的，怀敌意的；强烈反对的；敌人的，敌方的；艰苦的，不利的；不受（被购公司）欢迎的
n. 敌对分子

e.en: You use likely to indicate that something is probably the case or will probably happen in a particular situation.

ex.en: Experts say a "yes" vote is still the likely outcome.
ex.zh: 专家们表示投赞成票仍是可能的结果。

ex.en: If this is your first baby, it's far more likely that you'll get to the hospital too early.
ex.zh: 如果这是你的第一胎，你就非常有可能会太早到医院。

e.en: Likely is also an adverb.

ex.en: Profit will most likely have risen by about $25 million.
ex.zh: 利润将极有可能增长约2500万美元。

e.en: If someone or something is likely to do a particular thing, they will very probably do it.

ex.en: In the meantime the war of nerves seems likely to continue.
ex.zh: 同时心理战似乎很有可能要继续下去。

d: adj. 可能发生的；似乎合适的，仿佛恰当的；似乎真实的，可信的；看上去精力充沛（或有能力）的
adv. 大概，很可能

e.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

ex.en: Federal leaders continued their efforts to secure a ceasefire.
ex.zh: 联邦政府的领导人们继续他们争取停火的努力。

e.en: If you secure a place, you make it safe from harm or attack. 使 (某地)

ex.en: Staff withdrew from the main part of the prison but secured the perimeter.
ex.zh: 工作人员从监狱的主体区域撤了出来，但封锁了监狱四周。

e.en: A secure place is tightly locked or well protected, so that people cannot enter it or leave it. 锁牢了的;

ex.en: We'll make sure our home is as secure as possible from now on.
ex.zh: 我们将从现在起确保我们的家尽可能安全。

e.en: 锁牢了地;

ex.en: He locked the heavy door securely and kept the key in his pocket.
ex.zh: 他锁牢了那扇重门把钥匙放在了他的口袋里。

d: adj. 稳固的，可靠的；严密把守的，牢固的；安全的，稳妥的；（对自己和自己的能力）有自信的；感到有保障的，没有顾虑的；固定住的，系牢的；秘密的
v. （尤指经过努力而）获得，得到；使安全，保护；缚牢，将（某物）固定；确保，保证；为（债务或贷款）作抵押，作保；（外科）压迫（血管）止血；停止工作；船抛锚

e.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

ex.en: The president rebuked the House and Senate for not passing those bills within 100 days.
ex.zh: 总统谴责参众两院未在100天内通过那些法案。

e.en: Rebuke is also a noun.

ex.en: His statements drew a stinging rebuke from the chairman.
ex.zh: 他的申明受到了主席严厉的谴责。

d: v. 斥责，指责
n. 指责，叱责，训斥

e.en: Something that is massive is very large in size, quantity, or extent. (尺寸、数量、规模)

ex.en: There was evidence of massive fraud.
ex.zh: 有证据表明是巨额欺诈。

ex.en: ...massive air attacks.
ex.zh: …大规模的空袭。

e.en: 非常大地

ex.en: ...a massively popular game.
ex.zh: …一种非常受欢迎的游戏。

e.en: If you describe a medical condition as massive, you mean that it is extremely serious.

ex.en: He died six weeks later of a massive heart attack.
ex.zh: 他6周后死于一次严重的心脏病发作。

d: adj. 大而重的，结实的；非常严重的；大量的，大规模的；特别成功的，非常有影响的；（岩石或地层）均匀构造的，大块的；（矿物）外观非晶质的；极好的，非常妙的
n. （某一地区的年轻人群体）嬉蹦音乐迷（或丛林爵士音乐迷）

e.en: To transform something into something else means to change or convert it into that thing. 使改变;

ex.en: Your metabolic rate is the speed at which your body transforms food into energy.
ex.zh: 你的新陈代谢率就是你身体将食物转换成能量的速度。

e.en: 改变;

ex.en: Norah made plans for the transformation of an attic room into a study.
ex.zh: 诺拉制订了将阁楼间改造为书房的几个方案。

e.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and suddenly so that they are much better or more attractive. 彻底改变 (使更好、更有吸引力)

ex.en: Industrialization transformed the world.
ex.zh: 工业化彻底改变了世界。

e.en: 彻底改变

ex.en: In the last five years he's undergone a personal transformation.
ex.zh: 在过去的5年里，他完全变了个人。

d: v. （使）发生巨变，改造，转型；发生巨大变化；对（数学实体）进行变换；将（细胞）转化（transform 的现在分词）；变换（电流）的电压

e.en: When you turn or when you turn part of your body, you move your body or part of your body so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction. 转动 (身体);

ex.en: He turned abruptly and walked away.
ex.zh: 他突然转身走开了。

ex.en: He sighed, turning away and surveying the sea.
ex.zh: 他叹了口气，转过身去，眺望着大海。

e.en: Turn around means the same as turn.

ex.en: I felt a tapping on my shoulder and I turned around.
ex.zh: 我感到有人拍了一下我的肩膀，于是转过身去。

e.en: When you turn something, you move it so that it is facing in a different or opposite direction, or is in a very different position.

ex.en: They turned their telescopes toward other nearby galaxies.
ex.zh: 他们把望远镜转向附近的其他星系。

ex.en: She had turned the bedside chair to face the door.
ex.zh: 她已经把那张床边的椅子转过来对着门。

e.en: When something such as a wheel turns, or when you turn it, it continually moves around in a particular direction.

ex.en: As the wheel turned, the potter shaped the clay.
ex.zh: 随着轮子的转动，制陶工人给黏土塑形。

d: adj. 被转动的；翻转的；变质的；车削的
v. 转动，转身，转向；使变成，变成（turn 的过去式和过去分词）

e.en: Something that is blue is the colour of the sky on a sunny day. 蓝色的;

ex.en: There were swallows in the cloudless blue sky.
ex.zh: 燕子在无云的蓝天上飞翔。

ex.en: She fixed her pale blue eyes on her father's.
ex.zh: 她用那蔚蓝色的双眼盯着父亲的眼睛。

e.en: The blues is a type of music which was developed by African American musicians in the southern United States. It is characterized by a slow tempo and a strong rhythm.

ex.en: Can white girls sing the blues?
ex.zh: 白人女孩会唱蓝调吗？

e.en: If you are feeling blue, you are feeling sad or depressed, often when there is no particular reason.

ex.en: There's no earthly reason for me to feel so blue.
ex.zh: 我完全没有理由感到如此低落。

e.en: If a U.S. state is described as blue, it means that the majority of its residents vote for the Democratic Party in elections, especially in the presidential elections. 蓝色阵营的 (美国总统大选时民主党的主要选区)

ex.en: This issue could drive an even bigger wedge between the red and blue states.
ex.zh: 这个问题可能会进一步造成红色选区和蓝色选区之间的不和。

d: adj. 蓝色的；忧郁的，沮丧的； 保守的，守旧的；（笑话、故事等）黄色的，色情的；（由于冷或呼吸困难）发青的，青紫的
n. 天蓝色，蓝色；天空，大海；（剑桥或牛津大学的）校队运动员，蓝色荣誉者；红头发者；错误，纰漏；争论，殴打；近生的牛排
v. （使）变成蓝色；用蓝色漂白剂洗（白色衣服）；挥霍，乱花（钱财）
【名】 （Blue）（英、美、加、澳、新）布卢（人名）

e.en: An opportunity is a situation in which it is possible for you to do something that you want to do.

ex.en: I had an opportunity to go to New York and study.
ex.zh: 我曾有过一个去纽约学习的机会。

ex.en: ...equal opportunities in employment.
ex.zh: …平等的就业机会。

d: n. 时机，机会
n. 移民，迁徙；（计算机系统的）改变，（程序或硬件的）迁移，转移

e.en: A league is a group of people, clubs, or countries that have joined together for a particular purpose, or because they share a common interest. 联盟;

ex.en: ...the League of Nations.
ex.zh: …国际联盟。

e.en: A league is a group of teams that play the same sport or activity against each other. (各种运动队的)

ex.en: ...the American League series between the Boston Red Sox and World Champion Oakland Athletics.
ex.zh: …波士顿红袜队和世界冠军奥克兰运动家队之间的美国职业棒球联盟系列赛。

e.en: You use league to make comparisons between different people or things, especially in terms of their quality. 级别;

ex.en: Her success has taken her out of my league.
ex.zh: 她的成功使她和我不再处于同一个等级上了。

e.en: If you say that someone is in league with another person to do something bad, you mean that they are working together to do that thing. (与某人)

ex.en: There is no evidence that the broker was in league with the fraudulent vendor.
ex.zh: 没有代理人和奸商相勾结的证据。

d: n. 联盟，同盟；（体育项目）联合会，社团；联赛；级别，水平；里格（旧时长度单位，约等于5公里）
v. （与……）组成联盟，加入联盟
【名】 （League）（英）利格（人名）

e.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it.

ex.en: Tormented by her ignorance, Jenny delves into her mother's past.
ex.zh: 珍妮为自己不了解真相而痛苦，她开始深入调查母亲的过去。

d: v. 钻研，探究（常作 delve into）；伸手翻找（常作 delve into/in）；挖掘（古语）
n. 穴，洞（古语/方言）；Delve（英语姓氏“德尔夫”）

e.en: The demographics of a place or society are the statistics relating to the people who live there.

ex.en: ...the changing demographics of the United States.
ex.zh: …变化的美国人口统计数据。

e.en: In business, a demographic is a group of people in a society, especially people in a particular age group.

ex.en: The station has won more listeners in the 25-39 demographic.
ex.zh: 这个电台吸引了更多25-39岁年龄段的听众。

d: adj. 人口的，人口统计的
n. （具有某种特征的）群体；人口统计数据

e.en: A story is a description of imaginary people and events, which is written or told in order to entertain. (虚构的)

ex.en: The second story in the book is titled "The Scholar."
ex.zh: 这本书中的第2个故事标题为《学者》。

ex.en: I shall tell you a story about four little rabbits.
ex.zh: 我将给你讲个关于4只小兔子的故事。

e.en: A story is a description of an event or something that happened to someone, especially a spoken description of it. (尤指口头的)

ex.en: The parents all shared interesting stories about their children.
ex.zh: 那些家长们都会互相讲起有关自己孩子的趣事。

e.en: The story of something is a description of all the important things that have happened to it since it began.

ex.en: ...the story of the women's movement.
ex.zh: …妇女运动的史话。

e.en: If someone invents a story, they give a false explanation or account of something.

ex.en: He invented some story about a cousin.
ex.zh: 他们编造了一些关于一位表亲的谎话。

d: n. （真实或虚构的）故事，叙述；新闻报道；（尤指口头的）叙述，描述；谎言，虚假的借口；（书籍、电影、戏剧等的）情节；纪事，史话；楼层；情况；（公司的）商业前景，商业现状；谣言，传闻；一种测量单位（1 story 等于 3.3 米）
v. 用历史故事画装饰
【名】 （Story）斯托里（人名）

e.en: Rugby or rugby football is a game played by two teams using an oval ball. Players try to score points by carrying the ball to their opponents' end of the field, or by kicking it over a bar fixed between two posts. 英式橄榄球 (运动)

d: n. 英式橄榄球
【名】 （Rugby）（英、澳、俄、印、马）拉格比（人名）

e.en: Something that is slow moves, happens, or is done without much speed.

ex.en: The traffic is heavy and slow.
ex.zh: 车很多，走得慢。

ex.en: Electric whisks should be used on a slow speed.
ex.zh: 电子打蛋器应该慢速运转。

e.en: 缓慢地

ex.en: He spoke slowly and deliberately.
ex.zh: 他说得缓慢而慎重。

e.en: In informal English, slower is used to mean "at a slower speed" and slowest is used to mean "at the slowest speed." In nonstandard English, slow is used to mean "with little speed."

ex.en: I began to walk slower and slower.
ex.zh: 我开始走得越来越慢。

e.en: Something that is slow takes a long time.

ex.en: The distribution of passports has been a slow process.
ex.zh: 颁发护照一直是个漫长的过程。

d: adj. （移动，运行）低速的，缓慢的；慢速的，低速的；耗时的，太慢的；迟缓的，慢吞吞的；（钟表）慢的；迟钝的，愚笨的；（胶片）曝光慢的；（镜头）小孔径的；（生意）清淡的，不景气的；不曲折的，乏味的，无趣的；（火，烤箱）小火的，弱火的；（球场或地面）软的，阻球的，奔跑困难的
v. （使）放慢速度，（使）减速；（使）降低，（使）减少；（生活，工作）放松
adv. 低速地，缓慢地
【名】 （Slow）（英）斯洛（人名）

e.en: When there is a coup, a group of people seize power in a country.

ex.en: ...a military coup.
ex.zh: …一次军事政变。

e.en: A coup is an achievement which is thought to be especially good because it was very difficult.

ex.en: The sale is a big coup for the auction house.
ex.zh: 这次拍卖额对该拍卖行而言是极为难得的成就。

d: n. coup 的复数形式：政变，即通过非法或暴力手段突然夺取政权的行动；重大成就，即极为难得或影响突出的成功。

e.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

ex.en: Stories abound about when he was in charge.
ex.zh: 他负责时传闻很多。

d: v. 大量存在，有许多；富于，盛产（abound with/in sth.）

e.en: A festival is an organized series of events such as musical concerts or drama productions.

ex.en: Many towns hold their own summer festivals of music, theatre, and dance.
ex.zh: 很多城市都举办自己的夏季音乐、戏剧和舞蹈节。

e.en: A festival is a day or time of the year when people do not go to work or school and celebrate some special event, often a religious event.

ex.en: Shavuot is a two-day festival for Orthodox Jews.
ex.zh: 五旬节是正统犹太教教民为期两天的节日。

d: n. 活动节期，纪念活动；节日，节庆
adj. 节日的，喜庆的

e.en: An exhibition is a public event at which pictures, sculptures, or other objects of interest are displayed, for example at a museum or art gallery.

ex.en: ...an exhibition of expressionist art.
ex.zh: …一场印象主义艺术展览会。

e.en: An exhibition of a particular skilful activity is a display or example of it that people notice or admire. (技能的)

ex.en: He responded in champion's style by treating the fans to an exhibition of power and speed.
ex.zh: 他回报以冠军的风格，为仰慕者们呈现了一次力量与速度的展示。

d: n. exhibition 的复数形式：展览，展示会；（技能、品质等的）展示，表现

e.en: The skyline is the line or shape that is formed where the sky meets buildings or the land. (建筑物等在天空映衬下的)

ex.en: The village church dominates the skyline.
ex.zh: 那座乡村教堂独绝天际。

d: n. （建筑物或群山在天空映衬下的）轮廓线

e.en: If you open something such as a door, window, or lid, or if it opens, its position is changed so that it no longer covers a hole or gap.

ex.en: He opened the window and looked out.
ex.zh: 他打开窗户往外看。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open window.
ex.zh: …一扇开着的窗户。

e.en: If you open something such as a bottle, box, parcel, or envelope, you move, remove, or cut part of it so you can take out what is inside.

ex.en: I opened the letter.
ex.zh: 我拆开了那封信。

e.en: Open is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...an open bottle of milk.
ex.zh: …一瓶打开的牛奶。

d: v. （open 的第三人称单数）开，打开（门、窗、盖子等）；开封，开启（信件、包裹、瓶罐等）；展开，张开（书、伞、地图、手臂等）；开业，开幕，开始；（计算机）打开文件或程序；（常与 up 连用）开辟，使（机会、可能性等）变得可用
n. （电工）断路，电路意外断开（open 的复数）
abbr. 高音（等于 treble）

e.en: Western means in or from the west of a region, state, or country.

ex.en: ...hand-made rugs from Western and Central Asia.
ex.zh: …来自西亚和中亚的手工地毯。

e.en: Western is used to describe things, people, ideas, or ways of life that come from or are associated with the United States, Canada, and the countries of Western, Northern, and Southern Europe. 西方国家的 (指与北美、西欧、北欧、南欧各国相关的)

ex.en: Mexico had the support of the big western governments.
ex.zh: 墨西哥得到了西方大国政府的支持。

e.en: A western is a book or movie about life in the western United States and territories in the nineteenth century, especially the lives of cowboys. (有关19世纪美国西部的生活，尤指牛仔生活的) 西部小说;

ex.en: John Agar starred in westerns, war films and low-budget science fiction pictures.
ex.zh: 约翰·阿加出演过西部片、战争片和低投入的科幻片。

d: adj. 西方的，西部的；（Western）西方国家的（指与北美、西欧、北欧、南欧各国相关的）；美国西部的
n. （关于19世纪美国西部生活，尤指牛仔生活的）西部电影、西部小说；西方人
【名】 （Western）（英）韦斯顿（人名）
n. 数据中心，资料处理中心（等于 data center，即集中安放服务器、存储和网络设备并配备供电、冷却等支持系统的场所）

e.en: in the US National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations System (美国)
e.zh: 全国证券交易商自动报价系统协会

d: abbr. 纳斯达克股票交易所，全国证券交易商自动报价系统协会（National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotation）

e.en: When a man shaves, he removes the hair from his face using a razor or shaver so that his face is smooth. 刮 (脸);

ex.en: He took a bath and shaved before dinner.
ex.zh: 他在晚餐前洗了澡并刮了脸。

ex.en: He had shaved his face until it was smooth.
ex.zh: 他把脸刮到光滑为止。

e.en: Shave is also a noun. 剃须;

ex.en: He never seemed to need a shave.
ex.zh: 他似乎从不需要刮脸。

e.en: 剃须;

ex.en: ...a range of shaving products.
ex.zh: …一系列剃须产品。

e.en: If you shave off part of a piece of wood or other material, you cut very thin pieces from it. 削掉;

ex.en: I set the log on the ground and shaved off the bark.
ex.zh: 我把原木放在地上，然后刨掉树皮。

d: v. shave 的过去式和过去分词：剃须，刮脸；擦过，掠过，几乎碰到（如汽车擦边通过）；shave off 的过去式和过去分词：削掉，刨掉，切成薄片；少量削减，略微降低（成本、价格、纪录等）
adj. 剃光的，刮净的

e.en: The bourse of a European city or region is its stock exchange. (欧洲的)

d: n. 证券交易所（尤指欧洲城市或地区的）；（Bourse）巴黎证券交易所；（Bourse）人名（法）布尔斯

e.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

ex.en: ...advertisements aimed at curbing the spread of AIDS.
ex.zh: …旨在抑制爱滋病蔓延的广告。

e.en: Curb is also a noun. 控制;

ex.en: He called for much stricter curbs on immigration.
ex.zh: 他呼吁对移民实行更为严格的限制。

e.en: If you curb an emotion or your behaviour, you keep it under control. 控制 (脾气、行为等)

ex.en: He curbed his temper.
ex.zh: 他控制住了自己的脾气。

e.en: a swelling on the leg of a horse, below the point of the hock, usually caused by a sprain (马腿上由扭伤导致的)

d: n. curb 的名词复数：限制，抑制，约束（常与 on 连用）；路缘石，路边（美国英语，英国英语作 kerbs）；勒马绳（马具）
v. curb 的第三人称单数：控制，限制，勒住

e.en: Ripples are little waves on the surface of water caused by the wind or by something moving in or on the water.

ex.en: Gleaming ripples cut the lake's surface.
ex.zh: 闪着微光的涟漪打破了湖面的平静。

e.en: When the surface of an area of water ripples or when something ripples it, a number of little waves appear on it. 使泛起涟漪;

ex.en: You throw a pebble in a pool and it ripples.
ex.zh: 你把卵石扔进水池里，水面就泛起涟漪。

e.en: If something such as a feeling ripples over someone's body, it moves across it or through it. (感觉等)

ex.en: A chill shiver rippled over his skin.
ex.zh: 一阵寒颤传遍了他全身。

e.en: If an event causes ripples, its effects gradually spread, causing several other events to happen one after the other.

ex.en: If Brazil defaults on its foreign debt, it will cause ripples throughout the world.
ex.zh: 如果巴西不还外债的话，这将在全世界引起连锁反应。

d: n. 涟漪；（外观或运动）如波纹的东西；（声音的）传播起伏，（感情的）逐渐扩散；连锁反应；彩条冰淇淋；表面张力波；脉动
v. （使）如波浪般起伏；（情绪）波动，（声音）荡漾；发出潺潺声
【名】 （Ripple）（英）里普尔（人名）

e.en: If you worry, you keep thinking about problems that you have or about unpleasant things that might happen.

ex.en: Don't worry, your luggage will come on afterwards by taxi.
ex.zh: 不要担心，你的行李随后将由出租车送到。

ex.en: I worry about her constantly.
ex.zh: 我一直在为她担心。

e.en: If someone or something worries you, they make you anxious because you keep thinking about problems or unpleasant things that might be connected with them.

ex.en: I'm still in the early days of my recovery and that worries me.
ex.zh: 我仍处于恢复期的初始阶段，这使我担心。

e.en: If someone or something does not worry you, you do not dislike them or you are not annoyed by them. 使烦恼 (用于否定句中)

ex.en: The cold doesn't worry me.
ex.zh: 寒冷不会使我烦恼。

e.en: Worry is the state or feeling of anxiety and unhappiness caused by the problems that you have or by thinking about unpleasant things that might happen.

ex.en: Modern American life is full of worry: the job, the kids, money, the stock market.
ex.zh: 现代美国生活充满了忧虑：工作、孩子、金钱、股市。

d: n. 忧虑，担心；烦恼，令人担忧的事（worries 为 worry 的复数形式）
v. 担心；使担心，使烦恼，困扰（worries 为 worry 的第三人称单数形式）
int. （非正式）别担心；没问题；不用客气

e.en: The value of something such as a quality, attitude, or method is its importance or usefulness. If you place a particular value on something, that is the importance or usefulness you think it has. 重要性;

ex.en: The value of this work experience should not be underestimated.
ex.zh: 这项工作经验的重要性不应该被低估。

e.en: If something is of value, it is useful or important. If it is of no value, it has no usefulness or importance. 重要的/

ex.en: This weekend course will be of value to everyone interested in the Pilgrim Route.
ex.zh: 这个周末课程对于每一个对朝圣路线感兴趣的人来说都将是重要的。

e.en: If you value something or someone, you think that they are important and you appreciate them.

ex.en: I value the opinion of my husband and we agree on most things.
ex.zh: 我重视我丈夫的意见，而且我们在大多数事情上看法一致。

e.en: The value of something is how much money it is worth.

ex.en: The value of his investment has risen by more than $50,000.
ex.zh: 他的投资价值已经增长$50000多。

d: n. 价值；等值，等价，物有所值；重要性，有用性；重要特点，显著特点；价值观（values）；（数学中的）值；（音乐中的）时值（指音符的时间长度）；（词或其他语言单位）确切意义；（色彩）明暗度
v. 尊重，重视；给……估价，给……定价
n. 阿卜杜勒（人名）

e.en: The Senate is the smaller and more important of the two parts of the legislature in some US states and in some countries, for example, the United States and Australia. (美国、澳大利亚等国的)

ex.en: The Senate is expected to pass the bill shortly.
ex.zh: 预计参议院将很快通过这项议案。

e.en: The Senate is the governing council at some universities. (某些大学的)

ex.en: By the time I was vice chancellor, the Senate had become a much larger and a much more democratic body.
ex.zh: 到我做副校长的那个时候，大学评议会已经成为一个更大、更民主的机构了。

d: n. 参议院；大学理事会，大学评议会；（古罗马的）元老院

e.en: Preliminary activities or discussions take place at the beginning of an event, often as a form of preparation.

ex.en: Preliminary results show the Republican Party with 11 percent of the vote.
ex.zh: 初步结果显示共和党得到11%的选票。

e.en: A preliminary is something that you do at the beginning of an activity, often as a form of preparation. (程序性或礼节性的)

ex.en: You all know why I am here. So I won't waste time on preliminaries.
ex.zh: 你们都知道我为什么在这里。所以我就不浪费时间讲客套话了。

d: adj. 初步的，预备的
n. 初步行动，准备工作；预赛，预试
n. 密歇根人

e.en: Isolation is the state of feeling alone and without friends or help.

ex.en: Many deaf people have feelings of isolation and loneliness.
ex.zh: 许多失聪的人有孤独和寂寞的感觉。

e.en: If something is considered in isolation from other things that it is connected with, it is considered separately, and those other things are not considered.

ex.en: Punishment cannot, therefore, be discussed in isolation from social and political theory.
ex.zh: 因此，对惩罚进行讨论不能脱离社会和政治理论。

e.en: If someone does something in isolation, they do it without other people present or without their help.

ex.en: Malcolm, for instance, works in isolation but I have no doubts about his abilities.
ex.zh: 例如，马尔科姆虽然一个人独立工作，但我丝毫不怀疑他的能力。

d: n. 隔离，孤立；孤独；绝缘；（尤指对混合物或微生物的）离析

e.en: Royal is used to indicate that something is connected with a king, queen, or emperor, or their family. A royal person is a king, queen, or emperor, or a member of their family.

ex.en: ...an invitation to a royal garden party.
ex.zh: …一张参加皇家花园聚会的请帖。

e.en: Royal is used in the names of institutions or organizations that are officially appointed or supported by a member of a royal family.

ex.en: ...the Royal Academy of Music.
ex.zh: …皇家音乐学院。

e.en: Members of the royal family are sometimes referred to as royals.

ex.en: The royals have always been patrons of charities pulling in large donations.
ex.zh: 王室成员一直都是慈善机构的资助人，注入大量捐赠。

d: adj. 国王的，女王的，王室的；（用于机构或组织名称）皇家的 ；盛大的，隆重的；（用于强调某人或某物极度糟糕）极其的，极度的
n. 王室成员；（鸣钟术）敲奉十口钟的变换响

e.en: If you consider something as a unit, you consider it as a single, complete thing.

ex.en: Agriculture was based in the past on the family as a unit.
ex.zh: 农业过去以一个家庭单元为基础。

e.en: A unit is a group of people who work together at a specific job, often in a particular place. (工作)

ex.en: ...the environmental research unit.
ex.zh: …环境研究单位。

e.en: A unit is a group within an armed force or police force, whose members fight or work together or carry out a particular task.

ex.en: ...a firefighting unit.
ex.zh: …一个消防分队。

e.en: A unit is a small machine which has a particular function, often part of a larger machine.

ex.en: The unit plugs into any TV set.
ex.zh: 该部件可接入任何电视机。

d: n. 单位；一件（商品）；（公寓楼的）单元；部件，元件；（家具的）组合件，配件；科，室，部门；班组，小队；（课本）单元；（计量）单位；个位数；警车；学习量；股份单位

e.en: A specialist is a person who has a particular skill or knows a lot about a particular subject.

ex.en: Peckham, himself a cancer specialist, is well aware of the wide variations in medical practice.
ex.zh: 佩卡姆本人就是个癌症专家，非常清楚医疗实践中的广泛差异。

d: n. 专家；专科医生；美国陆军专业人员（高于一等兵低于下士的军衔）
adj. 专业的；专门的；专家的

e.en: Pesticides are chemicals that farmers put on their crops to kill harmful insects.

d: n. pesticide 的复数

e.en: If you prioritize something, you treat it as more important than other things.

ex.en: Prioritize your own wants rather than constantly thinking about others.
ex.zh: 优先考虑你自己的需要，而不要总想着别人。

e.en: If you prioritize the tasks that you have to do, you decide which are the most important and do them first. 确定 (任务)

ex.en: Make lists of what to do and prioritize your tasks.
ex.zh: 把你要做的事情列出来，确定任务的轻重缓急。

d: v. 按优先顺序列出；优先考虑（处理）
n. 紫面叶猴
n. （Maha）人名；（英）马哈，玛哈（女名）；（罗、捷、老、泰、阿拉伯）玛哈（女名），马哈

e.en: An incumbent is someone who holds an official post at a particular time.

ex.en: In general, incumbents have a 94 percent chance of being re-elected.
ex.zh: 一般情况下，现任官员有94%的几率会再次当选。

e.en: Incumbent is also an adjective.

ex.en: ...the only candidate who defeated an incumbent senator.
ex.zh: …惟一击败了现任参议员的候选人。

e.en: If it is incumbent on or upon you to do something, it is your duty or responsibility to do it.

ex.en: She felt it was incumbent on herself to act immediately.
ex.zh: 她感到立即采取行动是她义不容辞的责任。

d: adj. 在职的，现任的；职责所在的，义不容辞的；（公司）占市场份额大的
n. 在职者，现任官员；教区牧师，领圣俸者

e.en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.

ex.en: His guerrillas defeated the colonial army in 1954.
ex.zh: 他的游击队在1954年打败了殖民军。

e.en: If a proposal or motion in a debate is defeated, more people vote against it than for it. (以多数票)

ex.en: The bill was defeated with support from only two congressmen.
ex.zh: 由于只得到两位议员的支持，那个议案被否决了。

e.en: If a task or a problem defeats you, it is so difficult that you cannot do it or solve it.

ex.en: The book he most wanted to write was the one which nearly defeated him.
ex.zh: 他最想写的书恰恰是几乎难倒他的那一本。

e.en: To defeat an action or plan means to cause it to fail.

ex.en: The navy played a limited but significant role in defeating the rebellion.
ex.zh: 在平息叛乱中海军起了有限但却重要的作用。

d: v. 击败，挫败（defeat 的过去式和过去分词）
adj. 被击败的；受挫的，泄气的
n. 常作 the defeated：被击败的人（们）；失败者
n. 城市的
n. 男低音歌手；低音，低音部；低音吉他，低音提琴；鲈鱼；椴树
adj. 低音的，低声调的
【名】 （Bass）（英、法、德、俄、罗、捷、马里、匈）巴斯（人名）

e.en: a member of a Thai people of Myanmar

d: n. 凯伦（人名）；克伦邦（缅甸邦名）
n. 拉曼（姓氏）；拉曼（印度物理学家，也译喇曼）；（物理学）作定语：拉曼（用于拉曼效应、拉曼散射、拉曼光谱等复合术语）

e.en: Someone who is progressive or has progressive ideas has modern ideas about how things should be done, rather than traditional ones.

ex.en: ...a progressive businessman who had voted for Roosevelt in 1932 and 1936.
ex.zh: …在1932年和1936年投票支持罗斯福的一位进步商人。

ex.en: Willan was able to point to the progressive changes he had already introduced.
ex.zh: 威兰能够指出他已经带来的有进步意义的变化。

e.en: A progressive is someone who is progressive.

ex.en: The Republicans were deeply split between progressives and conservatives.
ex.zh: 共和党进步派和保守派之间分歧很大。

e.en: A progressive change happens gradually over a period of time.

ex.en: One prominent symptom of the disease is progressive loss of memory.
ex.zh: 这种病的一个突出症状是记忆的逐步丧失。

e.en: 逐步地

ex.en: Her symptoms became progressively worse.
ex.zh: 她的症状逐步恶化。

d: adj. 进步的，先进的；逐步发生的，逐步发展的；向前移动的；（音乐）现代的，新潮的；（税制，税种）累进的；（动词）进行式的；（纸牌游戏，舞蹈）搭档轮换的
n. 进步分子，改革派人士；进行时（或体）；（印刷）分色打样

e.en: A backlash against a tendency or recent development in society or politics is a sudden, strong reaction against it. (对政治或社会变化的)

ex.en: ...the male backlash against feminism.
ex.zh: …男性对女权主义的强烈反应。

d: n. （尤指对政治或社会事件的）强烈反应，反对；（机械的）反冲，反作用；（机械部件间的）间隙，轮齿隙

e.en: If someone or something overtakes a competitor, they become more successful than them.

ex.en: Lung cancer has now overtaken breast cancer as a cause of death for women in the U.S.
ex.zh: 肺癌作为一种美国女性死亡原因现已超过了乳腺癌。

e.en: If a feeling overtakes you, it affects you very strongly.

ex.en: Something like panic overtook me in a flood.
ex.zh: 一种类似恐慌的感觉在一次洪水中压倒了我。

e.en: If you overtake, or overtake a vehicle or a person that is ahead of you and moving in the same direction, you pass them.

d: v. 追上， 赶上并超过（汽车或人）；（发展或增长）超越，超过；突然降临于，意外发生在；（情感等）压倒，使难以承受
n. 斯特拉（女子名，也译“斯黛拉”“史黛拉”等）；弗兰克·斯特拉（Frank Stella，美国极简主义画家）；时代啤酒（Stella Artois 的简称，比利时啤酒品牌）

e.en: electronvolt

d: abbr. 预期节省值（expected value saved）；省油真空开关（Economy Vacuum Switch）

e.en: If people discuss something, they talk about it, often in order to reach a decision.

ex.en: I will be discussing the situation with colleagues tomorrow.
ex.zh: 我将于明天和同事们讨论这个情况。

e.en: If you discuss something, you write or talk about it in detail.

ex.en: I will discuss the role of diet in cancer prevention in Chapter 7.
ex.zh: 我将在第7章详述饮食在癌症预防中的作用。

d: v. discuss 的第三人称单数形式；讨论，谈论：就某个话题或问题交换意见、观点；论述，探讨：详细阐述或分析某个主题。
n. 丰田汽车公司（日本汽车制造商及品牌）；丰田车（丰田品牌生产的车辆）；丰田市（日本爱知县城市）

e.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem. (重要的) 法案;

ex.en: Local initiatives to help young people have been inadequate.
ex.zh: 当地对年轻人的扶助法案一直不够完善。

e.en: In a fight or contest, if you have the initiative, you are in a better position than your opponents to decide what to do next.

ex.en: We have the initiative; we intend to keep it.
ex.zh: 我们拥有主动权；我们想要保持主动权。

e.en: If you have initiative, you have the ability to decide what to do next and to do it, without needing other people to tell you what to do.

ex.en: She was disappointed by his lack of initiative.
ex.zh: 她对他缺乏主动性感到失望。

e.en: An initiative is a political procedure in which a group of citizens propose a new law or a change to the law, which all voters can then vote on.

ex.en: If they reject or ignore the initiative, the public will vote on it in November.
ex.zh: 如果他们拒绝或无视公民立法提案程序，公众将于11月对它进行投票表决。

d: n. 倡议，举措，方案；（美国英语）公民立法提案程序；initiative 的复数（主动性，积极性，首创精神；主动权，先手；创始，第一步，率先行动等义项见 initiative）

e.en: If something overturns or if you overturn it, it turns upside down or on its side. 打翻;

ex.en: The motorcycle veered out of control, overturned and smashed into a wall.
ex.zh: 摩托车转向失去了控制，翻倒在地，然后猛地撞到一面墙上。

ex.en: Alex jumped up so violently that he overturned his glass of wine.
ex.zh: 亚历克斯跃起得太猛，以至于打翻了他的那杯葡萄酒。

e.en: If someone in authority overturns a legal decision, they officially decide that that decision is incorrect or not valid.

ex.en: When the courts overturned his decision, he backed down.
ex.zh: 当法院推翻了他的决定时，他让步了。

d: v. （使）翻倒，（使）倾覆；推翻，撤销（判决等）；颠覆，破坏（政府或体系）；在英国大选中因获得多数席位而获胜
n. 颠覆，革命；（尤指水温分层的湖水每年两次的）湖水对流
n. 密苏里（美国州名，位于美国中西部、密西西比河西岸）；密苏里河（美国最长的河流，发源于蒙大拿州，在圣路易斯附近注入密西西比河）
adj. 更难的；更努力的；更坚固的（hard 的比较级）
adv. 更努力地；更困难地；更辛苦地；更接近地；更猛烈地；更牢固地（hard 的比较级）
n. （Harder）（英、德、瑞典）哈德（人名）
adj．公民主导的：由普通公民发起、组织或领导的，而非政府或其他官方机构。

e.en: When children, animals, or adults play, they spend time doing enjoyable things, such as using toys and taking part in games.

ex.en: ...invite the children over to play.
ex.zh: …邀请孩子们过来玩。

ex.en: They played in the little garden.
ex.zh: 他们在小花园里玩耍。

e.en: Play is also a noun.

ex.en: ...a few hours of play until the babysitter puts them to bed.
ex.zh: …直到保姆让他们上床睡觉之前的几小时的玩耍。

e.en: When you play a sport, game, or match, you take part in it. 参加 (体育运动、游戏、比赛等)

ex.en: While the twins played cards, Leona sat reading.
ex.zh: 那对双胞胎玩牌的时候，利昂娜坐着看书。

ex.en: I used to play basketball.
ex.zh: 我过去常打篮球。

e.en: Play is also a noun. (对运动、游戏、比赛等的)

ex.en: They've got more exciting players and a more exciting style of play.
ex.zh: 他们有更精彩的选手和更精彩的比赛风格。

d: v. 玩，玩耍；捉弄，戏弄；摆弄，玩弄；耍弄，愚弄；不认真地干，闹（play at）；参加（游戏、比赛等）；与……比赛；击，踢（球）；出（牌），走（棋子）；派（某人）上场；（在球队中）打（某位置）；扮演，演出；佯装，假装；假扮……玩；（戏剧或电影）上演，上映；演奏，弹奏；（使）播放；闪烁，浮现；（以某方式）行事，做事；（使）发射（或喷射、照射）；赌，投机；被接受，被认可；（喻）合作，买某人的账；寄于；让（上钩的鱼）挣扎得筋疲力尽；（板球场状况对比赛）产生影响
n. 剧本，戏剧；游戏，玩乐；比赛；比赛中的动作；（运动或游戏中的）打法，走法；活动空间，间隙；影响，作用；闪烁，变幻；玩笑；（音频或图像的）播放次数，播放时长；播放（功能）；（报纸或电视的）关注；（对文字的）巧用，妙用
【名】 （Play）（法、瑞典）普莱（人名）

e.en: Pointing is a way of filling in the gaps between the bricks or stones on the outside of a building so that the surface becomes sealed.

ex.en: He did the pointing in the stonework himself.
ex.zh: 他自己做了石结构的勾缝。

e.en: Pointing is the cement between the bricks or stones in a wall.

d: v. 指向；表明（point 的现在分词）
n. （勾墙砖、石缝用的）灰泥，灰浆；勾缝

e.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

ex.en: ...the need to rectify what is an obvious injustice.
ex.zh: …纠正明显不公行为的必要性。

e.en: If you describe something that someone says as obvious, you are being critical of it because you think it is unnecessary or shows lack of imagination.

ex.en: Such an explanation seems too simple, and too obvious.
ex.zh: 这样的一个解释似乎太简单而且太没新意。

e.en: If you say that someone is stating the obvious, you mean that they are saying something that everyone already knows and understands.

d: adj. 明显的，显然的；明确表示的，毫不掩饰的；平淡无奇的，缺乏想象力的；合情合理的，当然的

e.en: Something that is variable changes quite often, and there usually seems to be no fixed pattern to these changes.

ex.en: The potassium content of foodstuffs is very variable.
ex.zh: 食品中钾的含量是多变的。

e.en: 可变性

ex.en: There's a great deal of variability between individuals.
ex.zh: 个体之间存在着很大的可变性。

e.en: A variable is a factor that can change in quality, quantity, or size, that you have to take into account in a situation.

ex.en: Decisions could be made on the basis of price, delivery dates, after-sales service or any other variable.
ex.zh: 决定可以基于价格、送货日期、售后服务或是任何其他可变因素而做出。

d: n. variable 的复数：[数] 变量（或其表示符号）；可变因素

e.en: Tight clothes or shoes are small and fit closely to your body. (衣服或鞋子)

ex.en: She walked off the plane in a miniskirt and tight top.
ex.zh: 她穿着迷你裙和紧身上衣走下飞机。

e.en: 紧贴地

ex.en: He buttoned his collar tightly round his thick neck.
ex.zh: 他把衣领紧紧地扣在自己的粗脖子上。

e.en: If you hold someone or something tight, you hold them firmly and securely.

ex.en: She just fell into my arms, clutching me tight for a moment.
ex.zh: 她就倒在了我的怀里，一时间紧紧地抓着我。

ex.en: Just hold tight to my hand and follow along.
ex.zh: 只要紧紧地抓住我的手，跟着我。

e.en: Tight is also an adjective.

ex.en: As he and Hannah passed through the gate he kept a tight hold of her arm.
ex.zh: 他和汉娜经过大门时，他紧抓着她的胳膊。

d: adj. 牢固的，不松动的；紧身的；拉紧的，绷紧的；严厉的，严格的；紧的，拮据的；密集的，挤满的；亲密的，紧密的；急转的，陡的；憋闷的，不适的；紧张的，生气的；势均力敌的；困难的，棘手的；准确的，紧凑的；吝啬的；醉醺醺的；结实的
adv. 紧紧地，牢固地
【名】 （Tight）泰特（人名）

e.en: When you wait for something or someone, you spend some time doing very little, because you cannot act until that thing happens or that person arrives.

ex.en: I walk to a street corner and wait for the school bus.
ex.zh: 我走到一个街道拐角处等校车。

ex.en: I waited to see how she responded.
ex.zh: 我等着看她如何反应。

e.en: 等候

ex.en: The waiting became almost unbearable.
ex.zh: 等待变得几乎令人难以忍受了。

e.en: A wait is a period of time in which you do very little, before something happens or before you can do something.

ex.en: ...the four-hour wait for the organizers to declare the result.
ex.zh: …组织者们宣布结果前4个小时的等待。

e.en: If something is waiting for you, it is ready for you to use, have, or do. 等 (你) 使用; 等 (你)

ex.en: There'll be a car waiting for you.
ex.zh: 将会有辆车等着你。

ex.en: When we came home we had a meal waiting for us.
ex.zh: 我们回到家时，有一顿饭正等着我们去享用。

d: v. 等候；盼望，期待；推迟，延缓；（已备好）可处理，可取用；（用于鼓励或威胁）等着；（用于打断讲话）等一下，慢着；服侍，招待
n. 等待，等候的时间；（城镇）官方乐队（waits）
【名】 （Wait）（英）韦特，（捷）魏特（人名）

e.en: The winner of a prize, race, or competition is the person, animal, or thing that wins it.

ex.en: She will present the trophies to the award winners.
ex.zh: 她将给获胜者颁奖。

d: n. 获胜的人（或队、动物等），优胜者；（体育比赛中）致胜的一分，制胜的进球；可能成功的人（或事物），极好的人（或事物），成功的人（或事物）；获益者，赢家；（桥牌）能赢的牌
【名】 （Winner）（美、德、英）温纳（人名）

e.en: A lender is a person or an institution that lends money to people.

ex.en: ...the six leading mortgage lenders.
ex.zh: …6家最大的抵押贷款机构。

d: n. 放款人，出借方，贷方（lender 的复数）；（Lenders）人名；（德）伦德斯

e.en: If someone wakes up with a hangover, they feel sick and have a headache because they drank a lot of alcohol the night before. 宿醉 (过量饮酒后的恶心、头痛反应)

ex.en: It was a great night and I had a massive hangover.
ex.zh: 那是个愉快的夜晚，可第二天我出现了严重的宿醉。

e.en: Something that is a hangover from the past is an idea or way of behaving which people used to have in the past but which people no longer generally have. 遗留观念;

ex.en: As a hangover from rationing, they mixed butter and margarine.
ex.zh: 作为配给制的遗留习俗，他们把黄油与人造黄油混在一起吃。

d: n. 宿醉（尤指过量饮酒后次日出现的头痛、恶心等不适反应）；残留物，遗物，遗留观念或习俗（常与 from 连用，指从过去留存下来的事物或残余影响）

e.en: Wild animals or plants live or grow in natural surroundings and are not taken care of by people. (动物或植物)

ex.en: We saw two more wild cats creeping toward us in the darkness.
ex.zh: 我们看见还有两只野猫在黑暗中向我们爬来。

e.en: Wild land is natural and is not used by people.

ex.en: ...a wild area of woods and lakes.
ex.zh: …一片荒芜的森林和湖泊区域。

e.en: The wilds of a place are the natural areas that are far away from cities and towns.

ex.en: They went canoeing in the wilds of Canada.
ex.zh: 他们在加拿大的荒野地区划独木舟。

e.en: Wild is used to describe the weather or the sea when it is stormy. (天气或海面)

ex.en: The wild weather did not deter some people from taking an unseasonable dip in the sea.
ex.zh: 狂风暴雨的天气并没有使一些不合时宜地到海里游泳的人却步。

d: adj. （动植物）自然生长的，野生的；（土地）无人烟的，未开垦的；（人）未开化的，野蛮的；不受控制的，放荡的；暴风雨的，狂暴的；（做事或说话）轻率的，缺乏根据的；激动人心的；满腔热情的，十分热衷的；感情强烈的（尤指生气、高兴或激动）；（表情、外表等）走神的，不专注的；特别的，怪异的；（纸牌）百搭的；嘈杂混乱的
adv. 自然地，不受控制地
n. 偏远地区，人烟稀少的地区；自然环境，野生状态
v.  野蛮对待，残酷对待

e.en: African means belonging or relating to the continent of Africa, or to its countries or people. 非洲的;

ex.en: ...the African continent.
ex.zh: …非洲大陆。

ex.en: ...African countries.
ex.zh: …非洲国家。

e.en: African means belonging or relating to black people who come from Africa. 属于非洲人的;

ex.en: ...traditional African culture.
ex.zh: …非洲传统文化。

ex.en: ...dance music with African roots.
ex.zh: …源自非洲的舞曲。

e.en: African is used to describe someone, usually a black person, who comes from Africa.

ex.en: ...African women.
ex.zh: …非洲妇女。

e.en: An African is someone who is African.

ex.en: Fish is a staple in the diet of many Africans.
ex.zh: 鱼是很多非洲人饮食中的主食。

d: n. 非洲人（African 的复数）

e.en: You can refer to a child as a kid.

ex.en: They've got three kids.
ex.zh: 他们有三个孩子。

e.en: If you are kidding, you are saying something that is not really true, as a joke.

ex.en: I'm not kidding, Frank. There's a cow out there, just standing around.
ex.zh: 我不是在开玩笑，弗兰克。那边有一头奶牛，就在那里站着呢。

ex.en: I'm just kidding.
ex.zh: 我只是在开玩笑。

e.en: If you kid someone, you tease them.

ex.en: He liked to kid Ingrid a lot.
ex.zh: 他很喜欢戏弄英格里德。

e.en: If people kid themselves, they allow themselves to believe something that is not true because they wish that it was true. 欺骗 (自己)

ex.en: We're kidding ourselves, Bill. We're not winning, we're not even doing well.
ex.zh: 我们是在欺骗自己，比尔。我们不会赢的。我们做得甚至都不好。

d: n. （kid 的复数）小孩，孩子；年轻人；小山羊；小山羊皮革；（尤指水手食堂盛格罗酒或配额食物用的）小木桶
v. （kid 的第三人称单数）开玩笑，拿……开玩笑，（善意地）取笑；（山羊）产羔；欺骗，常与 oneself 连用时表示“欺骗自己”

e.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team of people in a particular sport.

ex.en: Tony Woodcock has joined the team as coach.
ex.zh: 托尼•伍德科克已经作为教练加入了队伍。

e.en: A coach is a person who is in charge of a sports team. (体育队的)

ex.en: ...the women's football coach at Rowan University.
ex.zh: …罗恩大学女子足球队的领队。

e.en: A coach is someone who gives people special teaching in a particular subject, especially in order to prepare them for an examination. (针对某科目，尤指进行考前指导的)

ex.en: What you need is a drama coach.
ex.zh: 你需要的是一位戏剧指导。

e.en: A coach is an enclosed vehicle with four wheels which is pulled by horses, and in which people used to travel. Coaches are still used for ceremonial events in some countries, such as Britain. (用于外出旅行或仪式活动的)

ex.en: ...a coach pulled by six black horses.
ex.zh: …一辆6匹黑马拉的4轮马车。

d: n. 教练；辅导教师；长途汽车；火车车厢（coach 的复数形式）
v. 训练，指导（coach 的第三人称单数形式）

e.en: A billionaire is an extremely rich person who has money or property worth at least a thousand million dollars.

d: n. 亿万富翁（billionaire 的复数）

e.en: A rich person has a lot of money or valuable possessions.

ex.en: You're going to be a very rich man.
ex.zh: 你将成为一个非常富的人。

e.en: The rich are rich people.

ex.en: This is a system in which the rich are taken care of and the poor are left to suffer.
ex.zh: 这是个富人受关照，而穷人遭罪的制度。

e.en: Riches are valuable possessions or large amounts of money.

ex.en: An Olympic gold medal can lead to untold riches for an athlete.
ex.zh: 一枚奥运金牌能为一名运动员带来数不尽的财富。

e.en: A rich country has a strong economy and produces a lot of wealth, so many people who live there have a high standard of living.

ex.en: There is hunger in many parts of the world, even in rich countries.
ex.zh: 饥饿在世界许多地方都存在，甚至在一些富国。

d: adj. 有钱的，富有的；富含……的，丰富的；非常有趣的，丰富多彩的；（食物）油腻的；（色彩、气味）浓郁的，（声音）浑厚的；肥沃的，丰产的；华丽昂贵的；（指某人的评论或批评）荒唐的，可笑的；值钱的，生财的；（内燃机内的混合燃料）可燃性成分高的
【名】 （Rich）（丹）里克，（捷）里赫，（英、西）里奇，（葡、法）里什（人名）

e.en: Super is used before adjectives to indicate that something has a lot of a quality.

ex.en: I'm going to Greece in the summer so I've got to be super slim.
ex.zh: 我这个夏天要去希腊，所以我得变得超级苗条才行。

e.en: Super is used before nouns to indicate that something is larger, better, or more advanced than similar things.

ex.en: Winners of each regional will advance to the super regionals.
ex.zh: 每个地区分支机构的获胜者们将会晋级为超级地区性人物。

e.en: Some people use super to mean very nice or very good.

ex.en: We had a super time.
ex.zh: 我们度过了一段超好的时光。

ex.en: That's a super idea.
ex.zh: 那是个超好的想法。

d: adj. 极好的，极优秀的；超级的
adv. 极其，非常
n. （英国的）警官，（美国的）警长；（大楼的）管理人；主管，上司；过磷酸盐，过磷酸钙；特级品，特优产品；跑龙套的角色，临时演员
【名】 （Super）休珀（人名）
vt.使动摇，使不稳定（destabilise 的过去式和过去分词）
四年的
四年制的

e.en: The Web is a computer system that links documents and pictures into a database that is stored in computers in many different parts of the world and that people everywhere can use. It is also referred to as the World Wide Web.

ex.en: The handbook is available on the Web.
ex.zh: 这本手册互联网上有。

ex.en: She recommended the service on her Web journal after trying it out.
ex.zh: 在经过试用后，她在自己的网络杂志中推荐了这项服务。

e.en: A web is a complicated pattern of connections or relationships, sometimes considered as an obstacle or a danger.

ex.en: He's forced to untangle a complex web of financial dealings.
ex.zh: 他被迫去理顺一大堆错综复杂的金融交易。

e.en: A web is the thin net made by a spider from a sticky substance that it produces in its body.

ex.en: ...the spider's web in the window.
ex.zh: …窗户上的蜘蛛网。

d: n. 网；骨架肋板；网状物（web 的复数）
vt. 危及，危害，使……陷入危险（等于 jeopardize，英式拼写）
